He also said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah does not cease looking at them and their sins continue to fall off them until they part.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah (Exalted is His Glory) is not describable. And how can He be described while Allah (Exalted is His Glory) has said, 'And they did not estimate Allah with the estimation that is due to Him.' Thus, He is greater than any description said to Him. The Prophet (peace be upon him) is also beyond description; how can such a servant be described while Allah (Exalted is His Glory) has elevated and drawn him near to Himself, making obedience to him on this earth like obedience to Himself! 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, accept it; and from whatever he forbids you, keep back.' Whoever has obeyed this (Prophet) has in fact obeyed Me, and whoever has disobeyed him has disobeyed Me? And He delegated to him? We, too, are beyond description; for how can those from whom Allah has removed impurity, which is polytheism, be described? The believer is also beyond description. When a believer meets his brother in faith and shakes hands with him, Allah continues to gaze at them whilst sins fall off them like leaves falling off a tree.
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When two believers meet, one hundred mercies are showered between them—ninety nine of these go to the one who loves the other more.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: That which the creatures are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of Allah (Exalted is His Glory), that is what they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him); and just as they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Messenger (peace be upon him), so too they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Imam; and just as they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Imam, so too they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the believer.

From Safwan al-Jammal, he said: I heard him saying: Whenever two believers meet and shake hands, the more faithful of them is the one who loves the other more. And no two believers ever meet, shake hands, remember Allah, and then part, except that Allah forgives them, if Allah wills.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Gabriel descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, your Lord says: One who humiliates My believing servant has confronted Me with war. And My believing servant draws closer to Me with nothing better than fulfilling the obligatory acts; and indeed, he performs supererogatory acts for Me until I love him. So, when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his leg with which he walks. And I did not hesitate in anything that I am to do as I hesitate in the death of My believing servant; he experiences death and I dislike his suffering. And among the believers there are some who will not be well except by destitution, and if I were to surround them with wealth, it would be evil for them; and among them are some who are not well except in affluence, and if I were to surround them with poverty, it would be evil for them. And indeed, My servant asks Me to fulfill a need, but I deny him that because of what is best for him.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah (Exalted is His Glory) said: One who humiliates My friend has prepared for a battle with Me. And My servant has never drawn closer to Me with anything better than what I have made obligatory on him; and indeed, he draws closer to Me with supererogatory actions until I love him. And when I love him, I become his ears that he hears with, his eyes that he sees with, his hands that he grasps with and his legs that he walks with. If he calls upon Me, I answer him; and if he asks from Me, I grant him. There is nothing I hesitate in doing like in taking the life of a believer. He dislikes death and I dislike causing him pain.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If the sins of a believer were as much as the sand of the desert or the froth of the sea, Allah would forgive them for him; so do not become bold (in sinning).
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A believer dies with his sins forgiven; by Allah, all of them.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him in Makkah: 'I have a request.' He said: 'Meet me in Makkah.' So I met him and said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I have a request.' He said: 'Meet me in Mina.' So I met him in Mina and said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I have a request.' He said: 'Present your request.' I said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I committed a sin that is between me and Allah, which no one else knows of, and I hold you in too high esteem to reveal it before you.' He said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will manifest Himself to His believing servant and make him stand accountable for his sins one by one, then He will pardon them for him. Neither an archangel nor a prophet ever sent will know of this. And in another tradition: He will conceal from him his sins that he dislikes to be made aware of, then He will say to his evil deeds: Become good deeds. And that is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "So those are they of whom Allah changes their evil deeds to good ones."'

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) A disbeliever calls out (for his needs) and Allah says, 'Hasten his wish to him,' out of aversion for his voice. And a believer supplicates for his needs and Allah says, 'Delay his wish,' out of a longing for his voice. So, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will say (to the believer), 'You asked Me for such-and-such and I delayed answering you; so, your reward (for the delay) is such-and-such.' A believer will at that time wish any of his supplications had been never answered in the world when he sees how excellent the reward is.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when a believer calls upon Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, He answers him. I stared at him in amazement at this. He said: Indeed, Allah is Bountiful (Wide) to His creatures.

And from Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from one of the scholars, that he said: When a believer dies, his two angels ascend (to the heavens) and say, 'O Lord, so-and-so has passed away.' So He (Allah) says (to them), 'Descend and pray beside his grave, glorifying and magnifying Me until the Day of Resurrection, and record what you do for him.'
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A believer's dream is a part of seventy parts of prophethood, and amongst them are some who have been given one-third.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah loves a servant, He safeguards him, places his richness within his soul, and places his reward before his eyes. And when He despises him, He leaves him to his own soul, and places his poverty before his eyes.

Ibn Abi al-Bilad, and from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A servant supplicates, and the Lord, Exalted and Majestic, says: 'O Gabriel, withhold his need,' so He suspends it between the heaven and the earth, yearning for his voice.
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created the essence of the believer from the essence of the Prophets, so it will never become wicked.
From Safwan al-Jammal, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The death of a believer leaves a gap in religion.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The deed of a believer goes forth and makes preparations for him in Paradise just like a man who sends ahead his servant to furnish and spread out things for him. Then he recited: 'And whoever does good, they prepare (good) for their own souls.'
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah drives away the believer from what He dislikes just as a man drives away a stray camel that does not belong to his flock.
And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah puts His Hand in between and it is shaken by the one who loves the other the most.
And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Just as there is nothing to gain with polytheism, so there is nothing to lose with faith.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I did not hesitate in anything that I am to do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant, because I love to meet him while he dislikes death; so I conceal it from him. And if there were on the earth only one believer, he would suffice for Me instead of all My creation, and I would make for him from his faith a companion so that he would not need anyone in it.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Any believer who dies in isolation on the earth, and his mourners are absent from him, the plains of the earth where he used to worship Allah weep for him, his garments weep for him, the portals of the heavens through which his deeds used to ascend weep for him, and the two angels appointed to him cry for him.
And from one of them (peace be upon him) he said: Verily, the sins of a believer are forgiven, so the believer makes a fresh start; but this is only for the people of faith.

From Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created a group of creatures whom He kept away from trials; He created them in well-being, gave them life in well-being, caused them to die in well-being, and entered them into Paradise in well-being.
From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believers are brothers from one father and mother; when one of them is struck, the others lose sleep.
And from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) that he said: The believer is the brother of the believer like one single body, when a part of it is lost, the rest of the body becomes affected.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The believer is the brother of the believer like one body; when one part of it suffers, the pain of that is found in the rest of its body, for their souls are from the Spirit of Allah (Exalted is He), and indeed the soul of the believer has a stronger connection to the Spirit of Allah than the connection of the sun's ray to it.

Jabir reported from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I sighed in his presence, then said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, a concern afflicts me without an actual calamity befalling me, or a matter descends upon me such that my family recognizes it on my face and my friend recognizes it.' He said: 'Yes, O Jabir.' I asked: 'What is that, O son of Allah's Messenger?' He said: 'What will you do with it?' I said: 'I love to know it.' He said: 'O Jabir, indeed Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) created the believers from the clay of Paradise and caused their souls to pass through the breeze of Paradise. Thus, the believer is the brother of the believer in terms of his father and mother. So when one of those souls in any of the lands is afflicted by something, these souls grieve for it, because they are of it.'

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The believer is the brother of the believer in terms of father and mother, because Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) created the believers from the earth of Paradise and brought about their forms from the breeze of Paradise, for that reason they are full brothers.

From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Souls are grouped in batches; they meet and recognize each other like horses recognize one another. Those that are familiar with each other unite, and those that are unfamiliar differ. And if a believer were to enter a mosque filled with many people, among whom there was only one other believer, his soul would incline towards that believer until he sat beside him.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Nay, by Allah! A believer is not a true believer ever until he acts as the body of his brother; when one vein in it is struck, it evokes the rest of the body.

And from him (peace be upon him) he said: For every thing there is a thing that gives it comfort; and a believer finds rest in the company of his fellow believer just as a bird finds comfort amongst its own kind.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believers in their reverence, affection and compassion for each other are like one body; when it falls ill, it affects all over with restlessness and fever.

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ḥātim ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated to us saying, 'We were informed by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥammād (from Ḥammād) from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār who said, 'One of our companions narrated to me from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said,' It is sufficient as a flaw in a person that he sees those faults in others which he is blind to [and disregards] in himself, or that he should fault other people for a matter which is also in himself, and which he cannot turn away from; and that he disturbs the one who sits with him by [discussing] that which does not concern [or benefit] him.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan al-Jammal, from al-Fadl who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Blessed is every servant who is unknown (or sleeps in obscurity), who recognizes people before they recognize him.'

Three - Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Who will guarantee for me four [things] in return for four houses in Paradise? Spend [in charity] and do not fear poverty, treat people fairly with yourself, spread peace throughout the world, and abandon argumentation even if you are right.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say,' One who knows the appropriate position of his speech in relation to his intellect reduces his speech about that which does not concern him. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Beware of arguing with a deluded individual, for indeed every deluded individual has an argument that lasts only until his time comes to an end, and when his time is up, his delusion burns him with the Fire.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Dāwūd, from Abū Shaybah al-Zuhrī, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him) who said: The worst servant is he who is of two faces and two tongues, who compliments his brother in his presence and devours him in his absence; when he is given, he envies him, and when he is wronged, he abandons him.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abū ʿAmmār Bayyāʿ al-Aksiyah, from al-Zaydī, from Abū Arākah who said: I heard ʿAlī (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, Allah has servants whose hearts have been broken by the awe of Allah, so they abstain from speech; and indeed they are eloquent, articulate, wise, and noble. They race towards Him with pure actions, not considering their many [good] deeds to be much, nor being satisfied with [only] little. They consider themselves to be vile, while they are truly like the sagacious and virtuous ones.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān and al-Ḥusayn ibn Mukhāriq, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of that for which an apology is required, for indeed the believer does not do wrong and does not apologize, while the hypocrite does wrong every day and apologizes for it.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Shall I not inform you about the worst of you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Those who go about spreading slander, those who cause separation between loved ones, and those who endeavor to find faults in one who is innocent.'

Fadalah ibn Nizar narrated from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One who refrains from [impugning] the honor of people, Allah will pardon him [and protect his reputation] on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever restrains his anger from the people, Allah will restrain His anger from him on the Day of Resurrection.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Haddha', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Modesty is part of faith, and faith leads one into Paradise. Immodesty is part of depravity, and depravity leads one into the Fire.

Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Speech is of three types: the profitable, the sound, and the detrimental. As for the profitable, it is that which mentions Allah. As for the sound, it is that wherein what Allah likes is spoken. And as for the detrimental, it is that in which one engages in idle talk about people.'

Uthman ibn Isa from Umayr ibn Adhinah from Sulayman ibn Qays said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Verily Allah has forbidden Paradise to every foul-mouthed, shameless person who does not care about what he utters and what is said to him. For if you investigate him, you will not find him except as a babler or a partner of Satan. A man asked: O Messenger of Allah, are there really people who are partners of Satan? He replied: Do you not read the statement of Allah: 'And partner with them in their wealth and children'? Then it was asked: And are there [really] some people who do not care about what they utter or what is said to them? He said: Yes. He who exposes himself to the people and speaks [negatively] about them while he knows that they will not leave him [and will react against what he has said]; such a person does not care about what he utters and what is said to utters and what is said to him.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Hamzah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: Verily, the good deed that brings the quickest reward is kindness (al-barr), and the evil deed that brings the quickest punishment is unjust aggression (al-baghy). And it is sufficient as a flaw for a person to perceive in others the faults of which he is blind regarding himself, and to censure people for that which he is incapable of abandoning, and to disturb his companion by discussing that which does not concern him.

Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Khālid, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Advise me, O Messenger of Allah!' He replied, 'Yes, I advise you to guard that which is between your legs.'

Uthman ibn Isa narrated from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him) that one of your companions is backbiting you, so beware of him. He said, 'O Lord, I do not know him; inform me of him so that I may know him.' He replied, 'O Musa, you found fault with him for his backbiting, and you wish Me to be a backbiter!' He said, 'Then what should I do, O Lord?' Allah, the Exalted, replied, 'Divide your companions into groups of ten, then cast lots between them; the lot will fall on the group of ten in which he is. Then divide them again and cast lots between them, and the lot will fall on him.' He said, 'When the man saw that the lots were being drawn, he stood up and said, O Messenger of Allah, I am your companion! By Allah, I will never repeat it again.'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Once, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was with ʿĀʾishah, a man sought permission to enter. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What a bad brother of the tribe [he is]!' ʿĀʾishah stood up and entered the inner chamber, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) allowed the man to enter. As he came in, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went to meet him and spoke to him until he had finished his talk and left. So ʿĀʾishah said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned him in that way [negatively], yet you still welcomed him with your face and a smile?' So he said to her, 'Verily among the worst servants of Allah is one whose company is disliked because of his foul-mouthedness.'

Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Paradise is forbidden to three: to the one who puts others under obligation, to the backbiter, and to the habitual drinker of wine.'

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, attributing it to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said: "And what will cast people into the Fire except the harvests of their tongues?"

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father say: 'Part of the beauty of a person's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from 'Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah loves the modest, the clement, the independent, the chaste. And indeed, Allah hates the shameless, the obscene, the scrounger, the importuner.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, who said: I was sitting with Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) when he sent one of his non-Arab servant boys on an errand to a person. The boy left and then returned, so Abū ʿAbdillāh began asking him for the answer/explanation, but the young lad did not understand him, and this happened a number of times. He (the narrator) said: When I saw that his speech did not change and he was not able to understand, I thought that Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) would get angry on him. He said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) looked at him sternly and then said: 'By Allah, even if you are unable to speak with your tongue, you are not unable to communicate with your heart [and mind].' Then he said: 'Verily modesty, chastity, and inarticulateness – the inarticulateness of the tongue, not of the heart – are part of faith, while immodesty, obscenity and insolence are part of hypocrisy.'

Ibn Maskan said, and al-Hasan said: 'We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' A foul-mouthed woman passed by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was eating, and said, 'O Muhammad, you are indeed eating the food of a slave and sitting as a slave sits.' So he said to her, 'Woe to you! And who is a more submissive slave than me?' She said, 'Then give me a morsel of your food.' So the Messenger of Allah gave her a morsel of his food. She said, 'No, by Allah, unless you bring a morsel from your mouth to my mouth.' He said: 'So he took out the morsel from his mouth and gave it to her, and she ate it.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'She did not utter an obscene word until she left this world.'

Fadalah ibn Ukeyem from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say in his sermon: 'Cursing a believer is transgression (fisq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr). Consuming his property is disobedience (ma'siyah), and the sanctity of his property is like the sanctity of his blood.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) broke his fast on a Thursday evening in Masjid Quba. He asked, 'Is there any drink?' So Aws ibn Khawla al-Ansari brought him a cup of buttermilk mixed with honey. When he placed it on his lips, he set it aside and then said: 'Two drinks, yet one would suffice for the other. I will not drink it, nor do I forbid it, but I humble myself before Allah. Indeed, whoever humbles himself before Allah, Allah elevates him; and whoever is arrogant, Allah abases him. Whoever is moderate in his livelihood, Allah grants him sustenance; and whoever is wasteful, Allah deprives him. And whoever remembers Allah often, Allah loves him.'

Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Ali ibn Shajarah, from his uncle Bashir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dark-skinned woman picking up manure or camel dung from the ground, so the Muslims said, 'The way, O Messenger of Allah!' The dark-skinned woman said, 'The path is wide.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave her alone, for she is insolent.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When it was the conquest of the day of Mecca, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood among the people as a preacher, praised Allah and glorified Him, then he said: 'O People, let the one present convey to the one absent that verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has removed from you through Islam the haughtiness of the Age of Ignorance and the boasting about forefathers and clans. O People, verily you are from Adam and Adam was from clay. Behold, verily the best of you in the sight of Allah and the noblest of you before Him on this day are those who are most Godwary and most submissive to Him. Behold, being Arab is not by parentage but a speaking tongue. So whoever is reviled among you and knows that it will make him attain the pleasure of Allah, that is sufficient for him. Behold, verily all blood, or injustice, or malice that was in the Age of Ignorance will remain under my feet until the Day of Judgment.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa, and al-Hasan ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said: I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'The foundation of a person is his religion, his status is his character, and his nobility is his God-wariness; verily all people from Adam are of equal origin.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Bistam al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ja'far ibn Abi Talib returned from Abyssinia, he said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Shall I tell you, O Messenger of Allah? I visited al-Najashi one day and found him not in his royal seat, nor dressed in his royal attire, nor in his usual appearance. I greeted him with the greeting of kings and said to him: O King, why do I see you not in your royal seat, nor in your royal attire, nor in your usual appearance?' He replied: 'We find in the Gospel that whoever Allah has blessed with a favor, let him thank Allah. And we find in the Gospel that there is nothing comparable to gratitude to Allah like humility. And indeed, word came to me this night that your cousin Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has been granted victory by Allah over the polytheists of Badr, so I wished to thank Allah, the Exalted, in the manner you see.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who informed him, from Abū Baṣīr who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, divine revelation was withheld from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (peace be upon him) for thirty mornings, so he ascended a mountain in al-Shām which was called Arīḥā, and said: "O Lord, why have You withheld Your revelation and Your communication from me? Is it because of the sin I committed? Then here I am before You, so do with me as You please! And if You have withheld Your revelation and communication from me due to the sins of the Banī Isrāʾīl, then Your pre-eternal forgiveness [is sufficient]." So Allah revealed to him saying: "O Mūsā, do you know why I chose you for My revelation and communication among My creation?" He said: "I do not know that, O Lord." He said: "O Mūsā, I examined My creation, inspecting them, but did not see anyone among them as intensely humble as you. That is why I chose you for My revelation and communication among My creation." He (the Imam) said: "When Mūsā (peace be upon him) used to pray, he did not turn aside [from his prayers] until he placed his right cheek on the earth and his left cheek upon the earth."'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not like the ignorant old man, nor the oppressive rich man, nor the vain poor man.'

Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated from Saif ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughirah, from his brother who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two hungry wolves among a flock of sheep that has been separated from their shepherd, one in front of it and the other behind it, are not more destructive to it than the love of wealth and status is [destructive] to the religion of a Muslim man.'

Ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated from Hammad ibn 'Isa who said: I never saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) eat while reclining. Then he remembered the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'He never ate while reclining until he passed away.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'People narrate from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) saw a woman in one of the ceremonial precincts of Makkah and was impressed by her, so he proposed to her and married her, and she stayed with him. He had a friend among the Ansar who was distressed by his marriage to that woman, so he asked about her and was informed that she was from the family of Dhī al-Jadayn from the Banu Shayban in a prestigious household among her clan. So he turned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said: 'May Allah make me your ransom! Your marriage to this woman was continually occupying my thoughts, and I said: Ali ibn al-Husayn has married an unknown woman, and people are also saying this. So I kept asking about her until I knew her and found her in her people's household as a Shaybaniyyah.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said to him: 'I used to consider you to have better judgement than what I now see. Verily, Allah brought Islam, and through it He raised the lowly one, perfected the deficient one, and ennobled [people] from blame. Hence, there is no blame upon the Muslim; rather, the blame is [that of] ignorance.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Husayn ibn Musa, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) married the slave-wife of his uncle, al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and married his mother to his (freed) slave. When that reached Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, he wrote to him: 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, it seems you do not know your position among your people and your station among the people! You married a slave woman and married your slave to your mother?' So Ali ibn al-Husayn wrote back to him: 'I understood your letter, and our exemplar is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He married off his cousin Zaynab to his slave Zayd, and he himself married his slave maiden Safiyyah bint Hayy ibn Akhṭab.'

Some of our companions narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from his uncle Bashīr al-Nabbāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A bedouin approached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, will you race me with this camel of yours?’ So he raced him and the bedouin won the race. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘You had all raised it but Allah liked that He should lower it. Verily the mountains vied for the ark of Nūḥ (peace be upon him), but al-Jūdī was the most humble, so Allah made the ark stop at al-Jūdī.’
Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who has even a [tiny] seed’s weight of pride in his heart will not enter Paradise.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: Verily, there are two angels in the sky who are assigned to the servants; whoever humbles himself for Allah, they elevate him, and whoever is arrogant, they abase him.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Pride is the robe of Allah, so whoever attempts to take Allah’s robe from Him, Allah will throw him face-first into the Fire.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Mansur from al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I would not like to have [even] the best of comforts [and wealth] if it entails humiliating myself, and I have not swallowed anything that I liked more than the suppressed rage for which I do not retaliate against the one who caused it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: A servant will be brought on the Day of Judgment having offered prayer, so he will say: 'O Lord, I prayed seeking Your pleasure.' He will be told: 'Rather, you prayed so that it would be said: How good is the prayer of so-and-so!' 'Take him to the Fire!' And a servant who fought will be brought, and he will say: 'O Lord, I fought seeking Your pleasure.' He will be told: 'Rather, you fought so that it would be said: How brave is so-and!' 'Take him to the Fire!' And a servant who learned the Quran will be brought, and he will say: 'O Lord, I learned the Quran seeking Your pleasure.' He will be told: 'Rather, you learned it so that it would be said: How good is the voice of so-and-so!' 'Take him to the Fire!' And a servant who spent his wealth will be brought, and he will say: 'O Lord, I spent my wealth seeking Your pleasure.' He will be told: 'Rather, you spent it so that it would be said: How generous is so-and-so!' 'Take him to the Fire!'

Uthman ibn Isa from Ali ibn Salm who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say,' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said, 'I am the most needless of all who are needless of a partner, so whoever ascribes to Me another as a partner in any action he undertakes, I will not accept it from him. And I do not accept anything but that which was done only for Me exclusively.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū  ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A scholar came to a worshipper and said to him, 'How is your prayer?' He replied, 'You are asking me about my prayer while I have been worshipping Allah since such-and-such a time?' So he asked him, 'How is your weeping?' He replied, 'Verily I do not weep until my tears flow.' So the scholar said to him, 'Indeed your laughter while you fear Allah is better than your weeping while you are self-conceited before Allah! Verily the one who is self-conceited due to his actions has none of his deeds ascend [to Allah].'

Al-Nadr narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) said, 'I will surely worship Allah today with such a worship, and will recite such a lovely recital, the likes of which I have never done before.' So he entered his prayer niche and did so. When he had completed his prayer, he [suddenly] saw a frog in the prayer niche. It said to him, 'O Dawud, are you pleased with yourself today due to your worship and recitation?' 'Yes,' he replied. It said, 'Do not be pleased [or impressed] by it, for verily I glorify Allah every night one thousand times, and with each glorification of mine three thousand praises branch out. And [at times] when I am in the depths of the water and a bird makes a sound in the air, I assume that it might be hungry so I come up to the surface of the water in order for it to eat me, while having committed no sin [to deserve that].'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: He heard him saying: 'Verily, the Prophet Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was once in his prayer niche when a small red worm crept by until it came to the place of his prostration. Dāwūd looked at it and said to himself, “Why was this worm created?” So Allah inspired it, “Speak!” So it said to him, “O Dāwūd, have you heard my sound as I move, or have you noticed my tracks on the smooth earth?” Dāwūd replied, “No.” So it said, “Verily Allah hears my crawl, my breathing, and my sound, and He sees the tracks of my movement, so lower your voice.”'

Al-Nuḍr narrated from Durust, from one of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah sent two angels to the people of a city in order to overturn it upon its inhabitants. When they arrived at the city, they found a man supplicating to Allah and beseeching Him. So one of them told the other, 'Do you see this supplicant?' He replied, 'I see him, but I will proceed to do as my Lord has commanded me.' The first said, 'But I will not do anything before returning to my Lord.' So he returned to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and said, 'My Lord, I went to the city and found Your servant so-and-so supplicating to You and beseeching You.' He said, 'Proceed to what I have commanded you, for indeed that man’s face has never changed out of anger for My sake, ever.'

Al-Nadr narrated from Muhammad ibn Hashim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily a group of people who believed in Musa (peace be upon him) said, 'If we were to go to the army of Fir'awn and join it, we would acquire some of his worldly wealth, and then when what we hope for from the arrival of Musa transpires, we will go to him.' So that is what they did. When Musa and those in his company turned to flee, they mounted their mounts and speedily rode towards Musa, hoping to catch up with him and his companions in order to join them. But Allah sent angels who struck the faces of their mounts thereby causing them to return towards the army of Fir'awn. Hence, they were among those who drowned with Fir'awn.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Yazid ibn Khalifah who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever does a deed for Allah, his reward is upon Allah, and whoever does a deed for the people, his reward is upon the people. Verily, every act of showing off is polytheism.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Fadalah from Jamil who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted: 'So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who is righteous' (Q53:32). He said: 'It is when a person says: I prayed last night and I fasted yesterday, and similar to this.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, some people would say in the mornings: We prayed last night and we fasted yesterday.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'But as for me, I sleep at night and during the day, and if I could find any time between them, I would have slept in it as well.'

Ibn Abi al-Bilād narrated from Sa’d al-Iskāf, from Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him), who said: There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel with whom David (peace be upon him) was impressed, so Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: 'Do not be impressed by anything from his affair, for indeed he is one who shows off.' Then the man died, and they came to David and said to him, 'The man has died.' He said, 'Bury your companion.' The Children of Israel said, 'How could he not attend [his funeral]?' When the man was washed, fifty men stood and bore witness by Allah that they knew nothing but good [about him]. When they prayed over him, another fifty men stood and bore witness by Allah that they knew nothing but good [about him]. So Allah, the Almighty, revealed to David (peace be upon him): 'What prevented you from testifying for so-and-so?' He said, 'That which You informed me of regarding his affair.' He said, 'If that is so for you, but a group of rabbis and monks testified, swearing by Me that they knew nothing but good, I accepted their testimony regarding him and forgave him despite My knowledge of him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I wrote to him asking him about a question, so he wrote back to me: Verily Allah says: 'Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but it is He who causes them to be deceived,' up to His saying: '[a] way.' They are not from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah, and they are not from the faithful believers, and they are not from the Muslims. They manifest belief outwardly but hide disbelief and rejection [of faith] in their hearts. May Allah curse them.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madai'ni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: (And does not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord) He said: It is the servant who performs an act of worship without seeking the pleasure of Allah; rather, he only seeks the commendation of people, desiring to be heard of. This is the one who associates others in the worship of his Lord. And he said: There is no servant who hides a good [deed] and days go by, but that Allah manifests good for him; and there is no servant who hides an evil [deed] and days pass, but that Allah will manifest evil for him.

Hamd ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the servant may commit a sin and then feel remorse for it, and later perform a deed by which he is pleased, such that he becomes remiss and turns away from his previous state [of remorse]. Indeed, it would have been better for him to remain in that previous state of his, rather than what he later entered into.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Thumali, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Indeed among My servants is one who asks Me for something from [the ability to perform] acts of worship so that I may love him, but I turn that away from him so that he would not be pleased with [himself and] his deed.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three things are deliverers and three things are destroyers.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the deliverers?' He said: 'Fearing Allah in secret as though you see Him, for if you do not see Him, surely He sees you; exercising justice in happiness and anger; and moderation in abundance and poverty.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, and what are the destroyers?' He said: 'Vain desire that is followed, stinginess that is obeyed, and a person being pleased with himself.'

Al-Nuḍr from al-Ḥalabī from Abū Saʿīd al-Makkārī from Abū Baṣīr from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: Then they will all be hurled headlong into Hell, along with the deviant ones. He said: “[O Abā Baṣīr], they are a group who described justice with their tongues then contravene it with something else [in action].”

One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Muḥammad ibn ṬalḈah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Whichever servant has a handsome appearance along with an untainted position, then he humbles himself before Allah, he will be among the special [chosen] ones of Allah.' He (the narrator) said, 'I asked, What is [the meaning of] an untainted position?' He replied, 'He should not have been sullied by debauchery.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali (al-Khazzaj) (al-Washsha') narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Verily, the Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) said: O Lord, I have never asked You for anything of this world, ever.' And an inkling of self-admiration entered his heart. Then a cloud approached him and called out to him: 'O Ayyub, who enabled you to do this?' He said: 'You, O Lord.'

Muhammad ibn Khālid narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever manifests for the people what Allah loves and confronts Allah by [doing] what He dislikes, he will meet Allah while He loathes him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Hafss, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: There is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of the day. If he repents, nothing is recorded against him; and if he does not, one evil deed is recorded against him. So 'Abbād al-Baṣrī came to him and said to him: We have been informed that you said: 'There is no servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of the day.' He said: 'That is not how I said it, but I said: There is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of his day. That is how I said it.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Zurari, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: There is no servant who commits a sin but that he is given respite from that morning until nightfall, so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, it is not written against him.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents in the year of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a year is too long. Whoever repents in the month of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a month is too long. Whoever repents on the day of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a day is too long. Whoever repents when his soul has reached here' — and he pointed with his hand to his throat — 'Allah forgives him.'

Muhammad ibn 'Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darrāj who said: I heard Abā Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'When the soul reaches this [place, i.e., the throat], there is no repentance for the knowledgeable, and there is repentance for the ignorant.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does an evil deed is given a respite of seven hours of the day. If he says: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, besides Whom there is no god, the Living, the Eternal,' three times, it will not be recorded for him.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, the Almighty: (O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance)?' He said: 'It is the sin which he never repeats again.' I said: 'And who among us has not repeated [a sin]?' So he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, verily Allah loves from among His servants the one who is tested [by sin] and repents often.'

Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a servant intends to do an evil deed, it is not recorded against him, but if he intends to do a good deed, it is recorded for him.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali al-Ahmasi, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: By Allah, no one is saved from the sin except the one who admits it.

Ali ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Muskān from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) say: 'Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he repents than a man whose mount got lost in a barren land, carrying his food and drink. While he was in that state, not knowing what to do or where to turn, he put his head down to sleep when suddenly a person came to him and said: 'O man, do you have your mount?' He replied: 'Yes.' He said: 'Here it is.'

Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥarth ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah loves the one who admits [his sins] and repents often. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn to Allah in repentance seventy times a day without having committed any sin. I asked: Would he say: I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn back to Him in repentance? He replied: He would say: I turn [penitently] to Allah.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' 'Verily we sin and we do wrong, then we turn back penitently to Allah.' Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id said, 'There is no difference of opinion among our scholars that they (peace be upon them) are infallible from every ugliness absolutely, and that they (peace be upon them) consider abandoning what is recommended as a sin and a misdeed in relation to their perfection (peace be upon them).'

One of our companions narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from ʿĪsā ibn Rāshid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'There is no believer who commits a sin but that he is given respite for seven hours; so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, he is forgiven. Indeed, he may recall his sin after twenty years and thus seek forgiveness from Allah and he is [thereby] forgiven. But as for the disbeliever, he forgets his sin so that he may not seek forgiveness from Allah.'

One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from a man who was known as Rūzbih and was one of the Zaydīs, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī who said, Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) said to me, ‘There is no servant who performs an action that Allah is not pleased with but that Allah initially conceals it [from the people]. If he repeats it a second time, Allah hides it [again], but if he repeats it once more, Allah sends down an angel in the form of a man to tell the people, ‘He did such and such.’”
Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād said Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Verily I seek forgiveness from Allah five thousand times every day.' Then he said to me, 'Five thousand is a lot.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil, from Bakir, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Verily Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, You allowed Shaytan to prevail over me and made him flow in me like blood, so grant me something.' He said: 'O Adam, I have granted you that whoever among your progeny intends an evil deed, it will not be recorded against him; if he does it, one evil deed is recorded against him. And whoever among them intends a good deed, if he does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him; and if he does it, ten good deeds are recorded for him.' He said: 'O Lord, give me more.' He said: 'I have granted you that whoever among them commits an evil deed and then seeks forgiveness, I shall forgive him.' He said: 'O Lord, give me more.' He said: 'I have granted them repentance' (or he said: 'I have extended their repentance until the soul reaches here [the throat]'). He said: 'O Lord, that is sufficient for me.'

Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says three times: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Great, and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from my Lord and turn penitently to Him,’ the Throne is struck as a chain strikes a bowl.

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: One who does not hold himself to account every day is not from us. If he has done a good (good) deed, he should seek more of it from Allah and praise Allah for it, and if he has done an evil deed, he should seek forgiveness from Allah for it and turn penitently to Him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: A man narrated to me from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: There is no drop more beloved to Allah than a drop of blood shed in the way of Allah, or a drop of tears from an eye in the darkness of the night out of fear of Allah. And there is no step more beloved to Allah than a step taken towards a near relative, or a step by which a march in the way of Allah is completed. And there is no gulp more beloved to Allah than the swallowing of anger, or a gulp by which a servant repels his calamity [with patience].

Faḍālah narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ghaylān, who attributed it to Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) saying: There is no eye that wells up with tears out of fear of Allah but that He makes it forbidden to the Fire. If its tears flow upon the cheeks of its owner, neither gloom nor disgrace will cover his face. There is nothing but that it has a measure, except tears; for verily a single drop of it can extinguish seas of fire. If a man were to weep among his nation and a teardrop fell from him, they would all be shown mercy due to his weeping.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Salih ibn Razin and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Judgment except three eyes: an eye that lowered its gaze from the prohibitions of Allah, or an eye that stayed awake in the worship of Allah, or an eye that wept in the middle of the night out of the fear of Allah.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from a man among his companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): 'My servants do not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than three qualities: detachment from the world, piety from sins, and weeping out of fear of Me.' So Moses said: 'O Lord, what is for the one who does this?' Allah, the Exalted, said: 'As for those who are detached from the world, I will establish them in Paradise; and as for those who eschew sins, I will not call them to account; and as for those who weep out of fear of Me, they shall be in the highest station.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated to us from Sa'dan al-Wasiti, from 'Ajlan Abi Salih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Aba Salih, when you carry a funeral bier, imagine that it is you who is being carried, or that you are asking your Lord to return you to the world so that you may do [good], and see what you will resume [doing]. Then he said: 'How astounding it is for a community whose former members have been confined away [in their graves] from their latter ones [who are alive], then a caller calls out among them for departure [from this world] while they are [busy] playing!'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Dawud al-Abzari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A caller cries out every day, 'O son of Adam, build for death, amass for annihilation, and construct for destruction!'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub from Abu Ubaydah who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Inform me of something that I may benefit from.' So he said, 'O Abu Ubaydah, remember death often, for a person does not remember death often but that he detaches himself from the [yearnings of the material] world.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd, from Abū Shaybah al-Zuhrī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Death! Death! Death comes with whatever is in it; it brings comfort and ease, and a blessed return to the lofty heavens for the people of the eternal abode – those who had struggled for it and yearned for it. And death comes with whatever is in it; it brings wretchedness and regret, and a return of [great] loss to a scorching fire for the people of the abode of delusion – those who strived for it and yearned for it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the guardianship of Satan and wretchedness is deserved, aspiration comes in front of the eyes and [remembrance of] death goes behind the back.' He [also] said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, “Who among the believers are cleverer?” He said, “Those among them who remember death more often and make more intense preparations for it.”'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who attributed it to Salmān al-Fārsī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Were it not for prostration before Allah and the gatherings of people who utter virtuous words, just as the best dates are plucked [and harvested], I would have wished for death.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from someone who heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: When al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) was near death, he wept, so it was said to him: 'O son of the daughter of Allah's Messenger, you are weeping despite your position with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) being the one you are in, and despite the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) having said about you what he said, and despite your having performed pilgrimage twenty times riding and twenty times on foot, and despite having given away your wealth to your Lord three times, even down to your sandals?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'I only weep for two things: the terror of what is to come and separation from loved ones.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Muhammad, live as you wish for you will indeed die, love whomever you wish for you will indeed be separated from them, do as you wish for you will indeed be requited for it, and act as you wish for you will surely meet it [in the Hereafter].' Ibn Abi Umayr said, 'Ibn Sinan added to it: O Muhammad, the honor of a believer is his night prayer, and his esteem is his refraining from harming people.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hadrami [al-Husayn] [al-Husayn] narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd [Yazid], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): He said: The Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) died suddenly on a Saturday, so the birds shaded him with their wings. Musa, the Word of Allah, died in the wilderness, so a caller cried out from the sky: 'Musa has died! And which soul does not die!'

Fadalah ibn Abi al-Maghra' said: Ya'qub al-Ahmar narrated to me saying, 'I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to console him for Ismail.' He invoked mercy upon him, then said: 'Verily Allah consoled His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) Himself, saying: "Verily you shall die, and they will die too" (Q39:30). And He said: "Every soul will taste death" (Q3:195).' Then he began speaking and said: 'Indeed, the inhabitants of the earth will die until no one remains. Then the inhabitants of the heavens will die until no one remains except the Angel of Death, the bearers of the Throne, Jibra'il, and Mika'il.' Then the Angel of Death comes and stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is said to him, 'Who has remained?' (while He knows better). He replies, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death, the bearers of the Throne, Jibra'il, and Mika'il.' He is told, 'Command Jibra'il and Mika'il to die.' So the angels say, 'O Lord, they are Your messengers and Your trusted ones!' He says, 'I have decreed for every soul possessing the spirit that it must die.' Then the Angel of Death comes and stands before Allah, the Almighty, and it is said to him, 'Who has remained?' (while He knows better). He replies, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death and the bearers of the Throne.' He is told, 'Command the bearers of the Throne to die.' Then the Angel of Death comes with his gaze lowered. He is asked, 'Who has remained?' So he says, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death.' He says to him, 'Die, O Angel of Death!' So he dies. Then He takes the earth in His left hand and the heavens in His right hand, shaking them severely many times. Then He says, 'Where are those who used to invoke associates with Me? Where are those who placed with Me another deity?'

Fadalah ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'He who has not given death its due status is he who counts his tomorrow among his days.' And Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'A servant does not lengthen his worldly aspiration but that he ends up doing evil deeds.' And he used to say: 'If the servant were to see his death and how quickly it is approaching him, he would have loathed [worldly] aspiration and seeking the world.'

Fadalah ibn Yasar, from al-Isma'il ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) used to say: 'It is that which you do not know when it will meet you; what prevents you from preparing for it before it strikes you suddenly?'

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'May Allah enhance you in righteousness! Whoever loves to meet Allah, does Allah also love to meet him? And whoever hates to meet Allah, does Allah also hate to meet him?' He replied, 'Yes.' I said, 'By Allah, I surely dislike death.' So he said, 'It does not mean what you think. It only applies at the time of viewing [what awaits a person after death]. Verily, when the believer sees what he loves, then there is nothing more beloved to him than proceeding [towards Allah], and Allah loves to meet him while he loves meeting Allah at that moment. And when he sees what he hates, then there is nothing more hateful to him than meeting Allah, the Almighty, and Allah [also] hates to meet him.' And Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Yahya ibn Sabur said: 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The eye of the deceased weeps at the time of death.' He said, 'That is at the time of viewing the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), seeing what pleases him.' He said: 'Then he said: Do you not see the man when he sees what pleases him and what he dislikes, his eyes weep and he smiles?'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Maskan, from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Salih ibn Mitham narrated to me from Ubayyah al-Asadi that he heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying: By Allah, no servant ever hates me and dies with hatred for me but that he sees me at the moment of his death in a way that he hates (in a way that he hates), and no servant ever loves me and dies with love for me but that he sees me at the moment of his death in a way that he loves (in a way that he loves).' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is on his right side (on the right hand side).'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the moment when your enemy will have the most intense hatred for this matter [of our wilayah] will be when the soul reaches here; and the moment when one of you will have the most intense delight is [also] when the soul reaches here – and he pointed to his throat. The terrors of this world and all that he was wary of in it will be cut off from him, and he will be told: In front of you is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Imams (peace be upon them).'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) that he said: Verily when a believer dies, he sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and ʿAlī (peace be upon him) present before him.

Al-Qasim from Kulayb al-Asadi said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May Allah make me your ransom, a tradition has reached us from you.' He asked: 'What is it?' I said: 'Your saying: The possessor of this affair will only be delighted when it reaches here,' and he pointed with his hand to his throat. He said: 'Yes, indeed the people of this affair will be delighted when it reaches here,' and he gestured with his hand to his throat. 'As for that which he feared from the world, it will have passed away from him, and his Imam will be the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them).'

Al-Nadr (ibn Suwayd) from Yahya al-Halabi from Ayyub who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the moment when your enemy will have the most intense hatred for this matter will be when the soul reaches here,' and he gestured towards his throat. Then he said: 'There was a man from the family of Uthman who would often curse Ali (peace be upon him), so one of his maid servants who would visit us told me about that. She said, “When he was about to die, he said, “What do I have to do with them?!””' I said [to the Imam (peace be upon him)], “May Allah make me your ransom! Why did he say this?” He said, “[It was] when he was shown some of the punishment [that awaits him for rejecting the wilayah].” Have you not heard the verse wherein Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: But no, by your Lord, they will never be [true] believers until they accept your judgement in all their disputes, and find no resistance within themselves against your decision and submit wholeheartedly (Q4:65)? Far be it! Far be it! No, by Allah [it will not be so] until this thing is well established in the heart, even if he prays and fasts.’”

Ṣafwān narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Abū ʿAmr al-Bazzāz who said: We were sitting with Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) when he stood up, entered the house, and came out. He held the two doorposts, greeted us, and we replied to his greeting. Then he said, 'By Allah, I surely love you, and the scent and spirit of your souls. Verily, you are upon the religion of Allah and the religion of His angels. And nothing stands between any of you and seeing that which would gladden his eye except his soul reaching here,' and he pointed to his throat with his hand. And he said, 'Be mindful of Allah and support that with piety.'

Ṣafwān narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing stands between any one of you and seeing that which would bring him delight except his soul reaching here (i.e. the throat). The Angel of Death will come to him and say, ‘As for that which you used to desire in the world, it has escaped you; but as for what you used to desire of the Hereafter, you are now on the verge of it, and in front of you are the forebears of truth: the Messenger of Allah, ʿAlī and Ibrāhīm (peace be upon them all).’

Ṣafwān narrated from Qutaybah al-Aʿshā who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) say, 'You made enemies of your fathers, children, and wives for our sake, and your reward for that is with Allah. The time when you will be most in need of our love is when the soul reaches here,' and he pointed towards his neck.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us saying: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated to us from 'Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: When a person is placed in his grave, two angels come to him, one from his right and one from his left, and Satan is made to stand before him, his eyes like copper. Then he is asked: 'What do you say about this man who was among you?' He is overwhelmed by fear; if he is a believer, he says: 'Are you asking me about Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' They say to him: 'Yes,' a sleep with no dream in it. And his grave is widened for him by nine cubits. Then he sees his place in Paradise. And that is the word of Allah, the Almighty: 'Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in this life and in the Hereafter.' If he is a disbeliever, they say to him: 'What is this man who came among you?' He says: 'I do not know.' So they leave him alone with Satan.

Al-Qasim and ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When Saʿd died, seventy thousand angels accompanied his funeral procession, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood at his grave and said, ‘Would the likes of Saʿd face the squeezing [of the grave]?’ His mother said, ‘Congratulations to you O Saʿd, and [what a great] honor!’ So the Messenger of Allah said to her, ‘O mother of Saʿd, do not impose anything upon Allah.’ She said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we have heard you say what you said about Saʿd [and how you praised him].’ So he said, ‘Verily Saʿd was harsh in his speech with his family.’

And Abū Baṣīr said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) say: When Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), died, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood by her grave, raised his hand towards the sky, and his eyes shed tears. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have seen you raise your head to the sky and your eyes shed tears.' He said: 'I asked my Lord to grant me Ruqayyah from the squeezing of the grave.'

Faḍālah ibn Sīnān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Bashīr al-Nabbāl, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the grave of Saʿd, and he would wipe it with his hand, and he would quiver between his shoulders. So it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, we see you addressing [the grave] and quivering between your shoulders, and you say: Saʿd is undergoing this [squeezing]. So he said: Verily, there is no believer but that he will undergo squeezing [in the grave].

Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Muskān from Sulaymān ibn Khālid who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about what will be faced by one who is [buried] in the grave, so he said, ‘Verily two angels who are called Munkar and Nakīr will come to the one who is in the grave and will ask him about the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying, “What do you have to say about this man who rose among you?” He will ask, “Who was he?” They will say, “The one who used to say that he is the Messenger of Allah. Was that true?” So if the man was one of the doubters, he will say, “I do not know. I heard the people saying [that] but I do not know whether it was the truth or a lie.” So they will strike him such a blow that it will be audible to the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of earth, except the polytheists. But if he was one of those with certitude, he will not fear and will say [confidently], “Are you asking me about the Messenger of Allah?” So they will ask, “Do you know that he is the Messenger of Allah?” He will say, “I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah in truth. He came with guidance and the religion of truth.” Thus he will see his position in Paradise and his grave will be expanded for him. They (the two angels) will then say to him, “Sleep a slumber wherein there is no dream, in the best state of any sleeper.”’

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wants to resurrect the creation, He makes the sky rain upon the earth for forty days, then the limbs come together and flesh grows.

Ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated from his father, from one of his companions, who attributed it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said to one of his companions: How will you be when the two examiners of the grave come to you? He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the examiners of the grave?' He said, 'Two angels, harsh and severe, with voices like rumbling thunder and eyes like blinding lightning. They will tread on their own hair and plough the ground with their fangs, and they will question you.' He asked, 'And you will be in a state such as this?' He replied, 'You will be as you are in your present state.' He said, 'Then I will be able to face them.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the souls of the believers, so he said: '[They are] in chambers in Paradise, eating from its food and drinking from its drink, and they will say: Our Lord, bring upon us the Hour and fulfill for us what You promised us, and join the last of us to the first.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the souls of the polytheists, so he said, '[They will be] in the Fire facing punishment and will say, "Our Lord, do not bring upon us the Hour [of Judgment], and do not fulfil for us what You promised us, and do not join the last of us with the first!"'

Al-Qasim from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Dhibyan who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said to me: 'What do the people say about the souls of believers?' I said: 'They say that they are in the craws of green birds in lanterns under the Throne.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! The believer is more honourable in the sight of Allah than His placing his soul in the craw of a green bird. O Yunus! When that [time of death] comes, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Fatimah, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and the close angels (peace be upon them) come to him. And when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, takes his soul, He places that soul in a form similar to its form in the world; so they eat and drink. Then when a newcomer comes to them, they recognize him by that appearance which he had in the world.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Zayd al-Qurashi, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'When Allah causes the inhabitants of the earth to die, He causes the inhabitants of the lowest heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the second heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the third heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the fourth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the fifth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the sixth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the seventh heaven to die. Then He causes Mikail to die — he said, or Jibrail — then He causes Jibrail to die, then He causes Israfil to die, then He causes the Angel of Death to die. Then the Horn will be blown and they will be resurrected.' Then Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will ask, 'To whom does the Kingdom belong this Day?' Then He will respond Himself saying, 'To Allah, the Creator, the Originator, and the Fashioner; and Exalted is Allah, the One, the Subduer.' Then He will ask, 'Where are the tyrants? Where are those who called upon another god besides Me? Where are the arrogant ones?' — and similar to this — then He will resurrect the creation.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah will favour His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection and bring him close to His Grace. Then He will show him that with which He blessed him. He, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, 'Did you not supplicate to Me on such and such day for such and such and I answered your supplication? Did you not ask Me on such and such day and I granted you what you asked for? Did you not seek My help on such and such day and I helped you? Did you not ask that I relieve you of such and such hardship so I relieved your hardship and showed mercy to your plea? Did you not ask Me for wealth so I granted you its possession? Did you not seek My assistance so I assisted you? Did you not ask Me to get you married to so and so while she was with her family and not [directly] approachable, yet I got you married to her?' So the servant will say, 'Yes indeed, O Lord! You have granted me everything I asked for, and I used to ask You for Paradise [as well].' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'Indeed, I will grant you what you have asked Me for – here is Paradise, you are permitted [to enter] it. Have I pleased you?' The believer will say, 'Yes, my Lord! I am pleased.' (Or: 'You have pleased me and I am satisfied.')' Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, 'O My servant, I was pleased with your deeds, so I selected for you the best of rewards. Verily the best of your rewards with Me is that I have made you reside in Paradise.'

Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him and his family) who said: When the believer is taken to account, his wives will be waiting for him at the thresholds of the doors, just as their wives wait for their husbands in this world during their absence. He said: Then a messenger comes and gives them glad tidings, saying: 'By Allah, so-and-so has returned from the reckoning.' He said: They will say: 'By Allah?' He will say: 'By Allah, I have seen him returning from the reckoning.' He said: When he comes to them, they will say: 'Welcome and greetings! Your family whom you were with in the world are not more deserving of you than we are.'

Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from 'Umar ibn Ibrahim al-Sabiri, from Hujr ibn Zaydah, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I have a need.' He said, 'Meet me at Mecca.' I said again, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I have a need.' He said, 'Present your need.' I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I have committed a sin between myself and Allah which no one else knows of, so it weighs heavily on me, and I revere you too much to mention it to you.' He said, 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, and Allah takes account of His believing servant, He stops him for his sins, one by one, then He forgives him. He is not made known to it, neither a close angel nor a chosen Prophet.' 'Umar ibn Ibrahim said, 'I was informed by more than one person that he said: And He conceals from him some of his sins that he dislikes to be questioned about.' He said, 'And He says to his misdeeds, They are the ones whose evil deeds Allah will change into good deeds, and Allah is Oft-forgiving, Merciful. He said, 'And that is the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.'
