Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' Verily, when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, wants to take account of the believer, He gives him his book in his right hand, and His reckoning is between Him and him privately. He says, 'My servant, did you do such and such, and perform such and such?' He says, 'Yes, my Lord, I have done that.' He says, 'I have forgiven it for you and replaced it with good deeds.' The people say, 'Glory be to Allah! Did this servant not have even a single evil deed?' As for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will have an easy reckoning, and will return to his people well pleased. I asked, 'Who are his people?' He said, 'His people in the world are his people in Paradise, if they were believers.' And if He wishes ill for His servant, He calls him to account in front of all the people, reproves him, and gives him his book in his left hand. And as for the one who is given his record from behind his back, he will cry for destruction and will burn in a blazing fire. He used to live among his people well pleased. I asked, 'Which people?' He replied, 'His people in the world.' I asked, '[What is the meaning of] His statement: He thought he would never return?' He said, 'He assumed that he would never return.'

Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'Verily the believer will be given, on the Day of Judgment, an opened scroll (a scroll displayed) in which is written: [This is] the Book of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. Admit so-and-so into Paradise.'

Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily people will pass over the Bridge in ranks, and the Bridge is thinner than hair and the edge of a sword. Some will pass like lightning, some like a galloping horse, some sliding along, some crawling, some walking, and some hanging from it, with fire taking part of him and leaving part.

Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, the light will be divided among the people on the Day of Judgment in accordance with their faith. The share of the hypocrite will be such that his light will extend only to the tip of his left toe, then it will be extinguished, and he will say, Were we not with you? Yes, but your own selves led you to temptation, so you awaited [our demise] and doubted, and false hopes deluded you until Allah's decree came to pass. And the Deceiver deluded you about Allah. So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from the disbelievers. Your home is the Fire; that is your guardian, and evil is the destination. Then he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, by Allah, this is not what Allah said to the Jews and Christians, but He meant the people of the Qiblah.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Fulan ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The registers on the Day of Judgment are three: a register containing blessings, a register containing good deeds, and a register containing sins. The register of blessings is juxtaposed with the register of good deeds, so the majority of the good deeds are consumed [to offset the blessings], and the sins remain.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The servant will remain standing on the Day of Resurrection in front of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until He asks him about four aspects: Your lifetime, what did you spend it on? Your body, what did you exhaust it for? Your wealth, from where did you earn it and where did you invest it? And [he will be asked] about our love, the Ahl al-Bayt.'

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb ibn Mītham who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) say: A fire will emerge from the depths of Aden, illuminating the necks of camels; it will be visible from the land of Shām, driving people towards the Gathering Place.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Ali who said, 'I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) said:' 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out, “Where are the patient ones?” So a group of people will stand up. Then a caller will call out, “Where are those who exercised self-control?” So a group of people will stand up.” I said, “May I be your ransom, who are the patient ones?” He said, “The patient ones are those who are patient in performing the obligatory duties, and those who exercise self-control are those who abandon sins.”'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Fadalah narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the inmates of Hell, so he said: My father Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: They will come out from it and will be taken to a spring at the gate of Paradise called the Spring of Life. They will then be showered with its water, and their flesh, skin, and hair will grow back just as plants grow.

Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from ʿUmar ibn Abān, from Udaym the brother of Ayyūb, from Ḥumrān who said: I said to Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'They say: Do not be impressed by the group which claims that Allah will remove some people from the Fire and place them among the inhabitants of Paradise with His friends.' So he said: 'Do they not read the verse in which Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: There are two other Gardens below these two (Q55:62)? It refers to a paradise besides Paradise and a fire besides the Fire. They will not dwell with the friends of Allah.' And he said: 'There is, by Allah, a level [or two levels] between them, but I cannot talk about it [here]. Their matter is more constricted than a [tight] noose. Indeed, were the Riser to rise, he would start with these people.'

Fadalah from 'Umar ibn Aban said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who entered the Fire, then was removed from it, and then entered Paradise. He said, 'If you wish, I will tell you what my father used to say about it.' He said, 'Verily, some people will come out of the Fire after having been burnt to coals, and they will be taken to a river at the gate of Paradise called al-Hayawan (the Life). Water from it will be showered upon them, and their flesh, blood, and hair will grow back.'
Fadalah from 'Umar ibn Aban who said: I heard a righteous servant say regarding the inmates of Hell: that they enter the Fire due to their sins, and they come out through the pardon of Allah

Uthman ibn 'Isa narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Abū Baṣīr who said: I heard Abā Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, a group will be burnt in the Fire until when they become coal-black (humam), they attain intercession.' Then they will be taken to a river that flows from the perspiration of the inhabitants of Paradise, so they will bathe therein, their flesh and blood will grow back, and the scorching of the Fire will be removed from them. They will enter Paradise and will be called al-Jahannamiyyūn (the inmates of the Fire). Together, they will cry out: 'O Allah, remove from us this name!' So He will remove it from them. Then he said: 'O Abā Baṣīr, verily the enemies of 'Alī will remain in the Fire forever, they will not attain intercession.'

Fadala ibn Ruba' narrated from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the last one to come out of the Fire will be a man called Hammam, who will call out therein for a lifetime: 'O Compassionate! O Munificent!'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A hadith that people are narrating, So he said: It is not as they are saying. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, the last servant to be ordered into the Fire, when he is ordered to be thrown into the Fire, he will turn [back].' So Allah, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, will say: 'Hasten with him.' So when he is brought, it will be said to him: 'O My servant, why did you turn [back]?' So he will say: 'O Lord, this was not how I had perceived You to be!' So the Majestic Lord will say: 'O My servant, what was your perception of Me?' He will reply: 'O Lord, I had thought that You would forgive my sins and admit me into Your Paradise [to dwell therein]!' So Allah, the All-Powerful, Majestic and Exalted is He, will say: 'O My angels, by My might and bounty, by My mastery and majesty, by My loftiness and exalted station,' 'My servant never thought positively of Me even for a moment in his life,' 'for if he had thought positively of Me even for a single moment of his life, I would not have frightened him with the Fire.' 'Yet let his lie stand, and place him in Paradise.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A servant does not think positively of Allah but that he will find Allah to be as he had thought of Him.' 'And he does not think negatively of Him but that he will find Allah to be as he had thought of Him.' 'That is the [interpretation of] the verse in which He, the Exalted, says: It was the [negative] thoughts you entertained about your Lord that has led to your ruin, so you have become losers.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr (he elevated it) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A servant will be brought on the Day of Judgment having no good deed [in his record], so it will be said to him, 'Remember and recollect, do you have any good deed?' So he will [try to] recall and will say, 'My Lord, I have no good deed except that Your believing servant so-and-so passed by [one day] and asked me for water so that he could perform ablution and pray, so I gave it to him.' So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, 'Admit My servant into Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from al-Ahwal, from Humran who said: I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the disbelievers and polytheists will taunt the monotheists in the Fire, saying: We do not see how your monotheism benefited you in any way; you and we are equal.' So the Lord, Exalted and Majestic, will feel disdain for them and will say to the angels: 'Intercede,' so they will intercede for whom Allah wills. And He will say to the believers: 'Do likewise,' until no one remains but that the intercession reaches him. He, the Blessed and Exalted, will say: 'I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Come out by My mercy,' so they will come out like moths. He said: Then Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then the columns will be extended and fixed over them, and it will be, by Allah, eternity.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Aḥwal, from Ḥumrān who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us that Hell will be filled until its gates are [crammed] shut.' He said: 'No, by Allah, it is [going to remain as it is] for eternity!' I asked: '[What about the verse that states:] [They will] remain therein forever, as long as the heavens and the earth will endure, except what your Lord wills (Q11:107)?' He said: 'That is for those who will come out from the Fire [with the permission of Allah].'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq who said: ʿAlī (peace be upon him) said: ‘I will surely tell you a ḥadīth that it behoves every believer to be aware of [and remember].’ He related it to us in the morning but we forgot it by nightfall. So we returned to him and said to him: ‘We have forgotten the ḥadīth you told us in the morning, and you had said that it behoves every believer to be aware of it, so please repeat it for us.’ So he said: ‘There is no Muslim who commits a sin and is then pardoned for it by Allah in this world, but that Allah is more majestic and noble than to punish him again for it in the Hereafter after having granted him respite in the world.’ Then he recited this verse: (And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have committed, and He pardons much).

Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Pray to Allah for me, for verily I have many sins.' So he said, 'Stop, O Abū ʿUbaydah! Let Satan not be a helper of your base-self. Verily the pardon of Allah cannot be compared to anything.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: When it is Friday, and the people of Paradise are in Paradise while the people of Hell are in the Fire, the inhabitants of Paradise will know that it is Friday due to what they witness of enhanced pleasure and joy, and the denizens of Hell will know that it is Friday because the wardens of Hell seize them.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab (Rabab), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the Day of Judgment comes, Paradise will call out to its Lord and say, 'O Lord, You are the Just, and You have filled Hell with its inmates as You promised it, yet You have not filled me as You promised me.' So Allah will create a creation who shall not have seen the world and will fill Paradise with them – blessed shall they be.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not say [there is but] a single garden [of Paradise].' Verily Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: '[There are] levels, some above others.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and the one who narrated it from him, that he said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken [to the heavens] by night, he did not pass by any one of the angels but that he became happy [to see him], until he passed by an angel who did not show happiness upon [seeing] him like the [other] angels did, and he did not say anything to him; rather, he found him morose and frowning. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O Jibra'il, I did not pass by any of the angels but that he was gladdened by [seeing] me, and I witnessed cheerfulness, graciousness, and joy from him, except this angel. Who is this?' He replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, this angel is the warden of Hell, and this is how Allah has made him.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Ask him to show me the creation of his Lord.' [Or] he said, 'I would like you to ask him to show me the Fire.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O angel, this is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he has told me that he did not pass by any of the angels but that they expressed their joy at meeting him, except you. So I told him that this is the warden of Hell and that is how Allah has made him. He has now asked me to request you to show it to him.' So one of its levels was unveiled for him. Then he (the Imam) said, 'After [seeing] that, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never smiled laughingly until the day he died.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab (Rabab), from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, in Hell there is a valley called Ghassaq, in which are three hundred and thirty castles. In each castle are three hundred and thirty chambers. In each chamber are three hundred and thirty scorpions. In the stinger of each scorpion are three hundred and thirty sacs of venom. If a single one of those scorpions were to spray its venom on the people of Hell, it would cover them all with venom.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abū al-Maghraʾ, from Abū Baṣīr who said: 'I do not know of it being mentioned except by Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him).' He said: 'When Allah places the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of Hell in Hell, death will be brought in the form of a ram until it is kept standing between Paradise and Hell.' He said: 'Then a caller will call out and the inhabitants of both abodes will hear him: “O people of Paradise! O people of Hell!” When they hear the voice, they will come forward.' He said: 'They will be asked, “Do you know what this is? This is the death that you used to fear in the world.”' He said: 'So the people of Paradise will say, “O Allah, do not allow death to enter upon us!” And the people of Hell will say, “O Allah, allow death to enter upon us!”' He said: 'Then it will be slaughtered the way a sheep is slaughtered.' He said: 'Then a caller will call out: “There is no [more] death forever! Be certain of eternal life!”' He said: 'So the people of Paradise will rejoice in such a manner that if one could die out of joy, they would die on that day.' [Then he will ask his fellow believers,] “Are we [truly] never going to die, except our first death, nor suffer punishment [like others]? This is truly the ultimate triumph!” For the likes of this should everyone strive (Q39:58-60). He [then] said, 'And the people of Hell will moan in such a manner that if one could die of sorrow, they would die.' And this is [referred to in] the verse wherein Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when all matters will be settled… (Q19:39).

Al-Hasan ibn Ulwan narrated from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, in Paradise there is a tree from whose top garments come forth, and from its bottom come horses of mixed black and white, saddled, bridled, and winged, that neither defecate nor urinate. They are mounted by the friends of Allah, and they fly with them in Paradise wherever they wish. So those who are below them will say, 'Our Lord, what has brought Your servants to this nobility?' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'Verily, they used to stand [in prayer] at night and not sleep, and fast during the day and not eat, and fight the enemy and not be cowardly, and give charity and not be miserly.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ulwan narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, this fire of yours is but one-seventieth of the fire of Hell. It has been extinguished seventy times with water and then rekindled. Were that not so, no human being would have been able to bear it once it is ignited. And indeed, it will be brought on the Day of Resurrection until it is placed upon the Fire, so it will scream a scream such that no close angel nor any sent Prophet will remain but that he will go down on his knees out of dread from its scream.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ulwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn 'Ali from his fathers from 'Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Verily, the lowest in rank among the inhabitants of Paradise, from among the martyrs, is one who will have twelve thousand wives from the wide-eyed houris, four thousand virgins, and twelve thousand non-virgins. Each of these wives will be served by seventy thousand servants, but the wide-eyed houris will have something more. He will go around their gatherings every week, and when the day or the hour of one of them comes, they will gather around her singing in voices so sweet and nice that no other voices can compare, until nothing remains in Paradise but that it is swayed by their voices. They will say, “Indeed, we are immortal, so we will never die; and we are [soft and] tender, so we will never become [wrinkled and] hard; and we are satisfied, so we will never get angry.”'

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from one of his learned companions (the jurists) who said: When Allah created Paradise, and made its rivers flow, and dangled its fruits and ornaments, He said: 'By My might, a miser will never be allowed into you.'

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (al-Husayn) from Abū Baṣīr from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah created with His hand a paradise that no eye has seen (other than Him), and no creature is familiar with. The Blessed and Exalted Lord opens it up every morning and says, ‘Increase in [your sweet smelling] fragrance, increase in [your fresh] breeze!’ So it says (or He says), ‘Successful indeed are the believers.’ That is the [interpretation of the] verse wherein Allah, the Exalted, says: No soul can imagine what delights are hidden in store for them as a reward for what they used to do (Q32:17).

Muhammad ibn Sinan said: A man narrated to me from Abu Khalid al-Sayqal, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the inhabitants of Paradise will have table spreads placed for them upon which will be all that they desire of foods that are incomparable in terms of their deliciousness and goodness, then [once they have partaken of it,] they will be moved from that to another.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a Houri of Paradise were to look down upon the people of this world and display one of her forelocks, the people of this world would be entranced, or they would die. And verily, when a worshipper prays and does not ask his Lord to marry him to the wide-eyed Houris, they say: 'How abstemious is this one regarding us!'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily in Hell there is a valley for the arrogant ones which is called Saqar. It complained to Allah about the intensity of its heat and asked Him to permit it to respire, so He permitted it and when it exhaled, it burnt [the entirety of] Hell.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Paradise will say, 'O Lord, You filled the Fire just as You promised it, so fill me [as well] just as You promised me!' So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will create a creation and make them enter Paradise. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Blessed are they, for they [shall] neither [have] witnessed the sorrows of the world nor its worries.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from 'Asim ibn Sulman mentioned in the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, [They are] made to drink from a scalding spring, he said: A sound [like moaning] will be heard from it due to the intensity of its heat.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abū Khālid al-Qammāṭ, who said, 'I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) [and in another version: Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him)]' 'When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of Hell into Hell, then what [happens next]?' So Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) said, 'If Allah wishes to create another creation and make a world for them to return to, He will do so – and I am not saying to you that this is what He will [surely] do.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, then what?' So he said: 'I do not assert to you that He, the Exalted, will create a creation who will worship Him.'

Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbaydillāh narrated from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr who said: I visited Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) while a group of his companions were with him, so he said to me, ‘O Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, have you read the Qurʾān?’ I said, ‘Yes, [in] this recitation.’ He said, ‘That is what I was asking you about, not any other.’ I said, ‘Yes, may I be your ransom! Why [do you ask]?’ He said, ‘Because Mūsā (peace be upon him) spoke to his people about something that they did not accept from him, so they came out against him in Egypt and fought him, so he fought against them and killed them. And because ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) [also] spoke to his people about something that they did not accept from him, so they came out against him in Takrīt and fought him, so he fought against them and killed them. This is what is being referred to in the verse wherein Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: …Then a group from the Banī Isrāʾīl believed while another disbelieved. We supported the believers against their enemies, so they prevailed (Q61:14). And the first Riser who will rise from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, will [also] speak to you about something that you will not accept from him, so you will come out against him at Rumaylah al-Daskarah and fight him, and he will fight you and kill you. That will be the last rebellion to ever take place. Then, O Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, Allah will gather the first and the last. Then Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family) will be brought among the people of his time and he will be told, ‘O Muḥammad, did you convey My message and provide arguments to the people in the way I had instructed you to speak to them?’ So he will reply, ‘Yes, O Lord.’ He will then ask the people, ‘Did he convey to you [the message] and provide arguments [for it] to you?’ But the people will say, ‘No.’ So He will [again] ask Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), and he will reply, ‘Yes [I did], O Lord.’ And Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will already know that he had done that. He will repeat this [question] three times, after which He will accept the [truthful] answer of Muḥammad and reject the [dishonest] answer of the people. Then they will be driven to the fire of Hell. Then ʿAlī (peace be upon him) will be brought among the people of his time and he will be asked the same thing that Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, and his people will lie

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abu al-Maghra', from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Hilal, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I do not meet you except in [long] years, so advise me with something so that I may adopt it.' He said, 'I advise you to be mindful of Allah, to practice piety, and to strive [in worship]. And beware of aspiring to the position of one who is above you.' And sufficient is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, told His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do not impress you their wealth and their children.' And He said: 'And do not extend your gaze [yearningly] at what We have provided their groups of the embellishment of the life of this world.' If you fear any of this [happening to you], then recall the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for his sustenance was from barley, his sweetness from dates, and his fuel was palm fronds if he found them. And if a calamity befalls you in your self, or your wealth, or your child, then recall your calamity with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for the creatures have never been afflicted with anything like it.

Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) say: 'Indeed I dislike a man who seeks to please his Lord with something while not having anything better than it [to offer]. So when I see him prolonging his bowing, I say: O [base] soul! And when I see him prolonging his prostration, I say: O [base] soul!'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Should I not inform you about Islam: its branch, its root, its summit and its peak? I said, Yes, indeed, may I be your ransom! He said: As for its root, it is prayer; as for its branch, it is alms-tax; as for its summit and peak, it is holy struggle.

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Yamānī, who attributed the statement to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (peace be upon him), that he would say: The best things through which the supplicants can entreat Allah are: faith in Allah and His Messenger, jihād in the way of Allah, and the word of oneness (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ) — for indeed it is the innate nature (fiṭrah); establishing prayer — for indeed it is the creed (millah); giving the zakāt — for indeed it is part of what is obligatorily due to Allah; fasting in the month of Ramaḍān — for indeed it is a shield from His chastisement; pilgrimage to the House — for indeed it alleviates poverty and wipes away sin; maintaining ties with near of kin — for indeed it is a means of increasing one’s wealth and delaying one’s death; giving charity in secret — for indeed it does away with sin and extinguishes divine wrath; and [doing] good turns — for indeed they repel tragic death and protect [one] from falling into disrepute. Ensure that you are [always] honest, for Allah is with the one who is truthful, and turn aside from falsehood, for indeed lies take one away from faith. Know that the truthful one is close to salvation and honor, while the liar is on the brink of humiliation and destruction. Speak [only] what is good and you will be known for it, act upon it and you will become one of its folk. Return the trust to the one who entrusted it to you, and keep ties with the near of kin and turn towards them in kindness.

Al-Qasim and Fadalah narrated from Aban, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is an hour of contemplation better than standing [in prayer] for a night?' He replied, 'Yes.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'An hour of contemplation is better than standing [in prayer] for a night.' I asked, 'How does one contemplate?' He said, 'One passes by ruins and dwellings, contemplates, and says: Where are your inhabitants? Where are those who built you? Why do you not respond!'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Nadr, from (Abi Sayyar) Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a sermon: 'Shall I not inform you of the best of creation in this world and the Hereafter? It is forgiveness towards those who wrong you, doing good to those who do evil to you, and giving to those who deprive you.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'In mutual hatred is the severer of hair; I do not mean the severing of hair [through shaving], but I mean the severing of faith.'

Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Let people not delude you from yourself, for verily recompense will reach you, not them. And let your day not be spent on this and that [trivialities], for indeed with you is one who records your deeds. And do not consider the little good [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a way that will please you. And do not consider the little evil [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a manner that will displease you. And do good, for I have not seen anything more intense in seeking out, nor quicker in catching up with, an old sin [and effacing it] than a good deed. Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: Verily good deeds wipe out evil deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful.'

Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to a man,' 'Why is it that you hurt the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So the man said to him, 'May I be your ransom! How do we hurt him?' He said, 'Do you not know that your actions are presented to him? So when he sees that they contain [acts of] disobedience to Allah, that hurts him. Do not hurt the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and please him [instead (by your good deeds)].'

Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Sama'ah who said, 'I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying,' 'Do not consider much good as abundant, and do not consider few sins as paltry, for verily few sins gather until they become many. And fear Allah in private and in public, until you give half of yourselves [to Him]. And hasten to the obedience of Allah, be truthful in speech, and fulfill the trust, for indeed that is for your own benefit. Do not oppress [anyone] and do not enter into that which is not permissible for you, for indeed that is to your detriment.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, and gives for the sake of Allah, is among those whose faith is complete.
And from him (peace be upon him) that he said: Among the firmest handles of faith are that you love for Allah, hate for Allah, give for Allah, and withhold for Allah.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zur'ah, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Guard yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is humans and stones.' I said: 'This is my soul that I am guarding, but how should I guard my family?' He replied: 'Instruct them to do what Allah has commanded, and forbid them from what Allah has forbidden. If they obey you, you will have guarded them; but if they disobey you, you will have fulfilled your responsibility.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Hassan, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Be mindful of Allah in the manner which He deserves,' so he said, 'He is to be obeyed and never disobeyed, remembered and never forgotten, thanked and never shown ingratitude.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Ya'qub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three things are such that people cannot [easily] bear them: pardoning [the wrongs of] others, assisting someone [else] with one’s wealth, and remembering Allah often.' Ibn Abi Ya'qub said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever speaks regarding [a matter pertaining to] justice yet goes against it [himself] to something else, he shall be burdened with [great] regret on the Day of Resurrection.'

From al-Nadr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Zayd al-Shahham who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' Beware of the violent strikes of Allah by night and by day. So I asked, 'What are the violent strikes of Allah?' He said, 'His punishment for sins.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) saying: 'One who acts upon what Allah has made obligatory upon him is among the best of people; and whoever avoids what Allah has forbidden him is among the most devoted of people; and whoever is content with what Allah has allotted for him is among the richest of people.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he said: Woe to the one who does not submit to Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil. He said: Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' will not enter the heavenly realms until his statement is completed with righteous action. And one who submits to Allah without following a just Imam has no religion; and one who submits to Allah yet obeys an unjust person has no religion. He also said: All communities were deluded by mutual boasting [about quantity], until they visited the graves. He said: One who does good and does not sin is better than one who does good and also sins. And one who does good and sins is better than one who only sins and does no good. He said: Stopping when in doubt is better than plunging into destruction.

Fadalah ibn 'Uthman narrated from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Advise me.' He said, 'I advise you to have God-consciousness, be truthful in speech, fulfill the trusts, and be a good companion to those who accompany you. When it is before sunrise and before sunset, you should engage in supplication. Strive [in this] and do not hold back from asking anything from your Lord, and do not say, "This is something He will not give," but supplicate, for indeed Allah does what He wills.'

Fadalah ibn Sinan, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from 'Ajlān Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Treat people fairly with yourself, assist them with your wealth, and be pleased for them with what you are pleased for yourself. Remember Allah often, and beware of laziness and ennui, for that is what my father used to advise me, and that is what his father would advise him, and that applies to the night prayer. Indeed, if you are lazy, you will not fulfill the right of Allah, and if you are lethargic, you will not fulfill anyone else's right.

Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Kalbi from Amr ibn Khald from Zayd ibn Ali from his fathers from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: A man from the family of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sought permission [to enter] and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said to him: 'I advise you not to associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut into pieces and burnt with fire; and do not disobey your parents, and if they wish you to leave your world, then leave it; and do not curse people; and when you meet your Muslim brother, greet him with a cheerful face and pour for him the extra water from your bucket. Convey to the Muslims you meet salutations from me, and invite people to Islam, and be sure that for each person who responds to you, you will gain the reward of freeing a slave from the descendants of Jacob, and teach them that al-Sughra is forbidden upon them, meaning Nabidh, which is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden.'

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bilād narrated from his father, from one of our companions, who attributed it to the Prophet (ṣ), saying: A bedouin came to the Prophet (ṣ) and took hold of the bridle of his mount as he was proceeding to one of his battles. Then he said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me an action by which I may enter Paradise!’ He (ṣ) replied, ‘Whatever you like people to give to you, give to them, and whatever you dislike them to give to you, do not give to them. Now let go of the mount.’

Ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:' Verily the righteous deed goes to Paradise and paves the way for its doer, just as a man sends his servant boy to prepare a place for him. As for those who believe and do good deeds, they prepare for themselves [their eternal abode].

Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from Uthman ibn Thabit, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'O Ali, I advise you regarding your soul concerning certain qualities, so preserve them from me - O Allah, help him -' As for the first, it is truthfulness - never let a lie be spoken from your mouth. The second is piety - never act treacherously. The third is fearing Allah as though you see Him. The fourth is crying out of fear of Allah - for each tear a mansion will be built for you in Paradise. The fifth is spending your wealth and tears for your religion. The sixth is adhering to my sunnah in my prayer, my fasting, and my charity. As for my prayer, it is fifty-one [rak'ahs]; as for my fasting, it is three days in every month, in its beginning, middle, and end; as for my charity, it is to spare no effort until it is said that you have been extravagant, while you have not been extravagant. And I bid you to maintain the nightly prayer, maintain the nightly prayer, maintain the nightly prayer! And I bid you to maintain the midday prayer, maintain the midday prayer, maintain the midday prayer! I bid you to recite the Qur'an in every condition. And I bid you to raise your hands in supplication and then turn them back [towards yourself]. I bid you to brush your teeth during every ablution and prayer. And I bid you to [espouse] beautiful moral traits so inculcate them [in yourself], and I warn you against evil traits so eschew them. Then if you do not act upon what I advise you [herewith], then do not blame anyone but yourself [for the consequences].

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Kulayb al-Asadi who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Maintain ties with each other, strive for excellence in goodness, have compassion for one another, and be righteous brothers as Allah has commanded you.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Kulayb al-Asadi, from Hasan ibn Mus'ab, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Soften your speech with the hypocrite, and sincerely direct your love to the believer; and if a Jew sits with you, then be gracious in his company.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Yusuf ibn 'Imran, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' Verily, Allah revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'I have gathered for you all speech in four statements.' He asked, 'What are they, O Lord?' He said, 'One is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people.' He said, 'O Lord, explain them to me so that I may act upon them.' He said, 'As for that which is for Me, it is that you worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for that which is for you, I will recompense you for your action when you are most in need of it. As for that which is between Me and you, it is upon you to supplicate and upon Me to answer. As for that which is between you and the people, it is that you should be pleased for the people what you are pleased for yourself.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Husayn ibn Usamah who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'You will not be a believer until you are fearful and hopeful, until you are an actor for what you fear and hope for.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Mu'adh, from Abu Arakah, who said: I prayed the Fajr prayer behind Ali (peace be upon him) in this mosque of yours, then he turned towards his right side, and a sorrowful disposition was upon him until the sun rose over the wall of this mosque of yours to the extent of a spear, and it is not there today. Then he turned to the people and said: 'By Allah, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would spend this night in it, alternating between their foreheads and their knees [in prostration and bowing]. When morning came, they rose up dusty and pale, with a mark between their eyes like the knee of a goat. When Allah was mentioned, they would bend as a tree bends on a windy day, and their eyes flowed [with tears] until their clothes became wet.' He said: Then he stood up while saying: 'By Allah, it is as though the people spent the night in negligence.' Then he was not seen laughing until the wicked one did what he did.'

Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty: 'Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful.' He said: '[They are fearful] out of their concern and their hope; they fear that their deeds will be rejected if they do not obey Allah – and He has power over all things – and they hope that He accepts [their deeds] from them.'

Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Sama'ah, from Abū Baṣīr and al-Naḍr, from 'Āṣim, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic: 'They give what they give with their hearts fearful,' he said: 'They perform [deeds] and know that they will be rewarded for it.'

Al-Nadr narrated from Ibn Sinan, from al-Yamani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, said: 'By My might and My majesty, by My greatness and My power, by My grandeur and exaltedness, [I swear that] My servant does not prefer My desire over his own desire but that I place needlessness [and contentment] in his soul, make his [primary] concern for his Hereafter, prevent him from suffering loss, guarantee his sustenance from the skies and the earth, and stand behind him [to ensure his benefit] in the transaction of every trader.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Maskan from Abu Hamzah from Yahya ibn Aqil from Habashi who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) addressed the people, praised Allah and glorified Him, and mentioned his cousin Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and sent blessings upon him. Then he said: 'Now then, verily those who came before you were destroyed due to the sins they committed while their rabbis and scholars did not forbid them from that. When they became excessive in sins, punishments descended upon them.' So enjoin good and forbid evil, and know that enjoining good and forbidding evil neither bring death closer nor do they sever [one's] livelihood. Indeed, the [divine] command descends from the sky to the earth like drops of rain; to every individual [comes] what is ordained by Allah to increase or decrease. So if any of you is afflicted by a calamity in his family, wealth, or self, and sees a punishment [upon] his brother, let it not be an ordeal for him; he awaits one of two good outcomes. Either a caller from Allah [in the form of death], in which case what is with Allah is better for him, or sustenance from Allah. If he possesses family, wealth, or children, that is the tillage of this world, and good deeds are the tillage of the Hereafter, and Allah may gather both for some groups.

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Woe be to the community that does not worship Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil.
Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Woe be to the one who enjoins evil and forbids good.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from 'Udhafir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, Allah chose Islam for Himself as a religion, so be its virtuous companions through generosity and good character.'

Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioned one day good character and said: A servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, so he ordered that they dig a grave for him. They went and dug, and a rock appeared to them in the grave, so they were unable to dig. They came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, we dug for so-and-so and a rock appeared to us, so we began to strike it until our pickaxes became notched. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: How is that? While he was of good character? Go back and dig. So they went back and Allah made it easy until they were able to bury him.

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If good character were a visible creature, there would be nothing more beautiful in creation than it; and if evil character were a visible creature, there would be nothing uglier in creation than it. Verily, Allah causes the servant with good character to attain the station of one who fasts and stands in prayer.'

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man of the Banu Hashim, who said: I heard him say: 'Four [traits] are such that whoever possesses them, his Islam is complete, even if what is between his horns and his feet [i.e., his whole body] is covered in sins, that will not diminish it: Truthfulness, Modesty, Good Character, and Gratitude.'

Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me one thing, for I am a man who journeys and stays in the desert.' He said, 'Do not get angry.' The bedouin found that to be too trivial, so he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me one thing, for I am a man who journeys and stays in the desert.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Do not get angry.' The bedouin took that to be trivial [advice] so he returned once more and repeated his request. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) answered him [in the same way]. The man thought to himself, 'I will not ask about anything else after this. I understand that he has advised me and warned me not to accuse [anyone] falsely when I get angry, and not to kill [or fight with anyone] when I get angry.' Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said, 'Anger is the key to all evil.' And he said, 'Iblīs used to be with the angels and the angels considered him to be one of them, yet in the knowledge of Allah he was not one of them. When the command to prostrate before Ādam was issued, he was filled with prejudice and anger, so Allah brought out what he held within himself of prejudice and anger.'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ribʿī who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to Yaḥyā al-Saqqāʾ: 'O Yaḥyā, verily good character is a means of ease, and verily bad character causes difficulty.'

Al-Mahamili narrated from Dharīḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When Allah wishes goodness for a household, He grants them moderation in livelihood and good character.'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al--Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Kāmil who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'When you mingle with people, if you are able to ensure that your hand is uppermost over any one of the people you mingle with, then do so. Verily, the servant may have some shortcomings in his worship, yet he possesses good character, so Allah elevates him by his character to the rank of the fasting one who stands [in night prayer].'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Those who will be closest to me tomorrow are the ones with the best character and the closest of you to the people.'

Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Rubayʿ, from al-Faḍl, from Abū  ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who among the people has the most perfect faith?' He said, 'Those who have the best character.'

Al-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulman who said: Al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to me from Zayd ibn ʿAlī who said: Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, revealed to His Prophet, Dāwūd (peace be upon him): 'When My servant remembers Me in his anger, I remember him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all My creation, and I do not cause him to perish along with that which I annihilate.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah is Gentle (Rafiq); He grants the reward and He loves every gentle person, and He grants for gentleness that which He does not grant for harshness.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from 'Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! By Allah, I surely know that you do not bring comfort to the people with your wealth, but rather with cheerfulness and good character.' He (the narrator) said: And I heard him say: 'May Allah have mercy on every easy-going, cheerful one.'

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Character (al-khalq) is a gift that Allah bestows upon whomever He wills from His creation. Some of it is a natural disposition (sajjiyyah) and some of it is acquired practice/intention (binyah). I asked: Which of the two is better? He said: The one with intention (niyyah) is better. For indeed, the one with natural disposition is compelled to act in that manner and cannot do otherwise, whereas the one with intention is the one who perseveres in obedience, so he is better.'

One of our companions narrated from Jābir ibn Sadr, from Muʿādh ibn Muslim who said: I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) while there was a man with him, and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) told him, ‘The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Gentleness is propitious, and roughness is inauspicious.’

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Sinan, verily the sustenance of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was barley without condiments. Indeed, righteousness and good character increase the longevity of homes and increase in lifespans.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, good character melts away sin the way the sun melts ice, and bad character corrupts action the way vinegar spoils honey.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'So-and-so died and we dug a grave for him, but the earth prevented it.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'He was of bad character.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you of the best among you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Those with the best character, those who are amiable and hospitable, and those who get along with people and with whom others get along well.'
Ibn al-Abbas from Ibn Shajarah from Ibrahim ibn Abi Raja who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Good character increases livelihood.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The practices of doing good protect from the falls of evil, and every good deed is charity. Those who do good in this world are the doers of good in the Hereafter, and those who do evil in this world are the doers of evil in the Hereafter. Indeed, the first of the inhabitants of Paradise to enter Paradise are those who do good, and the first of the people of Hell to enter Hell are those who do evil.'

Uthman ibn Isa from Ali ibn Salim * said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: A verse in the Book of Allah that is unrestrictedly applicable. I asked, 'Which is it?' He said: The saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, in His Book: 'Is there any reward for goodness except goodness?' It applies to the disbeliever and the believer, to the righteous and the wicked. Whoever is done a good turn, it is incumbent upon him to reciprocate; and reciprocation does not mean doing the same as what was done for him; rather, he must do good to the extent that he sees that by his action, he has attained the merit of the initiator.

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said: 'Whoever asks you by Allah, give to him; and whoever does a good turn to you, recompense him. If you do not find anything to recompense him with, then pray to Allah for him until you feel sure that you have recompensed him.'
Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Ibn ʿAbbād who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: A good turn is not considered a good turn except with one who possesses honor or religion.

Ibn Abi al-Bilād narrated from the one who informed him, from one of the scholars, who said: The poor believers will be stopped on the Day of Judgment, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, will say to them: 'Indeed, I did not make you poor due to your insignificance in My eyes; rather, I made you poor to test you. Go forth, and let there be no one who did good to you in the world but that you take his hand and make him enter Paradise [with you].'

Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from one who informed him, from some of the jurists, who said: The poor of the believers will be stopped [before God] on the Day of Resurrection, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, will say to them: 'Verily, I did not impoverish you because of your insignificance to Me, but I impoverished you to test you. Go forth, and no one who did you a favor in the world shall remain [unavenged]; you shall take his hand and bring him into Paradise.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from one of his companions, from Abu Ubaydah Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Do good to one who is worthy and to one who is not worthy, for if he is not worthy, then you are worthy.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Dawud al-Riqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:' Verily Allah, the Almighty, made among His creatures some who are worthy of goodness (al-ma'ruf). He made them love goodness and love doing it. He enjoined upon those who seek goodness that they should refer to them and that they should fulfill it, just as He made rain flow easily to the arid land to bring it to life and cause its inhabitants to thrive. And verily Allah made among His creatures some who are enemies of goodness. He made them detest goodness and hate doing it. He forbade those who seek goodness from referring to them and prevented them from fulfilling it, just as He prevents rain from falling on the arid land to destroy its inhabitants through it. And what Allah forgives is greater [than what He punishes].

One of our companions narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily Allah has created among His creatures some servants whom He has chosen for the poor among our followers, so that He may reward them for that.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It suffices for your praise of your brother when he does you a good turn that you say to him: may Allah reward you with goodness; and when he is mentioned in his absence that you say: may Allah reward him with goodness. Then you will have [adequately] recipated [his kindness].'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us saying: Safwan narrated to us from Isḥāq ibn Ghālib, from his father, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Kindness [to parents] and charity given secretly are two things that dispel poverty, increase lifespan, and protect one from seventy bad deaths.

Al-Nadr and Fadala ibn Sinan, from al-Hafsh, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, a servant may be dutiful to his parents in their lifetime, then they pass away, and he does not repay their debt, nor does he seek forgiveness for them, so Allah writes him as undutiful. And verily, he may not have been dutiful to them in their lifetime, but when they pass away, he repays their debt and seeks forgiveness for them, so Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, writes him as dutiful. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And if you wish for Allah to increase your lifespan, then please your parents.' He said: 'I heard him say: Indeed, dutifulness increases sustenance.'

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Husayn, from Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ubaydullah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, keeping ties with close relatives purifies deeds, makes the accounting easy, wards off afflictions, and increases one’s lifespan.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Fazari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Verily, there may be a family that is dutiful [to their elders], so their wealth grows, even if they are sinful.'

Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmīrah, from Ibn Muskān, from Ibrāhīm ibn Shuʿayb who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'Verily my father has become very old and weak, so we carry him when he needs to relieve himself.' He said: 'If you can continue doing that [yourself] then do so, and feed him morsels with your own hand, for that will be a shield for you tomorrow [from the Fire].'

Fadala ibn Sinan narrated from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Hakam ibn al-Husayn from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is no ugly action but that I have performed it; is there for me any repentance?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) replied: 'Are any of your parents alive?' He said: 'My father.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Then go and be kind to him.' So when he had left, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commented: 'If only it was his mother!'

Fadala ibn Sinan, from al-Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from al-Subbah, from al-Jabir, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have two parents who are opposite (to us).' He said to him: 'Be kind to them as you are kind to the Muslims who love us.'

Fadala ibn Sinan narrated from Sayf, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Jābir, from al-Waṣṣāfī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: Charity given secretly extinguishes the Lord’s wrath, and being kind to parents and keeping ties with near relatives increases lifespans.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zur'ah, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the womb is suspended from the Throne, and it will call out on the Day of Judgment: O Allah, bless the one who keeps my ties and cut off the one who severs my ties.' I asked: 'Is this [in reference to] the womb of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He replied: 'Rather, the womb of the Messenger of Allah is one of them.' And he said: 'Verily, the womb will come on the Day of Judgment like the hub of a wheel, which is the spindle. Whoever comes to it having established its ties, light will spread out for him until it enters him into Paradise; and whoever comes to it having severed its ties, it will constrict from him until it casts him into the Fire.'

Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Muskān from Abū Ḥamzah from Yaḥyā ibn Umm al-Ṭawīl who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (peace be upon him) gave a sermon to the people, praised Allah and glorified Him, then said: 'A man is never needless of his tribe, even if he is wealthy and has children, nor of their fellowship, respect, and their support of him with their hands and tongues. They are the greatest people in their defence of him in his absence, the most important for his affairs, and those who have the most sympathy for him when he is afflicted by some calamity or some mishap befalls him. Whoever withdraws his hands from his tribe, it is only a single hand he withdraws from them while many hands are withdrawn from him. Yet the one who offers pure and true affection to his tribe, and extends his hand to do good to them when possible, in order to please Allah, Allah compensates him for what he spends in this world and multiplies his reward in the Hereafter. True brothers among the people are better than wealth which one consumes and bequeaths. Let none of you ever increase in his apathy towards his brother, nor replace him with another when he sees no benefit from him, or if he is poor in terms of material wealth. Let none of you neglect any of the near of kin whom he finds to be in need, without fulfilling his need with that which would neither harm him if he spent it nor benefit him if he withheld it.'

Al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Mu'awiya who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Verily, keeping ties with relatives makes the accounting easier on the Day of Judgment.' They maintain the ties that Allah has ordered to be maintained, stand in awe of their Lord, and fear the harshness of reckoning.

Al-Qasim from Abd al-Samad ibn Hilal from a man among our companions who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Verily, the family of so-and-so are dutiful to one another and maintain ties.' He said: 'Then they will grow [in numbers] and their wealth will grow, and they will continue in this state until they sever ties. If they do that, it shall break away from them.'

Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Kindness [to parents] increases one's lifespan and charity given secretly calms the Lord's wrath.

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it [to a higher authority], and said: Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (peace be upon him) saw a man under the shade of the Throne and said, 'O Lord, who is this person whom You have brought so close that You have placed him under the shade of Your Throne?' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said, 'O Mūsā, this person was never undutiful to his parents, nor did he envy the people for what Allah had given them of His favors.' He asked, 'O Lord, are there any among Your creation who are undutiful to their parents?' He replied, 'The undutiful ones are not [counted as] theirs.'

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: If Allah knew [of anything] less than ‘uff [against parents], He would have forbidden it, and that is the smallest form of undutifulness. And among the forms of undutifulness is for a man to look at his parents with a stern [and angry] stare.

Ibn Abi al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said: 'Shall I not guide you to the best of moral traits of this world and the Hereafter?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Whoever establishes ties with the one who cuts him off, gives to the one who deprives him, and forgives the one who wrongs him. And whoever would be pleased to have his life asked for (extended) and his sustenance increased, then let him be mindful of Allah and keep ties with his near relatives.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted: 'And fear Allah by whom you ask one another, and the wombs [of kinship],' he said, 'It refers to the kinship ties of the people. Verily, Allah commanded their maintenance and magnified them. Do you not see that He placed it alongside Himself?'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said: In the book of Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), [it is stated]: There are three traits whose possessor never dies until he has seen their evil consequences: aggression, severing ties with near relatives, and giving false testimony under oath, by which he proceeds to fight against Allah. Indeed, the act of obedience that brings the quickest reward is keeping ties with near relatives. A community may be sinners but they keep ties with each other and [as a result] their wealth grows and they thrive. Verily, [giving] false oaths and severing ties with near relatives ruins abodes, turning them into wastelands for their inhabitants, and removes mercy – and verily in the removal of mercy lies the severance of one’s lineage.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should I be kind to?' He said, 'Your mother.' He asked, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He asked, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your father.'

Some of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Ḥakam al-Khayyāṭ, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Can a son recompense his father?' He said, 'No, except in two cases: if he finds him enslaved, he buys him and emancipates him; or if he has a debt, he pays it off on his behalf.'

Ḥanān narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said: He said: I heard him saying, 'A man came to Abū Dharr and gave him good news of his sheep that had given birth. He said, “O Abū Dharr, I bring glad tidings that your sheep have reproduced and increased in number!” He said, “I am not pleased by their increase in number. The few of them that are sufficient are more beloved to me than many that distract [me]. Verily I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: On the two sides of the path (ṣirāt) on the Day of Judgment will be the near of kin and the trusts, so when one who kept ties with the near of kin and returned the trusts passes by them, they will not throw him into the Fire.”'

One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAmr ibn Sahl, from Ruwāt who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) say: 'Verily, keeping ties of kinship increases wealth, enhances love among the family, and postpones death.'

One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān, who said: My father Miskān narrated to him from a man that they were in the house of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and Muyassir was among them. They spoke about keeping ties with near kinsfolk, so Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muyassir, your death had arrived on more than one occasion, but each time it was postponed for you by Allah due to your keeping ties with your near relatives.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: It may be that thirty years remain for a man to live, but he regularly keeps ties with his close kinsfolk and with his near relatives, so Allah increases it to thirty-three years. And it may be that thirty-three years remain of his life, but he is undutiful towards his close kinsfolk and cuts off ties with his near relatives, so Allah reduces it to thirty years.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I seek Allah’s protection from a bad neighbour in a residential abode – his eyes watch you and his heart scrutinises you. If he sees you [happy and] well, it upsets him and if he sees you in trouble, it pleases him.'
Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ishaq, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Raja, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Good neighborliness increases sustenance.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Al-Qasim ibn Ali narrated to us from Abi Basir from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father struck his servant boy with a single whip. He had sent him on an errand but he delayed [in doing what was required]. So the servant boy cried and said, 'Allah! O Ali ibn al-Husayn, you send me on an errand and then strike me?!' So my father began to cry and said [to me], 'O my son, go to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and offer two rak'ahs of prayer, and then say, "O Allah, forgive Ali ibn al-Husayn for his mistake on the Day of Judgment."' Then he told the servant boy, 'Go, for you are free in the way of Allah!' Abi Basir said, 'I asked him, "May I be your ransom! Was the emancipation [of his servant] an expiation for the sin?' But he remained silent.

Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd narrated from al-Dawa' ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: [It is written] in the book of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): When you employ what your right hand possesses for something that is difficult for them, then work with them in it. He [the narrator] said: And indeed, you would instruct them, saying: 'Stay as you are,' then he would come and look. If it was heavy [difficult], he would say: 'In the name of Allah,' then he would work with them; and if it was light, he would step aside from them.

Fadalah ibn 'Ukaym narrated from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and from Abu Sakhl, from Salman, who said: I was sitting in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when a man came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, [what is the ruling regarding] the slave?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'He has been tested by you and you have been tested by him, so that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may see how grateful you are and how patient he is.'

Faḍālah ibn Sīnān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: A man from Banī Fahd passed by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was beating his slave, and the slave was saying, 'I seek refuge with Allah,' yet the man did not desist from him. When the slave saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he said, 'I seek refuge with Muḥammad,' so the man stopped beating him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He seeks refuge with Allah, yet you do not grant him protection; he seeks refuge with Muḥammad, so you grant him protection? By Allah, His one who seeks refuge is more deserving of protection than [one who seeks refuge with] Muḥammad.' The man said, 'He is free for the sake of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By the One who sent me as a Prophet with truth, if you had not done so, your face would have fallen into the heat of the Fire.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) struck a slave, then he entered his house, brought out a whip, then stripped himself of his shirt for the slave, then said to him: 'Strike 'Ali ibn al-Husayn [for having struck you]!' but the servant refused, so he gave him fifty dinars.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: There is no person but that with him are two angels who write whatever he utters, then they send that up to two [other] angels above them who record what was good or evil from it, and cast aside anything other than that.

Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan from Amr ibn Shamar from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the position of the two angels in the human being, so he said: 'One is here and one is here,' meaning at his two jawbones.

Hammād narrated from Ḥurayz, from Zurārah, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: The angel does not write down except that which he hears. Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, said: Remember your Lord inwardly, in humility and awe… He said: No one knows the reward of that remembrance within the heart of the servant other than Allah, the Exalted.

Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Husayn ibn Musa, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, in the air there is an angel called Isma'il, who is over three hundred thousand angels; each of them is over a hundred thousand angels. They count the actions of the servants. And when the beginning of the year comes, Allah sends to them an angel called al-Sijill, and that [record] is gathered from them. On the Day we will roll up the sky as al-Sijill rolls up his scrolls [of recorded deeds]. This is the word of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān narrated from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the glance of the Angel of Death (peace be upon him). He said: 'Do you not see a group of people sitting together, then sudden speechlessness afflicts them, so none of them speaks? That is the moment in which the Angel of Death glances at them.'

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Buraiz al-Razzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O my son, know that the rank of the Shi'a is based upon the degree of their narrating and conscious knowledge, for indeed, conscious knowledge is comprehension of the narration. With comprehensions of the narrations, the believer elevates to the farthest levels of faith. Indeed, I have looked into the book of Ali (peace be upon him) and I found in the book: Indeed, the value and rank of every person is his conscious knowledge. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will judge people in accordance to the amount of what He has granted them of intellects in the life of this world.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur, may Allah be pleased with him, told us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir told us, from his paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: A narration that you comprehend is better than a thousand narrations which you narrate. A man from you will not be knowledgeable (faqih) until he is aware of the various indications (ma'arid) of our speech. Verily, the word from our speech does indeed turn to seventy indications, all of which we may intend.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from his fathers, from Umar ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The appearance of Monotheism is in its interior, and its interior is in its appearance; its appearance is characterized and cannot be seen, and its interior is existent and is not hidden. He is sought in every place, and no place is absent from Him by a wink of an eye. He is present, not limited, and hidden, not lost.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Aziz al-Samarqandi, the jurist in the land of Balkh, told us: He said, Abu Ahmad al-Zahid al-Samarqandi, with his chain, ascribed it to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) A man asked him and said to him: Indeed, the foundation of the religion is Monotheism and Justice, and its knowledge is abundant, and a rational person must have it. So, mention what can be easily stood upon and is attainable to memorize? He said: As for Monotheism, it is to proclaim as impossible upon your Lord that which is possible upon you, and as for Justice, it is to not attribute to your Creator that which He has blamed you for.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) was asked about the community of his nation, so he said: The community of my nation are the people of truth, even if they were few.

And with this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn Abdillah al-Alawi, that he ascribed it, saying: It was said to Allah’s Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family): What is the community of your nation? He said: Those who are on the truth, even if they were ten.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from 'Asem ibn Hameed, that he ascribed it, saying: A man came to the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, and said: Inform me about the tradition and innovation, and the community and schism?
