Then the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, said: The tradition is what was made a tradition by the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family. The innovation is what was invented after him. The community are the people of truth, even if they were a few. The schism are the people of falsehood, even if they were many.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Jamil ibn Amr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "What is 'Allah is Greater'?" I said: "Allah is Greater than everything." He said: "Was there a thing such that He is Greater than it?" I said: "Then what is it?" He said: "Allah is Greater than to be described."

We were told by Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, who said: He told me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from those he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man said in his presence: 'Allah is Greater.' So he said: 'Allah is Greater than what thing?' Then he said: 'Than everything.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have limited Him.' Then the man said: 'And how shall I say?' So he said: 'Allah is Greater than to be described.'

We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, that he said: We were told by Abu'l-Qasim, Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi, and Abu Yusuf, Ya'qub ibn Yazid al-Anbari, the Writer, from Abu Muhammad, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Sadiq, Abu Abdillah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers, peace be upon them, He said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The one who loves us, the Household, let him praise Allah, Exalted is He, for the first of graces. It was said: And what is the first of graces? He said: Having a good birth. None loves us except for the one whose birth is good, and none hates us except for the one whose birth is wicked.

We were told by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: We were told by my father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from more than one, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), that he said: The one who wakes up at the morning, finding the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him praise Allah for the initiator of graces. It was said: And what is the initiator of graces? He said: Having a good birth.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Tatana narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad al-Nahdi, from Abdullah ibn Salih, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father the Commander of the Believers Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: O Ali, whoever loves me, loves you, and loves the Imams from your offspring, let him praise Allah for the goodness of his birth, for indeed, none loves us except the one whose birth is good, and none hates us except the one whose birth is wicked.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who finds the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him recite prayer in abundance for his mother, for indeed, she did not betray his father.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qoub bin Yazid, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Abdullah bin Maskan, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Or the male attendants with no carnality' until the end of the verse, so he said: The fool who does not (sexually) approach women.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about: «the male attendants with no carnality». He said: It is the dumb, the imposed, who does not (sexually) approach women.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Hasan bin Mahboub, from Malik bin ‘Atiya, from Ibn Abi Ya’four, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: The one who slanders a believing man or a believing woman with what is not in them, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will detain him on the Day of Resurrection in a clay of lunacy until he leaves what he said: I said: And what is the clay of lunacy? He said: A pus that comes out from the genitals of harlots. Meaning adulteresses.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mihan ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd al-Iskafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The one who drinks wine or an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings, and if he returns, Allah will make him drink from the clay of lunacy. I said: And what is the clay of lunacy? He said: A pus that comes out from the genitals of adulteresses.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Buzay', from al-Mansur ibn Yunus, from an attendant of Abu Hamza, from Abu Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Everything is to perish, except for His Face" He said: Everything is to perish and the Face will remain. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is Greater than being characterized with a face, however, its meaning is: Everything is to perish, except for His religion and the face from which He is approached.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi told us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Rabi' al-Warraq, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Everything is to perish, except for His Face.' He said: We.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Mu'adhi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Fadl narrated to us, from his father, who said: I asked al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them), about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "No! Verily, they are, from their Lord, on that Day, indeed, obstructed" He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is not characterized by a place in which He is embodied and in which His servants will be obstructed from Him, however, He, Exalted and Glorious is He, means that they will be, from the reward of their Lord, obstructed. And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows." He said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is not characterized by coming and going. Exalted is He above movement. He only means by that: "And the commandment of your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows." And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Do they wait but that Allah will come to them in shadows of clouds, and so the Angels." He said: He says: "Do they wait but that Allah will bring to them Angels in shadows of clouds." This is how it was revealed. And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Allah ridiculed them" and about His saying: "Allah derides them" and about His saying: "And they plotted, and Allah plotted" and about His saying: "They attempt to deceive Allah, whilst He deceives them." He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, does not ridicule, nor mock, nor plot, nor deceive, however, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will reward them with the reward of ridiculing, and the reward of mocking, and the reward of plotting, and the reward of deception. Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a Great Highness.

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad, known as 'Allan al-Kulayni, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon them both) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The earth, all of it, is His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the Heavens are bent in His Right.' He said: That is the expression of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, to he who likened Him to His creation. Do you not see that He said: 'And they did not appraise Allah His true appraisal' when they said: 'The earth, all of it, is His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the Heavens are bent in His Right'? As He, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: 'And they did not appraise Allah His true appraisal, when they said: Allah did not send down unto a human being, anything.' Then, He, Exalted and Glorious is He, exalted Himself from the grasp and the right hand, so He said: 'Glorified is He, and Exalted, from what they associate.'

Muhammad ibn Muhammad 'Isam al-Kulayni narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad, known as 'Allan, narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid Imran ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn al-Qasim al-Raqqam, from al-Qasim ibn Muslim, from his brother Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He: «They forgot Allah, so He forgot them» He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, does not forget nor does He omit, but rather only the created, transient creature forgets and omits. Do you not hear Him, Exalted and Glorified is He, say: «And your Lord has never been forgetful»? Rather, He only rewards he who forgot Him and forgot the meeting of His Day by making them forget themselves, as He, Exalted and Glorified is He, said: «And do not be like those who forgot Allah, to which He made them forget themselves. They are the sinful.» And His saying, Exalted and Glorified is He: «So, today We will forget them like how they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs», meaning: We abandon them like how they abandoned preparation for the meeting of this day of theirs.

We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ya'qub bin Yazid, from Abbas bin Hilal, that he said: I asked al-Rida, peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the earth"? So he said: A Guide to the people of Heaven, and a Guide to the people of the earth. In the narration of al-Barqi: The Guidance of those who are in the Heavens, and a Guidance to those who are in the earth.

Ibrahim ibn Harun al-Haysi (in the City of Peace) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Thalj narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ayub narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ghalib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ayub, from al-Husayn ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhahli, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): I said: 'Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the earth.' He said: Thus is Allah, Exalted and Glorious. I said: 'The example of His Light'? He said to me: Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: 'Like a niche'? He said: The chest of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: 'In which is a lamp'? He said: In it is the Light of Knowledge, meaning Prophethood. I said: 'The lamp is within a glass'? He said: The knowledge of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family) issued to the heart of Ali (peace be upon him). I said: 'As if it is'? He said: For what thing are you reciting 'As if it is'? I said: And how do I read it, may I be sacrificed for you? He said: 'As if it is a glimmering planet.' I said: 'That is lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east, nor of the west'? He said: That is the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), neither a Jew nor a Christian. I said: 'Its oil is about to glow, although it has not been touched by fire'? He said: It is as if knowledge is about to exit the mouth of the knowledgeable from the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) before he utters it. I said: 'Light upon Light'? He said: The Imam following the Imam.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Hands?' He said: 'The hand, in the speech of the Arabs, means strength and grace.' He said: And mention Our servant Dawood, possessor of strength; and: The heavens We constructed with strength; meaning with strength; and: He strengthened them with a spirit from Him; meaning He empowered them. And it is said: 'So-and-so has a white hand with me,' meaning grace.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah told us, that Ahmad bin Muhammad bin 'Isa told us, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) will on the Day of Resurrection hold onto the Waist Cloth of Allah, and we will hold onto the Waist Cloth of our Prophet, and our party will hold onto our Waist Cloth. Then he said: The Waist Cloth is the Light.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, for Allah, Exalted and Glorious, there are creations whom He created from His Light, and a mercy from His mercy for His mercy; they are the Eye of Allah that sees, and His Ear that hears, and His Tongue that speaks among His creation by His permission, and His Trustees over what He has sent down of justification or warning or proof. By them Allah erases misdeeds, and by them He repels grievance, and by them He sends down mercy, and by them He gives life to the dead and causes the living to die, and by them He tests His creation, and by them He decides a decision among His creation. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, who are these? He said: The Successors.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Umar ibn Adheena, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And I blew into him from My Spirit» He said: It is a Spirit that Allah chose, selected, created, and attributed to Himself, and preferred over all other spirits. So He commanded and blew from him into Adam (peace be upon him).

More than one of our companions told me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: We were told by al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, who said: We were told by Bakr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from al-Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And I blew into him from My Spirit». How was this blowing? So he said: Indeed, the Spirit is moving like the wind, and it was only named a Spirit because its name was derived from wind, and He only extracted it on the phrase of Spirit because a spirit is homogenic to wind, and He only added it to Himself because He selected it over other spirits, like how He has selected one house among the houses and said: My House, and how He said to a Messenger among the Messengers: My Good Friend, and the likes of so. All of that is created, made, subject to a Lord and is managed.

With this chain: from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, that he said: We were told by Ali ibn al-Abbas, that he said: We were told by 'Ubees ibn Hisham, from Abdul-Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), with regards to His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And when I proportioned him and I blew into him from My Spirit» he said: From My Ability.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: I am the Guide, I am the Guided, and I am the father of the orphans and the needy, and the husband of the widows, and I am the refuge of every weak person, and the secure place of every fearful person, and I am the leader of the believers [into Paradise], and I am the Solid Rope of Allah, and I am the Strong Loop of Allah and the Word of Allah of Piety, and I am the Eye of Allah, and His Truthful Tongue, and His Hand, and I am the Regard of Allah, about which He says: «For a soul to say: How heartbroken am I for how undutiful I was towards the Regard of Allah» And I am the Hand of Allah that is extended towards His servants with mercy and forgiveness, and I am the Door of Humility. The one who knows me and knows my right, then he has known his Lord, because I am the Successor of His Prophet in His earth and His Proof upon His creation; none deny this except for one who rejects Allah and His Messenger.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from one who heard him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And the Jews said: The Hand of Allah is chained», they did not mean that it is literally so, but rather they said: The matter has been completed, so He does not add nor subtract. So Allah, Glorified be His Glory, said in denial of their saying: «Chained be their hands! And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His Hands are extended; He spends how He wishes.» Have you not heard Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, say: «Allah erases what He wishes, and He confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book».

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Mushriqi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'Rather, His Hands are extended.' So I said to him: 'Two hands, like this?' And I pointed with my hand towards his hands. Then he said: 'No, if He were like this, He would have been a created thing.'

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-'Ammar ibn Marwan, from al-Munkhil, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about this verse in the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And if you are killed in the Path of Allah, or die". He said: Then he said: Do you know what the Path of Allah is? I said: No, by Allah, except that I hear it from you. He said: The Path of Allah is Ali (peace be upon him) and his offspring, and the one who is killed in his Divine Authority is killed in the Path of Allah, and the one who dies in his Divine Authority dies in the Path of Allah.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Ubaydi, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from al-Husayn ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed to me (to spend) in the Path. He said: So he said to me: Spend it in Hajj. He said: I said: Indeed, he bequeathed to me in the Path. He said: Spend it in Hajj, for I do not know a path from His paths better than Hajj.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya bin Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubayd, from Hasan bin Rashid, that he said: I asked Abu'l-Hasan al-Askari, peace be upon him, in Medina about a man who bequeathed his wealth for the Path of Allah. He said: The Path of Allah is our Shi'a.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqteeni, from al-Mushriqi Hamza ibn al-Rabi', from those he mentioned, that he said: I was in the gathering of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when 'Amr ibn Ubayd entered and said to him: May I be your ransom, regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And he upon whom descends My wrath, has indeed fallen' [20:82]. What is that wrath? Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: It is the punishment, O 'Amr. Verily, he who claims that Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has moved from one thing to another thing, has indeed described Him with the characteristic of a created being. For indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is not incited by anything nor changed by anything.

With this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, ascribed to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And when they grieved Us' He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, does not grieve like our grieving, but He created Allies for Himself who grieve and are satisfied, and they are created and managed. So He made their satisfaction a satisfaction for Himself, and their anger an anger for Himself, and that is because He made them the callers to Him and the guides to Him, and for that they became as such. It is not that this reaches Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, like how it reaches His creation, but this is the meaning of what He said about that, He also said: 'He who humiliates an Ally to me, has indeed drawn a sword against Me in combat and invited Me to it.' He also said: 'He who obeys the Messenger, has indeed obeyed Allah.' He also said: 'Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, are only pledging allegiance to Allah.' All this and its similar is upon that which I mentioned to you, and so is satisfaction, wrath and other things than them that are similar to that. If it would be that for the created, it reaches grief and weariness, when He is the One who made them and created them, it would be possible for a sayer to say: Indeed, the created is to be annihilated one day, because if weariness and anger enter him, (it implies that) change enters him, and if change enters him, He cannot be secured from annihilation, and if it was as such, the Creator would not have been recognized from the created. Exalted is Allah above this saying, a great exaltation. He is the Creator of things, not for any need, and if it was for no need, limit and condition would be impossible in Him. Hence, understand that, Allah willing.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn Amr al-Faqimi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that a man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: Does He have satisfaction and anger? He said: Yes, and that is not like what is found in creatures. This is because satisfaction and anger are intrusions that enter into him, transferring him from one state to another; they are active, composite, with things having an entry into him. But our Creator has no entry for things into Him; He is One, One in Essence, One in Meaning. So His satisfaction is His reward and His anger is His punishment, without anything interlacing Him to agitate Him and transfer Him from one state to another, for that is indeed the characteristic of the created, the incapable and the needy. Whereas He, Blessed and Exalted, is the Strong, the Mighty. He has no need for anything from what He created, and all His creation is needy of Him. He created things not out of need nor cause, by invention and innovation.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, that he said: I asked Abu al-Hasan, the Last, peace be upon him, about the sincere repentance: What is it? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: That the internal is like the apparent and (even) better than that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Repent to Allah a sincere repentance" He said: It is the fasting of the day of Wednesday, the day of Thursday, and the day of Friday.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaydullah al-Yaqteeni told us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Sincent repentance is that a man's inner self is like his outer self and even better. It has been reported that sincere repentance is that a man repents from a sin and intends never to return to it.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Saqr al-Saigh narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq al-Qadi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', from Abu Dhibyan, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: The Home of Peace is Paradise, and its people have safety from all plagues, blemishes, illnesses and sicknesses, and they have safety from aging, death and the changing of circumstances upon them. They are the dignified who will never be insulted, and they are the honored who will never be humiliated, and they are the rich who will never become poor, and they are the happy who will never be miserable, and they are the rejoicing, the cheering, who will never be distressed or concerned, and they are the living who will never die. Hence, they are in palaces of gems and corals whose doors are open to the Throne of the Merciful, And the Angels will enter upon them from every door (saying): Peace be upon you for what you were patient. Thus, excellent is the final home (of yours).

Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq told us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told us, he said: Al-Abbas ibn Sa'id al-Azraq (who was from the 'Ammah) told us, he said: Abdul-Rahman ibn Salih told us, he said: Shareek ibn Abdullah, from Alaa' ibn Abd al-Karim, he said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: And Allah calls to the Home of Peace He said: Indeed, the Peace is Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and His Home that He created for His allies is Paradise.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Asad al-Asadi told us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar [ibn] Abi Ghailan al-Thaqafi and Isa ibn Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Qurashi told us, saying: Abu Ibrahim al-Turjumani told us [saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id al-Jarjani told us], saying: Nahshal ibn Sa'id told us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: The nobles of my nation are the carriers of the Qur'an and the people of the night.

We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Asad al-Asadi, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Jarir, and Hasan ibn ‘Urwa, and Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Wahbi, that they said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Hameed, that he said: We were told by Zafir ibn Sulayman, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn ‘Uyayna, from Abu Hazem, from Sahl ibn Sa’eed, that he said: Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and said: O Muhammad, live however you want, for indeed, you are to die, and love what you want, for indeed, you are to separate from it, and do what you want, for indeed, you are to be rewarded for it. Moreover, know that the honor of a man is his standing during the night, and his honor is his sufficiency from people.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab told us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said: The worst of servants is a servant who has two faces and two tongues; he praises his brother in his presence and eats him in his absence. If he is given, he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Musa ibn Imran al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Awn ibn Ma'yn, the cap seller, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), say: The one who meets people with one face and is absent from them with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection whilst having two tongues of fire.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Sama'ah ibn Mahran, who said: I asked him about faith and Islam, and I said to him: Do you differentiate between faith and Islam? He said: Shall I give you an example of it? I said: I would like that. He said: The example of faith from Islam is like the example of the Sacred Kaaba from the Sanctuary; a man may be in the Sanctuary and not be in the Kaaba, until he is in the Sanctuary. And he may be a Muslim and not be a believer, and he will not be a believer until he is a Muslim. I said: Then does anything exclude him from faith? He said to me: Yes. I said: Then to what does it turn him? He said: To Islam or disbelief. And he said: If a man enters the Kaaba and his urine slips from him, he is taken out of the Kaaba but does not go out of the Sanctuary. And if he goes out from the Sanctuary, washes his garment and purifies himself, he is not prevented from entering the Kaaba. But if a man enters the Kaaba and urinates in it intentionally, he is taken out of the Kaaba and from the Sanctuary, and his neck is struck.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Bakr bin Salih al-Razi, from Abu al-Salt al-Khurasani, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about faith, so he said: Faith is a contract in the heart, utterance by the tongue, and action by the limbs; faith is not except like this.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is not by adorning nor by wishing, but faith is what is sincere in the heart and confirmed by actions.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Maimoun, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Faith is (consisting of) saying and action, (the like of) two associating brothers.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) one day met Haritha ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, and he said to him: 'How have you become in the morning, O Haritha?' He said: 'I have become in the morning, O Messenger of Allah, a true believer.' He said: 'Indeed, for every faith there is a reality, so what is the reality of your faith?' He said: 'My self has turned away from the world, I kept awake my night and became thirsty during my day, and it is as if I am by the Throne of my Lord and the Reckoning is near, and it is as if I am with the people of Paradise in it, being enticed, and the people of the Fire in it, being tormented.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'You are a believer. May Allah enlighten faith in your heart, so remain firm, may Allah make you firm.' He said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is nothing on my self from which I am more fearful for me than my vision.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) supplicated for him, and his vision went away.

Muhammad ibn alhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Muhammad ibn 'Adhafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, a group of riders met him and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Who are you? They said: We are believers. He said: What is the reality of your faith? They said: Satisfaction with the decree of Allah, submission to the command of Allah, and entrustment to Allah, Exalted is He. He said: Wise scholars, who are on the verge of being prophets due to wisdom. If you are truthful, then do not build wealth that you will not dwell in, and do not accumulate what you will not consume, and fear Allah to whom you will return.

My father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: A man came to al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), and said: O son of Allah's Messenger, inform me about the noblest of moral traits. So he said: Pardoning those who wronged you, connecting with those who disconnected from you, giving those who prevented you, and saying the truth, even if it may be against yourself.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I not tell you about the noblest of moral traits?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: Pardoning people, for a man to console his brother with his property, and to mention Allah abundantly.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, specified the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the noblest of moral traits. Hence, test yourselves; if they are in you, then praise Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and desire towards Him for more of them. Then he mentioned them, the ten: certainty, contentment, patience, thankfulness, satisfaction, good mannerisms, openhandedness, sense of honor, courage and manliness.

We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant them both mercy, that they both said: We were told by Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: We were told by Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Abdul-Ghaffar al-Jazi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he mentioned that the weakened people are of different kinds, which some contradict the other, and that the one among the people of Qibla who is not a Nasib, is a weakened individual.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu al-Maghra Humayd ibn al-Muthanna al-Ajali, who said: Abu Hanifa, a man from our companions, narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: The one who knows the dispute (or difference/divergence), he is not a weakened individual.

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far al-Alawi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, from Hamdawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who knows the differences/disputes of people is not a weakened individual.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fadala ibn Ayub together, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children.' He said: It is the one who is unable to disbelieve, so he disbelieves, and is not guided to the path of faith so that he believes. And the children, and whoever of the men and women is upon the intellect of children, the pen is raised from them.

We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant them both mercy, that they both said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told us, that he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali and al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, Salem ibn Makram the Cameleer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children; they cannot devise a plan, nor are they guided to a path', so he said: They are unable to devise a plan towards Nusb [antagonism] by which they antagonize, nor are they guided to the path of the people of the truth by which they enter into it. These people will enter Paradise for good deeds and by refraining from the forbidden things which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has prohibited, and they will not attain the ranks of the righteous.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt al-Bajali, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say about the weakened ones? He said to me, as if terrified: And have you left anyone to be (in a state of being) weakened? And where are the weakened ones? For by Allah, your matter has been carried by shoulders to shoulders in their houses and it has been spoken of by rumor collectors in the roads of Medina.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya bin Imran al-Ash'ari, that he said: We were told by Ibrahim bin Ishaq, from Amr [and] bin Ishaq, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked: What is the limitation of the weakened individual whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious, mentioned? He said: The one who is unable to (properly recite) a chapter of the Qur'an, when Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has created him in a manner that he should not be one who is unable to (do so).

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children' - the verse - He said: O Sulayman, among these weakened ones, there are those with a thicker neck than you. The weakened are a people who fast, pray, whose bellies and private organs are modest; they do not believe that the truth is with other than us, holding onto the branches of the tree. For those, Allah might pardon them if they were to adhere to the branches. Moreover, if they were to not know those, then if Allah was to pardon them, it would be due to His mercy, and if He was to torment them, it would be due to their aberration from what He made them know.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Uthman bin Isa, from Musa bin Bikr, from Sulman bin Khalid, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about the weakened ones, so he said: The stupid one in her modest home; the servant to whom you would say: 'Pray' and she would pray, not knowing except what you would tell her. Also, it is the imported (servant) who does not know except what you tell him, and it is the dying old and the small child. They are the weakened ones. As for a man with a strong neck, fond to arguing and quarreling, who deals with buying and selling and whom you are unable to defraud in anything, would you say that he is a weakened? No, and there is no dignity (to him).

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the weakened who do not find a way out nor are guided to a path: They are unable to use a stratagem to enter into disbelief, nor are they guided to enter into faith; thus, they are of no consequence with regards to disbelief and faith.

We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Abdul-Rahman bin Muhammad al-Hussaini, that he said: We were informed by Abu Ja'far Ahmad bin Isa bin Abi Maryam al-'Ajali, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Ziyad al-'Azrami, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hatim al-Manqari, of Mufaddal bin Umar, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Throne and the Chair: What are they? He said: The Throne is, on one side, the totality of the creation, and the Chair is its vessel, and on the side of the last part of the Throne is the knowledge which Allah made His Prophets, Messengers and Proofs sight upon, and the Chair is the knowledge which Allah did not make anyone of His Prophets, Messengers and Proofs, peace be upon them, sight upon.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, of Qasim bin Muhammad, of Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, of Hafs bin Ghiyath, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «His Chair extends over the Heavens and the earth» He said: His Knowledge.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And when they fall on their sides' [22:36]. He said: If they fall (lifeless) on the ground, then eat from it. 'And feed the needy and the beggar' [22:36]. He said: The needy (al-Qa'in) is the one who is pleased with what you give him, does not become angry, does not frown, nor makes scum fill his mouth corner out of anger. And the beggar (al-Mu'tarr) is the one who passes by you whom you feed.

And with this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Saif al-Tammār, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Malik arrived as a pilgrim and met my father (peace be upon him) and said: I brought an offering animal, so what should I do? He said: Feed your family one third, feed the contented one third, and feed the beggar one third. I said: Is the beggar the one who asks? He said: Yes, and the contented is the one who is satisfied with what you send to him of the piece of meat and more than that, and the beggar is the one who approaches you and does not ask you.

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) said: The testimony of a traitorous male or traitorous female is impermissible, nor (that of) one with hatred, nor one of enmity towards his brother, nor one of dubiousity with regards to allegiance, nor kinship, nor the needy for a household (when the testimony is made) in favor of them.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Hussain bin Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, and Musa bin Umar, and Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Uthman, from Ibn Sinan, that he said: I asked Abu'l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, about the noun: What is it? He said: It is an attribute to that which is attributed.

My father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: Was Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He, consciously knowing of Himself before He created the creation? He, peace be upon him, said: Yes. I said: Was He seeing and hearing it? He said: He was not in need of that, because He was not asking it, nor requesting from it. He is His Self, and His Self is Him; His Might is Piercing, and so He does not need to name Himself. However, He indeed chose names for Himself, to others than Himself, that they may call upon Him with, because if He was not called upon by His Name, he would not have been recognized. Hence, the first He chose for Himself is the High, the Great, because He is the Highest of all things. So, His meaning is the God, and His Name is the High, the Great, which is the first of His Names, because He has exalted above everything.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who bequeaths a share of his wealth. He said: The share is one of eight, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The charities are only for the poor, the needy, those who work upon (acquiring) them, those with affectionate hearts, the necks (of human beings in captivity to be liberated), those in debt, for the sake of Allah and for the stranded traveler.'

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeaths a share of his property and does not know what a share is. He said: Is there among you nothing of what has reached you from Ja'far and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them both) regarding that? Then I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, we have not heard our companions mention anything about this from your fathers (peace be upon them). He said: A share is one of eight. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, how did it become one of eight? He said: Do you not read the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He? I said: May I be sacrificed for you, I do read it, but I do not know where its place is. He said: The saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The charities are only for the poor, the needy, those who work upon (acquiring) them, those with affectionate hearts, the necks (of human beings in captivity to be liberated), those in debt, for the sake of Allah and for the stranded traveler.' Then he counted eight with his hand. He said: And so did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) divide it into eight shares. A share is one of eight.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Jamil, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who bequeaths a part of his property, the part is one of ten. Because Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: 'Then place upon each mountain of them, a part.' And the mountains were ten and the birds were four, so He placed on each mountain of them, a part.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who bequeathed her third, with which the debt of her brother's son is to be paid, and a portion for such-and-such male and such-and-such female, and I did not know how to handle that, so we went to Ibn Abi Layla. He said: So what did he say to you? I said: He said: They have nothing. So he said: He lied by Allah. They have one-tenth of the third.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya bin Imran al-Ash'ari, that he said: I was told by Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Hussain bin Khalid, from Abu'l-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed a part of his property. He said: A seventh of his third.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, who said: I used to go to Ibn Abi Layla regarding inheritance cases, and he would dispute/delay with me. When that prolonged for me, I complained about him to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) ordered the return of the restrained (property/heir) and the execution of inheritances? He said: So I went to him, and he did as he used to do. I said to him: I complained about you to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and he said to me such-and-such. Then Ibn Abi Layla made me swear that he said that to me, so I swore to him, and he ruled in my favor regarding that.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ahmad al-Razi, from Bakr bin Salih, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Uyayna al-Basri, that he said: I was testifying at the presence of Ibn Abi Layla and he had judged with regards to a man who had made for some of his relatives benefit from a house and not specified a (particular) time for them, and then the man died and his inheritors were present at Ibn Abi Layla, and his relative to whom he made the house was (also) present. Then Ibn Abi Layla said: I see that I (should) leave it like how its owner left it. Then Muhammad bin Muslim al-Thaqafi said to him: Verily, Ali bin Abi Talib, Allah’s blessings be upon him, indeed, judged in this mosque to the contrary of what you have judged. He said: And how do you know? He said: I heard Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, say: Ali bin Abi Talib, Allah’s blessings be upon him, judged for the return of the restrained and the fulfilment of inheritance. Then Ibn Abi Layla said: Is it with you in a book? He said: Yes. He said: Then send to him and come to me with it. Then Muhammad bin Muslim said: (On the condition that) You must not look into the Book except in that narration. He said: You may do so. He said: Then he showed him the narration of Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, in the Book and he retracted his judgement.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Husayni narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Isa ibn Abi Maryam al-Ajali informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ziyad al-Azrami narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hatem al-Manqari narrated from Mufaddal ibn Umar, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Path. He said: It is the way to the knowledge of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and there are two Paths: a Path in this world, and a Path in the Hereafter. As for the Path that is in this world, it is the Imam whose obedience is obligatory; whoever knows him in this world and follows his guidance will pass over the Path that is the bridge of Hell in the Hereafter, and whoever does not know him in this world, his foot will slip from the Path in the Hereafter and he will fall into the Fire of Hell.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt, [from Abdullah ibn al-Salt], from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from those he mentioned, from Ubaidullah [ibn] al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Straight Path is the Commander of the Believers, Ali (peace be upon him).

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from my grandfather, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Guide us the Straight Path» He said: It is the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and the conscious knowledge of him, and the proof that it is the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) is His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And indeed, he is in the Foundation of the Book, for us, certainly, Ali, the wise.» And it is the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) in the Foundation of the Book, in His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Guide us the Straight Path».

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi, the Exegetist, narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to me from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them). Regarding His saying: 'Guide us the Straight Path', he said: Maintain for us Your success by which we obeyed You in the past of our days, so that we may obey You likewise in the future of our ages. The Straight Path is two paths: a path in this world, and a path in the Hereafter. As for the Straight Path in this world, it is that which is short of exaggeration, raised above deficiency, and straight so that it does not deviate to anything of falsehood. As for the other way, it is the path of the believers to Paradise, which is straight; they do not deviate from Paradise to the Fire, nor to other than Paradise, but to Paradise. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both) said regarding His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Guide us the Straight Path'. He said: He says: Direct us to the Straight Path, direct us to adhering to the way that leads to Your love, the transmitter to Your Religion, and the impediment from us following our desires so we become impaired, or taking by our opinions so we perish. Then he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, the one who follows his desire and is pleased with his own opinion is like a man whom I heard the waste material of the populace magnify and ridicule, so I wanted to meet him from where he does not know me to see his value and position. I saw that he was surrounded by a multitude from the waste material of the populace, so I stood in withdrawal from them, covered with a veil, looking at him and them. He continued to elude them until he went in an opposing direction, separated from them and did not stay, after which the populace dispersed from him to their needs. I followed him, tracing his steps, and he did not stay but that he passed by a baker, distracted him and took from his shop two loaves in theft, and so I was amazed by him, and then I said in myself: Perhaps it was a transaction? Then after it, he passed by an owner of pomegranates, and he remained with him until he distracted him and took from him two pomegranates in theft, and so I was amazed by him, and then I said in myself: Perha

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Mufaddal bin Umar, that he said: I was told by Thabit al-Thumali, from the Master of Worshippers, Ali bin Hussain (peace be upon them both), that he said: There is not, between Allah and His Proof, a veil, and so, there is not for Allah any cover before His Proof. We are the Gates of Allah, and we are the Straight Path, and we are the Bag of His Knowledge, and we are the Interpreters of His Revelation, and we are the Pillars of His Oneness, and we are the Place of His Secret.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Ubaidullah bin Musa al-‘Absi, from Sa’d bin Turayf, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: O Ali, when the Day of Resurrection shall be, I, you and Jibra’eel will sit upon the Path, and none will pass except for those who have a book that includes the acquittal of your befriendship.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi told us, saying: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi told us, saying: He told me Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Ibrahim, saying: Alwan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Hannan ibn Sadir told us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), saying: The saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, in al-Hamd: 'The Path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor' means: Muhammad and his Progeny, Allah's blessings be upon them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi narrated to us, saying: Furat ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Kathir narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Yahya ibn Mihran al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not the path of those upon whom is the anger, nor those who are mislead.' He said: The Shi'a of Ali (peace be upon him) are those upon whom You have bestowed favor with the Wilayah (Divine Authority) of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He was not angry at them, nor did He mislead them.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi, the Exegetist, narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to me from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them). Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «The Path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor» — meaning, recite: «Guide us the Path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor» by granting success to Your Religion and obedience. And they are those about whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said: «And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, they are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, from the Prophets, the Truthful, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.» This exact report was also narrated from the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), who said: Then he said: It is not these [people] who are bestowed favor with wealth and bodily health, although all this is an apparent grace from Allah. Do you not see that these might be disbelievers or sinners? You were not called to pray that you are directed to their path, but rather, you were ordered to pray that you are directed to the Path of those upon whom Allah has bestowed the favors of faith in Allah, belief in His Messenger, and befriendment to Muhammad and his Pure Family, and his good, noble companions, and of righteous Taqiya (prudent dissimulation) by which safety is granted from the evil among Allah’s servants, and from the increase in the evil deeds and disbelief of Allah’s enemies, by being affable with them and not imputing them for harming you and harming the believers, and by knowing the rights of the brothers among the believers. Verily, there is no servant nor maid who befriends Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) and antagonizes those who antagonized them, except that he took from the torment of Allah a protective shield and a strong fortress. And there is no servant nor slave who appeased the servants of Allah and did well in appeasement by which he did not enter into any falsehood and not deviate from any truth, except that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, makes his breathing a glorification, purifies his deeds, and gives him insight to conceal our secret and patience with anger due to what he hears from our

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: May Allah rectify you, is it that the one who loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and the one who hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him? He said: Yes. Then I said: By Allah, we surely hate death. He said: That is not where you think it goes; rather, it is at the time of direct encounter. When he sees what he loves, there is nothing more beloved to him than to advance, and Allah loves to meet him, and he loves to meet Allah at that time. And when he sees what he dislikes, there is nothing more hateful to him than to meet Allah, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, hates to meet him.

With this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Yahya ibn Sabur, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the dead person shedding a tear at the moment of death. He said: That is when he is to be observed by the Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family), during which he will see that which makes him rejoice and which he loves. He said: Then he said: Do you not see a man, he sees what rejoices him and what he loves, during which his eye will shed a tear and he will smile?

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri al-Jaloudi in Basra narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to us, from his father, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) He said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) passed by an epileptic man while people were gathered around him looking at him, and he said (peace be upon him and his Family): 'For what have these people gathered?' It was said to him: 'For an insane man who is undergoing epilepsy.' Then he looked at him and said: 'He is not insane. Shall I not inform you of the truly insane man?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Indeed, the truly insane man is the one who swaggers in his walk, looks at the height of the road, and moves his sides with his shoulders. That is the insane one, and this (man) is afflicted.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza ibn Hamran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the one who answers in all he is asked, is surely insane.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi, from Ali bin Nu’man, from Abdullah bin Talha, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Paradise will never be entered by a servant in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, and the Fire will not be entered by a servant in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of faith. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, a man might wear a robe or ride an animal, and he would be about to become known for arrogance. He said: It is not that. Arrogance is only to deny the truth, whereas faith is to acknowledge the truth.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Yazid ibn Farqad, from the one who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Paradise will not be entered by the one in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, and the Fire will not be entered by the one in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of faith. He said: Then I recited the Ruju' [1]. Then he said: What is it with you that you perform Ruju'? So I said: Due to what I hear from you. So he said: It is not as you think. I only mean that one knowingly rejects (the truth). It only applies to knowingly reject.

With this chain of narrators, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali bin 'Uqba, from Ayub bin Hurr, from Abdul-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Arrogance is that one disdains people and stultifies the truth.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah told us, that Ahmad bin Muhammad told us, from Ali bin Hakam, from Saif, from Abdul-A'la bin A'yan, that he said: Abu Abdillah (narrating) from his fathers, peace be upon them, said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Indeed, the greatest arrogance is disdaining the creation and stultifying the truth. I said: And what is it to disdain the creation and stultify the truth? He said: That one is ignorant of the truth and vilifies its people. The one who does that, has certainly challenged the Vesture of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Baqqah, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who enters Mecca free from arrogance, his sin will be forgiven. I said: And what is arrogance? He said: To disdain the creation and stultify the truth. I said: And how is that? He said: That one is ignorant of the truth and vilifies its people.

The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, in the book of Khalil ibn Ahmad, he says: Such-a-person disdains people. Disdaining the grace would be if he takes it lightly, and so with their rights. It is said: «He is disdained with regards to his religion» meaning that he is condemned. One would have disdained a grace and a (state of) comfort if one does not thank (for) it. Abu Ubaid said with regards to the saying of him, peace be upon him: «stultifies the truth» that one sees the truth as foolishness and ignorance. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: «And who desires other than the Religion of Ibrahim except for the one who fools himself?» Some exegetes said: «except for the one who fools himself» says that one (in this case) declares himself as being foolish. As for his saying: «disdains people» it is to despise them, spurn them and similar. He said: There is another language to it in other than this narration. Ghamasa with the Saad is not non-Arabic, and it is by the meaning of understating. Ghams is performed with regards to a physical object, and a part of it is (referred to as) ghamsa. Ghumaisa is a planet. Ghams with regards to entrails is roughness, cutting and pain.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Madeeni, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the wonder (or vanity) that invalidates deeds, he said: The wonder has ranks: among them is that evil deeds are beautified for the servant, so he sees them as good, admires them, and assumes that he is doing good; and among them is that the servant believes in his Lord, so he considers himself performing a favor upon Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, whereas Allah, Exalted is He, is the One who granted him the favor.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from some of his companions, that he ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who does not recognize for anyone a virtue (by having granted him a favor), is one who admires his own belief.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from al-Qasim bin Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, from al-Fadl bin 'Ayyadh, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do you know who the avaricious one is? I said: Is he the stingy one? He said: The avaricious one is worse than the stingy one. Indeed, the stingy one is stingy with what is in his hands, and the avaricious one is avaricious with what is in the hands of people as well as what is in his own hands, until he does not see anything in the hands of people except that he wishes for it to be his, whether through the lawful or the forbidden. He does not become satisfied, nor is he content, with what Allah, Exalted is He, has sustained him.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Ala' al-Arjani, from al-Ala' ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the stingy one is the one who acquires wealth from an unlawful source and spends it in an unjustified manner.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, conveyed by Sa'd ibn Turaif, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Al-Harith al-A'war, who said: Among what Ali, Allah's blessings be upon him, asked his son, Hasan, peace be upon him, is that he said to him: What is avarice? He said: That you see what is in your hand as an honor, and that what you have spent is a loss.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: The stingy one is not the one who pays the obligatory alms-tax from his wealth and gives the final portion to his people. Rather, the truly stingy one is the one who withholds the obligatory alms-tax from his wealth and withholds the final portion from his people, and who is spendthrift in other than that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar told us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The avaricious is only the one who prevented the right of Allah and spent in other than the right of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), that he said: The stingy person is the one who is stingy with regards to what Allah has obliged upon him.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Muawiya bin Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The stingy is the one who is stingy with the peace (greeting).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Hasan ibn Bandar ibn al-Muthanna al-Tabari narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Maqarri al-Riqqi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Ala' ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: Abu Zakariya narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated from Umara ibn Ghaziya, from Abdullah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: The truly stingy person is the one to whom you are mentioned, and he does not send blessings upon me.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who raised it to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) performed blood-letting (hijamah) in his head, between his shoulders, and on the back of his neck three times. He named one 'The Beneficial', the other 'The Refuging', and the third 'The Saving'.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Ibn Salama - and he is Abu Khadija, and his name is Salem ibn Makram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Blood-letting on the head is performed by a shibr from the tip of the nose and a fitr between the eyebrows. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to call it the saving. In another narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to perform blood-letting on his head and name it as the refuging or the saving.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abul-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Raqqi, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from his fathers, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and their most knowledgeable among them asked him. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: 'For what reason were you named Muhammad, Ahmad, Abul-Qasim, Bearer of Glad Tidings, Warner, and Caller?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for Muhammad, indeed I am praised on earth. As for Ahmad, indeed I am praised in Heaven. As for Abul-Qasim, indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will divide on the Day of Resurrection the division of the Fire, so whoever disbelieves in me from the first and the last will be in the Fire, and He will divide the division of Paradise, so whoever believes in me and acknowledges my Prophethood will be in Paradise. As for the Caller, indeed I call the people to the Religion of my Lord, Exalted and Glorious is He. As for the Warner, indeed I warn of the Fire to whoever disobeys me. As for the Bearer of Glad Tidings, indeed I give glad tidings of Paradise to whoever obeys me.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, who said: I asked al-Rida, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: Why was the Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) nicknamed Abu al-Qasim? He said: Because he had a son called Qasim, so he was nicknamed due to him. He said: Then I said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, do you see me deserving for more? He said: Yes. Have you not known that Allah's Messenger (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said: I and Ali are the fathers of this nation? I said: Sure. He said: Have you not known that Allah's Messenger (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) is a father to all his nation, and that Ali (peace be upon him) is in his position among them? I said: Sure. He said: Have you not known that Ali is the divider between Paradise and the Fire? I said: Sure. He said: Hence, he was called Abu al-Qasim because he is the father of the divider of Paradise and the Fire. Then I said to him: And what is the meaning of that? He said: Indeed, the compassion of the Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) upon his nation is as the compassion of fathers upon children, and the best among his nation is Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). After him, the compassion of Ali (peace be upon him) upon them is like the compassion of him (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family), because he is his Bequeathed, Successor and Imam after. Then he said: Hence, for that he (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said: I and Ali are the fathers of this nation. The Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) climbed the pulpit and said: He who leaves behind a debt or a wastage, it is upon me, and to me (shall one come), and he who leaves behind property, it is for his inheritors. By that, he became of more priority to them than their fathers and mothers, and he became of more priority to them than their own selves, and so was the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) after him, it applied to him the same as what applied to Allah's Messenger (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family).
