Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, he said: Tamim ibn Buhlul narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sulayman ibn Mahran, from 'Ubayah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?' He said: He was only named an orphan because he did not have any equal on the face of the earth from the first ones nor from the last ones. So Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said, bestowing favor upon him with His grace: 'Did He not find you an orphan?' Meaning: Lonely, there is no equal to you. 'And gave you refuge' — He gathered the people to you and made them know your virtue, until they came to know you. 'And found you astray' — He is saying: Among your people, you were attributed to aberration, and so He guided them to knowing you. 'And found you poor' — He is saying: Poor according to your people, as they say: You have no money. And then Allah enriched you with the wealth of Khadija, and then He increased you from His favor and made your supplication responded to. That even if you were to supplicate that a stone is made by Allah into gold, His gaze would turn to your wish. And He brought to you food where there was no food, and He brought you water where there was no water, and He succored you with Angels where there was no succorer. And He granted you victory over your enemies through them.

We were told by Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his brother Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Marwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, orphaned His Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, in order for there to be none upon him to obey.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sufi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon them) so I said: O son of Allah's Messenger, why was the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) named the Ummi? He said: What do the people say? I said: They claim he was named the Ummi because he did not write. He (peace be upon him) said: They have lied, upon them is the curse of Allah. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says in the clear text of His Book: 'It is He who sent among the Ummis a Messenger from themselves, reciting for them His signs, purifying them and teaching them the Book and the Wisdom.' How could he teach them what he does not know? By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to read and write in seventy-two or seventy-three languages. He was only named the Ummi because he was from the people of Mecca, and Mecca is the Mother of Towns. That is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'That you may warn the Mother of Towns and those surrounding it.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Idris, and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marouzi, that he said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Ghusl is a sa' of water, and Wudu is a mudd of water. The sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is five mudds, and a mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams, and one dirham is the weight of six daniqs, and one daniq is six kernels, and one kernel is the weight of two barley seeds from the average seeds, not from their small ones nor from their large ones.

With this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani, who said, and he was with us, performing pilgrimage. He said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) on the hands of my father: May I be sacrificed for you, our companions have disputed regarding the sa'. Some of them say that the Fitra is [given by] a sa' of Medina, and some of them say [by] a sa' of Iraq. Then he wrote to me: A sa' is six artals by the Medinan standard, and nine artals by the Iraqi standard. He said: He also informed me and said: By weight, it is one thousand and one hundred and seventy weights.

With this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, that he came with a mudd and mentioned that Ibn Abi Umayr gave him that mudd and said: It was given to me by such-a-person, a man from the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: It was given to me by Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: This is the mudd of the Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family). So we measured it and found it to be (equal to) four mudds, and that one and a quarter qafeez, as is measured by this qafeez of ours.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It was said to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him): What is abstinence in this world? He said: Avoiding its forbidden parts.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn 'Atiya al-Ahmasi, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharboudh, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: I heard the Commander of the Believers, Allah's blessings be upon him, say: Abstinence in this world is to have short aspiration. Thankfulness to every grace and piety with regards to (avoiding) what Allah has forbidden upon you.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, that he said: I was told by Jahm ibn al-Hukm, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Abstinence in this world is not by wasting property, nor by declaring the allowable as forbidden. Rather, abstinence in this world is that you are not, towards what is in your hand, more confident than towards what is in the Hand of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Ali ibn Hashim al-Bareed, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that a man asked him about abstinence. He said: Abstinence is ten things. The highest ranks of abstinence are the lowest ranks of piety, and the highest ranks of piety are the lowest ranks of certainty, and the highest ranks of certainty are the lowest ranks of satisfaction. Indeed, abstinence is in a verse from the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So that you will not despair over what has eluded you nor rejoice over what He has given you.'

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from Ali bin Hadid, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Isa bin Mariam (peace be upon him) said in a sermon in which he stood up among the sons of Isra’eel: I have awoken this morning among you, and my condiment is hunger, my food is what the earth vegetates for beasts and cattle, my lamp is the moon, my mattress is the sand and my pillow is the stone. I have no home that is to be demolished, nor property that is to be consumed, nor a child that is to die, nor a woman who will grieve. I have awoken this morning whilst I have nothing, and I slept at night whilst I had nothing, and I am the richest among the sons of Adam.

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, told me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i the Judge, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Iblis came to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) while he was conversing with his Lord, and an Angel from the Angels said to him: What do you seek from him while he is in this condition, conversing with his Lord? He said: I seek from him what I sought from his father, Adam, when he was in the Garden. Among what He conversed to him was that He said to him: O Musa, I do not accept the prayer except for he who humbled to My Greatness, constrained his heart to fear Me, covered his day with My remembrance, did not settle a night whilst insisting on intentional mistake, and knew the truth of My Allies and Beloved. Then he said: O Lord, do you mean by Your Beloved and Allies, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qoub? He said: They are as such, O Musa, however, I intended he because of whom I created Adam and Hawwa', and he because of whom I created Paradise and the Fire. Then Musa said: And who is he, O Lord? He said: Muhammad, Ahmad, I derived his name from My Name, because I am the Praised. Then Musa said: O Lord, make me among his nation. He said: You are, O Musa, from his nation if you know him, know his rank and the rank of his Household. Indeed, the example of him and the example of his Household and that which I have created, is like the example of Firdaus in the Gardens, whose trees never dry, nor does its taste change. Hence, those who know them and know their truth, I will make for him at the occasion of ignorance, forbearance, and at the occasion of darkness, a light, and I will respond to him before he calls unto Me and I will give him before he asks Me. The narration is long, we took from it the place of need.

Ahmad ibn al-Qattan narrated, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari al-Ghulabi al-Basri narrated, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammara narrated, from his father, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) was asked: 'Where were you when Adam was in the Garden?' He said: 'I was in his backbone, and I was descended to the earth whilst in his backbone, and I rode the ship whilst in the backbone of Noah's father, and I was thrown into the fire whilst in the backbone of Abraham. Never did two parents of mine meet in fornication. Allah, Exalted and Glorious, did not cease moving me from the good backbones into the pure, purified wombs, a guided guide, until Allah took Prophethood as my oath, and Islam as my covenant, clarified everything of my characteristic, established my mentioning in the Tawrat and the Injeel, ascended me to His Heaven, and derived for me a name from His Names. My nation are the praisers, the One with the Throne is the Praised, and I am Muhammad.' And this hadith has been narrated through many chains of transmission.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ajali told us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan told us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib told us, saying: Abu Muhammad Tamim ibn Buhlul told us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was sitting on a day, and with him were Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn, peace be upon them. Then he said: By He who sent me with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, there is no creation on the face of the earth more beloved to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, nor more honored for Him than us. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, derived for me a name from His Names, so He is al-Mahmud (the Praised) and I am Muhammad. He derived for you, O Ali, a name from His Names, so He is al-Aliyy al-A'la (the High, the Most Sublime) and you are Ali. He derived for you, O Hasan, a name from His Names, so He is al-Muhsin (the Beneficent) and you are Hasan. He derived for you, O Husayn, a name from His Names, so He is Dhu al-Ilhsan (the One of Good Deeds) and you are Husayn. He derived for you, O Fatima, a name from His Names, so He is al-Fatir (the Splitter/Originator) and you are Fatima. Then he, peace be upon him and his family, said: O Allah, I bear You as witness that I am at peace with those who are at peace with them, at war with those who are at war with them, a lover of those who love them, a hater of those who hate them, an enemy of those who antagonize them, and an ally of those who befriend them, because they are from me and I am from them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn [Ali ibn] al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl ibn Ja'far ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Sulayman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Za'farani al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Talaqani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the mawla of the Banu Hashim, narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Waqidi, from al-Hudhail, from al-Makhul, from al-Tabus, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): When Allah, Exalted and Glorious be His remembrance, created Adam and blew into him from His Spirit, and made His angels prostrate to him, and settled him in His Garden, and married him to Hawwa' (his wife), he raised his gaze towards the Throne and saw five lines written. Adam said: 'O Lord, who are these?' Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said to him: 'These are those whom if My creation intercede with, I will intercede for them.' Adam said: 'O Lord, by their position with You, what are their names?' He, Exalted, said: 'As for the first, I am the Praised and he is Muhammad; and the second, I am the High and he is Ali; and the third, I am the Splitter and she is Fatima; and the fourth, I am the Beneficent and he is al-Hasan; and the fifth, I am the One with Good Deeds and he is al-Husayn.' All of them praise Allah, Exalted and Glorious.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: My grandfather told me, saying: Dawud ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Isa informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qoub informed us, saying: 'Anbasa told us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrima, saying: When Fatima (peace be upon her) gave birth to Hasan, she brought him to the Prophet, and he named him Hasan. And when she gave birth to al-Husayn, she brought him to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, this one is more beautiful than that one, so he named him Husayn.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-A'lawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: My grandfather told me, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Isa told us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), saying: Jibra'il (peace be upon him) gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) the name of Hasan ibn Ali in a piece of silk from the clothes of Paradise, and he derived the name of al-Husayn from al-Hasan (peace be upon them both).

Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Jaludi in Basra told us, saying: Al-Mughira ibn Muhammad told me told me, saying: Rajaa' ibn Salama told us, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), saying: The Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (Allah's blessings be upon him), gave a speech in Kufa after his return from Nahrawan, and it had reached him that Mu'awiya was insulting him, cursing him, and killing his companions. So he stood to give a speech, praised Allah and commended Him, and sent blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and mentioned what Allah bestowed of grace upon His Prophet and upon himself. Then he said: Were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would not have mentioned what I am now mentioning in this position of mine. Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: 'And as for the grace of your Lord, then speak.' O Allah, to You belongs the praise for Your grace that cannot be counted, and Your favor that cannot be forgotten. O people, indeed, it has reached me what has reached me, and verily, I see that my time has come near. It is as if I am with you and you have forgotten my case, and I am leaving among you what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) left; the Book of Allah and my Family, that is the Family of the Guide to Salvation, the Seal of the Prophets, and the Master of Nobles and the Selected Prophet. O people, perhaps you might not hear a sayer say the like of my saying after me, except for a calumniator. I am the brother of Allah's Messenger, the son of his paternal uncle, the sword of his wrath, the pillar of his victory, his strength and intensity. I am the circling mill of Hell, its pulverizing grinders. I am the orphanizer of boys and girls, I am the grabber of souls and the punishment of Allah that He will not repel from the criminal people. I am the quarrelling with heroes, the slayer of knights, the executor of those who disbelieved in the All-Merciful, and the in-law of the Best of mankind. I am the Master of Successors and the Successor of the Best of Prophets. I am the Door to the City of Knowledge and the Keeper of the knowledge of Allah's Messenger and his inheritor. I am the husband of the Batul, the Mistress

We were told by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, that he said: We were told by Musa ibn Imran, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Munthir ibn Umar, from al-Thabit ibn Dinar, from al-Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: Yazid ibn Qa'nab said: I was sitting with al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and a group from the sons of Abd al-Uzza opposite to the Sacred House of Allah, when Fatima bint Asad, the mother of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), approached. She was pregnant with him for seven months and was taken by labor pain, so she said: My Lord, I am a believer in You and in what has come from You of Messengers and Books, and I declare belief in the words of my grandfather, Ibrahim the Good Friend, and indeed, he built the Old House. Hence, by the Prophet who built this House, and by the infant that is in my belly, please, ease for me my labor. Yazid ibn Qa'nab said: Then we saw the House as it opened from behind, Fatima entered into it, she became absent from our eyes and the wall merged. Then we hoped for the door’s lock to open to us, and it did not open, and so we knew that this was by the commandment of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. Then she went out after the fourth and in her hand was the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). Then she said: Indeed, I have been preferred over the women who have preceded me, because Asiya bint Muzahim worshipped Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, secretly in a place in which Allah does not like to be worshipped except in urgency, and Mariam bint Imran shook the dry palm tree with her hand until she ate harvested dates from it. I, though, entered into the Sacred House of Allah and ate from the fruits and leaves of Paradise, and when I wanted to exit, a caller called to me: O Fatima, name him Ali, for he is Ali, and Allah, the All-High, the Most Sublime, says: His name is from My Name, disciplined him with My Discipline and gave him success to (comprehend) My Occult Knowledge, and he is the one to break the idols in My House, and he is the one to recite the Adhan above the roof of My House and sanctify Me and glorify Me. Hence, Tuba is for those who love him and obey him, and woe to those who hate him and disobey him.

We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Yahya bin Zakariya al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Bakr bin Abdullah bin Habib, from Tamim bin Buhlul, from his father, from Abu'l-Hasan al-'Abdi, from Sulayman bin Mahran, from 'Abaya bin Rab'i, that he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: Tell me about the Anza' al-Batin, Ali bin Abi Talib, peace be upon him, for the people have differed about him. Then Ibn Abbas said to him: O man, by Allah, you have certainly asked about a man whom none stepped on pebbles after Allah's Messenger, peace be upon him and his Family, who was better than him. Indeed, he is, verily, the brother of Allah's Messenger, peace be upon him and his Family, the son of his paternal uncle, his Bequeathed and Successor over his nation. Indeed, he is, verily, stripped from polytheism, filled with knowledge. I have, verily, heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, say: The one who wants salvation tomorrow, let him hold onto the waist cloth of this Anza'. Referring to Ali, peace be upon him.

We were told by Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yaq'ub, from 'Allan al-Kulayni, that he ascribed to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: "The sword of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was only named Dhu'l-Faqar because at its center there was a line going along its length similar to the dorsal vertebrae, so it was named Dhu'l-Faqar for that. It was a sword with which Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended from Heaven, and its ring was of silver, and it was he who cried about it from Heaven: 'There is no sword but Dhu'l-Faqar, and there is no hero but Ali.'"

Al-Mudaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Mudaffar al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Jibril ibn Ahmad al-Faryabi told us, saying: Hasan ibn Khazrad told me, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Furat, from Ya'qub ibn Suwayd ibn Mazeed al-Harithi, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, why was the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) named the Commander of the Believers? He said: Because he grants them preeminence through knowledge. Have you not heard the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And We will provide for our family'?

Ahmad ibn al-Qattan told us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Sukkari told us, saying: Abu Abdillah al-Ghulabi told us, saying: Mahduj ibn Umayr al-Hanafi told us, saying: Bishr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari narrated from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from his father, from Abu Huraira, who said: Fatima was only named Fatima because Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, separated those who love her from the Fire.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from al-Husayn bin Mukharrq, from Zaid al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His saying: «The blemish of a believer upon another believer is forbidden», that he said: It is not that he is uncovered and something of him is seen. It is only that something bad is narrated about him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Is the 'awrah (blemish/secret) of a believer upon another believer forbidden?' He said: Yes. I said: Do you mean his lower organs? He said: It is not as you think. It is only the disclosure of his secret.'

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Hudhaifa bin Mansur, that he said: I said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: There is something said by the people: «The blemish of a believer upon another believer is forbidden.» He said: It is not as you think. The blemish of a believer is only that one sees him speak with speech that he will be disgraced with, and that one saves it for him in order to distress him if he is angered (at him) one day.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: What is the limit of openhandedness? He said: You extract from your property the right which Allah has obliged upon you, and you put it in its place.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Hariz bin Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The openhanded and generous one is he who spends his wealth in what is right.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi told us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Ali ibn Awf al-Azdi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Openhandedness (al-sakhā') is that the servant's soul elevates above seeking the forbidden (haram); if he achieves the permissible (halal), his soul is pleased to spend it in the obedience of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Faddal, from a man, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family) said: Openhandedness is a tree whose root is in Paradise and which shades upon this world. The one who adheres to a branch of it will be drawn to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib narrated to us, from Sabbah ibn Khaqan, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Tamimi the judge, who said: The Commander of the Believers, Allah's prayers be upon him, went out to his companions while they were discussing manliness. He said: Where are you from the Book of Allah? They said: O Commander of the Believers, in which place? He said: In His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Indeed, Allah commands to justice and good deed.' Justice is fairness, and good deed is bestowment.

Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Abbas said, and he ascribed it (to the Prophet or Imam), saying: Muawiya asked Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) about manliness (al-muru'ah), so he said: A man's avariciousness towards his religion, his rectification of his property, and his establishment of rights. Muawiya said: You did well, O Abu Muhammad! You did well, O Abu Muhammad! He said: Muawiya then used to say after that: I had wished that Yazid said it, and indeed he was half-blinded.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from Isma'il bin Mahran, from Ayman bin Mahraz, from Mu'awiya bin Wahb, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said: Hasan bin Ali, peace be upon them both, was among a group of his companions at the presence of Mu'awiya, and he said to him: O father of Muhammad, inform me about manliness (al-muru'ah). He said: A man's preservation of his religion, his act of rectifying his land/estate, his good manner during quarreling/disputes, the spreading of peace, the leniency of speech, maintaining abstinence/restraint, and endearment to people.

And with this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, that he ascribed it to Sa'd ibn Turaif, from Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Al-Harith al-A'war, that he said: The Commander of the Believers, Allah's blessings be upon him, said to Hasan, his son, peace be upon him: O my son, what is manliness? He said: Chasteness and rectification of property.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Jawhari, whose title is al-Qurashi, from a man from the Kufis of our companions, who is called Ibrahim, that he said: Hasan, peace be upon him, was asked about manliness, so he said: Chasteness with regards to religion, good dealing with regards to livelihood and patience during misfortunes.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Mahran, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Manliness (al-muru'ah) is the rectification/consolidation of property.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Hammad al-Ansari, that he ascribed it, saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man's tending to his land/estate is from (the trait of) manliness.

With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Haytham ibn Abdullah al-Nahdi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Manliness is two types: the manliness of the settled one, and the manliness of the traveler. As for the manliness of the settled one, it is recitation of the Qur'an, attending mosques, accompanying the people of goodness, and contemplation in jurisprudence. And as for the manliness of the traveler, it is providing provisions, joking in that which does not anger Allah, little dispute with the one who accompanies you, and abandoning narrating their faults when you depart from them.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abu Qatadah al-Qummi, who ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: What is manliness (al-muru'ah)? We said: We do not know. He said: Manliness is that a man places his dining table in the unroofed space of his home. Manliness consists of two types of manliness - then he mentioned the like of the narration that preceded.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Sahl ibn [Ismail ibn] 'Amir told us, saying: Zafir ibn Sulayman told us, from Shareek, from Abu Ishaq, saying: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both): What is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family): 'Whoever I am his Leader, then Ali is his Leader'? He said: He informed them that he is the Imam after him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Thaqafi told me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Safwan ibn Yahya, the seller of fine cloth, told us, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them) about the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family: 'Whoever I am his Mawla, then Ali is his Mawla.' He said: O Abu Sa'id, are you asking about such a thing? [It means] that he (Ali) holds the same position among them as he (the Prophet) held.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Muharibi told us, saying: 'Ubad ibn Ya'qoub told us, saying: Ali ibn Hashim told us, from his father, saying: The saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his Family, "Whoever I am his Mawla, then Ali is his Mawla," was mentioned in the presence of Zaid ibn Ali [ibn al-Husayn], peace be upon them both, he said: He appointed him as a banner, so that the Party of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, might be known by it during the schism.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Harith, Abu Bakr al-Wasiti, from the origin of his book, told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Sulaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, saying: Abu Mariam told us, from 'Ata', from Ibn Abbas, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Allah is my Lord, and there is no sign for me with Him, and I am the Messenger of my Lord, and there is no sign with me, and Ali is my Ally and the Ally of whoever I am his Ally, and there is no sign with him.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubaidullah al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bassam al-Harrani narrated to us from the original of his book, saying: Mu'allal ibn Nufail narrated to us, saying: Ayoub ibn Salama, the brother of Muhammad ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Bassam al-Sayrafi, from Atiya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever I am his Ally, then Ali is his Ally, and whoever I am his Imam, then Ali is his Imam, and whoever I am his Commander, then Ali is his Commander, and whoever I am his Warner, then Ali is his Warner, and whoever I am his Guide, then Ali is his Guide, and whoever I am his Means to Allah, Exalted is He, then Ali is his Means to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, for Allah, Glorified be He, will judge between him and his enemy.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ziyad, Abu Muhammad, told me, saying: My father told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qais narrated from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Ali is the Imam of every believer after me.

Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ziyad told me from the original book of his father, saying: His father told us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar al-Amri told us, saying: Isam ibn Taliq told us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.' He said: About the Wilayah (Divine Authority) of Ali: What did they do with his matter? And Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, had made them aware that he is the Successor after His Messenger.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Anbasa, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, he said: Darim ibn Qubaysa narrated to us, he said: Na'im ibn Salim narrated to us, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) say: On the Day of Ghadeer Khumm, while he was holding the hand of Ali (peace be upon him): Do I not have more authority over the believers than they have over themselves? They said: Yes. He said: Hence, whoever I am his Mawla, then this is Ali his Mawla. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be enemy to whoever opposes him, and support whoever supports him, and abandon whoever abandons him.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Charity is not permissible for a wealthy person, nor for one of sound constitution, nor for a professional, nor for a strong person. We said: And what is the meaning of this? He said: It is not permissible for him to take it when he is able to keep himself off it.

And in another narration from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said: Certainly, the Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family) said: Indeed, charity is not permissible for a wealthy person - and he did not say: nor for one of even creation -.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim bin Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn bin Sa'id, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Jameel bin Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, cursed the one who performed a sin in Medina or gave refuge to a sinner. I said: And what is that sin? He said: Murder.

Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarakhsi, the jurist in Sarakhs, told us, saying: Abu Lubaid Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isra'il told us, saying: Saif ibn Harun al-Barjami told us, from Amr ibn Qais al-Mula'i, from Umayya ibn Yazid al-Qurashi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Whoever performs a sin or gives refuge to a sinner, upon him is the curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. Neither ransom nor disbursal will be accepted from him on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the sin? He said: The one who kills a soul for other than (the cause of) another soul, or mutilates for other than retaliation, or invents an innovation with other than a tradition, or seizes a prey of value. He said: Then it was said: What is the ransom, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Redemption. He said: Then it was said: What is the disbursal, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Repentance.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin 'Isa, from Qasim bin Yahya, from his grandfather, Hasan bin Rashid, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about «Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Raheem», so he, peace be upon him, said: The Baa' is the Magnificence of Allah, the Seen is the Sublimity of Allah, and the Miim is the Nobility of Allah – and some narrated: the Kingdom of Allah – and Allah is the God of everything, and the Merciful to all in the world, and the Merciful in particular to the believers.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from the one who told him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim', so he said: The Baa' is the Magnificence of Allah, the Seen is the Sublimity of Allah, and the Miim is the Kingdom of Allah. He said: I said: Allah? He said: The Alif is the Bounties of Allah upon His creation from the bliss of our Divine Authority, and the Laam is the Binding of Allah for His creation to our Divine Authority. I said: And the Haa'? Then he said: Ignominy to he who opposes Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, upon whom are Allah's blessings. I said: The Rahmaan? He said: (The Merciful) With all the world. I said: The Raheem? He said: (The Merciful) With the believers in particular.

Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi in Kufa told us, saying: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mu'mmar told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ramli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Maruzi told us, saying: Amru ibn Mansur told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from his father, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, saying: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari about the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) to Ali (peace be upon him): 'You are to me in the same position as Harun to Musa, except that there is no Prophet after me.' He said: He appointed him as Successor by that, by Allah, over his nation during his life and after his demise, and He obligated upon them his obedience. Hence, the one who does not testify for him, after this saying, Successorship, then he is among the wrongdoers.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, saying: It was said to the Master of the Worshippers, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both): Indeed, the people are saying: Indeed, the best of people after the Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) are Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman, then Ali (peace be upon him). He said: So what do they do with a report narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) that he said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'You are to me in the same position as Harun is to Musa, except that there is no Prophet after me'? So, who was, during the era of Musa, like Harun?

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Musa bin Qasem, from Ali bin Asbat, from Hasan bin Jahm, that he said: Abu'l-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Believers, Allah’s blessings be upon him, used to say: None rejects generosity except for a donkey. I said: What is the meaning of that? He said: (Being offered) Wide sitting place and when perfume is offered to him.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Maysara, from Abu Ziyad al-Makki, that he said: I heard Abu'l-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: None rejects generosity except for a donkey. By that he meant (that one is offered) perfume and a pillow.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Uthman bin Isa, from Sama'a bin Mahran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who rejects perfume. He said: He should not reject generosity.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who said: He told me, Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: He told me, Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from Sajjada, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no feast (walimah) except in five occasions: marriage, circumcision, buying a house, or a man's return from Mecca. As for the 'urs, it is marriage; and the 'idhar is circumcision; and the wikar is the one who buys a house; and the rikaz is when a man arrives from Mecca.

The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I heard some of the people of language say with regards to the meaning of wikar: It is said about food to which people are invited when a house is built or bought: wakeera, and wikar stems from it. The food that is made for the arrival (of someone) from travel, is called naqee’a. It is also called wikar. Rikaz refers to profit. It is as if he indicates that making food for the approaching from Mecca includes a profit to its maker of abundant reward, and from this meaning is the saying of the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family: «Fasting during winter is the cold profit». The people of Iraq have said: rikaz applies to all metals. The people of Hijaz have said: rikaz refers exclusively to buried property from what has been saved by the sons of Adam before Islam. That is how it was mentioned by Abu Ubaida as well. And there is no saying except by Allah. We were informed of that by Abu’l-Hasan, Muhammed bin Harun al-Zanjani, among what he wrote to me, from Ali bin Abdul-Aziz, from Abu Ubaida, Qasem bin Salam.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the 'hameel' (captives claiming kinship), and he said: 'And what is the hameel?' I said: 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is a small child, so she says:

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed me, saying: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Abu Ubayd, who said: In the narration of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) concerning a people who will emerge from the Fire and grow like a seed vegetates in what is carried by overflowing water. Al-Asma'i said: The hameel is what the flood carries from all things; every carried thing is a hameel, just as it is said to the killed person: 'qateel' (the killed). From this stems the saying of Umar regarding the hameel: 'Inheritance is not passed except with proof.' It was called hameel because it was carried from its country as a small child and was not born into Islam. Al-Asma'i said: As for the seed (habbah), for every plant that has a seed, the name of the seed from it is habbah. Al-Farra' said: The habbah is the sown seed of legumes. Abu Ubayd said: There is another interpretation for hameel, which is better than this: It is said that it is called hameel because its lineage is unknown. This is when a man says: 'This is my brother' or 'my father' or 'my son', and he is not believed except with proof, because he intends thereby to repel the inheritance of his master who freed him. For this reason, the adopted/unknown lineage person is called 'hameel'. He said: Al-Kumait rebukes Qudha'a for their relocation to Yemen: 'Upon what you have settled, not from poverty * Nor hardship, is the station of the hameel.'

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sandi ibn Muhammad, from al-‘Alaa’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him), who said: Tranquility is faith.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him and said: May I be sacrificed for you, what was the coffin of Musa? And how much was its capacity? He said: Three cubits by two cubits. I said: What was in it? He said: The staff of Musa and the Sakinah. I said: And what is the Sakinah? He said: The Spirit of Allah that speaks. If they were to dispute in something, it would speak to them and inform them by clarifying what they seek.

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad Isa, that he said: Abu Humam Isma'il bin Humam narrated to us from al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said to a man: What is tranquility to you? The people did not know what it was, so they said: May Allah make us your ransom, what is it? He said: A good-smelling wind that departs from Paradise which has a shape like the shape of a human and stays with the Prophets (peace be upon them). It is the one that was sent down unto Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he built the Ka'ba, and it began to take such-and-such, and upon it he built the foundation.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hasham, the teacher, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, and Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hasham, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Abu Talib accepted Islam by the calculation of the camel, and he counted thirty-six with his hand. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the example of Abu Talib is like the example of the People of the Cave; they concealed faith and expressed polytheism, hence Allah gave them their reward two times.

Abu al-Faraj Muhammad ibn al-Mudaffar ibn Nafees al-Masri, the jurist, told us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Dawudi told us, from his father, saying: I was at the place of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah sanctify his soul, a man asked him about the meaning of Abbas's statement to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Indeed, your paternal uncle Abu Talib has accepted Islam by the calculation of the camel' - and he counted thirty-six with his hand. So he said: By that he meant 'Ilah Ahad Jawad', and the interpretation of that is that the Alif is one, the Laam is thirty, the Haa is five, the Alif is one and the Hhaa is eight, the Daal is four, the Jeem is three, the Waw is six, the Alif is one, and the Daal is four. Hence, that is thirty-six.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the exegete, al-Jarjani, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nasiri, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, al-Rida, from his father, Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, al-Husayn (peace be upon them). It was said to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him): Describe death to us. He said: You have fallen upon the acquainted. It is one of three things that will approach a person: either a glad tidings of the bliss of eternity, or a glad tidings of the torment of eternity, or grief and horror with an ambiguous matter, not knowing from which group he is. As for our ally, the obedient to our command, he is the one given glad tidings of the bliss of eternity. As for our enemy who opposes us, he is the one given glad tidings of the torment of eternity. As for the one whose matter is ambiguous, who does not know his condition, he is the believer who is extravagant towards himself, not knowing what his condition will lead to. The news comes to him ambiguous and frightening, then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will not equate him with our enemies, but He will take him out of the Fire by our intercession. So act and obey, do not be complacent and do not belittle the punishment of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, for indeed, among those who are extravagant, there is one whom our intercession will not reach except after a torment of three hundred thousand years.

Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) was asked: What is the death which they are ignorant of? He said: The greatest joy that approaches the believers when they are transferred from the home of miserableness to the bliss of the everlasting, and the greatest affliction that approaches the disbelievers when they are transferred from their paradise to a Fire that is not to extinguish nor cease. Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: When the matter of Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) was intensified, those who were with him looked at him, and at sudden he was behind them, because whenever the matter intensified, their colors changed, their shoulder flanks shivered and their hearts fell, whereas Husayn (peace be upon him) and some of those who were with him of his special companions, their colors would shine, their limbs would quieten and their inner selves would calm. They said to each other: Look, he does not care about death! Then Husayn (peace be upon him) said: Patience, O sons of the generous, for death is but a bridge that makes you cross from suffering and harm to the wide gardens and everlasting bliss, for which of you would dislike to relocate from a prison to a castle? For your enemies, it is not but like the one who relocates from a castle to prison and torment. Indeed, my father told me of the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, that this world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever, and that death is the bridge of those to their Gardens and the bridge of those to their Hell. I have not lied, nor been negated.

It was said to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both): What is death? He said: It is the sleep that comes to you every night, except that its duration is long and one will not awaken from it except on the Day of Resurrection. Who has seen in his sleep from the types of happiness what he cannot evaluate its value, and from the types of horrors what he cannot evaluate its value? How is the case of happiness and dread during sleep? That is death, so prepare for it.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, the exegete, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, peace be upon them. He said: Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) entered to a man who had drowned in the throes of death and was not answering a caller. They said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, we would love to know how death is and what the state of our companion is. He said: Death is the purifier; it purifies the believers from their sins, so the last pain that afflicts them is an expiation for the last burden that remains upon them, and it purifies the disbelievers from their good deeds, so it is the last delight or comfort that follows them, and it is the last reward for a good deed that is theirs. As for this companion of yours, he has been sieved from sins with a complete sieving, and purified from errors with a complete purification, and he has become clear until he is clean like how a garment is cleaned from filth, and he has become suitable for mingling with us, the Household, in our Home, the Home of Eternity.

With this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, that he said: A man from the companions of al-Rida, peace be upon him, became ill, and so he visited him and said: 'How do you find yourself?' He said: 'I met death after you.' [By that he meant what he met due to the intensity of his illness.] He said: 'How did you meet it?' He said: 'Severely painful.' He said: 'You did not meet it. You only met that which warns you about it and makes you know some of its condition. People are only two (types of) men: One who rests at death, and one from whom it is rested due to it. Thus, renew faith in Allah and in Divine Authority, and you will be one who rests.' Then the man did so. The narration is long. We took from it the spot of requirement.

With this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said: It was said to Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa, Allah’s blessings be upon them: What is it with these Muslims that they hate death? He said: Because they have become ignorant of it, so they hate it. If they were to know it and they were among the Allies of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, they would surely have loved it, and they would surely have known that the Hereafter is better for them than this world. Then he, peace be upon him, said: O father of Abdullah, what is it with a child or an insane person that he refrains from the medicine that cleans his body and negates the pain from him? He said: Due to their ignorance of the benefit of the medicine. He said: By He who sent Muhammad with the Truth as a Prophet, indeed, the one who prepares for death a true preparation, it is more beneficial to him than this medicine (that is given) to he who is treated. Verily, if they, indeed, were to know what death leads to of bliss, they would surely have called for it and loved it by the most intense of what a rational calls for medicine in order to repel misfortunes and draw safeties.

With this chain of narrators, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), that he said: Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) entered upon a sick man from his companions while he was weeping and grieving over death, so he said to him: O servant of Allah, you fear death because you do not know it. Tell me, if you became dirty, filthy, and harmed by the abundance of dirt and grime upon you, and ulcers and scabies afflicted you, and you knew that washing in a bath would remove all of that, would you not want to enter it and wash that away from yourself, or would you dislike not entering it so that it remains upon you? He said: Yes, O son of Allah's Messenger. He said: That is death; it is that bath, and it is the last thing remaining upon you of purifying your sins and cleansing you from your misdeeds. So when you approach it and cross it, you will certainly be saved from every sorrow, anxiety, and pain, and you will reach every joy and happiness. Then the man calmed down, submitted, became eager, closed the eye of his self, and departed on his way.

Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) was asked about death: What is it? He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when a believer dies, he is not dead, for the one who is truly dead is the disbeliever. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: «He brings out the living from the dead, and He brings out the dead from the living» That means the believer (is brought out) from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever (is brought out) from the believer.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashir al-Qazwini (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Al-Mudaffar ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Ahmari told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Thabit ibn Dinar told us, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn, from his father Ali (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: The best of wealth is a 'sikka ma'bura' and a 'mahr ma'mura'.

Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Daylami al-Jawhari told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asam told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubaidullah al-Munadi told us, saying: Ruh ibn Ubada told us, saying: Abu Na'ama al-Adawi told us, from Muslim ibn Badeel, from Iyas ibn Zuhair, from Suwayd ibn Habeera, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), that he said: The best wealth of a person is a filly that is ma'mura or a sikka that is ma'bura.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ya'qoub bin Yazid, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Dhuraih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The greater pilgrimage is the day of slaughter.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the day of the greater pilgrimage. So he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice, and the smaller one is Umrah.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mughaira, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said: The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, and al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, who said: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: I asked him about the greater pilgrimage, so he said: Do you have anything about it? I said: Yes. Ibn Abbas used to say: The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Arafah. He meant that whoever catches the Day of Arafah until the rising of the dawn from the Day of Sacrifice has indeed caught the pilgrimage, and whoever misses that has missed the pilgrimage. Hence, he considered the night of Arafah as a standard for what is before it and what is after it. The evidence for this is that whoever catches the night of Sacrifice until the rising of the dawn has indeed caught the pilgrimage, and it suffices for him from Arafah. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice. So, travel freely in the land for four months And they are twenty days from Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten days from the month of Rabi' al-Akhir. If the greater pilgrimage were on the Day of Arafah, the free travel would have been four months and one day. And (it is) an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage And I was the announcement among the people. Then I said to him: What is the meaning of this phrase 'the greater pilgrimage'? He said: It was only named the greater because it was a year in which both the Muslims and the polytheists performed pilgrimage, and the polytheists did not perform pilgrimage after that year.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "and mention the Name of Allah in known days", said: The days of the ten.

With this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-abi al-Sabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and mention the Name of Allah in known days». He said: They are the days of al-Tashriq.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and mention Allah in limited number of days». He said: The known and the limited are one, and they are the days of al-Tashriq.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Jarud, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And (it is) an announcement from Allah and His Messenger.' He said: The announcement is Ali, peace be upon him.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Saif ibn Umayra, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira ibn al-Nasri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And (it is) an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage» He said: It is a name whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gifted to Ali, Allah’s blessings be upon him, from the Heaven, because he was, indeed, the one who delivered on behalf of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, (the chapter of) Bara’a He had sent it with Abu Bakr at first, at which Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, descended unto him and said: «O Muhammed, indeed, Allah says to you: Indeed, none shall deliver on behalf of you except for you or a man from you» Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, sent Ali, peace be upon him, therein, and so he caught up with Abu Bakr, took the journal from his hand and went with it to Mecca Allah then named it an Announcement from Allah. It is, indeed, a name gifted by Allah from the Heaven to Ali, peace be upon him.

Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qushayri informed us, saying: Al-Mughira ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Dawud narrated to me, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiya al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am leaving among you two matters, one of which is longer than the other: The Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, a rope extended from heaven to earth, one end in the hand of Allah, and my Family (Ahl al-Bayt). Indeed, they will never separate until they come to me at the Basin (al-Hawd).' I said to Abu Sa'id: 'Who is his Family?' He said: 'His Household.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Hasan al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz (dictating) narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talha narrated from al-A'mash, from Atiyyah ibn Sa'id, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Indeed, I am about to be called and I will respond. So I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things: The Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and my Family (Ahl al-Bayt). The Book of Allah is a Rope extended between Heaven and earth, and my Family is my Household. Indeed, the All-Kind, the All-Acquainted, informed me that they will never be separated until they meet me at the Basin. So look into by what you will succeed me.

We were told by Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Baghdadi, who said: I heard Abu 'Amr and the companion of Abu al-Abbas Taghlib say: I heard Abu al-Abbas Taghlib asking about the meaning of the saying of him, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family: 'Indeed, I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things.' Why were they named the Two Weighty Things? He said: Because adherence to them is heavy.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn (peace be upon them). He said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was asked about the meaning of the saying of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Indeed, I am appointing as Successors among you, the Two Weighty Things, the Book of Allah and my Family.' Who is the Family? So he said: I, Hasan, Husayn, and the nine Imams from the offspring of Husayn, their ninth being their Guided One and their Rising One. They will not separate from the Book of Allah, nor will it separate from them, until they approach Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) at his basin.

Ahmad ibn al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umara, from his father, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Indeed, I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things: the Book of Allah, and my Family, my Household. And indeed, they will never be separated until they come to me at the Basin like these two – and he joined his two index fingers together. Then Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari stood up to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, and who is your Family? He said: Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the Imams from the descendants of al-Husayn until the Day of Resurrection.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from his narrators, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'That is a Day for which the people will gather, and that is a Day that is (to be) witnessed.' He said: That which is the witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and that for which people will gather is the Day of Resurrection.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, who said: I was told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) With regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The witness is Friday, and that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Arafah.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The witness is Friday, that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and that which is promised is the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The witness is the Day of Arafah.

With this chain of narrators, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Hashim, from the one who narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Al-Abrash al-Kalbi asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: What was said to you? He said: They said: The witness is Friday, and that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) then said: It is not like what was said to you. The witness is the Day of Arafah and that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Do you not read the Qur'an? Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: «That is a Day for which the people will gather, and that is a Day that is (to be) witnessed.»

With this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadala, from al-Aban, from Abu al-Jarud, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The witness is Friday, that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and that which is promised is the Day of Resurrection.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, the mawla of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And by the witness, and by what is to be witnessed». He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).

We were told by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: My father told me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Amr ibn Jumay', who said: I was at the place of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with a group of his companions. I heard him saying: Indeed, the womb of the Imams (peace be upon them) from the Family of Muhammad (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) will adhere to the Throne on the Day of Resurrection, and the wombs of the believers will adhere to it, and it will say: 'O Lord, connect to those who connected to us, and disconnect from those who disconnected from us.' He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will say: 'I am the Merciful (al-Rahman), and you are the womb; I split your name from My Name. Hence, the one who connects to you, I will connect him, and the one who disconnects from you, I will disconnect him.' And for this reason, the Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said: 'The womb is a shujna (part/branch) of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.'

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed me in what he wrote to me, saying: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: I heard Qasim ibn Salam say: Regarding the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'The womb is a shujna from Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He,' he means that it is a kinship that is interlocked like the interlocking of veins. And the saying of the speaker: 'The narration has shujun' is that some parts of it adhere to others. And some of the people of knowledge said: It is said: 'A tree that is mutashajjin' if some of its branches wrap around each other. And it is said: shujna and shujna, and al-shajn is like a branch that is from the tree. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has said: Indeed, Fatima is a shujna from me; that which hurts her, hurts me, and that which makes her happy, makes me happy. May the prayers of Allah be upon her.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan told us of that, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi, the freedman of the Banu Hashim, told us, saying: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us by reading, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Tamimi told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran told us, from 'Ubaya, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) [that] he said: Indeed, Fatima is a 'shajana' from me; that which hurts her, hurts me, and that which makes her happy, makes me happy. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is angered for the anger of Fatima and is pleased for her satisfaction. May Allah's blessings be upon her.

We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Sa'd bin Abdullah told us, from al-Haytham bin Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, who said: Al-Husayn bin 'Alwan told us, from 'Amr bin Khalid, from Zayd bin Ali, from his father Ali bin al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn, from his father Ali bin Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: A beast is a jubar, a well is a jubar, a metal mine is a jubar, and in rikaz is the khums. And the jubar is the hadr (killing in vain) for which there is no indemnity (diyah) nor retaliation (qad').

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani told us, saying: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Salam He said: The 'ajma' is the beast, and it was named 'ajma' because it does not speak, and everyone who is unable to speak is 'ajam' and 'musta'jam'. From this is the saying of al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'The daytime prayer is 'ajma,' meaning recitation is not heard in it. As for 'jubar', it is 'hadr' (liability without compensation). The wound of the beast is only considered 'hadr' if it is loose, having no leader, no driver, and no rider. If one of these three is with it, he is a guarantor, because the liability at that time is not for the beast, but for its owner who allowed people to ride it. As for his saying: 'And the well is jubar,' there is more than one saying. It is said: It refers to a well whose owner hires a man to dig it in his property, and it collapses on the digger; hence, there is no liability upon its owner. It is also said: It is a well that is in a man's ownership, and a human or an animal falls into it; hence, there is no liability upon him, because it is in his ownership.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Muhammad bin Hasan, from Ja’far ibn Basheer, from Hussain bin Abi’l-‘Alaa’, from Abdullah bin Maysara, that he said: I said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: We only say: «O Allah, send Your blessings upon Muhammed and the Family of Muhammed». Some people then say: «We are the Family of Muhammed». Then he said: The Family of Muhammed are only those whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, forbade Muhammed to marry.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom. Who are the Aal (Family)? He said: His offspring, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: And who are the Ahl (People)? He said: The Imams (peace be upon them). I said: His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Enter, (O) Family of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment.' He said: By Allah, he did not mean other than his daughter.

And my father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Who are the Aal of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)? He said: His offspring. I said: His Household? He said: The Succeeding Imams. I said: Who is his 'Itra? He said: The People of the Cloak. I said: Who is his Ummah? He said: The believers who verified what he brought from Allah, Exalted and Glorious, those adhering to the Two Weighty Things which they were ordered to hold fast to: The Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, and his 'Itra, his Household, from whom Allah removed impurity and purified them with a complete purification. And they are the Two Successors over the nation after him (peace be upon him).

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sa'd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We were with him eight men, and we mentioned Ramadan. He said: Do not say: 'This is Ramadan,' nor 'Ramadan has gone,' nor 'Ramadan has come.' Indeed, Ramadan is a Name from the Names of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. It does not come, nor does it go away, but it is only that which is perishable that comes and goes. However, say: 'The Month of Ramadan.' For the month added to the Name, and the Name is the Name of Allah, and that is the month in which the Qur'an was sent down, which Allah, Exalted is He, made as a sign and a warning.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), that he said: Ali (Allah's blessings be upon him) said: Do not say: 'Ramadhan', however, say: 'the Month of Ramadhan', for indeed, you do not know what Ramadhan is.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Bassam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sari narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Kinani, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said to me: 'O Ali, do you know the meaning of the Night of Destiny?' I said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, destined in it what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection.
