And among what He, Exalted and Glorious, destined, is your Divine Authority and the Divine Authority of the Imams from your offspring until the Day of Resurrection.'

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Mihran, from Salih ibn Uqba, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: It was mentioned before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): "Indeed, We sent it down during the night of destiny." He said: How clear is its preference over the other chapters. He said: I said: And what is its preference? He said: The Divine Authority of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was revealed in it. I said: In the night of destiny that we hope for during the month of Ramadan? He said: Yes, it is a night in which the Heavens and the earth were destined, and the Divine Authority of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was destined in it.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: Three [acts] from the practices of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance): pride in lineage, vilification due to status, and seeking rain through the anwaa' (star positions).

Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed me, saying: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Abu Ubayd, that he said: I heard several from the people of knowledge say: The Anwaa' are twenty-eight stars known for their rising times during the seasons of the year, all from summer, winter, spring, and autumn. In every thirteenth night, one star sets in the west with the rising of dawn, and another rises opposite to it in the east at that same time, and both are known and designated. The completion of all these twenty-eight coincides with the completion of the year, then the matter returns to the first star with the commencement of the coming year. The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance), when one of them set and another rose, would say: 'There must be wind and rain at that time,' and they would attribute every rain that occurred at that time to that star which set at that moment, saying: 'We were rained upon by the rising of Thuraiya, Dabran, Samak,' and whatever of these stars. Based on this, these are the Anwaa', and one of them is a 'Naw''. It was named 'Naw'' because when the setting star sets in the west, the rising star rises in the east with its rising, and it 'Naw'' (rises/turns away), and that rising is the 'Naw'', so the star was named by it. And so is everything that rises and moves with slowness, it 'Naw'' at its rising. He, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: 'That he might burden the band of the strong'.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra Humayd ibn al-Muthanna al-Ajali, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The middle prayer is the noon prayer, and it is the first prayer that Allah sent down upon His Prophet, peace be upon him and his Family.

Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan known as Ibn Maqbara al-Qazwini, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn [Abi] al-Sabah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Asem al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Na'im al-Fadl ibn Dakeen informed us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zaid ibn Aslam, from Abu Yunus, who said: I wrote for Aisha a Mushaf (copy of the Quran), and she said: When you pass by the verse of prayer, do not write it until I dictate it to you. Then, when I passed by it, she dictated to me: 'Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer and the prayer of the afternoon.'

Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini said: He narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah [who said: Ahmad] ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated from Sa'd ibn Dawud, from Abu Dahr, from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Nafi', who said: I was writing a Quran codex for Hafsa, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.'

Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Dawud narrated to us from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Yunus, the freedman of Aisha, wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), who said: Aisha ordered me to write for her a Mushaf (Quran codex), and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer (and the afternoon prayer), and stand before Allah devoutly,' then Aisha said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) by Allah. Aisha ordered me to write for her a Mushaf, and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer (and the afternoon prayer) and stand before Allah devoutly.' Then Aisha said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) by Allah.
The compiler of this book said: Hence, these reports are an argument in our favor against the opponents. The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id together, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Hariz ibn Abd Allah al-Sijistani, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked him, meaning Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), about what Allah, Exalted and Glorious, has obligated regarding prayer, so he said: Five prayers during the night and day. I said: Did Allah, Blessed and Exalted, name them and clarify them in His Book? He said: Yes, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to His Prophet, peace be upon him and his Family: 'Establish the prayer at the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night.' And its setting is its vanishing, so between the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night are four prayers which He named, clarified, and set a time for, and the darkness of the night is its midpoint, Then He said: 'And the Qur'an of the dawn. Indeed, the Qur'an of the dawn is ever witnessed.' This is the fifth. And He, Blessed and Exalted, said regarding that: 'Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day', and its two ends are the Maghrib (sunset) and al-Ghada (early morning) prayers. 'And at the approach of the night', and that is the 'Isha al-Akhira (last evening) prayer. And He, Exalted and Glorious, said: 'Maintain the prayers, and (in particular) the middle prayer.' And it is the Dhuhr (noon) prayer, and it was the first prayer the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, prayed, and it is in the middle of two prayers during the day, the al-Ghada (early morning) and al-Asr (afternoon) prayers. 'And stand before Allah, devoutly obedient' during the middle prayer.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazem, who said: 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn al-Qasim al-Ansari narrated to me, saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to us that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and said: 'I am ruined, I am ruined!' So he said: 'And what has ruined you?' He said: 'I approached my wife during the month of Ramadan while I was fasting.' The Prophet said to him: 'Free a slave.' He said: 'I cannot find [one].' He said: 'Then fast for two consecutive months.' He said: 'I cannot handle it.' He said: 'Give charity to sixty poor people.' He said: 'I cannot find [the means].' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) was brought a 'irq or a 'muktal containing fifteen sa's of dates. The Prophet said to him: 'Take it and give it as charity.' He said: 'By He who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, between its two 'laba's, there is no household more in need of it than us.' So he said: 'Take it and eat it, you and your family, for indeed, it is an expiation for you.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Maskan, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I was with Ziyad ibn Abdillah, and Rabee'at al-Ra'y was with him. Ziyad said to him: 'O Rabee', what did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declare forbidden in Medina?' He said to him: 'Mail for mail.' I said to Rabee': 'Was there mail during the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family)?' He became silent and did not answer me. Ziyad turned to me and said: 'O Abu Abdillah, then what do you say?' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declared forbidden in Medina, from the game, that which is between the two Labas.' He said: 'And what are their two Labas?' I said: 'That which is surrounded by the heat (climate/region).' He said to me: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declare forbidden from trees?' I said: 'From 'Eer to Wa'er.' Safwan said: Ibn Maskan said: Hasan said: Then a person asked him while I was sitting, and he said to him: 'And what are their two Labas?' He said: 'That which is between the two Suroon until the Thaniyyah.'

With this chain of narrators, from Al-Husayn Sa'eed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declared forbidden from Medina that which is from Dhubab to Al-Aqim, Al-Areedh, and Al-Naqb from the side of Mecca. Ibn Maskan said in his narration: And in another narration: From As-Sur to Ath-Thaniyyah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadala, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: That which is between the two laba's of Medina, from the shadow of 'A'ir until the shadow of Wa'ir, is a sanctuary (haram). I said: Is its bird like the bird of Mecca? He said: No, nor should its trees be cut.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban told us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Ruba'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath". He said: The cutting of the moustache and nails.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Then let them end their tafath' He said: It is shaving and what is in the skin of a person.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: He narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadala, from al-Aban, from Zurara, from Hamran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath" He said: Tafath is the abstention of the man from perfume. When he has completed his rites, perfume becomes permissible to him.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath, and let them fulfill their vows" He said: Tafath is the trimming of the nails, casting off filth, and casting off the Ihram from it.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath". He said: That which occurs from the man during his state of Ihram. When he enters Mecca, he performs the Tawaf and speaks with good speech, for indeed, that is an expiation for that which came from him.

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, from Hamdawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, from Abu Jameela, from Amr ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about tafath. He said: It is trimming the head.

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasir told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about tafath, so he said: It is shaving and what is in the skin of a person.

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ali narrated to us, from Abdul-Adheem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Then, let them end their tafath.' He said: It is trimming and untidiness. He said: Among tafath is that you speak during your state of Ihram with horrid speech. If you then enter Mecca, perform the circling around the House, and speak with good speech, that would be its expiation.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad, from Musa bin Umar, from Muhammad bin Isma'il bin Bazee', from Ibrahim bin Mahzam, from the one he narrates from, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you enter Mecca, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity due to what came from you during your state of Ihram for the Umrah. Then, when you are finished with your pilgrimage, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity. Then, if you enter Medina, do the same as that.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Ali ibn Sulayman, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Dhuraih al-Muharibi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Indeed, Allah has commanded me in His Book with a command, and I wish to know it. He said: And what is that? I said: The saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'Then let them end their tafath and let them fulfill their vows.' He said: 'Let them end their tafath' is the meeting with the Imam, and 'let them fulfill their vows' are those rites. Abdullah ibn Sinan said: Then I came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: May Allah make me a sacrifice for you, [regarding] the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'Then let them end their tafath and let them fulfill their vows.' He said: [It is] trimming the mustache and cutting the nails and similar to that. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, for Dhuraih al-Muharibi narrated to me from you that you said to him: 'Then let them end their tafath' is the meeting with the Imam, and 'let them fulfill their vows' are those rites? He said: Dhuraih spoke the truth, and you spoke the truth. Indeed, for the Qur'an has an apparent meaning and an internal meaning, and who can bear what Dhurain bears?

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do not abandon the standing during the night, for indeed, the defrauded is the one who is defrauded from the standing during the night.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Asha'ari, with his chain of narrators mentioned in his compilation, which he ascribed to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The defrauded is the one who is defrauded of his age, hour after hour.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, who said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The one to whom two days are equal, is defrauded. The one to whom the last of his two days was the better, is envied. The one to whom the last of his two days was the worst, is cursed. The one who does not look forward to increasement (of quality) in himself, is going towards decrement, and the one who goes towards decrement, death is better for him than life.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Nasr al-Bukhari al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah al-Kufi al-Alawi, the Jurist, in Fergana, narrated to us with a continuous chain to al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, that he was asked about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then We made the Book an inheritance to those whom We chose from Our servants. And among them is the one who wrongs himself, and among them is the moderate, and among them is the forerunner in good deeds by the permission of Allah." He said: The wrongdoer circles around his own self, the moderate circles around his heart, and the forerunner circles around his Lord, Exalted and Glorious is He.

Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Yahya al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Uwana Musa ibn Yusuf al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yahya, from Abu Hafs, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I was sitting in the Sacred Mosque with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when two men from the people of Basra came to him and said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, we wish to ask you about a matter. He said to them: Ask about what you have come for. They said: Inform us about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then We made the Book an inheritance to those whom We chose from Our servants. And among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who precedes in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great bounty." Until the end of the two verses. He said: It was revealed concerning us, the Household. Abu Hamza said: Then I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, who is the one who wrongs himself? He said: The one whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal among us, the Household, he is the one who wrongs himself. I said: Who is the moderate among you? He said: The one who worships Allah, his Lord, in both conditions (life and death), until certainty comes to him. I said: Then who is the forerunner in good deeds among you? He said: The one who calls by Allah to the path of his Lord, enjoins good, forbids evil, is not a supporter to the misleaders, nor an adversary to the traitors, and is not pleased with the rule of the sinners except for he who fears for himself and his religion and finds no assistants.

We were told by Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn al-Muaddab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bakr ibn Abdullah, from Nasr ibn Ubaid [Allah], from Nasr ibn Muzahim, that he said: I was told by Abdul-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-A'mash, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, that he said: Abu Sufyan approached, while Mu'awiya was following him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: 'O Allah, curse the follower and the followed. O Allah, it is upon You to ruin the Aqi'is.' Ibn al-Bara' said to his father: Who is the Aqi'is? He said: Mu'awiya.

The compiler of this book said: Al-Aq'as is the diminutive of al-Aq'as, and that is the one whose neck is curved. Al-Qa'as is a curvature that takes hold in the neck from a wind, as if it breaks it towards what is behind it. Al-Aq'as is the noble, the refraining one. It is also said: 'Azz Aq'as' (He is noble and refraining). Al-Qaw'as is the one with a thick neck, rigorous in his back in all things. Al-Qa'ous is the old man. Al-Qa's is the opposite of hunchbackedness. The verb is: Qa'sa yaq'su qas'an (he was swaybacked). The plural is Qasawāt and Qu's. Al-Qa'sa' is the ant that raises its chest and tail. Al-Aq'nās is intensity. Al-Taqā'us is from 'Such-a-person slacked' if he did not accomplish and did not move forward in what he was assigned to. Muqā'is is a tribe from Tamim.

Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ahmad... and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qazwini (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: We were told by Abu'l-Faraj al-Mudaffar ibn Ahmad al-Qazwini, who said: We were told by Abu'l-Fayd Salih ibn Ahmad, who said: We were told by Hasan ibn Musa ibn Ziyad, who said: We were told by Salih ibn Hammad, who said: We were told by Hasan ibn Musa al-Washsha' al-Baghdadi, who said: I was in Khorasan with Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both) in his gathering, and Zayd ibn Musa was present. He had approached a group in the gathering, boasting over them and saying: 'We are [the elite], we are [the elite].' Meanwhile, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was facing a people, speaking to them. He heard Zayd's statement, so he turned to him and said: 'O Zayd, has the saying of the food merchant of Kufa deceived you, that Fatima shielded her private organ, so Allah forbade her offspring from the Fire?' By Allah, that is only for al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the children of her belly exclusively. If Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) obeys Allah, fasts his day, and stands in prayer his night, while you disobey him, and then you both come on the Day of Resurrection as equal, you will be more honored to Allah, Exalted and Glorious, than him. Indeed, Ali ibn Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say: 'For our good-doer is a double portion of reward, and for our wrongdoer is double the torment.' Al-Washsha' said: Then he turned to me and said: 'O Hasan, how do you recite this verse: "He said: O Nuh, indeed, he is not from your family; indeed, he is an act that is not righteous"?' I said: 'Among the people are those who recite: "Indeed, he is an act that is not righteous" and among them are those who recite: "Indeed, he is the act of one who is not righteous." The one who recites: "Indeed, he is the act of one who is not righteous" has negated him from his father.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, he was certainly his son, but when he disobeyed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, Allah negated him from his father. So is the one who is from us who does not obey Allah, Exalted and Glorious; he is not from us. And you, if you obey Allah, then you are from us, the Household.'

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Indeed, Fatima shielded her private organ, so Allah forbade her offspring from the Fire'? He said: Yes, by that he meant Hasan, Husayn, Zainab, and Um Kulthum.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washha', from Muhammad ibn Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be sacrificed for you, what is the meaning of the saying of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family): 'Indeed, Fatima shielded her private organ, so Allah forbade her offspring from the Fire'? He said: Those who are freed from the Fire are the children from her belly: al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Zaynab, and Umm Kulthum.

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq the Trader, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Let none estimate for the Day of Resurrection by saying: O Lord, I did not know that the sons of Fatima are the Guardians, and that it was for the sake of Fatima’s sons, exclusively, that Allah sent down this verse: «O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair from the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the All-Merciful.»

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ishkeeb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abdul-A'la, who said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So, avoid the filth of idols and avoid false speech.' He said: The filth from idols is chess, and false speech is singing. I said: His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And among the people is he who buys amusement of speech.' He said: From it is singing.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa, from Muhammad bin Yahya, the silk maker, from Hammad bin Uthman, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about forged statement. He said: From it is the saying of a man to the one who sings: «You did well».

Ahmad ibn al-Qattan narrated, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Husayni narrated, saying: Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Hamid al-Lakhmi narrated, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Zakariya narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muhallabi narrated, saying: Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Hasan, from his mother Fatima bint al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). She said: When the illness of Fatima, daughter of Allah's Messenger, Allah's blessings be upon her, intensified, the women of the Muhajirun and the Ansar gathered at her place and said to her: O daughter of Allah's Messenger, how have you become this morning from your illness? She said: I have become at this morning, by Allah, one who will leave this world of yours and detests your men; I spat them before I chewed them, and I have become to disgust them after having examined them, Hence, ugliness (be to them) due to the roundedness of the edges (of swords), weakness of the spears and clumsiness of opinions. Moreover, evil is what their own selves presented for them, that (it caused) Allah to become angry at them, and that they are to abide in torment. Assuredly, I had certainly bound the nooses to them and poured its shame upon them. Hence, may mutilation, slaughter and crushing afflict the oppressive people. Woe to them, how did they remove it from the Mountains of the Message, the Foundations of Prophethood, the descension spot of the Trusted Revelation and the Knowledgeable of matters of materialism and Religion. Alas, that is the clear loss! Whatever they harbored of malice towards Abu Hasan, they harbored, and Allah will be, for his sake, in disavowal with His Sword. Severe shall His touch be, and by exemplary punishment shall His affliction be, due to his rage for the sake of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. By Allah, if they had refrained from the ropes cast by Allah's Messenger, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family, he would have taken it, and he would have walked with them in a suggestible manner by which its khashash will not cause injury, nor will its rider shake, and he would have made them approach a good, high-flowing spring whose banks are full to the brim, and he would have sent them off while they are full. He chose for them irrigation without seeking lawfulness to it with an enormous thing, except by a tu

And Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, known as Ibn Maqbara al-Qazwini, narrated to us this hadith, saying: He informed us that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn Hasan ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) said: He told me that Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hashimi said: He narrated to us that Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: He told me his father, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: When Fatima (peace be upon her) was about to die, she called me and said: Are you to fulfill my testament and covenant? He said: I said: Yes, I will fulfill it. She then bequeathed to me and said: If I die, bury me at night, and do not give permission to the two men whom she mentioned. He said: Then, when her illness became severe, the women of the Muhajirun and the Ansar gathered to her and said: How have you become this morning, O daughter of Allah's Messenger, from your illness? She said: I have become, by Allah, one who will leave this world of yours, and he mentioned the hadith similarly.

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasir told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ayub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (Allah's blessings be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So they did not yield to their Lord, nor did they humbly supplicate' He said: Tadharru' (humble supplication) is raising the hands.

Al-Mudaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Mudaffar al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad, who said: Al-'Amari told me, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: Tabattul is that you turn your palms during supplication when you supplicate. Ibtihal is that you extend them and bring them forward. Raghba is that you face the sky with your palms and face them with your face. Rahba is that you incline your palms by raising them to the face. Tadharru' is that you move your two fingers and point with them. And in another narration: Basbasa is that you raise your index fingers to the sky, move them and supplicate.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Muhammed bin Hamran, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: The one who says: «There is no god but Allah» sincerely, will enter Paradise, and his sincerity is that «There is no god but Allah» will constrain him from that which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has forbidden.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, all of them, from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Muhajir ibn al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), who said: Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely, will enter Paradise, and his sincerity is that 'There is no god but Allah' will constrain him from that which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has forbidden.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Indeed, We presented the trust upon the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to carry it and feared it, and it was carried by the human being. He is, indeed, wrong-doing, ignorant.» He said: The trust is the Divine Authority (Wilayah), and the human being is the one of evils, the hypocrite.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Indeed, We presented the trust upon the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to carry it and feared it, and the human being carried it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.' So he said: The trust is the Divine Authority (Wilayah); he who proclaims it without right, has disbelieved.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Laythi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'and an abandoned well and a lofty palace' He said: The Abandoned Well is the Silent Imam, and the Lofty Palace is the Speaking Imam.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from some of our companions, from Nasr ibn Qabus, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and an abandoned well and a lofty palace». He said: The Abandoned Well is the Silent Imam, and the Lofty Palace is the Speaking Imam.

Al-Mudaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Mudaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun informed me, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal, from Salih ibn Sahl, that he said: The Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, is the Lofty Palace, and the Abandoned Well is Fatima and her sons, who are abandoned from rulership.

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid al-Ash'ari, nicknamed Shanbula, said: An abandoned well and a high palace, an exquisite example of the Family of Muhammad, so, the speaking is the lofty palace, among them, and the silent is the well that does not bleed.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr [and] ibn Ali ibn Abdullah al-Basri narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Ali al-Karkhi narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq al-San'ani narrated to us, he said: Mu'ammar narrated from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) performed the dawn prayer, and when he turned from his prayer, he faced us with his noble face, in reverence to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and then he said: O people, whoever misses the sun, let him hold fast to the moon, and whoever misses the moon, let him hold fast to Venus (al-Zuhra), and whoever misses Venus, let him hold fast to the Two Farqads (the two bright stars). Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: I am the Sun, Ali is the Moon, Fatima is Venus, and Hasan and Husayn are the Two Farqads. And the Book of Allah will not be separated from them until they come to me at the Basin.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Saffar al-Nahawandi narrated to us in it, saying: Abu al-Faraj Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khuzay al-Samiri narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim al-Qantari narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Halwani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Follow the sun, and if the sun sets, follow the moon, and if the moon sets, follow Venus (al-Zuhra), and if Venus sets, follow the two Farqads (stars). Then they said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the sun? And what is the moon? And what is Venus? And what are the two Farqads? So he said: I am the Sun, Ali is the Moon, Venus is Fatima, and the Two Farqads are Hasan and Husayn.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Bandar narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Haysun narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Sari narrated from Muhammad ibn Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) that he said: "Follow the sun..." - and he mentioned the narration exactly the same.

Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Abi Ja'far al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ja'far al-Madini narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Dhaheer ibn Salih al-Amri narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Tamim narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman informed us, from his father, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) led us in the dawn prayer. When he finished from his prayer, he turned towards us with his generous face and said: O people, whoever misses the sun, let him hold fast to the moon; and whoever misses the moon, let him hold fast to Zuhra (Venus); and whoever misses Zuhra, let him hold fast to the Two Farqads (stars). It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what are the sun, the moon, Zuhra, and the two Farqads? He said: I am the Sun, Ali is the Moon, Fatima is Zuhra, and Hasan and Husayn are the two Farqads. And the Book of Allah will not be separated from them until they come to me at the Basin.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Qasim bin Yahya, from his grandfather, Hasan bin Rashid, from Abu’l-Hasan Musa bin Ja’far (peace be upon them both), who said: He was asked about the meaning of "Allah", Glorious and Exalted is He, so he said: He has taken possession over the tiny and the magnified.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jarjani, the exegete, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Abu Ya'qub Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar (who were from the Imami Shi'a) narrated to us from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them, regarding the saying of Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' He said: Allah is He to whom all creatures seek divinity at times of needs and hardships, when hope is cut off from everyone besides Him, and means are disconnected from all others. You say: 'In the name of Allah,' meaning: I seek assistance in all my affairs from Allah, to whom servitude is due alone, the Succorer when succor is sought, and the Responder when called upon. This is what a man said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'O son of Allah's Messenger, guide me to Allah, what is He? For the polemicists have overwhelmed me and confused me.' He said to him: 'O servant of Allah, have you ever boarded a ship?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then, did it break with you to the extent that no ship could save you, nor swimming suffice for you?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then, did it connect to your heart that there is a thing among things that is able to save you from your hazard?' He said: 'Yes.' Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'Then, that Thing is Allah, the One Able to rescue when there is no rescuer, and to succor when there is no succorer.'

Ali ibn Isa al-Mujawir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us in the Mosque of Kufa, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Maqarri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Thuwayr ibn Sa'id, from his father Sa'id ibn Aqalah, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) ascended the pulpit of Basra and said: O people, mention my lineage. Let he who knows me mention my lineage, otherwise, I will mention my lineage by myself. I am Zaid ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Amer ibn Amr ibn Mughirah ibn Zaid ibn Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up to him and said to him: O you, we do not know for you any lineage except that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said to him: O you, indeed, my father named me 'Zaid' by the name of his grandfather 'Qusay', and the name of my father is 'Abd-Manaf', then the kunya (nickname) overtook the name, and indeed, the name of Abd al-Muttalib is 'Amer', then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Hashim is 'Amr', then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Abd-Manaf is 'Mughirah', then the nickname overtook the name, and indeed, Qusay is 'Zaid', then the Arabs named him 'Mujamma' (the Gatherer) because he gathered them from the farthest land to Mecca, then the nickname overtook the name.

Hakim, Abu Hamid, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali in Balkh told us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Hasan ibn Mahran al-Isbahani in Baghdad told me, saying: Hasan ibn Hamza ibn Hammad ibn Bahram al-Farsi told me, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Aban al-Qazwini told us, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhali, from Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri, saying: The Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), ascended the pulpit and said: O people, mention my lineage. Let he who knows me mention my lineage, otherwise, I will mention my lineage by myself. I am Zaid ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Amer ibn Amr ibn Mughira ibn Zaid ibn Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up to him and said: O you, we do not know for you any lineage except that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abdul-Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Qusay ibn Kilab. Then he said to him: O ignoble, indeed, my father named me 'Zaid' by the name of his grandfather 'Qusay', and the name of my father is 'Abd-Manaf', then the kunya (nickname) overtook the name, and indeed, the name of Abdul-Muttalib is 'Amer', then the laqab (epithet) overtook the name, and the name of Hashim is 'Amr', then the laqab overtook the name, and the name of Abd-Manaf is 'Mughira', then the laqab overtook the name, and the name of Qusay is 'Zaid', then the Arabs named him jointly due to that he had gathered them from the farthest land to Mecca, then the laqab overtook the name. He said: For Abdul-Muttalib are ten names, among them are: Abdul-Muttalib, Shayba, and Amer.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Wahhab narrated to us, he said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn al-Baqi narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Ghani narrated to us [he said]: Al-Mughani, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, from Mandal, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas. Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.' Peace be upon the Family of Yasin. He said: The peace is from the Lord of all the worlds upon Muhammad and his Family, may Allah bless him and them, and safety is for those who befriend them in the Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abu Ahmad Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Isa al-Jaloudi al-Basri told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl told us, saying: Al-Khadhr ibn Abi Fatima al-Balkhi told us, saying: Wahb ibn Nafi' told us, saying: Kadih told me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon them). Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.' He said: Yasin is Muhammad (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family), and we are the Family of Yasin.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abu Ahmad Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Isa al-Jaludi al-Basri told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh told me, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Dhaheer told us, from al-Sanadi, from Abu Malik. Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.' He said: Yasin is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family), and we are the Family of Yasin.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Hasan, the Teacher, from Ahmad bin Ali al-Esbahani, from Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Thaqafi, that he said: I was informed by Ahmad bin Abi Umar al-Nahdi, that he said: I was told by my father, from Muhammad bin Marwan, from Muhammad bin Sa'ib, from Abu Saleh, from Ibn Abbas with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.» He said: Upon the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon them.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Jaloudi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Mu'ammar told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Dahir al-Ahmari told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Al-A'mash told us, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.' Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The Family of Yasin is the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon them.

We were told by Ali bin Fadl bin Abbas al-Baghdadi, that he said: I read for Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sulayman bin Harith. He said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ali bin Khalaf al-‘Attar, that he said: We were told by Hussain al-Ashqar, that he said: We were told by Amru bin Abi’l-Miqdam, from his father, from Sa’eed bin Jubair, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: I asked the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, about the Words which Adam received from his Lord, after which He accepted his repentance. He said: He asked Him: By the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, Hasan and Hussain, I beg that You accept my repentance. Then Allah accepted his repentance.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Mada'ini told me, attributing it to the Prophet (or Imam) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then Adam received from his Lord, Words" He said: I asked him by the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, peace be upon them.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Abbas ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said to the heretic - when he asked him about Allah, what is He? - He said: He is a Thing different to all things. Return my saying 'a thing' to confirming a meaning, and that He is a Thing by the truth of Thingness, except that He is not a body nor an image.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Aban, from one whom he mentioned, attributing it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He was asked: Is it permissible to say that Allah is a thing? He said: Yes, it removes it from the two limits: the limit of negation (of attributes/existence) and the limit of anthropomorphism.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maimun, from Zurara, from Abd al-Khaliq ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And the one whom He wants to lead astray, He will make his chest tight, uneasy.» He said: It might be tight and have an opening from which he hears and sees. The one that is aggravated (al-haraj) is that which is closed/adhesive, which has no opening by which he hears nor sees from it.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdous al-Attar in Nishapur, year 352, told us: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naisabouri, told us: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "So, the one whom Allah wants to guide, He expands his chest to Islam" He said: The one whom Allah wants to guide with his faith in this world to His Garden and the House of His Generosity in the Hereafter, He will expand his chest to submission to Allah, trust in Him and tranquility towards what He has promised of His reward until he is assured of Him. Moreover, the one whom He wants to lead astray from His Garden and House of Generosity in the Hereafter due to his disbelief and disobedience to Him in this world, He will make his chest tight, aggravated, until he doubts in his disbelief and his heart is distressed from his belief until he becomes as if he is elevating in the sky. Similarly, Allah makes impurity for those who do not believe.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Hisham bin Abdul-Malik, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about the meaning of «Glorified be Allah», to which he said: An honoring of Allah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulaym, the mawla of Tarbal, from Hisham al-Jawaleeqi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Glorified be Allah' — what does He mean by it? He said: Extolment (Tanzih).

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamza al-Sha'rani al-Amari, from the descendants of Ammar ibn Yasir, informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ubayd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi al-Adni (in Adna) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Ma'ani narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Uqba ibn Abi al-'Aizar, who said: Muhammad ibn Hajar narrated to us from Yazid ibn al-Asam, who said: A man asked Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the interpretation of 'Subhan Allah'?' He replied: 'In this wall, there is a man who, when asked, informs, and when left silent, he begins (to speak).' The man entered, and it was Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So he asked: 'O Abu al-Hasan, what is the interpretation of 'Subhan Allah'?' He replied: 'It is the glorification of the majesty of Allah Almighty and the declaration of His transcendence above what any polytheist has said about Him. When a servant says it, every angel prays for him.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who recites one hundred verses which he prays with at night, Allah will write for him, by them, the qunut of a night, and the one who recites two hundred verses at night in other than the night prayer, Allah will write for him in the Preserved Tablet a kantar of good deeds. A kantar is a thousand and two hundred okes, and one oke is greater than Mount Uhud.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever recites ten verses in a night will not be written among the heedless. And whoever recites fifty verses will be written among the remembrers. And whoever recites one hundred verses will be written among those who perform qunut. And whoever recites two hundred verses will be written among the humble. And whoever recites three hundred verses will be written among the winners. And whoever recites five hundred verses will be written among the diligent. And whoever recites one thousand verses, a kantar will be written for him. And the kantar is five thousand mithqals of gold. And the mithqal is twenty-four carats, the smallest of which is like Mount Uhud, and the largest of which is that which is between the heaven and the earth.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash‘ari, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Maskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Allah has not instituted baheera, nor sa’iba, nor waseela, nor haam.» He said: Indeed, the people of the Jahiliya, when a female camel gave birth to two children in one belly, they would say: «She connected» and they would not consider it allowable to slaughter it, nor eat it. If she gave birth to ten, they would make it a sa’iba, and they would not permit its back nor to eat it. The haam is the male camel which they did not consider allowable. Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, sent down that He had not forbidden anything of that.

It has been narrated that al-Bahira is the female camel when she has produced five offspring; if the fifth was a male, they would slaughter him and men and women would eat from him. And if the fifth was a female, they would slit her ear, meaning they cut it, and her flesh and milk would be forbidden for women and men. And if she died naturally, she would be allowed for women. Al-Sa'iba is the camel that walks freely due to an oath that is upon a man if Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, saves him from an illness or makes him reach his home, that he would do that. Al-Waseela from the sheep is a sheep that gives birth to seven offspring; if the seventh was a male, he would be slaughtered, and men and women would eat from him. And if it was a female, it would be left among the sheep. And if it was a male and a female, they said: 'It has connected with its brother,' so it would not be slaughtered, and its flesh would be forbidden for women, except if something dies from it, and so it would then be allowed to eat for men and women. Al-Ham is the male stud when he rides and produces his son; they would say: 'His back is heated.' It may be narrated that al-Ham is the camel that has produced ten offspring, due to which they would say: 'His back is heated,' and so it would not be ridden, nor prevented from care nor water.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, with his chain, that he ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that it was said to him: (What is the ruling of) A man who drinks in one breath? He said: There is no harm. I said: There are those before us who say that this is (like) the drinking of thirsty cattle? Then he said: The (like of the) drinking of thirsty cattle is only that which the Name of Allah has not been mentioned upon.

We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from Uthman bin Isa, from an old man from the people of Medina, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about a man who drinks and does not stop until he is satisfied. He said: Is satisfaction but that? I said: They say that it is (like) the drinking of thirsty cattle? He said: They have lied. The drinking of thirsty cattle is only that which the Name of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has not been mentioned upon.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman al-Na'ib, from Abdullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three breaths while drinking is better than one breath while drinking. He also said that it is disliked that it resembles thirsty cattle. I said: And what are thirsty camels? He said: Riding animals. And in another narration it is camels.

I was told by Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, that he said: I was told by Sahl ibn Ziyad, that he said: I was told by Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Nujayh, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said: We mentioned ill-omen at his place. He said: Ill-omen is in three: in a woman, a riding animal and a home. As for the ill-omen of a woman, it is her large amount of dowry and her disobedience to her husband. As for a riding animal, it is its ill manners and its prevention of its back. As for a home, it is its tight space, evil of its neighbors and amounts of defects.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Maimoun, from Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family) said: Ill-omen is in three things: in a riding animal, a woman, and a home. As for a woman, her ill-omen is the expensiveness of her dowry and difficulty of her labour. As for a riding animal, its ill-omen is its abundance of defects and ill manners. As for a home, its ill-omen is its tightness and wickedness of its neighbors. He also said: From the blessings of a woman is the lightness of her supplies and easiness of her labour, and her ill-omen is the heaviness of her supplies and difficulty of her labour.

Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “One day, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was sitting with Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah when he said to him: ‘O Muḥammad, bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer).’” So Muḥammad brought him the water, and he poured with his right hand onto his left hand, then said: “In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and all praise belongs to Allah, who made water purifying and did not make it impure.” He said: “Then he performed istinjāʾ and said: ‘O Allah, protect my private part and keep it chaste, cover my nakedness, and make me forbidden to the Fire.’” He said: “Then he rinsed his mouth and said: ‘O Allah, prompt me with my proof on the day I meet You, and loosen my tongue with Your dhikr and Your shukr.’” Then he sniffed water into his nose and said: “O Allah, do not forbid me the fragrance of Jannah, and make me among those who smell its fragrance, its gentle breeze, and its perfume.” He said: “Then he washed his face and said: ‘O Allah, brighten my face on the day when faces will be darkened, and do not darken my face on the day when faces will be brightened.’” Then he washed his right hand and said: “O Allah, give me my book in my right hand, and everlasting life in the gardens in my left, and reckon me with an easy reckoning.” Then he washed his left hand and said: “O Allah, do not give me my book in my left hand, and do not make it shackled to my neck, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from the severing torments of the fires.” Then he wiped his head and said: “O Allah, envelop me in Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your pardon.” Then he wiped his feet and said: “O Allah, make me steadfast upon the ṣirāṭ on the day when feet will slip, and make my striving in that which pleases You with me, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.” Then he raised his head and looked at Muḥammad and said: “O Muḥammad, whoever performs wudu (ablution) like my wudu and says the like of what I say, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, creates from every drop an angel that sanctifies Him, glorifies Him, and magnifies Him; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes the reward of that for him until the Day of Qiyamah.”

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he performed wudu (ablution), would not let anyone pour water over him. So it was said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why do you not let them pour water over you?” Then he said: I do not like to associate anyone in my salat (prayer). And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام wiped over the two sandals and did not pass beneath the two straps.”

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, when he performed wudu (ablution), would say: In the name of Allah and by Allah; and the best names belong to Allah, and the greatest names belong to Allah, and He is dominant over those in the heaven and dominant over those on the earth. All praise is due to Allah, who made from water every living thing. And He revived my heart with faith. O Allah, accept my repentance and purify me, decree for me the best, show me all that I love, and open for me the good things from Your presence, O Hearer of supplication.

Zurarah ibn A'yan said to Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام: Inform me about the limit of the face which should be washed in wudu (ablution), the one Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned. So he said: The face that Allah mentioned and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be washed is that to which no one should add and from which no one should subtract. If he adds to it, he will not be rewarded, and if he subtracts from it, he sins. It is that over which the middle finger and the thumb pass, from the hairline of the head to the chin; and whatever the two fingers encompass in a circular manner is of the face, and whatever is beyond that is not of the face. He said to him: Is the temple part of the face? He said: No. Zurarah said: I said to him: What do you think about that which is surrounded by hair? He said: Everything surrounded by hair is not upon the servants to seek out or investigate, but water is to be made to flow over it.

Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: Follow the sequence in wudu (ablution) as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: begin with the face, then the hands, then wipe the head and the feet. Do not put anything before another in a way that opposes what you have been commanded. So if you washed the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat on the forearm. And if you wiped the foot before the head, then wipe over the head and then repeat on the foot. Begin with what Allah began with.

And it has been narrated in another hadith: "Regarding one who begins by washing his left before his right, he repeats over his right, then repeats over his left." And it has also been narrated: "that he repeats over his left."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Wash your hand after urine once, after defecation twice, and after janabah (ritual impurity) three times."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Wash your hand once after sleep."

The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, wiping the outer part of his feet, I would have thought that their inner part was more deserving of wiping than their outer part."
And it has been narrated, concerning bandages, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "He washes what is around it."
And the Scholar, peace be upon him, said: "There are three matters in which I do not practice taqiyyah with anyone: drinking intoxicants, wiping over the khuffs, and Hajj al-Tamattu'."

ʿAʾishah narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that he said: "The people with the greatest regret on the Day of Resurrection are those who see their wudu (ablution) on the skin of someone else."
And it was narrated from her that she said: "For me to wipe over the back of a donkey in the wilderness is dearer to me than to wipe over my khuff."
Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man whose khuff is torn, so he inserts his hand and wipes the top of his feet: would that suffice him? So he said: “Yes.”

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man whose hand had been cut off from the elbow: how should he perform wudu (ablution)? He said: "He washes what remains of his upper arm." And likewise it was narrated regarding the cutting of the leg. And when a woman performs wudu (ablution), she removes her head covering from the place of wiping her head in the Fajr and Maghrib prayers and wipes over it, and in the rest of the prayers it suffices her to insert her finger and wipe over her head without removing her head covering.

And al-Riḍā عليه السلام said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed for the people in wudu (ablution) that the woman should begin with the inner part of her forearm, and the man with the outer part of the forearm."

And it is narrated: Whoever performs wudu (ablution) and mentions the name of Allah, his entire body becomes pure, and the wudu from one wudu to the next is an expiation for the sins between them. And whoever does not mention [the name of Allah] will not become pure from his body except that which the water touches.

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said: Whoever performs wudu (ablution) for the Maghrib prayer, that wudu (ablution) is an atonement for what has passed of his sins during his day, apart from the major sins. And whoever performs wudu (ablution) for the morning prayer, that wudu (ablution) is an atonement for what has passed of his sins during his night, except the major sins.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Open your eyes during wudu (ablution), so that they may not see the fire of Hell."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Whoever performs wudu (ablution) and wipes himself will have one good deed written for him; and whoever performs wudu (ablution) and does not wipe himself until his wudu (ablution) dries, Allah will write thirty good deeds for him.

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: When a man performs wudu (ablution), let him splash his face with water, for if he is drowsy, he will be stirred and awaken; and if there is cold, he will be stirred and not feel the cold.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "And if you forget until you stand in salat (prayer), then I do not command you to repeat it."

108 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Jibrīl, peace be upon him, continued to counsel me regarding the siwak until I feared that I might wear down [my teeth] or make them fall out. And he continued to counsel me regarding the neighbor until I thought that he would make him an heir. And he continued to counsel me regarding the owned servant until I thought that he would set for him a fixed term in which he would be freed.” And in another report: “And he continued to counsel me regarding the woman until I thought that her divorce should not be appropriate.”
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Jibril, peace be upon him, brought down the siwak, cupping, and khilal.
Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Consuming al-ushnan melts the body, rubbing oneself with pottery wears out the body, and using the siwak in the toilet causes bad breath."
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Four things are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the messengers: applying fragrance, the siwak (toothstick), women, and henna."
And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, your mouths are the pathways of the Qur'an, so purify them with the siwak."
And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said in his وصيّة to ʿAlī عليه السلام: "O ʿAlī, hold fast to the siwak at the wudu (ablution) of every salat (prayer)."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Siwak is half of wudu (ablution)."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: When the people entered the religion in crowds, the Azd came to them as the softest of them in hearts and the sweetest of them in mouths. So it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, this being the softest of them in hearts we have understood, but why did it become the sweetest of them in mouths?' He said, 'They used to use the siwak in the Age of Ignorance.'
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Everything has a means of purification, and the purification of the mouth is the siwak."
Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used the siwak frequently, but it is not obligatory, so it does not harm you to leave it for several days.”
Al-Baqir and Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Two rak'ahs of salat performed with siwak are better than seventy rak'ahs without siwak."
Abu Ja‘far al-Baqir (عليه السلام) said concerning the siwak: "Do not neglect it for three days; even if only by passing it once."
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Apply kohl in an odd number of strokes and use the siwak across the width of the mouth."
Al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) left off the siwak two years before he was taken, and that was because his teeth had become weak.

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who cleans his teeth once with his hand when he rises for Salat al-Layl, while he is able to use the siwak. So he said: "If he fears the coming of dawn, there is no harm in it."

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Were it not that I would cause hardship for my community, I would have commanded them to use the siwak at the wudu (ablution) of every salat (prayer)."
And it is narrated: "If the people knew what is in the siwak, they would surely keep it with them in their bedding."

And it has been narrated: "The Ka'bah complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about what it suffered from the breaths of the polytheists. So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed to it: 'Be at ease, O Ka'bah, for I shall replace them with a people who cleanse themselves with the branches of trees.' Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent His Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Trustworthy Spirit, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, descended upon him with the siwak.

126 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “There are twelve qualities in the siwak: it is from the sunnah (prophetic tradition), a purifier for the mouth, a polish for the sight, it pleases the All-Merciful, whitens the teeth, removes decay, strengthens the gums, stimulates appetite, removes phlegm, increases memory, multiplies good deeds, and the angels rejoice because of it.”

127 - A group of the Jews came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, and asked him about matters. Among what they asked him was: “Inform us, O Muhammad, for what reason are these four limbs washed in wudu (ablution), while they are the cleanest parts of the body?” The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “When Shaytan whispered to Adam, peace be upon him, he drew near to the tree and looked at it, so the water of his face departed. Then he stood and walked toward it, and that was the first foot that walked toward the sin. Then he took with his hand from it what was upon it and ate, so the ornaments and garments flew away from his body. Then Adam placed his hand upon the crown of his head and wept.” So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance, Allah made obligatory upon him and upon his descendants the purification of these four limbs. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the washing of the face because he had looked at the tree; He commanded him to wash the two hands up to the elbows because he had taken with them; He commanded him to wipe the head because he had placed his hand upon the crown of his head; and He commanded him to wipe the two feet because he had walked with them toward the sin.”

Abu al-Hasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān in what he wrote as a response to his questions: The reason for wudu (ablution), for the sake of which it became incumbent upon the servant to wash the face and the forearms, and to wipe the head and the feet, is his standing before Allah, the Exalted, and his facing Him with his outward limbs, and his encountering thereby the noble recording angels. So he washes the face for sajdah and humility; and he washes the hands so that he may turn them, seek with them, fear, and devote himself wholly; and he wipes the head and the feet because they are outward and uncovered, with which he faces all his states, and in them there is not the same degree of humility and devotion as there is in the face and the forearms.
Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, said: “There is no salat (prayer) except with taharah (purification).”

And it has been narrated: A man from among the scholars was made to sit in his grave, and it was said to him: “Indeed, we shall lash you with one hundred lashes from the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” He said: “I cannot bear it.” They kept pressing him until they reduced it to one. He said: “I cannot bear it.” They said: “There is no escape from it.” He said: “Then for what will you lash me?” They said: “We shall lash you because one day you performed salat without wudu (ablution), and you passed by a weak person and did not help him.” So they lashed him one lash from the punishment of Allah, the Exalted, and his grave was filled with fire.

131 - And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Eight people are such that Allah does not accept salat (prayer) from them: the runaway slave until he returns to his master; the recalcitrant wife toward her husband while he is displeased with her; the withholder of zakat; the Imam of a people who leads them in prayer while they dislike him; the one who abandons wudu (ablution); the mature woman who prays without a head covering; the zibbīn, who is the one resisting urine and feces; and the intoxicated person."

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Nine things have been lifted from my community: inadvertence, error, forgetfulness, what they are compelled to do, what they do not know, what they cannot bear, omens, envy, and reflecting upon whisperings concerning creation, so long as the human being does not utter it with a lip.”

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far عليه السلام was asked about a man for whom, when he performs wudu (ablution), a spot remains on his face that the water did not reach, so he said: "It suffices him to moisten it from some part of his body."

134 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "If you forget to wipe your head, then wipe it and your feet with the remaining moisture from your wudu (ablution). If there is nothing left in your hand of the moisture of your wudu (ablution), then take from what remains of it in your beard and wipe your head and your feet with it. If you do not have a beard, then take from your eyebrows and the lashes of your eyes and wipe your head and your feet with it. And if nothing remains of the moisture of your wudu (ablution), you repeat the wudu (ablution)."

And Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who forgot to wipe his head, he said: “Then let him wipe.” He said: He did not remember it until he entered into the salat (prayer). He said: “Then let him wipe his head with the moisture of his beard.”

Hadith 136 — And in the narration of Zayd al-Shahham and al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who performed wudu (ablution) and then forgot to wipe over his head until he had stood in salat (prayer), he said: “Then let him leave, wipe his head, and repeat the prayer.”

Zurarah ibn A'yan asked Abā Ja'far and Abā 'Abdillāh, peace be upon them, about what nullifies wudu (ablution), so they said: Whatever exits from your two lower openings, the front and the back, of excrement, urine, semen, or wind, and sleep until it takes away the intellect.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "There is no wudu (ablution) required due to taenia worms and small worms; rather, they are like lice." And this is when there is no excrement in it; but if there is excrement in it, then istinja' (cleansing of the private parts) and wudu (ablution) are required.

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: I feel wind in my stomach until I think that it has come out. So he said: “There is no wudu (ablution) upon you until you hear the sound or perceive the wind.” Then he said: “Indeed, Iblis sits between the buttocks of a man and causes an occurrence so as to make him doubt.”

Zurarah asked Abā Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, about a man who trims his nails, clips his mustache, and takes from the hair of his beard and his head: does that nullify the wudu (ablution)? So he said: O Zurarah, all of this is sunnah (recommended practice), and wudu (ablution) is an obligation. Nothing from the sunnah invalidates the obligation, and indeed that increases it in purification.
Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who takes from his nails and his mustache: should he wipe it with water? He said: “No, he is pure.”
He was asked about reciting poetry—does it nullify wudu (ablution)? So he said: No.
Sama‘ah ibn Mihrān asked him: About a man whose head nods off while he is in salat (prayer), standing or bowing, he said: “There is no wudu (ablution) upon him.”

Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who falls asleep while sitting: is wudu (ablution) required of him? He said: “No wudu (ablution) is required of him so long as he remains seated and does not slump apart.”
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: There is no wudu (ablution) in kissing, intimate contact, nor touching the private part.

146 - Hariz narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “If a man has urine or blood dripping from him, then when the time of salat (prayer) comes, he should take a pouch and place cotton in it, then attach it to himself and put his private part into it. Then he should pray, combining the two prayers, al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr: he delays al-Ẓuhr and brings al-ʿAṣr forward, with one adhan and two iqamahs; and he delays al-Maghrib and brings al-ʿIshāʾ forward, with one adhan and two iqamahs; and he does that in the morning prayer.”
