ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinated, then performed wudu (ablution), and stood for salat (prayer), then found wetness. He said: “There is nothing upon him, and he does not perform wudu (ablution) again.”

148 - And another narrated: concerning the man who urinates, then performs istinjāʾ, then afterward sees moisture: “If, when he urinates, he presses what is between the anus and the testicles three times, and massages what is between them, then performs istinjāʾ, then if that flows until it reaches the thighs, he need not worry.”
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام did not consider madhy to require wudu (ablution), nor washing of whatever of it affected the garment.
And it has been narrated: “Indeed, al-madhy and al-wadhy are like saliva and mucus, so neither the garment nor the urethral outlet is washed because of them.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who wears a garment in which there is janābah, then he sweats in it, so he said: “Indeed, the garment does not render the man junub.”
And in another report: A garment does not make a man junub, nor does a man make a garment junub.
Zayd al-Shahham asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a garment in which there is janābah, and the sky rains on me until it becomes wet upon me, so he said: “There is no harm in it.”
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to one of his wives: “Hand me the khumrah.” So she said to him, “I am menstruating.” He said to her, “Is your menstruation in your hand?”

Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became junub in his garment and had no garment with him other than it. He said: “He prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it.”
And in another narration: “And he repeated the prayer.”

It has been narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام that he said: The milk of the baby girl and her urine must be washed from the garment before she eats, because her milk comes out from her mother's bladder. And the milk of the baby boy is not washed from the garment before he eats, nor is his urine, because the milk of the baby boy comes out from the shoulders and the upper arms.

Ḥakam ibn Ḥukaym, the son of Khallād’s brother, asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and said: I urinate and do not find water, and some urine gets on my hand. So I wipe it on the wall and on the dust. Then my hand sweats, and I touch my face, or some of my body, or it reaches my clothing. So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

And Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام: about a rug and a mattress that are affected by urine—what should be done when it is thick and heavily padded So he said: 'What appears on its surface should be washed.'

Ḥanān ibn Sadīr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: Sometimes I urinate and cannot find water, and that becomes difficult for me. He said: If you urinate and wipe yourself, then wipe your private part with your saliva. If you find anything, then say: This is from that.
And he, peace be upon him, was asked about a woman who has only one shirt, and she has a child who urinates on her: what should she do? He said: 'She should wash the shirt once during the day.'

Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I come out from the place of relieving myself and perform istinjāʾ with water, then my garment falls into that water with which I performed istinjāʾ. So he said: “There is no harm in it, and there is nothing upon you.”

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said regarding the mud of rain: There is no harm in it touching the garment for three days, unless one knows that something has made it impure after the rain. Then if it touches it after three days, he should wash it; but if it is a clean path, he should not wash it.

Abu al-Aʿazz al-Nakhkhas asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, saying: I tend to the animals, and sometimes I go out at night when they have urinated and defecated, and one of them strikes with its hand or with its leg, so it splashes onto my garment. So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Ridha عليه السلام was asked about a man who steps in the bathhouse while there are cracks in his feet, then steps on urine and lime, and a black trace from the filth he stepped on enters the cracks. He has washed it, so what should he do regarding it and regarding the foot with which he stepped on it? Is washing sufficient for him, or should he clean between [his nails] with his nails? And he cleans himself and then notices an odor from his nails while seeing nothing. So he said: “There is nothing upon him because of the odor or the cracks after washing it.”
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "I do not concern myself with whether urine or water has touched me if I am unaware of it."

And it has been narrated: Concerning semen: if a man is junub and, when he rises, he looks and checks but finds nothing, then there is nothing upon him. But if he did not look and did not check, then he must wash it and repeat his salat (prayer).

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a eunuch who urinates, then encounters difficulty because of that, and sees wetness after wetness. He said: 'He should perform wudu (ablution), then sprinkle his garment once during the day.'

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, about a man whose garment fell upon a dead dog. He said: He should sprinkle it with water and pray in it, and there is no harm.

A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the most learned among them asked him about some questions. Among what he asked was that he said: “For what reason did Allah, Exalted is He, command washing from janabah, and not command ghusl from feces and urine?” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, when Adam ate from the tree, that spread through his veins, his hair, and his skin. Then when a man has intercourse with his wife, the fluid comes out from every vein and hair in his body. Therefore Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made ghusl from janabah obligatory upon his progeny until the Day of Resurrection.” “And urine comes out from the excess of the drink that a human being drinks, and feces comes out from the excess of the food that a human being eats, so because of that wudu (ablution) is upon him.” The Jew said: “You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad.”

171 - Al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān regarding what he wrote in reply to his questions: “The reason for the ghusl (ritual bath) of janābah is cleanliness: to purify the human being from what has affected him of harm, and to purify the rest of his body, because janābah comes forth from the whole body. Therefore, it is obligatory upon him to purify his whole body. And the reason for the easing in the case of urine and feces is that they are more frequent and more continuous than janābah, so concession was given in them with wudu (ablution) because of their frequency, their hardship, and their occurrence without intention from him and without desire. Janābah only occurs through enjoyment from themselves and compelling themselves.”

Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir عليه السلام said: “Ghusl (ritual bath) is in seventeen occasions: the night of the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan, the night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third, in which Laylat al-Qadr is hoped for; the ghusl of the two Eids; when you enter the two sanctuaries; the day you enter into ihram; the day of visitation; the day you enter the House; the day of Tarwiyah; the day of ʿArafah; when you have washed a deceased person and shrouded him, or touched him after he has become cool; the day of al-Jumuʿah; and the ghusl of the eclipse, when the whole disc is obscured and you awaken and have not performed the salat (prayer), then you must perform ghusl and make up the salat (prayer). And the ghusl of janabah is obligatory.”
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: The ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah and menstruation is one and the same.
And it is narrated: "Whoever kills a gecko must perform ghusl (ritual bathing)."
And it is narrated: “Whoever deliberately goes to a crucified person and looks at him, ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory upon him as a punishment.”

Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ghusl of Friday, so he said: “It is obligatory in travel and residence, except that women have been given concession during travel due to scarcity of water. The ghusl of janābah is obligatory, and the ghusl of menstruation is obligatory, and the ghusl of the mustaḥāḍah is obligatory. If she inserts cotton and the blood passes beyond the cotton, then ghusl is upon her for every two prayers, and for Fajr there is a ghusl. But if the blood does not pass beyond the cotton, then wudu (ablution) is upon her for every salat (prayer). The ghusl of the woman in nifās is obligatory, and the ghusl of the newborn is obligatory, and the ghusl of the dead is obligatory, and the ghusl of one who has washed a dead person is obligatory, and the ghusl of the muḥrim is obligatory, and the ghusl of the day of ʿArafah is obligatory, and the ghusl of ziyārah is obligatory except for one who has an illness. And the ghusl for entering the House is obligatory, and the ghusl for entering the Ḥaram is obligatory, and it is recommended that a man not enter it except with ghusl. And the ghusl of mubāhalah is obligatory, and the ghusl of istisqāʾ is obligatory. And the ghusl of the first night of the month of Ramaḍān is recommended, and the ghusl of the night of the twenty-first is sunnah (prophetic tradition), and the ghusl of the night of the twenty-third—do not leave it, for it is hoped that Laylat al-Qadr is in one of those two nights. And the ghusl of the day of al-Fiṭr and the ghusl of the day of al-Aḍḥā—I do not like that they be left. And the ghusl of istikhārah is recommended.”

The virtuous Shaykh and jurist, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī, the author of this book, may the mercy of Allah be upon him, said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: And We sent down from the sky pure water. And He, Mighty and Majestic, says: And We sent down from the sky water in due measure, then We lodged it in the earth, and indeed We are surely able to take it away. And He, Mighty and Majestic, says: And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you with it. So the origin of all water is from the sky, and all of it is purifying; the water of the sea is purifying, and the water of the well is purifying.
And al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: "All water is pure except that which you know to be impure."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Water purifies, and it is not purified."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "If the water is the amount of two qullas, nothing can make it impure, and the two qullas are two jars."

Hishām ibn Sālim asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: About a roof upon which urine is passed, then the rain falls upon it so it drips and reaches the garment. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it so long as what reaches it from the water is more than it.”
He (عليه السلام) was asked about the mud of rain that gets on the garment, in which there is urine, feces, and blood. So he said: “Rain-soaked mud does not cause impurity.”

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام: About a house whose roof is urinated upon and where ghusl from janābah is performed, then rain falls upon it: may water be taken from it and used for wudu for salat? So he said: “If it flows, there is no harm in it.”

And he asked him about a man who passes through rainwater into which wine has been poured, and it splashes onto his garment: may he pray in it before washing it? So he said: He does not wash his garment nor his foot, and he prays in it, and there is no harm in it.
And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about vomit that gets on the garment and is not washed, so he said: There is no harm in it.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Everything that chews the cud—its leftover water is halal (permissible), and its saliva is halal (permissible)."

The people of the desert came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, these reservoirs of ours are frequented by wild animals, dogs, and livestock.” So he صلى الله عليه وآله said to them: "What they have taken with their mouths is for them, and the rest of that is for you." If a beast, donkey, mule, sheep, cow, or camel drinks from the water, there is no harm in using it and performing wudu (ablution) from it. If a lizard falls into a vessel containing water, that water is to be poured out. If a dog licks it or drinks from it, the water is to be poured out, and the vessel washed three times: once with earth and twice with water, then it is dried. As for stagnant altered water, it is necessary to avoid it unless no other water is available. There is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) with water from which a cat drinks, and there is no harm in drinking it.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "I do not refrain from food that a cat has eaten from, nor from drink that it has drunk from."
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Regarding water in which beasts urinate, dogs lap, and the junub performs ghusl: “Indeed, if it is the measure of a kurr, nothing makes it impure.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The Children of Israel, when a drop of urine would touch one of them, would cut their flesh with scissors. But Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has granted you expansive ease, wider than what is between the heaven and the earth, and has made water purifying for you. So observe how you conduct yourselves.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about the skin of a pig being made into a bucket by which water is drawn, so he said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the skins of dead animals in which milk, water, and clarified butter are placed: what is your view regarding it? So he said: “There is no harm in putting in them whatever you wish of water, milk, or clarified butter, and performing wudu (ablution) from it, and drinking; but do not pray in them.”

And ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked: “Is it more beloved to you that wudu (ablution) be performed from the leftover water of a group of Muslims, or that wudu (ablution) be performed from a covered white vessel?” So he said: “No; rather, from the leftover water of the group of Muslims, for indeed the most beloved of your religion to Allah is the upright, tolerant, easy path.”
Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja‘far عليه السلام was asked about collected water in the bathhouse from the washings of people, some of which may get onto a garment. So he said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about water from which a chicken had drunk, so he said: If there is filth on its beak, wudu (ablution) is not to be performed with it, and do not drink. But if no filth is known to be on its beak, then perform wudu (ablution) with it and drink.
And al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon him, said: "The fire consumed what was in it."

Al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon him, was asked about a well from which water was drawn, then wudu (ablution) was performed with it, clothes were washed with it, and dough was kneaded with it; then it was learned that there had been a dead animal in it. So he said: “There is no harm, and the garment is not to be washed because of it, nor is the salat (prayer) to be repeated because of it.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about stagnant water in which there is a carcass. He said: “Wudu (ablution) is performed from the other side, and wudu (ablution) is not performed from the side of the carcass.”

He, peace be upon him, was asked about a pond in which there is a carcass. So he said: "If the water overpowers it, such that no odor is found from it, then perform wudu (ablution) and ghusl with it."
Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, said: "A well from which water is used for ghusl (ritual washing) and wudu (ablution) is not disliked, whether it is near or far, so long as the water has not changed."

And it was narrated from Abū Baṣīr that he said: We stayed in a house in which there was a well, and beside it was a drain, with only about two arm-lengths between them. They refrained from performing wudu (ablution) from it, and that caused them hardship. So we entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and informed him, and he said: “Perform wudu (ablution) from it, for that drain has channels that empty into a valley, which flows into the sea.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, it is from the heat of Hell."

ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who finds a mouse in his vessel after he had performed wudu (ablution) from that vessel several times, or performed ghusl from it, or washed his clothes with it, while the mouse had already become decomposed. He said: “If he had seen it in the vessel before performing ghusl, or wudu (ablution), or washing his clothes, and then did that after he had seen it in the vessel, then he must wash his clothes, wash everything that was touched by that water, and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer).” And if he only saw it after he had finished that and doing it, then he should not use any of the water, and there is nothing upon him, because he does not know when it fell into it.” Then he said: “Perhaps it only fell into it at that very hour in which he saw it.”

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام. About a man in janabah: would it suffice him for ghusl al-janabah to stand in the rain until his head and body are washed, while he has access to water other than that? So he said: If it washes him in the manner of his washing with water, that suffices for him.

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say: There is no harm in the leftover water of a mouse when it has drunk from the vessel, that you drink from it or perform wudu (ablution) from it.

ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام. About a man who slaughtered a sheep, and it convulsed and fell into a well of water while its veins were gushing blood: may wudu (ablution) be performed from that well? He said: "Between thirty and forty buckets should be drawn from it, then wudu (ablution) may be performed from it."

Ya'qub ibn 'Uthaym asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: A well of water has an odor in its water, and pieces of skin come out of it. He said: “It is nothing, because the lizard may sometimes cast off its skin. For that, one bucket is sufficient for you.”
Jābir ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a gecko falling into a well. So he عليه السلام said: “It is nothing; stir the water with the bucket.”

Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUthaym asked him about a gecko that we found in the well, having decomposed. So he said: "You only need to draw seven buckets from it." He said to him: "Then our clothes in which we prayed—should we wash them and repeat the salat (prayer)?" He said: "No."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “There was in al-Madinah a well in the middle of a garbage dump. The wind would blow and cast filth into it, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) from it.”
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the well. in which a dead animal falls, and he said: “If it has an odor, twenty buckets should be drawn from it.”

Kurdawayh al-Hamdani asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام. About a well into which water from the road enters, containing urine, feces, the urine of beasts, their dung, and dog excrement. So he said: “Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it, and if it is foul-smelling.”

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his letter to me: When you intend to perform ghusl for janabah, strive to urinate so that whatever remains of semen in your urethra comes out. Then wash your hands three times before putting them into the vessel, even if there is no filth on them. If you put them into the vessel while filth is on them, then pour out that water. If there is no filth on them, there is no harm. If semen has touched your body, then wash it from your body. Then perform istinja', wash, and cleanse your private part; then place three handfuls of water on your head and separate the hair with your fingertips until the water reaches the roots of all the hair. Take the vessel in your hand and pour it over your head and body twice, and pass your hand over your entire body. Work your fingers into your ears, and whatever the water reaches has become purified. So make sure that not a single hair of your head or beard remains except that water enters beneath it. Whoever deliberately leaves a hair unwashed in ghusl from janabah is in the Fire. Whoever leaves urination after janabah, or fears that the remainder of the fluid may circulate in his body, it may cause him a disease for which there is no cure. Whoever wishes to rinse the mouth and draw water into the nose during ghusl for janabah may do so, and that is not obligatory, because ghusl pertains to what is outward, not to what is inward. However, if a man wants to eat or drink before ghusl, it is not allowed for him unless he washes his hands, rinses his mouth, and draws water into his nose; for if he eats or drinks before doing that, it is feared for him that he may suffer from leprosy.
And it is narrated: Eating while in a state of janabah leads to poverty.
Ubaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man: is it proper for him to sleep while he is junub? He said: “That is disliked until he performs wudu (ablution).”
And in another hadith, he said: "I sleep in that state until morning, and that is because I intend to return."
And he said, from his father, peace be upon him: If a man is in a state of janabah, he should not eat or drink until he performs wudu (ablution).
And he said: “Indeed, I dislike janabah (ritual impurity) when the sun turns yellow and when it rises while it is yellow.”

183 - Al-Ḥalabī said: And I asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bathing) without a waist-covering where no one sees him. He said: “There is no harm in it.” 183 - And he said, and he was asked: About a man who has intercourse with a woman but does not ejaculate: is ghusl obligatory upon him? He said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “When the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, then ghusl has become obligatory.”
And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: "How can ghusl (ritual bath) not be obligatory when the hadd is applicable in it?" And he said: "The dowry and the ghusl become obligatory upon him."

And he was asked about a man who has contact with a woman in what is short of the private part: is ghusl required upon her if he ejaculates and she does not ejaculate? He said: “There is no ghusl upon her, and if he does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl upon him.”

And he was asked about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bath), then afterward finds some wetness, while he had urinated before performing ghusl. He said: He should perform wudu (ablution). But if he had not urinated before the ghusl, then he should repeat the ghusl.
And it was narrated in another hadith: If he has seen wetness and had not urinated, then let him perform wudu (ablution) and not ghusl, for that is only from the residual moisture.

He was asked about a man who sleeps, then wakes up and touches his private part and sees some wetness, while he did not see anything in his dream: should he perform ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: 'No. Ghusl is only from the greater fluid.'

And concerning a woman who sees in a dream what a man sees, he said: “If she has a discharge, then ghusl (ritual bath) is upon her; and if she does not have a discharge, then there is no ghusl upon her.”

191 - Al-Ḥalabī said: And one who heard him narrated to me that he was saying: If the junub immerses himself in the water in a single immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl. Whoever becomes junub during a day or a night multiple times, one ghusl suffices him, unless he becomes junub after the ghusl or has a wet dream. If he has a wet dream, then he should not have intercourse until he performs ghusl from the wet dream. There is no harm in the junub reciting the whole Qur'an except the passages of obligation of prostration in which one prostrates, and they are the sajdah of Luqmān, Ḥā-Mīm al-Sajdah, al-Najm, and Sūrat Iqraʾ bi-smi Rabbika. Whoever is junub or without wudu should not touch the Qur'an, though it is permissible for him to touch the paper or for another person to turn the pages for him, while he reads and remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is not permissible for the menstruating woman and the junub to enter the mosque except while passing through, and they may take something from it, but they may not place anything in it, because what is in it they cannot take from elsewhere, while they are able to place what is with them elsewhere. If a woman intends to perform ghusl from janabah and menstruation comes upon her, then she should leave the ghusl until she becomes pure. When she becomes pure, she performs one ghusl for janabah and menstruation. There is no harm in the junub applying dye, becoming junub while dyed, undergoing cupping, remembering Allah, Exalted is He, using depilatory treatment, slaughtering, wearing a ring, sleeping in the mosque and passing through it, or becoming junub at the beginning of the night and sleeping until its end. Whoever becomes junub in a land and finds no water except frozen water and cannot reach the earth, then let him pray with wiping, then let him not return to the land in which he imperils his religion. And my father, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his epistle to me: There is no harm in dividing the ghusl. You wash your hands, your private part, and your head, and delay washing your body until the time of salat, then wash your body when you wish to do so. If you incur a state of hadath from urination, defecation, or wind after washing your head and before washing your body, then repeat the ghusl from its beginning. If you begin with washing your body before the head, then repeat the ghusl over

When a woman gives birth, she refrains from salat (prayer) for ten days, unless she becomes pure before that. If the blood continues with her, she leaves salat (prayer) for up to eighteen days. Because Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays had postnatal bleeding with Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her to refrain for eighteen days.

Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who purchased a female slave, and she remained with him for months without menstruating, and this was not due to old age, and women stated that she was not pregnant. He asked: is it permissible that she be approached in the private part? So he said: “Menstruation may be held back by wind without pregnancy, so there is no harm in touching her in the private part.”
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “The first blood that fell upon the face of the earth was the blood of Hawwa' when she menstruated.”

Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: 'Indeed, menstruation for women is an impurity with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicted them. In the time of Nuh عليه السلام, women used to menstruate only once in the year, until some women came out from their dwellings, and they were seven hundred women. They went out, wore safflower-dyed garments, adorned themselves, and applied perfume. Then they went out and spread through the lands, sat with men, attended the festivals with them, and sat in their rows. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicted them at that point with menstruation every month—meaning those very women specifically. Their blood flowed, and they were removed from among the men. Thus they menstruated once every month, and Allah, Exalted is He, occupied them with menstruation and diminished their desire.' He said: 'As for other women, those who had not done what they had done, they would menstruate once every year.' He said: 'Then the sons of those who menstruated every month married the daughters of those who menstruated once every year, and the people became intermixed. Then the daughters of these and those menstruated once every month. So the children of those who menstruated once every [month] became many due to the regularity of menstruation, while the children of those who menstruated once every year were few due to the فساد of the blood.' He said: 'So the offspring of these increased, while the offspring of those decreased.'

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Indeed, Fāṭimah, may the blessings of Allah be upon her, is not like any one of you. She does not see blood in menstruation nor in postnatal bleeding, like a heavenly maiden.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "They will have therein purified spouses." He said: "The purified spouses are those who do not menstruate and do not experience postnatal bleeding."

And it is narrated: Regarding a woman who sees yellowish discharge: if that is two days before menstruation, then it is part of menstruation; and if it is two days after menstruation, then it is not part of menstruation.

Salman al-Farisi, may Allah have mercy on him, asked Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام about the sustenance of the child in its mother's womb. So he said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has withheld the menstrual blood for it and made it its sustenance in its mother's womb.'
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “When a woman reaches fifty years of age, she does not see menstrual blood, unless she is a woman from Quraysh.”
And it is narrated: If he has intercourse with her while she is menstruating, he should give charity to a needy person in an amount equal to that person's fill.

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whoever has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, and the child comes out afflicted with leprosy or vitiligo, then he should blame none but himself.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about those who are deformed in their creation. He said: “They are those whose fathers come to their wives during menstruation.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “No one harbors hatred toward us except one whose birth was impure or whose mother conceived him while she was menstruating.”

ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the menstruating woman, what is permissible for her husband from her. He said: “She should wrap herself with an izār down to the knees and leave her navel uncovered; then for him is what is above the izār.”

And he mentioned from his father, peace be upon him, That Maymūnah used to say: Indeed, the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, would instruct me, when I was menstruating, to wrap myself with a cloth, then lie down with him in bed.

206 – He said: “The wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله did not make up the salat when they menstruated. However, when the time of salat entered, they would use cotton, perform wudu (ablution), then sit near the mosque and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Regarding a woman who claimed that she menstruated three menstrual cycles in one month: women from her close circle should be asked whether her menstruation in the past was according to what she claimed. If they testify, she is to be believed; otherwise, she is lying.

And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a menstruating woman who performs ghusl while saffron remains on her body and the water does not remove it. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.” And about a woman who performs ghusl after combing with hair extensions, and she does not undo her hair: how much water is sufficient for her? He عليه السلام said: “The amount that her hair absorbs; and that is three handfuls over her head, two handfuls on the right, and two handfuls on the left. Then she passes her hand over all of her body.”
Some of the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to comb her hair and wash her head while she was menstruating.

And it has been narrated: The limit for the postnatal period of refraining from salat (prayer) became eighteen days, because the minimum of menstruation is three days, its maximum is ten days, and its middle is five days. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made for the postnatal woman the days of the minimum of menstruation, its middle, and its maximum.

211 - And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who is afflicted by labor pains for a day, or two days, or more than that, and she sees yellowish discharge or blood: what should she do regarding salat (prayer)? He said: “She performs salat (prayer) so long as she has not given birth; then if the pain overcomes her, she performs salat (prayer) when she recovers.”

Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said: And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from relieving himself, or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favour upon you so that you may be grateful.

212 - And Zurarah said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “Will you not inform me from where you knew and said that wiping is on part of the head and part of the two feet?” So he smiled and said: “O Zurarah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said it, and the Book from Allah was revealed with it, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:” “So wash your faces.” So we knew that the whole face should be washed. Then He said: “And your hands up to the elbows.” So He joined the two hands up to the elbows with the face, and we knew that they should be washed up to the elbows. Then He separated the speech and said: “And wipe your heads.” So we knew, when He said “with your heads,” that wiping is on part of the head because of the letter bāʾ. Then He joined the two feet to the head just as He had joined the two hands to the face, and He said: “And your feet up to the ankles.” So we knew, when He joined them to the head, that wiping is upon part of them. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم explained that to the people, but they neglected it. Then He said: “Then if you do not find water, perform tayammum with clean earth, and wipe your faces.” So when He lifted wudu from the one who did not find water, He established part of the washing as wiping, because He said, “with your faces.” Then He joined to it: “And your hands from it.” Meaning: from that tayammum, because He knew that all of that would not pass over the face, since some of that earth adheres to part of the palm and does not adhere to part of it. Then Allah said: “Allah does not intend to place upon you any hardship.” And hardship is constraint.

And Zurārah said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said one day to ʿAmmār during a journey of his: ‘O ʿAmmār, it has reached us that you became junub. So what did you do?’” He said: “I rolled in the dust, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” He said: So he said to him: “That is how a donkey rolls. Why did you not do like this instead?” Then he lowered his hands to the ground and placed them upon the earth, then wiped his forehead with his fingers and his two palms, one with the other, then he did not repeat that.

ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who becomes junub and does not find water, he said: "He performs tayammum with earth; then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and he does not repeat the salat (prayer)." And about a man who passes by a well while he does not have a bucket with him, he said: "It is not upon him to enter the well, because the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth; so let him perform tayammum." And about a man who becomes junub while he has with him only the amount of water sufficient for the wudu (ablution) of the salat (prayer): should he perform wudu with the water or perform tayammum? He said: "No; rather, he performs tayammum. Do you not see that only half of the wudu has been appointed upon him?"

Zurarah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim said: We said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, A man did not find water, and the time for salat arrived, so he performed tayammum and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he found water. Should he invalidate the two rakʿahs, or cut them off, perform wudu, and then pray? He said: “No. Rather, he continues in his salat and completes it, and he does not invalidate it on account of the presence of water, because he entered it while in a state of taharah through tayammum.” And Zurarah said: I said to him, He entered it while in tayammum, then prayed one rakʿah, then invalidated his wudu, and then found water. He said: “He goes out, performs wudu, then builds upon what has passed of his salat which he prayed with tayammum.”
And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about tayammum in place of wudu (ablution), and from janābah, and from menstruation for women—whether it is the same. So he said, “Yes.”
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who has sores and wounds and becomes junub, so he said: “There is no harm in his performing tayammum and not performing ghusl.”
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “The one suffering from an abdominal illness and the one with broken bones are to perform tayammum and are not to be given ghusl (ritual bathing).”

And it was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family: “O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so was afflicted with janabah while he had smallpox, so they washed him and he died.” So he said: “They killed him! Why did they not ask? Why did they not perform tayammum for him? Surely, the cure for ignorance is asking.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man afflicted with smallpox who was struck by janabah, and he said: “If he became junub himself, then let him perform ghusl, and if he had a nocturnal emission, then let him perform tayammum.”

And Mu'awiyyah ibn Maythara asked him about a man who is traveling and does not find water, so he performs tayammum and prays. Then he finds water while there is still some time remaining. Should he continue with his prayer or perform wudu and repeat the prayer? He said: 'He should continue with his prayer, for the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth.'

222 - Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined; I had marital relations without water.” He said: Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله ordered a litter-canopy, so we screened ourselves with it, and [he ordered] water, so I and she performed ghusl (ritual bath). Then he صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O Abā Dharr, clean earth is sufficient for you for ten years.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام: About three people who were traveling: one of them was junub, the second was dead, and the third was without wudu (ablution). The time of salat (prayer) arrived, and they had with them only enough water for one of them. Who should take the water, and what should they do? He said: 'The junub should perform ghusl (ritual bath), the deceased should be buried with tayammum, and the one who is without wudu (ablution) should perform tayammum, because ghusl from janabah is an obligation, washing the deceased is sunnah, and tayammum for the other is permissible.'

Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān al-Nahdī and Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About the Imam of a people who is afflicted with janābah during travel, and he does not have enough water with him for ghusl (ritual bath): should some of them perform wudu (ablution) and lead them in salat (prayer)? He عليه السلام said: 'No. Rather, the junub should perform tayammum and lead them in salat (prayer), for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made earth a purifier just as He has made water a purifier.'

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who is affected by janābah during a cold night and fears destruction for himself if he performs ghusl, so he said: "He performs tayammum and prays; then when he is safe from the cold, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: When the soul is taken, it hovers above the body—the soul of the believer and of other than him—looking at everything that is done with it. Then, when he is shrouded and placed upon the bier and carried on the shoulders of men, the soul returns to him and enters into him. Then his sight is extended for him, and he looks at his place in Paradise or from the Fire. So he calls out at the top of his voice: if he is among the people of Paradise, 'Hasten me, hasten me!' and if he is among the people of the Fire, 'Take me back, take me back!' And he knows everything that is done with him and hears the speech.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “There is no one whose death is more beloved to Iblis than the death of a faqih.”

And he, peace be upon him, was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no repealer of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning." So he said: "The loss of the scholars."

And he, peace be upon him, was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Did We not grant you life enough for whoever would remember therein to remember?" So he said: "It is a reproach for one who is eighteen years old."

He, peace be upon him, was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And there is no town but We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it." He said: "It is perishing through death."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “It is not for you to offer us condolences, while it is for us to offer you condolences. Rather, it is for you to congratulate us, because you share with us in the misfortune.”

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام was asked about a man who says to his son or daughter, “May my father and mother, or my parents, be for you.” Do you see any harm in that? He said: “If his parents are alive, then I regard that as disobedience toward them; and if they have died, then there is no harm.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Patience is of two kinds: patience at the time of calamity is good and beautiful, and better than that is patience regarding what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden to you, so that it becomes a barrier for you."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has graciously bestowed upon His servants three things: He cast upon them the wind after the spirit, and were it not for that, no dear one would bury a dear one; and He cast upon them solace after calamity, and were it not for that, offspring would be cut off; and He cast upon this grain the creeping creature, and were it not for that, their kings would hoard it just as they hoard gold and silver.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, we are a Household who grieve before the calamity; then, when the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends, we are content with His decree and submit to His command, and it is not for us to dislike what Allah has loved for us.
And he عليه السلام said: Whoever fears for himself from grief due to a calamity, then let him pour forth some of his tears, for it calms it from him.

And Ibn Abī Laylā said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “What thing is sweeter than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created?” So he said: “The young child.” He said: “What thing is more bitter than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created?” He said: “Losing him.” So he said: “I bear witness that you are the proofs of Allah over His creation.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no servant who passes his hand over the head of an orphan out of compassion for him except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants him a light for every hair on the Day of Judgment.
And it is reported: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, writes for him, for every hair over which his hand passes, one good deed.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever among you recognizes hardness in his heart, let him bring an orphan near and show him kindness, and let him wipe his head; his heart will soften by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the orphan has a right.” And it is narrated that he said: “He should seat him at his table and wipe his head; his heart will soften.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "When the orphan cries, the Throne trembles for him, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Who is this that has made My servant cry, the one from whom I took away his parents in his childhood? So by My might, My majesty, and My exaltedness in My station, no believing servant calms him except that I make Paradise obligatory for him."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever sends ahead children, counting them with Allah, they will shield him from the Fire by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, disliked six traits for me, and I disliked them for the awsiya' from my descendants and for their followers after me: frivolity in salat (prayer), indecent speech in sawm (fasting), reproach after charity, entering the mosques in a state of janabah, looking into houses, and laughing among the graves.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whatever is placed on the grave that is not from the soil of the grave itself is a burden upon the deceased."

And it is narrated that al-Sindī ibn Shāhak said to Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: I would like you to allow me to shroud you. So he said: “Indeed, we are a House whose first hajj, the dowries of our women, and our shrouds are from the pure part of our wealth.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, our enemies die by plague, while you die from ailments of the stomach. Verily, it is a sign among you, O assembly of the Shi'ah."
The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: "Whoever renovates a grave or fashions an image has indeed exited Islam."

And it was narrated from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about the deceased, whether his body decays, so he said: "Yes, until no flesh or bone remains except his clay from which he was created, for it does not decay. It remains in the grave, rounded, until he is created from it just as he was created the first time."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden our bones from the earth, and has forbidden worms from eating anything from our flesh.

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “My life is good for you, and my death is good for you.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, how is that?” So he, peace be upon him and his family, said: “As for my life, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And Allah would not punish them while you are among them.” “And as for my separation from you, your deeds are presented to me every day. So whatever is good, I ask Allah to increase it for you, and whatever is evil, I seek Allah’s forgiveness for you.” They said: “Even when you have decayed, O Messenger of Allah?”—meaning, when you have become dust. He said: “No. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden the earth to consume anything of our flesh.”

And it is reported: Indeed, the deeds of the servants are presented to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and to the Imams عليهم السلام every day, their righteous ones and their wicked ones. So beware. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And say: Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers." "

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the crucified one: does the punishment of the grave reach him? So he said: "Indeed, the Lord of the earth is the Lord of the air, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands the air, and it presses upon him more severely than the pressing of the grave."
And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “If you wash the head of the deceased and his beard with khitmi, there is no issue.”
And Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: "The ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of the person in janabah. If he has abundant hair, then pour the water over it three times."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: There is no issue in placing the deceased between your legs and standing over him to wash him. When you turn him to the right or left, hold him firmly with your legs so that he does not fall on his face.

And indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, walked behind the funeral of a man from the Ansar. Then it was said to him, "Will you not ride, O Messenger of Allah?" So he said, "Indeed, I dislike to ride while the angels are walking."

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said at the end of a hadith in which he mentions the ghusl of the deceased: "Beware of stuffing anything into his ears. If you fear that something may emerge from the nostrils, then there is no blame upon you to place cotton over it. But if you do not fear that, then do not place anything in it."
And he, peace be upon him, said at the end of a long hadith, in which he describes the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased: Do not interlace-clean his fingernails.

And he, peace be upon him, said: When one of you has a deceased person, then lay him down facing the qiblah, and likewise, when he is washed, the place of washing should be dug for him facing the qiblah.

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, the souls are in the form of bodies in a tree from Paradise, asking one another and recognizing one another. When a soul arrives upon the souls, they say: Leave it, for it has escaped from a tremendous terror. Then they ask it: What did so-and-so do, and what did so-and-so do? If it says to them: I left him alive, they hope for him; and if it says to them: He has perished, they say: He has fallen, he has fallen.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام: 'Bring out the bones of Yusuf عليه السلام from Egypt,' and He promised him the rising of the moon. But the moon's rising was delayed for him, so he asked about someone who knew its location. It was said to him: 'Here is an old woman who knows about it.' So he sent for her, and an elderly woman, crippled and blind, was brought. He said, 'Do you know the grave of Yusuf عليه السلام?' She said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then tell me its location.' She said, 'I will not do so until you give me certain things: free my legs, restore my sight to me, return my youth to me, and make me with you in Paradise.' That weighed heavily upon Musa, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'You are only giving on My behalf, so give her what she asked.' So he did, and she guided him to the grave of Yusuf عليه السلام. He brought him out from the bank of the Nile in a marble chest. Then when he brought him out, the moon rose, so he carried him to al-Sham. For that reason, the People of the Book carry their dead to al-Sham.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The greatest that a human being is, is on the day he is born, and the smallest that he is, is on the day he dies."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has not created a certainty in which there is no doubt that more closely resembles a doubt in which there is no certainty than death."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The first person for whom a bier was made was Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family."
Al-Ridha عليه السلام said: "Salat has four thousand gates."
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Salat (prayer) has four thousand limits."

36 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was the most cautious of people regarding urine, to the extent that when he intended to urinate, he would go to an elevated place of land or a place in which there was much soil, out of dislike that urine should splash onto him.”

37 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would, when he intended to enter the place of ablution, say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the vile, impure, evil, corrupting Satan, the accursed. O Allah, remove harm from me and grant me refuge from Satan, the accursed.” And when he had settled sitting for wudu (ablution), he would say: “O Allah, remove from me filth and harm, and make me among those who purify themselves.” And when he strained to relieve himself, he would say: “O Allah, just as You fed it to me wholesome in well-being, then bring it out from me foul in well-being.”

And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: There is no servant except that an angel is appointed over him, turning his neck so that he looks at his excrement. Then the angel says to him: O son of Adam, this is your provision, so look from where you took it and to what it has become. So it is fitting for the servant at that moment to say: O Allah, provide me with the halal and keep me away from the haram.

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he intended to relieve himself, would stand at the door of the place, then turn to his right and to his left toward his two angels and say: “Move away from me; for you two, by Allah, I am bound not to speak with my tongue anything until I come out to you.”

And he, peace be upon him, when he entered the place of relief, would say: “Praise be to Allah, the Preserver, the One who brings to fulfilment.” Then when he came out, he would wipe his abdomen and say: “Praise be to Allah, who removed from me its harm and left within me its strength. How great a blessing it is, one whose measure the capable cannot fully assess.”

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, when he entered the privy, would cover his head and say to himself: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and there is no god but Allah. My Lord, remove the harm from me freely without reckoning, and make me among those grateful to You for what You turn away from me of harm and distress, which, had You withheld it from me, I would have perished. To You belongs all praise. Protect me from the evil of what is in this place, bring me out of it safe, and place a barrier between me and obedience to the accursed Satan.

And I found, in the handwriting of Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, a hadith which he attributed to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, that he said: "Whoever has frequent forgetfulness in salat (prayer), let him say, when he enters the restroom: In the Name of Allah and by Allah; I seek refuge in Allah from the vile, impure, evil, defiling Shaytan, the accursed."

Abu Ja‘far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: When one of you uncovers himself for urination or for other than that, then let him say: 'In the name of Allah,' for indeed the Shaytan lowers his gaze away from him until he finishes.

A man said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, “Where should strangers relieve themselves?” So he said: “They should avoid the banks of rivers, through roads, beneath fruit-bearing trees, and places of cursing.” Then it was said to him, “And where are the places of cursing?” He said, “The doors of houses.” And in another report: “Allah has cursed the one who defecates in the shade of stopping places, the one who prevents access to frequented water, and the one who blocks the traveled road.”
And in another narration: "Do not face the crescent moon, nor turn your back to it."

Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام entered the restroom and found a morsel of bread in the filth. He took it, washed it, and handed it to a servant who was with him, saying: “Keep it with you so that I may eat it when I come out.” Then when he came out, عليه السلام said to the servant: “Where is the morsel?” He said: “I ate it, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.” So he said: “It has not settled in the stomach of anyone except that Paradise becomes obligatory for him. Go, for you are free, for I dislike employing a man from the people of Paradise.”
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم prohibited a man from casting his urine into the air from a rooftop or from an elevated thing.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Urinating while standing without a reason is from rudeness, and cleansing oneself with the right hand is from rudeness."
And it has indeed been narrated: "There is no harm if the left hand is incapacitated."

Hishām ibn Sālim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: May I perform ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and other reasons in the latrine in which urination takes place, while I am wearing Sindhī sandals, so I perform ghusl while the sandals remain on me as they are? He said: "If the water that flows from your body reaches the bottoms of your feet, then do not wash the bottoms of your feet."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man, when he wants to perform istinja', how he should sit. He said: “As he sits for relieving himself.”
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "When a man urinates, he should not touch his private part with his right hand."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Prolonged sitting in the place of relieving oneself causes hemorrhoids.

ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about tasbīḥ in the place of relieving oneself and about reciting the Qur'an. So he said: It has not been permitted in the lavatory to recite more than Āyat al-Kursī, or that one praise Allah, or the verse: “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

When Allah spoke intimately to Mūsā ibn ʿImrān [upon our Prophet and] upon him السلام, Mūsā said: “My Lord, are You far from me so that I should call upon You, or are You near so that I may converse with You?” So Allah, Majestic is His Glory, revealed to him: “I am the companion of the one who remembers Me.” Then Mūsā عليه السلام said: “My Lord, I am in circumstances in which I regard You too reverently to mention You in them.” He said: “O Mūsā, remember Me in every state.”

People used to perform istinja with stones, and a man from the Ansar ate some food, so his stomach became loose, and he performed istinja with water. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed concerning him: "Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves." So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله called him, and the man feared that something displeasing had been revealed about him. When he entered, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, "Have you done anything on this day of yours?" He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I ate some food, and my stomach became loose, so I performed istinja with water." So he said to him, "Rejoice, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has revealed concerning you: 'Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves.' So you were the first of the repentant and the first of those who purify themselves."
And al-Riḍā عليه السلام said: "In istinja, what appears on the anal area is washed, and the fingertip should not be inserted into it."
And it has been narrated: "Whoever speaks while at the place of relieving oneself, his need will not be fulfilled."

And indeed the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to some of his wives: "Tell the believing women to perform istinja with water and to be thorough, for it is a purification for the surrounding parts and a remover of hemorrhoids."

63 - What Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has angels whom He has entrusted with the vegetation of the earth, among the trees and the palm trees. There is no tree and no palm tree except that with it there is, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, an angel guarding it and what belongs to it. Were it not that with it there is one who protects it, the beasts and the creeping creatures of the earth would consume it when its fruit is in it.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, only forbade that any Muslim relieve himself beneath a tree or a palm tree that has borne fruit, because of the place of the angels entrusted with it. He said: And for that reason the trees and the palm trees are in a state of intimacy when their fruit is upon them, because the angels are present with them.

And it was narrated: That Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام used to awaken from his sleep, then perform wudu (ablution), and not perform istinjāʾ. And he said, as one expressing astonishment, about a man whom he named: “It has reached me that when wind comes out from him, he performs istinjāʾ.”

600 - Zurārah ibn Aʿyan said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Inform me about what Allah, Exalted is He, has made obligatory of the prayers. He said: “Five prayers in the night and the day.” I said to him: Did Allah name them and clarify them in His Book? So he said: “Yes. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: “Establish the salat from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night.” And its decline means its passing the zenith. So in what is between the sun’s decline and the darkness of the night are four prayers, which Allah named, clarified, and timed. And the darkness of the night is its midpoint. Then He said: “And the recitation of dawn; surely the recitation of dawn is witnessed.” So this is the fifth. And He said regarding that: “Establish the salat at the two ends of the day.” And its two ends are al-Maghrib and al-Ghadāt. “And near parts of the night.” And it is the salat of al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah. And He said: “Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer.” And it is the salat of al-Ẓuhr, and it is the first salat that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed. And it is between two daytime prayers: the salat of dawn and the salat of al-ʿAṣr.” And he said in some recitation: “ ‘Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer’ and the salat of al-ʿAṣr, ‘and stand before Allah devoutly,’ concerning the middle prayer.” And it was said: this verse was sent down on the day of al-Jumuʿah while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was on a journey, so he performed qunūt in it and left it as it was in travel and residence, and added two rakʿahs for the resident. The two rakʿahs which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله added on the day of al-Jumuʿah for the resident were only due to the place of the two sermons with the Imam. So whoever performs it on the day of al-Jumuʿah outside congregation, then let him perform it as four, like salat al-Ẓuhr on the rest of the days.
601 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, salat (prayer) has been decreed upon the believers as a timed prescription." He said: "Obligatory."

603 – And it is narrated from Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام that he said: I asked my father, Sayyid al-ʿĀbidīn عليه السلام, and said to him: O my father, inform me about our grandfather, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, when he was taken up to the heaven and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him with fifty prayers—how was it that he did not ask Him for a reduction on behalf of his Ummah until Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام said to him: Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your Ummah cannot bear that? He said: O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله does not make proposals to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor does he review with Him anything that He commands him. So when Mūsā عليه السلام asked him that, and became an intercessor to Him on behalf of his Ummah, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Mūsā عليه السلام. Thus he returned to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and asked Him for a reduction until He returned them to five prayers. He said: So I said to him: O my father, then why did he not return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and not ask Him for a reduction from five prayers, while Mūsā عليه السلام had asked him to return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for a reduction? He said: O my son, he عليه السلام intended to obtain lightening for his Ummah together with the reward of fifty prayers, due to the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten times its like." Do you not see that when he عليه السلام descended to the earth, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came down to him and said: O Muḥammad, indeed your Lord sends you salām and says to you: Indeed, they are five with fifty. "The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants." He said: So I said to him: O my father, is it not that Allah, majestic is His mention, is not described by place? He said: Yes, Allah is exalted above that in great exaltation. I said: Then what is the meaning of the statement of Mūsā عليه السلام to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, Return to your Lord? He said: Its meaning is the meaning of the statement of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me." And the meaning of the statement of Mūsā عليه السلام: "And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased." And the meaning of His saying, Mighty a
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day" then he should not spend the night except with witr.

And Zurārah ibn Aʿyan said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory upon the servants was ten rakʿahs, and in them is recitation, and there is no doubt in them, meaning forgetfulness. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله added seven, and in them there is forgetfulness, and in them there is no recitation. So whoever doubts in the first two must repeat until he preserves it and is upon certainty; and whoever doubts in the last two should act upon assumption.”

Zurarah and al-Fuḍayl said: We said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Have you considered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, salat (prayer) has been decreed upon the believers as a prescribed ordinance at appointed times." He said: "It means a prescribed obligation, and it does not mean the time of its lapse. If that time passed and then he performed it, it would not be a prayer performed on time. If that were so, then Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام would have perished when he performed it outside its time. Rather, whenever he remembered it, he performed it."

607 - It is narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, one day in the late afternoon, the horses were presented before Sulayman ibn Dawud عليه السلام, and he became occupied with looking at them until the sun disappeared behind the veil. So he said to the angels, 'Return the sun to me so that I may perform my salat (prayer) in its time,' and they returned it. Then he stood, wiped his legs and neck, and ordered his companions—those whose prayer had passed with him—to do the same. That was their wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer). Then he stood and prayed, and when he finished, the sun set and the stars appeared. That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We granted to Dawud Sulayman—an excellent servant; indeed, he was oft-returning. When the poised, swift horses were presented before him in the afternoon, he said: Indeed, I loved the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until it disappeared behind the veil. Return them to me. Then he began wiping their legs and necks.'

And it has been narrated: That Allah, Blessed and Exalted, returned the sun for Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn, the waṣī of Mūsā عليه السلام, so that he performed the salat (prayer) that had passed him by within its proper time.
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "In this Ummah, there will be everything that occurred in the Children of Israel, exactly alike, step by step and feather by feather."

It is narrated from Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays that she said: One day, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was asleep and his head was in the lap of ʿAlī عليه السلام, the ʿAsr prayer passed him by until the sun set. So he said: "O Allah, indeed ʿAlī was in obedience to You and obedience to Your Messenger, so return the sun for him." Asmāʾ said: "By Allah, I saw it set, then rise again after it had set, and no mountain or land remained except that it rose upon it, until ʿAlī عليه السلام stood, performed wudu (ablution), and prayed. Then it set again."

As for after the death of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then indeed: 611 - It was narrated from Juwayriyah ibn Mushir that he said: We came with Amir al-Mu'minin, Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, from the killing of the Khawarij, until when we had crossed into the land of Babil, the salat of al-'Asr became due. Then Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام dismounted, and the people dismounted. So Ali عليه السلام said: 'O people, this is a cursed land which has been punished in time three times.' And in another report: 'Twice, and it is expecting the third; and it is one of the overturned lands, and it is the first land in which an idol was worshipped, and it is not lawful for a prophet nor for the successor of a prophet to perform salat in it. So whoever among you wishes to perform salat, then let him perform salat.' Then the people moved to the sides of the road, praying, while he عليه السلام mounted the mule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and went on. Juwayriyah said: So I said, 'By Allah, I will surely follow Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and I will surely entrust my salat today to his lead.' So I went behind him, and by Allah, we had not crossed the bridge of Sura' until the sun had set, and I began to doubt. Then he turned to me and said: 'O Juwayriyah, did you doubt?' I said: 'Yes, O Amir al-Mu'minin.' So he عليه السلام dismounted to one side, performed wudu (ablution), then stood and uttered words that I could not make out, except that it was as though they were in Hebrew. Then he called the salat, and I looked, by Allah, at the sun, and it had come out from between two mountains, with a creaking sound. Then he performed the salat of al-'Asr, and I performed salat with him. So when we had finished our salat, the night returned as it had been. Then he turned to me and said: 'O Juwayriyah ibn Mushir, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great.' And I asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by His Great Name, so He returned the sun to me. And it was narrated: that when Juwayriyah saw that, he said: 'By the Lord of the Ka'bah, you are the successor of a prophet.'

Sulaymān ibn Khālid said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, inform me about the obligations that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed upon the servants—what are they?” He said: “Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, establishing the five salats (prayers), giving zakat, performing the hajj to the House, fasting the month of Ramaḍān, and the wilayah.” So whoever upholds them, acts correctly, keeps close to the right course, and avoids every evil shall enter Paradise.

The Commander of the Faithful, عليه السلام, used to say: Indeed, the best means by which those seeking nearness draw near are faith in Allah and His Messenger, jihad in the way of Allah, and the word of sincerity, for it is the fitrah; establishing salat, for it is the religion; giving zakat, for it is among the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; sawm, for it is a shield from His punishment; hajj of the House, for it drives away poverty and erases sin; maintaining kinship ties, for it brings increase in wealth and delay in lifespan; secret charity, for it extinguishes sin and extinguishes the wrath of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and acts of kindness, for they repel an evil death and protect from the falls of humiliation. Lo, be truthful, for Allah is with the truthful. Keep away from lying, for it keeps away from faith. Lo, the truthful one stands upon the edge of salvation and honor; lo, the liar stands upon the edge of disgrace and destruction. Lo, speak good so that you may be known by it, and act by it so that you may be among its people. Render the trust to the one who entrusted you, maintain ties with the relatives who cut you off, and return with فضل to the one who deprived you.

And it is narrated from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: "If you come having performed the five salat (prayers), you will not be questioned about any prayer; and if you come having observed the fast of the month of Ramaḍān, you will not be questioned about any fasting."

And it is narrated from 'A'idh al-Ahmasi that he said: I entered upon Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام while I intended to ask him about salat (prayer), but he began with me and said: "If you meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the five prayers, He will not ask you about anything besides them."

And it is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah that he said: Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام was asked: Why is it that you do not call the fornicator a disbeliever, while you call the one who abandons salat (prayer) a disbeliever? And what is the proof regarding that? So he said: Because the fornicator and those similar to him only do that because of desire, since it overcomes him. But the one who abandons salat (prayer) does not abandon it except out of belittlement toward it. That is because you do not find the fornicator approaching a woman except while taking pleasure in coming to her and intending her. And everyone who abandons salat (prayer), intending to abandon it, his purpose in abandoning it is not pleasure. So when pleasure is absent, belittlement occurs; and when belittlement occurs, kufr occurs.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever takes his salat (prayer) lightly is not of me; by Allah, he shall not come to me at the Hawdh. No, by Allah, whoever drinks an intoxicant is not of me; he shall not come to me at the Hawdh. No, by Allah."
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, our intercession will not reach one who takes salat (prayer) lightly."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever is overly cautious about his garment in his salat (prayer), then he has not clothed himself for Allah."

And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made salat (prayer) obligatory, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله established ten forms: the salat of travel, the salat of residence, the salat of fear in three forms, the salat for the eclipse of the sun and the moon, the salat of the two Eids, the salat of seeking rain, and the salat over the deceased.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Prostration upon the earth is an obligation, and upon other than the earth is a sunnah (recommended practice)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Salat (prayer) is a balance, so whoever fulfils it fully will receive in full."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is His service on the earth, and nothing from His service is equal to salat (prayer). For this reason, the angels called out to Zakariyya عليه السلام "while he was standing, performing salat (prayer) in the sanctuary."

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: There is no salat (prayer) whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before the people: 'O people, rise to the fires which you have kindled upon your backs, and extinguish them with your salat (prayer).'

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered the mosque while some of his companions were there, and he said: “Do you know what your Lord has said?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Indeed, your Lord says: These five obligatory prayers—whoever performs them at their appointed times and preserves them, he shall meet Me on the Day of Resurrection, and with Me he shall have a covenant by which I will admit him into Paradise. And whoever does not perform them at their appointed times and does not preserve them, then that is up to Me: if I will, I punish him, and if I will, I forgive him.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The first thing for which the servant will be held accountable is salat (prayer). If it is accepted, the rest of his deeds will be accepted from him; and if it is rejected against him, the rest of his deeds will be rejected against him.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, when the servant performs the salat (prayer) in its time and safeguards it, it rises white and pure, saying: You preserved me; may Allah preserve you. And when he does not perform it in its time and does not safeguard it, it rises black and dark, saying: You neglected me; may Allah neglect you.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “The closest that the servant is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is while he is in sajdah (prostration).”

And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: There is no servant from among our Shiʿah who stands for salat (prayer) except that angels, equal in number to those who oppose him, surround him, praying behind him and supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for him until he finishes his salat (prayer).

And it has been narrated from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him: "An obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj is better than a house filled with gold that is given in charity from it until it is exhausted."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Beware of laziness, for your Lord is Merciful and appreciates even a small deed. Indeed, a man may pray two rak'ahs seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Exalted is He, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of them. And indeed, he may give a dirham in voluntary charity, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it. And indeed, he may fast one day voluntarily, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Hope and fear do not come together in a heart except that Jannah becomes obligatory for it. So when you perform salat, turn your heart toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for there is no believing servant who turns his heart toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in his salat and his du'a, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns toward him the hearts of the believers, and supports him—along with their love for him—with Jannah."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "When the sun passes its zenith, the gates of the heaven and the gates of the Gardens are opened, and supplication is answered. So glad tidings to the one for whom a righteous deed is raised at that time."

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the best thing by which the servants draw near to their Lord, and which of that is most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So he said: "I do not know of anything after maʿrifah that is better than this salat (prayer). Do you not see that the righteous servant, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام, said: "And He has enjoined upon me salat (prayer)."
A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, and said: "Pray to Allah to admit me into Paradise." So he said to him: "Help me by increasing your prostration."
