Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: The one performing salat has three qualities: when he stands in his salat, the angels surround him from his feet to the heights of the sky, goodness scatters upon him from the heights of the sky to the parting of his head, and an angel appointed over him calls out: if the one performing salat knew whom he is intimately conversing with, he would not turn away.
And Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام said: "Salat (prayer) is the means of nearness for every pious person."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is salat (prayer), and it is the final counsel of the Prophets عليهم السلام. How excellent it is for a man to perform ghusl (ritual bath) or wudu (ablution), then complete the wudu thoroughly, then withdraw where no companion sees him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, looks upon him while he is bowing or prostrating. Indeed, when the servant prostrates and lengthens the sajdah, Iblis calls out: O woe to me! They obeyed Him while I disobeyed, and they prostrated while I refused.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The example of salat (prayer) is like the central pole of a tent: if the pole is firmly established, the ropes, pegs, and covering remain firm; and if the pole breaks, then neither a peg, nor a rope, nor a covering is of any use.

And he, peace be upon him, said: The example of salat among you is like that of a flowing stream—and it is a river—at the door of one of you; he goes out to it in the day and night and washes in it five times. So no filth remains with washing five times, and no sins remain with salat five times.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever has one salat (prayer) accepted by Allah will not be punished, and whoever has one good deed accepted by Allah will not be punished."

He عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say: Whoever restrains himself for an obligatory salat (prayer), waiting for its time, then performs it at the beginning of its time, completing its ruku' (bowing), its sujud (prostration), and its khushu' (humble attentiveness), then glorifies Allah, Mighty and Majestic, magnifies Him, and praises Him until the time of another salat (prayer) enters, and does not engage in idle speech between them, Allah will write for him the reward like that of the one performing hajj (pilgrimage) and the one performing 'umrah, and he will be among the people of 'Illiyyin.

643 - It is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said: A group of Jews came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and the most knowledgeable of them asked him about matters. Among what he asked was that he said: Inform me about Allah, Mighty and Majestic: for what reason did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, make these five salat (prayers) obligatory in five appointed times upon your Ummah during the hours of the night and the day? So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: Indeed, when the sun is at zenith, it has a ring into which it enters, and when it enters it, the sun declines. Then everything beneath the Throne glorifies with the praise of my Lord, majestic is His majesty. It is the hour in which my Lord, majestic is His majesty, sends blessings upon me. So Allah made the salat (prayer) obligatory upon me and upon my Ummah in it, and He said: Establish the salat (prayer) at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. And it is the hour in which Jahannam will be brought on the Day of Resurrection. So there is no believer who coincides with that hour while prostrating, bowing, or standing except that Allah will forbid his body to the Fire. As for Salat al-ʿAṣr, it is the hour in which Ādam عليه السلام ate from the tree, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought him out from al-Jannah. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded his progeny with this salat (prayer) until the Day of Resurrection, and chose it for my Ummah. So it is among the most beloved prayers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He instructed me to preserve it among the prayers. As for Salat al-Maghrib, it is the hour in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turned to Ādam عليه السلام in repentance. Between the time he ate from the tree and the time Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance were three hundred years from the days of the world, and in the days of the Hereafter one day is: Like a thousand years. From al-ʿAṣr to al-ʿIshāʾ. And Ādam عليه السلام prayed three rakʿahs: one rakʿah for his sin, one rakʿah for the sin of Ḥawwāʾ, and one rakʿah for his repentance. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made these three rakʿahs obligatory upon my Ummah. And it is the hour in which duʿa (supplication) is answered, so my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He will answer whoever supplicates to Him in it. And it is the salat (prayer) with which my Lord com

644 - What al-Husayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: “When Ādam was sent down from al-Jannah, a black mark appeared upon him on his face from the top of him to his feet, so his sorrow and weeping over what had appeared on him became prolonged. Then Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to him and said to him, ‘What makes you weep, O Ādam?’ He said, ‘Because of this mark that has appeared on me.’ He said, ‘Stand, O Ādam, and perform salat, for this is the time of the first prayer.’ So he stood and performed salat, and the mark descended to his neck. Then he came to him at the second prayer and said, ‘Stand and perform salat, O Ādam, for this is the time of the second prayer.’ So he stood and performed salat, and the mark descended to his navel. Then he came to him at the third prayer and said, ‘O Ādam, stand and perform salat, for this is the time of the third prayer.’ So he stood and performed salat, and the mark descended to his knees. Then he came to him at the fourth prayer and said, ‘O Ādam, stand and perform salat, for this is the time of the fourth prayer.’ So he stood and performed salat, and the mark descended to his feet. Then he came to him at the fifth prayer and said, ‘O Ādam, stand and perform salat, for this is the time of the fifth prayer.’ So he stood and performed salat, and when he came out of it, he praised Allah and extolled Him. Then Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام said, ‘O Ādam, the likeness of your offspring in these prayers is like your likeness regarding this mark. Whoever among your offspring performs five prayers in every day and night will come out of his sins just as you came out of this mark.’”

Al-Ridha, Ali ibn Musa عليه السلام, wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in what he wrote as a response to his questions: The reason for salat (prayer) is that it is an acknowledgment of the Lordship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a casting off of rivals, and a standing before the Compeller, exalted is His majesty, with humility, lowliness, submissiveness, confession, and seeking reprieve from previous sins, and the placing of the face upon the earth every day in magnification of Allah, exalted is His majesty. And so that he may be remembering, not forgetful nor insolent, and be humble, abased, desirous, seeking increase in religion and in worldly life, along with what is in it of obligation and persistence in the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by night and day. So that the servant does not forget his Master, his Regulator, and his Creator, and thus become insolent and transgress; and that this, in his remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Exalted, and his standing before Him, may be a restraint for him from acts of disobedience and a prevention for him from the various kinds of corruption.

Mālik al-Juhanī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of the Dhuhr prayer, and he said: "When the sun declines, the time of the two prayers has begun. So when you finish your supererogatory prayer, then perform the Dhuhr prayer whenever that appears suitable to you."

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah asked him about the time of the Dhuhr and ʿAsr prayers, and he said: “When the sun declines, the time of Dhuhr and ʿAsr both enters together, except that this one is before that one. Then you remain within the time of both of them together until the sun sets.”

And Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "When the sun declines, the two times enter: al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr. Then when the sun sets, the two times enter: al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿIjlī narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام that they said: "The time of Ẓuhr is two feet after the sun’s decline, and the time of ʿAṣr after that is two feet."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The beginning of the time is the decline of the sun, and it is Allah's first time, and it is the more excellent of the two."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The beginning of the time is the pleasure of Allah, and its end is the forgiveness of Allah, and forgiveness only comes in the case of a sin."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The merit of the earliest time over the later time is better for the believer than his children and his wealth."

Zurarah asked Abā Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام about the time of the Dhuhr prayer, so he said: "One cubit from the sun’s decline; and the time of ʿAsr is two cubits from the time of Dhuhr, so that is four feet from the sun’s decline." Then he said: "The wall of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was one stature high, and when one cubit of shadow had passed from it, he performed Dhuhr, and when two cubits had passed from it, he performed ʿAsr." Then he said: "Do you know why one cubit and two cubits were set?" I said: "Why was that set?" He said: "Because of the nafilah prayer. You may perform nafilah from the sun’s decline until one cubit passes; then when your shadow reaches one cubit, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the nafilah. And when your shadow reaches two cubits, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the nafilah."

Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said to Abū Baṣīr: “Whatever they may deceive you about, let them not deceive you concerning the ‘Asr prayer. Perform it while the sun is still white and clear, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘The one deprived of his family and wealth is the one who neglects the ‘Asr prayer.’” It was said: “What does it mean, deprived of his family and wealth?” He said: “He will have no family and no wealth in Paradise.” It was said: “What is neglecting it?” He said: “By Allah, it is that he leaves it until the sun turns yellow or the sun sets.”
Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: "The time of Maghrib begins when the disk disappears."

And Samāʿah ibn Mihrān said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding Maghrib: sometimes we pray while fearing that the sun may be behind the mountain, or that the mountain may have concealed it from us. So he said to me: “You are not required to climb the mountain.”

Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that a questioner asked him about the time of Maghrib, so he said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book concerning Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: “So when the night covered him, he saw a star. He said: This is my Lord.” So this is the beginning of the time, and the end of that is the disappearance of the twilight. Then the beginning of the time of the later ʿIshāʾ is the going away of the redness, and the end of its time is until the darkening of the night, meaning the middle of the night.
And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār The time for the last ʿIshāʾ prayer is until one-third of the night.

And it is narrated: “Regarding one who slept through the last ʿIsha prayer until the middle of the night, he must make it up and begin the morning fasting as a punishment. And that was only made obligatory upon him because he slept through it until the middle of the night.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform the Maghrib salat, and a clan from the Anṣār called Banū Salimah would pray with him. Their homes were at a distance of half a mile, then they would return to their homes while they could still see the places where their arrows fell.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Cursed, cursed is the one who delays the Maghrib prayer seeking its supposed extra merit.” And it was said to him: The people of Iraq delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars interlace, so he said: “This is from the practice of the enemy of Allah, Abī al-Khaṭṭāb.”

Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham said: One time, I climbed Mount Abu Qubays while the people were performing the Maghrib prayer. I saw that the sun had not set; rather, it had only gone behind the mountain from the sight of the people. Then I met Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and informed him of that, so he said to me: "Why did you do that? What you did was bad. You are only to perform it when you no longer see it behind the mountain, whether it has set or gone down, so long as no cloud or darkness covers it. Rather, what concerns you is your eastern horizon and your western horizon, and the people are not required to investigate."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "When the sun sets, iftar becomes permissible and the salat becomes obligatory. When you have performed the Maghrib prayer, then the time of the later night prayer has entered, until midnight.
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “An appointed angel says: Whoever passes the night having neglected the later evening salat (prayer) until the middle of the night, may Allah not let his eyes sleep.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever performs the Maghrib prayer, then does ta'qib and does not speak until he prays two rak'ahs, they are written for him in 'Illiyyin. If he prays four, an accepted hajj is written for him.

Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: The time of salat al-Jumu‘ah, on the day of al-Jumu‘ah, is the hour when the sun declines, and its time in travel and residence is one and the same, and it is of the restricted time. And salat al-‘Asr on the day of al-Jumu‘ah is in the time of the first prayer on the rest of the days.

And Ismāʿīl ibn Rabāḥ narrated from Abī ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام that he said: "If you performed salat (prayer) while believing that you were within the time, but the time had not yet entered, then the time entered while you were in the salat (prayer), it has sufficed for you."

Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked him about salat (prayer) during the night and the day when the sun, the moon, and the stars cannot be seen, so he said: "You exert your judgment and deliberately determine the qiblah to the best of your ability."

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Farra' narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: A man from among our companions said to him: “Sometimes the time becomes unclear to us on a cloudy day.” He said: “Do you know these birds that are with you in Iraq, which are called roosters?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “When their voices rise and they answer one another, then at that time perform salat (prayer).”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: I am a mu'adhdhin, so when it is a cloudy day and I do not know the time, he said: “When the rooster crows three consecutive calls, then the sun has passed its zenith and the time of salat (prayer) has entered.”

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "That I should perform salat (prayer) after the time has passed is more beloved to me than that I should perform salat (prayer) while I am in doubt about the time and before the time."

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: The muʾadhdhin would come to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in the heat at the time of salat al-zuhr, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would say to him, "Let it cool, let it cool."

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “The sun declines in the middle of Ḥazīrān by half a foot; in the middle of Tammūz by one and a half feet; in the middle of Āb by two and a half feet; in the middle of Aylūl by three and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Awwal by five and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Ākhir by seven and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Awwal by nine and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Ākhir by seven and a half feet; in the middle of Shubāṭ by five and a half feet; in the middle of Ādhār by three and a half feet; in the middle of Naysān by two and a half feet; in the middle of Ayyār by one and a half feet; and in the middle of Ḥazīrān by half a foot.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “The indication of the sun’s decline is that you take a stick whose length is one cubit and four fingers, then place four fingers into the ground. So when the shadow diminishes until it reaches its limit, then increases, the sun has declined. And the gates of the heaven are opened, the winds blow, and great needs are fulfilled.”

Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the stillness of the sun, and he said: "O Muhammad, how small is your frame and how difficult is your question; and indeed, you are worthy of an answer. When the sun rises, seventy thousand angels draw it, after five thousand angels from among the angels have taken hold of each of its rays, between one pulling and one pushing, until when it reaches the atmosphere and passes the opening, the angel of light turns it from back to front, so what had been facing the earth turns toward the heaven, and its rays reach the boundaries of the Throne. At that moment the angels call out: "Glory be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and "All praise is due to Allah, Who has not taken a consort, nor a son, and He has no partner in the dominion, nor does He have any protector out of weakness; and magnify Him with great magnification." He said to him, "May I be your ransom, should I preserve this speech at the sun's decline?" He said, "Yes, preserve it as you preserve your eye; for when the sun declines, the angels are behind it glorifying Allah in the orbit of the atmosphere until it sets.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the sun: how it comes to a stillness every day, while on Friday there is no stillness for it. He said: "Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Friday the most constricted of the days." Then it was said to him: And why did He make it the most constricted of the days? He said: "Because on that day He does not punish the polytheists, due to its sanctity with Him."

And it was narrated from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbdillāh that he said: I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and a man asked him. He said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, indeed the sun descends, then becomes still for a moment before it declines.” So he said: “It consults whether it should decline or not decline.”

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: I was given five things that no one before me was given: the earth was made for me a masjid and a means of taharah, I was aided by fear, spoils were made lawful for me, I was given comprehensive words, and I was given intercession.

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There are ten places where salat (prayer) is not performed: mud, water, the bathhouse, graves, the beaten parts of the road, ant colonies, camel resting places, the watercourse, saline land, and snow.
And it is narrated: That salat (prayer) is not performed in al-Baydāʾ, Dhāt al-Ṣalāṣil, the valley of al-Shuqrah, nor in the valley of Ḍajnān.

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: About salat (prayer) in the bathhouse, so he said: “If the place is clean, then there is no harm in salat (prayer),” meaning the changing area.

And al-Riḍā, peace be upon him, said: "Every path that is trodden and used as a thoroughfare, whether there is a main road in it or not, salat (prayer) should not be performed in it." It was said, "Then where should one pray?" He said, "To the right or to the left."

Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about prayer in sheep pens, and he said: “Pray there, but do not pray in camel enclosures unless you fear the loss of your belongings; then sweep it, sprinkle it with water, and pray in it.” He said: “Prayer in saline land is disliked unless it is a soft place upon which the forehead may rest evenly.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about salat (prayer) in the houses of the Magians while they are sprinkled with water, and he said: “There is no harm in it.” Then he said: “And I saw him on the road to Makkah at times sprinkling the place of his forehead, then performing sajdah (prostration) upon it while it was damp as it was; and perhaps at times he did not sprinkle the place which he considered to be clean.”

And Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Ḥakam said: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about salat (prayer) in synagogues and churches, so he said: “Pray in them.” He said: So I said: Even if they are praying in them, should I pray in them? He said: “Yes. Do you not recite the Qur’an: “Say: Each acts according to his manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided in way.” Pray facing the qiblah and leave them.
Zurārah asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about urine being on a rooftop or in the place in which one prays. So he said: “If the sun dries it, then pray on it, for it is tahir (ritually pure).”

And ʿĀmir ibn Nuʿaym al-Qummī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About the dwellings in which people stay, wherein there is the urine of animals and dung, and which are entered by the Jews and the Christians—what should we do regarding salat (prayer) in them? So he said: “Pray on your garment.”

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: About a man who comes to be in al-Baydāʾ, then an obligatory salat overtakes him, and he does not leave al-Baydāʾ until its time has passed: how should he deal with the salat, when praying in al-Baydāʾ has been prohibited? So he said: “He should pray in it, and avoid the main path of the road.”
Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: One should move away from the main roads to the right or to the left and pray.

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About a house and a dwelling that the sun does not reach, and urine reaches them, and ghusl from janabah is performed in them: may one perform salat in them when they have dried? He said: "Yes." He said: And I asked him about salat between the graves— is it valid? So he said: "There is no harm in it."

ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mat whose reeds had been moistened with impure water: is salat (prayer) permissible upon it? So he said: If it has dried, then there is no harm in performing salat (prayer) upon it.

And Zurarah asked Abā Ja‘far عليه السلام: About a cushion on which there is janābah: may one perform salat (prayer) on it in the litter? He said: “There is no harm in performing salat (prayer) on it.”
Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: There is no harm in performing salat (prayer) on any images or representations if you place them beneath you.

Laith al-Murādī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About cushions that are in the house with images on them, on the right or on the left. He said: “There is no harm in it so long as they are not facing the qiblah. And if any part of them is before you, from what is adjacent to the qiblah, then cover it and pray.”

And he was asked about images that are on a carpet, having two eyes, while you are performing salat (prayer). So he said: "If it has one eye, then there is no harm; but if it has two eyes while you are performing salat (prayer), then no."
And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no harm in salat (prayer) while you are looking at images if they have only one eye.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Do not perform salat (prayer) in a house in which there is a dog, unless it is a hunting dog and you have closed a door between yourself and it; then there is no harm. Indeed, the angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog, nor a house in which there are images, nor a house in which urine is collected in a vessel.
Abu Baṣīr narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: Whoever is in a place where he cannot reach the ground should gesture by indication, even if he is in an isolated land.

Sama‘ah ibn Mihrān asked him: About a captive whom the polytheists capture, then the time of salat (prayer) comes upon him, and the one who captured him prevents him from it; he said: "He should gesture, gesturing."

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about a man and a woman praying in one house. So he said: “If there is between them the measure of a handspan, she may pray beside him by herself and he by himself; there is no harm.”

And in the narration of Zurārah from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: "If there is between her and him a distance equal to what may be stepped over, or equal to the measure of a forearm bone or more, then there is no harm if she prays beside him alone."

Jamil narrated from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام that he said: There is no harm in a woman praying beside a man while he is praying. Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to pray while 'A'ishah was lying down in front of him and she was menstruating; when he wanted to prostrate, he would press her legs, so she would raise her legs until he prostrated.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Prostration on the earth is obligatory, and on other than that is sunnah (a recommended practice).
And he, peace be upon him (AS), said: "Prostrating on the clay of the grave of al-Husayn, peace be upon him (AS), gives light down to the seventh earth."
Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "Prostration is upon what the earth produces, except that which is eaten or worn."

And it was narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim that he said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed by me while I was praying on the ṭabarī, and I had placed something on it. So he said to me, “What is the matter with you that you do not perform sajdah on it? Is it not from the vegetation of the earth?”
Al-Mu‘allā ibn Khunays asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about salat on al-qufr and al-qīr. So he said: “There is no issue with it.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about gypsum that is fired with dung and the bones of the dead, then the mosque is plastered with it: may one perform sajdah upon it? So he عليه السلام wrote back to him in his own handwriting: “Indeed, the fire and the water have purified it.”
Dawud ibn Abi Zayd asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام about papers and documents written upon: is prostration upon them permissible? So he wrote: “It is permissible.”
ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man who performs sajdah on a misḥ and a carpet, so he said: "There is no issue if it is in a state of taqiyyah."
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) on qār. So he said: “There is no issue with it.”

Zurarah narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said: I said to him: A man prostrates while he is wearing a cap or a turban. He said: “If any part of his forehead touches the ground, in the area between his eyebrows and the hairline of his hair, then it has sufficed for him.”
And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb said: I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام leveling the pebbles at the place of his prostration between the two prostrations.

And it was narrated from ʿAlī ibn Bajīl that he said: I saw Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, whenever he prostrated and then raised his head, he would take the pebbles from his forehead and place them on the ground.

And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "What is between the hairline and the tip of the nose is a place of sajdah, so whatever part of it touches the ground has sufficed for you."
A man asked al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about a place in which there was dust: should I blow it away when I want to perform sajdah? So he said: “There is no issue.”
And it was narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: "That is only disliked for fear that the one beside him may be harmed."

844 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the Ka'bah the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and He made the mosque the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and He made the Haram the qiblah for the people of the world."

Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the deviation of our companions toward the left from the qiblah, and about the reason for it. He said: «When the Black Stone was sent down from Paradise and placed in its position, the boundary markers of the Haram were set according to where the light reached—the light of the Stone. So it is four miles on the right side of the Kaʿbah and eight miles on its left side, all together twelve miles. Thus, when a person inclines to the right, he exits the limit of the qiblah because of the lesser extent of the boundary markers of the Haram; but when a person inclines to the left, he is not outside the limit of the qiblah.»

Zurarah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "It suffices the one who is confused, at all times, whichever direction he turns, if he does not know where the direction of the qiblah is."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked him: about a man who stands in salat (prayer), then looks after he has finished, and sees that he had deviated from the qiblah to the right or the left. So he said to him: "His salat (prayer) has passed as valid, and what lies between the east and the west is qiblah."

And Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام that he said: "If seepage appears behind the latrine and it is in the direction of the qiblah, he should cover it with something."
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, forbade spitting in the direction of the Qiblah.

And he saw phlegm in the mosque, so he walked to it with a palm-stick from the palm-branches of Ibn Ṭāb and scraped it off, then he returned backward and continued his prayer. And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: 'And this opens many doors regarding the prayer.'
And he, peace be upon him and his family, forbade sexual intercourse while facing the qiblah or with one's back to it, and he forbade facing the qiblah while urinating or defecating.
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "None of you should spit in salat (prayer) in front of his face, nor to his right; rather, let him spit to his left and beneath his left foot."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever holds back his saliva out of reverence for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during his salat (prayer), Allah, Exalted is He, will grant him health until death."

And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "There is no salat (prayer) except toward the qiblah." He said: I said, "And where is the boundary of the qiblah?" He said: "What is between the east and the west is all qiblah." He said: I said, "Then whoever prays facing other than the qiblah, or on a cloudy day at other than the time?" He said: "He repeats."

856 - And he said in another hadith that he mentioned to him: Then face the Qiblah with your face, and do not turn your face away from the Qiblah, lest your salat become invalid. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: "So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." So stand upright." For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever does not straighten his spine, then there is no salat for him. And be humble with your gaze for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not raise it to the sky; rather let it be before your face at the place of your sajdah."
And he, peace be upon him, said to Zurārah: "The salat (prayer) is not to be repeated except for five things: taharah (purification), time, the qiblah, ruku' (bowing), and sujud (prostration)."
And it is narrated: "If the wind blows strongly upon one who is in the ship, and he is unable to turn toward the qiblah, he should perform salat facing the front of the ship."
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Every preacher is a qiblah, and every one being preached to is a qiblah for the preacher."

A man said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “Indeed, I am sometimes in travel and cannot find the qiblah at night.” So he said: “Do you know the star that is called al-Jady?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Then place it on your right, and when you are on the road of hajj, then place it between your shoulders.”

861 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “We command our children to perform salat (prayer) when they are five years old, so instruct your children to perform salat when they are seven years old. And we command our children to perform sawm (fasting) when they are seven years old, as much of the day’s fast as they can bear—whether until midday, more than that, or less. Then if thirst or hunger overcomes them, they break the fast, so that they become accustomed to fasting and are able to bear it. So instruct your children to perform sawm when they are nine years old, as much of the day’s fast as they are able to bear; then if thirst overcomes them, they break the fast.”

And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Qārin that he said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, or he was asked while I was listening, about a man who circumcises his son and he does not perform salat (prayer) for a day or two. So he said: “And how many years has the boy reached?” It was said: “Eight years.” He said: “Glory be to Allah! He leaves salat (prayer)?” He said: I said, “Pain afflicts him.” He said: “He should perform salat (prayer) according to the manner he is able.”

863 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Faḍālah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh and Abī Jaʿfar, peace be upon them, who said: I heard him saying: When a boy reaches three years of age, he is told: Say, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ seven times. Then he is left until he completes three years, seven months, and twenty days, then he is told: Say, ‘Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ seven times. Then he is left until he completes four years, then he is told: Say seven times, ‘May Allah bless Muḥammad and his family.’ Then he is left until he completes five years, then he is told: Which of them is your right and which of them is your left? When he knows that, his face is turned toward the qiblah and he is told: Prostrate. Then he is left until he completes seven years. When he completes seven years, he is told: Wash your face and your hands. When he has washed them, he is told: Perform salat (prayer). Then he is left until he completes nine years. When he completes them, he is taught wudu (ablution), and he is struck for it, and he is commanded to perform salat (prayer), and he is struck for it. Then when he learns wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives him and his parents, if Allah wills.

915 - It is narrated from Ḥammād ibn ‘Īsā that he said: Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said to me one day, “Do you know how to perform salat (prayer), O Ḥammād?” He said: I said, “My master, I have memorized the book of Ḥarīz concerning salat (prayer).” He said: So he عليه السلام said, “No matter, stand and pray.” He said: So I stood before him, facing the qiblah, and I began the salat (prayer), and performed ruku‘ and sajdah. Then he said, “O Ḥammād, you do not know how to perform salat (prayer). How ugly it is for a man that sixty years or seventy years pass over him, yet he does not establish even one salat (prayer) with its limits complete.” Ḥammād said: So humiliation struck me within myself, and I said, “May I be made your ransom, then teach me the salat (prayer).” Then Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام stood facing the qiblah, upright. He let both his hands hang upon his thighs, having joined his fingers together, and he brought his feet near each other until there were three spread fingers between them. He faced with the toes of both his feet together and did not turn them away from the qiblah, in humility and stillness, and he said: “Allāhu Akbar.” Then he recited al-Ḥamd with measured recitation, and “Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad.” Then he paused a little, for the measure of one breathing while standing. Then he said, “Allāhu Akbar,” while standing; then he performed ruku‘, and filled his palms from his knees with the fingers spread, and pushed his knees back until his back became level, such that if a drop of water or oil were poured upon it, it would not move because of the levelness of his back. He pushed his knees back, straightened his neck, and closed his eyes. Then he glorified three times with measured recitation and said: “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-‘Aẓīmi wa biḥamdih.” Then he stood upright; and when he had become settled in standing, he said: “Sami‘a Allāhu liman ḥamidah.” Then he said the takbīr while standing, raised his hands opposite his face, and performed sajdah, placing his hands on the ground before his knees. Then he said: “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-A‘lā wa biḥamdih” three times. He did not place any part of his body upon another part of it, and he performed sajdah upon eight bones: the forehead, the two palms, the two knee-caps, the tips of the two big toes, and the nose. So these seven are obligatory, and placing the nose upon the ground is sunnah, and that is a

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: When you stand for salat (prayer), then say: O Allah, I present Muhammad before You concerning my need, and I turn toward You through him, so make me through him... "honored in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near." And make my salat through him accepted, my sin through him forgiven, and my supplication through him answered. Indeed, You are the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful.

From Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم went out to the prayer while al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام had been delayed in speaking, to the point that they feared he would not speak and that there might be muteness in him. So he صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم went out with him, carrying him on his shoulder, and the people formed rows behind him. He placed him on his right side. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم began the prayer, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr. When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم heard his takbīr, he repeated it and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr, until the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said seven takbīrs and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr. Thus the sunnah proceeded according to that.

And Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam has narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: There is another reason for that, and it is that when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was taken on the night journey to the heaven, he passed through seven veils, and at each veil he pronounced one takbīrah. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought him by that to the utmost limit of honor.

919 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān mentioned from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: "Another reason is that the takbirs at the beginning of the salat (prayer) became seven because the original basis of the salat is two rak'ahs, and their opening is with seven takbirs: the takbir of the opening, the takbir of ruku', the two takbirs of the two sajdahs in the first rak'ah, then the takbir of ruku' in the second, and the two takbirs of the two sajdahs. So if a person says seven takbirs at the beginning of a salat, then afterward forgets something from the takbirs of the opening or is heedless regarding them, no deficiency enters upon his salat."

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was the most complete of people in salat (prayer) and the most concise of them. When he entered into salat (prayer), he would say: “Allahu Akbar” and “Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.”

A man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said to him: “O son of the cousin of the best of the creation of Allah, Exalted is He, what is the meaning of raising your hands in the first takbīrah?” So he عليه السلام said: “Its meaning is: Allah is the Greatest, the One, the Unique, the One who ‘There is nothing like unto Him.’ He is not touched by the limbs, nor perceived by the senses.”

And it has been narrated that he says, in the sajdah of the obligatory verses of prostration, "There is no god but Allah, truly, truly. There is no god but Allah, in faith and affirmation. There is no god but Allah, in servitude and bondage. I have prostrated to You, O my Lord, in devotion and bondage, not refusing nor acting arrogantly; rather, I am a lowly servant, fearful, seeking refuge." Then he raises his head, then says the takbir.

And al-Ridha عليه السلام said: "Recitation was only appointed in the first two rak'ahs, and tasbih in the last two, in order to distinguish between what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained from Himself and what Allah, Exalted is He, ordained from the direction of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله."

Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: For what reason is the recitation done aloud in Ṣalāt al-Jumuʿah, Ṣalāt al-Maghrib, Ṣalāt al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, and Ṣalāt al-Ghadāh, while in the other prayers, al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr, it is not recited aloud? And for what reason did tasbīḥ in the last two rakʿahs become better than recitation? He said: “Because when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was taken by night to the heaven, the first prayer Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained upon him was al-Ẓuhr on the day of al-Jumuʿah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, added the angels to him, praying behind him, and He commanded His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله to recite aloud so that He might make his excellence clear to them. Then Allah ordained al-ʿAṣr upon him and did not add to him anyone from the angels, and He commanded him to recite quietly because there was no one behind him. Then He ordained al-Maghrib upon him and added the angels to him and commanded him to recite aloud, and likewise al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah. Then when it was near al-Fajr, he descended, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained al-Fajr upon him and commanded him to recite aloud so that He might make its excellence clear to the people just as He had made it clear to the angels. For this reason recitation is done aloud in them. And tasbīḥ became better than recitation in the last two rakʿahs because when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was in the last two, he remembered what he had seen of the greatness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and was struck with awe, so he said: “Subḥāna Allāh, wa al-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa Allāhu akbar.” Therefore, tasbīḥ became better than recitation.

Yahya ibn Aktham, the judge, asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: about the salat of Fajr: why is the recitation done aloud in it, even though it is among the daytime prayers, while recitation aloud is only in the night prayer? So he said: “Because the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform it in the darkness at dawn, so he made it close to the night.”

926 - And in what al-Faḍl mentioned from the reasons, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, that he said: “People were commanded to recite in salat (prayer) so that the Qur’an would not be abandoned and neglected, but rather be preserved and studied, so that it would not disappear nor be unknown. And al-Ḥamd was begun with, apart from the rest of the surahs, because there is nothing in the Qur’an and speech in which there has been gathered, from the comprehensive matters of goodness and wisdom, what has been gathered in Surah al-Ḥamd. And that is because His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He,” “All praise is for Allah” is only a fulfilment of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon His creation of gratitude, and gratitude for the good by which He granted His servant success. “Lord of the worlds” is tawhid (divine unity) for Him, praise of Him, and affirmation that He is the Creator, the Owner, none other than Him. “The All-beneficent, the All-merciful” is seeking His tenderness and mentioning His favors and blessings upon all His creation. “Master of the Day of Judgment” is affirmation for Him of resurrection, reckoning, and recompense, and affirming His dominion over the Hereafter just as affirming His dominion over the world. “You alone we worship” is desire and drawing near to Allah, exalted is His mention, and sincerity to Him in action apart from any other than Him. “And You alone we seek help from” is seeking increase in His granting success and His worship, and seeking continuity of what Allah has blessed him with and supported him by. “Guide us to the straight path” is seeking right guidance to His religion, holding fast to His rope, and seeking increase in recognition of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. “The path of those whom You have blessed” is emphasis in supplication and desire, and mention of what has already preceded of His blessings upon His awliya’, and desire for the like of those blessings. “Not of those who are angered against” is seeking refuge from being among the obstinate disbelievers who treat Him, and His command and prohibition, lightly. “And not of those who have gone astray” is seeking protection from being among those who went astray from His path without knowledge. “While they think that they are doing good work” So there has been gathered in it, from the comprehensive matters of goodness and wisdom concerning the Hereafte

A man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and said: O son of the cousin of the best of Allah’s creation, Mighty and Majestic, what is the meaning of extending your neck in rukuʿ? He said: “Its interpretation is: I have believed in Allah, even if my neck were to be struck.”

Ṭalḥah al-Sulamī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: For what reason are the hands placed upon the ground in sajdah before the knees? He said: “Because the two hands are, through them, the key of salat (prayer).”

And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said: "When one of you performs sajdah, then let him place his palms directly upon the ground, so that Allah may ward off from him the shackles on the Day of Resurrection."

A man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said to him: O son of the cousin of the best of Allah’s creation, what is the meaning of the first sajdah (prostration)? He said: “Its interpretation is: O Allah, indeed from it You created us, meaning from the earth. The interpretation of raising your head is: and from it You brought us out. The interpretation of the second sajdah is: and to it You return us. And raising your head is: and from it You will bring us out another time.”

Abu Basir asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about the reason for the salat (prayer): how it came to be two rakʿahs and four sajdahs. He said: “Because one rakʿah from standing is equivalent to two rakʿahs from sitting.”

When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed "So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great." The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Make it in your bowing." Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed "Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High." The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Make it in your prostration."
Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the qunūt. Is there a specific wording in it? So he said: “Praise your Lord, send blessings upon your Prophet, and seek forgiveness for your sin.”
Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "The qunūt is in every two rakʿahs in both voluntary and obligatory prayers."
And Zurārah narrated from him that he said: "Qunoot is in all prayers."

The saying of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام: "There is no harm in a man speaking during the obligatory salat (prayer) with anything by which he privately converses with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic."
It is narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: Everything is unrestricted until a prohibition regarding it is issued.
Al-Ḥalabī said to him: "Should I mention the Imams, peace be upon them, in the salat (prayer)?" He said: "Mention them collectively."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whatever you use to converse privately with your Lord during the salat (prayer) is not considered speech."

Mansur ibn Yunus Buzurj asked him about a man who strives to cry during the obligatory salat (prayer) until he weeps. He said: “It is a comfort of the eye, by Allah.” And he, peace be upon him, said: “When that happens, then remember me at that moment.”

And it has been narrated: “Indeed, crying over the deceased cuts off the salat (prayer), while crying at the remembrance of Paradise and the Fire is among the best of deeds in the salat (prayer).” And it has been narrated: “There is nothing except that it has a measure or a weight, except crying out of the fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; for indeed a drop from it extinguishes seas of fires. And if one who weeps were to weep among a community, they would be shown mercy.”

Every eye will weep on the Day of Judgment except three eyes: an eye that wept out of the fear of Allah, an eye that was lowered from the things Allah has forbidden, and an eye that stayed awake in the way of Allah.

And it is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl that he said: I prayed behind Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام for several days, and he would perform qunut in every salat (prayer), whether it was recited aloud or not.
And it is narrated from Zurarah that he said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “All qunut is recited aloud.”

A man said to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: “O cousin of the best of Allah’s creation, what is the meaning of raising your right foot and placing down your left in the tashahhud?” He said: “Its interpretation is: O Allah, cause falsehood to die and establish the truth.” He said: “Then what is the meaning of the Imam’s saying: al-salāmu ʿalaykum?” So he said: “Indeed, the Imam conveys on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and says in his conveying to the people of the congregation: safety for you from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

For it has been narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: "Whoever recites the tasbih of Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ عليها السلام at the end of the obligatory prayer, before folding his legs, Allah will forgive him."

It is narrated that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to a man from Bani Sa'd: Shall I not tell you about myself and Fatimah al-Zahra'? She was with me, and she drew water with the waterskin until it left a mark on her chest, and she ground with the handmill until her hands blistered, and she swept the house until her clothes became dusty, and she kindled beneath the cooking pot until her clothes darkened. Great hardship afflicted her because of that, so I said to her: If only you would go to your father and ask him for a servant to spare you the hardship of what you are in of this work. So she went to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and found people with him, so she felt shy and turned back. He صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم understood that she had come for some need, so he came to us in the morning while we were in our covering and said, 'Peace be upon you.' We remained silent and were shy because of our state. Then he said, 'Peace be upon you,' and we remained silent. Then he said, 'Peace be upon you,' and we feared that if we did not reply to him he would leave; and he used to do that, greeting three times, and if permission was given to him, otherwise he would leave. So we said, 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah, enter.' Then he entered and sat near our heads, and then said: 'O Fatimah, what was your need yesterday with Muhammad?' So I feared that if we did not answer him, he would rise and leave. I brought out my head and said: By Allah, I will inform you, O Messenger of Allah. She drew water with the waterskin until it marked her chest, and turned the handmill until her hands blistered, and swept the house until her clothes became dusty, and kindled beneath the cooking pot until her clothes darkened. So I said to her: If only you would go to your father and ask him for a servant to spare you the hardship of what you are in of this work. He said: 'Shall I not teach you both something better for you than a servant? When you take to your bed, then say Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, and Subhan Allah thirty-three times, and Al-hamdu li-llah thirty-three times.' Then Fatimah عليها السلام raised her head and said: 'I am pleased with Allah and with His Messenger; I am pleased with Allah and with His Messenger.'

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “The minimum du'a that suffices you after the obligatory prayer is that you say: ‘O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, we ask You for every good encompassed by Your knowledge, and we seek refuge in You from every evil encompassed by Your knowledge. O Allah, we ask You for Your well-being in all of our affairs, all of them, and we seek refuge in You from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.’”

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: “Whoever loves to depart from this world having been purified of sins, just as gold is purified with no impurity in it, and with no one seeking any claim against him due to a wrong, then let him say after the five salats the attribution of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, twelve times, then spread out his hands and say:” O Allah, I ask You by Your hidden, stored, pure, utterly pure, blessed Name, and I ask You by Your mighty Name and Your eternal authority, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Giver of gifts, O Releaser of captives, O Freer of necks from the Fire, I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to free my neck from the Fire, and to bring me out of the world safe, and to admit me into Paradise sound, and to make my supplication—its beginning prosperity, its middle success, and its end rectitude. “Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen things.” Then the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: “This is from the hidden matters among what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم taught me and commanded me to teach al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Jibrāʾīl came to Yūsuf عليه السلام while he was in the prison and said: O Yūsuf, say after every obligatory prayer: O Allah, make for me from my affair relief and a way out, and provide for me from where I expect and from where I do not expect.

And Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “You say at the end of every salat (prayer): O Allah, guide me from Your presence, and pour upon me from Your bounty, and spread over me from Your mercy, and send down upon me from Your blessings.”
Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal said: I saw Aba Abdillah عليه السلام, when he had prayed and finished his salat (prayer), raise his hands above his head.

And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: No servant stretches out his two hands toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah is too gracious to return them empty, until He places in them, from His bounty and mercy, whatever He wills. So when one of you makes du'a, he should not withdraw his hands until he wipes them over his head and his face. And in another report: "over his face and chest."

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “When one of you finishes the salat (prayer), let him raise his hands toward the heaven and be earnest in du'a (supplication).” So Ibn Saba' said, “O Amir al-Mu'minin, is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not in every place?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then why does he raise his hands toward the heaven?” So he said, “Do you not recite: ‘And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are promised’?” Then from where should sustenance be sought except from its place? And the place of sustenance and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised is the heaven.

Hadith 956 — Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say, when he had finished at noontime: "O Allah, I seek nearness to You through Your munificence and Your generosity, and I seek nearness to You through Muḥammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, and I seek nearness to You through Your near angels and Your sent prophets. And through You, O Allah—Yours is independence from me, and mine is need toward You. You are the Self-Sufficient, and I am the needy one toward You. Overlook my slip, conceal my sins from me, fulfill today my need, and do not punish me for the ugliness of what You know from me; rather, Your pardon encompasses me, and Your generosity." Then he would fall in sajdah and say: "O Possessor of taqwa and O Possessor of forgiveness, O Benign, O Merciful, You are more benign toward me than my father, my mother, and all creatures. Turn me back with the fulfillment of my need, my supplication answered, my voice shown mercy. You have indeed removed the various kinds of affliction from me."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Whoever says, when he has performed the Maghrib prayer, three times: ‘All praise belongs to Allah, Who does whatever He wills and none other than Him does whatever he wills,’ he will be given abundant good.”

958 - And he, peace be upon him, used to say between the two evening prayers: "O Allah, in Your hand are the measures of the night and the day, the measures of the world and the Hereafter, the measures of death and life, the measures of the sun and the moon, the measures of victory and abandonment, and the measures of wealth and poverty. O Allah, repel from me the evil of the sinful among the jinn and humankind, and make my return to lasting good and bliss that does not pass away."

Hadith 959 — It was narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj that he said: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to me with this supplication and taught it to me, and said: “Whoever supplicates with it after the Fajr salat (prayer) will not seek any need except that it will be made easy for him, and Allah will suffice him regarding that which concerns him: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and may Allah bless Muḥammad and his family. “And I entrust my affair to Allah; indeed Allah is Seeing of the servants.” “So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted.” “There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.” “So We answered him and delivered him from distress; and thus do We deliver the believers.” “Allah is sufficient for us, and excellent is the Trustee.” “So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no evil touched them.” What Allah wills—there is no might and no power except by Allah. What Allah wills, not what the people will. What Allah wills, even if the people dislike it. My Lord is sufficient for me against those lorded over; my Creator is sufficient for me against the created; my Provider is sufficient for me against the provided for. Sufficient for me is the One who has never ceased to be sufficient for me; sufficient for me is the One who has been, since I came to be, sufficient for me; He has never ceased to be sufficient for me. “Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”

He عليه السلام said: “When you finish an obligatory salat (prayer), then say: I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with the Qur’an as book, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with Ali as wali, and al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja‘far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, al-Hasan ibn Ali, and al-Hujjah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali as Imams. O Allah, Your wali, al-Hujjah—so protect him from before him, from behind him, from his right, from his left, from above him, and from beneath him. Extend his life, make him the one who rises by Your command, the one granted victory for Your religion, and show him what he loves and by which his eye is gladdened in himself, his progeny, his family, his wealth, his Shi‘ah, and regarding his enemy. And show them from him what they fear, and show him regarding them what he loves and by which his eye is gladdened, and heal by him our breasts and...” “the breasts of a believing people.” And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say when he finished his salat (prayer): “O Allah, forgive me for what I have sent forth and what I have delayed, what I have concealed and what I have made public, my excess against myself, and what You know better than I. O Allah, You are the One who brings forward and You are the One who puts back; there is no god but You. By Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over all creation: if You know life to be better for me, then give me life; and cause me to die if You know death to be better for me. O Allah, I ask You for Your fear in secret and in public, for the word of truth in anger and contentment, and for moderation in poverty and wealth. I ask You for bliss that does not end, for coolness of the eye that does not cease, and I ask You for contentment with the decree, for the coolness of life after death, for the delight of looking toward Your Face, and longing to meet You without harmful affliction and without dark trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of iman (faith), and make us guiding and guided. O Allah, guide us among those You have guided. O Allah, I ask You for firm resolve in right guidance, steadfastness in the matter, right guidance, gratitude for Your blessing, the goodness of Your wellbeing, and fulfilling Your right. And I ask You, my Lord, for a sound heart and a truthful tongue. I seek You

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever says these words at every obligatory salat (prayer) will be protected in himself, his house, his wealth, and his children: I seek protection for myself, my wealth, my children, my family, my house, and everything that belongs to me through Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who "He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him." And I seek protection for myself, my wealth, my children, my family, my house, and everything that belongs to me "through the Lord of the Daybreak, from the evil of what He created" to the end of it, and through "the Lord of mankind" to the end of it, and through Ayat al-Kursi to the end of it.

962 - It is narrated from Hilqām ibn Abī Hilqām that he said: I came to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and said to him: “May I be your ransom, teach me a comprehensive supplication for this world and the Hereafter, and make it concise.” So he said: “Say after Fajr until the sun rises: ‘Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent, and with His praise. I seek forgiveness from Allah and ask Him from His bounty.’” Hilqām said: “I had been the worst off in condition among my household, and I did not realize until an inheritance came to me from a man whom I did not know there was kinship between me and him. And today I am the most well-off of my household in wealth, and that is only from what my master, the righteous servant, taught me عليه السلام.”
963 - Zurarah said: I heard Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: "Supplication after the obligatory prayer is better than performing prayer voluntarily."

Hisham ibn Salim said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “I go out, and I love to be in a state of ta'qib.” So he عليه السلام said: “If you are in a state of wudu (ablution), then you are in a state of ta'qib.”

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after dawn and for an hour after the afternoon, and I shall suffice you regarding what concerns you.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Sitting after the dawn prayer in ta'qib and supplication until the sun rises is more effective in seeking sustenance than traveling through the earth.”

967 - Abdullah ibn Jundab narrated from Musa ibn Ja‘far عليهما السلام that he said: In the Sajdah of Shukr, you say: 'O Allah, I call You to witness, and I call Your angels, Your prophets, Your messengers, and all of Your creation to witness that You are Allah, my Lord; Islam is my religion; Muhammad is my Prophet; and ‘Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, ‘Ali ibn Muhammad, al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, and al-Hujjah ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali are my Imams. Through them I profess loyalty, and from their enemies I dissociate. O Allah, I adjure You by the blood of the oppressed' three times. 'O Allah, I adjure You by Your pledge upon Yourself against Your enemies, that You most surely destroy them by our hands and the hands of the believers. O Allah, I adjure You by Your pledge upon Yourself for Your awliya’, that You most surely grant them victory over Your enemy and their enemy, and that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the entrusted ones from the family of Muhammad' three times. And you say: 'O Allah, I ask You for ease after hardship' three times. Then place your right cheek on the ground and say: 'O my refuge, when the ways leave me helpless and the earth, vast as it is, becomes constricted for me. O Originator of my creation, out of mercy toward me, while You had no need of my creation, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and upon the entrusted ones from the family of Muhammad' three times. Then place your left cheek on the ground and say: 'O Humiliator of every tyrant, and O Giver of honor to every abased one, by Your might, I have reached the limit of my endurance' three times. Then return to prostration and say one hundred times: 'Thanks, thanks.' Then ask for your need, if Allah wills. And do not perform the Sajdah of Shukr in the presence of an opponent, and employ taqiyyah in omitting it.

And Jahm ibn Abī Jahm narrated, saying: I saw Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, and he had performed sajdah after the three rakʿahs of Maghrib. So I said to him, “May I be your ransom, I saw you prostrate after the three [rakʿahs].” He said, “And you saw me?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Then do not abandon it, for du'a in it is answered.”

And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd: that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said to a man, “When distress afflicts you, then wipe your hand over the place of your sajdah, then wipe your hand over your face from the side of your left cheek and over your forehead to the side of your right cheek.” He said: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr said: In this manner Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd described it to us. “Then say: In the Name of Allah, ‘the One besides Whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the seen... the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.’ O Allah, remove from me grief and sorrow,” three times.

And it is narrated from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī that he said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to me: “Say in the sajdah of gratitude one hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran,’ and if you wish: ‘Afwan, afwan.’”
Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام used to prostrate after he prayed, and he would not raise his head until the day had risen high.

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام that he said: “Whoever performs the prostration of gratitude while in a state of wudu (ablution), Allah writes for him thereby ten blessings and erases from him ten grave sins.”

Saʿd ibn Saʿd asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the prostration of gratitude, and he said: I see our companions prostrating once after the obligatory prayer and saying that it is the prostration of gratitude. So he عليه السلام said: Gratitude is only when Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, that he says: Glory be to the One Who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and indeed to our Lord we shall surely return. And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام, when he prayed, would not conclude until he placed his right cheek on the ground and his left cheek on the ground.”

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام: ‘Do you know why I chose you for My speech over My creation?’ Musa said: ‘No, my Lord.’” He said: ‘O Musa, I examined My servants inwardly and outwardly, and I did not find among them anyone more humble in soul before Me than you. O Musa, when you perform salat (prayer), you place your cheeks upon the earth.’”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, when the servant prostrates and says, 'O Lord, O Lord,' until his breath is cut off, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says to him, 'Here I am; what is your need?'

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would say in his prostration: O Allah, if I have disobeyed You, then I have obeyed You in the most beloved of things to You, and that is faith in You, as a favor from You upon me, not as a favor from me upon You. And I have abandoned disobeying You in the most hateful of things to You, and that is that I should ascribe to You a child or ascribe to You a partner, as a favor from You upon me, not as a favor from me upon You. And I have disobeyed You in matters not by way of defiance, nor stubborn opposition, nor out of arrogance against Your worship, nor denial of Your Lordship; rather, I followed my desire, and Satan caused me to slip after the proof against me and the clarification. So if You punish me, then it is for my sins, without being unjust to me; and if You forgive me and have mercy on me, then it is by Your munificence and by Your generosity, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

And in the narration of Abī al-Ḥusayn al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the worshipper only performs a prostration after the obligatory prayer so that he may thank Allah, exalted is His mention, therein for what He has bestowed upon him of performing his obligation. And the least that suffices therein is: ‘Thanks be to Allah’ three times.”

979 - Ahmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥarīz, from Murāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "The sajdah of gratitude is obligatory upon every Muslim. By it you complete your salat (prayer), please your Lord, and the angels marvel at you. When the servant performs salat (prayer) and then performs the sajdah of gratitude, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, opens the veil between the servant and the angels, and He says: "O My angels, look at My servant: he has performed My obligation, fulfilled My covenant, then prostrated to Me in gratitude for what I have bestowed upon him. O My angels, what does he have with Me?" He said: Then the angels say, "Our Lord, Your mercy." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what does he have?" The angels say, "Our Lord, Your Paradise." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what?" The angels say, "Our Lord, sufficiency in his important affair." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what?" He said: Nothing of good remains except that the angels mention it. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says, "O My angels, then what?" The angels say, "Our Lord, we have no knowledge." He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says, "I give thanks to him just as he gave thanks to Me, and I turn toward him with My grace, and I show him My Face."

980 - ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿUtbah narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever says ten times before the sun rises and before its setting: 'There is no god but Allah, alone, having no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die. In His hand is all good, and He has power over all things'—it shall be an expiation for his sins on that day."

981 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from him that he said: Nuh عليه السلام used to say when he entered the morning and evening: “O Allah, I make You witness that whatever blessing and well-being in religion or worldly life has come to me in the morning and evening is from You alone, having no partner. To You belongs all praise, and to You belongs thanks for it upon me until You are pleased, and after pleasure.” He would say it ten times when morning came and ten times when evening came, and because of that he was called a grateful servant. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say after salat al-fajr (prayer): “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and sorrow, incapacity and laziness, stinginess and cowardice, the burden of debt and the dominance of men, the ruin of the unmarried, heedlessness, humiliation, hardness, poverty, and destitution. And I seek refuge in You from a soul that is not satisfied, a heart that does not humble itself, an eye that does not shed tears, a supplication that is not heard, and a salat (prayer) that does not benefit. And I seek refuge in You from a woman who makes me old before the time of my old age, and I seek refuge in You from a child who becomes increase against me, and I seek refuge in You from wealth that becomes a punishment against me, and I seek refuge in You from a deceitful companion who, if he sees a good deed, buries it, and if he sees an evil deed, spreads it. O Allah, do not place for a wicked person over me any hand or favor.”

A group of our companions narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: My father عليه السلام used to say, when he had performed the morning prayer: “O He who is nearer to me than the jugular vein” O He who “comes between a man and his heart” O He who is in the highest outlook, O He who “there is nothing like unto Him” “and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing” O most generous of those asked, O most expansive of those who give, O best One to be called upon, O best One hoped in, O most hearing of hearers, O most seeing of onlookers, O best of helpers, O swiftest of reckoners, O most merciful of the merciful, O wisest of judges, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, expand my provision for me, extend my life for me, spread over me from Your mercy, and make me among those through whom You grant victory to Your religion, and do not replace me with another. O Allah, You have guaranteed my provision and the provision of every creature, so expand for me and for my dependents from Your vast halal provision, and suffice us against poverty. Then he would say: Welcome to the two guardians, and may Allah greet you both among the two writers. Write down, may Allah have mercy on you both, that I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. And I bear witness that the religion is as He legislated, that Islam is as He described, that the Book is as He sent down, that the word is as He conveyed, and that Allah is the manifest Truth. O Allah, convey to Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad the best greeting and the best peace. I have entered the morning while my Lord is praised. I have entered the morning not associating anything with Allah, nor calling upon anyone along with Allah, nor taking besides Him any guardian. I have entered the morning as a possessed servant, owning nothing except what my Lord has granted me ownership of. I have entered the morning unable to bring to myself the good that I hope for, nor to turn away from it the evil that I fear. I have entered the morning held in pledge by my deed, and I have entered the morning poor, finding none poorer than myself. By Allah I enter the morning, by Allah I enter the evening, by Allah I live, by Allah I die, and unto Allah is the resurrection.” And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said

And it is narrated from Mismāʿ Kardīn that he said: I prayed with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام for forty mornings. When he finished, he would raise his hands toward the sky and say: We have entered the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah. O Allah, we are Your servants and the children of Your servants. O Allah, protect us from where we guard ourselves and from where we do not guard ourselves. O Allah, watch over us from where we take precautions and from where we do not take precautions. O Allah, conceal us from where we seek concealment and from where we do not seek concealment. O Allah, cover us with sufficiency and wellbeing. O Allah, grant us wellbeing, and the continuity of wellbeing, and grant us gratitude for wellbeing.

1033 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The sick person performs salat standing. If he is unable to do that, he performs salat sitting. If he is unable to perform salat sitting, he performs salat lying on his back. He says the takbir, then recites. When he wants to perform ruku', he closes his eyes, then recites tasbih. When he has recited tasbih, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes serves as the raising of his head from ruku'. When he wants to perform sajdah, he closes his eyes, then recites tasbih. When he has recited tasbih, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes serves as the raising of his head from sajdah. Then he recites the tashahhud and departs.
He was asked about a sick person who is unable to sit: may he pray while lying down and place something on his forehead? So he said: "Yes. Allah has not burdened him except to his capacity."

Samā‘ah ibn Mihrān asked him: About a man who has fluid in his eyes, and the fluid is removed from them, so he lies on his back for many days, forty days or less or more, and he is prevented from performing the salat except by gesture while he remains in that condition. So he said: “There is no harm in that.”

Baziʿ al-Muʾadhdhin asked him and said to him: I intend to undergo a procedure on my eye. He said to me: "Do it." I said: They claim that he will be laid on his back for so-and-so many days and will not perform salat (prayer) sitting. He said: "Do it."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The sick person performs salat (prayer) standing; if he is not able, he performs salat (prayer) sitting. If he is not able, he performs salat (prayer) on his right side; if he is not able, he performs salat (prayer) on his left side. If he is not able, he lies down and gestures by indication, and he places his face toward the qiblah, and makes his sajdah lower than his ruku'.

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم entered upon a man from the Ansar while the wind had afflicted him. He said: ‘O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, how should I perform salat (prayer)?’ So he said:” “If you are able to seat him, then seat him; otherwise, turn him toward the qiblah, and instruct him to gesture with his head. He should make the sajdah lower than the ruku'. And if he is not able to recite, then recite in his presence and make him hear it.”

1039 - And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the sick person: how should he perform sajdah? He said: "On a khumrah, or on a fan, or on a siwāk that is raised up to him, and that is better than gesturing. The one who disliked sajdah on a fan only disliked it because of the idols that used to be worshipped besides Allah. And we have never worshipped other than Allah at all, so perform sajdah on the fan, on the siwāk, and on a piece of wood."

Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the sick person: does he make up the prayers when he has been rendered unconscious? So he said: No, except for the prayer during which he regained consciousness.

Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام, asking him about one who has fallen unconscious for a day or more: should he make up the prayers (salat) that he missed, or not? So he wrote: “He does not make up the fasting (sawm), nor does he make up the prayer (salat).”
