ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār asked him about this issue, and he said: "He does not make up the sawm (fasting) nor the salat (prayer), and everything over which Allah has overcome him, then Allah is more deserving of the excuse."
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: The person afflicted with an overpowering stomach condition performs wudu (ablution) and continues on his salat (prayer).

Murazim ibn Hakim al-Azdi said: I was ill for four months and did not perform voluntary prayers during them, so I mentioned that to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. So he said: 'There is no making up upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever Allah, Exalted is He, has caused to overcome him, then Allah is worthier of excusing him.'

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About a man: is it permissible for him to lean against the wall of the mosque while he is praying, or to place his hand on the wall while standing, without illness or any ailment? He said: “There is no harm.” And about a man who is in an obligatory salat (prayer), and rises in the first two rakʿahs: is it permissible for him to take hold of the side of the mosque and then rise, seeking help through it in standing, without weakness or any ailment? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, Standing in the salat (prayer) has become very difficult for me. He said: “When you want to attain the salat (prayer) of one who is standing, then recite while you are sitting. Then when two verses remain from the surah, stand up and complete what remains, and perform rukuʿ and sajdah. That is the salat (prayer) of one who is standing.”

Sahl ibn al-Yasaʿ asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: about a man who performs the nāfilah prayer sitting while he has no illness, whether in travel or residence. He said: “There is no harm in that.”

Abu Basir said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: We discuss and say that whoever performs salat (prayer) while sitting, without any illness, then his prayer is two rak'ahs in place of one, and two prostrations in place of one. So he said: It is not like that; it is complete for you.

And it was narrated from Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: "My father, peace be upon him, when he prayed sitting, he would sit cross-legged; and when he bowed, he would fold his legs."
Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah narrated that he asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Can a man perform salat while sitting cross-legged and with his legs outstretched? So he said: “There is no harm in that.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Regarding salat (prayer) in a carriage (mahmil): "Pray sitting cross-legged, with the legs extended, and in whatever way is possible for you."

And it is narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ziyād al-Karkhī that he said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: An elderly old man is unable, due to his weakness, to rise for relieving himself, and he is not able to perform rukūʿ or sujūd. He عليه السلام said: He should gesture with his head as an indication, and if he has someone who can raise the khumrah up to him, then he should perform sajdah. But if that is not possible for him, then he should gesture with his head toward the qiblah as an indication. I said: And fasting? He عليه السلام said: If he has reached that limit, then Allah has lifted it from him. If he has some ability, then giving charity of one mudd of food in place of each day is more beloved to me. But if he does not have the means for that, then there is nothing upon him.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Sulaymān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about a man whom a nosebleed overtakes during salat (prayer), and he does no more than sniff it back; is that permissible? He said: “Yes.”

Bukayr ibn Aʿyan narrated: That Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saw a man who had a nosebleed while he was in salat (prayer), and he inserted his hand into his nose and brought out blood. So he gestured to him with his hand: "Rub it with your hand and pray."
Layth al-Murādī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a nosebleed from the sun’s zenith until the night passes. He said: "He gestures with his head for each salat (prayer)."

And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from him, peace be upon him: That he asked him about a man who gets a nosebleed while he is in salat (prayer), and he has already performed part of his salat (prayer). So he said: "If the water is on his right, or on his left, or behind him, then let him wash it without turning, and let him continue his salat (prayer). But if he does not find the water without turning, then let him repeat the salat (prayer)." He said: "And vomiting is like that.
And in the narration of Abū Baṣīr from him, peace be upon him: "If you speak or turn your face away from the qiblah, then repeat the salat (prayer)."

Abu Basir said to him: “I hear a sneeze, so I praise Allah, Exalted is He, and I send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while I am in salat (prayer).” He said: “Yes, even if there is a sea between you and your companion.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: “If a blind person prays facing other than the qiblah, then if it is within the prayer time, he should repeat it; and if the time has already passed, he does not repeat it.”

And it is narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār that he said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I am in the salat (prayer), and I feel a pain in my stomach, or rumbling, or throbbing. So he said: “Turn away and perform wudu (ablution), and build upon what has passed of your salat (prayer) so long as you have not invalidated the salat (prayer) by deliberate speech. But if you spoke forgetfully, then there is nothing upon you, and it is like one who spoke in the salat (prayer) forgetfully.” I said: And if he turns his face away from the qiblah? He said: “Yes, even if he turns his face away from the qiblah.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: About abdominal discomfort that affects a man while he is able to bear it: should he perform salat in that state, or should he not perform salat? So he said: “If he can endure patiently, and does not fear rushing the salat because of it, then let him perform salat and be patient.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Smiling does not invalidate the salat (prayer), but loud laughter does. And it does not break the wudu (ablution)."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who greets the people during salat (prayer). He said: “If a Muslim greets you while you are in salat (prayer), then return the greeting to him; you say, ‘Al-salāmu ʿalayka,’ and gesture with your finger.”

And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about greeting one who is praying, so he said: "If a man from the Muslims greets you while you are in salat (prayer), then reply to him within yourself and do not raise your voice."
1065 - Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from him that he said: If a man is greeted while he is performing salat (prayer), he should reply to him quietly, as he said.

Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “ʿAmmār greeted the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while he was in salat (prayer), and he responded to him.” Then Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Indeed, al-Salām is one of the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

Sama‘ah ibn Mihrān asked him: About a man who is in the obligatory salat (prayer), standing, and then forgets his bag or belongings, fearing their loss or destruction. He said: "He cuts his salat and secures his belongings." He said: I said, "Then if his animal breaks loose from him, and he fears that it may go away or that hardship may befall him concerning it?" So he said: "There is no problem in his cutting his salat, securing it, and returning to his salat."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man whom a creature harms while he is performing salat (prayer). He said: "He may cast it away from himself if he wishes, or bury it in the pebbles."
Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who scratches himself while he is in salat (prayer). He said: “There is no harm.”
He asked him about a man who kills a mosquito, a flea, a louse, and a fly while he is in salat (prayer): does that invalidate his salat (prayer) and his wudu (ablution)? He said: "No."

And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked him: About a man who is in salat (prayer) and sees a snake in front of him: is it permissible for him to reach for it and kill it? He said: "If there is one step between him and it, then let him step and kill it; otherwise, no."

And Ḥarīz narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you are in the obligatory salat (prayer) and you see a servant of yours who has run away, or a debtor of yours who has property owed, or a snake that you fear for yourself from, then break the salat (prayer), follow your servant or your debtor, and kill the snake.

And al-Ḥalabī narrated that he asked him about a man who wants a need while he is praying, so he said: "He gestures with his head, signals with his hand, and performs tasbih; and the woman, when she wants a need while she is praying, claps with her hands."

Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who wishes to attend to a need while he is in salat (prayer), he عليه السلام said: “He gestures with his head and signals with his hand; and a woman, when she wishes to attend to a need, claps.”

Ḥanān ibn Sadīr asked him: Can a man gesture during salat (prayer)? He said: "Yes. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله gestured in one of the mosques of the Ansar with a miḥjan that was with him." Ḥanān said: "And I only know it to have been the mosque of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal."

Ammār ibn Mūsā asked him: About a man who hears a sound at the door while he is in salat (prayer), so he clears his throat to make his servant-girl or his family hear, so that she may come to him, and he gestures to her with his hand to inform her who is at the door so that she may look and see who it is. He said: “There is no harm in that.” And about a man and a woman who are in salat (prayer) and want something: is it permissible for them to say, “Subḥān Allāh”? He said: “Yes, and they may gesture toward what they want, and when a woman wants something, she strikes upon her thighs while she is in salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn Bajīl, the brother of ʿAlī ibn Bajīl, narrated, saying: I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام praying, and a man passed by him while he was between the two prostrations. So Abū ʿAbdillāh threw a small stone at him, and the man came toward him.

And it was narrated from Abū Zakariyyā al-Aʿwar, who said: I saw Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام performing salat while standing, and beside him was an elderly man who wanted to stand up and had a staff with him. The man wanted to reach for it, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام bent down while remaining standing in his salat and handed the man the staff. Then he returned to his place, to his salat.

Abu Ḥabīb Nājiyah said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I have a mill in which I grind sesame, and I rise and perform salat (prayer), while knowing that the servant-boy is asleep, so I strike the wall to wake him. He عليه السلام said: “Yes, you are in obedience to your Lord, seeking your sustenance; there is no harm in that.”

There is no adhan or iqama upon a woman, nor Jumu'ah, nor congregational prayer. When a woman stands in her salat, she gathers her feet together and does not separate them, and she places her hands on her chest at the place of her breasts. When she performs ruku', she places her hands above her knees on her thighs so that she does not bend too much and her buttocks rise. When she intends sajdah, she sits and then prostrates, pressing herself close to the ground, and places her forearms on the ground. When she wishes to rise to standing, she lifts her head from sajdah and sits upon her buttocks, not as a man sits, then rises to standing without lifting her buttocks, moving gently upward. When she sits for the tashahhud, she raises her legs and keeps her thighs together. A free woman does not perform salat except with a head covering, while a bondwoman performs salat without a head covering.
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: “A woman performs salat (prayer) in a dirʿ and a miqnaʿah if it is thick, meaning concealing.”

Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man praying in a single garment; he said, “Yes.” He said: I said, “Then the woman?” He said, “No, and it is not proper for a free woman, when she has menstruated, except with a khimār, unless she does not find it.”

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a woman who has only one outer wrap: how should she pray? He said: "She should wrap herself in it, cover her head, and pray. If her legs become exposed and she is unable to do otherwise, then there is no harm."

And in the narration of al-Mu‘allā ibn Khunays, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a woman who prays in a dir‘ and a milḥafah, with no izār or miqna‘ah upon her. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm if she wraps herself in it, and if it is not sufficient for her in width, she should make it lengthwise.”

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There is no headcovering required upon the slave woman in salat (prayer), nor upon the mudabbarah is there a headcovering in salat (prayer), nor upon the mukatabah, if her master has stipulated that upon her, a headcovering in salat (prayer), while she remains owned until she completes all of her contract of manumission; and there applies to her whatever applies to the owned slave in all legal penalties.

1086 - He said: I asked him about a slave woman, when she gives birth, whether the khimar is upon her. He said: "If it were required for her, then it would be required for her when she menstruates; but covering the head in salat (prayer) is not required for her."

1087 - And ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who performs salat in a woman’s izār, in her garment, and uses her khimār as a turban, he عليه السلام said: “If she is trustworthy, then there is no harm.”

And it is narrated: The best masjids for women are the houses, and a woman’s salat in her house is better than her salat in her portico, and her salat in her portico is better than her salat in the courtyard of her house, and her salat in the courtyard of her house is better than her salat on the roof of her house. And it is disliked for a woman to perform salat on a roof that is not enclosed.

And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Do not lodge women in upper rooms, nor teach them writing, nor teach them Sūrat Yūsuf; and teach them spinning and Sūrat al-Nūr. And when a woman performs tasbīḥ, she should count upon the fingertips, for they will be questioned on the Day of Judgment."

1318 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān al-Naysābūrī, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in al-ʿIlal what he heard from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Indeed, salat was only shortened during travel because the obligatory salat as first prescribed was only ten rakʿahs, and the seven were only added to it afterward. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, lightened that addition from the servant due to the circumstance of his travel, his fatigue, his hardship, his preoccupation with his own affairs, his departure and his stay, so that he would not be distracted from what is indispensable of his livelihood, as a mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and out of compassion for him—except for Salat al-Maghrib, for it is not shortened because it is a prayer shortened in its original form. And shortening only became obligatory for eight farsakhs, no less than that and no more, because eight farsakhs is the distance of a day’s travel for ordinary people, caravans, and loaded transports. So shortening became obligatory in a day’s travel. And if it had not been obligatory in a day’s travel, it would not have been obligatory in the travel of a thousand years; because every day that comes after this day is only the counterpart of this day. So if it were not obligatory in this day, it would not be obligatory in its counterpart, since its counterpart is like it, with no difference between them. And the voluntary prayers of the day were only omitted, while the voluntary prayers of the night were not omitted, because every prayer in which there is no shortening, there is no shortening in its voluntary prayer. That is because al-Maghrib is not shortened, so there is no shortening in the voluntary prayer after it. Likewise, al-Ghadat is not shortened, so there is no shortening in the voluntary prayer before it. And al-ʿAtamah only became shortened, yet its two rakʿahs are not abandoned, because the two rakʿahs are not from the fifty; rather, they are an addition to the fifty as voluntary prayer, so that by means of them there may be completed, in place of each rakʿah of the obligation, two rakʿahs of voluntary prayer. And it is only permitted for the traveler and the sick person to perform Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night due to his preoccupation and weakness, and so that he may secure his prayer; then the sick person may rest at the time of his rest, and the traveler may attend to his engage

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and said to him: When was the salat (prayer) made obligatory upon the Muslims in the form it is upon today? He said: In al-Madīnah, when the daʿwah became manifest, Islam grew strong, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prescribed jihad upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله added seven rakʿahs to the salat (prayer): two in al-Ẓuhr, two in al-ʿAṣr, one in al-Maghrib, and two in al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, and he left al-Fajr as it had been prescribed in Makkah, in order to hasten the ascent of the angels of the night to the heaven and to hasten the descent of the angels of the day to the earth. So the angels of the day and the angels of the night would witness Salat al-Fajr with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله; therefore Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And the Qur'an of dawn; surely the Qur'an of dawn is witnessed.” The Muslims witness it, and the angels of the day and the angels of the night witness it.

ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) on a ship, and he said: “He should face the qiblah and set his feet properly. If it turns and he is able to turn toward the qiblah, then let him do so; otherwise, let him pray in whatever direction it turns him. If standing is possible for him, then let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.”

Jamīl ibn Darrāj said to him: The ship is close to the shore, so should I go out and perform salat (prayer)? He said: "Perform salat (prayer) in it. Are you not content with the salat (prayer) of Nūḥ (عليه السلام)?"

Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn said to him: We go out to al-Ahwāz in ships, and we combine the salat (prayer) in them. So he said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.” So he said to him: Then do we perform sajdah (prostration) upon what is in them and upon pitch? He said: “There is no harm.”
And Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim narrated from him that he said: "Pitch (tar) is from the vegetation of the earth."
And Zurārah asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about: a man performing the nawāfil prayers on a ship. He said: “He should pray toward its front.”

Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about salat (prayer) in the Euphrates and what is smaller than it among the rivers while on a ship. He said, “If you pray, it is good, and if you go out, it is good.” And he asked him about salat (prayer) in a ship while it is moving eastward and westward, so he said, “Face the qiblah, then say the takbīr, then turn with the ship wherever it turns with you.”

Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī asked him about salat (prayer) on a ship. He said: “If it is heavily loaded, such that when you stand in it, it does not move, then perform salat (prayer) standing. And if it is light and tilts, then perform salat (prayer) seated.”

ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام. About a man who is on a ship: is it permissible for him to place a mat over goods, or over clover, straw, wheat, barley, and other such things, and then perform salat (prayer) on it? So he said: “There is no harm.”
And Ali عليه السلام said: When you board a ship and it is moving, then perform salat (prayer) while seated; and if it is stationary, then perform salat (prayer) while standing.

Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to some of his companions: “When Allah grants you the undertaking of the sea, then say that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “In the Name of Allah shall be its sailing and its anchoring; indeed, my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” If the sea becomes turbulent for you, then lean on your right side and say: In the Name of Allah, be still with the tranquility of Allah, be settled with the settling of Allah, and be calm by the permission of Allah, and there is no power and no strength except by Allah.
And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: My father, peace be upon him, used to dislike riding upon the sea for trade.
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about riding upon the sea during its turbulence. He said: “Why should a man place his religion in jeopardy?”
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, forbade riding upon the sea during its turbulence.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "How commendable in seeking is the one who boards the sea."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله prayed with his companions during the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. He divided his companions into two groups: he stationed one group facing the enemy and another group behind him. Then he pronounced the takbīr and they pronounced the takbīr; he recited and they listened silently; he performed rukuʿ and they performed rukuʿ; he performed sajdah and they performed sajdah. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله remained standing, and they prayed one rakʿah for themselves. Then some of them gave salām to others, then they went out to their companions and stood facing the enemy. Their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and he pronounced the takbīr, so they pronounced the takbīr; he recited and they listened silently; he performed rukuʿ, so they performed rukuʿ; he performed sajdah, so they performed sajdah. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sat and recited the tashahhud, then gave salām to them. They then stood and completed one rakʿah for themselves, then some of them gave salām to others.
And he said: "Whoever performs the Maghrib salat (prayer) in a state of fear with a group, he performs one rak'ah with the first group and two rak'ahs with the second group."

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a man whom a wild beast encounters, while the time of salat (prayer) has arrived, and he is unable to walk out of fear of the beast. He said: "He should face the lion, perform the salat (prayer), and gesture with his head in indication while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah."

Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who encounters a wild beast, and salat has become due, but he cannot walk for fear of the lion. He said: He should face the lion and perform salat, gesturing with his head by way of indication while he is standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah.

Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man whom the polytheists seize, and the time of salat (prayer) comes upon him, so he fears that they will prevent him. He said: "He gestures by gesturing."

Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Are the salat of fear and the salat of travel both shortened? He said: "Yes, and the salat of fear is more deserving of being shortened than the salat of travel, because in it there is fear."

1340 - And I heard our shaykh, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah be pleased with him, say: It was narrated that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may afflict you.” So he عليه السلام said: “This is a second shortening, and it is that a man reduces two rakʿahs to one.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: Regarding the prayer of the advancing troops, he said: “You pronounce the takbīr and the tahlīl. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘But if you fear, then on foot or while riding.’

And it was narrated from Abū Baṣīr that he said: I heard Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام say: “If you are in a dangerous land and you fear a thief or a wild beast, then perform the obligatory prayer while you are upon your mount.”
And in the narration of Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: "One who fears robbers performs salat by gesturing while on his mount."

It has been permitted, in the salat of fear from a wild beast, when a man fears for his life, that he should pronounce the takbir and not make gestures. It was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them.

Zurarah narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: "One who fears robbers or wild beasts should perform the prayer of the stationary [traveler] with gestures while on their mount." I said: "What if the stationary one does not have wudu? What should they do, being unable to dismount?" He said: "They should perform tayammum from the saddlecloth of their mount, or its saddle, or its cover, for there is dust in it, and they should pray, making the prostration gesture lower than the bowing, and they should not turn to face the Qibla, but wherever their mount turns, provided that they face the Qibla with the first Takbir when they turn."

And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The salat of advancing combat is on the back with gesturing by your head and takbir. In close sword-fighting, it is takbir without gesturing. In pursuit, it is gesturing; each man prays according to his own situation."

And he, peace be upon him, said: The people missed the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers with ʿAlī عليه السلام on the day of Ṣiffīn, so he instructed them, and they recited takbīr, tahlīl, and tasbīḥ on foot and while mounted.

And in the book of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, it is reported that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “The minimum that suffices in the case of close combat is two takbīrs for every salat, except al-Maghrib, for it has three takbīrs.”

Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked him about the prayer during battle, so he said: "When they meet and engage in fighting, then the salat at that time is only takbīr. And if they are standing and unable to perform in congregation, then the salat is by gestures."

1350 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Whoever purifies himself and then goes to his bed, he spends the night while his bed is like his masjid. If he remembers that he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), then let him perform tayammum from his covering, whatever it may be; and he continues to be in salat (prayer) so long as he remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

1351 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to me: “When a man rests on his right side, he should say: ‘In the Name of Allah. O Allah, I have submitted my soul to You, turned my face toward You, entrusted my affair to You, sought support with my back in You, and relied upon You, in fear of You and in hope toward You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have sent down, and in Your Messenger whom You have sent.’ Then he should recite the tasbih of Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ عليها السلام. And whoever is afflicted by fear at the time of sleep should recite, when he goes to his bed, the two protective surahs and Āyat al-Kursī.

1352 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: “A man should not refrain from saying at the time of his sleep: I seek protection for myself, my offspring, the people of my household, and my wealth through the perfect words of Allah, from every Shaytan, every harmful creature, and from every afflicting eye.” For that is what Jibrāʾīl, peace be upon him, used as protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said to him: “Recite ‘Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad’ and ‘Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn’ at the time of your sleep for it is a disavowal of shirk.” And “‘Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad’” is the description of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Hadith 1354 — Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "Whoever says, when he takes his sleeping place, three times: All praise is due to Allah, Who is exalted and subdues. All praise is due to Allah, Who is hidden and thus fully aware. All praise is due to Allah, Who possesses dominion and thus has power. All praise is due to Allah, Who gives life to the dead and causes the living to die and He is powerful over all things he comes out from his sins as on the day his mother gave birth to him."

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever recites this verse at the time of his sleep: 'Say, I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is One God' to the end of it a light will shine for him to al-Masjid al-Haram, the midst of that light being filled with angels seeking forgiveness for him until morning.

And ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Judhāʿah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no servant who recites the end of al-Kahf when he sleeps except that he wakes from his sleep at the hour that he desires.

1357 - Saʿd al-Iskāf narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "Whoever says these words, I guarantee that no scorpion or harmful creature will afflict him until morning: I seek refuge in the complete words of Allah, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can surpass, from the evil of what He has created, from the evil of what He has brought forth, and from the evil of every creature "whose forelock He holds. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path."

Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “If you fear janabah, then say in your bed: O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from wet dreams, from evil dreams, and from Shaytan playing with me in wakefulness and sleep.”

1359 - Al-‘Abbās ibn Hilāl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: "No one has ever said, when he intended to sleep: "Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving." and then a house collapsed upon him.

Jibrīl عليه السلام descended upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he said to him: “O Jibrīl, admonish me.” So he said: “O Muḥammad, live as you wish, for indeed you will die; love whomever you wish, for indeed you will part from him; and do whatever you wish, for indeed you will meet it.” The honor of the believer is his salat (prayer) by night, and his dignity is in withholding harm from the people.

Bahr al-Saqqa' narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, among the comfort and mercy from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are three things: tahajjud in the night, the breaking of the fast of the fasting person, and meeting with the brothers."

Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "But monasticism—they innovated it; We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of Allah." He said: "The night prayer (salat al-layl)."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "You must engage in salat al-layl, for it is the sunnah of your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the practice of the righteous before you, and it drives away illness from your bodies."

Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from him that he said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, the rising by night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech." He said: "It is a man's rising from his bed, intending by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not intending by it other than Him."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: People rise from their beds in three categories: one for whom it is in their favor and not against them, one for whom it is against them and not in their favor, and one for whom it is neither against them nor in their favor. As for the category that is in their favor and not against them, they rise from their sleep, perform wudu (ablution), pray, and remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That is the one for whom it is in their favor and not against them. As for the second category, they remain in disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is the one for whom it is against them and not in their favor. And as for the third category, they continue sleeping until morning; that is the one for whom it is neither against them nor in their favor.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration." He said: "It is staying awake in salat (prayer)."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār narrated from him that he said: "Indeed, the houses in which salat (prayer) is performed at night with the recitation of the Qur'an shine for the inhabitants of the heaven just as the stars of the sky shine for the inhabitants of the earth."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds." He said: "The salat of the believer at night removes what he committed of sin during the day.

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He intends to afflict the people of the earth with punishment, says: Were it not for those who love one another for My Majesty, maintain My mosques, and seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours—were it not for them, I would surely send down My punishment.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever increases his salat (prayer) during the night, his face becomes beautiful during the day."

A man came to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and complained to him of need, and he went to excess in complaining until he was about to complain of hunger. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him, “O you, do you pray at night?” The man said, “Yes.” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام turned to his companions and said, “He has lied who claims that he prays at night and goes hungry by day. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed for the night prayer the sustenance of the day.”

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves one who engages in light-heartedness in a gathering without indecency, one who is alone in reflection, one who withdraws with lessons and contemplation, and one who stays awake for salat (prayer).

Jābir ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: That a man asked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام about standing in prayer during the night with recitation, so he said to him: “Receive glad tidings. Whoever prays a tenth of the night for Allah, sincerely seeking the reward of Allah, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels: “Write for this servant of Mine, among the good deeds, the number of what grows in the night of seed, leaf, and tree, and the number of every stalk, frond, and pasture.” Whoever prays a ninth of the night, Allah grants him ten answered supplications and gives him his book in his right hand. Whoever prays an eighth of the night, Allah grants him the reward of a patient martyr, sincere in intention, and he is granted intercession regarding his household. Whoever prays a seventh of the night rises from his grave on the day he is resurrected with his face like the moon on the night of fullness, until he passes over the Sirat with the secure ones. Whoever prays a sixth of the night is recorded among the oft-returning ones, and what has preceded of his sin is forgiven for him. Whoever prays a fifth of the night contends alongside Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of the All-Merciful, in his dome. Whoever prays a quarter of the night is among the first of the successful, until he passes over the Sirat like a violent wind and enters Paradise without reckoning. Whoever prays a third of the night, no angel remains except that he envies him for his rank with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is said to him: Enter from whichever of the eight gates of Paradise you wish. Whoever prays half a night, even if he were given the fill of the earth in gold seventy thousand times, it would not equal his reward; and by that, for him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is better than seventy slaves he frees from the descendants of Ismāʿīl. Whoever prays two-thirds of a night, he shall have of good deeds the measure of the sand of ʿĀlij, the least of which is a good deed heavier than Mount Uḥud ten times. Whoever prays a complete night, reciting the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and remembering, is given of reward such that at the very least he comes out from sins as his mother gave birth to him. There are written for him, of good deeds, the number of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created, and the like of

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he had performed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, would retire to his bed and would not perform any prayer until the middle of the night.
And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: "The time for the night prayer (salat al-layl) is from midnight until its end."

ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I remained for eighteen nights intending to rise, but I did not get up. Should I then pray at the beginning of the night? He said: “No. Make it up during the day, for I dislike that this be adopted as a habit.”

And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb that he said: I said to him: A man from among your followers, from among their righteous ones, complained to me about what he suffers from sleep. He said to me: I want to rise for salat al-layl, but sleep overcomes me until morning comes. So sometimes I make up my prayer continuously for a month or two, bearing its heaviness with patience. So he said: By Allah, it is a delight of the eye; by Allah, it is a delight of the eye. And he did not grant permission regarding al-Witr at the beginning of the night. He said: Making it up during the day is better.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān narrated from Layth al-Murādī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat in the summer, during the short nights, namely Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night. He said: “Yes, good is what you considered, and good is what you did.”
And he said: I asked him about a man who fears janabah during travel or in the cold, so he performs salat al-layl and al-witr at the beginning of the night. He said, 'Yes.'

Abu Jarir ibn Idris narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said: "Perform salat al-layl during travel at the beginning of the night in the carriage, and the Witr, and the two rak'ahs of Fajr."

1382 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: There is no servant except that he is awakened in his night once or twice. If he rises, that is so; otherwise, al-Shayṭān comes and urinates in his ear. Does not one of you see that when he rises, and that has not happened from him, he rises while he is sluggish, heavy, and lazy?

Al-Hasan al-Sayqal narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, I truly despise the man who comes to me and asks me about the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, then says, 'Shall I add more?' as though he sees that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fell short in something. And indeed, I truly despise the man who has read the Qur'an, then wakes during the night but does not rise, until when it is near dawn, he gets up rushing to it with his salat (prayer).

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام that he said: There is no servant who intends to rise at whatever hour he intends, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knows that from him, except that He appoints for him two angels who awaken him at that hour.

And ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “If a man is overcome by sleep while he is in salat (prayer), then let him put down his head and sleep, for I fear for him that if he intends to say, ‘O Allah, admit me to Paradise,’ he may say instead, ‘O Allah, admit me to the Fire.’”

And Zakariyyā al-Naqqāḍ narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic "Do not approach salat (prayer) while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying." He said: "Included in it is the intoxication of sleep."

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he would go to his bed, would say: In Your Name, O Allah, I live, and in Your Name, I die. And when he would wake up, he would say: All praise is due to Allah, who gave me life after He caused me to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "When one of you rises, let him say: Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the Prophets, the God of the Messengers, and the Lord of the oppressed; and all praise is due to Allah, who gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things." For when he says that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: "My servant has spoken the truth and given thanks."

1389 - And 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj narrated from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: That when he would rise at the end of the night, he would raise his voice until the people of the house could hear, and he would say: O Allah, help me against the terror of the ascenting place, make my resting place spacious for me, grant me the best of what is before death, and grant me the best of what is after death.

1390 - And in another report from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: "When you rise from your bed, then look at the horizon of the sky and say: All praise is for Allah, who has returned my soul to me; I worship Him and praise Him. O Allah, indeed no still night can conceal from You, nor a sky possessing constellations, nor an earth possessing expanse. Nor "like darknesses, some of them above others." Nor a deep sea moving along before the traveler from among Your creation can conceal anything; You know. "The treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal." The stars have set, and the eyes have slept, while You are "the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting"; slumber does not overtake You. "Neither drowsiness nor sleep." "Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds." And the God of the messengers and the Creator of the prophets. "And all praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds." O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and turn toward me. "Indeed, You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful." Then recite five verses from the end of Āl ʿImrān, from "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" to His saying, "Indeed, You do not fail in the promise."

Abu ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Their sides forsake their beds." He said, "Perhaps you think that these people did not sleep?" I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said, "This body must inevitably be given rest until its breath departs; when the breath departs, the body rests, and the spirit returns to it, and in it is strength for action. Rather, He only mentioned them and said:" "Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope." It was revealed about Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and his followers from our Shiʿah. They sleep in the first part of the night, then when two-thirds of the night have passed—or whatever Allah wills—they hasten to their Lord, desiring, fearing, and hoping for what is with Him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned them in His Book to His Prophet عليه السلام, informed them of what He gave them, that He settled them in His proximity, admitted them into His Paradise, and made their fear and dread secure." I said, "May I be your ransom, if I rise in the latter part of the night, what should I say when I rise?" He said, "Say: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the God of the Messengers; and all praise belongs to Allah, who gives life to the dead and raises those who are in the graves." For when you say it, the defilement of Shayṭān and his whispering will go away from you, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

1392 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “When you hear the crowing of the rooster, then say: ‘Glorified and Holy is the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Your mercy has preceded Your wrath. There is no god but You. Glory be to You, and with Your praise, I have done evil and ‘I have wronged myself, so forgive me’ Indeed, none forgives sins except You.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Learn five qualities from the rooster: its adherence to the times of salat (prayer), protective jealousy, generosity, courage, and frequent crowing."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Learn three qualities from the crow: its concealment when mating, its early rising in seeking sustenance, and its cautiousness.

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has an angel in the form of a white rooster. Its head is beneath the Throne, and its feet are in the depths of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the east and a wing in the west. The roosters do not crow until it crows. Then when it crows, it flaps its two wings and then says: Glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah, the Magnificent, the One of whom: “There is nothing like unto Him.” He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, answers it and says: “One who knows what you say will not swear falsely by Me.”
And it is narrated: "That concerning it, there was revealed 'And the birds with wings outspread; each knows its salat (prayer) and its glorification.' "

And it is narrated: “The bearers of the Throne today are four. One of them is in the form of a rooster, seeking sustenance from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the birds; one is in the form of a lion, seeking sustenance from Allah, Exalted is He, for the wild beasts; one is in the form of a bull, seeking sustenance from Allah, Exalted is He, for the livestock; and one of them is in the form of the children of Adam, seeking sustenance from Allah, Exalted is He, for the children of Adam عليه السلام. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will become eight. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:” “And the Throne of your Lord, above them, on that Day, will be carried by eight.”

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: "And during the night, perform Tahajjud with it as an extra for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station." Thus, the night prayer became obligatory upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'فَتَهَجَّدْ'; while for others it is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) and a supererogatory act.
1399 - The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said in his counsel to ‘Alī, peace be upon him: "O ‘Alī, hold fast to salat al-layl, hold fast to salat al-layl, hold fast to salat al-layl."

And it is narrated: That whoever recites in the first two rak'ahs of Salat al-Layl, in each rak'ah of them, al-Hamd once and "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad" thirty times, he finishes, and there is no sin between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that He forgives it.

And it is narrated: "Whoever recites in the Witr prayer the two protective chapters and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad,' it will be said to him: 'Rejoice, O servant of Allah, for Allah has accepted your Witr.'"
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: Qunoot is in every two rak‘ahs in the optional and obligatory prayers.

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, used to say in the qunut of the Witr prayer: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being to, take me under Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. Indeed, You decree and none may decree over You. Glory be to You, Lord of the House. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance. I believe in You and rely upon You. There is no power and no strength except through You, O Most Merciful.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The one among you who is longest in qunūt in the abode of this world will be the one among you with the longest rest on the Day of Resurrection at the Standing."
Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “The qunut on the Day of Jumu‘ah is the glorification of Allah, salat upon the Prophet of Allah, and the words of relief.” Then this supplication.

And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “Whoever says in his Witr, when he performs Witr: ‘I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, and I repent to Him,’ seventy times, and persists in that until a year passes, Allah will record him with Himself among ‘those who seek forgiveness at daybreak,’ and Paradise and forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, become obligatory for him.”

'Abdullāh ibn Abī Ya'fūr narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Seek forgiveness from Allah in the Witr seventy times, raising your left hand and counting the seeking of forgiveness with your right hand. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to seek forgiveness from Allah in the Witr seventy times and would say:" "This is the station of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire," seven times.

And ‘Abdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “You supplicate against the enemy in the Witr, and if you wish you may name them; and you seek forgiveness, and you raise your hands in the Witr level with your face, and if you wish, you open your garment.”
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them both, the Master of the Worshippers, used to say: "Al-ʿAfw, Al-ʿAfw (Pardon, pardon)," three hundred times in the Witr at dawn.

Hadith 1409 — Maʿrūf ibn Kharrabūdh narrated from one of them — meaning Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام — who said: "Say in the qunūt of Witr: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, and whatever is in them and whatever is between them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne. O Allah, You are: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth." And You are Allah, the adornment of the heavens and the earth. And You are Allah, the beauty of the heavens and the earth. And You are Allah, the support of the heavens and the earth. And You are Allah, the sustainer of the heavens and the earth. And You are Allah, the helper of those who cry out for help. And You are Allah, the aid of those who seek relief. And You are Allah, the one who relieves the distressed. And You are Allah, the one who eases the grief of the sorrowful. And You are Allah, the one who answers the supplication of the compelled. And You are Allah, the God of the worlds. And You are Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. And You are Allah, the remover of evil. And You are Allah; through You every need is brought down, O Allah. Nothing turns back Your anger except Your forbearance, and nothing saves from Your punishment except Your mercy, and nothing saves from You except humble entreaty to You. So grant me, from Your presence, O my God, a mercy by which You make me needless of the mercy of anyone besides You, by the power through which You gave life to all that is in the lands, and by which You raise the dead of the servants. And do not destroy me in grief until You forgive me, have mercy on me, make known to me the answering of my supplication, grant me well-being until the end of my term, pardon my stumble, do not let my enemy rejoice over me, and do not give him power over my neck. O Allah, if You raise me, then who is there that can lower me? And if You lower me, then who is there that can raise me? And if You destroy me, then who is there that can come between You and me, or object to You regarding anything of my affair? And I have known that there is no injustice in Your judgment, and no haste in Your vengeance. Only one who fears missing out acts hastily, and only the weak needs injustice. And You are exalted above that, O my God. So do

It is narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would say in the latter part of his Witr, while standing: “My Lord, I have done evil and wronged myself, and wretched is what I have done, and these are my two hands as recompense for what they have done.” He said: then he would stretch out both his hands together before his face and say: “And this is my neck, humbled before You for what it has brought.” He said: then he would lower his head and humble his neck, then say: “And here I am before You, so take for Yourself from my soul that by which You are satisfied, until You are pleased. To You belongs the return in reproach; I will not return, I will not return, I will not return.” He said: and by Allah, when he said, “I will not return,” he did not return.
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: "The qunūt in the witr prayer is seeking forgiveness, and in the obligatory prayer it is supplication."

Hadith 1412 — Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to supplicate in the qunut of the Witr with this supplication: "O Allah, You created me with decree, arrangement, and insight, without negligence, and You brought me forth from "three darknesses" by Your power and strength. I engage with the world, then I contend with it, then I part from it. You gave me therein pasture and provision, and You made me perceive guidance therein; so excellent a Lord You are, and excellent a Master. O One who honored me, ennobled me, and blessed me, I seek refuge in You from Zaqqum, and I seek refuge in You from al-Hamim, and I seek refuge in You from a resting place in the Fire, among the layers of the Fire, in the shades of the Fire, on the Day of the Fire, O Lord of the Fire. O Allah, I ask You for a resting place in Paradise among its rivers, its trees, its fruits, its fragrant herbs, its servants, and its spouses. O Allah, I ask You for the best of good: Your good pleasure and Paradise; and I seek refuge in You from the worst of evil: Your wrath and the Fire. This is the station of one seeking refuge in You from the Fire, three times. O Allah, place Your fear in all of my body, and make my heart more intensely fearful of You than it is, and appoint for me in every day and night a share and portion of action in obedience to You and pursuit of Your good pleasure. O Allah, You are the utmost end of my goal, my hope, my request, and my seeking. I ask You, O my God, for the perfection of faith, the completion of certainty, the truthfulness of reliance upon You, and good opinion of You. O my Master, make my beneficence multiplied, my salat (prayer) humble supplication, my du'a (supplication) answered, my deed accepted, my effort appreciated, my sin forgiven, and teach me from You "radiance and joy" And may Allah bless Muhammad and his family.
1414 - Zurarah narrated from him that he said: "Qunoot is in all prayers."
Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ḥalabī that he said: He said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Shall I mention the Imams عليهم السلام in the salat (prayer)?” He said: “Summarize them.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whatever you whisper to your Lord in salat (prayer) is not considered speech.

And it is narrated from Abū Wallād Ḥafṣ ibn Sālim al-Ḥannāṭ that he said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “There is no harm in a man praying two rakʿahs of al-Witr, then leaving to attend to his need, then returning to pray one rakʿah.”
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About the qunūt in the witr, he said: “Before the rukūʿ.” He said: “If I forget, do I perform qunūt when I raise my head?” So he said: “No.”

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: "Pray the two rakʿahs of Fajr before Fajr, at its time, or shortly after it. In the first rakʿah, recite al-Ḥamd and "Say: O disbelievers" and in the second, al-Ḥamd and "Say: He is Allah, One."
Then al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "What ending is more decisive than the taslim?"

It is narrated from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj that he said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, I may be in the Witr prayer, and I may already have intended the fast, and I may be in supplication, and I fear dawn, and I dislike cutting off my supplication for myself and drinking water, while the water jug is before me. He said: So he said to me, “Then step toward it one step, two steps, or three, and drink, and return to your place, and do not cut off your supplication for yourself.”

And Zurārah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "When you finish the Witr, say: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Mighty, the Wise' three times. Then say: 'O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O Self-Sufficient, O Generous, provide for me from trade its greatest in bounty, its broadest in sustenance, and its best in outcome for me, for there is no good in that which has no outcome.'

Lie down between the two rak'ahs of Fajr and the two rak'ahs of the morning prayer on your right side facing the qiblah, and say in your reclining: “I have held fast to the firm handhold of Allah, which has no breaking apart, and I have sought protection in the strong rope of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humankind. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn.” Then say: “In the Name of Allah, I have placed my side down for Allah. I have consigned my affair to Allah. I seek my need from Allah. I have relied upon Allah. Allah is sufficient for me, and excellent is the Trustee. And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed Allah accomplishes His command. Allah has appointed a measure for everything. O Allah, whoever begins the morning with his need directed to a created being, then indeed my need and my desire are toward You.” And recite five verses from the end of Surat Al 'Imran: “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...” up to His saying: “Indeed, You do not fail in the promise.” And send blessings upon Muhammad and his family one hundred times, for indeed it...

It has been narrated: "Whoever sends blessings upon Muḥammad and his family one hundred times between the two rakʿahs of al-Fajr and the two rakʿahs of al-Ghadāh, Allah will protect his face from the heat of the Fire. And whoever says one hundred times: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent, and with His praise; I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, and I repent to Him,' Allah will build for him a house in Paradise. And whoever recites twenty-one times "Say: He is Allah, One." Allah will build for him a house in Paradise; and if he recites it forty times, Allah will forgive him."
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah asked Abā Ibrāhīm Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a man who misses the Witr prayer. So he said: “He should make it up as Witr, always.”

1425 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whatever you miss during the night, make it up during the day. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.' "
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Making up the Night Prayer after the Morning Prayer and after the Afternoon Prayer is among the hidden secrets of the Family of Muhammad."

From Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, that there came to him, among what came in reply to his questions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAmrī, may Allah sanctify his soul: As for what you asked about regarding salat (prayer) at sunrise and at sunset: even if it is as people say, that the sun rises between the two horns of Shayṭān and sets between the two horns of Shayṭān, then Shayṭān’s nose is not humiliated by anything better than salat. So perform it, and humiliate the nose of Shayṭān.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family (SAWW), said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, boasts to His angels of the servant who makes up the night prayer during the day. So He says: O My angels, look at My servant making up what I did not make obligatory upon him; I make you witness that I have indeed forgiven him.

Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿIjlī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: “The best making-up of salat al-layl is in the hour in which it escaped you, at the end of the night; and there is no harm in making it up during the day, and before the sun declines.”

And it was narrated from Murāzim ibn Ḥakīm al-Azdī that he said: I had been ill for four months and did not perform any nāfilah prayer during them, so I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, I was ill for four months and did not perform any nāfilah prayer. So he said: There is no making up required upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever Allah has caused to overcome him, then Allah is more entitled to excuse him in it.

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man fell ill and so left the nafilah prayer. He said: O Muhammad, it is not obligatory. If he makes it up, then it is a good deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.
Sulaiman ibn Khalid asked him about making up the Witr after midday, so he said: "Make it up as Witr always, just as it was missed."
Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān asked him and said to him: "I reach the morning having missed the Witr until the night; so how should I make it up?" He said: "Like for like."
And Ḥarīz narrated from him that he said: "My father, peace be upon him, would sometimes make up twenty Witr prayers in a single night."
Ali ibn Atiyyah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "Fajr is that which, when you see it, appears spread out horizontally, as though it were the whiteness of the River Sūrā."
And it has been narrated: “The time of the morning prayer is when the dawn spreads across horizontally and gives a good light.”

And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "You say, when the dawn rises: "Praise be to Allah, the Splitter of the dawn. Glory be to Allah, the Lord of evening and morning. O Allah, bring morning upon the family of Muḥammad with blessing, well-being, joy, and comfort of the eye. O Allah, You send down in the night and the day whatever You will, so send down upon me and upon my household from the blessings of the heavens and the earth a lawful, good, abundant provision by which You make me free of need from all Your creation."

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about sleeping after the Fajr prayer. He said, “Indeed, sustenance is spread out during that hour, so I dislike that a man should sleep during that hour.”

Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Iblīs only spreads his soldiers of the night from the time the sun sets until the disappearance of the twilight, and he spreads his soldiers of the day from the time the fajr rises until the rising of the sun. And he mentioned that the Prophet of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say: "Increase the dhikr of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during these two hours, and seek refuge in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from the evil of Iblīs and his soldiers, and seek protection for your small children during these two hours, for they are two hours of heedlessness."

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The morning sleep is inauspicious: it drives away sustenance, causes the complexion to pale, makes it ugly, and changes it. It is the sleep of every unfortunate one. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distributes sustenance between the rising of al-Fajr and the rising of the sun, so beware of that sleep."

Al-Baqir عليه السلام said: "Sleeping at the beginning of the day is wastefulness, the midday nap is a blessing, sleeping after al-'Asr is foolishness, and sleeping between the two night prayers deprives one of sustenance."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever you see sleeping on his face, wake him up."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Three things contain that which is detested by Allah, Mighty and Majestic: sleeping without wakefulness, laughing without wonder, and eating while full.

A Bedouin came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: “O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I used to have a strong memory, and I have become forgetful.” He said: “Did you used to take a midday nap?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “And you left that?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Resume it.” So he resumed it, and his mental sharpness returned to him.

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: There are five who do not sleep: one distressed over blood he is to shed, the possessor of abundant wealth who has no trustworthy keeper, one who speaks falsehood and slander among people for a worldly gain he attains, one encumbered with much wealth while having no wealth himself, and one who loves a beloved and anticipates separation from him.
And it is narrated: “Take a midday nap, for indeed Allah nourishes the fasting person during his sleep and gives him drink.”
And it is narrated: "Take a midday nap, for indeed the Shaytan does not take a midday nap."

And he عليه السلام said: Sleeping in the early morning is a misfortune: it deprives one of sustenance and pales the complexion. The manna and the quails used to descend upon the Children of Israel between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun, so whoever slept during that hour, his share would not descend. Then when he awoke and did not see his share, he became in need of asking and seeking.

And Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'By those who distribute commands' He said: 'The angels distribute the sustenance of the children of Adam from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun. Therefore, whoever sleeps during this period sleeps away their sustenance.'

Muʿammar ibn Khallād narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: When he was in Khurāsān, after performing the Fajr prayer, he would sit in his place of salat until the sun rose. Then a pouch containing siwāks would be brought to him, and he would use them one by one. Then frankincense would be brought to him, and he would chew it, then leave that aside. Then the muṣḥaf would be brought to him, and he would read from it.
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever sits in his place of prayer from the Fajr prayer until the rising of the sun, Allah will shield him from the Fire."

And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from al-Sadiq, from his father, peace be upon them, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, had a staff with a pointed end. He would lean upon it, and he would bring it out on the two Eids and pray toward it.”
Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: "The prayer of the two Eids is obligatory, and the eclipse prayer is obligatory."

From Zurarah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "The prayer of the two Eids with the Imam is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and there is no salat (prayer) before them nor after them on that day until zawal (noon)."
And Samāʿah ibn Mihrān narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: "There is no prayer in the two Eids except with an Imam, and if you pray alone, then there is no harm."
And Zurārah ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There is no prayer on the day of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha except with a just Imam.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the salat of al-Adha and al-Fitr, and he said: "Pray them as two rak'ahs, in congregation or otherwise than in congregation, and say takbir seven times and five times."
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: "My father عليه السلام fell ill on the Day of al-Adha, so he prayed two rak'ahs in his house, then offered the sacrifice."

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever does not attend the congregation of the people in the two ʿĪds, then let him perform ghusl, apply whatever fragrance he finds, and pray in his house alone just as he prays in congregation."

And Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Going out on the day of al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā to the open prayer area is good for whoever is able to go out to it." He said: So I said, "What do you think if he is sick and is not able to go out—should he pray in his house?" He said: "No."
Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd, who said: I asked him about the ghusl (ritual bath) of al-Aḍḥā. He said: “It is obligatory except at Minā.”
And it has been narrated: "The ghusl (ritual bath) for the two Eids is a sunnah (recommended practice)."

1463 - Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the woman: is she to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on the day of Jumuʿah, al-Fiṭr, al-Aḍḥā, and the Day of ʿArafah? He said: “Yes, all of these ghusls are upon her.”
And ʿAlī عليه السلام would eat on the Day of al-Fiṭr before going out to the prayer place, and he would not eat on the Day of al-Aḍḥā until he slaughtered.

Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Do not go out on the Day of al-Fitr until you eat something, and do not eat anything on the Day of al-Adha except from your sacrificial offering and your udhiyah, if you are able to do so. If you are not able, then you are excused. He said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام also said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام would not eat anything on the Day of al-Adha until he ate from his udhiyah, and he would not go out on the Day of al-Fitr until he had eaten and given the fitrah.' Then he said, 'And likewise are we.'

And Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, عليهما السلام, who said: "The sunnah (prophetic tradition) for the people of the cities is that they go out from their cities on the two Eids, except the people of Makkah, for they perform salat (prayer) in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām."

1467 - And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "It is not appropriate for the prayer of the two Eids to be performed in a roofed mosque, nor in a house; rather, it is performed in the open desert or in an exposed place."

Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah, from his father, peace be upon them: That when he would go out on the day of al-Fitr and al-Adha, he refused to have a carpet brought for him to pray upon. He would say: “This is a day on which the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, would go out until he was exposed to the horizons of the sky, then he would place his forehead upon the earth.”

And Isma'il ibn Jabir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Tell me about the prayer of the two Eids—are there an adhan and an iqamah in them? He said: There is neither adhan nor iqamah in them, but it is called out, 'al-salat, al-salat,' three times. There is no minbar in them; the minbar is not moved from its place. Rather, something resembling a minbar is made of clay for the Imam, so he stands upon it and addresses the people, then he comes down.

And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Do not make up the Witr prayer of your night, meaning on the two Eids, if you missed it, until you have prayed the midday prayer on that day."

Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Hāshimī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "There are two rakʿahs from the sunnah which are not prayed in any place except in al-Madīnah, and they are prayed in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله before going out to the muṣallā on the two ʿEids. That applies only in al-Madīnah, because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed it."

Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā when they coincide on the day of al-Jumuʿah. He said: "They came together in the time of ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he said: 'Whoever wishes to come to the Jumuʿah, let him come; and whoever remains seated, it will not harm him, and let him perform the ẓuhr prayer.'" And he عليه السلام delivered two sermons, in which he combined the sermon of the ʿEid and the sermon of the Jumuʿah.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself." He عليه السلام said: "The one who gives the fitrah." Then it was said to him: "And remembers the name of his Lord, then prays." He عليه السلام said: "He went out to the prayer ground and performed the prayer."
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī: That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he went out to the Eid, would not return by the path in which he had begun; he would take a different path.

And Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If you intend to depart on the day of Eid, and dawn breaks while you are still in the town, then do not leave until you have witnessed that Eid."

1477 - Saʿd ibn Saʿd narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Regarding a traveler to Mecca and elsewhere: is the salat of the two Eids, al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā, incumbent upon him? He said: "Yes, except at Minā on the Day of Sacrifice."

Jābir narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: "When the first day of Shawwāl arrives, a caller calls out: O believers, go forth to your rewards." Then he said: "O Jābir, the rewards of Allah are not like the rewards of these kings." Then he said: "It is the Day of Rewards."

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام looked at some people on the day of Fiṭr playing and laughing, so he said to his companions, turning toward them: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the month of Ramaḍān a racetrack for His creation, in which they race through obedience to Him toward His good pleasure. So some people went ahead in it and won, while others fell behind and failed. So how astonishing, utterly astonishing, is the one who laughs and plays on the day in which the doers of good are rewarded and the deficient ones fail. By Allah, if the covering were removed, a doer of good would be occupied by his good, and an evildoer by his evil.

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "There is no Eid for the Muslims, whether Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr, except that grief is renewed therein for the family of Muhammad." It was said: "And why is that?" He said: "Because they see their right in the hands of others."

1481 - And Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the takbīr in the two Eids, and he said: “There are twelve takbīrs: seven in the first and five in the second. When you stand in the salat (prayer), say one takbīr and say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, You are worthy of majesty and greatness, and worthy of generosity, omnipotence, power, authority, and might. I ask You on this day which You have made an Eid for the Muslims, and a ذخْر and increase for Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, to send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and to bless Your near angels and Your sent prophets, and to forgive us and all the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O Allah, I ask You for the best of what Your righteous servants have asked You, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what Your sincere servants have sought refuge from.” Allah is the Greatest, the first of everything and its last, the originator of everything and its ultimate end, the knower of everything and its return, and the destination of everything is to Him and its return is to Him, and the arranger of affairs, and the raiser of... “those who are in the graves” the acceptor of deeds, the initiator of hidden things, and the manifester of secrets. Allah is the Greatest, tremendous in dominion, intense in might, living and not dying, everlasting and not passing away. “When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.” Allah is the Greatest. Voices are humbled to You, faces submit to You, eyes are bewildered before You, and tongues fall short of Your greatness. All forelocks are in Your hand, and the measures of all affairs are to You; none decides in them other than You, and nothing of them is completed without You. Allah is the Greatest. Your protection encompasses everything, Your might overpowers everything, Your command penetrates everything, everything stands through You, everything humbles itself before Your greatness, everything is abased before Your might, everything submits to Your power, and everything yields to Your dominion. Allah is the Greatest. And you recite al-Ḥamd and “Sabbihi sma Rabbika al-Aʿlā,” then pronoun

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام delivered a sermon on the day of Eid al-Fitr and said: "All praise belongs to Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve set up equals with their Lord." We do not associate anything with Allah, and we do not take any guardian besides Him. "All praise belongs to Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs all praise in the world and the Hereafter; and He is the All-wise, the All-aware. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it, and He is the All-merciful, the All-forgiving." Such is Allah. "There is no god but He; to Him is the return." And praise belongs to Allah, the One who "holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed Allah is surely most kind and merciful to mankind." O Allah, have mercy on us by Your mercy and encompass us with Your forgiveness; surely You are the Most High, the Most Great.
