And praise belongs to Allah, from whose mercy none is despaired, from whose blessing none is excluded, from whose relief none is made hopeless, and from whose worship none may turn away; by His word the seven heavens stood, the outspread earth became settled, the firm mountains were fixed, the fertilizing winds blew, the clouds moved in the atmosphere of the sky, and the seas stood within their bounds. He is the God over them and the Subduer; the mighty are humbled before Him, the arrogant become small before Him, and the worlds submit to Him willingly and unwillingly. We praise Him as He praised Himself and as He deserves; we seek His help, His forgiveness, and His guidance, and we bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone without partner. He knows what souls conceal, what the seas cover, what darkness hides, and no hidden thing is absent from Him. "And not a leaf falls" from a tree, nor any grain in darknesses, except that He knows it. There is no god but He. "And neither anything fresh nor dry except that it is in a clear book." And He knows what the doers do, along what course they proceed, and to what turning-place they will return. We seek guidance from Allah through guidance, and we bear witness that Muhammad is His servant, His Prophet, and His Messenger to His creation, His trustee over His r

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام delivered a sermon on Eid al-Adha and said: "Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no deity but Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, and to Him belongs gratitude for what He has bestowed upon us. And all praise belongs to Allah for what He has provided us from the cattle of the grazing livestock."

And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to begin with the takbīr when he prayed the ẓuhr prayer on the Day of Naḥr, and he would stop the takbīr on the last of the Days of Tashrīq at dawn. He would recite the takbīr after every salat (prayer), saying: “Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise.” When he reached the prayer ground, he stepped forward and led the people in salat (prayer) without an adhān or iqāmah. When he finished the salat (prayer), he ascended the minbar and began, saying: “Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, equal to the weight of His Throne, the pleasure of His Self, and the number of the drops of His sky and His seas. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names, and praise belongs to Allah until He is pleased, and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving. Allah is the Greatest, supremely great, exalted in majesty, and a God mighty in honor, merciful and tender; He pardons despite having power, and none despairs of His mercy except the misguided. Allah is the Greatest, greatly; there is no god but Allah abundantly; and glory be to Allah, ever-compassionate, all-powerful. Praise belongs to Allah: we praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, seek His guidance, and bear witness that there is no god but He, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided and attained a mighty success; and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly gone far astray and suffered a manifest loss.” I counsel you, servants of Allah, to have taqwā of Allah, to remember death often, and to renounce this world, which those before you did not truly enjoy and which will not remain for anyone after you. Your course in it is the course of those who have passed: do you not see that it has worn away, announced its passing, its familiar good has become strange, and it has turned away swiftly? It announces annihilation, and its inhabitant is driven on toward death. Its sweetness has turned bitter, its clarity has become turbid, and nothing remains of it except a remnant like the little left in a waterskin and a sip like the sip left in a vessel, which the thirsty one sips yet it does not quench his thirst. So resolve, servants of Allah, to depart from this abode, whose people are decre

1485 - And in al-ʿIlal, which is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān al-Naysābūrī, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is mentioned that he heard them from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: That the day of al-Fiṭr was only made the Eid so that it may be a gathering for the Muslims in which they gather and come forth to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and glorify Him for what He has bestowed upon them. Thus it is a day of Eid, a day of gathering, a day of breaking the fast, a day of zakat, a day of desire, and a day of humble supplication. And because it is the first day of the year in which eating and drinking become lawful, since the first of the months of the year according to the people of truth is the month of Ramaḍān, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loved that they should have in that a gathering in which they praise Him and sanctify Him. And the takbir was only made more numerous in it than in other salat because takbir is but magnification of Allah and glorification for what He guided to and granted well-being. "And that you may magnify Allah for what He has guided you to, and that you may be grateful." And twelve takbirs were only made in it because in every two rakʿahs there are twelve takbirs. Seven were made in the first and five in the second, and they were not made equal because the sunnah in the obligatory salat is that it begins with seven takbirs; therefore it was begun here with seven takbirs. And five takbirs were made in the second because the opening prohibition by takbir in the day and night is five takbirs, so that the takbir in the two rakʿahs together may be odd, odd.

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “In the salat of the two Eids, when the people are five or seven, then they perform the prayer in congregation just as they do on the day of al-Jumuʿah.” And he said: “He performs qunut in the second rakʿah.” He said: I said, “Is it permissible without a turban?” He said: “Yes, and the turban is more beloved to me.”

Hadith 1487 — Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the takbir in the two Eids, and he said: “They are twelve: seven in the first and five in the other. When you stand for the prayer, say one takbir, then say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, You are the Lord of majesty and greatness, and the Lord of generosity, might, power, authority, and honor. I ask You on this day which You have made an Eid for the Muslims, and for Muhammad—may Your blessings be upon him and his family—a ذخْر and increase, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You send blessings upon Your near angels and Your sent prophets, and that You forgive us and all believing men and believing women, and Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O Allah, I ask You from the good of what Your sent servants asked You for, and I seek refuge in You from the evil from which Your devoted servants sought refuge.” Allah is greater, the first of everything and its last, the originator of everything and its final end, knowing every thing and its return; the destination of every thing is to Him and its return is to Him; and He is the manager of affairs and the raiser of... “those who are in the graves” the accepter of deeds, the bringer forth of hidden things, the discloser of secrets. Allah is greater, tremendous in dominion, intense in might, living and never dying, everlasting and never passing away. “When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.” Allah is greater. Voices are humbled before You, faces submit before You, sights are bewildered before You, and tongues grow weary from describing Your greatness. All forelocks are in Your hand, and the measures of all affairs belong to You; none judges concerning them other than You, and nothing of them is completed without You. Allah is greater. Your preservation encompasses every thing, Your might subdues every thing, Your command penetrates every thing, and every thing stands by You. Every thing humbles itself before Your greatness, is abased before Your honor, surrenders to Your power, and yields before Your sovereignty. Allah is greater. And you recite al-Hamd and... “By the sun and its morning brightness” and you bow

69 - Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said: “For ghusl (ritual bath), a sāʿ of water, and for wudu (ablution), a mudd of water. The sāʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is five amdād, and the mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams. The dirham is six dānīqs, and the dānīq is the weight of six grains, and the grain is the weight of two grains of barley from the middle-sized grain, not from its small ones nor from its large ones.”

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Wudu (ablution) is a mudd, and ghusl (ritual bath) is a sa'. There will come people after me who will regard that as too little; those are against my sunnah (prophetic tradition). The one who remains firm upon my sunnah (prophetic tradition) will be with me in the enclosure of holiness."

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام was asked about a man who needed wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and could not obtain water, then found water in an amount sufficient for wudu for one hundred dirhams. Is it obligatory upon him to buy it and perform wudu with it, or should he perform tayammum? “Rather, he should buy it. Something similar happened to me, so I bought it and performed wudu, and a large amount of wealth would not grieve me because of that.”

Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his wife performed ghusl using five amdad from one vessel.” Zurarah said to him, “How was it done?” He عليه السلام said: “He began and put his hand into the water before her, then cleansed his private part. Then she put hers in and cleansed her private part. Then he poured water, and she poured water over herself, until they finished. The amount with which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله performed ghusl was three amdad, and that with which she performed ghusl was two mudd. It was only sufficient for both of them because they both shared in it together. But whoever performs ghusl alone by himself must have a saʿ.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "A man may worship Allah for forty years, yet he does not obey Him in wudu (ablution), because he washes what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be wiped."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: “When four things become widespread, four things appear: when fornication spreads, earthquakes appear; when zakat is withheld, livestock perish; when rulers act unjustly in judgment, rain is withheld from the sky; and when covenants are violated, the polytheists are given victory over the Muslims.”

And it is narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that he said: If Allah, the Exalted, becomes angry with a nation, then does not send down punishment upon it, its prices become high, its lifespans become short, its merchants do not profit, its fruits do not grow well, its rivers do not become abundant, its rains are withheld from it, and its wicked ones are set in authority over it.

Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام went out one day with his companions to seek rain. Then he found an ant that had raised one of its legs toward the sky while saying: “O Allah, we are a creation among Your creation; we have no independence from Your provision, so do not destroy us because of the sins of the children of Ādam.” So Sulaymān عليه السلام said to his companions: “Return, for you have been given rain by other than yourselves.”

1491 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He wishes to bring benefit through rain, He commands the clouds, so they take water from beneath the Throne; and when He does not intend vegetation, He commands the clouds, so they take water from the sea." It was said: "The water of the sea is salty." He said: "Indeed the clouds purify it."
Saʿdān narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: There is no drop that descends from the sky except that with it is an angel who places it in the location that has been decreed for it.

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Not a single day has come upon the people of the world since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created it, except that the sky in it sends down rain; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, places that wherever He wills."

1494 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: No wind has ever come forth except according to a measure, except in the time of ‘Ād, for it rebelled against its keepers and came out like the eye of a needle, so it destroyed the people of ‘Ād. And no rain has ever fallen except according to a weight, except in the time of Nūḥ, peace be upon him, for it rebelled against its keepers and came out like the eye of a needle, and Allah drowned the people of Nūḥ, peace be upon him, by it.
The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "The clouds are the sieve of the rain; were it not for that, it would spoil everything upon which it fell."

Abu Basir asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about thunder: what does it say? He said: “It is like a man who is among the camels and drives them on, saying, ‘Hai, Hai,’ something like that.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, then what is the case of lightning?” So he said: “Those are the whips of the angels; they strike the clouds and drive them to the place in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed the rain.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Thunder is the voice of the angel, and lightning is his whip."

And it is narrated: “Thunder is the sound of an angel, larger than a fly and smaller than a wasp. So it is fitting for the one who hears the sound of thunder to say: ‘Glory be to the One whom...’ ‘the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels [also] out of fear of Him.’ ”

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, used to say, when he prayed for rain: O Allah, give water to Your servants and Your animals, spread Your mercy, and revive Your dead land. He would repeat it three times.

And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon regarding the Prayer for Rain, saying: 'All praise is due to Allah, the Bestower of abundant blessings, the Reliever of distress, and the Creator of life.' He Who made the heavens a support for His Throne, the mountains pegs for the earth, and the earth a bedding for His servants. He placed His angels on its edges, and the bearers of the Throne on its sides. By His Might, He established the foundations of the Throne. With His Light, He illuminated the rays of the sun, and with His radiance, He dispelled the darkness of the shadows. He caused springs to burst forth from the earth, made the moon a light, and the stars as shining beacons. Then He ascended and reigned supreme. He created and perfected, established order and ruled. The arrogance of the proud humbled itself before Him, and the humility of the needy turned to Him in supplication. O Allah, by Your lofty status, Your exalted position, Your overflowing grace, and Your encompassing path, I ask You to bless Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, as he devoted himself to You, called others to Your worship, fulfilled Your covenant, enforced Your laws, followed Your signs, was Your servant, Your Prophet, and Your trustee upon Your covenant to Your servants, the upholder of Your laws, the supporter of those who obey You, and the one who dispels the excuses of those who disobey You. O Allah, grant Muhammad the greatest share of Your mercy, the brightest face of those who receive Your abundant gifts, and the nearest of the prophets to You in proximity on the Day of Resurrection, the most abundant of them in receiving Your pleasure, and the largest of them in the gathering of his followers in Your gardens, for he never prostrated to stones, never worshiped trees, never committed unlawful acts, nor shed blood unjustly. O Allah, we have come forth to You when harsh constraints have gripped us, difficulties have confined us, adversities have afflicted us, and our pastures have withered. The oppressive years have taken hold over us, and the signs of generosity have been withheld from us. We are thirsty and desire the sounds of showers to fill our hearts. You are the hope of the distressed and the trust of the seeker. We call upon You when the people despair, when the clouds are withheld, and livestock perish. O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, b

Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: "The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform two rak‘ahs for seeking rain and would seek rain while seated." And he said: "He began with the prayer before the sermon and recited aloud."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, turning his cloak when he sought rain. He said: "It was a sign between him and his companions that drought had turned into abundance."

A group from the people of al-Kufah came to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام and said to him, “O Commander of the Faithful, supplicate for us with supplications for seeking rain.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام called al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and said, “O Ḥasan, supplicate.” Then al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “O Allah, stir up for us the clouds by the opening of the gates, with abundant water and cloud-masses, with pouring and streaming, O Bestower. Give us covering, abundant, delightful rain. Open its closures, make easy its release, and hasten its driving with moist airs into the valleys, O Bestower, with the downpour of water, O Ever-Doer. Give us rain: drops, drizzle, pouring, layered and all-covering, general and comprehensive, abundant, thick, merciful, sprinkling and spreading, vast, sufficient, swift, wholesome, blessed, spreading broadly and striking the wide lands, overflowing, heaped, and brimful. And water our plains and our mountains, our desert-dwellers and our town-dwellers, until by it You make our prices low, and bless by it our estates and our cities. Show us provision present and dearness absent. Āmīn, O Lord of the worlds.” Then he said to al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, “Supplicate.” So al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said: “O Allah, Giver of good things from their proper places, Sender down of mercies from their sources, and Mover of blessings upon their people: from You is the saving rain, and You are the Help sought for help. We are the sinners and the people of sins, and You are the One from whom forgiveness is sought, the All-Forgiving. There is no god but You. O Allah, send the sky upon us as continuous abundant rain, and give us the saving rain, pouring and plentiful; life-giving rain, vast, ample, streaming, wholesome, fertile, abundant, overflowing, surging and resounding; incessant and sweeping, spreading and widespread, hanging low, general, a deluge, driving rain against rain in force, and from which drops emerge without false lightning and without thunder proving untrue. By it You revive the weak among Your servants and bring to life the dead of Your lands, as a grace upon us from You. Āmīn, O Lord of the worlds.” Before his speech was completed, Allah poured down water abundantly. Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه was asked, and it was said to him, “O Abā ʿAbdillāh, is this something they were taught?” He said, “Woe to you! Have you not heard the say

And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out to seek rain and said to al-ʿAbbās, “Stand and supplicate to your Lord and seek rain.” And he said, “O Allah, we seek a means to You through the uncle of Your Prophet.” So al-ʿAbbās stood, praised Allah, and extolled Him. Then he said: “O Allah, indeed with You are clouds, and indeed with You is rain, so spread the clouds and send down water in it, then send it down upon us, strengthen thereby the roots, bring forth thereby the branches, and revive thereby the crops. O Allah, we are intercessors to You on behalf of those among our beasts and our cattle who have no speech; accept our intercession for ourselves and our families. O Allah, we call upon none but You, and we desire none but You. O Allah, give us a gentle, beneficial, all-covering, resounding rain. O Allah, we complain to You of the hunger of every hungry one, the nakedness of every unclothed one, the fear of every fearful one, and the hunger of every famished one who calls upon Allah.”

1506 - Sayyid al-'Abidin 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام said: “Indeed, among the signs that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for the people, from that which they need, is the sea which Allah created between the heaven and the earth.” He said: “And indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has ordained therein the courses of the sun, the moon, and the stars, and He ordained all of that upon the celestial sphere. Then He appointed over the sphere an angel, with whom are seventy thousand angels, and they rotate the sphere. So when they rotate it, the sun, the moon, and the stars rotate with it, and descend into their stations which Allah the Exalted ordained for their day and night. Then when the sins of the servants become many, and Allah loves to make them seek His good pleasure by a sign from His signs, He commands the angel entrusted with the sphere to move the sphere away from its courses.” He said: “Then the angel commands the seventy thousand angels: Remove the sphere from its courses.” He said: “So they move it, and the sun comes to be in that sea in which the sphere had been, and its light is obscured and its color changes. Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills to magnify the sign, it is immersed in the sea according to how He wills to frighten His servants by the sign.” He said: “And that is at the time of the eclipse of the sun, and likewise is done with the moon. Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills to uncover it and return it to its course, He commands the angel entrusted with the sphere to return the sphere to its course. So he returns the sphere, and the sun returns to its course.” He said: “Then it emerges from the water while it is dim, and the moon is like that.” He said: Then 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام said: “Indeed, none is alarmed by the two signs, nor fears, except one who is from our Shi'ah. So when that occurs from them, then flee to Allah the Exalted and turn back to Him.”

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: Indeed, the sun and the moon are two signs from among the signs of Allah. They move according to His decree and end according to His command. They do not eclipse due to the death of anyone nor due to the life of anyone. So when one of them eclipses, hasten to your mosques.
The sun was eclipsed during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and he led them in prayer until a man could look at another man whose feet had become wet from his sweat.
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: about the wind, the darkness that occurs in the sky, and eclipses So al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “Their salat (prayer) is the same.”

And in the causes mentioned by al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said: The salat for the eclipse was only instituted because it is among the signs of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and it is not known whether it has appeared as a mercy or as a punishment. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم loved that his community should turn in alarm to its Creator and its Merciful One at that time, so that He may avert from them its evil and protect them from its harm, just as He turned it away from the people of Yūnus عليه السلام when they implored Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And it was only made ten rakʿahs because the original salat whose obligation was first sent down from the heaven in the day and the night was only ten rakʿahs, so those rakʿahs were gathered here. And prostration was only placed in it because there is no salat in which there is bowing except that there is also prostration in it, and so that they may also conclude their salat with prostration and humility. And it was only made four sajdahs because every salat whose prostration falls short of four sajdahs is not a salat, since the least obligatory amount of prostration in salat cannot be less than four sajdahs. And prostration was not made in place of bowing because salat while standing is more excellent than salat while sitting, and because the one standing sees the eclipse and what is above, while the one prostrating does not see. And it was only changed from the original salat that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory because it is performed for the cause of a change in one of the matters, namely the eclipse. So when the cause changed, the effect changed.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, when Dhu al-Qarnayn reached the barrier, he passed beyond it and entered into the darkness. Then suddenly he came upon an angel standing upon a mountain whose height was five hundred cubits. The angel said to him, 'O Dhu al-Qarnayn, was there not a path behind you?' Dhu al-Qarnayn said to him, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am an angel from among the angels of the Most Merciful, entrusted with this mountain. There is no mountain that Allah has created except that it has a vein connected to this mountain. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills to cause a city to quake, He reveals to me, and I make it quake.'"

1512 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the earth and commanded the whale, so it carried it. Then it said: 'I carried it by my strength.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent to it a whale the size of a fingertip, and it entered into its nostril, so it convulsed for forty mornings. Then, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wants to cause an earth to quake, that small whale appears to it, and the earth quakes out of fear." And the earthquake may also occur by other than this manner.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded the whale to carry the earth, and every land among the lands is upon a scale from its scales. So when Allah, Mighty and Glorious, wills to cause an earthquake in a land, He commands the whale to move that scale, and it moves it. And if the scale were lifted, the earth would be overturned by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Glorious.

Sulaiman al-Daylami asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the earthquake, what it is, and he said: "It is a sign." He said, "And what is its cause?" He said: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has entrusted the veins of the earth to an angel. So when Allah wishes to cause a land to quake, He reveals to that angel: Move such-and-such a vein." He said: "Then that angel moves the vein of that land which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has commanded, and it moves with its inhabitants." He said: I said, "When that happens, what should I do?" He said: "Pray Salat al-Kusuf, and when you finish, fall prostrating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and say in your سجود: O He who..." "holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him; indeed He is Forbearing, All-Forgiving." O He who "holds the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission," withhold evil from us; "indeed You have power over all things."

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said: I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and complained to him about the frequent earthquakes in al-Ahwāz, and I said: Do you consider relocation away from it advisable for me? So he عليه السلام wrote: “Do not move away from it. Fast on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, perform ghusl, purify your clothes, go out on Friday, and supplicate to Allah, for He will lift it from you.” He said: So we did that, and the earthquakes became still.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, the lightning strike affects the believer and the disbeliever, but it does not strike one who is engaged in dhikr (remembrance of Allah)."
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "The wind has a head and two wings."

And it is narrated from Kāmil, who said: I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام at al-ʿUrayḍ when a severe wind blew. Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام began saying takbīr, then he said: “Indeed, the takbīr repels the wind.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not send any wind except as a mercy or as a punishment. So when you see it, say: O Allah, we ask You for its good and the good of what it was sent for, and we seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what it was sent for. And recite takbīr, and raise your voices with takbīr, for it breaks it.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Do not curse the winds, for they are commanded, nor the mountains, nor the hours, nor the days, nor the nights, lest you commit sin and it returns to you."

And he, peace be upon him, said: No wind ever comes out except in measure, except in the time of ʿĀd, for it rebelled against its keepers and came out through something like the eye of a needle, and so it destroyed the people of ʿĀd.

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the four winds: the north, the south, the east wind, and the west wind. And I said to him: People say that the north wind is from Paradise and the south wind is from the Fire. So he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has hosts from among the wind by which He punishes those who disobey Him. Over each wind among them is an appointed, obeyed angel. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to punish a people with a punishment, Allah reveals to the angel appointed over that kind of wind which He intends to punish them with, and the angel commands it, so it surges as an enraged lion surges. And each wind among them has a name. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune." And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "the barren wind" And He, Exalted, said: "Then a whirlwind containing fire struck it, and it was burned." And what He mentioned in the Book of the winds by which He punishes those who disobey Him. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has winds of mercy: fertilizing winds, winds that stir the clouds and drive the clouds, winds that hold the clouds between the heaven and the earth, winds that press them so they rain by the permission of Allah, and winds that disperse the clouds, and winds among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has enumerated in the Book. As for the four winds, they are the names of the angels: al-Shamāl, al-Janūb, al-Ṣabā, and al-Dabūr. Over each wind among them is an angel appointed over it. So when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to make a north wind blow, He commands the angel whose name is al-Shamāl, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the north wind disperses wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills on land and sea. And when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to send al-Ṣabā, He commands the angel whose name is al-Ṣabā, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the wind of al-Ṣabā disperses wherever Allah, Exalted, wills on land and sea. And when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to send a south wind, He commands the angel whose name is al-Janūb, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strike
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Excellent is the south wind: it breaks the cold from the needy, pollinates the trees, and causes the valleys to flow."
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "The winds are five, and among them is the barren wind, so we seek refuge in Allah from its evil."

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when a yellow, red, or black wind blew, his face would change, his color would turn pale, and he would be like one fearful and anxious, until a drop of rain fell from the sky; then his color would return to him, and he would say: It has come to you with mercy.

Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام; they said: We said to him: What do you say about these winds and darknesses that occur? Is salat to be performed because of them? He said: For every fear-inducing occurrence of the sky, whether darkness, wind, or dread, then pray for it the eclipse salat until it becomes still.

1527 - Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon them, who said: "When an eclipse or some of these signs occurs, perform it so long as you do not fear that the time of the obligatory prayer will pass. But if you fear that, then begin with the obligatory prayer and cut short what you were engaged in of Salat al-Kusuf. Then when you have finished the obligatory prayer, return to where you had stopped and count what has already passed."

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Faḍl al-Wāsiṭī that he said: I wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: if the sun and the moon are eclipsed while I am riding and unable to dismount. So he عليه السلام wrote back to me: ‘Pray upon your mount which you are on.’

And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim and al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār that they both said: We said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Should one make up the salat of the eclipse if he comes to know in the morning, and if he comes to know in the evening? He said: "If both discs were completely eclipsed, you must make it up; but if only part of them was eclipsed, then its make-up is not upon you."

Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the salat of the eclipse, the eclipse of the sun and the moon. He said: “It is ten rakʿahs and four sajdahs. You perform rukuʿ five times, then perform sajdah in the fifth; then you perform rukuʿ five times, then perform sajdah in the tenth. If you wish, you may recite a surah in each rakʿah, and if you wish, you may recite half a surah in each rakʿah. فإذا recite a surah in each rakʿah, then recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; and if you recite half a surah, it suffices for you not to recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb except in the first rakʿah until you begin another one. And do not say, ‘Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah,’ when raising your head from rukuʿ except in the rakʿah in which you intend to perform sajdah.”
And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated: The qunut is in the second rakʿah before the rukuʿ, then in the fourth, then in the sixth, then in the eighth, then in the tenth.

Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: They mentioned in his presence the eclipse of the moon and the hardship that people experience from its severity, so he عليه السلام said: “If a part of it has cleared, then it has cleared.”

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib: 'O Ja'far, shall I not grant you, shall I not give you, shall I not favor you, shall I not teach you a salat that, if you pray it, even if you had fled from the battlefield and upon you were sins like the sand of 'Alij and the foam of the sea, you would be forgiven?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'You pray four rak'ahs whenever you wish: if you wish, every night; if you wish, every day; if you wish, then from one Jumu'ah to another; and if you wish, then from one month to another; and if you wish, then from one year to another. You begin the salat, then say fifteen times: Allahu Akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and la ilaha illa Allah. Then you recite al-Fatihah and a surah, and bow, and say them in your ruku' ten times. Then you raise your head from ruku' and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times in your sujud. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you rise and say them fifteen times. Then you recite Fatihat al-Kitab and a surah, then bow and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from ruku' and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you perform sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you recite the tashahhud and conclude with taslim. Then you stand and pray two other rak'ahs, doing in them the like of that, then you conclude with taslim.' Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: 'That is seventy-five times in each rak'ah, three hundred tasbihs; in the four rak'ahs it becomes one thousand two hundred tasbihs. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, multiplies it for you and writes for you by it twelve thousand good deeds, each good deed among them being like Mount Uhud, and greater.'

And it has indeed been narrated: "That the tasbih in the Salat of Jaʿfar is after the recitation, and that the order of the tasbih is: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar."
1535 - And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, he said: "Recite in the Salat of Jaʿfar عليه السلام 'Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad'" and 'Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn.'

1536 - And it is narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan, meaning Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: “What is there for one who performs the Salat of Jaʿfar?” He said: “If he had sins like the sand of ʿĀlij and the foam of the sea, Allah would forgive them for him.” He said: I said, “Is this for us?” He said: “For whom would it be except for you specifically?” He said: I said, “Then what should I recite in it?” He said—and I said, “Shall I recite various parts of the Qur’an?”—he said: “No; recite in it: ‘When the earth is shaken,’ and ‘When the help of Allah comes,’ and ‘Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr,’ and ‘Say: He is Allah, One.’”

Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام was asked about one who performs the Salat of Jaʿfar: would there be written for him, of reward, the like of what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to Jaʿfar? He said: “Yes, by Allah.”

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān that he said: I wrote to al-Māḍī al-Ākhir عليه السلام asking him about a man who prayed two rakʿahs of the Salat of Jaʿfar, then a need hastened him away from the final two rakʿahs, or he cut that off due to an occurring incident. Is it permissible for him to complete it after finishing his need, even if he has risen from his place, or is that not counted for him unless he restarts the salat (prayer) and prays all four rakʿahs together in a single place? So he عليه السلام wrote: “Yes. If a matter that he cannot do without interrupts him from that, then let him stop, then let him return and build upon what remains of it, if Allah wills.”

Abu Basir narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Pray the Salat of Ja'far at whatever time you wish, by night or by day. If you wish, you may count it as part of the supererogatory prayers of the night, and if you wish, you may count it as part of the supererogatory prayers of the day. It will be counted for you as part of your supererogatory prayers, and it will be counted for you as the Salat of Ja'far عليه السلام.
Abu Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If you are in a hurry, then perform the Salat of Jaʿfar in a stripped form, then make up the tasbih afterward."

1541 - And in the narration of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, he said: “You say in the final sajdah of the salat of Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام: O One who has clothed Himself with might and dignity, O One who has wrapped Himself in glory and has been ennobled by it, O One for whom glorification befits none but Him, O One whose knowledge has encompassed and counted every thing, O Possessor of blessing and abundance, O Possessor of favor and grace, O Possessor of power and generosity, I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and the utmost mercy from Your Book, and by Your greatest, highest Name, and Your perfect words, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to do for me such and such. ”

Murāzim narrated from the righteous servant Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: If a grave matter afflicts you, then give charity during your day to sixty needy people, giving each needy person half a sāʿ by the sāʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله from dates, wheat, or barley. Then, when it is night, perform ghusl in the last third of the night, then wear the humblest clothes worn by those whom you support, except that in those clothes you should have a waist-wrapper; then pray two rakʿahs. In them, you recite al-Tawḥīd and: «قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ». Then when you place your forehead in prostration in the final rakʿah, declare the oneness of Allah, sanctify Him, magnify Him, and glorify Him. Then remember your sins, admitting those you know of specifically, and those you do not know of in a general way. Then raise your head, and when you place your forehead in the second prostration, seek Allah's counsel one hundred times, saying: 'O Allah, indeed I seek Your counsel by Your knowledge.' Then supplicate to Allah by whatever of His names you wish, and say: 'O One existing before everything, O Originator of everything, O One existing after everything, do for me such-and-such and such-and-such.' And whenever you prostrate, press your knees to the ground and raise the waist-wrapper until you uncover them, and place the waist-wrapper behind you between your buttocks and the inner parts of your legs. For I hope that your need will be fulfilled, if Allah the Exalted wills. And begin with blessings upon the Prophet and the people of his Household, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all.

Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from their shaykhs, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If an important need arises for you before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then fast for three consecutive days: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Then when Friday comes, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills, perform ghusl, wear a new garment, then go up to the highest place in your house, pray two rakʿahs there, raise your hands to the sky, then say: O Allah, I have come into Your precinct by my recognition of Your oneness and Your absolute self-sufficiency, and that none has power over my need except You. And I have known, my Lord, that whenever Your blessing becomes manifest upon me, my need of You intensifies. A worry of such-and-such has come upon me, and You know how to remove it, without being taught, vast without strain. So I ask You by Your Name which You placed upon the mountains and they were blasted away, and You placed it upon the heaven and it split apart, and upon the stars and they scattered, and upon the earth and it was spread out. And I ask You by the truth which You placed with Muḥammad and the Imams عليهم السلام—and you name them to the last of them—that You send blessings upon Muḥammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, fulfill my need, make its difficulty easy for me, and suffice me regarding its burden. If You do so, then to You belongs all praise; and if You do not do so, then to You belongs all praise, while I do not hold You unjust in Your judgment, nor suspect in Your decree, nor unfair in Your justice. And place your cheek upon the ground and say: O Allah, indeed Yūnus ibn Mattā, Your servant, called upon You in the belly of the whale, and he was Your servant, so You answered him; and I am Your servant calling upon You, so answer me. Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Often I would have a need, and I would supplicate with this supplication, then return having had it fulfilled.

Sama‘ah narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, when one of you falls ill, he calls the physician and gives him payment; and when he has a need with a ruler, he bribes the gatekeeper and gives him. But if, when one of you is struck by a grave matter, he were to turn in alarm to Allah, the Exalted, purify himself, give charity—whether little or much—then enter the mosque and pray two rak‘ahs, then praise Allah and extol Him, and invoke blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, then say: “O Allah, if You grant me well-being from my illness, or return me from my journey, or grant me well-being from what I fear of such-and-such,” Allah would surely grant him that. And this is the binding oath, and that which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made incumbent upon him in gratitude.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, when a matter grieved him, would wear two of his roughest and coarsest garments, then perform two rakʿahs in the latter part of the night. Then, when he was in the last sajdah of his prostration, he would glorify Allah one hundred tasbihs, praise Allah one hundred times, declare the oneness of Allah one hundred times, and magnify Allah one hundred times. Then he would acknowledge all of his sins: whatever of them he knew, he would confess to Him, Blessed and Exalted, during his prostration; and whatever of them he did not remember, he would acknowledge collectively. Then he would supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and press his knees to the ground.

It is narrated from Yūnus ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I complained to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was harming me, so he said, "Pray against him." I said, "I have already prayed against him." He said, "Not like that. Rather, cease from sins, fast, pray, and give charity. Then, when it is the end of the night, perform the wudu (ablution) thoroughly, then stand and pray two rakʿahs. Then say while you are in sajdah (prostration): O Allah, indeed so-and-so son of so-and-so has harmed me. O Allah, make his body ill, cut off his trace, diminish his lifespan, and hasten that for him in this very year." He said: So I did that, and it was not long before he perished.

ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from a shaykh from the family of Saʿd, who said: There was between me and a man from the people of al-Madinah a dispute of great seriousness. So I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned that to him, and I said: Teach me something by which Allah may perhaps restore to me my wrongfully taken right. So he said: “When you seek to confront the enemy, then perform two rakʿahs or four rakʿahs between the grave and the minbar, or if you wish then in your house; and ask Allah to help you, and take something from whatever is easy for you, then give it in charity to the first needy person you meet.” He said: So I did what he commanded me, and judgment was given in my favor, and Allah returned my land to me.

Ziyād al-Qandī narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr, who said: I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: “May I be your ransom, I have devised a supplication.” He said: “Leave me out of your invention. When a matter befalls you, then turn in alarm to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and pray two rakʿahs, offering them as a gift to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” I said: “How should I do?” He said: “You perform ghusl, and pray two rakʿahs, beginning them with the opening of the obligatory prayer, and you recite the tashahhud of the obligatory prayer. When you finish the tashahhud and give salām, say: O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace, and to You peace returns. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and convey from me peace to the soul of Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad; and peace be upon them, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. O Allah, these two rakʿahs are a gift from me to Your Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, so reward me for them with what I have hoped and expected from You and through Your Messenger, O Guardian of the believers. Then fall in sajdah and say: O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Living One who does not die, O Living One, there is no god except You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Most Merciful of the merciful—forty times. Then place your right cheek upon the ground and say it forty times. Then place your left cheek and say that forty times. Then raise your head, extend your hands, and say that forty times. Then return your hand to your neck and cling with your forefinger forty times. Then take your beard with your left hand, weep or make yourself weep, and say: O Muḥammad, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I complain to Allah and to you of my need, and I complain to the rightly guided people of your household of my need, and through you I turn toward Allah regarding my need. Then you perform sajdah and say: O Allah, O Allah, until your breath is cut off; bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and do for me such-and-such and such-and-such.” Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “I guarantee before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that he will not depart until his need is fulfilled.”

In the book of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who raises it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a man whom a matter grieves and who seeks a need. He said: He should pray two rakʿahs and recite in one of them "Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad." a thousand times, and in the other once; then he asks for his need.

Harun ibn Kharijah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When one of you intends a matter, he should not consult anyone among the people about it until he begins by consulting Allah, Blessed and Exalted." He said: I said, "And what is consulting Allah, Blessed and Exalted? May I be your ransom." He said: "He begins by seeking istikharah from Allah regarding it first, then he consults about it. For when he begins with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, He causes what is best for him to flow upon the tongue of whomever He wills from among the creation."

1551 - Murazim narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: “If one of you intends something, then let him perform two rak'ahs, then let him praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and say: O Allah, if this matter is good for me in my religion and my worldly life, then make it easy for me and decree it for me; and if it is otherwise than that, then turn it away from me.” Murazim said: So I asked, “What is to be recited in them?” He said: “Recite in them whatever you wish. If you wish, then recite in them,” “‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal kafirun’” and “‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ is equivalent to one-third of the Qur'an.”

Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Qasrī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about istikhārah, so he said: "Seek guidance from Allah in the last rakʿah of salat al-layl while you are in sajdah, one hundred and one times." He said: "How should I say it?" He said: "You say: Astakhīru Allāha bi-raḥmatihi, astakhīru Allāha bi-raḥmatihi."

1553 - And Hammad ibn 'Uthman al-Naab narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: “Regarding istikhārah, a man should seek guidance from Allah in the last sajdah of the two rak'ahs of Fajr one hundred and one times, and praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family. Then he should seek guidance from Allah fifty times, then praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family, صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ, and complete the one hundred and one.”

1554 - And Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Najiyah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: That he would, whenever he intended to purchase a servant, an animal, a light need, or a small matter, perform istikharah with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concerning it seven times; and when it was a serious matter, he would perform istikharah with Allah one hundred times.

Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: No servant seeks Allah’s guidance seventy times with this istikhārah except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, casts choice for him. He says: O Most Seeing of those who see, O Most Hearing of those who hear, O Swiftest of reckoners, O Most Merciful of the merciful, O Wisest of judges, send blessings upon Muḥammad and the people of his household, and choose for me regarding such-and-such.
It is well-known among the companions that it is the prayer of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, as in the narration of al-Mufaddal.

Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever performs wudu (ablution) and completes the wudu thoroughly, then begins the salat (prayer) and prays four rakʿahs, separating between them with a taslim, reciting in each rakʿah Fātiḥat al-Kitāb once and "Say: He is Allah, One" fifty times, he will finish when he finishes, and there will remain no sin between him and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that He will forgive him."

1557 - As for Muḥammad ibn Masʿūd al-ʿAyyāshī, may Allah have mercy on him, he narrated in his book from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn al-Simāk, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever prays four rakʿahs and recites in each rakʿah fifty times "Say: He is Allah, the One," it is the salat of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and it is the salat of the oft-returning ones."
It appears that what is meant by al-Nawadir are uncommon reports that are not gathered under a chapter and are dispersed. The term may also be applied to irregular narrations.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Perform supererogatory prayers during the time of heedlessness, even if only with two light rak'ahs, for they bequeath the abode of honor."
And in another narration: "The Abode of Peace."
Bukayr ibn A‘yan narrated from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم never performed the Duha prayer.”

And ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn al-Mukhtār al-Anṣārī narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the Duḥā prayer, so he said: “The first ones to perform it were your people. Indeed, they were among the heedless, so they perform it; and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not perform it.” And he said: “Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام passed by a man while he was performing it, so ʿAlī عليه السلام said: ‘What is this prayer?’ He said: ‘Should I leave it, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn?’ He عليه السلام said: ‘Would I forbid a servant when he prays?’”

1563 - Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله never prayed al-Ḍuḥā at all." He said: So I said to him, "Did you not inform me that he عليه السلام used to pray four rakʿahs in the early part of the day?" He said: "Yes. He used to count them as part of the eight that are after al-Ẓuhr."

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan. He said: "Thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and two rakʿahs before Salat al-Fajr. That is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to pray, and if there had been any additional virtue, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would have acted upon it more and had the greatest right to it."

ʿUqbah ibn Khālid asked him: About a man whom another man called while he was praying, so he became distracted and responded to him regarding his need—what should he do? He said: “He should continue with his salat (prayer).”
And ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī narrated from him that he said: "It is appropriate to lighten the salat (prayer) because of forgetfulness."
Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "The charity of a boy is valid, as is his manumission, and he may lead the people if he is ten years old."
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: If you pray with them, you will be forgiven according to the number of those who oppose you.

1569 - And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from him that he said: "When you perform salat (prayer), then pray in your sandals if they are tahir (ritually clean), for indeed that is from the sunnah (prophetic tradition)."
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: "If you perform any of the prayers during travel outside its time, it will not harm you."

And it is narrated from ʿĀʾidh al-Aḥmasī that he said: I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I intended to ask him about salat (prayer), but he began speaking to me before I asked him, and he said: “If you meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the five obligatory prayers, He will not ask you about anything beyond that.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The believer remains in a state of devotional following and spiritual reward so long as he remains upon wudu (ablution)."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Inform me about a man who owes from the salat of the nawāfil so much that, due to their abundance, he does not know how much it is. What should he do? He said: "Let him pray until, due to their abundance, he no longer knows how much he has prayed; then he will have made up to the extent of what he knew of that." Then he said: I said to him: What if he is not able to perform the make-up? He said: "If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is necessary, or in a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his occupation is for gathering worldly gain and preoccupying himself with it away from salat, then the make-up is upon him; otherwise he will meet Allah while being one who treats lightly, is careless, and neglects the sanctity of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله." I said: What if he is not able to perform the make-up? Will it suffice that he gives charity? So he remained silent for a while, then he said: "Then let him give charity." I said: Then how much should he give in charity? He said: "According to the extent of his means, and the minimum of that is one mudd for each needy person in place of each salat." I said: And how much salat is that for which one mudd is required for each needy person? He said: "For every two rakʿahs of the night prayer, one mudd; and for every two rakʿahs of the day prayer, one mudd." So I said: He is not able. He said: "Then one mudd for every four rakʿahs of the day prayer." I said: He is not able. He said: "Then one mudd for the night prayer and one mudd for the day prayer; and salat is better, and salat is better, and salat is better."

74 - Abu Ja‘far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: “Shall I not describe to you the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?” It was said to him: “Yes.” Then he called for a bowl in which there was some water and placed it before him. Then he uncovered his forearms, then dipped his right palm into it and said: “This is when the palm is pure.” Then he scooped a palmful of water, placed it on his forehead, and said: “In the Name of Allah,” and let it flow over the edges of his beard. Then he passed his hand over his face and the outer part of his forehead once. Then he dipped his left hand and scooped with it a palmful, then placed it on his right elbow and passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed to the tips of his fingers. Then he scooped a palmful with his right hand and placed it on his left elbow, then passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed to the tips of his fingers. And he wiped the front of his head and the upper part of his feet with the remaining moisture of his water.

And it was narrated: “That the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, performed wudu (ablution), then wiped over his sandals. So al-Mughīrah said to him, ‘Did you forget, O Messenger of Allah?’ He said, ‘Rather, you have forgotten; this is how my Lord commanded me.’”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "By Allah, the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was only once once, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله performed wudu once once." Then he said: "This is a wudu (ablution) without which Allah does not accept the salat (prayer)."

With a broken chain of narration, narrated by Abū Jaʿfar al-Aḥwal, who mentioned it from one who narrated it from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Allah made wudu (ablution) obligatory once for each act, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prescribed for the people twice for each act.

And it has indeed been narrated: “Indeed, wudu (ablution) is a limit among the limits set by Allah, so that Allah may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him. And indeed, nothing renders the believer impure; rather, something like oil is sufficient for him.”
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever exceeds the prescribed limits in his wudu (ablution) is like one who nullifies it."

And concerning that, there is another hadith with a broken chain, narrated by ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, who said: Someone who heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام told me, saying: Indeed, I am amazed at one who desires to perform wudu (ablution) two by two, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed it two by two. For the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to renew the wudu (ablution) for every obligatory prayer and for every prayer.
And it was narrated: "Renewing wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer) of al-'Isha' erases [sins]—no, by Allah, rather yes, by Allah."

And it was narrated in another report: "Indeed, wudu (ablution) upon wudu is light upon light, and whoever renews his wudu without a further hadath, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, renews his repentance without istighfar (seeking forgiveness)."

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ascended the pulpit one day, then praised Allah, extolled Him, and sent blessings upon His Prophets عليهم السلام. Then he said: "O people, let those of you who are present convey it to those who are absent: whoever grants respite to an insolvent debtor shall have with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, every day the reward of charity equal to the amount of his wealth until he fully recovers it." And Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘And if someone is in hardship, then postponement until ease; and that you give in charity is better for you, if you only knew.’" If he is insolvent, then give charity to him from your wealth, for that is better for you.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Let the insolvent go free, just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has let him go free."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wishes that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, shade him on the Day when there will be no shade except His shade, then let him grant respite to an insolvent person or leave for him some of his due."

1705 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever Allah's blessing upon him becomes great, the burden of the people upon him also becomes intense. So preserve the blessing by bearing the burden, and do not expose it to disappearance; for seldom does a blessing depart from someone and then nearly return to him."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Treat the blessings of Allah well in your companionship with them, and beware lest they be transferred from you to others. Indeed, they have never departed from anyone at all and then nearly returned to him. And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, used to say: Little is it that a thing departs and then comes back."

1707 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The best of you are your generous ones, and the worst of you are your stingy ones. And from pure iman is righteousness toward brothers and striving in their needs. Indeed, the one who is righteous toward the brothers is surely loved by the Most Merciful, and in that is humiliation for Satan, distancing from the fires, and entry into the gardens." Then he said to Jamil: "O Jamil, inform the choicest of your companions of this." I said: "May I be made your ransom, who are the choicest of my companions?" He said: "They are those who are righteous toward the brothers in hardship and ease." Then he said: "O Jamil, indeed the possessor of much finds that easy upon him, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised in that the possessor of little. So He said in His Book: 'And they prefer others over themselves even though there is privation with them; and whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, then those are the successful ones.'"
And he, peace be upon him, said: "A young person who is generous, though overwhelmed by sins, is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than an old worshipper who is stingy."
And it is narrated: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa عليه السلام not to kill the Samaritan, for indeed he is generous."
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever fulfills what Allah has made obligatory upon him is the most generous of people."

1711 - And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Whoever guarantees for me four things, I guarantee for him four houses in Paradise: spend and do not fear poverty; deal fairly with people from yourself; spread peace in the world; and leave disputation, even if you are right.”

1712 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever is certain of recompense, his soul becomes generous in spending.” And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And whatever you spend of anything, He replaces it, and He is the best of providers.”

1713 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them." He عليه السلام said: "It is the man who leaves his wealth and does not spend it in the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, out of miserliness, then he dies and leaves it to one who acts with it in the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or in disobedience to Allah. If he acts with it in the obedience of Allah, he sees it in the scale of another, so he sees it as a regret, though the wealth had been his. And if he acted with it in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he strengthened him with that wealth until he acted with it in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The stingy one is not the one who pays the obligatory zakat from his wealth and gives openly among his people. Rather, the truly stingy one is he who does not pay the obligatory zakat from his wealth and does not give openly among his people, while he squanders in matters other than that."

And it is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah al-Samandī that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me, “Do you know who the miser is?” I said, “He is the stingy person.” He said, “Avarice is more severe than stinginess. Indeed, the stingy person withholds what is in his hand, while the avaricious person is avaricious regarding what is in the hands of people and regarding what is in his own hand, such that he does not see anything in the hands of people except that he wishes it would be his, by lawful and unlawful means, and he is not content with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has provided him.”

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Nothing has effaced Islam as anything has effaced it like miserliness." Then he said: "Indeed, this miserliness has a creeping like the creeping of ants, and branches like the branches of a net."
And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has no need for a servant, He tests him with miserliness."

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام heard a man saying, “The miser is more excusable than the oppressor.” So he said to him: “You have lied. Indeed, the oppressor may repent, seek forgiveness, and restore the wrong to its people. But the miser, when he is miserly, withholds zakat, charity, maintaining kinship ties, hospitality to the guest, spending in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the doors of goodness; and it is forbidden for Paradise that a miser should enter it.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The saving acts are feeding food, spreading salām, and salat (prayer) at night while the people are asleep."
And Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, said: No person who practices moderation becomes impoverished.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "I guarantee for the one who practices moderation that he will not become poor."
The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "The first thing with which one begins in the Hereafter is the charity of water"—meaning in reward.

And Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves the cooling of a burning liver. Whoever gives water to a burning liver, whether of a beast or otherwise, Allah will shade him in the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade.

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever gives water in a place where water is available is like one who frees a slave. And whoever gives water in a place where water is not available is like one who revives a soul. And whoever revives a soul, "it is as though he has revived all of humanity." "
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever extends a favor to any one of my Ahl al-Bayt, I will repay him on the Day of Judgment."

1726 - And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, I am an intercessor on the Day of Judgment for four types of people, even if they come with the sins of the people of the world: a man who supported my progeny, a man who spent his wealth for my progeny in times of hardship, a man who loved my progeny with his tongue and heart, and a man who strove in fulfilling the needs of my progeny when they were expelled or scattered."

1727 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “When it is the Day of qiyamah, a caller will call out: ‘O creation, be silent, for Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم will speak to you.’ So the creation will fall silent. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم will stand and say: ‘O assembly of creation, whoever has a favor, a kindness, or a good deed with me, let him stand so that I may recompense him.’” Then they will say: ‘By our fathers and our mothers, what favor, what kindness, and what good deed do we have? Rather, the favor, the kindness, and the good deed belong to Allah and His Messenger over all creation.’ So he will say to them: ‘Rather, whoever gave shelter to anyone from my Ahl al-Bayt, or treated them kindly, or clothed them from nakedness, or fed their hungry one, let him stand so that I may recompense him.’ Then some people who did that will stand, and the call will come from Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ‘O Muhammad, O My Beloved, I have placed their recompense with you, so settle them in Jannah wherever you wish.’ He said: So he will settle them in al-Wasilah, where they will not be veiled from Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all.
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The ground of the Day of Resurrection is fire, except for the shade of the believer, for indeed his charity gives him shade."
1729 - And Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: "Goodness and charity eliminate poverty, increase lifespan, and repel from their possessor seventy evil deaths."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Treat your sick ones with charity, ward off tribulation with du'a, and seek sustenance through charity. For it loosens from between the jaws of seven hundred devils, and there is nothing heavier upon Satan than charity given to a believer. And it falls into the hand of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, before it falls into the hand of the servant."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Charity given by hand protects against an evil death, wards off seventy kinds of calamities, and loosens the grip of seventy devils, all of whom urge him not to do it.
And he, peace be upon him, said: It is recommended for the sick person to give to the beggar with his own hand and to ask the beggar to supplicate for him.

And he عليه السلام said: "Give charity early, for calamities do not pass beyond it. Whoever gives charity at the beginning of the day, Allah protects him from the evil of what descends from the sky on that day. And if he gives charity at the beginning of the night, Allah protects him from the evil of what descends from the sky during that night."

1734 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Indeed, Allah, there is no deity but Him, surely wards off through charity illness, abscess, burning, drowning, collapse, and madness; and he, peace be upon him, enumerated seventy doors of evil."
And he, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Charity given in secret extinguishes the wrath of the Lord, majestic is His majesty."

Ammar narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام, who said: He said to me: O Ammar, charity given in secret, by Allah, is better than charity given openly; and likewise, by Allah, worship in secret is better than worship in public.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "If a male beggar comes to you at night, do not turn him away."
And he said, peace be upon him and his family: "Charity is rewarded tenfold, a loan eighteenfold, kindness to brothers twentyfold, and maintaining ties of kinship twenty-fourfold."
And he, peace be upon him, was asked: "Which charity is the best?" He said: "To a relative who harbors enmity."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "There is no charity while a relative is in need."
He عليه السلام said: "Cursed, cursed is the one who casts his burden upon the people. Cursed, cursed is the one who neglects those whom he supports."
And Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام said: "A man ought to provide generously for his family so that they do not wish for his death."

1743 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a beggar who asks, while it is not known what his condition is, so he said: "Give to the one for whom mercy falls into your heart." And he said: "Give him less than a dirham." I said: "What is the most that may be given?" He said: "Four daniqs."

1744 - Al-Wassafi narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: "Among that with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, confidentially addressed Musa عليه السلام was that He said:" "O Musa, honor the one who asks by giving a small amount or by a gracious reply. Indeed, there comes to you one who is neither human nor jinn, angels from among the angels of the Most Merciful, testing you concerning what I have entrusted to you, and asking you from what I have bestowed upon you. So consider how you will act, O son of 'Imran."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Give to the one who asks, even if you are on horseback."
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Do not interrupt the request of the beggar, for were it not that the needy sometimes lie, the one who turns them away would not prosper."

And it is narrated from al-Walīd ibn Ṣabīḥ, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a beggar came to him, and he gave him. Then another came, and he gave him. Then another came, and he gave him. Then another came, and he said, “May Allah grant you abundance.” Then he said, “Indeed, if a man had wealth reaching thirty or forty thousand dirhams, then wished to leave nothing of it except that he placed it in a rightful cause, he would do so, and then remain with no wealth. Thus he would be among the three whose supplication is rejected.” He said: I said, “Who are they?” He said, “One of them is a man who had wealth, then spent it in other than its proper way, then said: ‘My Lord, provide for me,’ and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not provide for you?’ And a man who sat in his house and does not strive in seeking sustenance, yet says: ‘My Lord, provide for me,’ and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not make for you a way to seek sustenance?’ And a man who has a wife who harms him, so he says: ‘My Lord, deliver me from her,’ and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not place her affair in your hand?’”
1748 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "With regard to the beggars, feed three of them; and if you wish to give more, then give more; otherwise, you have fulfilled the due of your day."
And he, peace be upon him, said: When you give to them, then teach them the du'a, for their du'a for you is answered, while their du'a for themselves is not answered.

1750 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding a man who gives dirhams to another to distribute, he said: He will receive from the reward the like of what accrues to the giver, and nothing will be diminished from his reward. Even if the act of kindness were to pass through seventy hands, all of them would be rewarded without anything being diminished from the reward of its owner.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked: “Which charity is best?” He said: “The effort of one who has little. Have you not heard the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in need.’ Do you see any surplus here?”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said: "I have taken a pledge from my Lord, the Mighty and Glorious, that no one asks without need except that one day begging will compel him to ask out of actual need."

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: "Follow the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, for he said: 'Whoever opens upon himself a door of begging, Allah will open upon him a door of poverty.'"

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There is no servant who asks without need except that he will die before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes him in need of it, and writes for him thereby the Fire.

1755 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves something for Himself and dislikes it for His creation. He, Mighty and Glorious, has disliked for His creation asking, and He has loved for Himself that He be asked. There is nothing more beloved to Him than that He be asked. So none of you should feel shy to ask Allah, Mighty and Glorious, from His bounty, even if it be the strap of a sandal.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Beware of asking people, for it is the humiliation of this world, a poverty that you hasten for yourselves, and a long reckoning on the Day of Judgment."
And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: If the one who asks knew what is in asking, no one would ask anyone; and if the giver knew what is in giving, no one would turn anyone away.

A clan from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we have a need to ask of you.” He said, “Present your need.” They said, “It is a great need.” He said, “Say what it is.” They said, “Will you guarantee Paradise for us with your Lord?” So he صلى الله عليه وآله lowered his head and traced in the ground. Then he raised his head and said, “I shall do that for you on condition that you do not ask anyone for anything.” It was said: a man among them would be on a journey and his whip would fall, yet he would dislike saying to anyone, “Hand it to me,” out of avoidance of asking; so he would dismount and take it himself. And he would be at the dining spread, while some of those seated were nearer than him to the water, yet he would not say, “Pass it to me,” until he himself stood and drank.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Be independent of people, even if it is with the splinter of a toothstick."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Reminding others of a favor destroys the good deed."
