1761 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, disliked for me six traits, and I have disliked them for the awsiya' from my progeny and their followers after me: fidgeting in salat (prayer), obscene speech in sawm (fasting), reminding others of one's charity after giving sadaqah, entering the mosques while junub, peering into houses, and laughing among the graves.”

1762 - It is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام: Indeed, Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام sent to a man five awsuq of dates from al-Bughaybighah. The man was among those who hoped for his voluntary generosity, was content with his gift and support, and did not ask anything from ʿAlī عليه السلام or anyone else. Then a man said to Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام, 'By Allah, so-and-so did not ask you for anything, and one wasq out of the five awsuq would have been enough for him.' So Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام said to him: 'May Allah not increase your kind among the believers. I give, while you are miserly with it. If I do not give to the one who hopes in me except after his asking me, and then I give him after the asking, then I have only given him the price of what I took from him. That is because I exposed him to offering me his face, which he places in the dust before my Lord and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, at the time of his worship of Him and his asking Him for his needs.' So whoever does this to his Muslim brother, while knowing that he is a proper recipient of his charity and kindness, has not been truthful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in his supplication for him, when he wishes Paradise for him with his tongue yet is miserly toward him with the trifles of his wealth. That is because a servant may say in his supplication: 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and the believing women'; so when he supplicates for him with forgiveness, he has indeed asked Paradise for him. So unfair is the one who does this in speech but does not make it real through action.'

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked: about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan?" He said: "It was revealed concerning maintaining connection with the Imam, peace be upon him."
1764 - And he, peace be upon him, said: “A dirham by which the Imam is supported is better than a thousand thousand dirhams spent on other than him in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

1765 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever is unable to maintain relations with us, then let him maintain relations with the righteous among our Shi'a; there shall be written for him the reward of maintaining relations with us. And whoever is unable to visit us, then let him visit the righteous among our followers; there shall be written for him the reward of visiting us."

The virtuous and learned Shaykh, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī, the author of this book—may Allah be pleased with him and grant him abode in His Paradise—said:

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made zakat obligatory just as He made salat (prayer) obligatory. So if a man were to carry the zakat and give it openly, there would be no blame upon him in that. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has apportioned for the poor, within the wealth of the rich, that by which they may be sufficiently provided. And if He knew that what He had apportioned for them would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. Rather, the poor are only afflicted regarding what they receive because of the withholding of those who withhold their rights from them, not because of the ordained obligation.”
Mubārak al-‘Aqarqūfī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Ja‘far, peace be upon them both, who said: "Zakat was instituted as sustenance for the poor and as a means of preserving their wealth."
Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: "Fortify your wealth through zakat."

1577 - Harīz narrated from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim that they both said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, “Indeed, charities are only for the poor, the needy, those employed over them, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, in freeing slaves, those in debt, in the way of Allah, and the stranded traveler, as an obligation from Allah.” Should all of these be given, even if he does not recognize? He said: “Indeed, the Imam gives to all of these together because they acknowledge obedience to him.” Zurārah said: I said: What if they do not recognize? He said: “O Zurārah, if he were to give to the one who recognizes instead of the one who does not recognize, no place for it would be found. He only gives to the one who does not recognize so that he may be inclined toward the religion and become firm upon it. But as for today, then neither you nor your companions should give it except to one who recognizes. So whomever you find among these Muslims to be knowing, then give him instead of the people.” Then he said: “The share of ‘those whose hearts are to be reconciled’ and the share of ‘the captives’ is general, while the remainder is specific.” He said: I said: What if they are not found? He said: “There cannot be an obligation that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained without there being people eligible for it.” He said: I said: What if the charities do not suffice them? He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for the poor in the wealth of the rich that which suffices them. Had He known that that would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. They were not deprived on account of the obligation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; rather, they were deprived because of the withholding of those who withheld their right from them, not because of what Allah ordained for them. If the people were to render their rights, they would be living well.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said to ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī: “O ʿAmmār, you are a man of much wealth.” He said, “Yes, may I be your ransom.” He said: “Then do you render the zakat which Allah has made obligatory upon you?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you give the known right from your wealth?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you maintain your kinship ties?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you keep ties with your brothers?” He said, “Yes.” So he said: “O ʿAmmār, wealth perishes, the body wears out, and deeds remain; and the Reckoner is Living and does not die. O ʿAmmār, indeed, whatever you have sent ahead will never outstrip you, and whatever you have left behind will never catch up with you.”

And in the narration of Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Barmakī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad, from al-Faḍl ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muʿattib, the mawlā of al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: "Zakat was only instituted as a test for the wealthy and as assistance for the poor. If people were to pay the zakat of their wealth, no Muslim would remain poor and needy, and he would become free of need through what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated for him. People have not become impoverished, needy, hungry, or unclothed except because of the sins of the wealthy. And it is fitting upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to withhold His mercy from one who withholds the right of Allah in his wealth. And I swear by the One who created creation and spread out sustenance: no wealth is lost on land or sea except through abandoning zakat, and no game is caught on land or sea except because of its abandoning glorification on that day. Indeed, the most beloved of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are those most generous in hand, and the most generous of people is the one who pays the zakat of his wealth and does not withhold from the believers what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated for them in his wealth."

1580 - Al-Riḍā ʿAlī ibn Mūsā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān, in what he wrote to him as a response to his questions: “The reason for zakat is for the sustenance of the poor and the safeguarding of the wealth of the rich, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has charged the people of health with attending to the affair of those afflicted with chronic disability and trial, just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said, “You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves.” In your wealth is the giving of zakat, and in yourselves is settling the souls upon patience, along with what is in that of rendering thanks for the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and hoping for increase, together with what it contains of increase, kindness, and mercy toward the people of weakness, tenderness toward the people of poverty, urging them toward mutual assistance, strengthening the poor, and helping them in the matter of religion. And it is an admonition for the people of wealth and a lesson for them, so that through them they may infer the poor of the Hereafter, and what there is for them in that of urging gratitude to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for what He has entrusted to them and given them, and supplication, humble entreaty, and fear lest they become like them in many matters in performing zakat, charities, maintaining kinship ties, and doing acts of goodness.”
Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said: "Whoever pays the full zakat on his wealth and places it in its proper place will not be questioned about from where he acquired his wealth."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only made zakat twenty-five dirhams in every thousand because He, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation, so He knew their rich and their poor, their strong and their weak. Thus He made from every thousand twenty-five needy ones. Were it not for that, Allah would have increased it for them, because He is their Creator and He knows them best.”

Hariz narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: There is no owner of wealth, of gold or silver, who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will confine him on the Day of Resurrection in a flat open plain and set over him a bald serpent pursuing him while he shrinks away from it. Then when he sees that he cannot escape from it, he will let it seize his hand, and it will gnaw it as a radish is gnawed; then it will become a collar around his neck. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "They shall be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection." And there is no owner of wealth consisting of camels, cattle, or sheep who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah will confine him on the Day of Resurrection in a flat open plain; every hoofed creature will tread upon him with its hoof, and every fanged creature will bite him with its fang. And there is no owner of wealth consisting of date-palms, grapevines, or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Exalted is He, will collar him with the produce of his land down to seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.

Maʿrūf ibn Kharrabūdh narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has paired zakat with salat (prayer), and so He said: "Establish salat (prayer) and give zakat (alms-tax)." So whoever establishes salat (prayer) but does not give zakat (alms-tax), it is as though he has not established salat (prayer)."

Ayyūb ibn Rāshid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "The withholder of zakat will be encircled by a bald snake that eats from his brain. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'They will be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection.' "
Mas‘adah narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: "Cursed, cursed is wealth that is not purified by zakat."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: There is no servant who withholds any part of the zakat of his wealth except that Allah will make it, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire encircled around his neck, biting from his flesh until the reckoning is finished. And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "They will be encircled by what they were miserly with on the Day of Resurrection." Meaning what they were miserly with from the zakat.

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: There is no man who withholds a dirham from its rightful due except that he will spend two in other than its rightful due. And there is no man who withholds a rightful due in his wealth except that Allah will collar him with it as a serpent of fire on the Day of Resurrection.

Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: “Two bloods in Islam are permissible from Allah, Blessed and Exalted; no one shall judge concerning them until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends forth our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt. Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends forth our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt, he will judge regarding them by the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The muḥṣan adulterer—he will stone him; and the withholder of zakat—he will strike his neck.”
1590 - And ‘Amr ibn Jumay‘ narrated from him that he said: No one paid zakat and it decreased his wealth, and no one withheld it and it increased in his wealth.

And in the narration of Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "Whoever withholds a qīrāṭ of zakat is not a believer nor a Muslim, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:" "Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back. So that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind." And in another narration: "And no salat (prayer) is accepted from him."

1592 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: While the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was in the mosque, he said, “Stand up, O so-and-so; stand up, O so-and-so; stand up, O so-and-so,” until he had brought out five persons. Then he said, “Leave our mosque; do not perform salat (prayer) in it while you do not pay zakat (alms-tax).”

Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "Whoever withholds a qīrāṭ of zakat is not a believer nor a Muslim, and he will ask for return at the time of death and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back, so that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind." "

1594 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "An obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given in charity in righteousness until it is exhausted." Then he said: "And no one prospers who wastes twenty houses of gold over twenty-five dirhams." So it was said to him: "What is the meaning of twenty-five dirhams?" He said: "Whoever withholds zakat, his salat (prayer) is suspended until he pays zakat."
And he, peace be upon him, said: No wealth is lost on land or sea except due to the neglect of zakat, and no bird is caught except that it neglected its glorification.

It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: A man died while zakat was due from him, and he instructed that the zakat be discharged on his behalf, but his children are needy. If they pay it, that would cause them severe harm. So he عليه السلام said: "They should pay it out, then have it returned to themselves, and they should take some of it out so that it is given to others."

And Isma'il ibn Jabir narrated, saying: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is it permissible for a man to take zakat while he is not in need of it, and then give it in charity?” He said: “Yes.” And he said the like of that regarding the fitrah.

1643 - And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What is upon the Imam concerning zakat?” So he said: “O Abū Muḥammad, do you not know that the world belongs to the Imam? He places it where he wills and gives it to whom he wills; that is permissible for him from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the Imam never spends a night at all while there is upon his neck a right belonging to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about which He will question him.”

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام was asked about what is extracted from the sea, such as pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and about mines of gold and silver: is there zakat on them? He said: “If its value reaches one dinar, then khums is due on it.”

ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He asked about buried treasure: how much is due on it? He said, "The khums." And about mines: how much is due on them? He said, "The khums." And about lead, brass, iron, and whatever is from the minerals: how much is due on them? He said, "It is taken from them just as it is taken from the mines of gold and silver."
1646 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: "Khums is only in spoils specifically."

And Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about that amount of buried treasure for which khums becomes obligatory, so he said: “Whatever amount whose like is subject to zakat, then khums is due in it.”

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the salt flats, so he said: "And what is the salt flat?" I said: "It is a barren salty land in which water gathers and then becomes salt." He said: "It is like a mine; khums is due on it." I said: "Then sulfur and oil are extracted from the earth?" He said: "This and its like, khums is due on it."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, there is no god but Him, when He prohibited charity for us, He sent down khums for us. So charity is forbidden to us, khums is an obligation for us, and honor-gifts are permissible for us.

And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “May Allah keep you well, what is the easiest thing by which a servant enters the Fire?” He said: “Whoever consumes a dirham from the wealth of the orphan—and we are the orphan.”

Zakariyyā ibn Mālik al-Juʿfī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And know that whatever you gain, a fifth of it is for Allah, the Messenger, the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler." He said: "As for Allah's khums, it is for the Messenger, who places it in the way of Allah. As for the khums of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, it is for his relatives. And the khums of the near relatives means his close kin. And the orphans are the orphans of his Ahl al-Bayt, so He made these four shares among them. As for the needy and the sons of the road, you have known that we do not eat charity, nor is it lawful for us; so it is for the needy and the sons of the road."
1652 - And in the written communications of al-Ridha عليه السلام to Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī: "Khums is due after expenses."
And Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: "Any dhimmī who buys land from a Muslim is liable for khums upon it."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of them عليهما السلام, who said: "Indeed, the most severe matter that people will face on the Day of Resurrection is that the صاحب of khums will stand and say: 'My Lord, my khums.' And we have made that lawful for our Shi'ah so that their births may be pure, or so that their births may be purified."

A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have acquired wealth in which I was not scrupulous. Is there repentance for me?” He said: “Bring me its khums.” So he brought him its khums. Then he said: “It is yours. Indeed, when a man repents, his wealth repents with him.”

Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام was asked about a man from whom these people take the zakat of his wealth, or the khums of his spoils, or the khums of what is extracted for him from the mines: is that counted for him toward his zakat and khums? He said: “Yes.”

And it is narrated from Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: “Something is brought to us, and it is said: ‘This belonged to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام and is with us.’ So how should we act?” So he said: “Whatever belonged to my father عليه السلام by reason of the Imamate, then it is mine; and whatever was other than that, then it is inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: “Indeed, I take a dirham from one of you, while I am surely among the wealthiest people of al-Madīnah in property. I intend by that nothing except that you may be purified.”

And it is narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man from among the qammāṭīn entered upon him and said: “May I be your ransom.” Profits, wealth, and trade come into our hands, and we know that your right in them is established, yet we fall short regarding that. So he عليه السلام said: “We would not have dealt justly with you if we had obligated you with that today.”

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār that he said: I read in a letter from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام to a man who was asking him to make lawful for him his food and drink from the khums. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: “Whoever is in need of something from my right, then he is permitted.”

And Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who dies and has no heir and no mawla for him, so he said, "He is among the people meant by this verse: 'They ask you about the anfal.'"
And Dāwūd ibn Kathīr al-Raqqī narrated from him that he said: "Indeed, all people live in the surplus of the wrong done to us, except that we have made that permissible for our Shīʿah."

And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, Jibril عليه السلام dug with his foot five rivers, and the tongue of the water followed him: the Euphrates, the Tigris, the Nile of Egypt, the Mehran, and the river of Balkh. So whatever they irrigated, or was watered from them, belongs to the Imam, as does the ocean encompassing the world."

Allah, the Exalted, said: “And give its due on the day of its harvest.” This means that you take in your hand one bundle after another and give it to the needy person, then another needy person, until you finish from it. At the time of date-cutting, a handful after a handful until you finish from it; and from the gathering, a handful after a handful until you finish from it. And something is left for the guard who is in the orchard as a known wage, and from the palm tree there is left ma‘āfārah and Umm Ja‘rūr, and there is left for the guard one cluster, two clusters, and three for his guarding it. As for His, the Exalted, saying: “And do not be wasteful; indeed, He does not love the wasteful.” Then wastefulness is that you give away everything with both your hands.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Do not harvest at night, do not reap at night, do not cut at night, do not sacrifice at night, and do not sow at night, because you give at the time of sowing just as you give at the time of harvest. Whenever you do that at night, the needy, the beggars, the content poor, and the one who comes asking will not be present before you.

And it is narrated from Muṣādif, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام on land belonging to him while they were harvesting, and a beggar came asking, so I said: “May Allah provide for you.” So he said: “Hold on. That is not for you, until you give three. Then if you give after that, it is for you, and if you withhold, it is for you.”

It is narrated from Mus'ab ibn Yazid al-Ansari, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام appointed me over four districts of al-Mada'in: al-Bihqubadhat, Bahurasir, Nahr Jawbar, and Nahr al-Malik. He instructed me to levy on each jarib of dense crops one and a half dirhams, on each jarib of medium crops one dirham, on each jarib of light crops two-thirds of a dirham, on each jarib of vineyards ten dirhams, on each jarib of date palms ten dirhams, and on each jarib of gardens that combine palms and trees ten dirhams. He also instructed me to leave every isolated date palm away from the villages for passersby and wayfarers, and not to take anything from it. And he instructed me to impose upon the dahqins, those who ride thoroughbred mounts and wear gold rings, forty-eight dirhams on each man among them; upon their middle class and their merchants, twenty-four dirhams on each man; and upon their lower class and their poor, twelve dirhams on each person among them. He said: So I collected from it eighteen million dirhams in one year.

1668 - Fudayl ibn 'Uthman al-A'war narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said: “There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah. Then it is his two parents who make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله granted dhimmah and accepted jizyah from the heads of those specific people themselves on the condition that they would not make their children Jews or Christians. As for the children of the people of dhimmah today, there is no dhimmah for them.”

1669 - And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accepted the jizyah from the people of the dhimmah on the condition that they would not consume usury, would not eat the flesh of swine, and would not marry sisters, nor daughters of a brother, nor daughters of a sister. So whoever among them does that, then the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله is absolved from him." And he said: "Today, they have no covenant."

And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the limit of the jizyah upon the People of the Book, and is there regarding that a fixed amount which should not be exceeded to something else? He said: That is up to the Imam. He takes from each person among them whatever he wishes according to his wealth and what he can bear. They are only a people who ransomed themselves so that they would not be enslaved or killed. So the jizyah is taken from them according to what they can bear. He may exact that from them until they accept Islam, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Until they give the jizyah out of hand while they are humbled. And he does not care about what is taken from him until he finds humiliation in what has been taken from him, so that he feels pain because of that and then accepts Islam.

1671 - And Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “What do you think about what these people take from this khums from the land of jizyah, and they take from the dahāqīn the jizyah of their heads? Is there upon them, in that, any fixed obligation?” So he said: “What was binding upon them was what they themselves accepted upon themselves, and the Imam has no more than the jizyah. If the Imam wishes, he places that upon their heads, and there is nothing upon their wealth; and if he wishes, then it is upon their wealth, and there is nothing upon their heads.” So I said: “Then this khums?” He said: “This is only something concerning which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله made an agreement with them.”
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding the people of the jizyah: is anything taken from their wealth and their livestock besides the jizyah? He said, "No."

1673 - He said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the sadaqat of the People of the dhimmah and what is taken from their jizyah from the price of their wines, the meat of their pigs, and their carrion. So he said: “The jizyah is due from them upon their wealth. It may be taken from them from the price of pork, or wine, and whatever they took from that, the burden of that is upon them, while its price is halal for the Muslims, who may take it as part of their jizyah.”

Talḥah ibn Zayd narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The sunnah (prophetic practice) has been established that the jizyah is not taken from the mentally impaired, nor from one overcome in his intellect."

1675 - Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated; he said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about women—how the jizyah was dropped and lifted from them. So he said: “Because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade the killing of women and children in Dār al-Ḥarb, unless they fight. And even if she fights as well, then refrain from her as much as you can, so long as you do not fear a breach. So when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade killing them in Dār al-Ḥarb, that was even more fitting in Dār al-Islām. And if she were to refuse to pay the jizyah, her killing would not be possible; so when her killing was not possible, the jizyah was lifted from her. But if the men withheld and refused to pay the jizyah, they would be breaking the covenant, and their blood and their killing would become lawful, because killing men is permissible in Dār al-Shirk and in the case of dhimmah. And likewise, the crippled among the people of shirk and dhimmah, the blind, the aged old man, the woman, and the children in the land of war—for that reason, the jizyah was lifted from them.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabī, who said: A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the Bedouins: Is jihad incumbent upon them? He said: “There is no jihad upon them unless Islam is feared for, in which case their help is sought.” He said: Then do they have any share from the jizyah? He said: “No.”

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the policy of the Imam regarding the land that was conquered after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. He said: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام conducted himself among the people of Iraq with a policy that is an exemplar for all other lands.” And he said: “The jizyah is not removed from the land of jizyah. Rather, the jizyah is the allotment of the mujāhidīn, while the charities belong to their people whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, named in His Book; they have no share of the jizyah.” Then he عليه السلام said: “How vast justice is! Indeed, people become free of need when justice is established among them, and the sky sends down its provision and the earth brings forth its blessing by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

And the Magians, the jizyah is taken from them, because the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Apply to them the sunnah (prophetic practice) of the People of the Book. They had a prophet whose name was Dāmasb, and they killed him, and a book called Jāmāsb, which used to be set down on twelve thousand hides of oxen, and they burned it."

Abū al-Ward asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a Christian slave belonging to a Muslim man: “Is jizyah due upon him?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then should his Muslim master pay the jizyah on his behalf?” He said: “Yes. He is only his property; he ransoms him if he is taken, paying on his behalf.”
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "The first to enter Paradise will be kindness and its people, and the first to come to me at the Pond."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The people of kindness in this world are the people of kindness in the Hereafter."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Every act of kindness is charity, and the one who guides to goodness is like the one who does it, and Allah loves relieving the distressed."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Perform acts of kindness toward everyone. If he is deserving of it, then it belongs to him; and if not, then you are deserving of it."
And he, peace be upon him, said: “Any believer who extends a kindness to his fellow believer has indeed extended that to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Al-ma'ruf is something apart from zakat, so draw near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through righteousness and maintaining kinship ties."

1686 - And he, peace be upon him, said: “I found kindness to be true to its name, and nothing is better than kindness except its reward, and that is what is intended from it. Not everyone who loves to do kindness to people does it, and not everyone who desires it is able to do it, nor is everyone who is able to do it given permission concerning it. So when desire, ability, and permission come together, then happiness is complete for the seeker and the one to whom it is done.”
And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Acts of kindness protect against evil downfalls."

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The best charity is charity given from a position of affluence. Begin with those whom you support. The upper hand is better than the lower hand, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not reproach for sufficiency.”
And he, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Indeed, blessing comes more swiftly to the house from which good is given than a blade passes into the hump of a camel, or a flood reaches its end."
And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Everything has a fruit, and the fruit of goodness is hastening it."

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: I observed that goodness is only set right through three qualities: minimizing it, concealing it, and hastening it. For when you minimize it, you magnify it in the eyes of the one for whom you do it; when you conceal it, you complete it; and when you hasten it, you make it pleasant. But if it is otherwise than that, you ruin it and embitter it.

1692 - And he, peace be upon him, said to al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar: “O Mufaḍḍal, if you wish to know whether a man is wretched or fortunate, then look at his kindness and to whom he gives it. If he gives it to one who deserves it, then know that he is upon good. And if he gives it to one other than its people, then know that he has no good with Allah, the Exalted.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, Allah has given you these surplus amounts of wealth so that you may direct them where Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has directed them, and He did not give them to you so that you would hoard them.

And he, peace be upon him, said: If people were to take what Allah commanded them to take and spend it on what He prohibited, He would not accept it from them. And if they were to take what Allah prohibited and spend it on what He commanded, He would not accept it from them until they take it from what is rightful and spend it in what is rightful.

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Whoever is shown kindness, let him reciprocate it. If he is unable, then let him offer praise. If he does not do so, then he has been ungrateful for the blessing."

1696 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "May Allah curse those who cut off the path of kindness." It was said: "Who are those who cut off the path of kindness?" He said: "A man is shown kindness, then he is ungrateful for it, so he prevents its doer from doing that to others."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "It is written on the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan is rewarded eighteenfold."

And he, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "There is no good in much of their secret conversation except for one who enjoins charity or kindness or reconciliation between people." He said: "Kindness refers to lending."

And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no believer who lends to another believer, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that its reward is counted for him according to the reckoning of charity until his wealth returns to him.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Lending to a believer is a gain and a hastening of goodness; if he becomes able, he repays it, and if he dies, it is counted as part of his zakat."

Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the reason for sawm (fasting), so he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only prescribed sawm (fasting) so that through it the rich and the poor may become equal. That is because the rich would not experience the touch of hunger and so have mercy on the poor, since the rich, whenever they desire something, are able to obtain it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted to make equality among His creation and to let the rich taste the touch of hunger and pain, so that he may become tender toward the weak and thus have mercy on the hungry."

1767 - Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān, in what he wrote as a response to his questions: “The reason for sawm (fasting) is to know the touch of hunger and thirst, so that one may become humble, meek, rewarded, seeking reward, and patient. That also serves as a proof for him regarding the hardships of the Hereafter, along with what it contains of breaking him away from desires, acting as an admonisher for him in the immediate world and as a guide to the final abode, so that he may know the severity of the condition of the people of poverty and destitution in this world and the Hereafter.”

1768 - Hamzah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Muhammad عليه السلام: Why did Allah make fasting obligatory? So the response came: “So that the rich may experience the touch of hunger, and thus show generosity to the poor.”

1769 - It is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said: "A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the most learned among them asked him about certain matters. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: 'For what reason did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, make sawm (fasting) obligatory upon your Ummah in the daytime for thirty days, while Allah made it obligatory upon the nations more than that?' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Indeed, when Adam عليه السلام ate from the tree, it remained in his belly for thirty days. So Allah imposed upon his progeny thirty days of hunger and thirst, and what they eat at night is a grace from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon them. And thus it was for Adam عليه السلام. So Allah imposed that upon my Ummah.' Then he recited this verse: "Prescribed for you is fasting as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may attain taqwa. [For] numbered days." The Jew said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muḥammad.' Then, 'What is the reward of one who fasts them?' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'There is no believer who fasts the Month of Ramaḍān seeking reward except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, makes obligatory for him seven qualities. The first of them is that the haram in his body melts away. The second is that he draws near to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The third is that he will have expiated the sin of Adam, his father, عليه السلام. The fourth is that Allah makes easy for him the agonies of death. The fifth is security from hunger and thirst on the Day of Resurrection. The sixth is that Allah gives him acquittal from the Fire. And the seventh is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, feeds him from the wholesome things of Paradise.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muḥammad.'"

It is narrated from the righteous servant, Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: "Recite this supplication in the month of Ramadan at the beginning of the year." He mentioned, "Whoever recites it sincerely and with intention will not be afflicted in that year with tribulation or calamity in his religion, worldly affairs, or body, and Allah will protect him from the harm of what comes in that year. O Allah, I ask You by Your Name to which all things yield, by Your mercy that encompasses all things, by Your might through which You overpower all things, by Your greatness to which all things humble themselves, by Your strength to which all things submit, by Your dominion that surpasses all things, and by Your knowledge that "encompasses all things." O Light, O Holy One, O the First before all things and the Remaining after all things, O Allah, O Merciful, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And forgive me the sins that change blessings, and forgive me the sins that bring down vengeance, and forgive me the sins that cut off hope, and forgive me the sins that bring adversaries near, and forgive me the sins that repel supplication, and forgive me the sins that bring down tribulations, and forgive me the sins that withhold the rains of the sky, and forgive me the sins that tear apart protections. And clothe me in Your impenetrable armor, which cannot be pierced, and grant me well-being from the harm of what I fear by night and by day in the coming year of mine. O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and what is within them and between them, and Lord of the Great Throne, and Lord of the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses and the Magnificent Quran, and Lord of Israfil, Mika'il, and Jibril, and Lord of Muhammad, master of the messengers and seal of the prophets. I ask You by You and by what You have named Yourself, O Magnificent. You are the One who bestows great blessings, averts all feared calamities, grants abundant rewards, multiplies abundant good deeds from little, and does whatever You will. O All-Powerful, O Allah, O Merciful, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And clothe me in the coming year of mine with Your protection, and illuminate my face with Your light, and enliven me with Your love, and bring me to Your satisfaction, the honor of Your noble gifts, and the greatness of Your bount

1849 - And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام used to supplicate with this supplication in the month of Ramadan. "O Allah, this is the month of Ramadan in which You sent down the Qur'an. This is the month of sawm (fasting), this is the month of turning back, this is the month of tawbah (repentance), this is the month of forgiveness and mercy, and this is the month of freedom from the Fire and triumph with Paradise. O Allah, deliver it safely to me and receive it from me, help me in it with the best of Your help, grant me success in it for Your obedience, free me in it for Your worship, Your supplication, and the recitation of Your Book, magnify for me in it the blessing, make well-being good for me in it, make my body sound for me in it, expand in it my provision, suffice me in it regarding what concerns me, answer in it my supplication, and let me attain in it my hope. O Allah, remove from me in it drowsiness, laziness, weariness, slackness, hardness, heedlessness, and delusion. O Allah, keep me away in it from ailments, sicknesses, anxieties, sorrows, afflictions, diseases, mistakes, and sins, and turn away from me in it evil, indecency, hardship, affliction, fatigue, and suffering." "Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication." O Allah, grant me refuge in it from the accursed Shaytan, his goading, his slander, his blowing, his puffing, his whispering, his plotting, his scheming, his deception, his false wishes, his trickery, his delusion, his temptation, his cavalry, his infantry, his partners, his factions, his helpers, his followers, his intimates, his partisans, his allies, and all of their plotting. O Allah, grant me in it the completion of its fasting, attainment of hope in its standing, and completion of what pleases You from me in patience, faith, certainty, and seeking reward; then accept that from me with many multiplied measures and great reward. O Allah, grant me in it earnestness, striving, strength, vigor, turning back, repentance, desire, fear, anguish, humility, tenderness, truthful speech, fear from You, hope in You, reliance upon You, trust in You, and scrupulousness regarding Your sacred limits, along with righteous speech and accepted striving. [And the completion of what pleases You from me in it in patience, certainty, faith, and seeking reward; then accept that from me with many multiplied measures and great reward. O Allah, grant me i

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he broke his fast, would say: "O Allah, for You we fasted, and upon Your sustenance we have broken our fast. So accept it from us. The thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward remains."

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “You say every night of the Month of Ramadan at the time of breaking the fast until its end: ‘All praise belongs to Allah, who helped us so we fasted, and provided for us so we broke our fast. O Allah, accept from us, help us in it, keep us safe in it, and receive it from us with ease and well-being from You. All praise belongs to Allah, who has completed for us a day of the Month of Ramadan.’”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The supplication of the fasting person is answered at the time of breaking the fast."
Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "The fasting person is not harmed by what he does so long as he avoids four qualities: food, drink, women, and immersing in water."
And in the narration of Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Indeed, lying against Allah and against the Imams عليهم السلام causes the fasting person to break the fast."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: "When you fast, then let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin fast as well," and he mentioned other things besides this. And he said: "The day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking the fast."

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has disliked six traits for me, and I have disliked them for the successors from among my progeny and their followers after me. One of them is indecency during fasting."

Abu Basir narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: “Indeed, sawm (fasting) is not from food and drink alone. Indeed, Maryam said, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast,’ meaning silence. So guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not envy one another, and do not quarrel. For indeed envy consumes faith just as fire consumes wood.”

And the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: During the month of Ramadan, hold fast to abundant seeking forgiveness and supplication. As for supplication, it repels affliction from you; and as for seeking forgiveness, your sins are erased by it.

1859 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite it during the nights or days of the month of Ramadan." Isma'il said to him, "O my father, even if it is about us?" He عليه السلام said, "Even if it is about us."

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: There is no fasting servant who is insulted and then says, 'Indeed, I am fasting. Peace be upon you. I will not insult you as you insult me,' except that the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'My servant has sought refuge through fasting from the evil of My servant; I have granted him protection from the Fire.'

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله heard a woman insulting a servant-girl of hers while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله called for food and said to her, “Eat.” She said, “Indeed I am fasting.” He said, “How can you be fasting when you have insulted your servant-girl? Indeed, fasting is not only from food and drink.”

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast from the unlawful and the reprehensible. Leave argumentation and harming the servant. Let the dignity of the fasting person be upon you, and do not make the day of your fast like the day of your breaking the fast.
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When we wish to perform cupping during the month of Ramadan, we do it at night."

He said: And I asked him, "Can a fasting person perform cupping?" So he said, "I fear for him what he might fear for himself." He said: I said, "What do you fear for him?" He said, "Fainting, or that bile may be stirred in him." I said, "What if he is strong enough for that and does not fear anything?" He said, "Yes, if he wishes."
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام disliked that a fasting person perform cupping, out of fear that he might faint and then break his fast.

1866 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: He was asked about regurgitation: “Does it invalidate the fast of the fasting person?” He said: “No.” There is no harm in rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose for the fasting person. When he rinses his mouth and nose, he should not swallow his saliva until he spits three times; and if he rinses his mouth and water enters his throat, then if that was for the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer), there is no make-up fast upon him.

Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who played with water, rinsing his mouth with it due to thirst, and it entered his throat. He said: "He must make it up. But if it was during wudu (ablution), there is no harm in it."

1868 - He said: And I asked him about vomiting during the Month of Ramadan. He said: "If it is something that overcomes him involuntarily, then there is no harm. But if it is something for which he compels himself, then he has broken the fast, and qada' is upon him."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who uses an enema due to an illness during the month of Ramadan. He عليه السلام said: "It is not permissible for a fasting person to use an enema."

It was narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim that he said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man places a date pit in his mouth while he is fasting. He said: “No.” I said: Then he places a ring? He said: “Yes.” And whoever experiences a wet dream during the daytime in the month of Ramaḍān, then he should complete his fast, and there is no makeup fast upon him.
And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a fasting person extracting his molar, he said: “No, and he should not make his mouth bleed.”
And it was narrated from al-Hasan ibn Rashid that he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, when he fasted, would apply perfume and say, "Perfume is a gift for the fasting person."

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. That he was asked about a man entering the bathhouse while he is fasting, so he said: “There is no harm so long as he does not fear weakness.”

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, was asked about a man kissing his wife while he is fasting. He said: "Is she anything but a fragrant flower that he smells?" And better than that is for the fasting person to refrain from kissing.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Does one of you not feel ashamed that he cannot endure one day until the night? Indeed, it used to be said: the beginning of fighting is slapping.” And if a man clung closely to his wife in the month of Ramadan and ejaculated, then freeing a slave would be obligatory upon him.

Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about a man who touched his female servant during the Month of Ramadan and emitted madhy. He عليه السلام said: “If it was unlawful, then he must seek Allah’s forgiveness with the seeking forgiveness of one who will never return to it ever, and he must fast one day in place of one day.”
Sama'ah asked him: About a man who closely attaches himself to his wife during the month of Ramadan, so he said: "As long as he does not fear for himself, there is no harm."

Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ al-Taymī narrated from Ibn Riʾāb, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام forbidding narcissus for the fasting person. So I said, 'May I be your ransom, and why?' He said: 'Because it is the fragrant herb of the non-Arabs.'

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the muhrim smelling rayhan. He said: "No." It was said: "What about the fasting person?" He said: "No." It was said: "May the fasting person smell perfumed compound and incense?" He said: "Yes." It was said: "How is it lawful for him to smell perfume but not smell rayhan?" He said: "Because perfume is a sunnah, while rayhan is an innovation for the fasting person."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام, when he fasted, would not smell الريحان, so he was asked about that, and he said: "I dislike mixing my fast with pleasure."
And it is narrated: “Whoever applies perfume at the beginning of the day while he is fasting will hardly lose his sanity.”

1882 - And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: That he asked him about a man who feels cold: may he enter under a blanket with his wife while he is fasting? He said, "He should place a cloth between them." And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān has narrated from him عليه السلام: "A concession for the elderly man regarding physical closeness."

Ḥanān ibn Sadīr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. About the fasting person immersing himself in water, he said: “There is no harm, but he should not submerge himself; and a woman should not immerse herself in water, because she carries the water by her private part.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who deliberately broke his fast during the month of Ramadan for one day without any excuse, he said: "He must free a slave, or fast for two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. If he cannot do so, he should give charity according to what he is able."

ʿAbd al-Muʾmin ibn al-Qāsim al-Anṣārī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: "A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said, 'I am ruined, and I have ruined myself.' He said, 'And what ruined you?'" He said, 'I went to my wife in the Month of Ramaḍān while I was fasting.' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said, 'Free a slave.' He said, 'I cannot find [the means].' He said, 'Then fast two consecutive months.' He said, 'I am unable.' He said, 'Give charity to sixty poor persons.' He said, 'I cannot find [the means].' Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was brought a date-cluster in a basket containing fifteen ṣāʿ of dates. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said, 'Take it and give it in charity.' He said, 'By the One Who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, there is no household between its two lava tracts more in need of it than us.' He said, 'Take it, then eat it, you and your family, for it is an expiation for you.'
And in the narration of Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "The basket that was brought to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم contained twenty sa's of dates."

And Idris ibn Hilal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who had relations with his wife during the month of Ramadan. He said: "He must give twenty sa's of dates; for that is what the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed the man who came to him and asked him about that."

Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from him, peace be upon him: that he was asked about a man who broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramaḍān, so he said: "His expiation is two jarībān of food, and that is twenty ṣāʿs."

And in the narration of al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who had relations with his wife while he was fasting and she was fasting, he said: “If he forced her, then two expiations are upon him. If she consented to him, then one expiation is upon him and one expiation is upon her. If he compelled her, then upon him is fifty lashes, half of the prescribed punishment. And if she consented to him, he is given twenty-five lashes and she is given twenty-five lashes.”

1890 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he broke his fast for three days during the Month of Ramadan. He said: "He is asked: 'Is there sin upon you in your breaking the fast in the Month of Ramadan?' If he says, 'No,' then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, 'Yes,' then it is upon the Imam to punish him with severe beating."

And in the narration of Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who was caught in the Month of Ramadan after having broken the fast three times, and had been brought before the Imam three times. He said: "Then he is executed on the third occasion."

1892 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever breaks a fast for one day of the Month of Ramadan, the spirit of faith departs from him. And whoever intentionally breaks the fast in the Month of Ramadan, upon him is one kaffarah and the making up of one day in its place; and how can he have the like of it?" As for the report that has been narrated regarding one who intentionally breaks the fast for a day in the Month of Ramadan, that three kaffarahs are upon him, then I give fatwa according to it concerning one who breaks the fast through intercourse forbidden to him or through food forbidden to him, due to the presence of that in the narrations of Abi al-Husayn al-Asadi — may Allah be pleased with him — in what came to him from al-Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Uthman al-'Umari — may Allah sanctify his soul.

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he was asked about a man who forgot and ate and drank, then remembered. He said: "His fast is not broken; rather, it is something Allah has provided for him, so let him complete his fast."

And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā asked him about a man who forgets while he is fasting and has intercourse with his wife. He said: He should perform ghusl (ritual bath), and there is nothing upon him. The author of this book—may Allah have mercy on him—said: And that applies in the month of Ramadan and other than it, and making up the fast is not obligatory in it. Thus it has been narrated from the Imams عليهم السلام.

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub at night in the Month of Ramadan, then forgets to perform ghusl until a week passes for that, or the Month of Ramadan ends. He said: “He is liable for the make-up of the salat and the sawm.”

And it is narrated in another report: If someone has intercourse at the beginning of the Month of Ramadan and then forgets the ghusl (ritual bath) until the Month of Ramadan ends, then he must perform ghusl and make up his salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting), unless he had performed ghusl for Jumu'ah, in which case he makes up his salat and fasting only up to that day and does not make up what comes after that.

And in the narration of Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Saʿīd al-Qammāṭ: That Abū ʿAbdِ ٱللَّهِ عليه السلام was asked about someone who became junub at the beginning of the night in the Month of Ramadan, then slept until morning. He said: “There is nothing upon him, and that is because his janābah occurred at a permissible time.”

And Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man becomes junub in the Month of Ramadan, then wakes up, then sleeps, then wakes up, then sleeps until morning. He said: He completes his fast and makes up another day. But if he did not wake up until morning, he completes his fast and it is valid for him.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: About a man making up the fasts of the Month of Ramadan, who becomes junub at the beginning of the night and does not perform ghusl until the end of the night, while thinking that dawn has already risen. He said: “He should not fast that day, and he should fast another day instead.”
Al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim asked him: About a man who sleeps during the month of Ramadan, then has a wet dream, then wakes up, then sleeps again before performing ghusl. He said: “There is no harm.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who fasted, then thought that the sun had set while there were clouds in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the clouds cleared, and suddenly the sun had not set. He said: “His fast has been completed, and he does not make it up.”

Hammad narrated from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: The time of Maghrib is when the disk disappears. If you see it after that, and you have already prayed, you must repeat the salat (prayer), while your sawm (fast) remains valid, and you must refrain from food if you had consumed any of it.

1903 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “A child is to be made to fast when he reaches nine years, according to the extent of what he can bear. So if he is able until noon or after it, he fasts until that time; then if hunger or thirst overcomes him, he breaks the fast.”
And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from him that he said: "If a boy is able to fast for three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan has become obligatory upon him."
Sama'ah asked him: About the child: when should he fast? He said, "When he is strong enough to fast."

And in the narration of Mu‘āwiyah ibn Wahb, he said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at what age a child is to be held to fasting. He عليه السلام said: 'Between fourteen and fifteen years. If he fasts before that, then leave him be. My son so-and-so fasted before that, and I left him.'
1907 - And in another report: "A boy is required to fast when he reaches puberty, and a woman is required to fast when she menstruates."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “When you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. It is not by opinion or conjecture. And sighting is not that ten people stand looking, then one of them says, ‘There it is, there it is,’ while nine look and do not see it. Rather, when one sees it, a thousand see it.”

Al-Faḍl ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He said: “There is no obligation upon the people of the qiblah except sighting, and there is no obligation upon the Muslims except sighting.”

And in the narration of al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "Fasting is for the sighting, and breaking the fast is for the sighting, and sighting is not that one person sees it, nor two, nor fifty."

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: "When you see the crescent, then break your fast, or if a just Muslim bears witness to it, and if you do not see the crescent except from the middle of the day or its end, then: "complete the fasting until the night." So if it is obscured from you, then count thirty nights, then break your fast."
And in the narration of al-Ḥalabī from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “I do not accept regarding the sighting of the crescent except the testimony of two just men.”

Sama'ah asked him about a day in the Month of Ramadan concerning which there is disagreement. He said: "If the people of the city agree upon fasting it on the basis of sighting, then observe it, if the people of the city are five hundred persons."
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: "The testimony of women is not accepted regarding the sighting of the crescent; only the testimony of two just men is accepted."

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About a man who sees the crescent in the Month of Ramadan by himself, and no one else sees it: should he fast? He said: "If he has no doubt, then let him break the fast; otherwise, let him fast it with the people."

Muḥammad ibn Murāzim narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If the crescent is encircled, then it is for two nights; and if you see the shadow of your head in it, then it is for three nights."

1917 - And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Ḥurr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If the crescent sets before twilight, then it is for one night; and if it sets after twilight, then it is for two nights."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "If the crescent of Rajab is confirmed, then count fifty-nine days and fast on the sixtieth day."
And he, peace be upon him, said: If you fasted the Month of Ramadan in the previous year on a known day, then in the coming year count five days from that day and fast on the fifth day.

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man was taken captive by the Romans, and the month of Ramadan was not established for him, and he did not know which month it was. He عليه السلام said: He should fast for a month, estimating and calculating. If the month that he fasted was before the month of Ramadan, it does not suffice for him; but if it was after the month of Ramadan, it suffices for him.
Al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim asked him: about the crescent: when the people all see it and agree that it is for two nights, is that permissible? He said: "Yes."
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was asked about the doubtful day. He said: “That I fast one day from Shaʿban is more beloved to me than that I break the fast for one day from the month of Ramadan.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man who embraced Islam in the middle of the month of Ramadan: what is required of him regarding his fasting? He عليه السلام said: “He is not required to fast except for what remains from the time in which he embraced Islam, and he is not required to make up what has already passed of it.”

Because the Commander of the Faithful, عليه السلام, said: "That I break my fast for one day of the month of Ramadan is more beloved to me than that I fast one day from Sha'ban and add it into the month of Ramadan."

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a group of people who accepted Islam during the Month of Ramadan after some days of it had already passed: are they required to fast what has passed of it, or their day on which they accepted Islam? He said: "There is no qada' upon them, nor [must they fast] their day on which they accepted Islam, unless they had accepted Islam on it before the rising of dawn."

Bashīr al-Nabbāl asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of Doubt, so he said: "Fast it. If it is from Shaʿbān, it is voluntary; and if it is from the month of Ramaḍān, then it is a day you were granted success to fast."

ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr asked him and said: I have made it binding upon myself to fast until al-Qāʾim عليه السلام rises. He said: “Do not fast during travel, nor on the two ʿEids, nor on the days of Tashrīq, nor on the day about which there is doubt.”

And it has been narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Abī Manṣūr that he said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام on the day about which the people were uncertain. So he said, “O boy, go and see whether the Amīr has fasted or not.” He went, then returned, and said, “No.” Then he called for the midday meal, and we ate with him.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "If I were to say that abandoning taqiyyah is like abandoning salat (prayer), I would be truthful."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "There is no religion for one who has no taqiyyah."

1929 - And ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī narrated from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام saying: “Fasting is upon sighting, and breaking the fast is upon sighting; and he is not from us who fasts before the sighting for the sighting, and breaks the fast before the sighting for the sighting.” He said: I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what do you hold regarding the fasting of the day of doubt?” So he said: “My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: ‘That I fast one day from the month of Shaʿbān is more beloved to me than that I break the fast one day from the month of Ramaḍān.’”

ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: When the disk disappears, the fasting person breaks the fast, and the time of salat (prayer) begins.

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he was asked about breaking the fast before the salat (prayer) or after it. He said: “If he is with a group and fears that he may keep them waiting from their dinner, then let him break his fast with them. But if it is otherwise, then let him perform the salat (prayer), then break his fast.”

1934 - 'Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr Layth al-Murādī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: 'When does food become forbidden for the fasting person, and when does the salat, the salat of al-fajr, become permissible?' So he said to me: 'When the dawn stretches across, and it is like a white cloth, then food becomes forbidden for the fasting person, and the salat, the salat of al-fajr, becomes permissible.' I said: 'Are we not still within the time until the rays of the sun rise?' He said: 'Far from it! Where are you being taken by that? That is the prayer of children.'

1935 - Abū Baṣīr narrated from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn." He عليه السلام said: "It was revealed concerning Khawwāt ibn Jubayr al-Anṣārī. He was with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the trench while he was fasting, and he entered the evening in that state. Before this verse was revealed, when one of them slept, food became forbidden to him. So Khawwāt came to his family when evening came and said, 'Do you have any food?' They said, 'Do not sleep until we prepare food for you.' Then he reclined and fell asleep. They said, 'You have done it.' He said, 'Yes.' So he spent the night in that state and entered the morning. Then he went out to the trench, and he began to faint. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by him, and when he saw what was with him, he informed him how his affair had been. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn." ".
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked: about: “the white thread from the black thread of dawn” So he said: “It is the whiteness of the day from the darkness of the night.”
And he said in another report: "And it is the dawn about which there is no doubt.

Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked him about two men who rose and looked toward the dawn. One of them said, "There it is," and the other said, "I do not see anything." He said: "Then let the one for whom dawn has not become clear eat and drink, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:" "And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn; then complete the fast until the night." Sama'ah said: And I asked him about a man who ate and drank after dawn had risen in the month of Ramadan. He said: "If he rose and looked, but did not see the dawn, then ate, and afterward looked again and saw the dawn, then he should complete his fast and there is no repetition upon him. But if he rose and ate and drank, then looked toward the dawn and saw that it had risen, then he should complete that fast and make up another day, because he began with eating before looking, so repetition is upon him."

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-ʿIs ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about a man who went out during the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating suhoor in a house. He looked at the dawn and called out to them that dawn had indeed risen. So some stopped, while some thought that he was joking, and so he ate. He said: “He completes the fast and makes it up.”

1940 - And Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: 'I instruct the servant girl to look toward the dawn, and she says that it has not yet risen, so I eat. Then I look and find that it had already risen when she looked.' He عليه السلام said: 'Make it up. However, if you had been the one who looked, there would have been nothing upon him.'

1941 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام what is the limit of the illness in which the fasting person breaks the fast and leaves the salat (prayer) from standing, so he said: "Rather, man is a witness against himself." And he knows best what he is able to bear.

And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I became feverish in al-Madinah one day in the month of Ramadan, so Abu Abdullah عليه السلام sent to me a bowl in which there was vinegar and oil, and he said to me, ‘Break your fast and perform salat (prayer) while you are sitting.’

Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: My father asked him while I was listening about the extent of illness in which a person leaves the fast. He said: 'When he is not able to take suhoor.'

Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, complained of her eye in the month of Ramaḍān, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her to break her fast and said: “The evening meal of the night is harmful for your eyes.”
And in the narration of Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "The fasting person, if he fears for his eyes from ophthalmia, breaks the fast."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Anything for which fasting causes harm, then breaking the fast is obligatory for him."
Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: "Islam is built upon five things: salat (prayer), zakat (alms-tax), hajj (pilgrimage), sawm (fasting), and wilayah (divinely appointed authority)."
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Fasting is a shield from the Fire."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The fasting person is in worship, even if he is sleeping on his bed, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim."

And he, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Fasting is for Me, and I reward for it.' And the fasting person has two joys: when he breaks his fast and when he meets his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the breath of the fasting person is more fragrant with Allah than the scent of musk."

Hadith 1774 — The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to his companions: “Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, Shaytan will be distanced from you as the east is distanced from the west?” They said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and mutual support in righteous deed cut off his remnant, and seeking forgiveness severs his life-vein. For everything there is a zakat, and the zakat of bodies is fasting.”

1775 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said to ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: "Shall I not inform you of the foundation of Islam, its branch, its summit, and its peak?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Its foundation is salat (prayer), its branch is zakat (alms-tax), and its summit and peak are jihad in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Shall I not inform you of the gates of goodness? Sawm (fasting) is a shield from the Fire."
1776 - And he, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And seek help through patience and prayer." He said: "What is meant by patience is fasting."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "If a calamity or hardship befalls a man, then let him fast, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And seek help through patience and prayer." "

1778 - And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has entrusted angels with supplicating for those who fast. And he said: Jibrīl عليه السلام informed me from his Lord, exalted is His mention, that He said:” “I have not commanded My angels to supplicate for any one of My creation except that I answered them concerning him.”

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Musa عليه السلام: "What prevents you from conversing with Me?" He said: "My Lord, I hold You too exalted for intimate conversation because of the odor of the fasting person's mouth." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "O Musa, the odor of the fasting person's mouth is more pleasant to Me than the fragrance of musk."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: The fasting person has two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

1781 - And he, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever fasts for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for one day in intense heat and is overcome by thirst, Allah appoints for him a thousand angels who wipe his face and give him glad tidings until, when he breaks his fast, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: How pleasant are your fragrance and your spirit. O My angels, bear witness that I have indeed forgiven him.”
Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام said: "Take a nap, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, feeds the fasting person and gives him drink in his sleep."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship, his silence is glorification, his deed is accepted, and his supplication is answered."

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “An elderly person and one afflicted with chronic thirst are under no hardship if they break their fast in the Month of Ramadan. Each one of them should give a mudd of food in charity for every day, and there is no make-up fast upon them. If they are unable, then there is nothing upon them.”

And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who is overcome by thirst until he fears for his life, He عليه السلام said: “He may drink in the measure that preserves his remaining strength, and he should not drink until he is fully quenched.”

And in the narration of Ibn Bukayr: that al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "And upon those who can fast with difficulty, there is a ransom: the feeding of a poor person." He said: "It applies to those who were able to fast, then old age, chronic thirst, or something similar afflicted them; so upon them is a mudd for each day."

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: “I heard him saying:” “A pregnant woman near term and a nursing woman with little milk are under no blame if they break their fast in the Month of Ramaḍān, because they are not able to fast. Each of them must give a mudd of food as charity for every day in which she breaks the fast, and they must make up every day they broke later.”

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUtbah al-Hāshimī asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: About an elderly man and an elderly woman who becomes too weak to fast in the month of Ramadan, he عليه السلام said: “He gives charity for each day a mudd of wheat.”
Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever provides iftar to a fasting person will have a reward equal to his.

1953 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Sadir entered upon my father عليه السلام during the month of Ramadan.
