He said to him: ‘O Sadir, do you know what nights these are?’ He said to him: ‘Yes, may I be your ransom, these are the nights of the month of Ramadan, so what is it?’ My father said to him: ‘Are you able to free, on every night of these nights, ten slaves from the descendants of Ismaʿil?’ Sadir said to him: ‘May my father and mother be for you, my wealth does not reach that.’ So he kept reducing it until he brought it down to one slave, while in all of that he was saying: ‘I am not able to do it.’ Then he said to him: ‘Then are you able to provide iftar each night to one Muslim man?’ He said to him: ‘Yes, and ten as well.’ My father عليه السلام said to him: ‘That is what I intended, O Sadir. Indeed, your providing iftar to your Muslim brother is equal to the freeing of one slave from the descendants of Ismaʿil عليه السلام.’”
Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that he said: "Providing ifṭār to your fasting brother is more virtuous than your own fasting."

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, when it was a day on which he would fast, would order for a sheep to be slaughtered, its limbs cut up, and it cooked. Then when it was evening, he would bend over the cooking pots until he found the smell of the broth while he was fasting, then he would say: “Bring the bowls. Serve for the family of so-and-so; serve for the family of so-and-so.” Then bread and dates would be brought, and that would be his evening meal.

1956 - And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever provides iftar in this month to a believing person who is fasting, there shall be for him by that, with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness for what has passed of his sins.” So it was said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to provide iftar to a fasting person.” So he said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Generous; He gives this reward among you to one who is not able except for a sip of milk by which he gives a fasting person iftar, or a drink of sweet water, or a few dates; he is not able to do more than that.”
1957 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Suhoor is a blessing.” And he عليه السلام said: “My Ummah should not abandon suhoor, even if it is only upon a single dried date.”

Sama'ah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about suhoor for one who intended to fast, so he said: As for the month of Ramaḍān, the merit is in taking suhoor, even if only with a drink of water. And as for voluntary fasting, whoever likes to take suhoor, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no harm.

Abū Baṣīr asked him about suhoor for one who intends to fast, saying: “Is it obligatory upon him?” So he said: “There is no harm in his not taking suhoor, if he wishes. But in the Month of Ramaḍān, it is better that he take suhoor. I prefer that it not be abandoned in the Month of Ramaḍān.”
And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Strengthen yourselves for the fasting of the day by eating suhoor, and for the standing of the night by sleeping at the time of the midday rest."

And it is narrated from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, that he said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and His angels send blessings upon those who seek forgiveness and those who partake in suhoor in the pre-dawn hours. So let one of you partake in suhoor, even if only with a drink of water."
A man asked al-Sadiq عليه السلام and said: I eat while I am unsure about dawn. So he said: "Eat until you are no longer in doubt."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "If people were to partake in suhoor and then not break their fast except with water, they would be able to fast continuously throughout the year."

Zurārah, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and al-Fuḍayl asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir and Abā ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq عليهما السلام about supererogatory prayer at night in the month of Ramadan in congregation. They both said: “The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to, when he had performed the last night prayer, return to his home. Then he would come out in the latter part of the night to the mosque and stand and pray. So he came out on the first night of the month of Ramadan to pray as he used to pray, and the people lined up behind him. He fled from them to his house and left them. They did that for three nights. Then on the third day, he صلى الله عليه وآله stood upon his pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: ‘O people, prayer by night in the month of Ramadan from the supererogatory prayers in congregation is an innovation, and the Duḥā prayer is an innovation. Lo, do not gather by night in the month of Ramadan for the night prayer, and do not perform the Duḥā prayer, for that is an act of disobedience. Lo, every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance, its path is to the Fire.’” Then he صلى الله عليه وآله descended while saying: ‘A little in sunnah (prophetic tradition) is better than much in innovation.’

1965 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan, so he said: “Thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and the two rakʿahs of al-Ṣubḥ before dawn. Thus the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to pray, and I likewise pray. If there had been something better, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would not have left it.”

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the salat in the month of Ramadan, and he said: Thirteen rakʿahs, including the witr and two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr. If it had been an additional merit, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would have acted upon it more and been more deserving of it.

He said: I asked him about the Month of Ramadan, how much is prayed in it. He said: “As is prayed in it.” He said: “As is prayed in other than it, except that the Month of Ramadan has, over all the other months, such merit that it is fitting for the servant to increase in his voluntary prayer. So if he wishes and has strength for that, he may increase in the first part of the month up to twenty nights, praying each night twenty rak'ahs in addition to what he used to pray before that. Of these twenty, he prays twelve rak'ahs between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight rak'ahs after 'Isha. Then he prays the night prayer that he used to pray before that: eight, and the witr is three; he prays two rak'ahs and gives taslim in them, then stands and prays one, making qunut in it, and that is the witr. Then he prays the two rak'ahs of Fajr until dawn breaks, so these are thirteen rak'ahs. Then when ten nights remain of the Month of Ramadan, let him pray thirty rak'ahs in every night besides these thirteen. Of them, he prays twenty-two rak'ahs between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight rak'ahs after 'Isha. Then he prays the night prayer of thirteen rak'ahs as I have described to you. And on the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third, in each one of them, if he has strength for that, he prays one hundred rak'ahs besides these thirteen rak'ahs. And let him remain awake in them until morning, for it is recommended that this be in prayer, supplication, and humble entreaty, for it is hoped that Laylat al-Qadr may be in one of them.”

Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about going out once the month of Ramadan has begun. He عليه السلام said: "No, except in matters about which I inform you: going out to Mecca, or military campaign in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or wealth whose loss you fear, or a brother whose destruction you fear, and he is not a brother from the same father and mother."

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who enters the month of Ramaḍān while resident and not intending to depart, then after the month of Ramaḍān has begun it appears to him to travel. He remained silent, so I asked him more than once, and he said: Staying is better, unless he has a need for which he must go out, or he fears for his wealth.

And al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: He was asked about a man to whom travel presents itself during the Month of Ramadan while he is resident, and some days of it have already passed. So he said, “There is no harm in his traveling, breaking his fast, and not fasting.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man who goes out accompanying his brother for the distance of two or three days. He said: “If it is in the month of Ramadan, then let him break his fast.” Then he was asked: “Which of the two is better: that he stays and fasts, or that he accompanies him?” He said: “He should accompany him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has lifted fasting from him when he accompanies him.”

Al-Washshāʾ narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man from among my companions has sent me news that he is coming from Al-Aʿwaṣ, and that is during the month of Ramadan. Shall I go to meet him and break my fast?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Shall I go to meet him and break my fast, or remain and fast?” He said: “Go to meet him and break your fast.”

Yahya ibn Abi al-ʿAlaʾ narrated from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: "A fasting person in the Month of Ramadan while traveling is like one who breaks his fast in it while resident." Then he said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should I fast the Month of Ramadan while traveling?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is easy for me.' So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has bestowed charity upon the sick of my community and its travelers through breaking the fast in the Month of Ramadan. Would any one of you love, when he gives a charity, that it be returned to him?'"

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it." He عليه السلام said: "How clear it is: whoever is present should fast it, and whoever travels should not fast it."
Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: "If a man were to die while fasting during travel, I would not perform the funeral prayer for him."

1976 - Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: "The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله called a group who fasted when he broke the fast and shortened the prayer, the disobedient." He said: "And they are the disobedient until the Day of Judgment, and we indeed recognize their sons and the sons of their sons up to this day of ours."

Al-‘Iys ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: "When a man travels during the month of Ramadan, he breaks his fast." And he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله departed from al-Madinah to Makkah during the month of Ramadan, and the people were with him, including pedestrians. When he reached Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, he called for a cup of water between zuhr and ‘asr, then drank and broke his fast, and the people broke their fast with him. But some people persisted in their fasting, so he called them ‘the disobedient.’ Indeed, one only acts according to the command of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله."

Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "The best of my Ummah are those who, when they travel, break their fast and shorten [the salat], and when they do good, they rejoice, and when they do wrong, they seek forgiveness. And the worst of my Ummah are those who were born in luxury and nourished in it: they eat fine food, wear soft clothes, and when they speak, they do not speak truthfully."

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: Whoever travels shortens the salat (prayer) and breaks the fast, unless he is a man whose travel is for hunting, or in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or as a messenger for one who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or in pursuit of an enemy, or out of enmity, or for talebearing, or to cause harm to a group of the Muslims.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "A man should not break his fast in the Month of Ramadan except for a rightful cause."
As for voluntary fasting while traveling Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “Fasting while traveling is not an act of righteousness.”

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he was asked about a man who leaves his house intending travel while he is fasting, so he said: "If he departs before the middle of the day, then let him break his fast and make up that day; and if he departs after midday, then let him complete his day."

1983 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If a man travels during the month of Ramaḍān and departs after midday, he must fast that day, and it is counted for him as part of Ramaḍān. وإذا he enters a land before the rise of dawn while intending to reside there, then he must fast that day. But if he enters after the rise of dawn, then no fasting is obligatory upon him, though if he wishes he may fast."

1984 - And in the narration of Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who comes during the month of Ramadan from a journey, such that he expects he will enter upon his family in the mid-morning or later in the day. He said: 'If dawn rises while he is outside and has not yet entered, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.'

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام that he said: Regarding a traveler who enters upon his family while he is junub before noon, and he has not eaten, then he must complete his fast and there is no qada' upon him. He said: that means if his janabah was from ihtilam.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who comes to his slave-girl during the daytime in the month of Ramadan while traveling, so he said: “This one has not recognized the due right of the month of Ramadan; indeed, he has in the night a long span.” He said: I said to him, “Does he not have the right to eat, drink, and shorten?” He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted the traveler a concession in breaking the fast and shortening out of mercy and lightening because of the place of fatigue, hardship, and the roughness of travel. But He did not grant him a concession in having intercourse with women during travel by day in the month of Ramadan; and He made obligatory upon him the qaḍāʾ of the fasting, and He did not make obligatory upon him the qaḍāʾ of completing the salat when he returns from his travel.” Then he said: “And the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is not subject to analogy, and indeed when I travel in the month of Ramadan, I do not eat all the food, nor do I drink to full quenching.”

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man fasted while traveling. He said: “If it had reached him that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prohibited that, then qada is upon him; and if it had not reached him, then there is nothing upon him.”

Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a woman who began the day fasting, then when the day had risen or it was evening, she menstruated: should she break her fast? He said, "Yes; and if it is before sunset, then she should break her fast." And about a woman who sees purity at the beginning of the day in the Month of Ramadan, but she has not performed ghusl (ritual bath) and has not eaten anything, what should she do regarding that day? He said, "Her breaking of the fast is only due to the blood."

And it was narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said: I wrote to him, peace be upon him, about a woman who became pure from her menstruation or from the blood of her postpartum bleeding at the beginning of a day in the Month of Ramadan, then experienced istihadha. So she performed salat and fasted the entire Month of Ramadan without doing what a mustahadah does of ghusl for every two prayers. Is her fasting and her salat valid or not? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “She must make up her fasting, and she does not make up her salat, because the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, used to command the believing women among his wives to do that.”

And it was narrated from Samāʿah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the woman experiencing istihādah. He said: "She fasts the month of Ramadan except for the days in which she used to menstruate, then she makes them up after it."

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: About a woman who gives birth after al-ʿAṣr: should she complete that day, or break her fast? He said: "She should break her fast, then make up that day."

Al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who menstruates in the month of Ramadan before the sun sets. He said, “She breaks her fast when she begins menstruating.”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who became ill during the month of Ramadan, or menstruated, or traveled, then died before the month of Ramadan ended. Should it be made up on her behalf? He said: 'As for menstruation and illness, no. But as for travel, yes.'

1994 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: My wife had made it binding upon herself to fast for two months, then she gave birth to her child and pregnancy came upon her, so she was unable to fast. He said: Let her give in charity, in place of each day, one mudd to a poor person.

Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who fell ill in the Month of Ramadan, then when he recovered he intended hajj; how should he deal with making up the missed fasting? He عليه السلام said: “When he returns, then let him fast it.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked him: About making up the fasts of the month of Ramadan in Dhū al-Ḥijjah and interrupting it, he said: “Make it up in Dhū al-Ḥijjah and interrupt it if you wish.”

Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: If a man has something due of the fasting of the month of Ramadan, then let him make it up in whichever month he wishes, on consecutive days. If he is unable, then let him make it up however he wishes, and let him keep count of the days. If he separates them, that is good, and if he does them consecutively, that is good.

Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has days due from the Month of Ramadan: may he make them up separately? He said: “There is no harm in separating the make-up fasts of the Month of Ramadan. The only fasting that is not to be separated is the fast of the expiation for ẓihār, the expiation for blood, and the expiation for an oath.”

And Jamil narrated from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a man who falls ill, then the Month of Ramadan reaches him, and it passes from him while he is ill, and he does not recover until another Month of Ramadan reaches him. He said: "He gives charity for the first and fasts the second. And if he had recovered in the period between them but did not fast until another Month of Ramadan reached him, he fasts them both together and gives charity for the first."

Ibn Mahbūb narrated from Al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad, from Burayd Al-ʿIjlī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who came to his wife on a day that he was making up from the month of Ramadan, he عليه السلام said: “If he came to his wife before midday, then there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day. And if he came to his wife after the sun’s zenith, then he must give charity to ten needy persons, for each needy person one mudd. If he is unable to do so, he fasts one day in place of one day and fasts three days as kaffarah for what he did.” And it has been narrated: “If he broke his fast before midday, then there is nothing upon him; and if he broke his fast after midday, then kaffarah is upon him similar to what is upon one who broke a day from the month of Ramadan.”

And Sama‘ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام about a woman making up the fasts of the month of Ramadan, and her husband compels her to break the fast. He عليه السلام said: “It is not appropriate for him to compel her after the sun has passed its zenith.”

Samaʿah asked him about his statement: “The fasting person has the option until the sun passes its zenith.” He said: “That applies to the obligatory fast. As for the voluntary fast, he may break the fast at whatever hour he wishes until sunset.”

Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who intends the fast, then his brother, who is upon his cause, meets him and asks him to break his fast. Should he break his fast? He عليه السلام said: "If it is voluntary, it suffices him and it is counted for him; but if it is making up an obligatory fast, then he must make it up."

He, peace be upon him, was asked about a person observing a voluntary fast who encounters a need, and he said: “He has the choice up until between himself and the time of ‘Asr. If he remains until ‘Asr and then it occurs to him to fast, though he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.” If a woman becomes pure from her menstruation while a portion of the day remains, she fasts that remaining amount as discipline, and she must make up that day. And if she menstruates while a portion of the day remains, she breaks the fast and must make it up.

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a man upon whom there is the fasting of a month, and he fasted fifteen days of it, then some matter occurred to him, he said: “If he has fasted fifteen days, then he may make up what remains. But if he has fasted less than fifteen days, it does not suffice him until he fasts a complete month.”

Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: Regarding a man who was fasting for ẓihār in Sha'ban and then the month of Ramadan came upon him, he said: “He fasts the month of Ramadan, then resumes the fasting. And if he had fasted in the ẓihār fast and exceeded the halfway point by a day, he completes its remainder.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man upon whom was the fasting of two consecutive months for zihar, and he fasted Dhu al-Qa'dah, then Dhu al-Hijjah began for him, he said: "He should fast the whole of Dhu al-Hijjah except the Days of Tashriq, then make them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so that he will have fasted two consecutive months." He said: "It is not proper for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three Days of Tashriq that he did not fast. And there is no problem if he fasts one month and then fasts some days from the month that follows it, then an illness occurs to him causing him to interrupt them; then he may complete them afterward, after the completion of the two months."

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū Maryam al-Anṣārī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man fasted some part of the month of Ramaḍān and then remained ill until he died, then there is no qaḍāʾ upon him. But if he recovered, then fell ill, then died, and he had wealth, charity should be given on his behalf in place of each day, a mudd for every day. And if he did not have wealth, his guardian should fast on his behalf.

It has been narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said: "If a man dies while he has outstanding sawm (fasting) from the month of Ramadan, then whoever wishes from his family may make it up on his behalf."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: Regarding a man who died while ten days of missed fasts from the month of Ramaḍān remained upon him, and he had two heirs: is it permissible for them both to make them up on his behalf together, one of the two heirs fasting five days and the other five days? So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “The elder of his two heirs should make up ten days on his behalf consecutively, if Allah wills.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Regarding a man who vowed upon himself that, if he recovered from an illness or was released from imprisonment, he would fast every Wednesday, and it was the day on which he was released. Then he became unable to do that because of an ailment that afflicted him or something else, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prolonged the man’s life, so many fasts accumulated upon him. What is the expiation for that? He said: “He should give charity for each day, a mudd of wheat or a mudd of dates.”
And in the narration of Idrīs ibn Zayd and ʿAlī ibn Idrīs, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: "He should give charity for each day with a mudd of wheat or barley."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: When a man enters a town, he is a guest of those among its people who share his faith until he departs from them. It is not appropriate for the guest to fast except with their permission, lest they prepare something and it be spoiled. And it is not appropriate for them to fast except with the permission of the guest, lest he feel constrained before them and desire something, then leave it for their sake.

Nashit ibn Salih narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Among the fiqh of the guest is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission of his host. Among the obedience of the woman to her husband is that she should not observe a voluntary fast except with his permission and command. Among the uprightness, obedience, and sincerity of the servant toward his master is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission of his master. Among the dutifulness of the child toward his parents is that he should not observe a voluntary fast except with the permission and command of his parents. Otherwise, the guest is ignorant, the woman is disobedient, the servant is corrupt and disobedient, and the child is undutiful.”
And it has been narrated that: "One should perform ghusl (ritual bath) on the night of the seventeenth."

Zurārah and Fuḍayl narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "The ghusl in the month of Ramaḍān is at the setting of the sun, shortly before it; then he performs salat (prayer) and breaks the fast."

And Samaʿah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when the last ten entered, would tighten the waist-wrapper, avoid women, stay awake through the night, and devote himself fully to worship.”

Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that he said: "Pray on the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third one hundred rakʿahs, reciting in every rakʿah al-Ḥamd once and Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad ten times."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: On the night of the nineteenth of the month of Ramadan is the decreeing, on the night of the twenty-first is the judgment, and on the night of the twenty-third is the confirmation of what will occur in the year until its like. And for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to do whatever He wills in His creation.
And Rifāʿah narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: The Night of al-Qadr is the beginning of the year, and it is its end.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was shown in his dream that Banī Umayyah would ascend his pulpit after him, leading the people astray from the path, backwards. So he awoke distressed and sorrowful. Then Jibrīl عليه السلام descended to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you distressed and sorrowful?" He said, "O Jibrīl, I saw Banī Umayyah on this night of mine ascending my pulpit after me, leading the people astray from the path, backwards." He said, "By the One Who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, this is indeed something of which I had no knowledge." Then he ascended to the heaven and soon came down to him with verses from the Qur'an by which He consoled him: "Have you then considered: if We let them enjoy themselves for years, then there came to them that which they had been promised, what would avail them that which they used to enjoy?" And He revealed to him: "Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr. And what will make you know what the Night of al-Qadr is? The Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months." He made Laylat al-Qadr for His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله better than a thousand months of the rule of Banī Umayyah."
A man asked al-Sadiq عليه السلام and said: Inform me about Laylat al-Qadr: was it, or does it occur in every year? So he said: "If Laylat al-Qadr were removed, the Qur'an would be removed."

Humran asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. "Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night." He said: "It is Laylat al-Qadr, and it is in every year in the month of Ramadan, in the last ten nights. The Qur'an was not sent down except on Laylat al-Qadr. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:" "In it every wise matter is made distinct." He said: "On Laylat al-Qadr, every thing that will occur in that year up to the like of it in the coming year is decreed: of good or evil, obedience or disobedience, a newborn, a term of life, or provision. So whatever is decreed on that night and decided is the inevitable, and for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, therein is the will." He said: I said to him, "Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months"—what did He mean by that? So he said: "Righteous deed in Laylat al-Qadr—were it not that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, multiplies for the believers, they would not attain; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, multiplies the good deeds for them."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked: How is Laylat al-Qadr better "than a thousand months" He عليه السلام said: "Righteous deed in it is better than deed in a thousand months in which there is no Laylat al-Qadr."

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The Tawrah was revealed on six nights having passed of the month of Ramadan, and the Injīl was revealed on twelve having passed of the month of Ramadan, and the Zabūr was revealed on the night of eighteen of the month of Ramadan, and the Qur’an [al-Furqān] was revealed on Laylat al-Qadr.”

And it is narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهم السلام, who said: I asked him about the sign of Laylat al-Qadr, so he said: "Its sign is that its breeze is pleasant; if it is during cold weather, it becomes warm, and if it is during hot weather, it becomes cool and pleasant."

He, peace be upon him, was asked about Laylat al-Qadr, so he said: On it, the angels and the scribes descend to the lowest heaven, and they write what will occur in the affair of the year and what will befall the servants. And there is a matter with Him, Mighty and Majestic, held in abeyance, in which belongs to Him the will; so He brings forward from it what He wills, and delays from it what He wills, and He effaces and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when Abū Baṣīr said to him, “May I be your ransom, which night is the one in which one hopes for what is hoped for?” He said, “On the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third.” He said, “If I am not able to manage both of them?” He said, “How easy two nights are for what you seek.” He said: I said, “Sometimes we see the crescent among us, and someone comes to us informing us of the contrary in another land.” He said, “How easy four nights are regarding what you seek in them.” I said, “May I be your ransom, is the twenty-third night the night of al-Juhanī?” He said, “Indeed, that is what is said.” I said, “May I be your ransom, Sulaymān ibn Khālid narrated that on the nineteenth the delegation of the pilgrims is written.” He said, “O Abā Muḥammad, the delegation of the pilgrims is written on Laylat al-Qadr, and deaths, afflictions, provisions, and what will occur until its like in the coming year. So seek it on the twenty-first and twenty-third, pray one hundred rakʿahs on each of them, keep both of them awake in worship if you are able until the light, and perform ghusl on them.” He said: I said, “What if I am not able to do that while standing?” He said, “Then pray while you are sitting.” I said, “What if I cannot?” He said, “Then on your bed.” I said, “What if I cannot?” He said, “There is no harm on you that you take a little sleep at the beginning of the night. Indeed, the gates of the heaven are opened in the month of Ramaḍān, the devils are shackled, and the deeds are accepted—the deeds of the believers. Excellent is the month, the month of Ramaḍān. It used to be called in the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ‘al-Marzūq.’”

And Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān narrated from Sufyān ibn al-Simṭ, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Which nights in the month of Ramaḍān are hoped for? He said: The nineteenth, the twenty-first, and the twenty-third. I said: If weakness or some illness overtakes a person, then which of these should be relied upon? He said: The twenty-third.

And in the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of the two عليهمَا ٱلسَّلَامُ, he said: I asked him about the nights in which ghusl (ritual bath) is recommended in the month of Ramadan, so he said: “The nineteenth night, the twenty-first night, and the twenty-third night.” And he said: “The twenty-third night is the night of al-Juhanī, and his report is that he said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘My dwelling is far from al-Madīnah, so designate for me a night in which I may come in.’ So he instructed him regarding the twenty-third night.”

Saʿīd al-Naqqāsh narrated, saying: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “Indeed, in al-Fiṭr there is takbīr, but it is a recommended sunnah.” He said: I said, “Then where is it?” He said: “On the night of al-Fiṭr, in al-Maghrib and the later ʿIshāʾ, and in salat al-Fajr and in salat al-ʿĪd.” And in a narration other than that of Saʿīd: “And in al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr, then it stops.” He said: I said, “How shall I say it?” He said: “You say: Allah is greater, Allah is greater, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greater, Allah is greater, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is greater for what He has guided us to, and all praise belongs to Allah for what He has tried us with.” And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And that you complete the number” meaning the fasting, “and that you magnify Allah for what He has guided you to.”
And it is narrated: "It is not said in it, 'and He provided us from the livestock of cattle,' for indeed that pertains to the days of Tashrīq."

2036 - Al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā narrated from his grandfather Al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The people say that forgiveness descends upon the one who fasted the month of Ramaḍān on Laylat al-Qadr.” So he said: “O Ḥasan, the wage-earner is only given his wage when he finishes his work, and that is the night of ʿĪd.” I said: “May I be your ransom, then what should we do on that night?” He said: “When the sun sets, pray the three of Maghrib, raise your hands, and say: O Possessor of bounty, O Possessor of power, O Chooser of Muḥammad and his Helper, send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and forgive me every sin I committed and forgot, while it is with You in a clear book. Then fall in prostration and say one hundred times: I repent to Allah, while you are prostrating, and ask for your needs.”

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If two witnesses testify before the Imam that they saw the crescent thirty days earlier, the Imam commands the breaking of the fast on that day if they testified before the sun’s zenith. And if they testify after the sun’s zenith, the Imam commands the breaking of the fast on that day and delays the prayer until the next day, then he leads them in prayer.

And in another report, he said: If the people begin the morning fasting and do not see the crescent, then a group of trustworthy people comes testifying to the sighting, they should break their fast and go out the following day, at the beginning of the day, to their Eid. And if the crescent of Shawwal is seen during the day before noon, then that day is from Shawwal; and if it is seen after noon, then that day is from the month of Ramadan.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Faddal, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام asking him about a group of people among us who pray but do not fast in the month of Ramadan. Sometimes I need them to harvest for me, but when I call them for harvesting, they do not respond to me until I feed them, while they find others who feed them, so they go to them and leave me, and I am constrained from feeding them in the month of Ramadan. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own hand: “I know it; feed them.”
And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "The month of Ramadan is thirty days and never decreases."

And in the narration of Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir—who is also said to be Mu'adh ibn Muslim al-Harra'—from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: The month of Ramadan is thirty days; by Allah, it never decreases.

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Shuʿayb, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I said to him: People narrate that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days of the month of Ramaḍān more often than he fasted thirty. He said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except completely, and the obligatory acts are not deficient. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the year as three hundred and sixty days, and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, so He withheld them from the three hundred and sixty days; thus the year is three hundred and fifty-four days. And the month of Ramaḍān is thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: and that you complete the number And that which is complete is full. And Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, and Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights So the month is thus and then thus, meaning: one month complete and one month deficient. And the month of Ramaḍān never diminishes, and Shaʿbān is never complete.
Abu Basir asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And complete the number” He said: “Thirty days.”

And it is narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: 'Can the month of Ramaḍān be twenty-nine days?' So he said: 'Indeed, the month of Ramaḍān never decreases from thirty days, ever.'

And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about fasting the Days of Tashrīq. He said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prohibited fasting them only in Minā; as for elsewhere, there is no harm.”

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, forbade continuous fasting in sawm. And he used to continue the fast, so it was said to him about that, and he, peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, I am not like any one of you. Indeed, I remain with my Lord, and He feeds me and gives me drink.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The wisal that has been prohibited is that a man makes his evening meal his pre-dawn meal."
Zurārah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about fasting continuously throughout the year, and he said: "It has always been disliked."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "There is no continuous fasting in fasting, nor silence for a day until the night."

And it is narrated from Al-Bazanti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sa‘d Al-Khaffaf, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: We were with him, eight men, and we mentioned Ramadan, so he said: Do not say, 'This is Ramadan,' nor, 'Ramadan has gone,' nor, 'Ramadan has come,' for Ramadan is a name from among the Names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It does not come and it does not go; rather, that which comes and goes is the passing thing. But say, 'The Month of Ramadan,' for the month is ascribed to the name, and the name is the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is the month "in which the Qur'an was sent down" Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it a symbol and a celebration.

Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father, from his grandfather عليهم السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ṣalawātu llāhi ʿalayhi, said: “Do not say: ‘Ramaḍān’; rather say: ‘Shahr Ramaḍān,’ for you do not know what Ramaḍān is.”

And the Commander of the Faithful, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "It is recommended for a man to go to his wife on the first night of the month of Ramadan, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Permitted for you on the night of the fasting is intimacy with your wives." ".

2053 - Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: To one of his followers on the Day of al-Fiṭr, while he was supplicating for him: “O so-and-so, may Allah accept from you and from us.” He said: Then he remained until it was the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and he said to him: “O so-and-so, may Allah accept from us and from you.” He said: So I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, you said one thing on al-Fiṭr, and you say on al-Aḍḥā something different from it.” So he said: “Yes. I said to him on al-Fiṭr, ‘May Allah accept from you and from us,’ because he did the like of my act, and he and I were equal in the act. And I said to him on al-Aḍḥā, ‘May Allah accept from us and from you,’ because we are able to offer sacrifice, while he is not able to offer sacrifice; so we did other than his act.”
Jarrah al-Mada'ini narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Eat on the Day of Eid al-Fitr before you pray, and do not eat on the Day of Eid al-Adha until the Imam departs."
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when perfume was brought to him on the day of al-Fiṭr, would begin with his tongue.

2056 - And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Nawfalī said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Indeed, I broke my fast on the Day of al-Fiṭr with the clay of the grave and dates. So he said to him: “You have combined between blessing and sunnah (prophetic tradition).”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام looked at the people on a day of Fiṭr while they were playing and laughing, so he said to his companions and turned toward them. "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the month of Ramaḍān as a racecourse for His creation, in which they compete through obedience to Him toward His good pleasure. So some people went ahead in it and thus succeeded, while others fell behind and thus failed. How astonishing—truly all astonishing—is the laughing, playing person on the day in which the doers of good are rewarded and the negligent fail. By Allah, were the covering to be lifted, a doer of good would be occupied with his goodness, and an evildoer with his evil."

Ḥannān ibn Sadīr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said: "O ʿAbd Allāh, there is no Eid for the Muslims, whether Eid al-Aḍḥā or Eid al-Fiṭr, except that sorrow is renewed for the family of Muḥammad in it." He said: I said, "And why?" He said: "Because they see their right in the hands of others."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Laṭīf al-Taflīsī narrated from Razīn, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “When al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام was struck with the sword and fell, then people hastened so that his head might be cut off, a caller called out from the depths of the Throne: ‘O bewildered, misguided community after its Prophet, may Allah not grant you success for Aḍḥā nor Fiṭr.’” And in another report: “for fasting nor for breaking fast.” He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, by Allah, they were not granted success, and they will not be granted success until the avenger of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام rises.”

And it is narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said: When the first day of Shawwāl comes, a caller calls out: O believers, go early to your rewards, Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: O Jābir, the rewards of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are not like the rewards of these kings, Then he said: It is the Day of Rewards.

Ibn Abī Najrān and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about zakat al-fiṭrah. He said: “It is upon the young and the old, the free and the enslaved. For every person, one sāʿ of wheat, or one sāʿ of dates, or one sāʿ of raisins.”

Muḥammad ibn Khālid narrated from Saʿd ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about zakat al-fiṭrah: how much is to be paid for each person from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins? He said: “One ṣāʿ, according to the ṣāʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, and he was with us as a pilgrim, who said: I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام by the hand of Abī: 'May I be your ransom, our companions have differed concerning the ṣāʿ. Some of them say that zakat al-fiṭrah is according to the Madanī ṣāʿ, while some of them say it is according to the ʿIrāqī ṣāʿ.' So he عليه السلام wrote to me: 'The ṣāʿ is six riṭls by the Madanī measure and nine riṭls by the ʿIrāqī measure.' He said: And he informed me, 'By weight, it comes to one thousand one hundred and seventy weight-units.'
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "Whoever does not find wheat or barley, wheat flour, spelt, emmer, or corn will suffice for him."

Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl al-Baṣrī wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, asking him about whether the guardian should pay Zakat al-Fiṭrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth. So he عليه السلام wrote: “There is no zakat upon an orphan.”

And Saif ibn ʿAmīrah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man has nothing of the fiṭrah except what would suffice to discharge it for himself alone. Should he give it on her behalf, or should he and his dependents eat it?" He عليه السلام said: "He gives it to some of his dependents, then the other gives it on behalf of himself; they pass it among themselves, and it thereby counts for all of them as one fiṭrah."

2067 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a guest from among his brethren staying with him, and the Day of al-Fiṭr arrives: should he pay the fiṭrah on his behalf? He عليه السلام said: “Yes. Al-fiṭrah is obligatory for everyone whom he supports, whether male or female, young or old, free or enslaved.”
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "There is no harm in a man giving to another man on behalf of two, three, or four persons, meaning Zakat al-Fitrah."
And in another report, he said: "There is no harm in giving on behalf of yourself and those whom you support to a single person."

That was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a newborn who is born on the night of al-Fiṭr, and a Jew or a Christian who accepts Islam on the night of al-Fiṭr, He عليه السلام said: “There is no fiṭrah upon them. The fiṭrah is only upon one who has reached the month.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Bilāl, who said: I wrote to al-Ṭayyib al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: Is it permissible that the fiṭrah on behalf of a man’s dependents—whether they are ten, fewer, or more—be given to one needy, like-minded man? So he عليه السلام wrote: “Yes, do that.”

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: About the mukātab: is the fiṭrah of the month of Ramaḍān upon him, or upon the one who contracted his emancipation for him? And is his testimony admissible? He said: "The fiṭrah is upon him, and his testimony is not admissible."

Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام. He asked him about a mamlūk whose master dies while he is away from him in another town, and in his hand is wealth belonging to his master. When al-Fiṭr arrives, should he pay zakat al-fiṭrah for himself from his master’s wealth, though it has now become the property of the orphans? So he said: “Yes.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "To give one sa' of dates in Zakat al-Fitrah is more beloved to me than to give one sa' of gold."

And Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from him that he said: "Dates in the fiṭrah are better than other than them, because they are quicker in benefit; that is because when they fall into the hand of their owner, he eats from them." He said: "And zakat was sent down while the people had no wealth, and there was only fiṭrah."
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about zakat al-fitrah, so he said: The neighbors have the greatest right to it, and there is no harm in giving its equivalent value in silver.

And ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal, peace be upon him: About zakat al-fitrah: Is it permissible that it be given to neighbors and close associates from among those who do not recognize and do not show enmity? So he said: “There is no harm in that if he is in need.”

And Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Muʿattib, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: "Go and give zakat al-fitrah on behalf of our household and for the servants, and include them all, and do not leave any one of them out; for if you leave out a person from them, I fear for him al-fawt." I said: "And what is al-fawt?" He said: "Death."

Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who spends on another man who is not among his dependents, except that he takes it upon himself to provide his maintenance and clothing. Is his zakat al-fitrah upon him? He said: “No. His fitrah is only upon his dependents as charity, not upon that one.” And he said: “Dependents are the child, the owned servant, the wife, and the umm al-walad.”

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about Zakat al-Fitr. He عليه السلام said: "If you have set it aside, then it does not harm you whenever you give it, whether before the salat (prayer) or after it." And he عليه السلام said: "It is obligatory upon you to give on behalf of yourself, your father, your mother, your child, your wife, and your servant."

And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about what is obligatory upon a man regarding the charity of fiṭrah for his household. He said: “Give charity on behalf of everyone whom you maintain, whether free or enslaved, young or old, among those who have reached the prayer.”

And Muḥammad ibn Masʿūd al-ʿAyyāshī narrated, saying: Muḥammad ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us; he said: Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated to us; he said: Manṣūr ibn al-ʿAbbās narrated to me; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Sahl narrated to us, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said: A slave is jointly owned among a group of people—are they liable regarding him for zakat al-fiṭrah? He عليه السلام said: If each person has a full head, then he must pay his zakat al-fiṭrah for him. And if the number of slaves and the number of masters are equal, and they are all together, then they are equal: they pay their zakat, each one of them according to the measure of his share. And if each person among them has less than a head, then there is nothing upon them.

And Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated; he said: I sent dirhams to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام on behalf of myself and others, and I wrote to him informing him that they were from the fiṭrah of the dependents. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received it.”

And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, with his chain of transmission, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: "Whoever pays Zakāt al-Fiṭrah, Allah will complete with it whatever is lacking in the zakat of his wealth."

Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Abū Baṣīr and Zurārah, who both said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Indeed, part of the completion of fasting is giving zakat, meaning zakāt al-fiṭrah, just as salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is part of the completion of salat. For whoever fasts and does not give the zakat, then there is no fast for him if he deliberately abandons it; and there is no salat for him if he abandons salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with it before salat. He said: "He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, then prays."
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: There is no iʿtikaf except with fasting in the congregational mosque.

He said: “When the last ten days arrived, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform i'tikaf in the mosque, and a tent of hair would be set up for him, and he would tighten the waist-wrapper, and fold up his bedding.” And some of them said: “And he kept away from women.” So Abū ʿAbdِ ٱللَّهِ عليه السلام said: “As for keeping away from women, no.”

And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Badr took place in the month of Ramaḍān, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not perform iʿtikāf. Then, when the following year came, he performed iʿtikāf for twenty days: ten for that year, and ten as a make-up for what had passed him by.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: What do you say about i'tikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques? He said: "Do not perform i'tikaf except in a congregational mosque in which a just Imam has led the congregation in prayer. There is no harm in observing i'tikaf in the مسجد of Kufa, Basra, the مسجد of Medina, and the مسجد of Mecca."
And it has also been narrated: “In the mosque of al-Madāʾin.”

Al-Bazanti narrated from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "I do not regard i'tikaf as valid except in al-Masjid al-Haram, or the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, or in a congregational mosque. It is not proper for the one in i'tikaf to leave the congregational mosque except for a need that is unavoidable; then he should not sit until he returns. And the woman is likewise in that."

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "The one performing iʿtikāf in Makkah may perform salat (prayer) in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether he performs salat (prayer) in the mosque or in its houses."

And in the narration of Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: “The one in iʿtikāf in Makkah may perform salat (prayer) in whichever of its houses he wishes, while the one in iʿtikāf elsewhere does not perform salat (prayer) except in the mosque that he designated.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a woman whose husband had been absent, then returned while she was in i'tikaf with her husband's permission. When news of his arrival reached her, she left the mosque in which she was and prepared herself for her husband until he had intimacy with her. He عليه السلام said: If she left the mosque before three days had passed, and she had not made a stipulation in her i'tikaf, then upon her is what is upon the muzahir.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "I'tikaf cannot be for less than three days. Whoever performs i'tikaf must fast, and it is appropriate for the one performing i'tikaf, when he enters i'tikaf, to make a stipulation just as the one who enters ihram makes a stipulation."

Abu Ayyub narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: If a man performs i‘tikaf for one day and has not made a stipulation, then he may leave and break his i‘tikaf. But if he remains for two days and has not made a stipulation, then he may not break his i‘tikaf until three days pass.

Abu Ayyub narrated from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: "The one performing i'tikaf must not smell perfume, take pleasure in fragrant plants, engage in disputation, buy, or sell." He said: "Whoever performs i'tikaf for three days has the choice on the fourth day: if he wishes, he may add another three; and if he wishes, he may leave the mosque. But if he remains for two days after the three, then he must not leave the mosque until he completes another three days."

And it is narrated from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, who said: I was in al-Madīnah during the month of Ramaḍān, so I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: 'I want to perform iʿtikāf, so what should I say, and what should I make obligatory upon myself?' He said: 'Do not leave the mosque except for a necessary need, and do not sit under shades until you return to your place.'

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is not appropriate for the one in iʿtikāf to leave the mosque except for an unavoidable need; then he should not sit until he returns. And he should not go out for anything except for a funeral or to visit a sick person, and he should not sit until he returns. He said: the iʿtikāf of a woman is like that.

And in the narration of Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: “If the person performing iʿtikāf falls ill, or if the woman performing iʿtikāf menstruates, then he may come to his house; then he resumes when he recovers and fasts.”

And in the narration of Al-Sakūnī, with his chain of transmission, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "I'tikaf for ten days in the month of Ramadan is equal to two hajj and two 'umrahs."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the one in i'tikaf who has sexual intercourse. He said: “If he does that, then upon him is what is upon the one who performs zihar.” And it has also been narrated: “If he has sexual intercourse during the night, then upon him is one expiation; and if he has sexual intercourse during the day, then upon him are two expiations.”

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated that from ʿAbd al-Aʿla ibn Aʿyan, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had sexual relations with his wife while he was in iʿtikaf at night during the month of Ramadan. He said: “One expiation is due upon him.” He said: I said, “Then if he had sexual relations with her during the day?” He said: “Two expiations are due upon him.”

2104 - Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a person in iʿtikāf who had intercourse with his spouse, so he said: “He is in the position of one who broke the fast on a day of the month of Ramaḍān.”

And Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed iʿtikāf in the month of Ramaḍān in the first ten days, then he performed iʿtikāf in the second, in the middle ten days, then he performed iʿtikāf in the third, in the last ten days. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله continued to perform iʿtikāf in the last ten days.

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a woman in iʿtikāf when she menstruates, he said: “She returns to her home, and when she becomes pure, she returns and makes up what is upon her.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the person in iʿtikaf who approaches his family. He said: “He must not approach his wife, neither by night nor by day, while he is in iʿtikaf.”

And it is narrated from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, who said: I was sitting with Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام when a man came to him and said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has money owed by me, and he wants to imprison me." So he said, "By Allah, I have no money with me to repay on your behalf." He said, "Then speak to him." He said: so he, عليه السلام, put on his sandals. Then I said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, have you forgotten your iʿtikāf?" So he said to him, "I have not forgotten, but I heard my father, عليه السلام, narrating from my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, that he said: 'Whoever strives in fulfilling the need of his Muslim brother, it is as though he worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for nine thousand years, fasting its days and standing its nights.'"

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would fast so much that it was said, he does not break the fast, and he would break the fast so much that it was said, he does not fast. Then he fasted one day and broke the fast one day. Then he fasted on Monday and Thursday. Then he came from that to fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: 'That is the fasting of the lifetime.' And my father عليه السلام used to say: 'There is no one more detested to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a man to whom it is said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to do such and such, and he says: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not punish me for striving in salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) — as though he sees that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله left something of merit out of inability to do it.'

1786 - And in the narration of Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fasted so much that it was said: he does not break the fast. Then he broke the fast so much that it was said: he does not fast. Then he fasted the fast of Dāwūd عليه السلام, one day and one day. Then he was taken عليه السلام while observing the fast of three days in the month, and he said: ‘They equal the fasting of a lifetime and remove the distress of the chest.’” And Ḥammād said: al-waḥar means whispering. Then Ḥammād said: So I said: which days are they? He said: “The first Thursday in the month, the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday in it.” I said: And how did these become the days that are fasted? He said: “Because those before us among the nations, when punishment descended upon one of them, it descended on these days. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fasted these days because they are the feared days.”

1787 - Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When one of you fasts the three days of the month, let him not dispute with anyone, act ignorantly, or hasten to swear and take oaths by Allah. If someone behaves ignorantly toward him, then let him endure it."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Ḥabīb al-Khathʿamī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Inform me about voluntary fasting and about these three days: if I become junub at the beginning of the night, and I know that I have become junub, then I deliberately sleep until dawn breaks, should I fast or should I not fast? He said: "Fast."

Hadith 1789 — The Commander of the Faithful, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, said: "Fasting the month of patience and three days of every month removes the anxieties of the chest. And fasting three days in every month is fasting for a lifetime. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever comes with a good deed shall have ten times the like of it. "

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked about fasting on two Thursdays with a Wednesday between them, so he said: As for Thursday, it is a day on which deeds are presented; as for Wednesday, it is a day on which the Fire was created; and as for fasting, it is a shield.

And in the narration of Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "Fasting is only observed on Wednesday because no nation in times past was punished except on a Wednesday in the middle of the month; so it is recommended that that day be fasted."

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “If there are two Thursdays at the beginning of the month, then fast the first of them, for it is more virtuous. And if there are two Thursdays at the end of the month, then fast the last of them, for it is more virtuous.”

ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about one who does not fast the three days of every month while fasting is difficult for him: is there any fidyah in it? So he said: “A mudd of food for each day.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muthannā, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Fasting three days in every month has become difficult for me, so what would suffice for me? That I give charity in place of each day with one dirham? So he said: “The charity of one dirham is better than fasting one day.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar or to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: 'The fasting of three days in the month—I delay it in the summer until the winter, for I find it easier upon me then.' So he said: 'Yes, but preserve it.'

Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: 'What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding fasting?' He said: 'Three days from every month: Thursday in the first ten days, Wednesday in the middle ten days, and Thursday in the last ten days.' He said: I said, 'Is this all of what the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has established in fasting?' He said: 'Yes.'
And Dāwūd al-Raqqī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Your breaking the fast in your brother's home is better than your fasting seventy times, or ninety times."

1798 - And Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said: "Whoever enters upon his brother while he is fasting, then breaks his fast with him and does not inform him of his fasting, lest he show favor to him, Allah will write for him the fasting of a year."
And it is narrated that al-ʿĀlim عليه السلام was asked about two Thursdays that coincide in the last ten days. So he said: “Fast the first, for perhaps you may not reach the second.”

Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Zurārah ibn Aʿyan asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said: "Its fasting was observed before the month of Ramaḍān; then when the month of Ramaḍān was revealed, it was abandoned."
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever fasts one day voluntarily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will admit him to Paradise."
Jabir narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever is sealed with the fasting of a day shall enter Paradise."
1803 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever fasts one day in the way of Allah, it is equivalent to a year that he fasts."
1804 - And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever applies perfume at the beginning of the day while he is fasting will not lose his mind."

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: There is no fasting person who is present among people who are eating except that his limbs glorify Allah for him, and the angels' salat is upon him, and their salat is seeking forgiveness for him.

And it is narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, upon them both be peace, that he said: "Whoever fasts the first day of the ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, Allah will record for him the fasting of eighty months. And if he fasts the nine days, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him the fasting of a lifetime."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Fasting on the Day of Tarwiyah is an expiation for one year, and fasting on the Day of Arafah is an expiation for two years."

1808 - And it is narrated: On the first day of Dhu al-Hijjah, Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, was born. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for sixty years. And on the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the repentance of Dawud, peace be upon him, was sent down. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for ninety years.

And it is narrated from Ya‘qūb ibn Shu‘ayb, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of ‘Arafah. He said: “If you wish, you may fast, and if you wish, you may refrain from fasting.” And he mentioned: “A man came to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and found one of them fasting and the other breaking the fast. So he asked them, and they said: ‘If you fast, it is good; and if you do not fast, it is permissible.’”

And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed solely to ʿAlī عليه السلام, and ʿAlī عليه السلام bequeathed jointly to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, and al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was his Imam. So a man entered upon al-Ḥasan عليه السلام on the Day of ʿArafah while he was eating the midday meal, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام was fasting. Then, after al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed away, he came and entered upon al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام on the Day of ʿArafah while he was eating the midday meal, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام was fasting. So the man said to him: Indeed, I entered upon al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was eating the midday meal and you were fasting; then I entered upon you and you are not fasting. He said: Indeed, al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was an Imam, so he broke his fast lest his fasting be taken as a sunnah (prophetic tradition) and the people follow him in that. Then when he was taken, I was the Imam, so I wanted that my fasting not be taken as a sunnah (prophetic tradition), such that the people would follow me in it.

And Ḥanān ibn Sudayr narrated from his father, who said: I asked him about fasting on the Day of ʿArafah, and I said: “May I be your ransom, they claim that it equals the fasting of a year.” He said: “My father, peace be upon him, would not fast it.” I said: “And why, may I be your ransom?” He said: “The Day of ʿArafah is a day of du'a and asking, so I fear that it may weaken me from du'a, and I dislike fasting it, and I fear that the Day of ʿArafah may be the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and that is not a day of fasting.”

1812 - What al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali عليه السلام was killed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded an angel, and he proclaimed: O oppressive nation, killer of the progeny of its Prophet, may Allah, Exalted is He, not grant you success in fasting nor in breaking the fast."
And in another hadith: "May Allah not grant you success for Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha."

1814 - And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said: I was with my father while I was a boy, and we had dinner with al-Riḍā عليه السلام on the night of the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah. So he said to him: 'On the night of the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, Ibrāhīm عليه السلام was born, and on it ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام was born, and on it the earth was spread out from beneath the Kaʿbah. So whoever fasts that day is like one who has fasted sixty months.'

And it is narrated: On the twenty-ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Ka'bah, and it was the first mercy that descended. So whoever performs sawm (fasting) on that day, it is an expiation for seventy years.

Al-Hasan ibn Rashid narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said, 'May I be your ransom, do the Muslims have a festival other than the two Eids?' He said, 'Yes, O Hasan, and it is the greatest of them and the noblest of them.' He said: I said to him, 'So which day is it?' He said, 'It is a day on which Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was appointed as a standard for the people.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, and which day is it?' He said, 'Indeed the days revolve, and it is the eighteenth day of Dhu al-Hijjah.' He said: I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what should we do on it?' He said, 'You fast it, O Hasan, and increase in it the salat upon Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, and declare disavowal before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from those who wronged them of their right. For indeed the Prophets عليهم السلام used to command the successors that the day on which the successor was established should be taken as an Eid.' He said: I said, 'What belongs to one of us who fasts it?' He said, 'The fasting of sixty months. And do not abandon fasting the twenty-seventh day of Rajab, for it is the day on which prophethood was sent down upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and its reward is like sixty months for you.'
Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Fasting on the Day of Ghadīr Khumm is an expiation for sixty years."

1818 - And on the first day of al-Muharram, Zakariyya عليه السلام supplicated to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. So whoever fasts on that day, Allah will answer him just as He answered Zakariyya عليه السلام.

Abu Basir asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a voluntarily fasting person who is confronted by a need. He said: He has the choice until the time of 'Asr. And if he remains until 'Asr, then it occurs to him to fast, and he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, Nūḥ عليه السلام boarded the Ark on the first day of Rajab." So he عليه السلام commanded those with him to fast that day, and said: "Whoever fasts that day, the Fire will be distanced from him by the journey of one year. Whoever fasts seven days, the seven gates of the Fires will be closed to him. Whoever fasts eight days, the eight gates of the Gardens will be opened for him. Whoever fasts fifteen days will be granted his request. And whoever increases beyond that, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will increase for him."

And Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام said: "Rajab is a river in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. So whoever fasts one day of Rajab, Allah will give him drink from that river."

And Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said: "Rajab is a great month. In it, Allah multiplies good deeds and effaces evil deeds. Whoever fasts one day of Rajab, the Fire is distanced from him by the journey of a year; and whoever fasts three days, the Garden becomes obligatory for him."

1823 - Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever fasts during Sha‘ban, it will be a purification for him from every slip, stain, and impulsive act." Abu Hamzah said: "So I said to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام: 'What is al-wasmah?' He said: 'An oath in disobedience, and a vow; and there is no vow in disobedience.'" I said: "Then what is al-badirah?" He said: "An oath made in anger, and repentance from it is regret over it."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Marhum al-Azdi, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: Whoever fasts the first day of Sha'ban, Paradise becomes absolutely obligatory for him. Whoever fasts two days, Allah looks at him every day and night in the abode of this world, and He continues His gaze upon him in Paradise. And whoever fasts three days, Allah visits him on His Throne from His Paradise every day.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Fasting the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan as two consecutive months is repentance, by Allah, from Allah."

And ʿAmr ibn Khālid narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to fast Shaʿbān and the month of Ramaḍān, joining them together, and he would forbid the people from joining them together. And he used to say: “They are the two months of Allah, and they are an expiation for the sins before them and after them.”

What Zur‘ah narrated from al-Mufaddal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “My father عليه السلام would separate between Shaʿbān and the month of Ramaḍān by a day, while ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would join them, and he would say: ‘Fasting two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.’”

The wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would, if they had fasts due upon them, delay that until Shaʿban, disliking to prevent the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله from his need. And when Shaʿban came, they would fast, and he would fast with them. And he عليه السلام used to say: “Shaʿban is my month.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever fasts three days from the end of Sha'ban and joins them to the month of Ramadan, Allah will record for him the fasting of two consecutive months."

1830 - Hariz narrated from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say regarding the night of the middle of Shaʿban? He عليه السلام said: “On it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives from His creation more than the number of the hairs of the goats of Kalb, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends down His angels to the lowest heaven and to the earth at Makkah.” And I have presented what I narrated on this meaning in the book Fada'il Shaʿban.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله addressed the people on the last Friday of Sha‘ban. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, indeed a month has approached you in which there is a night better than a thousand months And it is the Month of Ramadan. Allah has made its fasting obligatory, and He has made standing in one night of it like one who performs voluntary salat for seventy nights in other months. He has made for one who performs in it a trait from the traits of goodness and righteousness the reward of one who performs an obligation from the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And whoever performs an obligation from the obligations of Allah is like one who performs seventy obligations in other months. It is the month of patience, and indeed the reward of patience is Paradise. It is the month of mutual support, and it is a month in which Allah increases the provision of the believer. Whoever gives a fasting believer something with which to break the fast will have thereby with Allah the freeing of a slave and forgiveness for his past sins. So it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to give a fasting person something to break the fast with. So he said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Generous.
