He gives this reward from among you to one who is not able except for a sip of milk by which he gives a fasting person to break the fast, or a drink of sweet water, or a few dates, and is not able to do more than that. And whoever lightens the burden upon his servant in it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will lighten his reckoning. And it is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is response and freedom from the Fire. And you have no sufficiency in it without four qualities: two qualities by which you please Allah, and two qualities without which you have no sufficiency. As for the two by which you please Allah, they are the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. And as for the two without which you have no sufficiency, they are that you ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in it for your needs and for Paradise, and that you ask Allah in it for well-being and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.

1832 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: When the month of Ramadan approached, and that was with three days remaining of Sha‘ban, he said to Bilal, “Call out among the people.” So he gathered the people, then he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and extolled Him, then said: "O people, this month has come upon you, and it is the master of the months. In it is a night which is "better than a thousand months." In it the gates of the Fire are closed, and in it the gates of the gardens are opened. So whoever reaches it and is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him. And whoever reaches his parents and is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him. And whoever I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me, and he is not forgiven, then may Allah distance him."

1833 - Jabir narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would, when he saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, face the qiblah with his face, then say: ‘O Allah, let it appear over us with security, faith, safety, Islam, all-encompassing well-being, abundant provision, warding off illnesses, recitation of the Qur’an, and help in salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). O Allah, keep us safe for the month of Ramadan, keep it safe for us, and receive it from us until the month of Ramadan comes to an end while You have forgiven us.’” Then he would turn his face to the people and say: ‘O gathering of people, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises, the rebellious devils are chained, the gates of heaven, the gates of the gardens, and the gates of mercy are opened, and the gates of the Fire are closed. Supplication is answered, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has at every breaking of the fast those whom He frees from the Fire. And a caller calls out every night: Is there any repentant one? Is there any asker? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a replacement, and give every withholder loss. Until, when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are called: Go early to your rewards, for it is the Day of Reward.’ Then Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: ‘Indeed, by the One in whose hand is my soul, it is not a reward of dinars and dirhams.’

Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he returned from ʿArafāt and proceeded to Minā, entered the mosque. The people gathered around him asking him about Laylat al-Qadr, so he stood as a preacher and spoke after praising Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for what follows, you asked me about Laylat al-Qadr, and I did not conceal it from you because I knew it; rather, I was not knowledgeable of it. Know, O people, that whoever reaches the month of Ramaḍān while sound and healthy, then fasts its days, stands in worship for a portion of its nights, remains constant in his salat, goes forth to his Friday prayer, and goes out to his Eid, then he has attained Laylat al-Qadr and won the prize of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "By Allah, they have succeeded with rewards that are unlike the rewards of the servants."

1836 - Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said to Jabir: "O Jabir, whoever reaches the month of Ramadan, then fasts its days, stands for a portion of its night, guards his chastity and his tongue, lowers his gaze, and restrains his harm, will come out from sins like the day his mother gave birth to him." Jabir said: "I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, how beautiful this hadith is!'" He said: "How severe this condition is."

1837 - And Ali عليه السلام said: “When the month of Ramadan arrived, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله stood, praised Allah, and extolled Him, then said:” “O people, Allah has sufficed you against your enemy from among the jinn and humankind, and He said: ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.’ And He has promised you a response. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned seventy of His angels to every rebellious devil, so he is not released until this month of yours comes to an end. Indeed, the gates of heaven are opened from its first night. Indeed, supplication in it is accepted.”

Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in every night of the month of Ramadan there are those freed and released from the Fire, except one who breaks his fast upon an intoxicant. Then when its last night comes, He frees in it the like of what He freed in all of it.
And in the narration of ʿUmar ibn Yazīd: "Except one who breaks his fast upon an intoxicant, or one bearing enmity, or one involved with shāhayn, and it is chess."
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when the month of Ramadan began, would free every captive and give to every petitioner.
And Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramaḍān will not be forgiven until the coming year, unless he witnesses ʿArafah."

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام used to advise his children and say: When the month of Ramadan enters, then exert yourselves, for in it sustenances are apportioned, lifespans are written, and in it the delegation of Allah—those who come unto Him—is recorded; and in it is a night in which action is better than action in a thousand months.

1843 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, the number of the months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth." So the foremost of the months is the Month of Allah, and it is the Month of Ramadan; and the heart of the Month of Ramadan is Laylat al-Qadr. And the Qur'an was sent down on the first night of the Month of Ramadan, so receive the month with the Qur'an." The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The descent of the Qur'an was completed on Laylat al-Qadr.

Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth al-Nakhaʿī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, Allah did not make the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān obligatory upon any of the nations before us.” So I said to him: Then what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you”? He said: “Allah only made the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān obligatory upon the Prophets, not upon the nations. So He favored this community by it and made its fasting obligatory upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and upon his community.”

Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, said: When you see the crescent, do not leave without saying: 'O Allah, I ask You for the good of this month, its opening, its light, its help, its blessing, its purification, and its sustenance. I ask You for the good of what is in it and the good of what is after it. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what is in it and the evil of what is after it. O Allah, bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, blessing, taqwa, and success in what You love and are pleased with.'

1846 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, would face the qiblah, raise his hands, and say: "O Allah, bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, encompassing well-being, abundant sustenance, and the repelling of illnesses. O Allah, grant us its fasting, its standing, and the recitation of the Qur'an in it, and keep it safe for us, receive it from us, and keep us safe within it."

Among the sayings of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام upon sighting the crescent was: O obedient creation, tireless, swift, revolving in the orbit of governance, moving through the stations of decree. I believe in the One who illuminated the darkness by you, lit up obscurities through you, and made you a sign among the signs of His authority. He tested you with increase and decrease, rising and setting, illumination and eclipse. In all of that, you are obedient to Him and swift toward His will. Glorified is He—how excellent what He has arranged, and how precise what He has made in His dominion. May Allah make you the crescent of a new month for a new matter; may Allah make you a crescent of security, faith, safety, and Islam, a crescent of protection from afflictions and safety from evil deeds: O Allah, make us the most guided of those upon whom it rises, and the purest of those who look at it. And may Allah bless Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Prophet, and his family. O Allah, do for me such-and-such and such-and-such, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

2409 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Whoever goes out on a journey while carrying a staff of bitter almond wood and recites this verse: "And when he turned himself toward Madyan, he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way." up to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And Allah is Trustee over what we say." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will keep him safe from every harmful beast, every hostile thief, and every venomous creature until he returns to his family and his home; and there will be with him seventy-seven of the attendant angels seeking forgiveness for him until he returns and sets it down."
And he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Carrying a staff removes poverty, and al-Shaytan does not remain alongside it.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever desires that the earth be folded for him, let him take al-nuqūd from the staff, and al-nuqūd is a staff of bitter almond wood.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Use a staff, for it is among the sunnahs of my brothers, the Prophets, and the young and the old of Banu Isra'il used to walk with the staff so that they would not become haughty in their walk.
Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Give charity and set out on whichever day you wish.”

2405 - And it is narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Is travel disliked on any of the days regarded as unfavorable, such as Wednesday and others? So he عليه السلام said: "Begin your journey with charity, depart whenever it seems right to you, recite Ayat al-Kursi, and undergo cupping if it seems appropriate to you."

And it was narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr that he said: I used to observe the stars and know them, and I knew the ascendant, and because of that something would enter into me. So I complained about that to Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them both. So he said: “If something occurs in your soul, then give charity to the first needy person, then proceed, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will ward it off from you.”
And Kirdīn narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever gives charity in the morning, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, will avert the misfortune of that day from him."

And Hārūn ibn Khārijah narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, whenever he intended to go out to some of his properties, would purchase safety from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever was available to him. That would be when he placed his foot in the stirrup. Then, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, kept him safe and he returned, he would praise Allah, Exalted is He, thank Him, and give charity with whatever was available to him.

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from someone who asked him; he said: I said to him: A man bequeathed twenty dinars for a hajj. He said: “A man should perform hajj with it from wherever it suffices for him.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: I inform you, my master, that your servant ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār instructed in his will that hajj be performed on his behalf from an estate, a quarter of which he assigned for you: one hajj every year with twenty dinars. But since the route to al-Baṣrah was cut off, the expense upon the people has multiplied, so they are no longer content with twenty dinars. Likewise, a number of your followers made bequests concerning two hajj pilgrimages. So he عليه السلام wrote: “Three hajj pilgrimages are to be made into two, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.”

And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥuḍaynī wrote to him: My cousin instructed in his will that hajj be performed on his behalf with fifteen dinars in every year, but it is not sufficient, so what do you command me concerning that? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “You should combine two hajj pilgrimages into one hajj, if Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of that.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated, saying: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever is blind in this [life], he will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in way." So he عليه السلام said: "It was revealed about one who delays the hajj, the hajj of Islam, while he has what he can perform hajj with, and says, 'This year I will perform hajj, this year I will perform hajj,' until he dies before performing hajj."

And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had never performed hajj at all, while he had wealth, so he said: "He is among those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.'" So I said: "Glory be to Allah! Blind?" He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has blinded him from the path of الخير."

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Dharīḥ al-Muḥāribī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever dies and has not performed the hajj of Islam, while nothing prevented him from that—neither a need that would devastate him, nor an illness because of which he is unable to perform hajj, nor a ruler preventing him from it—then let him die a Jew or a Christian.

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: Whoever has the means by which he may perform hajj, then continues to delay that, while he has no occupation concerning it for which Allah would excuse him, until death comes, has indeed neglected one of the ordinances of Islam.

Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: “Whoever performs ʿumrah in Shawwal while intending to perform ʿumrah and return to his homeland, there is no harm in that. But if he remains until hajj, then he is performing tamattuʿ, because the months of hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qaʿdah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. So whoever performs ʿumrah in them and remains until hajj, then it is mutʿah. And whoever returns to his homeland and does not remain until hajj, then it is an ʿumrah. If he performs ʿumrah in the month of Ramadan or before it, then remains until hajj, he is not performing tamattuʿ; rather, he is a resident visitor who has separated the ʿumrah. If he wishes to perform tamattuʿ in the months of hajj through ʿumrah leading to hajj, then let him go out from it until he passes Dhat ʿIrq or passes ʿUsfan, then enter performing tamattuʿ by an ʿumrah leading to hajj. And if he wishes to perform hajj separately, then let him go out to al-Jiʿranah and recite the talbiyah from there.”

And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever performs an independent ʿumrah may go out to his family whenever he wishes, unless the departure of the people on the Day of Tarwiyah overtakes him."
And in the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: “ʿUmrah in the ten is tamattuʿ.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated, saying: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed Hajj as ifrād: may he perform ʿumrah after the hajj? He said: “Yes, when the razor has reached his head, then it is good.”
Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿUmrah is obligatory like hajj. So when one performs tamattuʿ, one has fulfilled the obligatory ʿumrah.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: About a mamluk who is out with the riding animals, grazing, and he wishes to perform ʿumrah and then depart. He said: “If he performed ʿumrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah, then it is good; but if it was in Dhū al-Ḥijjah, then nothing is suitable except hajj.”

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed three separate ʿumrahs, all of them in Dhu al-Qaʿdah: an ʿumrah for which he entered into iḥram from ʿUsfān, and it was the ʿUmrah of al-Ḥudaybiyah; and the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, for which he entered into iḥram from al-Juḥfah; and an ʿumrah for which he entered into iḥram from al-Jiʿrānah, and it was after he returned from al-Ṭāʾif after the campaign of Ḥunayn.

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If the mu‘tamir enters Makkah without tamattu‘, performs tawaf of the House, prays two rak‘ahs at the Maqām of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and performs sa‘y between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then he may return to his family if he wishes.

And it was narrated from him, عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, that he said: "Whoever brings a sacrificial animal during an Umrah, then he should slaughter it before shaving his head." He said: "And whoever brings a sacrificial animal while he is performing Umrah, he slaughters his sacrificial animal at the place of slaughter, and it is between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and it is al-Hazwarah."

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Mismaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who performs an independent ʿUmrah, then performs the obligatory tawaf of the House, then has relations with his wife before performing saʿy between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He عليه السلام said: “He has invalidated his ʿUmrah, and a camel is due from him. He shall remain in Makkah until the month in which he performed the ʿUmrah has passed, then he shall go out to the appointed miqat that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم designated for his people, enter into ihram from it, and perform ʿUmrah.”
And indeed, ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: That he goes out to one of the miqats, enters ihram from it, and performs ʿUmrah.

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salim ibn al-Fudhayl, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "We have entered for an Umrah, so should we trim or should we shave?" So he said: "Shave, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله invoked mercy upon those who shave three times, and upon those who trim only once."

Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī narrated from Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhdhā’, who said: I heard Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام saying: “If a man among you, when he intends to travel, stands at the door of his house facing the direction toward which he is heading, then recites Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in front of him, to his right, and to his left, and Āyat al-Kursī in front of him, to his right, and to his left, then says: ‘O Allah, protect me and protect what is with me; keep me safe and keep safe what is with me; convey me and convey what is with me with Your good conveyance,’ Allah will protect him and protect what is with him, keep him safe and keep safe what is with him, and convey him and convey what is with him.” He said: Then he said, “O Ṣabbāḥ, have you not seen a man being protected while what is with him is not protected, and remaining safe while what is with him does not remain safe, and arriving while what is with him does not arrive?” I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام, when he intended to travel, would say: "O Allah, clear our way, make our travel good, and magnify our well-being."

2416 - And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: He said to me: “When you leave your home, whether in travel or at home, then say: ‘In the Name of Allah, I believe in Allah, I rely upon Allah. Whatever Allah wills; there is no power and no strength except by Allah.’ Then the devils confront him, but the angels strike their faces and say: ‘What way do you have against him, when he has mentioned Allah, Mighty and Majestic, believed in Him, relied upon Allah, and said: Whatever Allah wills; there is no power and no strength except by Allah?’”

Hadith 2417 — Abu Basir narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: “Whoever says when he goes out from the door of his house: ‘I seek refuge in Allah from that from which the angels of Allah sought refuge: from the evil of this day, from the evil of the devils, from the evil of whoever has set himself against the friends of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, from the evil of the jinn and humankind, from the evil of wild beasts and creeping harmful creatures, and from the evil of committing all forbidden acts. I place myself under Allah’s protection from every evil’— Allah will forgive him, accept his repentance, suffice him regarding his concern, restrain him from evil, and protect him from الشر.”

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: He was asked, “Which 'umrah is better: an 'umrah in Rajab or an 'umrah in the month of Ramadan?” He said, “No, rather an 'umrah in the month of Rajab is better.”

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from him, peace be upon him: Regarding a man who entered iḥrām in one month and exited iḥrām in another, he said: "It will be written for him according to what he intended." And he said: "It will be written for him according to the better of them."
And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "If you enter ihram while there remains for you from Rajab a day and a night, then your ʿUmrah is Rajabiyyah."

ʿUmar ibn Yazid narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever wishes to leave Makkah to perform ʿumrah should enter ihram from al-Jiʿrānah, al-Ḥudaybiyah, or similar places. And whoever leaves Makkah intending ʿumrah and then enters as a muʿtamir should not stop the talbiyah until he looks at the Kaʿbah.
And it was narrated: “He discontinues the talbiyah when he looks upon al-Masjid al-Haram.”
And it was narrated: “He discontinues the talbiyah when he enters the beginning of the Haram.”

2955 - And in the narration of al-Fuḍayl, he said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. I said: “I entered for ʿumrah, so where should I cut off the talbiyah?” He said: “At the point parallel to al-ʿAqabah, the ʿAqabah of the people of Madinah.” I said: “Where is the ʿAqabah of the people of Madinah?” He said: “At the point parallel to the dyers.”
And it was narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man performing an independent ʿUmrah Mufradah, so he said: "When you see Dhā Ṭuwā, stop the talbiyah."
And in the narration of Murāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "The one performing ʿUmrah Mufradah stops the talbiyah when the camels place their hooves within the Haram."
And it was narrated: “He discontinues the talbiyah when he sees the houses of Makkah.”

Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Hajj is [during] well-known months." He عليه السلام said: "Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah. It is not for anyone to enter ihram for hajj in other than them."
And in another narration: "And a month designated specifically for 'Umrah is Rajab."

2961 - And he, peace be upon him, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not created on the earth any spot more beloved to Him than the Ka'bah, nor any more honored before Him than it. And for its sake Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the four sacred months sacred in His Book. "the day He created the heavens and the earth" Three of them are consecutive for hajj, and one separate month is for 'umrah: Rajab.

2962 - And he, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So travel freely throughout the land for four months." He said: "They are twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten days from the month of Rabi' al-Akhir; and the ten days from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah are not counted within the four months."
Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who entered into hajj outside the months of hajj, he said: “He should make it an 'umrah.”
Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated, saying: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "The year is twelve months; an Umrah may be performed in each month."

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: There is an ʿUmrah for every month. He said: So I said to him, "Can it be less than that?" He said, "There is an ʿUmrah for every ten days."
And Abān narrated from Abū al-Jārūd, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about performing ʿUmrah after hajj in Dhū al-Ḥijjah. He said: “It is good.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performs the hajj on behalf of his brother, or his father, or on behalf of another man among the people: should he say anything? He said: “Yes. At the time of his ihram, after he enters ihram, he should say: ‘O Allah, whatever fatigue, hardship, affliction, or dishevelment befalls me in this journey of mine, then grant so-and-so its reward in it, and reward me in my performing it on his behalf.’”

And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: If you wish to perform tawaf around the House on behalf of one of your brothers, then go to the Black Stone and say: In the Name of Allah, O Allah, accept from so-and-so.

2969 - And it was narrated from al-Bazanti that he said: A man asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man performing hajj on behalf of another man, whether he names him by his name. He said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nothing hidden is concealed from Him.”

Muthannā ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who performs hajj on behalf of another person, mentioning him in all the stations, he said: "If he wishes, he may do so, and if he wishes, he may not. Allah knows that he has performed hajj on his behalf; however, he should mention him عند the udhiyah when he slaughters it."

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated; he said: I said to Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: “My father has performed hajj, my mother has performed hajj, and my two brothers have performed hajj. I wanted to include them in my hajj, as though I loved that they should be with me.” So he عليه السلام said: “Include them with you, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign for them a hajj, and for you a hajj, and for you a reward for maintaining ties with them.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Salat (prayer), sawm (fasting), hajj, charity, and emancipation enter upon the deceased in his grave."

Hadith 2973 — A man said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, I had intended to include my mother or some of my family in my Hajj this year, but I forgot.” So he عليه السلام said: “Now, then include them both.”

It was narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: "Can a man depart early before the Day of Tarwiyah by a day or two because of the crowding and the pressure of the people?" He said: "There is no harm in it."
And he said in another report: He should not depart early by more than three days.

Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: It is incumbent upon the Imam to pray the zuhr salat in Minā, then spend the night there, and remain until the sun rises; then he should depart to ʿArafāt.

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله pray the Ẓuhr prayer at Minā on the Day of Tarwiyah He said: "Yes, and also the morning prayer on the Day of ʿArafah."

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār and Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The boundary of Minā extends from al-'Aqabah to Wādī Muḥassir, and the boundary of 'Arafāt extends from al-Ma'zimayn to the farthest point of the standing place.

And he, peace be upon him, said: “The boundary of ʿArafah is from the interior of ʿUranah, Thawiyyah, Namirah, and Dhī al-Majāz, and behind the mountain is a standing place up to beyond the mountain.”

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stood at ʿArafah on the left side of the mountain. The people began hurrying toward the hoofprints of his she-camel and stood beside it, so he moved it away, but they did the same again. He said: “O people, the place beneath the hooves of my she-camel is not itself the standing place; rather, all of this is a standing place.” He gestured with his hand and said عليه السلام: “All of ʿArafah is a standing place, and if there were nothing except what was beneath the hoof of my she-camel, that would not suffice for the people.” And he عليه السلام did likewise in al-Muzdalifah. So when you see an open space, move forward and fill it with yourself and your mount, for Allah, the Exalted, loves that those gaps be filled. Move away from the hills, and avoid al-Arāk, Namirah—which is the valley floor of ʿUranah—Thawiyyah, and Dhā al-Majāz, for they are not part of ʿArafāt.
And in another report, he said: "The people of the arāk have no hajj, and they are those who stand beneath the arāk trees."

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stood at Jamʿ, and the people began rushing toward the place of the hooves of his she-camel. So he gestured with his hand while standing and said: “Indeed, I have stood here, and all of this is a place of standing.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "My father عليه السلام used to stand at al-Mash'ar al-Haram where he would spend the night."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام used to when he placed his foot in the stirrup, say: "Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, and we could not have done so on our own." And he would glorify Allah seven times, praise Allah seven times, and declare Allah's oneness seven times.

2419 - It is narrated from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah that he said: I held the stirrup for Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام while he intended to mount, and he raised his head and then smiled. So I said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I saw you raise your head and smile. He said: “Yes, O Aṣbagh, I held the stirrup for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله just as you held it for me, and he raised his head toward the sky and smiled. I asked him just as you asked me, and I shall inform you just as he informed me. I held al-Shahbāʾ for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and he raised his head toward the sky and smiled. So I said: O Messenger of Allah, you raised your head toward the sky and smiled. He said: “O ʿAlī, there is no one who rides what Allah has bestowed upon him, then recites the verse of subjugation, then says: I seek forgiveness from Allah, the One who... There is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. and I repent to Him. O Allah, forgive my sins, for indeed none forgives sins except You—except that the Noble Master says: ‘O My angels, My servant knows that none forgives sins other than Me. Bear witness that I have indeed forgiven his sins.’”

2987 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When you pass through Wādī Muḥassir, and it is a great valley between Jamʿ and Minā, and it is closer to Minā, then hasten in it until you pass beyond it. For indeed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم quickened his she-camel there and said: "O Allah, keep my covenant secure, accept my repentance, answer my supplication, and succeed me with goodness among those whom I left behind after me."
Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The hastening in Wādī Muḥassir is one hundred steps.
And in another hadith: "One hundred cubits."

In the narration of ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever departs from ʿArafāt with the people, then does not remain with them at Jamʿ and goes on to Minā deliberately or out of disregard, then a badanah is incumbent upon him."

And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man departed from ʿArafāt and passed by al-Mashʿar, but he did not stop until he reached Minā, so he cast at the Jamrah, and he did not realize it until the day had risen high. He said: He should return to al-Mashʿar and stand there, then cast at the Jamrah.

Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm narrated, saying: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A blind man and a weak woman are with a Bedouin camel-driver, and when he departs with them from ʿArafāt, he passes on with them as they are to Minā and does not stop with them at Jamʿ. So he said: “Have they not prayed there? Then that has sufficed them.” I said: What if they did not pray there? He said: “They remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there; so if they had remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there, then that has sufficed them.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: There is no harm in allowing women to be sent ahead when the night has passed. They should stand at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām for a short while, then be taken to Minā, where they stone the Jamrah. Then they should wait a short while, then shorten their hair, and be taken to Makkah to perform tawaf, unless they want a sacrifice to be slaughtered on their behalf, in which case they appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Mismaʿ, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Regarding a man who stood with the people at Jamʿ, then departed before the people departed, he said: “If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him. But if he departed before the rising of dawn, then a sheep-sacrifice is upon him.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever reaches Jam‘ has indeed attained the hajj." And he said: "Any qārin, mufrid, or mutamatti‘ who arrives after the hajj has passed him by, then let him exit ihram with an ‘umrah, and hajj is due upon him the following year." He said: And he said regarding a man who reaches the Imam while he is at Jam‘: "If he thinks that he can go to ‘Arafāt and stand there for a short while, then reach Jam‘ before sunrise, then he should go to it. But if he thinks that he will not reach it until they have departed, then he should not go to it, and his hajj has been completed."

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at Minā when a man came and said, 'Some people have arrived, and the hajj has passed them by.' He عليه السلام said: 'We ask Allah for well-being. I hold that each man among them should slaughter a sheep, come out of iḥrām, and hajj remains due upon them the following year if they return to their homelands. But if they remain in Mecca until the days of Tashrīq have passed, then go out to the mīqāt of the people of Mecca, enter into iḥrām from there, and perform an ʿumrah, then hajj is not due upon them the following year.'

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "I went to perform the stoning, and then there were six pebbles in my hand." So he said, "Take one from beneath your feet."
And in another narration: "Do not take from the pebbles of the Jamarat that have already been thrown."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who took twenty-one pebbles and cast them, then one extra remained and he did not know which of them had been omitted, he said: “Let him return and cast one pebble at each one. And if a pebble falls from a man and he does not know which one it is, then let him take a pebble from beneath his feet and cast with it.” He said: “If you cast a pebble and it falls into a litter, then repeat in its place. But if it strikes a person or a camel and then falls upon the Jimār, it suffices you.” And he said regarding a man who cast at the Jimār, so he cast at the first with four pebbles, then cast at the last two with seven and seven: “He returns and casts three at the first, and he is done. And if he had cast at the middle with three, then cast at the last, then let him cast at the middle with seven. And if he had cast at the middle with four, he returns and casts three.” He said: I said, “A man casts the Jimār in reverse order?” He said: “He repeats it for the middle one and Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.”

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: For one who is fearful, there is no harm in stoning the Jamarat at night, slaughtering the sacrifice at night, and proceeding at night.

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār asked him about a woman who was ignorant that she should stone the Jamarāt until she departed to Mecca. He said: "She should return and stone the Jamarāt as she had been stoning, and the man is likewise."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from him: Regarding a man who departed from Jamʿ until he reached Minā, then something happened to him, so he did not stone the Jamrah until the sun had set. He عليه السلام said: “He should stone when morning comes, twice: one of them early in the morning, and it is for yesterday, and the other at the decline of the sun.”

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The injured person and the one suffering from an abdominal illness are to have the stoning performed on their behalf. He said: and the children, the stoning is performed on their behalf.

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā, peace be upon him, about the sick person: may the Jamarāt be stoned on his behalf? He said: "Yes, he should be carried to the Jamrah, and it should be stoned on his behalf." I said: "He is not able to do that." So he said: "He should be left in his lodging, and it should be stoned on his behalf."
Ibn Maskan narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Nājiyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about someone who spends the nights of Minā in Makkah. He said: "He must slaughter three sheep."

Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar asked him. About a man who visited the House and continued in his tawaf, his supplication, the sa'y, and supplication until dawn rose. He said: "There is nothing upon him; he was in the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from him that he said: "If you leave Mina before sunset, then do not let the morning come upon you except while you are there."

Jaʿfar ibn Nājiyah narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: If a man leaves Minā at the beginning of the night, then the night should not reach its midpoint except while he is in Minā. And if he leaves after the middle of the night, then there is no harm in his reaching the morning elsewhere.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Do not enter your homes in Mecca when you have visited, meaning the residents of Mecca."

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “If the pilgrim visits from Minā, then leaves Makkah, passes beyond the houses of Makkah, sleeps, and then reaches morning before coming to Minā, then there is nothing upon him.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, during his journey, when he descended, he would glorify Allah, and when he ascended, he would magnify Allah.”

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: "When you are on a journey, then say: O Allah, make my travel a source of lessons, my silence reflection, and my speech remembrance."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Abū al-Qāsim, no one declares Allah's oneness and no one magnifies Allah upon any elevated place except that what is behind him declares Allah's oneness and what is before him magnifies Him with his tahlīl and takbīr, until it reaches the limit of the soil.
Jamil narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm if a man goes to Mecca, performs tawaf during the days of Mina, and does not stay overnight there.

Laith al-Muradi asked him (peace be upon him): About a man who comes to Mecca during the days of Mina after finishing the visitation of the House, so he performs Tawaf around the House voluntarily, then he said: "Staying in Mina is more beloved to me."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you intend to depart in two days, then you may not depart until the sun passes the zenith. But if you delay until the last of the days of Tashrīq, which is the final day of departure, then there is no issue upon you whatever hour you depart, and you threw the pebbles before the zenith or after it.

3016 - He said: And I heard him saying regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for the one who is Godwary." So he said: "He avoids hunting until the people of Minā depart in the final departure."

3017 - And in the narration of Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn al-Mustaneer, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said: "For the one who avoids indecency, wrongdoing, argumentation, and whatever Allah has forbidden for him during his ihram."
And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: "For the one who has taqwa of Allah, the Mighty and Glorious."
And it is narrated: "Indeed, he emerges from his sins as though it were the day his mother gave birth to him."
And it is narrated: "Whoever fulfills for Allah, Allah fulfills for him."

And in the narration of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him." "Meaning: whoever dies, then there is no sin upon him. "And whoever delays." his appointed term. "Then there is no sin upon him, for the one who avoids the major sins."

Abu Basir asked him: about a man departing in the first departure. He said to him: "He may depart during the period between that and when the sun turns yellow. If he does not depart until it is near its setting, then he should not depart, and he should stay the night at Mina. Then when morning comes and the sun has risen, he may depart whenever he wishes."

Al-Ḥalabī narrated: He was asked about a man departing in the first departure before the sun declines, so he said: “No; rather, he may send out his belongings if he wishes, but he himself should not depart until the sun declines.” And it is narrated: “Whoever does that is among those who ‘hasten in two days.’”
3024 - And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from him, saying: "It is appropriate for one who hastens in two days to refrain from hunting until the third day has passed."

3025 - And Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from him that he said: “There is no harm in a man departing during the first departure, then remaining in Mecca.” And he said: “My father عليه السلام used to say: Whoever wishes may stone the Jamarāt at the rise of the day, then depart.” He said: So I said to him, “Until when does the stoning of the Jamarāt remain?” He said: “From the rise of the day until sunset. And whoever has taken game may not depart during the first departure.”

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him." He said: "It is not on the basis that this is simply unrestricted, so that if one wishes he does this and if one wishes he does that. Rather, it means that he returns forgiven—there is no sin upon him and no offense for him."

Aban narrated from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: That he was asked about al-Hasbah, so he said: "My father عليه السلام would stop briefly at al-Abtah, then enter the houses without sleeping at al-Abtah." So I said to him: "What do you think about one who hastened in two days?" Is al-Hasbah required of him? He said: "No."
And he said: "My father, peace be upon him, would stop briefly at al-Hasbah, then depart, and it is below Khabt and Hirman."

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is recommended for a man and a woman not to leave Makkah until they purchase dates with a dirham and give them in charity for what may have occurred from them during their ihram and for what occurred in the sanctuary of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Then let them complete their prescribed duties." He عليه السلام said: "It refers to what occurs from a man during the state of his ihram. Then when he enters Mecca, performs tawaf, and speaks good words, that is an expiation for that which had occurred from him."

And Dharih al-Muharibi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Then let them complete their prescribed duties." He said: "Al-tafath is meeting the Imam."

And Rib'i narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding His, Mighty and Majestic is He, saying "Then let them complete their prescribed grooming rites." He عليه السلام said: "It means trimming the mustache and the nails."
And in the narration of al-Naḍr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Indeed, al-tafath is shaving and what is on the skin of the human being."
3034 - And Zurārah narrated from Ḥumrān, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: "Tafath is a man's abstaining from perfume; then when he completes his rite, perfume becomes permissible for him."
And in the narration of al-Bazanti, from al-Ridha عليه السلام, he said: "Tafath is the clipping of the nails, the removal of dirt, and the removal of the ihram from oneself."

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I came to Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: “May Allah make me your ransom, what is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,” “Then let them complete their prescribed duties (tafath).” He said: “It is taking the mustache, trimming the nails, and the like of that.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, for indeed Zurayḥ al-Muḥāribī narrated to me from you that you said: ‘“Let them complete their prescribed duties” means meeting the Imam, and “and let them fulfill their vows” — those are the rites.’” He said: “Zurayḥ has spoken the truth, and you have spoken the truth. Indeed, the Qur’an has an outward meaning and an inward meaning, and who can bear what Zurayḥ can bear?”

Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the days of sacrifice in Mina. He said: “Four days.” And about the sacrifice in the rest of the towns, he said: “Three days.” And he said: “If a man arrives to his family two days after al-Adha, he may perform the sacrifice on the third day in which he arrives.”
And Kulayb al-Asadī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the nahr, and he said: “As for Minā, it is three days; and as for the towns, it is one day.”

3039 - What was narrated by Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “The sacrifice in Minā is for three days, so whoever wishes to fast must not fast until the three days have passed. And the sacrifice in the towns is one day, so whoever wishes to fast may fast from the next day.”
And it is narrated: "The Eid al-Adha lasts for three days, and the best of them is its first day."
It is narrated from Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār, who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام about the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage. He said, 'It is the Day of Sacrifice, and the lesser is the 'Umrah.'

And in the narration of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. At the end of a hadith, he says therein: "It was only called the Greater Pilgrimage because it was the year in which the Muslims and the polytheists performed Hajj, and the polytheists did not perform Hajj after that year."

It is narrated by Suwayd al-Qallāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The udhiyyah is obligatory upon whoever is able, whether young or old, and it is a sunnah (prophetic tradition).

And it is narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That a man asked him about the sacrificial offering, so he said: "It is obligatory upon every Muslim, except one who does not have the means." Then the questioner said to him: "What do you hold regarding the dependents?" He said: "If you wish, you may do it, and if you wish, you may not do it. But as for you, do not leave it."

Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: “O Messenger of Allah, the time of al-Aḍḥā has come, and I do not have the price of the sacrificial animal. Shall I borrow and offer the sacrifice?” He said: “Then borrow, for it is a debt that will be repaid.”

3046 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله offered two rams as sacrifice. He slaughtered one with his own hand and said: “O Allah, this is on behalf of me and on behalf of those of my Ahl al-Bayt who did not offer a sacrifice.” Then he slaughtered the other and said: “O Allah, this is on behalf of me and on behalf of those of my Ummah who did not offer a sacrifice.” And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام would offer a sacrifice on behalf of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله every year with a ram; he would slaughter it and say: “In the Name of Allah: ‘I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining upright,’ submitting, ‘and I am not among the polytheists.’ ‘Indeed, my salat (prayer), my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.’ O Allah, from You and for You.” Then he would say: “O Allah, this is on behalf of Your Prophet.” Then he would slaughter it, and he would slaughter another ram on behalf of himself.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded us regarding sacrificial animals that we inspect the eye and the ear, and he forbade us from the torn-eared, the split-eared, the one cut from the front, and the one cut from the back.”

3048 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "A lame animal with a clear limp, a one-eyed animal with evident blindness, an extremely thin animal, a mangy animal, a maimed animal, or one with a broken horn should not be offered as a sacrifice."

3049 - And it is narrated from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: One of the Khawārij asked me about this verse from the Book of Allah, the Exalted, "Eight pairs: of sheep two, and of goats two." up to His, the Exalted, saying: "And of camels two, and of cattle two." What is it from that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made halal, and what is it that He has forbidden? I had nothing with me regarding it, so I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was a pilgrim, and I informed him of what had happened. He said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has permitted in the sacrificial offering at Minā the domesticated sheep and goats, and He has forbidden that the mountain species be offered there in sacrifice. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic, "And of camels two, and of cattle two," then indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has permitted in the sacrificial offering at Minā the Arabian camels, and He has forbidden in it the Bactrian camels; and He has permitted the domesticated cattle to be offered in sacrifice, and He has forbidden the mountain species." So I went back to the man and informed him of this answer, and he said: "This is something the camels have carried from the Ḥijāz."
Aban narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: A ram suffices for a man and for his household; he offers it as a sacrifice on their behalf.
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a cow offered as a sacrifice, and he said: "It suffices for seven individuals."
3052 - Wuhayb ibn Hafs narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "A cow or a camel suffices for seven individuals, whether they are from one household or from different ones."

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Then when their sides fall down, eat from them and feed the contented one and the beggar." He عليه السلام said: "The contented one is the one who is satisfied with what you give him, and the beggar is the one who comes to you seeking."
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and Abū Jaʿfar عليهما السلام used to give in charity one-third to their neighbors, one-third to the beggars, and keep one-third for the people of the household.
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام disliked that the polytheist be fed from the meats of the sacrificial animals.

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “We used to forbid people from taking the meat of sacrificial animals out of Minā after three days due to the scarcity of meat and the large number of people. But today, the meat has become abundant, and the people have decreased, so there is no harm in taking it out.”
3057 - Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the atonement for hunted game: may its owner eat from its meat? He said: "He eats from his sacrificial offering and gives the atonement in charity."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "A sacrificial animal is not to be offered except from what is purchased during the ten days."

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About a man who purchases a sacrificial animal that is one-eyed, but he does not realize it until after buying it: does it suffice for him? He said: “Yes, unless it is a hady, for it is not permissible for it to be deficient.”
Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about an old animal whose front teeth had fallen out: would it suffice for the sacrificial offering? He said: “There is no harm in offering it as a sacrifice.”
And Ali عليه السلام said: "A sacrifice is not performed on behalf of one who is in the womb."
Jamil narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a sacrificial animal whose horn is broken, he said: “If the inner horn is sound, then it suffices.”

3063 - And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, who said: We were in Mecca, and high prices afflicted us regarding the sacrificial animals. So we bought for one dinar, then for two dinars, then it reached seven. Then we could not find any, whether for a little or for much. So Hishām al-Mukārī wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about that, and he wrote back to him: "Consider the first price, the second, and the third; add them together, then give in charity the equivalent of one-third of it."
And Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, said: "No sacrifice is to be made with anything from the domesticated birds."

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About the sacrificial animal: if the one slaughtering it makes a mistake and mentions someone other than its owner, does it suffice on behalf of the owner of the sacrifice? He said: “Yes. One only has what he intended.”

And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: If a man purchases a sacrificial camel while it is emaciated, it does not suffice for him. But if he purchases it as fat and then finds it emaciated, it suffices for him. And regarding the hady of the Mutamattiʿ, the same applies.

Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a group of people: does a cow suffice for them? He said: "As for the hady, no. But as for the uḍḥiyah, yes. And the hady suffices in place of the uḍḥiyah."

Al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿid ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who bought a sheep and did not announce it. So he said: “There is no harm; whether he announced it or did not announce it.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who drove a sacrificial camel, and it gave birth. He said: "He should slaughter it and slaughter its offspring. And if the hady was guaranteed and it perished, he should purchase another in its place and in place of its offspring."

3070 - Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man whose hady goes missing, then another man finds it and slaughters it, he عليه السلام said: "If he slaughtered it in Mina, then it suffices for its owner from whom it was lost. But if he slaughtered it in a place other than Mina, it does not suffice for its owner."
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If the hady (sacrificial animal) was identified and then was lost after that, then it has sufficed.

And it is narrated from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man brought a hady (sacrificial animal), and it perished in a place where he could not find anyone to give it in charity, nor would anyone know that it is a hady.' He said: 'He should slaughter it and place a written note on it so that whoever passes by it knows that it is charity.'

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who drove a sacrificial camel, then it broke down before reaching its appointed place, or death or destruction befell it. He عليه السلام said: 'He should slaughter it, if he is able to do that, and smear with blood its sandal by which it had been marked, so that whoever passes by it may know that it has been slaughtered, and may eat from its meat if he wishes. If the hady is guaranteed, then it is upon him to replace it, purchasing another in place of the offering when it breaks down or perishes. The guaranteed one is that which is obligatory upon him due to a vow or other than it. But if it is not guaranteed, and is only something he offered voluntarily, then it is not upon him to purchase another in its place, unless he wishes to do so voluntarily.'

And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who bought a sacrificial offering for his tamattuʿ, then brought it to his home and tied it up, but then it came loose and perished. Will it suffice for him, or must he replace it? He عليه السلام said: “It does not suffice for him unless he has no ability regarding it.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who purchased a ram and it perished from him. He said: “He should purchase another in its place.” I said: “What if he purchases another in its place, then finds the first one?” He said: “If both are still standing alive, then let him slaughter the first and sell the other; and if he wishes, he may slaughter it as well. And if he has already slaughtered the other, then let him slaughter the first along with it.”
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man comes across a lost sacrificial camel, then he should slaughter it and announce that it is a sacrificial animal.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about the obligatory hady: if it is afflicted by a fracture or injury, may he sell it? And if he sells it, what should he do with its price? He said: If he sells it, then he should give its price in charity and offer another sacrificial animal.
And in the narration of Hammad, from Hariz, in a hadith, he says at its end: "Indeed, the guaranteed hady is not to be eaten from when it perishes; so if he eats from it, he must compensate."
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Nahr is at the throat hollow, and dhabḥ is at the throat."
3080 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Every animal subjected to nahr but slaughtered as dhabh is haram, and every animal subjected to dhabh but slaughtered as nahr is haram."

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "A Jew or a Christian must not slaughter your sacrificial animal for you. If it is a woman, then she should slaughter for herself, face the qiblah, and say: "I have turned my face toward the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth." As a Muslim. O Allah, it is from You and for You."

3082 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "So mention the Name of Allah upon them while they are lined up [for sacrifice]." He عليه السلام said: "That is when it is lined up for slaughter, and its forelegs are tied from the hoof to the knee, and the falling of its sides is when it falls to the ground."
Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani asked him: “How is the badanah to be slaughtered?” He said: “It is slaughtered while it is standing, from the right side.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "When you purchase your hady, face it toward the qiblah and sacrifice it by nahr or slaughter it, and say: "I have turned my face toward the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining upright, as a Muslim, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my salat, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner, and with that I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims." O Allah, from You and for You. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from me. Then pass the knife over it, and do not sever its spinal cord until it dies."

Hammad narrated from Hariz that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Ali عليه السلام, when he drove the sacrificial camel, and passed by pedestrians, would carry them on a camel. And if a man's riding animal was lost while he had a sacrificial camel with him, he would ride it without harming it or overburdening it.

Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man: may he ride his hady if he needs it? So he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘He may ride it without overstraining it and without exhausting it.’”
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Ali عليه السلام used to milk the sacrificial camel and allow riding upon it, without causing harm.

Abu Basir narrated from him, peace be upon him. Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: For you, there are benefits in them until a specified term. He said: If one needs its back, he may ride it without being harsh upon it. And if it has milk, he may milk it in a manner that does not exhaust it.

It is narrated from Abī al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, who said: We were with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and the house was crowded with its people. He said: “He is not from us who does not excel in the companionship of the one who accompanies him, the accompanying of the one who travels with him, the courteous fellowship of the one who shares food with him, and good character toward the one who interacts with him.”

Safwan al-Jammal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: My father عليه السلام used to say: ‘There is no regard for the one who comes to this House if he does not possess three qualities: a character by which he deals well with those who accompany him, forbearance by which he controls his anger, and piety by which he is restrained from the prohibitions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.’
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “It is not from dignity that a man relate what he encounters during travel of good or evil.”

It is narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān al-Kalbī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام advised me and said: “I advise you to have taqwa of Allah, to render the trust, to speak truthfully, and to keep good companionship with whoever accompanies you, and ‘There is no power except by Allah.’”
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever you associate with, if you are able for your hand to be the upper one over him, then do so."

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who visits the House before shaving. He said, "It is not proper unless he has forgotten." Then he said, "Some people came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله on the Day of Sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered; and some of them said: I shaved before I cast the pebbles. They did not leave anything they were supposed to do earlier except that they delayed it, and nothing they were supposed to delay except that they advanced it. So he said: There is no harm."

3092 - And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who forgot to slaughter in Minā until he visited the House, then he bought in Makkah and then slaughtered it. He said: “There is no harm; it has sufficed for him.”

Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who, out of ignorance, did not shorten his hair or shave it until he departed from Mina. He said: "Then let him return to Mina so that he may cast his hair there, whether by shaving or shortening. And for the one performing hajj for the first time, shaving is required." And it is narrated: "He may shave in Mecca and carry his hair to Mina."
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would, on the Day of Sacrifice, shave his head, trim his nails, take from his mustache, and from the edges of his beard.

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When a man slaughters and shaves, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except women and perfume. Then when he visits the House, performs tawaf, and does saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except women. Then when he performs the tawaf of women, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except hunting.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who has stoned the jamarāt, slaughtered, and shaved his head: may he wear a shirt and a cap before he visits the House? He said, “If he is performing tamattuʿ, then no; and if he is performing ifrād for the hajj, then yes.”

It is narrated from the Imams (peace be upon them): That the Mutamatti' (pilgrim performing Hajj Tamattu'), if he finds the sacrificial animal but cannot afford its price, must fast for three days during Hajj: one day before the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Tarwiyah itself, and the Day of Arafah, and seven days when he returns to his family, 'That is ten complete days' as compensation for the hady. If he misses fasting these three days, he should partake in the pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasbah (the night of departure) and begin fasting in the morning, then complete the fast for two additional days afterward. If he misses fasting these three days until he departs and cannot stay, he may fast the three days while on the journey if he wishes, or he may fast all ten days when he reaches his family. He should separate the three days from the seven by one day, although fasting them consecutively is also permissible. However, he is not allowed to fast during the Days of Tashriq, for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) sent Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i on a gray camel to go through the tents and announce to the people in Mina: 'Beware, do not fast during these days, for they are days of eating, drinking, and marital relations.' If someone is unaware of the obligation to fast the three days during Hajj, he may fast them in Mecca if his camel driver stays, and if not, he may fast them on the way or in Medina if he wishes. When he returns to his family, he must fast the seven days. If he dies before returning to his family and fasting the seven days, there is no obligation upon his guardian to make them up.
Safwan narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever dies and does not have a hady for his tamattuʿ, his guardian should fast on his behalf.

And it is narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who performed tamattu' and did not find what he could offer as a sacrificial animal, so he fasted three days. Then, when he completed his rites, it occurred to him to remain for a year. He said: "Then let him consider the return point of the people of his town, and when he thinks that they have entered their town, then let him fast the seven days."

And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "If he has a residence in Makkah and wishes to fast the seven, he should leave the fasting for the measure of the time of his travel to his family, or for a month, then he fasts."

And Zurārah has narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "Whoever does not find the price of the sacrificial animal, and wishes to fast the three days during the last ten days, then there is no harm in that."

Yahya al-Azraq asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: About a man who entered on the Day of Tarwiyah as a mutamatti' and did not have a sacrificial animal, so he fasted on the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of 'Arafah. He said: “He should fast one more day one day after the Days of Tashrīq.” He said: And I asked him about a mutamatti' who had the price of a sacrificial animal with him, and he could find a sacrificial animal for the like of what he had, but he continued to delay and postpone that until it was the last of the Days of Tashrīq and the sheep became expensive, so he was unable to buy a sacrificial animal with what he had. He said: “He should fast three days after the Days of Tashrīq.”
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "His guardian fasts on behalf of the child if he does not find a sacrificial animal."

And it is narrated from ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days that are required of the mutamattiʿ when he cannot find the sacrificial animal, until he returned to his family. He عليه السلام said: “He should send a sacrificial blood-offering.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "The maḥṣūr is other than the maṣdūd." And he said: "The maḥṣūr is the sick person, and the maṣdūd is the one whom the polytheists turn back, just as they turned back the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his companions, not because of illness. The maṣdūd, women become lawful for him, while the maḥṣūr, women do not become lawful for him."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The one prevented and the one compelled slaughter their sacrificial camels in the place where they are compelled."

And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the mahsūr who did not bring the sacrificial animal, he said: “He performs his rites and returns.” It was said: “Then if he does not find a sacrificial animal?” He said: “He fasts.”

Rifa'ah ibn Musa narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Al-Husayn عليه السلام set out for 'umrah, having driven along a sacrificial camel. When he reached al-Suqya, he was afflicted with illness, so he shaved his head and slaughtered it there in its place. Then he came onward until he arrived and knocked at the door, and 'Ali عليه السلام said, 'My son, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, open for him.' They had heated water for him, and he bent over it and drank, then afterward he performed 'umrah.

Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the one who says: "Release me where You have prevented me." So he said: "He is released where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prevented him. He said: "Did he not say that? And the stipulation does not remove from him the Hajj in the following year."

It is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily, and it is not obligatory. He said: “He should arrange with his companions a day, and they should mark it. Then when that hour arrives, he avoids what the muhrim avoids until the Day of Sacrifice. Then when the Day of Sacrifice comes, it suffices for him. For indeed, when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was barred by the polytheists on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, he slaughtered, exited ihram, and returned to al-Madīnah.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “What prevents any of you from performing hajj every year?” It was said to him: “Our wealth does not reach that.” So he said: “Is none of you able, when his brother sets out, to send with him the price of a sacrificial animal and instruct him to perform a circumambulation of the House on his behalf and to slaughter on his behalf? Then, when it is the Day of Arafah, he should put on his clothes, prepare himself, and come to the mosque, and continue in supplication until the sun sets.”

It is narrated from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from his brother Zurarah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “May Allah make me your ransom, I have been asking you about hajj for forty years, and you continue giving me fatwas.” So he said: “O Zurarah, a House to which pilgrimage was made two thousand years before Ādam عليه السلام—do you want its questions to be exhausted in forty years?”

3112 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The valleys of the Haram flow into the Hil, but the valleys of the Hil do not flow into the Haram." And it is narrated from Abū Ḥanīfah al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit that he said: "Were it not for Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, the people would not have known the rites of their hajj."

Water and its heaviness were mentioned in the presence of al-Sadiq عليه السلام on the road to Mecca. He said: "Water is not heavy unless the camel is carrying only water and there is nothing upon it other than water."
And Ali عليه السلام used to dislike hajj and 'umrah on camels that feed on impurities.

Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: "When the days of the season arrive, Allah, Blessed is Allah, Exalted is He, sends angels in the forms of human beings who buy the goods of the pilgrim and the merchants." It was said: "What do they do with it?" He said: "They cast it into the sea." And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAmrī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: By Allah, the Master of this Affair surely attends the season every year. He sees the people and knows them, and they see him while they do not recognize him. It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī that he said: I asked Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAmrī, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: "Have you seen the Master of this Affair?" He said: "Yes, and my last meeting with him was at the Sacred House of Allah, while he was saying: "O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me." Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him and make him well-pleased, said: And I saw him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah in al-Mustajār, while he was saying: "O Allah, take vengeance for me against Your enemies."

It is narrated from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while a man owed me money, and I had feared its loss. So I complained of that to him, and he said to me: “When you arrive in Makkah, perform a tawaf on behalf of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Abū Ṭālib and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of ʿAbdullāh and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Āminah, the mother of Muḥammad, and pray two rakʿahs for her; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Fāṭimah bint Asad and pray two rakʿahs for her. Then supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, that He return your money to you.” He said: So I did that, then I went out from the gate of al-Ṣafā, and there was my debtor standing, saying: “O Dawud, you detained me; come and take your money.”

3117 - Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said: Whoever forgets the sa'i until he has proceeded through part of it or all of it, then remembers, should not turn his face away departing; rather, he should return backward to the place from which the sa'i is required.
Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari narrated from al-Ridha عليه السلام, who said: I said: "May the muhrim buy the slave girls or sell?" He said: "Yes."
And in the narration of Hariz, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who arrived in Mecca at the time of the Asr prayer, he said: “He should begin with the Asr prayer, then perform tawaf.”

Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission, saying: ʿAli عليه السلام said concerning a woman who vowed to perform tawaf on all fours: “She is to perform one week for her hands and one week for her feet.”

And it was said to al-Sadiq, peace be upon him: A man had blood on his garment, of a kind in which salat is not permissible, and he performed tawaf in his garment. So he said: “The tawaf sufficed for him in it; then he should remove it and perform salat in a pure garment.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Leave the tawaf while you still desire it."

Al-Haytham ibn ʿUrwah al-Tamimi said to Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: I carried my wife, then performed tawaf with her while she was ill, and I performed tawaf with her around the House in the obligatory tawaf, and at al-Safa and al-Marwah, and I counted that for myself; so will it suffice me? So he said: "Yes."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: “Our companions narrate that shaving the head outside of hajj or ‘umrah is mutilation.” So he said: “Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, when he completed his rites, would go to a village called Sāyah and shave his head there.”
It is narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said: Shaving the head outside of hajj or 'umrah is disfigurement for your enemies and beauty for you.
Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever rides a zāmilah and then falls from it and dies will enter the Fire."
As for the hadith that was narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: "Whoever rides a zāmilah should make a will."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had entered into iḥrām for Hajj al-Ifrād. When he entered Makkah, he performed tawāf of the House, then went to his companions while they were shortening their hair, so he shortened with them. Then, after he had shortened, he remembered that he was performing Hajj al-Ifrād. So he عليه السلام said: “There is nothing upon him. When he has prayed, then let him renew the talbiyah.”
