And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man who gives one Hajj to five persons, such that one of them goes out in it. Do they have a reward? He said: “Yes, each one of them has the reward of a pilgrim.” He said: So I said: Which of them has the greatest reward? So he said: “The one whom the heat and the cold afflicted. And if he is a ṣarūrah, that does not suffice for them, and the Hajj belongs to the one who performed Hajj.”

It is narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said: Salamah ibn Muḥriz asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was present, and he said: “I performed tawaf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then I came to Minā and had relations with my wife, and I had not performed Tawaf al-Nisāʾ.” So he said, “What an evil thing you have done.” Then he ascribed ignorance to me, so I said, “I was afflicted with this.” He said, “There is nothing upon you.”
And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “You have been commanded to perform hajj and 'umrah, so do not be concerned with which of the two you begin with.”

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “The first thing of justice that the Qa'im عليه السلام will manifest is that his caller will announce that those engaged in nafilah must yield the Black Stone and the circumambulation of the House to those engaged in the obligatory duty.”
And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Staying one day before hajj is better than staying two days after hajj."

When Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام bade farewell to Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir also accompanied him. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Bid farewell to your brother, for the one departing must go, and the one seeing him off must return.” Then each man among them spoke on his own. Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Dharr. The people only tried you with affliction because you withheld your religion from them, so they withheld their world from you. How greatly they will need tomorrow what you withheld from them, and how free of need you will be from what they withheld from you.” Abū Dharr said: “May Allah have mercy on you, O people of a Household. I have no grief-bound attachment in the world besides you. Indeed, whenever I remember you, through you I remember your grandfather, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he bade farewell to the believers, would say: May Allah provide you with taqwa, direct you to every good, fulfill for you every need, keep safe for you your religion and your worldly life, and return you safely to those who are safe.

And in another report, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم bid farewell to a traveler, he would take his hand and then say:" "May Allah grant you good companionship, complete assistance for you, ease the difficult terrain for you, bring near for you what is far, suffice you regarding what concerns you, preserve for you your religion, your trust, and the final outcomes of your deeds, and direct you to every good. Upon you is the taqwa of Allah. Entrust yourself to Allah. Travel upon the blessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

When you intend to depart for hajj, gather your family, perform two rak'ahs, glorify Allah abundantly, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and say: “O Allah, today I entrust to You my religion, my soul, my wealth, my family, my children, my neighbors, the people of my care, those present among us and those absent, and all that You have blessed me with. O Allah, place us in Your shelter, protection, refuge, and might. Mighty is Your protection and exalted is Your praise, and secure is the one who seeks refuge with You. There is no god but You. I rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a consort nor a child, and who has no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector out of humility, and magnify Him greatly. Allah is supremely great, and praise belongs to Allah abundantly, and glory be to Allah morning and evening.” When you leave your house, say: “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. There is no might nor power except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, the gloom of return, and an evil sight regarding family, wealth, and children. O Allah, in this journey I ask You for joy and for acting in that which pleases You of me. O Allah, remove from me its distance and hardship, accompany me in it, and be my successor among my family with goodness.” When you settle upon your mount and your conveyance is steady with you, say: “Praise be to Allah who guided us to Islam, taught us the Qur'an, and bestowed favor upon us through Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله. Glory be to Him who subjected this to us, though we were not capable of it, and indeed to our Lord we shall return. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, You are the carrier upon the back, the One sought for help in the matter; You are the companion in travel and the successor regarding family, wealth, and children. O Allah, You are my support and my helper.” When your mount proceeds with you, say on your way: “I have set out by Allah’s power and strength, without any power or strength from myself, but by Allah’s power and strength. I disavow before You, O my Lord, all power and strength. O Allah, I ask You for the blessing of this journey and the blessing of its people. O Allah, I ask You from Your vast bounty for lawful and wholesome provision that You drive toward me while

The Talbiyah. Then recite the four Talbiyah phrases silently, and they are the obligatory ones. You say: “Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka, wa al-mulka la sharika lak.” These four are obligatory. Then rise and proceed a little. When the land levels out for you, whether you are riding or walking, proclaim the Talbiyah and raise your voice with it. If you have taken the route of al-Madinah and entered ihram from Masjid al-Shajarah, then recite these four obligatory Talbiyah phrases silently until you come to al-Bayda' and reach the milestone on the left of the road. When you reach it, raise your voice with the Talbiyah and do not pass the milestone except while reciting the Talbiyah, and say: “Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulka la sharika lak. Labbayka dha al-ma'arij, labbayka labbayka tubdi'u wa al-ma'adu ilayk, labbayka labbayka da'iyan ila dar al-salam, labbayka labbayka ghaffar al-dhunub, labbayka labbayka marhuban wa marghuban ilayk, labbayka labbayka anta al-ghaniyyu wa nahnu al-fuqara'u ilayk. Labbayka labbayka dha al-jalali wa al-ikram, labbayka labbayka ilaha al-haqq, labbayka labbayka dha al-na'ma'i wa al-fadli al-hasani al-jamil, labbayka labbayka kashshaf al-kurabi al-'izam, labbayka labbayka 'abduka wa ibnu 'abdayk, labbayka labbayka ya karim. Labbayka labbayka ataqarrabu ilayka bi-Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad, labbayka labbayka bi-hijjahin wa 'umratin ma'an, labbayka labbayka hadhihi 'umratu mut'atin ila al-hajj, labbayka labbayka ahla al-talbiyah, labbayka labbayka talbiyatan tamamuha wa balaghuha 'alayk, labbayk.” Say this after every obligatory salat or supererogatory prayer, when your camel rises with you, when you ascend a height, descend a valley, meet a rider, awaken from your sleep, mount or dismount, and in the pre-dawn hours. If you omit some of the Talbiyah, it does not harm you, although it is better, except for the obligatory phrases, so do not leave out any of them, and frequently say “Dhi al-Ma'arij.” When you reach the Haram, perform ghusl from the well of Maymun or from Fakh. If you perform ghusl in your residence in Makkah, there is no harm. And say when entering the Haram: “O Allah, You have said in Your revealed Book, and Your word is truth: ‘And proclaim the hajj among the people; they shall come
When you intend to enter Makkah, make an effort to enter it in a state of ghusl (ritual bath), with tranquility and dignity.

When you intend to enter al-Masjid al-Haram, then enter through the Gate of Banu Shaybah barefoot. Put your right foot in before the left, and maintain tranquility and dignity, for whoever enters it with humility is forgiven. And say, while you are at the door of the mosque: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and as Allah has willed. Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah and his family. Peace be upon Ibrahim and his family. Peace be upon the Prophets of Allah and His messengers. And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Gazing at the Kaaba. When you enter the mosque, look toward the Kaaba and say: “All praise is due to Allah, who magnified you, honored you, ennobled you, and made you a place of return for the people, a sanctuary, blessed, and a guidance for the worlds.”

Looking at the Black Stone. Then look at the Black Stone, face it directly, and say: All praise is due to Allah, who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. Glory be to Allah, and all praise is due to Allah. There is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and causes death, and He causes death and gives life, and He is the Ever-Living who does not die. In His hand is all goodness, and He is powerful over all things. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with the best of what You have blessed and bestowed mercy upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. Peace be upon all the Prophets and the Messengers, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I believe in Your promise, affirm Your messengers, and follow Your Book.

Touching the Black Stone. Then touch the Black Stone and kiss it in every circuit. If you are not able to do so, then begin with it and end with it. If you are not able to do so, then wipe it with your right hand and kiss it. If you are not able to do so, then point toward it with your hand and kiss it. And say: “I have fulfilled my trust and upheld my covenant, so that it may testify for me to faithful completion. I have believed in Allah and disbelieved in al-jibt, al-taghut, al-Lat, al-'Uzza, the worship of Shaytan, the worship of idols, and the worship of every rival called upon besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Tawaf (circumambulation). Then circumambulate the House in seven circuits, and kiss the Stone in every circuit, and keep your steps close together. When you reach the door of the House, say: “Your beggar, Your needy one, is at Your door, so bestow charity upon him with Paradise. O Allah, the House is Your House, the sanctuary is Your sanctuary, the servant is Your servant, and this is the station of one seeking refuge, seeking protection through You from the Fire. So free me, my parents, my family, my children, and my believing brothers from the Fire, O Munificent, O Generous.” When you reach the point opposite the water spout, say: “O Allah, free my neck from the Fire, expand for me from lawful provision, and avert from me the evil of the sinful among the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and the evil of the sinful among the jinn and humankind.” And say while you pass: “O Allah, indeed I am poor before You, and indeed I am fearful of You and seeking refuge, so do not change my name, and do not alter my body.”

On the supplication during tawaf. And say during your tawaf: "O Allah, I ask You by Your Name through which one walks upon the surface of the water just as one walks by it upon the firm tracts of the earth. And I ask You by Your hidden, concealed Name with You. And I ask You by Your Greatest, Greatest, Greatest Name, which, when You are called by it, You answer, and when You are asked by it, You give, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You do for me such-and-such." When you reach the Yemeni Corner, hold fast to it, kiss it, and send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad and his family in every circuit.

The statement between the Yemeni Corner and the corner in which is the Black Stone. And say between these two corners: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us by Your mercy from the punishment of the Fire.

Standing at al-Mustajar. When you are in the seventh circuit, stand at al-Mustajar—and it is the rear of the Kaaba on the side near the Yemeni Corner, in line with the door of the Kaaba. Then spread your hands on the House, press your cheek and your belly against the House, and say: "O Allah, the House is Your House, the servant is Your servant, and this is the station of one seeking refuge in You from the Fire. O Allah, I have alighted in Your courtyard, so make my hospitality Your forgiveness, and grant me what is between me and You, and seek me as a gift from Your creation." And supplicate with whatever you wish, then confess your sins to your Lord and say: "O Allah, from You are the spirit, the comfort, the joy, and the well-being. O Allah, my deed is weak, so multiply it for me, and forgive me for what You have seen of me and what is hidden from Your creation. I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire." And make abundant du'a for yourself, then touch the Yemeni Corner, then touch the corner in which is the Black Stone, kiss it, and conclude with it. If you are not able to do that, it does not harm you, except that it is necessary to begin with the Black Stone and conclude with it, and say: "O Allah, make me content with what You have provided me, and bless for me what You have given me."

Maqam Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Then go to Maqam Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and perform two rak'ahs there, placing it before you. Recite in the first of them al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, and in the second al-Hamd and Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun. Then recite the tashahhud and taslim, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Ask Allah, Exalted is He, to accept it from you and not make it your last عهد. These two rak'ahs are the obligation, and it is not disliked for you to perform them at whatever hours you wish, at sunrise and at sunset. Their time is only when you have finished the tawaf, so long as it is not the time of an obligatory salat. If it is the time of an obligatory salat, then begin with it and then perform the two rak'ahs of tawaf. When you finish the two rak'ahs, then say: All praise belongs to Allah with all His praises for all His blessings, until praise reaches what my Lord loves and is pleased with. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, accept from me, purify my heart, and purify my deed. Strive in supplication and ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to accept from you. Then go to the Black Stone and touch it, and kiss it, or wipe it with your hand, or gesture toward it, and say what you said, or not, for that is unavoidable.

Drinking from the water of Zamzam. If you are able to drink from the water of Zamzam before going out to al-Safa, then do so, and say when you drink: "O Allah, make it beneficial knowledge, expansive provision, and a cure from every illness and sickness. Indeed, You are Powerful, O Lord of the worlds."

Proceeding to al-Safa. Then proceed to al-Safa and stand upon it until you can see the House and face the corner in which is the Stone. Praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, and mention as much as you can of His blessings and the goodness He has done to you. Then say: "There is no deity except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is powerful over all things" three times. And you say: "O Allah, I ask You for pardon, well-being, and certainty in this world and the Hereafter" three times. And you say: "O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire" three times. And you say: al-hamdu lillah one hundred times; Allahu akbar one hundred times; subhan Allah one hundred times; la ilaha illa Allah one hundred times; astaghfir Allah wa atubu ilayh one hundred times; and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad one hundred times. And you say: "O He who does not disappoint His supplicant, and whose gift does not run out, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and grant me refuge from the Fire by Your mercy." And supplicate for yourself with whatever you wish, and let your standing on al-Safa the first time be longer than the others. Then descend and stop at the fourth step facing the Ka'bah and say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, its trial, its estrangement, its loneliness, its darkness, its narrowness, and its hardship. O Allah, shade me in the shade of Your Throne on the day when there is no shade except Your shade." Then descend from the step while your back is uncovered and say: "O Lord of pardon, O He who commands pardon, O He who is most worthy of pardon, O He who rewards for pardon, pardon, pardon, pardon. O Generous, O Noble, O Near, O Far, restore Your blessing upon me, and employ me in Your obedience and Your good pleasure." Then walk with tranquility and dignity until you come to the minaret, which is the edge of the place of sa'y, then hasten with the fullest stride of your gait, and say: "In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know; indeed You are the Mightiest, the Most Generous, and guide me to that which is most upright. O Allah,

When you complete your sa‘i, descend from al-Marwah and trim some hair from the sides of your head, from your eyebrows, and from your beard. Take from your mustache and clip your nails, leaving some of them for your hajj. When you do that, you have exited from everything from which you had entered ihram, and it is permissible for you to perform tawaf of the House voluntarily as much as you wish. There is no harm in praying the two rak‘ahs of voluntary tawaf wherever you wish in the mosque, but it is only permissible to pray the two rak‘ahs of the obligatory tawaf at the Maqam. When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, perform ghusl, wear your two garments, and enter al-Masjid al-Haram barefoot, with tranquility and dignity upon you. Perform seven circuits around the House voluntarily, and if you wish then pray two rak‘ahs for your tawaf at the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام or in the Hijr, and sit until the sun declines. When the sun declines, pray six rak‘ahs before the obligatory prayer, then perform the obligatory prayer and begin ihram after Zuhr, or if you wish after ‘Asr, for hajj ifrad, saying: "There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answer You, believe in Your promise, and follow Your Book and Your command. For I am Your servant and within Your grasp. I do not protect myself except from what You protect, and I do not take except what You have given. O Allah, I intend that which You have commanded of hajj according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. So strengthen me for what I am weak in, make it easy for me, accept it from me, and receive my rites from me in ease from You and well-being. Make me among Your delegation and the pilgrims of Your House, those with whom You are pleased, whom You have approved, named, and written. O Allah, grant me the completion of my rites in ease from You and well-being, help me in it, and accept it from me. O Allah, if some obstacle should arise that restrains me, then release me where You restrain me, by Your decree which You have decreed against

Departure to Arafat. Then proceed to Arafat and say, as you are heading toward it: “O Allah, to You I have turned, upon You I have relied, Your Face I have sought, Your word I have affirmed as true, and Your command I have followed. I ask You to bless my lifespan for me, fulfill my need for me, and make me among those by whom You boast today before one who is better than me.” Then recite the talbiyah while you are going to Arafat, and do not depart from Mina before the rising of dawn in any way. When you come to Arafat, set up your tent at Namirah near the mosque, for there the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله set up his tent and his dome. Then when the sun declines on the Day of Arafah, stop the talbiyah, perform ghusl, and pray the zuhr and the 'asr with one adhan and two iqamahs. You only hasten the prayer and combine the two so that you may devote yourself to supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking. Then come to the standing place with tranquility and dignity. Stand at the foot of the mountain on its left side, supplicate with the supplication of the standing, and pray much for your parents, asking your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to grant them to you. Do not stand except while you are in a state of taharah and have performed ghusl, and do not depart from it until the sun sets; for if you depart before its setting, the blood-sacrifice of a sheep becomes binding upon you.

Hadith 3134 — Zur‘ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When you come to al-Mawqif, face the House and glorify Allah, the Exalted, one hundred times, and magnify Allah, the Exalted, one hundred times, and say: “Mā shā’a Allah, lā quwwata illā billāh” one hundred times; and say: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner. To Him belongs the kingdom and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and causes death, and causes death and gives life. In His hand is the good, and He is powerful over all things” one hundred times. Then recite ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqarah, then recite “Qul huwa Allahu Aḥad” three times, and recite Āyat al-Kursī until you finish it, then recite the verse of subjugation. “Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne; He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly” to the end of it. Then recite “Qul a‘ūdhu bi-Rabbi al-falaq” and “Qul a‘ūdhu bi-Rabbi al-nās” until you finish both of them. Then praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for every blessing with which He has blessed you, and mention His blessings one by one, as much of them as you can enumerate; and praise Him for what He has bestowed upon you of family or wealth; and praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for what He has tried you with; and say: “O Allah, to You belongs praise for Your blessings which cannot be counted by number and cannot be repaid by deed.” And praise Him with every verse in which He mentioned praise for Himself in the Qur’an; and glorify Him with every glorification by which He mentioned Himself in the Qur’an; and magnify Him with every magnification by which He magnified Himself in the Qur’an; and declare His oneness with every declaration of oneness by which He declared Himself in the Qur’an. And invoke blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and do so abundantly and strive in it; and call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by every name with which He named Himself in the Qur’an, and by every name that you know well, and call upon Him by His names that are at the end of al-Ḥashr, and say: I ask You, O Allah, O Raḥmān, by every name that belongs to You; and I ask You by Your strength, Your power, and Your might, and by all that Your knowledge encompasses, and by Your gathering and by all You

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: “Shall I not teach you the supplication of the Day of ʿArafah, and it is the supplication of those Prophets who were before me?” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Then say:” “There is no god but Allah,” alone, “with no partner for Him.” “To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise.” “He gives life and causes death,” and He causes death and gives life, and He is Living and does not die; in His hand is the good, “and He is over all things powerful.” O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are as You say, and better than what the speakers say. O Allah, to You belong my salat, my religion, my life, my death, and to You belongs my inheritance; through You is my power of movement, and from You is my strength. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, from the whispering of the breast, from the scattering of affairs, from the punishment of the Fire, and from the punishment of the grave. O Allah, I ask You for the good of what the winds bring, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what the winds bring, and I ask You for the good of the night and the good of the day.”

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān: O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and in my flesh, my blood, my bones, my veins, my joints, my sitting place, my standing place, my entrance, and my exit, light; and magnify light for me, O Lord, on the day I meet You. Indeed, You are powerful over all things. ".

[Departing from Arafat]
When the sun sets on the Day of Arafah, walk with calmness and dignity, and depart while seeking forgiveness, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Then depart from where the people depart, and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful." 3137 - And Zur‘ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام said: "When the sun sets on the Day of ʿArafah, say: O Allah, do not make this the last covenant from this standing place for me, and provide it for me forever as long as You keep me alive. Turn me back today successful, attaining success, answered for me, shown mercy, forgiven for me, with the best by which anyone from among Your delegation and the pilgrims of Your Sacred House returns today. Make me today among the most honored of Your delegation before You, and give me the best of what You have given any one of them of goodness, blessing, well-being, mercy, good pleasure, and forgiveness. Bless for me that to which I return, whether family, wealth, little, or much, and bless them through me." Then when you depart, be moderate in your travel and keep to calmness, and leave the rushing that many people do in the mountains and valleys, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was restraining his she-camel until its head reached the rump, and he would command calmness; and his sunnah is the sunnah that is followed. Then when you reach the red dune, which is on the right side of the road, say: O Allah, have mercy on my standing place, bless my deed, keep my religion safe for me, and accept my rites. Then when you come to Muzdalifah, which is Jamʿ, descend in the middle of the valley on the right side of the road, near al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. If you do not find a place there, then do not go beyond the basins that are near Wādī Muḥassir, for it is the boundary between Jamʿ and Minā. And pray Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with one adhān and two iqāmahs. Then pray the nawāfil of Maghrib after ʿIshāʾ. Do not pray Maghrib on the night of sacrifice except at Muzdalifah, even if a quarter of the night has passed toward its third. And stay the night at Muzdalifah. And let this be among your supplications there: O Allah, this is Jamʿ, so gather for me in it all-comprehensive good, all of it. O Allah, do not make me despair of the good that I asked You to gather for me in my heart. Make me know what You have made Your

Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jamʿ. If you wish, you may take them from your provisions at Mina. Do not take from the pebbles of the Jamarat that have already been thrown, and do not break the stones as the common people do. There is no harm in taking the pebbles of the Jamarat from wherever you wish within the Haram, except from al-Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Khayf. They should be speckled, dark, like a fingertip, or like the pebbles used for khadhf; wash them while they are seventy pebbles, tie them in the corner of your garment, and keep them محفوظ.

When dawn rises, perform the morning prayer, then stand there at the foot of the mountain. It is recommended for the one performing Hajj for the first time to tread upon al-Mashʿar with his foot, or with his mount if he is riding. Allah, the Exalted, says: "Then when you depart from ʿArafāt, remember Allah at al-Mashʿar al-Haram, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before that you were surely among those astray." Let your standing be while you are in a state of ghusl, and say: "O Allah, Lord of al-Mashʿar al-Haram, Lord of the Corner and the Station, Lord of the Black Stone and Zamzam, and Lord of the appointed days, free my neck from the Fire, expand for me from Your halal provision, and avert from me the evil of the sinful among jinn and humankind and the evil of the sinful among Arabs and non-Arabs. O Allah, You are the best sought, the best called upon, and the best asked; and every visitor has a gift, so make my gift in this place of mine that You overlook my stumble, accept my excuse, pardon my sin, make taqwa my provision from this world, and return me successful, prospering, and answered, with the best of what any of Your delegation and the pilgrims of Your Sacred House returns with." And supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abundantly for yourself, your parents, your child, your family, your wealth, and your believing brothers and believing sisters, for it is a noble and tremendous station, and standing in it is an obligation. Then when the sun rises, confess your sins to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seven times and ask Him for tawbah seven times. And when the people become many at Jamʿ and it becomes constricted for them, they go up to al-Maʾzimayn.

When the sun rises over Mount Thabir and the camels see the places of their hoofprints, then depart. Beware of departing from it before sunrise, lest the blood-offering of a sheep become obligatory upon you. Depart with tranquility and dignity, and be moderate in your walking if you are on foot, and in your movement if you are riding. Hold fast to seeking forgiveness, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Then depart from where the people depart and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful. Remaining at al-Mash'ar after the departure is disliked. When you come to Wadi Muhassir—and it is a great valley between Jam' and Mina, and it is the one nearer to Mina—hasten through it the measure of one hundred steps; and if you are riding, then move your mount a little, and say: My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook that which You know. Indeed, You are the Mightiest, the Most Generous. As you said in the mas'a at Makkah. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would move his she-camel in it and say: O Allah, safeguard my covenant, accept my repentance, answer my supplication, and succeed me concerning those whom I have left behind after me. Whoever omits the hastening in Wadi Muhassir must return until he hastens through it. So whoever does not know its location should ask the people about it; then proceed to Mina.

When you come to your camp at Minā, then proceed to Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, which is the furthest one, while you are in a state of taharah (ritual purity), and take out from the pebbles you have with you for the Jamarāt seven pebbles. Stand in the middle of the valley facing the qiblah, with ten or fifteen steps between you and the Jamrah, and say while facing the qiblah and the pebbles are in your left palm: “O Allah, these are my pebbles, so count them for me and raise them in my deed.” Then take one of them and throw at the Jamrah from the side of its face, and do not throw it from above it. Say with each pebble when you throw it: “Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, drive away from me Shaytan and his troops. O Allah, make it a hajj accepted, an act accepted, an effort appreciated, and a sin forgiven. O Allah, in faith in You, in affirmation of Your Book, and upon the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.” Continue until you throw seven pebbles. It is permissible to say one takbir with each pebble you throw. If a pebble falls from you into the Jamrah or on your path, then take another in its place from beneath your feet, and do not take from the pebbles of the Jamarāt that have already been thrown. When you have stoned Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, everything becomes permissible for you except women and perfume. And on the second, third, and fourth days, you stone each day with twenty-one pebbles. You stone the first Jamrah with seven pebbles and stand by it and make duʿa, and the second Jamrah with seven pebbles and stand by it and make duʿa, and the third Jamrah with seven pebbles and do not stand by it. So when you return from stoning the Jamarāt on the Day of Sacrifice to your camp at Minā, then say: “O Allah, in You I have placed my trust, and upon You I have relied. Excellent is the Lord You are, and excellent is the Master and excellent is the Helper.”

The slaughter. Purchase your sacrificial animal, whether it is from the camels, cattle, or sheep; otherwise, make it a fat ram, mature and uncastrated. If you do not find an uncastrated one, then a castrated sheep from the flock; if you do not find that, then a mature male goat. If you do not find that, then whatever is available to you. Magnify the sacred rites of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for they are from the piety of hearts. Do not give the butcher its hides, collars, or cloth coverings, but rather give them in charity, and do not give the flayer anything from it. For they are from the piety of hearts. When you have purchased your sacrificial animal, face the qiblah and sacrifice it or slaughter it, and say: I have turned my face toward the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining upright, submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my salat (prayer), my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner; with that I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, from You and for You. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from me. Then slaughter, and do not sever the spinal cord until it dies and cools. Then eat, give charity, feed others, and gift to whomever you wish. Then shave your head. I have already mentioned the sacrificial animals in this book, and I am repeating here what must necessarily be repeated in this place. Among sacrificial animals from the camels, only the thaniyy is permitted, which is one that has completed five years and entered the sixth. From cattle and goats, the thaniyy suffices, which is one that has completed one year and entered the second. From sheep, the jadha' of one year suffices. A cow suffices for seven persons in the towns, and in Mina for one. A camel suffices for seven, and a jazur suffices for ten separate persons. A ram suffices for a man and for the people of his household. When sacrificial animals become scarce, one sheep suffices for seventy.

When you wish to shave your head, then face the Qiblah, begin with the forelock, and shave your head up to the two protruding bones from the temples opposite the base of the two ears. Then when you have shaved, say: “O Allah, grant me light for every hair on the Day of Resurrection,” and bury your hair in Mina.

Visit the House on the Day of Sacrifice or on the following day while you are in a state of ghusl (ritual bath), and do not delay visiting it beyond your day or the next day, for it is not for the Mutamatti‘ to delay it, while latitude is given to the Mufrid to delay it. And say on your way, while heading toward the visitation, whatever you are able of glorifying Allah, praising Him, and sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family. Then when you reach the door of the mosque, stand there and say: “O Allah, help me in my rites, keep them sound for me, and keep me safe through them. I ask You with the plea of the sick, the humble, the one confessing his sin, that You forgive my sins and return me with my need fulfilled. O Allah, I am Your servant, the land is Your land, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and pursuing Your good pleasure, following Your command, content with Your decree. I ask You with the plea of the one driven to You, obedient to Your command, apprehensive of Your punishment, fearful of Your chastisement. I ask You to grant me Your pardon and protect me, by Your mercy, from the Fire.”

Then come to the Black Stone and touch it. If you are not able, then wipe it with your hand and kiss your hand. If you are not able, then face it, point toward it with your hand, kiss it, say takbir, and say the like of what you said on the day you circumambulated the House, on the day you arrived in Makkah. Circumambulate the House seven circuits as was described to you. Then pray two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام, reciting in them in the first: al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad; and in the second: al-Hamd and Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun. Then return to the Black Stone and kiss it if you are able, or touch it, and say takbir.

Proceeding to al-Safa. Then proceed to al-Safa and do there as you did on the day you arrived in Makkah. Perform the movement between them in seven circuits, beginning with al-Safa and ending with al-Marwah. When you have done that, you have exited the restrictions of ihram from everything for which you had entered ihram, except women.

Then return to the House and circumambulate it for seven rounds, and that is the Tawaf al-Nisa'. Then pray two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام, or wherever you wish in the mosque. Women have then become lawful for you, and you have completed all of your hajj except the casting of the pebbles, and you have exited from everything for which you had entered ihram.

Do not spend the nights of Tashreeq except in Mina. If you spend them elsewhere, then a sheep's blood-sacrifice is due from you for each night. And if you leave Mina at the beginning of the night, then midnight must not arrive except while you are in Mina, or after you have already departed from Mecca. Except if you are occupied with your tawaf and your sa'i, and you find yourself in Mecca in the morning; then there is nothing upon you. And if you leave after midnight, it does not harm you to spend the morning elsewhere.

Stone the Jamarat on each day after sunrise until zawal, and the closer it is to zawal, the better. A concession has also been narrated from the beginning of the day until its end. Say what you said on the day you stoned Jamrat al-'Aqabah. Begin with the first Jamarah and stone it with seven pebbles from its front side, and do not stone it from above. Then stand on the left side of the path, praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family. Then move forward a little, supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him to accept from you. Then move forward a little and supplicate to Allah, then move forward a little more. Then do the same at the middle one: stone it with seven pebbles, and do as you did at the first, standing by it and supplicating. Then proceed to the third, maintaining tranquility and dignity, and stone it with seven pebbles, and do not stand by it.

The takbir during the Days of Tashriq. The takbir in Eid al-Adha is from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer of the fourth day; that is in fifteen prayers, and that is in Mina. In the towns, it is after ten prayers, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer of the third day. The takbir is that you say: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He guided us to, and praise belongs to Allah for what He has bestowed upon us, and Allah is the Greatest for what He provided us from the cattle of the grazing livestock.

Departure from Mina. If you wish to depart from Mina on the fourth day of the Day of Sacrifice, then depart when the sun has risen, and there is no issue upon you whatever hour you depart, whether you performed the stoning before noon or after it. If you wish to depart in the first departure, which is the third day, then depart when the sun has passed the zenith, for it is not permitted for you to depart before the sun’s zenith. If you remain until the sun sets, then you may not leave Mina, and it becomes obligatory upon you to remain until the fourth day of the Day of Sacrifice, which is the final departure. Proceed to Mecca proclaiming tahlil, glorification, and supplication. When you reach the Mosque of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, which is Masjid al-Hasba', enter it and lie in it on your back for as long as you rest. Whoever departs in the first departure, there is no obligation upon him to perform tahsib.

Entering Makkah Then enter Makkah with tranquility and dignity, having completed everything that was required of you in hajj and Umrah. And buy dates for one dirham and give them in charity, so that it may be an expiation for what may have occurred to you during your ihram from what you do not know.
Hishām ibn al-Muthannā narrated from Sadīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said to him: "Begin with Mecca and conclude with us."

And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "People have only been commanded to come to these stones and circumambulate them, then come to us, inform us of their wilayah, and present to us their support."

Some of our companions asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام and said to him: Should I begin with Mecca or with Medina? He عليه السلام said to him: Begin with Mecca and conclude with Medina, for that is better.
Safwan narrated from Al-ʿĪṣ ibn Al-Qāsim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the pilgrims from Kūfah: is it better that they begin with Madinah or with Makkah? He said: "With Madinah."

For indeed, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Abān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: "Salat in Masjid al-Ghadīr is recommended, because the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم appointed Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام there, and it is a place in which Allah manifested the truth."

Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the Mosque of Ghadīr Khumm during the day while I was traveling. He said, "Pray in it, for indeed there is merit in it, and my father عليه السلام used to command that."

And it is narrated from Hassan al-Jammal, who said: I carried Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) from Medina to Mecca. When we reached the Mosque of Ghadir, he looked at the left side of the mosque and said, 'That is the spot of the foot of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), where he said, "Whomever I am his master, Ali is his master."' Then he looked to the other side and said, 'That is the spot where the tents of the hypocrites were pitched, including those of Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. When they saw him raising his hand, some of them said, "Look at his eyes—they are turning as if he is mad." Then Archangel Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with this verse: "Indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their glances when they hear the message, and they say, 'He is indeed mad.' But it is nothing except a reminder for the worlds."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated, saying: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “When you depart from Mecca to Medina and reach Dhū al-Ḥulayfah while returning to Medina from Mecca, then go to the Muʿarras of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. If you are in the time of an obligatory salat or a supererogatory prayer, then perform salat. And if it is not the time of salat, then dismount there for a little while, for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to halt there and perform salat there.”

And ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, our camel driver passed by us and did not stop at al-Muʿarras.” So he said: “You must return to it.” So we returned to it.

Al-‘Ays ibn al-Qasim asked Aba ‘Abdillah عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) at al-Mu‘arras. So he said: “There is no ghusl required of you in it, and ta‘rīs is that one prays in it and lies down in it, whether one passes by it at night or by day.”

Zurarah ibn A‘yun narrated from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم made al-Madīnah sacred between its two lava tracts, prohibiting its game; and he عليه السلام prohibited in what surrounds it, a barīd by a barīd, that its herbage be cut or its trees be lopped, except the two sticks of the water-drawing camel.
And it is narrated: "Its two rocky grounds encompass what the volcanic tracts surround."
And it has been narrated in another report: "The area between its two lava plains is what lies between al-Sawrayn and al-Thaniyyah."

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "The boundary of what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله declared sacred from al-Madinah is from Rabab to Waqim, and al-'Urayd and al-Naqb on the side of Makkah."
And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "What is hunted between the two Harras is forbidden from the game of al-Madīnah."

Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb asked him, saying: "Is what is forbidden for me in the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the same as what is forbidden for me in the sanctuary of Allah, the Exalted?" He said: "No."

Aban narrated from Abū al-ʿAbbās, meaning al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله declare al-Madīnah a sanctuary?" He said: "Yes, he declared a barīd by a barīd as sacred, [regarding] its ʿiḍāhā." I said: "Its game?" He said: "The people do not lie."

3155 - When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered al-Madinah, he said: "O Allah, make al-Madinah beloved to us as You made Makkah beloved to us, or even more so. Bless its saʿ and its mudd, and transfer its fever and its pestilence to al-Juhfah."

And it is narrated: that al-Sadiq عليه السلام mentioned the Dajjal and said: "No plain land of it shall remain except that he will tread upon it, except Makkah and al-Madinah, for upon every mountain pass of the two of them is an angel protecting them from plague and the Dajjal."

3157 - Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ḥujr al-Aslamī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever comes to Mecca as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Medina, I will shun him on the Day of Judgment. And whoever comes to me as a visitor, my intercession becomes obligatory for him. And whoever has my intercession made obligatory for him, Paradise becomes obligatory for him. And whoever dies in one of the two sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina, will neither be presented nor reckoned, and he dies as one emigrating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and will be raised on the Day of Judgment with the companions of Badr."

[Coming to Medina]
When you enter Medina, perform ghusl (ritual bath) before entering it or when you enter it. Then go to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and enter the mosque through the Gate of Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام. When you enter, send salutations upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then stand at the foremost column on the side of the grave, near the corner of the grave, while facing the qiblah, with your left shoulder toward the side of the grave and your right shoulder toward the minbar, for that is the place of the head of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Then say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and I bear witness that you are Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh. And I bear witness that you conveyed the messages of your Lord, sincerely advised your Ummah, strove in the way of Allah, and worshipped Allah with sincerity until certainty came to you. And you called to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good exhortation, and fulfilled the duty of truth that was upon you, and that you were compassionate toward the believers and stern against the disbelievers, so Allah caused you thereby to reach the noblest station of the honored. Praise belongs to Allah who rescued us through you from shirk and misguidance. O Allah, place Your blessings, and the blessings of Your near angels, Your righteous servants, Your sent prophets, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earths, and whoever glorifies You, O Lord of the worlds, from the first and the last, upon Muḥammad, Your servant, Your Messenger, Your Prophet, Your trustee, Your confidant, Your beloved, Your chosen one, Your special one, Your elite from among Your creation, and Your chosen from among Your creatures. O Allah, grant him the rank and the means from Paradise, and raise him to a praised station by which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, indeed You have said, and Your word is the truth:" "And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would surely have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful." And I have come to Your Prophet seeking forgiveness, repenting from my sins. O Messenger of Allah, I turn by means of you t
Then approach the pulpit and rub your eyes and face with its two knobs, for it is said that it is a cure for the eye. Stand near it, praise Allah and extol Him, and ask for your need.

For indeed the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Between my grave and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and indeed my pulpit is upon one of the pathways of Paradise."

If you stay in Medina for three days, fast on Wednesday and pray on Wednesday night at the Pillar of Repentance, which is the pillar of Abū Lubābah where he tied himself, and remain there on Wednesday. Then on Thursday night go to the pillar next to it near the station of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, remain there through your night and day, and fast on Thursday. Then go to the pillar next to the station of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his place of prayer on Friday night, pray there through your night and day, and fast on Friday. If you are able not to speak during these days except what is necessary, not to leave the mosque except for a need, and not to sleep by night or day except a little, then do so. Praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on Friday, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, then ask for your need, then say: O Allah, whatever need I may have with You, whether I have begun seeking and pursuing it or have not begun, whether I have asked You for it or have not asked You for it, I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, concerning the fulfillment of my needs, the small of them and the great of them.

Visiting Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet (peace be upon her and upon her father, husband, and sons). The compiler of this book—may Allah have mercy on him—stated: Narrations differ regarding the burial place of Fatimah, the Lady of the Women of the Worlds, peace be upon her. Some narrated that she was buried in al-Baqi', and some narrated that she was buried between the grave and the pulpit, and that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: 'What is between my grave and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise' because her grave is between the grave and the pulpit. And some narrated that she was buried in her house, so, and when the Banu Umayyah expanded the mosque, it became part of the mosque, and this is what I consider correct. And indeed, when I performed Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, my return was to Medina by the grace of Allah, the Exalted, whose name is glorified. When I finished visiting the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, I proceeded to the house of Fatimah, peace be upon her, which is from the column near which one enters through the Gate of Jibril, peace be upon him, to the rear of the enclosure in which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, is. So I stood near the enclosure, to its left, and made my back face the Qiblah, and faced it with my face while I was in a state of ritual bath, and I said: "Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Prophet of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Beloved of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Friend of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Chosen of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Trustworthy of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of Allah's creation. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the most excellent of Allah's Prophets, Messengers, and Angels. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of creation. Peace be upon you, O Mistress of the women of the worlds, from the first to the last. Peace be upon you, O wife of the Guardian of Allah and the best of creation after the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O mother of Hasan and Husayn, the chiefs of the youth of Paradise. Peace be upon you, O truthful martyr. Peace be upon you, O content and satisfied one. Peace be upon you, O virtuous and pure one. Peace be

Do not fail to visit all of the sacred sites: Masjid Quba, Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim, Masjid al-Fadhikh, the graves of the martyrs, and Masjid al-Ahzab, which is Masjid al-Fath. And perform whatever voluntary salat (prayer) you wish in them. When you come to the graves of the martyrs, say: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final abode.” When you come to Masjid al-Fath, say: “O Helper of the distressed, O Answerer of the supplication of the afflicted, remove from me my grief, my anxiety, and my distress, just as You removed from Your Prophet—peace be upon him and his family—his anxiety, his grief, and his distress, and protected him from the terror of his enemy in this place.”

Farewell to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his minbar. When you wish to leave al-Madinah, go to the place of the head of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and greet him. Then go to the minbar and send blessings there upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله as much as you are able, and supplicate for yourself with whatever you wish concerning religion and worldly life. Then return to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and place your left shoulder against the grave, near the pillar that is before the rear pillar at the head of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Then perform six rak'ahs or eight rak'ahs, and recite al-Hamd and a surah in every rak'ah, and perform qunut in every two rak'ahs. When you have finished them, face the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and say, bidding him farewell, upon him السلام: "May Allah send blessings upon you; peace be upon you. May Allah not make this my final greeting to you. O Allah, do not make this the last عهد of visiting the grave of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family. And if You cause me to die before that, then I testify in my death to what I testify in my life: that there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger."

Visiting the graves of the Imams al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon them, in al-Baqīʿ. When you come to the graves of the Imams, peace be upon them, in al-Baqīʿ, place them before you, then say: Peace be upon you, O Imams of guidance. Peace be upon you, O people of taqwa. Peace be upon you, O proofs of Allah upon the people of the world. Peace be upon you, O you who uphold justice among creation. Peace be upon you, O people of purity. Peace be upon you, O people of intimate divine counsel. I bear witness that you conveyed, gave sincere counsel, and were patient in the way of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and you were denied. Wrong was done to you, yet you forgave. I bear witness that you are the rightly guided Imams, that obedience to you is obligatory, that your word is truth, and that you called yet were not answered, and you commanded yet were not obeyed. You are the supports of the religion and the pillars of the earth. You have never ceased to be under the eye of Allah, being transferred through the loins of the purified and carried into the wombs of the purified women. The ignorant jāhiliyyah did not defile you, nor did the trials of vain desires involve you in shirk. You are pure, and pure is your origin. You are those through whom Allah has bestowed favor upon us, the Judge of the religion. So He placed you in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and His name to be mentioned therein. He made our salat upon you a mercy for us and an expiation for our sins when He chose you for us and made our creation good through the grace He bestowed upon us from your wilayah. Through your grace we were, in His sight, among those who acknowledge, and through our affirming you, among those who confess. In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned. And this is the station of one who has committed excess, erred, become humbled, and confessed what he has done, and who hopes through his standing here for deliverance, and that the rescuer of those doomed from the Fire may rescue him through you. So be intercessors for me, for I have come to you when the people of the world turned away from you, took the signs of Allah in mockery, and acted arrogantly toward them. O You who are ever-standing, who do not become heedless, everlasting, who
And that the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, only said: "What lies between my grave and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise."

3159 - Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: “O my father, what is the reward of one who visits you?” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O my son, whoever visits me while I am living or after my death, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it is binding upon me that I visit him on the Day of Judgment and deliver him from his sins.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, every Imam has a covenant upon the necks of his awliyāʾ and his Shiʿah, and indeed part of complete faithfulness to the covenant is the visitation of their graves. So whoever visits them out of desire for visiting them and in affirmation of that which they encouraged toward, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ziyād ibn Abī al-Ḥalāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no Prophet and no successor who remains in the earth for more than three days until he is raised, with his soul, his bones, and his flesh, to the heaven. Rather, people come to the places of their traces, and convey salām to them from afar, and make them hear it from nearby in the places of their traces.
Jabir narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: "Part of the completeness of hajj is meeting the Imam."

Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah narrated from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What is for one who visits one of you?” He said: “Like one who has visited the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

3164 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to Ali, peace be upon him: “O Ali, whoever visits me during my lifetime or after my death, or visits you during your lifetime or after your death, or visits your two sons during their lifetimes or after their deaths, I guarantee for him on the Day of Judgment that I will deliver him from its terrors and hardships until I bring him to be with me in my rank.”
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The place of the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, from the day he was buried in it, is a garden from the gardens of Paradise."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The site of the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام is a channel from the channels of Paradise."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "The sanctuary of the grave of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, extends five parasangs from the four sides of the grave."
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Between the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام and the seventh heaven is a place frequented by the angels."

3169 - Salih ibn Uqbah narrated from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Sometimes the hajj passes me by, so I observe the standing of Arafah at the grave of al-Husayn عليه السلام. He said: “You have done well, O Bashir. Any believer who comes to the grave of al-Husayn عليه السلام knowing his right, on a day other than a day of Eid, twenty hajj, twenty accepted and approved Umrahs, and twenty campaigns with a sent Prophet or a just Imam are written for him. And whoever comes to him on a day of Eid, one thousand hajj, one thousand accepted and approved Umrahs, and one thousand campaigns with a sent Prophet or a just Imam are written for him.” He said: So I said to him: And how can I attain the like of that standing? He said: Then he looked at me as one somewhat angered, then said: “O Bashir, when the believer comes to the grave of al-Husayn عليه السلام on the Day of Arafah, knowing his right, then performs ghusl in the Euphrates and then heads toward him, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, writes for him with every step one hajj with its rites.” And I only know that he also said: “and one Umrah.”

And it is narrated from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, and Abā al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā, عليه السلام, and they were saying: “Whoever comes to the grave of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, عليه السلام, on ʿArafah, Allāh, Exalted is He, will make him coolness of chest.”

3171 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام on the eve of ʿArafah." It was said to him: "Before His looking at the people of the standing-place?" He said: "Yes." It was said to him: "And how is that?" He said: "Because among those are children of zina, and among these there are no children of zina."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, peace be upon him, his sins will be made into a bridge at the door of his house; then he will cross over it, just as one of you leaves the bridge behind him when he crosses it.

3173 - And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has entrusted with al-Ḥusayn, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, seventy thousand angels who send blessings upon him every day, disheveled and dust-covered, and they supplicate for those who visit him, and they say: O Lord, these are the visitors of al-Ḥusayn; do for them, and do for them."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever comes to the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام recognizing his right, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, will record him in the highest of ʿIlliyyīn."
Zayd al-Shahham asked him, so he said to him: "What is for one who visits one of you?" He said: "Like one who has visited the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family."

3176 - And Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them both, said: “The least of that by which the visitor of Abī ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, at the bank of the Euphrates is rewarded—if he recognizes his right, his sanctity, and his wilayah—is that what has preceded of his sin and what comes later will be forgiven for him.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: "Instruct our Shi'ah to perform the ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, for indeed his ziyārah repels collapse, drowning, burning, and being devoured by beasts. And his ziyārah is obligatory upon the one who affirms al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام in the Imamate from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

And Hārūn ibn Khārijah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “When it is the middle of Shaʿbān, a caller from the highest horizon calls out: O visitors of the grave of al-Ḥusayn, return forgiven; your reward is with your Lord and Muḥammad, your Prophet.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Qummī narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said: "Whoever visits the grave of my father عليه السلام in Baghdad is like one who has visited the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the grave of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, except that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام have their superiority."

And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about visiting the grave of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام—whether it is like the visitation of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. He said, “Yes.”

And ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Thānī عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, "May I be your ransom, is the ziyārah of al-Riḍā عليه السلام superior, or the ziyārah of Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام?" He said, "The ziyārah of my father عليه السلام is superior, and that is because Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام is visited by all people, while my father عليه السلام is visited only by the select among the Shīʿah."

And it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I read the letter of Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Convey to my Shia that my visitation is equivalent before Allah, the Exalted, to one thousand Hajj.' I said to Abu Ja'far (meaning his son, peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajj?' He replied, 'Yes, by Allah, and one thousand thousand Hajj for the one who visits him knowing his right.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: A man from the descendants of Mūsā, whose name is the name of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, will emerge. He will be buried in the land of Ṭūs, and it is from Khurāsān. He will be killed there by poison and buried there as a stranger. So whoever visits him while recognizing his right, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, will grant him the reward of one who spent before the Victory and fought.
Al-Bazanti narrated from al-Ridha عليه السلام, who said: No one among my awliya' visits me, recognizing my right, except that I will intercede for him on the Day of Judgment.

And Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Ridha عليه السلام said: "Indeed, between the two mountains of Tus is a handful taken from Paradise; whoever enters it will be safe from the Fire on the Day of Judgment."
And he, peace be upon him, said: I guarantee Paradise with Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, for whoever visits the grave of my father in Tus, recognizing his right.

3187 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "A part of me will be buried in Khurasan. No distressed person visits her except that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, relieves his distress, and no sinner except that Allah forgives his sins."

Al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd narrated from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said: "A man from my progeny will be killed unjustly by poison in the land of Khurāsān. His name will be my name, and his father's name will be the name of the son of ʿImrān, Mūsā عليه السلام. Behold, whoever visits him in his estrangement, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his sins, those that have passed and those that come later, even if they are like the number of the stars, the drops of rain, and the leaves of the trees."

Hamdan al-Diwani narrated from al-Ridha عليه السلام that he said: Whoever visits me despite the distance of my abode, I will come to him on the Day of Judgment in three places until I deliver him from its terrors: when the records are scattered to the right and the left, at the Sirat, and at the Mizan.

Hamzah ibn Humran narrated; he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “My descendant will be killed in the land of Khurasan, in a city called Tus. Whoever visits him there, recognizing his right, I will take him by the hand on the Day of Judgment and admit him into Paradise, even if he is among the people of major sins.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, and what is recognition of his right?” He said: “That he knows that he is an Imam whose obedience is divinely mandated, a stranger, a martyr. Whoever visits him recognizing his right, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, gives him the reward of seventy martyrs from among those who were martyred before the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله on true faith.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said: A man from the people of Khurāsān said to him: “O son of the Messenger of Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in a dream, as though he was saying to me: ‘How will you be when a part of me is buried in your land, you are entrusted with my trust, and my star is concealed in your soil?’” So al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to him: “I am the one buried in your land, and I am a part of your Prophet, and I am the trust and the star. Indeed, whoever visits me while knowing what Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has made obligatory of my right and my obedience, then I and my forefathers are his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever we are intercessors for shall be saved, even if upon him were the like of the burden of the two weighty beings, the jinn and humankind. And indeed, my father narrated to me from my grandfather from his father عليه السلام that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Whoever sees me in his sleep has indeed seen me, for Shayṭān does not assume my form, nor the form of any of my awṣiyāʾ, nor the form of any one of their Shīʿah. Truly, the truthful vision is one part from seventy parts of prophethood.’”

And it is narrated from Abī al-Ṣalt ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Harawī, who said: I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام say: “By Allah, there is none among us except one who is killed as a martyr.” So it was said to him: “Who will kill you, O son of the Messenger of Allah?” He said: “The worst of Allah’s creation in my time will kill me by poison, then bury me in a confined dwelling and in a land of estrangement. Indeed, whoever visits me in my estrangement, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, will write for him the reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, one hundred thousand truthful ones, one hundred thousand pilgrims performing hajj and ʿumrah, and one hundred thousand mujahids. He will be raised in our company and placed in the highest درجات of Paradise as our companion.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said: "Indeed, in Khurāsān there is surely a spot over which a time will come when it will become a place frequented by the angels." Then he said: "A group will continue descending from the heaven, and a group ascending, until the Trumpet is blown." So it was said to him: "O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, which spot is this?" He said: "It is in the land of Ṭūs. By Allah, it is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. Whoever visits me in that spot is like one who has visited the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, writes for him the reward of one thousand accepted hajj and one thousand accepted ʿumrah, and I and my forefathers will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "A part of me will be buried in the land of Khurasan. No believer will visit her except that Allah will make Paradise obligatory for him and forbid his body from the Fire."

Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal narrated from al-Sadiq Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, who said: He was traveling, and I was with him in al-Qadisiyyah until he came upon al-Najaf, then he said: “It is the mountain to which the son of my grandfather Nuh عليه السلام sought refuge, when he said: ‘I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water.’ Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed to it: ‘O mountain, can anyone seek refuge from Me in you?’ So it sank into the earth and was broken apart toward al-Sham.” Then he عليه السلام said, “Turn us aside.” He said: So I turned with him, and he continued traveling until he came to al-Ghariyy. He stood at the grave and conveyed peace from Adam, upon each Prophet one by one عليهم السلام, and I conveyed peace with him until the peace reached the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Then he fell upon the grave, greeted it with peace, and his sobbing grew loud. Then he stood and performed four rakʿahs of salat, and in another report, six rakʿahs, and I prayed with him. I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is this grave?” He said, “This grave is the grave of my grandfather ʿAli ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام.”

Visiting the grave of the Commander of the Faithful, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. When you come to al-Ghariyy on the outskirts of al-Kufah, then perform ghusl (ritual bath) and walk with calmness and dignity until you come to the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام. Then face him with your face and say: Peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. You are the first wronged one and the first whose right was usurped. You were patient and sought reward until certainty came to you. I bear witness that you met Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while you were a martyr. May Allah punish your killer with various kinds of punishment and renew the punishment upon him. I have come to you recognizing your right, having insight into your station, showing enmity to your enemies and to whoever wronged you. I commit myself to that before my Lord, if Allah wills. Indeed, I have many sins, so intercede for me with your Lord, for indeed you have with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, a known station, and indeed you have with Allah rank and intercession. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: "And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves."

When you wish to bid farewell to him, say: “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I entrust you to Allah and place you under His care. I convey peace upon you. We believe in Allah, in the Messenger, and in what she brought and indicated.” “So write us down among those who bear witness.” I bear witness in my death to what I bore witness to in my life. I bear witness that you are the Imams, one after another. I bear witness that those who killed you and fought you are polytheists, and whoever opposed you is in the lowest depth of Hell. I bear witness that those who fought you are enemies to us, and we are free of them, and that they are the party of Satan. O Allah, I ask You after the salat and the salutation to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad”—and you name them, peace be upon them—“and do not make this the last of the covenant of visiting him; but if You make it so, then gather me with these named Imams. O Allah, make firm our hearts with obedience, sincere counsel, love, excellent support, and submission.” And recite the tasbih of al-Zahra' Fatimah عليها السلام, and it is: “Glory be to the Possessor of lofty and tremendous majesty. Glory be to the Possessor of elevated, exalted, and sublime might. Glory be to the Possessor of ancient and splendid sovereignty. Glory be to the Possessor of radiance and beauty. Glory be to the One who is clothed in light and dignity. Glory be to the One who sees the trace of the ant upon the hard rock and the movement of the bird in the air.”

This visitation is narrated by al-Hasan ibn Rashid from al-Husayn ibn Thuwair from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'When you come to Abu Abdullah al-Husayn (peace be upon him), perform ghusl on the bank of the Euphrates, then wear pure clothes, then walk barefoot, for you are in a sanctuary of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, and the sanctuary of His Messenger, peace be upon him and his family. Engage abundantly in takbir, tahlil, tamjid, and ta'zim for Allah, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, peace be upon them, until you reach the gate of the shrine. Then say: Peace be upon you, O proof of Allah and son of His proof. Peace be upon you, O angels of Allah and visitors to the grave of the son of the Prophet of Allah.' Then take ten steps, then stand and say 'Allahu Akbar' thirty times, then walk towards him until you reach him from the front. Face him with your face, and place the Qibla between your shoulders. Then say: Peace be upon you, O proof of Allah and son of His proof. Peace be upon you, O avenged by Allah on earth and son of His avenger. Peace be upon you, O solitary one of Allah, avenged in the heavens and the earth. I bear witness that your blood resides in eternity, causing the canopies of the Throne to tremble, and all creation wept for you. The seven heavens, the seven earths, all within and between them, and all beings in Paradise and Hell, both seen and unseen, wept for you. I bear witness that you are the proof of Allah and the son of His proof. I bear witness that you are the avenger of Allah and the son of His avenger. I bear witness that you are the solitary one of Allah, avenged in the heavens and the earth. I bear witness that you conveyed from Allah, advised sincerely, fulfilled and completed, and struggled in the path of your Lord. You departed as a witness, a martyr, a witness, and testified against. I am the servant of Allah and your master, in your obedience. I am the visitor to you, seeking thereby the highest rank with Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, and steadfastness in migration to you, and the path that cannot be replaced, by entering your guardianship, as commanded. Whoever seeks Allah begins with you. Whoever seeks Allah begins with you. Whoever seeks Allah begins with you. Through you, Allah reveals falsehood. Through you, Allah distances the age of deceit. Through you,

Hadith 3200 — From the narration of Yusuf al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "When you wish to bid him farewell, then say: Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. We entrust you to Allah, and we convey peace upon you.
