We believe in Allah, in the Messenger, and in what he brought and what he guided to. “And we followed the Messenger.” O Lord, “so write us among the witnesses.” O Allah, do not make this the last covenant between us and him. O Allah, we ask You to let us benefit through his love. O Allah, raise him to a praised station by which You support Your religion, kill Your enemy, and destroy those who have set up war against the family of Muhammad, for You have promised him that, and You are— “One who does not fail the promise.” Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I bear witness that you are noble martyrs; you strove in the way of Allah and were killed upon the path of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the son of His Messenger, much. Praise belongs to Allah, who fulfilled His promise to you and showed you what you love. May Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and upon them be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. O Allah, do not occupy me in the world away from gratitude for Your blessing, nor with abundance therein such that the wonders of its delight distract me and its adornment tempt me, nor with scarcity whose harm injures my deeds and fills my breast with its worry. Grant me from that a sufficiency from the evil ones among Your creation and provision by which I may attain Your pleasure, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And I have presented in the Book of Ziyarat, and in the Book of the Maqtal of al-Husayn عليه السلام, various forms of ziyarat, and I chose this one for this book because in my view it is the soundest of the ziyarat by way of transmission, and in it there is sufficiency and adequacy.
Visiting the graves of the martyrs. When you wish to visit the graves of the martyrs, then say: Peace be upon you for your patience; how excellent is the final abode.

3202 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “If the distance becomes great for one of you and the abode is far from him, then let him ascend the highest part of his dwelling, perform two rak'ahs, and gesture with salām toward our graves, for indeed that reaches us.”

Hadith 3203 — In the narration of Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: "O Sadīr, do you visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام every day?" I said, "May I be your ransom, no." He said, "How neglectful you are! Then do you visit him every month?" I said, "No." He said, "Then do you visit him every year?" I said, "That may sometimes happen." He said, "O Sadīr, how neglectful you are toward al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has a thousand thousand angels, disheveled and dust-covered, who weep and visit, and do not cease? And what would it cost you, O Sadīr, to visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn صلى الله عليه وآله in every Friday five times, or once every day?" I said, "May I be your ransom, there are many farsakhs between us and him." So he said to me, "Go up onto your roof, then turn right and left, then raise your head to the sky, then incline toward the grave and say: 'Peace be upon you, O Abā ʿAbdillāh. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' By that, a visitation will be written for you, and the visitation is a hajj and an ʿumrah." Sadīr said: Sometimes I did that more than twenty times in a month.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "In the clay of the grave of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, there is healing from every ailment, and it is the greatest remedy."

3205 - And he, peace be upon him, said: "When you consume it, then say: O Allah, Lord of the blessed soil and Lord of the Wasi whom it has covered, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and make it beneficial knowledge, abundant sustenance, and a cure from every illness."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “The sanctuary of the grave of al-Husayn عليه السلام extends five farsakhs from the four sides of the grave.”

It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The place of the grave of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, since the day he was buried in it, is a garden from the gardens of Paradise.
And he, peace be upon him, said: The location of the grave of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, is a channel from the channels of Paradise.

3212 - It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, who said: Al-Riḍā عليه السلام was asked about going to the grave of Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, and he said: "Pray in the mosques around it, and it suffices in all places that you say: Peace be upon the awliyāʾ of Allah and His chosen ones. Peace be upon the trustees of Allah and His beloved ones. Peace be upon the helpers of Allah and His successors. Peace be upon the loci of the maʿrifah of Allah. Peace be upon the dwellings of the dhikr of Allah. Peace be upon those who manifest the command of Allah and His prohibition. Peace be upon the callers to Allah. Peace be upon those firmly established in the pleasure of Allah. Peace be upon those made sincere in obedience to Allah. Peace be upon the guides to Allah. Peace be upon those such that whoever befriends them has befriended Allah, and whoever opposes them has opposed Allah; and whoever knows them has known Allah, and whoever is ignorant of them has been ignorant of Allah; and whoever holds fast to them has held fast to Allah, and whoever abandons them has abandoned Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And I call Allah to witness that I am at peace with those with whom you are at peace and at war with those with whom you are at war, believing in your secret and your openness, consigning all of that to you. May Allah curse the enemy of the family of Muḥammad from among the jinn and humankind, and I disavow myself before Allah from them. And may Allah bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad." [And] this suffices in all the ziyārāt, and you should abundantly invoke blessings upon Muḥammad and his family, the Imams, naming them one by one by their names, disavow yourself from their enemies, and choose whatever supplication you wish for yourself and for the believing men and the believing women.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated, saying: Musa ibn Abdullah al-Nakha'i narrated, 'I said to Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), When you reach the door, stand and testify to the two testimonies of faith while in a state of ritual bath. When you enter and see the grave, stand and say 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest' thirty times. Then walk a little with tranquility and dignity, keeping your steps close together. Then stand and glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, thirty times. Then approach the grave and glorify Allah forty times, completing one hundred glorifications. Then say: Peace be upon you, O people of the House of Prophethood, and the abode of the Message, the place of the angels' frequent visits, the descent of revelation, the source of mercy, the treasures of knowledge, the culmination of forbearance, the foundation of generosity, the leaders of nations, the custodians of blessings, the essence of righteousness, the pillars of virtue, the guides of servants, the anchors of lands, the gates of faith, the trustees of the Most Merciful, the progeny of the Prophets, the chosen ones among the messengers, the family of the best of the Lord of the Worlds. And the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon the Imams of guidance, the lamps in the darkness, the standards of piety, the possessors of wisdom, the masters of intellect, the refuge of humanity, the inheritors of the Prophets, the highest example, the bearers of the best call, and the proofs of Allah for the inhabitants of the world, the Hereafter, and this life. And the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon the repositories of the knowledge of Allah, the abodes of the blessings of Allah, the mines of the wisdom of Allah, the keepers of the secrets of Allah, the bearers of the Book of Allah, the successors of the Prophet of Allah, and the progeny of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family. And the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon the callers to Allah, the guides to Allah's pleasure, those who remain steadfast in Allah's command, those who are perfect in their love for Allah, those who are sincere in the oneness of Allah, and those who manifest Allah's command and prohibition, and His honored servants, 'who do not precede Him in speech and act according to His command.' And the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon the Imams who are

ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maslamah, from al-Sarrī ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Shall I not inform you of the worst of people?” They said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “The one who travels alone, withholds his aid, and strikes his servant.”

2433 - Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said, concerning the وصية of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to Ali عليه السلام: "Do not go out on a journey alone, for al-Shaytan is with the one person, and he is farther away from two. O Ali, when a man travels alone, he is misguided; and two are misguided; but three are a group. Some of them narrated: 'three are a journey.'"

2434 - And Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar, upon them both be peace, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, cursed three: the one who eats his provisions alone, the one who sleeps alone in a house, and the one who rides alone in the wilderness.”

Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in Mecca when a man from al-Madīnah came to him. He said to him, “Who accompanied you?” He said, “No one accompanied me.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him, “Indeed, had I instructed you beforehand, I would have improved your manners.” Then he said, “One is a shayṭān, two are two shayṭāns, three are companions, and four are fellow travelers.”
Al-Sakūnī narrated with his chain of transmission; he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "First the companion, then the journey."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whenever two people accompany one another, the one with the greater reward and the one more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the one who is gentler toward his companion.
And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: "Do not accompany in travel one who does not see for you over himself the same merit that you see for him over yourself."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "It is from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) that when people go out on a journey, they bring out their expenses together, for that is more pleasant for their souls and better for their character."
And Isḥāq ibn Jarīr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He used to say: “Accompany one by whom you are adorned, and do not accompany one who is adorned by you.”

2441 - Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated, saying: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: You know my condition, the extent of my means, and my generosity toward my brothers. I accompany a group of them on the road to Makkah and spend generously on them. He said: “Do not do that, O Shihāb. If you are generous and they also spend, you will overburden them; and if they hold back, you will humiliate them. So accompany your equals, accompany your equals.”
And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: "If you keep company with someone, then keep company with your equal, and do not accompany one who suffices you entirely, for that is a humiliation for the believer."
Abu Khadijah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "The one who spends the night alone in the house is a devil; two are a gathering of whisperers; and three bring companionship."

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The most beloved companions to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are four; and no group exceeds seven except that their commotion becomes much."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The right of the traveller is that his brothers should stay with him for three days when he falls ill."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no spending more beloved to Allah than moderate spending, and He dislikes extravagance except in hajj or ʿumrah.”

It is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “My family is with me, and I intend hajj, so I tie my expenses at my waist.” He said: “Yes, for my father عليه السلام used to say: ‘Part of the strength of the traveller is safeguarding his expenses.’”

And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I have dirhams with me that have images on them, while I am in a state of ihram, so I place them in my money-belt and tie it around my waist.” He عليه السلام said: “There is no problem. Are they not your expenses, and that upon which you rely after Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?”
2450 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "When you travel, prepare provisions for the journey and make them pleasant."

And it is narrated from Naṣr al-Khādim, who said: The righteous servant, Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, looked at a provision-cloth upon which there were brass rings, and said: "Remove these and place iron in their stead, for none of the creeping harmful creatures will come near anything in which there is something of it."

2452 - Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said to one of his companions: “Do you come to the grave of Abū ʿAbd Allāh, may the blessings of Allah be upon him?” He replied to him, “Yes.” He said: “Do you make provisions for that?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “If you were to visit the graves of your fathers and mothers, you would not do that.” He said: I said, “Then what thing should we eat?” He said: “Bread with milk.”

2453 - And in another report, al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "It has reached me that some people, when they visit al-Husayn عليه السلام, carry with them a travel spread containing young goats, sweet dishes, and the like. If they were to visit the graves of their loved ones, they would not carry this with them."
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Part of a man's dignity is that he makes his provisions pleasant when he sets out on a journey."
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, when he traveled to Mecca for hajj or ʿumrah, would take provisions from the finest supplies: almonds, sugar, and sawiq made sour and sweetened.

And it is narrated: that Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, stood by the Kaʿbah and said: I am Jundab ibn al-Sakan. Then the people gathered around him, and he said: If one of you intended a journey, he would take for it provisions that would set him right for his journey. So take provisions for the journey of the Day of Resurrection. Do you not desire therein that which will set you right? Then a man stood up to him and said: Guide us. He said: Fast on an intensely hot day for the Resurrection; perform a hajj for the tremendous matters; and pray two rakʿahs in the darkness of the night for the loneliness of the graves; a good word that you speak, and an evil word from which you remain silent; or charity from you to a needy person—perhaps by it, O poor one, you may be saved from a difficult day. Make the world into two dirhams: one dirham that you spend on your dependents, and one dirham that you send ahead for your Hereafter. The third harms and does not benefit, so do not desire it. Make the world into two words: a word in seeking the halal, and a word for the Hereafter. The third harms and does not benefit, so do not desire it. Then he said: The worry of a day I will not reach has slain me.

2457 - Luqman said to his son: O my son, the world is a deep sea, and many people have perished in it. So make your ship in it faith in Allah, make its sail reliance upon Allah, and make your provision in it taqwa of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you are saved, then it is by the mercy of Allah; and if you perish, then it is by your sins.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection, and the one who spends on them in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is like one extending his hand in charity and not withdrawing it." So when you prepare something, prepare it as one marked on the forehead, with a white mark on the muzzle, white on three legs, free on the right side, chestnut-colored, then white-blazed; you will be safe and gain spoils.

2460 - Bakr ibn Salih narrated from Sulaiman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: “Upon every nostril of a horse there is a devil. So when one of you wants to bridle it, then let him mention the Name of Allah.”

2461 - He said: And I heard him say: “Whoever keeps a noble horse, ten sins are erased from him and eleven good deeds are written for him every day. Whoever keeps a mixed-breed horse, two sins are erased from him every day and nine good deeds are written for him every day. Whoever keeps a workhorse, intending by it beauty, fulfilling a need, or repelling an enemy, one sin is erased from him every day and six good deeds are written for him. Whoever keeps a chestnut horse with a white blaze, or one marked on the forehead, then if it is bright-faced, with white on its legs, it is more beloved to me. Poverty will not enter his house so long as that horse is in it, and so long as it remains in the possession of its owner, unfairness will not enter his house.”

2462 - He said: And I heard him say: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gifted four horses from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. Then he came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have gifted you four horses.” He said, “Describe them.” He said, “They are of different colors.” He said, “Is there among them one with white markings?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Is there among them a chestnut with white markings?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then keep it for me.” And he said, “Are there among them two bay horses with white markings?” He said, “Give them to your two sons.” He said, “And the fourth is a solid black one.” He said, “Sell it and retain its price for your dependents. Indeed, the blessing of horses is in those possessing white markings.”

2463 - He said: And I heard him say: "Whoever leaves his house, or a house other than his house, at the beginning of the morning, then meets a chestnut horse with white markings, blessing is granted to him in his day. And if it has a flowing blaze, then it is prosperity, and he will encounter nothing on that day but joy, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, fulfills his need."

2464 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Horses were wild in the lands of the Arabs, and Ibrahim and Isma'il عليهما السلام ascended Abu Qubays and called out: 'Come! Come forward!' Then no horse remained except that it yielded its reins and allowed access to its forelock."

Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād narrated with his chain of transmission, saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: A riding animal has rights upon its owner: he begins by feeding it when he dismounts, offers it water when he passes by it, does not strike its face, for it glorifies its Lord with praise, does not remain standing upon its back except in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not burden it beyond its capacity, and does not compel it in walking except to what it can bear.
A man asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “When should I strike my riding animal beneath me?” He said: “When it does not walk under you as it walks toward its feeding trough.”
And it is narrated that he said: "Strike them for stumbling, but do not strike them for shying away, for they see what you do not see."

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “When the riding animal stumbles beneath the man and he says to it, ‘May you perish,’ it says: ‘Perished is the one among us who is most disobedient to the Lord.’”

2469 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: "Regarding animals: do not strike the faces, and do not curse them, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has cursed the one who curses them." And in another report: "Do not make faces ugly."
And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Indeed, when animals are cursed, the curse clings to them."
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Do not sit sideways on riding animals, and do not make their backs your seats."
And al-Baqir عليه السلام said: "Everything has a sanctity, and the sanctity of animals lies in their faces."

ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, that he used to say: "Beasts have not been left ignorant of four things: their knowledge of their Lord, Blessed and Exalted; their knowledge of death; their knowledge of the female from the male; and their knowledge of fertile pasture."
As for the report that was narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام, that he said: If the beasts knew of death what you know, you would never eat anything fat from them.

The obligations of hajj are seven: ihram; the four talbiyah phrases by which one recites privately, and they are: “Labbayka Allahumma labbayka labbayka, la sharika laka labbayka, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulka la sharika laka”; tawaf of the House; the two rak'ahs at the مقام of Ibrahim عليه السلام; the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah; standing at al-Mash'ar al-Haram; and the hady for the mutamatti'.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Standing at Arafah is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and at al-Mash'ar is an obligation, and whatever else of the rites is sunnah (prophetic tradition)."

It is narrated from Abī Dharr, may Allah have mercy upon him, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, saying: "Indeed, the animal says: O Allah, provide me with a truthful master who feeds me, gives me drink, and does not burden me with what I cannot bear."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "No one purchases an animal except that it says: 'O Allah, make him merciful to me.'"
2479 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from him that he said: "Acquire a mount, for it is an adornment, needs are fulfilled through it, and its sustenance is upon Allah, the Mighty and Glorious."

2480 - Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission; he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves gentleness and aids in it. So when you ride lean animals, let them stop at their stopping-places. If the land is barren, then hasten on them; and if it is fertile, then let them stop at their stopping-places.
And Ali, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever among you travels with a riding animal should begin, when stopping, by feeding it and giving it water."
And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: If you travel through fertile land, then be gentle in traveling; and if you travel through barren land, then hasten in traveling.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Beware of red camels, for they have the shortest lifespan among camels."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, upon the top of every camel there is a devil, so feed it well and keep it subdued."
And Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "Purchase black, unattractive camels, for they have the longest lifespans among camels."
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Camels are an honor for their owners."

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade stepping over the camel line. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, and why?" He said, "Because there is no camel line except that between one camel and the next there is a devil."

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was asked: “Which wealth is best?” He said: “A crop which its owner has sown, cultivated, and paid its due on the day of its harvest.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after crops?” He said: “A man among his sheep, having followed with them the places of rainfall, establishing salat and giving zakat.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after sheep?” He said: “Cattle; they go forth with خير and return with خير.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after cattle?” He said: “Those firmly rooted in the mud, those that provide food in drought. Excellent indeed is the date-palm. Whoever sells it, then its price is only like ashes upon the top of a lofty height.” “The wind intensified against it on a stormy day.” “Except that he replaces it in its place.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after date-palms?” So he remained silent. Then a man said to him: “Then where are camels?” He said: “In them are hardship, roughness, toil, and remoteness of abode. They go forth turning away and return turning away. Their benefit does not come except from their left side. Indeed, they are never without the wretched, the wicked.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding sheep: when they come forward, they come with blessing, and when they go away, they still come with blessing. Cattle: when they come forward, they come with blessing, and when they go away, they depart with it. Camels: when they come forward, they drive it away, and when they go away, they depart with it.

Al-Sakūnī narrated with his chain of transmission. That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم saw a she-camel tied up while its gear was still upon it, and he said: "Where is its owner? Tell him to prepare tomorrow for dispute."
And in another report, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Delay the loading, for the two forelegs are suspended and the two hind legs are bound."

Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ḥammād al-Laḥḥām, who said: A caravan passed by Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he saw a pack animal that had leaned. So he said: “O boy, adjust this load properly, for Allah, the Exalted, loves justice.”

2493 - And it is narrated from Ayyub ibn A‘yan, who said: I heard al-Walid ibn Sabih saying to Abi Abdullah عليه السلام: “Abu Hanifah saw the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah at al-Qadisiyyah and attended ‘Arafah with us.” So he said: “There is no salat (prayer) for this; there is no salat (prayer) for this.”
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام performed hajj on a she-camel of his forty times, and he never struck her with a whip.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Any camel on which hajj is performed for three years will be made among the livestock of Paradise." And it is narrated: "seven years."

2499 - Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission; he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Beware of resting upon the middle of the road and in the bottoms of the valleys, for they are the pathways of wild beasts and the shelter of snakes."

Hadith 2500 — And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever settles in a place where he fears a wild beast, and says: 'I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, alone, with no partner for Him, 'To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise,' 'in His hand is the good,' 'and He is powerful over all things,' 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every wild beast,' then he will remain safe from the harm of that wild beast until he departs from that place, if Allah, the Exalted, wills."
Munthir ibn Jayfar narrated from Yahya ibn Talhah al-Nahdi, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said to us: "Travel and slip away quietly, for it is easier for you."

And it is narrated that a group of people on foot met the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and they complained to him about the hardship of walking. So he said to them: “Seek assistance through brisk walking.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a debt: “Is hajj obligatory upon him?” He said: “Yes. Indeed, the hajj of Islam is obligatory upon whoever among the Muslims is able to walk. Most of those who performed hajj with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were walking. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed by Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, and they complained to him of strain, exertion, and fatigue. So he said, ‘Tighten your waist-wraps and bind your stomachs.’ They did that, and that went away from them.”

And Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find thereto a way.' He said: 'He sets out walking if he has nothing.' I said: 'If he cannot walk?' He said: 'He walks and rides.' I said: 'If he cannot do that?' He said: 'He serves the people and sets out with them.'

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If you lose your way, then call out: 'O Ṣāliḥ, or O Abā Ṣāliḥ, guide us to the path; may Allah have mercy upon you.'"
And it is narrated: "The wilderness is entrusted to Salih, and the sea is entrusted to Hamza."

Chapter on the causes and reasons of hajj. The Shaykh, the author of this book—may Allah have mercy on him—said: I have compiled the chains of transmission for the causes which I am going to mention from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and from the Imams عليهم السلام in my book Jāmiʿ ʿIlal al-Ḥajj.
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The Ka'bah was named Ka'bah because it is the center of the world."

And it has been narrated: that "The Ka'bah was only named Ka'bah because it is square. It became square because it is aligned with al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, and it is square. And al-Bayt al-Ma'mur became square because it is aligned with the Throne, and it is square. And the Throne became square because the words upon which Islam was built are four, and they are: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar."
The Sacred House of Allah was so named because it was made forbidden for the polytheists to enter it.
The House was named al-Bayt al-‘Atiq because it was saved from drowning.
And it is narrated: "It was named al-ʿAtīq because it is a house set free from people, and no one has ever owned it."

And the House was placed in the middle of the earth because it is the place from beneath which the earth was spread out, and so that the obligation would be equal in that for the people of the East and the West.
Al-Hatim was named al-Hatim because the people crush one another there.

The station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام came to be on its left because Ibrāhīm عليه السلام has a station on the Day of Resurrection, and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله has a station. So the station of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is on the right of the Throne of our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and the station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام is on the left of His Throne. Thus, the station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام is in accordance with his station on the Day of Resurrection, while the Throne of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, faces forward, not turned away. And the Syrian Corner came to be moving in winter and summer, and by night and day, because the wind is confined beneath it. And the House only came to be elevated, with ascent to it by steps, because when al-Ḥajjāj demolished the Kaʿbah, the people dispersed its soil. Then when they wanted to build it, a serpent came out against them and prevented the people from building. So al-Ḥajjāj was approached and informed, and al-Ḥajjāj asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام about that, and he said to him: ‘Order the people that no one among them who took anything from it should remain except that he returns it.’ Then when its walls were raised, he ordered the soil, and it was cast into its interior. For that reason the House came to be elevated, with ascent to it by steps. And the people came to circumambulate around the Ḥijr and not circumambulate within it because the mother of Ismāʿīl was buried in the Ḥijr, and her grave is there. So circumambulation was made in that manner so that her grave would not be trodden upon.
And it has been narrated: That within it are the graves of the Prophets, peace be upon them.
And it was named Bakkah because the people press against one another there with their hands.
And it is narrated: "It was named Bakkah because of the weeping of the people around it and within it."
And it is narrated: "It is announced at al-Ḥijr: Lo, whoever has had his provisions cut off, let him come forward, and it shall be given to him."
Indeed, Quraysh demolished the Kaaba because the flood used to come to them from the upper part of Mecca, then enter it, so it cracked.

2121 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious: "...wherein the resident and the visitor are equal..." He said: "It was not proper for doors to be made on the houses of Makkah, because the pilgrims had the right to stay with them in their houses, in the courtyard of the house, until they completed their rites. Indeed, the first one who made doors for the houses of Makkah was Mu'awiyah."
The mosque was made sacred because of the Ka'bah, the sanctuary was made sacred because of the mosque, and ihram became obligatory because of the sanctuary.

2124 - And in the narration of Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān al-Dārimī, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar, he said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the talbiyah and its reason, so he said: "Indeed, when the people enter iḥrām, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls out to them and says: "My male servants and female servants, I shall surely make you forbidden to the Fire just as you entered iḥrām for Me." So their saying, "Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk," is a response to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His call to them.

The Day of Tarwiyah was only named thus because there was no water at Arafat, and they used to draw water from Makkah for their quenching. Some of them would say to others, “Have you provided yourselves with water? Have you provided yourselves with water?” So it was called the Day of Tarwiyah for that reason.
Mina was named Mina because Jibril عليه السلام came to Ibrahim عليه السلام and said to him, “Wish, O Ibrahim.” It used to be called Munā, then the people named it Mina.
And it has been narrated: "It was named Minā because Ibrāhīm عليه السلام wished there that Allah would place, in place of his son, a ram that He would command him to slaughter as a ransom for him."
It was named al-Khayf because it is elevated above the valley, and everything that rises above the valley is called khayf.

The standing was appointed at al-Mashʿar and not within the Haram because the Kaʿbah is the House of Allah, the Haram is its veil, and al-Mashʿar is its door. When the visitors sought to approach it, He made them stand at the door, supplicating until He permitted them to enter. Then He made them stand at the second veil, which is Muzdalifah. When He saw the length of their supplication, He commanded them to draw near with their قربان. Then when they had offered, completed their untidiness-removal rites, and purified themselves from the sins that had been a veil for them before Him, He commanded them to visit in a state of purity.
And it has been narrated: “These are days of eating, drinking, and marital relations.”
Sitting with one’s knees drawn up in al-Masjid al-Haram is only disliked out of reverence for the Ka'bah.
It was only called al-Hajj al-Akbar because it was a year in which the Muslims and the polytheists performed hajj, and the polytheists did not perform hajj after that year.

The takbir came to be in Mina after fifteen prayers, and in the towns after ten prayers, because when the people depart in the first departure, the people of the towns stop the takbir, while the people of Mina continue saying takbir as long as they remain in Mina until the final departure.

Al-Abtah was named Abtah because Adam عليه السلام was commanded to lie prostrate in the flat expanse of Jamʿ, so he lay there until dawn broke. Adam عليه السلام was only commanded to make confession so that it would become a sunnah (prophetic tradition) among his descendants. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله permitted al-ʿAbbās to stay overnight in Makkah during the nights of Minā for the sake of providing water to the pilgrims. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله only entered ihram from al-Shajarah because when he was taken by night to the heaven, he was at the place aligned with the tree, and it was called out: 'O Muhammad.' He said: 'Labbayk.' He said: 'Did I not find you an orphan and give shelter, and find you astray and guide?' So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Praise, blessing, and sovereignty belong to You; there is no partner for You.' Therefore he entered ihram from al-Shajarah instead of all other places. As for garlanding the sacrificial camels, it is so that it may be known that it is a sacrificial animal, and its owner may recognize it by the sandal with which he garlands it. Ishʿār was only commanded so that its back would become forbidden to its owner from the point where he marked it, and so that Shaytan would not be able to mount it.

The command for ramy al-jamarat was only given because Iblis, the accursed, used to appear to Ibrahim عليه السلام at the place of the jamarat, and Ibrahim عليه السلام would stone him; thus the sunnah came to be established by that. And it has been narrated: "The first one to throw the pebbles at the jamarat was Adam عليه السلام, then Ibrahim عليه السلام."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Allah made this sacrifice so that your needy may be filled with meat, so feed them."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: No believer dies in a land of exile, where those who would weep for him are absent, except that the regions of the earth upon which he used to worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, weep for him; his garments weep for him; the gates of heaven through which his deeds used to ascend weep for him; and the two angels entrusted with him weep for him.

It was in the will of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to ʿAlī عليه السلام: "O ʿAlī, when you intend a city or a village, then say when you behold it: O Allah, I ask You for its goodness, and I seek refuge in You from its evil. O Allah, make us beloved to its people, and make the righteous of its people beloved to us."

2511 - And he عليه السلام said: Indeed, when the stranger is approached by death, he turns to the right and to the left and sees no one. He raises his head, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “To whom are you turning? To one who is better for you than Me? By My might and My majesty, if I release you from your bond, I shall surely place you in My obedience, and if I seize you, I shall surely place you into My honor.”

It is narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade a man from entering upon his family at night when returning from a journey, until he informs them beforehand.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Travel is a portion of torment, so when one of you has completed his journey, let him hasten to return to his family."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Traveling through stages depletes provisions, worsens character, and wears out clothes; and the travel is eighteen."
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated with his chain of transmission; he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "If you lose your way, then turn to the right."

Jaʿfar ibn al-Qāsim narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, at the top of every bridge there is a devil; so when you reach it, say: 'In the Name of Allah,' and it will depart from you."

And Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said: "I guarantee for one who sets out intending a journey, wearing a turban wrapped under his chin, three things: that theft, drowning, and burning will not afflict him."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The hajj is in well-known months." Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Whoever intends hajj should let his hair grow when he sights the crescent of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and whoever intends ʿumrah should let his hair grow for a month.
And it is narrated from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about cupping and shaving the nape during the months of hajj. He said: “There is no harm, and there is no harm in using nūrah or the siwāk.”

ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Ihram begins from five appointed locations that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله established. It is not proper for a pilgrim performing hajj or ʿumrah to enter ihram before them or after them. He appointed Dhā al-Ḥulayfah for the people of al-Madīnah, and it is Masjid al-Shajarah. He used to pray there and enter into the obligation of hajj; then when he left the mosque, proceeded, and al-Baydāʾ became level with him near the first milestone, he entered ihram. And he appointed al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, al-ʿAqīq for the people of Najd, Qarn al-Manāzil for the people of al-Ṭāʾif, and Yalamlam for the people of al-Yaman. No one should turn away from the appointed places set by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

And in the narration of Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم appointed al-ʿAqīq for the people of Najd, and he said: “It is an appointed time for whatever land rises toward Najd, and you are among them.” And he appointed al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, and it is said to it: Mahyaʿah.
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "It suffices you, if you do not know al-ʿAqīq, to ask the people and the Bedouins about that."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "The beginning of al-'Aqiq is Barid al-Ba'th, and it is a postal stage before Barid Ghamrah."

2526 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله designated al-'Aqiq as the miqat for the people of Iraq. Its beginning is al-Maslakh, its middle is Ghamrah, and its end is Dhat 'Irq. Its beginning is more virtuous.
Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about a man from the people of al-Madīnah who entered into ihram from al-Juḥfah So he said: “There is no harm.”

And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “It is narrated among us in Kūfah that ʿAlī عليه السلام said: ‘Indeed, part of the completion of your hajj is your entering into ihram from the vicinity of your family’s home.’” So he said: “Glory be to Allah! If it were as they say, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would not have remained enjoying the use of his clothes until al-Shajarah.”

Maysir asked al-Sadiq عليه السلام about a man who entered ihram from al-‘Aqiq and another who entered ihram from al-Kufah: which of the two had performed the better deed? So he said: "O Maysir, is it better that you pray al-‘Asr as four, or that you pray it as six?" I said: "I pray it as four." He عليه السلام said: "Thus, the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is better than anything else."
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man whose home is beyond al-Juhfah: from where should he enter into ihram? He said: “From his home.”
And in another narration: "Whoever's dwelling is within the miqats, between them and Makkah, must assume ihram from his dwelling."

2532 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “Whoever resides in Medina while intending hajj (pilgrimage) for a month or about that, then it occurs to him to depart by a route other than the road of Medina, then when he is opposite al-Shajarah and al-Bayda', at a distance of six miles, he should enter ihram from there.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “When you reach al-‘Aqīq from the direction of Iraq, or a miqāt from these mawāqīt, while intending ihram, if Allah wills, then remove the hair from your underarms, trim your nails, apply depilatory to your pubic area, and take from your mustache. It does not harm you whichever of that you begin with. Then use the siwāk, perform ghusl, and wear your two garments. Let your completion of that, if Allah the Exalted wills, be at the sun’s decline; and if that is not at the sun’s decline, then there is no harm, except that this is more beloved to me: that it be at the sun’s decline.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while we were in al-Madīnah, about preparing for ihram. So he said: "Apply depilatory in al-Madīnah, prepare yourself with everything you need, and perform ghusl (ritual bath) if you wish. And if you wish, you may continue wearing your shirt until you come to Masjid al-Shajarah."

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār asked: About a man who removes hair before coming to the miqat by six nights, he said: “There is no harm in it.” And he asked him about a man who removes hair seven or eight nights before coming to Makkah. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was present, saying: “When I apply depilatory for the first ihram, what should I do regarding the later depilation, and what is the limit of the interval between them?” He عليه السلام said: “If there are two Fridays between them, fifteen days, then apply the depilatory again.”

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: We sent to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, while we were a group in al-Madinah, that we wished to bid you farewell. So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام sent to us: “Perform ghusl in al-Madinah, for I fear that water may become scarce for you at Dhi al-Hulayfah. So perform ghusl in al-Madinah, wear your garments in which you will enter ihram, then come, one by one and two by two.” He said: We gathered before him, and Ibn Abi Ya‘fur said to him: “What do you say regarding oiling after ghusl for ihram?” He said: “Before, after, and with it, there is no harm in it.” He said: Then he called for a bottle of bān salīkhah, in which there was nothing, and he instructed us, so we anointed ourselves from it. Then when we intended to leave, he said: “There is no blame upon you to perform ghusl if you find water when you reach Dhi al-Hulayfah.”

Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī asked him. He asked about khayrī oil and violet oil: "May I anoint myself with it when we intend to enter iḥrām?" He said: "Yes." And he asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bath) in al-Madīnah for his iḥrām, so he said: "That suffices him instead of the ghusl at Dhī al-Ḥulayfah."

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from him, peace be upon him, who said: A man may apply whatever oil he wishes, so long as there is no musk, no ambergris, no saffron, and no wars in it, before he performs ghusl for ihram. He said: “And do not perfume a garment for your ihram with incense.”

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked him about a man who anoints himself with an oil containing fragrance while intending to enter ihram. He said: “Do not anoint yourself, when you intend to enter ihram, with oil containing musk or ambergris whose scent remains in your head after you enter ihram. Anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter ihram, before the ghusl and after it; but once you have entered ihram, oil has become forbidden for you until you exit ihram.”
And Hammad narrated from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. That he saw no harm in a woman applying kohl, anointing herself with oil, and performing ghusl after all of that for ihram.
And in the narration of Jamil, that he said: "The ghusl of your day suffices for your night, and the ghusl of your night suffices for your day."
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed ghusl for his ihram and then trimmed his nails. He said: "He should wipe them with water and does not repeat the ghusl."

Because al-‘Ays ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performs ghusl for ihram in al-Madīnah, wears two garments, then sleeps before entering ihram. He said: “There is no ghusl upon him.” And whoever performs ghusl at the beginning of the night, then enters ihram at the end of the night, his ghusl suffices him.

Mansur al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “The pilgrim with us is of three types: a pilgrim performing tamattu‘, a pilgrim performing ifrad for hajj, and one driving the sacrificial animal; and the one driving it is the qarin.”

2546 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “Whoever performs tawaf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah becomes permitted [to exit iḥrām], if he wishes or dislikes it, except one who performed ʿumrah in that same year, or drove the sacrificial animal and marked it and garlanded it.”

Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah, who said: A man came to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام while he was behind the Maqām, and said: “I have combined hajj and ʿumrah.” He said to him, “Have you performed tawaf of the House?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Have you driven the hady?” He said, “No.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام took hold of his hair, then said, “You have exited iḥrām, by Allah.”
Abu Ayyub narrated from Abu 'Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, one of them combines and drives the sacrificial offering, so I leave him as a punishment for what he has done.

2549 - And it is narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man enters iḥrām for a hajj and an ʿumrah, and he begins the ʿumrah—does he perform tamattuʿ?" He said: "Yes."

Ishaq ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdullah عليه السلام: A man performs ifrad hajj, then circles the House and performs sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then it occurs to him to make it an 'umrah. So he said: "If he recited the talbiyah after he had performed the sa'i and before he trims, then there is no tamattu' for him."

2551 - And ʿAlī ibn Muyassir wrote to Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī, peace be upon him: Asking him about a man who performed ʿUmrah in the month of Ramadan and then came to the Hajj season: should he perform Hajj as ifrād, or perform tamattuʿ? Which of the two is better? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “He should perform tamattuʿ for it.”

Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "By Allah, tamattuʿ is superior, and through it the Qur'an was revealed, and the sunnah has continued upon it until the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "ʿUmrah has entered into hajj until the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Uthman al-Khazzaz asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: "Which type of hajj is best?" He said: "al-Mut'ah. And how could anything be better than it, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله says: 'If I had known at the beginning of my affair what I came to know at its end, I would have done as the people did.'"

2555 - Durust narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Hāshimī, who said: I entered with my brothers upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and we said to him: “We intend hajj, and some of us are performing it for the first time.” So he عليه السلام said: “You must observe tamattuʿ, for we do not practice taqiyyah with anyone concerning tamattuʿ by ʿumrah up to hajj, and [concerning] avoiding intoxicants and wiping over the khuffayn.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: There is no ihram except after a prescribed prayer or a recommended prayer. If it is a prescribed prayer, you enter ihram after it, after the taslim. If it is a recommended prayer, you pray two rakʿahs and enter ihram after it. Then when you finish the prayer, praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and say: O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who respond to You, believe in Your promise, and follow Your command. For I am Your servant and in Your grasp; I am not protected except by what You protect, and I take nothing except what You give. You have mentioned hajj, so I ask You to determine it for me according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, strengthen me in what I am weak concerning, receive my rites from me in ease and well-being from You, and make me among Your delegation whom You have been pleased with, chosen, named, and written down. O Allah, I have come out from a distant land and spent my wealth seeking Your pleasure. O Allah, complete my hajj for me. O Allah, I intend tamattuʿ. with ʿumrah until hajj according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family. If some obstacle arises for me and restrains me, then release me where You have restrained me, by Your decree which You have decreed upon me. O Allah, if it is not a hajj, then an ʿumrah. My hair, skin, flesh, blood, bones, marrow, and nerves enter ihram for You, from women, clothes, and perfume, seeking thereby Your Face and the Hereafter. It suffices you to say this once when you enter ihram. Then stand and walk a little, and when the ground becomes level with you, whether you are walking or riding, then recite the talbiyah.

2559 - Al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله enter iḥrām at night or during the day?” So he said: “During the day.” I said: “At what time?” He said: “At the time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer).” Then I asked him: “When do you think we should enter iḥrām?” He said: “It is the same for you. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered iḥrām at the time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer) only because water was scarce; it used to be found on the tops of the mountains. A man would go out early toward such a place the next day, and they would hardly be able to obtain water. These waters have only recently come into existence.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I wish to perform tamattuʿ with ʿumrah up to hajj, so how should I say it?” He عليه السلام said: “You say: O Allah, I intend tamattuʿ with ʿumrah up to hajj, upon Your Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet. And if you wish, you may keep within yourself what you intend.”

Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan asked him about a man who says: "Release me where You have restrained me." He said: "He is released where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has restrained him, whether he said it or did not say it."

Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and al-Ḥalabī all narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When you perform salat in Masjid al-Shajarah, then say—while you are seated at the end of the salat, before you stand—the words that the muhrim says. Then stand and walk until you reach the mile marker and al-Baydā’ levels out with you. Then when al-Baydā’ has leveled out with you, recite the talbiyah.

2563 - And in the narration of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: "If you enter into ihram from Ghamrah or Barid al-Ba'th, you should pray and say what the muhrim says after your prayer. And if you wish, you may recite the talbiyah from your place, but what is more virtuous is that you walk a little and then recite the talbiyah."

And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. Regarding a man who comes to Dhā al-Ḥulayfah or some of the mawāqīt after salat al-ʿaṣr or at a time other than the time of salat. He said: “He does not wait until the hour in which salat is performed. He only said that out of fear of notoriety.”

And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding one who entered ihram in Masjid al-Shajarah, then had intercourse with his spouse before reciting the talbiyah, he said: “There is nothing upon him.”

And in the narration of Abān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام performed ghusl at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah for ihram, and prayed. Then he said, 'Bring what you have of the meat of game.' So two partridges were brought to him, and he ate them before entering ihram.

And in the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from him, peace be upon him: That he prayed two rakʿahs and entered iḥrām at Masjid al-Shajarah. Then he went out, and khabīṣ containing saffron was brought to him, and he ate from it before reciting the talbiyah.

Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih narrated from him: Regarding a man who had with him an umm walad of his, and she entered ihram before her master: is it permissible for him to nullify her ihram and have intercourse with her before he himself enters ihram? He said: "Yes."

One of our companions wrote to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Regarding a man who entered Masjid al-Shajarah, performed salat (prayer), and entered ihram. Then he left the mosque, and before reciting the talbiyah, it occurred to him: may he undo that by having intercourse with women? So he عليه السلام wrote: "Yes," or, "There is no harm in it."

2570 - ʿAmr ibn Shumr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “They only deemed the marking of the sacrificial camels commendable because with the first drop that falls from its blood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives him for that.”

And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: People used to garland the sheep and cattle, and the people only abandoned it recently, and they would garland them with a string or a leather strap.

And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who drove a sacrificial animal and did not garland it, nor mark it. He عليه السلام said: "It has sufficed for him; very often it is neither garlanded, nor marked, nor covered."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man entered ihram from the appointed place and proceeded on his way. Then, a day or two later, he purchased a sacrificial camel, marked it, garlanded it, and drove it along. So he said: “If he bought it before entering the Haram, there is no harm.” I said: Then if he bought it before reaching the miqat from which he enters ihram, then marked it and garlanded it, does that make obligatory upon him what is obligatory upon the muhrim at that point? He said: “No. But when he reaches the miqat, then let him enter ihram, then mark it and garland it, for his first garlanding is of no consequence.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the budn, how they are marked. He said: “They are marked while kneeling, by slitting the right side of their hump, and they are slaughtered while standing, from the right side.”

2575 - And in the narration of Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār, from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "You garland it with an old sandal in which you have prayed, and al-ish'ār and al-taqlīd are in the position of the talbiyah."
And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from him, peace be upon him: "It is marked (Ishʿār) while it is restrained."

Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I set out for an ʿUmrah and purchased a sacrificial camel while I was in al-Madīnah. So I sent to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him how I should deal with it. He sent back to me: “What were you going to do with this? It would have sufficed you to buy one there from ʿArafah.” And he said: “Go until you come to Masjid al-Shajarah, then face it toward the qiblah and make it kneel. Then enter the mosque and pray two rakʿahs. Then come out to it and mark it on the right side, then say: ‘In the Name of Allah. O Allah, from You and for You. O Allah, accept from me.’ Then when you ascend al-Baydāʾ, recite the talbiyah.”

Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم recited the talbiyah, he said: ‘Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, indeed all praise and blessing are Yours, and the kingdom; there is no partner for You, labbayk. Labbayka, O Possessor of the Ascents, labbayk.’ And he عليه السلام would frequently repeat ‘Dhī al-Maʿārij,’ and he would recite the talbiyah whenever he met a rider, ascended a hill, descended into a valley, in the latter part of the night, and after the prayers.

And in a narration of Ḥarīz: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered into ihram, Jibrīl عليه السلام came to him and said: “Command your companions to perform al-ʿajj and al-thajj. Al-ʿajj is raising the voice in the talbiyah, and al-thajj is the slaughtering of the sacrificial camels.”

Abu Saʿid al-Mukārī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has exempted women from four things: raising the voice in the talbiyah, the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah—meaning brisk walking—entering the Kaʿbah, and touching the Black Stone.
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "There is no harm in reciting the Talbiyah while you are not in a state of taharah (ritual purity), and in any condition."
Jābir narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: “There is no harm in the junub reciting the Talbiyah.”
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "It is disliked for a man to respond with the Talbiyah when he is called while he is in ihram."
And in another report: "If the muhrim is called, he should not say, 'Labbayk,' but rather say, 'Ya Sa'd.'"

2585 - Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام said: “Jibra'il عليه السلام came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said to him: Indeed, the talbiyah is the slogan of the muhrim, so raise your voice with the talbiyah: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika laka labbayk.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim al-Astarābādī narrated to me from Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad ibn Ziyād and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Yasār, from their fathers, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Mūsā ibn ʿImrān and chose him as one spoken to intimately, parted the sea for him, saved the Children of Israel, and gave him the Tawrah and the Tablets, he saw his rank before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ‘My Lord, You have honored me with an honor by which You have not honored anyone before me.’ Allah, Majestic is His Glory, said: ‘O Mūsā, do you not know that Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is more virtuous in My sight than all My angels and all My creation?’ Mūsā said: ‘My Lord, if Muḥammad is more honored in Your sight than all Your creation, then is there among the families of the Prophets anyone more honored than my family?’ Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘O Mūsā, do you not know that the excellence of the family of Muḥammad over all the families of the Prophets is like the excellence of Muḥammad over all the messengers?’ He said: ‘My Lord, if the family of Muḥammad is like that, then is there among the communities of the Prophets any community more virtuous in Your sight than my community?’ You shaded them ‘with the clouds,’ and sent down upon them ‘the manna and the quails,’ and parted the sea for them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘O Mūsā, do you not know that the excellence of the Ummah of Muḥammad over all communities is like his excellence over all My creation?’ Mūsā عليه السلام said: ‘My Lord, I wish that I could see them.’ Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: ‘O Mūsā, you will never see them, for this is not the time of their appearance. But you shall see them in the gardens, the Gardens of ʿAdn and al-Firdaws, in the presence of Muḥammad, turning about in their bliss and delighting in their good things. Would you like Me to let you hear their speech?’ He said: ‘Yes, my God.’ Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘Stand before Me and tighten your waist-wrapper, standing as a lowly servant stands before the majestic King.’ So Mūsā عليه السلام did that, and our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, called

Muḥammad ibn Muslim and al-Ḥalabī both narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Hajj is in well-known months; so whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, then there shall be no obscenity, no sin, and no disputation in the Hajj." He عليه السلام said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated a condition upon the people and stipulated for them a condition. So whoever fulfills for Him, Allah fulfills for him." They both said to him, "What is that which He stipulated upon them, and what is that which He stipulated for them?" He said, "As for that which He stipulated upon them, it is His saying: 'Hajj is in well-known months; so whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, then there shall be no obscenity, no sin, and no disputation in the Hajj.' And as for what He stipulated for them, it is His saying: 'So whoever hastens in two days, then there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, then there is no sin upon him, for the one who is Godwary.'" He said: "He returns and there is no sin for him." They both said to him, "What do you say about one who is afflicted with sinfulness—what is upon him?" He عليه السلام said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not assigned for him a fixed penalty; he seeks forgiveness from Allah and recites the talbiyah." They both said to him, "Then one who is afflicted with disputation—what is upon him?" He عليه السلام said: "If he disputes more than two times, then upon the one who is correct is blood-sacrifice that he pours forth: a sheep; and upon the one who is mistaken is a cow."

2588 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "If you have intercourse with your spouse after binding the ihram but before reciting the talbiyah, then there is nothing upon you. If you have intercourse while you are in ihram before standing at al-Mash'ar, then a camel is upon you, and the hajj must be performed again the following year. If you have intercourse after your standing at al-Mash'ar, then a camel is upon you, but the hajj of the following year is not upon you. And if you were forgetful, inattentive, or ignorant, then there is nothing upon you."

Abu Basir asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was in the state of ihram. He said: peace be upon him: “Upon him is a large camel (jazur kawmā’).” He said, “He cannot afford it.” He, peace be upon him, said: “It is fitting for his companions to gather for him, and they should not spoil his hajj for him.”

Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man in ihram who looked at a woman's leg or her private part and ejaculated, so he said: "If he is wealthy, then a camel is incumbent upon him; if he is of moderate means, then a cow is incumbent upon him; and if he is poor, then a sheep is incumbent upon him." And he said: "I did not impose this upon him because he ejaculated, but rather I imposed it upon him because he looked at what was not halal for him."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked him about a man who carries his wife or touches her, and then ejaculates or emits pre-seminal fluid, so he said: "If he carries her or touches her with desire, then whether he ejaculates, does not ejaculate, emits pre-seminal fluid, or does not emit pre-seminal fluid, a sheep's blood is upon him, which he must spill. And if he carries her or touches her without desire, then there is nothing upon him, whether he ejaculates, does not ejaculate, emits pre-seminal fluid, or does not emit pre-seminal fluid."

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muhrim who intends to do an act, and his companions say to him, “By Allah, do not do it,” and he says, “By Allah, I will surely do it,” and they exchange oaths repeatedly. Does there become binding upon him what is binding upon the one guilty of disputation? He عليه السلام said: “No. He only intended by this to honor his brother. What only becomes binding upon him is that which was disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

2593 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Beware of boasting, and hold fast to a scrupulous piety that restrains you from acts of disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Then let them complete their prescribed duties." And among the tafath is that you speak foul words during your ihram; so when you enter Makkah and perform tawaf around the House, you speak good words. And that would be an atonement for that."

Jamil narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, regarding: Regarding a muhrim who killed an ostrich, he عليه السلام said: “A camel is due upon him. If he cannot find one, then feeding sixty needy persons. If the value of the camel is greater than feeding sixty needy persons, he should not add beyond feeding sixty needy persons. And if the value of the camel is less than feeding sixty needy persons, then only the value of the camel is due upon him.”

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man upon whom a camel is obligatory as expiation, he said: 'If he cannot find [a camel], then seven sheep. If he cannot afford that, he should fast for eighteen days, either in Mecca or at his place of residence.'

2725 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muhrim who struck an ostrich or a wild donkey. He said, “A camel is due upon him.” I said, “If he is not able?” He said, “He feeds sixty needy persons.” I said, “If he is not able to give in charity, what is upon him?” He said, “Then let him fast eighteen days.” I said, “If he struck a cow, what is upon him?” He said, “A cow is due upon him.” I said, “If he is not able?” He said, “Then let him feed thirty needy persons.” I said, “If he is not able to give in charity?” He said, “Then let him fast nine days.” I said, “If he struck a gazelle, what is upon him?” He said, “A sheep is due upon him.” I said, “If he does not find it?” He said, “Then feeding ten needy persons is upon him.” I said, “If he does not find what he can give in charity?” He said, “Then fasting three days is upon him.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man shot at game while he was in ihram, and broke its foreleg or hind leg, then it went off on its way and he did not know what became of it. He said: “Its expiation is upon him.” I said: Then if he sees it afterward grazing and walking? He said: “A quarter of its value is upon him.”
Al-Bazanti narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a muhrim who struck a rabbit or a fox. He said: "For the rabbit, there is the blood of a sheep."
And in the narration of Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, he said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a rabbit that is struck by a muhrim, so he said: "A sheep as an offering, reaching the Kaaba."

And in the narration of al-Bazanti, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr. He said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muhrim who killed a fox. He said: "A blood sacrifice is upon him." I said: "What about a rabbit?" He said: "The same as what is for the fox."

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated, saying: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Ḥaram while he was in iḥrām, and he said: "If he killed it while he was in iḥrām in the Ḥaram, then a sheep is due from him, and the value of the pigeon is one dirham. If he killed it in the Ḥaram while he was not in iḥrām, then its value is due from him, which is one dirham, which he gives in charity or with which he buys food for the pigeons of the Ḥaram. And if he killed it while he was in iḥrām outside the Ḥaram, then the blood-sacrifice of a sheep is due from him."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Whatever you step on, or your camel steps on, while you are in ihram, then its expiation is upon you."

Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام passed by some people while they were eating locusts, and he said: "Glory be to Allah, while you are in the state of ihram?" They said, "It is only from the sea." He said, "Then dip it in the water, then."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about a muhrim who strikes game and then offers its expiation: should he eat it or discard it? He said: "Then another expiation would be upon him." It was said: "Then what should he do with it?" He said: "He should bury it."
That Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thānī, peace be upon him, said: "Slaughtering the game, eating it, and paying the expiation is more beloved to me than carrion."

Yūsuf al-Ṭāṭarī narrated, saying: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Game that was eaten by a group of people in ihram." He عليه السلام said: "Upon each of them is one sheep, and upon the one who slaughtered it there is only one sheep."

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a group of pilgrims in ihram who struck ostrich chicks and all ate of them, he said: “For them, in place of every chick that they ate, is a camel, in which they all share together. So they purchase it according to the number of the chicks and according to the number of the men.”

Zurārah and Bukayr narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Regarding two people in the state of ihram who struck game, he, peace be upon him, said: “Upon each one of them is the expiation.”

Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a group of people in the state of ihram who purchased game and shared it among themselves. A woman who was their companion said, 'Give me a portion of it for one dirham,' and they did so. He said: 'Upon each of them is a sheep.'

2739 - And he said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, as provision for you and for the travelers.” Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “It is its salted food which you eat.” And he said: “The distinction between the two is that every bird that is in the reed-beds, lays eggs on land, and hatches on land, then it is land game. And whatever bird is on land, but lays eggs in the sea and hatches in the sea, then it is from sea game.”
A person in the state of ihram must not guide others to game. If he does guide someone to it and it is killed, then the expiation is upon him.

2741 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “When you have completed your saʿy and you are a mutamattiʿ, then trim from the hair of your head, from its sides, and your beard, and take from your mustache, and clip your nails, while leaving some of them for your hajj. Then when you have done that, you have come out of iḥrām from everything from which the muḥrim becomes released. So perform tawaf of the House voluntarily as much as you wish.”

2742 - And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man performs tamattuʿ, then forgets to trim until he enters into iḥrām for hajj. So he said: “He must offer a sacrifice.” And in the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “He should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.”

Imran al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed tawaf of the House and the sa'i between Safa and Marwa while having performed tamattu', then hastened and kissed his wife before trimming his hair. He (the Imam) said: 'Upon him is a dam (sheep) which he must slaughter, and if he had intercourse, then upon him is a juzur (camel) or a cow.'

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about a man who bound up his hair while he was performing tamattuʿ, then came to Makkah, completed his rites, untied the braids of his head, trimmed, applied oil, and deemed himself released from ihram. He عليه السلام said: “He must offer the blood-sacrifice of a sheep.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked him about a man performing tamattuʿ who had intercourse with his wife and had not yet trimmed his hair; he said: "He must slaughter a camel, and I have feared that his hajj may have been impaired if he was knowledgeable; but if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him." He said: And I said to him, about a person performing tamattuʿ who clipped some of his nails with his teeth and took some of his hair with a sharp tool. So he said: "There is no harm in it; not everyone finds scissors."

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a person performing tamattu‘ who intended to trim the hair but shaved his head. He said: “He must offer a blood-sacrifice that he spills, and when it is the Day of Sacrifice, he should pass the razor over his head when he intends to shave.”

Abu al-Maghra' narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man exited his ihram, while his wife had not yet exited hers, and he had intercourse with her. He عليه السلام said: "She must offer a camel, and her husband must bear its cost."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: It is appropriate for the mutamattiʿ performing tamattuʿ with ʿumrah leading to hajj, when he exits ihram, not to wear a shirt and to resemble those who are in ihram.
And Ḥafṣ, Jamīl, and others narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a person in ihram who trims from some [of the hair] and does not trim from some, he said: “It suffices him.”

Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked him about a mutamatti‘ who shaved his head in Makkah, so he said: "If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him. If he did that intentionally during the first thirty days of the months of hajj, then there is nothing upon him. But if he did that intentionally after the thirty days in which the hair is left to grow for hajj, then a blood sacrifice is upon him which he must spill."

And it is narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: A man said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “May I be your ransom, when I completed my rites for the ʿUmrah, I went to my wife while I had not trimmed my hair.” He عليه السلام said: “A camel is upon you.” He said, “When I intended that from her, while she had not trimmed her hair either, she resisted; then when I overpowered her, she cut off some of her hair with her teeth.” He عليه السلام said: “May Allah have mercy on her. She was more understanding than you. A camel is upon you, and there is nothing upon her.”

2752 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: If a person performing tamattu‘ wishes to leave Makkah for some other places, that is not permitted for him, because he is bound to the hajj until he completes it, unless he knows that the hajj will not escape him. So if he knows, and leaves, and returns in the month in which he left, he enters Makkah in a state of being non-muhrim; but if he enters it in a month other than that month, he enters it in a state of ihram.
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Can a man enter Makkah without iḥrām? He said: “No, except one who is ill or one who has a stomach ailment.”

2754 - Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who enters Makkah once, twice, or three times in a year. What should he do?
