He said: “When he enters, then let him enter reciting the talbiyah, and when he leaves, then let him leave having exited iḥrām.”

2755 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr at al-Baydāʾ, with four days remaining of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, during the Farewell Pilgrimage. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her, and she performed ghusl, bound herself with a cloth, entered ihram, and recited the talbiyah along with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his companions. When they arrived in Makkah, she did not become pure until they departed from Minā, though she had attended all the ritual stations: ʿArafāt, Jamʿ, and she stoned the jamarāt; but she did not perform tawaf of the House, nor saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Then when they departed from Minā, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her, so she performed ghusl and performed tawaf of the House and of al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Her waiting lasted through four remaining days of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and three days of al-Tashrīq.”

And it is narrated from Durust, from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman performing tamattuʿ who entered Makkah and then menstruated. He said: “She performs saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then goes out with the people until she completes her tawaf afterward.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār asked him: About a woman who performed sa‘i between al-Safā and al-Marwah, then menstruated during it, so he said: “She should complete her sa‘i.” And he asked him about a woman who performed tawaf of the House, then menstruated before doing sa‘i. He said: “She should perform sa‘i.”

And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the two of them, peace be upon them; he said: I asked him about a woman in iḥrām when she becomes pure: may she wash her head with al-khiṭmī? He said: "Water suffices for her."

Jamil narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: Regarding a menstruating woman who arrives in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, she proceeds as she is to Arafat and makes it a hajj. Then she remains until she becomes pure, then she goes out to al-Tan'im, enters ihram, and makes it an 'umrah.

And Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a woman who comes performing tamattu‘, then menstruates before she performs tawaf of the House, until she goes out to Arafat. He said: "It becomes a separate hajj (hajj ifrad), and she must offer the blood of her sacrifice."

And Ṣafwān narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who had a woman with him, and she arrived in Makkah while she was not praying. She did not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, then she became pure and performed tawaf of the House, but she did not perform saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until she departed to ʿArafāt. Should she count that tawaf, or repeat it before al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah? He عليه السلام said: "She counts that first tawaf and builds upon it."

Aban narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked him about a woman who performed tawaf around the House, then menstruated before praying the two rakʿahs. He said: “When she becomes pure, only the two rakʿahs are upon her, and she has already completed the tawaf.”

And Abān narrated from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a woman performs Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ and completes more than half of it, then she menstruates, she may depart if she wishes.

Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a young woman who had not previously menstruated, who went out with her husband and family. She began menstruating but was too shy to inform her family or husband, so she completed the rituals in that state. Her husband had intercourse with her, and they returned to Kufa. She then told her family what had happened. He said: 'She must offer a camel as expiation and repeat the Hajj in the following year, but there is no penalty upon her husband.'

2765 - Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from al-Kāhilī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about women in their ihram, and he said: They may put in order whatever they wish to put in order. When they arrive at al-Shajarah, they enter ihram for hajj and recite the talbiyah at the milestone at the beginning of al-Baydāʾ. Then they are taken to Makkah, and they are hastened to the tawaf and the saʿy. When they complete their tawaf and saʿy, they trim [their hair], and mutʿah becomes valid. Then they enter ihram on the Day of al-Tarwiyah for hajj, and it is an ʿumrah and a hajj. If they fall ill, they remain upon their hajj and do not make their hajj separate.

Ibn Muskan narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq, from someone who asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a woman who performed four circuits while she was performing ʿUmrah, then she menstruated. He said: "She should complete her tawaf, and nothing else is due from her. Her tamattuʿ is complete, and she may perform saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah because she has gone beyond half, and she has completed her tamattuʿ. So let her recommence after Hajj. But if she had not performed except three circuits, then let her recommence after Hajj. If her camel-driver remains with her after Hajj, then let her go out to al-Jiʿrānah or to al-Tanʿīm and perform ʿUmrah."

And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who performed three circuits of tawaf or less than that, then saw blood. He said: “She should preserve her place, and when she becomes pure, she should perform tawaf from there and count what has already passed.” And al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام: Its like.

Zurārah ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a person in ihram in the Haram strikes a pigeon or anything up to the size of a gazelle, then a damm is due from him which he sheds, and he also gives in charity the equivalent of its price. But if he strikes any of that while he is halal, then he must give in charity the equivalent of its price.

Sulayman ibn Khalid asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: About a man who closed his door on a bird and it died, so he عليه السلام said: "If he closed the door on it after entering iḥrām, then a sacrificial blood-offering is upon him; and if he closed it before entering iḥrām while he was in a halal state, then its price is upon him."

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who closed the door of a house upon a bird from the pigeons of the Haram, and it died, he عليه السلام said: "He should give a dirham in charity, or feed with it the pigeons of the Haram."

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram while he was in the Haram and not in the state of ihram. He said: "Its value is due from him, and it is one dirham, which he gives in charity or uses to buy food for the pigeons of the Haram. But if he killed it while he was muḥrim in the Haram, then a sheep is due from him, along with the value of the pigeon."

And Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding one who catches a bird in the Haram, he said: "If it is sound of wing, then let it go. And if it is not sound of wing, he should tend to it, feed it, and give it water; then when its two wings become restored, he should release it."

2355 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who enters into ihram while he has game in his household, whether wild animals or birds. He said: “There is no harm.”

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Khallād, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who slaughtered a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram, He said: "Expiation is upon him." He said: I said, "May he eat it?" He said: "No." I said, "Then may he throw it away?" He said: "Then another expiation would be upon him." He said: I said, "Then what should he do with it?" He said: "He should bury it."

2357 - Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I sent to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that a brother of mine bought pigeons in al-Madīnah, and we took them with us to Makkah, performed ʿumrah, remained until hajj, then brought the pigeons out with us from Makkah to al-Kūfah. Is there anything due upon us in that? So he said to the messenger: “I think they were wild. Tell him to slaughter one sheep in place of each bird.”

2358 - Safwan narrated from Al-‘Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about purchasing doves in Mecca and Medina. He said: “I do not like that anything be taken out from them.”

And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah that al-Ḥakam asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man to whom, in the Haram, a pigeon with clipped wings had been gifted. He عليه السلام said: “Pluck its feathers, feed it well, and when its feathers have grown back evenly, let it go.”

And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man to whom domestic pigeons were gifted and brought while he was in the Ḥaram and not in iḥrām. He said: “If he takes any of it, then he should give charity in its place, approximately equivalent to its price.”

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who shot game in the Ḥill while heading toward the Haram, in the area between the post station and the mosque. He struck it in the Ḥill, then it continued from that shot until it entered the Haram and died from his shot. Is there a penalty upon him? He عليه السلام said: "There is no penalty upon him. The likeness of that is only like one who sets a trap in the Ḥill beside the Haram, then game falls into it and struggles until it enters the Haram and dies. Then its penalty is not upon him, because he set it where he set it while that was halal for him, and he shot where he shot while that was halal for him; so there is nothing upon him regarding what occurred after that." I said: "This is qiyas according to the people." He عليه السلام said: "I only compared one thing to another for you so that you may recognize it."

Al-Muthannā narrated from Karīb al-Ṣayrafī, who said: We were together, and we bought a bird, clipped its feathers, and entered Makkah with it. The people of Makkah disapproved of that, so Karīb sent to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him. He said: "Entrust it to a Muslim man from the people of Makkah, or to a Muslim woman, and when it becomes restored, then let it go free."

Ibn Muskan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “A man plucked a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram.” He عليه السلام said: “He should give charity to a needy person, and give with the hand by which he plucked, for he has indeed caused it pain.”

And Safwān narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Makkah, and our family ate it.” So he said: “The people of Makkah do not regard any harm in it.” I said: “Then what do you say, you?” He said: “Its price is upon them.”
And Safwan narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Game is not to be slaughtered in the Haram, even if it was hunted in the Hil."

2366 - Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Regarding the pigeons of Makkah: the domesticated bird is from the pigeons of the Haram. Whoever slaughters a bird from them, then he must give in charity something better than its price; and if he was in ihram, then one sheep is due for each bird.

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a domesticated bird that came and entered the Haram, and he said: "It is not to be taken nor touched, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, about a gazelle entering the Haram, and he said: "It is not to be taken, nor touched, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"

Ibn Maskān narrated from Yazīd ibn Khalīfah, who said: There was a basket beside my house in which there were two eggs from the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary. My servant went and overturned the basket, not knowing that there were two eggs in it, and he broke them. So I went out and met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan, and I mentioned that to him. He said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of flour.' He said: Then afterward I met Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and informed him, so he عليه السلام said to me: 'He is liable for the price of two birds, with which he feeds the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary.' Then I met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan and informed him, so he said: 'He has spoken the truth; act upon it, for he took it from his forefathers عليهم السلام.'

And it is narrated from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih that he said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I take suḥūr with chicks that are brought from outside Makkah, then slaughtered in the Sanctuary, and I take suḥūr with them.” So he عليه السلام said: “What an evil suḥūr your suḥūr is! Did you not know that whatever you brought into the Sanctuary alive has become forbidden for you to slaughter and to keep?”

Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: I was with ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them both, in the Sanctuary, and he saw me harming the swallows. So he said: O my son, do not kill them and do not harm them, for they do not harm anything.

It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about two young feathered birds that I slaughtered while I was in Mecca. He said to me, “Why did you slaughter them?” I said: “A servant-girl from the people of Mecca brought them to me and asked me to slaughter them, and I thought that I was in Kufa and did not remember the Haram.” He said, “Give charity equal to their value.” I said, “How much?” He said, “One dirham, and it is better than them.”
Zurārah asked him: About a man who took a bird out from Makkah to al-Kūfah, so he said: "He must return it to Makkah."

Al-Muthannā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ḥakam, who said: I said to a servant of ours, “Prepare our meal for us.” So he took for us some of the birds of Mecca, slaughtered them, and cooked them. Then I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “Bury them, and offer fidyah for each bird among them.”

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who killed a bird from the birds of the Haram while he was in a state of ihram in the Haram So he said: “He must offer a sheep, and the value of the bird is one dirham, with which he feeds the pigeons of the Haram. And if it was a chick, then upon him is a lamb, and the value of the chick is half a dirham, with which he feeds the pigeons of the Haram.”

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Do not purchase in the Haram except that which has been slaughtered in the Hill, then brought to the Haram already slaughtered; then there is no problem with it for one who is halal (not in ihram)."
Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'raj asked Abū 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام: About an ostrich egg that I ate in the Haram, so he said: “Give in charity its price.”
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated; he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “For the value of the pigeon, one dirham; for the chick, half a dirham; and for the egg, a quarter of a dirham.”

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, Murazim, and Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man performing tamattu‘ who enters on the night of Arafah, then performs tawaf and sa‘i, then enters ihram and comes to Mina, he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Maymun, who said: Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him, arrived performing tamattu‘ on the night of ‘Arafah. He performed tawaf, exited ihram, approached one of his servant women, then entered ihram for hajj and went out.

And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A woman comes performing tamattuʿ, then menstruates before she performs tawaf of the House, and her becoming pure is on the night of ʿArafah.” So he عليه السلام said: “If she knows that she will become pure, perform tawaf of the House, come out of her ihram, and join the people at Minā, then let her do so.”

Al-Naḍr narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, who said: I and Ḥadīd set out until we reached the orchard on the Day of Tarwiyah. I went ahead on a donkey, arrived in Makkah, performed tawaf and saʿy, exited from my tamattuʿ, then entered ihram for hajj. Ḥadīd arrived during the night, so I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, seeking his ruling regarding his case. So he wrote to me: “Tell him to perform tawaf and saʿy, exit from his mutʿah, enter ihram for hajj, join the people at Minā, and he must not spend the night in Makkah.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who set out performing tamattuʿ with ʿumrah toward hajj, but did not reach Makkah until the Day of Sacrifice, so he said: He remains in Makkah in his state of ihram, stops the talbiyah when he enters the Haram, then performs tawaf of the House, performs saʿy, shaves his head, slaughters his sheep, and then returns to his family. Then he said: This is for the one who made a condition with his Lord at the time of his ihram that He would release him wherever he was prevented. But if he did not make such a condition, then hajj and ʿumrah are upon him in the following year.
Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever reaches al-Mash'ar al-Haram with five people has indeed attained hajj."

And Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever reaches the standing at Jam‘ on the Day of Sacrifice before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained hajj (pilgrimage)."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever reaches al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained hajj (pilgrimage).
Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated, saying: Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “If he reaches the zawāl, then he has attained the standing.”

Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performed the Tawaf of hajj and the Tawaf al-Nisāʾ before he performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. He said: “It does not harm him; he performs the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and he has completed his hajj.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. Regarding hastening the tawaf before departing to Minā, he said: “They are the same, whether he delays that or brings it forward.”

Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and Jamīl narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That they asked them about the mutamattiʿ who brings forward his tawāf and his saʿy in the hajj, and they said: “They are the same, whether you perform them earlier or later.”

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about one performing tamattuʿ: if he is an elderly old man, or a woman who fears menstruation, may he hasten the tawaf for hajj before going to Mina? He said: “Yes, one who is like this may hasten it.” He said: And I asked him about a man who enters ihram for hajj from Mecca, then sees the House empty and so performs tawaf around it before going out— is there anything upon him? He said: “No.”

Tawaf al-Ziyadah is called ziyarah because the pilgrim comes from Mina to visit the House, does not stay in Mecca, and rather returns to Mina. It is preferable that he perform tawaf of the House on the Day of Sacrifice after completing the rites of Mina; if that is not possible, then on the eleventh day. It should not be delayed beyond that, and it has been said to be prohibited, as in Rawdat al-Mutayaqin.

It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about the visitation of the House being delayed until the third day. He said: “Performing it earlier is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in it if you delay it.”
And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "There is no harm in delaying the visitation of the House until the Day of Departure."

And Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who forgot to perform the visitation of the House until morning, so he said: 'There is no harm in that. I myself sometimes delay it until the days of Tashreeq have passed. However, he must not approach women or use perfume.'

And Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: I asked him about someone who forgot the visitation of the House until he returned to his family, so he said: "It does not harm him if he has completed his rites."

Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "There is no harm in delaying the visitation of the House until the days of Tashriq have passed, except that you must not approach women or use perfume."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man forgot Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ until he returned to his family. He عليه السلام said: "He should order that it be performed on his behalf if he is not going to perform hajj again, for women do not become permissible for him until he performs tawaf of the House."

Hadith 2787 — Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abū Ayyūb Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān al-Khazzāz, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in Makkah when a man entered upon him and said: “May Allah set you aright. We have with us a menstruating woman, and she has not performed Tawāf al-Nisāʾ, and the camel driver refuses to remain for her.” He said: Then he lowered his head while saying: “She is not able to stay behind her companions, and her camel driver will not remain for her.” Then he raised his head toward him and said: “She may proceed, for her hajj has been completed.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had to perform Tawaf al-Nisa' alone, he performed five rounds of the Kaaba, then his stomach was seized by discomfort, and he feared losing control, so he went to his house, relieved himself, and then had intercourse with his maidservant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform ghusl, then return and perform the remaining rounds of his tawaf with the Kaaba, and seek forgiveness from his Lord, and not repeat this.'

2789 - Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who forgot Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ, he said: “If he completed more than half and left forgetfully, he should instruct someone to perform tawaf on his behalf, and he may approach women if he completed more than half.” And it is narrated: “Whoever omitted Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ, if he had performed Ṭawāf al-Wadāʿ, then that is Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Isma‘il ibn Hammam al-Makki, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “Regarding one upon whom walking is obligatory, when he has stoned the Jamrah, he may visit the House riding.”
And it is narrated: “Whoever vows to walk barefoot to the House of Allah should walk; then if he becomes tired, he may ride.”
And it is narrated: “That he walks from behind the Maqam.”

Yunus ibn Ya‘qub narrated, saying: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, “I saw some blood on my garment while I was performing tawaf.” He عليه السلام said: “Identify the place, then go out and wash it, then return and continue your tawaf from where you left off.”

Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was in Ṭawāf al-Nisāʾ when the prayer was established. He said: “He should perform the obligatory prayer with them, and when he finishes, he should continue from where he had reached.”

And in the Nawadir of Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said: Regarding a man performing tawaf when a need arises for him: He said: “There is no harm in his going to attend to his own need or the need of someone else and interrupting the tawaf. And if he wishes to rest during his tawaf and sit, there is no harm in that. Then when he returns, he continues his tawaf from where he left off, even if it was less than half.”

And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who is in tawaf, having completed part of it while part of it remains upon him, so he leaves the tawaf to go to al-Ḥijr or to part of the mosque, if he has not performed the Witr, and then performs Witr, then returns and completes his tawaf. Do you consider that better, or should he complete the tawaf and then perform Witr, even if some brightness of dawn has appeared? So he said: "Begin with the Witr and interrupt the tawaf if you fear [missing it], then come back to the tawaf."

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding one who was performing tawaf around the House, then the entering of the Kaʿbah occurred to him, so he entered it, he said: “He restarts his tawaf from the beginning.”

Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Ḥabīb ibn Muẓāhir, who said: I began the obligatory tawaf and completed one round, when suddenly a person struck my nose and made it bleed. So I went out and washed it, then came back and began the tawaf again. Then I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. So he said: “What you did was bad; you should have built upon what you had already circled.” Then he said: “Indeed, there is nothing upon you.”

And it is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man comes upon his brother while he is in tawaf. So he said: He may go out with him regarding his need, then return and continue from his tawaf.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed tawaf around the Kaaba, then went out and performed sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa. While he was going between them, he remembered that he had left part of his tawaf of the House incomplete. He عليه السلام said: "He returns to the House and completes his tawaf, then returns to al-Safa and al-Marwa and completes what remains."

And it is narrated from Abū Ayyūb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed eight circuits around the House for the obligatory tawaf. He said: “Then let him add six to it, then perform four rakʿahs.” And in another report: “Indeed, the obligation is the second tawaf, and the first two rakʿahs are for the obligatory tawaf, while the other two rakʿahs and the first tawaf are voluntary.”

And in the narration of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: He was asked, while I was present, about a man who performed eight circuits around the House. So he said, "Voluntary or obligatory?" He said, "Obligatory." He said, "He should add six to it, and when he finishes, he should pray two rak'ahs at the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام, then go out to al-Safa and al-Marwah and perform tawaf between them. Then when he finishes, he should pray another two rak'ahs, so it will be a voluntary tawaf and an obligatory tawaf."

And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAṭiyyah, who said: Sulaymān ibn Khālid asked him, while I was with him, about a man who circumambulated the House in six circuits. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “And how does he circumambulate six circuits?” He said: “He faced the Stone, said: ‘Allāhu Akbar,’ and counted one.” He said: “He performs one circuit.” Sulaymān said: “If that escaped him until he came to his family?” He said: “He instructs someone to perform tawaf on his behalf.”
And Rifā‘ah narrated from him that he said: Regarding a man who does not know whether he performed six or seven rounds of tawaf, he said: “He should build upon what he is certain of.”

And he was asked about a man who does not know whether he performed three circuits or four. He said: "Was it a voluntary tawaf or an obligatory one?" He said: "Answer me regarding both of them together." He said: "If it is a voluntary tawaf, then build upon whatever you wish. And if it is an obligatory tawaf, then repeat the tawaf. So if you circled the House in the obligatory tawaf and did not know whether you performed six or seven, then repeat your tawaf. But if you left and that passed you by, then there is nothing upon you."

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed tawaf around the House, then shortened one circuit in the Hijr. What should he do? He said: "He repeats that one circuit."
2807 - And in the narration of Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: “Whoever shortens the tawaf in the Hijr must repeat his tawaf from the Black Stone.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibrahim ibn Sufyan, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام about a woman who performed the tawaf of hajj. When she was in the seventh circuit, she shortened it and performed tawaf through the Hijr. She then prayed the two obligatory rak'ahs, performed the sa'y, completed the tawaf of al-nisa', and then came to Mina. So he عليه السلام wrote: "She must repeat."
Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “Nothing is slaughtered in the Haram except camels, cattle, sheep, and chickens.”
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked him about the chickens of al-Ḥabash, so he said: "It is not from the game; rather, birds are those that fly between the sky and the earth and spread their wings."

2381 - Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about Sindhi chickens being taken out of the Haram, and he said: “Yes, because they cannot fly independently.” And in another report: “They only flutter lightly.”
Al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal asked him about the chickens of Mecca and its birds, so he said: “Whatever does not glide, then eat it; and whatever glides, then leave it to its way.”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man who brought his cheetah into the Haram: is he allowed to take it out? He said: "It is a predator, so whatever predator you bring into the Haram as a captive, you may take it out."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "There is no harm in killing ants and bedbugs in the Haram." And he said: "There is no harm in killing a louse in the Haram and elsewhere."
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: “Every bird that does not glide is in the same category as chicken.”

It is narrated from Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in completing all the rites without wudu (ablution), except the tawaf of the House; and wudu (ablution) is better.”

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf while not in a state of purity. He said: “He should perform wudu (ablution) and repeat his tawaf; and if it was voluntary, he should perform wudu (ablution) and pray two rakʿahs.”

And in the narration of ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: “There is no harm in a man performing the voluntary tawaf without wudu (ablution), then performing wudu and praying. And if he performed tawaf intentionally without wudu, then he should perform wudu and pray.”

Safwan narrated from Yahya al-Azraq, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: A man performed the sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa, completing three or four circuits, then urinated, then completed his sa‘i without wudu (ablution). So he عليه السلام said: 'There is no harm, though if he had completed his rites with wudu (ablution), that would have been more preferable to me.'

2814 - Hariz and Ibrahim ibn Umar narrated; they said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in a woman performing tawaf while not circumcised. As for a man, he does not perform tawaf unless he is circumcised.”

Ibn Maskān narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who accepts Islam and wants to be circumcised while the time of hajj has arrived: should he perform hajj or be circumcised? He said, “He should not perform hajj until he is circumcised.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Zurārah, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It is only disliked for a man to combine two sets of seven circuits and two tawafs in the obligatory rite. As for the voluntary one, there is no problem.”
And Zurārah said: Sometimes I performed tawaf with Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام while he was holding my hand for two tawafs and three, then he would depart and pray six rakʿahs.

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated, saying: I heard Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام say: My father narrated to me. That the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed tawaf on his mount, touched the Stone with his staff, and performed sa‘y upon it between al-Safa and al-Marwah.
And in another report: "It is mentioned that he would kiss the mihjan (staff)."

And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr: That Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام fell ill, so he ordered his attendants to carry him and perform tawaf with him. Then he ordered them to draw his foot along the ground so that his feet would touch the ground during the tawaf. And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym: That he would do this whenever he reached al-Rukn al-Yamānī.
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: About the sick person who is overcome: should ṭawāf be performed on his behalf around the Kaʿbah? He said: “No; rather, he should be taken around.”

And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from him, peace be upon him, he said: “The injured person is carried so that he may stone the Jamarāt, and the one afflicted with abdominal illness is stoned for on his behalf, and salat (prayer) is performed on his behalf.”
And he said: Regarding young children, they are carried for tawaf, and the stoning is performed on their behalf.

Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tawaf around the Ka'bah, then went out and performed Sa'y between Safa and Marwah. While he was performing Sa'y, he remembered that he had left part of his Tawaf around the House incomplete. He (the Imam) said: 'He should be done) said: 'He should return to the House and complete his Tawaf, then return to Safa and Marwah and complete what remains.' I said: 'What if he began with Safa and Marwah before beginning with the House?' He said: 'He should go to the House, perform Tawaf around it, then restart his Tawaf between Safa and Marwah.' I said: 'What is the difference between these two cases?' He said: 'Because in this case he had entered into part of the Tawaf, and in this case he had not entered into any part of it.'

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: about a man who arrives as a pilgrim, and the heat has become intense upon him, so he performs tawaf around the Kaʿbah and delays the saʿy until it becomes cooler. So he said: “There is no harm in it, and I have sometimes done it.”
And in another hadith: "He may delay it until the night."

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a man who circumambulated the House and became weary: may he delay the tawaf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until tomorrow? He said: "No."

Rifa'ah asked him: About a man who is performing tawaf around the House, then the time of al-'Asr enters: should he perform sa'y before he prays, or should he pray before he performs sa'y? He said: "There is no harm in praying and then performing sa'y."

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام that he said: "If you wish to perform tawaf on behalf of one of your brothers, then go to the Black Stone and say: In the Name of Allah, O Allah, accept from so-and-so."

Yahya al-Azraq asked him: About a man—whether it is permissible for him to perform tawaf on behalf of his relatives. He said: “When he has completed the rites of hajj, then let him do whatever he wishes.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Concerning a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf and forgot the two Rakʿahs until he had gone between al-Safā and al-Marwah, then remembered, he said: "He marks that place, then returns and prays the two Rakʿahs, then returns to his place." That was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: "Whichever of the two reports he follows is valid." He said: And I said to him, 'A man forgot the two Rakʿahs behind Maqām Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and did not remember until he departed from Makkah.' He said: 'Then let him pray them wherever he remembers; and if he remembers them while he is still in the town, then he must not leave until he makes them up.'

He said: And I said to him: A man forgot the two rakʿahs behind the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام and did not remember until he departed from Makkah. He said: "Then let him pray them wherever he remembers. And if he remembers them while he is still in the city, then he should not leave until he performs them."

And in the narration of ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "If he has gone only a little distance, then let him return and perform the two rakʿahs, or let him instruct some of the people, and let him perform them on his behalf."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who forgot the two rak'ahs of the obligatory tawaf and had already circumambulated the House until he came to Minā. He said: 'He should return to the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام and perform them.'

And in the narration of Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, The one who is ignorant in leaving the two rakʿahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام is in the position of one who forgets.

ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who performs tawaf and saʿy, then performs voluntary tawaf around the House before he shortens his hair. He said: “I do not approve of it.”

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Haytham al-Tamimi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man had with him his wife, who was unable to stand on her feet, so her husband carried her in a litter and performed with her the obligatory tawaf of the House and the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah. Would that tawaf, his performing tawaf with her, suffice for himself as well? So he said: "Yes indeed, by Allah, then it would."

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Hudhayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who relies on the counting of his female companion in the tawaf, whether it suffices for both of them and for the child, he عليه السلام said: “Yes. Do you not see that you follow the Imam when you perform salat (prayer) behind him, and it is similar to that?”
Saʿīd al-Aʿraj asked him: about the tawaf: can a man suffice with the counting of his companion? He said, "Yes."

And Safwan narrated from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saw me circumambulating around the Ka'bah while I was wearing a burṭulah, so he said: “After this, you circumambulate around the Ka'bah while wearing a burṭulah? Do not wear it around the Ka'bah, for it is from the attire of the Jews.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is recommended that you perform three hundred and sixty weeks of tawaf, equal to the number of the days of the year. If you are not able, then three hundred and sixty circuits. If you are not able, then whatever amount of tawaf you are capable of.

Aban asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله have a known pattern of tawaf?” So he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform tawaf by night and day in ten asbūʿ: three at the beginning of the night, three at the end of the night, two when morning came, and two after noon; and in between that was his rest.
Sa'id al-A'raj asked him: About the one who is fast and the one who is slow in tawaf, he said: "Both are permissible so long as no one is harmed."

And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “I performed four rounds of tawaf and became tired. Should I then pray its rakʿahs while I am sitting?” He said: “No.” I said: “And how does a man pray salat al-layl if he becomes tired or feels weakness while he is sitting?” So he said: “A man performs tawaf while sitting.” So I said: “No.” He said: “Then pray the two of them while you are standing.”

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who forgot to perform tawaf of the House until he returned to his family, so he said: "If it was on account of ignorance, he must repeat the hajj and a camel is due from him."

Hisham ibn al-Hakam narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever resides in Mecca for one year, tawaf is better for him than salat (prayer). Whoever resides for two years, he should combine between this and that. And whoever resides for three years, salat (prayer) becomes better for him.
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: “It is recommended that you count your weekly circumambulation in every day and night.”

Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Saʿd, who said: I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about the Gate of al-Ṣafā, and I said: Our companions have differed about it. Some of them say it is the one adjacent to the water station, and some of them say it is the one facing the Black Stone. So he said: “It is the one facing the Black Stone, and the one adjacent to the water station is a newly introduced one; Dāwūd made it and Dāwūd opened it.”

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a man who forgot to perform the going between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. He said: “It is performed on his behalf.”

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed six circuits between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah while thinking that they were seven, then remembered after he had exited iḥrām restrictions and had relations with women that he had only performed six. He said: "He must sacrifice a cow and perform one more circuit."

And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Concerning a man who performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in eight circuits, he said: “If it was by mistake, he should discard one and count seven.” And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, he said: “He should add six to it.”

Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A woman performs sa‘i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a riding animal or on a camel? He said: “There is no problem with that.” He said: And I asked him about a man doing that. He said: “There is no problem with it, and walking is better.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abā Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him: about women who perform the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on camels and riding animals: is it sufficient for them to stand beneath al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah where they can see the House? So he said, "Yes."
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "There is no saʿy for the one who is riding, but he should increase his speed somewhat."
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated from him, عليه السلام, and said: Do not sit between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah except out of exertion or necessity.

ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: In the wisdom of the family of Dāwūd عليه السلام, it is stated that the intelligent person should not set out in travel except for three things: provisioning for the Hereafter, mending one’s livelihood, or a pleasure that is not forbidden.

Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain, saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Travel and you will gain health; perform jihad and you will attain spoils; and perform hajj and you will become self-sufficient.”

And Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, apportions sustenance for a servant in a land, He places for him a need in it."

Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar narrated, saying: I said to Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: "A man begins the sa'i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and the time of salat enters. Should he shorten it, or perform salat and then return, or remain as he is until he finishes?" So he عليه السلام said: "Is there not a mosque for him by them both? No; rather, he should perform salat and then return." I said: "And may he sit on al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?" He عليه السلام said: "Yes."

ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān and Ṣafwān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, who completes three circuits or four, then a friend meets him and invites him to attend to a need or to food. He عليه السلام said: “If he responds to him, there is no harm in that, but that he fulfill the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more beloved to me than that he fulfill the right of his companion.”

And it was narrated from Ibn Faḍḍāl, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said to him: "I performed one circuit, then dawn rose." He said: "Pray, then return and complete your saʿy."

2858 - It was narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And [due] to Allah from the people is hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it." He said: "What do the people say about it?" It was said to him: "Provision and a mount." He عليه السلام said: "Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about this, and he said: 'The people would perish, then! If whoever had provision and a mount equal to what sustains his dependents and makes him independent of people were to set out to it and strip them of it, then they would indeed perish.'" So it was said to him: "Then what is the way?" He said: "Amplitude in wealth: that he performs hajj with part of it while part remains for the sustenance of his dependents. Has not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made zakat obligatory and only placed it upon one who possesses two hundred dirhams?"

And Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: “Whoever is offered the opportunity to perform hajj, even if on a maimed donkey with a cut-off tail, and he refuses, then he is considered capable of hajj.”
Abu Baṣīr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: No man refrains from hajj except because of a sin, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pardons is greater.

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: “There is no servant who gives preference over hajj to a need from the needs of this world, except that he will look upon those who have shaved their heads having already departed before that need is fulfilled for him.”

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a person is financially capable, but illness or another matter for which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excuses him prevents him from performing hajj, then it is incumbent upon him that hajj be performed on his behalf from his wealth by someone who has not performed hajj before and has no wealth.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام instructed an elderly man, who had never performed hajj and was unable to undertake the hajj because of his old age, to equip a man to perform hajj on his behalf.
Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār asked Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: about a man who performed hajj on behalf of someone else: would that suffice him for the Hajj of Islam? He said: “Yes.”

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If an impoverished man is enabled to perform hajj by another man, he will have a hajj. But if he later becomes financially able, then hajj is still obligatory upon him. Likewise, the nāṣib, if he comes to know, then hajj is obligatory upon him, even if he had already performed hajj.

Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Abū ʿAlī Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muṭahhar, who said: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: I gave one hundred and fifty dīnārs to six persons so that they might perform hajj with it. Then they returned, and some of them had not departed. Some came to me and mentioned that they had spent some of the dīnārs and that some remained, and that they would return to me what remained. I had intended to demand back what I had given to those who did not come to me. So he عليه السلام wrote: “Do not pursue the one who did not come to you, and do not take anything from the one who came to you of what he brings back to you, and the reward has already become due from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Al-Bazanti narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who took funds for hajj from a man, then the road was cut off against him. Then another man gave him another hajj fund. Is that permissible for him? He said: "That is permissible for him. It is counted for the first and the second, and there was no room for him to do other than what he did when he found someone who would provide him with the hajj funds."

And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who had no wealth, so he performed hajj on behalf of another man, or another sent him for hajj; then he later acquired wealth—does hajj remain obligatory upon him? He عليه السلام said: “It suffices for both of them.”

And it was said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man takes the Hajj-payment from another man, then he dies and leaves nothing behind.” So he said: “It suffices for the deceased, and if he had a Hajj with Allah, it will be recorded for its owner.”

Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Aʿraj asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ṣarūrah: can he perform hajj on behalf of a deceased person? He said: "Yes, if the ṣarūrah does not possess what he can perform hajj with. But if he has wealth, then that is not for him until he performs hajj from his own wealth. And it suffices on behalf of the deceased whether he had wealth or did not have wealth."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who gave another man funds for a hajj so that he might perform it on his behalf from Kufa, but he performed it on his behalf from Basra, he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm. If he completed all of his rites, then his hajj has been completed.”

And Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who gave another man dirhams so that he might perform on his behalf a single Hajj: is it permissible for him to perform Tamattu' with the 'Umrah to the Hajj? He said: Yes; he has only differed from him toward greater merit and goodness.

Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: "Can a man perform hajj on behalf of a Nasibi?" He said: "No." I said: "What if it was my father?" He said: "If it was your father, then perform hajj on his behalf."
And it was narrated: that al-Sadiq عليه السلام gave a man thirty dinars and said to him "Perform hajj on behalf of Isma'il, and do this and that, and nine are for you while one is for him."

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever performs hajj on behalf of a person, the two share until, when he completes the obligatory tawaf, the sharing is cut off. So whatever act occurs after that belongs to that pilgrim.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding a man who gave another man money to perform hajj on his behalf, but he performed hajj for himself instead, he said: "It is on behalf of the owner of the money."
And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ṣarūrah: "May he perform hajj using zakat funds?" He said: "Yes."

And it was narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man travels for trade to Mecca, or he has camels which he rents out. Is his Hajj considered incomplete or complete?' He said: 'No, rather his Hajj is complete.'

Umar ibn Udhaynah narrated, he said: I wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who performed Hajj without knowing or recognizing this matter, then Allah blessed him with knowledge and adherence to it. Is the Hajj of Islam still obligatory upon him? He replied: 'He has fulfilled the obligation of Allah, the Exalted, but performing Hajj again is more beloved to me.'

And it was narrated from Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ al-Khurāsānī, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: I performed hajj while I was a dissenter, and I have performed this hajj of mine, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed upon me the knowledge of you. And I came to know that what I had been upon was false. So what do you think regarding my hajj? He عليه السلام said: “Make this the Hajj of Islam, and that one supererogatory.”

Hafs ibn Ghayath al-Nakha'i narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever intends travel, then let him travel on Saturday, for even if a stone were to move from a mountain on a Saturday, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would return it to its place. And whoever finds needs difficult to attain, then let him seek pursuing them on Tuesday, for it is the day in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, softened iron for Dawud عليه السلام.
Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Madanī narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "There is no harm in setting out on a journey on the night of Friday."
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sulaymān narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to travel on Thursday.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Thursday is a day loved by Allah, His Messenger, and His angels."

Some Baghdadis wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thānī عليه السلام, asking him about going out on a Wednesday that does not rotate. So he عليه السلام wrote: “Whoever goes out on a Wednesday that does not rotate, in مخالفة to the people of bad omens, will be protected from every harm, cured of every affliction, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fulfill his need.”
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Travel by night, for the earth is folded during the night."
And in the narration of Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: "The earth is folded at the end of the night."
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī narrated from him, peace be upon him: "Do not go out on Friday for any need; then when it is Saturday and the sun has risen, go out for your need."

Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So when the salat (prayer) has been concluded, then disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah." So he عليه السلام said: "The salat (prayer) is on the day of Friday, and the dispersal is on the day of Saturday."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Saturday is for us, and Sunday is for Banū Umayyah."
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Do not travel on Monday, nor seek any need on that day."

And it is narrated from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz that he said: We intended to go out, so we came to greet Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said, 'It is as though you sought the blessing of Monday.' We said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So what day is greater in ominousness than Monday? On it we lost our Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and revelation was raised from us. Do not go out on Monday, and go out on Tuesday.'
Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever travels or marries while the moon is in Scorpio will not see goodness."

It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Indeed, I have been afflicted with this knowledge. I intend a need, and when I look at the ascendant and see the ascendant as evil, I sit and do not go regarding it; and when I see the ascendant as good, I go regarding the need.” So he said to me: “Do you get it done?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Burn your books.”

And Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: Ill omen for the traveler on his road is in six things: the crow cawing on his right, the dog spreading its tail, the howling wolf that howls in the man’s face while crouching on its tail, howling, then rising and then lowering itself three times, the deer crossing from right to left, the screeching owl, the gray-haired woman exposing her private part, and the mutilated she-donkey, meaning the one whose ear is cut off. So whoever senses within himself anything from them, let him say: ‘I seek protection in You, O my Lord, from the evil of what I find within myself, so protect me from that.’ He said: ‘Then he will be protected from that.’
Hariz narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whatever a slave in the state of ihram incurs during his ihram is upon the master, if he gave him permission to enter ihram.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said: I have female servants with me in Makkah. Should I instruct them to enter iḥrām for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, then take them out so they may witness the rites, or should I leave them behind in Makkah? He said: He عليه السلام said, “If you take them out with you, then that is better; and if you leave them behind with a trustworthy person, then there is no harm. There is no hajj nor ʿumrah upon the owned servant until he or she is freed.”

Misma‘ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a servant were to perform ten hajj pilgrimages, the Hajj of Islam would still remain obligatory upon him when he becomes able to find a way to it.

And in the narration of al-Naḍr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If the enslaved person performs hajj while he is enslaved, it suffices for him if he dies before he is freed. But if he is freed, then hajj is upon him.

Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated, saying: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about an umm walad belonging to a man, whom he had sent for hajj. Would that suffice for her as the Hajj of Islam? He said: "No." I said: "Is there a reward for her in her hajj?" He said: "Yes."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Shihab, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who freed a servant of his on the eve of Arafah, he عليه السلام said: "The Hajj of Islam suffices for the servant, and two rewards are written for the master: the reward of emancipation and the reward of Hajj."

And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A slave was emancipated on the Day of ʿArafah." He said: "If he reaches one of the two standing places, then he has attained the hajj."

Zurārah narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: If a man takes his young son for hajj, then he instructs him to recite the talbiyah and to enter into hajj. If he cannot recite the talbiyah properly, it is recited on his behalf, he is taken around for tawaf, and prayer is performed on his behalf. I said: They do not have what they can slaughter on his behalf. He said: A sacrifice is slaughtered for the young children, while the older ones fast. They are to be guarded from what the muhrim must avoid of clothing and fragrance. If he kills game, then it is upon his father.

And it was narrated from Ayyūb, the brother of Udaym, who said: Abū ʿAbdِ Allāh عليه السلام was asked, “From where are the children stripped (for ihram)?” So he said, “My father عليه السلام used to strip them at Fakh.”

And it was narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from his father, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I have young children with me, and I fear the cold for them. From where should they enter ihram?” So he said: “Take them to al-ʿArj, and let them enter ihram from there, for when you come to al-ʿArj, you will have entered Tihāmah.” Then he said: “If you fear for them, then take them to al-Juḥfah.”

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Look at the children who are with you, then bring them forward to al-Juḥfah or to Baṭn Marr, and do for them what is done for the muḥrim. Ṭawāf is performed with them, pebbles are cast on their behalf, and whoever among them does not find the hady, his guardian should fast on his behalf. And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام used to place the knife in the hand of the child, then the man would grasp his hand and slaughter.”

Samāʿah asked him about a man who instructed his servants to perform tamattuʿ. He said: "It is incumbent upon him to offer the sacrifice on their behalf." I said: "What if he gave them dirhams, and some of them offered the sacrifice while others kept the dirhams and fasted?" He said: "That has sufficed for them, and he has the choice; if he wishes, he may leave it." He said: "And if he had instructed them and they fasted, that would have sufficed for them."

Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a ten-year-old boy performing hajj. He said: "The hajj of Islam is upon him when he reaches puberty, and likewise the girl—the hajj is upon her when she menstruates."

And it was narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام about the child: when should ihram be entered on his behalf? He said: "When he begins to grow teeth."

And Abān narrated from al-Ḥakam, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “If a child is taken for hajj, then he has fulfilled the hajj of Islam only until he grows up; and if a servant is taken for hajj, then he has fulfilled the hajj of Islam only until he is freed.”

It was narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performs hajj with debt, while he has already performed the Hajj of Islam. He said: "Yes. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will settle it on his behalf, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills."

And it was narrated from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUtbah, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who has a debt and borrows in order to perform hajj. He said: “If he has a means in wealth, then there is no harm.”

And Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from him, عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: "May a man borrow and perform hajj if he has behind him that by which payment may be made on his behalf if something happens to him?" He said: "Yes."

And it was narrated from Abū Hammām, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A man has a debt upon him, and some wealth comes to him. Should he pay his debt or perform hajj? He said: "He should pay part of it and perform hajj with part of it." I said: But what if it is only equal to the amount of the expenses of hajj? He said: "He should pay the debt one year and perform hajj the next year." I said: The wealth is given from the side of the ruler. He said: "There is no harm upon you in that."
A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: “I am a man who has debt, so should I borrow and perform hajj (pilgrimage)?” So he said: “Yes, it is more effective in settling the debt.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Aban, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-'Attar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "I have debt, and dirhams come into my possession; if I distribute them among them, nothing significant will fall to them." "Should I perform hajj with it, or distribute it among the creditors?" He عليه السلام said: "Perform hajj with it, and pray to Allah to settle your debt for you, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills."

Aban narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who has a husband and is ṣarūrah, and he does not permit her regarding the hajj. He said: “She performs hajj, even if he does not permit her.”
And in the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, he said: "She performs hajj, even if it displeases him."

2909 - And Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a wealthy woman who has performed the Hajj of Islam, then says to her husband, 'Take me for hajj once again.' Does he have the right to prevent her? He said: 'Yes. He may say to her: My right over you is greater than your right over me in this matter.'

It was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who goes out to Makkah without a guardian, and he said: "There is no harm; she may go out with trustworthy people."

And in the narration of Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. Regarding a woman who wants to perform hajj and does not have a mahram with her: Is hajj proper for her? He عليه السلام said: "Yes, if she is safe/trustworthy."

2912 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: You know my occupation. A woman comes to me, and I know her by her Islam, her love for you, and her wilayah to you; she has no mahram. He said: "If the Muslim woman comes, then carry her, for the believing man is a mahram for the believing woman." Then he recited this verse: 'And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.'
Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: The divorced woman may perform hajj during her waiting period ('iddah).
Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman whose husband has died: "Can she perform hajj during her waiting period ('iddah)?" He said: "Yes."

ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ḍurays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who set out as a pilgrim for the Hajj of Islam, then died on the way. He عليه السلام said: “If he died in the ḥaram, then the Hajj of Islam has sufficed for him. But if he died short of the ḥaram, then his heir should perform the Hajj of Islam on his behalf.”

Hadith 2916 — And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who set out for hajj, and with him were his camel, expenses, and provisions, but he died on the way. He عليه السلام said: “If he was a ṣarūrah and then died in the Haram, then the Hajj of Islam has sufficed for him. But if he died while being a ṣarūrah before entering into ihram, his camel, his provisions, his expenses, and what was with him are to be applied toward the Hajj of Islam. Then if anything remains from that, it belongs to the heirs, provided that he had no debt upon him.” I said: “What do you think—if the hajj was voluntary, and then he died on the way before entering into ihram, to whom do his camel, his expenses, and what he had belong?” He عليه السلام said: “All that he had with him and what he left behind belongs to the heirs, unless he had a debt, in which case it is paid on his behalf, or he had made a bequest, in which case that is carried out for the one to whom he made the bequest, and that is to be taken from one-third of his estate.”

Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and he left behind nothing except the amount of the expenses of Hajj, and he had heirs. He عليه السلام said: "They have greater right to his inheritance. If they wish, they may consume it, and if they wish, they may perform Hajj on his behalf."

And it was narrated from Ḥārith, the seller of mats: that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who made a bequest for a hajj, so he said: "If he was a ṣarūrah, then it is from the principal of his wealth; it is only a debt upon him. And if he had already performed hajj, then it is from the one-third."

It was narrated from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “My daughter made a bequest for a hajj, and she did not perform hajj.” He said: “Then perform hajj on her behalf, for it is for you and for her.” I said: “My mother died and did not perform hajj.” He said: “Perform hajj on her behalf, for it is for you and for her.”

And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who made a bequest of wealth for charity, hajj, and the freeing of slaves. He said, “Begin with hajj, for it is obligatory. If anything remains, then allocate a portion to charity and a portion to freeing slaves.”

And it was narrated from Bashīr al-Nabbāl, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “My mother passed away and did not perform hajj.” He said: “A man or a woman may perform hajj on her behalf.” He said: I asked, “Which of them is more preferable to you?” He said: “A man is more preferable to me.”

And it was narrated from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who died and did not perform the Hajj of Islam, and did not make a will concerning it. Should it be performed on his behalf? He said: "Yes."

Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Wala' is a bond like the bond of lineage; it is neither sold nor gifted."

And it was said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “Why do you say that a man’s mawla is from him?” He said: “Because he was created from his clay, then they were separated, and captivity brought him back to him. So he showed compassion for what of him was in him, and freed him; therefore he is from him.”

And it is narrated from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who frees another man as an expiation for an oath or ẓihār: to whom does the walāʾ belong? He said: "To the one who set him free."

And in the narration of ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he mentioned: Barīrah was with a husband of hers while she was enslaved, then ʿĀʾishah bought her and set her free. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله gave her the choice: if she wished, she could remain with her husband, and if she wished, she could separate from him. Her masters who sold her had stipulated her walāʾ for ʿĀʾishah, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “The walāʾ belongs to the one who emancipates.” Meat was given to Barīrah as charity, and she gifted it to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so ʿĀʾishah hung it up and said that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله does not eat charity. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came while the meat was hanging and said: “What is the matter with this meat that it has not been cooked?” She said: “O Messenger of Allah, it was given as charity to Barīrah, and you do not eat charity.” So he صلى الله عليه وآله said: “It is charity for her and a gift for us.” Then he ordered that it be cooked, and three sunnahs occurred in it.

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-'Is ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who bought a slave who had children from a free woman, and then he freed him. He عليه السلام said: "The wala' of his children belongs to the one who freed him."

And it is narrated from Bakr ibn Muhammad that he said: I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and with me was ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. He said to me, "Who is this?" I said, "Our mawlā." He said, "Did you free him or his father?" I said, "Rather, his father." He said, "This is not your mawlā; this is your brother and your cousin. The mawlā is only the one upon whom the blessing has directly been bestowed; so if it was bestowed upon his father, then he is your brother and your cousin." He said: A man asked him while I was present, saying: "I have a غلام who drinks and becomes involved in these disliked matters, and I wish to free him. Is it more beloved to you that I free him, or that I sell him and give his price in charity?" He said, "Indeed, manumission is more virtuous at some times, and at other times charity is more virtuous. Manumission is more virtuous when the people are in a good condition, but when the people are in hardship, then charity is more virtuous. And selling this one is more beloved to me when he is in this state."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who owns a blood relative: is it proper for him to sell him or enslave him? He عليه السلام said: It is not proper for him to sell him, nor may he take him as a slave. He is his mawla and his brother in religion. Whichever of the two dies, the other inherits from him, unless he has an heir closer to him than the other.
And Hudhayfah ibn Mansur narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The one who frees is the mawla, and the child affiliates himself with whomever he wishes.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about al-sa'ibah. He said: It is a man who frees his غلام, then says to him: 'Go wherever you wish. I have no share in your inheritance, nor am I liable for any offense on your behalf,' and he has two witnesses testify to that.

And it is narrated from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he was asked about a slave who is freed as a sāʾibah, and he said: He may take whomever he wishes as his guardian, and upon the one whom he takes as guardian is his liability, and for him is his inheritance. He said: I said, then if he remains silent until he dies and does not take anyone as a guardian? He said: His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about the sa'ibah. He said: Look in the Qur'an: whatever in it contains the freeing of a slave, that, O Ammar, is the sa'ibah, who has no wala' belonging to any of the Muslims over him except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So whatever wala' belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then it is for His Messenger; and whatever is for His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, then indeed its wala' is for the Imam. His liability for offense is upon the Imam, and his inheritance belongs to him.

Yāsīn narrated from Ḥarīz, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a slave who wanted to purchase himself, so he secretly sent a man. Does the one secretly sent have the right to buy him entirely from the slave’s wealth and not inform the master that he is only buying him from the slave’s wealth? He عليه السلام said: “It is not proper. If he wants to render that lawful between himself and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that his wala' belongs to him, then let him add whatever he wishes, after there is an addition from his own wealth in the price of the slave. By that he makes the wala' lawful, and the wala' of the slave becomes his.”

3506 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who was under an obligation to free a slave, but died before he could free one. Then his son went and bought a man from his own earnings and freed him on behalf of his father. After that, the freed man acquired wealth, then died and left it behind. For whom would his inheritance be? He said, so he replied: "If the slave that had been due upon his father was in fulfillment of a vow, or gratitude, or was obligatory upon him, then the freed man is a sa'ibah, and no one has any claim over him." He said: "Then if he had affiliated himself, before dying, to one of the Muslims, and he guaranteed his offense and liability, he would be his mawla and his heir, if he had no Muslim relative to inherit from him. And if he had not affiliated himself to anyone until he died, then his inheritance belongs to the Imam, the Imam of the Muslims, if he has no relative from the Muslims to inherit from him." He said: "And if the slave due from his father was voluntary, and his father had instructed him to free a person on his behalf, then the wala' of the freed man is an inheritance for all the children of the deceased." He said: "And the one who bought him and then freed him by his father's instruction is like one of the heirs, when the freed man does not have free Muslim relatives who inherit from him." He said: "And if his son, who bought the slave and freed him on behalf of his father from his own wealth after his father's death, did so voluntarily from himself without his father having instructed him to do that, then his wala' and inheritance belong to the one who bought him from his own wealth and freed him on behalf of his father, if the freed man has no heir from among his kin."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام passed by me while I was sitting with the judge in al-Madinah. The next day I went to him, and he said to me: “What was that gathering in which I saw you yesterday?” He said: I said to him, “May I be your ransom, this judge honors me, so I sometimes sit with him.” He said to me: “And what makes you secure from the curse descending and encompassing you along with him?”
And it has been narrated in another report: Indeed, the worst of places are the houses of the rulers who do not judge with the truth.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, the graves complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about their intense heat. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to them: "Be silent, for the places of judges are hotter than you."
It is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Whoever judges concerning two dirhams and errs has committed kufr.”
Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: "Any judge who judges between two people and errs falls farther than the distance from the heaven."

It is narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding two men who agreed upon two just individuals and appointed them between themselves concerning a judgment in which a dispute had occurred between them, and they were satisfied with the two just individuals, but the two just individuals then differed between themselves: upon whose statement is the judgment to proceed?
