He عليه السلام said: "One should look to the one who is more learned in fiqh, more knowledgeable of our hadith, and more scrupulous; then his judgment is to be carried out, and no attention is to be paid to the other."

Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said regarding two men, each of whom chose a man, and they agreed that the two would act as arbiters concerning their right; then they differed in what they judged, and both differed regarding our hadith. He said: "The ruling is whatever is judged by the one who is more just, more versed in fiqh, more truthful in hadith, and more scrupulous; and no attention is given to what the other judges." He said: I said, what if both of them are just, approved among our companions, and neither of them has superiority over the other? He said: "Then one should look to what in their narrations from us, concerning that by which they judged, is agreed upon by your companions; it is then taken from our ruling, and the anomalous report that is not well known among your companions is left aside. Indeed, that which is agreed upon is our ruling, and there is no doubt in it. Matters are only three: a matter whose right guidance is clear, so it is followed; a matter whose error is clear, so it is avoided; and a problematic matter whose ruling is referred back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Halal is clear, and haram is clear, and doubtful matters lie between that. So whoever leaves the doubtful matters is saved from the prohibited matters, and whoever takes up the doubtful matters has committed the prohibited matters and perished from where he does not know." I said: What if the two reports from you are both well known, and trustworthy ones have narrated them from you? He said: "Then one should examine them: whichever ruling accords with the Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) and opposes the general public is taken." I said: May I be your ransom, we find one of the two reports in agreement with the general public and the other opposed to it; by which of the two reports is it to be taken? He said: "By that which opposes the general public, for in it is right guidance." I said: May I be your ransom, what if both reports agree with them? He said: "Then one should look at that toward which their rulers and judges are more inclined; that is left aside, and the other is taken." I said: What if their rulers and judges agree with both reports? He said: "If it is so, then defer it until you meet your Imam, for stopping at doubtful matters is
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is tested with judging should not pass judgment while he is angry.

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: If the judge says to the one on his right and to the one on his left, 'What do you say? What do you think?' then for that is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people together. He should rise from his seat and seat them in his place.

A man stayed as a guest with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام for some days, then he brought before him a legal dispute which he had not mentioned to ʿAlī عليه السلام. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “Are you a litigant?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Move away from us, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade that a litigant be hosted unless his opponent is with him.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever deals with people fairly from himself is accepted as a judge for others.

And it is narrated from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “If two men bring a case before you, then do not judge for the first until you hear from the other, for when you do that, the judgment will become clear to you.” ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “So I continued thereafter as a judge.” And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: “O Allah, grant him understanding of judgment.”

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to Shurayh: O Shurayh, do not speak privately with anyone in your court. And when you become angry, then stand up, and do not judge while you are angry.

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled that the one on the right should be given precedence in speaking in a gathering.
Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you appear with an opponent before a governor or before a judge, then stand at his right.
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whoever is tested with judging should treat them equally in gestures and glances within the gathering.

3243 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to Shurayḥ: O Shurayḥ, look into the cases of those given to withholding, delay, and oppression, and those who withhold the rights of people despite having means and ease, and those who channel the wealth of the Muslims to the rulers. So take the people's rights from them, and sell real estate and houses. For I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: “The delay of a wealthy Muslim is ظلم against a Muslim.” And whoever has no wealth, no real estate, and no house, then there is no recourse against him. And know that none can carry people upon the truth except one who restrains them from falsehood. Then treat the Muslims equally in your face, your speech, and your sitting, so that your relative may not hope for your bias, and your enemy may not despair of your justice. And return the oath to the claimant along with evidence, for that is more clarifying against blindness and more firmly established in judgment. And know that the Muslims are upright against one another, except one flogged in a hadd who has not repented from it, or one known for false testimony, or one under suspicion. And beware of weariness and annoyance in the judicial sitting, in which Allah, the Exalted, has made reward obligatory and made the provision therein excellent for the one who judges with truth. And appoint a term for one who claims absent witnesses between them; if he brings them, you shall take his right for him, and if he does not bring them, you shall decide the case against him. And beware of executing a judgment in retaliation, or a hadd from the limits concerning people, or a right from the rights of Allah عزّ وجلّ, until you present that to me. And beware of sitting in the judicial assembly until you have eaten something, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

In the narration of al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, attributed upward: A man swore that he would weigh an elephant, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "He should put the elephant into a boat, then look at the place reached by the water from the boat and mark it. Then he should remove the elephant and cast into the boat iron, copper, or whatever he wishes. When it reaches the place that he marked, he should remove it and weigh it."

And in the narration of ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jaʿfar ibn Ghālib al-Asadī, who raised the hadith, he said: While two men were sitting in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, a man in chains passed by them. One of the two men said, “If there is not such-and-such in his chain, then his wife is divorced three times.” The other said, “If there is in it as you said, then his wife is divorced three times.” So they went to the master of the slave, who was the one chained, and said to him, “We have sworn regarding such-and-such, so loosen the chain of your غلام so that we may weigh it.” The master of the slave said, “My wife is divorced if I loosen the chain of my غلام.” Then they brought the matter to ʿUmar and related the story to him. ʿUmar said, “His master has more right over him. Take him to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib; perhaps he may have something concerning this matter.” So they came to ʿAlī عليه السلام and told him the story. He said, “How easy this is.” Then he called for a large basin and ordered that a string be tied to the chain. He put the man’s feet and the chain into the basin, then poured water over it until it was full. Then he عليه السلام said, “Lift the chain.” So they lifted the chain until it was brought out of the water, and when it was taken out, the water decreased. Then he called for pieces of iron and cast them into the water until the water returned to its place while the chain was in the water. Then he said, “Weigh this iron; it is its weight.”

Ahmad ibn A'idh narrated from Abu Salamah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two slave men who were authorized to buy and sell with the wealth of their masters. A dispute arose between them, and they fought. Each ran to the master of the other. They were equal in strength. One purchased the other from his master, and the other did the same, purchasing his opponent from his master. Then each of them grabbed the collar of the other, saying, 'You are my slave; I have purchased you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should be judged based on the point where they separated. The path should be measured, and whichever one was closer to his master, he is considered to have reached first and thus has precedence over the one farther away. But if both distances are equal, they are returned to their respective masters.'

And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, he said: Two men entrusted a woman with a deposit and said to her, 'Do not hand it over to either one of us until we both come together before you.' Then they departed and were absent. One of them came to her and said, 'Give me my deposit, for my companion has died.' She refused until his repeated coming to her increased, then she gave it to him. Then the other one came and said, 'Bring me my deposit.' She said, 'Your companion took it and mentioned that you had died.' Then they took the dispute to ʿUmar, and ʿUmar said to her, 'I do not see except that you have become liable.' So the woman said, 'Appoint ʿAlī عليه السلام between me and him.' So he said to him, 'Judge between them.' Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said, 'This deposit is with her, and you both instructed her not to hand it over to either one of you until you both came together before her. So bring me your companion.' And he did not hold her liable. And ʿAlī عليه السلام said, 'They only intended to take away the woman’s wealth.'

And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: During the time of ‘Alī عليه السلام, a man had two female slaves, and both gave birth on the same night, one of them to a son and the other to a daughter. Then the mother of the daughter deliberately placed her daughter in the cradle in which the son had been, and took the son; so the mother of the daughter said, “The son is my son,” and the mother of the son said, “The son is my son.” So they sought judgment from Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام, and he ordered that their milk be weighed, and he said, “Whichever of the two has the heavier milk, then the son belongs to her.”

3250 - Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: A man struck another man on the head during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. The injured man claimed that he could not see anything with his eyes, that he could not smell any scent, and that he had become mute and could not speak. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “If he is truthful, then three full blood-money compensations have become due to him.” It was said to him: “How can that be determined from him, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, so that we may know he is truthful?” He said: “As for what he claims regarding his eyes, that he does not see with them, that is determined by telling him: ‘Raise your eyes toward the disc of the sun.’ If he is sound, he will be unable to refrain from closing his eyes; but if he is truthful, he will not see with them and his eyes will remain open. As for what he claims regarding his nostrils, that he does not smell any scent, that is determined by a burning substance brought near his nose. If he is sound, the smell of the burning substance will reach his brain, his eyes will water, and he will turn his head away. And as for what he claims regarding his tongue of muteness and that he does not speak, that is determined by a needle struck upon his tongue. If he speaks, the blood will come out red; and if he does not speak, the blood will come out black.”

And Sad ibn Tarif narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said: A girl was brought before Umar ibn al-Khattab, and witnesses testified against her that she had committed adultery. Her story was that she was an orphan raised in the house of a man who had a wife. The man would frequently be away from home. The orphan grew up to be beautiful, and the man's wife feared that her husband might marry the orphan upon his return. So, the wife called some women from her wife called some women from her neighbors, restrained her, and then violated her with her finger. When her husband returned, he asked his wife about the orphan, and she accused her of indecency and brought forth witnesses from her neighbors to support her claim. He said: That matter was presented to Umar ibn al-Khattab, but he did not know how to judge it. He said to the man, 'Go with her to Ali ibn Abi Talib.' They came to Ali and told him the story. He said to the man's wife, 'Do you have witnesses?' She said, 'Yes, these are my neighbors who testify against her for what I say.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) drew his sword from its sheath and placed it in front of him. Then he ordered each of the witnesses to be taken into a room. Then he called the man's wife and interrogated her from every angle, but she refused to deviate from her statement, so he sent her back to the room she was in. Then he called one of the witnesses, knelt on his knee, and said to her, 'Do you know me? I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this is my sword. The man's wife has said what she said and returned to the truth, and I have granted her safety. Now speak the truth, or I will fill my sword with your blood.' The woman turned to Ali and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, safety in exchange for the truth.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said to her, 'Speak the truth.' She said, 'No, by Allah, the orphan did not commit adultery. But the man's wife, when she saw her beauty, charm, and appearance, feared the ruin of her husband. So she gave her intoxicants to drink, called us, and we restrained her, and she violated her with her finger.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest! I am the first to separate the witnesses, except for Daniel.' Then Imam Ali sentenced the woman to the punishment for false accusation (hadd al-qadhf), and obligated her and those who assisted her in violating the orphan gir

And Abu Jafar (peace be upon him) said: During the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), a man was found slaughtered in a deserted place, and there was a man holding a knife stained with blood. He was taken to be brought before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and he confessed that he had killed him. Then a man approached them and said, 'Release this one, for I am the one who killed your companion.' He was also taken and brought with his companion before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). When they entered, they recounted the story to him, and he said to the first man, 'What compelled you to confess?' He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, I am a butcher, and I had slaughtered a sheep beside the deserted place. Urination hurried me, so I entered the deserted place with a knife in my hand stained with blood. These people took me and said, Then Ali (peace be upon him) said to the other, 'What do you say?' He said, 'I killed him, O Commander of the Faithful.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Go to my son Hasan so that he may judge between you.' So they went to him and recounted the story to him. He (peace be upon him) said, 'As for this one, if he has killed a man, he has given life to this one (the butcher). And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:

And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: A man died during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and left behind a son and a slave. Each one of them claimed that he was the son and that the other was his slave. So they came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and sought judgment from him. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ordered that two holes be made in the wall of the mosque. Then he ordered each one of them to put his head into a hole, and they did so. Then he said, “O Qanbar, unsheathe the sword,” and he secretly told him, “Do not do what I command you to do.” Then he said, “Strike the neck of the slave.” He said: the slave drew back his head, so Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام seized him and said to the other, “You are the son, and I have freed this one and made him a mawlā for you.”

3254 - And ʿAmr ibn Thābit narrated from his father, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: A woman was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. An old man had married her, and when he had intercourse with her, he died upon her stomach. Then she gave birth to a child, so his sons claimed that she had committed fornication and testified against her. ʿUmar ordered that she be stoned. Then they passed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, and she said: “O cousin of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I am wronged, and this is my proof.” So he said: “Bring your proof.” Then she handed him a document, and he read it. Then he said: “This woman informs you of the day he married her, the day he had intercourse with her, and how his intercourse with her was. Return the woman.” Then when the next day came, ʿAlī عليه السلام called for children of the same age who were playing, and among them was her son. He said to them: “Play.” So they played until, when the play had distracted them, he shouted at them, and they stood up. The boy who was the woman’s son stood up leaning on his palms. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام called him forward, gave him inheritance from his father, and flogged his brothers who had made the false accusation, each one with the prescribed punishment. Then ʿUmar said to him: “How did you do this?” He said: “I recognized the old man’s weakness from the boy’s leaning upon his palms.”

3256 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a woman who came to him and said: “Indeed, my husband had intercourse with my bondwoman without my permission.” So he said to the man, “What do you say?” He said, “I did not have intercourse with her except with her permission.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “If you are truthful, we will stone him; and if you are lying, we will administer the prescribed punishment to you.” And the salat was established, so ʿAlī عليه السلام stood praying. Then the woman reflected within herself, and she saw no relief for herself either in the stoning of her husband or in her receiving the prescribed punishment, so she left and did not return. And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام did not ask about her afterward.

3257 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام judged regarding a man whom two men brought and said: “This man stole a coat of armor.” The man began imploring him when he examined the evidence, and he kept saying: “By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were present, he would never cut off my hand.” He said: “And why?” He said: “My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, would inform him that I am innocent, and so he would declare me innocent through my innocence.” So when ʿAlī عليه السلام saw his imploring him, he called the two witnesses and said to them: “Fear Allah, and do not cut the man’s hand unjustly.” And he adjured them, then said: “Let one of you cut off his hand and let the other hold his hand.” Then when they went forward to the platform to cut off his hand, they struck at the people until they became mixed together. Then when they had become mixed together, they let the man go into the midst of the people, and the two fled until they blended in with the people. Then the man against whom they had testified came and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the two men testified against me unjustly. When they struck the people and they became mixed together, they let me go and fled. Had they been truthful, they would neither have fled nor released me.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Who will direct me to these two witnesses so that I may punish them?”

Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام: That he ruled: “A corrupt young boy should be placed under legal restriction until he becomes rational.” And he عليه السلام ruled regarding debt: “Its holder is imprisoned; then, if his insolvency and need become clear, his way is released for him until he acquires wealth.” And he عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who evades his creditors: “He is imprisoned, then action is ordered concerning him, so his wealth is divided among his creditors according to shares; if he refuses, it is sold and then divided among them.”

Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام. About a man who transfers a debt to another man: can he revert back against him? He عليه السلام said: “He does not revert back against him ever, unless he had become bankrupt before that.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about Umm al-Walad. He said: "She is a slave; she may be sold, inherited, and gifted, and her legal ruling is the ruling of a slave."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Wahb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who married his Umm al-Walad to a slave of his, then the master died. He عليه السلام said: “She has no choice regarding the slave; she is owned by the heirs.”

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Bazanṭī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, he said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies while he has an umm al-walad, and he has a child from her: is it permissible for a man to marry her? He said: I was informed that ʿAlī عليه السلام gave instruction regarding the mothers of children with whom he had relations: whoever among them had a child, she is from the share of her child; and whoever did not have a child, then she is free. And only those among them who had a child were made from the share of their child so that they would not marry except with the permission of their family.

And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, or I heard him say: “A free woman is not compelled to breastfeed the child, but an Umm al-Walad is compelled.”

3511 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from some of them, peace be upon them, who said: Ali, peace be upon him, when a man died and had a wife who was a slave, would purchase her from his estate, emancipate her, and then make her an heir.

ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, “May I ask you?” He said, “Ask.” I said, “Why did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام sell the mothers of children?” He said, “For the freeing of their necks.” I said, “And how was that?” He said, “Any man who bought a bondwoman and she bore him a child, then he did not pay her price and did not leave from the wealth that by which it could be paid on his behalf, her child was taken from her, and she was sold, and her price was paid.” I said, “So is she sold for debt other than that?” He said, “No.”

ʿĀṣim narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Any man who leaves a surriyyah, whether she has a child, or there is a child in her womb, or she has no child, then if her master had freed her, she is freed. But if he did not free her until he died, then the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has already preceded regarding her, and the Book of Allah has greater right. He said: If she has a child and he leaves wealth, she is placed in the share of her child, and the guardians of her child retain her until the child grows up. Then it is the child who frees her, if he wishes. They inherit her child so long as she remains a bondwoman. If her child frees her, she is freed. And if her child dies without having freed her, then if they wish they keep her enslaved, and if they wish they free her. And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who left a bondwoman who had borne him a daughter, while she was young, except that she could express speech; then she freed her mother. The patrons of the father of the bondwoman disputed concerning it, so he validated her freeing of her mother.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Walid ibn Hisham, who said: I came from Egypt with some slaves, and I passed by the tax collector, so he asked me, and I said: They are all free. Then I arrived in al-Madinah and entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and informed him of what I had said to the tax collector. So he said: There is nothing upon you. I said: Among them is a bondwoman with whom I had relations, and she is pregnant. He said: No; is not her child the one by whom she is freed? When her master dies, she becomes from the share of her child.

Safwan ibn Mihran narrated from Amir ibn al-Simt, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who has intercourse with his sister, he said: He is struck with a sword, and whatever it reaches of him, it reaches. If he survives, he is kept permanently in prison until he dies.

Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man and he killed him, he said: “Is the slave of a man anything but like his whip and his sword?” So the master was executed, and the slave was committed to prison.

3263 - Three men were brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام. As for one of them, he restrained a man; then the other came and killed him; and the third was present as an observer, watching them. So ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled regarding the one who was watching that his eyes should be gouged out; and he ruled regarding the one who restrained him that he should be imprisoned until he dies, just as he had restrained him; and he ruled regarding the one who killed that he should be killed.

And in the narration of Hammad from Hariz, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: No one is kept perpetually in prison except three: the one held for a capital case, who is kept until he is executed; the woman who apostasizes from Islam; and the thief after the cutting of the hand and the foot.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: It is upon the Imam to bring out those imprisoned for debt on the day of الجمعة prayer for الجمعة prayer, and on the day of the ʿEid for the ʿEid. Then he should send someone with them, and when they have completed the salat and the ʿEid, he should return them to the prison.

And in the narration of Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said: It is obligatory upon the Imam to imprison the corrupt among the scholars, the ignorant among the physicians, and the bankrupt among those who rent out property. And he عليه السلام said: The Imam's imprisonment after the legal punishment is oppression.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made. Reconciliation is permissible among the Muslims, except a reconciliation that makes a haram matter halal, or makes a halal matter haram.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Regarding two men, each of whom had food with his companion, and neither of them knew how much he had with his companion, each of them said to the other: “What is with you is yours, and what is with me is mine.” So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in that if they both mutually agree and their souls are content.”

3269 - And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated, saying: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A Jewish or Christian man had four thousand dirhams with me, then he died. Is it permissible for me to reach a settlement with his heirs without informing them how much it was? He عليه السلام said: “It is not permissible until you inform them.”

Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Concerning a man who owes a debt until a specified term, then his creditor comes to him and says: “Pay me such-and-such from what is owed to me, and I will remit the rest for you,” or he says: “Pay me part of it, and I will extend the term for you regarding what remains.” So he عليه السلام said: “I do not see any harm in it, so long as he does not add anything to his principal.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Then you shall have your principal sums; you shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged.” .

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who gives known qafiz-measures of wheat which they grind for dirhams; then when the miller has finished grinding it, he pays him the dirhams and a qafiz of it, and this is something they have mutually agreed upon among themselves. He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in it, even if he had not fixed a price with him for that.

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'I was with a judge from the judges of Medina when two men came to him. One of them said: I hired an animal from this man to carry me from such-and-such place to such-and-such place, but it did not deliver me to the destination. The judge asked the owner of the animal: Did you take him to the place? He replied: No, my animal became exhausted and did not reach. The judge said to him: You are not entitled to any fare since you did not deliver him to the place for which you hired your animal.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So I called them both to me and said to the hirer: You are not entitled, O servant of Allah, to take the entire fare of the man's animal. And I said to the other: O servant of Allah, you are not entitled to take the entire fare for your animal, but look at the portion of the journey that remained and the portion that was ridden, and come to an agreement on it.' So they did as instructed.

Mansur ibn Yunus narrated from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I was sitting with a judge, and Abu Ja'far عليه السلام was seated with him, when two men came to him. One of them said: I hired this man's camels to carry goods for me to some mines, and I stipulated that he should bring me into the mine on such-and-such a day, because there is a market there that I fear I may miss. So if I am delayed from that, I would deduct from the hire for every day he detained me such-and-such, and indeed he delayed me from that time for such-and-such a number of days. The judge said: This is an invalid condition; pay him his full hire. So when the man stood up, Abu Ja'far عليه السلام turned to me and said: His condition is valid so long as he does not reduce the whole of his hire.

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning two men who had two dirhams with them: one of them said, "The two dirhams are mine," and the other said, "They are between me and you." So he said, "As for the one who said, 'They are between me and you,' he has admitted that one of the two dirhams is not his and that it belongs to his companion; and the other is to be divided between them."

And 'Abdullah ibn Muskān narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about two men who had wealth, part of which was in their possession and part of which was scattered/absent from them. They divided equally what was in their possession and what was absent. Then, the share of one of them was lost from what was absent from him, while the other received his share in full. I asked: Should he return [compensate] to his partner? He said: 'Yes, so that he does not take all the wealth for himself.'
And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Ibn Ṭarafah: Two men claimed a camel, and each of them presented evidence, so ʿAlī عليه السلام placed it between them.

And in the narration of Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Ala' from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It concerns a man whom another man entrusts with thirty dirhams to buy a garment, and another [man] entrusts him with twenty dirhams for a garment. So he sent the two garments, but this one did not know his garment, nor did that one know his garment. He [the Imam] said: "The two garments are sold, and the owner of the thirty is given three-fifths of the price, and the other is given two-fifths of the price." I said: "What if the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty, 'Choose whichever you wish'?" He [the Imam] said: "He has treated him fairly."

And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who entrusted another man with two dinars, and another entrusted him with one dinar, then one dinar out of them was lost, he said: "The owner of the two dinars is to be given one dinar, and they are to divide the remaining dinar equally between themselves into two halves."

And it is narrated from Ṣabbāḥ al-Muzanī, raising it, that he said: Two men came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. One of them said, "O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, this man and I had a meal together. I brought three loaves of bread, and he brought five loaves of bread. Then we ate lunch, and a man passed by us, so we invited him to the meal. He came and ate with us. When we finished, he gifted us eight dirhams and departed. So I said, 'O this man, divide with me.' He said, 'I will only do so according to the measure of the shares of bread.' He said, 'Go and reconcile between yourselves.' He said, 'O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, he refuses to give me except three dirhams while he takes five dirhams, so decide the judgment for us.'" He said: then he said to him, "O servant of Allah, do you know that three loaves are nine thirds?" He said, "Yes." He said, "And do you know that five loaves are fifteen thirds?" He said, "Yes." He said, "So you ate eight of the nine thirds, and one remained for you. And this man ate eight of the fifteen, and seven remained for him. And the guest ate seven thirds from this man's bread and from your bread this one third that remained from your bread. Thus, each one of you was apportioned eight thirds. So for this man are seven dirhams, in exchange for each third one dirham, and for you, for your one third, is one dirham." "So take one dirham, and give this man seven dirhams."

It is narrated from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about those witnesses whose testimony is rejected, so he said: “The suspected one, the accused one, and the adversary.” He said: I said, “Then what about the immoral one and the dishonest one?” He said: “This falls under the suspected one.”

And in another hadith, he said: The testimony of one under suspicion, the adversary, one repelling a liability, a hired worker, a partner, an accused person, or a subordinate is not valid. And the testimony of a wine-drinker is not accepted, nor the testimony of one who plays chess and backgammon, nor the testimony of a gambler.

And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a group of travelers who were on a road and were ambushed by highway robbers. Then the robbers were seized, and some of them testified for others. So he said: “Their testimony is not accepted except with a confession from the robbers, or testimony against them from others.”
And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The testimony of the Muslim slave is valid against the free Muslim.

3285 - And al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, or he said: one of his companions asked him, about a man testifying for his father, or a brother for his brother, or a man for his wife. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in that if he is righteous. His testimony is accepted for his father, and a father’s for his son, and a brother’s for his brother.”
And in another report: “The testimony of the child against his parent is not accepted.”

3287 - Al-Hasan ibn Zayd narrated something similar to what he mentioned from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn, who had drunk wine. Two men testified against him: one of them was a eunuch, and he was ʿAmr al-Tamīmī, and the other was al-Muʿallā ibn al-Jārūd. One of them testified that he saw him drinking, and the other testified that he saw him vomiting wine. So ʿUmar sent for some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, among whom was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام. He said to ʿAlī عليه السلام, ‘What do you say, O Abū al-Ḥasan? For you are the one about whom the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “The most knowledgeable of this Ummah and the most judicial of it in truth.” These two have differed in their testimony.’ So ʿAlī عليه السلام said, ‘They have not differed in their testimony, and he would not have vomited it until he had drunk it.’ He said, ‘Is the testimony of a eunuch admissible?’ He عليه السلام said, ‘The loss of his testicles is nothing but like the loss of some of his limbs.’”

And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: “The testimony of one who possesses enmity, or one who has disgrace in religion, is not accepted.”
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever testifies before us with a testimony and then changes it, we will take the first and discard the latter."

And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Do not perform salat (prayer) behind one who seeks payment for the adhan and the salat (prayer) with the people, and his testimony is not accepted.

And Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The testimony of the player of nard, the player of al-arbaʿata ʿashar, and the player of chess is not accepted. He says, ‘No, by Allah,’ and ‘Yes, by Allah,’ and ‘By Allah, his king died,’ and ‘By Allah, his king was killed,’ while Allah, exalted is His mention, is his King; He neither died nor was killed.

And Samāʿah ibn Mihrān narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in the testimony of a guest if he is chaste and trustworthy. He said: The testimony of an employee for his employer is disliked, but there is no harm in his testimony for someone else, and there is no harm in it for him after his separation from him.

And Faḍālah narrated from Abān, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about two partners, one of whom testified for the other. He said: “His testimony is valid except regarding something in which he has a share.”

3294 - And it was narrated from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: "The testimony of children is valid among them so long as they have not dispersed or returned to their families."

And Ismaʿil ibn Muslim narrated from al-Sadiq Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAli عليه السلام: That the testimony of children, if they testified while they were young, is valid when they grow older so long as they have not forgotten it. Likewise, the testimony of the Jews and the Christians, if they accept Islam, is valid. And the slave, if he is called to bear testimony and then is emancipated, his testimony is valid if the judge did not reject it before he was emancipated. And he عليه السلام said: “If the slave was emancipated for the sake of the testimony, his testimony is not valid.”

And al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The testimony of a slave from the people of the qiblah is valid against the People of the Book.

And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The testimony of one who rushes ahead of the pilgrims is not accepted, for he has destroyed his mount, exhausted his provisions, wearied himself, and treated his salat (prayer) lightly. It was said: What about the muleteer, the camel driver, and the sailor? So he said: There is no harm in them; their testimony is accepted if they are righteous.

And it was narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A man divorced his wife and had two Nāṣibī witnesses testify. He said: “Everyone who is born upon the fiṭrah and is known for righteousness in himself, his testimony is accepted.”

And it was narrated from ʿUbaydillāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام whether the testimony of Ahl al-Dhimmah is valid against those not from their religion. He عليه السلام said: Yes. If none from the people of their own religion are found, then the testimony of others is valid. Indeed, it is not proper for the right of anyone to be lost.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Ahmad ibn 'Umar, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Two just ones from among you, or two others from outside you." He said: "The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from outside you are from the People of the Book. If you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Apply to them the sunnah of the People of the Book.' And that is when a man dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims to make them witnesses; then two men from the People of the Book [may serve]."

And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Regarding the mukātab, there was a period when people did not stipulate that if he became unable, then he would be returned to slavery. But today they do stipulate this, and the Muslims are bound by their conditions. And he is flogged in the hadd punishment according to the measure of what has been freed of him.” I said: “What do you think—if half of him has been freed, is his testimony in divorce admissible?” He said: “If there is with him a man and a woman, his testimony is admissible.”
And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: Whoever is born upon the fitrah and is known for righteousness in himself, his testimony is valid.

And it was narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the testimony of one who plays with pigeons. He said: “There is no harm, if he is not known for fisq.” I said: Those around us say that ʿUmar said: he is a devil. So he said: “Glory be to Allah! Did you not know that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Indeed, the angels flee at wagering and curse its participant, except in the case of the hoof, the hoofed foot, the feather, and the arrowhead, for the angels attend them.’ And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله raced Usāmah ibn Zayd and set horses running.”

3304 - And it was narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Establish testimony against the parents and the child, but do not establish it against a brother in religion out of harm.” I said: What is harm? He said: “It is when the person entitled to the right transgresses regarding it, in what he claims against him, contrary to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله have commanded. An example of that is when one man has a debt against another while he is in hardship, and Allah, the Exalted, has commanded granting him respite until he becomes able, so He said: “then a respite until ease.” And he asks you to establish testimony while you know his hardship, so it is not permissible for you to establish the testimony in the state of hardship.”

And Mismaʿ Kardīn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning four men who testified against a man for zina, and he was stoned, then one of them retracted and said, “I doubted my testimony.” He عليه السلام said, “The blood money is upon him.” He said: I said, “What if he said: ‘I testified against him deliberately’?” He عليه السلام said, “He is to be executed.”

And Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “I do not act upon the statement of a fortune-teller, nor a tracker, nor a thief, and I do not accept the testimony of the transgressor except against himself.”

And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man said to him: “Tell me, if I see something in a man’s hands, is it permissible for me to testify that it belongs to him?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “But perhaps it belongs to someone else.” He said: “Then from where is it permissible for you to buy it, and it becomes your property, then after ownership you say, ‘It is mine,’ and swear upon it, yet it is not permissible for you to ascribe it to the one from whom its ownership came to you?” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “If this were not permissible, no marketplace for the Muslims would stand.”

And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام: That a man came to testify before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, while his hand and foot had been amputated on the basis of testimony, so he accepted his testimony, and the man had repented and his repentance had become known.

3309 - And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudhayl, from Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about the testimony of women: is it valid in marriage, divorce, or stoning? He said: The testimony of women is accepted in matters that men are not able to look at. It is accepted in marriage if there is a man with them. It is not accepted in divorce nor in blood cases. It is accepted in the hadd of zina when there are three men and two women, and the testimony of two men and four women is not accepted.

And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the testimony of a midwife in childbirth. He said: The testimony of one woman is accepted, and the testimony of women regarding the newborn and virginity is accepted.

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, ruled regarding a boy against whom a woman testified that he had pushed another boy into a well and killed him, so he accepted the testimony of the woman.

And Zurārah narrated from one of them, peace be upon them: Regarding four men who testified against a woman for zinā, and she said, "I am a virgin," so the women examined her and found her to be a virgin, he said: "The testimony of the women is accepted."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: about a woman who testified against a man that he had pushed a boy into a well, and he died. He عليه السلام said: "Upon the man is one-fourth of the blood money of the boy, based on the testimony of the woman."

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid Al-Ṣayrafī, from Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Māḍī, peace be upon him, who said: I wrote to him regarding a man who died, and he had an umm walad, and her master had given her something during his lifetime, then he died. He said: So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “She is entitled to what her master gave her during his lifetime; that is recognized as hers. The testimony concerning that of a man, a woman, and servants who are not accused is accepted.”

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله approved the testimony of women in matters of debt while no man was with them.

3316 - And al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who died and left behind a wife while she was pregnant. She gave birth to a boy after his death, then the boy died after he had fallen to the ground. The woman who received him testified concerning him that he cried out and screamed when he fell to the ground, then died afterward. He عليه السلام said: "It is upon the Imam to approve her testimony regarding one quarter of the boy's inheritance."

And in another narration: If there are two women, their testimony is valid for half of the inheritance. If there are three women, their testimony is valid for three-fourths of the inheritance. And if there are four, their testimony is valid for the entire inheritance.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, ruled on the basis of the testimony of one witness and the oath of the claimant. And he, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Jibril عليه السلام descended upon me with the ruling of the testimony of one witness and the oath of the possessor of the right.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: If the matter were up to us, we would permit the testimony of one man, if goodness is known of him, along with the oath of the claimant, in the rights of people. But as for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the sighting of the crescent moon, then no.
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated that Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, said: If two women testify for the claimant of the right, along with his oath, then it is permissible.

Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم permitted the testimony of women together with the oath of the claimant in a debt case: he swears by Allah that his right is indeed true.”

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja‘far al-Bāqir عليه السلام: Regarding a man who witnesses the accounting between two men, then is called to testify, he عليه السلام said: “If he wishes, he may testify, and if he wishes, he may refrain from testifying.”

And Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Aḥmad ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who witnesses the accounting between two men, then is called to testimony, he said: “He should testify.”

And ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam narrated, saying: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan, peace be upon him, about a man whose wife had become pure from her menstruation, and he said, “So-and-so is divorced,” while people were hearing his words, but he did not say to them, “Bear witness.” Does the divorce take effect upon her? He said: “Yes, this is testimony. Would you leave her suspended?”
So he said. Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Knowledge is testimony when its possessor is wronged."
It is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: The Righteous Servant, peace be upon him, said: “It is not proper for one who is called to a testimony to hold back from it.”

3327 - Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And the witnesses should not refuse when they are called." He عليه السلام said: "Before the testimony." And regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful." He عليه السلام said: "After the testimony."

And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, “A man from among my brothers has testimony with me, but not all of it is accepted by the judges among us.” He said, “If you know that it is true, then validate it in every possible way until his right is established for him.”

Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Whoever conceals testimony, or testifies by it so as to unlawfully shed the blood of a Muslim man or to destroy the wealth of a Muslim man, shall come on the Day of Resurrection with darkness upon his face as far as the eye can see, and on his face will be scars by which the creatures will know him by his name and lineage. And whoever gives a true testimony in order to preserve thereby the wealth of a Muslim man shall come on the Day of Resurrection with light upon his face as far as the eye can see; the creatures will know him by his name and lineage. Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Do you not see that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And establish the testimony for Allah.
And he, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. He said: "His heart is disbelieving."

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding false testimony, who said: If the thing remains present in its very form, it is returned to its owner; and if it is no longer present, he is liable according to the amount of what he caused to be destroyed from the man's property.

And Sama'ah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: False witnesses are flogged as a punishment, and it has no fixed measure; that is left to the Imam. And they are paraded so that they may be recognized and not return to it. He said: I said, 'Then if they repent and reform, will their testimony be accepted afterward?' So he said: If they repent, Allah accepts their repentance, and their testimony is accepted afterward.

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام, when he apprehended a false witness, if he was a stranger, would send him to his own district, and if he was a market man, would send him to his market. Then he would have him paraded around, then imprison him for some days, then let him go.

And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a woman before whom two witnesses testified that her husband had died, so she married, then her first husband came back. He عليه السلام said: She is entitled to the dowry because the latter husband lawfully enjoyed her private part. The two witnesses are to be struck with the prescribed punishment and made liable for the dowry because they deceived the man. Then she must observe the ʿiddah and return to her first husband.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-‘Ala’ and Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام: Concerning two men who testified against an absent man before his wife that he had divorced her, so the woman observed her waiting period and married. Then the absent husband returned and claimed that he had not divorced her, and one of the two witnesses declared himself to have been false. He عليه السلام said: "The latter husband has no claim over her, and the dowry is taken from the one who testified and then retracted, and it is returned to the latter husband. They are to be separated, and she must observe a waiting period from the latter husband, and the first husband must not approach her until her waiting period is completed."

And ʿAlī ibn Maṭar narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Indeed, false witnesses are flogged with a punishment that has no fixed limit; that is up to the Imam. And they are paraded until the people recognize them. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic, is:” “And do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the transgressors, except those who repent.” I said: “By what is his repentance recognized?” He said: “He declares himself false before the heads of the witnesses where he is punished, and he seeks forgiveness from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. So if he does that, then his repentance has become manifest.”

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The speech of a false witness does not end before the judge until he has taken his seat in the Hellfire, and likewise one who conceals testimony.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Mītham narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There is no man who bears false testimony against a Muslim in order to cut off his wealth except that Allah writes for him in its place a warrant to the Fire.

Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from someone who informed him, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them. Regarding witnesses: if they testify against a man and then retract their testimony, and judgment has already been passed against the man, they are held liable for what they testified to and are made to pay compensation. But if judgment has not been passed, their testimony is discarded and the witnesses are not charged anything.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If the صاحبُ الْحَقِّ is satisfied with the oath of the one denying his right, and he asks him to swear, and he swears that he has no right against him, then the oath removes the claimant’s right, and he has no claim. I said: Even if he has just evidence? He said: Yes, even if after making him swear by Allah he were to produce fifty sworn testimonies, he would have no right, for the oath has nullified everything he had previously claimed against him concerning that over which he had made him swear.

3341 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever swears to you by Allah regarding a right, then believe him; and whoever asks you by Allah, then give him. The oath has removed the claimant’s claim, and there is no claim left for him.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say: Indeed, all people are free, except one who acknowledges servitude against himself while he is of sound understanding, whether male slave or bondwoman, and one against whom two witnesses testify to servitude, whether young or old.

And it was narrated from al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Abān, from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Hāshimī, who said: I said to Abū ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام: “A man admitted that he is a slave.” He said: “He is to be held by what he said, or he must return the wealth.”

Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “If a slave becomes blind, then there is no servitude upon him; and if a slave becomes leprous, then there is no servitude upon him.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: If the slave becomes blind, then he is emancipated.

Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding one who mutilated or severely mistreated his slave that he is free. There is no authority for him over him; he is a sāʾibah, free to go and attach himself to whomever he wishes, and if someone guarantees his liability, then he inherits him.
And it is narrated regarding a woman who cut off the breast of her female slave: That she is free, and her mistress has no authority over her.

And Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: Concerning a man who freed part of his slave, he said: “He is entirely free; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has no partner.”

Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: Regarding a man who freed a bondwoman while she was pregnant, but excluded what was in her womb, he said: "The bondwoman is free, and what is in her womb is free, because what is in her womb is part of her."
3523 - And it is narrated from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Is it permissible for a Muslim to free a slave who is a polytheist?” He said, “No.”

Abu al-Bakhtari narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام said: In emancipation, the blind, the one-eyed, and the crippled are not permissible; while the one with a paralyzed limb and the lame are permissible.

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man upon whom is the freeing of a slave, and he wished to free a person: which of the two is better, that he free an elderly old man or a beardless youth? He said: “Free the one who is more self-sufficient. The elderly old man is better than the beardless youth.”

And it is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, who said: I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: The freeing of a slave was obligatory upon me, then a slave of mine escaped, and I do not know where he is. Will his emancipation suffice for me? So he عليه السلام wrote: “Yes.”

And it is narrated from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who has a mamlūk who has run away from him: is it permissible for him to free him in the kaffārah of ẓihār? He said: “There is no harm in it, so long as he has not come to know of his death.”

Shuʿayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام, that he mentioned: That ʿAlī عليه السلام was approached by a people disputing over a mule. Evidence was established for these people that they had bred it at their feeding trough, and they had neither sold it nor gifted it; and evidence was established for those people that they had bred it at their feeding trough, and they had neither sold it nor gifted it. So he عليه السلام ruled for the side with the greater evidence and made them swear an oath.

It is narrated from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said: I said to the Shaykh, meaning Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: Inform me about a man who claims a right against another man, but he has no evidence for what belongs to him. He said: Then the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made. If he swears, then the claimant has no right. And if he refers the oath back to the claimant, and he does not swear, then he has no right. If the one from whom the right is sought has died, and evidence is established against him, then the oath is upon the claimant by Allah, other than Whom there is no god, that so-and-so has indeed died and that his right is indeed upon him. If he swears, otherwise he has no right. Because we do not know; perhaps he had already paid him with evidence whose whereabouts we do not know, or without evidence before death. Therefore, because of that, the oath became binding upon him together with the evidence. And if he makes the claim without evidence, then he has no right, because the one against whom the claim is made is not alive. If he had been alive, he would have been compelled to the oath, or the right, or to refer the oath back. Therefore, because of that, no right is established for him.

3345 - Abu Basir said: And I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who comes to a group of people and claims a house that is in their possession, and he establishes evidence, while the one in whose hand the house is also establishes evidence that he inherited it from his father, and he does not know how its matter was. So he said: "The one of them with the greater evidence is made to swear an oath, and it is handed over to him."

It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said: There is no issue with bearing witness to a woman’s acknowledgment while she is not unveiled, if she is recognized by her person, or someone who knows her is present.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon him: Concerning a man who wished to testify regarding a woman to whom he was not related as a maḥram: is it permissible for him to testify about her from behind a curtain and hear her speech, if two just witnesses testify that she is so-and-so daughter of so-and-so who is asking you to bear witness, and that this is her speech? Or is testimony about her not permissible until she comes forth and he verifies her with his own eyes? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "She should cover her face with a niqab and appear before the witnesses, if Allah wills."

Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that he said: Testimony is invalidated in cases of usury and janaf. If the witnesses say, "We do not know," then let them go; but if they knew, then discipline them with taʿzīr.

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: A man from the Anṣār came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I would like you to bear witness for me concerning date-palms that I have given to my son.” He said: “Do you have any child other than him?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then have you given them as you have given him?” He said: “No.” He said: “Indeed, we, the company of Prophets, do not bear witness to unfair deviation.”

And in the narration of Abī al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: Do not bear witness for one who divorces contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition).

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: If a man testifies based on the testimony of another man, then his testimony is accepted, and it counts as half a testimony. And if two just men testify based on the testimony of one man, then the testimony of one man has been established.

Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him. Indeed, ʿAli, peace be upon him, would not validate the testimony of one man based on the testimony of another man, except the testimony of two men based on the testimony of one man.

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who testified upon the testimony of another man, then the man came and said: “Indeed, I did not make him a witness.” He عليه السلام said: “The testimony of the more upright of the two is accepted, and if their uprightness is equal, his testimony is not accepted.”

Safwan ibn Yahya asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: About a man who made his employee witness a testimony, then parted from him: is his testimony valid after he parts from him? He said: "Yes." I said: Then if a Jew was made witness to a testimony and then embraced Islam, is his testimony valid? He said: "Yes."

3355 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a dhimmī and a slave who are made witnesses to a testimony, then the dhimmī becomes Muslim and the slave is emancipated: is their testimony regarding that to which they had been made witnesses valid? He said: "Yes, if goodness is known from them after that, their testimony is valid."
Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Testimony upon testimony is not valid in a hadd, nor is kafālah valid in a hadd.”

And it was narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from al-Bāqir Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding testimony upon the testimony of a man while he is present in the town, He said: "Yes, even if he is behind a column. That is permissible if he is unable to present it himself due to an excuse that prevents him from attending and presenting it; then there is no harm in establishing testimony upon his testimony."

3358 - And ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: "Have someone bear witness to your testimony who is sincere toward you." They said: "May Allah keep you well, how can it increase or decrease?" He said: "No, rather one who preserves it for you." And testimony upon a testimony upon a testimony is not permissible.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ghurāb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Do not testify to a testimony until you know it as clearly as you know your own palm.

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Suwayd, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام: "These people ask me to testify against my brothers." He عليه السلام said: "Yes, establish the testimony for them, even if you fear harm for your brother."

And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man asks me to bear testimony, and I recognize my handwriting and my seal, but I do not remember anything else, whether little or much. So he عليه السلام said: “If your companion is trustworthy, and you have a trustworthy man with you, then testify for him.”
3364 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “If you bury something in the ground, then have witnesses over it, for it will not return anything to you.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: “The first false testimony given in Islam was the testimony of seventy men when they came to the water of al-Haw'ab and its dogs barked at them. Their female companion wanted to return and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, saying to his wives: Indeed, one of you will be barked at by the dogs of al-Haw'ab while heading to fight my legatee, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. Then seventy men testified before her that this was not the water of al-Haw'ab, so this became the first testimony falsely given in Islam.”
And it was said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “Indeed, Sharik rejects our testimony.” So he said: Do not humiliate yourselves.

Talḥah ibn Zayd narrated from al-Ṣādiq, from his father, peace be upon them. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ruled in favor of shuf'ah so long as it had not been apportioned, meaning divided.

ʿUqbah ibn Khālid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled with shufʿah between partners in lands and dwellings. And he said: 'There is no harm and no reciprocating harm.'

3369 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “When the landmarks are established and the boundaries are defined, there is no shuf'ah. And there is no shuf'ah except for a partner who has not divided the property.”
And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: Ali, peace be upon him, said: "The right of pre-emption is according to the number of men."

And in the narration of Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: “The right of pre-emption is according to the number of men.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no right of pre-emption for a Jew or a Christian, and there is no pre-emption except for a partner who has not yet divided.
And in the narration of Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Pre-emption is not inherited.

And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAli عليه السلام. He said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no preemption in a ship, nor in a river, nor in a road, nor in a mill, nor in a bathhouse.”

3375 - And Ali, peace be upon him, said: “The guardian of the orphan is in the position of his father; he takes the right of preemption for him if he has an interest in it.” He, peace be upon him, said: “The absentee has the right of preemption.”
And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: When the shares are divided, the right of preemption is annulled.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about preemption: to whom it belongs, in what things it applies, whether there is preemption in animals, and how it is. He said: Preemption is obligatory in everything, whether animal, land, or goods, when the property is between two partners and no others, and one of them sells his share; then his partner has more right to it than anyone else. But if they are more than two, then there is no preemption for any one of them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked him about a slave jointly owned among partners, and one of them wanted to sell his share. He said: “He may sell it.” He said: I said, “What if they were two, and one of them wanted to sell his share, but when he proceeded to the sale, his partner said to him, ‘Give it to me’?” He said: “He has more right to it.” Then he, peace be upon him, said: “There is no shuf‘ah in an animal except when the partner in it is one.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who bought a house with slaves, goods, cloth, and jewels, he said: “There is no shuf‘ah for anyone in it.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman upon a house in a property belonging to him, while he had partners in that property. He said: “It is permissible for him and for her, and none of the partners has any right of pre-emption against her.”

Jabir ibn Yazid and Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: Whoever appoints a man as an agent to carry out a matter from among affairs, then the agency remains established permanently until he informs him of withdrawal from it, just as he informed him of entering into it.

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abū Hilāl al-Rāzī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man appointed another man as an agent for the divorce of his wife when she menstruates and then becomes pure, and then the man went away, but afterward a new view occurred to him, so he made witnesses that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do and that he had reconsidered in that matter. He said: "Then let him inform his wife and let him inform the agent."

And it is narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said to another: 'Propose so-and-so to me, and whatever you do of anything you negotiate regarding dowry, or guarantee of anything, or stipulate, then that is acceptable to me and binding upon me.' But he did not bring witnesses to that. So he went and proposed on his behalf, and offered the dowry for him and other than that from what they demanded of him and asked of him. Then when he returned, he denied all of that. He said: 'Half of the dowry is imposed for her against him, on his behalf, and that is because he is the one who caused her right to be lost. So when he did not have her witness against him regarding that which he said to him, it became lawful for her to marry, and she is not lawful for the first one, in what is between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, unless he divorces her, because Allah, the Exalted, says:' “Then retention in a fair manner or release with kindness.” So if he does not do that, then he is sinful in what is between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And the outward ruling is the ruling of Islam, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made it lawful for her to marry.

And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who appointed another as an agent in one of his affairs and had two witnesses testify to that, then the agent arose and went out to carry out the matter, and he said: Bear witness that I have dismissed so-and-so from the agency. So he said: If the agent executed the matter for which he had been appointed before he was dismissed from the agency, then the matter is established and effective according to what the agent executed, whether the principal disliked it or was pleased. I said: If the agent carried out the matter before he came to know of the dismissal, or before word reached him that he had been dismissed from the agency, then is the matter according to what he carried out? He said: Yes. I said: Then if notice of dismissal reached him before he executed the matter, and he then went and carried it out, would that be of no effect? He said: Yes. Indeed, when an agent is appointed and then rises from the session, his authority remains effective forever, and the agency remains established until notice of dismissal from the agency reaches him through a trustworthy person who informs him, or he is directly addressed with the dismissal from the agency.

Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding a man to whom a woman entrusted her affair—whether a relative or a neighbor—and he did not know the hidden reality of her condition, then he found that she had concealed a defect that was in her, he said: “The mahr is taken from her, and there is nothing upon the one who married her off.” And he said concerning a woman who entrusted her affair to a man and said, “Marry me to so-and-so.” He said, “I will not marry you until you testify that your affair is in my hand.” So she testified for him. Then at the time of the marriage contract he said to the one proposing to her, “O so-and-so, upon you is such-and-such and such-and-such.” He said, “Yes.” Then he said to the people, “Bear witness that that is due to her from me, and I have married her to myself.” So the woman said, “I would never marry you—no honor at all—and my affair is only in my own hand. I only entrusted you with my affair out of modesty in speech.” He said: “She is removed from him, and his head is to be struck.”

3387 - And in the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who collected the dowry of his daughter from her husband and then died: does she have the right to demand her dowry from her husband, or is her father's receipt considered her own receipt? So he عليه السلام said: "If she had authorized him to collect her dowry from her husband, then she has no right to demand it. But if she had not authorized him, then she has that right, and the husband may seek recovery of that from her father's heirs, unless she was at that time a minor under his care; then it is permissible for her father to collect her dowry on her behalf. And whenever he divorces her before consummation, then her father may waive part of the dowry and take part of it, but he has no right to leave all of it. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:" “Except that they forgo, or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie forgives.” Meaning the father, and the one whom the woman authorizes and entrusts with her affair, whether a brother, a relative, or someone else."

3388 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from someone who informed him, from Hariz, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The first upon whom lots were cast was Maryam bint 'Imran, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Maryam. And the lots were six. Then they cast lots concerning Yunus عليه السلام when he embarked with the people, and the ship was caught in the deep waters. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus three times. He said: Then Yunus عليه السلام went to the front of the ship, and there was the whale with its mouth open, so he cast himself in. Then 'Abd al-Muttalib had nine sons, so he vowed regarding the tenth that if Allah granted him a boy, he would sacrifice him. When 'Abd Allah was born, he was not able to sacrifice him, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was in his loins. So he brought ten camels and cast lots between them and 'Abd Allah, and the lots came out against 'Abd Allah. Then he added ten more. The lots continued to come out against 'Abd Allah, and he kept adding ten, until when they reached one hundred, the lots came out against the camels.
