Then 'Abd al-Muttalib said, 'I have not done justice to my Lord,' so he repeated the lots three times, and they came out against the camels. He said, 'Now I know that my Lord is pleased,' so he slaughtered them.

3389 - It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥakīm, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a matter, and he said to me, "For every unknown matter, there is qurʿah (casting lots) in it." So I said, "Indeed, qurʿah may miss and may be correct." Then he said, "Everything by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has judged is not mistaken."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: No people cast lots and then entrusted their matter to Allah, the Exalted, except that the lot of the rightful one came out.

And he, peace be upon him, said: “What judgment is more just than the casting of lots when the matter is entrusted to Allah?” “Does not Allah, the Exalted, say: ‘So he cast lots, and he was among the losers’?”

Al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If two or three men have intercourse with a bondwoman in one period of purity, then she gives birth, and all of them claim the child, the ruler draws lots between them. Whoever is selected by the lot, the child is his, and he returns the value of the child to the owner of the bondwoman. He said: If a man buys a bondwoman, then another man comes and rightfully establishes his claim to her, and she has given birth from the buyer, the bondwoman is returned to him, and her child belongs to the buyer for its value.

Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Two men disputed before ʿAlī عليه السلام over a beast, and each one of them claimed that it was born at his manger. Each one of them produced evidence equal in number. So he drew lots between them with two lots, and he marked the two lots for each one of them with a distinguishing sign, then he said: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, Lord of the seven earths, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful, whichever of the two is the owner of the beast and has the stronger right to it, I ask You to bring forth his lot. Then the lot of one of them came out, so he judged it to belong to him.

Al-Bazanti narrated from Dawood ibn Sirhan, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning two men who testified against a man regarding a matter, then two others came and testified to something other than that to which the first two had testified, he said: “Lots are drawn between them; whichever of them is selected by lot, upon him is the oath, and he has greater right to the judgment.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who said, “The first slave I come to own is free,” then he inherited seven all together. He عليه السلام said: “Lots are drawn among them, and the one whose lot comes out is set free.”

And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who has slaves and then wills the freeing of one-third of them. He said: "ʿAlī عليه السلام used to draw lots among them."

Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: ʿAlī عليه السلام, when two men came to him disputing, with witnesses whose number was equal and whose integrity was equal, would cast lots between them as to which of them the oath would fall upon, and he would say: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, whoever the right belongs to, deliver it to him. Then he would assign the right to the one upon whom the oath fell, if he swore.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a newborn who has neither what belongs to males nor what belongs to females. He said: For this one, the Imam conducts a lot-drawing. He writes on one lot: ʿAbdullāh, and on another lot: Amatullāh. Then the Imam, or the one drawing the lot, says: O Allah, You are Allah, there is no god but You... Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that wherein they used to differ. Make clear to us the matter of this newborn, so that he may inherit what You have ordained for him in Your Book. Then he places the two lots among unspecified lots, then they are mixed; whichever of the two comes out, inheritance is assigned according to it.

And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent ‘Alī عليه السلام to Yemen, and when he returned, he said to him: “Tell me of the most astonishing matter that came before you.” He said: “O Messenger of Allah, some people came to me who had jointly bought a slave-girl, then they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, and she gave birth to a boy. They disputed regarding him, each of them claiming him. So I cast lots among them, three times, and assigned him to the one whose lot came out, and I made him liable for their shares.” Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no people who draw lots and entrust their affair to Allah except that the lot of the one who is in the right comes forth.”

Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf narrated from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who guaranteed the person of another man that he should be detained, and he said to him: “Seek your companion.” And he عليه السلام ruled: “There is no kafalah in a hadd.”

Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام: Regarding two men between whom there is property: some of it is in their possession and some of it is absent from them. They divided what was in their possession, and each one assigned his share. Then one of them received his share, while the other did not receive his. He said: Whatever one of them receives is between them both, and whatever is lost is between them both.

And it is narrated: When ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan was at the point of death, his creditors gathered before him and demanded a debt owed to them. He said: “I do not have anything to give you, but be satisfied with whomever you wish from my brother and my cousin, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn or ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar.” The creditors said: “As for ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar, he is wealthy but delays payment. As for ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, he is a man with no wealth, but truthful, and he is more beloved of the two to us.” So they sent to him and informed him of the matter. He, عليه السلام, said: “I guarantee the money for you until a harvest,” though he had no harvest. The people said: “We are satisfied.” So he guaranteed it, and when the harvest came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided him with wealth, and he paid it.

3401 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said to Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik: “What has prevented you from hajj (pilgrimage)?” He said: “A guarantee that I undertook.” He عليه السلام said: “What have you to do with guarantees? Do you not know that the guarantee is what destroyed the earlier generations?”

Abu Ayyub asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who transfers a debt to another man by means of property: can recourse be made against him? He said: No, recourse is never made against him at all, unless he had already become bankrupt before that.

And it is narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said: I said to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, “May I be your ransom,” regarding the people’s saying: “The guarantor is liable.” So he عليه السلام said: “There is no liability upon the guarantor; liability is only upon the one who consumed the wealth.”

Al-Bazanti narrated from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who had dinars owed to him by another man, and he transferred him to another man for his dinars, so he takes dirhams with them. Is that permissible? He said: "Yes."

And Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who guarantees another man's person until a specified term, such that if he does not bring him, then such-and-such dirhams are upon him. He عليه السلام said: If he brings him by the appointed term, then what he mentioned is not upon him, and he remains guarantor of his person forever unless he begins with the dirhams. So if he begins with the dirhams, then he is liable for them if he does not bring him by the term that he set.
Dawud ibn Sirhan asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: About a guarantor and a pledge in a deferred sale, He said: "There is no harm in it."
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Guarantorship is loss, liability, and regret.

Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Abu Abdullah, from his forefathers, from Ali عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled regarding the floodwaters of the Valley of Mahzur that the upper land should retain the water over the lower land: for crops until it reaches the level of the sandal strap, and for palm trees until it reaches the ankle; then the water should be released to the lower land beyond that.
And in another report: For crops, up to the two sandal straps, and for palm trees, up to the two shins.

Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about an enclosure between two houses. So he mentioned: "That ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that it belongs to the owner of the house on whose side the boundary rope is."

And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī, peace be upon him. That he gave judgment concerning two men who disputed before him over a reed enclosure, and he said: “The reed enclosure belongs to the one on whose side the binding cords are attached.”

3414 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: "And Dawud and Sulayman, when they were judging concerning the field, when the sheep of the people strayed into it." He عليه السلام said: "They did not pass judgment; rather, they were discussing the matter: 'So We gave Sulayman understanding of it.'"

3415 - Al-Washsha' narrated from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And Dāwūd and Sulaymān, when they judged concerning the field." He عليه السلام said: "The judgment of Dāwūd عليه السلام was the ownership of the sheep, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Sulaymān عليه السلام understand was that he judged for the owner of the field by granting him the milk and wool for that entire year."

Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled regarding a man who sold his palm trees but excluded one palm tree. He ruled that he had the right of access to it for entry and exit, and the extent of its fronds.

Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام used to say: The protected area around an ancient well is fifty cubits, unless it is toward a watering place or toward a road; then it is less than that, up to twenty-five cubits.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The protected area of a palm tree is the length of its fronds.

And it has been narrated: "The protected area (harim) of a mosque is forty cubits from every side, and the protected area (harim) of a believer in the summer is a span." And it has been narrated: "The length of a cubit."

And ʿUqbah ibn Khālid narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who came to a mountain and split from it a channel whose water flowed for a year. Then another man came to that mountain and split from it another channel, and the channel of the latter carried away the water of the channel of the former. He عليه السلام said: 'They are to be measured by the water-skins of the well, night by night, and it is to be examined which of them has harmed its counterpart. If the later one has harmed the first, then it should be blocked.' And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم judged accordingly and said: 'If the first one took the water of the later one, then the owner of the later one has no claim against the first.'

He عليه السلام was asked about a group of people who had springs in land close to one another. One man wanted to make his spring lower than its original place, and some springs, when that is done to them, harm the others, while some do not cause harm because of the firmness of the land. So he عليه السلام said: Whatever is in a hard, firm place does not harm it, and whatever is in loose, level soil, then it does cause harm.
And he, peace be upon him, said: There should be between the two wells, if the land is solid, five hundred cubits; and if it is loose, then one thousand cubits.

Al-Hasan al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Samurah ibn Jundub had a date-palm tree in the garden of a certain family. Whenever he came to his tree, he would look at something of the man's household that the man disliked." He said: "So the man went to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and complained about him. He said: O Messenger of Allah, Samurah enters upon me without my permission, so if you would send to him and order him to seek permission, so that my family may take precautions against him. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم sent for him and called him, and said: O Samurah, what is the matter with so-and-so complaining of you and saying that you enter without my permission and then see of his family what he dislikes? O Samurah, seek permission when you enter." Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Would it please you to have a cluster in Paradise in exchange for your palm tree?" He said: No. He said: "You shall have three." He said: No. He said: "I see you, O Samurah, as nothing but one who causes harm. Go, O so-and-so, cut it down and strike his face with it."

A Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and claimed against him seventy dirhams as the price of a she-camel he had sold to him. He said, “I have already paid you.” The Bedouin said, “Appoint between me and you a man who will judge between us.” Then a man from Quraysh came forward, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “Judge between us.” He said to the Bedouin, “What do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him.” He said, “What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “I have paid him.” He said to the Bedouin, “What do you say?” He said, “He has not paid me.” He then said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, “Do you have evidence that you have paid him?” He said, “No.” He said to the Bedouin, “Will you swear that you have not received your due and then take it?” He said, “Yes.” Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “I shall certainly seek judgment with this man before one who will judge between us by the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, came to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, with the Bedouin. ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said, “What is the matter, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “O Abū al-Ḥasan, judge between me and this Bedouin.” Then ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said, “O Bedouin, what do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him.” He said, “What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “I have paid him its price.” He said, “O Bedouin, has the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, spoken the truth in what he said?” He said, “No, he has not paid me anything.” So ʿAlī, peace be upon him, drew his sword and struck his neck. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “Why did you do that, O ʿAlī?” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, we affirm your truthfulness regarding the command of Allah and His prohibition, and regarding Paradise and the Fire, reward and punishment, and the revelation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and should we not affirm your truthfulness concerning the price of this Bedouin’s she-camel? I killed him because he declared you false when I said to him, ‘Has the Messenger of Allah spoken the

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Baḥr al-Shaybānī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: Abū Ayyūb al-Kūfī narrated to us; he said: Isḥāq ibn Wahb al-ʿAllāf narrated to us; he said: Abū ʿĀṣim al-Nabbāl narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came out from the house of ʿĀʾishah, and a Bedouin met him while he had with him a she-camel. He said: “O Muḥammad, will you buy this she-camel?” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Yes. For how much will you sell it, O Bedouin?” He said: “For two hundred dirhams.” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Rather, your she-camel is better than this.” He said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم continued increasing the price until he bought the she-camel for four hundred dirhams. He said: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم handed the dirhams to the Bedouin, the Bedouin stretched his hand to the reins of the she-camel and said: “The she-camel is my she-camel, and the dirhams are my dirhams. If Muḥammad has any claim, then let him produce the evidence.” He said: Then a man came forward, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Do you accept the elder who is approaching?” He said: “Yes, O Muḥammad.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Will you judge regarding what is between me and this Bedouin?” He said: “Speak, O Messenger of Allah.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The she-camel is my she-camel, and the dirhams are the dirhams of the Bedouin.” The Bedouin said: “Rather, the she-camel is my she-camel, and the dirhams are my dirhams. If Muḥammad has any claim, then let him produce the evidence.” The man said: “The case in this is clear, O Messenger of Allah, and that is because the Bedouin has asked for evidence.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: “Sit.” So he sat. Then another man came forward, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Do you accept, O Bedouin, the elder who is approaching?” He said: “Yes, O Muḥammad.” So when he drew near, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Judge between me and the Bedouin.” He said: “Speak, O Messenger of Allah.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The she-camel is my she-camel, and the dirhams are the dirhams of the Bedouin.” The Bedouin said: “Rather, the she-camel is my she-camel, and the dirhams are my dir

Muhammad ibn Bahr al-Shaybani narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Dhuhli, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Naysaburi narrated to us; he said: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' al-Himsi narrated to us; he said: Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Dhuhli, who said: 'Umara ibn Khuzayma ibn Thabit narrated to me that his uncle narrated to him, and he was among the companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, purchased a horse from a Bedouin. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, then hurried in walking to pay him the price of his horse, but the Bedouin delayed. Men began approaching the Bedouin and bargaining with him over the horse, not realizing that the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, had already bought it, until some of them offered the Bedouin more than the agreed price. So the Bedouin called out and said: 'If you are buying this horse, then buy it; otherwise I will sell it.' When the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, heard the Bedouin, he stood and said: 'Have I not already bought it from you?' People then gathered around the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and the Bedouin while the two were disputing. The Bedouin said: 'Bring a witness to testify that I have sold it to you.' Whoever came from among the Muslims said to the Bedouin: 'Indeed, the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, would not speak except truthfully.' Then Khuzayma ibn Thabit came, listened to the exchange between the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and the Bedouin, and Khuzayma said: 'I bear witness that you have sold it to him.' The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, turned to Khuzayma and said: 'On what basis do you testify?' He said: 'By affirming your truthfulness, O Messenger of Allah.' So the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, made the testimony of Khuzayma ibn Thabit equal to two testimonies and named him Dhū al-Shahādatayn.

3428 - Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: That ʿAlī عليه السلام was in the Masjid of Kūfah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Qufl al-Taymī passed by him carrying Ṭalḥah's coat of mail. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “This is Ṭalḥah's coat of mail; it was taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah.” Ibn Qufl said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, appoint between me and yourself the judge whom you have approved for the Muslims.” So he appointed Shurayḥ between him and him. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “This is Ṭalḥah's coat of mail; it was taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah.” Shurayḥ said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, bring proof for what you say.” So he brought to him al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, and he testified that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah. Shurayḥ said: “This is one witness, and I do not judge by one witness unless another is with him.” Then he brought Qanbar, and he testified that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah. He said: “This is a slave, and I do not judge by the testimony of a slave.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام became angry and said: “Take the coat of mail, for this one has judged unjustly three times.” So Shurayḥ moved away from his seat and said: “I will not judge between two people until you inform me from where I judged unjustly three times.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him: “When I told you that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah, you said: ‘Bring proof for what you say,’ though the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘Wherever ghulūl is found, it is taken without proof.’ So I said: ‘A man who has not heard the hadith.’ Then I brought you al-Ḥasan and he testified, but you said: ‘This is one witness, and I do not judge by one witness unless another is with him,’ while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم judged by one witness and an oath; so those are two. Then I brought you Qanbar and he testified, but you said: ‘This is a slave,’ while there is no harm in the testimony of a slave when he is just; so this is the third.” Then he عليه السلام said: “O Shurayḥ, the Imam of the Muslims is entrusted in their affairs with what is greater than this.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “So the first one who rejected the testimony of the slave was Rumaʿ.”

Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd narrated from his brother Ja'far ibn 'Isa, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom. A woman dies, and her father claims that he had lent her some of the goods and servants that were with her. Is his claim accepted without evidence, or is his claim not accepted except with evidence?” So he عليه السلام wrote: “It is accepted without evidence.” He said: I also wrote to Abu al-Hasan, meaning 'Ali ibn Muhammad عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom. If the deceased woman’s husband, or her husband’s father, or her husband’s mother, claims regarding her goods or her servants something like what her father claimed, namely the loan of some goods and servants, are they in the same position as the father in the claim?” So he عليه السلام wrote: “No.”

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā al-Nakhkhās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If a man divorces his wife, and she claims that the belongings are hers while he claims that the belongings are his, then he is entitled to what belongs to men, and she is entitled to what belongs to women." And it has also been narrated: "The woman has a greater right to the belongings, because those within her region may know that a woman brings belongings with her to her husband's house."

Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام: About a man who frees his slave as a delayed emancipation and then becomes in need of his price. He said: "He may sell him." He said: I said, "Then if he has no need of his price?" He said: "If the slave agrees, then there is no harm."
Jamil narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the mudabbar: may he be sold? He said: If his owner needs his price and the owned slave is satisfied, then there is no harm.

It is narrated from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) Regarding a man who frees his male or female slave as a mudabbar (to be freed after his death) from himself, and then he needs the price of the slave: Does he sell him? He said: 'No, unless he stipulates to the one from whom he sells him that he must free him at the time of his death.'

Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام was asked about a woman who made a bondwoman of hers mudabbar. Then the bondwoman gave birth to a precious slave-girl, and it was not known whether she was mudabbar like her mother or not. So he said: “When did the pregnancy occur—while she was mudabbar, or before the tadbir?” I said: “May I be your ransom, I do not know. Answer me regarding both cases together.” He said: “If the bondwoman was pregnant before the tadbir, and what was in her womb was not mentioned, then the bondwoman is mudabbar, while what is in her womb remains in bondage. But if the tadbir was before the pregnancy, and then the pregnancy occurred, then the child is mudabbar along with his mother, because the pregnancy only occurred after the tadbir.”

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who made a bondwoman mudabbar while she was pregnant, and he said: "If he knew of the bondwoman's pregnancy, then what is in her womb has the same status as her. But if he did not know, then what is in her womb remains in bondage." He said: And I asked him about a man who makes a slave mudabbar while he is well-off, then later becomes needy; is it permissible for him to sell him? He said: "Yes, if he needs that."

And it is narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: The mudabbar is from the one-third, and a man has the right to retract regarding his one-third, whether he made a bequest in health or illness.

Abān narrated from Abī Maryam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who emancipates his bondwoman by tadbīr, whether he may have relations with her if he wishes, or marry her off, or sell her service during his lifetime. He said: "Yes, whichever of that he wishes, he may do."

And 'Asim narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a male slave and a female slave who are emancipated by tadbir. He said: The master may make a mukatabah contract with him if he wishes, and he does not have the right to sell him unless the slave wishes that he sell him during the term of his life. And he may take his property if he has property.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: About a woman who freed one-third of her servant at the time of her death: are her heirs required to enter into a mukātabah contract with her if they wish, or if they refuse? He said: "No. Rather, she owns one-third of herself, and the heir owns two-thirds of her. He may use her services in proportion to the share he has in her, and she has autonomy over herself in proportion to what has been emancipated of her."

Aban narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: I asked him about a man who said to his slave, "If something happens to me, then he is free," while the man is obliged to free a slave as expiation for an oath or ẓihār. Is it permissible for him to free his slave—the one for whom he assigned emancipation if something happens to him—as the expiation for that oath? He said: "It is not permissible—the one whom he has designated for that in this matter."

Wuhayb ibn Hafs narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made his slave mudabbar while he was in debt, fleeing from the debt. He عليه السلام said: “There is no tadbir for him; but if he made him mudabbar in a state of health and well-being, then the creditors have no claim over him.”

Hadith 3467 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who made a slave of his a mudabbar, and he was a merchant of means. Then the mudabbar bought a bondwoman by the order of his master, and she bore him children. Then the mudabbar died before his master. He عليه السلام said: “I hold that all that the mudabbar left behind of goods or estates belongs to the one who made him mudabbar. And I hold that the mother of his child remains a slave belonging to the one who made him mudabbar. And I hold that her children are mudabbar in the same state as their father; so when the one who made their father mudabbar dies, they are free.”
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “The one emancipated by tadbīr is from the one-third. And whatever offense he commits, he, the mukātab, and the umm al-walad, then the master is liable for their offense.”

Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام: He عليه السلام was asked about a man who saw a bird and followed it until it landed on a tree. Then another man came and took it, so he said: "What the eye saw belongs to the eye, and what the hand took belongs to the hand."

ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Warrāq, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the mute person: how does he swear an oath when a debt is claimed against him and the claimant has no evidence? He said: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was presented with a mute person against whom a debt was claimed. He denied it, and the claimant had no evidence against him. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: ‘Praise belongs to Allah, who has not taken me out of the world until I have clarified for the community all that it needs.’” Then he said: “Bring me a muṣḥaf.” It was brought to him. He said to the mute person: “What is this?” So he raised his head toward the sky and gestured that it was the Book of Allah. Then he said: “Bring me his guardian.” So they brought his brother to him, and he seated him beside himself. Then he said: “O Qanbar, bring me an inkpot and a tray.” He brought them both. Then he said to the mute person’s brother: “Tell your brother: this is between you and him; indeed it is ʿAlī.” So he conveyed that to him. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام wrote: “By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful, the seeker, the prevailing, the one who harms, the one who benefits, the destroyer, the one who reaches, the one who knows the secret and the open—indeed so-and-so son of so-and-so, the claimant, has no right and no claim whatsoever against so-and-so son of so-and-so, meaning the mute person, in any way among the ways and for any cause among the causes.” Then he washed it and ordered the mute person to drink it, but he refused, so he made the debt binding upon him.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whoever frees a believing slave, Allah will free a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of the slave. And if it is a female slave, Allah will free one limb of his from the Fire for every two limbs of hers, because a woman is half of a man.
Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: It is recommended for a man to draw near on the evening of Arafah and the Day of Arafah through emancipation and charity.

It is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, Abū al-ʿAbbās, and ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man comes to own his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, or his brother’s daughter, or his sister’s daughter—and he mentioned the women of this verse—then they all become free. A man may own his paternal uncle, his brother’s son, his sister’s son, and his maternal uncle; but he may not own his mother through nursing, nor his sister, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt. If he comes to own them, they are emancipated. He عليه السلام said: Whatever is prohibited among women by lineage is likewise prohibited by nursing. And he عليه السلام said: He may own males except the father and the son, and he may not own any woman who is a mahram. I said: And does the same apply in nursing? He عليه السلام said: Yes, the like of that applies in nursing.

And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a bondwoman who was between two owners, and one of them emancipated his share, he عليه السلام said: “If he is financially capable, he is required to guarantee compensation. And if he is financially incapable, she is made to serve according to the shares.”

And Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a slave who was jointly owned by two men. One of them freed his half while the slave was still a child, and the other retained ownership of his half. He said: "He shall be valued at the worth of the day the first [owner] freed [his share], and the freed slave is ordered to work to pay off the half that was not freed until he fulfills it."

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about two men who jointly have a female slave. One of them frees his half, and the slave says to the one who did not free his half, “I do not want you to appraise me; leave me as I am, and I will serve you,” while he wanted to marry the other half of her. He عليه السلام said: “It is not proper for him to do that, for a woman cannot have two private parts. Nor is it proper for him to keep her in service; rather, he should appraise her and have her work to pay off the remaining share.”

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about two men between whom there was a slave, and one of them emancipated his share. He عليه السلام said: "If he was acting to cause harm, he will be required to emancipate all of him. Otherwise, the slave is to be made to work for the other half."

And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man inherited a slave, and he has partners in him, so he freed his share for the sake of Allah. He عليه السلام said: If he frees his share to cause harm, while he is financially capable, he is liable to compensate the heirs. But if he frees his share for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then the portion of the one who freed is emancipated from the slave, and they use him in proportion to what they own in him. So if half of him remains, he works for them one day and has one day for himself. And if the partner frees his share harmfully, then there is no emancipation for him, because he intended to corrupt matters against the people, and the people revert to their shares.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There is no valid emancipation except that by which the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is intended.

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a man who has a bondwoman and says, “Whenever I approach her, she is free,” then he sells her to another man and later buys her back. He said: “There is no harm in approaching her; she has gone out of his ownership.”

And it is narrated from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about a man who said to three of his slaves, “You are free,” while he had four. Then a man from among the people said to him, “You have freed your slaves.” He said, “Yes.” Is the emancipation binding for all four when he spoke of them generally, or is it for the three whom he freed? He said: “Emancipation is binding only for those whom he freed.”

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. Regarding a man who married his bondwoman to another man and stipulated for him that whatever child she gave birth to would be free; then her husband divorced her or died, so he married her to another man. What is the status of her child? He عليه السلام said: 'The child is in her status. He only made that stipulation for the first one, and with respect to the latter he has the choice: if he wishes, he may emancipate, and if he wishes, he may retain.'
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: There is no divorce before marriage, and there is no emancipation before ownership.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked him about a man who said: to his غلام, “I will free you on the condition that I marry you to this bondwoman of mine. Then if you marry in addition to her or take a concubine, one hundred dinars will be due from you.” So he freed him upon that condition, then he married or took a concubine. Is one hundred dinars due from him, and is his condition valid? He said: “His condition is binding upon him.”

And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Concerning a man who freed his slave on the condition that he marry him to his daughter, and stipulated upon him that if he married another woman or took a concubine besides her, then such-and-such would be due from him. He said: “It is permissible.”

Jamil narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who emancipated a slave who had wealth: to whom does the slave's wealth belong? He said: "If he knew that he had wealth, then his wealth followed him; otherwise, it belongs to the emancipator." And regarding a man who sold a slave who had wealth, he said: "If his master who sold him knew that he had wealth, then the wealth belongs to the buyer; and if the seller did not know, then the wealth belongs to the seller."

Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: If a man has a slave and frees him, knowing that he has wealth, and the master did not exclude the wealth at the time he freed him, then it belongs to the slave.

And Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah asked him about a man who freed his slave, and the slave had wealth. Then the man who freed the slave passed away. To whom does the wealth of the slave belong? Does it go to the one who freed the slave, or does it belong to the slave? He said: "If he freed him knowing that he had wealth, then the wealth belongs to him. But if he did not know, then the wealth belongs to the children of his master."

Jamil narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who emancipated his slave at the time of his death while he had a debt, he said: “If the value of the slave is equal to what he owes and the like of it, his emancipation is valid; otherwise, it is not valid.”

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: Regarding a man who says, "If I die, then my slave is free," while the man has a debt, he said: "If he dies while he has a debt that has encompassed the price of the slave, the slave is sold. And if it has not encompassed the price of the slave, the slave is made to work toward repaying the debt of his master, and he is free by it when he has fully paid it."

Muḥammad ibn Marwān narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: My father, peace be upon him, left sixty slaves and instructed that one-third of them be freed. So I cast lots among them, brought out twenty, and then freed them.

And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a man who left a slave among several people, and one of them testified that the deceased had emancipated him. He said: If the witness is trustworthy, he is not liable to compensate, and his testimony is accepted regarding his own share; and the slave is made to work concerning what belonged to the heirs.
Sa‘īd ibn Yasār narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in emancipating the child of zina.

And ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: “A bondwoman of mine committed adultery; may I sell her child?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “May I perform hajj with its price?” He said: “Yes.”

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about the child of zina: may he be bought, sold, or employed for service? He عليه السلام said: "Yes, except for a foundling girl, for she is not to be bought."

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The abandoned child is free. If he wishes, he may assign his allegiance to those who raised him, and if he wishes, to others.

And in the narration of al-Muthannā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If the one who raised him seeks repayment for his maintenance, and he is financially capable, it is to be repaid to him. But if he is not financially capable, then what was spent is charity.

And Zurarah narrated from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, that he said: Regarding a foundling who was found, he said: "She is free and is not bought nor sold. And if a child is born to you from illicit intercourse, then keep him or sell him if you wish; he is your slave."
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: The runaway slave's salat (prayer) is not accepted until he returns to his master.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: If a slave runs away but does not leave his city, he is not considered a runaway.

Zayd al-Shahham narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who fears the absconding of his slave, or that the slave had already absconded: should he shackle him or place a mark on his neck? He said: "He is only in the position of a camel whose bolting is feared. So if you fear that, then secure him well, feed him fully, and clothe him." I said: "And how much is his fill?" He said: "As for us, we provide our dependents with two mudd of dates."

Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a bondwoman who was mudabbarah, who had absconded from her master for years, then came after her master had died with children and much property; and two witnesses testified for her that her master had made her mudabbarah during his lifetime before she absconded. He said: "I hold that all that is with her belongs to the heirs." I said: "And is she not freed from one-third of her master's estate?" He said: "No. She absconded in disobedience to Allah and to her master, so absconding invalidated the tadbīr."

Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: That ʿAlī عليه السلام was appealed to in a dispute concerning a man who had taken a runaway slave, and he remained with him, then escaped from him. He said: "He is to swear by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that he did not strip him of his clothes, nor anything from what was upon him, nor sell him, nor collude in sending him off. Then if he swears, he is cleared of liability."

Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim al-Darimi narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, that Ali عليه السلام said: Regarding the reward for the runaway slave: “Indeed, the Muslim is returned to the Muslim.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding a man who captured a runaway slave and then it escaped from him, he said: “There is nothing upon him.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who found an animal that had been stolen from a neighbor of his, so he took it in order to bring it back to him, but it died. He said: “There is nothing upon him.”

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, when a slave absconds from his masters and then steals, his hand is not cut off while he is a fugitive, because he is in the position of an apostate from Islam. Rather, he is called to return to his masters and to enter into Islam. Then if he refuses to return to his masters, his hand is cut off for the theft, then he is killed. And the apostate, if he steals, is in the same position.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abū Ḥabīb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, while the seller had two slaves. He said to the buyer, 'Take them both, then choose one of them and return the other,' after having already received the payment. Then the buyer took them both, and one of them absconded from his possession. He said: 'He should return the one that remains with him from the two, and take back half of the price that he paid from the seller, and go in search of the غلام. If he finds him, he may choose whichever of the two he wishes and return the other. But if he does not find him, then the remaining slave is to be between them: half of him belongs to the seller and half to the buyer.'

And it is narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Write for the runaway slave on a piece of paper or on parchment: ‘In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.’” “The hand of so-and-so is bound to his neck; when he brings it out, he can hardly see it. And whomever Allah has not made a light for, for him there is no light.” Then wrap it, then place it between two sticks, then cast it into a dark niche of the house in the place where he used to stay.

And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Supplicate with this supplication for the absconding slave, and write it on a sheet of paper: O Allah, the heaven is Yours, and the earth is Yours, and whatever is between them is Yours; so make what is between them tighter upon so-and-so than the skin of a camel, until You return him to me and grant me mastery over him. And let Āyat al-Kursī be written around the writing in a circular manner, then bury it and place something heavy over it in the place where he used to take shelter at night.”

Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: Any Muslim who is living among Muslims and then apostasizes from Islam, denies the prophethood of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and rejects him, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him. His wife becomes separated from him, so she must not approach him; his wealth is divided among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died. It is upon the Imam to execute him if he is brought before him, and he is not to be asked to repent.

Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them: A person who apostasizes from Islam is to be separated from his wife, his slaughtered animal is not to be eaten, and he is to be given an opportunity to repent for three days. If he returns, otherwise he is killed on the fourth day, provided he is of sound mind.

3548 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the apostate from Islam, he عليه السلام said: "She is not to be killed, but is to be subjected to hard service, prevented from food and drink except what keeps her alive, dressed in the coarsest clothes, and struck for the prayers."

And in the narration of Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام said: If a woman apostasizes from Islam, she is not to be killed, but rather she is to be imprisoned forever.

3550 - Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: When 'Alī عليه السلام had finished with the people of al-Baṣrah, seventy men from the Zutt came to him, greeted him, and spoke to him in their language. Then he said to them: Indeed, I am not as you have said; I am a servant of Allah, created. He said: But they refused him and said—may Allah curse them—No, rather you are, you are He. So he said to them: If you do not return from what you have said and do not repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, I will surely kill you. He said: But they refused to repent and return. He said: Then he عليه السلام ordered that wells be dug for them, so they were dug. Then he opened some of them into others, then cast them into them, then covered their tops. Then he kindled a fire in one well among them while none of them was in it, so the smoke entered upon them and they died.

And that is that two men in Kūfah, from among the Muslims— a man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and testified that he had seen them praying to an idol. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Woe to you, perhaps it is someone among those whose matter is confused to you.” Then he sent a man, and he looked at them while they were praying to an idol, so he brought them. He said: so he said to them, “Return,” but they refused. So he dug for them a trench in the ground, kindled a fire in it, and cast them into it. Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated that from al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

A servant wrote to Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: I have come across a group of Muslims who are heretics and a group of Christians who are also heretics. He said: As for those who were from the Muslims, born upon the natural disposition, then apostatized, strike their neck and do not seek their repentance. And as for those who were not born among them upon the natural disposition, seek their repentance. If they repent, [leave them]; otherwise, strike their neck. And as for the Christians, what they are upon is greater than heresy.

And in the narration of Mūsā ibn Bakr, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That a man from among the Muslims became Christian, so he was brought to ʿAlī عليه السلام. He asked him to repent, but he refused him. Then he seized his hair and said, "Trample him, O servants of Allah," so he was trampled until he died.

Fadalah narrated from Aban that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Regarding a child who matures and then chooses Christianity, while one of his parents is a Christian or both are Muslims, he said: He is not to be left alone, but rather he is to be compelled toward Islam.

Ibn Faddal narrated from Aban that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Regarding a man who dies as an apostate from Islam while he has children and wealth, he said: His wealth belongs to his Muslim children.

And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: If the father embraces Islam, he draws the child into Islam. Then whoever among his children reaches maturity is invited to Islam; if he refuses, he is killed. And if the child embraces Islam, he does not draw his parents [into it], and there is no inheritance between them.

Saʿd ibn Saʿd narrated from Ḥarīz, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who said to his slave, "You are free, and your wealth belongs to me." He عليه السلام said: "He begins with the wealth before the emancipation, saying: 'Your wealth belongs to me, and you are free,' with the consent of the slave."

Al-Hasan al-Sayqal asked him about a man who said: The first slave I acquire shall be free. Then he acquired six, so he said: His intention was only for one, so let him choose whichever of them he wishes and set him free.

And Ibrāhīm ibn Mahzīyār narrated from his brother, ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said: I wrote to him asking about an owned slave when death approaches him, and his master frees him at that hour, so he departs from the world as a free man. Is there for the master a reward in freeing him then, or is it better that he leave him as an owned slave, such that he would have reward if he dies while still owned by him? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "The slave is to be left as owned in the state of his death, for that is more rewarding for his master. And this emancipation at that hour was not beneficial for him."

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Faḍl ibn al-Mubārak that he wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام. Concerning a man who has a slave, and the slave became ill: is freeing him during his illness greater in reward for him, or should he leave him as a slave? He said: If it is during an illness, then emancipation is better for him, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, frees with every limb of him a limb from the Fire. But if it is at the state of the presence of death, then leaving him as a slave is better for him than emancipating him.

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Faḍl ibn al-Mubārak al-Baṣrī, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, "May I be your ransom, a man is obligated to free a believing slave, but he cannot find one. What should he do?" He عليه السلام said, "Resort to the children and free them. If they turn out to be believing, then that is it; and if they do not turn out to be believing, then there is nothing upon you."

Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who sells his slave for less than his price so that he may be freed, and the slave says to him privately, “I owe you such-and-such.” Is it permissible for him to take it from him? He said: He may take it from him voluntarily, and ask him for it gently; but if he refuses, then he should leave him.

Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said: Regarding a mukatabah whose master has intercourse with her and she becomes pregnant, he said: "He must pay to her the equivalent dowry of her like, and she must strive regarding her value; if she is unable, then she is among the mothers of children (umm al-walad)."

Ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Mukārī entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him: “Has Allah raised your rank to the point that you claim what your father claimed?” He عليه السلام said to him: “What is with you? May Allah extinguish your light and bring poverty into your house! Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to ʿImrān: ‘Indeed I am granting you a male,’ then He granted him Maryam, and granted to Maryam ʿĪsā. So ʿĪsā is from Maryam, and Maryam is from ʿĪsā, and ʿĪsā and Maryam are one thing; and I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.” Then Ibn Abī Saʿīd said to him: “So I ask you about a question.” He عليه السلام said: “I do not think that you will accept from me, and you are not of my flock, but bring it.” He said: “A man said at the time of his death: ‘Every slave of mine that is old is free for the sake of Allah, Exalted.’” So he عليه السلام said: “Yes. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:” “Until it returned like the old date-stalk.” “So whatever of his slaves has reached six months for him, then it is old and free.” He said: So he left and fell into poverty until he died, and he did not have a place to spend even one night. May Allah curse him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a Christian slave belonging to a Muslim man: is jizyah due upon him? He said: Yes. Rather, it is his owner who redeems him if he is taken, and pays on his behalf.

Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Then contract mukātabah with them if you know good in them.” He عليه السلام said: “If you know that they have wealth.” He said: I said, “And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you.” He عليه السلام said: “You reduce for him from his installments that which you had not been intending to reduce from them at all, and you do not increase it beyond what was in your mind.” So I said: “How much?” He عليه السلام said: “Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام reduced one thousand from six thousand for a slave belonging to him.”

And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a mukātab for whom it is stipulated that if he is unable, then he is returned to slavery, and he became unable before paying anything. He said: “He is not returned to slavery until three years have passed for him, and from him is emancipated in proportion to what he has paid as an installment. So when he has paid an installment, they have no right to return him to slavery.”

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about a mukātab who was unable to fulfill his manumission contract, though he had already paid part of it. He said: It should be paid on his behalf from the funds of charity. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: 'and for freeing slaves.'

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: About a man who entered into a mukātabah contract with his slave, and after making the contract he said: "Gift to me part of my mukātabah payment, and I will expedite your mukātabah payment." Is that permissible? He said: "If it is a gift, then there is no harm. But if he says, ‘Reduce it from me and I will expedite it for you,’ then it is not proper."

Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a mukatab (slave under contract of emancipation) jointly owned by two partners, and one of them frees his share: How should the servant act? He said: "He serves the second partner one day and serves himself one day." I asked: "What if he dies and leaves wealth?" He said: "The wealth is divided equally between the one who freed his share and the one who retained his share."

3474 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about a man who wanted to free a slave of his, while his master had been taking from him a yearly levy that he had imposed on him, and the master was satisfied with that from him. Then the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give his master from the levy. So he said: “When he has paid to his master what he had imposed upon him, then whatever he earns after the obligation belongs to the slave.” He said: Then Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: “Has not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed obligations upon the servants, and when they perform them for Him, He does not ask them about what is beyond them?” I said to him: “Then may the slave give charity from what he earned and be emancipated after the obligation that he pays to his master?” He said: “Yes, and the reward of that is for him.” I said: “If he frees a slave from what he had earned apart from the obligation, to whom does the walaʾ of the emancipated one belong?” He said: “He goes and affiliates himself with whomever he wishes, and when someone guarantees his liability and blood-money responsibility, he becomes his mawla and inherits from him.” I said to him: “Did not the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: ‘The walaʾ belongs to the one who emancipates’?” He said: “This is a saʾibah; his walaʾ does not belong to a slave like him.” I said: “If the slave who emancipated him guarantees his liability and incident, would that bind him, and would he become his mawla and inherit from him?” He said: “That is not permissible. A slave does not inherit from a free person.”

Aban narrated from Abu al-‘Abbas, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said: “My slave is free, and he must perform such-and-such labor for such-and-such a year.” He said: “He is free, and the labor is upon him.” I said: “Ibn Abi Layla claims that he is free and that nothing is upon him.” He said: “He has lied. Indeed, ‘Ali عليه السلام freed Aba Nayzar, ‘Iyadan, and Riyahan, while labor for such-and-such a number of years was upon them, and they had their provision and their clothing in a reasonable manner during those years.”

Al-Qasim ibn Burayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a mukatab for whom it was stipulated that if he became unable, he should be returned to slavery, he عليه السلام said: "The Muslims are bound by their conditions."
Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the mukātab, so he said: What you have stipulated upon him is binding upon him.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukatabah who died after having paid most of what was due from her, and she had given birth to a child during her contract. So he ruled concerning her child that a portion of him be freed equal to the portion of her that had been freed, and a portion of him remain in bondage equal to the portion of her that had remained in bondage.

And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a mukātab whose master stipulates upon him that he must not marry except with his permission until he fulfills his mukātabah contract. He عليه السلام said: “He should not marry except with his permission; indeed, they are entitled to their condition.”

And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a mukatab who dies after having paid part of his contract, and he has a son from his bondwoman and leaves behind wealth. He عليه السلام said: “His son shall pay the remainder of his contract, be freed, and inherit what remains.”

Samāʿah asked him about a slave whose master enters into a mukātabah contract with him while knowing that he possesses neither a little nor much wealth. He said: Let him enter into the mukātabah with him, even if he has to ask people. His lacking wealth should not prevent the mukātabah, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, provides the servants through one another, so the doer of good is aided.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Concerning a man who owned a slave belonging to him, and the slave asked his master for mukataba: is he allowed not to enter into the mukataba with him except at a high price? He said: "Yes."

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a mukātab who enters into a contract of emancipation, and whose masters stipulate against him that if he becomes unable, then he is owned, and whatever they have taken from him belongs to them, he said: "His masters take him according to their condition."

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Concerning a slave who entered into a contract of manumission over himself and his wealth, and he had a female slave, and it had been stipulated upon him that he should not marry, then he freed the female slave and married her, he said: “It is not proper for him to make any disposition in his wealth except a meal of food, and his marriage is invalid and rejected.” It was said: “If his master came to know of his marriage and did not say anything?” He said: “If he remains silent when he knows that, then he has approved it.” It was said: “If the mukātab is emancipated, do you see that he should renew his marriage contract, or proceed upon the first marriage?” He said: “He proceeds upon his marriage.”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a mukātab who pays half of his mukātabah contract, and the other half remains due from him, then he calls his masters to the rest of his contract and says to them: Take what remains in a single payment. He said: They take what remains, then he is emancipated. And he said regarding a mukātab who pays part of his mukātabah contract, then dies, leaving a son and leaving wealth greater than what he still owes from his mukātabah contract: His masters are to be paid what remains of his mukātabah contract, and whatever remains belongs to his child.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a mukatab who dies after having paid part of his contract, and he has a son from his bondwoman, he عليه السلام said: “If it was stipulated against him that if he became unable, then he would be a slave, his son would revert as a slave, as would the bondwoman. But if no such condition had been stipulated against him, then his son would pay what remained of his mukataba and inherit what remained.”

Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Mihzam, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mukatab who dies while he has children, and he said: "If a condition had been stipulated against him, then his children are slaves. But if no such condition had been stipulated against him, his children must strive in their father's contract of manumission, and they are freed when they complete the payment."

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If the owned mukātab stipulates with his master that no wala' will be due from him to anyone, or if the master stipulates the wala' of the mukātab and the mukātab who was contracted agrees, then his wala' belongs to him. He said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a mukātab upon whom his wala' had been stipulated when he was emancipated. He married a bondwoman belonging to another man, and she bore him a child. Then his child was freed. Then the mukātab died, and his child inherited from him. Then they differed concerning his child as to who would inherit him, so he attached his child to the mawālī of his father.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukātabah who died after having paid most of what was due upon her, and she had given birth to a child during her contract. So he ruled concerning her child that as much of him would be freed as the portion of her that had been freed, and as much of him would remain in bondage as the portion of her that remained in bondage.

ʿUmar, the companion of al-Karābīs, narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who made a mukātabah contract with his slave and stipulated against him that his inheritance would belong to him; that was then brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he invalidated his condition and said: The condition of Allah precedes your condition.

And Al-Ala' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then write [a contract of emancipation] for them if you know any good in them.' He said: 'The 'good' is that he bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that he possesses a skill by which he can earn a livelihood or has a trade.'

And it is narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: That Ali عليه السلام used to require the mukatab to continue working, because they did not used to stipulate that if he became unable, then he would be a slave. And Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "They have their conditions." And he عليه السلام said: "The mukatab is awaited for three installments; if he is unable, he is returned as a slave."

3493 - He said: And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. He said: I heard my father عليه السلام say: He should not make the contract of emancipation with him upon the amount he intended, then increase it for him, and then reduce from it; rather, he should reduce from what he had intended to contract him upon.

Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated from Abū Khadījah Sālim ibn Mukram al-Jammāl, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: Beware that some of you do not take others among you for judgment to the people of tyranny. Rather, look to a man from among you who knows something of our judgments, then appoint him among you, for I have indeed appointed him a judge; so seek judgment before him.

3217 - Muʿallā ibn Khunays narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: I said to him concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice." He said: "It is upon the Imam to hand over what is with him to the Imam who comes after him. The Imams have been commanded to judge with justice, and the people have been commanded to follow them."

And ‘Aṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn, upon them both be peace, who said: When you are under oppressive leaders, then judge according to their rulings and do not expose yourselves, lest you be killed. And if you conduct your dealings according to our rulings, it will be better for you.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Any believer who refers another believer in a dispute to a judge or a tyrannical ruler, and he rules against him contrary to the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has indeed shared with him in the sin.

3220 - Hariz narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام that he said: “Any man who has a dispute with his brother over a right, and he calls him to a man from among your brothers to judge between him and him, but he refuses and insists on taking him to these, is like those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:” “Have you not seen those who claim that they have believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to seek judgment from Taghut, though they were commanded to reject it.” (the verse).

Sulaymān ibn Khālid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Beware of judging, for judgment belongs only to the Imam who is knowledgeable in judicial matters and just among the Muslims, like a prophet or the executor of a prophet.
Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام said to Shurayh: O Shurayh, you have sat in a position that none has sat in except a prophet, the executor of a prophet, or a wretched person.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Seek refuge with Allah from the burden of debt, the dominance of men, and the ruin of the unmarried.
Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, عليهم السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah, صلى الله عليه وآله, said: Beware of debt, for it is a disgrace to religion.
And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: Beware of debt, for it is worry at night and humiliation during the day.
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: Beware of debt, for it is humiliation during the day, worry at night, accountability in this world, and accountability in the Hereafter.

And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “It was mentioned to us that a man from the Anṣār died while owing two dinars as a debt, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not pray over him and said, ‘Pray over your brother,’ until one of his relatives guaranteed them on his behalf.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “That is the truth.” Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم only did that so that they might take admonition, and so that some of them would respond for others, and so that they would not treat debt lightly. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم died while he had debt, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was killed while he had debt, and al-Ḥasan عليه السلام died while he had debt, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام was killed while he had debt.”

And it is narrated from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said: Whoever seeks sustenance through its lawful means and is overcome, then let him borrow in reliance upon Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and upon His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.

Al-Mīthamī narrated from Abū Mūsā, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, can a man borrow and perform hajj?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Can he borrow and get married?” He said: “Yes, for he awaits the provision of Allah morning and evening.”

And it is narrated from Abū Thumāmah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī, peace be upon him: “I wish to remain in Makkah and al-Madīnah, but I have a debt upon me, so what do you say?” He said: “Return to the place of paying your debt, and see to it that you meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while no debt remains upon you, for the believer does not betray.”

3687 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever has a debt and intends to repay it, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has with him two guardians who assist him in rendering the payment of his trust. But if his intention regarding repayment falls short, they fall short in assisting him in proportion to how much his intention falls short.
And it is narrated from Abān, from Bashshār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The first drop of the martyr’s blood is an expiation for his sins, except debt, for its expiation is its repayment.
Abu Khadijah narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Any man who goes to another man and borrows money from him while intending not to repay it, then he is a thief and a transgressor.

Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated that he said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man among us has something by which he sustains himself, while he has a debt upon him. Should he feed his dependents with it until Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, brings him ease so that he may repay his debt, or should he borrow burdening himself in the corruption of the times and the hardship of earnings, or should he accept charity? So he عليه السلام said: He should repay his debt with what he has, and he should not consume the wealth of the people unless he has what he can repay to them. Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, says: “And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly.”

And Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: Whoever withholds the right of a Muslim while he is able to give it to him, out of fear that if that right leaves his hand he will become poor, then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is more capable of impoverishing him than he is of enriching himself by withholding that right.

And Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated from Abu 'Abdillah, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, is with the debtor until he repays it, so long as he did not take it from that which is forbidden to him.

And it is narrated from Burayd al-‘Ijli, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I owe a debt to orphans, and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will be left with nothing.” He عليه السلام said: “Do not sell your estate; rather, give some and keep some.”

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: There is no debtor whose creditor departs from him satisfied except that the creatures of the earth and the fish of the seas pray for him. And there is no debtor whose creditor departs angry while he is able to pay except that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, records against him for every day or night that he withholds him, an act of injustice.

3695 - And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from Khaḍir ibn ʿAmr al-Nakhaʿī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who has wealth owed to him by another man, and he denies it. He عليه السلام said: "If he makes him swear an oath, then he has no right to take anything from him after the oath. And if he imprisons him, he has no right to take anything from him. And if he leaves him and does not make him swear, then he remains upon his right."

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who owed me property, but he disputed me over it and swore an oath. Then some of his property came into my possession. Should I take it in place of my property which he took and swear over it as he did? So he said: If he has betrayed you, then do not betray him, and do not enter into that for which you blamed him.

Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, "A man owes me a right, but he denies it to me, then he entrusts me with some wealth. May I take my due from what is with him?" He said: "No. This is betrayal."
Zayd al-Shahham narrated; he said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: Whoever entrusts you with a trust, then deliver it back to him; and whoever betrays you, do not betray him.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man had wealth owed to him by another man, but he denied it to him and took it away from him. Then after that, there came into his possession from that man—the man who had taken his wealth—wealth equal to it. May he take it in place of his wealth that he took from him? He said: "Yes. He should say: 'O Allah, I am only taking this in place of my property which he took from me.'"

And in another report from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, similarly to it, except that he said: He says: “O Allah, I did not take what I took from him as betrayal or injustice, but rather I took it in place of my due right.”
And in another narration: If he makes him swear regarding what he took from him, then it is permissible for him to swear if he says this statement.

Due to the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family: "Whoever swears by Allah should speak truthfully, and whoever is sworn to by Allah should be satisfied; and whoever is not satisfied is not from Allah in any respect."

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Dāwūd ibn Zurbī, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: I deal with some people, and sometimes they send to me and take from me a bondwoman and an animal, and they go away with it from me. Then some wealth belonging to them comes into my possession, so I take from it an amount equal to what they took from me. So he عليه السلام said: Take from them an amount equal to what they took from you, and do not add to it.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hudhayl ibn Ḥanān, the brother of Jaʿfar ibn Ḥanān al-Ṣayrafī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I gave some money to my brother Jaʿfar, and he gives me from it what I spend, what I perform hajj with, and what I give in charity. I asked those around us, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not halal, and I would love to conclude in this matter with your statement. So he said: Did he use to give to you before you handed your money over to him? I said: Yes. He said: Take from him what he gives you, and eat, and drink, and perform hajj, and give in charity. Then when you arrive in Iraq, say: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad has given me this ruling.

Sama'ah asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who stays with another man while owing him a debt: may he eat from his food? He said: “Yes, he may eat from his food for three days, and after that he should not eat anything.”

3706 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Exalted: There is no good in much of their secret talk except in one who enjoins charity, or kindness, or reconciliation between people. So he said: "What is meant by al-ma'ruf is a loan."

And it is narrated from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayābah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr instructed me to ask you. He said: We borrow bread from the neighbors, then we return bread smaller than it or larger.
