So he عليه السلام said: We borrow walnuts, sixty and seventy by number, and among them there may be small and large ones, so there is no harm in that.
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Whoever gives a loan until ease of repayment, his wealth is in zakat, and he remains in the salat of the angels upon him until he takes it back.
And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he used to say: If a man has a debt and then dies, the debt becomes due.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: When the deceased dies, what is owed to him and what he owes become due.

3711 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thawrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who dies while a debt is upon him, and a guarantor guarantees it for the creditors, he عليه السلام said: “If the creditors are satisfied with him, then the liability of the deceased is cleared.”

And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Khunays, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah has a debt owed to him by a man who has died, and we spoke to him to absolve it, but he refused. He عليه السلام said: Woe to him! Does he not know that for him there are ten for every dirham if he absolves it? But if he does not absolve it, then he only has a dirham in exchange for a dirham.

Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: A man came to Ali عليه السلام and said: Indeed, I have earned wealth, and I was careless in seeking it, [mixing] halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden). I have now intended tawbah (repentance), but I do not know what of it is halal and what is haram, for it has become mixed up for me. So Ali عليه السلام said: Take out the khums (one-fifth tax) of your wealth, for Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has accepted khums from a person, and the remainder of the wealth, all of it, is halal for you.

Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled concerning a man who died and left heirs, and one of the heirs acknowledged a debt against his father, that this is binding upon him only in his share according to the amount he inherited, and it does not apply to all of his property. فإذا two of the heirs acknowledge it and they are just, that is accepted against the heirs; but if they are not just, they are bound only in their own shares according to what they inherited. Likewise, if some of the heirs acknowledge a brother or a sister, it only binds them in their own share. And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Whoever acknowledges a brother, then he is a partner in the property, but his lineage is not established. And if two acknowledge him, then likewise, unless they are just, in which case his lineage is established and he is included with them in the inheritance.

Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated that Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, may Allah be pleased with him, was a cloth merchant. He lost his wealth and became poor, while a man owed him ten thousand dirhams. So the man sold a house of his in which he lived for ten thousand dirhams and carried the money to his door. Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr came out to him and said: “What is this?” He said: “This is your money which is due from me.” He said: “Did you inherit it?” He said: “No.” He said: “Was it gifted to you?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then is it the price of an estate that you sold?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then what is it?” He said: “I sold my house in which I live so that I may pay my debt.” Then Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “Ḏarīḥ al-Muḥāribī narrated to me from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:” “A man is not to be turned out from his home because of debt. Take it back, for I have no need of it. By Allah, I am indeed in need at this time of a single dirham, yet not one dirham of it will enter my possession.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: I had ten dirhams owed to me by a man, and the ruler invalidated those dirhams and brought dirhams higher than those dirhams in value. And in those first dirhams today there is depreciation. So what is due to me from him: the first dirhams which the ruler invalidated, or the dirhams which the ruler approved? So he wrote: “You are entitled to the first dirhams.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Trade increases intellect.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Abandoning trade diminishes the intellect.
And it is narrated from Al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saw me when I had delayed going to the market, so he said to me, "Go early to your source of honor."

And it is narrated from Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Exalted: "Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah." He عليه السلام said: "They were people of trade, but when the salat (prayer) became due, they left the trade and went to the salat (prayer), and they are greater in reward than one who did not engage in trade."

And Harun ibn Hamzah narrated from Ali ibn Abdul Aziz who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "What has Umar ibn Muslim done?" I said: "May I be your ransom, he has devoted himself to worship and abandoned trade." He said: "Woe to him! Does he not know that the one who abandons seeking sustenance will not have his supplication answered? Indeed, a group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the verse was revealed: 'And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect,' locked their doors and devoted themselves to worship, saying, 'We have been guaranteed provision.' When this reached the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he sent for them and said: 'What led you to do what you have done?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has guaranteed our provision, so we have devoted ourselves to worship.' He said: 'Indeed, whoever does this, Allah will not answer his supplication. You must continue seeking sustenance.' Then he said: "I hate a man who is impious, opening his mouth to his Lord, saying, 'Provide for me,' while he abandons seeking sustenance."

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: "Engage in trade—may Allah bless you—for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, say: 'Provision is ten parts: nine are in trade, and one is in other than it.'"
And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Engage in trade, for in it there is independence for you from what is in the hands of the people.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Do not abandon trade, lest you become insignificant. Engage in trade—may Allah bless you.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Whoever engages in trade without knowledge will fall into usury, and then fall into it again. So let no one sit in the marketplace except one who understands buying and selling.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام, in Kūfah, used to go out every morning and walk through the markets of Kūfah, market by market, while with him was the whip upon his shoulder. It had two ends, and it used to be called al-Sabībah. He said: He would stand before the people of each market and call out to them: “O company of traders, put al-istikharah first, seek blessing through ease, draw near to the buyers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, keep away from oppression, give justice to the wronged, and do not go near usury. “And give full measure and weight.” “And do not diminish the people’s goods, and do not act wickedly in the land as corrupters.” He said: Then he would go through all the markets of Kūfah, then return and sit for the people.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whoever buys and sells should safeguard five qualities; otherwise, let him neither buy nor sell: usury, swearing, concealing defects, praising when selling, and criticizing when buying.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: O company of traders, raise your heads, for the path has been made clear to you. You will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment as wicked sinners, except one whose speech is truthful.
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "The trader is sinful, and the sinful one is in the Fire, except for the one who takes what is right and gives what is right."

And he, peace be upon him, said: O group of traders, protect your wealth through charity; your sins will be expiated from you, and the oaths which you swear therein will be purified for you; your trade will be made wholesome for you.

And it is narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: I heard Ali عليه السلام saying from the pulpit: O group of traders, fiqh first, then trade; fiqh first, then trade. By Allah, riba in this ummah is more hidden than the crawling of an ant upon a smooth stone. Protect your wealth through charity. The trader is sinful, and the sinful one is in the Fire, except one who takes what is right and gives what is right.

And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Mundhir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: "My wife gave me money for me to use as I wished. May I buy a bondwoman with her money and have relations with her?" He عليه السلام said: "No. She only gave it to you so that her eye might be comforted, while you intend to make her eye burn with grief."

And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muyassir, who said: I said to him: “A man comes to me and says, ‘Will you buy for me?’ while what I have is better than the merchandise of the market.” He said: “If you are confident that he will not suspect you, then give him from what you have; but if you fear that he may suspect you, then buy for him from the market.”

And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: Allah, the Exalted, revealed to one of His prophets, peace be upon them: “With the generous, be generous; with the lenient, be lenient; with the stingy, be withholding; and in the presence of the harsh, be evasive.”

And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: “Leniency is a means of profit.” He عليه السلام said: “That applies to a man who is being advised while he has merchandise that he is selling.”
Ali عليه السلام passed by a bondwoman who had bought meat from a butcher while she was saying, “Give me more.” So Ali عليه السلام said to him, “Give her more, for it is greater for blessing.”

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves a servant who is easygoing in selling, easygoing in buying, easygoing in settling debts, and easygoing in demanding repayment.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Any Muslim who releases another Muslim from a sale due to his regret, Allah will release him from his stumble on the Day of Resurrection.
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by a man who had goods with him that he wanted to sell, and he said, "Keep to the beginning of the market."
And he, peace be upon him, said: The owner of the goods has more right to set the price.
And he, peace be upon him and his family, forbade bargaining between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun.

And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Bargain with the buyer, for it is more satisfying to the soul. Even if he gives generously, the one who is cheated in his selling and buying is neither praiseworthy nor rewarded.
And he عليه السلام said: Do not bargain in four things: the sacrificial animal, the shroud, the price of a slave, and the fare to Makkah.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn عليه السلام used to say to his steward: If you intend to buy something for me from the needs of hajj, then buy it and do not bargain.

Muyassir narrated from Hafs, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man intends fulfillment, but when he measures, he does not do the measuring well. He said: What do those around him say? He said: I said: They say he does not give full measure. He said: He is among those for whom it is not appropriate to measure.

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever takes the scales in his hand and intends to take a full measure for himself will only take it with excess; and whoever gives and intends to give an equal measure will only give deficiently.
Ḥammād ibn Bashīr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Fulfillment is not achieved until the tongue of the balance inclines.
And in another narration: "Fulfillment is not achieved until it outweighs."

And it is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I take dirhams from a man, then I weigh them, then I distribute them, and some surplus of them remains in my hand. He said: Did you not seek to give full measure accurately? I said: Yes. He said: There is no harm.
Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Earnest money is not permissible unless it is a cash portion of the price.

3751 - The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said: A Bedouin from Banū ʿĀmir came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and asked him about the worst places of the earth and the best places of the earth. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “The worst places of the earth are the markets, and they are the میدان of Iblis. He goes forth with his banner, sets down his throne, and spreads his offspring. Among them is one who gives short measure in a qafīz, one who is careless in a scale, one who steals in measuring length, or one who lies regarding merchandise. Then he says: ‘Attach yourselves to a man whose father has died while your father is alive.’ So he does not cease, despite that, to be the first to enter and the last to leave.” Then he عليه السلام said: “And the best places are the mosques, and the most beloved of them to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, are those who enter them first and leave them last.”
And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: The marketplace of the Muslims is like their mosque. So whoever reaches a place first has more right to it until the night.

Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever enters a marketplace or a congregational mosque and says once: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without any partner. Allah is the Greatest, immensely great. All praise belongs to Allah, abundantly. Glory be to Allah, morning and evening. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family. It is counted for him as an accepted Hajj.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥammād al-Anṣārī narrated from Sadīr, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “O Abā al-Faḍl, do you not have a place in the market where you sit and deal with the people?” He said: I said, “Yes.” He said: “Know that there is no man who goes out and returns to his place of sitting and his market, then says when he places his foot in the market: ‘O Allah, I ask You for its good and the good of its people, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of its people,’ except that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, appoints for him one who protects him and guards him until he returns to his home. Then he says to him: ‘I have granted you protection from its evil and the evil of its people on this day of yours.’” “Then when he sits in his place, as he sits, he says: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, صلى الله عليه وآله. O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty for lawful, pure provision, and I seek refuge in You from wronging or being wronged, and I seek refuge in You from a losing transaction and a false oath.’” “So when he says that, the appointed angel says: ‘Receive glad tidings, for there is no one in your market today with a fuller share than you, and what Allah has apportioned for you will come to you in full—lawful, pure, and blessed therein.’”

And it is narrated: Whoever remembers Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, in the marketplaces, Allah will forgive him according to the number of those in them, among the eloquent and the non-Arabic-speaking.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Whoever remembers Allah, Mighty and Exalted, in the marketplaces, He will forgive him by the number of their people.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: One of the two Imams, peace be upon them, said: When you purchase goods, then magnify Allah three times, then say: O Allah, I have purchased it seeking from Your goodness therein, so place goodness for me in it. O Allah, I have purchased it seeking from Your bounty therein, so place bounty for me in it. O Allah, I have purchased it seeking from Your provision therein, so place provision for me in it. Then repeat each one of them three times.
Al-Ridha عليه السلام used to write on merchandise: “A blessing for us.”

ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: Whoever buys an animal should stand on its left side, take its forelock with his right hand, and recite over its head Sūrat al-Fātiḥah. And: “Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad.” And the two Muʿawwidhatayn, and the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the end of Banī Isrāʾīl. “Say: Call upon Allāh or call upon al-Raḥmān.” And Āyat al-Kursī, for that is protection for that animal from afflictions.

Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “When you purchase a bondwoman, then say: O Allah, I seek Your counsel and I seek Your choosing. And when you purchase a riding animal or livestock, then say: O Allah, decree for me the one among them longest in life, greatest in benefit, and best in outcome.”
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For all animals, the buyer has a three-day option; he has the choice during that period whether he stipulated it or did not stipulate it.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whenever a man buys something from another man, they both retain the option until they part from one another; once they part, the sale becomes binding.

And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding a man who bought from another man a slave or an animal, and stipulated one day or two days; then the slave died, or the animal perished, or some incident occurred in it—upon whom is the liability? He said: There is no liability upon the buyer until the condition period ends and the sold item becomes his.
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said: "Whoever purchases a sale-item, and three days pass without his coming, then there is no sale for him."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Muslims are bound by their conditions, except every condition that contravenes the Book of Allah, Mighty and Exalted; then it is not permissible.

And Jamil narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man buys merchandise from another man, then leaves it with him, saying: I will bring you its price. So he عليه السلام said: If he brings it within the period between that and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.

3767 - And in another narration, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Ribāṭ, from one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "If an animal is afflicted by an occurrence within three days, then it is from the seller’s property liability."

It is narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: “My father عليه السلام purchased a land called al-ʿUrayḍ. When he made it binding, he stood up and went away. So I said to him, ‘O my father, you hastened to stand up.’ He said, ‘O my son, I wanted the sale to become binding.’”

Abu Ayyub narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Aba Ja‘far عليه السلام say: “I purchased land, and when I had concluded it, I stood and walked a few steps, then returned. I intended that the sale should become binding at the time of separation.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Defrauding the one who entrusts you is unlawful gain, and defrauding a believer is forbidden.
And in the narration of ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Defrauding the trusting party is riba.
And he, peace be upon him, said: If a man says to another man, ‘Come, I will improve your sale,’ then profit becomes forbidden for him.

It is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “We deal with some people from the rural districts and others. We sell to them and profit from them, such that ten becomes twelve and ten becomes thirteen. We defer that between us and them for a year or about that. Then a man writes it for us against his house or against his land for that amount of money in which there is the excess, which he took from us as a purchase, on the basis that he has sold it and taken the price. Then we promise him that if he brings the money at a time agreed between us and him, we will return the purchase to him. But if the time comes upon us and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is ours. So what do you think regarding the purchase?” He said: “I hold that it is yours if he does not do so; but if he brings the money at the appointed time, then you must return it to him.”

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man asked him while I was with him, and said: A Muslim man needed to sell his house, so he came to his brother and said: I sell you this house of mine, and for it to belong to you is more beloved to me than that it belong to someone else, on the condition that you stipulate for me that if I come to you with its price within a year, you will return it to me. So he said: There is no problem with this. If he brings its price within a year, he should return it to him. I said: If there was abundant yield in it, and he took the yield, to whom does the yield belong? He said: To the buyer. Do you not see that if it were to burn down, it would be from his property?

Aban narrated from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about selling pasture when it is flowing water, such that a man directs his water to the land and thereby irrigates the grass, and he is the one who dug the canal and the water belongs to him, planting with it whatever he wishes. So he عليه السلام said: If the water belongs to him, then let him plant with it whatever he wishes and sell it for whatever he likes.

Sama'ah asked him: About purchasing fodder crops: a man buys them, then does not cut them, and it occurs to him to leave them until their spikes emerge as barley or wheat. He had bought them from their roots, and whatever land tax was upon their owners was upon the cultivator. He said: "If, when he bought it, he stipulated that if he wished he could cut it as fodder, and if he wished he could leave it as it is until it becomes spikes, then that is acceptable. Otherwise, it is not proper for him to leave it until it becomes spikes."

Sama'ah asked him: About a man who purchased pasture in which he grazes for fifty dirhams, or less or more, and then wanted to admit with him others who would graze with him and take the price from them. He said: Let him admit with him whomever he wishes for part of what he paid. And if he admits others with him for forty-nine dirhams, so that his sheep graze for one dirham, then there is no harm. And he does not have the right to sell it for fifty dirhams and graze with them, unless he has done some work in the pasture: dug a well or split a stream, with the approval of the owners of the pasture. Then there is no harm in selling it for more than what he bought it for, because he has done work in it, and therefore it is permissible for him.

And Sulaymān ibn Khālid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, I dislike renting the millstone by itself and then leasing it out for more than what I rented it for, unless I make some alteration in it or incur some expense in it.

And in the narration of Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If you take land on lease for gold or silver, then do not lease it out for more than what you took it for, because gold and silver are fixed commodities.

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about wheat and barley: may I purchase their crop before it produces spikes, while it is still grass? He عليه السلام said: "No, unless he buys it as cut fodder to feed to the animals; then, if he wishes, he may leave it until it produces spikes."

And it is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a share of water usage with some people in their canal, while they are partners in it. Then some of them become in no need of their water share—may he sell it? He said: Yes, if he wishes he may sell it for silver coins, and if he wishes he may sell it for a measure of wheat.

Sama'ah asked him: About a man who cultivates one hundred jaribs of land with his own seed, producing food or other things that are sown. Then another man comes to him and says: Take from me half of your seed and half of your expenses in this land so that I may become your partner. He said: “There is no harm in that.”

And he asked him about a man who purchased cut fodder, then did not cut it and left it until it became barley, while he had stipulated with the landowner on the day he bought it that whatever misfortune came upon it would be upon the landowner. So he said: If he stipulated with the landowner on the day he bought it that, if he wished, he could make it into ears, and if he wished, he could make it fodder, then his condition is binding for him. But if he did not stipulate that, then it is not proper for him to leave it until it becomes ears; and if he does so, then its tax and expense are upon him, and whatever comes out of it belongs to him.

And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said: A man wrote to al-Faqīh عليه السلام concerning a man who had a mill on the river of a village, while the village belonged to one man or two men. The owner of the village wanted to channel the water to his village through other than this river on which this mill stood, and thereby disable this mill. Does he have that right or not? So he عليه السلام wrote: "He should fear Allah and act in that according to what is fair, and he should not harm his believing brother." And regarding a man who had a canal in a village, and another man wanted to dig another canal above it, then what distance should there be between them so that one does not harm the other, in land when it is hard or soft? So he عليه السلام wrote: "According to what ensures that neither of them harms the other, if Allah the Exalted wills."

3871 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled that there should be, between the two canals in width, if it is soft land, a distance of one thousand cubits between them; and if it is hard land, there should be five hundred cubits between them.
And he, peace be upon him, ruled concerning the people of the desert that they should not withhold surplus water, nor sell surplus pasture.
And he, peace be upon him, ruled that the protected area of a well is forty cubits; no other well is to be dug beside it for a watering place or for sheep.
Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the water of the valley, and he said: Indeed, the Muslims are partners in water, fire, and pasture.

And ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who sold a piece of land on the basis that it contained ten jarībs, and the buyer purchased that from him with its boundaries, paid the price, concluded the sale transaction, and they parted; then when the land was measured, it turned out to be five jarībs. He عليه السلام said: If he wishes, he may recover the excess of his money and take the land; and if he wishes, he may rescind the sale and take all of his money back, unless the seller also has lands adjoining the boundary of that land, in which case he completes it for him, and the sale becomes binding upon him, and fulfillment for him is by the completion of the sold property. But if he has nothing else in that place besides what he sold, then if the buyer wishes, he may take the land and recover the excess of his money; and if he wishes, he may rescind and take all of the money.

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about purchasing land from a Jew and a Christian. He said: “There is no harm in it. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conquered Khaybar and made an agreement with them that the land would remain in their hands, and they would work it and cultivate it. So there is no harm if you purchase something from it. And whichever people revive a piece of land and develop it, they have the greater right to it, and it belongs to them.”

3877 - And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Whoever plants a tree initially, or digs a valley to which no one had preceded him, or revives dead land, then it belongs to him as a decree from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger."

And it is narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who bought from another man a known amount of land for one hundred kurr, on condition that he would give him from the land. So he said: “It is forbidden.” I said: “May I be your ransom, then if he buys the land from him for a known measure and wheat from other than it?” He said: “There is no harm in that.”

And it is narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: No one should purchase anything from the lands of the people of al-Sawād except one who has a covenant, for indeed it is fayʾ for the Muslims.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked, while I was present, about a man who revived dead land, dug a canal in it, built houses, and planted palm trees and trees. So he said: "It belongs to him, and he is entitled to the rent of its houses. And upon him in it is the tenth for what is watered by the sky, or the flood of a valley, or a spring; and upon him, for what is watered by water-lifting devices and the bucket, is half of the tenth."

Sama'ah asked him about a man who entered into a farming partnership (muzara'ah) with a Muslim or a covenant holder (mu'ahid), spent expenses on it, and then decided to sell it. Is that for him? He said: "He may sell it for silver coins, for its origin is food."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked him: About staying with the people of al-kharaj, and he said: “Three days.”

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام about a house that belonged to a woman who had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared at sea, and the woman died. Her daughter claimed that her mother had assigned that house to her and had sold parts of it, and a portion remained in the house beside the house of a man from among our brothers. He disliked purchasing it because of the son's absence and because of what he feared, that purchasing it might not be permissible for him, while no news of the son was known. He said: “And for how long has he been absent?” I said: “For many years.” So he said: “He waits through an absence of ten years, then he may purchase it.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: Concerning a man who bought from another man a house in a property belonging to him, with all its rights, while there was another house above it: does the upper house enter into the rights of the lower house, or not? So he عليه السلام wrote: “He has no right except to what he purchased by its name and its location, if Allah wills.”

And he wrote to him regarding A man said to two men: "Bear witness that the entire house which he owns in such-and-such a place, with all its boundaries, belongs to so-and-so son of so-and-so, along with all that he has in the house of furnishings." But the witnesses did not know what the furnishings were, which thing they were. So he signed, عليه السلام: "It is valid if the purchase encompasses all of that, if Allah wills."

And he wrote to him regarding a man who had plots of lands, and departure to Mecca became imminent for him, while the village was several stages from his residence, and he did not have sufficient time to provide the boundaries of his land. So he identified the four boundaries of the village and said to the witnesses: Bear witness that I have sold to so-and-so — meaning the buyer — the whole village, one of whose boundaries is such-and-such, and the second, and the third, and the fourth. Yet he only had plots of land in this village. So is that valid for the buyer, while he only owns part of this village, though he has acknowledged it all for him? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: It is not permissible to sell what one does not own; and the purchase has become binding from the seller only with respect to what he owns.

And he wrote to him regarding a man who made him a witness that he had sold an estate from another man, and it consisted of several plots of land, but he did not specify the boundaries at the time he made him witness, and he said: When they bring you the boundaries, then testify to them. Is that permissible for him, or is it not permissible for him to testify? So he signed, عليه السلام: Yes, it is permissible, and all praise is due to Allah.

And he wrote to him: Is it permissible to testify regarding the boundaries when other people from the people of that village come and testify that the boundaries of this estate which the man sold are these? Then is it permissible for this witness, whom he had made witness concerning the estate, while he did not specify the boundaries, to testify to the boundaries based on the statement of those who identified this estate and testified for him? Or is it not permissible for them to testify, while the seller had said to them: Testify to the boundaries when they come to you with them? So he signed, peace be upon him: Do not testify except on the basis of the owner of the thing and his statement, if Allah wills.

And it is narrated from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a house in which there are three rooms, and they do not have enclosures. He said: "Permission pertains only to the rooms; there is no permission required for the house."

It is narrated from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who gives another man his land, in which there is water, palm trees, and fruit, and says: “Water this from the water and cultivate it, and you shall have half of what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, brings forth from it.” He said: “There is no harm in it.” He said: I also asked him about a man who gives another man ruined land and says: “Develop it, and it is yours for three years, or four, or five years, or whatever he wishes.” He said: “There is no harm in that.” He said: I further asked him about a man who owns land from the kharaj lands, upon which there is a known tax that may sometimes increase and sometimes decrease, and he gives it to another man on the condition that he cover its tax and give him two hundred dirhams in the year. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Sama'ah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who takes land on lease with the willing consent of its owners, upon a condition that he stipulates with them. He said: He is entitled to the rent of its houses, except for what is in the possession of its cultivators, unless he has stipulated with the owners of the land regarding what is in the possession of the cultivators.

Shu'ayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you take land by the willing consent of its owners upon a condition that you stipulated with them, then all surplus in its cultivation belongs to you, provided that you fulfill your agreement with them. And if you repair something in it or introduce a building in it, then you are entitled to the rent of its buildings, except what is in the hands of its dahāqīn.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who rented land for one thousand dirhams, then subleased part of it for two hundred dirhams. Then the owner of the land who had leased it to him said, 'I will enter with you in it according to what you rented it for, and we will spend together, and whatever surplus is in it will be between me and you.' He said: There is no harm in that.

And Aban narrated from Isma'il who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rented land from another man and said: 'Rent it to me for such-and-such amount, whether I cultivate it or not, I will pay you that amount.' However, the man did not cultivate the land. He (the Imam) said: 'The owner has the right to take it with his money; if he wishes, he may waive it, and if he wishes, he may not waive it.'

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Do not lease the land in exchange for dates, wheat, barley, water shares, or surplus water." I said, "And what are the arbīʿāʾ?" He said: "It is the water share, and nīṭāf is surplus water. But you may take it on lease for gold, silver, one-half, one-third, or one-quarter."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who rented a house in which there was a garden, and he planted in the garden, and planted date-palms, trees, fruits, and other things, and he did not seek the permission of the owner of the house concerning that. He said: He is liable for the rent, and the owner of the house assesses that planting and crop, then gives it to the planter if he had sought his permission concerning that. But if he had not sought his permission, then the rent is upon him, and the planting and crop belong to him; he may uproot it and take it wherever he wishes.

Idrīs ibn Zayd narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, we have landed properties with waterwheels, and in them are pastures, and one of us may have sheep and camels and need those pastures for his sheep and camels. Is it permissible for him to reserve the pastures due to his need for them?' He said: 'If the land is his land, then he may reserve it and assign that according to what he needs.' And I said to him, 'A man sells the pasture?' So he said: 'If the land is his land, then there is no harm.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: 'I enter into partnership with a polytheist non-Muslim, such that the land, cattle, and seed are from me, while the non-Muslim is responsible for supervision, effort, and work in the cultivation until it becomes wheat or barley. Then the division takes place, the authority takes its share, and what remains is left such that one-third of it is for the non-Muslim and the rest is for me.' So he عليه السلام said: 'There is no harm in that.' I said: 'Then is he required to return to me what I put forth of the seed, and then divide the remainder?' He عليه السلام said: 'No. You only entered into partnership with him on the basis that the seed, cattle, and land are from you, while the supervision and effort are upon him.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, the brother of Ishaq ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about land that a man wanted to take under qabalah, and which forms of qabalah are most permissible. He عليه السلام said: “He may take it from its people for a specified amount and for specified years, then cultivate it and pay the kharaj. But if there are ʿuluj in it, he must not include the ʿuluj in the qabalah, for that is not halal.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Khālid, from Abī al-Rabīʿ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who takes land from the dahāqīn and then leases it out for more than what he took it for, while undertaking in it the due of the authority. He said: “There is no harm in it. Indeed, land is not like a hired worker, nor like a house. Indeed, the surplus from a worker and a house is haram.”

If a man rents a house for ten dirhams, then lives in two-thirds of it and leases out one-third of it for ten dirhams, there is no harm in that. But he must not lease it out for more than what he rented it for.

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a man who rented land from the kharaj land for a specified amount of dirhams or a specified quantity of food. He then leases it out by the jarib or by separate plots for a known amount, so that he gains a surplus over what he rented from the authorities, while spending nothing. Or he leases that land in plots on condition that he gives them the seeds and the expenses, so that he gains a surplus over his rental payment, and the upkeep of the land is upon him. Is that permitted for him, or is it not? He عليه السلام said: If you rent land and spend something on it, or repair it, then there is no harm in what you mentioned.

It is narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say: If an orchard containing date-palms and trees is sold for one year, then it must not be sold until its fruit reaches maturity. And if it is sold for two years or three, then there is no harm in its sale after there is some greenery in it.

And it is narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who cultivates in another man's land on the condition that one-third is for the cattle, one-third is for the seed, and one-third is for the owner of the land. So he عليه السلام said: He should not designate cattle or seed, but rather he should say to the owner of the land: I will cultivate your land, and for you is such-and-such from what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, brings forth in it.

3905 - Abu al-Rabi' said, and Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Concerning a man who comes to the people of a village after the authority has oppressed them, so they became unable to undertake paying its land-tax, while the village is in their hands, and it is not known whether it belongs to them or whether others have some share in it. So they hand it over to him on condition that he pays its land-tax; then he takes it from them, pays its land-tax, and after that a great amount remains in surplus. So he عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that, if the condition was agreed upon with them accordingly.

3906 - And in the narration of Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about sharecropping with the people of kharaj land on the basis of a quarter, a third, or a half. He said: “There is no harm. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accepted Khaybar on terms with its people; he gave it to the Jews when it was conquered on the basis of al-khabr, and al-khabr is half.”

And Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated from Ibn Sayabah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: A man asked him and said to him: “May I be your ransom, I hear some people saying that agriculture is disliked.” So he said: “Cultivate and plant. No, by Allah, people have done no work more halal and better than it. By Allah, they will surely continue to cultivate crops and date palms after the خروج of the Dajjal.”
Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Do not rent land with wheat and then plant it with wheat.

Muḥammad ibn Sahl narrated from his father, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man whose ploughman cultivates saffron for him and guarantees for him that he will give him such-and-such dirhams for each measured jarīb of land. Sometimes it decreases and he incurs loss, and sometimes it increases. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it if the two mutually agree.”

And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who rents from another man a house or a ship for a year, more than that, or less. He said: “The lease is binding until the time for which it was rented, and the choice regarding taking the rent belongs to its owner: if he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it.”

And ʿAlī al-Ṣāʾigh asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: I take on work, then assign it to the young workers, who work with me for two-thirds. He عليه السلام said: “That is not proper unless you work along with them.” I said: “Then I melt it for them.” He عليه السلام said: “That is work, so there is no harm in it.”

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Khayyat, from Mujammi', who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: “I take garments on contract to sew them, then I give them to the young workers for two-thirds.” He said: “Do you not also work on them?” I said: “I cut them and buy the threads for them.” He said: “There is no harm in that.”

And it is narrated from Muḥammad al-Ṭayyār, who said: I entered al-Madīnah and looked for a house to rent. Then I entered a dwelling in which there were two rooms with a door between them, and in it was a woman. She said, "Will you rent this room?" I said, "There is a door between them, and I am a young man." She said, "I will close the door between me and you." So I moved my belongings into it and said to her, "Close the door." She said, "The air comes to me through it; leave it." So I said, "No, I am a young man and you are a young woman; close it." She said, "Sit in your room; I will not come to you nor approach you," but she refused to close it. So I went to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him about that, and he said: "Move out from it, for when a man and a woman are left alone in a house, the third of them is al-Shayṭān."

Abu Hammam wrote to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: Concerning a man who rented an estate from another man, then the lessor sold that estate in the presence of the tenant, and the tenant did not object to the sale and was present for it as a witness to it. Then the buyer died and left heirs. Does that property return as part of the deceased's inheritance, or does it remain in the hand of the tenant until his lease expires? So he عليه السلام wrote: "It remains in the hand of the tenant until his lease expires."

And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyyah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, chose tillage and cultivation for His prophets عليهم السلام so that they would not dislike anything from the rain of the sky.”
And ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious: “And upon Allah let the reliant rely.” He said: “The farmers.”

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who is given a garment to dye, but he ruins it. So he عليه السلام said: Every worker whom you have given a wage to repair something, but he damages it instead, then he is liable.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a launderer to whom goods are handed over, and he burns them or tears them. Is he held liable for compensation? He عليه السلام said: "Yes, make him liable for what his hand has caused, for you only gave it to him so that he might repair it, and you did not give it to him so that he might ruin it."

And he, peace be upon him, said: My father, peace be upon him, used to hold the launderer and the goldsmith liable for what they damaged, while ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them both, would show favor toward them.

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a camel driver who carries oil with him and says: it was lost, or spilled, or the road was cut off against him: "If he brings upright evidence against himself that the road was cut off against him or it was lost, then there is nothing upon him; otherwise, he is liable." And regarding a man for whom another man carried food in his boat, then it decreased, he said: "He is liable." I said to him: "Perhaps it sometimes increased." He said: "Do you know that he added anything to it?" I said: "No." He said: "It is yours."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding the washer and the goldsmith: if something is stolen from them, and they do not bring clear proof concerning a manifest matter that it was indeed stolen, then for any amount, small or great, they are liable. But if they do so, then nothing is upon them. And if he does not establish proof and claims that what was alleged has gone, then he is liable for it if he has no proof for his statement.

And he said: Regarding a man who hires an animal to a known place and then the animal is lost, he said: “If he exceeded the stipulated condition, then he is liable. If he entered a valley and did not secure it, then he is liable. And if it fell into a well, then he is liable, because he did not take sufficient precaution regarding it.”

And it is narrated from a camel driver from whom camels were hired, and oil was sent with him to a land. He claimed that some of the oil skins had torn and the oil had spilled. He said: If he wishes, he may take the oil. And he said: It was torn, but he is not to be believed except with just evidence. And whichever man hires an animal, and a wolf attacks it and splits its eye so it dies, then he is liable for it unless he is a just Muslim.

And it is narrated from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān, who said: My father sent goods to al-Shām with a camel-driver, and he mentioned that one load of it was lost. So I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said, “Do you accuse him?” I said, “No.” He said, “Then do not hold him liable.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a launderer to whom I gave a garment, and he claimed that it was stolen from among his clothes. He said: He must establish proof that it was stolen from among his belongings, and there is nothing upon him; and if it was stolen together with his belongings, then there is nothing upon him.

And ʿUthmān ibn Ziyād narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: We had a camel driver working for us, and he loaded it onto someone else, so it was lost. He said: Make him liable and take compensation from him.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to hold the dyer, the launderer, and the goldsmith liable, as a precaution for the belongings of the people. And he did not hold them liable for drowning, fire, or an overwhelming occurrence. And when the ship sinks along with what is in it, and people recover it, then whatever the sea casts onto its shore belongs to its owners, and they have the greater right to it. And whatever people dive for, after its owner has abandoned it, then it belongs to them.

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The goldsmith, the launderer, and the weaver are not held liable unless they are suspected. In such a case, they must bring evidence, and he is to be warned and made to swear an oath, so that perhaps something may be extracted from him.
And ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought the case of a bathhouse keeper with whom clothes had been placed, then they were lost, so he did not hold him liable, and he said: He is only a trustee.
Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام held a Muslim man liable for the value of a pig belonging to a Christian, which he had damaged.

And Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who hires a porter, and he breaks what he is carrying upon him or spills it, he said: “If he is trustworthy, then there is nothing upon him; and if he is not trustworthy, then he is liable.”

Ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who carried goods on his head, then struck a person so that he died, or something was broken because of it: then he is liable.

3933 - It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said: A man wrote to al-Faqīh عليه السلام concerning a man who gave a garment to the fuller to process it, then the fuller gave it to another fuller to process it, and the garment was lost. Is it obligatory upon the fuller to restore what he handed over to someone else, if the fuller was trustworthy? So he عليه السلام wrote: "He is liable for it unless he is trustworthy and reliable, if Allah wills."

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from more than one person, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a man who trades with another man over an item, he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm, if the origin of the item is halal (permissible).”

And Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated, saying: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A man has wealth, then he comes to his companion who sells him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and defers the payment for him until a time. He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in it. My father عليه السلام had instructed me, and I did that.

And it is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I assigned a man an ʿīnah, then it became due upon him, so I said to him: ‘Repay me.’ He said: ‘I do not have it with me, so assign me another ʿīnah until I repay you.’ He said: ‘Assign it to him until he repays you.’”

It is narrated from Bakkar ibn Abi Bakr, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who has money owed to him by another man, when the debt becomes due, the debtor says to him, 'Sell me some goods so that I may sell them and repay you what I owe.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
It is narrated from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man sells dirhams for dinars on credit. He said: There is no harm in it.

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Silver for silver must be equal, and gold for gold must be equal. There must be neither an increase nor a delay. The one who gives extra and the one who seeks extra are in the Fire.

Aban narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: A man is owed dinars by another man, so he takes dirhams from him, then the price changes. He said: They belong to him according to the rate at which he took them that day. And if he took dinars, and the other had no dirhams with him, then his dinars remain owed by him, and he may take them in their original amount whenever he wishes.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man comes to me with dirhams, and I buy them from him with dinars. Then I give him a pouch containing dinars greater than the value of his dirhams. I say to him: From these dinars, such-and-such dinars are the price of your dirhams. So he takes the pouch from me, then returns it to me and says: Keep them recorded with you for me. So he عليه السلام said: If the pouch contains sufficient amount to cover the price of his dirhams, then there is no harm in it.

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A man from the people of Sijistān came to him and said: “We have dirhams called al-Shāmiyyah that carry two dāniqs more than the dirhams.” So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it; that is permissible.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about two moneychangers who bought silver with dinars. One of them said to his companion, "Pay on my behalf," while he was well-off, and if he wished to pay, he would pay, so his companion paid on his behalf. Then it occurred to him to buy his companion's share with a profit. Is that valid? He عليه السلام said: "There is no harm in it."

It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Dirhams for dirhams, when one of the two contains lead, while being equal weight for equal weight. He said: Repeat it. So I repeated it to him. Then he said: Repeat it. So I repeated it to him. Then he said: “I see no harm in it.”

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked him about currency exchange, and I said to him: Sometimes the caravan hastens, and we are unable to obtain the Damascene and Basran currency, while in Nishapur only the Damascene and Basran currency is accepted. So he said: What is the caravan? I said: They are people who accompany one another and gather together for departure. Then when they hasten, they may be unable to obtain the Damascene and Basran currency, so we sell it in lower-quality coins, and they exchange one thousand and fifty of them for one thousand of the Damascene currency. He said: There is no good in it. Why do you not put gold into it because of its excess? So I said to him: May I buy one thousand and a dinar for two thousand dirhams? He said: There is no harm. My father, peace be upon him, was bolder with the people of al-Madinah than we are, and he used to do this. They would say: This is only fleeing. And if a man brought a dinar, he would not be given one thousand dirhams, and if he brought one thousand dirhams, he would not be given one thousand dinars. And he, peace be upon him, used to say: Excellent indeed is fleeing from the haram to the halal.

Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a man who owes me money and repays me partly in dinars and partly in dirhams. Then when he comes to settle the account with me in full, the price of the dinars has changed. Which of the two prices should I calculate by: the price that was on the day he gave me the dinars, or the price of the day I settle the account with him? He عليه السلام said: "The price of the day he gave you the dinars, because you withheld their benefit from him."

ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about buying silver that contains mercury and lead with silver coins, while, when it is melted, it decreases by two or three dirhams out of every ten. So he عليه السلام said: “It is not valid except with gold.”

It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man has with me some clear silver dirhams. He meets me and says: Do I not have with you such-and-such, a thousand clear dirhams? So I say: Yes. Then he says: Convert them into dinars at this rate and record them for me with you. So what do you think about this? He said: If you have precisely determined the rate for him on that day, then there is no harm in that. He said: So I said: I did not weigh it out for him, nor did I carry out a hand-to-hand exchange with him; it was only speech between me and him. So he said: Are not the dirhams from with you and the dinars from with you? I said: Yes. He said: There is no harm in that.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to Zaynab, the perfume seller, al-Hawlaʾ: When you sell, then act with excellence and do not deceive, for that is purer and more enduring for wealth.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "He who deceives a Muslim is not from us."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever deceives the Muslims will be resurrected with the Jews on the Day of Judgment, because they are the most deceitful of people toward the Muslims.

Abū ʿAbdillāh Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: None consume from lost property except those who are themselves astray.

And in the narration of Masʿadah ibn Ziyād, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said: Beware of lost property, for it is the lost possession of the believer, and it is a blaze from the blaze of Hell.

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: About a lost item found by a poor person—whether he is regarding it in the same position as a wealthy person. So he said: “Yes.” He said: “And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام used to say: ‘It belongs to its owners; do not touch it.’” He said: And I asked him about a man who finds a dirham, a garment, or an animal—what should he do? He said: “He should announce it for one year. If it is not recognized, he should place it among his property until its claimant comes, then he gives it to him. And if he dies, he should make a bequest concerning it, and he is liable for it.”

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man found a dinar in his house. So he said: "Does someone other than him enter his house?" I said: "Yes, many." He said: "This is luqaṭah (lost property)." I said: And a man found a dinar in his صندوق (box). He said: "Does anyone other than him put his hand into his box or place something in it?" I said: "No." He said: "Then it belongs to him."

4051 - And Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Raja' al-Khayyat, who said: I wrote to al-Tayyib عليه السلام: “I was in al-Masjid al-Haram and saw a dinar. I reached toward it to take it, and then I found another. Then I searched among the pebbles and found a third. So I took them and announced them, but no one identified them. So what do you see regarding that?” So he عليه السلام wrote: “I have understood what you mentioned regarding the matter of the dinars. If you are in need, then give one-third of them in charity; and if you are wealthy, then give all of them in charity.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya al-Jammal that he heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: Whoever finds lost property and does not announce it, then it is later found in his possession, it belongs to its owner, and an equivalent of it is due from the wealth of the one who concealed it.

4053 - And it is narrated from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man found some money and announced it, until when the year had passed, he bought with it a servant. Then the seeker of the money came and found that the slave-girl whom he had bought with the dirhams was his daughter. He عليه السلام said: He has no right to take anything except the dirhams, and the daughter is not his. He is only entitled to his principal amount. His daughter had only been the property of some people.

Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Mukram al-Jammal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that Dharih asked him: about a slave who picks up lost property, so he said: What has a slave to do with lost property? A slave does not own anything of himself, so the slave should not expose himself to it. Rather, it is fitting for a free person to announce it for a year in a public gathering. If its claimant comes, he should hand it over to him; otherwise, it becomes from his property. If he dies, it becomes an inheritance for his children and those who inherit from him. Then if its claimant comes after that, they should hand it over to him.
Dawud ibn Abi Yazid asked him: about a water container, a pair of sandals, and a whip that a man finds on the road: may he make use of it? He said: "He should not touch it."
And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no harm in picking up lost items such as a staff, a strap, a peg, a rope, a hobble, and similar things.

He was asked about a stray sheep in the wilderness, so he said to the questioner: “It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.” He said: “And I do not like to touch it.” And regarding the stray camel also, he said: “What do you have to do with it? Its belly is its container, its hoof is its shoe, and its stomach is its water carrier. Leave it alone.”

And it is narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said: A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about lost property while I was listening. So he said: "Announce it for one year. Then if you find its owner, otherwise you are more entitled to it."

4059 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: “Ali عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who left his animal due to hardship. He said: If he left it in pasture, water, and safety, then it remains his, and he may take it wherever he finds it. But if he left it in a place of danger, without water and without pasture, then it belongs to the one who finds it.”

And it is narrated from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the payment for a runaway slave and lost property. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Husayn ibn Zayd narrated from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say concerning a stray animal that a man finds and intends to take a reward for it, then it perishes: "He is liable for it. But if he did not intend to take a reward for it and it perished, then there is no liability upon him."

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, who said: I asked him, peace be upon him, in a letter, about a man who bought a camel, a cow, a sheep, or something else for sacrificial animals or otherwise. Then, when he slaughtered it, he found in its belly a pouch containing dirhams, dinars, jewels, or other such benefits. To whom does that belong, and how should he deal with it? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “Inform the seller about it. If he does not recognize it, then the thing is yours; Allah has provided it to you.”

Al-Hajjal narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A man said to him: "I have come upon some wealth, and I have feared for myself concerning it. If I were to find its owner, I would hand it over to him and be rid of it." He said to him: "Then by Allah, if you were to find him, would you hand it over to him?" He said: "Yes, by Allah." He عليه السلام said: "Then no, by Allah, it has no owner other than me." He said: And he made him swear that he would deliver it to whomever he instructed him. He said: So he swore. He said: "Go and divide it among your brothers, and you shall have safety regarding what you feared." He said: So he divided it among his brothers.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The best course a person may adopt regarding lost property, when he finds it, is not to take it and not to expose himself to it. If people were to leave what they find, its owner would come and take it.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: A gift in the Torah is an eye-coverer.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Exchange gifts with one another, and you will love one another.
And he, peace be upon him, said: A gift removes grudges.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Excellent indeed is a gift given before a need is presented.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: If I were invited to a trotter, I would accept, and if a trotter were gifted to me, I would accept it.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Hasten to return the containers of gifts, for that is quicker in bringing about their continued exchange.
He, peace be upon him, would not refuse perfume or sweets.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام was presented with a gift of Nayrūz, so he said عليه السلام: “What is this?” They said: “O Commander of the Faithful, today is Nayrūz.” So he said عليه السلام: “Make every day for us a Nayrūz.”
And it is narrated that he said, peace be upon him: "Our Nayrouz is every day."

Thuwair ibn Abī Fākhitah narrated from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: Kisrā sent a gift to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and he accepted it. Qayṣar sent a gift to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and he accepted it. And the kings sent gifts to him, and he accepted them.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Visit those who do not visit you, and give gifts to those who do not give gifts to you.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Gifts are of three types: a gift given in reciprocation, a gift given to seek favor, and a gift given for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who owns a large estate, and when the days of Mehregan and Nayrouz arrive, people gift him items; they do not gift him that item to seek closeness to him [as an obligation]. He (peace be upon him) said: "Are they not worshippers [Muslims]?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then let him accept their gifts and reciprocate them."
And he, peace be upon him, said: If a gift of food is given to a man and he has people with him, then they are partners in it, meaning fruit and other things.

And it is narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Aʿyan, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who gave a gift to another man while hoping for its recompense, but its owner did not recompense him until he died, and the man found his gift itself. Is it for him to take it back if he is able to do that? He said: There is no harm in his taking it.

And it is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to him: A poor man gives me a gift, seeking what I have; so I take it and do not give him anything. Is it permissible for me? He said: Yes, it is halal for you, but do not refrain from giving him something.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a matter concerning which Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qummī al-Ashʿarī had written to me. He said: We have estates in which there are fire temples, to which the Magians bring cattle, sheep, and dirhams. Is it permissible for the owners of the villages to take that, while the fire temples have caretakers who oversee them? Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Let the owners of the villages take from that; there is no harm in it.”

It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام or Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said: A borrowed item is not subject to liability upon its borrower unless that is stipulated, except what is of gold or silver, for indeed those two are guaranteed whether it is stipulated or not. And he عليه السلام said: If an item is borrowed without its owner’s permission and it perishes, then the borrower is liable.

And Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a borrowed item that a person borrows, and it then perishes or is stolen. So he said: “If he is trustworthy, then there is no liability upon him.”

And Aban narrated from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who borrowed a garment, then deliberately turned to it and pledged it as collateral; then the owners of the property came for their property, so he عليه السلام said: “They take their property.”

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله borrowed seventy smashing coats of mail from Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah al-Jumaḥī, and that was before his Islam. So he said, “Is it seizure or a loan, O Abā al-Qāsim?” He صلى الله عليه وآله said, “No, rather, it is a loan that will be returned.” Thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be regarding a borrowed item, when it is stipulated in it that it be returned. And Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, after his Islam, was sleeping in the mosque, and his cloak was stolen. So he followed the thief and took the cloak from him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and established against him two just witnesses. So he عليه السلام ordered that his right hand be cut off. Then Ṣafwān said, “O Messenger of Allah, will you cut him off because of my cloak? I have gifted it to him.” He عليه السلام said, “If only this had been before you brought him to me.” So he cut him off. Thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be regarding the hadd: when it is raised to the Imam and the proof is established against him, it is not to be suspended, and it is to be carried out.
Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The holder of a deposit and the holder of merchandise are both entrusted.
And he said: Regarding a man who hired a laborer and seated him over his goods, then they were stolen, he said: "He is entrusted."

4089 - And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said: A man wrote to al-Faqīh, peace be upon him, regarding a man who entrusted another man with a deposit and instructed him to place it in his house, or did not instruct him; then the man placed it in his neighbor’s house and it was lost. Is liability binding upon him if he went against his instruction or took it out of his possession? So he, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: “He is liable for it, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man has wealth with him as a deposit; may he take from it without the permission of its owner? He said: “He must not take, unless he has the means to repay.” And he said: I said: What do you think—if he finds someone who guarantees it for him, while he does not have the means to repay, and the one who guarantees him bears witness against himself, may he take from it? He said: “Yes.”

And it is narrated from Mismaʿ Abī Sayyār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I had entrusted a man with some wealth, but he denied it to me and swore concerning it to me. Then, after two years, he came to me with the wealth that I had entrusted to him, and said: This is your wealth, so take it. And these are four thousand dirhams that I earned as profit; they are yours along with your wealth. And put me in your absolution. So I took the wealth from him, but I refused to take the profit from him. And I withheld the wealth that I had entrusted, and I refused to take it until I could seek your opinion. So what do you think? He عليه السلام said: Take half of the profit and give him the other half, and absolve him, for this is a repentant man, and Allah "loves those who repent."

Ishaq ibn 'Ammar asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام. About a man who entrusted another man with one thousand dirhams, and they were lost. Then the man said to him: it was only a loan upon him, while the other said: it was only a deposit. So he عليه السلام said: The money is binding upon him unless he establishes proof that it was only a deposit.

4093 - A man said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “Indeed, I entrusted a man with some wealth, depositing it with him, but he betrayed me regarding it and denied my property.” So he عليه السلام said: “The trustworthy one did not betray you; rather, you entrusted a traitor.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said, concerning a man who pledged collateral with another man and the pledged property was lost: “It is from the property of the pledger, and the pledgee may recover his money from him.”

And in the narration of Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The back may be ridden when it is pledged, and the maintenance of it is upon the one who rides it. And the milk may be drunk when it is pledged, and the maintenance is upon the one who drinks the milk.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man takes a slave as collateral, then the slave is afflicted with loss of an eye or something from his body is diminished. Upon whom is the liability for that deficiency? He said: "Upon his master." He said: I said: The people say that if you pledge the slave as collateral and he falls ill, or his eye bursts and he suffers a bodily deficiency, then the man's property is reduced in proportion to what is diminished from the slave. He said: "Tell me, if the slave were to kill, upon whom would his crime be?" He said: "His crime is upon his own neck."

4097 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an item in the hands of two men: one of them says, "I entrusted it to you as a deposit," and the other says, "It is a pledge with me." So he said, "The statement is the statement of the one who says, 'It is a pledge with me,' unless the one who claimed that he had deposited it brings witnesses."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Wallād, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who takes a riding animal and a camel as collateral for his money: does he have the right to ride them? He said: "If he is feeding them, then he has the right to ride them; but if the one who pledged them with him is feeding them, then he does not have the right to ride them."

Hadith 4099 — Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who took as collateral for his money a piece of land or a house, both of which had abundant yield. He عليه السلام said: It is upon the one who took the land and the house as collateral for his money to calculate what he took from the yield for the owner of the land and the house, and deduct it from the debt owed to him.

Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān narrated from Abī ʿImrān al-Armanī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became bankrupt and owed a debt to some people, while some of them had pledged collateral and others did not. Then he died, and his wealth was not sufficient to cover the debt upon him. He عليه السلام said: 'All that he left behind, including the pledged collateral and other property, is to be divided among the creditors according to their proportional shares.'

4101 - He said: And I asked him about a man who pledged collateral with another man against one thousand dirhams, while the collateral was worth two thousand, and it was lost. He said: "He returns against him for the surplus of what he pledged; and if it was less than that for which it was pledged, he returns against the pledger for the surplus; and if the collateral was equal to that for which it was pledged, then the collateral stands for what is in it."

What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a pledge, if it is lost while in the possession of the creditor without his having consumed it, he may return to the pledger for his due and take it. But if he consumed it, then the two of them should settle the excess between themselves.

Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: If a man pledges a piece of land containing fruit, then its produce is counted as part of the reckoning of his property. He is also entitled to account for what he worked on and spent on it. So when he has fully recovered his property, he must return the land to its owner.

Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Regarding a pledged item over which the pledger and the pledgee differ, the pledger says, "It is worth such-and-such," and the pledgee says, "It is worth more"; the pledgee is to be believed until the value reaches the price, because he is trustworthy.

Hadith 4105 — Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who has a pledged item in his possession, but does not know to whom among the people it belongs.
