He said: “I do not like that he sell it until its owner comes.” I said: “He does not know to whom among the people it belongs.” He said: “Is there excess in it or deficiency?” I said: “If there is excess in it or deficiency, what should he do?” He said: “If there is deficiency in it, then it is easier: he may sell it, and he will be rewarded for what remains. But if there is excess in it, then that is more difficult for him: he should sell it and keep its surplus until its owner comes.”

What al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who pledged collateral until a specified time, then disappeared: is there a time at which his collateral may be sold? He said: “No, not until he comes.”

Abān narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man pledged two bracelets with another man, and one of them was destroyed. He said: "He may reclaim his right from what remains."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding a man who pledged a house with another man, and it burned down or collapsed, he said: "His wealth remains in the soil of the land."

And he, peace be upon him, said: Concerning a man with whom another man pawned a slave, and the slave became leprous; or he pawned goods with him, and he did not spread out those goods, nor look after them, nor move them, so they were consumed — meaning, eaten by worms — does that diminish from his wealth by that amount? He said: "No."

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who pledges collateral with another man, and it is destroyed or lost, he عليه السلام said: "He may reclaim his money from him."

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd narrated from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, who said: I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام concerning a man who died while owing a debt and left nothing except a pledged item in the possession of one of them, and its price did not amount to more than the property-right of the pledge-holder. May he take it for his claim, or are he and the rest of the creditors partners in it? So he عليه السلام wrote: “All the creditors in that are equal; they distribute it among themselves according to their shares.” He said: And I wrote to him concerning a man who died and had heirs, then a man came and claimed that the deceased owed him property and that he had a pledge in his possession. So he عليه السلام wrote: “If he has property due from the deceased and has no evidence for it against him, then let him take his property from what is in his hand and return the remainder to his heirs. And whenever he acknowledges what is in his possession, he is held to it and is required to produce evidence for his claim, and his right is fulfilled after the oath. And whenever he does not establish evidence and the heirs are denying, then he has against them an oath of knowledge: they swear by Allah that they do not know that he has any right against their deceased.”

Faḍālah narrated from Abān, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him: How is the pledge dealt with regarding what it contains, if it is an animal, a riding beast, silver, or goods, and a fire or thieves strike it, so his property is destroyed or his goods are diminished, and he has no evidence for his loss? He said: If all of his goods are gone and nothing is found remaining for him, then there is nothing against him. He said: But if he says, 'It went from among my property,' while he still has property, then he is not to be believed.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man with whom another man had pledged two slaves as collateral, and one of them perished. Would his right be in the other? He said: Yes. I said: Or a house, and it burned down—would his right be in the land? He said: Yes. I said: Or two animals, and one of them perished—would his right be in the other? He said: Yes. I said: Or goods that perished because of how long he left them, or food that spoiled, or a غلام whom smallpox struck and he became blind, or clothes that he left folded, not checking them and not unfolding them until they were ruined? He said: This is all one kind; his right remains upon him.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who takes a pledged item for one hundred dirhams while it is worth three hundred dirhams, then destroys it. Is the man required to return two hundred dirhams to its owner? He عليه السلام said: "Yes, because he took a pledge in which there was surplus value and then caused its loss." I said: If half of the pledged item is destroyed? He عليه السلام said: "According to that proportion." I said: Then should they return the surplus value between them? He عليه السلام said: "Yes."

Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding collateral that if it was greater than the amount of the creditor’s property and it was destroyed, the excess must be paid to the owner of the collateral. And if the collateral was less than his property and the collateral was destroyed, its owner must pay him the remainder of his property. And if the collateral was equal in value to what he pledged, then nothing is due upon him.

Faḍālah narrated from Abān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If two parties disagree concerning the pledge, and one of them says, ‘I pledged it for one thousand dirhams,’ while the other says, ‘I pledged it for one hundred dirhams,’ then the one claiming one thousand is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the one claiming one hundred swears an oath. And if the pledged property is less than what it was pledged for or more, and they disagree concerning the pledge, so one of them says, ‘It is a pledge,’ and the other says, ‘It is a deposit,’ then the one claiming it is a deposit is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the one claiming it is a pledge swears an oath.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a man who pledges a slave, a garment, jewelry, or household goods, and the owner of the goods says to the mortgage-holder: 'You are permitted to wear this garment; wear the garment, benefit from the goods, and use the servant.' He said: 'It is halal for him if he has made it halal for him, but I do not like that he should do it.' I said: 'If he takes a house in pledge that has yield, to whom does the yield belong?' He said: 'To the owner of the house.' I said: 'If he takes barren land in pledge, and the owner of the land says to him: Cultivate it for yourself?' He said: 'This is halal. This is not like that case. He cultivates it with his own wealth, so it is halal for him just as he has permitted it for him, because he cultivates it with his own wealth and develops it.'

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Qalla', who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man whose brother died and left a صندوق containing pledged items. Some of them had the name of their owner on them and the amount for which they had been pledged, while some of them it was not known whose they were, nor for how much they had been pledged. What do you say regarding this whose owner is not known? So he عليه السلام said: 'It is like the rest of his property.'

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about the report that was narrated: ‘Whoever places greater trust in the pledge than in his believing brother, then I am free from him.’ He said: ‘That is when the truth becomes manifest and our Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt rises.’ I said: Then what about the report that was narrated: ‘The profit of a believer over another believer is riba’? He said: ‘That is when the truth becomes manifest and our Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt rises. But as for today, there is no harm in selling to a believing brother and making a profit from him.’

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who pledges his bondwoman as collateral: is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said: “Those who have taken her as collateral stand between him and her.” I said: “What if he is able to reach her in private, and those who have taken her as collateral do not know?” He said: “Yes, I do not see any harm in this.”
Sama'ah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: It is not proper to drink from vessels of silver and gold.
Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Do not eat from vessels of gold or silver.

Thaʿlabah narrated from Burayd al-ʿIjli, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he disliked drinking from silver and from a cup plated with silver, and he disliked that one apply oil from a silver-plated oil container, and the comb likewise. If he found no alternative to drinking from a silver-plated cup, he would turn his mouth away from the place of the silver.
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The vessels of gold and silver are the possessions" "of those who do not have certainty."

And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from his brother Yūsuf: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام asked for water, and a cup made of brass containing water was brought to him. Then one of those sitting with him said to him, “Indeed, ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī dislikes drinking from brass.” He said, “Then ask him: is it gold or silver?”
And it is narrated from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام disliked that a man should eat with his left hand, drink with it, or take things with it.

4242 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, عليهما السلام, who said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah, صلى الله عليه وآله, at Tabūk, were drinking water in gulps. So the Messenger of Allah, صلى الله عليه وآله, said: “Drink with your hands, for they are among the best of your vessels.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Drinking water while standing during the day causes more perspiration and is stronger for the body.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Drinking water at night while standing causes yellow water.

One of his companions asked him about drinking in a single breath, so he said: "If the one handing you the water is owned by you, then drink in three breaths; but if he is free, then drink it in a single breath."

And in the narration of Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, he said: "Three breaths while drinking are better than drinking in one breath." And he used to dislike that one should resemble al-Hīm. I said: "What is al-Hīm?" He said: "The camel." And in another hadith: "The camels." And it is narrated: "Al-Hīm are the she-camels." And it is narrated: "Al-Hīm is that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned."
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Do not eat while you are walking, unless you are compelled to do that.

And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Abī Shuʿbah, who said: I saw Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام eating while reclining. Then he mentioned the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: "He did not eat while reclining until he died."
And it is narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Shuʿbah, from Abī Shuʿbah: That he saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام eating while sitting cross-legged.

And in the narration of Ismaʿil ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: When the table is set, four angels surround it. Then if the servant says, 'In the Name of Allah,' the angels say to the Shaytan, 'Be disgraced, O wicked one, for you have no authority over them.' Then when they finish and say, 'All praise is for Allah,' the angels say, 'They are a people upon whom Allah has bestowed blessing, so they rendered thanks to their Lord.' But if they do not say, 'In the Name of Allah,' the angels say to the Shaytan, 'Come near, O wicked one, and eat with them.' And when it is removed, if they do not praise Allah, the angels say, 'They are a people upon whom Allah has bestowed blessing, but they forgot their Lord.'
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "The owner of the provision drinks first among the people and performs wudu (ablution) last among them."
And Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated, saying: I was eating with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “O Sama'ah, eat with praise and gratitude, not eating with silence.”

Hadith 4253 — Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “I guarantee for whoever mentions the Name of Allah over his food that he will not suffer from it.” Then Ibn al-Kawwāʾ said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I ate food last night and mentioned the Name of Allah over it, then it caused me discomfort.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “You ate different kinds of food, and you mentioned the Name over some of them and did not mention it over others, O base fellow.” And it is narrated: “Whoever forgets to mention the Name of Allah over each type, then let him say: ‘In the Name of Allah, over its beginning and its end.’”

4254 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "I have never suffered indigestion at all, and that is because I never began any food except that I said: 'In the Name of Allah,' and I never finished any food except that I said: 'All praise is for Allah.'"
And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, when the stomach is full, it becomes rebellious.

And it has been narrated from ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Māṣir, who said: I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام in al-Madīnah, and before him was a dining spread, and he was eating. So I said to him: What is the proper etiquette of this dining spread? He said: When you place it, mention Allah, and when you lift it, praise Allah, and clean up what is around the dining spread, for this is its proper etiquette. He said: Then I turned, and there was a jug set down, so I said to him: What is the proper etiquette of the jug? He said: Drink from the side nearest to its lip, and mention Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then when you lift it away from your mouth, praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And beware of the place of the handle, that you drink from it, for it is the seat of Satan. This is its proper etiquette.

And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd al-Kirmānī, who said: I ate in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام. When I had finished and the dining cloth was lifted, the servant went to gather what had fallen from the crumbs of food. So he said to him: Whatever was in the open area, leave it, even if it were a sheep’s thigh; and whatever was in the house, then seek it out and pick it up.

4258 - And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the Banu Umayyah begin with vinegar at the start of the meal and conclude with salt, while we begin with salt at the start of the meal and conclude with vinegar.”
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Begin with salt at the start of the meal, for if people knew what is in salt, they would prefer it over the tried remedy.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah عليه السلام using a toothpick, so I looked at him. He said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used a toothpick, and it makes the mouth pleasant.”
And in another narration: Indeed, it is from the right of the guest that a toothpick be prepared for him.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whatever you move around with your tongue and then remove, swallow it; and whatever you remove with a toothpick, throw it away.
Safwan al-Jammal narrated from Abi Ghurrah al-Khurasani, who said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: "Wudu (ablution) before food and after it removes poverty."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever is pleased that the goodness of his house should increase, then let him perform wudu (ablution) when his food is brought."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever washes his hand before food and after it will live in ease and will be kept safe from affliction in his body.

And it is narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, that whenever he ate, he would say: All praise is due to Allah, Who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us, supported us, sheltered us, blessed us, and bestowed bounty upon us. All praise is due to Allah, Who feeds and is not fed.
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "What an excellent condiment vinegar is; a house in which there is vinegar does not become destitute."

Shu'ayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about garlic, onions, and leeks, so he said: There is no harm in eating them raw and in pots, and there is no harm in seeking treatment with garlic. But when that is the case, then he should not go out to the mosque.

And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about garlic, so he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله only forbade it because of its smell, and he said: Whoever eats this foul plant should not come near our mosque. But as for one who eats it and does not come to the mosque, there is no harm.

Ibrāhīm al-Karkhī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Regarding the dining table, there are twelve qualities which every Muslim must know: four of them are obligatory, four are sunnah (recommended practices), and four are manners. As for the obligatory ones, they are: recognition, contentment, naming Allah, and gratitude. As for the sunnah, they are: wudu (ablution) before food, sitting on the left side, eating with three fingers, and licking the fingers. As for the manners, they are: eating from what is nearest to you, making the morsel small, chewing well, and minimizing looking at people's faces.
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: It is appropriate for an elderly person not to sleep unless his stomach is full of food, for it makes his sleep more restful and his breath more pleasant.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: I am amazed at the one who abstains from food out of fear of illness; how does he not abstain from sins out of fear of the Fire?

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: None of you should intercept food outside the city, and no resident should sell on behalf of a desert-dweller. Leave the Muslims so that Allah may provide for some of them through others.

And it is narrated from Minhāl al-Qaṣṣāb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about intercepting sheep, so he said: “Do not intercept, do not buy what has been intercepted, and do not eat from the meat of what has been intercepted.”
And it is narrated: "The limit of intercepting is a day's short journey; then when it reaches four farsakhs, it is transportation."

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: He was asked about a man to whom I had advanced dirhams for food; then when the time for my food came due upon him, he sent dirhams to me and said: 'Buy food for yourself and take your due in full.' So he عليه السلام said: 'I hold that you should assign that to someone other than yourself, and stand with him until you receive what is yours, and do not you yourself undertake its purchase.'

And it was narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who pays one hundred dirhams in advance for wheat or dates. Then, when the debt becomes due, the seller comes and says, “By Allah, I do not have except half of what is yours; so take from me, if you wish, wheat for half of what is yours and silver coin for the other half.” He said: “There is no harm, if he takes the silver coin from him just as he had given it.” He said: And I asked him about a man who owes me a basket of unripe dates, and I take from him in its place a basket of fresh dates, while it is less than it. He said: “There is no harm.” I said: Then a basket of unripe dates is owed to me, and I take in its place a basket of dried dates, while it is more than it. He said: “There is no harm, if it is agreed and known between the two of you.” He said: And I asked him about a man who has against another one hundred kurrs of dates, and the latter has palm trees. So he comes to him and says, “Give me these palm trees of yours in exchange for what you owe.” Then it was as though he disliked it. He said: And I asked him about a man who is owed by another loads of fresh dates or dried dates, so he sends dinars to him and says, “Buy with these and take in full for me what is yours.” He said: “There is no harm, if he trusts him.”

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who enters into a salam contract for something other than crops or date-palms. He عليه السلام said: "He should specify a known measure up to a known term." He said: And I asked him about salam in animals and food, and whether a man may take collateral for his money as a pledge. He عليه السلام said: "Yes, secure your wealth properly."

And it is narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: A man had dirhams owed to him by another man from the price of sheep that he had bought from him. Then the creditor came to the debtor demanding payment, so the debtor said to him: I will sell you these sheep for the dirhams that you have with me. So he agreed. He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that.

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made an advance payment for something in which people make advance payments, from fruits, but its fruits were lost, and he did not fully receive his advance. He عليه السلام said: “Then let him take his principal capital, or let him grant him respite.”

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Al-ʿĪṣ ibn Al-Qāsim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who advanced dirhams to another man for wheat, then when the term became due, he did not have food, but he found that he had animals, slaves, and goods. Is it halal (permissible) for him to take those items from his property in exchange for his food? He said: Yes, he may specify such-and-such for such-and-such sāʿs.
And it is narrated from Ḥadīd ibn Ḥakīm, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man buys hides from a butcher and gives him a known amount every day.” He said: “There is no harm in it.”
And Aban narrated that he said: Regarding a man who advances dirhams to another man and pays them to him in another land, he said: “There is no harm in it.”
Sama'ah asked him: About a pledge that a man gives as security in a salam transaction, when he pays in advance for food, goods, or animals, he said: “There is no harm in securing your wealth.”

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salam transactions involving animals, and he said: “There is no harm in it.” I said: “What do you think if he makes a salam contract for known ages or a known type among slaves, and then he gives him less than the stipulated condition or more than it, with mutual willing consent from them?” He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Abān narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sold food for dirhams. When that term became due, he demanded payment from him, so he said: “I do not have dirhams; take food from me.” He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it. He is only entitled to dirhams, and with them he may take whatever he wishes.”

And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He was asked about a man who paid dirhams in advance for five measures of wheat or barley until a specified term. When the one who owed the wheat or barley was unable to pay all that had become due, and the صاحب of the right wished to take half of the food, or a third of it, or less than that, or more, and take the principal value of what remained of the food in dirhams, he said: There is no harm in it. He said: And he was asked about saffron, in which a man advances dirhams for twenty mithqāls, or less than that, or more. He said: There is no harm if the one who owes the saffron is unable to give him all that is due from him, that he take half of his due, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and take the principal value of what remains of his due in dirhams.

And he was asked about a man who pays in advance for sheep, two-year-olds and younger ones and other than that, until a specified term. He said: There is no harm if the one who owes the sheep cannot provide all that he owes: the owner of the sheep may take half of them, or a third of them, or two-thirds of them, and take the capital value of what remains of the sheep in dirhams; and he may take less than their stipulation, but he must not take more than their stipulation. He said: And garments also are like wheat, barley, saffron, and sheep.
3947 - Al-Washsha' narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام say: “It is not proper for a man to advance ghee in exchange for oil, nor oil in exchange for ghee.”

And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about advance payment for meat. He said: “Do not approach it, for at one time he may give you fat meat, at another time lean meat, and at another time emaciated meat. So buy it by direct inspection, hand to hand.” He said: And I asked him about advance payment for water-skins. So he said: “No, for at one time he may give you an incomplete one and at another time a complete one. Rather, buy them by direct inspection, for this is safer for you and for him.”

And Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: “There is no harm in advancing payment for what is weighed in exchange for what is measured, and for what is measured in exchange for what is weighed.”

And Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: There is no harm in salam with a known measure and to a known term, and it is not to be contracted to threshing or harvesting.

3951 - Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is it permissible to enter into a salam contract for food with a man who has neither food nor livestock with him, except that when the appointed term comes, he buys it and delivers it in full?” He said: “If he guarantees it until a specified term, then there is no harm in it.” He said: I said, “What do you think—if he delivers part of it to me and delays part of it, is that permissible?” He said: “Yes.”

And al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about collateral and a guarantor in a deferred sale. He said: There is no harm in it.
And in the narration of Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: There is no harm in salam for goods when you describe the length and width, and for animals when you describe their teeth.
It is narrated from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Hoarding applies only to wheat, barley, dates, raisins, ghee, and oil.

3955 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, passed by the hoarders and ordered that their hoarded goods be brought out into the open parts of the markets and where people could see them. Then it was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, “If only you would fix prices for them.” So he, peace be upon him, became angry until anger was recognized in his face, and he said: “Am I to fix prices for them? Indeed, pricing belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He raises it when He wills and lowers it when He wills.”

Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He was asked about hoarding, so he said: Hoarding is only when you buy food while there is no other food in the town besides it, then you hoard it. But if there is other food or merchandise in the town besides it, then there is no harm in seeking profit through your goods.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah al-Hannat, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: “What is your occupation?” I said: “A grain seller, and sometimes I come upon brisk demand, and sometimes I come upon stagnation, so I hold it back.” He said: “What do the people around you say about it?” I said: “They say: a hoarder.” He said: “Does anyone other than you sell it?” I said: “What I sell is only one part out of a thousand parts.” So he said: “There is no harm. Rather, that concerned a man from Quraysh called Hakim ibn Hizam. When food entered al-Madinah, he would buy all of it. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by him and said to him: ‘O Hakim ibn Hizam, beware lest you hoard.’”

Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding merchants who came to a land and agreed among themselves not to sell their merchandise except at whatever price they wished, he said: “There is no harm in that.”
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: No one hoards food except a sinner.
And it is narrated from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said: A man asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about storing food for a year. He said: "I do it."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The one who brings goods to the market is provided sustenance, and the hoarder is cursed.
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام forbade hoarding in the cities.

Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Hoarding in times of abundance is for forty days, and in hardship and affliction, three days. So whatever exceeds forty days in times of abundance, its owner is accursed; and whatever exceeds three days in hardship, its owner is accursed.
And Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: Whoever hoards food, mercy is removed from him.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Measure your food, for indeed, the blessing is in the measured food.

And it is narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī that he said: The rise in prices was mentioned in the presence of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, so he said: “What is the rise of its price to me? If it rises, then it is upon Him, and if it becomes cheap, then it is upon Him.”
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Buy, even if it is expensive, for indeed sustenance descends with purchasing.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Indeed, I see you in prosperity. So he said: "Their prices were low."

And it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family: “If only you would set a fixed price for us, for prices rise and fall.” So he, peace be upon him, said: “I would not meet Allah, the Exalted, with an innovation about which He has conveyed nothing to me. So leave the servants of Allah to benefit from one another. And when you are asked for sincere advice, then offer sincere advice.”

And it is narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, عليهما السلام, who said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has appointed an angel over pricing, who regulates it by His command.”

And it is narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: O Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, buying flour is humiliation, buying wheat is honor, and buying bread is poverty. So seek refuge in Allah from poverty.

And he, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, entered upon Aisha while she was counting the bread, and he said: "O Humayra', do not count, lest it be counted against you."
Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Do not withhold lending leavened dough and bread, for withholding them causes poverty.

3974 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “The sign of Allah’s pleasure with His creation is the justice of their ruler and the affordability of their prices, and the sign of Allah’s anger upon His creation is the oppression of their ruler and the high cost of their prices.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who bought an estate, and he had been entering it and leaving it. Then when he paid the money, he went to the estate and inspected it, then returned and asked the owner to revoke the sale, but he did not revoke it for him. So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “If he had turned it over and looked at ninety-nine parts of it, then one part remained that he had not seen, he would still have, in that case, the option of inspection.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muyassir ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man bought a skin-container of oil and found sediment in it, so he said: “If he was among those who know that such a thing occurs in oil, he should not return it to him. But if he did not know that such a thing occurs in oil, he may return it to him.”

3978 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام entered the market of the date sellers, and there was a woman crying while disputing with a date seller. So he said to her, “What is the matter with you?” She said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I bought dates from this man for one dirham, but its lower part turned out to be of poor quality and not like this which I had seen.” So he said to him, “Return it to her.” But he refused, until he said it to him three times, and he still refused. Then he struck him with the whip until he returned it to her. And he عليه السلام used to dislike that the dates be covered over.

It is narrated from Zurarah ibn Aʿyun that he said: Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام was asked about the creation of Hawwa, and it was said to him: some people among us say that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Hawwa from Adam’s leftmost rib. So he said: “Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He far above that with a great exaltation. Does the one who says this claim that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not have the power to create a spouse for Adam from other than his rib, and thus give a way for the fault-finders among the people of disparagement to speak, saying that Adam was having relations with part of himself if she was from his rib? What is with these people? May Allah judge between us and them.” Then he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created Adam عليه السلام from clay and commanded the angels, so they prostrated to him, He cast sleep upon him. Then He originated Hawwa for him and placed her in the place of the hollow that is between his hips, and that was so that the woman would be subordinate to the man. Then she began to move, so he awoke because of her movement. When he awoke, she was called to move away from him. When he looked at her, he saw a beautiful creation resembling his form, except that she was female. So he spoke to her, and she spoke to him in his language. He said to her, ‘Who are you?’ She said, ‘A creation whom Allah created, as you see.’ Adam عليه السلام then said, ‘My Lord, what is this beautiful creation whose nearness has given me comfort, and looking at whom has pleased me?’ So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said, ‘O Adam, this is My maidservant Hawwa. Do you love that she should be with you, give you comfort, speak with you, and be subject to your command?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Lord, and to You is upon me for that praise and thanks as long as I remain.’ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘Then ask for her hand from Me, for she is My maidservant, and she is also suitable for you as a wife for desire.’ And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cast desire upon him, and He had taught him before that knowledge of everything. So he said, ‘My Lord, I ask for her hand from You, so what is Your pleasure regarding that?’ He, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘My pleasure is that you teach her the features of My religion.’ He said, ‘That is for You, my Lord, upon me, if You will that for me.’ He, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘And I have

Zurarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That Ādam عليه السلام had a son born to him, Shīth, and that his name was Hibatullāh, and he was the first successor to whom testamentary authority was entrusted among humankind on the earth. Then after Shīth, Yāfith was born to him. When the two reached maturity, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to bring forth through progeny what you see, and that there be established what the Pen had already decreed regarding the prohibition of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had forbidden of sisters for brothers. So, after al-ʿAṣr on a Thursday, He sent down a heavenly maiden from Paradise whose name was Nazlah, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam to marry her to Shīth, so he married her to him. Then, after al-ʿAṣr on the following day, He sent down a heavenly maiden from Paradise whose name was Munzalah, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam to marry her to Yāfith, so he married her to him. Then a boy was born to Shīth, and a girl was born to Yāfith. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam, when they reached maturity, to marry the daughter of Yāfith to the son of Shīth, and he did so. Then the chosen ones from among the Prophets and the Messengers were born from their offspring. And far be it from Allah that this should have been as they have said regarding the matter of brothers and sisters.

Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah narrated from Burayd al-'Ijli, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down to Adam a huri from Paradise, and he married her to one of his two sons. The other married a daughter of the jinn. So whatever abundant beauty or good character there is among people is from the huri, and whatever bad character there is among them is from the daughter of the jinn.

It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Among the blessings of a woman are the lightness of her expenses and the ease of her childbirth. And among her misfortunes are the heaviness of her expenses and the difficulty of her childbirth.”
And it is narrated: Among the blessings of a woman is the smallness of her dowry, and among her misfortunes is the largeness of her dowry.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Marry blue-eyed women, for indeed there is blessing in them."
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Marry a dark-skinned, wide-eyed, full-figured, medium-height woman; if you dislike her, then the dowry is upon me.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, when he intended to marry a woman, would send someone to look at her, and he said: "Smell her neck; if her neck is pleasant, her scent will be pleasant. And if her ankles are fleshy, her body will be well-developed."
And he, peace be upon him, said: If any of you intends to marry, then let him inquire about her hair just as he inquires about her face, for hair is one of the two aspects of beauty.

And he, peace be upon him, said: The best of your women is the one of pleasant fragrance and good food, who, if she spends, spends in a proper manner, and if she withholds, withholds in a proper manner. Such a woman is among the workers of Allah, and the worker of Allah does not fail.

Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The best of your women is the one who, if she becomes angry or causes her husband to become angry, says to her husband: 'My hand is in your hand; I will not sleep until you are pleased with me.'

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family. He said: We began discussing women and the superiority of some of them over others, so the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Shall I not inform you of the best of your women? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah, then inform us. He said: Among the best of your women is the fertile, loving, modest, chaste one; honored among her family, humble with her husband; adorned for her husband, guarded from others; the one who listens to his speech and obeys his command; and when he is alone with her, she gives him what he desires from her, and she does not present herself to him in the manner of a man.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: A Muslim man does not gain a benefit after Islam better than a Muslim wife who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and safeguards herself and his wealth when he is absent from her.

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, and said: “I have a wife who, when I enter, receives me, and when I go out, sees me off. When she sees me worried, she says: ‘What concerns you? If you are concerned about your sustenance, then another than you has guaranteed it for you; and if you are concerned about the matter of your afterlife, then may Allah increase your concern.’” So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Indeed, Allah has workers, and this woman is among His workers; she shall have half the reward of the martyr.”
It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The most overpowering enemy of a believer is a bad wife.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “I have not seen those weak in religion and deficient in intellect more capable of overpowering a person of understanding than you.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, women are dependence and vulnerability; so conceal the vulnerability with houses, and conceal the dependence with silence.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Were it not for women, Allah would truly be worshiped, truly.

4374 - Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: In the last days and with the approach of the Hour, which will be the worst of times, women will appear who are uncovering, naked, and displaying themselves. They will be outside the religion, entering into trials, inclining toward desires, hastening toward pleasures, and deeming the forbidden to be permissible; in Jahannam they shall abide forever.

4375 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by some women, stopped by them, then said: "O assembly of women, I have not seen those deficient in intellect and religion more capable of taking away the minds of people of understanding than you. Indeed, I have seen that you are the majority of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, so seek nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as much as you are able." Then one woman among them said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the deficiency in our religion and our intellect?" He said, "As for the deficiency in your religion, it is the menstruation that affects you, so one of you remains, as Allah wills, not performing salat (prayer) and not fasting. And as for the deficiency in your intellect, it is your testimony: the testimony of a woman is only half the testimony of a man."

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Shall I not inform you of the worst of your women?” They said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah, then inform us.” He said: “Among the worst of your women is the one who is lowly among her family, mighty with her husband, barren, rancorous, who does not refrain from anything vile, who displays herself when her husband is absent, but is chaste with him when he is present; the one who does not listen to his speech nor obey his command; and when he is alone with her, she resists with the resistance of a difficult mount when it is ridden; she does not accept any excuse from him, nor forgive any fault of his.”

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up to deliver a sermon and said: "O people, beware of the green growth in a dung heap." It was asked: " It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the green growth in a dung " He said: "A beautiful woman raised in a bad environment."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Know that a dark-skinned woman, if she bears many children, is more beloved to me than a beautiful woman who is barren.

Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Bashshār, who said: I wrote to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning a man who proposed to me, so he wrote: Whoever proposes to you, if you are satisfied with his religion and his trustworthiness, then marry him, whoever he may be; and if you do not do so there will be fitnah in the earth and great corruption.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "I am only a human being like you." I marry among you and I give you in marriage, except Fāṭimah, for indeed her marriage descended from the heaven.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Were it not that Allah, the Exalted, created Fatimah for Ali, there would have been no equal for her on the face of the earth, from Adam and those below him.
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم looked at the children of ʿAlī and Jaʿfar عليهما السلام and said: “Our daughters are for our sons, and our sons are for our daughters.”
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: The believers are equals to one another.
And he عليه السلام said: "A suitable match is one who is chaste and possesses financial means."
Muhammad ibn Humran narrated from his father, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever marries while the moon is in al-‘Aqrab will not see the good outcome.
And it is narrated: That it is disliked to marry during the waning phase of the month.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him): About a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still small, then she grows up before her husband enters into her (consummates the marriage). Is the marriage valid for her, or is the matter in her hands? He said: 'The marriage performed by her father is valid for her.'

Ibn Bukayr narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A young girl—her father wants to marry her to one man, and her grandfather wants to marry her to another man. So he said: “The grandfather has more right in that, if the father has not already married her off before him.”

And in the narration of Hishām ibn Sālim and Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If the father and the grandfather both arrange the marriage, then the marriage arranged by the one who acted first takes precedence. But if they both arranged it at one and the same time, then the grandfather has greater authority.

And Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated from Muslim ibn Bashīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman and did not bring witnesses. He said: “As for what is between him and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then there is nothing against him. But if a tyrannical ruler were to seize him, he would punish him.”

And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAwwāḍ, from ʿAbd al-Khāliq, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a previously married woman who seeks marriage for herself. He said: “She has greater authority over herself. She may entrust her affair to whomever she wishes, if he is a suitable match, after she has previously married a husband before that.”

And Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Regarding a man who wishes to marry off his sister, he said: "He should consult her. If she remains silent, then that is her consent; and if she refuses, he should not marry her off. If she says, 'Marry me to so-and-so,' then he should marry her to whomever she approves of. And the orphan girl in the care of a man, he should not marry her off except to one whom she is pleased with."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, Zurārah, and Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A woman who possesses authority over herself, being neither foolish nor under guardianship, her marriage without a guardian is permissible.

4398 — Abū Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, delivered a speech when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله married Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, may Allah have mercy on her, after he had proposed for her to her father, and some people say to her uncle. So he took hold of the two doorposts, while those of Quraysh who witnessed him were present, and he said: All praise belongs to Allah, who made us from the offspring of Ibrāhīm and the descendants of Ismāʿīl, and made for us a House visited in pilgrimage. and a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of all things are brought. And He made us rulers over the people in our land in which we are. Then indeed my nephew Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib is not weighed against any man of Quraysh except that he outweighs him, nor is he compared with any of them except that he is greater than him. Even if he has little wealth, wealth is passing provision and a vanishing shade. He has desire for Khadījah, and she has desire for him. The dowry—its immediate and deferred portions, whatever you ask—shall be from my wealth. And he possesses immense worth, lofty rank, and an eloquent, weighty tongue. So he married her to him, and he consummated the marriage with her the following day. The first child she bore was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله.

When Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام married the daughter of al-Maʾmūn, he delivered the marriage sermon for himself and said: All praise belongs to Allah, the Completer of blessings through His mercy, and the Guide to gratitude through His favor. And may Allah send blessings upon Muḥammad, the best of His creation, in whom He gathered of excellence what He had distributed among the messengers before him, and He made his inheritance belong to the one whom He singled out for his succession; and may He grant abundant peace. And this Amīr al-Muʾminīn has married me to his daughter upon what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for Muslim women over believing men: either retention in a fair manner or release with kindness. And I have given her as dowry what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله gave to his wives, and that is twelve uqiyyahs and a nashsh, and the completion of the five hundred is upon me. And I have additionally bestowed upon her from my wealth one hundred thousand. You have married me to her, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn? He said: “Yes.” He said: “I accept and am satisfied.”
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Whoever marries a woman and does not intend to pay her dowry is, with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a fornicator.
And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Indeed, the most deserving of conditions to be fulfilled are those by which you make lawful access to private parts.

It is narrated from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī that he said: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم married Fāṭimah to ʿAlī عليه السلام, some people from Quraysh came to him and said: “You have married ʿAlī with a paltry dowry.” So he said to them: “It was not I who married ʿAlī, but rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, married him on the night that I was taken on the Night Journey at Sidrat al-Muntahā.” “Scatter.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the lote tree: “Scatter.” So it scattered pearls and jewels upon the wide-eyed maidens, and they exchanged them as gifts among themselves and boasted of them, saying: “This is from the scattering of Fāṭimah, daughter of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.” Then when the night of the wedding came, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم brought his gray mule and folded a cloak upon it, and said to Fāṭimah عليها السلام: “Mount.” And he instructed Salmān, may Allah have mercy on him, to lead it, while the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم drove it from behind. Then while he was on part of the road, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم heard a sound, and there was Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام among seventy thousand, and Mīkāʾīl among seventy thousand. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “What has brought you down to the earth?” They said: “We have come to escort Fāṭimah عليها السلام to her husband.” And Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام proclaimed takbīr, and Mīkāʾīl عليه السلام proclaimed takbīr, and the angels proclaimed takbīr, and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم proclaimed takbīr. Thus takbīr was established over brides from that night.
Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "Escort your brides at night and serve food in the morning."

Sulaimān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “Whoever approaches his wife during the moon’s dark phase at the end of the month, then let him resign himself to the miscarriage of the child.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him, ‘Is intercourse disliked at any particular time among the times?’ He said, ‘Yes, it is disliked on a night in which the moon is eclipsed, on the day in which the sun is eclipsed, between sunset and the disappearance of the twilight, from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun, during the black, red, and yellow wind, and during an earthquake.’ And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم once spent a night with one of his wives, and the moon was eclipsed on that night, so nothing occurred from him. His wife said to him, ‘O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, is all this due to dislike?’ He said, ‘Woe to you, this event has occurred in the heaven, so I disliked to take pleasure and to enter into anything.’ And Allah, the Exalted, has indeed reproached a people and said: ‘And if they were to see a fragment from the sky falling, they would say: piled-up clouds.’ By Allah, no one has intercourse during these times that I have described, then is granted a child from that intercourse, while having heard this hadith, except that he will see what he dislikes.

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Do not have intercourse at the beginning of the month, nor in its middle, nor at its end. For whoever does that should be prepared for miscarriage of the child; and if it is carried to term, it is likely to be mentally unstable. Do you not see that the insane are most often afflicted at the beginning of the month, its middle, and its end?
And he, peace be upon him, said: Janabah is disliked when the sun turns yellow and when it rises while it is yellow.
Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, saying: “May I have intercourse while I am naked?” He said: “No, and do not face the qiblah, nor turn your back to it.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Do not engage in intercourse on a ship.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: It is disliked for a man to approach a woman while he has had a nocturnal emission, until he performs ghusl (ritual bath) from the emission that he saw. If he does so and the child is born mentally disordered, then he should blame none but himself.

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, and a child is born afflicted with leprosy or vitiligo, let him blame none but himself."

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAbdillah, who said: Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: A woman is returned for four things: vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and al-qaran and al-ʿafal, so long as he has not had intercourse with her; but if he has had intercourse with her, then no.

Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who married a woman from a people, then found her to be one-eyed, and they had not made that clear to him. Does he return her? He said: “He does not return her. Marriage is only annulled because of insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo.” I said: What do you think—if he has entered upon her, what should he do? He said: “She is entitled to the dowry because of what he lawfully enjoyed of her private part, and her guardian who married her off must pay him the like of what he gave.”
ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The blind woman, the woman with baras, the woman with leprosy, and the lame woman are returned.

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding a man who marries into a people and then finds that his wife is one-eyed, and they did not make this clear to him, he said: “She is not to be returned. Marriage is only annulled on account of vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and al-'afal.” I said: “What do you think—if he has already consummated the marriage with her, what should be done regarding her dowry?” He said: “The dowry belongs to her because of what he made lawful from her private part, and her guardian who married her off must pay him an amount equal to what he had given to her.”

4499 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who married a woman and found her to be qarnāʾ. He said: “This one does not conceive; she is to be returned to her family.” I said: What if he had entered upon her? He said: “If he knew before having intercourse with her, then had intercourse with her, he has accepted her. But if he did not know about her until after he had intercourse with her, then afterward, if he wishes, he may keep her, and if he wishes, he may send her to her family; and she is entitled to whatever she took from him because of what he made lawful from her private part.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir al-Qaṣabānī narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And the mothers shall suckle their children for two full years." He عليه السلام said: "So long as the child is in suckling, it is shared equally between the two parents. Then when it is weaned, the father has more right to it than the mother. Then if the father dies, the mother has more right to it than the agnatic relatives. And if the father finds someone to suckle him for four dirhams, and the mother says, 'I will not suckle him except for five dirhams,' then he has the right to remove him from her, except that it is better for him and gentler for the child that he leave him with his mother."

And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, or someone else, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who divorced his wife, and they had a child between them. Which of the two has more right to him? He عليه السلام said: "The woman, so long as she does not remarry."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: Any free woman who marries a slave and bears children from him, she has more right to her children than he does, and they are free. Then, when the man is emancipated, he has more right to his children than she does, because of the position of the father.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, who said: One of his companions wrote to him, peace be upon him, saying: "I had a wife, and I have a child from her, and I let her go." So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "The woman has more right to the child until he reaches seven years of age, unless the woman chooses otherwise."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz narrated from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: “A woman’s direct physical contact with her daughter, when she has reached six years, is a branch of zinā.”

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī narrated; he said: Aḥmad ibn al-Nuʿmān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: “I have a young bondwoman between whom and me there is no blood relation, and she is six years old.” He عليه السلام said: “Do not place her in your lap.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: A boy is instructed to perform salat (prayer) when he is seven years old, and a woman does not cover her hair from him until he reaches puberty.
And it is narrated: That children should be separated in their sleeping arrangements at six years of age.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "A boy and a boy, a boy and a girl, and a girl and a girl are to be separated from one another in sleeping places at ten years."

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from al-ʿUbaydī, from Zakariyyā al-Muʾmin, who raised it, that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “When a girl reaches six years of age, a boy should not kiss her, and a boy should not kiss a woman once he has passed seven years of age.”

It is narrated from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “What prevents the believer from taking a spouse? Perhaps Allah will provide him with a soul who will make the earth weighty with ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

And it is narrated from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “Three things are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the messengers: perfume, removing hair closely, and frequent intercourse.”

And al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever marries has safeguarded half of his religion.” And in another hadith: “So let him have taqwa of Allah regarding the remaining half.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: No structure in Islam is more beloved to Allah, Exalted is He, than marriage.

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Marry, for I will outnumber the nations through you tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection, such that even the miscarried child will come lingering at the gate of Paradise. Then it will be said to him, ‘Enter Paradise,’ and he will say, ‘No, not until my parents enter Paradise before me.’”
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Take a spouse, for it is more conducive to sustenance for you."

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the free man: does a bondwoman confer iḥṣān upon him? He عليه السلام said: “A bondwoman does not confer iḥṣān upon a free man, nor does a slave man confer iḥṣān upon a free woman. A Christian man confers iḥṣān upon a Jewish woman, and a Jewish man confers iḥṣān upon a Christian woman.”

4512 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And married women [are forbidden to you]." He said: "They are women who have husbands." I said: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you." He said: "They are the chaste women."

4513 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband over the woman?” So he said to her: “She is to obey him and not disobey him. She is not to give anything in charity from his house except with his permission, and she is not to observe a voluntary fast except with his permission. She is not to withhold herself from him, even if she is upon the back of a saddle. And she is not to leave her house except with his permission. If she leaves without his permission, the angels of the heaven, the angels of the earth, the angels of wrath, and the angels of mercy curse her until she returns to her house.” She said: “O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right over a man?” He said: “His parents.” She said: “Then who has the greatest right over a woman?” He said: “Her husband.” She said: “So do I have over him a right similar to what he has over me?” He said: “No, not even one out of every hundred.” So she said: “By the One who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, no man shall ever possess my neck.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: A woman has no authority, alongside her husband, regarding emancipation, charity, tadbīr, gifting, or making a vow concerning her wealth except with her husband's permission, except in hajj, zakat, dutifulness to her parents, or maintaining ties with her relatives.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Sulaiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: A group of people came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we have seen people prostrating to one another.” The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “If I were to command anyone to prostrate to another, I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband.”

Muhammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Shurays al-Wābishī, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed jihad upon men and upon women. So the jihad of the man is that he gives his wealth and his blood until he is killed in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and the jihad of the woman is that she remains patient over what she sees of the harm of her husband and his jealousy.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, those who are saved from among the men are few, and from among the women, even fewer and fewer.
And in another hadith, he said: “The jihad of a woman is excellent conduct toward her husband.”

Muhammad ibn al-Fudhayl narrated from Saʿd ibn ʿUmar al-Jallab, who said: Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: “Any woman who spends the night while her husband is displeased with her regarding a rightful matter, no salat (prayer) from her is accepted until he becomes pleased with her.”

Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Any woman who leaves her house without her husband’s permission has no maintenance due to her until she returns.”

And he, peace be upon him, said: Any woman who applies perfume for someone other than her husband, no salat (prayer) from her will be accepted until she washes from her perfume as she washes from her janabah.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: It is not appropriate for a woman to perfume her garment with incense when she leaves her house.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Any woman who removes her clothing outside her husband's home or without his permission remains under the curse of Allah until she returns to her house.
Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Any woman who says to her husband, “I have never seen any good from you,” then her deeds are rendered void.

Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام enjoined me concerning the woman so much that I thought her divorce should not be appropriate except for a clear indecency.

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the right of the woman over her husband. He said: "He should satisfy her hunger, clothe her body, and if she acts ignorantly, he should forgive her."

Hadith 4527: “Indeed, Ibrāhīm, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the temperament of Sārah. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: ‘The likeness of a woman is the likeness of a rib: if you straighten it, it will break; and if you leave it, you will enjoy benefit from it.’” I said, “Who said this?” So he became angry, then said: “By Allah, this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.”
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: My father عليه السلام had a wife who used to harm him, yet he would forgive her.

4529 - And 'Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Aba Ja'far عليه السلام say: Whoever has a wife and does not clothe her with what covers her nakedness, nor feed her with what sustains her strength, it is a binding duty upon the Imam to separate them.

Rabi' ibn Abdullah and Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him." He said: "If he provides for her what sustains her strength along with clothing, then it is sufficient. Otherwise, they shall be separated."

Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: If a woman performs her five daily prayers, fasts her month, performs hajj to the House of her Lord, obeys her husband, and recognizes the right of ʿAlī عليه السلام, then let her enter from whichever gates of the gardens she wishes.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man from the Anṣār, during the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, went out for some of his needs and instructed his wife not to leave her house until he returned. He said: Her father became ill, so the woman sent to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: My husband has gone out and instructed me not to leave my house until he returns, and my father is ill, so do you command me to visit him? He said: No, stay in your house and obey your husband. He said: Then he died, so she sent to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, my father has died, so do you command me to perform the funeral prayer over him? He said: No, stay in your house and obey your husband. He said: Then the man was buried, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent to her: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forgiven you and your father because of your obedience to your husband.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire." How do we protect them? He said: "You command them and forbid them." It was said to him: "We command them and forbid them, but they do not accept." He said: "When you have commanded them and forbidden them, then you have fulfilled what is upon you."
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Inspire them with the love of ʿAlī عليه السلام and leave them simple-minded.

Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Do not lodge your women in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, and do not teach them Surah Yusuf. Rather, teach them spinning and Surah al-Nur.

4536 - Durays al-Kunasi narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله for some need, and he said to her: “Perhaps you are one of those who delay.” She said: “Who are those who delay, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “It is the woman whose husband calls her for some need, but she continues delaying him until her husband becomes drowsy and then sleeps. Such a woman continues to be cursed by the angels until her husband wakes up.”

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: May Allah have mercy on a servant who acts well in what is between him and his wife, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given him authority over her and made him her guardian.
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The best of you is the one who is best to his wives, and I am the best of you to my wives.

4540 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "My father Ibrāhīm عليه السلام was protective, and I am more protective than him, and may Allah humble the one among the believers who is not protective."
And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, protective jealousy (ghayrah) is part of faith.

4542 - And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, the fragrance of Paradise is perceived from a distance of five hundred years, yet neither one undutiful to his parents nor a dayyuth will perceive it." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what is a dayyuth?" He said: "The one whose wife commits adultery while he knows of it."

4543 - Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Shurays al-Wābishī, from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: He said to me: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not assign ghayrah to women; rather, He assigned ghayrah to men, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful for a man four free women and those whom his right hand possesses, and He did not make lawful for the woman except her husband alone. So if she seeks other than him while she is with her husband, then with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, she is an adulteress. It is only the women who reject that show such jealousy; as for the believing women, they do not.

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I buy a bondwoman from a trustworthy man, and he informs me that he has not touched her since she menstruated in his possession and then became pure. He عليه السلام said: It is not permissible for you to have intercourse with her until you ensure her freedom from pregnancy by one menstrual cycle. But what is short of the private part is permissible for you. Indeed, those who purchase bondwomen and then have intercourse with them before performing istibrāʾ regarding them—those are adulterers by means of their wealth.

And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: If a man purchases a bondwoman while she has not yet reached maturity, or she has despaired of menstruation, then there is no harm in his not observing istibrāʾ for her.

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a man who purchased a bondwoman, and her owner had not been having relations with her. Should he still observe istibrā’ for her womb? He said: "Yes." I said: "A bondwoman who has not menstruated—what should he do with her?" He said: "Her case is serious. If he goes to her, then he must not ejaculate until it becomes clear to him whether she is pregnant or not." I said to him: "In how long will that become clear to him?" He said: "In forty-five nights."

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man whose slave married a woman without his permission and consummated the marriage with her, then his master came to know of that. He said: That is for his master: if he wishes, he may separate them, and if he wishes, he may approve their marriage. If he does so and separates them, then the woman is entitled to whatever dower he gave her, unless he exceeded bounds and gave her a large dower. But if he approves his marriage, then they remain upon their first marriage. So I said to Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام: then in the basis of the marriage, he had been disobedient. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: He only did something lawful, and he was not disobedient to Allah. He only disobeyed his master, and he did not disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, that is not like his doing what Allah has forbidden him of marriage during a waiting period and the like of that.

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated that a man called Ibn Ziyād al-Ṭāʾī said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I had been a slave, and I married without the permission of my masters. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, set me free, so should I renew the marriage contract?” So he said: “Did they know that you had married?” I said: “Yes, they knew, remained silent, and did not say anything to me.” So he said: “That is an acknowledgment from them. You remain upon your marriage.”

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had two slave sisters and had relations with one of them, then had relations with the other. He said: “If he has relations with the other one, then the first becomes prohibited to him until the other dies.” I said: “What do you think—if he sells her, does the first become permissible for him?” He said: “If he sold her out of a need, and nothing concerning the other occurs in his mind, then I see no harm in that. But if he sells her in order to return to the first, then no, and no honor.”

And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I said to him: A man purchases two sisters and has relations with one of them, then has relations with the other. He said: If he had relations with the other one out of ignorance, the first does not become prohibited for him. But if he had relations with the latter while knowing that she was prohibited for him, then both of them become prohibited for him.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Two rakʿahs performed by a married person are better than seventy rakʿahs performed by an unmarried person.

He said: And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Two units of prayer performed by a married person are better than an unmarried man who spends his nights in prayer and his days fasting."
And it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Indeed, the most despicable of your dead are the unmarried."
It has been narrated that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Most of the inhabitants of the Fire are the unmarried."

Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about two men who jointly owned a bondwoman and married her to a man. Then that man purchased part of the two shares. He said: "She becomes prohibited to him by his purchasing her, and that is because her sale is her divorce, unless he purchases her completely."

And Ismaʿil ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Any free woman who marries herself to a slave without the permission of his masters has made her private part permissible, and there is no dowry for her.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who purchased a mature bondwoman who did not menstruate while with him until six months had passed for her, and there was no pregnancy. He عليه السلام said: "If someone like her normally menstruates, and that is not due to old age, then this is a defect for which she may be returned."

Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him being asked about a man who bought a bondwoman and then had relations with her before ensuring her womb was clear. He said: “How evil is what he did.
