He should seek forgiveness from Allah and not repeat it.” He said: Then if he sold her to another man, and he had relations with her without ensuring her womb was clear, then the second sold her to another man, and he had relations with her without ensuring her womb was clear, and her pregnancy became apparent while she was with the third, then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The child belongs to the bed, and for the fornicator is the stone.”

Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever acquires more bondwomen than he can marry or give in marriage, then the sin is upon him if they commit immorality.”

4559 - Harun ibn Muslim narrated from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad, who said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: Ten categories of bondwomen are prohibited: you may not combine between a mother and her daughter; nor between two sisters; nor your bondwoman when she is pregnant by someone other than you until she delivers; nor your bondwoman when she is your paternal aunt through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is your maternal aunt through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is your sister through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is the daughter of your brother through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she has a husband; nor your bondwoman when she is in a waiting period ('iddah); nor your bondwoman when another shares ownership in her with you.

Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated from Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Baqbāq, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Does a man marry a bondwoman without the knowledge of her owners?" He said: "It is zinā. Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Then marry them with the permission of their owners. ".

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: In the book of ʿAlī عليه السلام: "The child does not take anything from the wealth of his father, while the father may take from the wealth of his child whatever he wishes. And he may have relations with the bondwoman of his son, if the son has not had relations with her."
And in another narration: It is not permissible for him to have relations with the bondwoman of his daughter except with her permission.

Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who owns a bondwoman: does she become permissible for his son? He said: As long as there has been no intercourse or intimate contact like intercourse, then there is no harm.
And he, peace be upon him, said: My father, peace be upon him, had two bondwomen who served him, and he gifted one of them to me.
And he, peace be upon him, was asked about the male slave: what is permissible for him of women? He said: Two free women or four bondwomen.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had a bondwoman with whom he used to have relations. Then he sold her, and she was freed and married, and gave birth to a daughter. Is her daughter permissible for her former master? He said: "She is forbidden to him."
And he said: Regarding a bondwoman belonging to a man, with whom he used to have relations, and she miscarried a fetus from him after three months, he said: "She is an Umm Walad."

He said: And I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. About a free woman who married a slave on the basis that he was free, then later came to know that he was owned. He عليه السلام said: "She has greater authority over herself. If she wishes, after learning, she may affirm him and remain with him; and if she wishes, she may not remain. If the slave had consummated with her, then she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part. And if he had not consummated with her, then the marriage is invalid. But if she remains with him after learning that he is an owned slave, then he has the stronger claim over her."

Hadith 4569 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Concerning a man who married off his bondwoman to a free man for four hundred dirhams, and he paid two hundred dirhams in advance for him, then delayed two hundred dirhams from him. Her husband then consummated the marriage with her. After that, her master sold her to another man. Upon whom are the two hundred dirhams that were deferred? So he said: If he had not paid her the remainder of the mahr before he sold her, then nothing is due from him to her or to anyone else. And when the master sells her, she has become separated from the free husband, if he knew this matter.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a slave belonging to a man who fled from him and went to a land. There he told them that he was a free man from the clan of Banu so-and-so, and that he married a woman from the people of that land and she bore him children. Then the woman died and left in his hand wealth, landed property, and her children. After that, his master came to that land, took the slave and all that was in his hand, and the slave admitted to him that he was in bondage. So he said: "As for the slave, he is his slave; and as for the wealth and the landed property, they belong to the children of the deceased woman. A slave does not inherit from a free person." I said: "May I be your ransom, if the woman had no child and no heir on the day she died, then to whom would the wealth and landed property that she left in the hand of the slave belong?" He said: "All that she left belongs exclusively to the Imam of the Muslims."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hakam al-A'ma and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who gave permission to his slave regarding a free woman, so he married her. Then the slave fled from his masters, and the slave’s wife came seeking her maintenance from the master of the slave. So he said: She has no maintenance due from the master of the slave, and her marital bond with him has been severed, because the slave’s flight is the divorce of his wife, and he is in the position of one who has apostatized from Islam. I said: Then if he returns to his master, does his wife return to him? He said: If her waiting period from him has ended and she then married another husband, then he has no way to her. But if she has not married, then she is his wife upon the first marriage.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a woman who made herself available to a slave of hers and he had relations with her, that she be struck one hundred lashes, and that the slave be struck fifty lashes, and that he be sold away from her. And it is forbidden upon every Muslim to sell her a mature slave after that.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Aziz, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Concerning a slave jointly owned by two men: one of them married him off while the other did not know of it; then later he came to know of it. Does he have the right to separate the two of them? He عليه السلام said: The one who did not know and did not give permission has the right to separate them when he comes to know, and if he wishes, he may leave him upon his marriage.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who marries his slave to a free woman for a dowry of one hundred dirhams, then he sells him before entering (consummating the marriage) with her. He said: 'The master gives her half of what was prescribed for her from the price (he received). It is in the position of a debt that he incurred with the permission of his master.'

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a woman who made her bondwoman lawful for her husband. So he said: “That is for him.” He said: “Then what if he fears that she may be joking?” He said: “If he knows that she is joking, then no.”

4576 - Jamil narrated from Fudayl, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: "May I be your ransom! Some of our companions have narrated from you that you said: if a man makes lawful for his believing brother the private part of his bondwoman, then she is lawful for him." So he said to him: "Yes, O Fudayl." I said: "What do you say regarding a man who has a precious bondwoman, and she is a virgin; he makes lawful for a brother of his what is short of the private part. Does he have the right to deflower her?" He said: "No. He has only what was made lawful for him from her. Even if he made lawful for him a kiss from her, what is beyond that would not be lawful for him." I said: "What if he made lawful for him what is short of the private part, but desire overpowered him and he deflowered her?" He said: "That is not proper for him." I said: "If he did that, would he be a fornicator?" He said: "No, but he would be treacherous, and he must pay her owner one-tenth of her value."

4577 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who makes his bondwoman lawful for his brother, and she goes out in his needs, he said: "She is lawful for him." I said: "What if she gives birth to a child? What is to be done with him?" He said: "He belongs to the master of the bondwoman, unless he had stipulated to him at the time he made her lawful for him that if she came with a child from me, then he is free. So if he did that, then he is free." I said: "Then can he own his child?" He said: "If he has wealth, he may buy him at the proper value."

And Sulaymān al-Farrāʾ narrated from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man permits his bondwoman for his brother. He said: “There is no harm in it.” I said: Then if she comes with a child? So he said: “Let him take his child to himself and return the bondwoman to the man.” I said to him: He did not permit him in that. He said: “He has indeed permitted him, and he cannot be secure that such a thing would occur.”

4579 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a bondwoman jointly owned by two men, who both designated her as mudabbar. Then one of them permitted his partner access to her private part. He said: "She is halal for him, and whichever of the two dies before his companion, then half of her has become free on account of the one who died, while half of her remains mudabbar." I said: "What do you think—if the one remaining of them wants to touch her, does he have that right?" He said: "No, unless her freedom is established and he marries her with her consent whenever he wishes." I said to him: "Has not half of her become free, and has she not come to own half of herself, while the other half belongs to the one remaining of them?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Then if she makes her master exempt regarding her private part?" He said: "That is not permissible for him." I said to him: "Why is that not permissible for her, and how did you allow the one who owned half of her, when he permitted her private part to his partner regarding her?" He said: "Because a woman does not gift her private part, nor lend it, nor make it lawful. Rather, she has one day from herself, and the one who designated her as mudabbar has one day. So if he wishes to marry her in mut'ah for something on that day in which she owns herself, then let him contract mut'ah with her for something, whether small or great."

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a free man who marries a bondwoman belonging to a people: are the children slaves or free? He said: "The children are free." Then he said: "If one of his parents is free, then the child is free."

And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated, saying: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who married a bondwoman, and she came with a child. He said: “The child is attributed to his father.” I said: “Then a slave who marries a free woman?” He said: “The child is attributed to his mother.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "He is not from us who does not believe in our return and does not consider our mut'ah lawful."
And al-Ridha, peace be upon him, said: Temporary marriage (mut'ah) is not lawful except for one who understands it, and it is forbidden for one who is ignorant of it.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about mut'ah, and he said: "Mut'ah today is not as it was before today. At that time, they used to be trusted, but today they are not trusted, so ask about them."

Dāwūd ibn Isḥāq narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about mutʿah. He said: “Yes, if she is knowledgeable.” I said: “May I be your ransom, what if she is not knowledgeable?” He said: “Then present it to her and tell her. If she accepts, then marry her. If she refuses and is not satisfied with your statement, then leave her. And beware of al-kawāshif, al-dawāʿī, al-baghāyā, and women with husbands.” I said: “What are al-kawāshif?” He said: “Those who expose themselves, whose houses are known, and who are approached.” I said: “Then al-dawāʿī?” He said: “Those who invite others to themselves and have become known for فساد.” I said: “Then al-baghāyā?” He said: “Those known for zinā.” I said: “Then women with husbands?” He said: “Those divorced contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition).”

4587 - And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said: A man asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام: About a man who marries a woman in mutʿah and stipulates with her that he will not seek her child; then afterward she brings a child, and he denies the child. So he spoke sternly regarding that and said, “He denies it? And how can he deny it?” magnifying the seriousness of that. The man said: “Then if he suspects her?” He said: “It is not proper for you to marry except a trustworthy woman. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress—none marries her except a fornicator or a polytheist; and that has been forbidden to the believers.”
Saʿdān narrated from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام, who said: He should not marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman alongside a free woman, whether as mutʿah or otherwise.

4590 - And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated, saying: I wrote to him asking about a man who contracted mutʿah with a woman, then gifted her her days before consummating with her, or gifted her her days after he had consummated with her. Does he have the right to revoke what he gifted her from that? So he, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: “He does not take it back.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a bondwoman with whom a man engages in mutʿah. He said: "Yes, unless she is a young girl who can be deceived." I said: "May Allah rectify you, and what is the limit such that when she reaches it, she cannot be deceived?" He said: "A girl of ten years."
And Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who marries a virgin in mutʿah, he said: "It is disliked due to the reproach against her family."
And Abān narrated from Abī Maryam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The virgin who has a father is not to marry in mutʿah except with her father's permission.
Ḥammād narrated from Abī Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about al-mutʿah: whether it is among the four. He said, “No, and not even among seventy.”
Al-Fudhayl ibn Yasār asked him. About mut'ah, so he said: "It is like some of your bondwomen."

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "May I marry a woman for a month with a specified dowry, and she comes for part of the month but does not fulfill the rest of the month?" He عليه السلام said: "You withhold from her dowry in proportion to what she withheld herself from you, except the days of her menstruation, for they are hers."

Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal asked him: He said: "The minimum by which a man may contract a mutʿah marriage is a handful of wheat. He says to her: 'Marry me to yourself in mutʿah according to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet, as a marriage not fornication, on the condition that I do not inherit from you, nor do you inherit from me, and that I do not seek your child, until a specified term. Then if it appears desirable to me, I increase for you, and you increase for me.'"

Jamil ibn Salih narrated, saying: One of our companions said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: “I feel some discomfort regarding mut'ah, so I have sworn that I will never contract a temporary marriage ever.” So Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said to him: “Indeed, if you do not obey Allah, then you have disobeyed Him.”

And it is narrated from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who married a woman in mutʿah, then her family learned of it and married her to another man openly, while she was a truthful woman. He said: “She must not allow her husband access to herself until her waiting period and her stipulated term have ended.” I said: “If her stipulated term is a year, and her husband cannot be patient for her?” He said: “Then her husband should have taqwa of Allah and cede to her whatever remains of his term. For indeed she has been afflicted, and the abode is an abode of truce, and the believers are in taqiyyah.” I said: “If he cedes to her her remaining days and her waiting period ends, what should she do?” He said: “She should say to her husband when she enters upon him: ‘O man, my family rushed upon me and married me off without my command, and they did not seek my permission. But now I am pleased, so begin today and marry me in a valid marriage between me and you.’” He said: And I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “A woman marries in mutʿah, then her stipulated term ends, and she marries another man before her waiting period ends?” He said: “What is that upon you? The sin of that is only upon her.”

Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: “Is there a reward for the one who practices mutʿah?” He said: “If by that he seeks the Face of Allah, the Exalted, and opposition to those who deny it, he does not speak to her a single word except that Allah, the Exalted, writes for him thereby a good deed. And he does not extend his hand toward her except that Allah writes for him a good deed. Then when he draws near to her, Allah, the Exalted, forgives for him thereby a sin. Then when he performs ghusl, Allah forgives for him according to the amount of water that passes over his hair.” I said: “By the number of the hairs?” He said: “Yes, by the number of the hairs.”

And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was taken on the night journey to the heaven, he said: Jibra'il عليه السلام came to me and said: O Muhammad, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Indeed, I have forgiven those of your Ummah who practice mut'ah with women. .

Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about mutʿah. So he said: “Indeed, I dislike for a Muslim man to leave this world while there remains upon him a practice from the practices of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that he has not fulfilled.”

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I read in a man's letter to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A man married a woman in mutʿah for a specified term, so when the term between them ended, is it permissible for him to marry her sister? He said: It is not permissible for him until her waiting period has ended.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr asked al-Ridha (peace be upon him): About a man who marries a woman in temporary marriage (mut'ah), is it permissible for him to marry her daughter permanently? He said: "No."

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: The waiting period of mutʿah is forty-five days. It is as though I am looking at Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام counting forty-five days with his hand. Then when the term comes, the separation takes place without divorce.

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman whom a man marries in mutʿah, and then he dies, whether she must observe the waiting period. He said: “She observes a waiting period of four months and ten days; then if her days expire while he is alive, it is one and a half menstrual cycles, like what is required of a female slave.” He said: I said, “Then does she observe mourning?” He said: “Yes. And if she remained with him for a day, or two days, or an hour of the day, then the waiting period has become obligatory, but she does not observe mourning.”

ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What is the waiting period of the mutʿah if the one who had contracted mutʿah with her dies? He said: “Four months and ten days.” He said, then he said: “O Zurārah, every marriage in which the husband dies, then the woman—whether she is free or a slave, and in whatever form the marriage may have been, whether mutʿah, marriage, or possession by the right hand—her waiting period is four months and ten days. And the waiting period of the divorced woman is three months, and the divorced female slave has half of what is upon the free woman. Likewise, the mutʿah woman has upon her the like of what is upon the female slave.”

And it was said to Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: “Why did He make, in zina, four witnesses, and in killing, two witnesses?” He said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made mutʿah lawful for you, and He knew that it would be denied against you, so He made the four witnesses as a precaution for you.” “And were it not for that, false accusations would have been brought against you, and rarely do four gather to testify to one matter.”

And it is narrated from Bakkār ibn Kardam, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man meets a woman and says to her, "Marry me to yourself for a month," but he does not specify the month itself; then he meets her after years. So he عليه السلام said: "He has his month if he had specified it; and if he had not specified it, then he has no claim over her."

And Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who took a bondwoman for temporary marriage but forgot and had intercourse with her. Does he deserve the punishment of a fornicator? He replied: 'No, but he should perform the temporary marriage contract with her again and seek forgiveness from Allah for what he has done.'

And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from someone he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about temporary marriage with virgins. He said: “Was that made except for them? So let them be discreet about it and let them observe chastity.”

And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man married a young virgin bondwoman on the condition that he would not deflower her, then afterward she gave him permission. He عليه السلام said: If she gave him permission, then there is no harm in it.
And it is narrated: Indeed, the believer does not attain completeness until he practices mut'ah.

And it is narrated from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī: That the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله addressed the people and said: O people, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made lawful for you intimate relations in three meanings: an inherited union, and it is permanent marriage; a non-inherited union, and it is mutʿah; and those whom your right hands possess.

4615 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Indeed, I dislike for a man to die while there still remains upon him a trait from the traits of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that he has not practiced.” So I said to him: “Then did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله practice mut'ah?” He said: “Yes.” And he recited this verse: “And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement” up to His, Exalted is He, saying: “previously married and virgins.”

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden the intoxicant from every drink for our Shiʿah, and compensated them for that with mutʿah.
It was narrated from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Breastfeeding is twenty-one months, so whatever is less than that is an injustice to the child.

4662 - Saʿd ibn Saʿd asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the child: may he be breastfed for more than two years? So he said: "Two years." I said: "If it exceeds two years, is there anything upon his parents because of that?" He said: "No."
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: There is no milk with greater blessing for a child to be nursed with than the milk of his mother.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام looked at Umm Ishaq bint Sulayman while she was breastfeeding one of her two sons, Muhammad or Ishaq, and he said: O Umm Ishaq, do not nurse him from one breast only; rather, nurse him from both of them. One of them will be food and the other drink.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “What do you think about the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, ‘What becomes unlawful through breastfeeding is what becomes unlawful through lineage’? Explain it to me.” He said: “Every woman who suckles, from the milk of her husband, the child of another woman, whether a girl or a boy, then that is the breastfeeding about which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله spoke. And every woman who suckles, from the milk of two husbands that she had, one after another, a girl or a boy, then that is a breastfeeding that is not the breastfeeding about which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said, ‘What becomes unlawful through breastfeeding is what becomes unlawful through lineage.’”
And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning.
And Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Breastfeeding after two years, before the child is weaned, establishes prohibition.

4668 - It was narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, who said: ʿAlī ibn Shuʿayb wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “A woman breastfed one of my children. Is it permissible for me to marry one of her children?” So he wrote: “That is not permissible, because her children have become like your own children.”

ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: Concerning a woman who breastfed a man's child: is it permissible for that man to marry the daughter of this wet nurse or not? So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “That is not permissible for him.”

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: If a man marries a young slave-girl who is still nursing, and his wife breastfeeds her, the marriage becomes invalid.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who marries a woman and she gives birth to his child, then she breastfeeds a bondwoman with her milk: Is it permissible for his child from another woman to marry that bondwoman whom she breastfed? He said: 'No, she is like a sister through breastfeeding because the milk comes from the same father.'

4672 - Hariz narrated from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "Breastfeeding does not create prohibition except that which is compelled/established." He said: I said, "What is meant by al-majbur?" He said: "A mother who raises, or a wet nurse who is hired, or a bondwoman who is purchased."
Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Breastfeeding does not create a prohibition except for that in which one suckles from a single breast for one year."

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah narrated from Zurārah from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about breastfeeding, and he said: “Breastfeeding does not create prohibition except that which was suckled from one breast for two complete years.”
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Zurārah narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Breastfeeding does not create a prohibition except that which is within two complete years."
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “Forbid your women from nursing right and left, for they forget.”
Fuḍayl narrated from Zurārah from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Choose healthy wet nurses, for milk transmits.

Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) about a woman who committed adultery, is she suitable to be taken as a wet nurse? He said: She is not suitable, nor is the milk of her daughter who was born from the adultery.

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Do not employ a foolish woman as a wet nurse, for milk transmits traits, and the boy inclines toward the milk—that is, toward the wet nurse—in rashness and foolishness.

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said: I asked him about a man who gives his child to a Jewish, Christian, or Magian woman to breastfeed him in her house or to breastfeed him in his house. He said: "A Jewish woman or a Christian woman may breastfeed him for you, and you should prevent her from drinking wine and from what is not halal, such as pork. And they must not take your child to their houses. And an adulteress must not breastfeed your child, for that is not permissible for you. And a Magian woman must not breastfeed your child unless you are compelled to resort to her."

Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The milk of a Jewish, Christian, or Magian woman is more beloved to me than the milk of a child born from zina. And he did not consider there to be any harm in the milk of a child born from zina if the master of the bondwoman, with whom the immoral act was committed with the bondwoman, renders it permissible.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman whose milk flowed without childbirth, and she breastfed a girl and a boy with that milk. Does that milk make unlawful what becomes unlawful through breastfeeding? He said: No.
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: A child's taking in milk by sucking is equivalent to breastfeeding.
And he, peace be upon him, said: A free woman is not compelled to breastfeed the child, while an umm al-walad is compelled to do so.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who died and left behind a small child for whom a wet nurse was sought. That the payment for the child's breastfeeding is to be taken from what he inherits from his father and his mother.

And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him: That a man came to ʿAlī, peace be upon him, and said: “Indeed, my bondwoman has breastfed my child, and I have wanted to sell her.” He said: “Take her by the hand and say: Who will buy from me the mother of my child?”
In the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: A righteous child is a flower from the flowers of Paradise.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Allah's inheritance from His believing servant is a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him.
Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said: Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, intends good for a servant, He does not cause him to die until He shows him the successor.
And it is narrated: Whoever dies without leaving behind a successor, it is as if he had not been among the people. And whoever dies while having a successor, it is as if he did not die.
Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Daughters are good deeds, and sons are a blessing. Good deeds are rewarded for, and a blessing is questioned about.

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, was given glad tidings of a daughter. Then he looked at the faces of his companions and saw displeasure in them. So he said: What is the matter with you? She is a sweet flower that I smell, and her sustenance is upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And he, peace be upon him, was a father of daughters.
And Ali, peace be upon him, said: Concerning the illness that afflicts a child: indeed, it is an expiation for his parents.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, surely has mercy on a man because of the intensity of his love for his child.

ʿUmar ibn Yazīd said to him: “I have daughters.” He said: “Perhaps you wish for their death. Indeed, if you were to wish for their death and they died, you would not be rewarded on the Day of Resurrection, and you would meet your Lord, when you meet Him, while you are disobedient.”

And Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān narrated through his chain of transmission: A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله with a man beside him, and informed him of a newborn he had. The man’s color changed, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said, “What is the matter with you?” He said, “Good.” He said, “Speak.” He said, “I left while the woman was in labor, and I was informed that she had given birth to a girl.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, “The earth carries her, the sky shades her, and Allah provides for her; and she is a fragrant flower that you smell.” Then he turned to his companions and said, “Whoever has one daughter is afflicted with care; whoever has two daughters, then seek help from Allah for him; whoever has three daughters, jihad and every hardship are lifted from him; and whoever has four daughters, O servants of Allah, help him; O servants of Allah, lend to him; O servants of Allah, have mercy on him.”

4698 - And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever takes care of three daughters or three sisters, Paradise becomes obligatory for him." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, and two?" He said: "And two." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, and one?" He said: "And one."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever supports two daughters, two sisters, two paternal aunts, or two maternal aunts, they will shield him from the Fire.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: When a man is given a daughter, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends to her an angel, who passes his wing over her head and chest and says: 'A fragile being created from weakness; whoever spends on her will be aided.'

4701 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Know that one of you will meet his miscarried child waiting anxiously at the gate of Paradise. Then when he sees him, he will take him by his hand until he admits him into Paradise. And indeed, when one of your children dies, you are rewarded regarding him; and if he remains after him, he seeks forgiveness for him after his death.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Love the children and have mercy on them. And when you promise them something, fulfill it for them, for they only see that you are the ones who provide for them.

Rifa'ah ibn Musa narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who has sons whose mother is not one; may he favor one of them over another? He said: “Yes, there is no harm in that, and my father عليه السلام used to favor me over 'Abd Allah.”

And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله saw a man who had two sons, and he kissed one of them and left the other. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, "Why did you not treat them equally?"
And he, peace be upon him, said: The parents are liable for disobedience toward the child just as the child is liable toward them for disobedience.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: A man's kindness to his child is his kindness to his own parents.
And in another report, he said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Whoever has a child should act childlike for him.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Among the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon a man is that his child resembles him.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He wills to create a being, He gathers every form between him and Adam, then creates him upon the form of one of them. So no one should ever say to his child, 'This one does not resemble me, nor does he resemble anything from my forefathers.'
Abu Malik al-Hadrami narrated from Abu al-'Abbas, who said: I heard al-Sadiq عليه السلام saying: "The servant, whenever he increases in love for women, increases in faith in excellence."
And in the narration of Abān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I do not think that a man increases in faith and goodness except that he also increases in love for women.

ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: Every person is held in pledge on the Day of Judgment by their ʿaqīqah, and the ʿaqīqah is more obligatory than the sacrificial offering (uḍḥiyah).
And in the narration of Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Every person is held in pledge by the fitrah, and every newborn is held in pledge by the ʿaqīqah.

And it was narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “By Allah, I do not know whether my father performed the ʿaqīqah for me or not.” So he عليه السلام instructed me, and I performed the ʿaqīqah for myself while I was an old man.

And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, he said: The ʿaqiqah is obligatory when a child is born to a man. If he wishes to name him on the day of his birth, he may do so.

ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “ʿAqīqah is binding upon one who is wealthy, and whoever is poor, then when he becomes financially able, he should perform it. If he is not able to do that, then there is nothing upon him. If no ʿaqīqah was performed for him until an udḥiyyah was offered on his behalf, then the udḥiyyah has sufficed for him. Every newborn is held in pledge by his ʿaqīqah.” And he said concerning the ʿaqīqah: “A ram is to be slaughtered on his behalf. If a ram is not found, whatever suffices in the udḥiyyah will suffice for him. Otherwise, then a lamb—the largest that may be found among the lambs of the year.”

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Mārid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about the ʿaqīqah. He said: “A sheep, or a cow, or a camel. Then he names the child, shaves the head of the newborn on the seventh day, and gives charity in gold or silver equal to the weight of its hair. If the child is male, a male animal is sacrificed on his behalf, and if female, a female animal is sacrificed on her behalf.”

Abu Talib, may Allah have mercy on him, performed the 'aqiqah for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم on the seventh day, then he invited the family of Abu Talib, and they said, “What is this?” So he said: “The 'aqiqah of Ahmad.” They said, “For what reason did you name him Ahmad?” He said, “I named him Ahmad because of the praise of the people of the heaven and the earth for him.”

And in the narration of ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If the midwife is a Jewess who does not eat from the slaughtered animal of the Muslims, she is to be given one-fourth of the value of the ram; that is purchased from her with it.

And in the narration of 'Ammār also: That he gives the midwife a quarter of it; and if there is no midwife, then it is for his mother—she may give it to whomever she wishes. And she should feed from it ten Muslims, and if he gives more, then it is better.
And it is narrated: That the best thing with which it is cooked is water and salt.

ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī said: And he was asked about the ʿaqiqah: when it is slaughtered, should its bones be broken? He said: “Yes, its bones should be broken, its meat should be cut up, and after the slaughter you may do with it whatever you wish.”

Idris ibn Abdullah al-Qummi asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: about a newborn who is born and dies on the seventh day: should the 'aqiqah be performed for him? He عليه السلام said: "If he died before noon, the 'aqiqah is not performed for him; and if he died after noon, the 'aqiqah should be performed for him."

ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When you intend to slaughter the ʿaqīqah, you say: O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate. Indeed, I have turned my face toward the One Who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining upright, submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my salat (prayer), my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner, and with that I have been commanded. And I am among the Muslims. O Allah, it is from You and for You. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from so-and-so son of so-and-so—and you name the newborn by his name. Then you slaughter.

4723 - In another hadith, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "It is said at the time of the ʿaqīqah: O Allah, from You and for You is what You have bestowed, and You have given. O Allah, so accept it from us according to the sunnah of Your Prophet. And seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, and name [the child], and slaughter, and say: For You I have shed the blood; there is no partner for You." "And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." "O Allah, drive away from us the accursed Satan." As for circumcision, it is a sunnah for men and an honorable practice for women.

Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “There is no harm if a woman is not circumcised, but as for a man, it is necessary for him.”

ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, saying: It has been narrated from the Righteous Ones عليهم السلام: “Circumcise your children on the seventh day so that they may be purified, for the earth cries out to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because of the urine of the uncircumcised.” May Allah make me your ransom, but the barbers in our town are not skilled in that, and they do not circumcise him on the seventh day. We have a barber from the Jews; is it permissible for the Jews to circumcise the children of the Muslims, or not? So he عليه السلام wrote back: “On the seventh day; so do not oppose the sunnah (prophetic tradition), if Allah wills.”

It was narrated from Murazim ibn Hakim Al-Azdi from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): Regarding the infant when he is circumcised, He said: 'One should say: O Allah, this is Your Sunnah and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, may Your prayers be upon him and his family, and it is our following of You and Your Prophet by Your will, Your desire, and Your decree for a matter You have willed, a decision You have made obligatory, and a command You have executed, so You made him taste the heat of iron in his circumcision and cupping for a matter You know better than I do. O Allah, purify him from sins, increase his lifespan, protect his body from afflictions and his flesh from pain, increase him in wealth, and remove poverty from him. Indeed, You know while we do not.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) also said: 'Whoever does not say this at the time of his child's circumcision should say it for him before he reaches puberty. If he says it, he will be protected from the heat of iron, whether from killing or anything else.'

And it was narrated from Hārūn ibn Muslim, who said: I wrote to Ṣāḥib al-Dār عليه السلام: “A child was born to me, and I shaved his head, weighed his hair in dirhams, and gave its equivalent in charity.” He عليه السلام said: “It is not permissible to weigh it except with gold or silver, and thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has been established.”
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked: What is the reason for shaving the head of the newborn? He عليه السلام said: "It is to purify him from the hair of the womb."

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a newborn whose head was not shaved on the seventh day, so he said: “If seven days have passed, then there is no shaving required of him.”
4730 - And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "O Fāṭimah, pierce the ears of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn in مخالفة to the Jews."

Abu Zakariyya narrated from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: When a child from the children of the believers dies, a caller announces in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth: Indeed, so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, has died. If his parents, one of them, or some of his household from among the believers had died, he is entrusted to them so that they may nourish him. Otherwise, he is entrusted to Fatimah عليها السلام, and she nourishes him until his parents, one of them, or some of his household arrive, then she hands him over to them.

And in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has entrusted Ibrahim and Sarah with the children of the believers. They nourish them from a tree in Paradise having teats like the teats of cattle, in a palace of pearl. Then when the Day of qiyamah comes, they will be clothed, perfumed, and presented to their parents; so they will be kings in Paradise with their parents. And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith—We shall join their descendants with them.

4733 - And in the narration of Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith—We will join their descendants with them." He said: "The children fell short of the deeds of the fathers, so Allah joined the children with the fathers so that their eyes might be comforted by that."
Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the children of the Prophets عليهم السلام, and he said: They are not like the children of ordinary people.

He asked him about Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whether, if he had remained alive, he would have been a truthful prophet. He said: “If he had remained alive, he would have been upon the path of his father, may the blessings of Allah be upon him.”

And in the narration of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdullāh, he said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: There was a palm branch over the grave of Ibrāhīm, son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, which shaded it from the sun wherever it moved. Then when the branch dried up, the trace of the grave disappeared, and its place was no longer known.
And he, peace be upon him, said: Ibrahim died when he was eighteen months old, so Allah completed his breastfeeding in Paradise.

4738 - He عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overwhelm them with transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better than him in purity and closer in affection.” He عليه السلام said: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, replaced their son with a daughter, and from her were born seventy prophets.”

Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “The children of the polytheists are with their fathers in the Fire, and the children of the Muslims are with their fathers in Paradise.”

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the children of the polytheists who die before reaching the age of responsibility. He said: "They are disbelievers, and Allah knows best what they would have done; they will enter the same places as their fathers."

And he, peace be upon him, said: A fire will be kindled for them, and it will be said to them, 'Enter it.' If they enter it, it will be cool and peaceful for them. But if they refuse, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to them: 'Behold, I had commanded you, and you disobeyed Me.' Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will command that they be taken to the Fire.

And in the narration of Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will establish the proof against seven: the child, the one who died between the prophets, the very old man who lived to the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while not comprehending, the simple-minded, the insane one who does not comprehend, the deaf, and the mute. Each one of them will present an argument before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will send to them a messenger, who will kindle for them a fire and say: Indeed your Lord commands you to leap into it. Whoever leaps into it, it will be coolness and peace upon him; and whoever disobeys will be driven to the Fire.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Let your son play for seven years, and let him be disciplined for seven years, and keep him close to yourself for seven years. Then if he succeeds, otherwise he is among those in whom there is no good.

Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī used to go about in the lanes of the Anṣār in al-Madīnah, saying: ʿAlī is the best of mankind, so whoever refuses has committed kufr. O assembly of the Anṣār, discipline your children upon the love of ʿAlī; so whoever refuses, then look into the matter of his mother.
4745 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Whoever finds the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him frequently make du'a for his mother, for she did not betray his father.”

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: A child is nurtured for seven years, disciplined for seven years, and employed for seven years. The limit of his physical growth is at twenty-three years, and that of his intellect at thirty-five years. Whatever is after that is through experiences.
And in the narration of Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, he said: A child grows every year by four finger-widths, measured by his own finger.

And Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah narrated, saying: I heard al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام saying: "It is recommended for a boy to be lively and energetic in his childhood so that he may be forbearing in his adulthood."

A man asked the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and said: Why is it that we find in ourselves toward our children what they do not find toward us? He said: Because they are from you, but you are not from them.
Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked: Why did Allah make His Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family, an orphan? He said: So that no one would have obedience due from him.

It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥarīz, from al-Walīd, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Whoever abandons marriage out of fear of poverty has thought poorly of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: If they are poor, Allah will enrich them out of His bounty.

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: Whoever is pleased to meet Allah in a state of purity and purification, then let him meet Him with a spouse. And whoever abandons marriage out of fear of poverty has thought poorly of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Sayyid al-ʿĀbidīn, عليه السلام, said: Whoever marries for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to uphold kinship ties, Allah, the Exalted, will crown him with the crown of sovereignty and honor.

Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “The best women of my nation are those with the brightest faces and the least dowry.”

It is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ziyād, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Women are of four categories: among them is a fertile spring; among them is one who is gathering and abundant; among them is a burden that is subduing; and among them is a shackle infested with lice.

4358 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Dawud al-Karkhi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: My wife has died, and she was compatible with me, and I have intended to marry. So he said: Consider where you place yourself, and whom you make a شریک in your wealth, and to whom you disclose your religion, your secret, and your trust. If you must do so, then choose a virgin attributed to goodness and to good character, Indeed, women have been created in different ways: among them is the gain and the burden, among them is the crescent when it appears to its possessor, and among them is darkness. So whoever attains the righteous among them will be fortunate, and whoever is defrauded has no revenge. And they are three: a woman who is fertile and loving, who helps her husband through his time in his world and his hereafter, and does not assist time against him; a barren woman, neither possessing beauty nor character, and who does not help her husband in any good; and a loud, intrusive, fault-finding woman who deems much to be little and does not accept even a small amount.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Miskān narrated from Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Baqbāq, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill, so he said: She inherits from him during his illness for up to one year if he dies from that illness. She observes the waiting period from the day he divorced her, the waiting period of a divorced woman. Then she may marry when her waiting period ends, and she inherits from him within one year if he dies in that illness. But if he dies after a year has passed, then there is no inheritance for her.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a sick man who divorces his wife in that state. He said: “No. But he may marry if he wishes. If he consummates the marriage with her, she inherits from him; and if he does not consummate the marriage with her, then his marriage is invalid.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Rabīʿ al-Aṣamm, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ and Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, both from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: If a man divorces his wife with one divorce during his illness, then remains in that illness until her waiting period ends, and then dies in that illness after the completion of the waiting period, then she inherits from him so long as she has not remarried. فإذا كانت she has remarried after the completion of the waiting period, then she does not inherit from him.

And in the narration of Samāʿah, he said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, then died before her waiting period had ended. He said: She must observe the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died, and she has the inheritance.

And in the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abān, that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Regarding a man who divorced with two divorces in good health, then pronounced the third divorce while he was ill: she inherits from him so long as he remains in his illness, even if it is up to a year.
4880 - And in the narration of Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "A sick man does not have the right to divorce his wife, but he may marry."

And in the narration of Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, he said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill, so he said: “She inherits from him so long as she remains in her waiting period. If he divorced her in a state of causing harm, then she inherits from him up to one year. And if there remains in her waiting period, beyond the year, even a single day, she does not inherit from him.”

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about a man whom death approaches and he divorces his wife: is his divorce valid? He said: “Yes. If he dies, she inherits from him; and if she dies, he does not inherit from her.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from al-ʿAbd al-Salih عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A young girl who does not menstruate, though others like her do menstruate, and her husband divorces her? He said: Her waiting period is three months.

Muhammad ibn Hakim narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying regarding a woman who has despaired of menstruation, whose husband divorces her: He said, "She is separated from him, and there is no waiting period upon her."

4798 - And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The waiting period ('iddah) of a woman who does not menstruate, a mustahadah who does not become pure, and a young girl who has despaired [of menstruation] is three months; and the waiting period of one whose menstruation is regular is three menstrual cycles.

And in the narration of Jamil, he said: Regarding a man who divorces a young girl who has not reached puberty and one of her like does not conceive, though he had consummated marriage with her, and a woman who has despaired of menstruation, whose menses has ceased, and one of her like does not give birth, he said: There is no waiting period ('iddah) upon either of them.

Al-Bazanti narrated from Al-Muthanna, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who does not menstruate except once in three years or four years. He said: She observes a waiting period of three months, then she may marry if she wishes.

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said: Regarding a woman who menstruates once every three months or once every year, the mustaḥāḍah, the one who has not yet reached puberty, the one who menstruates once and then her menstruation stops once, the one who does not hope for a child, the one whose menstruation has ceased and claims that she has not despaired, and the one who sees yellow discharge from irregular menstruation, he mentioned that the waiting period of all of these women is three months.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and al-Bazanṭī both narrated from Jamīl, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There are two matters; whichever of them comes first for her, the divorced woman under uncertainty, who is uncertain regarding menstruation, becomes separated by it. If three white months pass over her in which there is no blood, she becomes separated by that. And if three menstrual periods pass over her, with there not being three months between the two menstrual periods, she becomes separated by menstruation.

Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a woman who menstruates once every three years: how should she observe her waiting period? He عليه السلام said: “She should consider the menstrual cycles she used to have when her menstruation was regular, and let her observe a waiting period of three menstrual cycles. Then let her marry, if she wishes.”

4804 - And Muhammad ibn Muslim asked him about the waiting period of the mustahadah, so he said: “She waits for the measure of her menstrual cycles, adding one day or subtracting one day. If she does not menstruate, then she should look to some of her women and observe her waiting period according to their menstrual cycles.”
And it is narrated: “When a woman reaches fifty years of age, she no longer sees redness, except if she is a woman from Quraysh.”

Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Isma'il ibn Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: There are five who may be divorced in any condition: the pregnant woman whose pregnancy has become evident, the woman with whom her husband has not consummated the marriage, the woman whose husband is absent from her, the woman who has not menstruated, and the woman who has ceased menstruating.
And in another narration: And the woman who has despaired of menstruation.

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his letter to me: Know, my son, that the origin of giving the choice is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was displeased for His Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, because of a statement said by some of his wives: 'Does Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family, think that if he divorces us, we will not find our equals from Quraysh to marry us?' So Allah commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, to withdraw from his wives for twenty-nine nights, and the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, withdrew from them in the upper chamber of Umm Ibrahim. Then this verse was revealed: O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a gracious manner. But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Hereafter, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward. So they chose Allah and His Messenger, and divorce did not take place. Had they chosen themselves, they would have been separated.

4810 - And in the narration of Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī: “Zaynab said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘You do not act justly, while you are the Messenger of Allah.’ And Ḥafṣah said: ‘If he divorces us, we will find among our people our equals from Quraysh.’ So revelation was withheld from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله for twenty-nine days. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, showed zeal for His Messenger, so Allah revealed:” “O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment...” “Up to His saying, ‘a great reward.’ So they chose Allah and His Messenger, and divorce did not occur. Had they chosen themselves, they would have been separated.”

Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If he gives her the choice or places her affair in her hand outside the period before her ʿiddah, without having two witnesses testify, then it is nothing. And if he gives her the choice or places her affair in her hand with the testimony of two witnesses in the period before her ʿiddah, then she has the choice so long as they have not separated. فإذا she chooses herself, then it is one divorce, and he has the greater right to take her back; and if she chooses her husband, then it is not a divorce.

Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Divorce is that a man says to his wife, ‘Choose.’ If she chooses herself, then she has separated from him, and he is [only] a suitor among the suitors. But if she chooses her husband, then it is nothing. Or he says, ‘You are divorced.’ Whichever of these he does, she becomes forbidden to him. And there is no divorce, no khulʿ, no mubārāʾah, and no takhyīr except in a state of purity, without intercourse, and with the testimony of two witnesses.

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who gives his wife the choice, or her father, or her brother, or her guardian, he said: “All of them are in the same position, if she consents.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who said to his wife, "I have given the choice to you," and she chose herself before standing up. He عليه السلام said, "That is valid against him." I said, "Then is there mutʿah for her?" He عليه السلام said, "Yes." I said, "Then is there inheritance for her if the husband dies before her waiting period ends?" He عليه السلام said, "Yes, and if she dies, the husband inherits from her."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: He said: “What do women have to do with takhyīr (being given the choice in divorce)? That is only something which Allah specifically granted to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

Discord may arise from both the woman and the man together, and this is among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said. And if you fear discord between them, then appoint an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family. So the man chooses a man, and the woman chooses a man; then the two meet upon separation or upon reconciliation. If they intend reconciliation, they reconcile without seeking permission; but if they intend to separate, then they have no right to separate except after seeking the permission of the husband and the wife.

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “Then appoint an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family.” He عليه السلام said: “The two arbitrators do not have the right to separate until they seek the permission of the man and the woman, and stipulate upon them that if they wish they reconcile them, and if they wish they separate them. So if they reconcile them, it is valid, and if they separate them, it is valid.”

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام was asked about a woman whose husband was afflicted in his mind after he married her, or insanity befell him. He said: "She has the right to separate herself from him if she wishes."

And in another narration: If his insanity reaches the point where he does not recognize the times of salat (prayer), they are to be separated. But if he recognizes the times of salat (prayer), then the woman should remain patient with him, for she has been tested.

Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding khulʿ: if she says to him, 'I will not perform ghusl for you from janabah, nor will I fulfill an oath for you, and I will surely let into your bed one whom you dislike,' then when she says this to him, it becomes permissible for him to divorce her by khulʿ, and it becomes lawful for him what he has taken from her.

And in the narration of Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "The waiting period of the woman who undergoes khulʿ is the waiting period of the divorced woman. Her khulʿ is her divorce, and it suffices without explicitly naming it as divorce. And the woman seeking khulʿ, her khulʿ is not lawful until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not keep any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor perform ghusl for you from janabah, and I will surely let another tread upon your bed, and I will surely admit against you without your permission.' People in his presence had been allowing less than this. So when the woman says that to her husband, what he takes from her becomes lawful for him, and she remains before him with two remaining divorce counts, and khulʿ is one divorce." And he عليه السلام said: "The statement should come from her own side." Meaning: without her being taught.

Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā asked him. He was asked about a woman who undergoes khulʿ: does she have housing and maintenance? So he said: “She has no housing and no maintenance.” And he was asked about a woman who undergoes khulʿ: does she have mutʿah? He said: “No.”

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: If a woman says to her husband, in a statement, ‘I will not obey any command of yours,’ whether explained in detail or not explained, then what he has taken from her becomes permissible for him, and he has no return to her.

4824 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who abandons his wife without divorce and without an oath for a year, and does not come to her bed. He said: “Let him go to his wife.” And he عليه السلام said: “Any man who makes īlāʾ regarding his wife—and īlāʾ is that he says, ‘By Allah, I will not have relations with you for such and such,’ or, ‘By Allah, I will surely anger you,’ then he continues to anger her—then he is to be given a waiting period of four months. Then after the four months, he is brought and made to stand. If he returns, that is, that he reconciles with his wife…” “Then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.” And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce. No divorce takes place between them until he is made to stand, and if it is also after the four months, then he is compelled either to return or to divorce.” And it is narrated: “If he returns, meaning that he goes back to intercourse; otherwise, he is imprisoned in an enclosure of reeds, and hardship is imposed upon him in food and drink until he divorces.” And it has been narrated: “Whenever the Imam of the Muslims commands him to divorce and he refuses, his neck is struck because of his refusal against the Imam of the Muslims.”

And in the narration of Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Manṣūr, he said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made an oath of abstinence from his wife, and then four months passed. He said: "He is to be detained; if he resolves upon divorce, she becomes separated from him, and she must observe the waiting period of a divorced woman. Otherwise, he must expiate his oath and retain her."

ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the missing person: what should his wife do? He said: So long as she remains silent about him and is patient, she is to be left as she is. But if she brings her case to the authority, he gives her a term of four years, then writes to the region in which he went missing and inquiry is made about him. If news comes that he is alive, she remains patient. If no news comes of his being alive until the four years pass, the guardian of the missing husband is summoned and asked: does the missing man have wealth? If he has wealth, maintenance is spent on her from it until his life or death becomes known. If he has no wealth, the guardian is told: spend on her. If he does so, then she has no way to remarry so long as he spends on her. But if he refuses to spend on her, the authority compels him to issue one divorce at the beginning of the waiting period while she is in a state of purity. Then the divorce of the guardian becomes the divorce of the husband. If her husband comes before her waiting period ends from the day the guardian divorced her, and he then decides to take her back, then she is his wife, and she remains with him with two divorces left. But if the waiting period ends before he comes and takes her back, then she becomes lawful for husbands, and the first has no claim over her.

And in another narration: If the husband has no guardian, the ruler divorces her and brings two just witnesses to witness it. Then the ruler’s divorce is the husband’s divorce, and she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days; then she may marry if she wishes.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr al-Khathʿami from Zurarah from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a man is reported dead to his family, or they inform her that he has divorced her, and she observes the ʿiddah and then marries, then her husband comes afterward, the first has more right to her than this latter one, whether the latter consummated with her or did not consummate. And she is entitled from the latter to the mahr for what he lawfully enjoyed of her private part. And ʿAbd al-Karim added in his hadith: and it is not for the latter ever to marry her again.

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man whose family thought that he had died or been killed, so his wife married, and his concubine also married, and each one of them bore a child from her husband. Then her first husband and the master of the concubine came back. So he said: He takes his wife, for he has more right to her, and he takes his concubine and her child, or he takes compensation by agreement from their price.

And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, it is reported that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Regarding two witnesses who testified to a woman that her husband had divorced her, so she remarried, and then her husband came back, he said: “The two shall be subjected to the prescribed punishment, and they shall be made liable for the dowry to the husband. Then the wife shall observe her waiting period and return to her first husband.”

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman to whom news of her husband's death was conveyed, so she observed her waiting period and married. Then her first husband came back, so he separated from her and the other also separated from her. How long should she observe a waiting period before becoming lawful for people? He عليه السلام said: “Three menstrual cycles. Her womb is only cleared by three menstrual cycles, making her lawful for all people.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whose marriage contract is in place and who performed ẓihār regarding his wife, So he said: “There is no ẓihār, and there is no īlāʾ, until he consummates the marriage with her.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Ẓihār does not occur except in a case where divorce is applicable.

4828 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام about zihar, and he said: “It is from every unmarriageable kin, or from a mother, or sister, or paternal aunt, or maternal aunt; and zihar does not occur in an oath.” So I said: “And how does it occur?” He said: “A man says to his wife, while she is in a state of purity and without intercourse, ‘You are forbidden to me like the back of my mother or my sister,’ while intending by that zihar.”

4829 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān and others, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There was a man in the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله named Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, and he had a wife named Khawlah bint al-Mundhir. One day he said to her, “You are to me like the back of my mother.” Then he regretted it immediately and said to her, “O woman, I think that you have become unlawful for me.” So she came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said, “O Messenger of Allah, my husband said to me, ‘You are to me like the back of my mother,’ and this statement in former times used to make a woman unlawful to her husband.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “O woman, I think that you have indeed become unlawful for him.” Then the woman raised her hand to the sky and said, “I complain to You of separation from my husband.” Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “O Muḥammad:” “Allah has indeed heard the speech of the woman who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears the dialogue between you both. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Those among you who pronounce ẓihār against their wives—they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. Indeed they surely utter an objectionable word and a falsehood, and indeed Allah is surely Pardoning, Forgiving.” Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the expiation regarding that, and said: “And those who pronounce ẓihār against their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before the two touch one another—that is what you are admonished by, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do. Then whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months before the two touch one another; then whoever is unable, then feeding sixty poor persons.”
And it is narrated: If he is unable to provide the feeding, he should give charity according to what he is capable of.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who performed ẓihār against his wife and then divorced her with one divorce. He said: "If he divorces her with one divorce, then the ẓihār has become null, and the divorce has demolished the ẓihār." So I said to him: "Does he have the right to take her back?" He said: "Yes, she is his wife. So if he takes her back, what is required of one who has performed ẓihār becomes obligatory upon him." "Before they touch one another." I said: "If he leaves her until her term ends and she comes to possess herself, then he marries her after that, does the ẓihār remain binding upon him" "Before they touch one another?" He said: "No. She has separated from him and has come to possess herself." I said: "If he performs ẓihār against her, then does not touch her, and leaves her without touching her, except that he sees her uncovered without touching her, does anything become obligatory upon him in that?" He said: "She is his wife, and intercourse with her is not forbidden to him; however, what is required of one who has performed ẓihār becomes obligatory upon him before he has intercourse with her, while she is his wife." I said: "If she raises the matter to the authority and says: 'This is my husband; he has performed ẓihār against me and is keeping me without touching me, fearing that what is required of one who has performed ẓihār would become obligatory upon him,' then what?" He said: "It is not required of him that he be compelled to emancipation, fasting, and feeding if he does not have what he may emancipate, is not able to fast, and does not find what he may give in charity. But if he is able to emancipate, then it is upon the Imam to compel him to emancipation and charity before he touches her and after he touches her."

Aban narrated from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performs ẓihār against his wife. He said: "Then he must offer expiation." I said: "What if he has intercourse before he offers expiation?" He said: "Then he has committed a violation of one of Allah's limits, so let him seek Allah's forgiveness and abstain until he offers expiation."

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who pronounced zihar against his wife three times, and he said: "He must offer expiation three times." I said: "If he has intercourse before he offers expiation?" He said: "He must seek Allah's forgiveness and refrain until he offers the expiation."
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked him about a man who pronounced ẓihār against his wife five times or more, so he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “In place of every single time, there is an expiation.”

Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked him about ẓihār. When does the expiation become due upon the one who declares it? He said: "When he intends to have intercourse with his wife." I said: "If he divorces her before having intercourse with her, is expiation required of him?" He said: "No, the expiation has fallen from him." I said: "If he fasts and then becomes ill and breaks the fast, should he begin again or complete what remains upon him?" He said: "If he fasted for a month and then became ill, he begins again; but if he exceeded a month by a day or two, he continues from that point."
