He said: "The free man and the slave are the same, except that upon the slave is half of what is upon the free man in expiation."

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: I said to him: If a man performs zihar in Sha'ban and does not find what he can free, he said: He should wait until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he should fast two consecutive months If he performs zihar while he is traveling, he should wait until he returns. And if he fasts and then acquires wealth, then he should continue with what he had begun.

And Sama'ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have performed ẓihār against my wife. He said: Go and free a slave. He said: I do not have one. He said: Go and fast two consecutive months. He said: I am not able. He said: Go and feed sixty needy persons. He said: I do not have the means. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: I will give charity on your behalf. He said: So he gave him dates to feed sixty needy persons, then said: Go and give it as charity. The man said: By the One who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, I do not know anyone between its two lava tracts who is more in need of it than me and my dependants. He said: Then go, eat, and feed your dependants.

And in the narration of Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, a man said: I said to Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: I said to my wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother if you leave the door of the room,' and she left. So he said: 'There is nothing upon you.' So I said: 'But I am able to offer expiation.' He said: 'There is nothing upon you.' So I said: 'I am able to offer expiation by freeing one slave or two slaves.' He said: 'There is nothing upon you, whether you are capable or not.'
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Ali عليه السلام said: Regarding a man who made īlāʾ from his wife and performed ẓihār in a single statement, he said: "Upon him is one expiation."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated from Ḥumrān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man said to his female slave, “You are to me like the back of my mother,” intending by that to please his wife. He said: “He may approach her, and there is nothing upon her nor upon him.”

Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ narrated from Ṣafwān, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If the man who has performed ẓihār fasts one month and fasts one day from the other month, then he has maintained consecutiveness. Then if he wishes, let him complete the remainder separately, and if he wishes, let him give for each day one mudd of food.

Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abū al-Ward: That Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked, while I was with him, about a man who said to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," one hundred times, So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: "Is he able, for each time, to free a slave?" He said: "No." He said: "Is he able to feed sixty needy persons one hundred times?" He said: "No." He said: "Then is he able to fast two consecutive months one hundred times?" He said: "No." He said: "They are to be separated."

And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Concerning a man who performed ẓihār against four women, he said: “Upon him is one expiation.”
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "Zihar does not take effect in place of divorce, nor does divorce take effect in place of zihar."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Ẓihār does not occur through an oath, nor in a case of harm, nor in a state of anger. Ẓihār is only valid upon a state of purity, without intercourse, with the testimony of two Muslim witnesses.
ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the obligatory ẓihār. He said: It is that by which a man intends ẓihār itself specifically.
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: If a woman says, 'My husband is to me as the back of my mother,' then there is no expiation upon her.
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: about a man who performs ẓihār against his bondwoman, so he said: “The free woman and the bondwoman are equal in this matter.”

Muhammad ibn Humran asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the slave: is ẓihār binding upon him? So he said: "Upon him is half of what is upon the free man: fasting for one month; and there is no expiation upon him in the form of charity or emancipation."
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Ali عليه السلام said: “The umm al-walad suffices in ẓihar.”

4851 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Basir, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: "Li'an does not take place unless the man has consummated the marriage with his wife."

Al-Bazanti asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, saying to him: “May Allah rectify your affairs, how is the procedure of liʿān?” He said: “The Imam sits and places his back toward the qiblah, and places the man on his right, and the woman and the child on his left.”

And in another report: Then the man stands and swears four times by Allah. Indeed, he is surely among the truthful. Concerning what he accused her of. Then the Imam says to him: Fear Allah, for the curse of Allah is severe. Then the man says: The curse of Allah be upon him. If he is among the liars. Concerning what he accused her of. Then the woman stands and swears four times by Allah. Indeed, he is surely among the liars. Concerning what he accused her of. Then the Imam says to her: Fear Allah, for the anger of Allah is severe. Then the woman says: The anger of Allah be upon her. If he is among the truthful. Concerning what he accused her of.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a free man performing liʿān against a female slave. He said: "Yes, if it was her master who married her to him."

As for the report of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A free man does not perform liʿan against a female slave, nor against a dhimmiyyah, nor against a woman with whom he is in mut'ah.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: Regarding a man who accused his wife, then left and returned after she had died, he said: "He is given a choice between two options. It is said to him: If you wish, you may hold yourself guilty, then the ḥadd will be carried out upon you and you will be given the inheritance. And if you wish, you may affirm your claim, then you perform liʿān with her nearest relative to her, and there is no inheritance for you."

4857 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, "May I be sacrificed for you, how is it that when a man accuses his wife, his testimony is four testimonies by Allah, but when someone else accuses her—whether a father, brother, son, or a stranger—he is flogged with the hadd punishment unless he establishes proof for what he said?" He said, "Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام was asked about that, and he said: 'When a husband accuses his wife and says: “I saw that with my own eye,” then his testimony is four testimonies by Allah. But if he says that he did not see it, he is told: “Establish proof for what you said,” otherwise he is in the same position as anyone else.'" And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for the husband an access which He has not made for anyone else, whether a father or a son; and he enters upon her by night and day. So it is permissible for him to say, 'I saw.' But if someone else says, 'I saw,' it is said to him, 'What gave you access to the place in which you saw this, alone by yourself? You are under suspicion, and it is unavoidable that the hadd which Allah has made obligatory upon you be carried out against you.'

Hadith 4858 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while I was present with him, “How does a man perform liʿān against a woman?” So he عليه السلام said: A man from among the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if a man enters his house and sees with his wife a man having intercourse with her—what would he do concerning them?” He said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله turned away from him, so the man departed. That man was the very one who had been afflicted with that matter concerning his wife. He said: Then revelation came down from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with the ruling concerning them. He said: So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent for that man and summoned him, and said: “Are you the one who saw a man with your wife?” He said: “Yes.” So he said to him: “Go and bring me your wife, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent down the ruling concerning you and her.” He said: Her husband brought her, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله made her stand and said to the husband: “Bear witness four testimonies by Allah that you are surely among the truthful regarding what you have accused her of.” He said: So he testified. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Stop,” and admonished him. Then he said to him: “Have taqwa of Allah, for the curse of Allah is severe.” Then he said: “Bear the fifth testimony that the curse of Allah be upon you if you are among the liars.” He said: So he testified. Then he ordered that he be moved aside. Then he عليه السلام said to the woman: “Bear witness four testimonies by Allah that your husband is surely among the liars regarding what he has accused you of.” He said: So she testified. He said: Then he said to her: “Stop,” and admonished her. Then he said to her: “Have taqwa of Allah, for the anger of Allah is severe.” Then he said to her: “Bear the fifth testimony that the anger of Allah be upon you if your husband is among the truthful regarding what he has accused you of.” He said: So she testified. He said: Then he separated them and said to them: “Do not ever come together again in marriage after you have performed liʿān.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The divorce of a slave, when he marries a free woman or marries a bondwoman belonging to other people, belongs to the slave himself. But if he marries the bondwoman of his master, then the master has the right to separate them or keep them together if he wishes, and if he wishes, he may take her away from him without divorce.

Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurarah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام, who said: "The owned slave, his divorce is not valid, nor his marriage, except with the permission of his master." I said: "Then if the master had married him off, in whose hand is the divorce?" He said: "In the hand of the master: ‘Allah sets forth a parable: an owned slave who has no power over anything’—and the ‘thing’ is divorce."

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who marries off his bondwoman to a free man or to a slave belonging to another people. He said: “He does not have the right to take her away from him. But if he sells her, and the one who bought her wishes to remove her from her husband, he may do so.”

Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a slave who married without the permission of his master. He said: “That is up to the master; if he wishes, he approves it, and if he wishes, he separates them.” I said: “May Allah rectify you, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and their companions say that the basis of the marriage is invalid, so the master’s approval does not render it lawful.” He said: “He only disobeyed his master and did not disobey Allah; so if he approves it for him, then it is valid.”

Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, “If a free woman is married to a slave, how many divorces can he pronounce against her?” So he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Divorce and the waiting period are determined according to the women.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The divorce of a free woman, when she is married to a slave, is three divorces; and the divorce of a bondwoman, when she is married to a free man, is two divorces.

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man is free and his wife is a bondwoman, then her divorce is two pronouncements. And if the man is a slave and she is a free woman, then her divorce is three pronouncements.

Faḍālah narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a free man divorces a bondwoman and she observes part of her waiting period from him, then she is freed, then she observes the waiting period of a bondwoman.
And in the narration of Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The waiting period (ʿiddah) of the bondwoman who does not menstruate is forty-five nights.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: The divorce of a bondwoman is through her sale or the sale of her husband. And he said regarding a man who marries his bondwoman to a free man and then sells her: this is separation between them, unless the purchaser wishes to leave them together.

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a bondwoman is sold while she has a husband, then the one who bought her has the choice: if he wishes, he may separate them, and if he wishes, he may leave her with him. But if he leaves her with him, then he has no right to separate them after he has consented. He said: And if the male slave is sold, then if his master who bought him wishes to do the like of what the owner of the bondwoman did, then that belongs to him. But if he accepts, then he has no right to separate them after he has accepted.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whose father was a slave, and whose father had a wife who was a mukātabah and had already paid part of what she owed. The son of the slave said to her: "Would you like me to help you with your manumission contract so that you may pay what you owe, on condition that you will not have the option against my father when you gain ownership of yourself?" She said, "Yes." So he gave her for her manumission. Then: would she have the option after that? He عليه السلام said: "She does not have the option. The Muslims are bound by their conditions."

Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If a slave had a bondwoman as his wife and he divorced her once, then both of them were freed, she would remain with him on the basis of one divorce.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a bondwoman who was divorced and then freed before her waiting period had ended, he عليه السلام said: "She observes an ʿiddah of three menstrual cycles. But if her husband died and she was then freed before her waiting period had ended, then her ʿiddah is four months and ten days."

And Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a bondwoman who is married to a slave man and then she is freed. He said: “She is given the choice; if she wishes, she remains with her husband, and if she wishes, she separates.”

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام ruled concerning a concubine belonging to a man, who bore a child to her master. Then he married her to his slave. Then her master died and freed her, so she married him, and her child inherited from him. Then her child died, and she inherited her husband, the slave. Then the two came disputing, so he said: 'She is my wife; I will not divorce her.' And she said: 'He is my slave; he has not had intercourse with me.' So she was asked: 'Has he had intercourse with you since he became your slave?' She said: 'No.' He said: 'If he had had intercourse with you since he became your slave, I would have punished you. Go, for he is your slave. He has no authority over you. You may sell him if you wish, keep him enslaved if you wish, and free him if you wish.'

Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said to his wife, “You are separate from me,” or “absolved,” or “final,” or “separated,” or “forbidden.” He said: “It is nothing.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazantī narrated from Muhammad ibn Samāʿah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are forbidden to me.' He said: "If I had authority over him, I would have struck his head and said to him: Allah, the Exalted, has made her lawful for you, so who made her forbidden to you? He has done nothing more than lie, claiming that what Allah has made lawful for him is forbidden. Neither divorce nor expiation takes effect upon him." So I said to him: then what about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. So He made expiation binding upon him in it. He said: "He only forbade to himself his bondwoman Māriyah and swore that he would not approach her. The expiation was only imposed upon him for the oath, and it was not imposed upon him for the prohibition itself."

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, or a man asked him, about a man whose wife claimed against him that he was impotent, while the man denied that. He said: The midwife should apply khaluq to her without the man knowing, and he should enter upon her. Then if he comes out and khaluq is on his private part, he has spoken the truth and she has lied; otherwise, she has spoken the truth and he has lied.

And in another report, al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: If a woman claims against her husband that he is impotent and the man denies being so, then the ruling in that case is that the man should sit in cold water. If his private part becomes relaxed, then he is impotent; and if it becomes tense, then he is not impotent.

And it is narrated in another report: That he is fed fresh fish for three days, then it is said to him: Urinate upon ashes. So if his urine pierces the ashes, then he is not impotent; and if his urine does not pierce the ashes, then he is impotent.

4894 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Aban, from Ghiyath, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Regarding an impotent man: if it is known that he is impotent and does not approach women, they are to be separated. But if he has intercourse with her even once, they are not to be separated. And a man is not rejected on account of a defect.
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: "Whoever has intercourse with a woman once, then is taken away from her, then she has no option."

And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked him about a man who has been prevented from his wife, such that he is unable to have intercourse with her. He said: If he is unable to have intercourse with other women besides her, then he should not keep her unless she is content with that. But if he is able to have intercourse with other women, then there is no harm in his keeping her.

And it has been narrated in another report: Whenever a woman remains with her husband after she has learned that he is impotent and she accepts him as he is, she no longer has any option after acceptance.

4899 - It has been narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم advised ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, saying: “O ʿAlī, when the bride enters your house, remove her shoes when she sits, wash her feet, and pour water from the door of your house to the farthest part of your home. If you do that, Allah will remove from your house seventy thousand kinds of poverty, admit into it seventy thousand kinds of blessing, and send down upon her seventy mercies fluttering over the head of the bride until their blessing reaches every corner of your house. The bride will be safe from insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo so long as she remains in that house. And keep the bride, during her first week, away from milk, vinegar, coriander, and sour apples.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “O Messenger of Allah, for what reason should I keep her from these four things?” He said: “Because the womb becomes barren and cold toward childbearing from these four things, and a mat in a corner of the house is better than a woman who does not give birth.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with vinegar that you forbid it?” He said: “If she menstruates while taking vinegar, she will never become fully pure; coriander stirs menstruation in her belly and makes childbirth difficult for her; and sour apples cut off her menstruation and so become an illness for her.” Then he said: “O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife at the beginning of the month, its middle, or its end, for insanity, leprosy, and mental disorder may quickly affect her and her child. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife after noon, for if a child is decreed between you at that time, he will be cross-eyed, and Satan rejoices in cross-eyedness in the human being. O ʿAlī, do not speak during intercourse, for if a child is decreed between you, it is feared he may be mute. And let no one look at the private part of his wife; rather let him lower his gaze during intercourse, for looking at the private part causes blindness in the child. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife with desire for another man’s woman, for I fear that if a child is decreed between you, he may be effeminate or feminine and mentally impaired. O ʿAlī, whoever is junub in bed with his wife should not recite the Qur'an, for I fear that a fire may descend upon them fro

A man from the companions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام complained about his women, so he عليه السلام stood as an orator and said: O assembly of people, do not obey women in any situation, do not entrust them with wealth, and do not leave them to manage the affair of the dependents. For indeed, if they are left with what they want, they will bring about destruction and transgress the command of the owner. Indeed, we have found that they have no wara' in their need, and no patience in their desire. Extravagance is bound to them even if they grow old, and self-admiration remains attached to them even if they become weak. They do not give thanks for much when they are denied a little; they forget the good and preserve the evil; they rush headlong into calumny, persist in rebellion, and set themselves up for Satan. So deal with them tactfully in every circumstance, and speak well to them, so that they may act well.

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Miskān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distinguished His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله with noble character traits. So examine yourselves; if they are found in you, then praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and desire from Him an increase in them. Then he mentioned them as ten: certainty, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, good character, generosity, protective jealousy, courage, and manliness.

Hadith 4902 — The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Whoever desires continuance, though there is no permanence, should take the morning meal early, make the footwear good, lighten the cloak, and reduce intimacy with women." It was said, "O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what is the lightness of the cloak?" He said, "Few debts."
And he, peace be upon him, said: When a woman rises from her seat, no one should sit in that place until it has cooled down.
4904 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Three things ruin the body and may even kill: entering the bathhouse on a full stomach, intercourse upon fullness, and marrying elderly women."
And he, peace be upon him, said: There are three things that whoever becomes accustomed to them will not abandon them: trimming the hair, shortening the garment, and marrying bondwomen.
And he, peace be upon him, said: It is a disgrace for a man of dignity to spend the night away from his home in the city where his family resides.
And he, peace be upon him, said: "Cursed, cursed is the one who neglects those under his care."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: The best of you is the one who is best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family.
And he, peace be upon him, said: A man's family are his captives, and the most beloved of servants to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the one who treats his captives in the best manner.

4910 - Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said: A man's family are his captives. So whoever Allah blesses with a blessing, let him expand his provision upon his captives. If he does not do so, that blessing is close to being taken away.

4911 - Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said in his will to his son Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah: O my son, when you are strong, then be strong in obedience to Allah, and when you are weak, then be weak from disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And if you are able not to give a woman control over any of her affair beyond herself, then do so, for that is more lasting for her beauty, more relaxing for her mind, and better for her condition. Indeed, the woman is a delicate flower and not a caretaker. So treat her gently in every circumstance, and keep good companionship with her, so that your life may be pleasant.

And it is narrated from Khālid ibn Najīḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: They discussed misfortune in his presence, so he said: "Misfortune is in three things: in a woman, a mount, and a house. As for the misfortune of a woman, it is the largeness of her dowry and her disobedience to her husband. As for the mount, it is its bad temperament and its withholding of its back. And as for the house, it is the narrowness of its courtyard, the evil of its neighbors, and the abundance of its defects."

4913 - And it is narrated from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "The mother of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd said to Sulaymān عليه السلام: O my son, beware of excessive sleep at night, for excessive sleep at night leaves a man poor on the Day of Judgment."

4914 - It is narrated from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Baṣrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may the blessings of Allah be upon them, from his father, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has disliked for you, O community, twenty-four traits and has forbidden you from them. He has disliked for you idle play in salat (prayer), reminding others of one’s favor in charity, laughing among graves, peering into houses, and looking at the private parts of women.” And he said: “It causes blindness.” And he disliked speaking during intercourse. And he said: “It causes muteness. And he disliked sleeping before the last ʿIshāʾ prayer, and disliked conversation after the last ʿIshāʾ prayer, and disliked ghusl (ritual bath) under the sky without a waist-wrapper, and disliked intercourse under the sky, and disliked entering rivers without a waist-wrapper.” And he said: “In the rivers are inhabitants and dwellers from among the angels. And he disliked entering bathhouses except with a waist-wrapper, and disliked speaking between the adhān and the iqāmah in the morning salat (prayer) until the prayer is completed, and disliked riding upon the sea when it is turbulent, and disliked sleeping on a roof that is not enclosed.” And he said: “Whoever sleeps on a roof that is not enclosed, protection is cleared from him. And he disliked that a man sleep alone in a house, and disliked for a man to approach his wife while she is menstruating. If he approaches her and the child comes out leprous or afflicted with vitiligo, then let him blame none but himself. And he disliked that a man approach a woman while he has had a wet dream until he performs ghusl (ritual bath) from the wet dream that he saw. If he does so and the child comes out insane, then let him blame none but himself.” And he disliked that a man speak to a leper unless there is between him and him the measure of an arm’s length.” And he said: “Flee from the leper as you flee from a lion. And he disliked urinating on the bank of a flowing river, and disliked that a man relieve himself beneath a fruit-bearing tree that has ripened, or a palm tree that has ripened, meaning borne fruit. And he disliked that a man put on sand

4915 - And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "It is not permissible for anyone to be in a state of janabah in this mosque except me, and 'Alī, and Fāṭimah, and al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, and whoever is from my family, for indeed he is from me."

4916 - And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: It was said to 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him: “What is the matter with you that you do not marry?” So he said: “What would I do with marriage?” They said: “Children would be born to you.” He said: “What would I do with children? If they live, they cause trial; and if they die, they cause sorrow.”

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say in his supplication: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a child who becomes a master over me, from wealth that becomes loss upon me, from a wife who makes me gray before the time of my grayness, and from a deceitful close friend whose eyes see me while his heart watches for my harm. If he sees good, he buries it, and if he sees evil, he spreads it. And I seek refuge in You from stomach pain, [and from those who are] deaf: when they hear good by which I am mentioned, and if I am mentioned with evil in their presence, they listen."

4918 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There are three traits in one from whom no good is ever hoped: one who does not fear Allah in private, does not restrain himself in old age, and does not feel shame from fault.

4919 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, one of you comes to his wife, then she departs from beneath him; if she were to encounter a black man, she would cling to him. So when one of you comes to his wife, let there be mutual foreplay between them, for that is more pleasant for the matter.

And Sama'ah narrated from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: "The woman has been favored over the man with ninety-nine portions of pleasure, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has cast modesty upon her."

And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: The son of Adam will not do a deed greater before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a man who kills a Prophet, or demolishes the Ka'bah which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made a qiblah for His servants, or pours his fluid unlawfully into a woman.

4922 - Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله returned from a military expedition in which many of the Muslims had been struck down. The women came out to meet him, asking about their slain ones. A woman came near him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what happened to so-and-so?' He said, 'And what is he to you?' She said, 'My brother.' He said: Praise Allah and say the words of return, for he has been martyred. So she did that. Then she said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what happened to so-and-so?' He said, 'And what is he to you?' She said, 'My husband.' He said: Praise Allah and say the words of return, for he has been martyred. Then she said, 'Oh, what humiliation!' So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said, 'I did not think that a woman would feel this much over her husband until I saw this woman.'

Some of the companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “O Messenger of Allah, why is it that we feel toward our children what they do not feel toward us?” So he said: “Because they are from you, and you are not from them.”

And it is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah al-Rabaʿī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: He was asked: “Why is the believer so severe?” He said: “Because the honor of the Qur’an is in his heart, and pure iman is in his breast, and he is a servant obedient to Allah and to His Messenger, affirming the truth.” He was asked: “Then why is the believer sometimes the stingiest of people?” He said: “Because he earns sustenance from its halal source, and the pursuit of halal is precious and difficult. So he does not like any of his possessions to leave him because of what he knows of the preciousness of obtaining it. And if his soul is generous, he does not place it except in its proper place.” He was asked: “Then why is the believer sometimes most inclined toward marriage?” He said: “To protect his private part from private parts not lawful for him, and so that his desire may not incline him this way or that way. So when he attains what is halal, he is content with it and becomes free of need from anything else.” And he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the strength of the believer is in his heart. Do you not see that you may find him weak in body, thin in frame, while he stands at night and fasts by day?”

And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام, when the childbirth of a woman was at hand, would say: 'Remove whoever of the women is in the house, so that a woman is not the first to look at his private parts.'

And in the narration of Al-Husayn ibn Alwan from Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) mentioned jihad, and a woman said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Messenger of Allah, do women have any share in this?' He replied: 'Yes, for a woman, from the time of her pregnancy until she gives birth and until she weans her child, she receives a reward equal to that of a person stationed in the way of Allah. And if she dies during that period, she will have the same status as a martyr.'
Women were mentioned in the presence of Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, so he said: It is not appropriate for a woman to walk in the middle of the road; rather, she should walk along the side of the wall.

And Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is not appropriate for a woman to uncover herself in front of a Jewish woman or a Christian woman, for they describe that to their husbands.

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Marry off the foolish man, but do not marry the foolish woman, for the foolish man may produce noble offspring, whereas the foolish woman does not produce noble offspring.

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, or from someone else, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Four are never satisfied with four: the earth with rain, a female with a male, the eye with looking, and a scholar with knowledge."

ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān al-Wāsiṭī narrated from his uncle, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the major sins are seven; concerning us they were revealed, and against us they were deemed permissible. The first of them is shirk with Allah, the Magnificent, the killing of the soul which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, consuming the wealth of the orphan, disobedience to parents, accusing the chaste woman, fleeing from the battlefield, and denying our right. As for shirk with Allah, the Magnificent, Allah revealed concerning us what He revealed, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said concerning us what he said; yet they denied Allah and denied His Messenger, so they associated partners with Allah. And as for the killing of the soul which Allah has forbidden, they killed al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام and his companions. And as for consuming the wealth of the orphan, they took away our fayʾ, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had assigned to us, and gave it to others instead of us. And as for disobedience to parents, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed that in His Book, and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: The Prophet has a greater claim on the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. So they were undutiful to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله regarding his progeny, and they were undutiful to their mother Khadījah regarding her progeny. And as for accusing the chaste woman, they accused Fāṭimah عليها السلام upon their pulpits. And as for fleeing from the battlefield, they gave their bayʿah to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام willingly, without compulsion, then they fled from him and abandoned him. And as for denying our right, this is among that concerning which they do not dispute.

ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, who said: I heard my father Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام saying: “ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd al-Baṣrī entered upon Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. When he greeted him and sat down, he recited this verse: ‘Those who avoid the major sins,’ then he stopped. So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: ‘What made you stop?’ He said: ‘I would like to know the major sins from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.’ He said: ‘Yes, O ʿAmr.’” “The greatest of the major sins is shirk with Allah. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:” “Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him.” And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, then Allah has forbidden Jannah for him, and his refuge is the Fire, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.” And after it is despair of the mercy of Allah, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Indeed, none despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.” Then feeling secure from the plan of Allah, because Allah, Exalted, says: “None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.” And among them is disobedience to parents, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the disobedient one arrogant and wretched in His saying, Exalted is He: “And dutiful to my mother, and He did not make me arrogant and wretched.” And killing the soul which Allah, Exalted, has forbidden except with right, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Jahannam, abiding in it.” To the end of the verse. And accusing chaste women, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.” And consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly only consume fire into their bellies, and they shall enter a Blaze.” And fleeing from the battlefield, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless maneuvering for battle or joining another group, has incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Jahannam, and evil is the destination.” And consuming riba,
And it has been narrated in another report: "Indeed, injustice in a will is among the major sins."

And ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān, in what he wrote as an answer to his questions: Allah has forbidden the killing of the soul because of the corruption of creation that would result from permitting it, their destruction, and the corruption of order. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden disobedience to parents because of what it contains of departing from reverence for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and reverence for the parents, ingratitude for the blessing, nullifying gratitude, and what that leads to of a decrease in offspring and its cessation, due to what is in undutifulness of diminished respect for the parents, recognizing their right, severing kinship ties, the parents becoming disinclined toward the child, and abandoning upbringing because of the child's abandonment of dutifulness toward them. And Allah, Exalted, has forbidden zina because of the corruption in it: killing souls, loss of lineages, neglect of children's upbringing, corruption of inheritances, and other similar aspects of corruption. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden accusing chaste women because of what it contains of corruption of lineages, denial of the child, nullifying inheritances, abandoning upbringing, loss of social knowledge and ties, and because of the grave sins and causes that lead to the corruption of creation. And He has forbidden consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly for many reasons among the aspects of corruption. The first of that is that when a person consumes the wealth of the orphan unjustly, he has assisted in killing him, for the orphan is not self-sufficient, cannot manage for himself, has no one standing over his affairs, and has no one to care for him sufficiently like the care of his parents. So when one consumes his wealth, it is as though he has killed him and reduced him to poverty and need, along with what Allah has forbidden regarding it and what He has assigned for it of punishment in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: And let those fear who, if they left behind weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them be wary of Allah and speak a right word. And due to the saying of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: 'Indeed Allah has promised, regarding consuming the wealth of the orphan, two punishments: a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.' Thus, in forbidding the orphan's wealth there is p
And Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, only forbade usury so that they would not refrain from acts of kindness.
And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only forbade usury so that kindness would not disappear.

Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the reason for the prohibition of ribā, so he said: If ribā had been halal, people would have abandoned trade and the things they need. So Allah made ribā haram so that people would flee from the unlawful to the lawful, and to trade, buying, and selling, so that this may remain among them in lending.

And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: The magician among the Muslims is to be killed, and the magician among the disbelievers is not to be killed. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, why is the magician among the disbelievers not killed? He said: Because shirk is greater than magic, and because magic and shirk are joined together.
And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden wine because of its effects and its corruption.

4940 - And it is narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jābir, from Zaynab bint ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: Fāṭimah عليها السلام said in her sermon concerning the matter of Fadak: Allah has among you a covenant that He advanced to you, and a remainder that He appointed over you: the Book of Allah, whose insights are clear, whose signs are evident, whose inner meanings are unveiled, and whose outward proofs are manifest. Its hearing is enduring for creation; it leads its followers to good pleasure and brings its adherents to salvation. In it is the clarification of Allah’s illuminated proofs, His defined prohibitions, His recommended virtues, His sufficient summaries, His granted dispensations, His prescribed laws, and His clear evidences. So Allah made faith a purification from shirk, salat (prayer) a cleansing from arrogance, zakat an increase in provision, fasting a clarification of sincerity, hajj a strengthening of the religion, justice a settling of hearts, obedience an order for the community, Imamate a uniting against division, jihad an honor for Islam, patience an aid toward seeking response, enjoining what is right a benefit for the public, dutifulness to parents a protection against wrath, maintaining kinship ties a cause of increase in number, legal retribution a preservation of blood, fulfillment of vows an exposure to forgiveness, giving full measure and weights a reproach against deficiency, slandering chaste women a barrier from curse, abandoning theft an obligation of chastity, consuming the wealth of orphans a protection from wrongdoing, justice in judgments a reassurance for the subjects; and Allah has forbidden shirk as sincerity to Him in Lordship. So fear Allah as He should truly be feared. Regarding what Allah has commanded you with, and desist from what He has forbidden you.
And in the narration of Abū Khadījah Sālim ibn Mukram al-Jammāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Lying against Allah, His Messenger, and the awṣiyāʾ عليهم السلام is among the major sins.
4942 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire."

And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sulaymān, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “Whoever grants a man safety over his life, then kills him, will come on the Day of Judgment carrying the banner of treachery.”

Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbbād, from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the major sins, and he said: "Every sin for which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has threatened the Fire."

Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍramī narrated from Samā‘ah ibn Mihrān, who said: I heard him say: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has promised two punishments for consuming the wealth of the orphan. As for one of them, it is the punishment of the Hereafter by the Fire; and as for the punishment of this world, it is His statement, Mighty and Majestic: Let those fear who, if they left behind weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them be wary of Allah and speak a right word. This means: let him fear that He may treat his offspring after him as he dealt with these orphans.

And he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Insulting a believer is wickedness, fighting him is disbelief, consuming his flesh is disobedience to Allah, and the sanctity of his wealth is like the sanctity of his blood.
And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Whoever applies kohl with a stick from an intoxicant, Allah will apply kohl to him with a stick of fire.

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man asked him and said: “May Allah rectify you, is drinking wine worse, or abandoning salat (prayer)?” He said: “Drinking wine.” Then he said: “Do you know why that is?” He said: “No.” He said: “Because he comes into a state in which he does not recognize his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”
And he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, those who are sated in this world by intoxicant die thirsty, are resurrected thirsty, and enter the Fire thirsty.

Aban ibn Uthman narrated from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام say: "Whoever drinks wine and becomes intoxicated from it, no salat (prayer) will be accepted from him for forty days. If he abandons the salat (prayer) during these days, the punishment will be doubled for him due to his abandoning the salat (prayer)."
And in another narration: Indeed, his salat (prayer) will be suspended between the sky and the earth. But if he repents, it will be returned to him and accepted from him.

And Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Kātib, from his father, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام came into al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and some of them said: “If only you would send one of yourselves to ask him.” So a young man from among them came to him and said: “O uncle, what is the greatest of the major sins?” He said: “Drinking alcohol.” Then he came back to them and informed them. They said to him: “Return to him.” They kept at him until he returned to him and asked him, so he said to him: “Did I not tell you, O son of my brother, [it is] drinking alcohol? Indeed, drinking alcohol causes its companion to enter into adultery, theft, and killing a soul...” which Allah has forbidden and into shirk with Allah. And the effects of alcohol rise above every sin, just as its tree rises above every tree.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Whoever intentionally kills himself shall be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance leads to the Fire.
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “The slightest form of shirk is that a man innovates an opinion, then loves on its basis and hates on its basis.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, “What is the least degree of nasb?” He said, “That a man innovates something, then loves on account of it and hates on account of it.”
4957 - And he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Whoever walks toward a person of innovation and shows him respect has indeed striven in the destruction of Islam.

Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: There was a man in earlier times who sought the world through halal means but could not attain it, and he sought it through haram means but could not attain it. Then al-Shaytan came to him and said: O this one, you have sought the world through halal and could not attain it, then you sought it through haram and could not attain it; shall I guide you to something by which you will increase your worldly gains and increase your followers? He said: Yes. He said: Invent a religion and call the people to it. So he did so, and the people responded to him and obeyed him, and he gained from the world. Then he reflected and said: What have I done? I invented a religion and called the people to it, and I see no tawbah for myself except that I go to those whom I called and turn them away from it. So he began going to his companions who had answered him, saying: What I called you to is false, and I only invented it. But they began saying: You have lied; it is the truth, but you have doubted your religion and so turned back from it. When he saw that, he went to a chain and fixed for it a peg, then placed it around his neck and said: I will not remove it until Allah accepts my tawbah. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet from among the prophets: Say to so-and-so, by My Might and My Majesty, even if you were to call upon Me until your limbs are cut apart, I would not answer you until you bring back those who died upon what you called them to, so that they turn away from it.

4959 - Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Indeed, the one characterized by doubt and disobedience is in the Fire; they are neither from us nor directed to us.

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, he said: The adulterer has six traits: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, he loses the light of the face, brings about poverty, and hastens destruction. And as for those in the Hereafter, they are the wrath of the Lord, an evil reckoning, and abiding forever in the Fire.

4961 - And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Isḥāq ibn Hilāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: 'Shall I not inform you of the gravest form of zina?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a woman who gives access to her husband's bed, then brings a child from other than him and imposes him upon her husband.' So that is the one whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at on the Day of Judgment, nor purify her, and for her is a painful punishment.'

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Saʿīd al-Azraq, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who killed a believing man, he said: "It will be said to him: Die whichever death you wish: as a Jew, if you wish, or as a Christian, if you wish, or as a Magian, if you wish."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Indeed, my intercession is only for the people of major sins from my nation.

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Our intercession is for the people of major sins from among our Shi'ah; as for those who repent, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: There is no way against the doers of good.
And he said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “There is no intercessor more successful than tawbah (repentance).”

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Do the major sins enter into the will of Allah? He عليه السلام said: Yes, that belongs to Him, the Mighty and Majestic; if He wills, He punishes for them, and if He wills, He pardons.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Whoever avoids the major sins, Allah will expiate all his sins from him, and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance.' "

Talaq al-ʿiddah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he divorces her in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse, with two just witnesses. Then he takes her back that same day or later before she menstruates, and he has witnesses to her return, until she menstruates. When she becomes pure from that menstruation, he divorces her again, a second divorce, without intercourse, and has witnesses to that. Then he may take her back whenever he wishes before she menstruates, and he has witnesses to her return, and has intercourse with her, and she remains with him until she menstruates a second time. When she becomes pure from that menstruation, he divorces her a third time while she is pure and without intercourse, and has witnesses to that. If he does that, she has become separated from him and is not halal for him until she marries another husband. The minimum form of taking back is that he kisses her or denies the divorce, so his denial of the divorce counts as taking her back. Taking back is permissible without witnesses just as marriage is permissible, but taking back without witnesses is only disliked because of matters of hudud, inheritances, and the ruler. Whoever divorces his wife for the waiting period three times, one after another as described, and then the woman marries another husband, but he does not consummate with her and then divorces her or dies before consummation, and the woman completes her waiting period, it is not permissible for her first husband to marry her until another man marries her, consummates with her, and tastes her sweetness, then divorces her or dies from her, and she completes her waiting period from him. Then if the first wishes to marry her, he may do so. If a man marries her in mutʿah and consummates with her, then separates from her or dies from her, it is not permissible for her first husband to marry her until another man marries her in a definitive permanent marriage and consummates with her, so that she has entered into the like of what she exited from; then he divorces her or dies from her, and she completes her waiting period from him. Then if the first wishes to marry her, he may do so. If a slave marries her, then he is one of the husbands. Everyone who divorces his wife for the waiting period, then she marries another husband, then he marries her again, then divorces her for the waiting p

Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: And do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress. He said: It refers to a man who divorces, then when her term is about to expire, he takes her back, then divorces her again. He does that three times, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade that.

It has been narrated from the Imams, peace be upon them, that talaq al-sunnah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he waits until she menstruates and then becomes pure. Then he divorces her at the beginning of her waiting period, with two just witnesses, in a single sitting, and with a single utterance. If he calls one man to witness the divorce and then later calls the second, that divorce is not valid unless he makes them both witnesses together in one session. When three periods of purity have passed for her, she has become separated from him, and he is then a suitor among the suitors. The matter rests with her: if she wishes, she marries him, and if she wishes, she does not. If he marries her after that, he marries her with a new dowry. If he then wishes to divorce her, he divorces her according to the sunnah as I have described. Whenever he divorces her with talaq al-sunnah, it is permissible for him to marry her again after that. Talaq al-sunnah is called talaq al-hadm, because when she completes her cycles and he marries her a second time, the first divorce is annulled. Every divorce that goes against the sunnah is invalid. Whoever divorces his wife according to the sunnah may take her back so long as her waiting period has not ended. When her waiting period ends, she is separated from him and he becomes a suitor among the suitors. The testimony of women is not valid in divorce. The man who divorces according to the sunnah must provide the woman’s maintenance and lodging as long as she remains in her waiting period, and the two inherit from one another until the waiting period comes to an end.

Al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: It is not proper for a man to divorce his wife and then take her back while he has no desire for remaining with her, and then divorce her again. This is the harmful treatment that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, except when he divorces and then takes her back while intending to keep her.

Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "There is no divorce except according to the sunnah (prophetic tradition). Indeed, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar pronounced divorce three times in one sitting while his wife was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم rejected his divorce and said:" "Whatever contradicts the Book of Allah must be referred back to the Book of Allah." ".

4763 - Al-Qasim ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Saḥḥāf narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān that Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to him, among what he wrote in reply to his questions: “The reason for divorce being three times is because of the respite in it between the first and the third, for a desire that may arise, or the subsiding of anger if it was present. And let that be a warning and discipline for women, and a deterrent for them from disobeying their husbands. Thus the woman deserves separation and estrangement for entering into what is not proper through abandoning obedience to her husband. And the reason for the woman becoming forbidden after nine divorces, such that she is not lawful for him, is as a punishment so that he may not take divorce lightly nor treat the woman as weak. And so that he may be observant in his affairs, vigilant, and reflective, and so that there may be despair for both of them of reunion after nine divorces.”

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who said to his wife, "If I marry over you or spend a night away from you, then you are divorced." So he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: 'Whoever stipulates a condition contrary to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is not valid against him nor for him.'" He said: And he was asked about a man who said, "Every woman whom I marry, so long as my mother lives, is divorced." So he said: "There is no divorce except after marriage, and no emancipation except after ownership."

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from his father, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the reason for which the woman divorced by ṭalāq al-ʿiddah does not become lawful again for her husband "until she marries another husband." So he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has only permitted divorce twice, and the Mighty and Majestic said: Divorce is twice; then keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. Meaning in the third pronouncement of divorce: because he entered into that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked for him of the third divorce, He made her unlawful for him, so she is not lawful for him "until she marries another husband." This is so that people may not treat divorce lightly and may not harm women."

4753 - And in the narration of al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: About a man who said: “His wife is divorced and his slaves are free if I ever drink anything forbidden, or anything lawful, from al-ṭilāʾ, ever.” So he said: “As for what is forbidden, then he must never approach it, whether he swore an oath or whether he did not swear. And as for al-ṭilāʾ, he has no right to forbid what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:” “O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?” “So no oath is valid in forbidding what is lawful, nor in making lawful what is forbidden, nor in severing kinship ties.”

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A woman divorced three times has no right to maintenance or lodging from her husband. That applies only to the woman whose husband still has the right to take her back.

And it was narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A man stood before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: I divorced my wife for the ʿiddah without witnesses. So he said: Your divorce is not a divorce; therefore return to your family.

Bukayr ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “If a man divorces his wife and brings two just witnesses during the beginning of her waiting period ('iddah), then he has no right to divorce her again after that until her waiting period ends or he takes her back.”
A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, I have divorced my wife.” So he said: “Do you have evidence?” He said: “No.” So he said: “Be gone.”

Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “If I were to govern the people, I would teach them divorce and how they ought to divorce.” Then he said: “If a man who had opposed it were brought to me, I would strike his back severely. Whoever divorces contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, even if he dislikes it.”

Samaʿah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about where a divorced woman should observe her waiting period. He said: In her house; she should not go out. If she wishes to make a visit, she may go out before midnight and return after midnight. She should not go out during the day, and she is not permitted to perform hajj until her waiting period is completed.

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. He said: “Except if she commits adultery, then she is to be expelled, and the hadd is to be carried out upon her.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon him. Regarding a woman whom her husband divorced, and he did not provide her maintenance during the waiting period, while she was in need: is it permissible for her to go out and spend the night away from her home for work and need? So he, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: There is no harm in that if Allah knows sincerity from her.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said to another man, 'Write, O so-and-so, to my wife regarding her divorce,' or said, 'Write to my slave regarding his emancipation.' Would that constitute divorce or emancipation? He عليه السلام said: 'There is no divorce and no emancipation until the tongue utters it or he writes it with his own hand while intending divorce or emancipation, and that is done by him with the proper times and witnesses, while he is absent from his family.'

Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Regarding the absent man who divorces, how long must his absence be? He said: "Five months or six months." I said: Is there a limit in it less than that? He said: "Three months."
Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If an absent man wants to divorce his wife, he should leave her for one month.

ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the divorce of the mentally impaired one whose intellect has departed: is it valid? He said: “No.” And about the woman, if she is in that same condition, is her sale and her charity valid? He said: “No.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he was asked about the maʿtūh: is his divorce valid? He said, “What is he?” I said, “The foolish one whose intellect has gone.” He said, “Yes.”

What Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Khālid al-Qammāṭ, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man who recognizes his own view at one time and denies it at another, is the divorce of his guardian over him permissible?” So he said: “What is the matter with him? Does he not divorce himself?” He said: I said, “He does not know the limit of divorce, and one cannot feel secure about him that if he divorces today, he may say tomorrow: I did not divorce.” So he said: “I do not see him except in the position of the Imam, meaning the guardian.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, then she is entitled to half of her dowry. And if he had not specified a dowry for her, then provision should be made in a fair manner, according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor. And there is no waiting period for her; she may marry whomever she wishes immediately.

And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "Then if you divorce them before you have touched them, there is no waiting period for you to count against them. So provide for them and release them in a gracious manner." He عليه السلام said: "Provide for them," meaning: honor them with whatever kindness you are able to give, for they return with sorrow, loneliness, great grief, and as an object of gloating from their enemies. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Generous, is shy, and loves the people of modesty. Verily, the most noble of you are those most intense in honoring their wives."
And in the narration of Al-Bazanti: "The mut'ah (compensatory gift) for a divorced woman is an obligation."
And it is narrated: The wealthy man provides a house or a servant as a parting gift, the middle-income man provides clothing, and the poor man provides a dirham or a ring.
And it is narrated: That its minimum is a khimār (headscarf) or something similar to it.

4778 - Al-Halabi, Abu Basir, and Sama'ah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified a dowry for them, then half of what you have specified must be paid, unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes it.” He عليه السلام said: “It is the father, or the brother, or the man entrusted with her affairs, and the one whose authority concerning the woman’s property is valid, so he purchases for her and trades; then if he waives it, it is valid.”
And in another narration: He may take a part and leave a part, but he does not have the right to forgo all of it.

ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman whose husband died before consummating the marriage. He said: She is entitled to inheritance, and she must observe the complete waiting period. If he had specified a dowry for her, then she is entitled to half of it; and if he had not specified a dowry for her, then she is entitled to nothing.

Shihab asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, then paid it to her, and she gifted it back to him and said, “I desire you more,” then he divorced her before consummating with her. He عليه السلام said: “He returns against her for five hundred dirhams.”

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The compensation (mutʿah) for women is obligatory, whether consummation took place with her or consummation did not take place with her, and she is to be provided this compensation before she is divorced.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a woman whose husband died and had not consummated marriage with her; he said: She must not marry until she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days, the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: Regarding a woman whose husband has died while she is in her waiting period, and she is in need and finds no one to provide for her, and she works for people: is it permissible for her to go out, work, and stay away from her home at night for work and need during her waiting period? He said: so he عليه السلام wrote in reply, 'There is no harm in that, if Allah wills.'

And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman whose husband dies, whether it is permissible for her to leave her home during her waiting period ('iddah). He عليه السلام said: “Yes. She may apply henna, use oil, apply kohl, comb her hair, dye it, wear dyed garments, and do whatever she wishes, without adornment for a husband.”
And in another report, he said: There is no harm in a woman whose husband has passed away performing hajj while she is in her waiting period, and moving from one house to another.
Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: The divorce of a pregnant woman is a single divorce, and when she delivers what is in her womb, she has become separated from him.

4788 - And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: A pregnant divorced woman is to be provided for until she delivers her child, and she has more right to nurse her child so long as she accepts what another woman would accept. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'No mother should be harmed because of her child, nor should any father because of his child. And upon the heir is the like of that.' No harm is to be caused through the infant, nor to his mother regarding his nursing. She has no right to take compensation for his nursing beyond two complete years; then if they desire weaning before that, 'by mutual consent of both of them,' it is good. And al-fiṣāl means weaning.

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a pregnant woman whose husband has died, maintenance is to be spent on her from the wealth of her child who is in her womb.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام said: The maintenance of a pregnant woman whose husband has died is from the entirety of the wealth until she gives birth.

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant. She gave birth before four months and ten days had passed, then she married. So he ruled that he should separate from her, then not propose to her until the later of the two terms has expired. Then if the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may withhold her. If they withhold her, they must return his wealth to him.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a pregnant woman whose husband divorces her and then she miscarries, whether the miscarriage was fully formed or not, or she delivered a lump of flesh: does her waiting period end by that? So he said: Everything that she delivers which makes it clear that it was a pregnancy, whether fully formed or not, then her waiting period has ended by it, even if it was a lump of flesh. He said: And I heard him saying: If a man divorces his wife and she claims pregnancy, she waits nine months. Then if she gives birth, otherwise she observes a waiting period of three months; then she has become separated from him.

And Salamah ibn al-Khattab narrated from Isma'il ibn Ishaq, from Isma'il ibn Aban, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: The minimum period a woman carries a pregnancy is six months, and the maximum period she carries is two years.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr al-Ṣayqal, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning a man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant. He said: "He may divorce her." I said: "Then may he take her back?" He said: "Yes, he may take her back." I said: "If it then occurs to him, after he has taken her back, to divorce her?" He said: "No, not until she gives birth."

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about a pregnant woman whom her husband divorces, then takes back, then divorces again, then takes back, then divorces a third time, and he said: She has become separated from him, and she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband.

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام: Regarding one who accuses his wife, he said: "He is to be flogged." I said: "What if she pardons him?" He said: "No, and no honor."

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ḥammād ibn Ziyād, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who said to his wife, after he had consummated the marriage with her, “I did not find you a virgin,” he عليه السلام said: “There is no legal punishment upon him.”
And in another report, he said: "Indeed, the hymen may be lost without intercourse; it may go due to injury, stumbling, or falling."

5066 - And in the narration of Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: “Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام would not administer the legal punishment in the case of insinuation until one came with an explicit slanderous accusation, such as: ‘O adulterer,’ or ‘O son of an adulteress,’ or ‘You are not your father’s son.’”

5067 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a Christian who slanderously accused a Muslim and said to him, “O adulterer.” He عليه السلام said: “He is to be flogged eighty lashes for the right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes minus one for the sanctity of Islam. His head is to be shaved, and he is to be paraded among the people of his religion so that others may be deterred.”

And it was narrated from Ṣafwān, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who slanders a man from the pre-Islamic Arabs. He said: "He is to be given the legal punishment." I said: "Is he to be given the legal punishment?" He said: "Yes, indeed that reaches the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله."

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Makhlad al-Sarrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he ruled concerning a man who called another, “the son of a madman,” and the other said to him, “Rather, you are the son of a madman.” So he commanded the first to flog his companion twenty lashes and said, “Know that you will be followed with the like of it: twenty.” Then when he had flogged him, he gave the whipped man the lash, so he flogged him twenty lashes, as a punishment disciplining them both.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl narrated from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said to his wife, “O adulteress.” He عليه السلام said: “He is to be flogged as a hadd punishment, and they are to be separated after he has been flogged, and she will no longer be his wife.” He عليه السلام said: “But if he said words that slipped out from him without knowing anything, intending thereby only to anger her, then they are not to be separated.”
And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: If, in the hadd punishment, there is 'perhaps' or 'it may be,' then the hadd punishment is suspended.

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The one who accuses a foundling of fornication is subjected to the prescribed punishment. And if a woman accuses her husband of fornication while he is deaf, they are separated, then she is never lawful for him again.

Ibn Mahbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who accused his wife of zinā while she was mute and deaf, not hearing what he said. He said: "If she has evidence—witnesses who testify for her before the Imam—he is flogged with the legal punishment, and the two are separated; then she is never lawful for him again. But if she has no evidence, then she is forbidden to him so long as he remains with her, and there is no sin upon her from him."
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī that ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Whoever acknowledges a child and then denies him shall be flogged with the legal punishment and made responsible for the child.
