And in the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Every adult, male or female, who falsely accuses a minor or an adult, a male or a female, a Muslim, a free person, or a slave, then upon him is the prescribed punishment of slanderous accusation; and upon one who is not yet an adult is the disciplinary punishment.
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: There is no legal punishment upon a mad person until he regains sanity, nor upon a child until he reaches maturity, nor upon a sleeping person until he wakes up.

5077 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-'Ala' and Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a man who said to his wife, “O adulteress, I committed adultery with you,” he عليه السلام said: “One legal punishment is upon him for his accusing her. As for his saying, ‘I committed adultery with you,’ there is no legal punishment upon him in that unless he testifies against himself four times to zina before the Imam.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding four men who testified against a woman for adultery, one of whom was her husband, he عليه السلام said: “The three are to be flogged, and her husband is to engage in li'an with her. They are to be separated, and she is never lawful for him again.”
And it has been narrated: Indeed, the husband is one of the witnesses.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: “If a man were brought to me who had accused a Muslim slave of zinā, and we knew nothing of him except goodness, I would administer to him the hadd, the hadd of a free person, except for one lash.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ḥammād ibn Ziyād, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked about a mukātab who falsely accused a Muslim man, so he said: “He is to be given the hadd of a free man, eighty lashes, whether he has paid anything of his mukātabah or has not paid.” It was said to him: “What if he commits zina while he is a mukātab and has not paid anything of his mukātabah?” He said: “This is the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Fifty lashes are removed from him, and he is given fifty.”

5082 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a woman who slanderously accused a man, he عليه السلام said: “She is to be flogged eighty lashes.”

Hadith 5083 — Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man disavows his child after having acknowledged him. He said: "If the child is from a free woman, the father is to be flogged fifty lashes, the hadd of a slave. But if he is from a slave woman, then there is nothing upon him." If a man says to another man, "You do the deed of the people of Lūṭ; you have relations with men," he is to be struck with eighty lashes. Likewise, if he says to him, "O maʿfūj, O one penetrated," he is flogged with the hadd of the slanderer: eighty lashes. If a man accuses a group with a single statement, then only one hadd is due upon him if he did not name them individually; but if he named them, then for each man he named there is a hadd upon him. That was narrated by Burayd Al-ʿIjlī from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. And it has been narrated: "If they come with him separately, one hadd is administered for each man among them; but if they come with him together, one hadd is administered. If a man accuses another man and is flogged, then returns to accuse him again, then if he says, 'What I said to you is true,' he is not flogged. But if he accuses him of zinā after he has been flogged, then the hadd is upon him. And if he accuses him ten times before he is flogged, there is only one hadd upon him."

And Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who said to another man, 'O son of the adulteress,' meaning adultery. He (as) said: 'If his mother is alive and present, and she comes forward to claim her right, he is to be flogged eighty lashes. And if she is absent, he is to be delayed until she arrives and claims her right. And if she has passed away and nothing is known of her except goodness, the one who falsely accused her is to be given the legal punishment - eighty lashes.'

And Abu Ayyub narrated from Hariz from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the son of a violated woman, against whom a man fabricates an accusation and says to him, 'O son of an adulteress.' He عليه السلام said: 'I hold that the legal punishment of eighty lashes is upon him, and he must repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for what he said.'

And it was narrated from Abī Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ that he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought two men, each of whom had accused the other regarding his body, so he waived the hadd punishment from both of them and administered taʿzīr to them."

Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Askari (peace be upon him) about a man who made a bequest of wealth in the way of Allah, so he said: 'The way of Allah is our Shia.'

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “A man made a bequest to me regarding something in the way of Allah,” so he said to me, “Spend it on hajj.” He said: I said, “He made a bequest to me for the way.” He said, “Spend it on hajj, for I do not know any way among His ways better than hajj.”

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who made a bequest for a hajj and made it a bequest concerning a person. He said: His executor must bear its cost and place it in a hajj just as he had bequeathed. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Then whoever changes it after he has heard it, its sin is only upon those who change it.”

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Marid who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who made a will to another man, instructing him to free a soul for six hundred dirhams from his one-third share. The executor went and gave the six hundred to a man to perform Hajj on his behalf. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: "I see that the executor must bear the cost of six hundred dirhams from his own wealth and place it in what the deceased had willed for freeing a soul."

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Zayd al-Narsī, from ʿAlī ibn Mazyad, the companion of al-Sābirī, who said: A man entrusted me with his estate and instructed me to perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and found it to be a small amount that was not sufficient for hajj, so I asked Abū Ḥanīfah and the fuqahāʾ of Kūfah, and they said: Give it as charity on his behalf. Then when I met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan during tawaf, I asked him and said: A man from your followers from the people of Kūfah died and entrusted his estate to me, instructing me to perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and it was not enough for hajj, so I asked the jurists among us, and they said: Give it as charity on his behalf. So I gave it as charity. What do you say? He said to me: Here is Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad in the Hijr, so go to him and ask him. I entered the Hijr, and there was Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام beneath the Mīzāb, facing the House and making du'a. Then he turned and saw me and said: What is your need? I said: A man died and entrusted his estate to me so that I should perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and it was not enough for hajj, so I asked the jurists among us, and they said: Give it as charity. He said: What did you do? I said: I gave it as charity. He said: You have become liable, unless it was not enough to cover what one could perform hajj with from Makkah. If it did not reach the amount by which hajj could be performed from Makkah, then there is no liability upon you. But if it did reach the amount by which hajj could be performed from Makkah, then you are liable.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and maternal uncles, he عليه السلام said: “Two-thirds are for his paternal uncles, and one-third is for his maternal uncles.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) A man had male and female children, and he acknowledged a piece of land as belonging to his children without mentioning that it should be divided among them according to Allah's shares and obligatory portions, where the male and female are equal in it. He (peace be upon him) replied: "They execute their father's will according to what he specified. If he did not specify anything, they return it to the Book of Allah, the Exalted, if Allah wills."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: A man bequeathed one-third of his wealth concerning his male and female freed slaves: are the male and the female equal in it, or... "For the male is the like of the share of two females." with respect to the bequest? So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: "It is valid for the deceased whatever he bequeathed, according to what he bequeathed, if Allah, the Exalted, wills."

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd narrated from his brother Jaʿfar ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who appointed a woman as his executor and joined with her in the bequest a young boy. He said: “That is permissible. The woman carries out the bequest and does not wait for the boy to reach maturity. Then when the boy reaches maturity, he has no right to withhold approval except in the case of alteration or change; then he has the right to return it to what the deceased had bequeathed.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: A man appointed his children as executors, and among them were adults who had reached maturity and among them were minors. Is it permissible for the adults to carry out the bequest and pay his debt to the one who established it against the deceased through just witnesses before the minors reach maturity? So he عليه السلام wrote: "It is upon the adult children to pay their father's debt and not withhold it on account of that."

ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar, meaning the second, peace be upon him, about a man who appointed me as his executor and instructed me to give something to his uncle every year, then the uncle died. So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "Give it to his heirs."

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled concerning a man who made a bequest to another while the one for whom the bequest was made was absent, and then the one to whom the bequest had been made died before the testator. He عليه السلام said: "The bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom it was made." And he عليه السلام said: "Whoever makes a bequest to someone, whether present or absent, and the beneficiary dies before the testator, then the bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom it was made, unless he retracts his bequest before he dies."

Al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir narrated from Muthannā, who said: I asked him about a man for whom a bequest was made, but he died before receiving it and left no offspring. He said: “Seek an heir or a mawlā for him, then give it to him.” I said: “What if no guardian/heir is known for him?” He said: “Strive to find a guardian for him, and if you do not find one, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows your effort, then give it in charity.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: A woman from my household made a bequest to me from her wealth and instructed that a slave be emancipated on her behalf, that hajj be performed, and that charity be given. But that amount was not sufficient, so I asked Abū Ḥanīfah, and he said: It should be made into three parts: one-third for hajj, one-third for manumission, and one-third for charity. Then I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: A woman from my family died and made a bequest to me of one-third of her wealth, and instructed that a slave be emancipated on her behalf, that hajj be performed on her behalf, and that charity be given on her behalf; then I examined it, and it was not sufficient. So he عليه السلام said: “Begin with hajj, for it is an obligation from among the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and make what remains into one portion for manumission and one portion for charity.” So I informed Abū Ḥanīfah of the statement of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he withdrew from his opinion and adopted the statement of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a man who was on a journey, and with him were a bondwoman of his and two male slave servants. He said to them, “You are both free for the sake of Allah, so bear witness that what is in the womb of this bondwoman of mine is from me.” Then she gave birth to a boy. When they came to the heirs, they denied that and enslaved them. Then later the two male slaves were emancipated, and after they had been emancipated, they testified that their former master had made them witness that what was in the womb of his bondwoman was from him. He عليه السلام said: “Their testimony is valid for the boy, and the boy for whom they testified cannot enslave them, because they established his lineage.”

5493 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Ḥumrān, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Concerning a man who made a bequest at the time of his death and said: 'Free so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so,' until he mentioned five. Then his one-third was examined, but his one-third did not reach the prices of the value of the five slaves whom he ordered to be freed. He عليه السلام said: 'The ones whom he named are to be considered in the order he named them and began with freeing them. They are to be appraised, and his one-third is considered; then the first thing he mentioned is freed from it, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth. If the one-third falls short, it applies to the one he named last, because he ordered emancipation beyond the amount of the one-third with what he does not own, so that is not permissible for him.'

Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whom death approached, so he freed his غلام and made a bequest, and it amounted to more than one-third. He عليه السلام said: "The emancipation of the غلام is to be carried out, and the reduction is to be in what remains."

And Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū Hammām Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Regarding a man who, at the time of his death, made a bequest of wealth to his relatives and freed a slave, and the total of all that he bequeathed exceeded one-third, how should his will be handled? So he عليه السلام said: "The manumission is begun with first, and it is carried out."

Al-Naḍr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from Khālid ibn Mādd, from al-Jāzī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who died and left behind a slave-girl, of whom he had freed one-third, then the executor married her before anything from the inheritance had been divided. That she is to be appraised, and she and her husband are to work to pay the remainder of her price after she is appraised. So whatever befalls the woman of freedom or servitude applies likewise to her child.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Ahmad ibn Ziyad, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man upon whom death is approaching, and he has slaves belonging exclusively to himself and slaves in partnership with another man. Then he states in his bequest: 'My slaves are free, except my slaves who are in partnership.' So he عليه السلام wrote: 'They are to be appraised against him; if his wealth can bear it, then they are free.'

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Suwayd al-Qallāʾ, from Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: ʿAlqamah ibn Muḥammad made a bequest that I should free a slave on his behalf, so I freed a woman on his behalf. Will that suffice for him, or should I free one on his behalf from my own wealth? He said: It suffices him. Then he said: Fāṭimah, the mother of my son, made a bequest that I should free a slave on her behalf, so I freed a woman on her behalf.

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who died and made a bequest that hajj be performed on his behalf. He said: “If he was a ṣarūrah, hajj is to be performed on his behalf from the middle of the wealth; and if he was not a ṣarūrah, then from one-third.”

And he said: Regarding a woman who bequeathed wealth for emancipation, hajj, and charity, but it was insufficient, he said: “Begin with hajj, for it is obligatory. Then if anything remains, assign a portion to charity and a portion to emancipation.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who bequeathed thirty dinars so that a man from among our companions might be emancipated with it, but none was found for that amount. He عليه السلام said: "A person should be purchased from among the people and then emancipated."
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from him that he said: Then let them purchase from the general people, so long as he is not a Naṣibī.

And Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from the Shaykh — meaning Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar — from his father عليه السلام, that he said: Indeed, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام died and left sixty owned slaves, so he freed one-third of them; then I cast lots among them and freed the one-third.

Al-Qasim Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام about a freed woman whom my brother had emancipated. She used to serve the maidservants and was among his dependents, and he instructed me to spend on her in a moderate manner. So he said: “If she remains with the maidservants and continues attending to them, then spend on her and follow his bequest.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made a bequest that a slave be freed on his behalf from one-third of his estate with five hundred dirhams. Then the executor bought a slave for less than five hundred dirhams, and an excess remained. What do you say regarding the excess? He عليه السلام said: “It is to be given to the slave before he is freed, then he is freed on behalf of the deceased.”

Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a mukatab who had a free woman as his wife, and she made a bequest for him at the time of her death. He said: 'The heirs are not to allow her bequest for him, for he is a mukatab who has not been freed.' Then he عليه السلام ruled that he would inherit in proportion to the amount of him that had been freed, and that the bequest would be valid for him in proportion to the amount of him that had been freed. And he عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukatab for whom a bequest had been made, and he had paid half of what was due from him, that half of the bequest was valid for him. And he ruled regarding a mukatab who had paid a quarter of what was due from him, and a bequest had been made for him, that a quarter of the bequest was valid for him. And he عليه السلام said concerning a man who made a bequest for his female mukatabah, and she had paid one-sixth of what was due from her, that he validated it for her in proportion to the amount of her that had been freed.

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Ubaydah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had an Umm al-Walad (a slave woman who bore her master a child) and from him) and he had a son from her. When death approached him, he bequeathed for her two thousand dirhams or more, and instructed the heirs to enslave her. He (the Imam) said: 'No, rather she should be freed from one-third of the deceased's estate and given what he had bequeathed for her.'

5508 - And it was narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī, who said: I copied from a book in the handwriting of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A certain person, your mawla, passed away. A son of his brother died, and he left behind an umm walad belonging to him who had no child. He bequeathed to her one thousand dirhams. Is the bequest valid, and does emancipation take effect upon her? What is her status? Your opinion in that matter—may my soul be your ransom. So he عليه السلام wrote: She is freed from the one-third, and the bequest belongs to her.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abu Jamilah, from al-Ridha عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed a sword to another man, and it was in a sheath and had adornment upon it. The heirs said to him, "Only the blade belongs to you, and the sword does not belong to you." So he said, "No; rather, the sword with what is in it belongs to him." He said: I said to him, a man bequeathed a صندوق to another man, and there was wealth in it. The heirs said, "Only the صندوق belongs to you, and the wealth does not belong to you." So he said, "The صندوق with what is in it belongs to him."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who said, “This ship belongs to so-and-so,” and he did not specify what was in it, while there was food in it. Is the man to be given the ship and what is in it? He عليه السلام said: “It belongs to the one for whom it was bequeathed, unless its owner excluded what was in it. The heirs have no share in it.”

Zur‘ah narrated from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked him about a man who died and left sons and daughters, young and old, without any bequest, and he had servants, slaves, and jewelry. How should the heirs divide that inheritance? He said: "If a trustworthy man undertakes the division of all that among them, then there is no harm."

5512 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a man between whom and me was kinship, who died and left young children, and left male and female slaves, and did not leave a bequest. So what do you see regarding one who buys from them a slave-girl and takes her as an umm walad? And what do you see regarding their sale? So he said: “If they have a guardian who undertakes their affairs, sells on their behalf, and looks after them, he is rewarded concerning them.” I said: “Then what do you see regarding one who buys from them a slave-girl and takes her as an umm walad?” He said: “There is no harm in that if the custodian responsible for them, looking to what benefits them, sells on their behalf. And they have no right to go back on what the custodian responsible for them, looking to what benefits them, has done.”

Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said: If a man entered Islam, acknowledged it, and then drank alcohol, committed adultery, and consumed usury, while nothing of the halal and haram had yet become clear to him, I would not carry out the legal punishment upon him if he was ignorant, unless proof were established against him that he had recited the surah in which adultery, alcohol, and consuming usury are mentioned. If he was ignorant of that, I would teach him and inform him. Then if he committed it after that, I would flog him and carry out the legal punishment upon him.

And in the narration of ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who attributed it upward: That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought al-Najāshī al-Ḥārithī, the poet, who had drunk wine in the month of Ramaḍān. So he struck him with eighty lashes, then detained him for a night. Then he called for him the next day and struck him with twenty lashes. He said, "O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, you struck me with eighty lashes for drinking wine, so what are these twenty?" He said, "This is for your audacity in drinking wine in the month of Ramaḍān."
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Do not sit with those who drink wine, for when the curse descends, it encompasses whoever is in the gathering.

5091 - And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: “If a wine drinker falls ill, do not visit him; if he dies, do not attend him; if he gives testimony, do not validate him; and if he proposes to you, do not marry him off. For whoever marries his daughter to a wine drinker, it is as though he has led her to zina. And whoever marries his daughter to one who opposes him in his religion has severed her kinship. And whoever entrusts a wine drinker, there shall be no guarantee for him with Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.”

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Five things from five are impossible: honor from a transgressor is impossible, compassion from an enemy is impossible, sincere advice from a jealous person is impossible, loyalty from a woman is impossible, and awe from a poor person is impossible.

Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "So avoid the filth of idols and avoid false speech." He عليه السلام said: "The filth of idols is chess, and false speech is singing, and backgammon is more severe than chess. As for chess, adopting it is kufr, playing it is shirk, teaching it is a grave destructive sin, greeting one who is occupied with it is disobedience, and turning it over is like turning over the flesh of swine, and looking at it is like looking at the private part of one's mother. The one who plays backgammon as gambling is like one who eats the flesh of swine, and the example of the one who plays it without gambling is like one who puts his hand in the flesh of swine or in its blood. And it is not permissible to play with rings, the fourteen, and all that and their likes are gambling, even the play of children with walnuts is gambling. Beware of striking the small stones together, for indeed Shayṭān runs with you and the angels flee from you. And whoever has a ṭunbūr remaining in his house for forty mornings, then he has incurred wrath from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

5094 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: Indeed, the angels withdraw at betting and curse its participant, except in the case of the hoof, the padded foot, the feather, and the arrowhead. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله raced with Usamah ibn Zayd and held horse races.

It has been narrated: “That the she-camel of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was outrun, so he عليه السلام said:” “It transgressed and said: ‘Upon me is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.’ And it is a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that nothing transgresses against anything except that Allah abases it. And if a mountain were to transgress against a mountain, Allah would surely bring down the transgressing one of them.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, forbade inciting animals against one another, except dogs.
A man asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام about purchasing a bondwoman who had a voice, so he said: There is no harm upon you if you buy her and she reminds you of Paradise.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the executor of 'Ali ibn al-Sari, who said: I said to Abū al-Hasan عليه السلام: 'Indeed, 'Ali ibn al-Sari has died and appointed me as his executor.' So he said: 'May Allah have mercy on him.' I said: 'And indeed his son Ja'far committed an act with an umm walad belonging to him, so he ordered me to exclude him from the inheritance.' He said to me: 'Exclude him, if you are truthful, for an affliction will strike him.' He said: So I returned, and he brought me before Abū Yūsuf the judge. He said to him, 'May Allah rectify you, I am Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn al-Sari, and this is my father's executor, so order him to hand over to me my inheritance from my father.' He said to me, 'What do you say?' So I said, 'Yes, this is Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn al-Sari, and I am the executor of 'Ali ibn al-Sari.' He said, 'Then hand over his wealth to him.' I said to him, 'I wish to speak to you.' He said, 'Come near me.' So I came near, where no one could hear my speech, and I said to him, 'This one committed an act with his father's umm walad, so his father ordered me and enjoined upon me that I exclude him from the inheritance and not let him inherit anything.' Then I came to Mūsā ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام in al-Madinah, informed him, and asked him; so he ordered me to exclude him from the inheritance and not let him inherit anything. Then he said, 'By Allah, Abū al-Hasan ordered you?' I said, 'Yes.' Then he made me swear three times, then said to me, 'Carry out what he ordered you; the word is his word.' The executor said: Then affliction struck him after that. Abū Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' said: I saw him after that.

And the confirmation of that is what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Muhtadī, from Saʿīd ibn Saʿd, who said: I asked him—meaning Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام—about a man who had a son whom he claimed, then he disowned him and excluded him from the inheritance, while I am his executor, so what should I do? So he عليه السلام said: “The child remains binding upon him because of his acknowledgment in public view. The executor must not withhold him from anything that he already knows [to be established].”

Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Hisham, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The end of an orphan’s state of orphanhood is puberty, and that is his full strength. But if he reaches puberty and no sound maturity is perceived in him, and he is foolish or weak, then his guardian should withhold his wealth from him.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muthannā ibn Rāshid, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about an orphan who had read the Qur'an, whose intellect had no defect, and who had wealth in the custody of a man. The one holding the wealth wanted to use it productively until he reached puberty and then hand over his wealth to him. He عليه السلام said: “Even if he reaches puberty, if he does not have sound intellect, nothing should ever be handed over to him.”

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: When the boy reaches his full strength at thirteen years and enters his fourteenth year, whatever is obligatory upon those who have reached puberty becomes obligatory upon him, whether he experiences a wet dream or not. His evil deeds are recorded against him, and his good deeds are recorded for him. Everything becomes valid for him except if he is weak-minded or foolish.

5520 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the orphan girl: when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: "When you know that she neither corrupts nor wastes it." So I asked him: if she has married? He said: "When she marries, the authority of the guardian over her has ended." The author of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: By that he means when she reaches nine years of age.
Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A girl is not to be consummated with until nine years, or ten, come for her.

Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: When a girl reaches nine years of age, her wealth is handed over to her, her decisions regarding her wealth become valid, and the full legal punishments are applied for her and upon her.

And it has been narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then deliver their wealth to them. He said: "Perceiving sound judgment means safeguarding wealth."

And in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. That he said concerning the interpretation of this verse: If you see them loving the family of Muhammad عليهم السلام, then raise them one degree.

Hadith 5527 — Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zakariya ibn Abi Yahya al-Sa'di, from al-Hakam ibn Utaibah, who said: We were at the door of Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, while we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said: “Which of you is Abu Ja'far?” The people said to her: “What do you want from him?” She said: “I want to ask him about an issue.” They said to her: “This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.” She said: “My husband died and left one thousand dirhams, and he owed me a debt from my dowry of five hundred dirhams. So I took my dowry and I took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed that my husband owed him one thousand dirhams, and I testified for him.” Al-Hakam said: While I was calculating, Abu Ja'far عليه السلام came out and said: “What is this by which I see you moving your fingers, O Hakam?” I said: “This woman mentioned that her husband died and left one thousand dirhams, and that he owed her five hundred dirhams from her dowry. So she took from it her dowry, and she took from it her inheritance. Then a man came and claimed against him one thousand dirhams, and she testified for him.” Al-Hakam said: By Allah, I had not completed the speech before he said: “She has admitted to two-thirds of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her.” Al-Hakam said: By Allah, I have never seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far عليه السلام. Ibn Abi Umayr said: The explanation of that is that there is no inheritance until the debt is paid. He only left one thousand dirhams, while he owed one thousand five hundred dirhams in debt, to her and to the man. So she gets one-third of the thousand because she is owed five hundred dirhams, and the man gets its two-thirds because he is owed one thousand dirhams.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who freed his slave at the time of his death while he had a debt upon him He عليه السلام said: “If his value is equal to what is due upon him, and equal to it again, his emancipation is valid; otherwise, it is not valid.”

In the narration of Aban ibn Uthman, it is reported that a man asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had appointed an executor, stating that he had a debt upon him. He said: "The man should pay what is due from his debt and divide what remains among the heirs." I said: "Should the executor distribute what was bequeathed for the debt? From whom should the debt be taken: from the heirs or from the executor?" He said: "It is not taken from the heirs, but the executor is responsible for it."

It is narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said: A servant continues to steal until, when the value of what he has stolen reaches the blood money of his hand, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, exposes him.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: The thief is not to have his hand cut off during a year of drought.

And in the narration of Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, that ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought, in al-Kūfah, a man who had stolen a pigeon, so he did not cut off his hand, and he said: “I do not cut off for birds.”
Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered cutting in the case of an iron helmet and a shield whose weight was thirty-eight ratls.

5102 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who came to another man and said, “So-and-so sent me to you so that you may send to him such-and-such,” so he gave it to him and believed him. Then he met his companion and said to him, “Indeed, your messenger came to me, so I sent with him to you such-and-such and such-and-such.” He said, “I did not send him to you, nor did anyone bring me anything.” Then the messenger claimed that he had indeed sent him and that he had delivered it to him. He said: “If he finds proof against him that he never sent him, his hand is cut off. But if he does not find proof against him, then his oath is by Allah that he did not send him, and the other recovers the property from the messenger.” I said, “Then if he claims that need drove him to that?” He said, “His hand is cut off, because he stole the man’s property.”

And it is narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said: The thief is not to be cut off until he confesses to the theft twice. فإذا he retracts, he is liable for the stolen property, and he is not cut off if he has no witnesses against him.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Every place that is entered without permission, and a thief steals from it, then there is no cutting off upon him."

Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a child who steals. He said: “If he is seven years old or younger, it is lifted from him. If he repeats it after seven, his fingertip is cut off or scraped until it bleeds. If he repeats it, then what is below his fingertip is cut from him. If he repeats it after that, and he has reached nine years of age, his hand is cut off. And no prescribed limit from the limits of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to be neglected.”

A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and confessed to theft. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?” He said: “Yes, Sūrat al-Baqarah.” So he said: “I have granted your hand for the sake of Sūrat al-Baqarah.” Then al-Ashʿath said: “Are you suspending one of the limits of Allah, Exalted is He?” He said: “And what do you know of what this is?” When the evidence is established, it is not for the Imam to pardon; but when the man confesses against himself, then that belongs to the Imam: if he wills, he pardons, and if he wills, he cuts.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “There is no cutting for stealing fruit, nor kathar; and kathar is al-jummar.”

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a group who slaughtered a camel and ate it. They were examined as to which of them had slaughtered it, and they testified against themselves that they had all slaughtered it together, without singling out one person over another. So he ruled that their right hands be cut off.

And Yūnus narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man stole from the war spoils an amount for which cutting off the hand would become obligatory. He عليه السلام said: It is to be considered how much his share is. If what he took was less than his portion, he is to be disciplined and the remainder of his property is to be given to him. If he took the like of what belonged to him, then there is nothing upon him. And if he took an excess equal to the price of a shield, and that is a quarter of a dīnār, his hand is cut off.

And Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who rented a donkey and came to the cloth merchants, bought a garment from them, and left the donkey with them. He عليه السلام said: “The donkey is to be returned to its owners, and the one who went off with the garment is to be pursued. But there is no cutting upon him; rather, it is betrayal.”

5111 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, when a man stole for the first time, would cut off his right hand. If he returned to it, he would cut off his left foot. If he returned a third time, he would confine him permanently in prison and spend on him from the public treasury.”
And it has been narrated: "If he steals in prison, he is to be executed."
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about the minimum amount for which the thief is to be cut off. He said: "A quarter of a dinar."
And in another report: "One-fifth of a dinar."

Hadith 5115 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Concerning a man who stole, so his right hand was cut off; then he stole again, so his left foot was cut off; then he stole a third time, he said: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would confine him permanently in prison and would say: ‘Indeed I am ashamed before my Lord to leave him without a hand with which he cleans himself and without a foot with which he walks to his need.’” He said: “And when he cut the hand, he cut it below the joint; and when he cut the foot, he cut it from the ankle.” He said: “And he did not hold that anything from the hudud should be remitted.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: When the legal punishment is carried out on a thief, he is exiled to another town. If a man steals and is not apprehended until he steals another time, then is seized, and the evidence comes and they testify against him concerning the first theft and the last theft, then his hand is cut off for the first theft, and his foot is not cut off for the last theft, because the witnesses testified against him together in a single proceeding regarding the first theft and the last theft before his hand had been cut off for the first theft. But if the witnesses testified against him for the first theft and his hand was cut off, then afterward they testified against him for the last theft, his left foot would be cut off.

5117 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “There is no cutting for open and public theft, which is snatching, but I would discipline him with taʿzīr. However, the one who takes and conceals is to have the cutting applied.” There is no cutting for one who snatches clothes, and there is no cutting for the pickpocket if he picks from the outer garment. But if he picks from the inner garment, then cutting applies to him. There is also no cutting for a hired worker or a guest, because both are entrusted. And it has been narrated that if a guest hosts another guest and he steals, he is cut. If a paralyzed person steals, his right hand is cut in every case, whether it is paralyzed or sound. If he returns and steals again, his left foot is cut. If he returns again, he is kept permanently in prison, provision is made for him from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims, and he is restrained from the people. That was narrated by al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb from al-ʿAlāʾ from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Zurārah from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام. And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb also narrated it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. And there is no cutting for the slave if he steals from the property of his master, because it is the man’s property: one part of him has stolen from another part.
The grave robber, if he is known for doing that, is to have his hand cut off.
And it has been narrated: That ʿAlī عليه السلام cut off the grave-robber, so it was said to him, “Do you cut off for the dead?” He said, “Indeed, we cut for our dead just as we cut for our living.”

And it has been narrated: That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a grave robber. So he took him by his hair and struck him against the ground, then said, "Step on him, O servants of Allah." So he was trampled until he died.

5121 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “The punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is only that they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be exiled from the land.” He said: “If he kills and does not wage war and does not take wealth, he is killed. If he wages war and kills, he is killed and crucified. If he wages war and takes wealth but does not kill, his hand and foot are cut off. And if he wages war but does not kill and does not take wealth, he is exiled.”

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The crucified person is taken down from the wooden structure after three days, washed, and buried. It is not permissible for his crucifixion to remain for more than three days.

And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام: Indeed, ʿAli عليه السلام crucified a man in al-Hirah for three days, then took him down on the fourth day, prayed over him, and buried him.
And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ḍurays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Whoever carries a weapon at night is a muharib, unless he is a man who is not among the people of suspicion.

And Safwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Ṭalḥah al-Nahdī, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man leaves his house intending the mosque or intending some need, and another man meets him or confronts him, then strikes him and takes his garment. He said: “What do the people where you are say about it?” He said: I said: “They say: this is open violent aggression, and the muḥārib is only in villages of the polytheists.” So he said: “Which of the two is greater in sanctity: the abode of Islam or the abode of shirk?” He said: So I said: “The abode of Islam.” He said: “These are among the people meant by this verse: ‘The only recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger’” to the end of the verse.

And it was narrated from Ṭarīf ibn Sinān al-Thawrī, who said: I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام about a man who stole a free woman and sold her, so he said: There are four legal punishments in it. As for the first of them: he is a thief, so his hand is cut off. The second: if he had intercourse with her, he is flogged with the legal punishment. And upon the one who bought her, if he had intercourse with her while knowing, then if he was muḥṣan, he is stoned, and if he was not muḥṣan, he is flogged with the legal punishment. And if he did not know, then there is nothing upon him, nor upon her. And if he forced her, then there is nothing upon her. And if she consented to him, she is flogged with the legal punishment.

Hadith 5127 — Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Hilāl narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: “Inform me about the thief: why is his right hand and his left foot cut off, and not his right hand and his right foot?” He said: “How excellent is what you have asked. If his right hand and his right foot were cut off, he would fall onto his left side and would not be able to stand. But if his right hand and his left foot are cut off, he remains balanced and stands upright.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, how can he stand when his foot has been cut off?” He said: “The cutting is not from where you think it is cut. Rather, the foot is cut from the ankle, and part of his foot is left for him upon which he may stand, perform salat (prayer), and worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” I said: “Then from where is the hand cut?” He said: “The four fingers are cut off, and the thumb is left for him, so that he may rely upon it in salat (prayer) and wash his face with it for salat (prayer).”
And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who stole a cluster of dates from an orchard, its value being two dirhams, he said: “The hand is cut off for it.”

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a male slave confesses against himself once before the Imam that he stole, he is to have his hand cut off; and if a female slave confesses against herself before the Imam to theft, she is to have her hand cut off.

5130 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated that from Abu Ayyub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: “If a slave confesses against himself to theft, he is not to have his hand cut off; but if two witnesses testify against him, his hand is cut off.”

Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: A woman is not to be appointed as the executor entrusted with a bequest, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And do not give the weak-minded your wealth.

And in another report: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "And do not give the foolish your wealth." He عليه السلام said: "Do not give it to a drinker of wine, nor to women." Then he عليه السلام said: "And what foolish person is more foolish than a drinker of wine?"

ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: I said to him: A man bequeathed to another man a bequest from his wealth, a third or a fourth, then the man is killed by mistake, meaning the testator. So he said: "This bequest is to be carried out for him from his wealth and from his blood money (diyyah)."

And in another report: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth, and then was killed by mistake. He عليه السلام said: "One-third of his blood money is included in his bequest."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Asimi narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mathanna ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام. He was asked about a man who appointed another man as guardian over his children and wealth belonging to them, and at the time of the bequest gave him permission to conduct business with the wealth, with the profit being between him and them. So he said: There is no harm in it, because their father had given him permission for that while he was alive.

5539 - Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Khālid al-Ṭawīl, who said: My father called me when death approached him and said: “O my son, take charge of your younger brothers’ wealth, invest it, take half of the profit, and give them the other half; and there is no liability upon you.” Then, after my father’s death, my father’s umm walad brought me before Ibn Abī Laylā and said: “This man is consuming the wealth of my children.” He said: So I related to him what my father had instructed me to do. Ibn Abī Laylā said: “If your father instructed you with something invalid, I will not permit it.” Then Ibn Abī Laylā had me affirm that if I put it into use, then I would be liable for it. Then afterward I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and related my story to him. Then I said to him: “What do you think?” He said: “As for the statement of Ibn Abī Laylā, I cannot overturn it; but as for what is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is no liability upon you.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who acknowledged a debt in favor of one of his heirs while he was ill. He said: "It is permissible if that which he acknowledged is less than one-third."
Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man acknowledges a debt owed by him to an heir. He said: "It is permissible if he is solvent."

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who bequeathed to some of his heirs that he owed him a debt. He said: “If the deceased was acceptable/reliable, then give him that which he bequeathed for him.”

Hadith 5543 — And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Ibn Miskān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, the seller of al-Sābirī cloth, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who entrusted a man with some wealth. When death approached her, she said to him: “The wealth which I gave to you belongs to so-and-so,” and then the woman died. Then her heirs came to the man and said: “Our relative had wealth, and we only consider it to be with you, so swear to us that you have nothing belonging to her.” Should he swear to them? He عليه السلام said: “If she was regarded as trustworthy by him, then he should swear. But if she was under suspicion, then he should not swear, and he should leave the matter upon what it was. Indeed, she only has a right to one-third of her wealth.”

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind a slave, and one of his children testified that their father had freed him, he said: 'His testimony is accepted, and he is not held financially responsible, and the slave must work to compensate the share that belonged to the other heirs.'

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah and Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who died, and some of his heirs acknowledged a debt to a man, he عليه السلام said: “That is binding upon him in his share.”
And in another hadith: If two of the heirs testify, and they are both just, that is accepted against the heirs. But if they are not just, then that is binding only in their own shares.

Hadith 5548 — Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and others, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “Abu Ja'far عليه السلام freed the worst of his servants at the time of his death and kept the best of them. So I said to him: ‘O my father, you free these and keep these?’ He said: ‘They have received beating from me, so this is in exchange for that.’”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام fell ill three times, and in each illness he would make a bequest; then when he recovered, he carried out his bequest.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about what people say regarding the bequest of one-third and one-fourth at the time of his death: is it something correct and well-known, or how did your father do? He said: “One-third — that is what my father عليه السلام did.”

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Salma, the servant of the children of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah عليه السلام when death approached him, and he lost consciousness. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Give al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn," and he was al-Aftas, "seventy dinars." I said: "Would you give to a man who attacked you with a blade?" He said: "Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious:" And those who join that which Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام): “My father was overtaken by death, so I said to him, ‘Make a will.’ He said, ‘This is my son’—meaning Umar—‘whatever he does is valid.’” So Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: “Your father has indeed made a will, and he was concise.” He said: I said, “He instructed and made a bequest for you of such-and-such.” He said: “Approve it.” I said: “He made a bequest for a believing, knowledgeable slave, but when we emancipated her, it became clear that she was not of proper lineage.” He said: “It has sufficed for him. The likeness of that is only like a man who bought a sacrificial animal thinking it was fat, then found it thin; it has still sufficed for him.”

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mālik, who said: I wrote to him, meaning ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, about a man who died and had assigned everything in his lifetime to you, while he had no child. Then afterward he came to have a child, and the amount of his wealth is three thousand dirhams. I have sent to you one thousand dirhams, so if you see fit, may Allah make me your ransom, inform me of your view so that I may act by it. So he عليه السلام wrote: “Release it to them.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, who said: I wrote to ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: A man set aside something from his wealth for you—may Allah make me your ransom—then he came to need it. Should he take it for himself, or send it to you? So he said: He has the choice in that so long as he has not removed it from his hand. And if it reached us, we would consider consoling and assisting him with it, since he has come to need it. He said: And I wrote to him: A man bequeathed to you—may Allah make me your ransom—some specified part of his wealth, and he also made a bequest to his relatives from his father's and mother's side. Then he changed the will, depriving those whom he had given and giving to those whom he had deprived. Is that permissible for him? So he wrote عليه السلام: He has the choice in all of that until death comes to him.

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said: I asked al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام about a man who bequeathed one-third of his estate after his death and said: “My one-third after my death is to be divided among my male and female mawālī.” While his father also had mawālī, are his father’s mawālī included in his bequest on the basis that they are called his mawālī, or are they not included? So he عليه السلام wrote: “They are not included.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Muhammad, who said: Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan, meaning Ali ibn Muhammad عليه السلام. A Jew died and left a bequest concerning something for his creditors, which I am able to take. Is it permissible for me to take it and hand it over to your followers, or should I carry it out regarding what the Jew had bequeathed? So he عليه السلام wrote: "Send it to me and inform me of it, so that I may carry it out in the proper manner, if Allah, the Exalted, wills."

Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission, saying: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said regarding a man who acknowledged at the time of his death and said to so-and-so and so-and-so: one of the two has one thousand dirhams owed by me; then he died in that state. So he عليه السلام said: Whichever of the two establishes the proof, then the money belongs to him. If neither of them establishes the proof, then the money is between them in two equal halves.

And ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Aḥmad ibn Ḥamzah, who said: I said to him: Indeed, in our town, wealth is sometimes bequeathed to the family of Muḥammad, so they bring it to me, and I dislike bringing it to you until I seek your permission. So he said: “Do not bring it to me, and do not involve yourself with it.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man bequeathed thirty dīnārs to the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. He said: Then the man brought it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Give it to a certain elder from the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام,” and he was burdened with dependents and of limited means. The man said to him: “The man only bequeathed it to the descendants of Fāṭimah.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It does not make a real difference among the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, whereas it does make a difference for this man, and he has dependents.”

Hadith 5560 — Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man appointed me as his executor, and I asked him to include with me a relative of his, so he did. And the one who appointed me mentioned that he had against the one whom he included with me in the executorship one hundred and fifty dirhams, and with him as collateral for it was a silver cup. Then when the man died, the executor began claiming that he had against him loads of wheat. He عليه السلام said: If he establishes proof, otherwise he has no right to anything. He said: I said to him: Is it permissible for him to take anything from what is in his hand? He said: It is not permissible for him. I said: What do you think—if a man wronged him and took his property, and he was able to take from his property the like of what he took, would that be permissible for him? So he said: Indeed, this is not like that.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥabīb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had dinars with me and who was ill. He said to me, “If something happens to me, then give so-and-so twenty dinars, and give my sister the remainder of the dinars.” Then he died, and I did not witness his death. Then a truthful Muslim man came to me and said, “He instructed me to tell you: Look to the dinars which I ordered you to pay to my sister, and give ten dinars from them in charity; distribute them among the Muslims.” And his sister did not know that I had anything with me. So he عليه السلام said: “I view that you should give ten dinars from it in charity, as he said.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mehran, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "The bequest is for the parents and the near relatives, in a fair manner, a duty upon the Godwary." He عليه السلام said: "It is something that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned for the صاحب of this أمر." I said: "Is there a limit for that?" He said: "Yes." He said: I said: "And what is it?" He said: "The least that it may be is one-third of one-third."

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, from al-Fuḍayl, the mawlā of Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had four of the great angels witness his bequest to ʿAlī عليه السلام: Jabrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl, and another whose name I did not retain.

Hadith 5564: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Samāʿah, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man from your followers died and left behind young children, and he left some property, but he also owed a debt of which the creditors are unaware. If it is paid to his creditors, his children will remain with nothing. So he said: Spend it on his children.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: I asked him about a man who designates his owned slave for posthumous emancipation. Does he have the right to go back on it? He said: "Yes, it is like a bequest."

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ziyād ibn Abī al-Ḥallāl, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: did he make a bequest to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام along with Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام? He said: "Yes." I said: "While they were at that age?" He said: "Yes, and this would not be for anyone other than those two at less than five years."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali, peace be upon him. Regarding endowments and what has been narrated about them from his forefathers, peace be upon them. So he, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: Endowments are to be according to how their owners designate them, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Abī al-Ḥusayn, who said: I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: I have endowed a piece of land for my children, for hajj, and for charitable causes, and you have a right in it after me, and for those after you; but I have removed it from that course. So he said: “You are absolved, and it has been made expansive for you.”

And ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated, saying: I said to him: Some of your followers have narrated from your forefathers, peace be upon them: "Every endowment fixed to a known term is binding upon the heirs, and every endowment to an unspecified term is ignorance, unknown, invalid, and returned to the heirs." And you are more knowledgeable of the saying of your forefathers, peace be upon you and them. So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "It is like that according to me."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-ʿUbaydi, from ʿAli ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, who said: I wrote to him: May I be your sacrifice, I have no child, and I have estates which I inherited from my father, and some of them I acquired myself. I do not feel secure from unforeseen events. If I do not have a child and something happens to me, then what do you think, may I be your sacrifice: should I dedicate some of them as a waqf for the poor among my brothers and the weak, or should I sell them and give their price in charity to them during my lifetime? For I fear that the endowment may not be carried out after my death. If I endow them during my lifetime, may I eat from them during the days of my life, or not? So he wrote, peace be upon him: I have understood your letter regarding your estates. It is not for you to eat from them, nor from the charity. If you eat from them, it will not be carried out, if you have heirs. So sell, and give some of their price in charity during your lifetime. If you give in charity, keep for yourself what sustains you, like what Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام did.

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated, saying: Aḥmad ibn Ḥamzah wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. A mudabbar was made waqf, then his owner died while a debt was upon him that his wealth could not cover. So he عليه السلام wrote: "Its endowment is to be sold for the debt."

Hadith 5572 — Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, who said: I wrote to him, peace be upon him, about a deceased person who had made a bequest that what remained of his one-third be spent on a man, but he did not instruct that his entire one-third be executed. Does the executor have the right to make the deceased’s one-third into an endowment because of this ongoing expenditure? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “His one-third is to be carried out, and it is not to be made into an endowment.”

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who endows an estate, then it appears to him that he should alter something in that. He said: If he endowed it for a child or for others, then appointed a caretaker for it, he has no right to revoke it. If they were minors and he stipulated its guardianship for them until they reached maturity, so that he would hold it on their behalf, then he has no right to revoke it. But if they were adults and he did not deliver it to them, and they did not dispute with him until they took possession of it from him, then he may revoke it, because they do not take possession of it from him while they have already reached maturity.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar al-Baghdādī, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Nawfalī, who said: I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام asking him about a land that my grandfather had endowed for the needy among the descendants of so-and-so ibn so-and-so, the man who gathers the tribe, while they are many and scattered through the lands. And among the descendants of the one who made the endowment there is severe need, so they asked me to single them out for it, to the exclusion of the rest of the descendants of the man who gathers the tribe. So he عليه السلام replied: You mentioned the land which your grandfather endowed for the poor among the descendants of so-and-so. It belongs to those who are present in the town in which the endowment is, and it is not for you to seek out one who is absent.

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan, peace be upon him, and said: "May I be your ransom, I purchased a piece of land next to mine for one thousand dirhams. When I gathered the money, I was informed that the land was a waqf." So he said: "The purchase of waqf property is not permissible, and do not mix its yield with your wealth. Give it to those for whom it was endowed." I said: "I do not know any rightful owner for it." He said: "Give its yield in charity."

5577 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Ḥanān, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who endowed the yield of his property for relatives of his from his father's side and relatives from his mother's side, and he made a bequest from that yield for a man and his descendants—between whom and him there was no kinship—of three hundred dirhams every year, and the remainder was to be divided among his relatives from his father and mother. He said: “It is permissible for the one for whom he made that bequest.” I said: “What do you think if only five hundred dirhams come out from the yield of the land that he endowed?” He said: “Is it not in his bequest that the one for whom he made the bequest should be given from the yield three hundred dirhams, and the remainder be divided among his relatives from his father and mother?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “His relatives have no right to take anything from the yield until they fully give the one bequeathed to three hundred dirhams. Then whatever remains after that is theirs.” I said: “What if the one for whom the bequest was made dies?” He said: “If he dies, the three hundred dirhams belong to his heirs; they inherit it so long as any one of them remains. Then when his heirs come to an end and none of them remains, the three hundred dirhams belong to the relatives of the deceased, returned to what comes forth from the endowment, then divided among them; they inherit that so long as any one of them remains and the yield remains.” I said: “Do the heirs from the relatives of the deceased have the right to sell the land if they need it and what comes from the yield is not enough for them?” He said: “Yes, if all of them agree and the sale is better for them, they may sell.”

Al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Mihrān ibn Muḥammad, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: He instructed that mourning be held for him for seven seasons, and he endowed wealth for each season to be spent in it.

And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “Shall I not tell you about the will of Fāṭimah عليها السلام?” I said: “Yes.” Then he brought out a box or a basket, and took out from it a document and read it: “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. This is what Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed. She bequeathed her seven orchards: al-‘Awāf, al-Dalāl, al-Burqah, al-Mīthab, al-Ḥusnā, al-Ṣāfiyah, and the property of Umm Ibrāhīm to ‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام. If ‘Alī passes away, then to al-Ḥasan; if al-Ḥasan passes away, then to al-Ḥusayn; and if al-Ḥusayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children. Allah is witness over that, and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī and al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwām.” And it was written by: “‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام.”

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim wrote to him in the year two hundred and thirty-three, asking him about a man who died and left behind a wife, sons, and daughters, and left for them a غلام whom he had endowed for them for ten years; then he would be free after the ten years. He asked: Is it permissible for these heirs to sell this غلام while they are in need, if it is as I have described to you? May Allah make me your ransom. So he, peace be upon him, wrote: They are not to sell him until the appointed time of his condition, unless they are compelled to do so; then it is permissible for them.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I was present with Ibn Abī Laylā when he gave judgment concerning a man who had assigned the yield of his house to one of his relatives without setting a time limit. Then the man died, and his heirs came before Ibn Abī Laylā, and the relative for whom the yield of the house had been assigned was also present. So Ibn Abī Laylā said: “I think that I should leave it as its owner left it.” Then Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafī said: “Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام had judged in this mosque contrary to what you have judged.” He said: “And what knowledge do you have of that?” He said: “I heard Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام saying:” “ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled by returning the ḥabīs and carrying out the inheritances.” So Ibn Abī Laylā said: “Do you have this in a book?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then send for it and bring it to me.” Muḥammad ibn Muslim said to him: “On the condition that you do not look in the book except at that hadith.” He said: “You have that.” He said: “So he brought the book and showed him the hadith from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام in the book, and he retracted his judgment.”

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Juʿfī, who said: I used to go repeatedly to Ibn Abī Laylā regarding inheritances belonging to us so that he might divide them, and there was a ḥabīs in it, so he kept putting me off. When that became prolonged, I complained about him to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. So he said: “Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered the return of the ḥabīs and the execution of the inheritances?” He said: So I went to him, and he acted as he had been acting. Then I said to him: “I complained about you to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he said to me such-and-such and such-and-such.” He said: Ibn Abī Laylā then made me swear that he had indeed said that, so I swore to him, and he judged for me accordingly.

Ya'qub ibn Zayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi Kahmas, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Six things reach the believer after his death: a child who seeks forgiveness for him, a mushaf that he leaves behind, a planting that he plants, a well that he digs, a charity that he sets in motion, and a sunnah that is acted upon after him.
And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who gives a shared charity, he said: “It is permissible.”

And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who gave charity to his children who had reached maturity, he said: 'If they do not take possession of it before he dies, then it becomes inheritance. But if he gives charity to those among his children who have not reached maturity, it is permissible, because the parent is the one who manages their affairs.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'One should not take back the charity once it has been given sincerely for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

5586 - And in the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, he said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who gave charity to his son in the form of wealth or a house: does he have the right to return to it? He said: "Yes, unless he is a minor."

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Al-Ḥakam, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “My father gave me a house in charity, then it occurred to him to take it back, while our judges rule for me regarding it.” So he said: “Excellent is what your judges ruled by, and evil is what your father did. Charity is only for Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so whatever is made for Allah, there is no return in it for him. If you dispute with him, then do not raise your voice over him, and if he raises his voice, then lower your voice.” He said: I said to him, “He has indeed passed away.” He said: “Then be at ease with it.”

Rubayʿ ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام gave as charity his house that was in al-Madīnah among Banī Zurayq, and he wrote: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. This is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib gave in charity while he was alive and sound: he gave his house in Banī Zurayq as a charity that is neither to be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited. Until Allah, Who inherits the heavens and the earth, inherits it. And he settled his maternal aunts in this charity for as long as they lived and their descendants remained; then when they pass away, it shall belong to the needy among the Muslims. Allah has witnessed.

Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “My mother gave me her share in a house as charity. So I said to her: ‘The judges do not approve this, but write it as a sale.’ She said: ‘Do from that whatever appears proper to you, and whatever you see to be permissible for you.’ So I secured it accordingly. Then some of the heirs wanted to make me swear that I had paid this price, while I had not paid her anything. So what do you think? He عليه السلام said: “Swear to him.”

Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who gives part of his house in charity to a stranger, then dies. He said: “That should be appraised at its value, then its price should be paid to him.”
Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Whoever gives a charity, and inheritance returns it to him, then it belongs to him.”
And in the narration of al-Sakuni: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to reject a gift in a will, and whatever one acknowledged at the time of his death without proof and without evidence, he rejected it.

Hadith 5593 — Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام made this charity-endowment: “This is what Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام has given as charity. He gave in charity all of his land in such-and-such a place, and the boundary of the land is such-and-such. He gave all of it in charity, together with its palm trees, its land, its canal, its water, its mills, its rights, its watering share from the water, and every right belonging to it in elevation or exposure, width or length, utility, open area, watercourses, branches, runoff, cultivated or uncultivated land.
