He gave all his rights in that as charity for his direct offspring among men and women. Its administrator shall distribute what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings forth of its yield, in the amount sufficient for its upkeep and its utilities; after thirty date-clusters, he shall distribute among the needy of the village and among the children of so-and-so.” “For the male is the like of the share of two females.” If a woman from the daughters of so-and-so marries, then she has no right from this charity-endowment until she returns to it without a husband. If she returns, then she shall have the like of the share of one of the daughters of so-and-so who did not marry. And whoever dies among the children of so-and-so and has a child, then his child has his father’s share. “For the male is the like of the share of two females.” According to what so-and-so stipulated among his direct offspring. And whoever dies among the children of so-and-so and leaves no child behind, his right is returned to the people of the charity-endowment. And the children of my daughters have no right in this charity-endowment unless their fathers are from my offspring. And no one has any right in my charity-endowment along with my children, the children of my children, and their descendants so long as any of them remain. If they pass away and none of them remain, that shall be divided among the children of my father through my mother, so long as any of them remain, according to the like of what I stipulated among my children and my descendants. Then when the children of my father through my mother pass away and none of them remain, my charity-endowment is for the children of my father and their descendants, so long as

Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir narrated from Abū al-Ṣaḥārī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man bought a house, and an empty plot remained, so he built on it a revenue-generating house. Should he endow it for the mosque? He said: Indeed, the Magians endowed property for the fire temple.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Husayn ibn Nu'aym, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who granted the residence of his house to another man for the days of his life, or made it for him and his descendants after him. He said: "It is for him and for his descendants according to what he stipulated." I said: "If he needs to sell it, may he sell it?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Does his sale of the house invalidate the right of residence?" He said: "The sale does not invalidate the right of residence. Thus did I hear my father عليه السلام say, Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: 'The sale does not invalidate the lease nor the residence, but he sells it on the condition that the one who buys it does not take ownership of what he bought until the residence ends according to what was stipulated, and likewise the lease.'" I said: "If he returns to the tenant his money and all that he incurred in maintenance and repair regarding what he rented?" He said: "If it is with good pleasure of the soul and the tenant's consent to that, there is no harm."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Khālid ibn Nāfiʿ al-Bajalī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who granted another man residence in a house belonging to him for the duration of his life, meaning the life of the owner of the house. Then the one who granted the residence died, while the one to whom the residence had been granted remained alive. Do you think that if the heirs want to remove him from the house, they have that right? He said: "I hold that the house should be appraised with a fair valuation, and the deceased's one-third should be examined. If in his one-third there is that which covers the value of the house, then the heirs have no right to remove him. But if the one-third does not cover the value of the house, then they have the right to remove him." It was said to him: "Do you think that if the man to whom the residence was granted dies after the death of the owner of the house, the residence would belong to the descendants of the one to whom the residence was granted?" He said: "No."

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from his father, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who allowed another man to reside in his house for the duration of his life. He said: “It is valid for him, and he has no right to evict him.” I said: “And for him and his descendants?” He said: “It is valid for him.” And I asked him about a man who allowed another man to reside [in his house] and did not set any time for him. He said: “The owner of the house may evict him whenever he wishes.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Ḥumrān, who said: I asked him about al-suknā and al-ʿumrā. He said: “People are held to their conditions in this matter. If he stipulated it for his lifetime, then it is for his lifetime. And if it was for his descendants, then it is for his descendants as stipulated until they perish; then it is returned to the owner of the house.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about al-suknā and al-ʿumrā, and he said: “If he assigned the residential right during his lifetime, then it is according to the condition he stipulated. And if he assigned it to him and to his descendants after him until his descendants come to an end, then they have no right to sell the house, nor to pass it on by inheritance. Then the house returns to its first owner.”

Sama'ah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “Indeed, the One who counted the sand of ʿĀlij knows that the shares do not undergo ʿawl beyond six; if they were to perceive their proper aspects, they would not exceed six.”

Saif ibn Umayrah narrated from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say: Indeed, the One who counted the sand of Alij surely knows that the inheritance shares do not undergo 'awl from six.

5602 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said: My father narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: Al-Zuhrī narrated to me from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah, who said: I sat with Ibn ʿAbbās, and the mention of the obligatory shares of inheritance was presented before me. Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent! Do you think that the One who counted the sands of ʿĀlij in number made in one estate a half, a half, and a third? These two halves have already taken the estate, so where is the place of the third?” Then Zufar ibn Aws al-Baṣrī said to him: “O Ibn ʿAbbās, who was the first to apply ʿawl to the shares?” He said: “Rumaʿ, when the shares became intertwined before him and some of them pressed against others.” He said: “By Allah, I do not know which of you Allah has given precedence and which of you Allah has deferred, and I do not find anything broader than to divide this wealth among you according to the shares, and to enter upon every entitled person whatever enters upon him from the ʿawl of the prescribed share. By Allah, if the one whom Allah has given precedence were given precedence, and the one whom Allah has deferred were deferred, no prescribed share would undergo ʿawl.” Then Zufar ibn Aws said to him: “Which of them did Allah give precedence to, and which did He defer?” He said: “Every prescribed share which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not lowered from one prescribed share except to another prescribed share, that is what Allah has given precedence. As for what Allah has deferred, it is every prescribed share which, when it departs from its appointed share, has nothing except what remains; that is the one Allah has deferred. As for those Allah gave precedence to: the husband has a half, then if something enters upon him that removes him from it, he returns to a quarter, and nothing removes him from that. The wife has a quarter, then if she is removed from it, she becomes entitled to an eighth, and nothing removes her from that. The mother has a third, then if she is removed from it, she becomes entitled to a sixth, and nothing removes her from that. These are the prescribed shares that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave precedence to. As for those Allah deferred, the prescribed share of daughters and sisters is a half

5603 - Al-Faḍl said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Walīd al-ʿAdanī, the companion of Sufyān, narrated, saying: Abū al-Qāsim al-Kūfī, the companion of Abū Yūsuf, narrated to me from Abū Yūsuf, who said: Layth ibn Abī Sulaym narrated to us from Abū ʿAmr al-ʿAbdī, from Ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, that he used to say: "The obligatory shares are out of six portions: two-thirds are four portions, one-half is three portions, one-third is two portions, one-fourth is one and a half portions, and one-eighth is three-quarters of a portion. None inherits along with the child except the two parents, the husband, and the wife. Nothing prevents the mother from one-third except the child and the siblings. The husband is not increased above one-half, nor reduced from one-fourth. The wife is not increased above one-fourth, nor reduced from one-eighth. If they are four or fewer than that, then they are equal in it. The maternal siblings are not increased above one-third, nor reduced from one-sixth, and in that the male and the female are equal. Nothing prevents them from one-third except the child and the father. The blood money is divided among those who have secured the inheritance."

Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: The shares of inheritance came to be six portions and do not exceed that because the human being was created from six things, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And indeed, We created man from an extract of clay. the verse. And another reason is that the people of inheritance who inherit permanently and are never excluded are six: the two parents, the son, the daughter, the husband, and the wife.

If a man leaves behind a son and does not leave a wife or parents, then the entire estate belongs to the son. Likewise, if there are two or more than that, then the estate is divided equally among them. Likewise, if he leaves a daughter and does not leave a husband or parents, then the entire estate belongs to the daughter, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned the estate to the child, and He did not designate for the daughter the half except along with the parents. Likewise, if they are two daughters or more, then the entire estate belongs to them equally. If he leaves a daughter, a son's daughter, and a son's son, and there is no spouse and no parents, then the entire estate belongs to the daughter. The children of the child inherit nothing alongside the direct child, because whoever is connected by himself is more entitled and worthier to the estate than one connected through another, and whoever is nearer to the deceased by one degree of descent is more entitled to the estate than one who is further away by a degree of descent. If he leaves a son and a daughter, or sons and daughters, then the entire estate belongs to them, with the male receiving the like of the share of two females, when there is no spouse and no parents with them. If he leaves a daughter, a brother, a sister, and a grandfather, then the entire estate belongs to the daughter. No one inherits along with the daughter except the son, the spouse, and the parents. Likewise, no one inherits along with a male child except the spouse and the parents, according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned in His Book.

Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: ʿAlī عليه السلام inherited from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله his knowledge, and Fāṭimah عليها السلام inherited his estate.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Hannat, from al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام say: No, by Allah, neither al-'Abbas nor 'Ali عليه السلام inherited from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and none inherited from him except Fatimah عليها السلام. And 'Ali عليه السلام only took the weapons and other things because he settled his debt on his behalf. Then he عليه السلام said: And blood relatives are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.

And it is narrated from al-Bazantī, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام: “May I be sacrificed for you, a man died and left behind his daughter and his paternal uncle.” So he said: “The wealth belongs to the daughter.” He said: And I said to him, “A man died and left behind a daughter of his and a brother,” or he said, “his brother’s son.” He said: He remained silent for a long time, then said: “The wealth belongs to the daughter.”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a neighbor of mine who died and left daughters, so he said: "The wealth belongs to them."

5609 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a man who died and left behind his daughter and his full sister, he عليه السلام said: "The wealth belongs to the daughter, and the sister from the father and mother has no share at all."

Al-Bazanti wrote to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام concerning a man who died and left behind his daughter and his brother. He said: “Give the wealth to the daughter if you do not fear anything from her paternal uncle.”

Mu'awiyah ibn Hukaym narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Zayd, from Mushma'il, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a woman who died and left her husband, and she had no heir besides him. He said: "If there is no one besides him, then the property belongs to him; and the woman has one-fourth, and whatever remains belongs to the Imam."

5613 - That which Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a woman who died and left her husband, he عليه السلام said: “So all the wealth belongs to him.” I said: “A man dies and leaves his wife?” He عليه السلام said: “The wealth belongs to her.”

If a woman leaves behind her husband and her two parents, then the husband receives one-half, the mother receives a complete one-third, and whatever remains belongs to the father, which is one-sixth. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “But if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third.” So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigned the mother a complete one-third when he has neither child nor siblings. Al-Faḍl said: Among the proofs that she has one-third of the entire estate is that all those who oppose us did not say that she has one-sixth in this prescribed share. Rather, they said that the mother has one-third of what remains, and one-third of what remains is one-sixth. They wished not to oppose the wording of the Book, so they affirmed the wording of the Book but opposed its ruling; and that is obfuscation and opposition to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to His Book. Likewise, in the inheritance of the wife together with the two parents, the wife has one-fourth, the mother has one-third, and whatever remains belongs to the father, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has specified in this prescribed share and in the one before it the husband’s half, the wife’s quarter, and the mother’s third, and He did not specify anything for the father. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only said: “and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third”; and He assigned to the father whatever remains after the allotted shares are taken. The father only inherits what remains after the allotted shares are taken.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام read to me the scroll of obligations of inheritance, which was dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and written in the hand of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام. So I read in it: “A woman died and left behind her husband and her two parents; for the husband is one-half, three shares; for the mother is one-third, two shares; and for the father is one-sixth, one share.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Jamil, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man died and left behind his wife and his two parents. He said: For his wife is one-fourth, for the mother is one-third, and whatever remains is for the father. If a woman leaves her husband and her mother, then for the husband is one-half, and whatever remains is for the mother. If she leaves her husband and her father, then for the husband is one-half, and whatever remains is for the father.

If a man leaves a full brother from the same father and mother, then the entire estate belongs to him. Likewise, if there are two full brothers or more than that, the estate is divided equally among them. If he leaves a full sister, then she has one-half by explicit designation, and the remainder is returned to her because she is the nearest of kin and one possessing an assigned share. Likewise, if he leaves two full sisters or more, they have two-thirds by explicit designation, and the remainder is returned to them by the share of the kindred. If they are full brothers and sisters, then the estate is divided among them, with the male receiving the portion of two females. Likewise, paternal brothers and sisters take the place of full brothers and sisters in every case when there are no full brothers and sisters. So if he leaves a full brother and a paternal brother, the entire estate belongs to the full brother from the father and mother, and the paternal brother is excluded. Paternal siblings, male or female, inherit nothing alongside full siblings, male or female. So if he leaves a full brother and a paternal sister, the entire estate belongs to the full brother from the father and mother. Likewise, if he leaves a full sister and a paternal brother, the entire estate belongs to the full sister from the father and mother: she has one-half by explicit designation, and what remains belongs to the nearest of kin, and she is the nearest of kin.

Due to the saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: “The full siblings from the same mother are more entitled to inheritance than the half-siblings from different mothers.” If the deceased leaves full sisters, paternal sisters, and a paternal nephew, then the full sisters receive two-thirds, and the remainder is returned to them, because they are the closer relatives. If he leaves a paternal brother and a nephew from both parents, then the entire estate belongs to the paternal brother, because he is nearer in degree. If he leaves a full brother and a maternal brother, the maternal brother receives one-sixth, and the remainder belongs to the full brother. If he leaves full brothers and sisters together with a maternal sister, the maternal sister receives one-sixth, and the remainder is divided among the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females. If he leaves a full sister and a maternal brother or sister, then the maternal sibling receives one-sixth, and the full sister takes the remainder. If he leaves two maternal brothers or two maternal sisters, or more than that, along with full siblings, then the maternal siblings receive one-third equally among themselves, and the remainder belongs to the full siblings. A maternal sibling, whether male or female, if only one, receives one-sixth; if they are more than one, whether male or female, they receive one-third. They are not increased beyond one-third, nor reduced below one-sixth when there is only one. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then each one of the two shall have a sixth; but if they are more than that, they are partners in one-third.” If he leaves a paternal brother, a maternal brother, and a full brother, then the maternal brother receives one-sixth, the remainder belongs to the full brother, and the paternal brother is excluded. If he leaves maternal siblings, full siblings, and paternal siblings, then the maternal siblings receive one-third, with male and female equal in that share, and the remainder belongs to the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females, and the paternal siblings are excluded. If he leaves a maternal sister, a full sister, and a paternal sister, the maternal sister receives one-sixth, the remainder belongs to the full sister, and the pater

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A woman died and left behind her husband, her maternal brothers, and her paternal brothers. He said: The husband has one-half, which is three shares. The maternal brothers have one-third, in which the male and the female are equal. One share remains, and it belongs to the paternal brothers and sisters. For the male is the like of the share of two females. .

5644 - And in the narration of Yūnus, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, he said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Regarding six brothers and a grandfather, he said: “The grandfather receives one-seventh.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the prescribed inheritance share of the grandfather. He said: “I do not know anyone among the people who spoke about it except by personal opinion, except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, for he spoke about it according to the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

Yahya ibn Abi Imran narrated from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The grandfather and grandmother from the father's side, and the grandfather and grandmother from the mother's side, all of them inherit.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله granted the paternal grandmother, the father’s mother, one-sixth while her son was alive; and he granted the maternal grandmother, the mother’s mother, one-sixth while her daughter was alive.

5627 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated, saying: Hammad ibn Uthman narrated to me from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah al-Basri, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: My daughter has died while my mother is still alive. Aban ibn Taghlib said: She has no share. So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Glory be to Allah! Give her a share, meaning one-sixth.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Saʿd ibn Abī Khalaf, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the daughters of a daughter and a grandfather, and he said: “The grandfather has one-sixth, and the remainder belongs to the daughters of the daughter.”

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله granted the grandmother one-sixth, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not prescribe anything for her.”

5630 - Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Abu Jamilah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Regarding two parents and a maternal grandmother, he said: “The mother receives one-sixth, the grandmother receives one-sixth, and what remains, which is two-thirds, belongs to the father.”

5631 - And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, who raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The grandmother has one-sixth along with her son and along with her daughter.

5632 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Concerning a man who died and left behind his wife, his sister, and his grandfather, he عليه السلام said: “This is divided into four shares: for the wife is one-fourth, for the sister is one share, and for the grandfather are two shares.”

Aban narrated from Bukayr and al-Halabi, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: The maternal siblings have one-third along with the grandfather, and he is a sharer with the paternal siblings.

5634 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who left his maternal brother and did not leave any heir other than him. He said: “The estate belongs to him.” I said: “What if there is a grandfather along with the maternal brother?” He said: “The maternal brother is given one-sixth, and the grandfather is given the remainder.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the maternal siblings along with the grandfather, and he said: “The prescribed share of the maternal siblings is one-third along with the grandfather.”

5636 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding the grandfather with maternal siblings, he said: "Indeed, in the Book of Ali عليه السلام, it is stated that the siblings from the mother inherit one-third along with the grandfather."
And Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a paternal brother and a grandfather. He said: "The property is equally between them."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Ali عليه السلام used to make the brother from the father's side inherit along with the grandfather, placing him in the same rank as him.

Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurarah, Bukayr, Muhammad ibn Muslim, al-Fuḍayl, and Burayd ibn Muawiyah, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them. The grandfather, together with the brothers from the father's side, is like one of the brothers.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who died and left behind his brother from the same father and mother and his grandfather. He عليه السلام said: “The property is divided between them, whether they are two brothers or a hundred. The grandfather is with them as one of them; the grandfather has the like of the share of one of the brothers.”

And Ḥammād narrated from Ḥarīz, from al-Fuḍayl or someone else, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the grandfather is a partner with the siblings, and his share is like the share of one of them, however many they may be, whether many or few.

And Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman from Isma'il al-Ju'fi who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: The grandfather shares the inheritance with the siblings, even if they were one hundred thousand.
Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man died and left six brothers and a grandfather. He said: “He is like one of them.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who left brothers and sisters from a father and mother, along with a grandfather. He said: The grandfather is like one of the brothers, and the estate is divided among them. For the male is the like of the share of two females.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a paternal cousin and a grandfather. He said: “The property belongs to the grandfather.”

Al-Bazanti narrated from Al-Muthanna, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A nephew and a grandfather. He said: The estate is between them in two equal halves.

5648 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Saʿd ibn Abī Khalaf, from one of the companions of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding daughters of a sister and a grandfather, He said: "The daughters of the sister receive one-third, and whatever remains belongs to the grandfather."
Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Abdullah ibn Numayr, from al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd. That Ali عليه السلام gave the grandmother the entire estate.
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said: Whoever wishes to plunge into the depths of Hell, then let him speak concerning the grandfather.

What Firas narrated from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام wrote to me concerning six brothers and a grandfather: “Consider him as one of them, and erase my letter.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding a man who left behind two maternal aunts and his freed slaves, he said: "Those who are related by blood are more entitled to one another." The wealth is to be divided between the two maternal aunts.

ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who dies and leaves behind his sister and his mawālī. He said: "The estate belongs to his sister." Whenever a man leaves a blood relative, whether male or female, such as a daughter of a sister, a daughter of a daughter, a daughter of a maternal uncle, a daughter of a maternal aunt, a daughter of a paternal uncle, a daughter of a paternal aunt, or anyone more remote than them, then all the estate belongs to the blood relatives, even if they are of lower degree. The mawālī do not inherit anything along with any one of them. Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned them, assigned for them, and informed that they have greater right in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And those related by blood are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah.” And He did not mention the mawālī.
And Jabir has narrated from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him: That Ali, peace be upon him, used to give to the blood relatives instead of the mawali.

And they narrated from Hanan, who said: I was sitting with Suwayd ibn Ghafalah when a man came to him and asked him about a daughter, a wife, and freed slaves. He said: I will inform you concerning it with the judgment of Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام: he assigned half to the daughter and one-eighth to the wife, and returned what remained to the daughter, and he gave nothing to the freed slaves.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Rahman, who said: I asked Aba Abd Allah عليه السلام about a group of people who drown in a ship, or a house falls upon them and they die, and it is not known which of them died before the other. He said: “Some of them inherit from others.”

5657 - And ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a woman and her husband upon whom a house collapsed, He عليه السلام said: “The woman is inherited from the man, then the man is inherited from the woman.”

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام ruled concerning a man and a woman upon whom a house collapsed and killed them, and it was not known which of them died before the other. So he said: Each one of them is made to inherit from his or her spouse according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed for their heirs.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a house that fell upon a group gathered together, and it was not known which of them died before the other. He said: “Some of them inherit from others.” I said: “Abū Ḥanīfah introduced another view into it.” He said: “And what did he introduce into it?” I said: “He said that if two men, one of whom had one hundred thousand and the other had nothing, were in a ship and drowned, and it was not known which of them died first, then the inheritance would go to the heirs of the one who had nothing, and the heirs of the one who had wealth would receive nothing.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “He has indeed heard it, and it is like this.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: Abū Ḥanīfah entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him: “What do you say about a house that collapsed upon a people, and two boys remained from them, one of them free and the other owned by his master, but it was not known which was the free one and which was the owned one?” Abū Ḥanīfah said: “Half of this one and half of that one should be freed, and the wealth should be divided equally between them in two halves.” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It is not like that. Rather, lots are to be cast between them, so whichever one the lot falls upon, he is the free one; and this one is freed and made a mawlā to him.”

Ḥarīz narrated from al-Fuḍayl, who said: Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about an infant that falls from his mother without crying out—does he inherit? He turned away from him, and when he repeated it to him, he said: “If he moves with clear movement, he is given inheritance, for he may perhaps have been mute.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Sawwar, from Al-Hasan, who said: Indeed, when Ali عليه السلام defeated Talhah and Al-Zubayr, the people came fleeing in defeat. They passed by a pregnant woman on the roadside, and she was frightened by them, so she cast out what was in her womb alive; then he convulsed until he died, and afterward the woman died. He said: Then Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام and his companions passed by her while she was lying there, and her child was on the road. He asked them about her case, and they said to him: She had been pregnant and was frightened when she saw the fighting and the defeat. So he asked them: Which of the two died before the other? They said: Her son died before her. He said: Then he summoned her husband, the father of the deceased boy, and made him inherit two-thirds of the diyyah from his son, and made his deceased mother inherit one-third of the diyyah. He said: Then he made the husband inherit from his deceased wife half of the diyyah which she had inherited from her deceased son, and he made the relatives of the deceased woman inherit the remainder. He said: Then he also made the husband inherit from the diyyah of the deceased woman half of the diyyah, which was two thousand five hundred dirhams, because she had no child other than the one whom she cast out when she was frightened; and he made the relatives of the deceased inherit the remainder. He said: Then all of that was paid from the treasury of Basra.

Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: He asked him about a boy being married to a girl: do they inherit from one another? He said: “If it was their parents who married them, then yes.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a man who marries his son to an orphan girl under his care, while his son is mature and the orphan girl is not yet mature, he said: “Her marriage is valid for his son. Then if he dies, her inheritance from him is set aside until she reaches maturity. When she reaches maturity, she is made to swear by Allah that nothing prompted her to take the inheritance except her acceptance of the marriage. Then the inheritance and half of the dowry are given to her.” He said: “But if she dies before reaching maturity and before the husband dies, the husband does not inherit from her, because she has the option regarding him once she reaches maturity, while he has no option regarding her.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A boy is ten years old, and his father marries him off while he is still young. Is his divorce valid while he is the son of ten years? He said: As for the marriage, it is valid. But as for his divorce, his wife should be withheld for him until he reaches maturity, and it is ascertained that he had indeed divorced. If he acknowledges that and ratifies it, then it is one irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor among the suitors. But if he denies that and refuses to ratify it, then she is his wife. I said: What if she dies or he dies? He said: The inheritance is to be withheld until whichever of the two remains reaches maturity. Then he is made to swear by Allah that nothing called him to take the inheritance except acceptance of the marriage, and the inheritance is handed over to him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad Al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who married during his illness. He said: “If he consummated the marriage with her and then died during his illness, she inherits from him. But if he did not consummate the marriage with her, she does not inherit from him, and his marriage is invalid.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man divorces a woman during his illness, she inherits from him so long as he remains in that illness, even if her ʿiddah has ended, unless he recovers from it. I said: What if the illness lasts a long time for him? He said: She inherits from him for up to one year.

And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man whom death approaches and he divorces his wife—whether his divorce is valid. He said: "Yes, and she inherits from him; but if she dies, he does not inherit from her."

Salih ibn Sa'id narrated from Yunus, from some of his companions, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him: What is the reason that when a man divorces his wife while he is ill, in a state of causing harm, she inherits from him but he does not inherit from her? He عليه السلام said: It is because of the harm. The meaning of harm here is his preventing her from her inheritance from him, so inheritance was imposed as a punishment.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who marries a woman and then dies before consummating the marriage with her. He عليه السلام said: She is entitled to the full inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period of four months and ten days. If he had specified a mahr, meaning a dowry, for her, then she is entitled to half of it; and if he had not specified a mahr for her, then there is no mahr for her.
And he, peace be upon him, said in another hadith: If he had consummated the marriage with her, then she is entitled to the full dowry.

Ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man married a woman according to her determination, then he died before she could determine it. He عليه السلام said: She has no dowry, but she inherits from him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibn Mihzam, from Talhah ibn Zayd, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "The hamīl is not given inheritance except with clear proof." He said: "The hamīl is one whom a woman brings while pregnant, having been taken captive while she was pregnant; then afterward his father or his brother recognizes him by that."

Safwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ḥamīl, and he said: “And what thing is the ḥamīl?” So I said: A woman is taken captive from her land, with her young child with her, and she says, “He is my son.” And a man is taken captive and meets his brother, and he says, “He is my brother.” They have no proof except their own statement. He said: “What do the people among you say about it?” I said: They do not allow him to inherit when they do not have proof of his birth; rather, his birth had occurred in shirk. He said: “Glory be to Allah! If she comes with her son, she has continued acknowledging him as such; and if he recognizes his brother, and that was in a state of soundness from both of them, then they have continued acknowledging that, and some of them inherit from others.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man from the Anṣār came to my father عليه السلام and said: 'I have been afflicted with a grave matter. I had a slave-girl with whom I used to have relations. I had relations with her one day, then went out for a need of mine after performing ghusl (ritual bath) from her. I forgot some provision of mine, so I returned home to take it, and found my غلام on her belly. Then I counted for her from that day of mine nine months, and she gave birth to a girl.' So he said: 'It is not fitting for you to approach her, nor to sell her. Rather, spend on her from your wealth as long as you remain alive; then instruct at your death that provision be spent on her from your wealth until Allah makes for you and for her an outlet.'

And it was narrated from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had a slave-girl with whom he had intimate relations, and she used to go out for his needs. Then she became pregnant, and he feared that the pregnancy might not be from him. What should he do? Should he sell the slave-girl and the child? So he said: He may sell the slave-girl, but he must not sell the child, and he does not make him inherit anything from his wealth.

And Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Sulaym, the freedman of Tirbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who used to have intimate relations with his maid and would send her out to fulfill his needs, and she became pregnant, and rumors of her misconduct reached him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: "Tell him: when she gives birth, keep the child and do not sell him, and allocate a share for him from your house." It was said to him: "What about a man who had intimate relations with his maid but did not send her out for errands, and he suspected her and she became pregnant?" He said: "When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and allocate a share for him from his house and wealth. This case is not like that one."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our companions wrote to Abū Ja'far al-Thānī عليه السلام through me, asking him about a man who committed fornication with a woman and she became pregnant. Then he married her after the pregnancy, and she gave birth to a child, and the child resembled him more than anyone in Allah's creation. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting and with his seal: “The child is of fornication and does not inherit.”

Yūnus narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him and said to him, ‘May I be your ransom, what is the blood money for the child of zinā?’ He said, ‘The one who spent on him is given what he spent on him.’ I said, ‘If he dies and has wealth, then who inherits him?’ He said, ‘The Imam.’ And it has also been narrated that the blood money for the child of zinā is eight hundred dirhams, and his inheritance is like the inheritance of the child of mulāʿanah.

5688 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who intentionally drank medicine while she was pregnant and did not inform her husband of that, so she miscarried her child. He said: “If it had a bone upon which flesh had grown, then upon her is a diyyah which she gives to its father. And if it was an ʿalaqah or a muḍghah, then upon her is forty dinars or a ghurrah, which she pays to its father.” So I said to him: “Then she does not inherit her child from his blood money along with his father?” He said: “No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit from him.”

5687 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who was killed, and he had one brother in Dār al-Hijrah and another brother in Dār al-Badw who had not migrated. I said: “If the migrant pardons, and the Bedouin wants to kill, does he have that right?” He said: “The Bedouin has no right to kill a migrant until he migrates; and if the migrant pardons, then his pardon is valid.” I said to him: “Does the Bedouin have any share of the inheritance?” He said: “As for the inheritance, it belongs to him, and he has his share from the blood money of his slain brother, if the blood money is taken.”

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who killed his father, He, peace be upon him, said: "He does not inherit from him. And if the killer has a son, the son inherits from the murdered grandfather."

And 'Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: If a man kills his mother by mistake, he inherits from her; and if he kills her intentionally, he does not inherit from her.

Al-Naḍr narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A woman is entitled to a share of the blood money of her husband, and a man is entitled to a share of the blood money of his wife, so long as neither of them has killed the other.

5686 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning the blood money of a slain person that it is inherited by the heirs according to the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and according to their prescribed shares, if the slain person has no debt upon him, except that the maternal brothers and sisters do not inherit anything from his blood money.”

Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, and she miscarried a stillborn fetus. Then the woman’s husband sought legal redress against him. So the woman said to her husband: 'If there is a blood money compensation for this miscarried fetus, and I have an inheritance share in it, then my share in it is for my father.' He said: 'What she gifted to her father is permissible for him.'

Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad عليه السلام about two groups among the believers, one of them rebellious and the other just, who fought one another. Then a man from the people of Iraq killed his father, or his son, or his brother, or his close relative, while he was from the people of rebellion and was his heir. I asked: “Does he inherit from him?” He said: “Yes, because he killed him rightfully.”

5698 - Muhammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Mufaḍḍal, from Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the son of al-mulāʿanah, who inherits from him? He عليه السلام said: “His mother inherits from him.” I said: “What do you say if his mother dies, and he inherits from her, then he dies—who inherits from him?” He عليه السلام said: “The agnatic relatives of his mother inherit from him, and he inherits from his maternal uncles.”

And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the mula'anah in which her husband accuses her, disowns her child, and performs li'an with her, then afterward her husband says, 'The child is my child,' and declares himself to have been lying. He said: 'As for the woman, she never returns to him. As for the child, I assign him back to him if he acknowledges him, and I do not leave his child with no inheritance. The son inherits from the father, but the father does not inherit from the son. His inheritance goes to his maternal uncles. And if anyone calls him a child of zina, he is flogged with the hadd punishment.'

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The inheritance of the child of mulāʿanah belongs to his mother. If his mother is not alive, then it goes to the closest people from his mother’s side, his maternal uncles.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: The child of mulāʿanah is inherited by his mother with one-third, and the remainder belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Aban and others, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the son of mula'anah that his mother inherits one-third of him, and the remainder belongs to the Imam, because liability for his offense rests upon the Imam.

Abū al-Jawzāʾ narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام: Regarding a man who accused his wife of adultery, then left, and when he came back the woman had died. He said: "He is given a choice between one of two options. It is said to him: if you wish, you bind the sin upon yourself, so the hadd is carried out on you and you are given the inheritance. And if you wish, you affirm it and perform liʿān with her nearest relative to her, and there is no inheritance for you."

Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Ali عليه السلام used to say: If the son of al-mulāʿanah dies and he has brothers, his estate is divided according to the shares ordained by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who performed li'an against his wife while she was pregnant and her pregnancy had clearly become apparent, and he denied what was in her womb. Then when she gave birth, he claimed the child, acknowledged him, and alleged that he was from him. So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "His child is returned to him, and he inherits from him, and he is not flogged, because the li'an has already passed."

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The son of liʿān is attributed to his mother, and all his matters and affairs belong entirely to her.
Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: In the case of the missing person, his wealth is held back for four years, then it is divided.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Jundub, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Hafs al-Aʿwar asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام while I was present, and he said: My father had a hired worker, and that worker had something with him. Then the worker died, leaving behind neither an heir nor any relatives, and I have become distressed over that; what should I do? He said: “The needy are your concern; the needy are your concern.” So I said: “May I be your ransom, I have indeed been troubled by that; what should I do?” He said: “It is like the way of your own wealth; if a claimant comes, you should give it to him.”

Ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Ḥammād, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked him about a man who died and left children, while some of them were absent and it was not known where he was. He said: "His inheritance is to be divided, and the absent one's share is to be set aside." I said: "Is zakat due on it?" He said: "No, not until he returns, takes possession of it, and a year passes over it." I said: "What if it is not known where he is?" He said: "If the heirs are financially well-off, they may divide his inheritance; then if he comes, they must return it to him."

And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who had a right against another man, then lost him and did not know where to seek him, and did not know whether he was alive or dead, and did not know any heir, lineage, or child for him, he عليه السلام said: "He should keep searching." He said: "That has gone on for a long time for him, so may he give it in charity?" He said: "He should keep searching."

5711 - And another report has also been narrated regarding this: “If you do not find an heir for him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, knows that you have made every effort, then give it in charity on his behalf.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad Al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who apostatized from Islam: to whom does his inheritance belong? He said: His inheritance is divided among his heirs according to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: If a Muslim man apostatizes from Islam, his wife becomes separated from him just as a woman becomes separated after a third divorce, and she observes the waiting period from him as a divorced woman observes it. If he returns to Islam and repents before she marries, then he is only a suitor, and there is no waiting period upon her for him; rather, the waiting period upon her is only for another man. If he is killed or dies before the completion of the waiting period, she observes from him the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died; thus she inherits from him during the waiting period, but he does not inherit from her if she dies while he is an apostate from Islam.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Whoever dies and has no heir from kinship, nor a master of emancipation who has guaranteed his liability, then his wealth is from the anfal.
And it has indeed been narrated in another report: Whoever dies and has no heir, then his wealth belongs to his hamshahrīj. Meaning, the people of his town.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a Muslim man who was killed and had a Christian father: to whom does his blood money belong? He عليه السلام said: “It is taken and placed in the treasury of the Muslims, because his liability is upon the treasury of the Muslims.”

Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "Who carries out the hudud: the ruler or the judge?" He said, "The implementation of the hudud belongs to the one to whom judgment belongs."

It has been narrated that two boys approached Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام holding two tablets in their hands, and they said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, judge between us.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Indeed, injustice in this is like injustice in legal rulings. Convey to your teacher on my behalf that if he strikes you more than three times, that will be retribution on the Day of Judgment.”

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Yūnus, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: Those guilty of all major sins, if the hadd punishment is carried out upon them twice, are killed on the third time.

And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Whoever we strike with a hadd from the limits of Allah and he dies, then there is no blood money upon us for him. And whoever we strike with a hadd from the limits of the people and he dies, then indeed his blood money is upon us.”

5140 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “My mother does not resist the hand of one who touches her.” He said: “Then confine her.” He said: “I have already done that.” He said: “Then prevent anyone from entering upon her.” He said: “I have already done that.” He said: “Then restrain her, for you do not honor her with anything better than preventing her from violating the prohibitions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: “The legal punishments that belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are not pardoned apart from the Imam. As for what is from the rights of people within a legal punishment, there is no harm in it being pardoned apart from the Imam.”

And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who said: to a woman, 'O adulteress,' and she replied, 'You are more adulterous than me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The legal punishment (hadd) is upon her for what she accused him of. As for her self-admission, she is not to be punished unless she confesses to that before the Imam four times.'

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "It is not permissible for a ruler who believes in Allah and the Last Day to administer more than ten lashes except in the case of a legal punishment (hadd)."

5144 - And in the narration of Ziyād ibn Marwān al-Qandī, from someone whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The thief is not subject to amputation in a year of deprivation for anything that is eaten, such as bread, meat, and cucumbers.

And it was narrated from Ādam ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī, who said: I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and a letter from Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to him regarding a man who had exhumed a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and had intercourse with her. The people here had differed before us: one group said, "Kill him," and another group said, "Burn him." So he عليه السلام wrote back to him: "The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living. His punishment is that his hand be cut off for his grave-exhumation and stripping of the clothes, and the hadd punishment for zina is to be carried out upon him. If he was muḥṣan, he is to be stoned, and if he was not muḥṣan, he is to be flogged one hundred lashes."
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Avert the prescribed punishments through doubts. There is no intercession, no guarantee, and no oath in a hadd case.”

And in the narration of Al-Sakuni, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him: That ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought a drinker, so he asked him to recite the Qur'an, and he recited it. Then he took his cloak and cast it among the cloaks of the people, then said to him, 'Pick out your cloak.' So he could not pick it out, and thus he administered the hadd punishment to him.

Abu Ayyub narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, in the Book of Ali عليه السلام it is stated that he would strike with the whip, with half the whip, and with part of it—that is, in the prescribed punishments—when a boy or a girl who had not yet reached maturity was brought, and he would not nullify any punishment from the punishments of Allah. So he was asked: How would he strike with part of it? He said: He would take the whip in his hand from its middle and strike with it, or from one-third of it and strike with it, according to their ages. In this way he would strike them with the whip and would not nullify any punishment from the punishments of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام addressed the people and said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has set boundaries, so do not transgress them; and He has made obligations binding, so do not diminish them. And He was silent about certain matters—not out of forgetfulness regarding them—so do not burden yourselves concerning them, as a mercy from Allah for you; so accept it.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Halal is clear, and haram is clear, and doubtful matters lie between that. So whoever leaves what is doubtful to him of sin, then he will be even more likely to leave what has become clear to him. And acts of disobedience are the sanctuary of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so whoever grazes around it is about to enter it.”

The followers of two different religions do not inherit from one another. A Muslim inherits from a disbeliever, but a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim. That is because the foundational ruling regarding the wealth of the polytheists is that it is fay' for the Muslims, and the Muslims have more right to it than the polytheists. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only forbade inheritance to the disbelievers as a punishment for their disbelief, just as He forbade it to the killer as a punishment for his killing. As for the Muslim, then for what crime and punishment should he be deprived of inheritance? And how could Islam make his condition worse, along with the saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
With the statement of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: "Islam increases and does not decrease."
And along with his saying, peace be upon him and his family: "There is no harm and no reciprocation of harm in Islam."
And with his statement, peace be upon him: "Islam prevails and is not prevailed over."

And it was narrated from Abī al-Aswad al-Duʾalī: That Muʿādh ibn Jabal was in Yemen, and people gathered around him and said: “A Jewish man has died and left behind a Muslim brother.” So Muʿādh said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله say: ‘Islam increases and does not diminish.’” Thus he allowed the Muslim to inherit from his Jewish brother.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Aʿyan from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a Christian who dies and has a Muslim son, He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has only increased us in honor through Islam; therefore, we inherit from them, and they do not inherit from us.”

Zur‘ah narrated from Samā‘ah from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the Muslim: does he inherit from the polytheist? He said: “Yes. As for the polytheist, he does not inherit from the Muslim.”

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aʿyan, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The people of two different religions do not inherit from one another. We inherit from them, but they do not inherit from us. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has only increased us in honor through Islam.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The Muslim bars the disbeliever and inherits from him, while the disbeliever does not bar the believer and does not inherit from him.”
5725 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad al-Hannat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: "A Muslim inherits from his dhimmi wife, while she does not inherit from him."

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz narrated from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, and a Muslim may inherit from a disbeliever, unless the Muslim has bequeathed something to the disbeliever in a will.

And 'Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام say: "A Jew and a Christian do not inherit from Muslims, while Muslims inherit from the Jew and the Christian."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a Muslim man who died and had a Christian mother, and he also had a wife and Muslim children. He said: “If his mother accepts Islam before his inheritance is divided, she is given one-sixth.” I said: “What if he has no wife, no child, and no Muslim heir who has an allotted share in the Book, while his mother is Christian and his relatives are Christians among those who would have a share in the Book if they were Muslim? For whom is his inheritance?” He said: “If his mother accepts Islam, then all of his inheritance belongs to her. If his mother does not accept Islam, but some of his relatives from among those who have a share in the Book accept Islam, then his inheritance belongs to that relative. If none of his relatives accepts Islam, then his inheritance belongs to the Imam.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan or Malik ibn Aʿyan, from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a Christian man who died, leaving a Muslim son of his brother and a Muslim son of his sister, while the Christian had children and a Christian wife. He said: I hold that his Muslim brother’s son should be given two-thirds of what he left, and his Muslim sister’s son should be given one-third of what he left, if he has no young children. But if he has young children, then the two heirs must spend on the minors from what they inherited from their father until they reach maturity. It was said to him: How should they spend on the minors? He said: The heir of the two-thirds share pays two-thirds of the maintenance, and the heir of the one-third share pays one-third of the maintenance. Then when they reach maturity, they stop the maintenance for them. It was said to him: What if his children embrace Islam while they are young? He said: What their father left should be delivered to the Imam until they reach maturity. If they remain upon Islam when they reach maturity, the Imam gives his inheritance to them. But if they do not remain upon Islam when they reach maturity, the Imam gives his inheritance to his Muslim brother’s son and his Muslim sister’s son: he gives two-thirds of what he left to his brother’s son and one-third of what he left to his sister’s son.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A Christian accepted Islam, then returned to Christianity, then died. He said: “His inheritance is for his Christian children.” And a Muslim became Christian, then died. He said: “His inheritance is for his Muslim children.”

Hanan ibn Sadir narrated from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A mawla of Ali عليه السلام died, so he said, 'Look and see whether you can find an heir for him.' It was said to him that he had two daughters in al-Yamamah who were enslaved. So he purchased them from the wealth of the deceased, then gave them the remainder of the inheritance.

Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام used to say regarding a free man who dies while he has a slave mother: "She should be purchased from the wealth of her son, then freed, then inheritance is effected for her."

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies and leaves behind an enslaved son. He said: "His son should be purchased from his wealth, then freed, and he will inherit whatever remains."

And in the narration of Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Ali عليه السلام, when a man died and had a slave woman as his wife, would purchase her from his wealth, then free her, and then grant her inheritance.

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning one who claimed the slave of a man and asserted that he was his son, that he is to be freed from the wealth of the one who claimed him. If the claimant dies and his wealth is divided before the slave is freed, then the wealth has preceded him; but if he is freed before his wealth is divided, then he has his share from it.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who had an umm walad, and her child from him died. Then he married her to another man, and she bore him a child. Then that man died, and she returned to her master. So does he have the right to be intimate with her before marrying her? He must not be intimate with her until she completes the waiting period for the deceased husband, which is four months and ten days. Then he may be intimate with her by ownership, without nikah. I said: What about her child from the husband? He said: If he left wealth, the child is to be purchased from it at the assessed value, then freed, and made to inherit. I said: If he left no wealth? He said: Then the child remains with his mother in the same condition as her.
Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The slave does not inherit, and the divorced person does not inherit.”

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus Buzurj, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “A free person and a slave do not inherit from one another.”

And ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the male slave and the female slave: do they bar others from inheritance when they themselves do not inherit? He said: “No.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A mukātab who purchased his freedom and left behind wealth valued at one hundred thousand dirhams, and he has no heir to inherit from him—who inherits him? He عليه السلام said: “The one who assumes responsibility for his liability inherits from him.” I said: “And who is the guarantor of his liability?” He عليه السلام said: “The one responsible for the liabilities of the Muslims.”

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man entered into a mukātabah contract with his slave and stipulated against him that his inheritance would belong to him. So that was referred to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and he invalidated his condition and said: "The condition of Allah comes before your condition."

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukātab who died while having wealth, and he said: His wealth is to be reckoned in proportion to the part of him that had been freed for his heirs, and in proportion to the part that had not been freed it is to be reckoned for his masters who made the contract with him, from his wealth.
And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The mukātab inherits and is inherited from according to the proportion of what he has paid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a mukatab who enters into a manumission contract, then pays part of his contract and dies, leaving a son and leaving wealth greater than what remains due of the contract, he عليه السلام said: His masters are to be paid what remains of his contract, and whatever remains thereafter belongs to his child.

The Magians inherit through blood relations, and they do not inherit through invalid marriage. So if a Magian man dies and leaves behind his mother, and she is his sister and she is his wife, then the estate belongs to her on account of her being a mother; and she has nothing on account of her being a sister and that she is a wife.

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Kūfī narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān al-Nakhaʿī, from his uncle al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Sālim, from his father, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: How did the inheritance come to be for the male is the like of the share of two females So he said: Because the grains that Ādam عليه السلام and Ḥawwāʾ ate in Paradise were eighteen grains. Ādam ate twelve grains of them, and Ḥawwāʾ ate six. Therefore the inheritance came to be for the male is the like of the share of two females .

And in the narration of al-Sakūnī: That ʿAlī عليه السلام used to give inheritance to the Magian, if he married his mother, his sister, or his daughter, from two aspects: from the aspect that she was his mother, and from the aspect that she was his wife.

Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Rabiʿ ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: When a man dies, his sword, his Qur'an, his ring, his books, his saddle, and his clothing belong to his eldest child. If the eldest is a daughter, then they belong to the eldest of the sons.

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When the deceased dies, then the sword, the saddle, and the clothes — the clothes of his person — belong to his eldest son.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān al-Aḥmar, from Muyassir, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about women: what share do they have of inheritance? He said: “They have the value of bricks, buildings, wood, and reeds; but as for land and properties, they have no inheritance in them.” He said: I said, “Then what about clothing?” He said: “The clothing is for them.” He said: I said, “How did this come to be, while they have an appointed one-eighth or one-fourth?” He said: “Because a woman has no lineage by which she inherits; rather, she is an entrant among them. This was made thus so that a woman does not marry and then her husband, or the children of other people, come and contend with a people regarding their properties.”

Al-Ridha عليه السلام wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan, in what he wrote as a reply to his questions: The reason a woman does not inherit anything from landed properties except the value of the bricks and demolition materials is that real estate cannot be altered or transformed. A woman may have what is between her and him severed from the bond, and she may be changed and replaced. A child and a parent are not like that, because it is not possible to separate oneself from them, whereas a woman may be replaced. So that which may come and go, its inheritance is in what may be substituted and altered, since it resembles them both; and that which is fixed and enduring in its state is for one who is like it in firmness and permanence.

And in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said: I heard him saying: Women do not inherit anything from real estate, but they are entitled to the value of buildings, trees, and palm trees.

Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The woman was only given the value of the wood and the bricks so that she would not marry and bring upon them someone who would corrupt their inheritances.

And in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Khaṭṭab Abu Muhammad al-Hamdani, from Ṭirbal, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said: Indeed, the woman does not inherit from what her husband leaves behind of villages, houses, weapons, and animals; and she inherits from wealth, slaves, clothing, and the household goods from what he leaves behind. Then he said: And the dismantled materials of trunks, reeds, and doors are appraised, and she is given her rightful share from it.

Abān narrated from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik or Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man: does he inherit his wife's house and her land, anything from the soil, or is he in that regard like the woman, so that he does not inherit anything from that? He said: He inherits from her, and she inherits from him, from everything that he leaves and that she leaves.
Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Udhayna. Regarding women: if they have a child, they are given from the landed property.

Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan regarding what he wrote in reply to his questions: "The reason women are given half of what men are given from inheritance is that when a woman marries, she receives, while the man gives; therefore, more has been allotted to men." And another reason for giving the male twice what is given to the female is that the female is among the dependents of the male if she is in need, and it is upon him to maintain her and upon him is her financial support. It is not upon the woman to maintain the man, nor is she charged with his expenses if he is in need. So more has been allotted to the man for that reason, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ۝ Men are maintainers of women because Allah has given some of them an advantage over others and because they spend from their wealth. ۝

And in the narration of Ḥamdān ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Walīd, from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān. He said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: For what reason did the inheritance become for the male, the like of the share of two females He said: Because of what Allah has assigned for her of the dowry.

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām that Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ said to Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal: Why does the weak woman have one share, while the strong and wealthy man has two shares? He said: I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “A woman has no ʿāqilah obligation, nor is maintenance upon her, nor jihad.” And he listed other things besides this, and this is upon the man; therefore two shares were assigned to him, and one share to her.

Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Ayyūb ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: “I have greater authority over every believer than his own self. Whoever leaves behind wealth, it belongs to the heir, and whoever leaves behind debt or dependents in need, then it comes to me and is upon me.”

And Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, from Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: “When the deceased dies during travel, do not conceal his death from his family, for it is a trust regarding the waiting period of his wife, so that she may observe it, and so that his inheritance may be divided among his family before one of them dies and his share is thereby lost.”

And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, established brotherhood between the souls in the realm of shadows two thousand years before He created the bodies. Then, when our Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt, peace be upon them, rises, he will give inheritance to the brother with whom brotherhood was established between them in the realm of shadows, and he will not give inheritance to the brother through birth.

Zur'ah narrated from Samā'ah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله stood at Minā when he had completed his rites during the Farewell Hajj and said: 'O people, listen to what I say to you and understand it, for I do not know; perhaps I shall not meet you in this place after this year of ours.'" Then he said: 'Which day is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This day.' He said: 'Then which month is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This month.' He said: 'Then which town is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This town.' He said: 'Then indeed your blood and your wealth are forbidden among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours in this month of yours in this land of yours, until the day you meet Him and He asks you about your deeds. Lo, have I conveyed?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'O Allah, bear witness.
