Lo, whoever has a trust with him, let him return it to the one who entrusted him with it, for indeed the blood of a Muslim man is not lawful for him, nor his wealth, except with the good pleasure of his own soul. So do not wrong yourselves, and do not return after me as disbelievers.'

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Manṣūr Buzurj, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Do not let one who is free-handed in shedding blood deceive you, for indeed he has, with Allah, a killer that does not die.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die?” He said: “The Fire.”

Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The believer remains in a state of latitude within his religion so long as he does not shed unlawful blood.” And he said: “The intentional killer of a believer is not granted success for repentance.”

Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: On the Day of qiyāmah, a man will come to another man and smear him with blood while the people are in the reckoning. He will say, “O servant of Allah, what do I have to do with you?” He will reply, “You helped against me on such-and-such a day with a word, so I was killed.”
And in the narration of Al-ʿAlāʾ from Al-Thumālī, he said: If a man were to strike another man with a whip, Allah would strike him with a whip of the Fire.

Jamil narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم cursed the one who commits an offense in al-Madinah or shelters an offender, I said, "And what is that offense?" He said, "Killing."

5157 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from more than one person, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: “Whoever assists against a believer with even half a word will come on the Day of Judgment with this written between his eyes: ‘Despairing of the mercy of Allah.’”

5158 - Abān narrated from Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm al-Ṣayqal, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: A scroll was found in the hilt of the sword of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and in it was written: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. Indeed, the most rebellious of people against Allah on the Day of Resurrection is one who kills someone other than his killer, strikes someone other than the one who struck him, and whoever takes as guardian other than his rightful guardians is a disbeliever in what Allah sent down upon Muḥammad. And whoever innovates a grave offense or gives shelter to an offender, Allah, Exalted is He, will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any compensation nor ransom. He said: Then he said, “Do you know what is meant by his saying, ‘whoever takes as guardian other than his rightful guardians’?” I said, “What does it mean?” He said, “It means the people of the religion.”

And it is narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "that whoever kills a soul without [its being for] a soul or corruption in the earth, it is as though he has killed all mankind" He said: "It is a valley in Jahannam; if he were to kill all mankind, he would be in it, and if he were to kill one soul, he would be in it."

And it has been narrated: “He will be placed in a spot in Hell to which the intensity of the punishment of its inhabitants reaches. If he had killed all the people, he would only enter that very place.” It was said: “Then if he killed another?” He said: “It will be doubled upon him.”

And Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed defending his wealth is a martyr.' He (the Imam) said: 'And he said: If it were me, I would have abandoned the wealth and not fought.'

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muḥassin ibn Aḥmad, from ʿĪsā al-Ḍaʿīf, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man has killed another man; what is his repentance?" He said: "He should surrender himself." I said: "He fears that they will kill him." He said: "Then let him give them the blood money." I said: "He fears that they will come to know of that." He said: "Then let him marry a woman among them." I said: "He fears that she might inform them of that." He said: "Then let him take the blood money, make it into small bundles, then watch the times of salat, and cast it into their house."
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: "Whoever intentionally kills himself will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever."

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Sa'id al-Azraq from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who kills a believing man, he said: "It will be said to him: Die whichever death you wish—if you wish, as a Jew; if you wish, as a Christian; and if you wish, as a Magian."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān and Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a believer who intentionally kills another believer: does he have repentance? So he said: "If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or due to some worldly cause, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If no one knew about it, he should go to the heirs of the slain person and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he must give them the blood money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons as repentance to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: The first matter concerning which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will judge on the Day of qiyamah is bloodshed. Then the two sons of Adam عليه السلام will be made to stand, and judgment will be made between them; then those after them among the people of bloodshed, until none of them remains from among the people. After that, the slain one will come with his killer, and his blood will gush upon his face, and he will say: You killed him; so he will not be able to conceal any statement from Allah.

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who intentionally killed another man's slave, he said: “He is made to pay his value and is given a severe beating.” And he said regarding a man who killed his own slave: “He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons; then repentance after that.”

And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā and Zurʿah narrated from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about one who intentionally kills a believer: does he have repentance? He said: "No, not until he pays his blood money to his family, frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, seeks forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repents to Him, and humbly implores; for I hope that repentance will be accepted from him if he does that." I said: "May I be your ransom, what if he does not have wealth by which he can pay his blood money?" He said: "He should ask the Muslims until he pays his blood money to his family."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Kulayb al-Asadi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who is killed in a sacred month: what is his blood money? He said: "It is a full blood money and one-third."

5170 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Ḥamzah, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was approached, and it was said: “O Messenger of Allah, there is a slain man in Juhaynah.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله stood up and went until he reached their mosque, and the people heard of it and came to him. Then he عليه السلام said: “Who killed this one?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, we do not know.” He said: “A slain man from among the Muslims, in the midst of the Muslims, and it is not known who killed him? By the One who sent me with the truth, if the people of the heaven and the people of the earth were to gather together, participate in the blood of a Muslim man, and approve of it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would cast them down upon their noses into the Fire.” Or he said: “upon their faces.”

5171 - Samāʿah asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. "And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell." He عليه السلام said: "Whoever kills a believer on account of his religion, that is the intentional killer about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in His Book: and He has prepared for him a great punishment." I said: "Then a man may have something occur between him and another man, so he strikes him with his sword and kills him." He عليه السلام said: "That is not the intentional killing which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, referred to."

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū al-Safātij, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell. He said: “If He requites him.”

And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād, from someone who mentioned it, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said: During the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, there was a truthful woman known as Umm Fattān. A man from the companions of ʿAlī عليه السلام came to her and greeted her, and found her distressed. He said to her, 'Why do I see you distressed?' She said, 'A bondwoman of mine—I buried her, but the earth cast her out twice.' He said: 'So I went in to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and informed him, and he said:' Indeed, the earth accepts the Jew and the Christian, so there is no reason for this except that she is being punished with the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' Then he said, 'Indeed, if some soil were taken from the grave of a Muslim man and cast upon her grave, it would settle.' He said: So I went to Umm Fattān and informed her. She took some soil from the grave of a Muslim man and it was cast upon her grave, and it settled. Then I asked about what she used to do, and they said: 'She was intensely attached to men, and whenever she gave birth, she would throw her child into the oven.'

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Saʿdān [Saʿdān, variant] from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There was, in the hilt of the sword of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, a scroll in which was written: The curse of Allah, the angels, and all people be upon the one who kills someone other than his killer, or strikes someone other than the one who struck him, or commits an offense, or shelters an offender. And disavowal of one’s lineage, even if slight, is kufr in Allah, the Magnificent.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has ruled regarding your blood differently from how He has ruled regarding your wealth. He ruled concerning your wealth that the proof is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made; and He ruled concerning your blood that the oath is upon the claimant and the proof is upon the one against whom the claim is made, so that the blood of a Muslim man may not be nullified.

Mansur ibn Yunus narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Isa ibn Musa, with Ibn Shubrumah beside him, asked me about a slain person found in the land of a people, with no one else there. So I said: The Ansar found a man in one of the irrigation channels of Khaybar. The Ansar said: 'The Jews killed our companion.' The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to them: 'Do you have evidence?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Will you then swear?' The Ansar said: 'How can we swear to what we did not see?' He said: 'Then the Jews shall swear.' The Ansar said: 'Will they swear concerning our companion?' He said: So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم paid his blood-money from his own side. Then Ibn Shubrumah said: 'What do you think, had the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم not paid it?' He said: I said: 'We do not speak concerning what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم has done by saying: had he not done it.' He said: So I said to him: 'Then upon whom is the qasamah?' He said: 'Upon the family of the slain person.'

Muḥammad ibn Sahl narrated from his father, from some of his shaykhs, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام was asked about a man who was sitting with a group of people and died while among them, or a man who was found in a tribe or at the house of some people, and they were accused regarding him. He said: There is no retaliation upon them, and his blood is not to be left unavenged; the blood money is upon them.

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Qasāmah was only instituted so that severity may be imposed thereby upon a man known for evil and under suspicion. If they testify against him, their testimony is accepted."

5179 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about al-qasamah: where did it begin? He said: “It was from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. After the conquest of Khaybar, a man from the Ansar lagged behind his companions. They returned to search for him and found him writhing in his blood, slain. The Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, the Jews killed our companion.’ He said: ‘Let fifty men from among you swear that they killed him.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, shall we swear to what we did not see?’ He said: ‘Then the Jews shall swear.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, who would believe the Jews?’ He said: ‘Then I shall pay for your companion.’” So I said to him: how is the ruling in it? He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ruled concerning bloodshed in a way that He has not ruled in anything from the rights of people, due to His magnifying blood. If a man claimed against another man ten thousand dirhams, less than that or more, the oath would not be upon the claimant; rather, the oath would be upon the one claimed against. But when a man claims blood against a people, alleging that they killed, then the oath is upon the claimant of blood before those claimed against. The claimant must bring fifty who swear that so-and-so killed so-and-so, then the one against whom the oath was sworn is delivered to them. If they wish, they pardon him; if they wish, they kill; and if they wish, they accept the blood money. If they do not swear, then those claimed against must have fifty men among them swear: ‘We did not kill him, nor did we know a killer for him.’ If they do that, the people of the village in which he was found must pay his blood money. And if he was in open land, his blood money is paid from the Bayt al-Mal. For Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام used to say: ‘The blood of a Muslim man is not to be left wasted.’”

Sama'ah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is found slain in a village or between two villages. He said: "The distance between them is measured, and whichever of the two is closer to him is held liable."

Zurarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Qasāmah was only instituted as a precaution for the people, so that if a wicked person wanted to kill a man or assassinate a man where no one could see him, he would fear that and refrain from killing.

Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: While the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was in one of his rooms, a man looked through a crack in the door. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had a combing stick in his hand and said: "If I were close to you, I would have gouged out your eye with it."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who looked in upon a group of people in order to see their private parts, and they struck him, killing him, wounding him, or gouging out his eye. So he said: There is no blood money for him. A man once peeped into the room of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله through an opening in it, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came to him with a broad arrowhead to gouge out his eye with it, but found that he had already gone away. Then he called out to him: 'O wicked one, had you remained for me, I would have gouged out your eye with it.'
Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAbdillah, peace be upon them, said: Whoever is killed through legal retribution (qisas), there is no blood money (diyyah) for him.
Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Whoever initiates aggression and is then retaliated against, there is no retribution for him.”
And al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who falls onto another man and kills him, he said: “There is nothing upon him.”

5187 - Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There were some children in the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام playing with their arrows. One of them threw his arrow and broke his companion’s front tooth. That was brought to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and the thrower established proof that he had said, ‘Beware!’ So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام waived qiṣāṣ from him, then said: The one who warned has excused himself.

And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say regarding a man who sought a woman for something unlawful against herself, and she struck him with a stone and hit a fatal spot on him. He said: There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if she is brought before a just Imam, he would declare his blood without liability.

Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: If any man attacks another man to strike him, and the latter defends himself and injures or kills the attacker, then there is nothing upon him.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who killed a mentally ill person. He عليه السلام said: "If he had intended him and he defended himself from him and killed him, then there is nothing upon him in the way of retaliation or blood money, and his heirs are to be given his blood money from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims." He عليه السلام said: "But if he killed him without the mentally ill person having intended him, then there is no retaliation for one from whom retaliation is not taken, and I hold that the killer must pay the blood money from his own property, giving it to the heirs of the mentally ill person, and he must seek forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and repent to Him."

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Muʿallā Abī ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whom an animal approached and wanted to trample, and he feared that from it, so he drove the animal away, and it bolted with its rider and threw him down, resulting in a wound or something else. He said: “There is no liability upon him; he only drove it away from himself, and it is al-jubār.”

5192 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "The privacy of the believer is forbidden to another believer." And he said: "Whoever spies upon a believer in his home, then his two eyes are lawful to the believer in that situation. And whoever storms upon a believer in his home without his permission, then his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation. And whoever denies the prophethood of a sent prophet and rejects him, then his blood is lawful." He said: So I said to him, "What is the condition of one who rejects the Imam from among you?" He said: "Whoever rejects an Imam has dissociated himself from Allah, and He is dissociated from him and from his religion. So he is a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, because the Imam is from Allah and his religion is the religion of Allah. And whoever dissociates himself from the religion of Allah, then he is a disbeliever, and his blood is lawful in that situation, unless he returns and repents to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from what he said." He said: "And whoever assaults a believer, intending his wealth and his life, then his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation."

And Ibn Faddal narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him: Regarding a man who falls upon another man and kills him, and the one on top dies, he said: “There is no liability upon the one below.”

Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was struck with a stick and was not released from it until he was killed. Should the killer be handed over to the heirs of the slain? He said: Yes, but he should not be left for them to abuse; rather, retribution should be carried out upon him.

Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: If a man strikes with an iron weapon, then that is intentional killing. He said: I asked him about accidental killing in which there are blood money and expiation: is it the case of a man striking another man without intending to kill him? He said: Yes. I said: Then if he throws something and it strikes a man? He said: That is the accidental killing about which there is no doubt, and upon him are expiation and blood money.

Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: In mistaken killing resembling intentional killing, such as when one is killed with a whip, a stone, or a stick, the diyyah for that is aggravated, and it is one hundred camels: among them forty pregnant camels, between a thaniyyah and a bāzil in its year, thirty hiqqahs, and thirty bint labūns. As for accidental killing, in it there are thirty hiqqahs, thirty bint labūns, twenty bint makhāḍs, and twenty male ibn labūns. The value of each camel in silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams or ten dinars, and in sheep, the value of each one of the camels is twenty sheep.

Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood money for intentional killing, and he said: "One hundred mature male camels. If they are not available, then in place of each camel there are twenty mature male sheep."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Hayy, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was found murdered. Then two men came to his guardian, and one of them said: “I killed him intentionally,” while the other said: “I killed him by mistake.” He عليه السلام said: “If he accepts the statement of the one who confessed to intentional killing, then he has no claim against the one who confessed to accidental killing. And if he accepts the statement of the one who confessed to accidental killing, then he has no claim against the one who confessed to intentional killing.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla say: “In the pre-Islamic era, the blood money was one hundred camels, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله affirmed it. Then he imposed upon the people of cattle two hundred cows, upon the people of sheep one thousand sheep, and upon the people of garments one hundred garments.” Abd al-Rahman said: So I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about what Ibn Abi Layla narrated, and he said: “Ali عليه السلام used to say: ‘The blood money is one thousand dinars, and the value of a dinar is ten dirhams. Upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars; upon the people of silver is ten thousand dirhams; ten thousand for the people of the cities; for the people of the deserts, the blood money is one hundred camels; and for the people of the rural lands, two hundred cows or one thousand sheep.’”
Kulayb ibn Mu'āwiyah heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Whoever kills during a sacred month is liable for a blood money and one-third more.
And Aban narrated from Zurarah that he said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام say: "If a man kills during a sacred month, he must fast for two consecutive months from the sacred months."

5204 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who intentionally killed a Muslim man, and the slain man had no heirs among the Muslims except relatives from the Ahl al-Dhimmah from among his kin. He عليه السلام said: “It is upon the Imam to present Islam to his relatives from the people of his household. Whoever among them accepts Islam, then he is his heir, and the killer is handed over to him. If he wishes, he may kill; if he wishes, he may pardon; and if he wishes, he may take the blood money. But if none of his relatives accepts Islam, then the Imam is the authority over his affair. If he wishes, he may kill; and if he wishes, he may take the blood money and place it in the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain man was upon the Imam, and likewise his blood money belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.” I said: “Then if the Imam pardons him?” He عليه السلام said: “It is only a right belonging to all the Muslims. The Imam is only to kill or to take the blood money, and he has no right to pardon.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who pushed another man onto a man, causing him to kill him, he said: The diyyah is upon the one who fell upon the man and killed him, for the heirs of the slain. He said: And the one who was pushed may recover the diyyah from the one who pushed him. He said: And if anything happens to the one who was pushed, then that too is upon the one who pushed him.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say: “The diyyah for accidental killing is to be paid over three years, and the diyyah for intentional killing is to be paid within one year.”

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Muʿallā Abī ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: But whoever remits it as charity, then it is an expiation for him. He عليه السلام said: Some of his sins are expiated according to the extent to which he pardoned in the case of intentional killing.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who intentionally killed another man, then was brought before the governor, and the governor handed him over to the heirs of the slain so that they might kill him. Then a group attacked them and rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs, so he said: "I hold that those who rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs should be imprisoned forever until they bring the killer back." It was said to him: "What if the killer dies while they are in prison?" He said: "If he dies, then the blood money is upon them; they must pay it to the heirs of the slain."

Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: What do you say regarding intentional and accidental killing, and regarding injuries? So he said: Accidental wrongdoing is not like intentional wrongdoing. In intentional killing, there is killing in retaliation, and in injuries there is qiṣāṣ. In accidental killing and injuries, in both of them there is diyyah. And he said: Then he said to me: O Hakam, if the accidental act is from the killer or the accidental act is from the one who inflicts the injury, and he is a Bedouin, then the diyyah of what the Bedouin committed by mistake is upon his Bedouin kinsfolk. He said: And if the one who inflicted the injury is a villager, then the diyyah of what he committed by mistake is upon his villager kinsfolk.

And Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a man who ordered a free man to kill another man, and he killed him, he عليه السلام said: “The one who directly carried out the killing shall be executed for him, and the one who ordered his killing shall be imprisoned in prison forever until he dies.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed his mother. He said: "He does not inherit from her, and he is executed for her in humiliation, and I do not think that his being killed for her would be an expiation for his sin."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed another man by mistake during the sacred months. He said: "He is liable for the blood money and the fasting of two consecutive months from the sacred months." I said: "This includes the Eid and the days of Tashriq." So he said: "He must fast it, for it is a binding right that has become obligatory upon him."
And in the narration of Abān from Zurārah from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: He must pay a diyyah (blood money) and one-third.

And Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdِ اللهِ عليه السلام said: “If a man were to strike another man with a piece of pottery or with a brick, and he died, it would be considered intentional.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim and more than one person, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: He was asked about a woman against whom a man used excessive force, and he claimed that she died from his violence against her. He عليه السلام said: "The full blood money must be paid, and the man is not to be executed."

And in the Nawadir of Ibrahim ibn Hashim: That al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man who acted violently against a woman, or a woman who acted violently against her husband, and one of them killed the other. He عليه السلام said: "There is nothing upon them if they are deemed trustworthy. But if they are suspected, an oath by Allah is binding upon them that they did not intend the killing."

And Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding two men who killed a man, he عليه السلام said: “If the heirs of the slain wish to pay a blood money compensation and kill both of them together, they may kill them both.”

Samaah narrated from Abu Basir from Abu Jafar (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, the Almighty and Majestic: 'But if any remission is made by the brother of the slain, then grant [him] a suitable follow-up.' I asked: 'What is that thing?' He said: 'It is when a man accepts the blood money. Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, commanded the one who has the right to pursue it in a good manner and not to make it difficult, and He commanded the one who owes the right not to wrong him and to pay it to him with kindness when he becomes able.' But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment. He said: 'It is the man who accepts the blood money or agrees to a settlement, and then later comes back to mutilate or kill. Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, has promised him a painful punishment.'

And Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who carried goods on his head and struck a person, who then died, or broke something of his, he said: “He is exempt from liability.”

Muḥammad ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: I said to him: “May I be your ransom, a man killed another man, intentionally or by mistake, and he had a debt and property. Then his heirs wanted to remit his blood to the killer.” So he said: “If they remit his blood, they become responsible for the debt.” I said: “What if they want to execute him?” He said: “If he was killed intentionally, his killer is executed, and the Imam pays the debt on his behalf from the share of the debtors.” I said: “If he was killed intentionally and his heirs made a settlement with his killer for the diyyah, then upon whom is the debt: upon his heirs out of the diyyah, or upon the Imam of the Muslims?” He said: “Rather, they pay his debt from his diyyah which his heirs agreed upon in settlement, for he has more right to his diyyah than anyone else.”
And in the narration of Ibn Bukayr, he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "Whoever kills with anything, small or great, after doing so intentionally, then qiṣāṣ is upon him."

Al-Bazanti narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who struck another man on the head with a stick, and his tongue became heavy, he said: “The letters of the alphabet should be presented to him. For whatever of them he articulates clearly, there is nothing due in it; and whatever he cannot articulate clearly, the diyyah is due for it, and they are twenty-eight letters.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a boy who had not reached maturity and a woman who killed a man, so he said: Indeed, the mistake of the woman and the boy is treated as intentional. So if the heirs of the slain wish to kill both of them, they may kill them both, and they return five thousand dirhams to the boy’s heirs. And if they wish to kill the boy, they may kill him, and the woman returns a quarter of the blood money to the boy’s heirs. He said: And if the heirs of the slain wish to kill the woman, they may kill her, and the boy returns a quarter of the blood money to the woman’s heirs. He said: And if the heirs of the slain wish to take the blood money, then half of the blood money is upon the boy and half of the blood money is upon the woman.

And Abu Usamah narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a woman who intentionally killed a man, he عليه السلام said: “If his family wishes to kill her, they may kill her, and no one commits a crime for more than his own soul.”

Al-Sakūnī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man and a boy who joined together in killing a man and killed him, he said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: "If the boy has reached five hand spans, qiṣāṣ is carried out against him and for him; but if the boy has not reached five hand spans, then judgment is made for the diyyah."

5227 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a blind man who intentionally gouged out the eye of a sighted person. He said: “O Abū ʿUbaydah, the intentional act of a blind man is like a mistake; in this case there is diyyah from his wealth. If he has no wealth, then the diyyah for that is upon the Imam, and the right of a Muslim is not to be invalidated.”

And Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام asking him about a mentally ill man who killed another man intentionally. So he عليه السلام assigned the blood money to his people and treated his accidental and intentional acts as the same.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Aban, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Ten men killed one man. He عليه السلام said: If his heirs wish, they may kill them all together and pay nine blood monies. And if they wish to choose one man and kill him, they may kill him, and the remaining nine shall pay to the family of the slain last one one-tenth of the blood money, each man among them. He عليه السلام said: Then indeed the governor undertakes their discipline and imprisonment.

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Ali عليه السلام ruled regarding two men, one of whom restrained while the other killed. He said: The killer is to be executed, and the other is to be imprisoned until he dies in grief, just as he held him until he died in grief.

And he said regarding ten people who jointly participated in killing a man: “The family of the slain may choose whichever of them they wish and kill him, and his heirs may then return against the rest for nine-tenths of the blood money.”

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning six people who were in the water, and one man from among them drowned. Then three of them testified against two that those two had drowned him, and two testified against three that those three had drowned him. So he obligated all of them to pay the diyyah. He made the two liable for three shares based on the testimony of the three against them, and he made the three liable for two shares based on the testimony of the two against them.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled regarding four men who looked into the lion's pit, then one of them fell, so he clung to the second, and the second clung to the third, and the third clung to the fourth, until some of them caused the others to fall onto the lion. So he ruled concerning the first that he was the lion’s prey, and he imposed upon his family one-third of the diyyah for the family of the second. And he imposed upon the family of the second, for the family of the third, two-thirds of the diyyah. And he imposed upon the family of the third, for the family of the fourth, the full diyyah.

And it is narrated from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, who said: I was present at al-Bayt al-Haram when a man was calling out to Abū Jaʿfar al-Dawānīqī while he was performing tawaf, saying: “O Commander of the Faithful, these two men came to my brother at night and took him out of his house, and he did not return to me. By Allah, I do not know what they did with him.” So he said to them: “What did you do with him?” They said: “O Commander of the Faithful, we only spoke with him, then he returned to his house.” He said to them: “Come to me tomorrow at the time of salat al-ʿAsr in this place.” They came to him the next day at salat al-ʿAsr, and he said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, while holding his hand: “O Jaʿfar, judge between them.” He said: “You judge between them.” He said to him: “By my right over you, you must judge between them.” He said: Then Jaʿfar عليه السلام came out, and a reed prayer-mat was spread for him, and he sat on it. Then the disputants came and sat before him, and he said to the claimant: “What do you say?” He said: “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, these two came to my brother at night and took him out of his house. By Allah, he did not return to me, and by Allah, I do not know what they did with him.” He said: “What do you two say?” They said: “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, we spoke with him, then he returned to his house.” Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام said: “O servant, write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.” The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Whoever comes to a man at night and brings him out of his house is liable for him, unless he establishes clear proof that he returned him to his house.” O servant, remove this one of the two and strike his neck. He said: “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I did not kill him, but I only restrained him, then this one came and stabbed him and killed him.” He said: “I am the son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. O servant, remove this one, and strike his neck for the other.” He said: “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, by Allah, I did not torture him, but I killed him with a single blow.” So he ordered concerning his brother, and his neck was struck. Then he ordered regarding the other, and his sides were beaten, and he was imprisoned. And he wrote

And As-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: A group of people were drinking and became intoxicated, so they began to attack each other with knives they had with them. They were brought before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and he imprisoned them. Two of them died, and two remained alive. The families of the two killed men said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Retaliate against these two for our two relatives.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asked the group: 'What do you think?' They replied: 'We think you should retaliate against them.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Perhaps those two who died killed each other.' They said: 'We do not know.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) then said: 'Rather, I will distribute the blood money of the two killed among the four tribes, and I will deduct the compensation for the injuries of the survivors from the blood money of the deceased.'

5237 - It was reported to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: Three men: one of them restrained a man, another came and killed him, and the third was watching them. So he, عليه السلام, ruled regarding the watcher that his eyes be gouged out; and he ruled regarding the one who restrained [the victim] that he be imprisoned until he dies, just as he held him; and he ruled regarding the one who killed that he be killed.

And he, peace be upon him, ruled regarding a man who ordered his servant to kill a man, and he said: Is a man's servant anything but like his sword and his whip? The master is executed for it, and the servant is consigned to prison until he dies.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What do you say about a man who cuts off one finger of a woman? How much is due for it?” He said: “Ten camels.” I said: “If he cuts off two?” He said: “Twenty.” I said: “If he cuts off three?” He said: “Thirty.” I said: “If he cuts off four?” He said: “Twenty.” I said: “Glory be to Allah! He cuts off three, so thirty are due from him; then he cuts off four, so twenty are due from him? This used to reach us while we were in Iraq, and we would dissociate ourselves from whoever said it, and we would say: the one who said it was a shayṭān.” So he said: “Take it gently, O Abān. This is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ruled. Indeed, a woman is equal to a man in compensation up to one-third of the diyah; then when it reaches one-third, the woman returns to one-half. O Abān, you confronted me with qiyās, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition), when subjected to analogy, destroys the religion.”

Jamīl and Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about whether there is qiṣāṣ between a woman and a man. He عليه السلام said: “Yes, in wounds, up to one-third they are equal. Then when it reaches one-third, the man rises and the woman decreases.”

Abū Baṣīr narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: I said: A man killed a woman. He said: If the family of the woman wishes to kill him, they must pay half of his diyyah and then kill him; otherwise, they should accept the diyyah.

Al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) said regarding a woman who intentionally killed her husband, and he said: If his family wishes to kill her, they may kill her, and no one commits more than his own crime against himself.

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasaʿ narrated from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Mihran, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman into whose home a thief entered while she was pregnant, and he assaulted her and killed what was in her womb. Then the woman sprang upon the thief and killed him. He said: “As for the woman who killed him, there is nothing upon her, and the diyyah for her unborn child is upon the ʿaṣabah of the slain thief.”

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (AS), who said: “A father is not executed for killing his son, but a son is executed for killing his father.” And he said: “Two men do not inherit from one another when one of them has killed the other.”

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said: Regarding a man who killed his mother, he said: “If it was by mistake, then he has a share in her inheritance; but if he killed her intentionally, then he inherits nothing from her.”

And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jabir from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who kills his son or his slave, he said: “He is not to be killed for that, but he should be severely beaten and exiled from his place of birth.”

ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, about a man who killed his mother. He said: "He does not inherit from her, and he is to be killed for her while humiliated; and I do not think that his being killed for her would be an expiation for his sin."

4969 - It is narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Uqbah, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "The glance is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis. Whoever abandons it for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not for other than Him, Allah will cause him to inherit a faith whose taste he finds."
And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-Kāhilī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: A glance after a glance plants desire in the heart, and it is sufficient as a trial for its beholder.
Al-Asbagh ibn Nubātah narrated from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: O ʿAlī, the first glance is for you, and the second is against you and not for you.

And Abū Baṣīr said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: A woman passes by a man, and he looks at her from behind. He said: Would any of you be pleased that his family and his close female relatives be looked at? I said: No. He said: Then approve for people what you approve for yourself.
Hisham, Hafs, and Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said: Are those who look at the backs of women secure from being afflicted with that in their own women?

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.” He said: “Shu'ayb عليه السلام said to her: My daughter, this one is strong—you recognized that from his lifting the rock. But from where did you know that he is trustworthy? She said: O my father, I walked in front of him, and he said: Walk behind me, and if I lose the way, then direct me to the path, for we are a people who do not look at the backs of women.”
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: O people, indeed the glance is from Satan. So whoever finds something of that, let him go to his family.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who examines a slave woman in order to buy her. He said: “There is no harm in looking at her attractive features and touching her, so long as he does not look at what is not appropriate for him to look at.”

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood money for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian. He said: “They are equal: eight hundred, eight hundred.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, if they are apprehended in the land of the Muslims while committing an indecent act, is the hadd punishment carried out upon them?” He said: “Yes, they are judged according to the rulings of the Muslims.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-Baḥrayn, where he shed the blood of some people from among the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians. He then wrote to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: “I have shed the blood of some people from among the Jews and the Christians, so I paid their blood money as eight hundred, eight hundred; and I have shed the blood of some people from among the Magians, but you had not given me any prior instruction concerning them.” He said: So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله wrote to him: “Indeed, their blood money is like the blood money of the Jews and the Christians,” and he said: “Indeed, they are People of the Book.”

5251 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a Christian who killed a Muslim, then when he was captured he accepted Islam: 'Should I kill him for him?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Then if he does not accept Islam?' He said: 'He is handed over to the heirs of the slain; if they wish, they kill him; if they wish, they pardon him; and if they wish, they enslave him. And if he has any specific property belonging to him, it is handed over to the heirs of the slain—he and his property.'

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The blood money for a Jew and a Christian is four thousand, four thousand, and the blood money for a Magian is eight hundred dirhams. And he said: Indeed, the Magians have a book called Jamasf.
And it has been narrated: The blood money (diyyah) for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is four thousand dirhams, four thousand dirhams, because they are People of the Book.
And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Manṣūr, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The diyyah of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is the diyyah of a Muslim.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever was granted protection by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, his diyyah is complete.

As narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Maghrāʾ, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a Muslim kills a Christian and the family of the Christian wishes to execute him, they may kill him, and they must pay the difference between the two blood monies.

5257 - And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood of the Magians, the Jews, and the Christians: is there anything upon one who kills them if they deceive the Muslims and openly display hostility and treachery toward them? He said: “No, unless he is one who is habituated to killing them.” He said: And I asked him about whether a Muslim is killed in retaliation for the people of dhimmah and the People of the Book if he kills them. He said: “No, unless he is accustomed to that, not refraining from killing them; then he is killed while humbled.”
And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever harms those under my protection has indeed harmed me."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Buraid al-'Ijli, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a Muslim who gouged out the eye of a Christian, and he said: “Indeed, the blood money for the eye of a dhimmi is four hundred dirhams.”

And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A slave is killed for a free man, and a free man is not killed for a slave. However, he is made to pay his value and is beaten severely so that he does not return to doing that.

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding a man who intentionally kills his slave, he said: “I prefer that he frees a slave, fasts two consecutive months, and feeds sixty needy people; then repentance should be after that.”
Humran asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: about a man who struck a slave belonging to him, and he died from his beating. He said: "He must free a slave."

Yahya ibn Abi al-‘Ala’ narrated from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: If a slave kills a free man, then the family of the one killed has the choice: if they wish, they may kill him, and if they wish, they may enslave him.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukatab who was killed and said: “The portion of him that had become free is calculated, so the diyah of a free man is paid for it, and for the portion that remained in bondage, the diyah of a slave is paid.” And he said: “A slave does not impose upon his family any liability beyond himself.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said: Regarding a slave who injures a free man, he said: “If the free man wishes, he may exact retribution from him; and if he wishes, he may take him, if the wound reaches his neck. But if it does not reach his neck, his master must ransom him. فإذا the master refuses to ransom him, then the injured free man has a share in the slave equal to the diyyah of his injury, and the remainder belongs to the master. The slave is sold, the injured man takes his due, and the remainder is returned to the master.”

5266 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who inflicted a mudihah wound on a slave, he عليه السلام said: “He is liable for half of one-tenth of his value.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Regarding a slave who injured two men, he عليه السلام said: “He is to be divided between them if his offense encompasses his full value.” It was said to him: “What if he injured one man at the beginning of the day and injured another at the end of the day?” He عليه السلام said: “He is between them so long as the governor has not ruled regarding the first injured person. But if the governor had ruled regarding the first injured person and handed him over to him on account of his offense, then he committed an offense after that, his offense is upon the latter.”

And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a free man kills a slave, he must pay his value and be disciplined. It was said to him: Then what if his value is twenty thousand? He said: The value of a slave is not to exceed the blood money of a free person.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “The injuries of slaves are according to the manner of the injuries of free people in the value.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a group of people who claimed against a slave an offense encompassing his neck, and the slave confessed to it. He said: “The confession of a slave is not valid against his master.” He said: “If they establish the evidence for what they claimed against the slave, they may take the slave for it, or his master may ransom him.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام about a mudabbar who intentionally killed a man. He said: “He is to be killed for him in retaliation.” I said: “Then if he killed him by mistake?” He said: “He is handed over to the heirs of the slain, and he becomes their slave. If they wish, they may enslave him, and if they wish, they may sell him, but they have no right to kill him.” Then he said: “O Abu Muhammad, indeed the mudabbar is owned property.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a mukatab who killed a man by mistake, and he said: If his master, when making the contract with him, stipulated that if he became unable, he would return to slavery, then he is in the position of a slave: he is handed over to the heirs of the slain person, and if they wish they may enslave him, and if they wish they may sell him. But if his master, when making the contract with him, did not stipulate that, and he had already paid something of his mukatabah, then ʿAli عليه السلام used to say: 'The mukatab is freed in proportion to what he has paid of his mukatabah, and it is upon the Imam to pay to the heirs of the slain person in proportion to what has been freed of the mukatab, and the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left uncompensated.' And I hold that, for the portion that remains upon the mukatab of what he has not paid, he remains as a slave for the heirs of the slain person; they may make him serve them for his lifetime in proportion to what remains upon him, and they do not have the right to sell him.

And Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAli ibn Riʾab from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who placed his slave on a riding animal, and it trampled a man, he عليه السلام said: "The liability is upon the master."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu al-Ward, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed a slave by mistake. He said: "His value is due from him, and his value is not to exceed ten thousand dirhams." I said: "Who appraises him when he is dead?" He said: "If his master has witnesses that his value on the day he killed him was such-and-such, then his killer is charged accordingly. If his master has no witnesses, then the valuation rests with the one who killed him together with his oath: he swears four times by Allah that he had no value greater than what I assessed for him. If he refuses to swear and returns the oath to the master, the master is given what he swore to, and his value is not to exceed ten thousand dirhams." He said: "If the slave was a believer and he killed him intentionally, he must pay his value, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, feed sixty needy persons, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a mukatab who committed an offense against a free man, and he said: “If he has paid something from his mukatabah, he is held liable in his offense in proportion to what he has paid from his mukatabah to the free man. And if he is unable to meet the liability of the offense, that is taken from the master who contracted him.” I said: What if the offense was against a slave? He said: “Likewise, he is handed over to the master of the slave whom the mukatab wounded, and there is no retaliation between the mukatab and the slave if the mukatab has paid something from his mukatabah. But if he has not paid anything from his mukatabah, then retaliation is taken for the slave from him, or the master is made liable for all that the mukatab has committed, because he is still his slave so long as he has not paid anything from his mukatabah.” He said: “And the child of a mukatabah woman is like his mother: if she remains a slave, he remains a slave; and if she is freed, he is freed.”

In the narration of al-Sakūnī, it is reported that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: For the private part of the male child, there is diyyah, and for the private part of the impotent man, there is diyyah.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had struck another man until his eyesight was diminished. So he called men of his age, then showed them something, and he examined how much of his eyesight had diminished; then he gave him the blood money for the amount by which his eyesight had diminished.

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام: Regarding a man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift the stick from him until he died, He عليه السلام said: “He is to be handed over to the heirs of the slain, but he is not to be left so that pleasure may be taken in torturing him; rather, retribution is to be carried out against him by the sword.”

Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The diyah for the hand, when it is cut off, is fifty camels. As for wounds less than complete severance, two just individuals among you shall judge regarding them. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—then they are the disbelievers.

Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them: Concerning a man who gouged out another man's eye, cut off his nose and his ears, then killed him. He, peace be upon him, said: "If he inflicted that upon him separately, retaliation is taken from him, then he is killed. But if he struck him with a single blow and that resulted in it, his neck is struck, and retaliation is not taken from him."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Buraid al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: “For the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the private part and testicles of a free eunuch, one-third of the diyah is due. And for the private part of a young boy, the diyah is due in full.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: "Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who is struck on his hips, so that he can no longer control his stool or his urine, that in such a case the full diyah is due."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who struck another man on his head with the pole of a tent in a single blow, causing a penetrating wound until the blow reached his brain, and his intellect departed. He said: "If the one struck does not comprehend the salat (prayer) because of it, and does not understand what he said nor what was said to him, then he is to be observed for a year. If he dies between that time and the year, his striker is subject to retaliation (qisas) for him. But if he does not die between that time and the year, and his intellect does not return to him, his striker must pay the blood money (diyyah) from his own wealth for the loss of his intellect." He said: So I said to him: Then what do you hold against him regarding the head wound? He said: "No, because he only struck him a single blow, and that blow caused two injuries. So I imposed upon him the more severe of the two injuries, which is the blood money (diyyah). And if he had struck him with two blows, and the two blows caused two injuries, I would have imposed upon him the liability of what the two blows caused, whatever they may have been, except if death were in one of them, in which case his striker would be subject to retaliation (qisas) for it, and the other would be set aside." He said: "And if he struck him three blows, one after another, and they caused three injuries, I would impose upon him the liability of what the three blows caused, whatever they may have been, so long as there was no death in them; then his striker would be subject to retaliation (qisas) for it." He said: "And if he struck him ten blows and they caused a single injury, I would impose upon him that injury which the ten blows caused, whatever it may have been, so long as there was no death in it."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who cut off the two right hands of two men. He said, “O Habib, his right hand is cut off for the man whose right hand he cut off first, and his left hand is cut off for the one whose right hand he cut off last, because he only cut off the hand of the latter man while his right hand is retaliation for the first man.” I said: “Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام used only to cut off the right hand and the left foot.” He said, “He only did that in matters that are due from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But as for the rights of the Muslims, O Habib, their rights are taken for them in full: a hand for a hand in retaliation when the cutter has a hand, and a foot for a hand when the cutter does not have two hands.” I said to him: “Is blood money not imposed upon him, and his foot left for him?” He said, “Blood money is only imposed upon him if he cuts off a man’s hand and the cutter has neither two hands nor two feet. Then blood money is imposed upon him, because he has no limb from which retaliation may be taken.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For the hand, there is half of the diyah, and for both hands together, the full diyah. And for both legs likewise. And for the male organ, if the glans and what is above that are cut, then the diyah is due. And for the nose, if the soft part is cut, the diyah is due.

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For the lower lip, the compensation is six thousand, and for the upper one, four thousand, because the lower lip holds water.

And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام ruled concerning a man whose one eye was injured that an ostrich egg should be taken and he should be made to walk with it, and his sound eye should be bound so that he cannot see with it, until the extent of his vision is reached. Then the difference between the limit of the vision of his injured eye and his sound eye should be calculated, and compensation should be paid according to that calculation.

And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Everything in the human body that exists in pairs carries the full blood money (diyyah) for both, and half the blood money for one of them. And whatever exists as a single part carries the full blood money.

And Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn al-Sabbah, from ʿAli, from Abi Basir, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding a man who was struck in his ear and claimed that one of his ears had lost some of its hearing, he said: “The one that was struck should be bound tightly and well, and the healthy one should be left open. Then a bell should be rung for him in front of his face, and he should be told: Listen. When the sound of the bell becomes hidden from him, its place is marked. Then the bell should be taken behind him and rung behind him until the sound becomes hidden from him; when it becomes hidden from him, its place is marked. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken truthfully. Then it should be taken to his right and rung until it becomes hidden, then that is marked. Then it should be taken to his left and rung until it becomes hidden, then that is marked. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken truthfully.” He said: “Then his affected ear should be opened, and the other should be bound tightly and well. Then the bell should be rung in front of him, then its place should be marked until it becomes hidden. It should be done to him just as was done the first time with his healthy ear. Then the difference between the healthy ear and the affected ear is measured, and the compensation is assessed according to that.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who struck another man’s ear with a bone, and he claimed that all of his hearing had gone. He said: “He is to be given a delay of one year, and he is to be watched by two just witnesses. If they come and testify that he heard and that he responded upon hearing, then he has no right. But if it is not discovered that he heard, he is made to swear an oath, then he is given the blood money.” He said: I said, “What if he hears after he has been given the blood money?” He said: “It is something Allah, the Exalted, has given him.” He said: And I asked him about the eye, whose owner claims that he does not see with it. He said: “He is to be given a delay of one year, then after the year he is made to swear that he does not see, then he is given the blood money.” I said, “What if he sees after that?” He said: “It is something Allah has given him.”
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī: That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that, regarding the spine, if it is broken, the blood money is due.

Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man whose coccyx was broken, so he could no longer control his anus. He said: "The full blood money is due." He said: And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with a slave girl and caused ifda' to her, and when she reached that condition, she would not bear children. He said: "The full blood money is due."

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who married a slave girl, then had intercourse with her and caused ifda' to her. He said: "He is responsible for maintaining her as long as she remains alive."
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “An eye is not to be assessed on a cloudy day.”

ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the fingers: whether some of them have superiority over others in the blood money. He said: “They are equal in the blood money.”

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a tooth and an arm that are broken intentionally: is there indemnity payment for them or retaliation? He said: “Retaliation.” He said: I said, “Then if they offer him the diyah in increased amount?” He said: “If they satisfy him with whatever he wishes, then it is his.”
And in the narration of Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: For a finger, there are ten camels if it is cut off from its base or becomes paralyzed.

And in the narration of Jَمِيل from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, he said: Regarding the tooth of a child: a man strikes it, so it falls out, then it grows back. He عليه السلام said: “There is no qisas against him, but arsh is upon him.” And he عليه السلام said regarding a man whose hand is broken, then his hand heals: “Retaliation is not carried out against him, but arsh is given.” And Jamil was asked: how much is the arsh for the tooth of the child and the breaking of the hand? He said: “A small amount.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: "The fingers of the hands and feet are equal in compensation (diyyah)." And he said: "Regarding a tooth, when it is struck, one should wait with it for a year. If it falls out, the striker must pay five hundred dirhams. If it does not fall out but turns black, he must pay two-thirds of its compensation."

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the teeth for which the diyyah is apportioned that they are twenty-eight teeth: sixteen in the back of the mouth and twelve in its front. So the compensation for each tooth from the front teeth, when it is broken such that it is lost, is fifty dinars, making that six hundred dinars. And the compensation for each tooth from the back teeth, when it is broken such that it is lost, is half the compensation of the front teeth: twenty-five dinars, making that four hundred dinars. Thus that is one thousand dinars. Whatever is less than this has no diyyah, and whatever is more than this has no diyyah.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Fudayl ibn Yasar who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the forearm when it is struck and the wrist bone fractures from it. He said: 'If the hand becomes withered/paralyzed from it, or all the fingers of the hand become immobile, then in it is two-thirds of the blood money of the hand.' He said: 'And if some of the fingers become immobile and some remain, then for each finger that becomes immobile, two-thirds of its blood money is applicable.' He said: 'And the same ruling applies to the leg and the foot if the toes of the foot become immobile.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz narrated from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding the extra finger: if it is cut off, then one-third of the diyyah of a normal finger is due.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a wound in the fingers that, if it exposes the bone, then one-tenth of the diyyah of the finger is due, if the injured person does not wish to seek qisas.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May Allah rectify you. Some people have thirty-two teeth, while others have twenty-eight. Upon how many teeth is the blood money calculated?' He said: 'The natural creation is twenty-eight teeth: twelve in the front of the mouth and sixteen in the back. Based on this, the blood money of the teeth is distributed. The blood money for each of the front teeth, if broken until it is lost, is five hundred dirhams; since there are twelve, their total blood money is six thousand dirhams. The blood money for each of the molars, if broken until it is lost, is two hundred and fifty dirhams; since there are sixteen, their total blood money is four thousand dirhams. Thus, the total blood money for both the front and back teeth is ten thousand dirhams. The blood money was set according to this, so any extra teeth beyond twenty-eight have no blood money, and any missing teeth have no blood money.' And thus we found it in the book of the Commander of the Faithful. Al-Hakam said: I asked, 'Wasn't blood money previously taken from camels, cows, and sheep?' He said: 'That was in the desert communities before Islam. When Islam became widespread and silver became abundant among people, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) set it in terms of silver.' Al-Hakam said: I asked him, 'What about those who live in the desert today? What is taken from them as blood money - silver or camels?' He said: 'Camels are equivalent to silver, rather, they are better than silver for blood money. Indeed, they used to take one hundred camels for unintentional killing, with each camel valued at one hundred dirhams, making a total of ten thousand dirhams.' I asked: 'What are the ages of the one hundred camels?' He said: 'They must be male camels that have completed one full year.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad Al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and had a father, a mother, and a son. The son said, "I want to kill the killer of my father," and another said, "I pardon," and another said, "I want to take the blood money." He عليه السلام said: "Then the son should give the mother of the slain one-sixth of the blood money, and give the heirs of the killer one-sixth of the blood money as the right of the father who pardoned, and then kill him."

5307 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and had young and adult children. I said: What do you think if his adult children pardon? He عليه السلام said: “He is not to be killed, and the pardon of the adults is valid regarding their shares. Then when the minors become adults, they have the right to seek their share from the blood money.” And it has also been narrated: “If one of the heirs pardons concerning the blood, retaliation is lifted.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah from his father from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام was brought a man who had killed another man by mistake. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “Who are your clan and your relatives?” He said, “I have no relatives or clan in this town.” He said, “From the people of which towns are you?” He said, “I am a man from the people of al-Mawṣil. I was born there, and I have relatives and a household there.” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn inquired about him, but found that he had no relatives or clan for him in al-Kūfah. He said: So he wrote to his governor over al-Mawṣil: “To proceed: so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such, killed a Muslim man by mistake, and he has stated that he is a man from the people of al-Mawṣil and that he has relatives and a household there. I have sent him to you with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such. So when they arrive to you, if Allah wills, and you have read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his relatives among the Muslims. If he is from the people of al-Mawṣil, from those born there, and you find for him there relatives from among the Muslims, then gather them to you. Then look: if there is there a man who inherits from him, having a share in the Book, whom none of his relatives bars from his inheritance, then obligate him to the blood money and exact it from him over three years. And if he has no relative having a share in the Book, and his relatives are equal in lineage, then distribute the blood money over his relatives from his father’s side and his relatives from his mother’s side, from among the adult Muslim men. Then place upon his relatives from his father’s side two-thirds of the blood money, and place upon his relatives from his mother’s side one-third of the blood money. And if he has no relatives from his mother’s side, then distribute the blood money over his relatives from his father’s side from among the adult Muslim men. Then exact it from them and seek payment of the blood money from them over three years. And if he has no relatives from his father’s side and no relatives from his mother’s side, then distribute the blood money over the people of al-Mawṣil from among those born there and raised there, and do not include among them others from the people of the towns. Then seek

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: There is no collective liability among Ahl al-Dhimmah regarding what they commit of killing or injury. Rather, that is taken from their property. If they do not have wealth, then liability for the offense returns to the Imam of the Muslims, because they pay the jizyah to him just as a slave pays a levy to his master. He عليه السلام said: And they are under the ownership of the Imam, so whoever among them accepts Islam, he is free.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to assign the liability for the offense of the mentally impaired person to his ʿāqilah, whether accidental or intentional.

And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: “The ʿĀqilah is only liable for that which has been established by evidence. And if a man came to him and confessed before him, he assigned it specifically to his own wealth and did not place any of it upon his ʿĀqilah.”
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام, who said: The ʿAqilah is not liable for intentional acts, nor for confession, nor for settlement.

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who struck another man's head with a pickaxe, so his eyes flowed down onto his cheeks. Then the injured man sprang upon his striker and killed him. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "These two were both aggressors. I do not hold that qiṣāṣ applies against the one who killed the man, because he killed him at the time he killed him while he was blind, and the offense of a blind person is deemed a mistake. His ʿāqilah is liable for it; they are made to pay it over three years, in each year an installment.
