If the blind man has no ʿāqilah, then the diyah of what he committed is binding upon him from his own wealth, to be taken over three years. And the blind man may recourse against the heirs of the one who struck him for the diyah of his two eyes."

5314 - It was narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar that he said: A man asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, while I was present, about a man who struck another man, and his urine did not stop. He said: “If the urine continues until the night, then the diyyah is due upon him. If it continues until midday, then two-thirds of the diyyah is due upon him. If it continues until the rising of the day, then one-third of the diyyah is due upon him.”

5315 - Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him: That ʿAlī, peace be upon him, ruled concerning a man who was struck until his urine became continuous that the full diyyah applies.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Buzayʿ narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Sulaymān ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, for the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the ʿalaqah forty dinars, for the muḍghah sixty dinars, and for the bone eighty dinars. Then when it is clothed with flesh, it is one hundred. Then it remains one hundred until it cries out, and when it cries out, the diyyah is complete.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Yūnus al-Shaybānī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What if a drop of blood appears in the nutfah?” He said: “For one drop, one-tenth of the compensation of the nutfah applies, which is twenty-two dinars.” He said: I asked, “What if two drops fall?” He said: “Then twenty-four dinars.” I said: “What if three drops fall?” He said: “Then twenty-six dinars.” I said: “Then four?” He said: “Twenty-eight; and for five, thirty. If it exceeds half, then it is calculated according to that until it becomes an ʿalaqah; and when it is an ʿalaqah, then it is forty dinars.”

Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated from Abu Shibl, who said: I was present with Yunus al-Shaybani while Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was informing him about the blood monies. So I said to him: If the nutfah came out mixed and stirred with blood? He said: “It has become an ʿalaqah. If it is pure blood, then in it is forty. And if it is black blood, then nothing is due upon him except taʿzir, because whatever is of pure blood, that is for the child, and whatever is of black blood, that is only from the inside of the body.” Abu Shibl said: What if the ʿalaqah has come to have in it something like a vein of flesh? He said: “In it are forty-two and a tenth.” I said: One-tenth of forty is four. He said: “It is only one-tenth of the muḍghah, because only one-tenth of it has gone. And whenever it increases, it is increased until it reaches sixty.” He said: I said: I saw in the muḍghah something like a knotted form, a dry bone. He said: “That is the bone, for which at the first stage there are four dinars. If it increases, then add four, until it completes eighty. And likewise when the bone is clothed with flesh, then likewise.” He said: I said: If he struck her and the child fell, and it is not known whether it had been alive or not? He said: “Far from it, O Abu Shibl. When five months have passed, life has come to be in it, and it has incurred the blood money.”

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A woman came seeking redress against a Bedouin who had frightened her, so she miscarried her fetus. The Bedouin said: “It did not cry out, nor did it make a sound, and the like of this is disregarded without compensation.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Be quiet, O rhyming speaker. Upon you is a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave.”
And Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The ghurrah is sometimes one hundred dīnārs and sometimes ten dīnārs.” So he said: “Fifty.”

And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who drank medicine while pregnant to abort her child, and she miscarried. He said: "If the fetus had bones with flesh grown upon them, and its hearing and sight were formed, then she must pay a diyyah (blood money) which she hands over to the father." He said: "And if it was a 'alaqah (clot) or a 'mudghah (chewed flesh), then she must pay forty dinars or a ghurra (compensation) which she hands over to the father." I asked: "Does she inherit from her child's diyyah?" He said: "No, because she killed him."

5322 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who killed the fetus of a female slave belonging to a group of people while it was in her womb, he عليه السلام said: “If it died in her womb after he struck her, then half of one-tenth of the value of the female slave is upon him. And if he struck her and she cast it out alive, then it died, then one-tenth of the value of the female slave is upon him.”

Sama'ah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, and she miscarried a stillborn fetus. Then the woman's husband sought legal redress against him, so the woman said to her husband: If there is a diyyah for this miscarried fetus, and I have an inheritance share from it, then my inheritance from it belongs to my father. He عليه السلام said: It is permissible for her father to receive what she has gifted to him.

Al-Husayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Al-Fuḍayl, who said: I asked Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a thief who entered upon a pregnant woman and fell upon her, so she cast out what was in her womb. Then the woman leapt upon him and killed him. He said: “The blood of the thief is unavenged, and upon the slain man is the blood money for her miscarried fetus.”
And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: "Adultery brings about poverty and leaves homes deserted."

And he, peace be upon him, said: The earth has not cried out to its Lord, Mighty and Majestic, as it cries out because of three things: unlawful blood that is shed upon it, bathing from zina, and sleeping upon it before the rising of the sun.

4980 - And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: “Yaʿqūb said to his son Yūsuf عليه السلام: ‘O my son, do not commit fornication, for if a bird were to commit fornication, its feathers would scatter.’”

4981 - And ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: It was among what Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام: O Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, whoever commits adultery will have adultery committed against him, even if it be among his descendants after him. O Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, be chaste and your family will remain chaste. O Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, if you desire that the good of your household increase, then beware of adultery. O Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, as you deal, so shall you be dealt with.

4982 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ascended the pulpit and said: "Three Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment, nor will He look at them... nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment." An old man who commits adultery, a tyrannical king, and a poor person who is arrogant.

4983 - And in the narration of Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: "Three people Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: the old man who commits adultery, the dayyūth, and the woman who lets her husband's bed be approached."

And ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī narrated from Bashīr, who said: I read in some of the books: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "I do not grant My mercy to one who exposes Me to false oaths, nor do I bring near to Me on the Day of Resurrection one who was an adulterer."
And the Imam (peace be upon him) said: "Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you. Remain chaste concerning the women of others, and your women will remain chaste."

And in the narration of Ibrahim ibn Abi Al-Bilad, he said: There was a woman during the time of Dawud (peace be upon him) to whom a man would come, forcing himself upon her. So Allah, the Exalted and Almighty, inspired her heart, and she said to him: 'You do not come to me once except that there is someone with your family.' So the man went to his family and found a man with his family. He brought that man to Dawud (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, something has happened to me that has not happened to anyone else.' He said: 'And what is that?' He replied: 'I found this man with my family.' So Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Tell him' As you deal, so shall you be dealt with.

4987 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “When the fornicator commits fornication, the spirit of faith departs from him; then if he seeks forgiveness, it returns to him.” He said: “And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘The fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, the drinker does not drink while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer.’” Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “My father عليه السلام used to say: ‘When the fornicator commits fornication, the spirit of faith separates from him.’” I said: “Does any part of faith remain in him, or has it been entirely stripped from him?” He said: “No, rather some of it remains in him; then when he rises from it, the spirit of faith returns to him.”
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a woman who was subjected to ifdaʾ that the diyyah is due.

And in Nawādir al-Ḥikmah, it is narrated that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: Regarding a man whose wife caused ifḍāʾ to his bondwoman with her hand, he ruled that she should be appraised at one value while sound and at another value while afflicted with ifḍāʾ, then he would make her liable for the difference between soundness and defect, and he compelled her to keep her because she was no longer suitable for men.

Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man poured hot water on another man's head, so his hair fell out and never grew back. He said: “The diyyah is upon him.”

And it is narrated from Salamah ibn Tammam, who said: A man poured a pot containing broth over another man's head, and his hair went away. They disputed over that before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he gave him a delay of one year. When his hair did not grow back, he ruled against him with the diyyah.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who kicked a woman in her private area, and she claimed that she no longer menstruates, while her menstruation had been regular. He said: 'She is observed for one year. If her menstruation returns, then nothing is required. But if it does not return, the man must pay one-third of her blood money for the damage to her menstruation and the harm caused to her womb.'

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What is your ruling regarding a man who struck a young woman on her abdomen, injuring her womb and disrupting her menstruation, and she stated that her menstruation had ceased because of that, while her menstruation had previously been regular? He عليه السلام said: “She is to be observed for one year. If her womb recovers and her menstruation returns to what it was, otherwise she is to take an oath, and the one who struck her must pay one-third of her diyyah for the damage to her womb and the cessation of her menstruation.”

Zur‘ah and ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Īsā narrated from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked him about a man who digs a well in his house or on his land. He said: “As for what he digs in his own property, there is no liability upon him. But as for what he digs in the road or in other than his property, then he is liable for whatever falls into it.”

And in the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a man among our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about bridges: are their owners liable for anything? He said: “No.”

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Whoever extends a water spout, or a drain, or drives a peg, or ties an animal, or digs a well in the path of the Muslims, and it strikes something so that it is damaged, then he is liable for it.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Hilāl narrated from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Among the rulings of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was: “The mine entails no liability, the well entails no liability, and the animal entails no liability.”

And Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a boy who entered the house of some people to play, then fell into their well. Are they liable? He said: They are not liable; but if they are under suspicion, they are liable.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: "Whoever causes harm to anything belonging to the path of the Muslims is liable for it."

And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about a thing that is placed on the road, and then a riding animal passes by it, becomes startled with its rider, and injures him. He said: "Everything that harms on the road of the Muslims, its owner is liable for whatever it causes."

Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man passing along one of the roads of the Muslims, and his animal strikes a person with its leg, so he said: He is not liable for what it strikes with its hind leg, but he is liable for what it strikes with its front legs, because its hind leg is behind him if he is riding. But if he is leading his animal, then by the permission of Allah, he controls its front legs and places them wherever he wishes.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning a man who mounted his servant upon an animal, and it trampled a man. He عليه السلام said: "The liability is upon its master."
And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated it, raising it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The owners of livestock are not liable for anything so long as the animals are left roaming freely.
And in the narration of al-Sakuni: Indeed, ʿAli عليه السلام used to hold the leader, the driver, and the rider liable.

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning an animal upon which there were two riders: if the animal killed a man or injured him, then he ruled that the compensation should be divided equally between the two riders.

And in the narration of Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام held the owner of the animal liable for what it trampled with its front legs and what it struck with its hind legs. So there is no liability upon him unless a person strikes it.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: The diyyah for the fetus, if its mother is struck and it falls from her womb before the soul is formed in it, is one hundred dinars, and it belongs to its heirs. And the diyyah of the deceased, if his head is cut off and his abdomen is split open, does not belong to his heirs; rather, it belongs to him apart from the heirs. I said: What is the difference between them? He said: The fetus is a future matter whose benefit is hoped for, whereas this one has already passed and his benefit has gone. So when mutilation is done to him after his death, the diyyah for the mutilation becomes for him, not for anyone else. Hajj is performed with it on his behalf, or with it the various acts of righteousness are carried out, such as charity and other than that. I said: If a man entered to dig for him a pit in which he would wash him, and the man became distracted while digging before him, then his shovel slipped in his hand and struck his abdomen and split it open, what is upon him? He said: If it was thus, then it is a mistake, and only expiation is upon him: the freeing of a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or charity to sixty poor persons, one mudd for each poor person according to the mudd of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.
And in the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, it is narrated that al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: "Severing the head of the deceased is more severe than severing the head of the living."

And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a man who severed the head of a deceased person, he said: "The blood money is upon him, because his sanctity in death is like his sanctity while he is alive."

And it is narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A deceased person whose head was cut off?” He said: “The diyah is upon him.” I said: “Then who takes his diyah?” He said: “The Imam. This belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And if his right hand or anything from his limbs is cut off, then the arsh is upon him for the Imam.”

5363 - Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī narrated from Muḥammad ibn Nājiyah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Any wet nurse of a people who kills their infant while she is asleep, by rolling over onto him and thereby killing him, then only the blood money is upon her from her own wealth if she had only taken up wet nursing in pursuit of honor and pride. But if she had only become a wet nurse because of poverty, then the blood money is upon her ʿāqilah.

Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who hired a wet nurse and gave her his child, and the child remained with her. Then the wet nurse went and hired another wet nurse, and the wet nurse disappeared with the child, so it was not known what had been done with him, and the wet nurse could not be matched in retaliation. He عليه السلام said: The full blood money is due. And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated it from Ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, similarly. And Ḥammād narrated it from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, similarly.

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a man who hired a wet nurse and entrusted his child to her. She disappeared with him for years, then came back with the child, and his mother claimed that she did not recognize him. He عليه السلام said: “They have no right to do that, so they must accept him, for the wet nurse is trusted.”

Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man came to another man. He said: “If he was muḥṣan, then execution is upon him; and if he was not muḥṣan, then the hadd punishment is upon him.” I said: Then what is upon the one to whom it was done? He said: “Execution is upon him in every case, whether he was muḥṣan or not muḥṣan.”

And in the narration of Hisham and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari: A group of women entered upon Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, and one woman among them asked him about sihaq (tribadism). So he said: "Its legal punishment is the legal punishment of the adulterer." A woman said: "Allah has not mentioned that in the Qur'an." He said: "Yes, indeed." She said: "Where is it?" He said: "They are the People of al-Rass."

And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ‘Ali عليه السلام said: If it were appropriate for anyone to be stoned twice, the one who commits liwat would be stoned.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim al-Bajalī narrated from Abū Khadījah, who said: It is not appropriate for two women to sleep under one blanket unless there is a barrier between them. If they do so, they are to be forbidden from that; then if they are found after the prohibition under one blanket, each one of them is to be lashed with a hadd punishment. If they are found a third time under one blanket, they are to receive the hadd punishment; and if they are found a fourth time under one blanket, they are to be killed. And when a man goes to his wife and she carries his semen, then performs musāḥaqah with her slave-girl by means of it and she becomes pregnant, the woman is to be stoned, the slave-girl is to be lashed, and the child is to be affiliated to his father.

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a thief who entered upon a woman to steal her belongings. When he had gathered the clothes, his desire overcame him, and he had intercourse with her. Then her son stirred, so he went to him and killed him with an axe that he had with him. When he had finished, he carried the clothes and went to leave, but she attacked him with the axe and killed him. The next day, his family came demanding retaliation for his blood. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "His associates who sought retaliation for his blood are liable for the blood money of the boy. The thief is liable, from what he left behind, for four thousand dirhams because he forced her regarding her private part, since he is a fornicator, and it is to be paid from his wealth. There is nothing against the woman for her killing him, because he was a thief."

Muhammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a thief who entered upon a pregnant woman and killed what was in her womb. Then the woman took a knife and stabbed him with it, and she killed him. He said: “The blood of the thief is void.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say regarding a man who sought to induce a woman to commit something unlawful against herself, and she threw a stone at him, striking a fatal spot. He عليه السلام said: “There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” And if she is brought before a just Imam, he will deem his blood without liability.
Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام: A man forces himself upon a woman. He said: “He is to be killed.”

5377 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Talhah ibn Zayd, from al-Fadl ibn Uthman, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: Regarding a man who is killed, then his head is found in one tribe, his middle, chest, and hands in another tribe, and the remainder in another tribe, he عليه السلام said: "His diyah is upon the one in whose tribe his chest and hands are found, and the salat (funeral prayer) is upon him."

And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was killed and his limbs were found scattered, how should the funeral prayer be performed for him? He said: The prayer should be performed over the part that contains his heart.

5051 - Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from al-Asbagh ibn al-Asbagh, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Misri narrated to me from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah or from Burayd al-Ijli—the doubt is from Muhammad—who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A slave committed zina. He said: "He is to be lashed half of the hadd." I said: Then if he repeats it? He said: "Then he is struck the same as that." He said: I said: Then if he repeats it? He said: "No more than half of the hadd is added upon him." He said: I said: Is stoning ever incumbent upon him for any of his acts? He said: "Yes, he is killed on the eighth [offense] if he does that eight times." He said: I said: What is the difference between him and the free man, when their act is one and the same? He said: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had mercy on him by not combining upon him the bond of slavery and the hadd of the free man." He said: Then he said: "And it is upon the Imam of the Muslims to pay his price to his master from the share of the riqab."

5052 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Harith ibn Al-Ahwal, from Burayd Al-ʿIjli, from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a slave woman who commits adultery, he عليه السلام said: "She is to be lashed half the prescribed punishment, whether she has a husband or does not have a husband."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: "The prescribed punishment of the umm al-walad is the prescribed punishment of the slave woman if she does not have a child."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Nuʿaym ibn Ibrahim, from Mismāʿ Abū Sayyār, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: “The liability of the umm al-walad concerning the rights of people is upon her master.” He عليه السلام said: “As for what is of the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the prescribed punishments, then that is upon her own body.” And he عليه السلام said: “Retaliation applies from her in favor of slaves, and there is no qisas between the free person and the slave.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: If a bondwoman of mine commits adultery, should I administer the prescribed punishment to her? He said: Yes, but let that be in secret, for I fear the ruler's authority over you.

And Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who had a slave woman, and the slave woman said to him, “Whatever I have paid of my emancipation contract, I am free in proportion to that.” So he said to her, “Yes.” Then she paid part of her emancipation contract, and her master had intercourse with her after that. He عليه السلام said: “If he forced her into that, he is to be struck with the hadd punishment in proportion to what she has paid of her emancipation contract, and the hadd punishment is averted from him in proportion to what remained for him of her emancipation contract. And if she complied with him, she was his partner in the hadd punishment and is to be struck the like of what he is struck.”

Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: Concerning a slave jointly owned by two men, one of whom freed his share, then the slave committed an offense involving one of the prescribed limits of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, he said: If, when half of the slave was freed, he had been appraised so that the one who freed him would be made to pay half of his value, then half of him is free: he is to receive half the hadd of a free person and half the hadd of a slave. But if he had not been appraised, then he is a slave and is to receive the hadd of a slave.

And ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr al-Baṣrī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said: Regarding two mukātab slaves, if they commit fornication, they are to be struck with the hadd of a free person in proportion to what they have paid of their manumission contract, and for the remainder they are struck with the hadd of a slave.

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who intentionally killed another man, then fled, and could not be apprehended until he died. He عليه السلام said: “If he had wealth, it is taken from it; otherwise, it is taken from the closest relatives, then the next closest.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a man who is apprehended while multiple hudud are due upon him, one of them being execution. He said: "ʿAlī عليه السلام used to carry out the hudud upon him first, then execute him, and do not oppose ʿAlī عليه السلام."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: For the al-mudiḥah, there are five camels. For the as-simḥaq, which is below the al-mudiḥah, there are four camels. For the al-munaqqilah, there are fifteen camels. For the al-jaʾifah, there is one-third of the blood money: thirty-three camels. And for the al-maʾmumah, there is one-third of the blood money.
And in the narration of Ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For the bāḍiʿah, there are three camels.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn Razīn, from Dharīḥ al-Muḥāribī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whom one person wounded with a muḍiḥah wound and another wounded with a dāmiyah wound in a single incident, and then the man died. He عليه السلام said: "The diyah is upon both of them from their property, in two equal halves."

Ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn Hayy, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the muḍiḥah in the head, whether it is like it is in the face. He said: “The muḍiḥah and the shijaj in the face and the head are equal in the diyyah, because the face is part of the head; and injuries in the body are not like they are in the head.”

And in the narration of Aban, he said: "Al-ja'ifah is that which enters the inner cavity; there is no qisas for its victim, only hukumah. Al-munaqqilah, from which the bones are displaced, there is no qisas in it, only hukumah. And in al-ma'mumah there is one-third of the diyah; there is no qisas in it, only hukumah."
And in the narration of al-Sakūnī: Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that for the hāshimah, the compensation is ten camels.
And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Regarding a slave who inflicted a muḍiḥah wound upon one man and then inflicted another upon a second, he said: “It is between them.”

ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Saʿd al-Iskāf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a slave girl who rode upon another slave girl. Then another slave girl prodded her, so the one being ridden bucked and threw down the rider, and she died. So he ruled that her diyah be divided into two halves between the one who prodded and the one who was prodded.

And it is narrated from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Whoever kills a close relative of a people, then let him seek reconciliation with them as much as he is able, for that is lighter for his reckoning.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from al-Thumālī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said: If a man strikes another man with a whip, Allah will strike him with a whip of fire.

And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The diyah for a hunting dog is forty dirhams, and the diyah for a livestock dog is twenty dirhams. And the diyah for a dog that is neither for hunting nor for livestock is a basket of dirt; the killer must give it, and its owner must accept it.

5392 - And Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Abū al-Jārūd, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “The mule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was not turned back from anything it entered.” He said: “Then a man from Banū Mudlij came while it had entered a reed field belonging to him, so he fitted an arrow for it and killed it.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him: “By Allah, you shall not leave me until you pay compensation for it.” He said: “So he compensated for it with six hundred dirhams.”

And Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام: Regarding a man who broke another man’s hand, and then the man’s hand healed, he عليه السلام said: “There is no qisas in this case, but he must give al-arsh.”

5394 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn al-Rawwasi, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: A woman fears pregnancy, so she drinks medicine and casts out what is in her womb. He said: "No." So I said: It is only a drop of fluid. He said: "Indeed, the first thing that is created is a drop of fluid."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Dawud ibn 'Ali asked me about a man who used to come to another man's house, and he forbade him from coming to his house, but he refused to comply. So he went to the ruler, and the ruler said, 'If he does it, then kill him.' He said: 'So he killed him. What do you think about it?' I said: 'I hold that he should not kill him. If this were upheld, then any person could wish to say of his enemy: he entered my house, so I killed him.'

And in the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said: If the guardian of the slain person dies, his child takes his place after him regarding the blood claim.

Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled concerning the eye of a horse that was gouged out that the compensation is one quarter of its price on the day the eye was gouged out.

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding four persons who were partners in a camel. One of them hobbled it, then the camel moved off, toyed with its hobble, fell down, and was injured. So his companions said to the one who had hobbled it, “Compensate us for our camel.” So he عليه السلام judged between them that they must compensate him for his share, because he had secured his share, and their shares were lost along with his share.

And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, through his chain of transmission, he said: A man was brought before al-Maʾmūn who had pushed another man into a well and he died, so he ordered that he be killed. The man said: “I was in my house when I heard the cry for help, so I came out quickly with my sword. I passed by this man while he was at the edge of a well, so I pushed him and he fell into the well.” Al-Maʾmūn asked the jurists about that. Some of them said retaliation should be taken against him, and some of them said this and that should be done to him. So he asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about that and wrote to him, and he replied: “His blood money is upon the people of the cry for help, those who shouted for help.” He said: The jurists considered that very grave, and they said to al-Maʾmūn: “Ask him from where you said this.” So he asked, and he عليه السلام said: “A woman once sought judgment from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام against a wind. She said: ‘I was on top of my house, and a wind pushed me so I fell into the courtyard and my hand was broken.’ So Sulaymān عليه السلام summoned the wind and said to it: ‘What made you do what you did to this woman?’ The wind said: ‘O Prophet of Allah, the ship of such-and-such people was in the sea, and its people were on the verge of drowning. I passed by this woman while I was hurrying, so she fell and her hand was broken.’ Then Sulaymān عليه السلام ruled that the compensation for her hand was upon the people of the ship.”

And in the narration of Abān ibn ʿUthmān: That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a man who had killed another man's brother. So he handed him over to him and ordered him to kill him. The man struck him until he thought that he had killed him. Then he was carried to his home, and they found in him some remaining life, so they treated him until he recovered. When he came out, the brother of the first slain man seized him and said: “You are the killer of my brother, and I have the right to kill you.” He said to him: “You have already killed me once.” So he took him to ʿUmar, and he ordered that he be killed. Then he went out while saying: “O people, by Allah, he has already killed me once.” Then they passed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ, and informed him of his case, so he said: “Do not hasten against him until I come out to you.” Then he, peace be upon him, entered upon ʿUmar and said: “The ruling concerning him is not like this.” He said: “What is it, O Abā al-Ḥasan?” He said: “This one should exact retribution from the brother of the first slain man for what he did to him, then he should kill him for his brother.” So the man thought that if he exacted retribution from him, it would finish him off, so he pardoned him, and they let one another go.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Muqatil ibn Sulayman from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "I am the master of the prophets, and my successor is the master of the successors, and his successors are the masters of the successors. Indeed, Adam عليه السلام asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to appoint for him a righteous successor, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him. "Indeed I have honored the prophets with prophethood, then I selected from My creation a creation, and I made the best of them the successors." So Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, revealed to him: "O Adam, appoint Seth as your successor." Then Adam عليه السلام appointed Seth, and he was Hibat Allah, son of Adam. Seth appointed his son Shabban, and he was the son of Nazlah al-Hawra', whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down upon Adam from Paradise, and he married her to his son Seth. Shabban appointed Mahlath, and Mahlath appointed Mahuq, and Mahuq appointed Ghathmisha, and Ghathmisha appointed Akhnukh, and he was Idris the Prophet عليه السلام. Idris appointed Nahur, and Nahur passed it to Nuh عليه السلام. Nuh appointed Sam, and Sam appointed Athamir, and Athamir appointed Barghithasha, and Barghithasha appointed Yafith, and Yafith appointed Barrah, and Barrah appointed Jafsiyyah, and Jafsiyyah appointed Imran, and Imran passed it to Ibrahim al-Khalil عليه السلام. Ibrahim appointed his son Ismail, and Ismail appointed Ishaq, and Ishaq appointed Yaqub, and Yaqub appointed Yusuf, and Yusuf appointed Bathriya', and Bathriya' appointed Shu'ayb, and Shu'ayb passed it to Musa ibn Imran عليه السلام. Musa ibn Imran appointed Yusha' ibn Nun, and Yusha' ibn Nun appointed Dawud, and Dawud appointed Sulayman عليه السلام. Sulayman appointed Asif ibn Barkhiya, and Asif ibn Barkhiya appointed Zakariyya, and Zakariyya passed it to Isa ibn Maryam عليه السلام. Isa ibn Maryam appointed Sham'un ibn Hammun al-Safa, and Sham'un appointed Yahya ibn Zakariyya, and Yahya ibn Zakariyya appointed Mundhir, and Mundhir appointed Sulaymah, and Sulaymah appointed Burdah." "Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Burdah passed it to me, and I pass it to you, O Ali. And you will pass it to your successor, and your successor will pass it to your successors from your offspring, one after another, until it is passed to the best of the people of the earth

5403 - Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir عليه السلام, who said: "Indeed, the name of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in the scriptures of Ibrahim is al-Mahi, in the Torah of Musa al-Hadd, in the Gospel of Isa Ahmad, and in the Furqan Muhammad." It was said: "What is the interpretation of al-Mahi?" He said: "Al-Mahi [is the eraser of] the form of idols, the remover of idols and divining arrows, and of every object worshipped besides al-Rahman." And it was said: "What is the interpretation of al-Hadd?" He said: "He opposes whoever opposes Allah and His religion, whether near or far." It was said: "What is the interpretation of Ahmad?" He said: "The praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for him in the scriptures is beautiful, because of the praiseworthy deeds for which he was praised." It was said: "What is the interpretation of Muhammad?" He said: "Indeed Allah, His angels, all His Prophets, His Messengers, and all their communities praise him and send blessings upon him, and indeed his name written upon the Throne is: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And he عليه السلام used to wear Yemeni caps, white caps, and striped headgear with two flaps in wars. He had a short spear upon which he would lean, and he would bring it out on the two Eids and deliver the sermon with it. He had a rod called al-Mamshuq, a tent called al-Kinn, a bowl called al-Sa'ah, and a drinking vessel called al-Riyy. He had two horses, one called al-Murtajiz and the other al-Sakb; two mules, one called al-Duldul and the other al-Shahba'; two she-camels, one called al-'Adhba' and the other al-Jad'a'; two swords, one called Dhu al-Faqar and the other al-'Awn; and two other swords, one called al-Mikhdham and the other al-Rasum. He had a donkey called al-Ya'fur, a turban called al-Sahab, a coat of armor called Dhat al-Fudul with three silver rings, one in front of it and two behind it, a banner called al-'Uqab, a camel used for carrying loads called al-Dibaj, a standard called al-Ma'lum, and a helmet called al-As'ad. So he delivered all of that to Ali عليه السلام at the time of his death, and he took out his ring and placed it on his finger. Then Ali عليه السلام mentioned that he found in the hilt of one of his swords a sheet containing three phrases: "Maintain ties with one who cuts you off; speak the truth

Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad al-Baṣrī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥakam, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Indeed, ʿAlī is my legatee and my khalifah, and his wife Fāṭimah, my daughter, is the leader of the women of the worlds. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the leaders of the youths of the people of Paradise, and they are my two sons. Whoever befriends them has befriended me; whoever opposes them has opposed me; whoever shows hostility to them has shown hostility to me; whoever shuns them has shunned me; and whoever honors them has honored me. Allah maintains ties with whoever maintains ties with them, severs whoever severs from them, supports whoever aids them, and forsakes whoever forsakes them. O Allah, for whoever among Your Prophets and Messengers had entrusted ones and a household, then ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn are my Ahl al-Bayt and my entrusted ones; so remove defilement from them and purify them with a thorough purification.

And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: I heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say to ʿAlī عليه السلام: “O ʿAlī, you are my legatee; I have entrusted to you by the command of my Lord, and you are my successor; I have appointed you as successor by the command of my Lord. O ʿAlī, you are the one who will make clear to my Ummah that wherein they differ after me, and you will stand among them in my place. Your word is my word, your command is my command, obedience to you is obedience to me, and obedience to me is obedience to Allah; and disobedience to you is disobedience to me, and disobedience to me is disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Kūfī narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān al-Nakhaʿī, from his uncle al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī al-Qāsim, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “The Imams after me are twelve. The first of them is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and the last of them is al-Qāʾim. They are my successors, my trustees, my authorities, and the proofs of Allah over my ummah after me. The one who acknowledges them is a believer, and the one who denies them is a disbeliever.”

And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has one hundred and twenty-four thousand prophets. I am their master, their most excellent, and their most honored before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And every prophet had a successor whom he designated by the command of Allah, exalted is His mention. Verily, my successor, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, is surely their master, their most excellent, and their most honored before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī, who said: I entered upon Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and before her was a tablet in which were the names of the successors from her offspring. I counted twelve; one of them was al-Qāʾim. Three of them were Muḥammad, and four of them were ʿAlī عليه السلام.
Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the bequest, and he said: “It is a duty upon every Muslim.”

Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Making a bequest is a right and an established matter, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله indeed made a will; therefore, it is appropriate for the Muslim to make a bequest.

Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام said: “Bequesting one-fifth is recommended, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has been pleased for Himself with one-fifth.” And he said: “One-fifth is moderation, one-fourth is exertion, and one-third is unfairness.”

Hammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who dies, how much of his wealth belongs to him. He عليه السلام said to him: "One-third of his wealth, and the same applies to the woman as well."

And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام used to say: “That I bequeath one-fifth of my wealth is more beloved to me than that I bequeath one-fourth, and that I bequeath one-fourth is more beloved to me than that I bequeath one-third. Whoever bequeaths one-third and leaves nothing behind has gone to excess.” And he said: “Whoever bequeaths one-third of his wealth and leaves nothing behind has reached the utmost limit.”

And in the narration of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, he said: Whoever bequeaths one-third has harmed the heirs, and bequeathing one-fifth or one-fourth is better than bequeathing one-third. And he said: Whoever bequeaths one-third has not left anything behind.

Aṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn ruled concerning a man who died and bequeathed all of his wealth, or most of it, saying: “The bequest is to be returned to what is proper, and the inheritance of the inheritors is to be left for them.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Murāzim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The deceased has the greatest right to his wealth so long as the soul remains in him and he is able to express himself by it. He عليه السلام said: But if he exceeds, then he is entitled only to one-third.

And Hārūn ibn Muslim narrated from Mas‘adah ibn Ṣadaqah al-Raba‘ī, from Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام: That a man from the Anṣār passed away, and he had young children, and he had six slaves. So he freed them at the time of his death, and he had no property other than them. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was approached and informed, so he said: What did you do with your companion? They said: We buried him. He said: Had I known, I would not have had him buried among the people of Islam. He left his children begging from the people.

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr al-Anṣārī was in al-Madīnah, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was in Makkah. When death approached him, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Muslims were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr instructed that his face be turned toward the direction of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, toward the qiblah. He also bequeathed one-third of his wealth, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be established by that.

And it is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq: He wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that Durrah bint Muqātil had died and left an estate consisting of shares in such-and-such a place. She had bequeathed to our master, from her shares, more than one-third, and we are her executors. We wished to convey that to our master, so if he commands us to carry out the bequest in the manner it stands, we will carry it out; and if he commands us otherwise, we will comply with his command in all that he commands us, if Allah, Most High, wills. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: "No more than one-third is binding for her in her estate. But if you show generosity, and you are the heirs, then it is permissible for you, if Allah wills."

And Ṣafwān narrated from Murāzim, from some of our companions: Regarding a man who gives something from his wealth during his illness He said: “If he makes it distinct and hands it over, then it is valid; but if he bequeaths it, then it is from the one-third.”

Hadith 5431 — ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥāzim al-Kalbī, the nephew of Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar — and he was not al-Jaʿfarī — from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever does not make his bequest well at the time of death, that is a deficiency in his dignity and intellect.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, how does the dying person make a bequest?” He said: “When his death comes near and the people gather around him, he says:” “O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. O Allah, I make a covenant with You in the abode of this world that I bear witness that there is no god but You, alone, without partner; and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; and that Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and that resurrection is true, and reckoning is true, and the sirat is true, and divine decree and the scale are true; and that the religion is as You have described, and that Islam is as You have legislated, and that the word is as You have conveyed, and that the Qur’an is as You have sent down, and that You are Allah, the Manifest Truth. May Allah reward Muḥammad on our behalf with the best reward, and may Allah greet Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad with peace. O Allah, O my provision at my distress, O my companion at my hardship, O guardian of my blessing, my God and the God of my forefathers, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, for if You leave me to myself, I would be nearer to evil and farther from good. So bring intimacy to my loneliness in the grave, and appoint for me a covenant spread open on the day I meet You.” Then he makes bequest concerning his need. The confirmation of this bequest is in the Qur’an, in the surah in which Maryam is mentioned, in His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “They do not possess intercession except one who has taken a covenant with the All-beneficent.” So this is the covenant of the dying person, and the bequest is a duty upon every Muslim, and it is incumbent upon him to preserve this bequest and teach it. And Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib صلوات الله عليه said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله taught it to me.” And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام t

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated; he said: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Thābit, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: “O ʿAlī, I counsel you regarding traits for yourself, so preserve them.” Then he said: “O Allah, help him. As for the first, it is truthfulness, and never let a lie ever come out of your mouth. The second is waraʿ, such that you never dare commit betrayal. The third is fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as though you see Him. The fourth is abundant weeping out of fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; with every tear, a house will be built for you in Paradise. The fifth is to give your wealth and your blood for the sake of your religion. The sixth is to follow my sunnah in my salat, my fasting, and my charity. As for the salat, it is fifty rakʿahs. As for fasting, it is three days in every month: a Thursday in its beginning, a Wednesday in its middle, and a Thursday in its end. As for charity, it is your utmost effort, until you say: I have been excessive, though you have not been excessive. And adhere to the night prayer, and adhere to the night prayer, and adhere to the night prayer. And adhere to the salat of zawāl. And adhere to recitation of the Qur'an in every state. And adhere to raising your hands in the salat and turning them both. And adhere to the siwāk at every wudu for every salat. And adhere to the noble traits of character, so adopt them; and the blameworthy ones, so avoid them. For if you do not do that, then blame none but yourself.”

5433 - It is narrated from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, who said: I witnessed the وصيّة of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام when he entrusted authority to his son al-Ḥasan, and made al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad, all of his children, the leaders of his Ahl al-Bayt, and his Shiʿah witnesses to his وصيّة. Then he handed over to him the book and the weapon, then he said عليه السلام: “O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded me to bequeath to you and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon; and he commanded me to instruct you that when death comes to you, you should hand it over to your brother al-Ḥusayn.” He said: then he turned to his son al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام and said: “And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded you to hand it over to your son ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.” Then he turned to his son ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and said: “And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded you to hand your وصيّة to your son Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, so convey to him salām from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and from me.” Then he turned to his son al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said: “O my son, you are the guardian of the affair and the guardian of the blood. If you pardon, that is yours; and if you kill, then one blow in place of one blow, and do not sin.” Then he said: “Write:” “In the Name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.” This is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib bequeathed: he testifies that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent “with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it.” Then: “Indeed, my salat, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner, and with that I have been commanded,” and I am of the Muslims. Then I advise you, O Ḥasan, and all my children, my Ahl al-Bayt, and every believer whom my writing reaches, to have taqwa of Allah your Lord: “and do not die except while you are Muslims; and hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah and do not become divided; and remember Allah’s blessing upon you when you were enemies and He joined your hearts together.” For I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sa

Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: O you who believe, the witness between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of bequest, shall be two just men from among you, or two others from outside of you. He said: “They are two disbelievers.” I said: “Two just men from among you?” He said: “Two Muslims.”

And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding the testimony of a woman who was present when a man was making a will, and there was no man with her, he عليه السلام said: “Her testimony is accepted for one-fourth of the bequest.”

And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: O you who believe, the testimony between you, when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest, shall be of two just men from among you, or two others from other than you. He said: The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from other than you are from the People of the Book. If you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because among the Magians there is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the People of the Book regarding the jizyah. That is when a man dies in a foreign land and two Muslims are not found; then two men from the People of the Book are taken as witnesses and are detained after the ʿAṣr prayer. Then they shall swear by Allah, if you doubt: We shall not sell it for any price, even if he were a near relative, nor shall we conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, then we would surely be among the sinful. He said: And that is if the guardian of the deceased doubts their testimony. If it is discovered that they testified falsely, then he has no right to invalidate their testimony until he brings two witnesses who stand in the place of the first two witnesses. Then they shall swear by Allah: Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; indeed, then we would surely be among the wrongdoers. So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated, and the testimony of the latter two is accepted. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: That is more likely that they will give testimony in its proper manner, or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths. .
Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The first thing to be taken care of from the wealth is the shroud, then the debt, then the will, then the inheritance.

And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Indeed, the debt comes before the will, then the will follows after the debt, then the inheritance comes after the will. For the foremost matter to be fulfilled is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: The shroud is to be provided from the entirety of the wealth.
And he, peace be upon him, said: The shroud of a woman is upon her husband if she dies.

5441 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said: I asked him about a man who died while owing a debt equal to the price of his shroud. He said: "What he left behind should be used for the price of his shroud, unless some people undertake it for him, then they shroud him, and what he owed is paid from what he left behind."
The author of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The report that was narrated is: “There is no bequest for an heir.”

And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who gives preference to some of his children over others. He said: “Yes, and his wives as well.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Baṣrī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Inform me about the qawwād; what is his prescribed punishment?" He said: "There is no hadd upon the qawwād. Is it not that he is only given payment for facilitating?" I said: "May I be your ransom, he is only bringing together a male and a female unlawfully." He said: "That is the one who brings together a male and a female unlawfully." So I said: "That is indeed the one, may I be your ransom." He said: "He is to be struck with three-quarters of the hadd of the fornicator—seventy-five lashes—and he is to be exiled from the town in which he is."
And in another report: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, cursed al-wāṣilah and al-muttaṣilah.

Hammad ibn ʿIsa narrated from Ribʿi ibn ʿAbdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: If a man appoints someone as his executor while that person is absent, then he does not have the right to reject his bequest. And if he appoints him while he is in the town, then he has the choice: if he wishes he accepts, and if he wishes he does not accept.

And Ribʿī narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man to whom a bequest/executorship is entrusted, He said: “If it is sent to him from another town, then he has no right to refuse it. But if he is in a city in which someone else besides him is found, then that is up to him.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from ʿAli ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man whose father called him to accept his bequest. Does he have the right to refrain from accepting his father’s bequest? So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “He does not have the right to refuse.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who entrusts another man with a bequest, and he dislikes accepting it. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “He should not abandon him in this situation.”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man entrusts a bequest to his brother while he is absent, then he has no right to reject his executorship, because if he had been present and refused to accept it, he would have sought someone else.

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: When a boy reaches ten years of age, his bequest becomes valid.

5451 - And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “When ten years have passed over the boy, then whatever he does with his wealth—whether he frees a slave, gives charity, or makes a bequest within a known limit and in a rightful matter—is valid.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abī al-Maghrāʾ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: If a boy reaches ten years of age and makes a bequest of one-third of his wealth for a rightful cause, his bequest is valid. And if he is seven years old and bequeaths a small amount of his wealth for a rightful cause, his bequest is valid.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام say: “If a boy is approached by death and he makes a bequest before reaching maturity, his bequest is valid for blood relatives, and it is not valid for strangers.”

Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I entered upon Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and his tongue had become paralyzed, so I instructed him to make his will, but he did not respond. He said: So I ordered a basin, then I put sand in it, and it was placed before him. Then I said to him, 'Write with your hand,' so he wrote his will with his hand in the sand, and I copied it onto a sheet.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Ashʿarī narrated from al-Sindī ibn Muḥammad, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Maryam, who mentioned it from his father: Umāmah bint Abī al-ʿĀṣ—whose mother was Zaynab bint Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله—was married to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام after Fāṭimah عليها السلام. After ʿAlī عليه السلام, al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nawfal succeeded him as her husband. He mentioned that she became severely ill until her tongue was restrained, so al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, the two sons of ʿAlī عليهما السلام, came to her while she was unable to speak. They began speaking to her, while al-Mughīrah disliked that. "Did you free so-and-so and his family?" She began indicating with her head, yes. "And such-and-such?" She again began indicating with her head that yes, while not speaking clearly, so that was deemed valid for her.

And it was narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, who said: I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A man wrote a document in his own handwriting, but he did not say to his heirs, "This is my will," nor did he say, "I have made a bequest." Rather, he only wrote a document containing what he wished to bequeath. Is it obligatory upon his heirs to carry out what is in the document in his handwriting, even though he did not command them to do so? So he عليه السلام wrote: "If he has children, they are to carry out everything they find in their father's document, whether in the way of righteousness or otherwise."

Al-Hasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The one who makes a bequest has the right to go back on it and make changes in his bequest as long as he is alive.

And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “The one making a will has the right to revoke it, whether he is in good health or ill.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Miskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that the mudabbar is from the one-third, and that a man may revoke his bequest, adding to it or reducing from it, so long as he has not died.

And in the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, with his chain of transmission, he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said: “A man may alter his bequest: he may free the one whom he had ordered to be given ownership, and give ownership to the one whom he had ordered to be freed; and he may give to the one whom he had deprived, and deprive the one whom he had given to, so long as he has not retracted from it.”

Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made a bequest of his wealth in the way of Allah. So he said: "Give it to the one for whom he made the bequest, even if he is a Jew or a Christian. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:" "But whoever changes it after hearing it, then its sin is only upon those who change it."

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: A man in Hamadhan mentioned that his father had passed away, and he was unaware of this matter, so he made a will at the time of death, instructing that something be given in the way of Allah. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how it should be done, and we informed him that the deceased was unaware of this matter but had made a will at the time of death. He said: 'If a man had made a will to me to place his wealth with a Jew or a Christian, I would place it with them. Indeed, Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, says: So whoever changes it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. Look for someone who is engaged in these paths (meaning the frontier defense posts), and send it to him.

5464 - It was narrated from Abū Ṭālib ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣalt al-Qummī that he said: Al-Khalīl ibn Hāshim wrote to Dhū al-Riʾāsatayn, who was the governor of Naysābūr, that a man from the Magians had died and bequeathed something from his wealth to the poor. The executor in Naysābūr took it and distributed it among the poor Muslims. So al-Khalīl wrote to Dhū al-Riʾāsatayn about that, and he asked al-Maʾmūn about it. He said, 'I have nothing on this matter.' Then he asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: "The Magian did not bequeath it to the poor Muslims. Rather, an amount equal to that wealth should be taken from the charity funds and returned to the poor among the Magians."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Jabalah narrated from Samāʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man who has children—does it lie within his right to assign his wealth to his relatives? He said: “It is his wealth; he may dispose of it as he wishes until death comes to him.”

And the confirmation of this is what Ṣafwān narrated from Murāzim regarding a man who gives something from his wealth during his illness. He said: 'If he clearly transfers it (during his lifetime), then it is valid. However, if he bequeaths it (for after his death), then it is only from one-third of his wealth.'

5468 - As for the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Thaʿlabah, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAmr ibn Shaddād al-Azdī, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man has the greatest right over his wealth so long as the soul remains in him. If he bequeaths all of it, then it is permissible for him.

And the confirmation of that is what was narrated by Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him: That he was asked about a man who dies while having no heir and no ʿaṣabah. He said: “He may bequeath his wealth wherever he wishes among the Muslims, the poor, and the wayfarer.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: A man appointed two individuals as executors of his will. Is it permissible for one of them to act independently with half of the estate and the other with the other half? So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: "It is not appropriate for them to go against the deceased, and they should act according to what he instructed them, if Allah wills."

5472 - In the book of Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah have mercy on him: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from his two brothers Muḥammad and Aḥmad, from their father, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: A man died and appointed two men as executors. One of them said to his companion, “Take half of what he left, and give me half of what he left.” But the other refused him. So they asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about that, and he said: “That belongs to him.”

Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them: He was asked about a man who made a bequest of something from his wealth, so he said: "The thing, in the Book of ʿAlī, peace be upon him, is one out of six."

Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: He was asked about a man who bequeaths a share of his wealth, so he said: The share is one out of eight, based on the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. "Indeed, the charities are only for the poor, the needy, those employed over them, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, for freeing slaves, for those in debt, in the way of Allah, and the stranded traveler."
And it has been narrated: "The share is one out of six."

And Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth, so he said: 'A portion is one-tenth.' Allah, the Almighty, said: 'Then place on every mountain a portion of them,' and the mountains were ten.
Al-Bazanti narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth. He said: "It is one-seventh of his one-third."

Everything in this book that is narrated from Khalid ibn Najeeh, I have transmitted from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Khālid ibn Najeeh al-Jawwān.

And everything in it that is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri, I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Hasan ibn Matil Al-Daqqaq, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri.

Whatever is in it from Zurārah ibn Aʿyun, I have narrated it from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, al-Ḥasan ibn Ẓarīf, and ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, all of them from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyun.
Likewise, whatever was in Hāʾ from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, I have transmitted it through this chain of transmission.
Likewise, whatever was in it from Hammad ibn Isa.

And whatever was in it from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashīm, I have narrated it from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Mājīlawayh—may Allah be pleased with him—from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Qāsim, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashīm.

And whatever is in it from Ali ibn Maṭar, I have narrated it from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar Al-Hamadani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ali ibn Maṭar.

Everything in this book that is from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muslim, I have narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with him—from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf and Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Saʿd together, from Saʿdān ibn Muslim.

As for what is in it from al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, I have transmitted it from my father, and Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Mājīlawayh; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Ibrāhīm—may Allah be pleased with them—from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt.

And whatever is in it from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni - may Allah have mercy on him - I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Asam Al-Kulayni, and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Sanani - may Allah be pleased with them - from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni; and likewise all of the book Al-Kafi, I have narrated it from them from him through his transmitters.

And whatever is narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, I have narrated it from my father; and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah; and Al-Himyari; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, and Ahmad ibn Idris, all together from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab Al-Zayyat, and the name of Abi Al-Khattab is Zayd.

And whatever is in it from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Khaffāf, I have narrated it from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillah, from al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Thābit, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Khaffāf.
The chains of transmission for the book Man La Yahḍuruhu al-Faqih have been completed by the praise of Allah and His favor, and blessings be upon Muḥammad and his pure family.

Usul al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said: I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying: The friend of every man is his intellect, and his enemy is his ignorance.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): We have a group who have love (for us), but they do not have that firm resolve, though they profess this belief? He (peace be upon him) said: Those are not those whom Allah admonished; rather, Allah said: So take lesson, O men of insight.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Dawud ibn Farqad who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: My companions are the people of discernment and god-consciousness, so whoever is not from the people of discernment and god-consciousness, then he is not from my companions.

Ali, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: We were with al-Ridha (peace be upon him) when we began discussing the intellect and moral virtue, so he said: O Abu Hashim, the intellect is a free gift from Allah while virtue is an effortful acquisition, whoever strives to acquire virtue is able to possess it but whoever strives to acquire intellect he achieves naught by that except further ignorance.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I hear the narration from you, so do I add and decrease (words)? He said: If you intend its meanings, then there is no harm.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A group of people come to me and listen to your narrations from me, but I become weary and do not have the strength.' He said: 'Then read for them from the beginning of it a narration, and from the middle a narration, and from the end a narration.'

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the soul reaches here – and he pointed with his hand to his throat – there will be no repentance for the scholar, Then he recited: 'Verily repentance is upon Allah only for those who work evil in ignorance'

Al-Khasa'is: From his father, who said: From al-Himyari, from Harun, from Ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). That Ali (peace be upon him) said: There is in Hell a millstone which grinds – will you not ask what it grinds? It was said to him: And what does it grind, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: Corrupt scholars, and sinful reciters, and unjust tyrants, and treacherous ministers, and lying officials. And there is in Hell a city called 'The Fortified' – will you not ask me what is in it? It was said: And what is in it, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: In it are the hands of the oath-breakers.

Ma'ani al-Akhbar: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) In the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the poets – only the astray follow them.' He said: Have you seen anyone following a poet? Rather, they are a group who gained understanding (became learned) for the sake of something other than the religion, so they themselves went astray and caused others to go astray.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The best assistant to faith is knowledge, and the best assistant to knowledge is forbearance, and the best assistant to forbearance is gentleness, and the best assistant to gentleness is patience.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muammar ibn Khallad who said: I heard Aba al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: Worship is not the abundance of prayer and fasting; rather, worship is reflecting upon the affair of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: Preserve your books, for you will have need of them.
