Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Arabize our narrations, for we are an eloquent people.

From the father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Tha'laba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Men are of three kinds: a man by his wealth, a man by his status/prestige, and a man by his tongue, and he is the best of the three.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Abi Ubayda al-Hadhdha, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever gives fatwa to the people without knowledge or true guidance, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment curse him, and the burden of the one who acts by his fatwa attaches to him.

Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was seated in the study-circle of Rabia al-Rayy, when a bedouin came and asked Rabia al-Rayy about a matter, and he answered him. When he fell silent, the bedouin said to him: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent and did not reply to him with anything. He repeated the question to him, and he answered him in the same way. The bedouin said to him again: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is upon his neck.' He said: 'Did he not say: And every giver of Fatwa is liable?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Say what you know, and if you do not know then say: 'Allah is more knowing.' Indeed, a man may pick out a verse from the Qur'an and fall into it (misinterpret it) a distance farther than what is between the sky and the earth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the right of Allah over His creation? He said: That they should say what they know, and refrain from what they do not know, so if they do that, they have fulfilled the right of Allah.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: And what do you have to do with analogical reasoning (qiyas)? Verily, those who perished before you perished because of analogical reasoning. Then he said: If that which you know comes to you, then speak it; and if that which you do not know comes to you, then [point] here – and he pointed with his hand to his mouth …

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, Allah has given us understanding in the religion and made us self-sufficient through you from the people, so much so that a group of us in a gathering, one man asks his companion about a matter that comes to his mind and receives an answer for it, which is from the mercy of Allah upon us through you; however, it may happen that something is referred to us about which we have received nothing from you or your forefathers, so can we look for the best-match in what we have and the closest to that which has come down to us from you and take it [as the answer]? So he said: Not at all, not at all, in doing that — by Allah — were destroyed those who were destroyed, O Ibn Hakim. Then he said: May Allah curse Abu Hanifa, he used to say: 'Ali said, but I say.' Muhammad ibn Hakim then reported to Hisham ibn al-Hakam that: By Allah, I did not want anything [in asking this] except that he permit Qiyas (analogical reasoning) for me.

Ma'ani al-Akhbar and al-Amali: Muhammad ibn Ali Majlawayh narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from his brother, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: … The believer takes his religion from his Lord and does not take it from his own opinion …

Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words based on his opinion.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi Basir who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Things are referred to us which we do not know in the Book of Allah nor the Sunna, should we exercise reason in them? He said: No, for indeed if you were to get it right you would not be rewarded, and if you were to err you would have lied upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Tawhid al-Saduq: From Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdallah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Exempted from my Umma are nine things: error, forgetfulness, what they are coerced to do, what they do not have the strength for, what they do not know, what they have to do out of necessity, jealousy, bad omen, and thinking about the whispered (Shaytan-inspired) prompts in regards the creation – so long as it is not voiced aloud.

From Ibn Mahbub from Abdallah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Everything in which there is Haram and Halal, it is Halal for you forever until you know the Haram in it specifically so you abandon it.

From the man (al-Ukhu), from his father, from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'My garment was affected by blood from a nosebleed or otherwise, or by some semen. Prayer time arrived and I forgot that there was something on my garment, so I prayed, and then I remembered afterwards?' He said: 'You repeat the prayer and wash it.' I said: 'If I only suspect that it affected it and am not certain of that, and I looked but found nothing, then I searched for it and found it on my garment after the prayer?' He said: 'You wash it and do not repeat the prayer.' I said: 'Why is that?' He said: 'Because you were certain of its purity, then you doubted; so it is not appropriate for you to overturn certainty with doubt ever.' I said: 'What if I see it on my garment while I am praying?' He said: 'You break the prayer and repeat it if you had doubt about its location, then you see it in it. And if you had no doubt, then you see it wet, you cut it off and wash it, then you continue with the prayer, because you do not know perhaps it is something that fell on you; so it is not appropriate for you to overturn certainty with doubt.'

By the chain from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara who said: I said to him: If a man falls asleep while in a state of wudu, does the 'khafqah' (a light sleep/dozing) and the 'khafqatan' (two light sleeps) oblige him to renew wudu? He said: O Zurara, the eye may sleep while the heart and the ear are awake. When the eye, the ear, and the heart all sleep, then wudu becomes obligatory. I said: What if something moves him to his side and he is not aware of it? He said: No [wudu is not broken], unless he is certain that he has fallen asleep, until a clear matter comes from that [indicating sleep]. Otherwise, he remains upon certainty of his wudu, and certainty is never broken by doubt, but it is broken by another certainty.

Al-Khasa'is: In the 'Four Hundred' Narration: the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Whoever is upon certainty – and then doubts – should continue upon his certainty for doubt does not override certainty.

A number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir, from Abdallah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: If you are certain that you have broken your Wudu, then renew it, and beware of ever renewing the Wudu unless you are certain that you have broken it.

Al-Khisal: From his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abi al-Husayn the servant, seller of pearls, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father asked him about the orphan while I was present: When does his affair become permissible? He said: When he attains his maturity. He said: What is his maturity? He said: Nocturnal emission. I said: The boy may be eighteen years old, or less, or more, and yet not have a nocturnal emission? He said: When he becomes pubescent and something is written for him, his affair is valid unless he is a fool or weak-minded.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washsha, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If he reaches his maturity, that is, completes thirteen years and enters the fourteenth – then it becomes obligatory on him what is obligatory on those who have nocturnal emissions whether he himself has emissions or not, and his sins are written down for him, and his good-deeds are also written down for him, and everything becomes permissible for him [in financial terms] except if he is mentally incapacitated or foolhardy.
From his father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The threshold for a woman’s pubescence is nine years.

Via his chain from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas ibn al-Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): At what age is the boy taken to task over prayer? He said: Between seven and six years of age. I said: At what age is fasting demanded from him? He said: Between fifteen or fourteen years, and if he fasts before that then leave him, for one of my sons began fasting before that and I let him.

Via his chain from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a boy of ten years – can he make the Hajj? He said: upon him is the Hajj of Islam if he has begun getting nocturnal emissions, and the same is the case for the girl – Hajj is upon her if she has begun menstruating.

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is not proper for the girl if she has begun menstruating to not veil herself, unless she cannot find it.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar all together, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a girl who has not attained puberty: when is it incumbent on her to cover her head from the one with whom she does not share any relation? and when is it obligatory on her to veil her head fully in the prayer? He said: She does not cover her head until the prayer starts becoming prohibited on her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no suckling after weaning, and no joining [consecutive days] in fasting, and no orphanhood after nocturnal emission, and no vow of silence for a day until night, and no return to nomadic ways after migration, and no Hijra after the Conquest, and no divorce before marriage, and no manumission before ownership, and no oath from a child with his father, and no oath from a slave with his master, and no oath from a woman with her husband, and no vow in disobedience, and no oath to sever ties. The meaning of His words: 'There is no suckling after weaning' is that if the child drinks the milk of the woman after she has weaned him, that suckling does not prohibit marriage [between them].

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The termination of the orphanhood of the orphan is by nocturnal emission, and it is considered his maturity; however, if he begins to have nocturnal emissions but signs of intellectual maturity are not detected from him, such that he is foolhardy or mentally incapacitated, then his guardian withholds from handing over his wealth to him.

From al-Bazzani from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: A boy is taken to task over prayer when he is seven years old, and a woman does not cover her hair from him until he begins to have nocturnal emissions.

Via his chain to Umar ibn Udhayna from Zurara from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the sick person – how does he prostrate? He said: on a small palm-leaf mat or on a hand-held fan or on a tooth-stick which is raised to him [made to touch his forehead], and it is better than gesturing [without the forehead touching anything], verily the one who dislikes prostrating on the hand-held fan dislikes it because of the idols which used to be worshiped apart from Allah, and we never worship anything besides Allah ever – so prostrate on the fan and on the tooth-stick and on a piece of wood.

Kamal al-Din: From a group, among them Ali ibn Abdallah al-Warraq, from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi who said: … Among what reached me from the Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman (may God sanctify his soul), in response to my questions to the Master of the Age (peace be upon him): … As for what you asked about regarding the one who prays while the fire, or an image, or a lamp is in front of him – is his prayer permissible? The people differed about this before you, then it is permissible for the one who is not from the descendants of the idol-worshippers or fire-worshippers to pray while the fire, or the image, or the lamp is in front of him, and it is not permissible for the one who is from the descendants of the idol and fire worshippers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying: There is nothing except that there is about it a Book or a Sunna. There is nothing [of legal ruling] except that there is about it a Book or a Sunna.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Umaira, from Abi al-Maghra, from Sama'a, from Abi al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: Is everything in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) or do you have a say in it? He said: Rather, everything is in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Al-Faqih: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn via his reliable chain from Abdallah ibn al-Mughira from more than one of our companions from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) In regards to two men who had two Dirhams between them, one of them said: 'The two Dirhams are mine,' and the other said: 'They are between me and you,' he said: 'As for the one who said: 'They are between me and you,' then he has acknowledged that one of the two Dirhams is not his and that it belongs to his companion, and the remaining one is divided between them.'

Via his chain from al-Sakuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them. In the case of a man who deposited two dinars with another man, and another man deposited one dinar with him, and one of the dinars was lost, he said: The owner of the two dinars is given one dinar, and the remaining dinar is divided between the two of them equally.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that two men disputed in front of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding an animal … it was said to him: what if it is not in the possession of either one of them, but both produce evidence? He said: I make them both swear an oath, and whichever one swears and the other reneges, I award it to the one who swore; if both of them swear, I award it to them as two halves …

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had two men dispute before him regarding an animal, and both produced evidence that they foaled it, so he ruled it for the one in whose hand it was, and he said: If it had not been in his possession, I would have divided it equally between them.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Abu Jamila, from Simak ibn Harb, from Tamim ibn Tarafa, that two men recognized a camel, so each one of them produced evidence, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made it out to both of them.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In regards to a woman who dies before her husband or a man before his wife, he said: Whatever of the possessions which [conventionally] belong to women then it is for the wife, and whatever of the possessions which [conventionally] belong to both men and women then it is to be divided between them

Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him saying about the one who loses consciousness: What Allah has power over, then Allah is more entitled to excuse.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Hariz, who said: Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah had gold coins, and a man from Quraysh wanted to travel to Yemen. Ismail said: 'O father, so-and-so wants to go to Yemen, and I have such-and-such gold coins; do you think I should give them to him to buy me goods from Yemen?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, has it not reached you that he drinks wine?' Ismail said: 'That is what the people say.' He said: 'O my son, do not do that.' But Ismail disobeyed his father and gave him his gold coins, so he lost them all and did not bring him back anything of them. He said: 'O my son, verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: “He believes in Allah and believes the believers” — meaning: he confirms the truth of Allah and considers the believers truthful. So if the believers witness something to you, then accept it from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Follow in the wudu the way Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said – begin with the face… begin with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all together from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Will you not inform me from where you knew and ruled that the wiping is [limited] to part of the head and part of the two feet? He laughed and then said: … Then he said: 'Allah intends not to place upon you any difficulty' and 'difficulty' is 'discomfort/constriction'.

Tawhid al-Saduq: From al-Attar, from Sa'd, from Ibn Yazid, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Nine things have been raised (excused) from my Umma: error, forgetfulness, what they were coerced to do, what they do not have the strength for, what they are ignorant of, what they have to do out of necessity, jealousy, bad omen, and thinking about the whispered prompts in regards the creation – so long as it is not voiced by the tongue.

From Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: If a man comes to the market and buys a cloak of fur but does not know whether it is pure or impure, can he pray in it? He said: Yes, you do not have to inquire about it, for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The Khawarij straitened things for themselves due to their ignorance; the religion is more expansive than that.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd al-Ijli who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): … he said: … and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not place in the religion any discomfort; for 'difficulty' is more extreme than 'discomfort'.

Via his chain from al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) In His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'as ruled by two just men among you' – the just man is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him; he rules on it whilst being just, so if you know how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam ruled, then it is enough for you and do not inquire beyond that.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'as ruled by two just men among you' He said: The just man is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him Then he said: This is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'two just men among you' He said: The just one is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him Then he said: This is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ayyub ibn al-Hur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Everything is referred back to the Book and the Sunna, and every Hadith that does not agree with the Book of Allah is mere embellishment (or worthless decoration).

Rijal al-Kashi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh and al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Bundar together from Sa’d from al-Yaqtini from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman … he said: Hisham b. al-Hakam narrated to me that he heard Aba Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Do not accept a narration on our authority except that which is in agreement with the Qur’an and the Sunna …

Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words based on his opinion.

Tafsir al-Ayyashi: From Safwan who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah: 'so wash your faces and your hands with the elbows and wipe part of your head and feet to the ankles' He said: A man asked Aba al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'Surat al-Maida is enough for you' – meaning – wiping the head and the two feet…

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all together from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Will you not inform me from where you knew and ruled that the wiping is of part of the head and part of the two feet? He laughed and then said: O Zurara, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled it to be so and the Book from Allah descended with it — because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Wash your faces' so we understood that the entire face ... then he said: 'So we understood when He said 'with part of your heads' that the wiping is of part of the head because of the position of the letter 'Ba' (ب) ...'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: Abu Qurra the Hadith scholar asked me to facilitate his entrance into the presence of Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) … so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: If the narrations contradict the Qur’an then I reject them, and what the Muslims have all unanimously agreed upon is that He cannot be fully comprehended by knowledge, and the eye-sight cannot overtake Him, and there is nothing like Him.

Irshad of al-Mufid: The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I leave behind in your midst the two weighty things, as long you hold on to them you will not go astray after me: the Book of Allah and my descendants …

Ma'ani al-Akhbar: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Khashab, from Ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whatever you find in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then acting upon it is incumbent upon you; you have no excuse for abandoning it …

Rijal al-Kashshi: From Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub bin Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali bin Ismail bin Ammar, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban bin Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I sit in the Masjid, and people come and ask me questions; if I do not answer them, they do not accept from me, and I dislike answering them with your verdicts and what has come from you (i.e., Shia sources), so he (peace be upon him) said to me: Look at what you know is from their own verdicts and inform them about that.

Rijal al-Kashshi: From Hamduwayh, from Ya`qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Taghlib who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Sit and attend to the people of Madina, for I like it that someone like you be seen amongst our Shia.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Fudhayl and Ibrahim, the two sons of Muhammad al-Ash'ari, who said: When the news of the death of Bukayr ibn A'yan reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: By Allah, Allah has placed him between the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them).

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ubaydah ibn Zurara; and al-Hasan ibn Jahm ibn Bukayr, from his uncle Abdallah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara He said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Bukayr bin A'yan was mentioned, so he (peace be upon him) said: May Allah have mercy on Bukayr, and He has done it [already], so I looked at him [in surprise], and I was then young in age, so he (peace be upon him) said: I do say 'If Allah wills'.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Khatli, from Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: No Hashimite woman among us combed her hair or applied dye [to it] – until al-Mukhtar sent to us the heads of those who killed al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Uthman ibn Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Yazdad al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdallah al-Muzakhraf, from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Mukhtar used to lie about Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from al-Ubaydi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the vicinity of Makka, when he said to me: O Ismail, proceed until you reach Marra or Usfan, and ask if any incident has occurred in Madina. He said: I went out until I reached Marra but did not encounter anyone. Then I proceeded until I reached Usfan but did not encounter anyone. I set out from Usfan, and when I left it, a caravan carrying olives from Usfan met me. I said to them: Is there any incident which has occurred in Madina? They said: No, except the killing of this Iraqi called al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays. He said: I returned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so when he saw me he said to me: O Ismail, al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays has been killed? I said: Yes. He said: By Allah, he has entered paradise.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad al-Nab, from al-Mismai who said: When Dawud ibn Ali arrested al-Mualla ibn Khunays, imprisoned him, and wanted to kill him, al-Mualla ibn Khunays said to him: Take me out to the people, for I have much debt and wealth, so that I may bear witness to that. So he took him out to the market, and when the people had gathered, he said: O people, I am al-Mualla ibn Khunays, whoever knows me has known me. Bear witness that what I leave of wealth, whether in kind, or debt, or a slave-girl, or a slave, or a house, whether little or much, is for Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Then Dawud's head of security struck him and killed him. He said: When that reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he came out dragging his cloak until he entered upon Dawud ibn Ali, with his son Ismail behind him, and said: O Dawud, you killed my Mawla and took my property. He said: I did not kill him, nor did I take your property. He said: By Allah, I will surely supplicate Allah against the one who killed my Mawla and took my property. He said: I did not kill him, but it was my head of security who killed him. He said: By your permission or without your permission? He said: Without my permission. He said: O Ismail, have your way with him. He said: So Ismail came out with the sword and killed him in his seat. Hammad, from al-Mismai, from al-Mu'tab who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) remained in prostration and standing throughout the night. I heard him at the end of the night while in prostration calling out: O Allah, I ask You by Your strong power, and by Your overpowering awe, and by Your might for which You created the abased, that You bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You take him this moment. He said: By Allah, he did not raise his head from his prostration until we heard the cry, and they said: Dawud ibn Ali has died. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I supplicated Allah against him with a supplication due to which Allah sent an angel to him who struck his head with a hammer, and his bladder split from it.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih who said: Dawud ibn Ali said to Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him): I am not the one who killed him – that is Mualla. He said: then who killed him? He said: al-Sayrafi – who was the man in charge of his guards. He said: grant us retaliation. He said: I have. So when al-Sayrafi was taken and was about to be killed he began saying: O masses of the Muslims, they order me to kill people so I kill them for them then they kill me. al-Sayrafi was then executed.

Rijal al-Kashi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh and al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd b. Abdallah, from Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubayd, from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman – that one of our companions asked him while I was present – so he said to him: O Aba Muhammad, how stringent you are in the matter of Hadith and how great is your repudiation of what is narrated by our companions – so what leads you to reject the narrations? He said: Hisham b. al-Hakam narrated to me that he heard Aba Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Do not accept a Hadith on our authority except that which agrees with the Qur'an and the Sunna or you find for it a witness [corroboration] from our past narrations, for al-Mughira b. Said – may Allah curse him – has interpolated into the books of the companions of my father narrations which were not narrated by my father. Therefore fear Allah, and do not accept on our authority that which opposes the words of our Lord the Exalted and the Sunna of our prophet (peace be upon him and his family) …

From Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id used to deliberately lie about my father, and take the books of his companions. And his companions, who were concealed among my father's companions, would take the books from my father's companions and deliver them to al-Mughira. So he would interpolate into them Kufr (disbelief) and al-Zanadiqa (heresy), and attribute them to my father. Then he would send them back to his companions and order them to establish them among the Shia. So whatever in the books of my father's companions was of Ghulu (exaggeration), that is what al-Mughira ibn Sa'id had interpolated in their books.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Go to Mufadhal and say to him – O Kafir, O Mushrik, what do you want for my son? Do you want to kill him?!

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to go to al-Mufadhal and condole him for Ismail. He said: Convey my greetings of peace to al-Mufadhal and say to him: We have been tried through Ismail and have remained patient, so be patient as we have been patient. We wanted a thing, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted a thing, so we submitted to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), whenever he wanted some necessities for himself or something of a personal nature, would write to my father, meaning Ali: 'Purchase for me this and that, and acquire for me such and such, and let Hisham ibn al-Hakam undertake that for you.' But if it had to do with his more general responsibilities, he would just write to him: 'Purchase for me this and that,' and not mention Hisham unless it was personal. It is mentioned that his care and attention towards him was so great that he sent him fifteen thousand dirhams, saying to him, 'Work with it and keep all the profits, but return the principal to us.' Hisham, may Allah have mercy on him, did so, and prayers upon Abu al-Hasan.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus who said: I said to Hisham: Your companions relate that Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent a message to you via Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj saying: 'Abstain from speaking.' Hisham ibn Salim said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj came to me and said to me: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) says to you: 'Abstain from speaking in these days.' Al-Mahdi had compiled for him the theological positions of the people, and among them was the position of the Jawaliqiyya, Hisham ibn Salim. He read that book in al-Sharqiyya but did not mention Hisham's speech. Yunus claimed that Hisham ibn al-Hakam said to him: 'So I abstained from speaking entirely until al-Mahdi died, for he had said to me 'in these days,' so I abstained until al-Mahdi died.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Nusayr, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa, from al-Husayn b. Sai’d, from Ahmad b. Muhammad, from Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: Is there not for you in [the case of] Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him) a warning! What do you think is the state of Hisham b. al-Hakam? For he is the one who did to Abi al-Hasan what he did, and he informed them and divulged to them [the secrets of the Madhhab]. Do you think Allah will forgive him what he has perpetrated on us!

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of Allah and their derivation: From what is 'Allah' derived? He said: So he said to me: O Hisham, 'Allah' is derived from 'ilah' (god/deity), and 'al-ilah' connotes 'the one who is worshipped'. The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning, he has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning, he has disbelieved and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name, that is true monotheism. Have you understood, O Hisham? He said: I said: Increase for me. He said: Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names. If the name were identical to the named, then every one of these names would be a god. But Allah is a meaning to which these names point, and each of them is other than Him. O Hisham, 'bread' is a name for what is eaten, 'water' is a name for what is drunk, 'clothes' is a name for what is worn, 'fire' is a name for what burns. Have you understood, O Hisham, an understanding through which you can repel and defeat our enemies and those who take other deities alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic? I said: Yes. He said: May Allah benefit you by it and make you firm, O Hisham. Hisham said: By Allah, no one has defeated me in the subject of Monotheism until I stood in this position.

Irshad al-Mufid: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from a number of his men, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said: I was at the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the people of Sham came … then he [the Imam] said: O Hisham, you never fall flat [settle on the ground], every time it seems that you are about to come to ground [i.e. be defeated] you just bend your legs [to able to leap] and off you fly away again. The likes of you should debate the people. Therefore be wary of slipping and you will find that succor is around the corner if Allah wills.

Masabih al-Nur of al-Mufid: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Abi Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari who said: I presented to Abu Muhammad, the Master of the Army (peace be upon him), the book 'Yawm wa Layla' of Yunus. He said to me: 'Who authored this?' I said: 'It is authored by Yunus, the client of the family of Yaqtin.' He said: 'May Allah give him for every letter a light on the Day of Judgment.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from his father, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) (regarding the book of Yunus): This is my religion and the religion of my forefathers, and it is the whole truth.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus who said: The Righteous Servant [al-Kadhim] (peace be upon him) said: O Yunus, be lenient towards them, for your words are hard-hitting on them. I said: But they call me a Zindiq [Gnostic/Disbeliever]. He said to me: What will it harm you if you have in your hands a pearl but the people say to you 'it is a stone', and what will it benefit you if you have in your hand a stone but the people say 'it is a pearl'.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Ja'far ibn al-Rida (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about Yunus, so he said: The client of the family of Yaqtin? I said: Yes. He said to me: May Allah have mercy on him, he was a righteous servant.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi who said: I said to Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, I cannot always reach you to ask you all that which I need from the teachings of my religion, is Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman trustworthy (thiqa) and can I take from him what I need from the teachings of my religion? He said: Yes.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim the sons of Nusayr, from al-Ubaydi, from Hisham ibn Ibrahim al-Khatli, who is al-Mashriqi, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) said to me: What do you say regarding Istita’a (capacity) after Yunus? For he (Yunus) has subscribed to the opinion of Zurara while the opinion of Zurara is wrong!

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hisham al-Mashriqi, that he entered upon Abi al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) and said: The people of Basra asked about speech (kalam), saying: Yunus says that speech is not created. I said to them: Yunus has spoken the truth, speech is not created. Has the statement of Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) not reached you when he was asked about the Qur'an: 'Is it creator or created?' He said to them: It is not creator nor created, rather it is the speech of the Creator. Thus the position of Yunus was strengthened. And they said: Yunus says that it is from the Sunnah for a man to pray two units while seated after the late night prayer? I said: Yunus has spoken the truth.
Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa who said: Yunus informed me that Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) guaranteed me Paradise from the Fire.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I wrote to Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, should I pray behind the one who believes in 'a corporeal body' and the one who follows the position of Yunus, that is, the son of Abd al-Rahman? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Do not pray behind them, nor give them anything of the Zakat, and disassociate from them - Allah has disassociated from them.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, what you did for Yunus has pleased me. He said to me: Is it not part of what Allah did for Yunus that He transferred him from Iraq to the vicinity of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?

Rijal al-Kashshi: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abbas ibn A'mir, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him to supplicate to Allah that He makes me among those through whom He gives victory to His religion, but he did not answer me, so I became saddened because of that. Yunus said: One of our companions informed me that he had written to him with a similar request and was answered by him, and he wrote at the bottom of the letter: 'May Allah have mercy on you, verily Allah gives victory to His religion via the worst of His creatures.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh and al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd b. Abdallah b. Abi Khalaf al-Qummi, from al-Hasan b. Musa al-Khashshab and Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubid, from Ali b. Asbat, from Abdallah b. Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Muhammad b. Abi Bakr - May Allah’s mercy be upon him - his noble descent (nisabah) was from his mother Asma bt. Umays

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That Asma bint Umays had the post-natal bleeding (nifas) of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, when she wanted to assume Ihram from Dhi al-Hulayfa, to stuff herself with cotton and rags and enter into Ihram for Hajj.

Al-Khasa'is: My father, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: May Allah have mercy on the sisters among the inhabitants of Paradise and he named them: Asma bint Umays al-Khathamiyya who was married to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and Salma bint Umays al-Khathamiyya who was married to Hamza. And five from Bani Hilal: Maymuna bint al-Harith who was married to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and Umm al-Fadhl with al-Abbas, her name was Hind. Al-Ghumaysa, mother of Khalid ibn al-Walid. Azza who was with Thaqif, with al-Hajjaj ibn Ghiladh. And Hamida, and she had no offspring.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal who said: Our companions differed regarding the narrations of Jabir al-Ju'fi, so I said to them: I will ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When I entered, he began by saying: May Allah have mercy on Jabir al-Ju'fi, he used to tell the truth about us; may Allah curse al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, he used to lie about us.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, the two sons of Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the narrations of Jabir, he said: I never saw him with my father – ever – except for one time, and he never entered upon me [to take Hadith] ever.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban, from al-Harith who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Humran used to say: We stretch out the rope; whoever oversteps it, whether he be an Alawi or otherwise, we disassociate from him.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Hujr ibn Zaida, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I have given Allah an oath that I will not leave Medina until you inform me of what I ask you. He said to me: Ask. I said: Am I of your Shia? He said: Yes, in this world and the next.

Ghayb of al-Tusi: Via his chain to Abdallah b. Ja'far who said: A Tawqi [signed rescript] came out to the Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad b. Uthman b. Sai'd al-Amri (may God sanctify his soul) condoling him for the death of his father (may God be pleased with him). In it was written: … May Allah amplify your reward and beautify your mourning. We grieve just as you grieve. It has left you bereft just as it has left us bereft. May Allah delight him after his return. One aspect of the perfect felicity he attained is that Allah the Exalted granted him a son like you, who succeeds him after his departure, stands in his place as per his command, and supplicates for mercy for him. I say 'All praise belongs to Allah' for the souls are comforted due to the position you have assumed and because of what Allah Mighty and Majestic has bestowed in you and with you. May Allah support and strengthen you. May He aid you and facilitate you. May He be a Guardian over you, a Protector, a Guide and Sufficient for you.

Via his chain to Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari who said: I asked Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri (may Allah be pleased with him): Have you seen the Master of this Order (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes. My last meeting with him was at the Sanctified House of Allah [the Ka'ba], and he was saying: 'O Allah, fulfill for me what You promised me.' Muhammad ibn Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him and be pleased with him) said: I also saw him (may Allah's prayers be upon him) clinging to the coverings of the Ka'ba at the Mustajar [place of refuge] while he was saying: 'O Allah, take revenge for me from Your enemies.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd and Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaq, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Four are the most beloved of people to me, alive and dead: Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, Zurara ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal. They are the most beloved of people to me, alive and dead.

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq who said: I was at Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) one night when al-Ahwal came in to see him. There overcame him an extreme state of humility and submissiveness. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter with you?' And he began conversing with him until he returned to normal. Then he said to him: 'How do you debate with the people?' He said: 'So he described to him how he argues against the people, and I did not memorize that from him.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Debate them using such and such.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Qummi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdallah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Abdallah ibn Abi Ya'fur who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'It is not every hour that I meet you, and it may be impossible to travel [to reach you]. A man from among our companions comes and asks me, but I do not have [an answer] for everything that he asks me about [what should I do?].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from [going to] Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi, for he had heard [narrations] from my father and had a most favorable position with him.'

Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdallah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said: Abu Kurayb al-Azdi and Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi gave witness in the presence of Sharik while he was the judge. He looked at their faces for a long moment and then said: 'Two Ja'faris, two Fatimis!' so they began to cry. He said to them: 'What makes you cry?' They said to him: 'You have attributed us to a group who are not pleased with the likes of us being counted among their fellows because of what they see of the deficiency in our worship, and you have attributed us to a man who is not pleased that the likes of us be associated among his Shia. If he does us a favour and accepts us, then he is the one who bestows favour upon us and excels.' Sharik smiled, then said: 'If there are men, let them be like you. O Walid, permit them this time (and do not return them a second time).' They said: 'We made the pilgrimage and recounted to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the incident, so he said: 'What is with Sharik? May Allah partner him up on the Day of Resurrection with two strips of fire.'

Ibn Idris, from his father, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked: By what did you know your Lord? He said: By the dissolution of resolution and the invalidation of plan. I resolved but He dissolved my resolution, and I planned but He invalidated my plan.

Al-Tawhid and Ma'ani al-Akhbar: My father, from Muhammad al-Attar, from Ibn Isa, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: I asked Aba Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): What is the meaning of 'the One'? He said: (He is) the One upon whom all tongues agree, in Oneness.

Al-Ilal: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Isa, from Muhammad al-Barqi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And they said: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr." He said: They used to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then they died. Their people cried out and it weighed heavily on them. Iblis (curse of Allah be upon him) came to them and said: 'Shall I make for you idols in their images, so you look at them and find comfort in them while you worship Allah?' So he made for them idols in their likeness. They used to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and look at those idols. When winter and the rains came, they brought the idols into their houses. They continued worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until that generation perished and their children grew up. They said: 'Our fathers used to worship these,' so they began worshipping them instead of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. That is the meaning of the words of Allah, Blessed and Elevated: 'And do not abandon Wadd nor Suwa'.'

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is One, Compact, He does not have any hollowness, while the spirit (al-Ruh) is a creation from among His creations and is an aid, support and power which Allah places in the hearts of the messengers and believers.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. He remained three days not answering them Say: He is Allah the One to its end

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab and from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever worships Allah by imagining Him (in his mind) then he has disbelieved. And whoever worships the Name without the Meaning (the reality behind the name) then he has disbelieved. And whoever worships both the Name and the Meaning then he has associated partners with Him. And whoever worships the Meaning while applying the Names to Him with the attributes by which He described Himself, fixing his heart upon that and expressing it with his tongue in his secrets and his public life, then those are the true companions of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And in another report: those are the true believers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran who said: I wrote to Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) or I said to him: May Allah make me your ransom - Do we worship The Beneficent, The Merciful, The Unique, The One, The Eternal? He said: He said: Indeed, whoever worships the name rather than the one named by the names has committed shirk, disbelieved, and denied, and has not worshipped anything. Rather, worship Allah the Unique, The One, The Eternal, who is called by these names and not the names themselves. Indeed, the names are attributes which He has described Himself with.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdallah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Hanifan Musliman.' He said: Sincere and devoted, having in it nothing whatsoever of the worship of idols.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of Allah and their derivation: From what is 'Allah' derived? He said: So he said to me: O Hisham, 'Allah' is derived from 'ilah' (god/deity), and 'al-ilah' connotes the one who is worshipped. The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning has disbelieved and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name, that is true monotheism. Have you understood, O Hisham? He said: I said: Increase for me. He said: Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names. If the name were identical to the named, then every one of these names would be a god. But Allah is a meaning to which these names point, and each of them is other than Him. O Hisham, 'bread' is a name for what is eaten, 'water' is a name for what is drunk, 'clothes' is a name for what is worn, 'fire' is a name for what burns. Have you understood, O Hisham, with an understanding by which you can repel and contend with our enemies and those who take other than Allah as a deity? I said: Yes. He said: May Allah benefit you by it and make you firm, O Hisham. Hisham said: By Allah, no one has defeated me in the subject of Monotheism until I stood in this position.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazm who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I debated a group and said to them: Verily Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, is more Majestic, Stronger, and More Generous than that He be known through His creatures, rather the slaves are known through Allah. He said: May Allah have mercy on you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqah, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Ibrahim ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The affair of Allah is totally strange (unknowable), however, He only holds you to account over that part which He has given you knowledge of about Himself.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abdallah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate'. He said: The Ba is the Baha (Splendor) of Allah, the Sin is the Sana (Exaltedness) of Allah, and the Mim is the Majd (Magnificence) of Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of Allah and their derivation: From what is 'Allah' derived? He said: So he said to me: O Hisham, 'Allah' is derived from 'ilah' (god/deity), and 'al-ilah' connotes the one who is worshipped (ma'luh). The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning, he has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning, he has disbelieved and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name, that is Tawhid (divine unity). Have you understood, O Hisham? He said: I said: Increase for me. He said: Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names. If the name were identical to the named, then every one of these names would be a god. But Allah is a meaning to which these names allude, and each of them is other than Him. O Hisham, 'bread' is a name for what is eaten, 'water' is a name for what is drunk, 'clothes' is a name for what is worn, 'fire' is a name for what burns. Have you understood, O Hisham, with an understanding by which you can repel and contend with our enemies and those who take other than Allah as a deity? I said: Yes. He said: May Allah benefit you by it and make you firm, O Hisham. Hisham said: By Allah, no one has defeated me in Tawhid until I stood in this position.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abi al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the meaning of Allah, so he said: The one who rules over what is lowly and great.

Al-Tawhid: Al-Hamdani, from Ali, from his father, from al-Harawi, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ninety-nine names. Whoever calls upon Allah by them is answered, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.

Al-Kafi: From him, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq who said: I wrote to Abi al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) asking him about the vision (of God) and the differences of people regarding it, so he wrote: Vision is not valid unless there is air between the viewer and the viewed that the eye can penetrate. If the air is cut off between the viewer and the viewed, vision does not become valid, and this entails confusion/likening, because whenever the viewer equals the viewed in the cause necessitated between them for vision, confusion becomes obligatory, and that is likening (anthropomorphism), because causes must necessarily be connected to their effects.

Al-Kafi: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from A'sim ibn Humayd, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I discussed with Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding what they narrate about the vision (of God). He said: The sun is one part out of seventy parts of the light of the Chair. The Chair is one part out of seventy parts of the light of the Throne. The Throne is one part out of seventy parts of the light of the Veil. The Veil is one part out of seventy parts of the light of the Covering. If they are truthful, let them fill their eyes with the sun, with no cloud below it.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was made to ascend to Heaven, Jibril led me to a place where Jibril had never tread before. It was then unveiled for him, and Allah showed him of His Light of Grandeur what He wished.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His words: Sights do not reach Him He said: It means the encompassing of imagination (al-wahm). Do you not see His words: 'There have come to you insights (basair) from your Lord'? He does not mean the sight of the eyes. 'Whosoever sees (absara) then it will be for his own self' — He does not mean by 'see' through the eye. 'And whoever is blind is against it' — He does not mean the blindness of the eyes. He means the encompassing of imagination, as it is said: So-and-so is insightful (basir) in poetry, and so-and-so is insightful in jurisprudence, and so-and-so is insightful in coins, and so-and-so is insightful in clothes. Allah is greater than to be seen by the eye.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about Allah, can He be described? He said: Do you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. He said: Do you not read His words the Exalted: 'Sights do not encompass Him, while He encompasses sights'? I said: Yes. He said: Do you know what 'sights' means? I said: The sight of the eyes. He said: The imaginings of the hearts are greater than the sight of the eyes, so He is not encompassed by the imaginings, while He encompasses the imaginings.

Al-Tawhid: Al-Hamdani, from Ali, from his father, from Al-Harawi who said: I said to Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the report narrated by the Ahl al-Hadith that 'the believers will visit their Lord from their homes in Paradise'? He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Salt, indeed Allah Blessed and Exalted favored His prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) over all His creation from the prophets and the angels. He made obedience to him obedience to Him, and pledging allegiance to him pledging allegiance to Him, and visiting him in this world and the hereafter visiting Him. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' and He said: 'Those who pledge allegiance to you are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah, the hand of Allah is over their hands.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever visits me in my lifetime or after my death has visited Allah.' The station of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise is the highest of stations, so whoever visits him to his station in Paradise from his home has visited Allah Blessed and Exalted. He said: I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of the report they narrate that 'the reward of 'La ilaha illa Allah' is looking at the Face of Allah'? He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Salt, whoever describes Allah with a face like the faces (of humans) has disbelieved. But the Face of Allah is His prophets, His messengers, and His proofs, may the prayers of Allah be upon them. They are the ones through whom one turns towards Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and towards His religion and knowledge of Him. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Everyone upon it will perish, and will remain the Face of your Lord' and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Every thing is perishing except His Face.' Thus, looking at the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His proofs (peace be upon them) in their stations is a great reward for the believers on the Day of Judgment. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever hates my Ahl al-Bayt and my progeny will not see me, nor will I see him on the Day of Judgment.' And he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among you is one who will not see me after he separates from me.' O Abu Salt, in

Al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Yaqtini, from Ibn Abi Najran who said: I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) about Tawhid, saying: Should I imagine a thing? He said: Yes, (something) neither cognisable nor delimited. Whatever your imagination falls upon is different than He. Nothing is like Him and imaginations do not reach Him. How can imaginations reach Him when He is other than what can be cognised and other than what is represented in the imaginations? It is imagined something neither cognisable nor delimited.

Ibn al-Walid, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw his Lord, Mighty and Majestic - that is - by his heart.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali b. Mahziyar who said: I wrote to Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, should I pray behind the one who says 'the body' (God is corporeal), or the one who says the saying of Yunus - meaning Ibn Abd al-Rahman? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Do not pray behind them nor give them from the Zakat, and disassociate from them. Allah has disassociated from them.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Barqi, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: I heard Ali b. Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying: My God, Your power is manifest but Your form is not. Because of this they became ignorant of You and with that (ignorance) estimated You. While the (true) estimation is other than how they described You. And I am disassociated, O My God, from those who sought You by likening You (to Your creatures). There is nothing like You. My God, they will never reach You. What is apparent of Your blessings around them is an indicator towards You. If only they recognized You. And in Your creation, O My God, there is ample to understand You. However, they equated You to Your creation and because of that did not attain recognition of You. They took some of Your signs as Lord (instead of You) and with that (imperfect attributes) described You. Elevated are You, My Lord, from that which the Likeners impute to You.

Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He has lied the one who claims that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is from a thing, or in a thing, or upon a thing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Everything is to perish except His face.' He said: Whoever comes to Allah with what He commanded in terms of obeying Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), he is the 'face' that will not perish. And similarly He said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah.'

Al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Judgment will hold onto the waist-knot of Allah, and we will hold onto the waist-knot of our Prophet, and our Shia will hold onto our waist-knot. Then he said: The waist-knot means light.

Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan, from al-Ridha, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words by his opinion. He has not known Me the one who likens Me to My creatures. He is not upon My religion the one who uses analogy in My religion.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'Subhanallah', and he said: 'Exaltation to Allah'.

Al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub al-Sarraj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): One of our companions claims that Allah has a form like that of a human, and another says that He is in the form of a beardless youth with very curly hair! Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) fell down in prostration, then he raised his head and said: Glory be to Allah whom there is nothing like Him. Vision cannot reach Him. Knowledge cannot encompass Him. He does not give birth, for an offspring resembles his parent. He was not born so that He could resemble one who came before Him. He will never have among His creatures any rival. Elevated is He from the description of the one who equates Him - a great elevation.

Amali of al-Saduq: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam, from al-Kulayni, from 'Allan, from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhaji who said: I wrote to Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) asking him about what Hisham ibn al-Hakam said regarding 'the body', and what Hisham ibn Salim said regarding 'the form'. He wrote (peace be upon him): Leave aside the confusion of the confused, and seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan, the (true) position is not what was said by the two Hishams.

Ibn 'Isam, from al-Kulayni, from al-'Ulani, from al-Yaqtini, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon them) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the earth entirely [will be] His grip on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded in His right hand.' He said: That is a rebuke of Allah, Blessed and Elevated, for the one who likens Him to His creation. Do you not see that He said: 'And they have not estimated Allah with true estimation'? And its meaning is when they said: 'The entire earth is His grip on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens are folded in His right hand,' just as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And they have not estimated Allah with true estimation' when they said: 'Allah has not sent down anything to a human being.' Then He, Mighty and Majestic, declared Himself free of 'grip' and 'right hand' by saying: 'Glorified is He and Elevated above what they associate [with Him].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was there and there was nothing other than Him. He always knew what would come into being, so His knowledge of it before it came into being is like His knowledge of it after it came into being.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, that he wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Did He have knowledge of things before He created the things and brought them into existence, or did He not know that until He created them and intended their creation and formation, so He knew what He created at the moment of creation and what He formed at the moment of formation? He wrote in his handwriting: Allah never ceased to be Knower of the things before He created the things, just as His knowledge of the things after He had created the things.

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: Tell me, regarding all that which was and all that which is to be until the Day of Judgment, was it not in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted? He said: Yes, before He created the heavens and the earth.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): We have narrated that Allah is Knowledge with no ignorance in Him, Life with no death in Him, Light with no darkness in Him. He said: That is who He is.

Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, for Allah is a special knowledge and a general knowledge. As for the special knowledge, it is the knowledge which He did not grant access to His brought-near angels and His sent prophets. As for His general knowledge, it is His knowledge which He granted access to His brought-near angels and His sent prophets. And this has reached us from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: His Chair extends over the Heavens and the Earth He said: The Heavens, the Earth, and what is between them are in the Chair, and the Throne is the Knowledge whom no one can estimate its limit.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today which was not in the Knowledge of Allah yesterday? He said: No. May the one who says that be abased by Allah. I said: Consider whatever has happened and whatever will happen up to the Day of Judgment - is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He said: Yes. Before He created the creation.

Al-Tawhid: Ibn Idris, from his father, from al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Ismail and Ibn Hashim together, from Safwan, from Ibn Hazim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today which was not in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: No. Rather it was in His knowledge before He generated the Heavens and the Earth.

Basair al-Darajat: Abdallah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ruba'i, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah has a knowledge which His angels, prophets, and messengers know. Behold! We too know it. And Allah has a knowledge which His angels, prophets, and messengers do not know.

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ruba'i ibn Abdallah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described (as He really is). He said: Zurara said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described with incapacity. How can He be described when He has said in His Book: 'And they have not estimated Allah with true estimation'? Thus, He is not described with power except that He is greater than that.

Al-Tawhid: Ibn Masrur, from Ibn A'mir, from his uncle, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban b. Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Is Allah capable of inserting the Earth into an egg without the Earth becoming smaller or the egg becoming larger? He said: Woe upon you - Incapacity cannot be attributed to Allah. Who is more capable (of doing that) than the One who diminishes the Earth and enlarges the egg?!

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Bazanti who said: A group came from Beyond the River to Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: We have come to ask you three questions. If you answer us in them we will know that you are the Scholar. He said: Ask. They said: Inform us about Allah - Where was He? How was He? Upon what thing was His reliance? He said: Allah Mighty and Majestic howed the how so he is without ‘how’ and whered the where so He is without ‘where’ and His reliance was on His Power. They said: We bear witness that you are the Scholar.

Al-Tawhid: Hamza al-Alawi, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic: There is no private conversation of three but He is the fourth of them, nor of five but He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them wherever they are He (the Imam) said: He is One. Unique in Essence. Distinct from His creation. That is how He described Himself. He encompasses everything in terms of supervision, awareness and power. Nothing escapes Him even the weight of a particle in the Heavens and in the Earth nor smaller than that or larger - in terms of awareness and knowledge not by (His) essence, for locations (space) are bounded, delimited by the four bounds, so if it was (that He was encompassing) by essence than that would necessarily imply containment.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: In the description of The Eternal: He is One, Besought, One in meaning, not in multiple divergent meanings. He said: I said: May I be your ransom, a group from the people of Iraq claim that He hears with other than that which He sees by, and He sees with other than that which He hears by. He said: They have lied, deviated and likened (Allah to His creation) - Far elevated is Allah from that. He is Hearing, Seeing. He hears with what He sees by and sees with what He hears by. I said: They claim that He sees using that which they understand. He said: Elevated is Allah. Only that which has the attribute of the created can be understood and Allah is not like that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said: Did Allah not cease to be Willing? He said: The one who wills cannot be (considered as such) except that what is willed is (present) with Him. (Instead say:) Allah never ceased being Knowledgeable and Powerful and then He willed.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Inform me about the Will of Allah and that of the creatures? He said: The Will of the creatures is the conception (thought in the heart) and what becomes apparent to them thereafter in the form of action. As for Allah the Exalted, His Will is His bringing into existence, nothing other than that, for He does not deliberate, does not desire, and does not ponder. These attributes are negated from Him, and they are the attributes of the creatures. The Will of Allah is the Act itself, nothing other than that.
