He says to it 'Be' and it 'is', without wording or articulation by the tongue, without desire or pondering, and there is no 'how' to it, just as there is no 'how' to Him.

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Will (of God) is originated (temporal).

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Yaqtini, from al-Ja'fari, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: The Will is from the attributes of actions. So whoever asserts that Allah never stopped willing and intending is not a monotheist.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Alaa ibn Rasin, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah created the Will on its own (by itself). Then He created the things through (the intermediacy of) the Will.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar and Sa'd together, from Ibn Isa, from his father, and al-Husayn b. Sa'id and Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham b. Salim who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said to me: Can you describe Allah? I said: Yes. He said: Bring it forth. I said: He is The Hearing, The Seeing. He said: This is an attribute shared by the created beings. I said: So how do we describe Him? He said: He is Light with no darkness in Him, Life with no death in Him, Knowledge with no ignorance in Him, Truth with no falsehood in Him. I came out from him being the most knowledgeable of people in Tawhid.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Fadil ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'He is the First and the Last.' I said: As for the 'First,' we know it, but explain to us the interpretation of 'the Last.' He said: There is nothing except that it perishes or changes, or change and extinction affect it, or it transitions from color to color, from form to form, from attribute to attribute, from increase to decrease, and from decrease to increase, except the Lord of the Worlds, for He never ceased and will never cease being in one state. He is the First before everything, and He is the Last as He has never ceased, and attributes and names do not differ for Him as they differ for others. Like a human who is at one time clay, at another time flesh and blood, and at another time remains and decay; and like the date fruit which is at one time green (balah), at another time semi-ripe (busr), at another time fresh (rutab), and at another time dry (tamr), so that names and attributes change for it, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the opposite of that.

Al-Tawhid: Al-Hamdani, from Ali, from his father, from Al-Harawi, from Ali ibn Musa Al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ninety-nine names. Whoever calls upon Allah by them is answered, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abi Ishaq Tha'laba, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from One of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said: Allah has not been worshipped by something like Bada'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Concerning this verse: 'Allah erases what He wills and establishes,' he said: 'Does He erase other than that which was established? And does He establish other than that which was not?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah did not appoint a prophet unless He took from him three qualities: Affirming worship as due only to Him, renouncing the rivals (idols set up besides Allah), and that Allah brings forward what He wills and puts back what He wills.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "He decreed a term and the appointed term is with Him" He said: There are two terms. A term that is final and another term which is deferred.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abi Basir, and Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah has two kinds of knowledge: a hidden and stored-up knowledge, which He alone knows, from that comes Bada'; and a knowledge which He taught His angels, messengers, and prophets, so we know it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing becomes apparent to Allah concerning something except that it was in His knowledge before it appears to Him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) say: Allah has never sent a prophet except with the prohibition of wine and that he acknowledge to Allah the Bada’.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from more than one, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: A man from the Children of Israel had a son whom he loved greatly. He was visited in his sleep and it was said to him: 'Your son will die the night he enters upon his wife.' He said: When that night came, and he consummated the marriage, the father anticipated that [death] would happen, but he woke up finding his son healthy. His father came to him and said to him: 'O my son, did you do anything of good yesterday?' He said: 'No, except that a beggar came to the door and they had kept preserved for me some food, and I gave it to the beggar.' He (the father) said: 'Through this, Allah averted [death] from you.'

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah Mighty and Majestic has not been magnified with the like of Bada’.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rubay ibn Abdallah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Knowledge is of two kinds: A knowledge with Allah which is hidden, no one from His creation has seen into it; and a knowledge which He taught His angels and His messengers. So as for that which He taught His angels and messengers, then it will occur. He does not belie Himself, nor His angels, nor His messengers. As for the hidden knowledge with Him, then He brings forward from it what He wills, and puts back from it what He wills, and establishes what He wills.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from al-Ruba'i, from al-Fudayl, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Among the matters are matters which are deferred with Allah; He brings forward from them what He wills and puts back from them what He wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today that was not in the knowledge of Allah yesterday? He said: No. May the one who says this be abased by Allah! I said: Consider - whatever has happened and whatever will happen up to the Day of Judgment is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He said: Yes. Before He created the creation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad, people remain in speculation until they begin speaking about Allah. So when you hear that, say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Unique, the one whom there is nothing like Him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abi Ubayda al-Hadhdha, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Ziyad, beware of argumentation/debates, for it breeds doubt, causes deeds to descend (be nullified), and degrades its practitioner. It may happen that a man speaks a word for which he is not forgiven. Indeed, in the past there were people who abandoned the knowledge of what they were commanded to know, and sought the knowledge of what they were commanded to refrain from, until their speech reached Allah, and they became confused. So much so that a man would be called from in front of him but he would answer the one behind him, and he would be called from behind but he would answer the one in front of him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And to your Lord is the End (finality).' So if your speech reaches to Allah, then remain silent.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There was a king of great status who was in a council of his when he touched upon (started discussing) the Lord Blessed and Elevated. Suddenly he disappeared and it was not known where he was (could not be found).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then it was revealed 'Say: He is Allah the One' to its end.

Ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad al-Attar, from al-Ash'ari, from al-Maythami, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then this chapter was revealed to its end. I said: What is 'As-Samad'? He said: The one who is not hollow. The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then this chapter was revealed to its end. I said: What is 'As-Samad'? He said: The one who is not hollow.

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Blessed and Elevated, is One, Compact, He does not have any hollowness, while the spirit is a creation from among His creations and is an aid, support and power which Allah places in the hearts of the messengers and believers.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humid (he raised it) (he said): He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about Tawhid, so he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that there would be in the last age peoples who delve deep (speculate). So Allah the Elevated brought down 'Say: He is Allah One' and the verses in Surat al-Hadid until His words 'and He is Knowing of that within the hearts'. So whoever looks (desires) beyond that then he has perished.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Yaqtini, from Ibn Abi Najran who said: I asked Aba Ja’far the Second (peace be upon him) about Tawhid, saying: Should I imagine a thing? He said: Yes, (something) neither cognizable nor delimited. Whatever your imagination falls upon is different than He. Nothing is like Him and imaginations do not reach Him. How can imaginations reach Him when He is other than what can be cognized and other than what is represented in the imaginations? It is imagined something neither cognizable nor delimited.

Ma'ani al-Akhbar: My father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him.' I said: What is the Hanifiyya? He said: The Fitra.

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said: 'The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon'? He said: 'Tawhid.'

Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Hashim and Ibn Yazid together, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon,' he said: 'He created them upon Tawhid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Sharia (Law-code) of Nuh (peace be upon him) was that Allah be worshipped by Tawhid (divine unity) and Ikhlas (sincerity) and to shun the idols - and it is the Fitra (innate disposition) which He created the people upon …

Ibn al-Mutawakkhill narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon' — what is that Fitra? He said: It is Islam. Allah created them upon it when He took their Covenant upon Tawhid, saying: 'Am I not your Lord?' and among them were the believer and the disbeliever.

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ahmad and Abdallah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The fitra of Allah which He created the people upon.' He said: 'He created them all upon Tawhid.'

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May Allah set you aright, the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic in His book: "The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon" He (the Imam) said: He created them upon Tawhid, at the Covenant, upon His Ma'rifa (Recognition) that He is their Lord. I said: Did they address Him? He (Zurara) said: so he (the Imam) lowered his head and then said: If it were not for that they would not know who their Lord is nor who their Sustainer is.

Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Hashim and Ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ibn Yazid all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Hunafa for Allah, not associating with Him,' and about Hanifiyya (the state of being Hanif). He said: It is the Fitra (innate nature) upon which Allah created the people, there is no change in the creation of Allah. He said: Allah created them upon Ma'rifa (Recognition/Knowledge). Zurara said: And I asked him about the words of Allah: 'And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their backs their descendants.' He said: He brought forth from the back of Adam his descendants until the Day of Judgment, and they came out like small particles, then He made them known to them and showed them His creation, and if it were not for that, no one would recognize his Lord. And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every newborn is born upon the Fitra,' meaning upon the Ma'rifa (Recognition) that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is his Creator. This is His words: 'And if you were to ask them, who created the heavens and the earth? They will surely say, Allah.'

Ilal al-Shara'i: My father, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants and made them bear witness against their own selves - am I not your Lord? They said: Indeed." He said: The recognition was confirmed but they forgot the time and they will remember it one day. If it were not for that, no one would know who his Creator is nor who his Sustainer is.

Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily the All-Mighty, the Almighty, has sent down unto you His Book, and He is Truthful and Good. In it is news of you, news of those who came before you, news of those who will come after you, and news of Heaven and Earth. If there comes to you one who can inform you of that, you will be amazed.

Al-Kafi: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abi Basir who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Qur’an is a Chaser and a Caller. It calls to the Garden and chases away from the Fire.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathers the first ones and the last ones, behold, they will see a person approaching, whose form has never been seen to be more handsome. When the believers look at him, and he is the Qur'an, they will say: 'This is from us, this is the most beautiful thing we have seen.' When he reaches them, he passes them. Then the martyrs look at him, and when he reaches the last of them, he passes them, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them all. Until he reaches the Messengers, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them until he reaches the Angels, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them, until he comes to stand on the right side of the Throne. Then the Almighty will say: 'By My Might and Majesty, and the loftiness of My position, I will honour today the one who honoured you, and humble the one who humiliated you.'

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who has memorized the Qur'an and acts upon it is with the Honourable and Virtuous Scribes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The one who labours over the Qur'an and memorizes it with difficulty on his part and having poor memory - for him is double the reward.

Al-Saduq's Book of Unity and his Amali: My father, from Sa'd, from al-Yaqtini, who said: Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) wrote to one of his Shia in Baghdad: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah protect us and you from the trial. If He does, then count it a great blessing, and if He does not, then it is perdition. We consider argumentation about the Qur'an to be an innovation, in which both the questioner and the respondent have partaken. So the questioner has engaged in what is not for him, and the respondent has borne what is not on him. There is no creator except Allah, and what is other than Him is created. The Qur'an is the Speech of Allah. Do not make for it a name from yourself, so you will be among the astray. May Allah make us and you of those who 'fear their Lord without seeing Him and are of the Hour apprehensive.'

Ibn Masrur, from Muhammad al-Himyari, from his father, from Ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan who said: I said to al-Ridha (peace be upon him): What do you say about the Qur’an? He said: The Speech of Allah. Do not go beyond it nor search for guidance in other than it - for you will be led astray.

From Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: Hisham al-Mashriqi narrated to me, He entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) and said: The people of Basra inquired about Divine Speech, saying: Yunus says that Speech is not created. I said to them: Yunus has spoken the truth, Speech is not created. Has not reached you the statement of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when he was asked about the Qur'an: Is it a Creator or created? He said to them: It is neither a Creator nor created, rather it is the Speech of the Creator. Thus the position of Yunus was strengthened. And they said: Yunus says that it is from the Sunnah for a man to pray two units while seated after the night prayer (Isha). I said: Yunus has spoken the truth.

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abi al-Maghra', from Abi Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who forgets a Chapter from the Qur'an, it will be presented to him in a beautiful form and on an elevated level in Paradise. When he sees it, he will say: 'What are you? How beautiful you are! If only you were mine!' It will say: 'Do you not know me? I am such and such Chapter. And if you had not forgotten me, I would have elevated you to this (level).'

Al-Kafi: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all together, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man -if he used to know a chapter and then forgets it or abandons it and then enters paradise- she appears to him from above in a most beautiful form and says: 'Do you know me?' He says: 'No' She says: 'I am such and such chapter, you did not act by me and abandoned me, by Allah if you had acted by me I would have made you reach this station,' and she points with her hand above her

My father from al-Himyari from al-Yaqtini from Yunus from Abdallah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has three Inviolables, there is nothing comparable to them: His Book, and it is His Wisdom and Light; His House which He made a Qibla for the people, it is not accepted from anyone a facing other than towards it; and the Descendants of your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Learn the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Judgment to its companion in the form of a handsome, pale-faced youth. The Qur'an will say to him: I am the one who kept awake your nights, made thirsty your mid-days, dried your saliva, and caused your tears to flow. I will accompany you wherever you recite, and just as every merchant is behind his merchandise (seeking profit), so am I today behind you, the merchant of every merchant. An honour will come to you from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so receive glad tidings.' Then a crown will be brought and placed on his head, and he will be given the Writ of Security in his right hand and the Writ of Eternity in the Gardens in his left hand, and he will be attired with two robes. Then it will be said to him: 'Recite and ascend!' So every time he recites a verse, he ascends a level. And his two parents will be attired with two robes if they were believers, then it will be said to them: 'This is for what you taught him the Qur'an.'

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Abdullah al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Qur'an then forgets it, then recites it again then forgets it, is there any difficulty/sin upon him regarding this? He said: No.

Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Qur’an is the covenant of Allah to His creatures, it is incumbent therefore on a Muslim man to look into his covenant and that he recite fifty verses from it every day

Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad; and Sahl ibn Ziyad; and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: What prevents a merchant among you who is busy in his marketplace from, when he returns to his home, not sleeping until he recites a Chapter from the Qur'an? So it will be written for him, in place of every verse he recites, ten good deeds, and ten evil deeds will be effaced for him.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: In how many (days) should I recite the Qur'an? He said: Recite it in fifths, recite it in sevenths. As for me, I have a codex divided into fourteen parts.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Qul Huwa Allah Ahad' is a third of the Qur'an, and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' is a fourth of the Qur'an.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all together, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abi Usama who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever recites Qul Huwa l-Llāhu Aḥad a hundred times when he betakes himself to his bed-spread (i.e. before sleeping) - it is forgiven for him what he has committed (of sins) fifty years prior to that. Yahya said: I asked Sama’a about that, so he (i.e. Sama’a) said: Abu Basir narrated (it) to me and said ‘I heard Aba Abdillah saying that’ and he (i.e. the Imam) added: O Aba Muhammad (i.e. Abu Basir) indeed if you were to try it you will find it to be true .

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who recites a hundred verses in his prayers at night - Allah Mighty and Majestic records for him devotion of the whole night (in reward) for it. The one who recites two hundred verses [at night] outside (his) prayers - the Qur’an will not dispute against him on the Day of Judgment. And the one who recites five hundred verses (total) in his prayers by day and at night - Allah Mighty and Majestic records for him in the Preserved Tablet a Qinṭār of good-deeds, and a Qinṭār is a thousand and two hundred Ūqiyya, and a (single) Ūqiyya is greater than the mountain of Uhud

Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If you recited al-Hamd upon a dead body seventy times and the soul was returned into it, that would not be surprising.

Khasa'il of al-Saduq: Ibn al-Walid from al-Saffar from al-Barqi from Ismail ibn Mihran from Ubays ibn Hisham from more than one from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The reciters of the Qur'an are three: A man who recited the Qur'an and took it as merchandise, attracted the rulers by it, and gained prominence over the people by it; and a man who recited the Qur'an and preserved its letters but neglected its bounds; and a man who recited the Qur'an and applied the medicine of the Qur'an to the ailment of his heart, so he kept awake by it his night, thirsted by it his day, stood in prayer by it in his mosques, and abandoned his bed for it. Because of them does Allah the All-Mighty, the Almighty, avert tribulation, and because of them does Allah grant victory over the enemies, and because of them does Allah send down rain from the sky. And by Allah, these reciters of the Qur'an are rarer than red sulphur.

Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever recites Sūrat al-Kahf every Friday eve, it becomes an expiation for him for what is between one Friday to another Friday.

Reward of Deeds: From his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (from his father), peace be upon them, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Whoever prays the dawn prayer and then recites 'Qul Huwa Allah Ahad' eleven times, no sin will follow him on that day, though the Devil's nose be soiled.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Qur'an came down as four fourths: a quarter concerning us, a quarter concerning our enemies, a quarter is Sunan (Precedents) and Amthal (Similitudes), and a quarter is Faraid (Obligations) and Ahkam (Rulings).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The people say that the Qur'an came down upon seven Ahruf.' He said: 'The enemies of Allah have lied! Rather, it came down upon one Harf from the One.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Qur'an that Jibril (peace be upon him) brought to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was seventeen thousand verses.

Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Salama who said: A man recited for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, wordings (huruf) from the Qur'an that were not as the people recite them. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Desist from this recitation! Recite as the people recite, until the Qaim (the Rising One) rises. So when the Qaim (peace be upon him) rises, he will recite the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, according to its true bounds, and he will bring out the Codex which Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) had written down.

He said: Ali (peace be upon him) took it out to the people when he had completed it and written it down, and said to them: This is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah sent it down upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and I have gathered it between the two boards. They said: Here it is with us, a comprehensive Codex in which the Qur'an is gathered; we have no need of it. He said: By Allah, you will not see it after this day of yours ever, It was only (an obligation) upon me to inform you after gathering it so that you recite (from) it.

Tafsir al-Qummi: My father narrated to me from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he recited: 'Guide us to the Straight Path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who are astray.' He said: The Maghdub Alayhim (those who have incurred wrath) are the Nussab (haters of the Ahl al-Bayt), and the Dhalin (those astray) are the Jews and Christians.

Tafsir al-Qummi: From him (Ibrahim ibn Hashim) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) concerning His words: “Non of the angered upon them and non of the astray” He said: The Maghdub Alayhim (those angered upon) are the Nussab (haters of the Ahl al-Bayt), and the Dhalin (the astray) are the Shakkak (doubters) who do not know the Imam.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Imran ibn Miytham, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man recited for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, they do not call you liar, but the wrongdoers reject the signs of Allah.' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes, by Allah, they rejected him with a most severe rejection, but it (the word in the verse) is softened (pronounced without Shadda): 'La yukadhdhibunaka' (they do not call you a liar), meaning: they will not come with a falsehood by which to negate your truth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said: I recited in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) 'Dhawa Adlin minkum' (two just men among you), so he said: 'Dhu Adlin Minkum' (a just man among you). This is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), which is a comprehensive statement, it justifies the fighting of the opponents, calls to the obedience of Allah, and ascends therein to ensure success.

By my life, there is no slackening or leniency on my part in fighting those who oppose the truth and grope in misguidance. So fear Allah, O servants of Allah, and flee unto Allah from His wrath; proceed on the path He has laid out for you, and stand firm in what He has bound upon you. In that case, Ali is the guarantor of your success eventually, even if you do not attain it immediately.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), in which he censures the followers of Satan.

They have made Satan the master of their affairs, and he has taken them as partners. He has laid eggs and hatched them in their bosoms. He creeps and crawls in their laps. He sees through their eyes, and speaks with their tongues. In this way he has led them to sinfulness and adorned for them foul things like the action of one whom Satan has made partner in his domain and speaks untruth through his tongue.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) concerning the Messenger of Allah and his Ahl al-Bayt.

Praise be to Allah, the Spreader of His bounty among the creation, and the Extender of His hand of generosity among them, We praise Him in all His affairs, and seek His assistance for the observance of His rights, and we bear witness that there is no god but He, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, He sent him to proclaim His command and speak of His remembrance; so he fulfilled it trustworthily, and passed away on the right path,

Beware! The example of the descendants (Ãl) of Muḥammad — peace and blessing of Allāh be upon him and his descendants — is like that of stars in the sky. When one star sets another one rises. So you are in a position that Allah's blessings on you have been perfected and He has shown you what you used to wish for.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), which is from his sermon that includes mention of the great events (al-Malahim).

All praise is due to Allah, the First before every first, and the Last after every last, His Firstness necessitates that there is no first before Him, and His Lastness necessitates that there is no last after Him, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, a testimony in which the secret matches the open declaration, and the heart matches the tongue.

O people Do not let my division make you guilty, nor my disobedience seduce you, and do not throw glances at each other when you hear it from me. By the One who split the grain and created the soul, indeed, what I inform you about from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), neither the conveyer lied nor the hearer was ignorant.

Well, it is as though I see a misguided man who is shouting in Syria and has put his banners in the outskirts of Kūfah. When his mouth would be fully opened, his recalcitrance would become intense and his steps on earth would become heavy (and tyrannic) then the disorder (so created) would cut the people with its teeth and war would rage with (all) its waves, days would become severe and nights full of toil. So when the crop grows and stands on stalks, its foam shoots forth and its lightning shines, the banners of misguiding rebellion would fire up and shoot forth like darkening night and surging sea. This and how many other storms would rend Kūfah and gales would sweep over it, and shortly heads would clash with heads, the standing crop would be harvested and the harvest would be smashed.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) that follows this pattern and in it is mention of the Day of Resurrection and the conditions of the people approaching [it]

[The Day of Resurrection] That is a day in which Allah will gather the first and the last for the reckoning of accounts and the recompense of deeds, in humility, standing, with sweat reaching their mouths, and the earth trembling beneath them; the best of them in condition is he who finds a place for his two feet and an open space for his breath.

May Allah have mercy on a man who ponders and takes lesson thereby, and when he takes lesson he achieves enlightenment. Whatever is present in this world would shortly not exist, while whatever is to exist in the next world is already in existence. Every countable thing would pass away. Every anticipation should be taken to be coming up and everything that is to come up should be taken as just near.

And from it, regarding the attribute of the learned one: The learned one is he who knows his worth, and sufficient for a man is ignorance that he does not know his worth. And indeed, among the most hated of men to Allah is a servant whom Allah has left to himself, deviating from the straight path, moving without a guide. If he is called to the cultivation of this world, he works, but if he is called to the cultivation of the Hereafter, he is sluggish. As though what he works for is obligatory upon him, and as though what he delays is excused from him.

And from it, concerning the end of time: That is a time wherein only a sleeping (inactive) believer would be safe; if he is present he is not recognized, and if he is absent he is not sought after. Those are the lamps of guidance and banners of night journeys. They do not spread calumnies nor divulge secrets, nor slander. They are those for whom Allah would open the doors of His mercy and keep off from them the hardships of His chastisement.

O people, a time will come to you when Islam would be capsized as a pot is capsized with all its contents. O people, Allāh has protected you from that He might be hard on you but He has not spared you from being put on trial. Allāh the Most Sublime of all speakers has said : Verily in this are signs and We do only try (the people).

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: As regards Amīr al-mu’minīn’s words “kullu mu'minin nuwamah” (every sleeping believer), he implies thereby one who is talked of little and causes no evil. And the word “al-masayiḥ” is the plural of “misyaḥ”. He is one who spreads trouble among people through evils and calumnies. And the word “al-madhāyi'” is the plural of “midhyā'”. He is one who on hearing of an evil about some one spreads it and shouts about it. And “al-budhur” is the plural of “badhur”. He is one who excels in foolishness and speaks rubbish.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) About the condition of the people before the descent of revelation and his performance in conveying the message

So now, certainly Allāh, Glorified is He, deputed Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), while no one among the Arabs read the Book, nor claimed prophethood or revelation, He fought those who disobeyed him in company with those who followed him, leading them towards their salvation, and hastening with them lest death overtook them, When any weary person sighed or a distressed one stopped he stood at him till he got him his aim, except the worst in whom there was not virtue at all. Eventually he showed them their goal and carried them to their places (of deliverance). Consequently their affairs moved on and their hand-mill began to rotate (i.e. position gained strength), their spears got straightened.

By Allāh, I was among their rear-guard till they turned back on their sides and were flocked in their rope. I never showed weakness or lack of courage, nor did I betray or become languid. By Allāh, I shall split the wrong till I extract right from its flanks!

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: I have quoted a selected part of this sermon before, but since I have found in this narration that it differs from the previous one in terms of addition and omission, the circumstance necessitated establishing it again.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding some of the attributes of the Noble Messenger, and the admonition to the Banu Umayya, and the exhortation to the people.

For the Noble Messenger, Until Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), a witness, a giver of good tidings and a warner, the best of creation as a child, and the most chaste as a grown man, the purest of the purified in character, and the most generous of those approached for generosity.

He exhorted the people: O people, secure light from the flame of the lamp of the preacher who follows what he preaches and draw water from the spring which has been cleaned of dirt. O creatures of Allāh, do not rely on your ignorance, do not be obedient to your desires because he who stays at this place is like one who stays on the brink of a bank undermined by water carrying ruin on his back from one portion to the other following his opinion which he changes (one after the other). He wants to make adhere what cannot adhere and to bring together what cannot keep together.

So fear Allāh and do not place your complaints before him who cannot redress your grievance, nor undo with his opinion what has been made obligatory for you. Certainly, there is no obligation on the Imam except what has been devolved on him from Allāh, namely to convey warnings, to exert in good advice, to revive the Sunnah, to enforce penalties on those liable to them and to issue shares to the deserving. So hasten towards knowledge before its vegetation dries up and before you turn yourselves away from seeking knowledge from those who have it. Desist others from the unlawful and abstain from it yourself, because you have been commanded to abstain (yourself) before abstaining (others).
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), in which he explains the virtue of Islam and mentions the Noble Messenger, then he reproaches his companions.

Praise be to Allah who established Islam, making its rulings easy for those who approach it, and strengthening its pillars against those who oppose it, So He made it a source of security for him who clings to it, peace for him who enters it, proof for him who speaks of it, witness for him who argues with it, light for him who seeks illumination from it, understanding for him who comprehends, essence for him who reflects, a sign for him who perceives, insight for him who resolves, a lesson for him who takes heed, salvation for him who believes, confidence for him who trusts, rest for him who entrusts, and a shield for him who endures.

It is the most bright of all paths, the clearest of all passages. It has dignified minarets, bright highways, burning lamps, prestigious field of activity, and high objective. It has a collection of race horses. It is approached eagerly. Its riders are honourable. Certification (of Allāh, Prophet etc.) is its way, good deeds are its minarets, death is its extremity, this world is its race-course, the Day of Judgement is its horses and Paradise is its point of approach.

He lit a flame for the seeker, and illuminated a sign for the one who was impeded. So he is Your trustworthy trustee, Your witness on the Day of Judgement, Your deputy as a blessing, and Your messenger of truth as mercy. O Allah, distribute to him a share from Your Justice, and award him multiples of good by Your bounty. O Allah, heighten his construction over the constructions of others, honour him when he comes to Thee, dignify his position before Thee, give him the intercession, and award him glory and distinction. And bring us out (on Day of Judgement) among his party, neither ashamed, nor repentant, nor deviators, nor pledge-breakers, nor strayers, nor misleads.
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: This discourse had already passed [appeared] in what preceded, except that we repeated it here because of the difference between the two narrations.

And from it, in his address to his companions: You have reached a station of Allah's honour for you such that your slave-girls are honoured by it, your neighbours are connected to you by it, and those who have no superiority over you honour you, and those who have no power over you fear you. You see the covenants of Allah being broken yet you do not get angry! While you are indignant at the breaking of the pledges of your fathers! The affairs of Allah used to come to you, originate from you, and return to you; so you gave the oppressors authority over your position, threw your reins into their hands, and surrendered Allah's affairs to them. They act in doubts and walk in desires. By Allah, if they scattered you under every star, Allah would surely gather you for the evil of their day!
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) on one of the days of Siffin

I have seen your flight and your dispersal from the lines, You were surrounded by rude and low people and Bedouins of Syria (ash-Shām), although you are the chiefs of Arabs and summit of distinction, and possess dignity as that of high nose and big hump of camel. The sigh of my bosom can subside only when I eventually see you surrounding them as they surrounded you, and see you dislodging them from their position as they dislodged you, killing them with arrows and striking them with spears so that their forward rows might fall on the rear ones just like the thirsty camels who have been turned away from their places of drink and removed from their water-points.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), which is one of the sermons of Al-Malhama.

Praise be to Allah, the Manifest to His creation through His creation, and the Apparent to their hearts through His Proof, He created the creation without deliberation, since deliberation does not befit except those with thinking organs, while He has no thinking organ in Himself. His knowledge pierces the inner hiddenness of the veils, and encompasses the obscurity of the core beliefs.

[A part of the same sermon about the Holy Prophet :] Allāh chose him from the lineal tree of prophets, from the flame of light, from the forehead of greatness, from the best part of the valley of al-Baṭha', from the lamps for darkness, and from the sources of wisdom.

The tribulation of the Banu Umayyah: The inner secrets have been revealed to those of insight, and the path of truth has become clear for its walker, and the hour has disclosed its face, and the sign has appeared for the observer. What is the matter with me? I see you as shapes without souls, and souls without shapes, devotees without piety, traders without profit, wakeful but sleeping, present but unseen, seeing but blind, hearing but deaf, and speaking but dumb! The banner of misguidance has stood on its pole, and spread through its branches, it measures you with its sa' and confuses you with its cubit. Its leader is one out of the religion, persisting on misguidance; so on that day none from among you will remain except as the sediment like the sediment of a cooking pot, or the dust like the dust of a bundle.

It would scrape you as leather is scraped, and trample you as harvest is trampled, and pick out the believer as a bird picks out a big grain from the thin grain. Where are these ways taking you, glooms misleading you, and falsehoods deceiving you? Whence are you brought and where are you driven? For every period there is a written document and everyone who is absent has to return. So listen to your godly leader and keep your hearts present. If he speaks to you be wakeful.

The forerunner must speak truth to his people, should keep his wits together and maintain presence of mind. He has clarified to you the matter as the stitch-hole is cleared, and scraped it as the gum is scraped (from the twigs). Nevertheless, now the wrong has set itself on its places and ignorance has ridden on its riding beasts. Unruliness has increased while the call for virtue is suppressed. Time has pounced upon like devouring carnivore, and wrong is shouting like a camel after remaining silent. People have become brothers over ill-doings, have forsaken religion, are united in speaking lie but bear mutual hatred in the matter of truth.

When such is the case, the son would be a source of anger (instead of coolness of the eye to parents) and rain the cause of heat, the wicked would abound and the virtuous would diminish. The people of this time would be wolves, its rulers beasts, the middle class men gluttons and the poor (almost) dead. Truth would go down, falsehood would overflow, affection would be claimed with tongues but people would be quarrelsome at heart. Adultery would be the key to lineage while chastity would be rare and Islam would be worn overturned like the skin.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), meaning az-Zubayr, at a time for which it was appropriate [and he invited him to enter into the allegiance a second time].

He asserts that he swore allegiance with his hand, but did not swear with his heart. So he does admit allegiance. As regards his claiming it otherwise than with his heart he should come forward with a clear argument for it. Otherwise, he should return to wherefrom he has gone out.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the pillars of religion. The pillars of religion are four: the truthfulness of faith, the practice of the law, good character, and the distribution of intellect.

Indeed, the best means by which seekers of nearness to Allah, the Glorified, seek nearness, is belief in Him and His Prophet, and fighting in His cause, for it is the pinnacle of Islam, and the Kalimatu'l-Ikhlas (expression of Divine purification) for it is the nature (fitrah), and the establishment of prayer for it is the religion (millah), and paying the alms-tax for it is a compulsory obligation, and fasting the month of Ramadan for it is a shield against chastisement, and the pilgrimage to the House and its consecration for these two acts banish poverty and wash away sins, and maintaining kinship for it increases wealth and lengthens life, and secret alms for it covers shortcomings, and open alms for it protects against a bad death, and acts of kindness for it saves from positions of disgrace.

Go ahead with the remembrance of Allāh for it is the best remembrance, and long for that which He has promised to the pious, for His promise is the most true promise. Tread the course of the Prophet for it is the most distinguished course. Follow the sunnah of the Prophet for it is the most right of all behaviours.

[The Virtue of the Qur'an:] Learn the Qur'an, for it is the fairest of discourses; understand it thoroughly, for it is the blossoming of the hearts; seek cure with its light, for it is the cure for the chests; and recite it beautifully, for it is the most beneficial of narratives. Indeed, the scholar who acts without his knowledge is like the bewildered ignorant who does not recover from his ignorance; rather, the argument against him is greater, the regret for him is more incumbent, and he is more blameworthy before Allah.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) He mentioned therein the Angel of Death, and the departing of the souls, and the incapacity of creation to describe Allah

Do you feel when the Angel of Death enters a house? Or do you see him when he takes out the life of anyone? Rather, how does he take out the life of an embryo in the womb of his mother? Does he reach it through any part of her body? Or did the spirit respond to his call with the permission of its Lord? Or does he stay with him in the mother’s interior? How can he describe his God, who is unable to describe a creature like himself?
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which there are exhortations for the people. Regarding abstemiousness, fear of Allah, and the importance of preparing for the Hereafter.

Praise be to Allah, the One who connects praise with bounties and bounties with gratitude, We praise be upon Him for His favors as we praise Him for His trials, and we seek His help against these souls that are slow to obey what they were commanded and quick to rush to what they were forbidden, and we seek His forgiveness for that which His knowledge encompasses and His book records: knowledge that does not fall short, and a book that does not omit anything, and we believe in Him with the faith of one who has seen the unseen with his own eyes, and has attained the promised [rewards], a faith whose purity eliminates polytheism, and whose certainty removes doubt.

We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the One, without any partner for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, These two testimonies elevate the speech and raise the deed, A scale upon which they are placed will not be light, nor will a scale from which they are removed become heavy.

I advise you, O creatures of Allah, to have fear of Allah, which is the provision and with it is the return. The provision is that which reaches its destination and the return is that which succeeds. The best caller has called to it, and the best listener has listened to it. So the caller has proclaimed and the listener has succeeded.

O creations of Allah Certainly fear of Allah has saved the lovers of Allah from unlawful items and gave His dread to their hearts till their nights are passed in wakefulness and their noons in thirst. So they achieve comfort through trouble and copious watering through thirst. They regarded death to be near and therefore hastened towards (good) actions. They rejected their desires and so they kept death in their sight.

And among its changes is that you see the pitiable man becoming enviable, and the enviable man becoming pitiable, This is because the wealth has gone and misfortune has come to him. And among its lessons is that a man reaches near (the realization of) his desires when (suddenly) the approach of his death cuts them; then neither the desire is achieved nor the desires spared. Glory to Allāh, how deceitful are its pleasures, how thirst-rousing its quenching and how sunny its shade. That which approaches (i.e. death) cannot be sent back, he who goes away does not return. Glory to Allāh, how near is the living to the dead because he will meet him soon and how far is the dead from the living because he has gone away from him!

Certainly that which you have been commanded to do is wider than what you have been refrained from, and what has been made lawful for you is more than what has been prohibited. Then give up what is less for what is much, and what is limited for what is vast. Allah has guaranteed your livelihood and has commanded you to act. Therefore, the pursuit of that which has been guaranteed to you should not get preference over that whose performance has been enjoined upon you.

Although, by Allah, doubt has certainly overtook and certainty entered, so it seems as if what was guaranteed to you has become obligatory upon you, and as if what was obligatory upon you has been lifted from you. So hasten to action, and fear the suddenness of death, for the return of age is not hoped for as the return of livelihood is hoped for, whatever is missed from livelihood today, its increase is hoped for tomorrow, but whatever is lost from age yesterday, its return is not hoped for today. Hope is for "Fear Allah as He ought to be feared and do not die except while you are Muslims."

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding seeking rain. O Allah, have mercy upon us with abundance and productivity, and grant us wealth after poverty, and open for us from Your mercy, O Most Merciful.

O Allah, we have come out to You when the years of drought have crowded over us like (herd of) thin camels, and rain clouds have abandoned us. Thou art the hope for the afflicted and succour for the seeker. We call Thee when the people have lost hopes, cloud has been denied and cattle have died, that do not seize us for our deeds and do not catch us for our sins, and spread Thy mercy over us through raining clouds, rain-fed blossoming, amazing vegetation, and heavy down-pours with which all that was dead regains life and all that was lost returns.

O Allah! Give rain from Thee which should be life giving, satisfying, thorough, wide-scattered, purified, blissful, plentiful and invigorating. Its vegetation should be exuberant its branches full of fruits and its leaves green. With it Thou reinvigorates the weak among Thy creatures and bringest back to life the dead among Thy cities.

O Allah! A drink from Thee with which our high lands get covered with green herbage, streams get flowing, our sides grow green, our fruits thrive, our cattle prosper, our far-flung areas get watered and our dry areas get its benefit with Thy vast blessing and immeasurable grant on Thy distressed universe and Thy untamed beasts. And pour upon us rain which is drenching, continuous and heavy; wherein one cycle of rain clashes with the other and one rain drop pushes another (into a continuous chain), its lightning should not be deceptive, its cheek not rainless, its white clouds not scattered and rain not light so that the famine-stricken thrive with its abundant herbage and the drought stricken come to life with its bliss. Certainly, Thou pourest down rain after the people lose hopes and spreadest Thy mercy, since Thou art the Guardian, the praiseworthy.

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: The explanation of the rare expressions in this sermon. His words (peace be upon him): 'Our mountains cracked' means they split due to drought. It is said 'the garment cracked' when it tore. It is also said 'the vegetation cracked' or 'it dried and withered' when it dried up and became dry. All of it means the same.
His words “wa hamat dawābbuna” means became thirsty, as “huyam” means thirst.

His words: 'Hadābiru's-sinin' (the thin camels of the years). This is the plural of 'hidbār', which is the camel made thin by long travel. So he likened the year to such a camel, in which drought had become widespread. The Arab poet Dhū ar-Rummah said: 'These thin camels remain in their places, facing hardships, or we cast them into a barren land.'
His words: "and no scattered pieces of its upper part." Al-Qaza' means the small pieces scattered from the clouds.

His words: "And not two lips of its going away." For its construction is: "And not the owner/possessor of two lips of its going away." Al-shaffan means the cold wind, and adh-dhihab means the light rain. He omitted "dhata" because of the listener's knowledge of it.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), in which he advises his companions.

He was sent as a caller to the Truth, and a witness over the creation, So he conveyed the messages of his Lord without being lazy or deficient, and he fought the enemies of Allah without being weak or making excuses, He is the Imam of those who practice piety, and the power of perception of those who achieve guidance.

I do long that Allāh may cause separation between me and you, and give me those who have a better right to be with me than you. By Allāh, they are people of blissful ideas, enduring wisdom and true speech. They keep aloof from revolt. They trod forward on the path (of Allāh) and ran on the high-road. Consequently, they achieved the everlasting next life and easeful honours.
Beware! By Allah, a tall lad of swinging gait from Banū Thaqīf would be placed over you. He would eat away your vegetation and melt your fat. So, O Aba Wadhāḥah,

As-Sayyid al-Sharif said: “Al-Wadhah” means “al-khunfasa’ (dung-beetle).” In this sentence, he refers to al-Hajjaj, and there is a narration concerning him and “al-khunfasa’” which is not the place to mention it here.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him): Rebuking the misers regarding wealth and the self.

You spend no wealth in the cause of Him Who gave it, nor do you risk your lives for the sake of Him Who created them. You enjoy honour through Allāh among His creatures, but you do not honour Allāh among His creatures. You should derive lessons from your occupying the places of those who were before you and from the departure of your nearest brothers.
And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning the righteous among his companions As for the righteous, they are those who do not fear for their souls nor grieve over what has passed

You are the supporters of Truth, and the brethren in faith, the shields on the day of tribulation, and the inner circle among the people, With you I strike the one who turns away, and I hope for the obedience of the one who advances forward, Therefore, assist me with sincere advice free from deceit, pure from doubt; By Allah, I am the most deserving of the people [to be followed]!

And from his sayings (peace be upon him), and he had gathered the people and exhorted them to jihad, but they remained silent for a long time, so he said (peace be upon him): "What is the matter with you? Have you become dumb?" A group of them replied: "O Commander of the Faithful, if you go forth, we shall be with you." Whereupon he said (peace be upon him):

What has happened to you? You may not be guided aright or shown the right path. Should in these circumstances I go forth? In fact, at this time one of the brave and the valorous among you whom I select should go out. It does not suit me to leave the army, the city, the public treasury, the land revenue, the dispensation of justice among Muslims and looking after the demands of the claimants, and to follow one contingent after the other moving here and there like featherless arrow moving in the quiver.

I am the axis of the mill, It rotates on me while I remain in my position, As soon as I leave it the centre of its rotation would be disturbed and its lower stone would also be disturbed. By Allāh, this is a very bad advice. By Allāh, if I had not been hoping for martyrdom by my meeting with the enemy—and my meeting with him has been ordained, I would have secured my carrier and went away from you and would not have sought you so long as North and South differed.

There is no benefit in the majority of your numbers because of lack of unity of your hearts. I have put you on the clear path whereon no one will perish except who perishes by himself. He who sticks to it would achieve Paradise and he who deviates goes to Hell. He who sticks to it would achieve Paradise and he who deviates goes to Hell.
And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning his description and the description of his opponents, and it is said that it is among the Companions of the Camel.
They thundered and flashed lightning, but with these two things was failure, and we do not thunder until we strike, nor do we flow (of words) until we rain.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), mentioning his virtue and admonishing the people.

By Allāh, I have been taught the conveyance of messages, the fulfilment of waiting periods, and the completion of words. And with us—the People of the House—are the doors of wisdom and the light of authority. Beware, the laws of religion are one, and its paths are straight. He who adheres to them attains and succeeds, and he who refrains from them goes astray and regrets.

Do act for the day for which provisions are stored, and when the intentions would be tested. If a person’s own intelligence which is present with him does not help him, the wits (of others) which are remote from him are more unhelpful and those which are away from him more useless. Dread the fire whose flame is severe, whose hollow is deep, whose dress is iron and whose drink is bloody puss. Beware! The good name of a man retained by Allāh, the Sublime, among the people is better than wealth inherited by those who would not praise him.

And from his words (peace be upon him), after the Night of Hirr, when a man from among his companions stood up and said: “You forbade us from arbitration, then ordered us to do it, so we do not know which of the two was more appropriate.” He (peace be upon him) struck one hand over the other and said:

This is the reward of one who breaks pledge. By Allāh, when I gave you my orders (namely) to abide by arbitration I had led you to an undesirable thing (namely war) in which Allāh had ordained good. If you had been steadfast I would have guided you, if you had been bent I would have straightened you and if you had refused I would have rectified you. This was the surest way. But with whom and to whom. I wanted my treatment from you but you proved to be my disease, like the extractor of thorn with the thorn when he knows that the thorn bends towards itself. My Allāh, the physicians have despaired of this fatal ailment and water-drawers have become tired with the rope of this well.

Where are the people who were invited to Islam and they accepted it? They read the Qur'an and decided according to it? They were exhorted to fight and they leapt (towards it) as she-camels leap towards their youngs. They took their swords out of the sheaths, and went out into the world in groups and rows?! Some of them perished and some survived. The good news of survival does not please them nor do they get condoled about the dead. Their eyes have turned white with weeping. Their bellies are emaciated because of fasting. Their lips are dry because of (constant) praying. Their colour is pale because of wakefulness. Their faces bear the dust of God-fearing. These are, my comrades who have departed. We should be justified if we feel eager for them and bite our hands in their separation!

Certainly, Satan has made his ways easy for you, and wants to unfasten the knots of your religion one by one, and to give you division in place of unity, and strife in place of division; so turn away from his whisperings and breathings, and accept the advice of one who offers it to you, and hold it fast in your minds.
And from his words (peace be upon him), he said to the Kharijites, and he had gone out to their camp while they were persisting in rejecting the Arbitration, so he said (peace be upon him):

Were all of you with us in Ṣiffīn? They replied that some of them were but some of them were not. Amīr al-mu’minīn said: Then you divide yourselves into two groups. One of those who were in Ṣiffīn and other of those who were not present there, so that I may address each as I see suitable. Then he shouted to the people: Stop talking and keep quiet to listen to what I say. Turn your hearts to me. Whomever we ask for evidence, he should give it according to his knowledge about it.

Then he had a long conversation with them (peace be upon him) Among the things he said was: Did you not say when they raised the Qur'ans - as a stratagem and a trick, and deception and fraud - 'They are our brothers and our comrades in calling [to Islam]. They have asked us to cease [fighting] and have found rest in the Book of Allah, Glorified is He. So the opinion is to accept from them and to relieve them [of fighting]'? So I said to you: 'This matter has an outward appearance of faith, but an inward reality of enmity. Its beginning is mercy, and its end is regret. So remain steadfast on your position, and adhere to your path, and press your teeth [in effort] in jihad, and do not pay heed to the caller who calls: If he is answered, he will mislead; and if he is left [unanswered], he will be disgraced.' And this action [of arbitration] has taken place, and I have seen you agreeing to it.

By Allah, if I had refused it, its obligation would not have been incumbent upon me, nor would Allah have burdened me with its sin, and by Allah, now that I have accepted it, I am the rightful one who should be followed, and certainly the Book is with me; I have not forsaken it since I kept company with it. For we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and killing revolved among fathers, sons, brothers, and relatives, so we did not increase in every calamity and hardship except in faith, and perseverance upon the truth, and submission to the command, and patience with the pain of wounds.

But we have only become fighting our brethren in Islam because of what entered it of misguidance, crookedness, doubts and (wrong) interpretation, if we find any way by which we may come near each other in whatever common remains between us, we would accept it, and would give up everything else.

And from his words (peace be upon him), he said to his companions in the hour of battle at Siffin: Behold, I command you to God-consciousness, and I advise you sincerely, and I wish that you do not go astray after having been guided, and I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for myself. Indeed, I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Whoever does not show mercy to our young, honor our elders, appreciate our few, and recognize the rights of our many, is not one of us.'

Whoever among you feels spiritedness of heart during the action, and finds any of his comrades feeling disheartened, should ward off (the enemies) from him just as he would do from himself, because of the superiority he enjoys over the other, for if Allāh had willed He would have made the former also like him. Certainly death is a quick seeker. Neither does the steadfast escape it nor can the runner-away defy it. The best death is to be killed. By Allāh in Whose hand (power) lies the life of the son of Abū Ṭālib, certainly a thousand strikings of the sword on me are easier to me than a death in bed which is not in obedience to Allāh.

It is as if I see you uttering voices like the rustling sound of lizards! You do not seek your own claims nor do you defend against oppression. You have been let free on the path. He who rushes (into the battle) achieves salvation, while he who lags behind, hesitating, gets destruction.
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the meaning of the Khawarij, when they rejected the arbitration of men, and he censures them in it, he said (peace be upon him):

We did not appoint men as arbitrators, but we appointed the Qur'an as the arbitrator. And this Qur'an is merely writing concealed between the two covers, it does not speak with a tongue, and it necessarily requires an interpreter. And men alone are those who speak on its behalf. And when the people invited us to appoint the Qur'an as the arbitrator between us, we could not be the party turning away from the Book of Allah, since Allah said, Exalted is He: 'So if you differ over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger.'

Its return to Allah is that we judge by His Book, and its return to the Messenger is that we take by his Sunnah; So if judgment is rendered with truth in the Book of Allah, then we are more rightful among the people for it; and if it is judged by the Sunnah of his Messenger, then we are more preferable of them for it.

As for your saying: Why did you set a time limit between yourself and them regarding the Arbitration? I did so only so that the ignorant may become clear (about the truth), and the knowledgeable may hold firm, and perhaps Allah will rectify the affairs of this community during this truce, and they will not be seized by their throats, so that they hasten to recognize the truth and submit to the first deviation. Indeed, the best of people before Allah is he who loves acting according to the truth more—even if it diminishes and grieges him—than acting according to falsehood, even if it brings him benefit and increase.

So, where are you being mislead?! And from where have you been brought (to this state)? Be prepared to march to the people who have deviated from the right and do not see it, have been entangled in wrongdoing and are not corrected. They are away from the Book, turned from the (right) path. You are not trustworthy to rely upon, nor are you holders of honour to be adhered to. You are very bad in kindling the fire of fighting. Woe to you! I had to bear a lot of worries from you. Some day I call you (to jihād) and some day I speak to you in confidence, you are neither true free men at the time of call, nor trustworthy brothers at the time of speaking in confidence!
And from his speech (peace be upon him) to the Kharijites also And from his speech (peace be upon him) to the Kharijites also

If you refuse except to claim that I erred and went astray, why do you lead astray the general public of the Ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) by my misguidance, and hold them accountable for my error, and declare them disbelievers on account of my sins! Your swords are on your shoulders; you place them in places of purity and disease, and you mix up the one who sinned with the one who did not sin. And you know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stoned the adulterer [the married one], then he prayed over him, then he allowed his family to inherit from him, and he killed the murderer and allowed his family to inherit his estate, and he cut off the thief and whipped the unmarried adulterer, then he distributed to both of them from the booty, and they married Muslim women; so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took them to task for their sins, and established Allah's right in them, and did not withhold their share from Islam, nor did he remove their names from among His people.

Then you are the worst of people, and those whom Satan has cast into his targets and struck with his pride! And two types of people will be ruined with regard to me: an excessive lover whose love takes him away from the truth, and an excessive hater whose hatred takes him away from the truth, and the best of people in status with regard to me is the moderate one, so hold to him, and hold to the Great Majority, for the hand of Allah is with the community, and beware of division! For the isolated one from the people is to Satan, just as the isolated one from the sheep is to the wolf. Behold, whoever calls to this banner, kill him, even if he be under this turban of mine.

Indeed, the two arbitrators were appointed to revive what the Qur'an revives and to destroy what the Qur'an destroys. Its revival is unity upon it, and its destruction is division from it. If the Qur'an drives us to them, we follow them; and if it drives them to us, they follow us. I did not bring you misfortune, nor did I deceive you in your matter, nor did I confuse it for you. Your own group unanimously suggested the choice of two men. We bound them that they would not exceed the Qur'an. But they deviated from it, and abandoned the truth while both of them were aware of it. And injustice was their desire, so they proceeded upon it. And our exclusion of them had preceded—in judging with justice and adhering to the truth—their evil opinion and the injustice of their verdict.
And from his words (peace be upon him), which is among the things he used to report regarding the great battles at Basra.

O Aḥnaf! It is as though I see him advancing with an army which has neither dust nor noise, nor rustling of reins, nor neighing of horses. They are trampling the ground with their feet as if they are the feet of ostriches.
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: He (peace be upon him) pointed thereby to the Chief of the Negroes.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: Woe to your inhabited streets, and your decorated houses which have wings like the wings of vultures and trunks like the trunks of elephants; [they are] from those people whose killed are not mourned, and whose missing are not searched for. I turn this world over on its face, value it only according to its (low) value, and look at it with an eye suitable to it.

And from it, and pointing to it at that time, is the description of the Turks I can see a people whose faces are like shields covered with rough-scraped skins. They dress themselves in silken and woollen clothes and hold dear excellent horses. Their killing and bloodshed shall take place freely till the wounded shall walk over the dead and the number of runners-away shall be less than those taken prisoner

One of his companions said to him: You have been given knowledge of hidden things, O Commander of the Faithful! He (peace be upon him) laughed and said to the man—who was from the tribe of Kalb: One of his companions said to him: You have been given knowledge of hidden things, O Commander of the Faithful! He (peace be upon him) laughed and said to the man—who was from the tribe of Kalb:

O brother of Kalb This is not knowledge of the unseen Rather, it is learning from the One who has knowledge And indeed, the knowledge of the unseen is the knowledge of the Hour And what Allah, Glory be to Him, enumerated by His saying Indeed, Allah is with Him the knowledge of the Hour and He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. And no soul knows in what land it will die.. The Verse

Therefore, He alone knows what is in the wombs, whether male or female, ugly or handsome, generous or miserly, wretched or happy, and who will be the fuel for Hell and who will be in the company of the Prophets in Paradise. This is the knowledge of the hidden things which is not known to anyone save Allah. All else is that whose knowledge Allah passed on to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he passed it on to me, and prayed for me that my bosom may retain it and my ribs may hold it.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) Satan intends, or I allude through it to a people

Beware! Satan has collected his group and assembled his horse-men and foot-soldiers. Surely, with me is my sagacity. I have neither deceived myself nor ever been deceived. By Allāh I shall fill to the brim for them a cistern from which I alone would draw water. They can neither turn away from it nor return to it.
And from his words (peace be upon him) to Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him), when he was exiled to ar-Rabadhah.

O Abū Dharr, You showed anger in the name of Allāh, therefore have hope in Him for whom you became angry. The people were afraid of you in the matter of their world, while you feared them for your faith. Then leave to them that for which they are afraid of you, and get away from them taking away what you fear them about. How needy are they for what you dissuade them from, and how heedless are you towards what they are denying you. You will shortly know who is the gainer tomorrow (on the Day of Judgement) and who is more enviable. Even if these skies and earth were closed to some individual and he feared Allāh, then Allāh would open them for him. Only rightfulness should attract you while wrongfulness should detract you. If you had accepted their worldly attractions they would have loved you, and if you had shared in it they would have given you asylum.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him): In it, he explains the reason for his seeking the caliphate and describes the Righteous Imam.

O differing minds and divided hearts, whose bodies are present but wits are absent. I am leading you (amicably) towards truthfulness, but you run away from it like goats running away from the howling of a lion! How hard it is for me to uncover for you the secrets of justice, or to straighten the curve of truthfulness.
