O Allah You know that what we did was not a competition for power, nor seeking anything from the vanities of the world, but rather to restore the signs of Your religion and to manifest reform in Your lands, so that the oppressed among Your servants may be safe and the suspended commands of Yours may be established.
O my Allah! I am the first who leaned (towards Thee) and who heard and responded (to the call of Islam). No one preceded me in prayer (salat) except the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

And you certainly know that he who is in charge of honour, life, booty, legal commandments and the leadership of the Muslims should not be a miser, as his greed would aim at their wealth, nor be ignorant as he would then mislead them with his ignorance, nor be of rude behaviour who would estrange them with his rudeness, nor should he deal unjustly with wealth thus preferring one group over another, nor should he accept a bribe while taking decisions, as he would forfeit rights and hold them up without finality, nor should he ignore sunnah as he would ruin the people.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), in which he gives advice and encourages detachment from the world.

Praise of God: We praise Him for whatever He takes or gives, and for whatever He tests and tries us with, The Hidden One is aware of every secret, the Present One is aware of every inner state, the All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, and what the eyes betray. And we bear witness that there is no god but He, and that Muhammad is His noble one and His messenger, a testimony in which the secret matches the public declaration, and the heart matches the tongue.

For by Allah, it is seriousness (reality), not play, and truth, not falsehood, and it is none other than death; its caller is made to be heard, and its dragsman is made to hasten, so let not the multitude of people deceive you regarding yourself, for you have seen those who were before you, who amassed wealth, feared poverty, and felt safe from its consequences—the longevity of desire and the apparent distance from death— how death overtook them, turning them out of their homelands, and took them from their places of safety, borne on the beams of the coffins, with people busy about them one after another, carrying them on their shoulders and supporting them with their hands.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), he glorifies Allah, the Exalted, mentions the Quran and the Prophet, and exhorts the people.

The greatness of God, the Exalted This world and the next have submitted to Him their reins, and the skies and earths have flung their keys towards Him. The thriving trees bow to Him in the morning and evening, and produce for Him — flaming fire from their branches, and at His command, turn their own feed into ripe fruits.

[A part of the same sermon about the Holy Qur’ān :] The Book of Allāh is among you. It speaks and its tongue does not falter. It is a house whose pillars do not fall down, and a power whose supporters are never routed.

[A part of the same sermon about this world :] Certainly this world is the end of the sight of the (mentally) blind who see nothing beyond it. The sight of a looker (who looks with the eye of his mind) pierces through and realizes that the (real) house is beyond this world. The looker therefore wants to get out of it while the blind wants to get into it. The looker collects provision from it (for the next world) while the blind collects provision for this very world.

[A part of the same sermon — A caution:] You should know that a man gets satiated and wearied with everything except life, because he does not find for himself any pleasure in death. It is in the position of life for a dead heart, sight for the blind eye, hearing for the deaf ear, quenching for the thirsty and it contains complete sufficiency and safety.

And upon you be the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah. And upon you be the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah. Know that there is no thing except that its owner is likely to become sated with it and weary of it, except for life, for he does not find rest for it in death. And that is only in the position of wisdom, which is life for the dead heart, and sight for the blind eye, and hearing for the deaf ear, and refreshment for the thirsty, and in it is all wealth and safety.
And from his words (peace be upon him), when Umar ibn al-Khattab consulted him about going out to the campaign against the Romans.

And Allah has relied upon for the people of this religion the strengthening of the boundary (Hawzah), and the covering of the defect (Awrah), He who helped them when they were few and could not help themselves, and protected them when they were few and could not protect themselves, the Living who does not die. Indeed, whenever you proceed to this enemy with your own self, and meet them with your person and suffer defeat, you will not be a refuge for the Muslims beyond the furthest parts of their lands, and there will be no place after you to which they return, so send to them a warrior, and gather with him the people of experience and sincerity, if Allah grants victory, then that is what you love; and if it is otherwise, you will be a support for the people and a returning place for the Muslims.
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the matter of allegiance. Give the allegiance with sincerity, a good intention, and support for the oppressed against the oppressor.

Your allegiance to me was not without thinking, nor is my and your position the same. I seek you for Allāh’s sake but you seek me for your own benefits. O people! support me despite your heart’s desires. By Allāh, I will take revenge for the oppressed from the oppressor and will put a string in the nose of the oppressor and drag him to the spring of truthfulness even though he may grudge it.
And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning the matter of Talha and az-Zubayr and regarding the allegiance (bay'ah) to him.

Talha and Al-Zubayr: By Allāh, they did not find any disagreeable thing in me, nor did they do justice between me and themselves. Surely, they are now demanding a right which they have abandoned and blood which they have themselves shed. If I pertook in it with them then they too have a share in it, but if they committed it without me the demand should be against them. The first step of their justice should be that they pass verdict against themselves. I have my intelligence with me. I have never mixed matters nor have they appeared mixed to me.

Certainly, this is the rebellious group, in which is the near one (Zubayr), the scorpion's venom ('A'ishah), and the doubt that casts a veil (on facts). And the matter is clear, and the falsehood has been shaken from its foundation, and its tongue has ceased from its mischief. By Allah, I will not let their cistern be drained; I am the one who controls it. They will not draw from it with ease, nor will they drink from it after it is finished.

[A part of the same sermon :] You advanced towards me shouting “allegiance, allegiance” like she-camels having delivered newly born young ones leaping towards their young. I held back my hand but you pulled it towards you I drew back my hand but you dragged it. O my Allāh! these two have ignored my rights and did injustice to me. They both have broken allegiance to me, and roused people against me. Unfasten Thou what they have fastened, and do not make strong what they have woven. Show them the evil in what they aimed at and acted upon. Before fighting I asked them to be steadfast in allegiance and behaved with them with consideration but they belittled the blessing and refused (to adopt the course of) safety.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) in which he alludes to the mention of the great events (al-Malahim).

He will direct desires towards (the path of) guidance while people will have turned guidance towards desires, and he will turn their views to the direction of the Qur’ān while the people will have turned the Qur’ān to their views.

[A part of the same sermon :] (Before this Enjoiner of Good, matters will deteriorate) till war will rage among you with full force, showing forth its teeth, with udders full of sweet milk but with a sour tip. Beware, it will be tomorrow and the morrow will come soon with things which you do not know. The Man in power, not from this crowd, will take to task all those were formerly appointed for their ill deeds and the earth will pour forth its internal treasures and fling before him easily her keys. He will show you the just way of behaviour and revive the Qur’ān and sunnah which have become lifeless (among people).

[A part of the same sermon :] As if I see (him), he (the Enjoiner of Evil) [2] is shouting in Syria (ash-Shām) and is extending his banners to the outskirts of Kūfah. He is bent towards it like the biting of the she-camel. He has covered the ground with heads. His mouth is wide open and (the trampling of) his footsteps on the ground have become heavy. His advance is broad and his attacks are severe.

By Allah, he will surely disperse you throughout the ends of the earth until only a few of you remain, like kohl in the eye. You will continue in this state until the Arabs return to their senses. Therefore, adhere to the established ways, the clear signs, and the close era upon which the remainder of Prophethood stands. And know that Satan only makes his paths easy for you so that you may follow him closely.
And from his words (peace be upon him) on the occasion of the Consultative Committee

No one preceded me in inviting people to truthfulness, in giving consideration to kinship and practising generosity. So, hear my word and preserve what I say. Maybe you will see soon after today that over this matter swords will be drawn and pledges will be broken, so much so that some of you will become leaders of the people of misguidance and followers of people of ignorance.

And it is fitting for those who possess infallibility and upon whom safety is bestowed, that they show mercy to the people of sins and disobedience, and that gratitude should be dominant over them and a barrier preventing them from [fault-finding], so how [is it] about the fault-finder who blamed his brother and reproached him with his affliction/sin! Does he not remember the place of Allah's concealment of him from his sins [of which] is greater than the sin he blamed him for! And how can he vilify him for a sin that he has himself committed like it?! If he has not committed that specific sin, then he has disobeyed Allah in what is other than it, from what is greater than it, and by Allah, if he did not disobey Him in the major [sins], and disobeyed Him in the minor [sins], his boldness in faulting people is greater!

O servant of Allah Do not be quick in exposing anyone’s sin for he may be forgiven for it, and do not feel yourself safe even for a small sin because you may be punished for it Therefore, every one of you who comes to know the faults of others should not expose them in view of what he knows about his own faults, and he should remain busy in thanks that he has been saved from what others have been indulging in
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) regarding the places of generosity/kindness. Against misplaced generosity.

The act of generosity (al-ma'ruf) when given to those not entitled to it He who shows generosity to those who have no claim to it or who are not fit for it would not earn anything except the praise of the ignoble and appreciation of bad persons, although as long as he continues giving, the ignorant will say how generous his hand is, even though in the affairs of Allāh he is a miser.

[Deserving recipients of generosity:] Therefore, to whosoever Allah gives wealth he should use it in extending good behaviour to his kinsmen, in entertaining, in releasing prisoners and the afflicted; in giving to the poor and to debtors, and he should endure (the troubles arising out of) the fulfilment of rights (of others) and hardships in expectation of reward. Certainly, the achievement of these qualities is the height of greatness in this world and achievement of the distinctions of the next world; if Allah so wills.

And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) regarding praying for rain And in it is a reminder to the servants of the obligation of seeking help through the mercy of Allah when the mercy of rain is withheld from them

Beware; the earth which bears you, and the sky which overshadows you, are obedient to their Lord, and they have not been bestowing their blessings on you for any feeling of pity on you or inclination towards you, nor for any good which they expect from you, but they were commanded to bestow benefits on you and they are obeying, and were asked to maintain your good and so they are maintaining it.

Certainly, Allāh tests His servants when they commit evil deeds by decreasing fruits, holding back blessings, and closing the treasures of goodness so that the repentant may repent, the one turning away may turn away, the mindful may be mindful, and the heedful may take heed. And Allāh, the Glorified, has made seeking forgiveness a means for the pouring down of livelihood and mercy upon the creation so He said: 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.' He will send [down from] the sky rain in pouring showers. And give you wealth and children And make for you gardens and make for you rivers.
Allāh may shower mercy on him who took up repentance, gave up sins and hastened (in performing good acts before) his death.

O Allah! we have come out to Thee from under the curtains and coverings (of houses) when the beasts and children are crying, seeking Thy Mercy, hoping for the generosity of Thy bounty and fearing Thy chastisement and retribution.

O Allah, cause us to drink from Your rain and do not make us among the despairing and do not destroy us by years (of drought) and do not punish us 'for what the foolish among us have committed' O the Most Merciful of all!

O Allah, we have come out to You to complain to You what is not hidden from You, when the severe hardships have forced us, the drought-stricken famines have driven us, the difficult needs have made us helpless, and the troublesome tribulations have clung to us.
O Allah, we ask You not to send us back disappointed, nor to turn us back with downcast eyes, nor to address us for our sins, nor to deal with us according to our deeds.

O Allah, Pour upon us Your rain, Your blessing, Your sustenance and Your mercy, And give us a drink that is beneficial, quenching, and producing herbage, With which You cause to grow what has been lost, and revive what has died, Beneficial for freshness, abundant in yield, With which You water the dry plains, and make flow the valleys, And cause the trees to leaf out, and lower the prices, Surely, You are Powerful over whatever You will.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the sending of the Messengers, the virtue of the People of the House, and the mention of the people of misguidance.

Allah sent His messengers with what He distinguished them with from His revelation, and made them a proof for Him upon His creation, so that the proof should not be established against them by their leaving excuses to Him, He called them with the tongue of truth to the path of truth. Know that Allah has fully known the creation, not that He was ignorant of what they concealed from among the guarded secrets of their inner selves and the hidden contents of their souls, but in order to test them [as to] 'Which of them is best in deed?' so that the reward is a recompense, and the punishment is a destination.

[The position of Ahlu’l-bayt (the Household of the Holy Prophet) :] Where are those who falsely and unjustly claimed that they are deeply versed in knowledge, as against us, although Allāh raised us in position and kept them down, bestowed upon us knowledged but deprived them, and entered us (in the fortress of knowledge) but kept them out. With us guidance is to be sought and blindness (of misguidance) is to be changed into brightness. Surely Imams (divine leaders) will be from the Quraysh. They have been planted in this line through Hāshim. It would not suit others nor would others be suitable as heads of affairs

Where are the minds which seek light from the lamps of guidance, and the eyes which look at minarets of piety?! Where are the hearts dedicated to Allāh, and devoted to the obedience of Allāh?! They are all crowding towards worldly vanities and quarrelling over unlawful issues. The ensigns of Paradise and Hell have been raised for them but they have turned their faces away from Paradise and proceeded to Hell by dint of their performances. Allāh called them but they showed dislike and ran away. When Satan called them they responded and proceeded (towards him).

O people You are, in this world, the target for the arrows of death. With every drinking there is choking, and with every eating there is suffocation! You do not attain any benefit in it except by foregoing another, and no one among you advances in age by a day except by the taking away of a day from his life. Nothing more is added to his eating unless it reduces what was there before of his sustenance, and no mark appears for him unless a mark disappears for him, and nothing new comes into being for him unless the new becomes old for him, and no new crop comes up for him unless a crop has been reaped from him. Those roots are gone whose off-shoots we are. How can an offshoot live after the departure of its root?

[A part of the same sermon on innovation (bid‘ah) :] No innovation is introduced unless one sunnah is forsaken, keep away from innovations and stick to the broad road. Surely the old tested ways are the best and the innovated ones are bad.
And a saying of his (peace be upon him) when ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb consulted him about taking part himself in fighting the Persians.

In this matter, victory or defeat is not dependent on the smallness or greatness of forces. It is Allah’s religion which He has raised above all faiths, and His army which He has mobilised and extended, till it has reached the point where it stands now, and has arrived its present positions. We hold a promise from Allah, and He will fulfil His promise and support His army.

The position of the one who holds authority is like the thread of the beads, which gathers and unites them. If the thread is broken, they disperse and are lost, and never come together again in their entirety. The Arabs today, even though few in number, are many because of Islam, and strong because of unity. So be their axis, and rotate the mill with the Arabs, and be their root; avoid the fire of war. For if you leave this land, the Arabs will attack you from its edges and corners, until the weak points you leave behind become more important to you than those before you.

If the Persians see you tomorrow they will say, 'He is the root (chief) of Arabia. If we do away with him we will be in peace.' In this way this will heighten their eagerness against you and their keenness to aim at you. You say that they have set out to fight against the Muslims. Well, Allah detests their setting out more than you do, and He is more capable of preventing what He detests. As regards your idea about their (large) number, in the past we did not fight on the strength of large numbers but we fought on the basis of Allah’s support and assistance.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the purpose of the deputation and the coming time That Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, sent His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to bring people out from the narrow path to the broad one, and from difficulty to ease, and from certainty to doubt.

So Allah sent Muhammad with the Truth, to take out His servants from the worship of idols to His worship, and from the obedience of Satan to His obedience, with a Qur'an which He had explained and perfected, so that the servants may know their Lord when they were ignorant of Him, and acknowledge Him after they had denied Him, and affirm Him after they had rejected Him. So He, the Glorified, revealed Himself to them in His Book without their having seen Him, by means of what He showed them of His power, and made them fear His sway, and how He destroyed those whom He wished to destroy through His chastisements, and reaped those whom He wished to reap through His retributions!

The holders of the book will throw it away, and its memorizers will forget it. The Book and its people on that day will be exiled and expelled, two companions keeping together on one path, but no one will offer them asylum. Consequently, at that time the Book and its people will be among the people but not among them, will be with them but not with them. Because misguidance cannot accord with guidance, even though they may be together. The people will have united on division, and will therefore have cut away from the community. As though they were the leaders of the Book and not the Book their leader. Nothing of it will be left with them except its name, and they will know nothing save its writing and its words. Before that, they will inflict hardships on the virtuous, naming the latter’s truthful views about Allah false allegations, and enforcing for virtues the punishment of the vice.

Those before you passed away because of the lengthening of their desires and the forgetting of their death, till that promised event befell them about which excuses are turned down, repentance is denied and punishment and retribution is inflicted.

The exhortation to the people: O people, he who seeks counsel from Allāh is guided, to that which is more straight for the neighbor of Allāh feels secure, and His opponent feels afraid, and it does not behoove one who knows the greatness of Allāh to assume greatness, for the elevation of those who know His greatness is that they should humble themselves to Him, and the safety of those who know His power lies in submitting to Him. Do not be scared away from the truth like the scaring of the healthy from the scabbed person, or the sound person from the sick.

And hold fast to the Book of Allah, for it is the strong rope of Allah, the clear path, the call, and the remembrance. He who clings to it will not go astray, and he who holds onto it will not perish. And hold fast to the Sunnah of his Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), for they will not separate until they reach the Pool (al-Kawthar) for you. And hold fast to the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), for they are the life of knowledge and the death of ignorance. They are the ones whose rulings inform you of their knowledge, their silence informs you of their speech, and their outward appearance informs you of their inner self. They do not contradict the religion, nor do they differ within it regarding it; so it is among them a truthful witness and a silent speaker.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the mention of the people of Basra. The people of Basra were mentioned in the sermon, highlighting their role in the early caliphate disputes. They initially pledged allegiance to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) but later broke their oath and rose against their Imam, being among the first in the community to do so. The sermon references the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) prediction regarding their future status and actions.

Each of the two (Talha and Zubayr) desires the Caliphate for himself, and directs it towards himself against his companion, They do not employ any connection for getting access to Allah, nor proceed towards Him through any means. Each of the two bears malice against the other; shortly his veil over it will be uncovered! By Allah, if they achieve what they aim at, one of them will kill the other, and one will finish the other, The rebellious party has stood up. Where are the seekers of virtue? The paths have already been determined and they have been given the news, For every misguidance there is a cause, and for every break of pledge there is a misrepresentation. By Allah, I shall not be like him who listens to the voice of mourning, hears the man who brings news of death and also visits the mourner, yet does not take lesson!
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he points to the battles (future events) and describes a faction of the people of misguidance.

They took to the right and the left, traveling through the ways of evil, and leaving the paths of guidance, Do not make haste for a matter which is to happen and is awaited, and do not wish for delay in what the morrow is to bring for you, For, how many people make haste for a matter, but when they get it they begin to wish they had not got it. How near is today to the dawning of tomorrow. O my people, this is the time for the occurrence of every promised event and the approach of things which you do not know. Whoever from among us will be during these days will move through them with a burning lamp and will tread on the footsteps of the virtuous, in order to unfasten knots, to free slaves, to divide the united and to unite the divided. He will be in concealment from people. The stalker will not find his footprints even though he pursues with his eye. Then a group of people will be sharpened like the sharpening of swords by the blacksmith. Their sight will be brightened by revelation, the (delicacies of) commentary will be put in their ears and they will be given drinks of wisdom, morning and evening.

When Allah took the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), a group of men went back on their tracks. The ways (of misguidance) ruined them and they placed trust in deceitful intriguers, showed consideration to other than kinsmen, abandoned the kin whom they had been ordered to love, and shifted the building from its strong foundation and built it in other than its (proper) place. They are the source of every shortcoming and the door of gropers in the dark. They were moving to and fro in amazement and lay intoxicated in the way of the people of the Pharaohs. They were either bent on this world and taking support on it or away from the faith and removed from it.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him), he warns against the trials. O people, the trial has drawn near, and perishment has approached, the veil has been lifted, and the trial has become clear, death has advanced, and deeds have lagged behind, hope has been cut off, and the trials have appeared, and blood has been made lawful, and wealth has been made lawful, and conditions have changed, and times have altered, and defects have been exposed, and the ignorant have taken leadership, and the chaste women have been modest from the bold, and excellence has lagged behind its people, and evil has seized hold of good, and ignorance has advanced over knowledge, and knowledge has lagged behind ignorance.

And I praise Allah and seek His help from the punishment of Satan and his deceitful acts, and (seek) protection from his traps and way-layings. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His Prophet, and His chosen and His selected one. His distinction cannot be paralleled, nor can his loss be made good. Lands were brightened through him after dark misguidance, overpowering ignorance, and rude habits, and people regarded unlawful as lawful, humiliated the man of wisdom, passed lives when there were no prophets, and died as unbelievers!

The Warning from the Fitnah (Calamities/Strife): Then indeed, you O people of Arabia, are the targets of calamities which have drawn near, so fear the intoxication of prosperity, and beware the disasters of retribution, and remain steadfast in the darkness and crookedness of the Fitnah when its embryo emerges, its hidden nature appears, its axis stands firm, and the pivot of its mill turns. It begins in imperceptible stages, and ends in manifest hideousness; its youth is like the youth of a boy, and its marks are like the marks of being struck by a stone.

The oppressors inherit it by (mutual) agreement! The first of them serves as a leader for the latter one and the latter one follows the first one. They vie with each other in (the matter of) this lowly world, and leap over this stinking carcass. Shortly the follower will denounce his connection with the leader, and the leader with the follower. They will disunite on account of mutual [animosity] and curse one another when they meet. Then after this there will appear another arouser of mischief who will destroy ruined things. The heart will become wavering after being normal, men will be misled after safety, desires will multiply and become diversified and views will become confused.

Whoever proceeds towards this mischief will be ruined, and whoever strives for it will be annihilated. They will be biting each other during it as the wild asses bite each other in the herd. The coils of the rope will be disturbed and the face of affairs will be blinded. During it sagacity will be on the ebb, and the oppressors will (get the opportunity to) speak. This mischief will smash the Bedouins with its hammers and crush them with its chest. In its dust the single marchers will be lost, and in its way the horsemen will be destroyed. It will approach with the bitterness of destiny and will give pure blood (instead of milk). It will breach the minarets of faith and shatter the ties of firm belief. The wise will run away from it while the wicked will foster it. It will thunder and flash (like lightning). It will create a severe disaster. In it kinship will be forsaken and Islam will be abandoned. He who declaims it will also be affected by it, and he who flees from it will (be forced to) stay in it.

From it: Among them some will be unavenged martyrs and some will be stricken with fear and seek protection. They will be deceived by pledges and fraudulent belief. You should not become landmarks of mischiefs and signs of innovations, but should adhere to that on which the rope of the community has been wound and on which the pillars of obedience have been founded. Proceed towards Allah as oppressed and do not proceed to Him as oppressors. Avoid the paths of Satan and the places of revolt. Do not put in your bellies unlawful morsels, because you are facing Him Who has made disobedience unlawful for you, and made the path of obedience easy for you.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the attributes of Allah, Exalted is His Majesty, and the qualities of the Imams of Religion.

Praise be to Allah who is proof of His existence through His creation, of His being external through the newness of His creation, and through their mutual similarities of the fact that nothing is similar to Him. Senses cannot touch Him and curtains cannot veil Him, because of the difference between the Maker and the made, the Limiter and the limited and the Sustainer and the sustained.

He is the One, but not by the meaning of number; the Creator, but not through the sense of movement and exertion; the Hearer, but not by means of an organ; the Seer, but not by the differentiation of an organ; the Witness, but not by nearness; the Distinct, but not by the distance of space; the Manifest, but not by being seen; the Hidden, but not by subtlety of body. He is distinct from things by overpowering them and having ability over them, and things are distinct from Him by their subjugation to Him and their return to Him.

He who describes Him limits Him. He who limits Him numbers Him. He who numbers Him rejects His eternity. He who said 'how' sought a description for Him. He who said 'where' bounded Him. He is the Knower even though there be nothing to be known. He is the Sustainer even though there be nothing to be sustained. He is the Powerful even though there be nothing to be overpowered.

A part of the same sermon about the Divine leaders (Imāms): The riser has risen, the sparkler has sparkled, the appearer has appeared and the curved has been straightened. Allāh has replaced one people with another and one day with another. We awaited the occultation as the famine-stricken await the rain. Certainly the Imāms are the vicegerents of Allāh over His creatures and they make the creatures know Allāh. No one will enter Paradise except he who knows them and knows Him, and no one will enter Hell except he who denies them and denies Him.

Allah distinguished you with Islam and chose you for it, and this is because it is the name of safety and the collection of honour. Allah the Exalted chose its way and disclosed its proofs, from the apparent knowledge and the inner wisdom, its wonders are not exhausted and its marvels do not end. It contains blossoming bounties and lamps of darkness. The virtues cannot be opened save with its keys, nor can the glooms be dispelled save with its lamps. He has protected its inaccessible points and allowed grazing in its pastures. It contains cure for the seeker of cure and sufficiency for the seeker of sufficiency.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) in which he mentions the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them).

He who has an intelligent mind looks to his goal, and knows his low road as well as his high road. The caller has called, and the shepherd has tended (his flocks). So respond to the caller and follow the shepherd.

They (the opposers) have entered the oceans of disturbance and have taken to innovations instead of the sunnah, while the believers have sunk down, and the misguided and the liars are speaking. We are the standard, the companions, the treasure holders and the doors. Houses are not entered save through their doors. Whoever enters them from other than the door is called a thief.

[A part of the same sermon :] The delicacies of the Qur’ān are about them, When they speak they speak the truth, but when they keep quiet no one can speak unless they speak. The forerunner should report correctly to his people, should retain his wits and should be one of the children (a man) of the next world, because he has come from there and would return to it.

The one who sees with the heart, the one who acts with the eyes, the beginning of his action is that he knows: is his action against him or for him? If it is for him, he proceeds in it, and if it is against him, he stops at it. For, he who acts without knowledge is like one who travels without a path, so his distance from the clear path only increases his distance from his need, and he who acts with knowledge is like one who travels on the clear path, so let the one who sees see: is he proceeding or returning?!

And to you be peace, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings. And know that for every outward appearance there is an inward reality corresponding to it; so whatever is good in its outward appearance is good in its inward reality, and whatever is bad in its outward appearance is bad in its inward reality. And the truthful Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) has said: 'Verily Allah loves the servant but hates his action, and loves the action but hates the body.'

You should know that every action is like vegetation, and every vegetation cannot do without water, and the waters are different. So where the watering is good, the planting is good and its fruit is sweet, and where the watering is bad, the planting is bad and its fruit is bitter.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) in which he mentions the wonderful creation of the bat.

He is Allah, the True, the Manifester of Truth. He is more True and more manifest than eyes can see. Intellects cannot comprehend Him by fixing limits for Him since in that case to Him would be attribute shape. Imagination cannot catch Him by fixing quantities for Him for in that case to Him would be attributed body. He created creatures without any example, and without the advice of a counsel, or the assistance of a helper. His creation was completed by His command, and bowed to His obedience. It responded (to Him) and did not defy (Him). It obeyed and did not resist.

[The Creation of the Bat :] An example of His delicate production, wonderful creation and deep sagacity which He has shown us is found in these bats which keep hidden in the daylight although daylight reveals every thing else, and are mobile in the night although the night shuts up every other living being; and how their eyes get dazzled and cannot make use of the light of the sun so as to be guided in their movements and so as to reach their known places through the direction provided by the sun.

Glorified is He who made the night for them as a time of activity and livelihood, and made the day for them as a time of rest and stability! And He gave them wings of flesh with which, when needed, they ascend for flying; they look like pieces of the ear, without feathers or bones, yet you can see the places of the veins as clear signs, It has two wings that are neither so thin that they tear, nor so thick that they become heavy. It flies while its young clings to it, seeking refuge with it; it falls when it falls, and rises when it rises. The young does not leave it until its limbs become strong, its wings support it for rising, and it begins to recognize its places of living and its interests. Glorified is the Creator of everything, without a prior model, creating from nothing.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), urging people towards piety And from his sermon (peace be upon him), urging people towards piety

O creatures of Allāh! Time will deal with the survivors just as it dealt with those gone by. The time that has passed will not return and whatever there is in it will not stay for ever. Its later deeds are the same as the former ones. Its trouble try to excell one another. Its banners follow each other. It is as though you are attached to the last day which is driving you as rapidly as are driven the she-camels which are dry for seven months. He who busies himself with things other than improvement of his ownself becomes perplexed in darkness and entangled in ruination. His evil spirits immerse him deep in vices and make his bad actions appear handsome. Paradise is the end of those who are forward (in good acts) and Hell is the end of those who commit excesses.

Know, O creatures of Allah, that piety is a strong house of protection, while impiety is a weak house which does not protect its people, and does not give security to him who takes refuge therein. Know that the sting of sins is cut by piety and the final aim is achieved by conviction of belief.

O creatures of Allah! Fear Allah, fear Allah, in the matter of your own selves, which are the most beloved and dear to you, because Allah has clarified to you the way of truthfulness and lighted its paths. So (you may choose) either ever-present misfortune or eternal happiness! You should therefore provide in these mortal days for the eternal days. You have been informed of the provision, ordered to march and told to make haste in setting off. You are like staying riders who do not know when they would be ordered to march on. Beware, what will he, who has been created for the next world, do with this world? What will a person do with wealth which he would shortly be deprived of while only its ill effects and reckoning would be left behind for him?

Know, O creatures of Allāh! that your ownself is a guard over you; your limbs are watchmen and truthful vigil-keepers who preserve (the record of) your actions and the numbers of their breaths. The gloom of the dark night cannot conceal you from them, nor can closed doors hide you from them. Surely tomorrow is close to today.

Today will depart with all that it has, and tomorrow will come in its wake. It is as though every one of you has reached that place on earth where he would be alone, namely the location of his grave. So, what to say of the lonely house, the solitary place of staying and the solitary exile. It is as though the cry (of the Horn) has reached you, the Hour has overtaken you and you have come out (of your graves) for the passing of judgement. (The curtains of) falsehood have been removed from you and your excuses have become weak. The truth about you has been proved. All your matters have proceeded to their consequences. Therefore, you should (now) take counsel from examples, learn lessons from vicissitudes and take advantage of the warners.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he draws attention to the virtue of the Most Great Messenger and the virtue of the Qur'an, then the state of the dynasty of Banu Umayya.

[The Prophet and the Quran:] Allah sent him at a time when there had been no prophets for some time, and the peoples had been in slumber for a long time, and the twist of the rope had loosened, so he came to them with confirmation of what was before it, and with the light to be followed. That is the Quran, so ask it to speak, and it will not speak; but I will inform you about it: Know that it contains knowledge of what is to come, stories of the past, cure for your ills, and regulation for whatever faces you.

Part of it, in the era of the Umayyad dynasty: At that time, no house of stone or tent of hair will remain but that the oppressors will enter it with grief, and they will inject it with vengeance. On that day, no excuse will remain for them in the sky, nor any helper on the earth. You selected for the authority one who was not its fit person, and you raised him to a position not meant for him, and Allah will take revenge from whoever oppressed, food for food and drink for drink, namely (they will be given) colocynth for eating, myrrh and aloes for drinking, and fear for an inner garment, and the sword for an outer covering.

They are nothing but carrier-beasts laden with sins and camels laden with evil deeds. I swear and again swear that the Umayyads will have to spit out the caliphate as phlegm is spat and there after they will never taste it nor relish its flavour so long as day and night rotate.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), in which he explains his good conduct with his subjects.

I lived as a good neighbour to you, and tried my best to look after you from behind, and freed you from the snare of humbleness and the fetters of oppression. This was out of gratitude from me for the little good (from your side), and closing my eyes to what the sight perceived and the body witnessed, of the many misdeeds.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) concerning the condemnation of Basra and its people [after the Battle of the Camel].

You were the army of a woman, and the followers of a quadruped, When it grumbled you responded, and when it was wounded (hamstrung) you fled away. Your character is low and your pledge is broken. Your faith is hypocrisy. Your water is brackish. He who stays with you is laden with sins and he who forsakes you secures Allah’s mercy secures forsakes you. As though I see your mosque prominent, resembling the surface of a boat, while Allah has sent chastisement from above and from below it and every one who is on it is drowned.
And in another narration By Allah, your city would certainly be drowned so much so that as though I see its mosque like the upper part of a boat or a sitting ostrich.
And in another narration Like the chest/bosom of a bird in the deep sea.

And in another narration: Your city is the most stinking of all the cities as regards its clay, the nearest to water and remotest from the sky. It contains nine tenths of evil. He who enters it is surrounded with his sins and he who is out of it enjoys Allah’s forgiveness. It seems as though I look at this habitation of yours that water has so engulfed it that nothing can be seen of it except the highest part of mosque appearing like the bosom of a bird in deep sea.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the greatness of Allah, His praise, and the mention of the prophets.
The Greatness of Allah: His command is decree and wisdom, His pleasure is security and mercy. He decrees with knowledge and forgives with forbearance.

[Praise of Allāh :] O my Allāh! praise be to Thee for what Thou takest and givest and for that from which Thou curest or with which Thou afflictest; praise which is the most acceptable to Thee, the most liked by Thee and the most dignified before Thee; praise which fills all Thy creation and reaches where Thou desirest; praise which is not veiled from Thee and does not end, and whose continuity does not cease.

And what we see of Your creation, and wonder at it because of Your might, and describe it as (a result of) Your great authority, and what is hidden from us of it, of which our sight has fallen short, which our intelligence has not attained, and between which and ourselves curtains of the unknown have been cast, is far greater.

He who frees his heart, and exerts his thinking, to know how You established Your throne, and how You created Your creatures, and how You suspended Your skies in the air, and how You spread Your earth upon the waves of water, his gaze returns exhausted, his intellect bewildered, his hearing captivated, and his thought wandering.

[A part of the same sermon about hope and fear in Allāh :] He claims according to his own thinking that he hopes from Allāh. By Allāh, the Great, he speaks a lie. The position is that his hope (in Allāh) does not appear through his action although the hope of every one who hopes is known through his action. Every hope is so, except the hope in Allāh, the Sublime, if it is impure; and every fear is established except the fear for Allāh if it is unreal.

The Prophet of Allah (peace and blessing of Allah be upon him and his family): Certainly, in the Prophet of Allah — peace and blessing of Allah be upon him and his progeny — was sufficient example for you and a proof concerning the vices of the world, its defects, the multitude of its disgraces and its evils, because its sides had been constringed for him, while its flanks had been spread for others; he was deprived of its milk and turned away from its adornments.

[The example of Mūsā (Moses) :] If you want, I will, as a second example, relate to you concerning Mūsā, the Interlocutor of Allāh (a.s.) when he said: “O Allāh! I need whatever good Thou mayest grant me.” (Qur’ān, 28:24) By Allāh, he asked Him only for bread to eat because he was used to eating the herbs of the earth, and the greenness of the herbs could be seen from the delicate skin of his belly due to his thinness and paucity of his flesh.

[The example of Dāwūd (David) :] If you desire I can give you a third example of Dāwūd (a.s.). He is the holder of the Psalms and the reciter among the people of Paradise. He used to prepare baskets of date palm leaves with his own hands and would say to his companions : “Which of you will help me by purchasing it?” He used to eat barley bread (bought) out of its price.

Follow your Prophet, the purest, the most chaste (peace be upon him and his family). For in him is an example for the follower, and a consolation for the seeker of consolation. The most beloved of servants to Allah is he who follows His Prophet, and who treads in his footsteps. He took the least (share) from this world and did not take a full glance at it. Of all the people of the world he was the least satiated and the most empty of stomach. The world was offered to him but he refused to accept it. When he knew that Allah, the Glorified, hated a thing, he too hated it; that Allah held a thing low, he too held it low; that Allah held a thing small, he too held it small. If we love what Allah and His Prophet hate and hold great what Allah and His prophet hold small that would be enough isolation from Allah and transgression of His commands.

And indeed, he (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat on the ground, and sit like a slave, He repaired his shoe with his hand, and patched his clothes with his hand. He would ride an unsaddled ass and would seat someone behind him. If there was a curtain on his door with pictures on it he would say to one of his wives, “O such-and-such, take it away out of my sight because if I look at it I recall the world and its allurements.” Thus, he removed his heart from this world and destroyed its remembrance from his mind. He loved that its allurements should remain hidden from his eye so that he should not secure good dress from it, should not regard it a place of stay and should not hope to live in it. Consequently he removed it from his mind, let it go away from his heart and kept it hidden from his eyes. In the same way he who hates a thing should hate to look at it or to hear about it.

Certainly there was in the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that which would apprise you of the evils of this world and its defects namely that he remained hungry along with his chief companions, and despite his great nearness the allurements of the world remained remote from him Now, one should see with one’s intelligence whether Allah honoured Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a result of this or disgraced him If he says that Allah disgraced him, he certainly lies and perpetrates a great untruth. If he says Allah honoured him he should know that Allah dishonoured the others when He extended the (benefits of the) world for him but held them away from him who was the nearest to Him of all men

Therefore, follow the one who followed His Prophet, tread in his footsteps, and enter through his entrance, Otherwise, he will not be safe from ruin. Certainly, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) made Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) a sign for the Hour, a bringer of glad tidings of Paradise, and a warner of retribution. He left this world hungry, and entered the Hereafter safe. He did not lay one stone upon another, until he departed and answered the call of his Lord, How great is Allah's blessing upon us when He bestowed upon us Him as a predecessor whom we follow, and a leader behind whom we tread.

By Allah, I have patched this shirt of mine so much that I became shy of the one who patched it. And a speaker said to me: 'Will you not discard it?' So I said: 'Get away from me.' For in the morning people praise the night journey.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the description of the Prophet, his Household, and the followers of his religion, and in it he exhorts with piety.

The Messenger, his family, and the followers of his religion: Allah deputed him with a sparkling light, a clear argument, an open path, and a guiding book. His tribe is the best tribe, and his lineal tree the best lineal tree, whose branches are in good proportion and fruits hanging (in plenty). His birth-place was Mecca, and the place of his immigration Taybah (Medina), from where his name rose high and his voice spread far and wide.
I trust in Allah, the trust of bending towards Him, and I seek His guidance for the way that leads to His Paradise and takes to the place of His pleasure.

So close your eyes, O creatures of Allāh, from its worries and engagements, because you are sure about its separation and its changing conditions. Fear it like a sincere fearer and one who struggles hard, and take a lesson from what you have seen about the falling places of those before you, namely that their joints were made to vanish, their eyes and ears were destroyed, their honour and prestige disappeared and their pleasure and wealth came to an end. The nearness of their children changed into remoteness. The company of their spouses changed into separation with them. They do not boast over each other, nor do they beget children nor meet each other nor live as neighbours.

Therefore, fear, like the fear of one who has control over himself, who can check his passions and perceive with his wisdom; Surely, the matter is quite clear, the banner is standing, the course is level and the way is straight.
And one of his words (peace be upon him) to some of his companions, after he had asked him: 'How did your people deprive you of this position while you are more deserving of it?' Then he said:

O brother of Banū Asad, Your girth is loose and you have put it on the wrong way. Nevertheless you enjoy in-law kinship and also the right to ask, and since you have asked, listen. As regards the oppression against us in this matter although we were the highest as regards descent and the strongest in relationship with the Messenger of Allāh. It was a selfish act over which the hearts of people became greedy, although some people did not care for it. The Arbiter is Allāh and to Him is the return on the Day of Judgement.
And leave aside for you the plunder about which there was a cry in its fortresses. But [listen to] a narration, what is the narration of the beasts of burden?
And from his sermon (peace be upon him): The Creator, Exalted and Great,

Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the servants. He who spread the earth, made the streams flow, and caused the vegetation to grow on high lands. His primality has no beginning, nor has His eternity any end. He is the First, He has been without ceasing, and the Everlasting without limit. Foreheads bow before Him, and lips declare His oneness. He determined the limits of things at the time of creating them, keeping Himself away from any likeness.

Imagination cannot surmise Him within the limits of movements limbs or senses It cannot be said about Him: “whence”?; and no time limit can be attributed to Him by saying “till” He is apparent, but it cannot be said “from what”. He is hidden, but it cannot be said “in what” He is not a body which can die, nor is He veiled so as to be enclosed therein He is not near to things by way of touch, nor is He remote from them by way of separation

The gazing of people’s eyes is not hidden from Him, nor the repetition of words, nor the glimpse of hillocks, nor the tread of a footstep in the dark night or in the deep gloom, where the shining moon casts its light and the effulgent sun comes in its wake, through its setting and appearing again and again with the rotation of time and periods, by the approach of the advancing night or the passing away of the running day. He precedes every extremity and limit, and every counting and numbering.

He is exalted above what those who define (limit) attribute to Him, from the qualities of measures and extremities, and the inhabiting of dwellings and dwelling in places. So the limit is struck for His creation, and is attributed to other than Him.

From it: O creature who has been equitably created, and who has been nurtured in the darkness of the wombs, and behind multiple veils, You were originated from [an essence of] clay, And placed in a firm resting place, to a known measure and an appointed time. You move in the womb of your mother as an embryo, neither understanding a call, nor hearing a summons,

Then you were taken out from your place of stay to a place you had not seen, and who guided you to eke out your sustenance from the udder of your mother, and, when you were in need, appraised you of the location of what you required or aimed at?! Alas! Certainly he who is unable to understand the qualities of a being with shape and limbs is the more unable to understand the qualities of the Creator and the more remote from appreciating Him through the limitations of creatures.

And from his words (peace be upon him): When the people gathered to him and complained about what they held against Uthman, and asked him to speak to him and admonish him for their sake, he entered upon Uthman and said:

The people are behind me, and they have made me an ambassador between you and themselves; but by Allāh, I do not know what to say to you. I know nothing (in this matter) which you do not know, nor can I lead you to any matter of which you are not aware. You certainly know what we know, we have not come to know anything before you which we could tell you; nor did we learn anything in secret which we should convey to you. You have seen as we have seen and you have heard as we have heard. You sat in the company of the Prophet of Allāh as we did. (Abū Bakr) Ibn Abī Quḥāfah and (‘Umar) Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb were no more responsible for acting righteously than you, since you are nearer than both of them to the Prophet of Allāh through kinship, and you also hold relationship to him by marriage which they do not hold.

Then (fear) Allāh, in your own self; for, by Allāh, you are not being shown anything as if you are blind or being apprised of anything as if you are ignorant. The ways are clear while the banners of faith are fixed. You should know that among the creatures of Allāh, the most distinguished person before Allāh is the just Imām who has been guided (by Allāh) and guides others. So, he stands by the recognized ways of the Prophet’s behaviour and destroys unrecognized innovations. The (Prophet’s) ways are clear and they have signs,

Certainly, the innovations are apparent, having their signs. And certainly, the worst of people before Allah is an oppressive Imam who has gone astray and through whom others go astray, so he kills an accepted Sunnah and revives an abandoned innovation. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'On the Day of Resurrection, the oppressive Imam will be brought without any supporter or one to advance excuses on his behalf, so he will be thrown into the Fire of Hell, and he will rotate in it as the millstone rotates, then he will be tied in its bottom.'

And I implore you by Allah, that you should not be that Imam of this nation who will be killed, for it has been said: An Imam of this nation will be killed, after which killing and fighting will be made open for them until the Day of Judgment, and he will confuse their affairs and spread trials in them, so they will not discern the truth from falsehood, they will surge in it like waves, and be tossed about in it. So do not become a carrying beast for Marwan, so that he may drag you wherever he wishes, despite your seniority of age and length of life.

Then 'Uthman said to him Speak to the people to give me time until I redress their grievances. Amir al-mu'minin then said: So far as Medina is concerned there is no question of time. As for remoter areas you can have the time needed for your order to reach there.

[About the creation of birds :] He created them with a wonderful creation, from the living and the lifeless, the stationary and the moving. He established from the clear proofs regarding the subtlety of His craftsmanship and the greatness of His power, that which the intellects submit to, acknowledging it and yielding to it. And His evidences crowed in our ears regarding His oneness. And He created the various forms of birds, which He housed in the burrows of the earth, the openings of its passes, and the peaks of its mountains.

Among them are those with different kinds of wings, and various characteristics, controlled by the rein of (Allāh’s) authority, and fluttering with their wings in the expanse of the vast firmament and the open atmosphere. He brought them into existence from nonexistence in strange external shapes, and composed them with joints and bones covered with flesh. He prevented some of them from flying easily in the sky because of their heavy bodies, and allowed them to use their wings only close to the ground.

He has arranged them, in their diversity of colours, with delicate might and exquisite craftsmanship; among them are those dyed in a single hue, unmingled by any other colour than that in which they were immersed, and others dyed in one colour, encircled by a contrasting band different from the dye used.

If you likened it to what the earth produces, you would say: a bouquet gathered from the flowers of every spring. And if you compared it to clothes, it would be like embroidered garments or like the fine, variegated cloth of Yemen. And if you compared it to ornaments, it would be like gems of various colors, set with crowned lujayn (a type of precious stone/silver).

It walks with the walk of the joyous and proud, and displays its tail and wings, laughing at the beauty of its dress and the hues of its necklace; but when it casts its glance at its legs, it crows loudly with a voice that almost reveals its call for help, and testifies to its true grief, because its legs are thin like the legs of the cross-bred cock. And from the end of its shin there emerges a hidden spur, and on the crown of its head there is a green, variegated bunch of feathers, and the base of its neck is like a goblet, and its stretch up to where its belly is is like the dye of Yemeni henna, or like silk cloth put on a polished mirror, and it seems as if it is wrapped in a black veil; except that on account of its excessive lustre and extreme brightness, it appears that a lush green colour has been mixed with it, and along the opening of its ear there is a line like the thin end of a pen in the colour of the daisy, bright white, so its whiteness shines against the blackness of what is there.

There is hardly a hue from which it has not taken a bit and improved it further by regular polish, lustre, silken brightness and brilliance It is therefore like scattered blossoms which have not been seasoned by the rains of spring or the sun of the summer It also sheds its plumage and puts off its dress. They all fall away and grow again They fall away from the feather stems like the falling of leaves from twigs and then they begin to join together and grow till they return to the state that existed before their falling away The new hues do not change from the previous ones, nor does any colour occur in other than its own place If you carefully look at one hair from the hairs of its feather stems it would look like red rose, then emerald green and then golden yellow

How can the sharpness of intellect reach the description of this [creation], or the faculties of minds attain it, or the utterances of describers manage to tell of it? And even its smallest parts have made it impossible for the imagination to grasp it, and for the tongues to describe it!

Glorified is He who has dazzled the intellects from describing His creation, which He made clear to the eyes, so they perceive it as bounded, shaped, arranged, and coloured; and He has rendered the tongues incapable of summarizing His description, and prevented them from fulfilling the expression of His attributes!

[The smallness of the creatures:] Glorified is He who assigned feet to the minute ant and the gnat, and to those above them in creation, the whales and the elephants! He made it obligatory upon Himself that no skeleton in which He infused the spirit would move, except that He made death its appointed time and destruction its final end.

They are a people whom honour has always followed till they were made to settle in the house of eternal abode, and they obtained rest from the movement of journeying. O listener! If you busy yourself in advancing towards these wonderful scenes which will rush towards you, then your heart will certainly die due to eagerness for them, and you will be prepared to seek the company of those in the graves straight away from my audience here and hasten towards them.
May Allah make us and you among those who strive with their hearts for the abodes of the virtuous, by His mercy.

[Note explaining some of the wonderful and obscure portions of this sermon :] as-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: In Amīr al-mu’minīn’s words “ya’urru bimalāqiḥihi”, “al-arr” implies “copulation”, e.g. When it is said “arra’r-rajulu al-mar’ata ya’urruhā”, it means “he copulated with the woman.” In his words “ka’annahu qal‘u dāriyyin ‘anajahu nūtiyyuhu”, “alqal‘” means the sail of a boat. “dārī” means belonging to Dārīn which is a small town on the coast from where scents are bought. And “‘anajahu” means “turned it”. It is said “‘anajtun’n-nāqata — like naṣartu — a ‘najuhā ‘anjan”. “When you turn the she-camel.” And “an-nūtī” means sailor. His words “daffatay jufūnihi” means edges of the eyelids, since “aḍ-ḍaffatān” means the two edges. His words “wa filadhu’z-zabarjadi”: “al-filadh” is the plural of “al-fildhah ” it means piece. His words “ka bā’isi’llu’lu’i’r-raṭibi”. “al-kibāsah” means bunch of dates. “al-‘asālīj”. means twigs. Its singular is “‘uslūj”.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) at the beginning of his Caliphate. Fulfill the obligations of God, and attend to the affairs of the creatures, and fear God regarding the lands and the beasts, for you will be questioned about them and other things.

Allah, the Glorified, has sent down a guiding Book wherein He has explained virtue and vice. You should adopt the course of virtue whereby you will have guidance, and keep aloof from the direction of vice so that you remain on the right way. (Mind) the obligations, (mind) the obligations. Fulfil them for Allah and they will take you to Paradise. Surely, Allah has made unlawful the things which are not unknown and made lawful the things which are without defect. He has declared paying regard to Muslims as the highest of all regards. He has placed the rights of Muslims in the same grade (of importance) as devotion (to himself and His oneness). Therefore, a Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand every (other) Muslim is safe save in the matter of truth. It is not, therefore, lawful to molest a Muslim except when it is obligatory.

Hasten towards the common matter which is peculiar to every one; and that is death. Certainly, people (who have already gone) are ahead of you while the hour (Day of Judgement) is driving you from behind. Remain light, in order that you may overtake them. Your backs are being awaited for the sake of the fronts. Fear Allāh in the matter of His creatures and His cities because you will be questioned even about lands and beasts. Obey Allāh and do not disobey Him. When you see virtue adopt it, and when you see vice avoid it.
And among his sayings (peace be upon him): after allegiance was sworn to him for the caliphate, some people from among the companions said to him: "Should you not punish those who assaulted Uthman?"

This demand is certainly that of the pre-Islamic (al jāhiliyyah) period and these people have support behind them. When the matter is taken up, people will have different views about it. One group will think as you do, but another will not think as you think, and there will be still another group who will be neither this way nor that way. Be patient till people quieten down and hearts settle in their places so that rights can be achieved for people easily. Rest assured from me, and see what is given to you by me. Do not do anything which shatters your power, weakens your strength and engenders feebleness and disgrace. I shall control this affair as far as possible, but if I find it necessary the last treatment will, of course, be branding with a hot iron (through fighting).
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) when the people of Jamal set off for Baṣrah He said: When you march towards Baṣrah, face the Qiblah and proclaim Takbir.

Discouraging [people] from his opponents: Certainly, these people are in agreement in disliking my authority. I will carry on till I perceive disunity among you; because if, in spite of the unsoundness of their view, they succeed, the whole organization of the Muslims will be shattered. They are hankering after this world out of jealousy against him on whom Allāh has bestowed it. So they intend reverting the matters on their backs (pre-Islamic period), while on us it is obligatory, for your sake, to abide by the Book of Allāh (Qur’ān), the Sublime, and the conduct of the Prophet of Allāh, to stand by His rights and the revival of his sunnah.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) in similar [circumstances]

Your earth is close to the sea and away from the sky. Your wits have become light and your minds are full of folly. You are the aim of the archer, a morsel for the eater and an easy prey for the hunter.

And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the obligation of following the truth when the Proof (Imam) rises. An Arab spoke to him, as a group of people from Basra had sent him when he (peace be upon him) approached Basra, to inquire on their behalf about the reality of his situation with the People of Jamal, so that doubt might be removed from their hearts. He (peace be upon him) explained to him from his affair with them that which made him know that he was upon the truth. Then he said to him: 'Swear allegiance.' He said: 'I am a messenger of a people, and I will not do anything until I return to them.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him:
He said: I would leave them and go towards greenery and water.
Amīr al-mu’minīn then said: So then extend your hand.
The man said: By Allah, I could not refrain [from allegiance] when the proof was established against me, so I gave him allegiance, peace be upon him.
This man was known as Kulayb al-Jarmi.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), when he decided to meet the people at Siffin:

The supplication: O Allah, Lord of the raised roof and the covered firmament, Who made it a shelter for the night and the day, an orbit for the sun and the moon, and a path for the rotating stars, And for populating it Thou hast created a group of Thy angels who do not get weary of worshipping Thee. O Sustainer of this earth which Thou hast made an abode for people and a place for the movement of insects and beasts and countless other creatures seen and unseen. O Sustainer of strong mountains which Thou hast made as pegs for the earth and (a means of) support for people. If Thou givest us victory over our enemy, save us from excesses and keep us on the straight path of truth, But if Thou givest them victory over us, then grant us martyrdom and save us from mischief.

[Calling to battle:] Where are those who protect honour, and those self-respecting persons who defend respectable persons in the time of hardship? Shame is behind you while Paradise is in front of you.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) About the Consultative Committee of Umar and the People of Jamal
Praise be to Allah All praise is for Allah, from whose view one sky does not conceal another sky, nor one earth another earth.

[A part of the same sermon About the Consultative Committee after the death of ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb :] Someone [1] said to me, “O son of Abī Ṭālib, you are eager for the caliphate.” Then I told him: “Rather, you are, by Allāh, more greedy, although more remote, while I am more suited as well as nearer. I have demanded it as my right, while you are intervening between me and it, and you are turning my face from it.” When I knocked at his ears with arguments among the crowd of those present he was startled as if he was stunned not knowing what reply to give me about it.

O Allah I seek Thy succour against the Quraysh and those who are assisting them, because they are denying me (the rights of) kinship, have lowered my high position, and are united in opposing me in the matter (of the caliphate) which is my right, and then they said, 'Know that the rightful thing is that you have it and also that you may leave it.'
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) in the admonition, and explaining his closeness to the Messenger of Allah. Warning to neglectful people, and about the vastness of his own knowledge

O the negligent, who are not forgiven, and the abandoners, from whom [their deeds] will be taken, What is it that I see you departing from Allah and desiring others? You are like camels upon which a herdsman has driven [them] to a pasture that is diseased, and a watering place that is disastrous, And indeed they are like beasts that are fed in order to be slaughtered, but they do not know what is intended for them! When treated well, they consider their day to be their whole life, and their fullness to be their aim.

By Allah, if I wished, I could inform every one of you of his origin, his destination, and all his affairs, and I would do so, but I fear that you would disbelieve in the Messenger of Allah on my account. Indeed, I shall convey it to the select few from whom that is trusted. By the One who sent him with the Truth and chose him above creation, I do not speak except truthfully, and He has charged me with all of that, and with the death of whoever perishes, the salvation of whoever is saved, and the final outcome of this matter, and He left nothing that passes through my mind without pouring it into my ears and conveying it to me.
O people! I do not impel you to any obedience unless I practise it before you and do not restrain you from any disobedience unless I desist from it before you.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) In it, he admonishes and expounds the excellences of the Qur'an and forbids innovation

And know that every obedience to Allah is unpleasant in appearance while every disobedience to Allah has the appearance of enjoyment. Allah may have mercy on the person who kept aloof from his desire and uprooted the appetite of his heart, because this heart has far-reaching aims and it goes on pursuing disobedience through desires.

And to you, O servants of Allah, that a believer does not pass the morning or the evening except that his soul is suspect in his eyes, so he should continually visit it and ask it to increase (in good), so be like those who preceded you and those who passed before you, they dismantled the world as a traveler dismantles (his camp), and covered it as distances are covered.

[The Greatness of the Qur'an:] And know that this Qur'an is the Adviser who does not deceive, the Guide who does not mislead, and the Narrator who does not lie, and no one sits with this Qur'an but that he rises from it with an addition or a diminution: an addition in guidance, or a diminution from blindness. And know that no one is in need after (the guidance of) the Qur'an, and no one is free from want before (the guidance of) the Qur'an; so seek cure from it for your ailments, and seek its assistance in your distresses, for indeed in it is a cure for the greatest disease, which is unbelief and hypocrisy, deviation and misguidance, so ask Allah through it, and turn to Him with its love, and do not ask the creation through it, for indeed the servants have not turned to Allah with anything like it.

[Exhortation to Action:] Action! Action! Then the end, the end, and steadfastness, steadfastness. Then endurance, endurance, and piety, piety! You have an objective. Proceed towards your objective. You have a sign. Take guidance from your sign. Islam has an objective. Proceed towards its objective. Proceed towards Allah by fulfilling His rights which He has enjoined upon you, and which He has clarified for you as your duties. I am a witness for you, and shall plead excuses on your behalf on the Day of Judgement.

[Counselling people:] Beware! What had been ordained has occurred, and that which had been destined has come into play. And I am speaking to you with the promise and proof of Allah, Allah the Sublime, has said: 'Verily, those who say: Our Lord is Allah! and persevere aright, the angels descend upon them (saying): ‘Fear ye not, nor be grieved, and receive the glad tidings of the Garden which ye were promissed’.'

You have said, 'Our Lord is Allah.' Then keep steadfast to His Book, to the way of His command, and to the virtuous course of His worship. Thereafter do not go out of it, do not introduce innovations in it, and do not turn away from it. Because those who go away from this course will be cut off from (the mercy of) Allah on the Day of Judgement.

Then, beware of destroying your manners and changing them, and make the tongue one, and let a man guard his tongue, for this tongue is obstinate with its master. By Allah, I do not see a servant who fears Allah with a fear that benefits him unless he guards his tongue, and certainly the tongue of the believer is behind his heart, and the heart of the hypocrite is behind his tongue; because when the believer intends to speak a word, he reflects upon it in himself. If it is good, he reveals it, and if it is bad, he conceals it, and the hypocrite speaks whatever comes to his tongue, not knowing what is for him and what is against him.

The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: “The belief of a servant cannot be firm unless his heart is firm, and his heart cannot be firm unless his tongue is firm.” So whoever of you can manage to meet Allah, the Sublime, in such a position that his hands are unsmeared with the blood of Muslims and their property and his tongue is safe from exposing them, he should do so.

Know, O creatures of Allāh, that a believer should regard lawful this year what he regarded lawful in the previous year, and should consider unlawful this year what he considered unlawful in the previous year. Certainly people’s innovation cannot make lawful for you what has been declared unlawful; rather, lawful is that which Allāh has made lawful and unlawful is that which Allāh has made unlawful. You have already tested the matters and tried them; you have been preached by those before you. Illustrations have been drawn for you and you have been called to clear fact. Only a deaf man can remain deaf to all this, and only a blind man can remain blind to all this.

He whom Allah does not allow to benefit from trials and experiences cannot benefit from any preaching, and deficiency comes to him from the front, so that he approves what he should disapprove of, and disapproves what he should approve of. And people are but two: a follower of a religious law, and an innovator of an innovation, to whom Allah, Exalted is He, has not given the proof of a sunnah, nor the light of a plea.

[The Qur'an:] Indeed, Allah, Glorified is He, has not counseled anyone with a like this Qur'an, for it is the strong rope of Allah and His trustworthy means, and in it is the springing forth of the heart, and the springs of knowledge, and there is no other gloss for the heart than it. although those who remembered it have passed away, while those who forgot or pretended to have forgotten it have remained. So when you see good, support it, and when you see evil, turn away from it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'O son of Adam, do good and leave evil; then you will be a swift, straight-going one.'

[Categories of oppression:] Know that injustice is of three kinds: one that is not forgiven, one that is not left (unpunished), and one that is forgiven and not sought after. As for the injustice that is not forgiven, it is duality (associating partners) with Allah. Allah the Exalted said: 'Verily Allah forgiveth not that (anything) be associated with Him'. Verily Allah forgiveth not that (anything) be associated with Him As for the injustice that is forgiven, it is the injustice a man does to himself by committing small sins; and the injustice that is not left (unpunished) is the injustice of men against other men. The retribution in such a case is severe. It is not wounding with knives, nor striking with whips, but it is so severe that all these things are small against it. You should therefore avoid change in the matter of Allah's religion, for indeed a group united upon what you dislike of the truth is better than a group scattered upon what you like of falsehood. And indeed Allah, Glorified is He, has not given any person, whether among those who passed away or among those who remain, any good from separation.
