Not all of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) were those who would ask him and seek clarification from him, indeed, they would love for a Bedouin or a stranger to come and ask him (peace be upon him) so that they could listen. Whenever any such thing came before me, I asked him about its meaning and preserved it.
These are the grounds/reasons upon which the people stand in their differences, and the causes of their differences in their traditions (narrations).
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he would rouse his companions to jihad against the people of Syria in his time.

O Allah! Whoever of Your servants hears our utterance which is just and not deviant, and after hearing it refuses nothing but to turn away from supporting You, and to delay in strengthening Your religion, then we call You to witness against him, O Greatest of Witnesses, with a testimony, and we call all whom You have settled on Your earth and in Your skies to witness against him, then You alone are the One who makes us needless of his support, and the One who takes him to account for his sin.

Praise be to Allah, the Exalted above the similarity of creatures, The Prevailing over the speech of describers, the Apparent through the wonders of His management for the observers, the Hidden by the majesty of His might from the thought of those who imagine, the Knowing without acquisition or increase, and without acquired knowledge, the Ordainer of all matters without reflection or thinking, He who is not covered by darkness, nor does He seek light from lights, nor does night overtake Him, nor does day pass over Him, His comprehension is not by sight, and His knowledge is not by being informed.

And from it, in the mention of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): Allāh sent him with light, and accorded him the highest precedence in selection. Through him Allāh united those who were divided, overpowered the powerful, overcame difficulties and levelled rugged ground, and thus removed misguidance from right and left.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), he describes the essence of the Messenger, describes the scholars, and exhorts with piety.

I stand witness that He is just and does justice; He is the arbiter Who decides (between right and wrong). I also stand witness that Muḥammad is His slave. His Messenger and the Chief of His creatures. Whenever Allāh divided the line of descent, He put him in the better one, and therefore, no evil-doer ever shared with him nor was any vicious person his partner.

Beware! Surely Allāh has provided for virtue those who are suited to it, for truth pillars (that support it), and for obedience protection (against deviation). In every matter of obedience you will find Allāh's succour that will speak through tongues and accord firmness to hearts. It has sufficiency for those who seek sufficiency, and a cure for those who seek cure.

[The characteristics of the scholars:] Know that, certainly, those creatures of Allah who preserve His knowledge offer protection to those things which He desires to be protected and make His springs flow (for the benefit of others). They contact each other with guardianship/friendship and meet each other with affection. They drink from cups of satiety and return with distinction. Misgiving does not affect them and backbiting does not gain ground with them. In this way Allah has tied their nature with good manners. Because of this they love each other and meet each other. They have become superior, like seeds which are selected by taking some and throwing away others. This selection has distinguished them and the process of choosing has purified them.

The exhortation to piety: Therefore, man should secure honour by adopting these qualities. He should fear the day of Doom before it arrives, and he should appreciate the shortness of his life and the shortness of his sojourn in the place of stay which has only to last for his change over to the next place. He should therefore do something for his change over and for the known stages of his departure.

Blessed is he who possesses a virtuous heart, obeys one who guides him, keeps away from one who takes him to ruin, catches the path of safety with the help of him who provides him light (of guidance) and by obeying the leader who commands him, hastens towards guidance before its doors are closed, gets open the door of repentance and removes the (stain of) sins. He has certainly been put on the right path and guided towards the straight road.
And from his supplications (peace be upon him), he often recited it.

Praise be to Allah, the One in whom I have not become dead nor sick, nor have my veins been struck with evil, nor have I been taken for the worst of my deeds, nor is my progeny cut off, nor have I reverted from my religion, nor do I deny my Lord, nor do I feel strangeness in my faith, nor is my intellect confused, nor have I been punished with the punishment of the nations before me. I have become a slave, owned (by You), wronging myself, You have the argument against me and I have no argument (against You), I cannot take except what You have given me, and I cannot ward off except what You have saved me from.

O Allah I seek Thy protection from becoming destitute despite Thy riches, from being misguided despite Thy guidance, from being molested in Thy realm, and from being humiliated while authority rests with Thee.
O Allah Let my spirit be the first of those good objects that Thou takest from me and the first trust out of Thy favours held in trust with me.
O Allah, we seek refuge in You from turning away from Your command, or being tested/led astray from Your religion, or our desires following us without the guidance that came from You!
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the grievance and complaint from the Quraysh And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the grievance and complaint from the Quraysh

O Allah, I call You to witness against the Quraysh, for they have cut asunder my kinship and over-turned my cup and have joined together to contest a right to which I was entitled more than anyone else. They said to me: 'If you get your right, that will be just, but if you are denied the right, that too will be just. Endure it with sadness or kill yourself in grief.'

I looked around but found no one to shield me, protect me or help me except the members of my family. I refrained from flinging them into death and therefore closed my eyes despite the dust, kept swallowing saliva despite (the suffocation of) grief and endured pangs of anger although it was more bitter than colocynth and more grievous than the bite of knives.
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: This utterance of Amīr al-mu’minīn has already appeared in an earlier Sermon (172), but I have repeated it here because of the difference of versions.
And from his words (peace be upon him), when he passed by Talhah ibn Abd Allah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Itab ibn Asid, while they were corpses killed on the day of Jamal,

Abū Muḥammad has become a stranger in this place! By Allāh, I did not like that the Quraysh should lie killed under the stars! I have avenged myself with the descendants of ‘Abd Manāf, but the chief persons of Banū Jumaḥ have escaped me, They had stretched their necks towards a matter for which they were not suited, and therefore their necks were broken before they reached the goal.

And from his words (peace be upon him): He said to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays while he was on the pulpit of Kufah delivering a sermon, something of his speech was interrupted by al-Ash'ath, so he said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, this is against you, not for you.' So he (peace be upon him) lowered his gaze to him and then said:

How do you know what is for me and what is against me?! Curse of Allāh and others be on you. You are a weaver and son of a weaver. You are the son of an unbeliever and yourself a hypocrite. You were arrested once by the Unbelievers and once by the Muslims, but your wealth and birth could not save you from either. The man who contrives for his own people to be put to sword and invites death and destruction for them does deserve that the near ones should hate him and the remote ones should not trust him.

As-Sayyid al-Radi says: He (peace be upon him) means that he was captured once as an unbeliever and once in Islam. As for his saying: 'The sword was brought upon his people by his guidance,' he meant the incident of al-Ash'ath with Khalid ibn al-Walid at Yamamah, where he deceived his people and plotted against them until Khalid attacked them. After that, his people called him 'Urf an-Nar,' which is the name for the traitor among them.

And from his words (peace be upon him) describing the one who walks the path to God, Exalted is He. He who is patient prevails, he who is ignorant is incapacitated, he who is lazy perishes, he who is greedy has bad opinion of God, he who is content is pleased with God, he who relies on God God suffices him, he who is grateful God increases him, he who remains silent is safe, he whose character is good is loved by people, and he whose character is bad is disliked by people.

He kept his mind alive and killed his desires, until his body became thin, his bulk turned light, and an effulgence of extreme brightness shone for him. It lighted the way for him and took him on the path. Different doors led him to the door of safety and the place of permanent stay. His feet, balancing his body, became fixed in the position of safety and comfort, because he kept his heart in good acts and pleased his Lord.

And from his words (peace be upon him), he said it upon reciting it: Therein declare glory unto Him in the mornings and the evenings; Men whom neither merchandise nor any sale diverteth from the remembrance of Allah.

Certainly, Allāh, the Glorified, the Sublime, has made His remembrance the light for hearts which hear with its help despite deafness, see with its help despite blindness and become submissive with its help despite unruliness. In all the periods and times when there were no prophets, there have been persons with whom Allāh, precious are His bounties, whispered through their wits and spoke through their minds. With the help of the bright awakening of their ears, eyes and hearts they keep reminding others of the remembrance of the days of Allāh and making others feel fear for Him like guide-points in wildernesses. Whoever adopts the middle way, they praise his ways and give him the tidings of deliverance, but whoever goes right and left they vilify his ways and frighten him with ruin. In this way, they served as lamps in these darknesses and guides through these doubts.

If you picture them in your mind in their admirable positions and well-known sittings, when they have opened the records of their actions and are prepared to render an account of themselves in respect of the small as well as the big things they were ordered to do but they failed to do, or were ordered to refrain from but they indulged therein, and they realised the weight of their burden (of bad acts) on their backs, and they felt too weak to bear them, then they wept bitterly and spoke to each other while still crying and bewailing to Allāh in repentance and acknowledgement (of their shortcomings), you would find them to be emblems of guidance and lamps in darkness, angels would be surrounding them, peace would be descending upon them, the doors of the sky would be opened for them and positions of honour would be assigned to them in the place of which Allāh had informed them.

Therefore, He has appreciated their actions and praised their position. They call Him and breathe in the air of forgiveness, they are ever needy of His bounty and remain humble before His greatness, The length of their grief has pained their hearts, and the length of weeping their eyes. They knock at every door of inclination towards Allāh. They ask Him Whom generosity does not make destitute and from Whom those who approach Him do not get disappointed. Therefore, take account of yourself for your own sake because the account of others will be taken by one other than you.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him): He expresses detachment from oppression. The condition of Aqil regarding poverty and hunger.

By Allah, I would rather spend a night in wakefulness on the thorns of the sa'dan plant, or be dragged in chains as a prisoner, than meet Allah and His Messenger on the Day of Resurrection as an oppressor to any of the servants, or a usurper of anything out of worldly wealth. And how can I oppress anyone for a life that hastens towards destruction in its return, and remains long in the earth in its settlement?!

By Allah, I certainly saw 'Aqil fallen in destitution to the point that he asked me for a sa' of your wheat, and I saw his children with dishevelled hair and dusty colors due to their poverty, as if their faces had been blackened with indigo. He renewed his request to me emphatically, and repeated the saying to me repeatedly, so I directed my hearing to him, and he thought that I would sell him my religion and follow his lead, leaving my own way. So I heated a piece of iron for him, then brought it near his body so that he might take a lesson from it, then he cried with the cry of one suffering from a chronic ailment due to its pain, and he was about to burn from its branding.

Then I said to him: May the moaning women moan over you, O Aqil! Do you cry on account of this iron which its maker heated for his play, while he is driving me towards the fire which its Creator prepared for His wrath! Should you cry from pain, but I should not cry from the flames?

And more astonishing than that a stranger came to us in the night with a closed flask in its container, and a paste which I disliked, as though it had been kneaded with the saliva of a serpent or its vomit. So I said: Is it a reward, or zakat, or charity? For that is forbidden to us, the People of the House! He said: Neither this nor that, but it is a gift. So I said: May childless women weep over you! Have you come to me from the religion of Allah to deceive me? Or are you mad, or possessed by jinn, or speaking without senses?
And from his supplications (peace be upon him), he seeks refuge with Allah that He should suffice him.

O Allah, preserve my face (dignity) with ease (of livelihood) and do not disgrace my status with poverty (destitution) lest I beg for sustenance from those who seek Your sustenance and seek the favour of the evil of Your creatures and be tested by praising those who give to me and be tempted by abusing those who withhold from me and You are, beyond all that, the Bestower and the Withholder Verily, You are All-Powerful over all things.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) on discouraging [people] from the world. The world is the house of one who does not criticize it except a wise man, and the house of one who does not understand it except a fool, and the house of one who does not remain in it except a deceived one, and the house of one who does not leave it except a perishing one. It is a dwelling of permanence for one who has no permanence, and a dwelling of transience for one who has no transience. It is a dwelling of action without reward, and a dwelling of planting without harvest. It is a dwelling of change and alteration, and the changing of things one after another, and the changing of the living one after another. It is a dwelling in which transience has preceded, and permanence has lagged behind, and death has preceded, and life has lagged behind. It is a dwelling in which God has made transience a permanence, and permanence a transience, and has made death its end, and life its beginning. It is a dwelling in which God has made action little, and reward abundant, and has made death its end, and life its beginning. It is a dwelling in which God has made transience a permanence, and permanence a transience, and has made death its end, and life its beginning.

Know, O creatures of Allah, that you and all that you have in this world (are treading) on the path of those who have passed before you, from among those who had longer lives than you, more populated houses, and more lasting traces, their voices have become silent, their movements have become stationary, their bodies have become rotten, their houses have become empty, and their traces have been obliterated.

They exchanged the fortified palaces and the spread-out carpets, the rocks and the leaning stones, and the flat, hollowed-out graves, whose courtyards are built upon ruins, and whose construction was raised with soil, so their location is contiguous, but their inhabitants are like strangers, among the people of their neighborhood yet feeling lonely, and those free from work yet engaged (in activity), they do not feel attachment to their homelands, nor do they maintain contact like neighbors, despite what is between them of nearness of neighborhood and proximity of abodes, and how can there be mutual visiting among them when decay has ground them with its millstone, and stones and earth have eaten them?

It is as though you too have gone where they have gone, the same sleeping place has caught you and the same place has detained you. What will then be your position when your affairs reach their end and graves are turned upside down (to throw out the dead)? “There shall every soul realise what it hath sent before, and they shall be brought back to Allāh, their true Lord, and what they did fabricate (the false deities) will vanish (away) from them.”
And from his speech (peace be upon him), referring to one of his companions, those who died before the occurrence of the tribulations (fitan).

May Allāh reward such and such man who straightened the curve, cured the disease, abandoned mischief and established the sunnah. He departed (from this world) with untarnished clothes and little shortcomings. He achieved good (of this world) and remained safe from its evils. He offered Allāh’s obedience and feared Him as He deserved. He went away and left the people in dividing ways wherein the misled cannot obtain guidance and the guided cannot attain certainty. and the guided cannot attain certainty.
And from his words (peace be upon him) describing his allegiance to the Caliphate Al-Sharif said: And a similar one has preceded with different phrasings

You drew out my hand towards you for allegiance but I held it back, and you stretched it but I contracted it. Then you crowed over me as the thirsty camels crowd on the watering cisterns on their being taken there, so much so that shoes were torn, shoulder-cloths fell away and the weak got trampled, and the happiness of people on their allegiance to me was so manifested that small children felt joyful, the old staggered (up to me) for it, the sick too reached for it helter skelter and young girls ran for it without veils.

Certainly, fear of Allah is the key to guidance provision for the next world freedom from every slavery and deliverance from all ruin With its help the seeker succeeds and he who makes for safety escapes and achieves his aims

The virtue of action: So perform (good) acts while such acts are being raised (up to Allāh), while repentance can be of benefit, prayer can be heard, conditions are peaceful and the pens (of the two angels) are in motion (to record the actions). Hasten towards (virtuous) actions before the change of age (to oldness), lingering illness or snatching death (overtakes you). Certainly, death will end your enjoyments, mar your pleasures and remove your objectives.

It is an unwanted visitor, an invincible adversary and an unaccounting killer. Its ropes have entrapped you, its evils have surrounded you, its arrowheads have aimed at you, its sway over you is great, its oppression on you is continuous and the chance of its missing you is remote.

Very soon you will be overwhelmed with the gloom of its shades, the severity of its illness, the darkness of its distresses, the nonsense utterances of its pangs, the grief of its destruction, the darkness of its encompassment and the unwholesomeness of its taste.

It will seem as if it has come to you all of a sudden, silenced those who were whispering to you, separated your group, destroyed your doings, devastated your houses and altered your successors, distribute your estate among the chief relatives, who did not give you any benefit, or the grieved near ones who could not protect (you), or those rejoicers who did not lament (you).

The virtue of diligence: Therefore, it is upon you to strive, make effort, equip yourself, get ready and provide yourself from the place of provision. And let not the life of this world deceive you as it deceived those before you among the past people and by-gone periods -- those who extracted its milk, benefited from its neglectfulness, passed a long time and turned its new things into old (by living long).

Their abodes turned into graves, and their wealth into inheritable estate. They do not know who came to them, nor do they pay heed to those who weep over them, nor do they respond to those who call them. Therefore, beware of this world, for it is treacherous, deceitful, and cheating; it gives and takes back, covers with clothes and uncovers. Its pleasure does not last, its hardship does not end, and its calamity does not stop.

And from it, regarding the description of the ascetics: They were a people from among the people of this world but were not its people, so they were in it as though they did not belong to it. They acted in it based on what they perceived, and hastened in it to avoid what they feared. Their bodies moved among the people of the Hereafter. They see the people of this world attaching importance to the death of their bodies, while they themselves attach greater importance to the death of the hearts of those who are alive.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) which he delivered at Dhi Qar while he was heading towards Basrah; al-Waqidi mentioned it in the book 'Al-Jamal'.

He manifested whatever he was commanded, and conveyed the message of his Lord. Consequently, Allah repaired the cracks through him, joined the slits through him, and reconciled through him the relatives, after the deep-seated enmity in the chests and the burning grudges in the hearts.
And among his sayings (peace be upon him): 'Abdullah ibn Zama'ah, who was from his followers, came to him during his caliphate seeking money from him, so he (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, this money is neither for me nor for you, but it is the collective property of the Muslims and the acquisition of their swords, If you had taken part with them in their fighting you would have a share equal to theirs, otherwise the earning of their hands cannot be for other than their mouths.

And from his sayings (peace be upon him), after one of them stepped forward to speak, he was constrained, while he was [speaking] of the virtue of the Ahl al-Bayt and describing the corruption of the times.

Know that the tongue is a part of a man’s body. If the man desists, speech will not co-operate with him and when he dilates, speech will not give him time to stop. Certainly, we are the masters of speaking. Its veins are fixed in us and its branches are hanging over us.

And from his sayings (peace be upon him): Dhi‘lib al-Yamāmī narrated from Aḥmad ibn Qutaybah, from ‘Abdullāh ibn Yazīd, from Mālik ibn Diḥyah, who said: We were with Amīr al-mu’minīn (peace be upon him) when the differences of people were mentioned before him, so he said:

The sources of their clay are what differentiate them, and this is because they are a portion from the saltish soil and the sweet soil of the earth, and from the rugged earth and the soft earth. Therefore, they resemble each other according to the proximity of their soil, and differ according to its difference. Thus, the one with handsome features is weak in intelligence, the tall-statured is short in courage, the virtuous in deed is ugly in appearance, the one close to the bottom is far in depth, the well-known in trait is unknown in essence, the one with a perplexed heart has a scattered mind, and the loose-tongued has a sharp heart.
And one of his sayings (peace be upon him) was when he was attending to the funeral ablution (ghusl) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and shrouding him.

If it were not for the fact that you ordered endurance and prevented us from bewailing, we would have produced a store of tears for you, and even then the pain would not have subsided, and this grief would not have ended, and they would have been too little of our grief for you. But this (death) is a matter that cannot be reversed nor is it possible to repulse it.
May my father and my mother die for you do remember us with Allāh and take care of us
And from his words (peace be upon him), in this sermon he recounted the mention of what was from him after the migration of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then his joining him.
I began following the path adopted by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), treading on the lines of his remembrance, until I reached al-'Arj.

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī (may Allah be pleased with him) says in a long hadith: His words (peace be upon him): 'fa aṭa’u dhikrahu' constitute the highest forms of brevity and eloquence. He means to say that he was being given news about the Prophet from the commencement of his setting out till he reached this place, and he has expressed this sense in this wonderful expression.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding hastening to action. O people, prepare for departure, and take provision for the Hereafter before death comes between you and it, for a standing [in regret] after the opportunity has passed is of no avail, nor is a return for what has passed.

Perform (good) acts while you are still in the vastness of life, the books are open (for recording of actions), repentance is allowed, the runner away (from Allāh) is being called and the sinner is being given hope (of forgiveness) before the (light of) action is put off, time expires, life ends, the door for repentance is closed and angels ascend to the sky.

Therefore a man should derive benefit from himself for himself, from the living for the dead, from the mortal, for the lasting and from the departer for the stayer. A man should fear Allāh while he is given age to live upto his death, and is allowed time to act. A man should control his self by the rein and hold it with its bridle, thus by the rein he should prevent it from disobedience towards Allāh, and by the bridle he should lead it towards obedience to Allāh.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) concerning the two arbitrators and the disparagement of the people of Syria.

Rude, low people, mean slaves. They have been collected from all sides and picked up from every pack. They need to be taught the tenets (of Islam), disciplined, instructed, trained, supervised and led by the hand. They are neither muhājirūn (immigrants from Mecca), nor anṣār (helpers of Medina) nor those who made their dwellings in the abode (in Medina) and in belief.

Look! They have chosen for themselves one who is nearest of all of them to what they desire, while you have chosen one who is nearest to what you dislike. You may certainly recall that the other day ‘Abdullāh ibn Qays (Abū Mūsā) was saying: “It is a mischief, therefore, cut away your bow-string and sheathe your swords.” If he was right (in what he said) then he was wrong in marching (with us) without being forced, but if he was lying then he should be viewed with suspicion. Therefore, send ‘Abdullāh ibn al-‘Abbās to face ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ. Make use of these days and surround the borders of Islam. Do you not see that your cities are being attacked and your prowess is being aimed at?
And from his sermon (peace be upon him), which is a comprehensive word containing admonition and wisdom.

Your aim (reward or punishment) is before you, and behind your back is the Hour (of Resurrection) which is driving you on; keep light and overtake (the forward ones). Your last ones are being awaited by the first ones (who have proceeded).

And I say: If this utterance is weighed against any other utterance, after the word of Allah (Exalted is He) and the word of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), it would prove heavier and superior in every respect. For example, ‘Ali’s saying “Keep light and over-take” is the shortest expression ever heard with the greatest sense conveyed by it. How wide is its meaning and how clear its spring of wisdom! We have pointed out the greatness and meaningfulness of this phrase in our book al-Khaṣā’iṣ.
And from his words (peace be upon him), in which he exhorts his companions to jihad. He exhorts his companions to jihad.

And Allah seeks from you the thanksgiving due to Him, and assigns to you His affairs, He grants you respite in a limited field, so that you may vie with each other for precedence (in reward). Therefore, tighten the knots of your girdles, and fold up the excess of your loincloths, And high resolve and feasting do not go together, And sleep causes weakness in the major affairs of the day, It obliterates the darkness from the remembrance of the spirits (or: it clears the darkness for the recollection of the resolve)!
Allāh may bless our master Muḥammad, the Prophet, and his descendants who are lamps of darkness and trustworthy support, and may bestow peace (upon them) abundantly and profusely.

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) When successive news reached him that the companions of Mu'awiya were occupying the lands, and his two officers in Yemen, namely Ubayd Allah ibn al-Abbas and Sa'id ibn Numayran, came to him after Busr ibn Abi Artaq had overpowered them, he was much disturbed by the slackness of his companions in jihad and their difference with his opinion. He proceeded to the pulpit and said:
And he illustrated with the verse of a poet: O ‘Amr! By your good father’s life. I have received only a small bit of fat from this pot (fat that remains sticking to it after it has been emptied).

O Allah, I have become weary of them and they have become weary of me, I have grown sick of them and they have grown sick of me. So replace them with better ones for me, and replace me with worse ones for them, O Allah, melt their hearts as salt melts in water,
By Allah, I would wish that I had a thousand horsemen from among you, of the Banu Firas ibn Ghanm: there, if you called them, they would come to you like the shooting of the summer cloud.
(Thereafter Amīr al-mu’minīn alighted from the pulpit)

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: I said: The word 'al-armiyah' is the plural of 'ramiyy', which means cloud, and 'al-hamīm' in this context means the time of summer, and the poet specifically mentioned the clouds of summer because they are more fleeting and move more swiftly, for they contain no water. Clouds are slow-moving only when filled with water, which generally does not occur except in the season of winter. The poet's intent was to describe their speed when called and their swift aid when cried for. The evidence for this is His saying: 'There, if you call them, they will come to you...'

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he describes the Arabs before the Proclamation, then he describes his own state before the pledge of allegiance to him [The Arabs before the Proclamation].

Allah, Glorified is He, sent Muhammad as a warner to the worlds, and a trustee over the Revelation, while you, O people of Arabia, are upon the worst religion, and in the worst abode, resting among rough stones and deaf serpents, you drink muddy water, and eat coarse food, and shed your own blood, and sever your kinship ties. Idols are erected among you, and sin is bound to you.

Part of it I looked and found that there is no supporter for me except my family, so I refrained from thrusting them unto death. I kept my eyes closed despite motes in them. I drank despite choking of throat. I exercised patience despite trouble in breathing and despite having to take sour colocynth as food.

Part of the same sermon on the settlement between Mu'āwiyah and ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ : He did not swear allegiance till he got him agree that he would pay him its price. The hand of this purchaser (of allegiance) may not be successful and the contract of the seller may face disgrace. Now you should take up arms for war and arrange equipment for it. Its flames have grown high and its brightness has increased. Clothe yourself with patience for it is the best to victory.

And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), which he delivered to rouse the people when the news of the campaign of Al-Anbar with the army of Muawiya arrived, but they did not rise [to fight]. In it, he mentions the virtue of jihad, rouses the people, mentions his knowledge of war, and places the blame upon them for their lack of obedience to him.

Now then, surely jihād is one of the doors of Paradise, which Allāh has opened for His chief friends. It is the dress of piety and the protective armour of Allāh and His trustworthy shield. Whoever abandons it Allāh covers him with the dress of disgrace and the clothes of distress. He is kicked with contempt and scorn, and his heart is veiled with screens (of neglect). Truth is taken away from him because of missing jihād. He has to suffer ignominy and justice is denied to him.

Beware! I have called you to fight these people night and day, secretly and openly, and I said to you: Attack them before they attack you, for by Allah, no people have ever been attacked in the heart of their homes but they suffered disgrace; but you procrastinated and forsook one another until raids were launched against you and your homelands were conquered. And this is the brother of Ghamid; his cavalry has reached al-Anbar and killed Hassan ibn Hassan al-Bakri, and has removed your cavalry from their garrisons.

And I have come to know that a man from them would enter upon a Muslim woman, and another under treaty (protection) and would take away her leg ornaments, armlets, necklaces, and ear-rings from which she could not resist except by reciting the verse of return and seeking mercy Then they returned abundant (with wealth) not a single man among them was struck (wounded) nor was his blood shed So if a Muslim man died after this of grief, he would not be blamed, but rather he would be deserving (of it) in my view.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) [which is a section of the sermon that begins: 'All praise is for Allah, from whose mercy one is not hopeless,' and it contains eleven exhortations]
So now, surely this world has turned its back and announced its departure while the next world has appeared forward and proclaimed its approach.

As-Sayyid ar-Radi (may Allah be pleased with him) says: And I say: If there could be an utterance which would drag by the neck towards renunciation in this world, and force to action for the next world, it is this sermon. It is enough to cut off from the entanglements of hopes and to ignite the flames of preaching (for virtue) and warning (against vice).

And among its most wonderful [words] is his (peace be upon him) saying: Behold, today is the day of preparation (the racecourse), and tomorrow is the day of the race; the starting point is Paradise and the destination is Hell, for within it—besides the sublimity of the wording, the greatness of the meaning, the truthfulness of the simile, and the factual nature of the illustration—lies a wonderful secret and a delicate implication,

It is his saying (peace be upon him): "The place to proceed to is Paradise, and the place of doom is Hell." He differentiated between the two words due to the difference in their meanings, and did not say: 'The place to proceed to is Hell,' as he said: 'The place to proceed to is Paradise,' because proceeding (al-istibaq) is only towards something beloved and a desired goal, which is the attribute of Paradise. This meaning is not present in Hell, may we seek refuge in Allah from it! Therefore, it was not proper for him to say: 'And the place to proceed to is Hell,' but he said: 'And the doom is Hell,' because the end (al-ghayah) is reached by one who may or may not be pleased with reaching it, and by one who is pleased with it. Thus, it was suitable to use it to express both matters together.

So it is in this place like the destination and the end, Allah, the Exalted, said: "Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is to the Fire'" And it is not permissible in this place to say: 'You have been preceded to the Fire', so ponder over that, for its inner meaning is wondrous, and its depth is far-reaching, and so is most of his speech (peace be upon him). And in another narration: "And the Sibtah" with a dammed Sin, and the Sabbaqah is a name among them for what is set for the winner if he wins from wealth or property, and the two meanings are close, because that is not a reward for the action of the blameworthy matter, but rather it is a reward for the action of the commendable matter.

O people, your bodies are together but your desires are divergent. Your talk softens the hard stones and your action attracts your enemy towards you. You claim in your sittings that you would do this and that, but when fighting approaches, you say (to war), ‘turn thou away’ (i.e. flee away). If one calls you (for help) the call receives no heed. And he who deals hardly with you his heart has no solace. The excuses are amiss like that of debtor unwilling to pay. The ignoble cannot ward off oppression. Right cannot be achieved without effort. Which is the house besides this one to protect? And with which leader (Imām) would you go for fighting after me?

Deceived is one whom you have deceived, and he who is successful with you receives only useless arrows, and he who throws you is like throwing a broken arrow. I have become, by Allah, one who neither confirms your views nor hopes for your support, nor challenges the enemy through you. What is the matter with you? What is your ailment? What is your cure? The other party is also men of your shape (but they are so different in character). Will there be talk without action, carelessness without piety and greed in things not right?!
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), which includes refining the poor through asceticism and disciplining the rich through affection/compassion.

Now then, verily Divine orders descend from heaven to earth like drops of rain, bringing to every one what is destined for him whether plenty or paucity. So if any one of you observes for his brother plenty of progeny or of wealth or of self, it should not be a worry for him. So long as a Muslim does not commit such an act that if it is disclosed he has to bend his eyes (in shame) and by which low people are emboldened, he is like the gambler who expects that the first draw of his arrow would secure him gain and also cover up the previous loss.

Similarly, the Muslim man who is free from dishonesty expects one of the two good things from Allah: either a call [to death] from Allah, and whatever is with Allah is better for him, or the livelihood of Allah, in which case he is a man of family and wealth, and with him are his faith and lineage. Certainly, wealth and children are the plantation of this world, and virtuous deeds are the plantation of the next world, and Allah may gather both for some people.

Beware of Allah against what He has cautioned you and keep afraid of Him to the extent that no excuse is needed for it. Act without show or intention of being heard, for if a man acts for some one else then Allah makes him over to that one. We ask Allah (to grant us) the positions of the martyrs, company of the virtuous and friendship of the prophets.

And from it: Behold! Let not one of you turn away from his relatives, who sees in them neediness, that he should fill their need with that which will not increase if he withholds it, nor decrease if he spends it. And whoever holds back his hand from his kinsmen, only one hand is held back from him by them, but many hands are held back from him by them. And whoever is gentle in his disposition retains the affection of his people.

As-Sayyid al-Sharif says: I say: 'Al-ghafirah' here means abundance and multitude, from their saying regarding a large crowd: 'al-jamm al-ghafir' or 'al-jama' al-ghafir'. And it is narrated as '‘afwatan min ahli aw mal' (a choice from the people or wealth), and 'al-'ifuwah' means the best or selected part of something; it is said: 'I ate the 'ifuwah of the food,' meaning its best part. And how beautiful is the meaning intended by Him (peace be upon him) in His saying: 'And whoever withholds his hand from his kin...' until the end of the speech, for he who withholds his help from his kin only withholds the benefit of one hand; but when he needs their support and is compelled to seek their assistance, they stay back from helping him and lag behind in responding to his call, thus preventing the mutual support of many hands and the vigorous advance of numerous feet.

And from his words (peace be upon him): When Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah have mercy on him) was sent to Az-Zubayr before the outbreak of the war on the Day of the Camel, to advise him back to obedience, he said to him on that occasion:

Do not meet Ṭalḥah for if you meet him, you will find him like an unruly bull whose horns are turned towards its ears. He rides a ferocious riding beast and says it has been tamed. But you meet az-Zubayr because he is soft-tempered so tell him: Your maternal cousin says to you I knew you in the Hijāz and did not know you in Iraq So, what has dissuaded (you) from what was shown (by you previously)?
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: He (peace be upon him) is the first from whom I heard this word, namely: “Famā ‘adā mimmā badā”.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) when he set out to fight the people of Basra [In it is the wisdom of the sending of the messengers, then he mentions his virtue and condemns the rebels]

Verily, Allah, Glory be to Him, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), when none among the Arabs read a book or claimed prophethood. He guided the people until he settled them in their place and brought them to their salvation. So their spears (officers) became straight and their conditions settled down.

By Allah, surely I was in their lead till it took shape with its walls. I did not show weakness or cowardice. My existing march is also like that. I shall certainly pierce the wrong till right comes out of its side.

What (cause of conflict) is there between me and the Quraysh? By Allāh, I have fought them when they were unbelievers and I shall fight them when they have been misled. I shall be the same for them today as I was for them yesterday!

By my life, you continued drinking fresh milk every morning, And (continued) eating fine stoned dates with butter; We have given you the nobility which you did not possess before; And surrounded (protected) you with thoroughbred horses and tawnycoloured spears (strong spears).

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) after the Arbitration and what reached him concerning the matter of the two arbitrators, in which he praises God for His trial, then explains the cause of the affliction.

All praise is due to Allah, even though time has brought (for us) crushing calamity and great occurrence. And I stand witness that there is no god but Allah, the One, there is no partner for Him nor is there with Him any god other than Himself, and that Muhammad is His slave and His Prophet (May Allah’s blessing and greeting be upon him and his progeny).

So now, certainly the disobedience of the sympathetic counsellor who has knowledge as well as experience brings about disappointment and result in repentance. I had given you my orders about this arbitration and put before you my hidden view, if Qasir’s orders were fulfilled but you rejected it (my orders) like rough opponents and disobedient insurgents till the counsellor himself fell in doubt about his counsel and the flint (of his wit) ceased to give flame. Consequently, mine and your position became as the poet of Hawāzin says:
I gave you my orders at Mun‘araji’l-liwã but you did not see the good of my counsel till the noon of next day (when it was too late).
And from his utterances (peace be upon him) which runs like a Sermon [in which he mentions his virtues (peace be upon him), he said it after the Battle of Nahrawan]

I stood firm in the matter when they faltered, and I came forward when they hesitated, and I proceeded with the light of Allah when they stood still. I was the quietest of them in voice but the foremost in going forward; I flew with its rein and monopolized its pledge, like the mountain which neither sweeping winds move nor storms displace. No one had a spur (to urge me on) in me, nor any speaker had a flaw (to criticize) in me.

The lowly is in my view worthy of honour till I secure (his) right for him, and the strong is in my view weak till I take (others') right from him, We are happy with the destiny ordained by Allah and have submitted to the command of Allah. Do you think I would speak lie about the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, I am surely the first to testify him, so I will not be the first to falsify him. I looked at my affairs and found that my obedience should have precedence over my allegiance while my pledge with him is a burden on my neck.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) In it is the reason for naming doubt 'doubt' (shubha), then the description of the state of people within it.

Doubt is named doubt because it resembles truth, As for the lovers of Allah, their conviction serves them as light, and the direction of the right path serves as their guide; while the enemies of Allah, in time of doubt call to misguidance, and their guide is blindness; One who fears death cannot escape it, nor can one who loves it secure eternal life.

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) [he delivered it upon knowing about the battle of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, the companion of Mu'awiya, at 'Ayn al-Tamr] [and in it he presents his excuse, and rouses the people to support him]

I am faced with men who do not obey when I order and do not respond when I call them, May you have no father! (Woe to you!) What are you waiting for to rise for the cause of Allah? Does not faith join you together, or sense of shame rouse you?! I stand among you shouting and I am calling you for help, but you do not listen to my word, and do not obey my orders, till circumstance show out their bad consequences. No blood can be avenged through you and no purpose can be achieved with you. I called you for help of your brethren but made noises like the camel having pain in stomach, and became loose like the camel of thin back. Then a wavering weak contingent came to me from amongst you: “as if they are being led to death and they are only watching.”

As-Sayyid ar-Radi says: I say: His (peace be upon him) word 'mutadhā'ib' means 'muḍṭarib' (i.e. moved or troubled), as they say 'tadhā'abat ar-rīḥ' (i.e. the winds blow in troubled manner), and from this the wolf was named 'dhi'b', because of its troubled movement.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) regarding the Kharijites, when he (peace be upon him) heard their saying: 'No verdict/judgment except for Allah,' he (peace be upon him) said:

The sentence is right but what (they think) it means, is wrong. It is true that verdict lies but with Allāh, but these people say that (the function of) governance is only for Allāh. The fact is that there is no escape for men from ruler good or bad. The faithful persons perform (good) acts in his rule while the unfaithful enjoys (worldly) benefits in it. During the rule, Allāh would carry everything to end. Through the ruler tax is collected, enemy is fought, roadways are protected and the right of the weak is taken from the strong till the virtuous enjoys peace and allowed protection from (the oppression of) the wicked.
In another version that he (peace be upon him), when he heard their judgment, said: I am awaiting Allah's verdict upon you. And he said:
As for the good government, the pious man performs good acts in it, and as for the bad government, the wicked person enjoys in it, until his term ends and death overtakes him.
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), In it, he forbids treachery and warns against it.

Surely fulfilment of pledge is the twin of truth, and I do not know a better shield (against the assaults of sin) than it, One who realises the reality of return (to the next world) never betrays. We are in a period when most of the people regard betrayal as wisdom. In these days the ignorant call it excellence of cunning. What is the matter with them? Allāh may destroy them. One who has been through thick and thin of life finds the excuses to be preventing him from orders and prohibitions of Allāh but he disregards them despite capability (to succumb to them and follows the commands of Allāh), while one who has no restraints of religion seizes the opportunity (and accepts the excuses for not following the commands of Allāh).
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) In it, he warns against following desires and prolonging hope in the world

O people! What I fear most for you are two things: following desires and extending hopes; as for following desires, it turns one away from the truth, and as for extending hopes, it makes one forget the Hereafter. Know that this world has passed away rapidly, and nothing remains of it except the dregs, like the dregs of a vessel which the drinker has emptied. Know that the Hereafter has approached, and each of them has sons (followers); so be among the sons of the Hereafter, and do not be among the sons of this world, for every son will be joined to his mother on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, today is a day of action and no reckoning, and tomorrow is a day of reckoning and no action.

My preparation for war with the people of Syria while Jarīr is still there, would be closing the door for Syria, and preventing its people from good if they intend doing it, but I have fixed a time limit for Jarīr after which he would not stay without either deception or in disobedience, my opinion is in favour of patience, so wait a while. I do not dislike your getting ready.

I have observed this matter thoroughly from all sides, and turned it over, but I found no way except war or heresy regarding what Muhammad (peace be upon him) brought. Certainly, there was over the people a ruler who brought about new (unIslamic) things and compelled the people to speak out. So they did speak, then rose up and thereafter changed the whole system.

And from his sayings (peace be upon him): When Masqalah ibn Hubayrah al-Shaybani fled to Mu'awiya, for he had purchased the captives of Banu Najiyah from an agent of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and freed them, when he (peace be upon him) demanded the money from him, he cheated him and fled to Syria.

Allah may be bad to Maṣqalah! He acted like the noble but fled away like a slave! Before his admirer could speak (about him) he silenced him and before his eulogist could testify to his good deeds he closed his mouth. If he had stayed behind we would have taken from him what he could easily pay and waited for the balance till his money increased.
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the mention of Kufah.

As though I see you, O Kufah, you are being drawn out like the tanning of the leather of 'Ukaz, you are being scraped by calamities, and you are being ridden by severe troubles, and I certainly know that if any tyrant intends evil for you, Allah will afflict him with worry and fling him with a killer!
And from one of his sermons (peace be upon him), and in it is a collection of the attributes of Lordship and Divine Knowledge.

Praise be to Allah Who lies inside all hidden things, and towards Whom all open things guide. He cannot be seen by the eye of an onlooker, but the eye which does not see Him cannot deny Him while the mind that proves His existence cannot perceive Him. He is so high in sublimity that nothing can be more sublime than He, while in nearness, He is so near that no one can be nearer than He. But his sublimity does not put Him at a distance from anything of His creation, nor does His nearness bring them on equal level to Him. He has not informed (human) wit about the limits of His qualities. Nevertheless, He has not prevented it from securing essential knowledge of Him. So He is such that all signs of existence stand witness for Him till the denying mind also believes in Him. Allah is sublime beyond what is described by those who liken Him to things or those who deny Him.

One of his (peace be upon him) sermons, after his departure from Ṣiffīn in which he describes the state of the people before the Proclamation, the characteristics of the family of the Prophet, and then the characteristics of another group of people.

I praise Him seeking completion of His Blessing, submitting to His Glory, and seeking safety from His disobedience, I invoke His help [as one] in need of His Sufficiency, Indeed, He whom He guides does not go astray, and He with whom He is hostile gets no protection, and He whom He supports does not remain needy; For He is the heaviest of all that is weighed, and the most valuable of all that is treasured.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah a testimony whose sincerity has been tested, whose essence is our belief; we cling to it forever as long as we live, and store it against the tribulations that befall us, for it is the firm resolve of faith, the opener of goodness, the pleasure of the Merciful, and the defeat of Satan.

And I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His Messenger, He sent him with the renowned religion, the established standard, the written Book, the radiant light, the shining gleam, and the clear command, to dispel doubts, present clear proofs, warn through signs, and instill fear through examples. And the people were in trials wherein the rope of religion was broken, the pillars of certainty were shaken, the course diverged, the matter became scattered, the exit was narrow, and the source was darkened, so guidance was obscure, and blindness prevailed.

Allah was disobeyed, Satan was given support, and Belief was forsaken. As a result, the pillars of religion fell down, its traces could not be discerned, its passages had been destroyed, and its streets had fallen into decay. People obeyed Satan and tread his paths. They sought water from his watering places. Through them Satan's emblems got flying and his standard was raised. In vices which trampled the people under their hoofs, and treaded upon them with their feet. The vices stood on their toes (in full stature). And the people immersed in them were strayed, perplexed, ignorant and seduced. As though in a good house with bad neighbours. Instead of sleep they had wakefulness and for antimony they had tears in the eyes. They were in a land where the learned were in bridle (keeping their mouths shut) while the ignorant were honoured.
In the same sermon: And he meant the Household of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

They are the repository of His secret, the refuge for His affairs, the container of His knowledge, and the shelter for His wisdom; the caves of His books and the mountains of His religion. Through them, He straightened the bend of His back and removed the trembling of His limbs.
Among them: meaning by it other people.
They sowed vices, watered them with deception and harvested destruction.

None in this community can be taken at par with the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them), nor can one who was under their obligation be matched with them. They are the foundation of religion and the pillar of Belief, to them the forward runner turns back, and by them the follower overtakes, they possess the chief characteristics for vicegerency, and in their favor exists the will and succession, This is the time when right has returned to its owner and diverted to its centre of return.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which is an explanation of that by which the world is destroyed, namely the fitnas (strife/tribulations), and an explanation of these fitnas.

The basis of the occurrence of evils is desires which are acted upon, and rulings which are innovated, They are against the Book of Allah. People cooperate with each other about them even though it is against the Religion of Allah. If wrong had been pure and unmixed it would not be hidden from those who are in search of it. And if right had been pure without ad-mixture of wrong those who bear hatred towards it would have been silenced. What is, however, done is that something is taken from here and something from there and the two are mixed! At this stage Satan overpowers his friends and they alone escape for whom virtue has been apportioned by Allah from before.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) whose summary had previously appeared in one narration, we mention it here in another narration due to the difference between the two narrations.

(The reward of the ascetics) By Allah, if you weep with the weeping of a she-camel for her young, call out with the cooing of pigeons, and cry out with the crying of devoted monks, and depart to Allah from your wealth and children seeking nearness to Him in the elevation of a rank with Him or the forgiveness of a sin recorded by His books and preserved by His angels, it would be little of what I hope for you from His reward and fear for you from His punishment.

(May God be pleased/Gracious God) By Allah, if your hearts were to melt thoroughly, and your eyes shed tears of blood from hope for Him and fear of Him, and then you were granted long life in this world as long as it lasts, your actions would not repay the great bounties He has bestowed upon you, and His guiding you to faith, even if you did not leave any of your effort.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the mention of the Day of Sacrifice and the description of the sacrificial animal. As for what follows, indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has designated for people days by which they recognize what is permissible for them and what is forbidden to them. He has made for you in them your rituals (manasik) which are the symbols of Allah. He has made for you in them days to remember Allah's favors upon you, and He has made for you in them days to recognize the limits of Allah, and He has made for you in them days to be mindful of Allah, your Lord.

And from the perfection of the sacrifice animal is the facing upwards of its ear, and the health of its eye. So if the ear and the eye are sound, the sacrifice animal is sound and perfect, even if it be hornless, dragging its leg to the place of sacrifice.
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: Here, place of sacrifice means place of slaughter.

And from his speech (peace be upon him), regarding the mention of the allegiance. And therein he describes his companions at Siffin when they prolonged preventing him from fighting the people of Syria.

They leapt upon me as the camels leap upon each other on their arrival for drinking water, having been let loose after unfastening of their four legs till I thought they would either kill me or kill one another in front of me. I thought over this matter in and out to the extent that it prevented me from sleeping. But I found no way except to fight them or else to reject whatever has been brought by Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), I found that to face war was easier for me than to face the retribution, and the hardships of this world were easier than the hardships of the next world.
And from his words (peace be upon him), when his companions showed impatience at his delaying permission for them to fight in Siffin,

As for your saying: Is it all due to the dislike of death? Then by Allah, I do not care whether I enter into death or death comes out to me. And as for your saying: Doubt regarding the people of Syria! Then by Allah, I did not delay war for a day except that I hoped a group would join me, find guidance through me, and see my light with their weak eyes, This is dearer to me than to kill them in their misguidance, although they would be bearing their own sins.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), describing the companions of the Messenger of Allah, that was on the day of Siffin, when he ordered the people to peace.

And indeed, we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), we would kill our fathers, sons, brothers, and uncles; this did not increase us except in faith and submission, and perseverance on the path, and patience over the pangs of pain, and zeal in fighting the enemy, and indeed, a man from us and another from our enemy would pounce upon each other like two strong bulls, exchanging blows with each other, seeing which one would give his companion the cup of death, so sometimes our man prevailed over the enemy, and sometimes the enemy's man prevailed over ours.

When Allah observed our truthfulness, He sent ignominy to our foe and sent His succour to us, till Islam got established with neck on the ground and resting in its place. By my life, if we had also behaved like you, no pillar of (our) religion could have been raised, nor the tree of faith could have borne leaves. By Allah, certainly you will now milk our blood (instead of milk) and eventually you will face shame!

And from his speech (peace be upon him) concerning the description of a blameworthy man, then regarding his excellence. Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan said to him: 'It has reached me that you say: I am an Imam.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'How do you say it?' He said: 'I am an Imam by knowledge, and he is an Imam by dominance/force.'

Indeed, a man will appear among you after me, broad-throated and pot-bellied, He will eat whatever he finds and crave what he does not find. Kill him, but you will not kill him! Know that he will command you to curse me and to renounce me; As for cursing, curse me, for it is purification for me and salvation for you; As for renunciation, do not renounce me, for I was born upon the natural disposition, and I was foremost in faith and migration.
And from his words (peace be upon him): He addressed the Kharijites when they separated from the government and called out, 'No judgment except for Allah.'

A storm may overtake you, and there may be none to prick you (for reforms). Shall I be witness to my becoming heretic after acceptance of Faith and fighting in the company of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)? "In that case I shall be misguided and I shall not be on the right path." So you should return to your evil places, and get back on the traces of your heels. Beware! Certainly you will meet, after me, overwhelming disgrace and sharp sword and tradition that will be adopted by the oppressors as a norm towards you.
He (peace be upon him) said: When he resolved to fight the Kharijites, it was said to him: 'Indeed, the people have crossed the bridge of Nahrawan.'
Their falling place is on this side of the river. By Allāh, not even ten of them will survive while from your side not even ten will be killed.

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) known as Ash-Shiqshiqiyyah, which includes complaining about the matter of the caliphate, then preferring his patience over it, then the people's allegiance to him.
Preferring patience in the absence of supporters

I found that endurance upon them was wiser, so I was patient although there was pricking in the eye and suffocation in the throat, I saw my inheritance being plundered, until the first one went his way, and then handed it over to Ibn al-Khattab after himself.

It is strange!! It is strange that during his lifetime he wished to be released from the caliphate but he confirmed it for the other one after his death. No doubt these two shared its udders strictly among themselves. This one put the Caliphate in a tough enclosure where the utterance was haughty and the touch was rough. Mistakes were in plenty and so also the excuses therefore. One in contact with it was like the rider of an unruly camel. If he pulled up its rein the very nostril would be slit, but if he let it loose he would be thrown. Consequently, by Allāh people got involved in recklessness, wickedness, unsteadiness and deviation.

So I remained patient during the long period and the severity of the trial, until when he went his way (of death), he placed the matter in a group, claiming that I was one of them. By God and the Consultation! When did doubt overtake me alongside the first of them, so that I became paired with these counterparts?
The allegiance paid to 'Ali (peace be upon him)

Nothing took me by surprise, but the people coming to me like the mane of the hyena, They rushed upon me from every side, so much so that the two shoulders were crushed and the ends of my shoulder garment were torn, as they gathered around me like a herd of sheep. When I took up the reins of government, one party broke their pledge, another turned disobedient, and a third acted wrongfully as if they had not heard Allah (Exalted is He) saying: 'That abode in the Hereafter, We assign it for those who intend not to exult themselves in the earth, nor (to make) mischief therein; and the end is (best) for the pious ones.'

Yes, by Allah, they had heard it and understood it but the world appeared glittering in their eyes and its embellishments seduced them! Behold, by Him who split the grain (to grow) and created living beings, if people had not come to me and supporters had not exhausted the argument, and if there had been no pledge of Allah with the learned to the effect that they should not acquiesce in the gluttony of the oppressor and the hunger of the oppressed, I would have cast the rope of Caliphate on its own shoulders, and would have given the last one the same treatment as to the first one. Then you would have seen that in my view this world of yours is no better than the sneezing of a goat.

They said: And a man from the people of As-Sawad stood up to him when he reached this point in his sermon, he handed him a letter, and he began looking at it. When he finished reading it, Ibn 'Abbas said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, if only your speech had continued from where you stopped! He replied (peace be upon him): Far off, O Ibn 'Abbas! That was a camel's roar that surged forth and then subsided! Ibn 'Abbas said: By Allah, I never grieved over any speech as I grieved over that speech, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did not reach it to the extent he wished.

Al-Sharif al-Radi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: His words (peace be upon him) in this sermon: 'Like the rider of a difficult camel, if he pulls the rein stiffly, it bruises its nose; if he lets it loose, it throws him and he cannot control it.' He means: when he tightens his grip on the rein while the camel resists and pulls its head, it bruises its nose; but if he loosens it slightly despite its difficulty, it throws him and he loses control. It is said: 'ashnaq an-naqah' (he pulled the she-camel), meaning he pulled its head with the rein and raised it. 'Shanaqaha' is also used. Ibn al-Sikkit mentioned this in 'Islah al-Mantiq'. And indeed, he (peace be upon him) said 'ashnaqa laha' (he pulled for it) and not 'ashnaqaha' (he pulled it), because he placed it in correspondence with his words 'aslasa laha' (he loosened for it), so it is as if he (peace be upon him) said: 'if he raises its head for it,' meaning he holds it back with the rein.
He (peace be upon him) said: When the Kharijites were killed, it was said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, The people perished entirely.
No, by Allah They still exist in the loins of men and wombs of women. Whenever a chief would appear from among them he would be cut down till the last of them would turn thieves and robbers.
Amīr al-mu’minīn also said concerning the Khārijites:
Do not kill the Kharijites after me because one who seeks right but does not find it, is not like one who seeks wrong and finds it.
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: He means Mu‘āwiyah and his men.
And from his words (peace be upon him), when he was warned of being killed by deceit,
Surely, there is a strong shield of Allah over me. When my day would come it would get away from me and hand me over to death. At that time neither an arrow would go amiss nor a wound would heal up.
And from one of his sermons (peace be upon him), and in it are subtle discussions from Divine Knowledge.

Praise be to Allah, for whom no condition precedes another condition, so that He may be the First before being the Last, and He may be Manifest before being Hidden. Everyone called one (alone) save Him is by virtue of being small; and everyone enjoying honour other than Him is humble. Every powerful person other than Him is weak. Every master other than Him is slave. Every knower other than Him is seeker of knowledge. Every controller other than Him is sometimes imbued with control and sometimes with disability, Every listener other than Him is deaf to light voices while loud voices make him deaf and distant voices also get away from him, Every onlooker other than Him is blind to hidden colours and delicate bodies, Every manifest thing other than Him is hidden, but every hidden thing other than Him is incapable of becoming manifest.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) regarding the teaching of war and fighting, in some of the days of Siffin.

O crowd of Muslims! Make fear of Allāh the routine of your life. Cover yourselves with peace of mind and clinch your teeth because this makes the sword slip off from the skull. Complete your armour and shake your swords in their sheathes before showing them out. Have your eyes on the enemy. Use your spears on both sides and strike (the enemy) with swords. Keep in mind that you are before Allāh and in the company of the Prophet’s cousin.

Repeat your attacks, and feel ashamed of running away, because it is a shame for posterity and (cause of awarding you) fire on the Day of Judgement. Give your lives (to Allāh) willingly, and walk towards death with ease. Beware of this great majority, and the pitched tent and aim at its centre because Satan is hiding in its corner. He has extended his hand for assault and has kept back his foot for running away. Keep one enduring till the light of Truth dawns upon you. “While ye have the upper hand, and Allāh is with you, and never will He depreciate your deeds.”

And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the meaning of the Ansar They said: When the news of the Saqifah reached Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) after the death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he (peace be upon him) said: What did the Ansar say? They said: They said: One chief from us and one chief from you, he (peace be upon him) said:

He (peace be upon him) said: Why did you not argue against them that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had left a will that whoever is good among them should be treated well and whoever is bad should be forgiven? They said: "What is there against them in it?" He said (peace be upon him): "If the authority/government was for them, there would have been no will in their favour." Then he said: "What did the Quraysh plead?" They said: "We argued that they belong to the lineal tree of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)." Then Amīr al-mu’minīn said: "They argued with the tree but spoiled the fruits."
And from his words (peace be upon him): When he appointed Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr [as governor of] Egypt, he was overpowered and killed.

I had intended to appoint Hāshim ibn ‘Utbah as governor of Egypt, and had I done so, he would not have left the field open for them, nor allowed them the opportunity (to capture him). This is without reproach to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, for he was dear to me and I had brought him up.
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the censure of his companions Amir al-mu'minin said: He censured his companions for their lack of retention and abundance of forgetfulness

How long shall I accord you consideration that is accorded to camels with hollow humps, or to worn clothes! Whenever they are stitched on one side, they give way on the other, Whenever a vanguard force of Syria hovers over you, everyone of you shuts his door, And hides himself like the lizard in its hole, or the badger in its den.

By Allāh, he whom people like you support must suffer disgrace, and he who throws arrows with your support is as if he throws arrows that are broken both at head and tail. By Allāh, within the courtyard you are quite numerous but under the Banner you are only a few. Certainly, I know what can improve you and how your crookedness can be straightened. But I shall not improve your condition by marring myself. Allāh may disgrace your faces and destroy you. You do not understand the right as you understand the wrong and do not crush the wrong as you crush the right.
He (peace be upon him) said on the morning of the day when he was struck
As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: “al-awad” means crookedness and “al-ladad” means enmity, and this is the most eloquent expression.
And from his words (peace be upon him) in the condemnation of the people of Iraq [And in it he rebukes them for abandoning fighting, while victory is about to be achieved, then their denying him.]

Now then. O people of Iraq! You are like the pregnant woman who, on completion of the period of pregnancy delivers a dead child and her husband is also dead and her period of widowhood is long while only remote relation inherits her. By Allāh, I did not come to you of my own accord. I came to you by force of circumstances. I have come to know that you say ‘Alī speaks lie? May Allāh fight you! Against whom do I speak lie? Whether against Allāh? But I am the first to have believed in him. Whether against His Prophet? But I am the first who testified to him! Certainly not. By Allāh it was a way of expression which failed to appreciate, and you were not capable of it. Woe to you. I am giving out these measures of nice expression free of any cost. I wish there were vessels good enough to hold them. “Certainly, you will understand it after some time.”

And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he taught the people the invocation of divine blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). [And in it is an explanation of the attributes of God, exalted He is, and the attribute of the Prophet, and supplication for him.]
O Allah, the Spreader of the surfaces (of earth), and Keeper (intact) of all skies, Creator of hearts on their good and evil nature.

The Description of the Prophet Send Thy choicest blessings and growing favours on Muḥammad Thy servant and Thy Prophet who is the last of those who preceded (him) and an opener for what is closed, proclaimer of truth with truth, repulser of the forces of wrong and crusher of the onslaughts of misguidance. As he was burdened (with responsibility of prophethood) so he bore it standing by Thy commands, advancing towards Thy will, without shrinking of steps or weakness of determination, listening to Thy revelation, preserving Thy testament, proceeding forward in the spreading of Thy commands till he lit fire for its seeker and lighted the path for the groper in the dark. Hearts achieved guidance through him after being ridden with troubles. He introduced clearly guiding signs and shining injunctions. He is Thy trusted trustee, the treasurer of Thy treasured knowledge, Thy witness on the Day of Judgement, Thy envoy of truth and Thy Messenger towards the people.

O Allah, make a wide place for him in Your shade, and reward him with multiplied goodness from Your bounty. O Allah, elevate his structure above the structures of the builders, and honor his station with You, and perfect his light for him, and reward him for Your sending him with accepted testimony, pleasing speech, possessing just eloquence, and clear-cut oratory. O Allah, unite us and him in the coolness of life, the stability of grace, the fulfillment of desires, the inclinations of pleasures, the ease of comfort, the peak of tranquility, and the gifts of honor.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding the exhortation to righteous action. O People, indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not create you in vain, nor leave you aimlessly, but He intended good for you, and commanded you to do righteous deeds, to reward you for them and grant you the best recompense.

May Allah bless a man who hears a point of wisdom and retains it, when he is invited to the right path he approaches it, he follows a leader (by catching his waist band) and finds salvation, keeps Allah before his eyes and fears his sins, performs actions sincerely and acts virtuously, earns treasure of heavenly rewards, avoids vice, aims at (good) objective and reaps recompense, faces his desires and rejects (fake) hopes, makes endurance the means to his salvation and piety the provision for his death, rides on the path of honour and sticks to the highway of truth, makes good use of his time and hastens towards end and takes with him the provision of (good) actions.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him) And that was when Sa'id ibn al-'As deprived him of his right
The Banu Umayyah are allowing me the inheritance of Muhammad (S) bit by bit. By Allah, if I live I would throw them away as the butcher removes the dust from the dust-covered piece of flesh.
And among his words (peace be upon him) is that he would supplicate with it.
O my Allāh! Forgive me what Thou knowest about me more than I do. If I return (to the sins) Thou return to forgiveness.
O Allah, forgive me what I had promised to myself, but did not find its fulfilment with me.
O Allah, forgive me for what I sought nearness to Thee with my tongue, but my heart opposed and did not perform it.
O Allah, forgive me the winking of the eye, the slips of the tongue, the desires of the heart, and the errors of speech.

And from his words (peace be upon him): When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) died, 'Abbas and Abu Sufyan addressed him regarding that he should pay allegiance to him for the Caliphate (and this was after the allegiance had been completed for Abu Bakr in Al-Saqifah, and therein he forbids fitnah and clarifies his character and knowledge):

O People! Steer clear through the waves of mischief by boats of deliverance, turn away from the path of dissension and put off the crowns of pride. Prosperous is one who rises with wings (i.e. when he has power) or else he remains peaceful and others enjoy ease. It (i.e. the aspiration for Caliphate) is like turbid water or like a morsel that would suffocate the person who swallows it. One who plucks fruits before ripening is like one who cultivated in another’s field.

If I speak, they will say: He is greedy for power, and if I remain silent, they will say: He is grieving from death! Far off is that, after the ups and downs! By Allah, the son of Abu Talib is more familiar with death than an infant with the breast of its mother, Rather, I have merged with the hidden reservoir of knowledge; if I were to disclose it, you would tremble with the trembling of the ropes in deep wells!
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), after he had finished the Battle of Jamal, regarding the censure of women by explaining their deficiency.
