O ye peoples! Women are deficient in faith, deficient in shares and deficient in intelligence. As regards the deficiency in their faith, it is their abstention from prayers and fasting during their menstrual period. As regards deficiency in their intelligence it is because the evidence of two women is equal to that of one man. As for the deficiency of their shares that is because of their share in inheritance being half of men. So beware of the evils of women. Be on your guard even from those of them who are (reportedly) good. Do not obey them even in good things so that they may not attract you to evils.
And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding asceticism. Asceticism is not in much fasting and prayer, but rather asceticism is in the hearts of people.

O people! Abstinence is to shorten desires, to thank for bounties and to keep off prohibitions. If this is possible then (at least) the prohibitions should not overpower your patience; and do not forget gratitude when receiving blessings For Allāh has exhausted the excuses before you through clear, shining arguments and open, bright books.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which are eight attributes from the attributes of Majesty.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He is One, there is no partner with Him: He is the First, such that nothing was before Him, and the Last, such that there is no limit for Him, Imagination cannot catch any of His qualities, and hearts cannot entertain belief about His nature, Analysis and division cannot be applied to Him, and eyes and hearts cannot encompass Him.

A part of the same sermon: Take lesson from useful items of instruction, be cautioned by shining indications, be warned by effective warnings, and benefit from remembrance and preaching. It is as though the claws of death have clung to you, the ties of hope have been cut from you, terrifying affairs have befallen you, and the march is towards the place where everyone has to go. (And with every person there is a driver and a witness) A driver drives her towards her gathering (resurrection); and a witness testifies against her about her deeds.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which is an explanation of the attributes of the Truth, may His majesty be glorified, then an exhortation of the people to piety and consultation.
Allāh knows hidden matters and is aware of inner feelings. He encompasses everything. He has control over everything and power over everything.

The exhortation to the people So let the worker among you work during his days of respite, before the exhaustion of his term, and in his leisure before the time of his busyness, and in his breathing space before he is seized by suffocation, and let him prepare for himself and his journey, and let him take provision from his place of departure for his place of stay.

So remember Allah, O people, regarding what He has entrusted to you from His Book, and what He has deposited with you from His rights, for indeed Allah, Exalted is He, did not create you in vain, nor leave you aimless, nor leave you in ignorance and blindness, He has named your traces, known your deeds, and recorded your terms of life, and sent down to you, "sent down to you the Book as an explanation" (for all things), and made His Prophet live among you for long periods, until He completed for him and for you, from what He sent down of His Book, His religion which He was pleased with for Himself, and conveyed to you through his tongue what He loves of deeds and what He dislikes, His prohibitions and His commands, so He presented to you the excuse, established the proof against you, put forward to you the warning, and alerted you before the face of severe punishment.

So make up for the remainder of your days, and let yourselves practice endurance in them, for they are few compared to the many days during which you were heedless and preoccupied away from admonition; and do not grant yourselves concessions, lest the concessions lead you on the paths of the wrongdoers, and do not be easy-going, lest the yielding push you towards sin.

O creatures of Allah The best adviser for himself is he who is the most obedient to his Lord, and the most deceiving for himself is he who is the most disobedient to his Lord. Deceived is he who deceived his own self. Enviable is he whose faith is safe. Fortunate is he who takes lesson from others, while unfortunate is he who fell victim to his desires and illusions.

And upon you be peace. You should know that even the smallest hypocrisy is like believing in more than one God, and keeping company of people who follow their desires is the key to obliviousness from religion, and is the seat of Satan. Be on your guard against falsehood because it is contrary to Faith. A truthful person is on the height of salvation and dignity, while the liar is on the edge of ignominy and degradation. Do not be jealous because jealousy eats away Faith just as fire eats away dried wood. Do not bear malice because, it is scraper (of virtues). And know that desires make wit forgetful and make memory oblivious. You should falsify desire because it is a deception, and he who has desires is in deceit.

And from his sermon (peace be upon him), which is in explaining the qualities of the God-conscious and the qualities of the dissolute, and drawing attention to the status of the Pure Progeny and the wrong assumption of some people.

O creatures of Allah, the most beloved of Allah's creatures to Him is a servant whom Allah has empowered against his own self, so he immersed himself in grief and donned fear; the lamp of guidance shone in his heart, and he prepared refreshment for the day that will befall him. He regards the distant as near and the difficult as easy; he looks and perceives, he remembers and increases [in good deeds], and he quenches his thirst from sweet, flowing water whose sources were made easy for him. So he drinks to satisfaction and walks a new path, having cast off the garments of desires and freed himself from worries, except for one worry in which he is unique. He has emerged from the quality of blindness and the company of people of whim, and has become one of the keys to the doors of guidance and the locks on the doors of ruin.

He has seen his way, and walked his path, and known his beacon, and crossed his deep waters. He has held fast to the most secure ties, and from the ropes the strongest, so he is of certainty upon the like of the light of the sun. He has set himself for Allah, the Glorified, in the highest of matters, from dismissing every incoming thought to him, and directing every branch to its root. Lamp of darkness, remover of veils, key to obscurities, remover of complexities, guide in vast deserts. He speaks so he makes understood, and he remains silent so it is safe. He has purified himself for Allah so He purified him; he is from the mines of His faith, and the stakes of His earth.

He has enjoined upon himself justice. The first step of his justice is the rejection of desires from his self; he describes the truth and acts according to it. There is no good which he has not aimed at, nor any likely place (of virtue) which he has not sought. He has given the Book control over his rein, so it is his guide and his leader. He settles where the Book settles and descends where the Book descends.

The Characteristics of the Unfaithful And another is he who calls himself learned but is not so; he has gleaned ignorance from the ignorant and misguidance from the misguided. He has set for the people traps made of ropes of deceit and untrue speech. He has carried the Book according to his own views and bent the truth to his passions. He makes people feel safe from major sins and trivializes serious crimes. He says: 'I pause at doubts,' yet he remains plunged therein; and he says: 'I keep aloof from innovations,' yet he is immersed in them. His form is that of a man, but his heart is that of a beast. He does not know the door of guidance to follow it, nor the door of misguidance to keep aloof from it. So he is the living dead!

About the Descendents (‘Itrah) of the Holy Prophet: “So wither are you going to”? “So wither are you going to”? and “how are you then turned away?” Ensigns (of guidance) are standing, indications (of virtue) are clear, and the minarets (of light) have been fixed. Where are you being taken astray? How are you groping while you have among you the descendents of the Prophet? They are the reins of Right, ensigns of Faith and tongues of truth! According to them the same good position as you accord to the Qur’ān, and come to them (for quenching the thirst of guidance) as the thirsty camels approach the water spring.
And from one of his sermons (peace be upon him), in which is an explanation of the causes that destroy people.

O wonder! And why should I not wonder at the error of these groups, given the difference in their proofs within their religion! They do not follow the trace of a Prophet, nor do they imitate the action of a Vicegerent, nor do they believe in the unseen, nor do they refrain from fault. They act amidst doubts, and they walk in passions, Good is what they recognize, and evil is what they reject, Their refuge in difficulties is themselves, and their reliance in ambiguous matters is on their own opinions, As if every one of them is the Imam of himself, who has taken from it what he sees as reliable proofs and firm reasons.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) concerning the Greatest Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam's conveyance of it from him.

He was sent at a time of hiatus among the Prophets, and a long slumber among the nations, and a concentration of trials, and a spread of affairs, and a blazing of wars, and the world was devoid of light, full of deceit, at a time when its leaves had turned yellow, hope had faded from its fruit, and its water had gone underground, the signs of guidance had faded, and the signs of destruction had appeared, so it was stern to its people, frowning in the face of its seeker, its fruit was trial, its food was carcasses, its banner was fear, and its covering was the sword.

So take lesson O creatures of Allāh and recall that (evil doing) with which your fathers and brothers are entangled, and for which they have to account. By my life, your time is not much behind theirs, nor have long periods or centuries lapsed between you and them, nor are you much distant from when you were in their loins.

By Allah, whatever the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told them, I am here telling you the same today. And what you hear today is not different from what they heard yesterday. And the eyes that were opened for them and the hearts that were made for them at that time, just the same have been given to you at this time.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), it encompasses the antiquity of the Creator and the greatness of His creations, and he concludes it with exhortation.

Praise be to Allah, known without being seen, The Creator without pondering, Who has ever been existing, permanent; since there was no sky with domes, nor curtains with lofty doors, nor gloomy night, nor peaceful ocean, nor mountains with broad pathways, nor curved mountain roads, nor earth of spread floors, nor self-reliant creatures. He is the Originator of creation and their Master. He is the God of the creation and its feeder. The sun and the moon are steadily moving in pursuit of His will. They make every fresh thing old and every distant thing near.

He distributed their sustenance, and has counted their traces and their deeds, and numbered their breaths, and [knows] the darting of their eyes, and whatever their bosoms hide of the inner self, and their place of residence and their deposit in the loins and the wombs, until the limits are reached for them.

He is the One whose punishment on His enemies is harsh despite the extent of His Mercy, and His compassion for His friends is vast despite His harsh punishment. He overpowers one who wants to overcome Him, and destroys one who clashes with Him. He disgraces one who opposes Him and gains sway over one who bears Him hostility. He is sufficient for one who relies on Him. He gives one who asks Him. He repays one who lends to Him. He rewards one who thanks Him.

O creatures of Allah, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and assess yourselves before you are assessed. Breathe before the constriction of the throat, and submit before the harsh driving, and know that whoever is not helped by himself until he has from himself an adviser and a warner, will not have from others a warner or an adviser.
And from his words (peace be upon him): When the people decided to swear allegiance to him after the murder of Uthman,

Leave me and seek someone else. For we are facing a matter which has (several) faces and colours, which neither hearts can stand nor intelligence can accept. Clouds are hovering over the sky, and faces are not discernable. You should know that if I respond to you I would lead you as I know and would not care about whatever one may say or abuse. If you leave me then I am the same as you are. It is possible I would listen to and obey whomever you make in charge of your affairs. I am better for you as a counsellor than as a chief!
And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) In it, he draws attention to the excellence and knowledge of the Commander of the Faithful, and explains the tribulation of the Umayyads.

So now, O people, I have put out the eye of revolt, and no one except me advanced towards it when its gloom was swelling and its madness was intense. Ask me before you miss me, by Allah, who has my life in His hands, if you ask me anything between now and the Day of Judgement or about the group who would guide a hundred people and also misguide a hundred people, I would tell you who is announcing its march, who is driving it in the front and who is driving it at the rear, the stages where its riding animals would stop for rest and the final place of stay, and who among them would be killed and who would die a natural death.

And if I were to be lost to you, and the distressing events would befall you, and the gripping calamities, many of the askers would remain silent, and many of the replied-to would lose courage, and that would be when your war has contracted, and rolled up its sleeve, and the world has become narrow for you with constriction, you would prolong the days of tribulation upon you, until Allah would grant victory to the remaining virtuous among you.

When mischiefs come they confuse (right with wrong) and when they clear away they leave a warning. They cannot be known at the time of approach but are recognized at the time of return. They blow like the blowing of winds, striking some cities and missing others.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him), in which he praises Allah the Exalted, then clarifies the virtue of the Noble Messenger and his Ahl al-Bayt, then admonishes the people.

[Allah the Exalted] Blessed is Allah, He whom the height of aspirations cannot reach and the subtlety of intellects cannot attain Him The First, He who has no limit so that He might be contained within it and no end for Him so that He might cease

[A part of the same sermon about the Prophet] Allāh kept the Prophets in deposit in the best place of deposit and made them stay in the best place of stay. He moved them in succession from distinguished fore-fathers to chaste wombs. Whenever a predecessor from among them died the follower stood up for the cause of the religion of Allāh.

[About the Holy Prophet and his Descendants (‘Itrah)] Until this distinction of Allāh, the Glorified, reached Muḥammad — peace and blessing of Allāh be upon him and his descendants. Allāh brought him out from the most distinguished sources of origin and the most honourable places of planting, namely from the same (lineal) tree from which He brought forth other Prophets and from which He selected His trustees. Muḥammad’s descendants are the best descendants, his kinsmen the best of kin and his lineal tree the best of trees. It grew in esteem and rose in distinction. It has tall branches and unapproachable fruits.

He is the Imam of those who fear (Allah), and the clear-sighted guide of those who seek guidance. He is a lamp whose light shines, a meteor whose radiance beams, and a flint whose spark flashes. His conduct is uprightness, his tradition is guidance, his speech is decisive, and his judgment is justice. Allah sent him during an interval of the Prophets, a lapse in action, and ignorance among the leaders.

The exhortation to the people Act, may Allah have mercy on you, upon clear signs, for the path is a straight way that leads to the House of Peace, and you are in a place of seeking favor, with leisure and ease. The books are spread open, the pens are flowing, the bodies are healthy, the tongues are free, repentance is accepted, and deeds are accepted.
And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) in which he establishes the virtue of the noble Messenger.

He was sent while the people were astray in perplexity, and moving here and there in mischief. Desires had deflected them and self-conceit had swerved them. Extreme ignorance had made them foolish: Confounded by the unsteadiness of matters and the evils of ignorance, Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did his best in giving them sincere advice, himself trod on the right path and called (them) towards wisdom and good counsel.
And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding Allah and regarding the Most Honorable Messenger.

Praise be to Allah the First, so there is nothing before Him, and the Last, so there is nothing after Him, and the Manifest, so there is nothing above Him, and the Hidden, so there is nothing below Him.

[A part of the same sermon about the Holy Prophet] His place of stay is the best of all places, and his origin the noblest of all origins in the mines of honour and the cradles of safety. Hearts of virtuous persons have been inclined towards him and the reins of eyes have been turned towards him. Through him Allah buried mutual rancour and put off the flames of revolt. Through him He gave them affection like brothers and separated those who were together (through unbelief). Through him He gave honour to the low and degraded honour (of unbelief). His speaking is clear and his silence is (indicative) like tongue.
And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning his companions and the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Although Allah gives time to the oppressor, His catch would not spare him. He watches him on the passage of his way and the position of that which suffocates the throats. By Allah in Whose power my life lies, these people (Mu‘āwiyah and his men) will overcome you not because they have a better right than you but because of their hastening towards the wrong with their leader and your slowness about my right (to be followed). People are afraid of the oppression of their rulers while I fear the oppression of my subjects.

The nations have become fearing the oppression of their shepherds (rulers), and I have become fearing the oppression of my subjects. I called you to jihad but you did not respond, and I made you hear but you did not listen, and I invited you secretly and openly but you did not answer, and I gave you sincere counsel but you did not accept it. Present like the absent, and slaves like masters! I recite wisdom before you but you turn away from it, and I advise you with profound advice but you disperse from it, and I urge you to jihad against the people of revolt, but before I finish the end of my speech, I see you dispersing like the sons of Saba, You return to your places, and deceive one another regarding your counsel. I straighten you in the morning, and you return to me in the evening as curved as the back of a bow. The straightener has become weary, and those to be straightened have become incorrigible.

O those whose bodies are present, whose wits are absent, whose desires are scattered, whose rulers are on trial, Your leader obeys Allāh but you disobey him, while the leader of the people of Syria disobeys Allāh but they obey him. By Allāh, I wish Mu‘āwiyah exchanges with me like Dinars with Dirhams, so that he takes from me ten of you and gives me one from them!

O people of Kūfah I have experienced in you three things and two others: deaf with ears, dumb with speech, and blind with sight, neither true supporters in combat nor dependable brothers in distress! Your hands may be soiled with earth. O examples of those camels whose herdsman has disappeared! if they are collected together from one side they disperse from the other. By Allāh, I see you in my imagination that if war becomes intense and action is in full swing you would run away from the son of Abī Ṭālib like the woman who becomes naked in the front. I am certainly on clear guidance from my Lord (Allāh) and on the path of my Prophet and I am on the right path which I adhere to regularly.

[About the Companions of the Holy Prophet] Look at the people of the Prophet’s family. Adhere to their direction. Follow their footsteps because they would never let you out of guidance, and never throw you into destruction. If they sit down, you sit down, and if they rise up you rise up. Do not go ahead of them, as you would thereby go astray and do not lag behind of them as you would thereby be ruined.

I have seen the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so I do not see anyone among you resembling them! They would begin the day with disheveled hair and dust-covered faces, having spent the night in prostration and standing (in prayer). They would alternate between their foreheads and their cheeks, and stand firm on the coals from the remembrance of their return (to God)! It was as if between their eyes were the knees of goats due to the length of their prostration! When Allah was mentioned, their eyes would flow with tears until they soaked their shirt collars, and they would sway as trees sway on the day of a stormy wind, out of fear of punishment and hope for reward!
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), in which he points to the oppression of the Banu Umayya.

By Allah, they would continue [in this state] until there would be left no unlawful act before Allah but they would make it lawful, and no pledge but they would break it, until there would remain no house of bricks or woolen tent but their oppression would enter it, and their bad dealings would make them wretched, till two groups of crying complainants would rise, one would cry for his religion and the other for this world, and the help of one of you to one of them would be like the help of a slave to his master, namely when he is present he obeys him, but when the master is away he backbites him. The highest among you in distress would be he who bears best belief about Allah. If Allah grants you safety accept it, and if you are put in trouble endure it, because surely “(good) result is for the God-fearing.”

And from his sermon (peace be upon him) regarding abstinence from the world The world is a dwelling of trial and affliction, a dwelling of separation and transience, a dwelling of worry and grief, a dwelling of toil and dampness, a dwelling of perishing and passing away, a dwelling of defect and trial, a dwelling of change and alteration, a dwelling of fluctuation and reversal, a dwelling of transformation and shifting, a dwelling of modification and substitution, a dwelling of annihilation and perishing, a dwelling of passing away and perishing.
We praise Him for what has happened, and seek His succour in our affairs for what is yet to happen, and we beg Him for safety in the debts, just as we beg Him for safety in our bodies.

I advise you, O creatures of Allah, to detach from this world. Which is leaving you even if you do not like its departure, and aging your bodies even if you like to renew them, For your example and its example is like a journey where they traveled a path as if they had crossed it, and aimed at a landmark as if they had reached it, How short is the distance for the runner to the goal to run towards it until he reaches it! And how short is the stay of one who has a day he cannot exceed, while a swift driver is driving him in this world until he departs from it!

So do not compete for the honor and pride of the world, and do not be amazed by its adornment and bliss, nor grieve over its hardships and misery, for its honor and pride will come to an end, its adornment and bliss will perish, and its hardships and misery will cease. and every period within it has an end, and every living being in it is destined to die. Is there not a warning for you in the traces of the predecessors, and an insight and lesson in your forefathers, if you use your intellect? Do you not see that those who passed away from you do not return, and the remaining successors do not remain forever?

Do you not observe the people of the world pass mornings and evenings in different conditions? Thus, (somewhere) the dead is wept for, someone is being condoled, someone is prostrate in distress, someone is enquiring about sick, someone is passing his last breath, some-one is hankering after the world while death is looking for him, someone is forgetful but he is not forgotten (by death), and on the footsteps of the predecessors walk the survivors.

Beware! So remember the destroyer of joys, the spoiler of pleasures, and the severer of hopes, at the time of deliberating for evil deeds, and seek Allah's assistance in fulfilling His obligatory right, and for (thanking Him) for His countless bounties and favors.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to the people of Kufah at the time of his march from Medina to Basrah
From the servant of Allah, Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, to the people of Kufah, who are the forefront of the Ansar and the crest of the Arabs.

And know that the abode of migration (Medina) has been vacated by its residents and they have abandoned it. It is boiling like a huge cooking pot and rebellion is fixed on its axis moving with full force. So, hasten towards your amīr (commander) and proceed forward to fight your enemy, if so wills Allāh to Whom belongs Might and Majesty.
And from a letter from him (peace be upon him) to him also.

Therefore, keep off from this affair, take heed of the accounting (on the Day of Judgement), get ready for death that will soon overtake you and do not give your ears to those who have gone astray. If you do not do so I shall recall to you whatever you have forgotten, because you are a man living in ease and luxury. Satan has taken you in his clutches, has secured his wishes in you and has taken complete control of you like your soul and blood.

O Mu'awiya, when were you all protectors of the ruled and guardians of the affairs of the people? Without any forward step or conspicuous distinction? We seek Allah's protection against the befalling of previous misfortunes, and I warn you lest you continue being deceived by desires and your appearance becomes different from your innerself.
You have called me to war, so leave the people to one side and come out to me, and spare both parties from fighting, so that it may be known which of us has a rusted heart and covered eyes!

I am Abu al-Hasan, the one who killed your grandfather, your uncle, and your brother by cutting them to pieces on the day of Badr. That sword is with me, and with that heart I meet my enemy. I have not changed the religion, nor introduced a new prophet, and indeed I am upon the path which you left willingly and entered into reluctantly.

You claim that you have come seeking to avenge the blood of 'Uthman, and you certainly know where the blood of 'Uthman was shed; so seek it from there, if you are a seeker, it is as though I have seen you crying out from war when it bites you, like the crying of camels under heavy loads, and it is as though I see your party calling me in anxiety from the incessant striking [of swords], the occurrence of death, and falling bodies after falling bodies, to the Book of Allah, while they are either disbelievers, deniers [of truth], or those who broke their allegiance after swearing it.
And from his instructions (peace be upon him), he instructed a contingent that he sent to the enemy.

When you encamp against the enemy or he encamps against you, let your camp be on the approaches of the high ground, or on the edges of the mountains, or along the rivers, so that it may serve you as a help and a place to return to. And your fighting should be from one side or two sides. Place watchers on the peaks of the mountains and the raised sides of the high ground, so that the enemy may not approach you from any place, whether of danger or safety.

And with you be tranquility and dignity, for they are from the character of the Imams (peace be upon them). And with you be tranquility and dignity, for they are from the character of the Imams (peace be upon them).
And from his instruction to him (peace be upon him) for Ma'qil ibn Qays al-Riyahi when he dispatched him to Syria at the head of a vanguard of three thousand.

Fear Allah, before Whom attendance is inevitable, and with other than Whom there is no meeting. Do not fight except with those who fight you. Travel in the two cool periods, Let the men have a midday sleep. March easily, and do not travel during the early night, for Allah has made it for resting, and has ordained it for staying, not for journeying. Therefore, give rest to your body in the night, and let your carrier-beasts also rest. When you are sure that morning has appeared and when dawn has dawned, commence your journey with Allah’s blessings.

So when you meet the enemy, stand in the midst of your comrades, do not draw near to the people with the nearness of one who wants to ignite the war, nor keep too far from them with the distance of one who fears the combat, until my command comes to you, and let not their hatred drive you to fight them, before inviting them and presenting your excuses to them.
And from his testament (peace be upon him) to his army before the encounter with the enemy at Siffin.
Do not fight them unless they initiate the fighting, because, by the grace of Allāh, you are in the right and to leave them till they begin fighting will be another point from your side against them.

If, by the will of Allah, the defeat occurs then do not kill the runner away, do not strike a helpless person, do not finish off the wounded, and do not inflict pain on women even though they may attack your honour with filthy words and abuse your officers, because they are weak in character, mind and intelligence, We have been ordered to desist from them although they may be unbelievers. Even in pre-Islamic period if a man struck a woman with a stone or a stick he was rebuked along with his posteriors after him.
And he (peace be upon him) used to say when he faced the enemy in battle:
O Allah hearts are drawn to You, necks are stretched, eyes are fixed, steps are in motion, and bodies have turned lean.
O' my Allah! hidden animosity has become manifest and the pots of malice are boiling.
O Allah we complain to You of the absence of our Prophet, the numerousness of our enemy and the diffusion of our passions.
Invocation when he faced the enemy Our Lord! Decide between us and between our people with truth, and You are the Best of Deciders.

Let not the retreat after which a return is intended press heavily upon you, nor the withdrawal after which an attack is in view; And give the swords their due rights, And prepare for the flanks their places of falling (of the enemy); And accustom yourselves to thrusting with a strong thrust, And striking with a heavy strike, And quiet the voices, for that is more consistent with preventing cowardice.

By Him Who broke open the seed (for growing) and created living beings, they had not accepted Islam but they had secured safety (by verbally professing it) and had hidden their misbelief. Consequently when they found helpers for their misbelief they disclosed it.
From a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Mu'awiya, in reply to a letter from him to him.
As for your demand to me to (hand over) Syria, I cannot give you today what I denied you yesterday.
As for your saying: 'War has consumed the Arabs, leaving only the core of their souls.' Know that he whom Right has consumed goes to Paradise, and he whom Falsehood has consumed goes to Hell.

As for our equality in (the art of) war and in (numbers of) men, certainly you cannot be more penetrating in doubtfulness (of belief) than I am in certainty (of belief), and the people of Syria are not more greedy for this world than the people of Iraq are for the next world.

As for your saying: 'We are both sons of 'Abd Manaf,' it is so, we are. But Umayyah is not like Hashim, nor Harb like 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor Abu Sufyan like Abu Talib. Nor the immigrant (Mu'awiya) is like the one set free (Zubayr), nor the pure (by lineage) like the adopted (by status), nor the pursuer of truth like the adherent to wrong, nor the believer like the hypocrite. And how bad a successor is one who follows predecessors who have fallen in the fire of Hell.

Besides that, we also have the distinction of prophethood among us, by virtue of which we subdued the strong and raised up the down-trodden. When Allāh made Arabia enter (the fold of) His religion, and the people submitted to it willingly or unwillingly, you were among those who entered the religion either from greed or from fear, at a time when those who had gone first had preceded and the first muhājirūn had acquired their (peculiar) distinction.
So do not allow Satan to have a share in you, nor a way to dominate over your self; and peace.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to 'Abdullah ibn al-Abbas, while he was his governor over Basra.
You should know that Basrah is the place where Satan descends and the source of trials. So deal with its people with goodness, and untie the knot of fear from their hearts.

I have come to know of your strictness with Banū Tamīm and your harshness over them, And indeed, Banū Tamīm are such that if one star sets, another rises for them, And they were never exceeded in the art of war in pre-Islamic times or after Islam, And they have a special kinship with us and a particular relationship, We shall be rewarded if we pay heed to the kinship and be deemed sinful if we disregard it.

So restrain yourself, Abu al-Abbas, may Allah have mercy on you, in whatever passes through your tongue and hand of good and evil! For we are partners in that, and be in accordance with my good opinion of you, and let my opinion of you not be proven wrong; and peace.
To one of his officers.

Now, for the cultivators of your city have complained of your strictness, hard-heartedness, humiliating treatment and harshness. I thought over it and found that since they are unbelievers they cannot be brought near nor kept away or treated severely because of the pledge with them. Behave with them in between strictness and softness and adopt for them a mingling of remoteness and aloofness with nearness and closeness if Allāh so wills.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to them after the conquest of Basra.

May Allah reward you, people of Egypt, on behalf of a member of your Prophet's family, with the best reward that He gives to those who work in obedience to Him, and to those who are grateful for His blessings, for indeed you heard (me) and obeyed, and when you were called you responded.

And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Ziyad ibn Abi, when Abdullah ibn al-Abbas was the governor of Basra, and Abdullah was the deputy of the Commander of the Faithful at that time over it, and over the suburbs of Ahwaz, Fars, and Kerman (and others).

And I swear by Allah with a true oath, if it reaches me that you have been dishonest with a small or large portion of the spoils (fay') of the Muslims, I will surely inflict upon you a severe punishment that will leave you with little strength, heavy-backed, and diminished in authority; and peace.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to him also.
So give up lavishness and be moderate, and remember in the day the tomorrow, and hold back from the wealth according to your need, and send forward the surplus for the day of your need.

Do you expect that Allah may give you the reward of the humble while you yourself remain vain in His view? And do you covet that He may give you the reward of those practising charity while you enjoy comforts and deny them to the weak and the widows? Certainly, a man is awarded according as he acts and meets what he has sent forward; and that is an end to the matter.

And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Abdullah ibn al-Abbas, and Ibn Abbas used to say, 'I did not benefit from any speech after the speech of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) more than I benefited from this speech.'

Now then, for a man may be pleased by securing what he was not going to miss at all, and displeased by missing what he would not in any case get, so let your pleasure be in what you have secured of your Hereafter, and let your grief be for what has escaped you from it, and what you have secured from your worldly life, do not rejoice much over it, and what has escaped you from it, do not grieve excessively over it. Let your concern be for what is after death.
And from his sayings (peace be upon him), he said shortly before his death, in the manner of a will, when Ibn Muljam struck him, may Allah curse him.

My will/enjoin upon you: That you do not associate anything with Allah, and Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so do not neglect his sunnah, Establish these two pillars, and light these two lamps You will then be free from evil/blame.

By Allah, no sudden death came upon me that I disliked, nor an event I rejected, and I was but like a traveler who reached (his destination), and a seeker who found (his aim), And whatever is with Allah is the best for the righteous ones.

As-Sayyid ar-Radi (may Allah be pleased with him) says: I say: And a part of this speech has already passed in what preceded from the sermons, except that there is here an addition which necessitated its repetition.
And from his will (peace be upon him), he used to write it to whoever he appointed over the charities.

(As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says:) We have recorded a few portions here so that it may be known that he (peace be upon him) was establishing the pillar of truth and legislating examples of justice, in small matters and large, subtle and significant:

Move on with the fear of Allah Who is One and has no partner. Do not frighten any Muslim. Do not pass over his lands so as to make him feel unhappy. Do not take from him more than Allah’s share in his property. When you go to a tribe, you should get down at their watering place instead of entering their houses. Then proceed towards them with peace and dignity till you stand among them. Then salute them, and do not be remiss in greeting them, then say to them, “O’ servants of Allah, the vicegerent of Allah and His caliph has sent me to you to collect from you Allah’s share in your properties. Is there anything of His share in your properties? If so, give it to His vicegerent.”

If someone among them says 'No', then do not repeat the demand. If someone speaks to you in the affirmative, then go with him without frightening him, threatening him, pressuring him or oppressing him. Take what he gives you such as gold or silver (coins). If he has cattle or camels do not enter upon them save with his permission, because their major part is his. Therefore, when you get there do not enter upon them like one who has full control over them or in a violent manner. Do not scare any animal, do not tease anyone and do not let the owner feel grieved about anyone.

Divide the property into two parts Then let the owner choose one. When he has chosen do not object to it. Then divide the remaining into two parts And let him choose one and when he has chosen do not raise any objection. Continue like this till only that much remains which is enough to satisfy Allah’s dues. Then take Allah’s due from it. If he disputes your action allow his views, then mix the two (separated) parts and repeat what you had done before till you take Allah’s due from his property.

Do not take an old, decrepit, broken-limbed, sick or unsound animal. Do not entrust the animals (for custody) except to one whom you trust to take care of Muslims’ property till he hands it over to their chief who will distribute it. Do not entrust it to anyone except he who is a well wisher, God-fearing, trustworthy and watchful, and who is not harsh on Muslims’ property, nor makes them run too much, nor tires them, nor labours them. Then send to us all that you have collected and we shall deal with it as Allāh has ordered.

When your trustee takes over (the animal), instruct him: He should not separate the she-camel from its young and should not milk all its milk because that would affect its young, and also that he should not exert it in riding. In this matter, he should behave justly between it and all its companions. He should allow rest to camels (who are tired), and drive with ease those whose hoofs have been rubbed off. When you pass a water spring stay the camels there for drinking and do not take them away from vegetated land to barren paths. He should allow them rest now and then, and give them time near water and grass. In this way, when they reach us by leave of Allāh, they will be fat with plenty of marrow and would not be fatigued or distressed. We will then distribute them according to the (commands of) the Book of Allāh and the sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny). Certainly, this will be a great source of reward for you and a means to secure guidance, if Allāh so wills.
And from his testament (peace be upon him) to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), when he appointed him as the Governor of Egypt.

So lower for them your wing (of humility), and soften for them your side, and spread out for them your face (with a smile), and make equal among them in the glance and the look, so that the great do not hope for injustice to them (partiality), and the weak do not despair of your justice towards them. For indeed Allah, the Exalted, will question you, O community of His servants, about the small of your actions and the large, and the apparent and the concealed, if He punishes, then you are more oppressive, and if He pardons, then He is the Most Generous.

And upon you be peace. Know, O servants of Allah, that the God-fearing have taken both the immediate [joys] of this world and the enduring [rewards] of the Hereafter, so they shared with the people of this world in their worldly matters, while the people of this world did not share with them in their Hereafter. They dwelled in the world in the best manner in which it was dwelled, and consumed it in the best manner in which it was consumed, so they obtained from the world what the opulent obtained, and took from it what the haughty tyrants took, then they turned away from it with sufficient provision and a profitable trade. They tasted the pleasure of renouncing the world while in this world, and they became certain that they would be neighbors of Allah tomorrow in their Hereafter, their supplication will not be repelled, nor will their share of pleasure be diminished.

You are being chased by death. If you stop, it will catch you, and if you run away from it, it will grip you. It is more attached to you than your shadow. Death is tied to your fore-locks while the world is being wrapped up from behind you. Therefore, fear the Fire whose hollow is deep, whose flames are severe and whose punishment is novel. It is a place wherein there is no mercy. No call is heard in it. No pain is healed in it.

If you are able to have your fear of Allah intensify, and your good opinion of Him be refined, then combine the two, for the servant's good opinion of his Lord is only to the extent of his fear of his Lord, and indeed the people who have the best opinion of Allah are those who fear Him the most.

Pray the prayer at its appointed time, and do not hasten its time for the sake of leisure, nor delay it from its time due to preoccupation, and know that every act of yours is dependent on your prayer.

A part of the same : The leader of guidance and the leader of destruction cannot be equal, nor the friend of the Prophet and the enemy of the Prophet. The Messenger of Allāh (S) has told me that: “In respect of my people I am afraid neither of a believer nor of an unbeliever. As for the believer Allāh will afford him protection because of his belief and as for the unbeliever, Allāh will humiliate him because of his unbelief. But I am afraid about everyone of you who is a hypocrite in his heart and learned of speech. He speaks what you hold good but does what you dislike.”
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Mu'awiya, in reply, (The Sharif said:) And it is one of the elegant letters.

Now, your letter has reached me wherein you recall that Allāh chose Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family) for His religion and helped him through those companions who helped him. Strange things about you have remained concealed (by the irony of fate) from us, since you have started telling us of Allāh’s trials for us and His bounties to us through our Prophet. In this matter, you are like the person who carries dates to Hajar, or who challenges his own master to a duel in archery.

O man, why do you not see your own lameness and remain within bounds, and why do not you realize the shortness of your measure and stay back where destiny has placed you. You have no concern with the defeat of the defeated or the victory of the victor. You are wandering in bewilderment and straying from the right path.

Do you not realize? I am not giving you any news, but I am recounting by the bounty of Allah, that a number of people from among the muhajirun and the ansar fell as martyrs in the way of Allah the Exalted, and each of them has a distinction, until when one of our martyrs was killed, he was called the Chief of the Martyrs, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) singled him out with seventy takbirs during his funeral prayer!

Do you not see that a number of people had their hands cut off in the way of Allah, and that everyone is distinguished (on that account), but when the same thing occurred to one of us he was given the name “the flier in Paradise”; and “the two winged”!

If it were not for what Allah forbade regarding a person praising himself, a narrator would have mentioned numerous virtues, which the hearts of believers know well, and which the ears of listeners do not tire of. So leave aside those whose arrows miss the mark; for we are the handiwork of our Lord, and people after us are the handiwork of us.

Our ancient honour did not prevent us, nor our long-standing superiority over your people, We mixed with you by marriage, we married you and gave our daughters in marriage to you, as equals, although you were not so! And how could you be so when among us is the Prophet and among you is the opposer? Among us is the Lion of Allah and among you is the Lion of the Confederates? Among us are the two masters of the youth of Paradise and among you are the children of Hell? Among us is the choicest of the women of the worlds and among you is the bearer of firewood? In many things that are for us and against you!

Our Islam is well-known, and our pre-Islamic period (greatness) cannot be denied, and the Book of Allah gathers for us what was exceptional/distinguished among us, and it is His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: 'And those of blood relationship are closer [to one another] in the decree of Allah'... and His Exalted saying: 'Verily, the most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believe; and Allah is the Guardian of the faithful.'

Thus, we are superior firstly because of kinship and secondly because of obedience. When at Saqīfah the muhājirūn contended kinship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) against the anṣār, they scored over them. If that success was based on kinship then the right would be ours better than yours. Otherwise, the anṣar’s contention stands.

You claimed that I was jealous of every caliph and revolted against them. If that is so, then the blame is not on you, so the excuse is due to you. "And that is a complaint from which your disgrace is apparent."

You said: I was dragged like a camel with a nose string until I swore allegiance, By the Eternal Allāh, you had intended to revile me but you have praised me, and to humiliate me but have yourself been humiliated! What humiliation does it mean for a Muslim to be the victim of oppression so long as he does not entertain any doubt in his religion, nor any misgiving in his firm belief! This argument of mine is intended for others, but I have stated it to you only in so far as it was appropriate.

I am not going to offer my excuse for reproving him for (some of) his innovations, for if my good counsel and guidance to him was a sin then very often a person who is blamed has no sin and “sometimes the only reward a counseller reaps is suspicion (of evil)”.
And I desired naught but reform what I am able to (do); and my guidance is not but with Allāh; On Him (alone) do I rely, and unto Him (alone) do I turn.

You have mentioned that for me and for my followers you have only the sword, This makes even a weeping person laugh. Did you ever see the descendants of ‘Abd al-Muṭṭalib running away from battle, or being frightened by swords,? “Wait a little till Ḥamal joins the battle” shortly, Then he whom you are seeking will seek you and he whom you think to be far away will approach near you. I am (shortly) speeding towards you with a force of muhājirūn and anṣār and those who follow them in virtue. Their number will be great and their dust will spread all round. They will be wearing their shrouds, their most coveted desire is to meet Allāh. They will be accompanied by the descendants of those who took part in the battle of Badr, and they will have Hāshimite swords whose cut you have already seen in the case of your brother, maternal uncle, your grandfather and your kinsmen. Nor are they far distant from the unjust ones.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him and his family) to Mu'awiya.

Fear Allah regarding what you have amassed and find out your true right therein and turn to understand for what you will not be excused on the grounds of ignorance Certainly, for (following the path of) obedience there are clear signs shining ways straight highways and a fixed aim The shrewd proceed towards them while the mean turn away from them Whoever turns his face from them deviates from the right and gropes in bewilderment Allah takes away His bounty from him and afflicts him with His chastisement

Therefore, beware of yourself, beware of yourself! Allāh has already shown you your way, and the end where your affairs will terminate. You are speeding towards the aim of loss and the position of unbelief. Your ego has pushed you towards evil, thrown you into misguidance, conveyed you to destruction, and created difficulties in your way.
And from his speech (peace be upon him) to Mu'awiya

You have ruined a large group of people, deceived them by your misguidance, and cast them into the waves of your sea, where darkness covers them and doubts toss them about. So they strayed from their direction, turned on their heels, turned their backs, and relied on their nobility, except those who returned from the people of insight; indeed, they parted from you after knowing you, and fled to Allah from your assistance, when you burdened them with hardship and turned them away from the straight path.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Qutham ibn al-Abbas, while he was his governor over Mecca.

Now then, My spy in the West has written to me informing me that some people from the people of Syria have been sent to the Season [of Hajj], who are blind of heart, deaf of hearing, and mute of sight. They seek to dress the truth with falsehood, and obey the created in disobedience to the Creator. They milk the world, extracting its milk through religion, and trade its immediate pleasures for the delayed rewards of the virtuous and God-fearing. No one will achieve success in good except he who acts for it, and no one will be recompensed for the evil except its doer.

Therefore, stand firm in what is in your hands, with the steadfastness of the decisive, the shrewd, the follower of his authority, the obedient to his Imam. And beware of what you may have to excuse yourself from, and do not be arrogant in prosperity, nor weak in adversity; and peace.

Now then, I have come to know of your anger at the posting of al-Ashtar in your place, but I did not do so because of any shortcoming on your part or to get you to increase your efforts, but when I had taken away what was under your authority I would have placed you at a position which would have been less exacting and more attractive to you.

The man whom I appointed as the governor of Egypt, was a man who was sincere to us, and severe and hostile towards our enemies. May Allah have mercy on him! He has indeed completed his days and met his death, while we were pleased with him. May Allah grant him His pleasure, and multiply the reward for him.

Now get ready for your enemy, and act according to your intelligence, and prepare for fighting him who fights you, and call to the path of your Lord, and seek Allah's help exceedingly. If Allah wills, He will suffice you against what worries you, and assist you with what befalls you.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to 'Abdullah ibn al-Abbas after the killing of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr.

Now then, Egypt has been conquered, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, has been martyred. We seek his reward from Allah. He was a son who was a well-wisher, a hard worker, a sharp sword and a bastion of defence. I had roused the people to join him and ordered them to reach him to help before this incident. I called to them secretly as well as openly repeatedly. Some of them came half-heartedly, some put up false excuses and some sat away leaving me.

I ask Allah the Sublime to make for me an early relief from them, for by Allah, had it not been for my hope of meeting my enemy in martyrdom, and my preparing myself for death, I would have loved not to remain with these people for a single day, nor to meet them ever.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to the people of Egypt, when he appointed al-Ashtar as their governor, may Allah have mercy on him.

From the slave of Allah, 'Ali, Commander of the Faithful, to the people who became wrathful for the sake of Allah when He was disobeyed on His earth and His rights were ignored, and oppression had spread its coverings over the virtuous as well as the vicious, on the local as well as the foreigner. Consequently, no good was acted upon nor any evil was avoided.

Now, I have sent to you a man from among the servants of Allāh who allows himself no sleep in days of danger, nor does he shrink from the enemy at critical moments. He is severer on the wicked than a blazing fire. He is Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith, our brother from (the tribe of) Madhḥij.

Therefore, listen to him and obey his command in what accords with the truth, for he is a sword among the swords of Allah, whose edge is not dull and which does not miss its victim. If he orders you to advance, advance, and if he orders you to stay, stay, for he surely neither advances nor retreats, nor delays nor hastens, except by my command. And I have preferred him for you over myself because of his sincerity to you, and the severity of his harshness upon your enemy.

And from his book (peace be upon him) to 'Amr ibn al-'As When you begin a matter, begin with God-consciousness, then with the Sunnah, then with Khums, then with Zakat, then with Salat, then with Sawm, then with Jihad, then with Hajj, then with 'Ilm, then with 'Aql, then with Niyyah, then with Sabr, then with Shukr, then with Rahmah, then with Nafs, then with Dhikr, then with enjoining good and forbidding evil, then with trustworthiness and fulfillment, then with good character and generosity, truthfulness and correctness, then with fear and hope, then with Hijrah and Jihad, then with sincerity and correctness, then with fear and hope, then with good character, generosity, truthfulness, and correctness.

For you have made your religion subservient to the worldly seekings of a man whose misguidance is evident and whose veil has been torn away, He mars an honourable man with his company and befools those who keep his society. You are following in his footsteps and seeking his favours like the dog that follows the lion, clinging to its paws and waiting for whatever remnants of its prey fall down to it. In this way, you have ruined your world as well as the next life! Although if you had stuck to the right, you would have got what you were after. If Allāh grants me power over you and Ibn Abī Sufyān (Mu‘āwiyah), I shall award you both recompense of what you have done, but if you escape and survive then hereafter there is only evil for you both; and that is an end to the matter.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to one of the officers of his army.

If they return to the umbrella of obedience, then this is what we desire. And if matters turn for the people towards discord and disobedience, then advance with those who obey you against those who disobey you. And be content with those who submit with you, making them sufficient over those who lag behind from you. For indeed, the absence of the reluctant one is better than his presence, and his sitting is more sufficient than his rising up.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to one of his officers.
Now, I have come to know such a thing about you that if you have done so then you have displeased your Lord, disobeyed your Imām and betrayed your trust.

I have come to know that you have razed the ground and taken away whatever was under your feet and devoured whatever was in your hands, Send me your account, and know that the accounting to Allah will be severer than that to the people; and that is an end to the matter.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to one of his officers.

Now, I had made you a partner in my trust, and made you my chief man. And for me no other person from my kinsmen was more trustworthy than you in the matter of sympathizing with me, assisting and respecting my trusts. But when you saw that time had attacked your cousin, the enemy had waged war, the trust of the people was being humiliated, and the whole community was trackless and disunited, you turned your back against your cousin and forsook him when others forsook him, you abandoned him when others abandoned him, and you betrayed him when others betrayed him. Thus, you showed no sympathy to your cousin, nor discharged the trust.

It seems as if you do not want (to please) Allāh by your jihād, and as if you do not stand upon a clear sign from your Lord, and as if you have been playing tricks with this ummah (Muslim community) to earn (the pleasure of) this world and watching for the moment of their neglectfulness to usurp their share of the wealth. As soon as it was possible for you to misappropriate the ummah’s trust, you hastened to turn around and attack (them), and made a swift leap to snatch away whatever you could from their property meant for their widows and their orphans as a wolf snatches a wounded and helpless goat. Then, you happily loaded it off to the Ḥijāz without feeling guilty for having appropriated it. Allāh’s woe be to your ill-wishers; it was as though you were sending to your family what you had inherited from your father and mother.
Glory be to Allah! Do you not believe in the Day of judgement, or do you not fear the exaction of account?

O you who were counted among us, how can you enjoy food and drink when you know that you are eating the unlawful and drinking the unlawful. You are purchasing slavemaids and wedding women with the money of the orphans, the poor, the believers and the participants in jihād to whom Allāh had dedicated this money and through whom He had strengthened these cities.

Fear Allah and return to these people their properties for if you do not do so and Allah grants me power over you I shall excuse myself before Allah about you and I shall strike you with my sword with which I did not strike anyone but that he went to Hell

By Allah even if Ḥasan and Ḥusayn had done what you did there would have been no leniency with me for them and they could not have won their way with me till I had recovered from them the right and destroyed the wrong produced by their unjust action.
I swear by Allah, the Lord of all beings, that I would not be pleased to regard their money which you have appropriated as lawful for me, and to leave it to my successors by way of inheritance,

Mind yourself and consider for a while, as though you had reached the end of life and had been buried under the earth. Then your actions will be presented before you in the place where the oppressor cries “Alas” while he who wasted his life yearns for return (to the world), but time was none to escape.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah al-Makhzumi, who was his governor over Bahrain; so he dismissed him and appointed an-Nu'man ibn 'Ajlan al-Zurqi in his place.

Now, I have posted an-Nu'man ibn 'Ajlan az-Zuraqi at Bahrain and have released you from that position without anything bad from you nor reproach on you, because you managed the governorship well and discharged the obligations. Therefore, proceed to me when you are neither suspected nor rebuked, neither blamed nor guilty. I have just intended to proceed towards the recalcitrant of Syria and desired that you should be with me because you are among those on whom I rely in fighting the enemy and erecting the pillars of religion, if Allāh wills.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Masqalah ibn Hubayrah ash-Shaybani, while he was his governor over Ardashir Khurrah.

By Allah Who germinated the seed and created living beings, if this is true you will be humbled in my view and you will become light in weight. Therefore, do not treat lightly the obligations of your Lord and do not reform your world by ruining your religion, since then you will be among losers by the way of (your) actions.
Know that the right of those Muslims who are around you and those who are around me in the distribution of this booty is equal; they come to me regarding it and take from it.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to Ziyad ibn Abih, and it had reached him that Mu'awiya had written to him, wanting to deceive him by attaching him to himself in kinship.

I have learned that Mu'awiya has written to you, to deceive your wit and blunt your sharpness. You should be on guard against him, for he is the Satan who approaches a person from before him and from behind him, and from his right and from his left, to catch him suddenly in the hour of his carelessness and overcome his intelligence.
When Ziyād read the letter, he said, "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, he has testified to it." This remained in his mind until Mu'āwiyah claimed him (as his brother by his father).

As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: His (peace be upon him) word 'al-wāghil' means the man who joins the drinking group so as to drink with them, but he is not one of them. He is therefore constantly turned out and pushed off. As for the words 'an-nawṭu ’l-mudhabdhab', it is a wooden cup or a bowl or the like attached to the saddle of the rider so that it dangles when the rider drives the beast or quickens its pace.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to one of his officers.

Now, you are surely one of those whose help I take in establishing religion and with whose help I break the haughtiness of the sinful and guard critical boundaries. You should seek Allāh’s help in whatever causes you anxiety. Add a little harshness to the mixture of leniency and remain lenient where leniency is more appropriate. Adopt harshness when you cannot do without harshness. Bend your wings (in humbleness) before the subjects. Meet them with your face broad and keep yourself lenient (in behaviour) with them. Treat them equally in looking at them with half eyes or full eyes, in signalling and in greeting so that the great should not expect transgression on your part and the weak should not lose hope in your justice and that is an end to the matter.
And from his will (peace be upon him) to al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), when 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam (may Allah curse him) struck him.

I advise you (both) to fear Allāh and that you should not hanker after the (pleasures of this) world even though it may run after you. Do not be sorry for anything of this world that you have been denied. Speak the truth and act (in expectation) for reward. Be an enemy of the oppressor and helper of the oppressed.

I advise you (both), and all my children and my family, and whoever my letter reaches, to fear Allah, to keep your affairs in order, and to maintain good relations among yourselves. For I have heard your Grandfather (peace be upon him and his family) saying, 'Improvement of mutual differences is better than general prayers and fastings.'
(Fear) Allah, keep Allah in view So do not allow them to starve and they should not be ruined in your presence.
(Fear) Allāh (and) keep Allāh in view because they were the subject of the Prophet’s advice. He went on advising in their favour till we thought he would allow them a share in inheritance.
(Fear) Allāh (and) keep Allāh in view in the matter of the Qur’ān. No one should excel you in acting upon it.
(Fear) Allāh and keep Allāh in view because it is the pillar of your religion.
(Fear) Allah, keep Allah in view Do not forsake it so long as you live because if it is abandoned you will not be spared
(Fear) Allāh (and) keep Allāh in view in the matter of jihād with the help of your property, lives and tongues in the way of Allāh.

You should keep to a respect for kinship and spending for others. Avoid turning away from one another and severing mutual relations. Do not give up bidding for good and forbidding from evil lest the mischievous gain positions over you, and then if you will pray, the prayers will not be granted.

Then he said: O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, certainly I do not wish to see you plunging harshly into the blood of Muslims shouting, 'Amir al-Mu'minin has been killed.' Beware, do not kill on account of me except my killer.

Look, when I die from this stroke of his, then strike him one stroke for his stroke, and do not dismember the man, for I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'Beware of mutilation, even if it is for a rabid dog.'
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him and his family) to Mu'awiya.

Surely, revolt and falsehood abase a man in his religious as well as worldly matters and manifest his shortcomings before his critic. You know that you cannot catch what is destined to remain away from you. Many people had aims other than right (ones) and began to swear by Allāh (that they will attain their goal) but He falsified them. Therefore, fear the Day when happy is he who made his end happy (by good actions) while repentant is he who allowed Satan to lead him and did not resist him.
You called us to the judgement of the Qur'an, although you were not of its people; and we did not respond to you, but we responded to the Qur'an in its judgement; and peace.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays (the Governor of Azerbaijan).

Certainly, your assignment is not a morsel for you, but it is a trust round your neck, and you have been charged with the protection (of the people) on behalf of your superiors. It is not for you to be oppressive towards the ruled, nor to risk yourself save on strong grounds. You have in your hands the funds which are the property of Allāh, to Whom belongs Might and Majesty, and you hold its charge till you pass it on to me. Probably, I will not be one of the bad rulers for you, and that is an end to the matter.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to the officers of the armies.
From the servant of Allāh, ‘Alī, Amīr al-mu’minīn to the Officer-in-charge of garrisons :

Now, it is obligatory on an officer that the distinction he achieves, or the wealth with which he has been exclusively endowed, should not make him change his behaviour towards those under him, and that the riches Allāh has bestowed on him should increase him in nearness to his people and kindness over his brethren.

Beware, that it is obligatory for you on me that I should not keep anything secret from you except during war, nor should I decide any matter without consulting you except the commands of religion, nor should I ignore the fulfillment of any of your rights nor desist till I discharge it fully, and that for me all of you should be equal in rights.
From a letter of him (peace be upon him) to his collectors of the land tax To his collectors of the land tax
From the servant of Allah, Ali, Commander of the Faithful, to the tax collectors:
So now, he who does not fear where he is going, does not send forward for himself that which could protect him.

Be just with the people regarding yourselves, and be patient for their needs, for indeed you are the treasurers of the subjects, and the representatives of the community, and the ambassadors of the Imams,

Do not deny good counsel to yourself, good behaviour to the army, succour to the subjects and strength to the religion of Allāh. Strive in the way of Allāh as is obligatory on you, because Allāh the Glorified, desires us and you to be thankful to Him as best as we can and that we should help Him to the best of our power. And there is no power save with Allāh, the All-high, the All-glorious.

And from his letter (peace be upon him) to the governors of the lands, concerning the meaning of prayer. As for what follows, indeed Allah, the Exalted, did not make anything of His servants closer to Him than prayer, nor anything closer to Allah, Glory and Highness, than prayer. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O Children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your nakedness and as adornment, and the clothing of righteousness - that is best.' So be steadfast in connecting to your Lord, and be maintainers of justice, and fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
Now, say the ẓuhr (noon) prayers with the people when the shade of the wall of the goats’ pen is equal to the wall.
Say the ‘aṣr (afternoon) prayers with them when the sun is still shining in a portion of the day enough for covering the distance of two farsakhs (about six miles).
Say the maghrib (sunset) prayers when he who is fasting ends the fast and the pilgrim rushes (from ‘Arafat) to Minā.
Say the ‘ishā’ (night) prayers with them when twilight disappears and upto one third of the night.
And pray the morning prayer with them, and the man should recognize the face of his companion.
Say the prayers with the people as the weakest of them would do, and do not be a source of trouble to them.
And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to Talha and az-Zubayr (through 'Imran ibn al-Husayn al-Khuzai).
Abū Ja‘far al-Iskāfī has mentioned this in his “Kitāb al-maqāmāt” on the excellent qualities (manāqib) of Amīr al-mu’minīn (peace be upon him).

Now, both of you know, although you conceal it, that I did not approach the people till they approached me, and I did not ask them to swear allegiance to me till they themselves swore allegiance to me, and both of you were among those who approached me and swore me allegiance. Certainly, the common people did not swear me allegiance under any force put on them or for any money given to them. If you two swore allegiance to me obediently, come back and offer repentance to Allāh soon, but if you swore allegiance to me reluctantly, you have certainly given me cause for action, by showing your obedience and concealing your disobedience.

By my life, you were not more entitled than other muhājirūn to conceal and hide the matter. Your refusing allegiance before entering into it would have been easier than getting out of it after having accepted it. You have indicated that I killed ‘Uthmān; then let someone from among the people of Medina who supported neither me nor you decide the matter between me and you. Then one of us shall face (the command of law) according to (their) involvement.
Return, you two sheikhs, from your opinion, for now the greatest of your matters is the disgrace, before the disgrace and the Hellfire are joined together; and peace.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Mu'awiya

Now, for Allāh, the Glorified, has made this world for what is to come hereafter, and put its inhabitants to trial as to which of you is good in action, and we have not been created for this world, nor ordered to strive for it, but we have been made to stay in it to stand trial therein. So, Allāh has tried me with you and tried you with me. He has therefore made either of us a plea for the other. Now, you have leapt on the world by a wrong interpretation of the Qur’ān, and wanted me to account for what neither my hand nor tongue was responsible, but you and the Syrians put the blame on me, and your scholar incited against me the ignorant and one who is sitting incited the one who is standing.

Fear Allah regarding yourself, and struggle against Satan so he does not take the reins of your affairs, and turn your face towards the Hereafter, for it is our path and your path. and beware lest Allah strike you with a sudden affliction from him that touches the root and cuts off the branches, for I swear to you by Allah an oath that is not broken, if destiny brings me and you together, "Until Allah judges between us, and He is the Best of the judges."
And from his instruction to him (peace be upon him): He issued this instruction to Shurayh ibn Hanī when he appointed him at the head of the vanguard contingent to Syria.

Fear Allah every morning and evening and remain apprehensive about yourself of this deceitful world and do not regard it safe in any case Know that if for fear of some evil you do not refrain yourself from things which you love, then passions will fling you into a lot of harm Therefore, be for yourself a refrainer and protector, and for your anger a suppressor and killer
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him and his family) to the people of Kufa at the time of his march from Medina to Basra.
Now, I have come out of my city either as an oppressor or as the oppressed, either as a rebel or one against whom rebellion has been committed.

And I [indeed] remind by the name of Allah whosoever reaches him this letter of mine when he set out for me, if I am doing good, let him help me; and if I am doing wrong, let him try to win me back [to the right].
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him and his family) which he wrote to the people of the provinces describing in it what took place between him and the people of Siffin

And with the correct interpretation is his saying (peace be upon him): 'The beginning of our matter was that we met, and the people were from the people of Syria.' And it is apparent that our Lord is One, and our Prophet is One, and our call in Islam is one, and we do not ask them to add anything to belief in Allah and confirmation of His Messenger, nor do they ask us to add anything; the matter is one. Except for what we differed over regarding the blood of Uthman, while we are free from it.

We suggested to them to appease the situation by calming the temporary irritation and pacifying the people till matters settled down and stabilized when we would gain strength to put matters right. They however said that they would settle it by war.

Thus, they refused until war spread its wings and came to stay, Its flames rose and became strong. When the war had bitten us as well as them and pierced its talons into us as well as them, they accepted what we had proposed to them. So, we agreed to what they suggested and hastened to meet their request. In this way, the plea became clear to them and no excuse was left to them.

Now, whoever among them adheres to this will be saved by Allāh from ruin, and whoever shows obstinacy and insistence (on wrong) is the reverser whose heart has been blinded by Allāh and evils will encircle his head.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to al-Aswad ibn Quṭbah, the governor of Ḥulwān.

Now, if the actions of a governor follow the passions he will be greatly hampered in justice. All the people should be equal in right before you, because injustice cannot be a substitute for justice. Avoid that thing the like of which you would not like for yourself. Exert yourself in what Allāh has made obligatory on you, hoping for His reward and fearing His chastisement.

And know that this world is the place of trial. Whoever here wastes any hour of his time will repent it on the Day of Judgement, and nothing can ever make you free of need of what is right. One of the rights on you is that you should protect yourself (from sins) and look after the subjects to your best. The benefit that will come to you from this will be greater than that which will accrue (to people) through you; and that is an end to the matter.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to Mu'awiya

Verily, those who swore allegiance to Abū Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Umān have sworn allegiance [1] to me on the same basis on which they swore allegiance to them. (On this basis) he who was present has no choice (to consider), and he who was absent has no right to reject; and consultation is confined to the muhājirūn and the anṣār. If they agree on an individual and take him to be Caliph it will be deemed to mean Allāh’s pleasure. If any one keeps away by way of objection or innovation they will return him to the position from where he kept away. If he refuses they will fight him for following a course other than that of the believers and Allāh will put him back from where he had run away.
And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to the officers through whose jurisdiction the army passed.
From the servant of Allah, Ali, Commander of the Faithful, to whoever the army passes by, from the collectors of the tax and the officials of the lands.

Now, I have sent an army that will pass by you, if Allāh wills. I have instructed them about what Allāh has made obligatory on them, namely that they should avoid molestation and avert harm. I hold myself clear before you and those (unbelievers) who are under your protection from any annoyance committed by the army except when one is compelled by hunger and there is no other way of satisfying it. If anyone of them takes anything through force you should punish him. None of you should be foolish enough to obstruct them or intervene in matters which we have allowed them by way of exception.

I am myself within the army. So, refer to me their high-handedness and any hardship which is caused by them and which you cannot avert except through Allāh and through me. I shall then avert it with the help of Allāh, if He so wills.
