He said: “He should wipe it, and wipe his hand on the wall or on the ground, and he should not cut short the salat (prayer).”

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Murādī, who said: I said to Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A man has boils and sores, so his skin and his clothes are filled with blood and pus, and his clothes are in the same condition as his skin. He said: “He prays in his clothes, and there is nothing upon him, and he does not wash them.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūs, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Layth al-Murādī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about one afflicted with nosebleed, whose nose continues bleeding from the sun’s decline until the night passes. He said: “He should gesture with his head at the time of every salat (prayer).” And regarding a man whose bowels have exhausted him, he said: “He should gesture with his head.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb al-Hāshimī, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about cupping: is there wudu (ablution) in it? He said: “No, and he does not wash its place, because the cupper is trusted when he cleans it, so long as he is not a small boy.”

With this chain of transmission, from Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is affected by flowing blood. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and repeats.” He said: “And if it is not flowing, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues from where he left off.” He said: “And that is done between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The meaning of his saying عليه السلام, “he performs wudu (ablution),” is that he washes the place, as we explained previously.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who performed wudu (ablution) and then ate meat or fish: may he perform salat (prayer) without washing his hand? He said: "Yes. But if it was milk, he should not perform salat (prayer) until he washes his hand and rinses his mouth. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform salat (prayer) after eating meat without washing his hand; but if it was milk, he would not perform salat (prayer) until he washed his hand and rinsed his mouth."

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about wudu (ablution) from that which the fire has changed, so he said: “There is no wudu upon you concerning it. Wudu is only from that which exits, not from that which enters.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Is wudu (ablution) to be performed because of food, or drinking milk—the milk of cattle, camels, and sheep—and their urine and their meat? He said: “Wudu (ablution) is not performed because of it.”

Muḥammad ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “One afflicted with overpowering bowel disturbance performs wudu (ablution), then returns to his salat (prayer) and completes what remains.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said: He was asked about the dripping of urine. He said: “He should place a pouch when he performs salat (prayer).”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: When you enter the privy, then say: I seek refuge in Allah from the impure, filthy, wicked, corrupting Satan, the accursed. And when you finish, then say: All praise is for Allah, who has granted me well-being from affliction and removed harm from me.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام: that when he would come out from the privy, he would say: All praise is for Allah, who gave me its pleasure, kept its strength in my body, and removed from me its harm. What a blessing these three are.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he intended to relieve himself, would stand at the door of the place and then turn right and left toward his two angels and say: ‘Move away from me; for you two I owe before Allah that I shall not produce any act until I come out to you both.’”

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from Ismā‘īl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abā Ja‘far عليه السلام say: “Luqmān said to his son: Prolonged sitting at the place of relieving oneself causes hemorrhoids, so this was written on the door of the latrine.”

And from him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about saying tasbīḥ in the place of relieving oneself and reciting the Qur'an. So he said: "No concession was given in the toilet for more than Āyat al-Kursī; and he may praise Allah, or [recite] a verse."

From him, from al-Haytham ibn Masrūq al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and in his house there was a toilet facing the qiblah. I heard him say: “Whoever urinates facing the qiblah, then remembers and turns away from it out of reverence for the qiblah and magnification of it, he will not rise from that seat of his before Allah forgives him.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Saʿdān, from Ḥakam, from a man, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: May a man urinate while he is standing? He said: “Yes, but it is feared that the Shayṭān may become mixed up with him—that is, confound him.” Then I said: May a man urinate in water? He said: “Yes, but it is feared for him from the Shayṭān.”

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Mismaʿ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “It is disliked for a man—or the man is forbidden—to cast his urine from the rooftop into the open air.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both. That he disliked that one enter the privy while having with him a white dirham, unless it is wrapped up.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “When one of you uncovers himself for urination or something else, then let him say: ‘In the Name of Allah,’ for indeed the Shaytan lowers his gaze.”

From him, from Aḥmad, from al-Barqī, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade relieving oneself on the edge of a water well from which sweet water is drawn, or by a river from which water is sought, or beneath a tree bearing its fruit.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: If the state of hadath occurs in the masjid, then there is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) in the masjid.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥannān ibn Sadīr, who said: I heard a man ask Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “Sometimes I urinate and cannot manage to use water, and that becomes difficult for me.” So he said: “When you urinate and wipe yourself, then wipe your private part with your saliva; then if you find something, say: this is from that.” Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, who said: I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام regarding a castrated man who urinates and encounters hardship because of that, and then sees wetness after wetness. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and sprinkles water once during the day.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O company of the Anṣār, indeed Allah has praised you well, so what is it that you do?” They said: “We cleanse ourselves with water.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man's istinja' using a bone, dung, or a stick. He said: "As for the bone and dung, they are the food of the jinn, and that is among the things they stipulated to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله." Then he said: "It is not proper with anything of that."
Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: He used to perform istinja' from urine three times, and from feces with clods of earth and rags.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام would wipe himself after defecation with cotton, and he would not wash.”
Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Istinjāʾ with cold water cuts off hemorrhoids.

Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he performed wudu (ablution), would not allow anyone to pour water for him. So it was said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why do you not let them pour water for you?” He said: “I do not like to make anyone a شریک in my salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the purification of a woman in nifās when she becomes pure, while she is unable to perform istinjāʾ with water, such that if she were to perform istinjāʾ she would become injured. Is there a concession for her to perform wudu (ablution) externally and dry it with cotton or with a cloth? He said: “Yes. Let her cleanse the inside with cotton or with a cloth.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who said: I said to him: What do you say about a ring-stone made from the stones of Zamzam? He said: “There is no harm in it, but when he intends al-istinjāʾ, he should remove it.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you mention the name of Allah during wudu (ablution), your whole body becomes purified; and if you do not mention it, nothing of your body is purified except what the water passes over.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man wants to perform istinja'; how should he sit? He said: "As he sits for defecation." And he said: "He is only required to wash what is outwardly visible of it, and he is not required to wash its interior."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said: Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام urinated while I was standing by his head, and I had with me a small water vessel—or he said: a jug. When the stream of urine stopped, he gestured with his hand, saying, "Like this, to me," so I handed him the water, and he performed wudu (ablution) in that very place.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man urinated and did not have water with him. He said: "He should squeeze the root of his penis to the tip of his penis three squeezes, and shake its tip. Then if something comes out after that, it is not from urine, but rather it is from the passages."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Banu Isra'il used to be such that when a drop of urine struck one of them, they would cut their flesh with scissors. But Allah has granted you vast ease, as vast as what lies between the heaven and the earth, and He has made water a purifier for you, so consider how you will be.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "When the dribble of urine has ceased, then pour the water."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: “If the hadath occurs in the mosque, then there is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) in the mosque.”
From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Rifāʿah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wudu (ablution) in the mosque, and he disliked it when it was due to urination or defecation.

Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: May a woman wash her husband's private part? He said, "Why? Is it due to illness?" I said, "No." He said, "I do not like for a free woman to do that; as for a bondwoman, it does not harm him." He said: I said to him, "May a man perform ghusl in the presence of his family?" He said, "Yes; what he exposes in intimacy is greater."

From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said: I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), then he wiped his face with the lower part of his shirt. Then he said: “O Ismāʿīl, do like this, for indeed this is how I do.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Rubbing with the thumb and the forefinger at the time of wudu (ablution) is siwak."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ibn al-Mughirah, from a man, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: When a man performs wudu (ablution), let him splash his face with water, for if he is drowsy he will be startled and awaken, and if there is cold, he will be startled and not feel the cold. And this report does not contradict.

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Do not strike your faces with water when you perform wudu (ablution), but rather pour the water gently.” Because the way to reconcile the two is that the first report is understood as indicating the permissibility of that, and that its opposite is not obligatory; while the second is understood to mean that something else is preferable. Thus, there is no contradiction between them on this basis.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever mentions the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, over his wudu (ablution), it is as though he has performed ghusl (ritual bath).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: When you mention the Name of Allah during wudu (ablution), your entire body becomes pure; and if you do not mention it, nothing of your body becomes pure except that over which the water has passed.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: A man performed wudu (ablution) and prayed, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Repeat your prayer and your wudu (ablution).” So he did so, and performed wudu (ablution) and prayed. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer.” So he did so, and performed wudu (ablution) and prayed, and he said: “Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer.” Then he went to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and complained of that to him. He said: “Did you name Allah when you performed wudu (ablution)?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then mention the name of Allah over your wudu (ablution).” So he mentioned it, performed wudu (ablution), and prayed, then came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and he did not instruct him to repeat it. Thus, the proper way to understand this report is that the naming in it is to be understood as the intention whose obligatoriness we have already established. As for other uttered phrases besides that, they are only recommended, not obligatory as a prescribed duty. What indicates that is his statement عليه السلام in the first report: “Whoever does not mention the name, only that part of his body over which the water passed becomes purified.” So if it were an obligatory duty, then whoever abandoned it, nothing of his body would become purified in any state, because he would not have become purified.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dāwūd al-ʿIjlī, the mawlā of Abū al-Miʿzā, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “O Abā Muḥammad, whoever performs wudu (ablution) and mentions the name of Allah, Exalted is He, his entire body is purified; and whoever does not mention [His name], nothing of his body is purified except that which the water reaches.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from Sa'dan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “Whoever seeks a need while he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), and it is not fulfilled, then he should blame none but himself.”

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh, from Rifā‘ah, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about one whose hand and foot are amputated: how does he perform wudu (ablution)? He said: “He washes that place from which it was cut.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dyes his head with henna and then wishes to perform wudu (ablution). He said: “He wipes over the henna.”

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated, raising it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding one who dyes his head with henna and then wishes to perform wudu (ablution), he said: “It is not valid until the water reaches the skin of his head.” So the correct way of reconciling the two reports is that if it is possible to convey the water to the skin without hardship, then anything else is not permissible; but if that is not possible, it is permissible for him to wipe over the henna. And that which clarifies what we have said is:

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad, from al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: A man shaves his head, then applies henna to it, and performs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer). He said: “There is no harm in his wiping his head while the henna is upon it.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who is not in a state of wudu (ablution), and rain falls upon him until his head, beard, body, hands, and feet become wet. Does that suffice him for wudu (ablution)? He said: “If he washes with it, then that suffices him.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report does not contradict what we have mentioned regarding the obligation of sequence, because the proper understanding of this report is that when rain falls upon a person and he washes his limbs in the order required by wudu (ablution), then it suffices him. But if he were to limit himself merely to the rain falling upon him, without himself washing his limbs, that would not be permissible.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Indeed Allah is One, and He loves oddness; so three handfuls may suffice you for wudu (ablution): one for the face, and two for the two forearms. And you wipe with the moisture of your right hand your forelock, and with what remains of the moisture of your right hand the top of your right foot, and you wipe with the moisture of your left hand the top of your left foot.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a man performing wudu (ablution): should he pass water through the inner part of his beard? He said: "No."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about one whose hand and foot are amputated. He said: “He washes them both.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whose hand had been cut off from the elbow: how should he perform wudu (ablution)? He said: "He washes whatever remains of his upper arm."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I asked him about wiping over the khuffayn and the turban, so he said: "The Book has preceded the khuffayn," and he said: "Do not wipe over a khuff."

From him, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wiping over the khuffs, So he said: “Do not wipe.” And he said: “Indeed, my grandfather said: The Book has preceded the khuffs.”

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī, from Fuḍayl al-Rassān, from Raqabah ibn Maṣqalah, who said: I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and asked him about some matters. He said: “I see that you are among those who give fatwa in the mosque of al-ʿIrāq.” I said: “Yes.” He said to me: “From whom are you?” I said: “A cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.” He said: “Welcome to you, O cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.” So I said to him: “What do you say regarding wiping over the khuffs?” He said: “ʿUmar used to hold it to be for three days for the traveler and one day and one night for the resident, while my father did not hold it to be valid whether in travel or in residence.” Then when I came out from his presence and stood on the threshold of the door, he said to me: “Come forward, O cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.” So I came toward him, and he said: “Those people used to speak according to their own opinion, so they would err and be correct, while my father did not speak according to his own opinion.”

“Do not wipe over them.” From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, He said: I heard him saying: “ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab gathered the companions of the Prophet عليه السلام, and among them was ʿAli عليه السلام, and he said: ‘What do you say regarding wiping over the khuffs?’ Al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah stood and said: ‘I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم wiping over the khuffs.’ So ʿAli عليه السلام said: ‘Before al-Ma’idah or after it?’ He said: ‘I do not know.’ So ʿAli عليه السلام said: ‘The Book preceded the khuffs. Al-Ma’idah was only revealed two or three months before he was taken.’”

From him, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abī al-Ward, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Abū Ẓabyān narrated to me that he saw ʿAlī عليه السلام pour water and then wipe over the khuffs. So he said: “Abū Ẓabyān lied. Has the statement of ʿAlī عليه السلام not reached you among yourselves: ‘The Book has preceded the khuffs’?” Then I said: Is there any concession in it? He said: “No, except against an enemy from whom you are protecting yourself, or snow such that you fear for your feet.”

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to him: Is there taqiyyah in wiping over the khuffayn? He said: There are three matters in which I do not practice taqiyyah toward anyone: drinking intoxicants, wiping over the khuffayn, and Mutʿat al-Ḥajj. So this does not contradict the first report regarding the permissibility of taqiyyah in it, because it is possible that the intended meaning in this report is what Zurārah said: for he said, and he did not say, 'It is obligatory upon you not to practice taqiyyah in these toward anyone.' It is also possible that what is meant by it is that there is no taqiyyah in it when the fear does not reach the level of alarm for one’s life or property; in that case, slight hardship should be borne and the khuff should be removed.

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a person with a fracture who has splints upon him, or who has a wound—how should he act regarding wudu (ablution), and during ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and during the Friday ghusl (ritual bath)? He عليه السلام said: 'He washes whatever the washing can reach of what is exposed, of that upon which there are no splints; and he leaves whatever is beyond that, which he is unable to wash. He should not remove the splints, nor should he meddle with his wound.'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He was asked about a man who has a sore on his forearm, or something like that, in a place of wudu (ablution), so he binds it with a cloth, performs wudu (ablution), and wipes over it when he performs wudu (ablution). So he said: “If the water harms him, then let him wipe over the cloth; and if the water does not harm him, then let him remove the cloth and then wash it.” He said: And I asked him about a wound—how should one deal with it in washing? He said: “Wash what is around it.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a wound: how should its possessor deal with it? He said: “He washes what is around it.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abd al-A'la, the mawla of Al Sam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: I stumbled and my nail broke off, so I placed a bandage upon my finger. So how should I perform wudu (ablution)? He said: This and what resembles it is known from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah has said: “He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.” Wipe over it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Aba Ibrahim عليه السلام about a person with a broken limb who has splints upon him: how should he perform wudu (ablution), ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday? He عليه السلام said: "He washes whatever he can reach of what is exposed, from that over which there are no splints; and he leaves aside the rest of that which cannot be washed. He should not remove the splints, nor should he tamper with his wound."

From him, from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the junub who has a wound and fears water if it reaches him. He said: “Then he should not wash it if he fears for himself.”

From him, from Faḍālah, from Kulayb al-Asadī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man, when he has a fracture, how he should perform the salat (prayer). He said: "If he fears for himself, then let him wipe over his splints and let him perform salat (prayer)."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about drying oneself with a cloth before it dries, and he said: “There is no problem with it.”

From him, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in a man wiping his face with a cloth when he performs wudu (ablution), if the cloth is clean.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said: May I be your ransom, I wash my face, then I wash my hand, and Shayṭān causes me to doubt that I have not washed my forearm and my hand. He عليه السلام said: “If you find the coolness of the water on your forearm, then do not repeat.”

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Musa ibn Jaʿfar, from Abi Jaʿfar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Luʾluʾi, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Faḍḍal, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام saying: “Everything from your salat and your taharah that has already passed, then you remember it afterward by recollection, let it pass, and there is no repetition upon you regarding it.”

Sa'd, from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about medicine when it is on a man's hand: is it sufficient for him to wipe over the coating of the medicine? He said: “Yes, it is sufficient for him to wipe over it.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Zurārah, who said: I said to him: What do you think about what is beneath the hair? He said: “Everything that the hair encompasses, it is not for the servants to wash it, nor to search into it; rather, water is to be made to flow over it.”

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad and 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', who said: I entered upon al-Rida عليه السلام, and before him was a ewer from which he wanted to prepare himself for salat (prayer). So I came near to pour water for him, but he refused that and said: “Stop, O Hasan.” So I said: Why do you forbid me from pouring it onto your hand? Do you dislike that I should be rewarded? He said: “You would be rewarded, and I would bear a burden.” So I said to him: How is that? He said: “Have you not heard Allah say: “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.” And here I am, when I perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer)—and it is an act of worship—I dislike that anyone should share with me in it.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: “My father performed ghusl from janabah, and it was said to him: A small spot on your back has remained which the water did not reach. So he said to him: What would it have been upon you had you remained silent? Then he wiped that spot with his hand.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He said to his companions: “Indeed, tomorrow you will come to a place in which there is no water, so perform ghusl today for tomorrow.” So we performed ghusl on Thursday for Friday.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from his mother and the mother of Aḥmad ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: We were with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in the desert, and we were heading to Baghdad. So he said to us on Thursday, "Perform ghusl today for tomorrow—Friday—for water there tomorrow will be scarce." So we performed ghusl on Thursday for Friday.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from 'Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام how ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday became obligatory, so he said: Indeed Allah, the Exalted, completed the obligatory salat (prayer) with the supererogatory salat, and He completed the obligatory fasting with the supererogatory fasting, and He completed the obligatory wudu (ablution) with the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday, for whatever may have occurred in that of inadvertence, deficiency, or forgetfulness.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān ibn Muslim, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: The Anṣār used to work with their water-carrying camels and their property. Then, when Friday came, they would come, and the people were bothered by the odors of their armpits and their bodies. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded them to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on Friday, and thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be established by that.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī, from Durust, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered upon ʿĀʾishah while she had placed her water vessel in the sun. He said: “O Ḥumayrāʾ, what is this?” She said: “I am washing my head and body.” He said: “Do not do it again, for it causes leprosy.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating a kind of dislikedness, not prohibition, because there is no harm in using water that has been left in the sun. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned [follows].
Some of our companions narrated to me from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no objection to performing wudu (ablution) with water that is placed in the sun.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Hashimi, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who finds water in a watercourse or a pool, and fears that beasts may have drunk from it. Should he perform ghusl (ritual bath) from it for janabah and make wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer), if he finds no other than it, while the water does not amount to a sa' for janabah nor a mudd for wudu, and it is scattered? What should he do? He said: If his palm is clean, then let him take a handful of water with one hand and sprinkle it behind him, in front of him, to his right, and to his left. Then if he fears that it will not suffice him, he should wash his head three times, then wipe his skin with his hand; for that will suffice him, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: When you perform ghusl from janābah, then say: O Allah, purify my heart, accept my effort, and make what is with You better for me. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent, and make me among those who purify themselves. And when you perform ghusl for Friday, then say: O Allah, purify my heart from every affliction by which my religion is effaced and my deeds are nullified. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent, and make me among those who purify themselves.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who finds semen on his garment, while not knowing that he had experienced a wet dream. He said: “Let him wash whatever he finds on his garment and perform wudu (ablution).”

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him, peace be upon him, about a man who sees semen on his garment after morning has come, and he had not seen in his sleep that he had experienced a wet dream. He said: "Then let him perform ghusl, wash his garment, and repeat his salat." And he narrated this hadith with another wording.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who sleeps and does not see in his sleep that he had a wet dream, then he finds moisture in his garment and on his thigh. Is ghusl obligatory upon him? He said: "Yes." So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because the way to reconcile them is that when a garment that no one else shares with him in using is found to have semen on it, ghusl and the repetition of salat (prayer) are obligatory upon him if he had already prayed, since it is possible that he forgot the wet dream. But as for that in which someone else shares with him, it does not make ghusl obligatory upon him unless he becomes certain of the wet dream.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who had a nocturnal emission, then when he awoke he found only a small amount of moisture. He said: “It is nothing, unless he is ill, for then he becomes weakened; in that case ghusl is obligatory upon him.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had a wet dream, then when morning came he looked at his garment and did not see anything on it. He said: “He may perform salat in it.” I said: Then a man saw in a dream that he had a wet dream, then when he arose he found a small amount of moisture on the tip of his private part. He said: “Ghusl is not upon him. Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: ‘Ghusl is only from the greater fluid.’”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a woman whose shift or waist-wrapper is with her, and it is affected by moisture from the private part while she is in janabah: may she perform salat (prayer) in it? He said: “When she performs ghusl, she may perform salat (prayer) in them both.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, used to leave the yellow trace of perfume on their bodies when they performed ghusl from janabah, and that was because the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, instructed them to pour water thoroughly over their bodies.

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ḥarīz, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Abī Ya‘fūr, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man sees in sleep and feels desire, then he wakes up and looks but finds nothing; then after a short while, it comes out. He said: “If he is ill, then let him perform ghusl (ritual bath), and if he is not ill, then there is nothing upon him.” He said: I said to him: So what is the difference between the two? He said: “Because when a man is healthy, the fluid comes with a strong gush, and if he is ill, it does not come except afterward.”

From him, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Wahb, from Dāwūd ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man saw in his sleep and experienced pleasure and desire, then he rose and did not see anything on his garment. He said: So he replied, “If he is ill, then ghusl is upon him; and if he is healthy, then there is nothing upon him.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “A man may sleep while he is junub, and a woman may sleep while she is junub.”

From him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked him about the junub who enters janabah and then wants to sleep. He said: “If he wishes to perform wudu (ablution), then let him do so, and ghusl is better than that. And if he sleeps without performing wudu (ablution) and without performing ghusl, then there is nothing upon him, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

Ahmad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman with whom a man has intercourse, then she begins menstruating while she is in the place of غسل; should she perform ghusl or not? He said: "That which invalidates salat has come, so she should not perform ghusl."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: If you are ill and desire comes upon you, then perhaps it is the emitting fluid, but it comes forth weakly and has no force because of your illness, little by little, from time to time; so perform ghusl (ritual bath) from it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far and Abi 'Abdillah عليهما السلام, that they both said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl (ritual bath) with one sa'.” Then he said: “He and his wife performed ghusl with five mudds from a single vessel.” Zurarah said: So I said to him, “How did he do that?” He said: “He began, so he dipped his hand into the water before her and cleaned his private part. Then she dipped and cleaned her private part. Then he poured water over himself and she poured water over herself until they finished. So the amount with which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed ghusl was three mudds, and that with which she performed ghusl was two mudds. It only sufficed for them because they shared together entirely. But whoever performs ghusl alone by himself must have one sa'.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about ghusl for janābah, so he said: You begin by washing your hands, then pour with your right hand onto your left, then wash your private part. Then rinse your mouth and draw water into your nose. Then wash your body from the top of your head to your feet. There is no wudu (ablution) before it nor after it. Whatever thing you have caused the water to touch, then you have cleansed it. And if a man in janābah were to immerse himself in water in a single immersion, that would suffice him, even if he did not rub his body.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: The junub and the menstruating woman may open the mushaf from behind a cloth, and may recite from the Qur'an whatever they wish except the sajdah; and they may enter the mosque while passing through, but they must not sit in it, and they must not approach the two sacred mosques.

Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me, from his father, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd al-ʿAṭṭār—and he is Dāwūd ibn Farqad—from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿIjlī, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man has intercourse with his slave-girl in the water? He said: “There is no problem with it.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a person in janabah sleeping in the mosque, and he said: "He performs wudu (ablution), and there is no harm in his sleeping in the mosque and passing through it."

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil ibn Baziʿ, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who recites in the الحمّام and has intercourse in it. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a man who recites in the bathhouse and has intercourse in it. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with his wife: may he sleep in that state? He عليه السلام said: “Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, takes the souls during their sleep, and he does not know what affliction may come upon him. When he has finished, then let him perform ghusl.” I said: May the junub eat before performing wudu (ablution)? He عليه السلام said: “We do at times become lax, but let him wash his hand, and wudu (ablution) is better.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bahr, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: It was said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: “May the junub apply oil and then perform ghusl?” He said: “No.” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah, as shown by the reports we have previously presented.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUtbah al-Hāshimī, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a woman: is it permissible for her husband to uncover himself and perform ghusl in the presence of her servant? He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in whatever of that she has made permissible for him, so long as he does not go beyond it.”

From him, from Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, from his father Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a female servant belonging to a man’s child, or to his father, or to his family: is it lawful for him to uncover himself in front of her, or not? He said: “As for the child, I do not see any harm in it.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who leaves the Friday ghusl, forgetfully or otherwise. He said: “If he was forgetful, then his salat is complete. But if he did so deliberately, then ghusl is more beloved to me; and if he has done that, then let him seek forgiveness from Allah and not return to it.”

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari, from a group, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: On which nights should I perform ghusl in the month of Ramadan? He said: "On the nineteenth, the twenty-first, and the twenty-third; and the ghusl is at the beginning of the night." I said: What if he sleeps after the ghusl? He said: "It is like the ghusl of Friday: if you perform ghusl after dawn, it suffices you."

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Hamzah ibn Ahmad, from Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said: I asked him, or someone else asked him, about the bathhouse. He said: "Enter it wearing a waist-wrapper, lower your gaze, and do not wash from the well in which the bathhouse water gathers, for into it flows that with which the junub, the child of zina, and the nasibi hostile to us Ahl al-Bayt wash, and he is the worst of them."

Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, who said: When one of you undresses, al-Shayṭān looks at him and becomes desirous concerning him, so cover yourselves.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from some of his companions, from Mismā‘, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, from Amir al-Mu'minin, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. That he forbade a man from entering the water except with a waist-wrapper.

From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Darir, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: It was said to him: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Malik enters the bathhouse with his slave-girls. He said: There is no harm in that if waist-wraps are upon him and upon them, such that they are not naked like donkeys, looking at one another's private parts.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-ʿAbbās together, from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, who said: I was in the bathhouse, in the middle room, when Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام entered upon me. He had depilatory substance on him, and he was wearing a waist-wrapper over the depilatory substance. He said, "Peace be upon you." So I returned the greeting of peace to him, and hurriedly went into the room in which there was the basin, then I washed myself and came out.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: May a man perform ghusl in an open place? He said, “If no one sees him, then there is no harm.”
From him, from al-‘Abbās, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man should not look at the private part of his brother.

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Alī ibn Ismā‘īl, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, who said: al-Mīthamī—I only know that he said: I saw Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, or one who saw him, unclothed while there was a cloth over his private part, and he said: “Indeed, the thigh is not part of the ‘awrah.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: "The private part is of two parts: the front and the rear. The rear is concealed by the buttocks, so when you cover the penis and the testicles, then you have covered the private part."

From him, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Sinān, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: There is something people say: “The ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer.” So he said: “It is not as they take it. Rather, what is meant by the ʿawrah of the believer is that he slips in a misstep or speaks of something for which he may be blamed, and then someone preserves it against him in order to shame him with it one day.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked him about: “The ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer.” He said: “Yes.” I said: “I mean his lower private parts.” He said: “It is not where you are going; rather, it means divulging his secret.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning the believer’s ʿawrah being forbidden to another believer, he said: “It is not that it is uncovered and you see something of him; rather, it is that you disparage him or find fault with him.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who recites in the bathhouse and has intercourse in it. He said: “There is no problem with it.”

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAmr ibn Ibrāhīm, from Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from Hārūn ibn Ḥukaym al-Arqaṭ, the maternal uncle of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I came to him for a need and found him in the bathhouse applying depilatory. So I mentioned my need to him, and he said: “Will you not apply depilatory?” I said: “I only used it most recently the day before yesterday.” He said: “Apply it, for indeed al-nūrah is a purifier.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding nūrah is once in fifteen days; and if twenty days come upon you and you have nothing, then borrow against Allah.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hajjal, from Aban, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: “Remove the hair from yourselves, for it improves [one’s condition/appearance].”
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam and Ḥafṣ: That Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام used to apply depilatory lime to his armpits in the bathhouse.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from a man whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: We are sometimes on the road to Makkah intending ihram, and we do not have with us bran with which we rub ourselves after using depilatory lime, so we rub ourselves with flour, and because of that something enters my mind of which Allah knows best. He said: "Out of fear of extravagance in using it?" I said: Yes. He said: "There is no extravagance in what benefits and restores the body. I myself have at times ordered fine flour to be moistened with oil, then I rub myself with it; extravagance is only in that which wastes wealth and harms the body." I saw Abā Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام come out of the bathhouse, and from the top of his head to his feet he was like a rose from the effect of henna.

From him, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī, who said: I became ill until my flesh wasted away. Then I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he said: “Would it please you that your flesh return to you?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Keep to the bathhouse every other day, for it will restore your flesh to you; and beware of making it habitual constantly, for constant use of it causes consumption.”

From him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Rabīʿ ibn Muḥammad, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he mentioned the bathhouse, then said: “Beware of pottery, for it harms the body. Use cloths.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Aslam, the mawlā of ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I wanted to write to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام to ask him: may a man use depilatory paste while he is in a state of janābah? He said: So he wrote to me, to begin with: “Depilatory paste increases the cleanliness of the person in janābah, but a man should not have intercourse while dyed, and a woman who is dyed should not be approached for intercourse.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Ubays ibn Hisham, from Karram, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked him about recitation in the bathhouse, so he said: “If you have a waist-wrapper on, then recite the Qur'an, if you wish, all of it.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hāshimī, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام and ʿUmar entered the bathhouse, and ʿUmar said: “How evil a house the bathhouse is; hardship is abundant in it, and modesty is little in it.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “How excellent a house the bathhouse is: it removes filth and brings the Fire to mind.”
And from him, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, passed by a place in al-Mabādiʿ and said: “An excellent place is the bathhouse.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Bakr ibn Ḥabīb, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “There is no harm in the water of the bathhouse if it has a supply source.”

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, said: I heard a man saying to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I enter the bathhouse at dawn, and in it are the junub and others besides them. Then I stand and perform ghusl, and some of their water splashes onto me after I have finished.” He said: “Is it not flowing?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “There is no problem.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, “What do you say regarding the water of the bathhouse?” He said, “It is in the position of flowing water.”

From him, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Hāshimī, who said: He was asked about men standing by the pool in the bathhouse: I do not distinguish the Jew from the Christian, nor the one in janabah from the one who is not in janabah. He said: “You may perform ghusl from it, and do not perform ghusl from other water, for it is purifying.” And about a man who enters the bathhouse while he is in janabah, then touches the water without having washed it, he said: “There is no بأس in it.” And he said: I enter the bathhouse and perform ghusl, then after the ghusl a person in janabah or not in janabah comes into contact with my body. He said: “There is no بأس in it.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “In the bathhouse, the junub and others bathe in it; may I bathe from its water?” He said: “Yes, there is no harm in the junub bathing from it. I have indeed bathed in it, then I came and washed my feet, and I only washed them because of the dirt that had stuck to them.”

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Faḍālah, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I saw Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام coming from the bathhouse, and between him and his house there was filth. So he said: “Were it not for what is between me and my house, I would not have washed my foot, nor would I have removed the bathhouse water.”
From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: I saw Aba Ja'far عليه السلام come out of the bathhouse, then go on as he was, not washing his feet until he performed salat (prayer).

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about the water of the bathhouse, and he said: “Enter it wearing a waist-wrapper, and do not perform ghusl from another water source unless there is a junub in it, or its people are many such that you do not know whether among them there is a junub or not.” So this report is to be understood as referring to when the water has no source supply; for in that case, the contact of the junub with it renders it corrupted.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of our companions, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about the collected water in the bathhouse from the washings of the people that comes onto a garment. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥusayn al-Fārisī, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Water that is heated in the sun—do not perform wudu (ablution) with it, do not perform ghusl with it, and do not knead dough with it, for it causes leprosy.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who prayed one rakʿah on tayammum, then a man came carrying two waterskins of water with him. He said: "He cuts off the salat (prayer), performs wudu (ablution), then builds upon one [rakʿah]." Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean that if he had prayed one rakʿah and then had an occurrence that nullifies wudu (ablution), forgetfully, then at that point he performs wudu (ablution) and builds on [what he has prayed]. Had he not invalidated [his state of purity], it would not have been obligatory for him to depart [from the prayer]; rather, he would have had to continue in his salat (prayer). And it is not possible to say regarding this report what we said concerning others: that departure is only obligatory because he entered the salat (prayer) before the end of the time; because if that were so, it would not have been permissible for him to build on [what he had prayed], and he would have had to restart. So if that is so, then there is no valid interpretation for it except what we have stated.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: They asked him about the Imam of a people who is affected by janabah during a journey, and does not have enough water with him for ghusl: should he perform wudu and lead them in salat? He said: “No. Rather, he should perform tayammum and pray, for Allah, Exalted is He, has made earth a purifier just as He has made water a purifier.”

From him, from al-‘Abbās, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man led a people in prayer while he was junub, and he had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of taharah. He said: “There is no harm. So when a man performs tayammum, let that be at the end of the time, for if water escapes him, the earth will not escape him.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from al-Qāsim, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub while he has with him only enough water to suffice for his wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer): should he perform wudu (ablution) with the water, or perform tayammum? He said: “He performs tayammum. Do you not see that half of purification has been appointed for him?”

Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: Concerning a man who is affected by janabah during travel, and he has with him only a small amount of water, fearing that if he performs ghusl he will become thirsty, He said: 'If he fears thirst, then let him not pour out from it even a drop, and let him perform tayammum with the earth, for indeed the earth is more beloved to me.'

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman: when she performs tayammum after menstruation, does she become lawful for her husband? He said: “Yes.”

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man whose family is with him on a journey, and he does not find water: may he approach his wife? He said: “I do not like that he should do that, unless he is overcome by desire or fears for himself.”
This is water for the sake of the pastures and the well-being of the camels. He said: “No.”

From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who is in an open land, and he becomes junub while he has only one garment, and he has become junub in it, and he cannot find water. He said: "He performs tayammum and prays naked, standing, indicating by gesture."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them: Regarding a man who became junub during travel while he had water only enough for wudu (ablution), he said: "He performs tayammum and does not perform wudu (ablution)."
From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. The like of it.

Al-Ḥusayn, from Al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has water with him during travel, but fears its scarcity. He said: "He performs tayammum with earth and preserves the water, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made both of them means of purification: water and earth."

From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān and Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A person in janabah may have only a small amount of water with him, and if he performs ghusl with it, he fears thirst. Should he perform ghusl with it, or do tayammum? He said: “Rather, he should do tayammum; and likewise if he intends wudu (ablution).”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Ṣafwān, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who needs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) while he is unable to obtain water, then he finds enough water for wudu (ablution) being sold for one hundred dirhams or one thousand dirhams, and he does possess that amount. Should he buy it and perform wudu (ablution), or perform tayammum? He said: “No, rather he should buy it. Something like this happened to me, so I bought it and performed wudu (ablution), and what is bought for that is not a great amount of wealth.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from al-Muthanna, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A man performed tayammum, then stood to pray, and a river passed by him after he had already prayed one rak'ah. He said: “Then let him perform ghusl and begin the prayer anew.” So I said: He has already completed all of his prayer. He said: “He does not repeat.” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have already discussed earlier the meaning of this report, and it is possible that the report is to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated to me from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who is affected by janabah while he is in an open desert, and he has only one garment, and semen has affected his garment, he عليه السلام said: "He performs tayammum, removes his garment, sits with himself drawn together, then performs salat (prayer) and gestures by indication." And this report does not contradict.

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: That he was asked about a man who has only one garment, and salat (prayer) is not permissible in it, and he cannot find water to wash it—what should he do? He said: «He performs tayammum and prays; then when he finds water, he washes it and repeats the salat (prayer).» Because the intended meaning in this report is the state of necessity in which he is unable to remove the garment due to cold or something else; at that point he prays in it, and after that he repeats the salat (prayer).

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi Hamzah, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: If a man is sleeping in al-Masjid al-Haram or the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and then experiences a wet dream, and janabah comes upon him, then let him perform tayammum, and let him not pass through the mosque except in a state of tayammum. There is no harm in his passing through the rest of the mosques, but he should not sit in any of the mosques.

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who has two vessels containing water, and impurity fell into one of them, but he does not know which of the two it is, and he is not able to obtain any water other than it, he said: "He pours both of them out completely and performs tayammum."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Mālik al-Juhanī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about what comes out of the nostril of a beast and then gets onto me. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If something from the urine of the cat gets onto the garment, then salat (prayer) in it is not valid until you wash it.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man whose nose bleeds: is it upon him to wash its interior, meaning the inside of the nose? He said: “It is only upon him to wash what is outwardly visible of it.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a garment in which a man becomes junub and sweats in it. He said: “As for me, I do not like to sleep in it; but if it is winter, then there is no harm, so long as he has not sweated in it.”

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I asked him about a man who enters janabah in his garment: may he dry himself with it after his ghusl? He said: “Yes, there is no harm in it, unless the semen in it is still wet; but if it is dry, then there is no harm.”

From him, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinated in a place where there was no water, so he wiped his private part with a stone, and his private part and thighs had perspired. He said: «He washes his private part and his thighs.» And I asked him about one who wiped his private part with his hand, then his hand perspired and touched his garment—should he wash his garment? He said: «No.»

From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who urinates at night and thinks that urine has touched him, but is not certain. Is it sufficient for him, when he urinates, to pour water over his private part and not dry himself? He عليه السلام said: “He washes what has become clear to him that it was touched, and he sprinkles water over what he doubts concerning from his body or his clothes, and he dries himself before performing wudu (ablution).”

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said: Blood from a nosebleed or something else, or some semen, got onto my garment, and I marked its trace until I could get water for it. Then I got [the water], and the salat came, and I forgot that there was something on my garment, so I prayed. Then afterward I remembered. He said: “You repeat the salat and wash it.” I said: What if I had not seen its place, but I knew that it had affected it, so I searched for it and could not find it, then when I had prayed I found it? He said: “You wash it and repeat [the salat].” I said: If I thought that it had affected it, but I was not certain of that, so I looked and did not see anything, then I prayed and later saw it there? He said: “You wash it and do not repeat the salat.” I said: Why is that? He said: “Because you were upon certainty of your taharah, then you doubted, so it is not proper for you ever to overturn certainty with doubt.” I said: If I know that it has affected it, but I do not know where it is so that I may wash it? He said: “You wash the area of your garment which you think it has affected, until you are certain of your taharah.” I said: Is it upon me, if I doubt whether something has affected it, to inspect it? He said: “No, but you only want to remove the doubt that has occurred within yourself.” I said: If I see it on my garment while I am in the salat? He said: “You invalidate the salat and repeat it if you had doubted about a place on it and then saw it. But if you had not doubted and then saw it wet, you cut short the salat, wash it, then continue on with the salat, because you do not know—perhaps it is something that fell upon you. So it is not proper to overturn certainty with doubt.”
From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the urine of the cat, the dog, the donkey, and the horse. He said: “Like the urine of the human being.”

From him, from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man whom the urine of beasts reaches: should he wash it or not? He said, “He washes the urine of the horse, the mule, and the donkey; and he sprinkles water over the urine of the camel and the sheep. And everything whose meat is eaten, there is no harm in its urine.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What these two reports contain of the command to wash the urine of donkeys and riding animals is to be understood as recommendation, in light of the reports we have mentioned earlier; and what further clarifies that is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام: Concerning the urine of riding animals that gets onto the garment, he disliked it. So I said: “Are not their meats halal (permissible)?” He said: “Yes, but it is not from that which Allah has made for eating.”
Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ghiyath, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, from his father, who said: Nothing is washed with saliva except blood.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked him about vomit that affects the garment and it is not washed. He said: “There is no harm.”
From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wuhayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about ink that gets on a garment and is not washed. He said: “There is no harm in it.”
The narration of Sa'd from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn: Like that, and he added: “There is no harm in fat and oil, when they affect the garment, that one should pray in it.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from al-ʿAmrakī al-Būfakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man: is it proper for him to pour water from his mouth and wash with it the thing that may be in his garment? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, meaning Ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who is praying, then notices blood on his garment, he said: “He completes [the prayer].” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What is meant in it is when the blood is less than the amount of a dirham.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whose garment is affected by something that makes it impure, then he forgets to wash it and prays in it, then later remembers that he had not washed it. Should he repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: “He does not repeat it; the salat (prayer) has passed, and it has been recorded for him.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report is to be understood as referring to a slight impurity whose removal is not obligatory, such as a small amount of blood. As for anything else, then repeating the salat (prayer) that he performed while it was on his garment is obligatory, after it is established that he had prior knowledge of that, according to what we have explained in the narration of Zurārah and others. What further clarifies this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Maymun, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man was affected by janabah during the night, so he performed ghusl and offered salat. Then when morning came, he looked and found janabah on his garment. He said: “All praise belongs to Allah, Who has not left anything without appointing a limit for it. If, at the place where he stood, he had not looked, then repeating is upon him.” Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, said: I wrote to Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام asking him about a castrated man who urinates and faces hardship from that, and then sees moisture after moisture. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and sprinkles his garment once during the day.”

Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abi 'Abd Allah, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in washing blood with saliva.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who both said: We were at a funeral, and near us was a donkey that urinated. Then the wind carried its urine until it struck our faces and our clothes. So we went in to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام and informed him, and he said: 'There is nothing upon you.'

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man whose nail breaks off: is it permissible for him to put gum upon it? He عليه السلام said: “No. And he should not put upon it anything except what he is able to remove from it at the time of wudu (ablution), and he should not put upon it that to which the water does not reach.”

With this chain of transmission, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: About a basin in which there are images, or a jug, or a large bowl in which there are images or silver, he said: “Wudu (ablution) is not performed from it, nor in it.” And about a man, when he trims his nails with iron, or takes from his hair, or shaves the back of his neck, he said: “Then it is upon him to wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer).” He was asked: if he performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: “He wipes with water and repeats the salat (prayer), because iron is najas (ritually impure).” And he said: “Indeed, iron is the attire of the people of the Fire, and gold is the attire of the people of Paradise.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains in his statement عليه السلام, “He was asked: if he performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that,” it is possible that the one asked was the narrator, not Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. If there is no explicit wording identifying the one asked, we interpret it according to what we have stated, because touching iron is not something that necessitates repeating the salat (prayer).

With this chain of transmission: concerning a man whose forearm, or a place among the places of wudu (ablution), is broken, and he is unable to wipe over it in the state of splinting when it has been set—how should he act? He said: If he wishes to perform wudu (ablution), then let him place a vessel containing water, and place the site of the splint in the water until the water reaches his skin; that will suffice him without having to undo it. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This is to be understood as a form of recommendation, because we have already explained that with splints it suffices to wipe over them if undoing them is not possible; and if undoing them is possible, then that is necessary. So this is to be understood according to what we said regarding recommendation. (1355) 28 — Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said: Sulaymān ibn Rushayd wrote to him, informing him that he had urinated in the darkness of the night, and that the coolness of a drop of urine had touched his palm; he had no doubt that it had touched him, though he did not see it.
