He wiped it with a cloth, then forgot to wash it, and then applied oil and wiped his two palms, his face, and his head with it. Then he performed the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer) and prayed. So he replied with an answer that I read in his own handwriting: As for what you merely supposed regarding what touched your hand, it is nothing unless it is something you ascertain. If you did ascertain that, then you would indeed be required to repeat the prayers that you had performed with that very wudu (ablution): those of them whose time still remained, while those whose time had passed, there is no repetition upon you for them. That is because when a man's garment is impure, he does not repeat the salat (prayer) except what remains within its time; but if he is in janabah, or he prayed without wudu (ablution), then he must repeat the prescribed prayers that he missed, because the garment is different from the body. So act upon that, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.
The most eminent Shaykh, Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmad ibn ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn al-‘Abbas al-Najashi.
The virtuous jurist, Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Qudāmah.
The trustworthy and eminent one, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-'Abbas al-Duristi.
Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Nayshaburi.
The shaykh, the jurist, Abū Yaʿlā Sallār ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Daylamī.
Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Farisi.
Al-Sharif al-Sayyid al-Murtada, 'Alam al-Huda, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa al-Musawi.
Abu al-Fawaris ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Farisi, previously mentioned.
Al-Sharif al-Sayyid al-Radi, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa al-Musawi.
Shaykh al-Ta'ifah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi.
Abu Ya'la Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hamzah al-Ja'fari, his son-in-law, his successor, and the one who sat in his place during his lifetime in his assembly.
Abu al-Fath, the jurist and judge, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Karajaki, who died in the year 449.
Abu Muhammad, the brother of ʿAli ibn Muhammad al-Farisi, whose mention has preceded.
The trustworthy Shaykh Abū al-Faraj al-Muẓaffar ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥamdānī was among the envoys of Imam al-Ḥujjah, may Allah hasten his relief.
Al-Sharif Abu al-Wafa' al-Muhammadi al-Mawsili.
Abu Shuja', Taj al-Millah—'Adud al-Dawlah—'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Buwayh al-Daylami learned fiqh from him according to the Imamiyyah school.

Al-Qadi Aba Bakr Ahmad ibn Sayyar — he met him in Baghdad, at the residence of al-Sharif Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Musawi. In the gathering there were more than one hundred people, among them nobles from Banu Ali and Banu al-Abbas, and prominent merchants and others. They were present concerning the settlement of a right due to al-Sharif, may Allah have mercy on him.
Al-Kutaybi, and ‘Arzalah al-Mu‘tazili, and Aba ‘Amr al-Shatawi—and all of them were from the Mu‘tazilah.
The session of al-Naqib Abi al-Hasan al-'Umari. Al-Qadi Aba Muhammad al-'Umani, and Aba Bakr ibn al-Daqqaq in
The house of al-Sharif Abi 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir. Al-Warthani, al-Jarahi, and the first of the jurists among our companions, in...
A man from the people of hadith, among those who adhered to the school of al-Karabisi.
A gathering, and in it was Abu 'Isa al-Warraq.
The gathering of Abū Manṣūr ibn al-Marzubān, and in the gathering there was a group of the theologians of the Muʿtazilah.
Al-Tabarani was a shaykh from the Zaydiyyah. A discussion occurred with him through a young man from the children of the Ansar who used to visit the shaykh and learn from him.
Ibn Lu'lu' was a shaykh from the Isma'iliyyah in... Some of the commanders of the state went around.
Abu al-Qasim al-Daraki in A gathering whose host was the leader of his time, and he was al-Sharif Abi al-Hasan Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Muhammadi.

The gathering of his friend Abū al-Hudhayl Sabīʿ ibn al-Munabbih al-Mukhtārī, and al-Sharīf Abū Muḥammad ibn al-Maʾmūn was present there. The two shaykhs, Abā al-Ḥasan and Abā Ṭāhir al-Jawhariyyayn, in...

His mosque, while the Shaykh was heading toward Surrā man Raʾā. And to others besides them, among those whose names were not stated explicitly, and they are: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Naṣr, the witness in ʿAkbarā, in...
The gathering of some of the judges. A large group of the fuqaha' and the mutakallimin in...
Another session. Some of the Mu'tazilah in...

Some of the Mujabbirah, some from among the Mu'tazilah, and a man from the Zaydiyyah, in... The gathering of al-Sharif Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-'Alawi al-Muhammadi. The shaykhs of the 'Abbasids and others. All of this is in addition to his discourse with many of the sects that existed at that time, such as the group of the Mu'tazilah, the people of doctrines, the theologians of the Mujabbirah, the Hashawiyyah, the Nasibiyyah, the Kaysaniyyah, the Isma'iliyyah, the Qaramitah, the Mubarakiyyah, the Nawusiyyah, the Shamtiyyah, the Fathiyyah, the Waqifah, and the Bashariyyah. This is what the reader comes upon in the sections from al-'Uyun and al-Mahasin mentioned above; so how would it be if one were to investigate the rest of his books and what was transmitted from him. It is noted that, sanctified be his secret, even during his travels he never ceased debating, calling to his principle, and defending his school. To demonstrate that, here is his conversation with a Zaydi man who wanted to defame him and bring him down, since his presence weighed heavily upon him and those like him, because wherever he settled, people gathered around him to benefit from him and receive from him. It happened that he once visited the sacred 'Alawi shrine and passed by the Mosque of Kufah, where more than five hundred people from its inhabitants and others gathered around him. A Zaydi man came forward, intending discord and defamation, and said to him: 'By what right did you permit yourself to deny the Imamate of Zayd?!' The Shaykh said to him: 'You have held a false assumption about me, and my statement concerning Zayd is one in which no one from the Zaydiyyah disagrees with me. Zayd, may Allah have mercy on him, was an Imam in knowledge, zuhd, enjoining good, and forbidding evil. What I deny of him is the Imamate that necessitates for its possessor 'ismah, explicit designation, and miracle. And on this no one from the Zaydiyyah disagrees with me.' None of those present from the Zaydiyyah could refrain from thanking him and praying for him, and the man's stratagem in what he intended of defamation and discord was nullified. In any case, the rank of this great scholar is too evident to require explanation, for tongues proclaimed in his name praise and commendation, and his merit became so well known that it rendered unnecessary extended mention of him and elaboration on his life. His

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Intentional killing is when someone deliberately targets a thing and strikes it with an iron object, or with a stone, or with a stick, or with a thrust; all of that is intentional. Mistake is when someone intends a thing but strikes someone else.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of his companions, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said: "Intentional killing is every case in which one deliberately meant the blow; in it there is qiṣāṣ. Error is only that he intends a thing but strikes other than it." And he said: "If he confesses against himself to the killing, he is to be killed, even if there is no evidence against him."

Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the mistake for which there are blood money and expiation: is it that a man intentionally strikes another man but does not intend to kill him? He said: “Yes.” I said: If he shot at a sheep and struck a human being? He said: “That is the mistake about which there is no doubt; upon him are the blood money and the expiation.”

Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: "Intentional killing is that in which one strikes with a weapon or a stick and does not desist from it until he is killed; and accidental killing is that which he did not intend."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “If a man were to strike another man with a shard of pottery, or a brick, or a piece of wood, and he died, it would be considered intentional.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd opposes your judges.” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Bring me something from that over which they differed.” I said: “Two غلامs fought in the open square. One of them bit his companion, so the one who had been bitten took hold of a stone and struck with it the head of his companion who had bitten him, wounding him. Then he dealt him a blow, and he died. The matter was brought before Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and he exacted qiṣāṣ from him. That was deemed grave by Ibn Abī Laylā and Ibn Shubrumah, and much discussion arose about it. They said: ‘This is only a mistake,’ so ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī paid his blood-money from his own wealth.” He said: Then he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, those with us would exact qiṣāṣ for the blow; rather, mistake is when one intends a thing but strikes something else.”

Yūnus, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man strikes another man with a staff or with a stone, and he dies from a single blow before speaking, then it is quasi-intentional killing, and the diyyah is upon the killer. But if he repeatedly struck him and persisted against him with the staff or stones until he killed him, then it is intentional killing, and he is to be killed for it. And if he struck him a single blow, and he spoke, then remained for a day or more than a day, then died, then it is quasi-intentional killing.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from 'Abd Salih عليه السلام: Concerning a man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift the stick until he died, he said: “He is to be handed over to the heirs of the slain, but he is not to be left so that they take pleasure in tormenting him; rather, the sentence is to be carried out against him with the sword.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, all together from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. They said: We asked him about a man who struck another man with a staff and did not desist from him until he died. Is he to be handed over to the guardian of the slain so that he may kill him? He said: "Yes, and he is not to be left for people to abuse him, but rather the prescribed judgment is to be carried out against him."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: I throw at a man something the like of which does not kill. He said: “This is a mistake.” Then he took a small pebble and threw with it. I said: He threw at a sheep, but struck a man. He said: “This is the mistake about which there is no doubt; and deliberate killing is when he strikes with something by the like of which one is killed.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan, all together from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who struck another man with a staff and did not stop striking him until he was killed: should he be handed over to the heirs of the slain? He said: “Yes, but he is not to be left for them to abuse; rather, the prescribed retribution is to be carried out against him.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The diyah for accidental killing, when the man did not intend the killing, is one hundred camels, or ten thousand of silver coins, or one thousand sheep." And he said: "The aggravated diyah, which resembles intentional killing but is not intentional, is weightier than the diyah of accidental killing in the ages of the camels: thirty-three ḥiqqahs, thirty-three jadhaʿahs, and thirty-four thaniyyahs, all of them covered by a stud camel." And I asked him about the diyah, so he said: "The diyah of a Muslim is ten thousand of silver, or one thousand mithqals of gold, or one thousand sheep according to their ages in three divisions, and of camels one hundred, for they are according to their ages, and of cattle two hundred."

ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: For accidental killing, there is one hundred camels, or one thousand sheep, or ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars. If it is paid in camels, then it is twenty-five bint makhāḍ, twenty-five bint labūn, twenty-five ḥiqqah, and twenty-five jadhaʿah. The aggravated blood-money in mistaken killing that resembles intentional killing—where one strikes with a stone or with a stick, one strike or two, not intending to kill him—is in thirds: thirty-three ḥiqqah, thirty-three jadhaʿah, and thirty-four khalifah, all of them covered by the stallion. If it is sheep, then it is one thousand rams. Intentional killing is subject to retaliation, unless the guardian of the slain is satisfied.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from some of his companions, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah and al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, all together from Ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: In mistaken killing resembling intentional killing, it is that one kills with a whip, a stick, or a stone. Indeed, the diyah for that is made heavier, and it is one hundred camels: among them forty khalifah camels, ranging between a thaniyyah and a bāzil in its year, thirty ḥiqqah, and thirty bint labūn. As for mistake, in it there are thirty ḥiqqah, thirty bint labūn, twenty bint makhāḍ, and twenty male ibn labūn from the camels. The value of each camel is one hundred and twenty dirhams or ten dīnārs, and from sheep, the value of each aged camel from the camels is twenty sheep.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the blood money for intentional killing, and he said: "One hundred of the mature male camels. If there are no camels, then in place of each camel there are twenty male sheep."

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said: The diyah is one thousand dinars or ten thousand dirhams. And from the people who possess garments, garments are taken; from the people who possess camels, camels are taken; from the people who possess sheep, sheep are taken; and from the people who possess cattle, cattle are taken.

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī; and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah and al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, all from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: "Whoever kills a believer deliberately, retaliation is taken from him, unless the heirs of the slain are satisfied to accept the blood-money. If they are satisfied with the blood-money and the killer approves that, then the blood-money is twelve thousand, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels. If he is in a land where dinars are used, then one thousand dinars; if he is in a land where camels are used, then one hundred camels; and if he is in a land where dirhams are used, then dirhams according to the reckoning of twelve thousand."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad and al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: “The diyyah is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams, or one hundred camels.” And he said: “If you strike a man with a piece of iron, then that is intentional killing.”

From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I heard Ibn Abī Laylā saying: The blood-money in the Jāhiliyyah was one hundred camels, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله confirmed it. Then he imposed upon the people of cattle two hundred cows, and he imposed upon the people of sheep one thousand sheep, and upon the people of Yemen one hundred garments. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: So I asked Abā ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about what was narrated from Ibn Abī Laylā, and he said: ‘ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: The blood-money is one thousand dinars, and the value of the dinars is ten thousand dirhams. Upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars, and upon the people of silver is ten thousand dirhams for the people of the towns; for the people of the deserts, the blood-money is one hundred camels; and for the people of the Sawād, two hundred cows or one thousand sheep.’

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: "Whoever kills a believer intentionally, then qiṣāṣ is carried out against him, unless the heirs of the slain are satisfied to accept the diyah, or they mutually agree upon more than the diyah or less than the diyah. If they do that among themselves, it is permissible; and if they do not come to a mutual agreement, qiṣāṣ is carried out." And he said: "The diyah is ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels."

ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked him about the blood-money for intentional killing, where a man kills another man deliberately. He said: He said, “One hundred of the mature male camels; and if there are no camels, then in place of each camel there are twenty of the male sheep.”

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās and Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Deliberate killing is that he intentionally targets him and kills him with something by which the like of him is killed. Mistaken killing is that he acts deliberately but does not intend to kill him, yet kills him with something by which the like of him is not usually killed. And the mistake about which there is no doubt is that he intends something else, then strikes him.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said, may Allah be pleased with him: What we rely upon concerning the blood-money is that one hundred camels, or two hundred cattle, or one thousand sheep, or one thousand dinars, or ten thousand dirhams are binding upon the killer. Most of the narrations that we presented indicate this. As for what has been narrated, that the owner of camels, if he does not have camels with him, gives for each camel twenty head from the mature male sheep, so that they become two thousand sheep, this admits two possibilities: one of them is that camels are only binding upon the people of the desert lands, so whoever refuses to give camels, the governor compels them to give the value of each camel as twenty head from the mature male sheep, because the refusal comes from their side. But if they do not have camels, or they have sheep and are given the choice regarding it, then no more than one thousand sheep is due from them. And what clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from Abi Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said: “The diyah of a man is one hundred camels; if that is not available, then from cattle at the value of that; and if that is not available, then one thousand rams. This is in intentional killing, and in mistaken killing it is like intentional killing: one thousand mixed sheep.” And the second possibility is that this is specific to the slave when he kills a free man intentionally; then in that case that becomes binding upon him, and that has indeed been narrated.

Ahmad, al-Hasan, and Abu Shu'ayb, from Abi Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning Regarding a slave who kills a free man intentionally, he said: “One hundred mature camels; and if there are no camels, then in place of each camel, twenty head from the male sheep.” As for dirhams, no more than ten thousand dirhams are binding, and most of the narrations have come with that. As for what was narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan and 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, the two reports that contained twelve thousand dirhams, al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa both mentioned that our companions narrated that this was according to a weight of six; and if that is so, then it returns to ten thousand, and there is no contradiction between the reports.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: ʿAli عليه السلام used to say: “The blood money for accidental killing is collected over three years, and the blood money for intentional killing is collected within one year.”
Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: "All iron is deliberate [killing/injury by a weapon]."
Ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Everyone who kills something, small or great, after doing so intentionally, then retaliation is upon him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man kills a man deliberately. He said: "Three kaffarahs are upon him: he must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons." And he said: "Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام gave a ruling similar to that."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Jamīlah, from Abū Usāmah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: A man who killed a believer intentionally while knowing that he was a believer, except that anger drove him to kill him—does he have any tawbah, and what is his tawbah if he wishes to repent, or does he have no tawbah? He said: “Retaliation is carried out against him. If it was not known about him, he should go to his heirs and inform them that he killed him. If they pardon him, he should give them the blood-money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and give charity to sixty needy persons.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a believer who kills a believer intentionally: is there repentance for him? He said: If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or for some worldly cause, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If no one knew of it, he should go to the heirs of the slain and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he should give them the blood-money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty poor persons.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad al-Minqarī, from ʿĪsā al-Ḍaʿīf, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man killed another man intentionally; what is his tawbah? He said: “He should submit himself.” I said: He fears that they will kill him. He said: “Then let him give them the diyah.” I said: He fears that they will come to know thereby. He said: “Then let him marry a woman from among them.” I said: He fears that she may inform them of that. He said: “Then let him consider the diyah, make it into purses, then watch for the times of salat, and let him cast it into their house.”

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and Ibn Bukayr and more than one person, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام was in tawaf, and he looked toward one side of the mosque at a group, and said: “What is this gathering?” They said: “This is Muḥammad ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī. His mind has become disturbed, so he does not speak. His family brought him out, hoping that when he sees the people, he may speak.” When he عليه السلام finished his tawaf, he went out until he drew near to him. When Muḥammad ibn Shihāb saw him, he recognized him. So ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said to him: “What is the matter with you?” He said: “I was appointed to an office, and I became involved in bloodshed. I killed a man, and what you see entered me.” So ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said to him: “My fear for you because of your despair of the mercy of Allah is greater than my fear for you because of what you have done.” Then he عليه السلام said to him: “Give them the blood money.” He said: “I have already done so, but they refused.” He said: “Make it into purses, then watch for the times of salat (prayer), and cast it into their house.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī. And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr also narrated it from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a man who kills a slave by mistake, he said: "He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and give charity to sixty needy persons." He said: "If he is unable to provide the slave, then fasting is upon him; and if he is unable to fast, then charity is upon him."

Al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about one who kills a believer deliberately: is there tawbah (repentance) for him? He said: “No, not until he pays his blood money to his family, frees a slave, fasts two consecutive months, seeks Allah’s forgiveness, turns to Him in tawbah (repentance), and supplicates humbly. For I hope that tawbah (repentance) will be accepted from him when he does that.” I said: Then if he does not have what he can pay as his blood money? He said: “He should ask the Muslims until he pays his blood money to his family.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning His saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And whoever kills a believer intentionally” He عليه السلام said: “Whoever kills a believer on account of his religion, then that is the intentional killer about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has spoken in His Book.” “And He has prepared for him a tremendous punishment.” I said: Then a matter occurs between a man and another man, and he strikes him with his sword and kills him. He عليه السلام said: “That is not the intentional one meant by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Sa'id al-Azraq, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning A man who killed a believing man, he said: "It will be said to him: Die whatever kind of death you wish—if you wish, as a Jew; if you wish, as a Christian; and if you wish, as a Magian."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī al-Safātij, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, “And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell.” He عليه السلام said: “His recompense is Hell, if He recompenses him.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a believer who kills a believer intentionally: does he have repentance? So he said: "If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or because of some worldly matter, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If it had not become known, he should go to the heirs of the slain and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he must give them the blood-money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons, as repentance to Allah."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: "The believer remains within breadth in his religion so long as he does not shed forbidden blood." And he said: "The killer of a believer is never granted success for repentance."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about al-qasāmah, and he said: “In all claims, the evidence is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made, except specifically in cases of bloodshed. For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was once at Khaybar when the Anṣār lost a man from among themselves, then found him slain. The Anṣār said: So-and-so, the Jew, killed our companion. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to the claimants: “Produce two just men from other than yourselves, and I will hand him over in full retaliation; but if you do not find two witnesses, then produce a qasāmah of fifty men, and I will hand him over in full retaliation.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, we do not have two witnesses from other than ourselves, and we dislike swearing to what we did not see. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله paid the blood-money for him from his own side. And he said: “The blood of the Muslims has only been protected by qasāmah so that when a wicked, immoral person sees an opportunity against his enemy, the fear of qasāmah restrains him lest he be killed for it, and so he refrains from killing him. Otherwise, the one against whom the claim is made is made to swear a qasāmah of fifty men: ‘We did not kill him, nor do we know any killer’; otherwise they are liable for the blood-money when they find a slain person in their midst if the claimants do not swear.”

Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about al-qasāmah, and he said: “It is true and established. A man from the Anṣār was found slain in a well among the wells of the Jews. So they came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, we found one of our men slain in a well among the wells of the Jews.’ He said: ‘Bring me two witnesses from other than yourselves.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, we do not have two witnesses from other than ourselves.’ So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to them: ‘Then let fifty men from among you swear against one man, and we will hand him over to you.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can we swear to what we did not see?’ He said: ‘Then the Jews shall swear.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can we accept the Jews, while what is in them of shirk is greater?’ So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم paid his blood-money. Zurārah said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: ‘Al-qasāmah was only instituted as a precaution for the blood of the Muslims, so that when a wicked person wishes to kill a man where no one sees him, he will fear that and refrain from killing.’

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about al-qasāmah: where did it begin? He said: “It was from the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. After the conquest of Khaybar, a man from the Anṣār fell behind his companions. They went back searching for him and found him rolling in his blood, slain. The Anṣār came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: O Messenger of Allah, the Jews killed our companion. He said: Let fifty men from among you swear that they killed him.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we swear to what we did not see? He said: “Then let the Jews swear.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and who would believe the Jews? So he said: “Then I shall pay for your companion.” So I said to him: How is the ruling in it? He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ruled concerning bloodshed in a manner unlike what He has ruled in any other matter among the rights of the people, because of His magnification of blood. If a man were to claim against another man ten thousand dirhams, or less or more, the oath would not be upon the claimant; rather, the oath would be upon the one claimed against. But when a man claims against a group that they killed, then the oath belongs to the claimant of blood before those claimed against. So the claimant must bring fifty who swear that so-and-so killed so-and-so, then the one sworn against is handed over to them. If they wish, they may pardon; and if they wish, they may accept the diyah. If they do not swear, then those against whom the claim was made must have fifty of them swear: We did not kill him, nor do we know any killer for him. If they do that, then the people of the village in which he was found must pay; and if he was in an open land, his diyah is paid from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims.” For Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “The blood of a Muslim man is not left unavenged or uncompensated.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ḥannān ibn Sadīr, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said to me: “Ibn Shubrumah asked me, ‘What do you say regarding al-qasāmah in bloodshed?’ So I answered him with what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did. He said: ‘What do you think—if the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله had not done this, what would the position concerning it have been?’ He said: “I said to him: As for what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did, I have already informed you of it; and as for what he did not do, I have no knowledge of it.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about al-qasāmah: whether a sunnah (prophetic precedent) had been established regarding it. He said, then said: “Yes. Two men from the Anṣār went out, obtaining provisions from Banī al-Najjār. Then they separated, and one of them was found slain. His companions said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘Only the Jews killed our companion.’ So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘The Jews shall swear an oath.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can you make the Jews swear regarding our brother while they are a disbelieving people?’ He said: ‘Then you swear.’ They said: ‘And how can we swear about what we did not know and did not witness?’ He said: So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله paid his blood-money from his own possession.” He said: I said, ‘How was al-qasāmah?’ He said, then said: “Indeed, it is true; and were it not for that, people would kill one another. Al-qasāmah is only a protective measure by which the people are safeguarded.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about al-qasamah: upon whom is it—upon the family of the killer or upon the family of the slain? He said: "It is upon the family of the slain; they swear by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that so-and-so certainly killed so-and-so."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “The qasāmah is fifty men in intentional killing, and in accidental killing, twenty-five men, and they must swear by Allah.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl and Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, all together from al-Riḍā عليه السلام; and Sahl ibn Ziyād from al-Ḥasan ibn Ẓarīf, from his father Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ayyūb, from Abī ʿAmr al-Mutaṭabbib, who said: I presented to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام what Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام had ruled regarding blood-money. Among what he had ruled regarding the body, he made it six assessed categories: the life, sight, hearing, speech, diminution of light from the eye, hoarseness, and paralysis in the hands and feet. Then he assigned with each of these a qasāmah in accordance with the amount its diyah reached. He set the qasāmah for a life in intentional killing at fifty men, and for a life in accidental killing at twenty-five men. For injuries of the limbs whose diyah reached one thousand dinars, he set six persons, and whatever was less than that was according to its proportion out of six persons. The qasāmah in life, hearing, sight, intellect, the light of the eye, hoarseness, and impairment of the hands and feet is based on six parts of the man. Its explanation is this: when a man is afflicted in one of these six parts, that is measured. If it is one-sixth of his sight, hearing, speech, or other than that, he swears by himself alone. If it is one-third of his sight, he swears and one man swears with him. If it is half of his sight, he swears and two men swear with him. If it is two-thirds of his sight, he swears and three men swear with him. If it is five-sixths, he swears and four men swear with him. If it is all of his sight, he swears and five men swear with him. Likewise, all qasāmah in wounds is in this manner. If the injured person has no one to swear with him, the oaths are multiplied upon him: if it is one-sixth of his sight, he swears once; if it is one-third, he swears over it twice; if it is half, he swears three times; if it is two-thirds, he swears four times; if it is five-sixths, he swears five times; and if it is all of it, he swears six times, then he is given [the compensation].

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Maryam, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that nothing is to be borne by the ʿāqilah except the injury of al-mūḍiḥah and above. And he said: “For what is less than al-simḥāq, there is the physician’s fee in addition to the indemnity.”

From him, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The ʿāqilah does not bear liability for intentional killing, nor for a confession, nor for a settlement.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who killed another man intentionally, then the killer fled and could not be apprehended. He said: “If he has property, the blood-money is taken from his property; otherwise, then from the nearest relatives and then the next nearest, because the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left without redress.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning A man who killed another man intentionally, then fled, and it was not possible to apprehend him until he died. He عليه السلام said: “If he has wealth, it shall be taken from it; otherwise, it shall be taken from the nearest relative, then the nearest.”

Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: The 'aqilah does not bear liability for intentional killing, nor for a confession, nor for a settlement.

“There is no mutual liability among the Ahl al-Dhimmah for what they commit of killing or injury. Rather, that is taken from their own property; and if they do not have property, the liability returns to the Imam of the Muslims, because they pay the jizyah to him just as a slave pays tax to his master.” He said: “And they are owned dependents of the Imam, so whoever among them embraces Islam, he is free.” And (675) 15 — Ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from his father, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: A man who had killed another man by mistake was brought to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام. Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to him: “Who are your clan and your relatives?” He said: “I have no clan or relatives in this town.” He said: “From which land are you?” He said: “I am a man from the people of al-Mawsil; I was born there, and I have relatives and household there.” He said: So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام inquired about him, and he did not find for him in al-Kufah any relatives or clan. He said: So he wrote to his governor over al-Mawsil: “Now then, so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such, has killed a Muslim man by mistake. He mentioned that he is a man from the people of al-Mawsil and that he has relatives and household there. I have sent him to you with my messenger so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such. When he arrives to you, Allah willing, and you have read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his Muslim relatives. If he is from the people of al-Mawsil, among those born there, and you find for him there Muslim relatives, then gather them to yourself. Then see: if among them there is a man who inherits him, having an apportioned share in the Book, not barred from his inheritance by any of his relatives, then impose the diyah upon him and collect it from him in installments over three years.” And if he has no one among his relatives who has an apportioned share in the Book, and they are relatives equal in lineage, and he has relatives from his father’s side and his mother’s side equal in lineage, then distribute the diyah among his relatives from his father’s side and among his relatives from his mother’s side, from the adult Muslim men. Then assign to his relatives from his father’s side two-thirds of the diyah, and assign to his relatives from his mother’s side one-third of the diyah. And if he has no rel

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from one who narrated it, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, that he said: Regarding a man who killed another man by mistake, then died before the diyah could be paid out to the heirs of the slain: indeed, the diyah is upon his heirs; and if he has no ʿāqilah, then it is upon the ruler from the public treasury.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was found killed, then two men came to his heir. One of them said, “I killed him intentionally,” and the other said, “I killed him by mistake.” He said: “If he accepts the statement of the one who claims intentional killing, then he has no recourse against the one who claims mistaken killing. And if he accepts the statement of the one who claims mistaken killing, then he has no recourse against the one who claims intentional killing.”

From him, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who was killed, then carried to the governor, and some people came and testified against a man that he had killed him intentionally. So the governor handed the killer over to the heirs of the slain so that retaliation might be carried out against him. But before they proceeded, a man came to them and confessed before the governor that he had intentionally killed their companion, and that this one against whom the witnesses had testified was innocent of killing your companion. So do not kill him, and take me for his blood. He said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “If the heirs of the slain wish to kill the one who confessed against himself, then let them kill him, and they have no claim against the other. And the heirs of the one who confessed against himself have no claim against the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given. But if they wish to kill the one against whom testimony was given, then let them kill him, and they have no claim against the one who confessed. Then the one who confessed against himself must pay half of the blood money to the one against whom testimony was given.” I said: What if they wish to kill both of them together? He said: “That is for them, but they must pay half of the blood money specifically to the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given, not to the other man’s heirs; then they may kill them both for him.” I said: What if they wish to take the blood money? He said: “The blood money is divided equally between the two, because one of them confessed and against the other testimony was given.” I said: Then how was half of the blood money made due from the one who confessed to the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given when he was killed, while nothing was made due to the heirs of the one who confessed against the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given and who did not confess? He said: “Because the one against whom testimony was given is not like the one who confessed. The one against whom testimony was given did not confess and did not absolve his companion, while the other confessed and absolved his companion. So what became binding upon the one who confessed and absolved his companion did not become binding upon the one against whom testimony was given, who did not

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, said: Some of our companions informed me, raising it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had been found in a ruin, with a knife in his hand stained with blood, while there was a slaughtered man writhing in his blood. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “What do you say?” He said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I killed him.” He said: “Take him away and execute retribution upon him.” So when they took him away to kill him, a man came rushing and said: “Do not hasten; return him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.” So they brought him back, and he said: “By Allah, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, this man did not kill his companion; I killed him.” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to the first man: “What led you to confess against yourself?” He said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, what could I say, when men like these had testified against me, and they seized me while there was in my hand a knife stained with blood, and the man was writhing in his blood while I was standing over him? I feared beating, so I confessed. I am a man who had slaughtered a sheep beside this ruin, then I was overcome by the need to urinate, so I entered the ruin and found the man writhing in his blood. I stood there in astonishment, then these men came upon me and seized me.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Take these two and go with them to al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and say to him: What is the ruling concerning them?” He said: So they went to al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and related to him their story. Then al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Say to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: If this one killed that man, then he has given life to this one, and Allah, the Exalted, has said:” “And whoever gives it life, it is as though he has given life to all mankind.” So he let them both go, and he paid the blood-money of the slain man from the public treasury.”

Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام. Regarding a man who accepted Islam and then killed a man by mistake, he said: “I distribute the blood-money among those like him from among the people who have accepted Islam and have no mawali.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I said: What do you say regarding intentional and mistaken acts in killing and wounds? He said: “Mistake is not like intentionality. In intentionality there is killing, and in wounds there is retaliation; but in mistaken killing and wounds there are blood-monies.” He said, then he said: “O Hakam, when the mistake is from the killer or the one who wounds, and he is a Bedouin, then the blood-money for what the Bedouin has committed by mistake is upon his paternal kin from among the Bedouins.” He said: “And if the killer or the one who wounds is a townsman, then the blood-money for what he has committed by mistake is upon his paternal kin from among the townspeople.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from some of his companions, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: When the guardian of the slain person dies, his child takes his place after him regarding the blood money.

Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would detain in a blood accusation for six days; then if the heirs of the slain came with proof, otherwise he would let him go free.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: "The ʿāqilah does not bear liability except for that over which clear proof has been established." He said: A man came to him and confessed in his presence, so he assigned it to his own property alone and did not place anything upon the ʿāqilah.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever seeks refuge with a people and they acknowledge his wilayah, then his inheritance belongs to them, and his blood-money liability is upon them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was killed, and he had a father, a mother, and a son. Then the son said: I want to kill the killer of my father. And the father said: I pardon. And the mother said: I take the blood money. He عليه السلام said: Then the son should give the mother of the slain one one-sixth of the blood money, and he should give the heirs of the killer one-sixth of the blood money, representing the right of the father who pardoned him, and then he may kill him.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Concerning two men who intentionally killed a man, and he had two heirs, then one of the two heirs pardoned, So he said: “If some of the heirs pardon them, killing is averted from them, and from the blood-money there is deducted according to the share of the one who pardoned, and the two of them shall pay the remainder from their own wealth to the one who did not pardon.” And he said: “The pardon of every share-holder is valid.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who killed two men intentionally, and both had heirs. Then the heirs of one of them pardoned, while the others refused. He said: He said, “Those who did not pardon may kill him, and if they prefer to take the blood-money, they may take it.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: So I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Two men killed one man intentionally, and he has two heirs, then one of the two heirs pardoned. He said: He said, “When some of the heirs pardon, killing is averted from the two of them, and from the blood-money there is deducted from them according to the share of the one who pardoned, and they shall pay the remainder from their wealth to those who did not pardon.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Wallad, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and who had children, some minors and some adults. What do you say if his adult children pardon? He said: “He is not to be killed, and the pardon of the adult children is valid regarding their own shares. Then when the minors grow up, they have the right to demand their shares of the blood money.”

Al-Saffar narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Wait regarding the minors whose father was killed until they grow up. Then, when they reach maturity, they are given the choice: if they wish, they may kill, or pardon, or make a settlement.

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who was killed, and he had a brother in the abode of migration, and a brother in the abode of the Bedouin, and he had not migrated. What do you say: if the Emigrant pardons, but the Bedouin wants to kill, does he have that right? He said: He عليه السلام said: “The Bedouin does not have the right to kill an Emigrant until he migrates.” He said: “So when the Emigrant pardons, then his pardon is valid.” I said: Does the Bedouin have any share of the inheritance? He عليه السلام said: “As for inheritance, he has his allotted share from the blood-money of his brother, if it is taken.”

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abi al-'Abbas, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Women have neither pardon nor retaliation.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Maryam, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning one who pardons among those having a share, that his pardon is valid. And he ruled regarding four brothers, one of whom pardoned; he said: the rest of them are to be given the blood-money, and from him there is to be remitted according to the share of the one who pardoned.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of his companions, who raised it to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, concerning: Concerning a man who was killed and he had two heirs: one of them pardoned, while the other refused to pardon. He عليه السلام said: “If the one who did not pardon wishes to kill, he may kill, and he must return half of the blood-money to the heirs of the slain person against whom retaliation is carried out.”

Al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father عليهما السلام, that Ali عليه السلام used to say: Whoever pardons regarding the blood, from among those who have a share in it, then his pardon is valid, the blood-claim is dropped, the indemnity becomes due, and the share of the one who pardoned is lifted from him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad, who said: Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Regarding a man who is killed and has no heir except the Imam: indeed, it is not for the Imam to pardon; rather, he may kill [in retaliation] or take the blood-money and place it in the treasury of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain person was upon the Imam, and likewise his blood-money belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.”

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a Muslim man who intentionally killed a Muslim, and the slain person had no heirs among the Muslims except heirs from among the Ahl al-Dhimmah from his relatives. He said: "It is upon the Imam to present Islam to his relatives from the people of his household. So whoever among them accepts Islam, then he is his heir; the killer is handed over to him. If he wishes, he may kill; if he wishes, he may pardon; and if he wishes, he may take the diyah. But if none of them accepts Islam, then the Imam is the guardian of his affair. If he wishes, he may kill; and if he wishes, he may take the diyah and place it in the Bayt Mal of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain person was upon the Imam, and likewise his diyah belongs to the Imam of the Muslims." I said to him: What if the Imam pardons him? He said: "It is only the right of all the Muslims, and it is only upon the Imam either to kill or to take the diyah, and he has no right to pardon."

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jamilah, from al-Halabi, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment." He said: "It is the man who pardons or takes the blood money, then wounds his companion or kills him; for him is a painful punishment."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "But whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then follow-up should be according to what is right, and payment to him should be with excellence." What is that thing? He said: "It is when a man accepts the blood money. So the man who has the right was commanded to pursue it in a fair manner and not to make things difficult for him, and the one upon whom the right is due was commanded to pay it to him with excellence when he is able." I said: What do you say about His saying, the Exalted: "Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment"? He said: "It is the man who accepts the blood money or makes a settlement, then afterwards commits an offense by mutilating or killing; so Allah has promised him a painful punishment."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “But whoever gives it in charity, then it is an expiation for him.” He عليه السلام said: “It is expiated for him from his sins in proportion to what he has pardoned of a wound or other than it.” He said: And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “So whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then there should be a follow-up in a fair manner and payment to him with excellence.” He عليه السلام said: “It is the man who accepts the blood-money; then the claimant ought to deal gently with him and not make things hard for him, and the one from whom it is sought ought to pay it to him with excellence, so he should not delay him when he is able.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then there should be a follow-up in a fair manner and payment to him with excellence." He said: "It is fitting for the one who has the right not to make things difficult for his brother when he has made peace with him for a diyah, and it is fitting for the one upon whom the right rests not to delay his brother when he is able to give him what he owes, and that he should render it to him with excellence." He said: And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment." So he said: "It is the man who accepts the diyah, or pardons, or makes a settlement, then transgresses and kills; for him is a painful punishment, just as Allah, Exalted is He, said."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: When the guardian of the slain person dies, his child takes his place after him.

Yūnus, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was killed while he owed a debt and had no property: do his heirs have the right to forgo his blood in favor of his killer while he still has a debt? He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the holders of the debt are the claimants against the killer. So if his heirs forgo his blood in favor of the killer, they become liable for the blood money to the creditors; otherwise, no.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Kulayb ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Whoever kills in a sacred month, then upon him is a blood-money and a third more.”
From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “When a man kills in a sacred month, he fasts two consecutive months from the sacred months.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who killed another man by mistake during the Sacred Months. He said: "He must pay the blood-money and fast two consecutive months from the Sacred Months." I said: This includes the 'Id and the days of al-Tashriq. So he said: "He fasts it, for it is a duty that has become binding upon him."

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning a man who killed in the Sanctuary: He said: “Upon him is the blood money and one-third extra, and he must fast two consecutive months from the sacred months.” He said: I said, “This includes the ʿĪd and the days of Tashrīq.” He said: So he said, “He fasts, for it is an obligation that has become binding upon him.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jamil and Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Jamil, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم cursed whoever introduces an offense in al-Madinah or gives shelter to an offender.” I said: “What is that offense?” He said: “Killing.”

Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: regarding A man who commits an offense outside the Haram, then seeks refuge in the Haram—he said: “The hadd is not carried out upon him, and he is not to be fed, nor given drink, nor spoken to, nor traded with. For when that is done to him, he will soon come out, and then the hadd will be carried out upon him. But if he commits an offense in the Haram, the hadd is carried out upon him in the Haram, for he did not regard the Haram as having sanctity.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Maythamī, from Abān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Ten men killed a man. He said: “If his heirs wish, they may kill them all together and pay nine blood-monies; and if they wish, they may choose one man and kill him, and the remaining nine shall pay to the family of the last slain man one-tenth of the blood-money, each man among them.” He said: “Then indeed the wālī undertakes their discipline and imprisonment.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding two men who killed one man, he عليه السلام said: “If the heirs of the slain wish to kill them both, they shall pay one full diyah and then kill them both, and the diyah shall be divided between the heirs of the two slain men. If they wish to kill one of them, they shall kill him, and the one left shall pay half of the diyah to the family of the slain. If they do not pay the diyah for one of them and do not kill either one of them, he shall accept the diyah of his companion from both of them. And if his heirs accept the diyah, then it shall be upon both of them.”

Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: If two men or three kill a man, and they wish to kill them, they shall return the excess of the diyah. And if his awliya' accept the diyah, it shall be upon them; otherwise, they take the diyah of their companion.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding ten people who jointly killed a man, he said: 'The family of the slain may choose any one of them to kill, and his heirs will claim nine-tenths of the blood money from the remaining nine.'

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abi al-'Abbas and others, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: When a group gathers to kill one man, the wali rules that whichever one they wish may be killed, and they do not have the right to kill more than one. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority, so let him not exceed limits in killing.” And if three kill one person, the wali is given the choice of which of the three he wishes to kill, and the other two are liable for two-thirds of the diyah to the heirs of the slain. So this does not contradict the reports we mentioned earlier, that the heirs of the slain may kill two, or one more than that number, because that is only for them when they pay the diyah of the remainder. This report only addresses one who wants to kill a group for one person without paying the diyah of the rest, and they have no such right. There is nothing in the apparent wording of the report to indicate that if he were to offer the diyah of the remainder, it would not be permissible for him to kill them for him. Since that is not in its apparent meaning, and the earlier reports clarify that, this concise report should be understood in light of those detailed reports. And what further clarifies what we have presented is what he narrated:

Al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning Two men who killed a man—he said: “They are to be killed if the family of the slain wishes, and one blood-money is to be returned to their families.”

ʿAlī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man who charged at another man to kill him while the man was fleeing from him. Then another man came from the front and held him for the attacker until the man came and killed him. He ruled that the man who killed him should be killed, and he ruled concerning the other one who had restrained him for him that he should be cast into prison forever until he dies in it, because he had held him for death.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: The like of it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning two men: one of them held [the victim], and the other killed [him]. He said: The killer is to be killed, and the other is to be imprisoned until he dies of grief, just as he had restrained him until he died of grief.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Three men were brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. One of them had restrained a man, then another came and killed him, while the other was watching them. So he ruled concerning the lookout that his eyes be put out, concerning the one who restrained him that he be imprisoned until he dies just as he had restrained, and he ruled concerning the one who killed that he be killed.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning a man who ordered another man to kill a man: So he killed him. He said: “The one who killed him shall be killed for him, and the one who ordered his killing shall be imprisoned in confinement until he dies.”

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning A man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him—he said: “The master is to be killed for him.”

ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said concerning a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Is the slave of a man anything but like his sword? The master is to be killed, and the slave is to be confined in prison.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These two reports have been transmitted as we have cited them, but practice should rest upon the first report, because it accords with the apparent meaning of the Book of Allah and the many reports that we have mentioned earlier. For the Qur'an has stated that a life is for a life, and we know that it intended only the life that kills. The reports we cited regarding those who participated through watching, restraining, and killing also support this, because qiṣāṣ in them was imposed only upon the killer, and it was not imposed upon the one who restrained nor upon the one who watched. And we know that the one who restrains is graver in matter than the one who orders. So when the two reports conflict with the Qur'an and the reports, their force should be set aside, and practice should be according to what is besides them. However, the two reports can bear one interpretation: that they refer to one whose habit is to order his slaves to kill people, inciting them to that and compelling them toward it. In that case, it is permissible for the Imam to kill one whose state is such as this, because he is a corrupter in the land.
ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man kills two men, or more than that, he is killed for them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abi al-Mi'za, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever kills his slave intentionally, then it is upon him to free a slave, feed sixty needy persons, and fast two consecutive months.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ḥumrān, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Regarding a man who kills a slave owned by him, he عليه السلام said: "He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who killed a mamlūk. He said: “He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a man who kills his owned slave deliberately, he said: “It is pleasing to me that he should free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons; then repentance would be after that.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismā' ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام. That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was presented with the case of a man who had tortured his slave until he died. So he struck him with one hundred lashes as a deterrent, imprisoned him for a year, and fined him the value of the slave, then gave it in charity on his behalf.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muthannā, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning a man who kills his slave intentionally. What expiation is upon him? He said: “The freeing of a slave, fasting two months, and charity upon sixty needy persons.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning a man who kills his slave by mistake, he said: He must free a slave, fast for two months, and give charity to sixty poor persons. If he is unable to free a slave, then fasting is upon him; and if he is unable to fast, then charity is upon him.

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Murrār, from Yūnus, from them, peace be upon them, who said: He was asked about a man who killed his mamluk. He said: “If he is not known for killing, he is to be beaten severely, and the value of the slave is to be taken from him and paid to the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims. But if he is accustomed to killing, he is to be killed.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a woman who cut off the breast of her bondwoman that she is free, and her mistress has no authority over her. And he ruled that whoever mutilates his slave, then he is free, and he has no authority over him; he is set free, going and affiliating himself with whomever he wishes, and if someone guarantees his liability, then he inherits from him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who struck a slave belonging to him, and he died from his beating. He said: "He must free a slave."

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning A man who kills his son or his slave—he said: “He is not killed for him, but he is to be beaten severely and banished from the place of his birth.”

Yūnus, from one of those who narrated it to him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning a man who killed his owned slave: he is to be beaten severely, and the slave’s value is to be taken from him for the public treasury.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Humran, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: A father is not subjected to retaliation for his child, while the child is killed in retaliation for his father if he kills his father deliberately.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The father is not killed for his son if he kills him, while the son is killed for his father if he kills his father.

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who kills his son: is he to be killed for him? He said, “No.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed his mother. He said: “He is to be killed for her, in humiliation, and I do not think that his being killed is an expiation, nor does he inherit from her.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Yusuf ibn 'Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said: Concerning a man who killed his mother, he said: “If it was by mistake, then he has his share of her inheritance; but if he killed her deliberately, then he does not inherit anything from her.”

Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “A father is not killed in retaliation for his child, but a child is killed in retaliation for his father; and a man does not inherit from another man if he kills him, even if it was by mistake.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: We have already explained in the Book of Inheritances the manner of reconciling these two reports, so there is no point in repeating it.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, and she miscarried her child. Then the woman's husband brought a claim against her father, so the woman said: If there is a diyah for this miscarried fetus, then my share of inheritance from it is a gift to my father. He عليه السلام said: "What she has assigned to him from her share is valid for her father." He عليه السلام said: "And her father must pay to her husband two-thirds of the diyah of the miscarried fetus."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who kills his son: is he to be killed for him? He said: “No, and neither of the two inherits from the other if he kills him.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi Ubaydah, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a woman who deliberately drank medicine while she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that, so she cast down her child. He said: "If it had bone and flesh had grown upon it, then its indemnity is upon her, which she must deliver to its father. And if it was a fetus, a clot, or a morsel, then forty dinars or a ghurrah are upon her, which she must pay to its father." I said to him: Then she does not inherit from her child’s indemnity along with its father? He said: "No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit from him."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that Ali, peace be upon him, used to say: A father is not killed in retaliation for his child if he kills him, while the child is killed in retaliation for the father if he kills him. And the father is not given the hadd punishment for the child if he slanders him, while the child is given the hadd punishment for the father if he slanders him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding four men who looked down into the lion's pit. One of them fell, then he clung to the second, the second clung to the third, and the third clung to the fourth. So he judged the first to be the lion's prey, and imposed upon his family one-third of the blood-money for the family of the second, and imposed upon the second, for the family of the third, two-thirds of the blood-money, and imposed upon the third, for the family of the fourth, the full blood-money.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismāʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: “A group of people dug a pit for a lion in Yemen, and the lion fell into it. There was the lion, so the people crowded around it, looking at the lion. Then a man fell, and he clung to another, and the other clung to another, and another to another, and the lion wounded them. Among them were those who died from the lion’s wounds, and among them were those who were brought out and then died. They disputed over that until they took up swords. Then Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام said, “Come, I will judge between you.” So he ruled that “the first is entitled to one-quarter of the blood-money, the second to one-third of the blood-money, the third to one-half of the blood-money, and the fourth to the full blood-money.” And he placed that liability upon the tribes of those who had crowded together. So some of the people were satisfied and some were displeased. Then that was referred to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he was informed of the judgment of Ali, Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام, and he approved it.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Six غلامs were brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام who had been in the Euphrates, and one of them drowned. Then three of them testified against two, saying that those two had drowned him, and two testified against the three, saying that the three had drowned him. So ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that three-fifths of the diyah was upon the two, and two-fifths upon the three.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, from 'Ali عليه السلام. Its like.

Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: There was a group who would drink and become intoxicated, then wound one another with knives that were with them. They were brought before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and he imprisoned them. Two men among them died, and two men remained alive. The families of the two slain said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, exact retaliation from these two for our two companions.' So 'Ali عليه السلام said to the people: 'What do you think?' They said: 'We think that you should exact retaliation from them.' 'Ali عليه السلام said: 'Perhaps those two who died each killed his companion.' They said: 'We do not know.' So 'Ali عليه السلام said: 'Rather, I will place the blood-money of the two slain upon the tribes of all four, and I will take the compensation for the wounds of the two remaining from the blood-money of the two slain.'
