And Isma'il ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Artat mentioned, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: 'I was the fourth of them, and 'Ali عليه السلام gave this judgment concerning us.'

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning four men who drank and became intoxicated. Then some of them took up weapons against the others and they fought, so two were killed and two were wounded. He ordered regarding the two wounded that each one of them be flogged with eighty lashes, and he ruled that the blood-money of the two slain was upon the two wounded. He also ordered that the wounds of the two wounded be assessed and deducted from the blood-money; and if one of the two wounded dies, then nothing is due from any of the heirs of the two slain.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi Maryam al-Ansari, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: concerning Regarding two men who joined together in cutting off a man's hand, he عليه السلام said: "If he wishes to have both of their hands cut off, he pays to them the compensation of one hand, and they divide it between themselves; then he cuts off both of their hands. And if he wishes, he may take from them the compensation of one hand." He عليه السلام said: "And if he cuts off one of them, then the one whose hand was not cut off must return to the one whose hand was cut off one quarter of the compensation."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭalḥah, from Ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a wall in whose demolition three men participated. It fell upon one of them and he died, so he held the remaining two liable for his blood money, because each one of them is liable for his companion.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of his companions, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: regarding Concerning a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said: “If he wishes, he may kill the free man; and if he wishes, he may kill the slave. And if he chooses to kill the free man, he strikes the two sides of the slave.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abi Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Mihran, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abi Jamilah, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a slave-girl who rode upon another slave-girl, then another slave-girl poked her, so the one being ridden jolted and threw down the rider, and she died. So he ruled that her blood money be divided into two halves between the one who poked and the one who was poked.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of his companions, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Abī Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said: “If he wishes, he may kill the free man; and if he wishes, he may kill the slave. And if he chooses to kill the free man, he shall strike the two sides of the slave.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman and a slave who killed a man by mistake. He said: “Indeed, the mistake of the woman and the slave is like intentional killing; so if the heirs of the slain wish to kill them both, they may kill them both.” He said: “And if the value of the slave is more than five thousand dirhams, then they must return to his master whatever exceeds five thousand dirhams. And if they wish to kill the woman and take the slave, they may do so, unless his value is more than five thousand dirhams; then they must return to the master of the slave whatever exceeds five thousand dirhams and take the slave. Or his master may ransom him. And if the value of the slave is less than five thousand dirhams, then they have no claim except the slave.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a boy who had not reached maturity and a woman who killed a man by mistake, so he said: "Indeed, the mistaken killing of the woman and the boy is treated as intentional. If the heirs of the slain wish to kill them both, they may kill them both, and they must return to the heirs of the boy five thousand dirhams. And if they wish to kill the boy, they may kill him, and the woman must return to the heirs of the boy one quarter of the blood-money." He said: "And if the heirs of the slain wish to take the blood-money, then half of the blood-money is upon the boy and half of the blood-money is upon the woman." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: I have cited these two narrations because of what they contain of the rulings of intentional killing. As for his statement in the first report, "the mistake of the woman and the slave is intentional," and in the other narration, "the mistake of the woman and the boy is intentional," this contradicts the saying of Allah, the Exalted, because Allah has ruled blood-money rather than retaliation in mistaken killing. So it is not permissible for mistake to be intentional, just as it is not permissible for intentional killing to be mistaken killing, except in the case of one who is not legally responsible, such as the insane and those who are not rational. Also, we have previously presented reports indicating that if a slave kills by mistake, he is handed over to the heirs of the slain, or his master redeems him, and they do not have the right to kill him. Likewise, we have explained that if a child has not reached maturity, then his intentional act is mistaken killing, and his 'aqilah bears the blood-money. So how can it be permissible for us to say in this narration that his mistake is intentional? And if the two reports are as we have said, affected by confusion, then it is not proper to act upon them in what pertains to treating mistake as intentional. However, it appears that the meaning may be that their mistake is intentional according to what some of our opponents regard as mistaken, because among them are those who say that everyone who kills without an iron weapon, then his killing is mistaken. We have already explained the contrary to that, and that killing by any thing whatsoever, if intended, is intentional.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated that from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Regarding a man and a boy who jointly participated in killing a man and so killed him, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: If the boy has reached five spans, qisas is carried out against him; and if he has not reached five spans, judgment is made with the diyah.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about two women who killed a man intentionally. He said: “They shall both be killed for him; no one differs concerning it.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a group of slaves who joined together to kill a free man: what is their ruling? He said: “They are killed for him.” And I asked him about a group of free men who joined together to kill a slave: what is their ruling? He said: “They pay his value.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about four persons who killed a man: a slave, a free man, a free woman, and a mukātab who had paid half of his mukātabah. He said: “The diyah is upon them: upon the free man is one quarter of the diyah, and upon the free woman is one quarter of the diyah. As for the slave, his master is to be given the choice: if he wishes, he pays on his behalf; and if he wishes, he surrenders him in his entirety; his family is not liable for anything. As for the mukātab, half of the quarter is upon him from his property, and half of the quarter is upon those who contracted his mukātabah. That quarter is so because half of him has been emancipated.”
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: For the eye of the one-eyed person, there is the full blood-money.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a one-eyed man whose sound eye was struck and gouged out: that one of the offender’s two eyes should be gouged out, and that half of the diyah should be paid to him; and if he wishes, he may take a full diyah and pardon the eye of his offender.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān, from Abī ʿImrān al-Armanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a sound man who gouged out the eye of a one-eyed man. He said: “The full diyah is upon him. If the one whose eye was gouged wishes to take qisas from his companion and take five thousand dirhams from him, he may do so, because the full diyah belongs to him, and he has taken half of it through qisas.”
ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: For the eye of the one-eyed person, there is a complete blood-money.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abi Jamilah, from Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding the one-eyed eye that remains standing and is sunken, he said: "Ali عليه السلام ruled concerning it that there is half of the diyah of the sound eye."

ʿAlī, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Jamīlah Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who gouged out the eye of a man whose sight was gone while the eye itself remained in place, he said: “Upon him is one quarter of the indemnity (diyah) of the eye.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said: For the tongue of the mute, the eye of the blind, and the penis of the free castrated man and his two testicles, there is one-third of the diyah.

Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Some of the family of Zurārah asked him about a man who cut out the tongue of a mute man. He said, and so he said: If his mother gave birth to him while he was mute, then one-third of the diyah is due upon him. And if his tongue was taken away by pain or an affliction after he had been speaking, then upon the one who cut out his tongue is one-third of the diyah of his tongue. He said: “And likewise is the judgment concerning the two eyes and the limbs.” He said: “And thus we found it in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who cut off the withered hand of another man, he said: "Upon him is one-third of the diyah."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, from some of our companions, who said: Al-Rabīʿ came to Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr while he was the caliph and was in ṭawāf, and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, so-and-so, your mawlā, died last night, and so-and-so, your mawlā, cut off his head after his death.” He said: So he became enraged and angry. He then said to Ibn Shubrumah, Ibn Abī Laylā, and a number of judges and fuqahāʾ: “What do you say regarding this?” Each one said: “We have nothing on this matter.” He continued repeating the question and saying: “Should I kill him or not?” They said: “We have nothing on this matter.” Then some of them said to him: “A man has just arrived now; if anyone has an answer to this, then he has the answer to it, and he is Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he has entered the saʿy.” So he said to al-Rabīʿ: “Go to him and say to him: Were it not for our knowing of the engagement you are in, we would have asked you to come to us; but answer us regarding such-and-such.” He said: So al-Rabīʿ came to him while he was on al-Marwah and conveyed the message to him. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “You can see the occupation I am engaged in, and before you are the fuqahāʾ and the scholars, so ask them.” He said to him: “He has asked them, but they had nothing on it.” He said: So he repeated it to him, and said: “I ask you only that you answer us regarding it, for the people have nothing on this matter.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him: “Until I finish what I am engaged in.” He said: Then when he had finished, he came and sat at the side of al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and said to al-Rabīʿ: “Go and say to him: ‘One hundred dinars are due upon him.’” He said: So he conveyed that to him, and they said to him: “Then ask him how one hundred dinars became due upon him.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “For the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the ʿalaqah twenty, for the muḍghah twenty, for the bone twenty, and for the flesh twenty: ‘ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ’; and this dead person is in his rank like that before the spirit is breathed into him in his mother’s womb, as a fetus.” He said: So he returned to him and informed him of the answer, and that impressed them. They said: “Go back to him and ask him: the dinars, for whom are they? For his heirs or not?” So Abū ʿAbdillāh ع

As for what Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "Cutting off the head of the dead is more severe than cutting off the head of the living."

Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Safwan said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Allah has refused that anything be thought of the believer except good, and your breaking his bones, whether he is alive or dead, is the same.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Mismāʿ Kirdīn, said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who broke the bone of a dead person. He said: “His sanctity when dead is greater than his sanctity while he is alive.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports do not contradict the first report stating that the diyah of the dead person is one hundred dinars, because there is nothing in any of these reports stating that the sanctity of the dead person is exactly like the sanctity of the living person, or that breaking his hand is more severe than breaking the hand of the living person, and whatever is of that kind in requiring diyah equal to the diyah of the living. If that is not present in them, then it is possible that what is intended is that his sanctity is like the sanctity of the living in that whoever breaks one of his limbs or cuts it deserves punishment and some portion of the diyah, even if it is not complete. This is not found with any of the dead besides the human being, so from this aspect his sanctity is like the sanctity of the living.

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Abī Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said: A dead person whose head was cut off? He said: “The diyah is due upon him.” I said: Then who takes his diyah? He said: “The Imam. This is for Allah; and if his right hand or anything from his limbs is cut, then the indemnity is due to the Imam.”

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān and Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning a man who cut off the head of a dead person: He said: “The diyah is upon him, because his sanctity in death is like his sanctity while he is alive.”

And among what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from one who informed him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who cut off the head of a dead man. He said: «The indemnity is upon him, for indeed his sanctity in death is like his sanctity while he is alive.»

Concerning a man who cut off the head of a dead person, he said: “The diyah is upon him, because his sanctity when dead is like his sanctity while he is alive.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports also do not contradict what we have presented earlier, because in his statement, peace be upon him, “the diyah is upon him,” there is nothing explicit in their outward wording specifying the amount of that diyah, nor whether it is the diyah of a person or the diyah of a fetus. Since that is not stated in them, we interpret them to mean that in this case there is the diyah of a fetus, and the term diyah may be applied to that; and what indicates this is what he narrated: And what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: concerning...

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid. And it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ashyam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said: We have narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام a hadith that I would like to hear from you. He said, “And what is it?” I said: It has reached me that he said regarding a man who cut off the head of a dead man, that he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Indeed Allah has made unlawful from the Muslim when dead what He made unlawful from him when alive; so whoever does to a dead person that by which the life of a living person would be destroyed, then blood money is due upon him.” He said: “Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام spoke the truth; this is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said it.” I said: If someone cuts off the head of a dead man, or splits open his abdomen, or does to him an act such that, were it done to a living person, it would destroy his life, is full blood money for a life due upon him? He said, “No.” Then he pointed to me with his little finger and said to me, “Is there not blood money for this?” I said: Yes. He said, “Do you consider it the blood money of a whole life?” I said: No. He said, “You have spoken correctly.” I said: Then what is the blood money for this, if his head is cut off while he is dead? He said, “Its blood money is the blood money of the fetus in its mother’s womb before the spirit is formed in it, and that is one hundred dinars.” He said: Then I fell silent, and what he answered me about it pleased me. He said, “Why do you not complete your question?” I said: I do not have anything more about it than what you have answered me, unless there is something I do not know. He said: “The blood money of the fetus, when its mother is struck and it falls from her womb before the spirit is formed in it, is one hundred dinars, and it belongs to its heirs. But the blood money of this one, if his head is cut off or his abdomen is split open, does not belong to his heirs; rather it belongs to him, apart from the heirs.” I said: And what is the difference between them? He said: “The fetus is one facing the future, whose benefit is hoped for, whereas this one has passed on and his benefit has gone. So when he is mutilated after his

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from his father, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them: “It was established concerning...” For the blackened tooth, one-third of its diyah; for the paralyzed hand, one-third of its diyah; for the standing eye when its sight is effaced, one-third of its diyah; for the earlobe, one-third of its diyah; for the lame leg, one-third of its diyah; and for the soft parts of the nose, in each one there is one-third of the diyah.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled, regarding injuries of the body, that there is qisas in them, or the injured person may accept the compensation for the wound, and it is to be given to him.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام: Regarding a man who broke another man’s hand, then the man’s hand healed, he عليه السلام said: “There is no qiṣāṣ in this, but al-arsh is to be given.”

From him, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a tooth and an arm that are broken intentionally: is there indemnity for them, or retaliation? He said: "Retaliation." He said: I said: then if they satisfy him with whatever he wishes, it is his.

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A one-eyed man put out the eye of a sound man. So he said: “His eye is to be put out.” He said: I said: He would remain blind? He said: “The truth has blinded him.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a one-eyed man who deliberately put out the eye of a sound man. He said: “His eye shall be put out.” I said: Then he would become blind. He said: “The right has made him blind.”

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "A man's hand and his two legs are cut in qisas."

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Sulaymān al-Dahhān, from Rifāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “ʿUmar was approached by a man from Qays with a mawlā of his who had struck his eye, causing fluid to descend into it while it remained standing, yet he could not see anything with it. So he said to him: ‘I will give you the diyah,’ but he refused.” He said: “So he sent them both to ʿAlī عليه السلام and said: ‘Judge between these two.’ So he offered him the diyah, but he refused.” He said: “They continued offering him more until they offered him two diyahs.” He said: “Then he said: ‘I want nothing but qiṣāṣ.’” He said: “Then ʿAlī عليه السلام called for a mirror and heated it. Then he called for cotton and moistened it. Then he placed it upon the edges of his eyes and around them. Then he faced the sun directly with his eyes.” He said: “And he brought the mirror and said: ‘Look.’ So he looked, and the fatty substance melted while his eye remained standing, and the sight went away.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn al-'Abbas ibn al-Harish, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Awwal عليه السلام said to 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas: “O Ibn 'Abbas, I adjure you by Allah, is there any difference in the حكم of Allah?” He said: So he replied: “No.” He said: “Then what do you think regarding a man whose fingers were struck by the sword until they fell off and were lost, then another man came and cut off the palm of his hand? Then he was brought to you while you were a judge—what would you do?” He said: “I would say to this cutter: Give him the diyah of a palm; and I would say to this injured man: Make a settlement with him on whatever you wish; or I would send to them two just men.” He said: So he said to him: “Difference has entered into the حكم of Allah, and you have contradicted the first statement. Allah refuses that He should institute in His creation anything from the prescribed limits without its explanation being on the earth. Cut off the hand of the one who cut off the palm at its root, then give him the diyah of the fingers. This is the حكم of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who intentionally killed a man, while the one killed had his right hand severed. So he said: If his hand had been cut off due to an offense that he committed against himself, or he had been cut and had taken the compensation for his hand from the one who cut it off, then if his heirs wish to kill his killer, they must pay to the heirs of his killer the blood-money of the hand by which equality was deficient, and then kill him. And if they wish, they may deduct the blood-money of his hand from him and take the remainder. He said: If his hand had been cut off without an offense that he committed against himself, and no compensation had been taken for it, they may kill his killer and he is not liable for anything. And if they wish, they may take the full blood-money. Thus did we find it in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a slap whose mark turns black on the face that its compensation is six dinars. If it does not turn black but turns green, then its compensation is three dinars. If it turns red and does not turn green, then its compensation is one and a half dinars. Then he said: As for wounds of the body, retaliation applies in them, unless the injured person accepts the indemnity for the wound, in which case it is given to him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, 'Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, ordered Qanbar to administer a hadd punishment to a man, but Qanbar erred and gave him three lashes more than eighty. So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام exacted retribution from Qanbar, and Qanbar was flogged three lashes.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abī al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about one upon whom the prescribed punishment was carried out and he died: is retaliation to be taken from him, or is his blood-money to be paid? He said: “No, unless there was an excess beyond the retaliation.”

ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from one who informed him, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a man who had killed another man’s brother. So he handed him over to him and ordered him to kill him. The man struck him until he thought that he had killed him, and he was carried to his home. They found in him some remaining life, so they treated him until he recovered. Then when he came out, the brother of the slain man seized him and said: “You are the killer of my brother, and I have the right to kill you.” He said to him: “You have already killed me once.” So he took him to ʿUmar, and he ordered that he be killed. Then he came out saying: “O people, by Allah, he has killed me.” They passed by with him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and he informed him of his case. So he said: “Do not hasten against him until I come out to you.” Then he entered upon ʿUmar and said: “The judgment regarding him is not like this.” He said: “What is it, O Abā al-Ḥasan?” He said: “This man should exact retaliation from the brother of the first slain man equal to what he did to him, then he may kill him for his brother.” So he realized that if he were to exact retaliation from him, it would destroy his own life; thus he pardoned him, and they left one another.

ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl, from some of his companions, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them: Concerning a man who broke another man's hand, then the man's hand healed, he said: “There is no qisas in this case, but the arsh is to be given.”

Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: A man was brought before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام who had stepped on a man's stomach until he defecated in his clothes. So he judged against him that his stomach be stepped on until he defecates, or else he must pay one-third of the blood-money.
ʿAlī narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever retaliation is carried out upon, and he dies, then he is one slain by the Qur'an.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Whoever is killed by qisas by the order of the Imam, then there is no diyah for him in the killing nor for any wound.

From him, from Abī Jaʿfar, from Abī al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: There is no qisas between men and women except in the case of life; and there is no qisas between free persons and slaves except in the case of life, intentionally; and there is no qisas among children in anything except in the case of life.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both. A man cut off something from part of another man's ear, and that was brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he exacted retaliation from him. Then the other man took what had been cut from his ear and replaced it onto his ear with its blood, and it reattached and healed. So the first man returned to ʿAlī عليه السلام and sought retaliation, so he ordered it, and it was cut a second time, and he ordered that it be buried. And he عليه السلام said: “Retaliation is only on account of the disfigurement.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: There is no qisas between slaves and free persons in matters short of the life, and there is no qisas between the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian in matters short of the life.

And with this chain of transmission: Concerning a slave who put out the eye of a free man, while the slave had a debt upon him, he said: Let his eye be put out, and let the debt of the creditors be nullified.

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn, from Ḥarīz and Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked him about a dhimmī who cut off the hand of a Muslim. He said: "His hand is cut off, if his heirs wish, and they take the difference between the two blood-monies. And if the Muslim cuts off the hand of the muʿāhad, the heirs of the muʿāhad are given the choice: if they wish, they take the blood-money for his hand; and if they wish, they cut off the hand of the Muslim and pay him the difference between the two blood-monies. And if the Muslim kills him, it is done likewise."

Al-Saffar, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far عليه السلام, that Ali عليه السلام used to say: “There is no qisas in a bone.” And Ja'far عليه السلام said: “A man killed a woman, so Ali عليه السلام did not establish qisas between them, and he obligated him to pay the diyah.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, in the book of ʿAlī عليه السلام, it is stated: “If a man were to sever a woman’s private part, I would make him liable to pay her its blood-money. Then if he did not pay her its blood-money, I would sever his private part for her, if she requested that.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: The blood-money of the fetus is five portions: one-fifth for the drop of fluid, twenty dīnārs; for the clot, two-fifths, forty dīnārs; for the lump of flesh, three-fifths, sixty dīnārs; for the bone, four-fifths, eighty dīnārs. When the fetus is complete, it is one hundred dīnārs. When the spirit is produced in it, then its blood-money is one thousand dīnārs, or ten thousand dirhams, if it is male; and if it is female, then five hundred dīnārs. If a woman is killed while she is pregnant, and it is not known whether her child was male or female, then its blood-money for the child is in two halves: half of the blood-money of a male and half of the blood-money of a female; and her blood-money is complete.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Sulayman ibn Salih, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: For the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the 'alaqah forty dinars, for the mudghah sixty dinars, and for the bone eighty dinars. Then when it is clothed with flesh, it is one hundred dinars; then it remains one hundred dinars until it cries out at birth. He said: “Then when it cries out at birth, the diyah is complete.”

ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghālib, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام about a man who struck a pregnant woman with his foot, and she cast out what was in her womb dead. He said: “If it was a drop of fluid, then twenty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the drop of fluid? He said: “It is that which has fallen into the womb and remained settled there for forty days.” He said: “If she cast it out while it was a clot, then forty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the clot? He said: “It is that which, when it falls into the womb, remains settled there for eighty days.” He said: “If she cast it out while it was a morsel of flesh, then sixty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the morsel of flesh? He said: “It is that which, when it falls into the womb, remains settled there for one hundred and twenty days.” He said: “If she cast it out while it was a formed living being, having bone and flesh, with its limbs arranged, and the spirit of intellect had been breathed into it, then a full indemnity is due from him.” I said to him: Inform me about its transformation in her womb from one state to another—was that with a spirit, or without a spirit? He said: “With the spirit of the nourishment of life, ancient and transmitted through the loins of men and the wombs of women. Were it not that the spirit of the nourishment of life was in it, it would not have transformed from one state after another in the womb, and then there would not be indemnity upon the one who killed it while it was in that state.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abi Jarir al-Qummi, who said: I asked al-ʿAbd عليه السلام about the nuṭfah, what diyah is due for it, and what is due for the ʿalaqah, and what is due for the formed muḍghah, and that which becomes established in the wombs. He said: 'Indeed, it is created in its mother's womb, one creation after another: it is a nuṭfah for forty days, then it becomes an ʿalaqah for forty days, then a muḍghah for forty days. So for the nuṭfah there are forty dinars, for the ʿalaqah sixty dinars, for the muḍghah eighty dinars, and when the bones are clothed with flesh, then for it there are one hundred dinars. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:' “Then We produced him as another creation; so blessed is Allah, the best of creators.” 'So if it is male, then for it is the diyah, and if it is female, then for her is her diyah.'

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who strikes a woman and she miscarries the nuṭfah, and he said: “He is liable for twenty dinars.” I said: If he strikes her and she miscarries the ʿalaqah? He said: “Forty dinars.” I said: If he strikes her and she miscarries the muḍghah? He said: “He is liable for sixty dinars.” I said: If he strikes her and she miscarries it after bone has formed for it? He said: “He is liable for the full diyah, and by this Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام judged.” I said: What is the description of the nuṭfah by which it is recognized? He said: “The nuṭfah is white, like thick mucus, and it remains in the رحم; when it has been there for forty days, it then becomes an ʿalaqah.” I said: What is the description of the formation of the ʿalaqah by which it is recognized? He said: “It is an ʿalaqah like a clotted mass of cupped blood, congealed; it remains in the رحم for forty days after its transformation from the nuṭfah, then it becomes a muḍghah.” I said: What is the description of the formation of the muḍghah and its form by which it is recognized? He said: “It is a muḍghah, red flesh, in which are interwoven green veins; then it becomes bone.” I said: What is the description of its creation when it is bone? He said: “When it is bone, hearing and sight are opened for it and its limbs are arranged; when it is like that, then the full diyah applies for it.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning two horsemen who collided, and one of them died; so he held the surviving one liable for the blood money of the deceased.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah; and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Yūnus al-Shaybānī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: If a drop of blood appears in the nuṭfah? He said: “The drop is one-tenth of the nuṭfah; in it there are twenty-two dinars.” He said: I said: If it drips two drops? He said: “Twenty-four dinars.” He said: I said: If three drops drip? He said: “Twenty-six dinars.” I said: Then four? He said: “Twenty-eight dinars; and for five, thirty. Whatever exceeds the half is calculated accordingly until it becomes an ʿalaqah; when it becomes an ʿalaqah, then in it there are forty.” Then Abū Shibl said to him—and Abū Shibl informed us, saying: I was present with Yūnus while Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was informing him about blood-money. He said: I said: What if the nuṭfah came out mixed and stirred with blood? He said, and said to me: “Then it has become an ʿalaqah, if it is pure blood; in that case, there are forty dinars. But if it is black blood, then nothing is due upon him except taʿzīr, because whatever is pure blood belongs to the child, and whatever is black blood, that is from the interior.” Abū Shibl said: If the ʿalaqah has developed something resembling veins of flesh? He said: “Forty-two dinars, one-tenth.” He said: I said: One-tenth of forty is four. So he said: “No, rather it is one-tenth of the muḍghah, because only one-tenth of it has gone; so whenever it increases, it is increased until it reaches sixty.” He said: I said: If you see in the muḍghah something like a knot, a dry bone? He said: “Then that is bone; thus is the first stage at which bone begins. It begins at five months, and in it there are four dinars. If it increases, then add four by four until it completes eighty.” He said: I said: And likewise when the bone is clothed with flesh? He said: “Likewise.” He said: I said: If he strikes her and the child falls, and it is not known whether it was alive or not? He said: “Far from it, O Abū Shibl. When the five months have passed, life has come into it, and the blood-money has become due.”

Salih ibn 'Uqbah narrated from Yunus al-Shaybani, who said: I was present, along with Abu Shibl, before Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, so I asked him about these issues concerning blood-money. Then Abu Shibl asked, and he was more intense in pressing the matter, so I left him until he had exhausted it thoroughly.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl and Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, all of them said: We presented the Book of Inheritances from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and he said: “It is sound.” And among what it contained was: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام fixed the diyah of the fetus at one hundred dinars, and he made the semen of the man, until it becomes a fetus, into five parts. So when it is a fetus before the spirit enters into it, it is one hundred dinars. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the human being from an extract, and that is the drop of fluid; this is one part. Then a clot, so that is two parts. Then a lump of flesh, three parts. Then bone, so that is four parts. Then it is clothed with flesh; at that point it has become a complete fetus, and its five parts are complete: one hundred dinars. And the one hundred dinars are five parts, so he assigned to the drop one-fifth of the hundred, twenty dinars; to the clot, two-fifths of the hundred, forty dinars; to the lump of flesh, three-fifths of the hundred, sixty dinars; and to the bone, four-fifths of the hundred, eighty dinars. Then when another creation is produced in it, namely the spirit, then at that point it is a soul: one thousand full dinars if it is male, and if it is female then five hundred dinars. And if a woman is killed while pregnant, and the pregnancy had become complete but she did not cast out her child, and it is not known whether it was male or female, and it is not known whether it died after her or before her, then its diyah is two halves: half the diyah of a male and half the diyah of a female. And the diyah of the woman is complete after that, and that is six parts in relation to the fetus. And he عليه السلام gave the ruling regarding the semen of a man who is startled away from his bride, so he withholds the fluid from her without intending that: half of one-fifth of the hundred, ten dinars; and if he discharges in her, then twenty dinars. And he ruled regarding the diyah for injuries to the fetus from the basis of the hundred, according to what applies in the injuries of the male and female, the man and the woman, in full. And he assigned for it retaliation concerning its injury and its indemnity in proportion to its diyah, which is one hundred dinars.”

As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: If a man strikes a pregnant woman and she miscarries what is in her womb dead, then upon him is a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave, which he gives to her.

ʿAlī narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled concerning the fetus of the Hilāliyyah woman, when she was struck with a stone and miscarried what was in her womb dead, that there is upon him a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave.

From him, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: A woman came and lodged a complaint against a Bedouin who had terrified her, causing her to miscarry her fetus. The Bedouin said, “It did not cry out, nor did it make a sound, and the like of it is disregarded without compensation.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Be silent, rhyming speaker. Upon you is a ghurrah: a servant youth, male or female.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and had struck a pregnant woman, causing her to miscarry a stillborn fetus. Then the woman’s husband came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and sought redress against him, and he said: The assailant said: O Messenger of Allah, it neither ate nor drank, nor did it cry out, nor scream, nor show any sign of life. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, you are a rhyming man.” Then he ruled concerning it that a slave be given.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī ʿUbaydah and al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who killed a woman by mistake while she was in labor with her child. He said: “Five thousand dirhams, and upon him is the diyah of the one in her womb: a ghurrah, a male servant or a female servant, or forty dinars.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports do not contradict what we presented earlier, that the diyah of the fetus is one hundred dinars, because those reports are to be understood as referring to a fetus that had become complete and full-formed, except that the spirit had not yet entered it. This report is to be understood as referring to a woman who miscarries a clot or a lump of flesh, so its diyah is a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave. Thus there is no contradiction between them in any way, and what indicates what we have said is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning A woman drank medicine while she was pregnant in order to cast out her child, and she expelled her child. He said: “If it had bone and flesh had grown upon it, and hearing and sight had been opened for it, then its blood-money is upon her, which she gives to its father.” He said: “And if it was a fetus, a clot, or a morsel of flesh, then forty dinars or a ghurrah are upon her, which she gives to its father.” I said: So she does not inherit from her child’s blood-money? He said: “No, because she killed him.” And this interpretation does not conflict with the narration of al-Halabi and Abi 'Ubaydah that the woman was in labor, because it is not impossible that she was in labor even if the child had not reached full development when it was a miscarriage; therefore, there is no objection on any account.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I said to Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, the ghurrah may be one hundred dinars, and it may be ten dinars. So he said: “Fifty.”
From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the ghurrah may increase and decrease, but its value is forty dinars.

Ibn Mahbub, from Nuʿaym ibn Ibrahim, from Mismāʿ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning A man who killed the fetus of a slave-woman belonging to some people while it was in her womb—he said: "If it died in her womb after he struck her, then half of one-tenth of the value of the slave-woman is due from him; and if he struck her and she cast it out alive, then one-tenth of the value of its mother is due from him."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, and she miscarried a stillborn fetus. So the woman's husband sought legal redress against him. Then the woman said to her husband: If there is blood money for this fetus, and I have an inheritance share in it, then my share of inheritance from it belongs to my father. He said: "What she has bestowed upon her father is permissible for him."
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid: the like of it. And he said: “Her father pays to her husband two-thirds of the blood-money of the miscarried fetus.”
Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sukuni, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: "The ghurrah increases and decreases, but its value is five hundred dirhams."
And from him, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Regarding the fetus of a beast, if she miscarries it, then one-tenth of its price is due.”
And from him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: For the fetus of a female slave, one-tenth of her price is due.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام. That he ruled concerning the fetus of a Jewish, Christian, and Magian woman that its compensation is one-tenth of the blood-money of its mother.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sa'id ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: For the mudihah, there are five camels; for the simhaq, which is less than the mudihah, there are four camels; for the munaqqilah, there are fifteen camels; for the ja'ifah, there is one-third of the diyah, thirty-three camels; and for the ma'mumah, there is one-third of the diyah.

From him, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For the muwaddiḥah injury there are five camels; for the simḥāq, four camels; for the bāḍiʿah, three camels; for the maʾmūmah, thirty-three camels; for the jāʾifah, thirty-three camels; and for the munaqqilah, fifteen camels.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For the muwaddiḥah there are five camels; for the simḥāq there are four camels; for the bāḍiʿah there are three camels; for the maʾmūmah there are thirty-three camels; and for the munaqqilah there are fifteen camels.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: ‘The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled that for the ma'mumah there is one-third of the diyah, for the munaqqilah fifteen camels, for the mudihah five camels, for the damiyah one camel, for the badi'ah two camels, and he ruled for the mutalahimah three camels, and he ruled for the simhaq four camels.’

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ruled concerning the dāmiyah: one camel; the bāḍiʿah: two camels; the mutalāḥimah: three camels; and the simḥāq: four camels."

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding wounds in the fingers: when the bone becomes exposed, it is one-half of one-tenth of the blood-money of the finger, if the injured person does not wish to retaliate in equal measure.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: We asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the maʾmūmah wound, so he said: In it is one-third of the diyah, and in the jāʾifah is one-third of the diyah, and in the mūḍiḥah are five camels.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the maʾmūmah wound, and he said: “One-third of the diyah; and the jāʾifah wound is one-third of the diyah.” And I asked him about the mūḍiḥah, and he said: “Five camels.”

From him, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Maryam, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “O Abā Maryam, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has written a document for Ibn Ḥazm regarding the charities, so take it from him and bring it to me so that I may look at it.” He said: So I went to him and took the document from him, then I brought it to him and presented it before him. In it were chapters on charities and chapters on blood-money, and in it was: “For the eye, fifty; for the jāʾifah wound, one-third; for the munaqqilah, fifteen; and for the mūḍiḥah, five camels.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thawrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the muwaddiḥah wound on the head—whether it is as it is on the face. He said: “The muwaddiḥah and the shijaj wounds on the head and the face are equal in the indemnity, because the face is part of the head; and wounds on the body are not like those on the head.”

And from him, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Razīn, from Dharīḥ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who inflicted upon another man a wound exposing the bone, and another inflicted upon him a bleeding wound in one and the same incident, then the man died. He said: “The diyyah is upon the two of them from their property, in two equal halves.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from 'Abd Allah ibn Talhah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Concerning a man who inflicted upon another man a wound of the type muwdihah, then reparation for it was sought, but he remitted it to him, then it worsened in him and killed him. He said: “He is liable for the diyah, except for the value of the muwdihah, because he remitted that to him, and he did not remit the life.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام; and from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, who said: I presented the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and he said: “It is authentic. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning the blood-money for injuries to all the limbs—in the head, the face, and the rest of the body; hearing, sight, voice, intellect, the two hands, and the two legs—in cases of severing, fracture, cracking, crushing, exposing the bone, bleeding wounds, displacement of bones, and penetrating wounds, whenever any of that occurs. So whatever bone is broken and then heals without deformity or defect, and no bone is displaced from it, then its blood-money is known. If it exposes the bone and no bones are displaced from it, then its fracture and the blood-money of its exposing wound are established; and the blood-money of every bone that is broken is known, and the displacement of its bones is half the blood-money of its fracture, and the blood-money of its exposing wound is one quarter of the blood-money of its fracture, in those parts covered by clothing, excluding the two bones of the forearm and the fingers. And regarding the blood-money of the amputated part, it is one third of the blood-money of that bone in which it is found. And he gave the legal ruling concerning a penetrating wound, when it penetrates from a spear or a dagger into some part of a man’s limbs, that its blood-money is one tenth of the blood-money of the man: one hundred dinars.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the forearm when it is struck and broken at the wrist joint. He said: “If the hand withers from it, and all the fingers of the hand become paralyzed, then in that there is two-thirds of the diyah, the diyah of the hand.” He said: “And if some of the fingers are paralyzed while some remain, then for every finger that is paralyzed there is two-thirds of its diyah.” He said: “And likewise is the ruling regarding the leg and the foot when the toes of the foot become paralyzed.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a penetrating wound that occurs in a limb that its compensation is one-third of the diyah of that limb.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ẓarīf, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: For the ḥārisah, which is like a scratch, there is one camel; for the dāmiyah, two camels; for the bāḍiʿah, which is less than the simḥāq, three camels; for the simḥāq, which is less than the mūḍiḥah, four camels; and for the mūḍiḥah, five camels.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni. That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning the hashimah that it carries compensation of ten camels.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: For injuries less than al-simhāq, the compensation is the physician’s fee.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Concerning a man who inflicted a muḍiḥah wound upon a slave, he said: “Upon him is one-half of one-tenth of the slave’s value, payable to the slave’s master, and the slave’s price is not to exceed the blood-money of a free person.”

Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sukuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning a slave who inflicted a clarifying head wound upon a man, then another inflicted a wound; he said: “It is divided between the two of them.”

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Zarif, from Abi Hamzah: For the wound that exposes the bone there are five camels; and for the simhaq, below the mudihah, there are four camels. For the munaqqilah there are fifteen camels, a tenth and a half of a tenth. As for the ja'ifah, which penetrates into the body cavity, there is no qisas in it, only assessed compensation. And the munaqqilah is that from which the bones are displaced, and there is no qisas in it, only assessed compensation. As for the ma'mumah, there is no fixed assessed compensation for it. The ma'mumah is a blow that lands on the head: if it is from a sword, then it cuts through everything and cuts the bone, reaching the struck person’s brain; and sometimes his tongue becomes heavy, and sometimes his hearing becomes heavy, and sometimes confusion overtakes him. And if he is struck with a pillar or with a severe staff, then it reaches even more intensely than cutting; from it the skullcap is broken, the skullcap of the head.
Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sukuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Indeed, the muwaddihah in the face and the head are equal.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a slap whose mark turns black on the face that its compensation is six dinars. If it does not turn black but turns green, then its compensation is three dinars. If it turns red and does not turn green, then its compensation is one dinar and a half. He said: As for injuries of the body, then in them there is qisas, unless the wounded person accepts the blood-money compensation for the injury, in which case it is given to him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub ibn Fiyhas al-Bajali, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far عليه السلام, that 'Ali عليه السلام used to say: No judgment is to be passed regarding any of the wounds until it heals.

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: “The wounds of slaves are assessed in accordance with the wounds of free persons, in proportion to the price.”

A man called ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ayyūb narrated to me. He said: Abū ʿAmr al-Mutaṭabbib narrated to me. He said: I presented this narration to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. And ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, and Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, all from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: We presented the book to him, and he said: “Yes, it is true, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to command his officials according to it.” He said: “He عليه السلام gave a stated legal assessment for every bone containing marrow when it is broken and then heals without deformity or defect. He divided the prescribed blood-money into six parts, and assigned for the spirit, the fetus, the eyelids, paralysis, the limbs, and the thumb, six prescribed shares for each part. He set the blood-money of the fetus at one hundred dinars, and made the semen of the man up until it becomes a fetus five stages. If it is a fetus before the spirit enters it, it is one hundred dinars. For the drop of fluid he assigned twenty dinars—when a man is startled away from his bride and emits the drop without intending it, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام fixed twenty dinars in it, one-fifth. For the clot he assigned two-fifths of that, forty dinars; and likewise for a woman if she is struck or attacked and miscarries it. Then for the lump of flesh, sixty dinars, if the woman miscarries it in such a case. Then for the bone, eighty dinars, if the woman miscarries it. Then for the fetus also, one hundred dinars, if an enemy attacks them and the women miscarry in such a case; he imposed that upon the women from the side of the collective indemnity likewise. If the child is born and cries out—meaning the crying—and then they attack by night and kill the children, then for them there is one thousand dinars for the male, and for the female according to this same reckoning, five hundred dinars. As for the woman, if she is killed while carrying a full-term pregnancy and she does not cast out her child, and it is not known whether it is male or female, and it is not known whether it died after her or before her, then its blood-money is two halves: half the blood-money of a male and half the blood-money of a female; and then the blood-money of the woman is complete after that. He also gave a ruling concerning the semen of a man who is startled away from his bride and withdraws the fluid from her with
Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from Abī al-ʿAbbās, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Whoever puts out the eye of a beast, then one-quarter of its price is due upon him.”

And from him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام asking him about a narration of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī which he narrates from ʿAlī عليه السلام. "Regarding the eye of a four-legged animal, if it is gouged out, then one quarter of its price is due." So he said: "Al-Ḥasan has spoken the truth; ʿAlī عليه السلام indeed said that."

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled concerning the eye of a horse that was gouged out: one quarter of its price on the day the eye was gouged out.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mismā‘ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام. That Ali عليه السلام ruled regarding the eye of a beast that its compensation is one quarter of the price.

And with this chain of narration, from Mismāʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was presented with a man who had killed a pig, so he held him liable for compensation; and a man was presented to him who had broken a barbat, so he nullified it.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Walīd ibn Ṣabīḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The blood-money for the Salūqī dog is forty dirhams. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded that, that he should pay its compensation to Banū Judhaymah.

From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: The diyyah of the Saluqi dog is forty dirhams; the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم assigned that for it. The diyyah of the sheep dog is a ram, the diyyah of the farm dog is a jarib of wheat, and the diyyah of the house dog is a qafiz of dust for its owner.

Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Regarding one who kills a hunting dog, he said: its value is to be assessed; and likewise the hunting hawk, and likewise the sheep dog, and likewise the orchard/watch dog.”

From him, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Regarding the fetus of a beast, if it is struck and it miscarries, one-tenth of its price is due.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Khalaf, from Mūsā ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazawfarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning two horsemen who collided, and one of them died; so he held the surviving one liable for the blood-money of the deceased.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام would not impose liability for what grazing animals damaged during the day, and he would say: “The owner of the crop is responsible for protecting his crop.” But he would impose liability for what grazing animals damaged at night.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about four who testified against a man for zina, then after he was killed, one of them retracted his testimony. He said: So he said, "The one who retracts is killed, and the other three shall pay to his family three-quarters of the diyah."

Concerning two men who testified against a man that he stole, so his hand was cut, then one of them retracted and said, “I was mistaken about this one, but it was someone else”: half of the blood-money of the hand is due from him, and his testimony regarding the other person is not accepted. If both retract together and say, “We were mistaken; rather, the thief was so-and-so,” then the blood-money of the hand is due from them, and their testimony regarding the other person is not accepted. If they say, “We did it deliberately,” the hand of one of them is cut in return for the hand of the one whose hand was cut, and the one whose hand is not cut pays back one quarter of the full blood-money of a man to the guardians of the man whose hand was cut. If the first amputee says, “I do not consent unless both of their hands are cut together,” then he returns the blood-money of one hand, to be divided between them, and both of their hands are cut.

Ibn Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning Four men testified against a muhsan man for zina, then one of them retracted after the man had been killed. He said: “If the one who retracts says, ‘I was mistaken,’ he is given the hadd punishment and made liable for the blood-money; but if he says, ‘I did it deliberately,’ he is killed.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mismāʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning four men who testified against a man that they had seen him with a woman, having intercourse with her, so he was stoned; then one of them recanted. He said: He is liable for one quarter of the diyah if he says, ‘It was made to seem so to me.’ If two recant and say, ‘It was made to seem so to us,’ they are liable for half of the diyah. If they all recant and say, ‘It was made to seem so to us,’ they are liable for the full diyah. But if they say, ‘We gave false testimony,’ they shall all be killed.

ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to detain in a blood accusation for six days; then if the heirs of the slain came with a proof that established it, otherwise he would let them go.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿĀṣimī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There was a woman in al-Madīnah to whom men used to come. That reached ʿUmar, so he sent for her, frightened her, and ordered that she be brought to him. The woman became terrified, labor pains seized her, and she went off to one of the houses and gave birth to a boy. The boy cried out at birth, then died. Because of the woman’s terror and the death of the boy, distress entered upon him. Some of those sitting with him said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, there is nothing upon you in this.” And some of them said, “What is this?” He said, “Ask Abā al-Ḥasan.” So Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to them: “If you exercised ijtihad, then you were not correct; and if you spoke by your own opinion, you have certainly erred.” Then he said: “The blood-money of the child is upon you.”

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Khalid, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: I was with Dawud ibn ʿAli when a man who had killed another man was brought to him. Dawud ibn ʿAli said to him, “What do you say? Did you kill this man?” He said, “Yes, I killed him.” He said, “Dawud then said to him, ‘And why did you kill him?’” He said, “He replied: He used to enter upon me in my house without my permission, so I sought help against him from the governors who were before you, and they instructed me that if he entered without my permission, I should kill him. So I killed him.” He said: Dawud then turned to me and said, “O Aba ʿAbdillah, what do you say regarding this?” He said: I said to him, “I hold that he has confessed to killing a Muslim man, so execute him.” He said: So he ordered concerning him, and he was executed. Then Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: “Some people from the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were gathered, and among them was Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah. They said, ‘O Saʿd, what would you say if you went to your house and found in it a man upon the belly of your wife—what would you do to him?’ He said: Saʿd replied, ‘By Allah, I would strike his neck with the sword.’ He said: Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came out while they were in that conversation and said, ‘O Saʿd, who is this one about whom you said: I would strike his neck with the sword?’” He said: “So he was informed of what they had said and what Saʿd had said.” He said: “Thereupon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘O Saʿd, then where are the four witnesses whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned?’” He said: “Saʿd said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, even after the sight of my own eyes and Allah’s knowledge concerning him that he has indeed done it?’” The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Yes, by Allah, O Saʿd—even after the sight of your own eyes and Allah’s knowledge that he has indeed done it. Allah, Exalted is He, has set for everything a limit, and has set a penalty upon whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, and He has made what is short of four witnesses concealed among the Muslims.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام: Concerning a man who made a bequest of his one-third, then was killed by mistake, he said: one-third of his blood-money is included in his bequest.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from al-Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAmr, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: that Muʿāwiyah - may Allah curse him - wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī that Ibn Abī al-Jasrayn found a man with his wife and killed him, and judgment regarding it had become unclear to me, so ask ʿAlī about this matter for me. He said: Abū Mūsā said: I met ʿAlī, and ʿAlī said: “By Allah, this is not in these lands,” meaning al-Kūfah, “nor has this occurred in my presence, so from where did this come to you?” I said: Muʿāwiyah - may Allah curse him - wrote to me that Ibn Abī al-Jasrayn found a man with his wife and killed him, and judgment concerning it had become unclear to him, so what is your view regarding this? He said: “I am Abū al-Ḥasan: if he brings four witnesses testifying to what he witnessed, otherwise he is to be handed over with his rope.”

Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated from Hamzah ibn Zayd, from 'Ali ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام, who said: When our Qa'im عليه السلام rises, he will say: ‘O company of horsemen, travel in the middle of the road; O company of pedestrians, travel along the sides of the road. So whichever horseman takes to the sides of the road and injures a man, we shall impose the blood-money upon him; and whichever man takes to the middle of the road and is injured, then there is no blood-money for him.’

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who is killed while he owes a debt and has no property. Do his heirs have the right to forgo his blood in favor of his killer while he still has a debt? He said: “Indeed, the holders of the debt are the litigants against the killer. So if his heirs forgo his blood in favor of his killer, they must guarantee the debt to the creditors; otherwise, they may not.”

From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from one of his mawālī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to me: “The diyah of the child born of zinā is the diyah of a Jew: eight hundred dirhams.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from some of his men, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood money for a child born of zina, and he said: “Eight hundred dirhams, like the blood money of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “The diyah of the child of zina is the diyah of a dhimmi: eight hundred dirhams.”

From him, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever unsheathes a sword, then his blood is without compensation.”

From him, from Ibrahim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them: A man had two camels that ran off, so another man took them and tied them together with a rope. One of them was strangled and died. The matter was referred to Ali عليه السلام, and he did not hold him liable, and he said: “He only intended to set things right.”

Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: "The qasāmah was only instituted so that the matter may be made weightier thereby against a man known for concealment who is accused; so if they testify against him, their testimony is admissible."

And Ibn Abi ʿUmayr narrated from some of his companions, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: concerning A Muslim man who was in the land of shirk, and the Muslims killed him; then the Imam came to know of him afterward, so he said: “In his place, a believing slave is to be freed, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” “And if he was from a people hostile to you, while he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave.” The Book of Blood-Money is complete, and it is the end of the book. And praise belongs to Allah, at the beginning and the end. Completed, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, what we intended of the commentary upon the tenth part—according to our division—of the Book Tahdhib al-Ahkam; and with it the book is complete. And our final call is that praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, who guided us to this and granted us success for the completion. That was in the afternoon of Sunday, the sixteenth of the exalted month of Shaʿban, one thousand three hundred and eighty of the Prophetic Hijrah—upon his migration be thousands of praises and salutations. And I am the least, Hasan al-Mousawi al-Khursan.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man and his wife, and her husband had committed liwat with her son from another man and had penetrated him, and the witnesses testified against him regarding that. So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered concerning him, and he was struck with the sword until he was killed. And the boy was struck with less than the hadd, and he said: “Indeed, if you had been mature, I would have killed you for enabling him against yourself so that he penetrated you.”

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Kufi, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Azrami, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “A man was found with another man during the rule of 'Umar. One of the two fled, and the other was seized and brought to 'Umar. He said to the people, ‘What do you think?’” He said: “So one said, ‘Do this,’ and another said, ‘Do that.’” He said: “Then he said, ‘What do you say, O Aba al-Hasan?’” He said: “So he said, ‘Strike his neck.’ So his neck was struck.” He said: “Then he wanted to carry him away, so he عليه السلام said, ‘Wait, for there still remains something of his hadd.’” He said: “What thing remains?” He said: “‘Call for firewood.’ So 'Umar called for firewood, and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered concerning him, and he was burned with it.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Sulaymān ibn Hilāl, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a man who does that with a man, he said: He said, “If it is short of penetration, then the hadd punishment applies; but if he has penetrated, he is to be made to stand, then struck with the sword, and the sword takes from him whatever it takes.” I said to him: Is that killing? He said: “That is so.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from his father Abd al-Rahman, from Abi Abd Allah, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: Umar was brought a man who had been penetrated in his anus, and he intended to flog him. So he said to the witnesses: “Did you see him insert it as the probe-stick enters the kohl container?” They said: “Yes.” Then he said to Ali عليه السلام: “What do you think about this?” So he sought the male who had penetrated him, but did not find him. Then Ali عليه السلام said: “My view concerning him is that you strike his neck.” He said: So he ordered it, and his neck was struck. He said: “Take him.” Then he said: “There still remains for him another punishment.” He said: “And what is it?” He said: “Call for a load of firewood.” So he called for a load of firewood, and he was wrapped in it, then he brought him out and burned him with fire. He said: Then he said: “Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has servants who have in their loins wombs like the wombs of women.” He said: “Then why do they not carry in them?” He said: “Because it is inverted, and they have in their rears a gland like the gland of a camel; when it is aroused, they become aroused, and when it becomes still, they become still.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “If it were proper for anyone to be stoned twice, the one who commits liwat would have been stoned.”

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about liwat, and he said: “Between the thighs.” He said: And I asked him about the one who penetrates, so he said: “That is disbelief in what Allah sent down upon His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”
