ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: While Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was among a gathering of his companions, a man came to him and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed penetration with a boy, so purify me.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “O this one, go to your home; perhaps a black bile episode has been stirred in you.” Then when it was the next day, he returned to him and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed penetration with a boy, so purify me.” He said to him: “O this one, go to your home; perhaps a black bile episode has been stirred in you.” He did that three times after his first time. Then when it was the fourth time, he said to him: “O this one, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled in the case of one like you with three rulings, so choose whichever of them you wish.” He said: “And what are they, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn?” He said: “A strike with the sword upon your neck, reaching whatever it reaches; or casting you down from a mountain while your hands and feet are bound; or burning with fire.” He said to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, which of them is most severe upon me?” He said: “Burning with fire.” He said: “Then I have chosen it, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn.” He said: “Then prepare yourself for that.” He said: “Yes.” Then he performed two rakʿahs, then sat in his tashahhud and said: “O Allah, I have committed of sin what You already know, and I have feared because of that, so I came to the legatee of Your Messenger and the cousin of Your Prophet, and I asked him to purify me. So he gave me the choice between three kinds of punishment, and I have chosen the most severe of them. O Allah, I ask You to make that an expiation for my sins, and not to burn me with Your Fire in my Hereafter.” Then he stood while weeping until he sat in the pit that Amīr al-Muʾminīn had dug for him, while he saw the fire blazing around him. He said: Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام wept, and all his companions wept, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “Rise, O this one, for you have made the angels of heaven and the angels of earth weep, and Allah has indeed accepted your repentance. So rise, and do not ever return to anything of what you had done.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās, a غلام of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, known as the غلام of Ibn Shurāʿah, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Sayf al-Tammār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام was brought a man with a boy with whom he had intercourse, and the evidence was established against them for that. He said, “O Qanbar, the leather mat and the sword.” Then he ordered that the man be placed on his face and the boy be placed on his face, then he ordered regarding them, and they were struck with the sword until he split them both with the sword together. He said: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought two women who were found under one covering, and the evidence was established against them that they had been engaging in musāḥaqah. So he called for the leather mat, then ordered regarding them, and they were burned with fire.

As for what Yūnus narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The legal punishment of the one who commits liwāṭ is like the legal punishment of the fornicator.” And he said: “If he is muḥṣan, he is stoned; otherwise, he is flogged.”

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A man came to a man. He said: "If he is muhsan, then upon him is execution; and if he is not muhsan, then upon him is flogging." He said: So I said: Then what is upon the one to whom it was done? He said: "Upon him is execution in every case, whether he was muhsan or not muhsan."
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: "The punishment of the one who commits liwat is the punishment of the fornicator."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: In the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام: “If a man is found with a boy in one cover while both are unclothed, the man is to be beaten and the boy disciplined; and if he has penetrated and is muḥṣan, he is to be stoned.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports can bear two interpretations. One of them is that what is intended by them is when the act is short of penetration; then iḥṣān and non-iḥṣān are considered in it. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام explained that in what Sulaymān ibn Hilāl narrated from him, in his saying: “If it is short of penetration, then the hadd is upon him; and if it is penetration, then a blow with the sword.” The doer of that was also called a lūṭī in the narration of Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr which we presented earlier. That does not contradict what we previously presented from Abū Baṣīr from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “That if he penetrates and is muḥṣan, then stoning is upon him.” For when the doer of that has become liable to killing, the Imam may choose between carrying out the hadd on him by striking the neck, casting down from a mountain, burning, or stoning; whichever of these he wills, he may do. Restricting that to his being muḥṣan only indicates, by way of the implication of the wording, that if he is not muḥṣan then that is not upon him; but that may be set aside due to evidence, and we have already presented what indicates that. Nor does that contradict what he narrated: — (204) 13 — Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd said: I read in the handwriting of a man whom I know, addressed to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and I read the reply of Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in his own handwriting: “Is there a hadd upon a man who played with a boy between his thighs? For some of the group have narrated that there is no harm in a man playing with a boy between his thighs.” So he wrote: “The curse of Allah be upon the one who does that.” This man also wrote, though I did not see the reply: “What is the hadd of two men, one of whom had intercourse with the other willingly between his thighs, and what is his repentance?” So he wrote: “Killing.” “And what is the hadd of two men found sleeping in one garment?” So he عليه السلام wrote: “One hundred lashes.” Because we interpret this narration as referring to one from whom the

It is only what we have previously mentioned regarding taqiyyah, and nothing else. As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a number of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Concerning the one who commits īqāb: upon him is stoning if he is muḥṣan, and upon him is the hadd punishment if he is not muḥṣan." So the correct way regarding this is in...

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “A muhrim kissed a boy out of desire.” He said: “He is to be struck with one hundred lashes.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, who said: One of our companions asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام and said: May I be made your ransom, a man sleeps with another man under one blanket. He said: “Is he a relative by kinship?” He said: No. He said: “Is it out of necessity?” He said: No. He said: “They are each to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.” He said: But if he has done it? He said: “If it was short of penetration, then the hadd applies; and if he penetrated, he is made to stand, then struck one strike with the sword—the sword takes from him whatever it takes.” I said to him: Is that killing? He said: “That is so.” I said: And regarding a woman who slept with another woman under one blanket? He said: “Is she one of forbidden kin?” I said: No. He said: “Is it out of necessity?” I said: No. He said: “They are each to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.” I said: But she has done it. He said: That weighed heavily upon him, so he said: “Uff, uff, uff,” three times, and said: “The hadd.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said: I asked him about two women who are found in a single coverlet. He said: “Each one of them is to be given one hundred lashes.”
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: “The woman who commits siḥāq is flogged.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, and Hishām, and Ḥafṣ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. That some women entered upon him, and one woman among them asked him about siḥāq, so he said: “Its hadd is the hadd of the fornicator.” So the woman said: “Allah has not mentioned that in the Qur’an.” He said: “Yes, indeed.” She said: “And where?” He said: “They are the companions of al-Rass.”

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A group came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام seeking his legal verdict, but they did not find him. So al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to them: “Bring me your question. If I am correct, then it is from Allah and from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and if I err, then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام is behind you.” They said: “A woman whose husband had intercourse with her then arose with the heat of his intercourse, and she engaged in siḥāq with a virgin slave-girl, casting the semen upon her, and she became pregnant.” He عليه السلام said: “Immediately, this woman is to be charged with the dower of this virgin, because the child does not come out until the virginity is removed. She is to be awaited until she gives birth, then the legal punishment is to be carried out upon her, the child is to be ascribed to the owner of the semen, and the married woman is to be stoned.” Then they departed and met Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. They said: “We asked al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥasan said to us such-and-such.” He said: “By Allah, had you met Abā al-Ḥasan, there would have been with him nothing except what al-Ḥasan said.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Ziyād called us and said: Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn wrote to me: I ask you about this issue. So I said: What is it? He said: A man came to a woman, and she retained his fluid, then engaged in musāḥaqah with a slave-girl. So I said to him: Ask the people of al-Madīnah about it.” He said: “Then he handed me a letter, and in it was: Ask Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad about it; if he answers you, otherwise bring him to me.” He said: “So I said: The woman is stoned, the slave-girl is flogged, and the child is ascribed to his father.” He said: “And I only know that he said: and he is the one who was tried by it.”

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-'Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife, then she transferred his semen to a virgin slave-girl and she became pregnant. He عليه السلام said: "The child belongs to the man; upon the woman is rajm, and upon the slave-girl is the hadd."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is not permissible for two women to spend the night in one blanket unless there is a barrier between them. If they do so, they are to be forbidden from that; and if they are found after the prohibition, each one of them is to be flogged with a hadd punishment. Then if they are found again in one blanket, they are flogged; and if they are found a third time, they are killed.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. Concerning a woman who deflowered a slave-girl with her hand, he عليه السلام said: “Upon her is her dower, and she is to be lashed eighty times.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said, “O Messenger of Allah, my wife does not repel the hand of one who touches.” He said, “Then divorce her.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I love her.” He said, “Then keep her.”

From him, from al-Ḥusayn, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who saw his wife committing zina: is it proper for him to keep her? He said: “Yes, if he wishes.”

Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام; and Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Ibrāhīm Mūsā عليه السلام: concerning About a man who approaches a beast sexually, they all said: “If the beast belongs to the perpetrator, it is to be slaughtered; then when it dies, it is to be burned with fire, and no benefit is to be taken from it. And he is to be struck with twenty-five lashes, one quarter of the hadd of the fornicator. If the beast does not belong to him, it is to be appraised, its price taken from him and given to its owner, and it is to be slaughtered and burned with fire, and no benefit is to be taken from it, and he is to be struck with twenty-five lashes.” So I said: “What is the fault of the beast?” He said: “It has no fault, but the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did this and commanded it, so that people would not suffice themselves with beasts and the progeny would not be cut off.”

Yunus, from Sama'ah, said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a beast, whether a sheep, a she-camel, or a cow, He said: “He is to be flogged with a penalty short of the fixed hadd, then banished from his town to another; and they mentioned that the meat of that beast is forbidden, as is its milk.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, from Sadīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning: About a man who has intercourse with a beast, he said: “He is to be flogged less than the hadd punishment, and he must pay the value of the beast to its owner because he has ruined it for him. It is to be slaughtered and burned if it is from those whose meat is eaten. If it is from those ridden on their backs, he must pay its value, and he is to be flogged less than the hadd punishment, and it is to be taken out from the town in which he did that with it to another land where it is not known, then sold there, so that he is not shamed by it.”

Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Regarding a man who has intercourse with an animal, he said: He said, “There is no hadd punishment upon him, but there is taʿzīr.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān and Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār and Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a man who has intercourse with a beast, he عليه السلام said: “There is no fixed hadd punishment upon him, but he is to be beaten as taʿzīr.”
As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding a man who approached a beast sexually, he said: “He is to be killed.”
From him, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: concerning A man who came to a beast and penetrated it—he said: “The hadd punishment is upon him.”

The narration of Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, through his chain, from Yūnus, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning one who comes to a beast and penetrates, he said: “Upon him is the hadd of the fornicator.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Sulaymān ibn Hilāl, who said: Some of our companions asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a beast, So he said: “He is made to stand upright, then he is struck with a blow of the sword; whatever the sword takes from him, it takes.” He said: So I said, “Is it killing?” He said: “That is so.”

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Zayd Abi Usamah, from Abi Farwah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: "The one who commits the obscene act, and the one who goes to a beast, his hadd is the hadd of the fornicator." So the interpretation of these reports is one of two possibilities. One of them is that they are to be understood to mean that when the act is short of penetration, then there is ta'zir in it; and when there is penetration, then upon him is the hadd of the fornicator, just as the report of Abi Basir contains by restricting that to penetration, and in that is an indication that if it is short of penetration, the hadd of the fornicator is not obligatory. The other possibility is that they are to be understood regarding one from whom the act was repeated and the hadd was established upon him; without ta'zir, at that point he is killed, or the hadd of the fornicator is established upon him according to what the Imam sees fit, because we have already explained that the people of major sins are killed on the third or fourth time. On this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports.

“The people of major sins, all of them, when the hadd is carried out upon them twice, they are killed on the third time.” 12 - ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ādam ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī, who said: I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام when a letter from Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to him concerning a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and had intercourse with her. For indeed the people have disagreed with us concerning this: one group said, ‘Kill him,’ and another group said, ‘Burn him.’ So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام wrote to him: “Indeed, the sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living. His hadd is that his hand be cut off for his grave-digging and stripping of the clothes, and the hadd for zina is to be carried out upon him: if he was muḥṣan, he is stoned; and if he was not muḥṣan, he is flogged one hundred times.” And Yūnus has narrated what we mentioned from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said:

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: Concerning the one who has intercourse with a woman while she is dead, he said: “His sin is greater than that of the one who has intercourse with her while she is alive.”

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAbd al-Salām, from Abū Ḥanīfah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who committed zinā with a dead woman. He said: “There is no hadd upon him.” So this report admits of two possibilities. One of them is that the meaning is: there is no fixed hadd upon him such that no other than it would be permissible in all circumstances, because we have already explained that iḥṣān and its absence are considered in this matter. So if he is muḥṣan, then the hadd is rajm, and if he is not muḥṣan, then the hadd is one hundred lashes; and this is not upon one single hadd. And the other possibility is that the report is specific to one who had intercourse with his own wife after her death. In that case, the hadd is not carried out upon him, and he is given taʿzīr according to what the Imam sees fit.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام. That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man who had played with his penis, so he struck his hand until it became red; then he married him from the Bayt al-Mal.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought a man who had manipulated his private part until he ejaculated, so he struck his hand with a whip until it became red. And I only know that he said: and he married him from the treasury of the Muslims.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Barqī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn and Ḥusayn ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who manipulates with his hand until he ejaculates. He said: “There is no fixed penalty in it, and that has not reached any prescribed measure.” So the proper understanding of this report is that it has not reached a fixed, prescribed punishment from which deviation is not permitted, because when the ruling involves taʿzīr, that is left to the Imam, who enacts it according to what he deems appropriate in the circumstance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Every intoxicant among drinks incurs, in its case, the same hadd punishment as is incurred in the case of wine.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “In the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام: the drinker of wine and the drinker of an intoxicant are both to be struck.” I said: “How much?” He said: “Their hadd is one.”

Yūnus narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Indeed, when a man drinks wine, he becomes intoxicated; when he becomes intoxicated, he raves; and when he raves, he fabricates. So flog him with the punishment of the fabricator.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Hakam, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: Al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah, when testimony was given against him for drinking wine, ʿUthmān said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘Judge between him and these who claim that he drank wine.’ So ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered, and he was flogged with a whip having two branches, forty lashes.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, in the book of ʿAlī عليه السلام, it is written: the drinker of wine is lashed eighty times, and the drinker of nabīdh is lashed eighty times.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was brought forth, having drunk wine, and ʿUmar ordered that he be struck. But no one stepped forward against him to strike him, until ʿAlī عليه السلام stood up with a folded strap and struck him with it forty times.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who drank a sip of wine. He said: “He is to be flogged eighty lashes; a small amount of it and a large amount of it are haram (forbidden).”

Yūnus narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله strike lashes? He said: "He used to strike with sandals, and he would increase it each time the drinker was brought. Then the people continued increasing it until that settled at eighty. ʿAlī عليه السلام indicated that to ʿUmar, and he approved of it."

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Tell me, how did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله punish in cases of wine? He said: “He would strike with sandals, and he would increase it when the drinker was brought forward. Then the people continued increasing it until that settled at eighty; Ali عليه السلام indicated that to Umar.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: “ʿAlī عليه السلام used to administer eighty lashes for wine and nabīdh, upon the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian.” I said: “What is the case of the Jew and the Christian?” He said: “They are not permitted to make their drinking public; that is to be in their houses.”

Yūnus, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: “ʿAlī عليه السلام used to flog the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian eighty lashes for wine and nabīdh.” So I said, “What is the case of the Jew and the Christian?” He said, “If they manifest that in a city among the cities, because they do not have the right to manifest drinking it.”

Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: "The hadd of the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and false accusation is the same. The People of the Covenant were only granted terms that they may drink it in their homes." He said: And I asked him about the drunken person and the fornicator. He said: "They are to be flogged with whips, stripped, between the shoulders. But as for the hadd in slander, he is flogged over his clothes, with a beating of moderate severity."

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: How much is taʿzīr? He said: “Less than the hadd.” He said: I said: Less than eighty? He said: “No, rather it is less than forty, for that is the hadd of the slave.” He said: I said: And how much is that? He said: “ʿAlī عليه السلام said: According to the measure that the governor sees of the man’s offense and the strength of his body.” So the first point in it is that it is not apparent in the outward wording of the report that the hadd of the slave, which is forty, is only in his drinking wine. And when that is not apparent in its wording, it is permissible that this be his hadd in matters other than it. Even if it were explicit that this is his hadd in drinking wine, it would be permissible for us to interpret it as a form of taqiyyah, because that agrees with the doctrine of some of the ʿāmmah.

As for what al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an owned slave who slanders a free man. He said: “He is lashed eighty times. This is from the rights of the Muslims. As for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then he is struck with half of the hadd.” I said: What is that which is from the rights of Allah? He said: “If he commits zina or drinks wine, then this is among the rights in which half of the hadd is administered.” So this is an anomalous report, by which the mutawatir reports concerning the inclusion of the wine-drinker and his deserving eighty lashes are not opposed. Those reports are general regarding slaves and free persons, and we have also narrated what specifically includes them in wording as well, and their deserving the complete hadd; therefore, it is not appropriate to object to all of them with this report. It is possible that the narrator heard that only concerning zina in particular, because it is from the rights of Allah, and since the hadd of the wine-drinker is from the rights of Allah, he applied it to that; but it is not proper for us to apply it thus, because it is not impossible that the fornicator among them be specified with half of the hadd, while the wine-drinker is given the hadd in full, even though both are from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then it is also possible that the explanation in it is what we mentioned in the first report, namely taqiyyah, due to its accordance with the doctrines of some of the ʿAmmah.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: My father used to say: ‘The hadd of the slave is half the hadd of the free person.’ So this report is general, and it is permissible to specify it by the hadd of zina, and we have already explained what necessitates specifying it.

Ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Nafi', from Abi Khalid al-Qammat, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to flog the Jew and the Christian, concerning wine and intoxicating nabidh, with eighty lashes when they drank it openly in a city among the cities; but if they drank it in their churches and synagogues, he would not interfere with them unless they came to be among the Muslims.

Yūnus narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “The prescribed penalty concerning wine applies when some of it or much of it is drunk.” He said, then he said: “ʿUmar was brought Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn after he had drunk wine, and the proof had been established against him. So he consulted ʿAlī عليه السلام, and he ordered that he be struck eighty lashes. Then Qudāmah said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, there is no prescribed penalty upon me; I am among the people of this verse.” “There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed.” He said: So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “You are not among its people. The food of its people is lawful for them; they do not eat or drink except what Allah has made lawful for them.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Indeed, when the drinker drinks, he does not know what he eats or what he drinks, so flog him with eighty lashes.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A man drank wine during the time of Abū Bakr, so he was brought before Abū Bakr. He said to him, “Did you drink wine?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “And why, when it is forbidden?” He said: The man said to him, “I accepted Islam, and my Islam became good, and my dwelling is among a people who drink wine and deem it permissible. Had I known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.” Then Abū Bakr turned to ʿUmar and said, “What do you say regarding the matter of this man?” ʿUmar said, “It is a difficult problem, and none is fit for it except Abū al-Ḥasan.” He said, “Call ʿAlī for us.” ʿUmar said, “The judge is to be approached in his house.” So they rose, with the man accompanying them, along with those of the people who were present with them, until they came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. They informed him of the man’s story, and the man himself related his account. He said: Then he said, “Send with him someone who will take him around to the gatherings of the Muhājirīn and the Anṣār. Whoever had recited to him the verse of prohibition, let him testify against him.” So they did that, but no one testified against him that he had recited to him the verse of prohibition. So he let him go and said to him, “If you drink after this, we will carry out the hadd punishment upon you.”

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who raised it from Abi Maryam, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought al-Najashi the poet, who had drunk wine in the month of Ramadan. So he flogged him with eighty lashes, then imprisoned him for a night. Then he called for him the next day and flogged him with twenty lashes. He said to him, “O Amir al-Mu'minin, these eighty lashes you gave me were for drinking wine, but what are these twenty?” He said, “This is for your audacity in drinking wine in the month of Ramadan.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from al-Asbagh, or from Habbah al-'Urani, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said upon the minbar of al-Kufah: “Whoever drinks a draught of khamr, then flog him; if he returns, then flog him; and if he returns, then kill him.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever drinks wine, then flog him; if he returns, then flog him; and if he returns a third time, then kill him.” 365-22 — From him, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: The like of that.

Yūnus, from al-Muʿallā, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when a drinker of wine was brought to him, would strike him once; then if he was brought a second time, he would strike him; then if he was brought a third time, he would strike his neck.
Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abi Ubaydah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: "Whoever drinks wine, then flog him; if he returns, then flog him; if he returns, then kill him."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: Regarding the drinker of wine: if he drinks, he is flogged; if he returns, he is flogged; if he returns again, he is killed on the third occasion.
Yūnus narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: "The people guilty of all major sins, when the hadd is carried out upon them twice, they are killed on the third time."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was brought one who drank wine, he would strike him. If he was brought a second time, he would strike him. If he was brought a third time, he struck his neck.” I said: And nabidh? He said: “If its drinker is seized while he has become intoxicated, he is struck eighty lashes.” I said: What do you say if he is seized for it a second time? He said: “I strike him.” I said: Then if he is seized for it a third time? He said: “He is killed just as the drinker of wine is killed.” I said: What do you say if the drinker of nabidh is seized and he has not become intoxicated—should he be flogged? He said: “No.” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains regarding the distinction between nabidh and wine, and that flogging is not carried out for it except when intoxication occurs, is to be understood as a form of taqiyyah, because that is the view of the jurists of some of the generality. For we have already clarified that there is no distinction between wine and nabidh in its small amount or large amount, and that it necessitates the hadd. The same ruling applies to what he narrated:

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. I said: Tell me, if a drinker of nabīdh is seized but he has not become intoxicated, is he to be flogged eighty lashes? He said: No. And every intoxicant is haram (forbidden). So the explanation in this also is taqiyyah, according to what we have stated earlier. As for what he narrated:

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about the drinker, and he said: “As for a man from whom there occurred a slip, then I would administer taʿzir to him. But as for another who persists habitually, then I would exhaust him with punishment, because he deems all sanctities lawful; and if the people and that were left alone, they would become corrupted.” So this report is anomalous and rare; it is not permissible to act upon it because it conflicts with all the reports. Moreover, in the apparent wording of the report there is nothing more than that he asked him about the drinker, and he did not clarify to him whether he was a drinker of khamr, nabidh, or another drink; and it is possible that this ruling is specific to one who drank some of the forbidden beverages even if it was not intoxicating. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned—that the ruling of nabidh in its small amount is the ruling of its large amount, and that its ruling is equal to the ruling of khamr—is what has been narrated:

Yūnus, from Hishām ibn Ibrāhīm al-Mashriqī, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to flog for a small amount of nabīdh just as he flogged for a small amount of khamr, and he would execute on the third offense of nabīdh just as he would execute on the third offense of khamr.

Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to administer eighty lashes for intoxicating nabidh, just as he would administer for wine, and he would execute on the third offense just as he would execute the wine-drinker.

From him, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man whom we invited to the totality of what we are upon from the totality of Islam, and he affirmed it, then he drank wine, committed fornication, and consumed usury, while nothing of the halal and the haram had been explained to him—should the hadd be carried out upon him if he was ignorant of it? He said: So he said, “No, unless there is established against him clear proof that he had already acknowledged their prohibition.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from al-Ḥusayn al-Qalānisī, who said: I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام asking him about al-fuqqāʿ, so he said: “Do not go near it, for indeed it is from wine.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu 'Abd Allah, from Mansur ibn al-'Abbas, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Faddal and Ibn al-Jahm, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام. They said: We asked him about al-fuqqa', and he said: "It is khamr, and regarding it is the hadd of the drinker of khamr."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about al-fuqqa', and he said: "It is khamr, and upon it is the hadd of the drinker of khamr."

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Abū Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār and Samāʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said: The one who consumes usury after the proof has been established? He said: “He is disciplined; then if he returns, he is disciplined; then if he returns, he is killed.”

And with this chain of narration, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: “The one who eats carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine—upon them is disciplinary punishment; and if he repeats it, he is disciplined.” I said: “Then if he repeats, is he to be disciplined?” He said: “He is to be disciplined, and there is no fixed hadd punishment upon him.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a Christian man who had become Muslim, and with him was a pig that he had roasted and garnished with basil. He said: “What led you to this?” The man said: “I became ill and craved meat.” So he said: “Why did you not turn to goat meat?” Then he said: “Had you eaten it, I would have carried out the hadd punishment upon you; but I will strike you a beating, so do not repeat it.” Then he beat him until he urinated.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abi 'Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi 'Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: Is zina worse, or drinking wine? And how is it that for wine there are eighty, while for zina there are one hundred? So he said: "O Ishaq, the hadd is one, but more was added in this case because of his wasting the drop and placing it in other than its place which Allah has commanded for it."

What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd al-Aḥwaṣ al-Qummī narrated to me, saying: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: How many rakʿahs is the salat (prayer)? He said: “Fifty-one rakʿahs.” In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. And to Him belongs all praise, and through Him we seek help.

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The obligatory and supererogatory prayers are fifty-one rakʿahs. Of them are two rakʿahs after al-ʿatamah, performed sitting, which are counted as one rakʿah while standing. The obligatory prayers among them are seventeen rakʿahs, and the supererogatory prayers are thirty-four rakʿahs.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and Bukayr, who said: We heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform, in supererogatory prayer, twice the amount of the obligatory prayer, and he used to fast, in supererogatory fasting, twice the amount of the obligatory fasting.

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ḥanān, who said: ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was sitting there, and he said to him: Inform me—may I be made your ransom—about the salat of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. He عليه السلام said to him: "The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform eight rakʿahs at zawāl, and four for the first prayer, and eight after it, and four for al-ʿaṣr, and three for al-maghrib, and four after al-maghrib, and four for al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah, and eight for salat al-layl, and three for al-watr, and the two rakʿahs of al-fajr, and salat al-ghadāh as two rakʿahs." I said: May I be made your ransom, if I am stronger and able to do more than this, would Allah punish me for the abundance of salat? He said: "No, but He punishes for abandoning the sunnah (prophetic tradition)."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "The salat (prayer) of the daytime is sixteen rak'ahs: eight when the sun declines, and eight after al-Zuhr, and four rak'ahs after al-Maghrib. O Harith, do not leave them whether in travel or residence. And two rak'ahs after al-'Isha' al-Akhirah—my father used to perform them while sitting, and I perform them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform thirteen rak'ahs in the night."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the best of what the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has established regarding salat (prayer). He said: “Completing the fifty.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله by day, so he said: “And who can manage that?” Then he said: “But shall I not inform you how I myself act?” So I said: Yes. He said: “Eight rak'ahs before al-Zuhr and eight after it.” I said: And al-Maghrib? He said: “Four after it.” I said: And al-'Atamah? He said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform al-'Atamah, then sleep.” And he gestured with his hand like this, moving it. Ibn Abi 'Umayr said: Then he عليه السلام described it as our companions have mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The nafilah prayer is eight rak‘ahs when the sun declines before al-zuhr, and six rak‘ahs after al-zuhr, and two rak‘ahs before al-‘asr, and four rak‘ahs after al-maghrib, and two rak‘ahs after al-‘isha’ al-akhirah in which you recite one hundred verses, standing or sitting, though standing is better; and do not count these two among the fifty. And eight rak‘ahs are in the latter part of the night; in salat al-layl you recite: “Say: He is Allah, One.” and “Say: O disbelievers.” in the first two rak‘ahs, and in the remainder of it you recite whatever of the Qur’an you wish. Then al-watr is three rak‘ahs; in all of them you recite: “Say: He is Allah, One.” and you separate between them with taslim. Then the two rak‘ahs that are before al-fajr: in the first of them you recite: “Say: O disbelievers.” and in the second: “Say: He is Allah.” . As for the hadiths which have been narrated regarding a lesser number than what we have mentioned of the prayer, such as what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Aba ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام saying: “Do not pray less than forty-four rak‘ahs.” He said: And I saw him praying four rak‘ahs after al-‘atamah. There is no prohibition in this report against what exceeds forty-four; rather, he عليه السلام only prohibited reducing it below that. And it is not impossible that he عليه السلام encouraged these forty-four rak‘ahs because of their emphasis and the strength of their recommendation by this report, while encouraging what is besides them by another hadith. We have already presented hadiths that include that. And as for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yahya ibn Habib, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the most excellent thing by which the servants draw near to Allah, the Exalted, from prayer. He said: “Forty-six rak‘ahs, its obligatory acts and its nawafil.” I said: This is the narration of Zurarah. He said: “Do you see anyone who was more outspoken with the truth than him?” This hadith also contains no prohibition regarding prayers besides these; rather, he was asked about the most excellent means by which the servants draw near, so he mentioned these forty-six and single

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about voluntary prayer during the night and the day, and he said: That which is recommended such that one should not fall short of it is eight rakʿahs at the sun’s decline, and after the ẓuhr two rakʿahs, and before the ʿaṣr two rakʿahs, and after the maghrib two rakʿahs, and before the ʿatamah two rakʿahs, and from the time of saḥar eight rakʿahs, then he performs witr, and the witr is three separate rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr; and the most beloved night prayer to them is the end of the night. So he clarified in this hadith that these forty-six rakʿahs are among what is recommended such that one should not fall short of them, and that what is besides them does not share with them in recommendation. As for the other hadiths besides these which imply a reduction from fifty rakʿahs, their common basis is all Zurārah, even if they are repeated through different chains, such as.

Among what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) that has been established regarding the salat (prayer)? He said: “Eight rakʿahs at zawāl, two rakʿahs after al-ẓuhr, two rakʿahs before al-ʿaṣr, two rakʿahs after al-maghrib, thirteen rakʿahs in the latter part of the night, including al-watr, and the two rakʿahs of al-fajr.” I said: So is this all that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has established? He said: Yes. Then Abū al-Khaṭṭāb said: What do you think if he is strong enough and adds more? He said: So he sat up, and he had been reclining, and said: “If you have strength, then perform it as it used to be performed; and just as it is not in any hour of the day, neither is it in any hour of the night. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘And during parts of the night, then glorify [Him].’ It is therefore possible that he permitted Zurārah to limit himself to these prayers because of an excuse that Zurārah had, due to the abundance of his occupations, the neglect of which would bring harm upon him, or because of some reason among the reasons that would justify that for him; otherwise it would not have been permissible. If the matter is as such, then it is permissible for him to restrict himself to them, because in our view, whenever a person has an excuse such that his occupation with the nawāfil would harm him with respect to it, it is permissible for him to leave them altogether, since they are not among those things for whose omission punishment is deserved. We shall present later what indicates that, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills; and that which clarifies what we have mentioned, namely that the excuse was in Zurārah.

Among what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I am a merchant man; I go about and engage in trade. So how can I manage the noon decline time and maintain the prayer of zawāl, and how many rakʿahs is it prayed? He said: You pray eight rakʿahs when the sun declines, and two rakʿahs after al-ẓuhr, and two rakʿahs before al-ʿaṣr; these are twelve rakʿahs. And you pray two rakʿahs after al-maghrib, and after the middle of the night thirteen rakʿahs, among them al-witr and among them the two rakʿahs of al-fajr. Those are twenty-seven rakʿahs besides the obligatory prayer. All of this is supererogatory and not obligatory. Indeed, the one who abandons the obligatory prayer is a kāfir, but the one who abandons this is not a kāfir; rather, it is a sin, because it is recommended that when a man performs an act of good, he should be constant in it. So this hadith contains Zurārah's mention of his excuse due to trade and other matters. Thus, the Imam عليه السلام allowed him to suffice with less than fifty, which indicates what we have mentioned: that the prescribed sunnah is fifty-one rakʿahs so long as there is no excuse there.

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Our companions differ regarding the supererogatory salat; some of them pray forty-four, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me of that which you yourself practice, how it is, so that I may act likewise. He said: “I pray fifty-one rakʿahs.” Then he said: “Count,” and he folded with his hand: “At zawāl, eight; four after ẓuhr; four before ʿaṣr; two rakʿahs after maghrib; two rakʿahs before the later ʿishāʾ; and two rakʿahs after ʿishāʾ while sitting, which are counted as one rakʿah while standing; and eight for salat al-layl; and al-witr, three; and the two rakʿahs of fajr; and the obligatory prayers, seventeen. That is fifty-one rakʿahs.” And this also indicates that the sunnah (recommended practice) is what we have mentioned.

What was narrated by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from some of our companions, who said: He said to me: “The salat of the day is sixteen rakʿahs. Pray it at whichever part of the day you wish: if you wish, at its beginning; if you wish, in its middle; and if you wish, at its end.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from al-Ḥārith al-Naṣrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “The salat (prayer) of the day is sixteen rakʿahs: eight when the sun declines, and eight after al-ẓuhr, and four rakʿahs after al-maghrib. O Ḥārith, do not leave them in travel or in residence. And two rakʿahs after al-ʿishāʾ—my father used to perform them while seated, and I perform them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform thirteen rakʿahs of the night.”

And from him, from ʿAmmār ibn al-Mubārak, from Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd al-Ghifārī, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, how many are the supererogatory prayers of the daytime? He said: “They are sixteen rakʿahs. Whichever hours of the day you wish to pray them, you may pray them, except that if you pray them at their appointed times, it is better.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I asked him about supererogatory prayer during the day, and he mentioned: “That eight rakʿahs are prayed before al-Ẓuhr and eight after it.” The manner of inference from these hadiths for what we have mentioned is that every hadith narrated concerning a reduction from fifty rakʿahs only pertains to the daytime nawafil. As for the night nawafil, there is no disagreement concerning them among our companions. If these hadiths indicate the detailed explanation of what we have mentioned regarding the daytime salat, then what we intended is established. No one may say that the narration of Zurārah which you cited earlier included mention of the two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib, and that this is a disagreement regarding the night nawafil, because the narration—even if it is as he said—it is possible that he mentioned the four rakʿahs in detail, such that he said: two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib and two rakʿahs before the later ʿIshāʾ, in accordance with what was contained in the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, previously mentioned. These two rakʿahs, even if they are attached to the later ʿIshāʾ, are part of the nawafil of al-Maghrib, because the later ʿIshāʾ has no nafilah apart from the two rakʿahs performed sitting, which we mentioned earlier; this indicates that.

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is there anything before the later ʿishāʾ prayer and after it?” He said: “No, except that I pray two rakʿahs after it, and I do not count them as part of salat al-layl.” As for that which indicates the permissibility of omitting these nawāfil in cases of excuses: it is what is established of their being nawāfil, and nawāfil are that for whose omission punishment is not deserved. For if punishment were deserved for omitting them, they would be like the obligatory acts, and there would be no difference between them and those. This also indicates that.

Among what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Hannat, who said: I, Jamil ibn Darrāj, and 'Ā'idh al-Ahmasi went out as pilgrims. On the way, 'Ā'idh would often say to us: “I have a need to ask of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, something I wish to ask him about.” So I would say to him: “Wait until we meet him.” Then when we entered upon him, we greeted him and sat down. He turned his face toward us, initiating the speech, and said: “Whoever comes to Allah with what He has made obligatory upon him, He will not ask him about anything beyond that.” So 'Ā'idh nudged us. Then when we rose, we said: “What was your need?” He said: “What you heard.” We said: “How was this your need?” He said: “I am a man who cannot endure standing in prayer at night, so I feared that I might be taken to account for it and thus perish.”
He narrated to me from one who asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man upon whom prayers had accumulated. So he said: “Cast them aside and begin anew.”

Sa'd narrated from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Regarding the witr: Allah has only prescribed the five, and the witr is not prescribed as an obligation. If you wish, you may pray it, but leaving it is unbecoming.”

23 - Sa'd narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abū al-Hasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: "Abū al-Hasan عليه السلام, when he became distressed, would leave the fifty." His statement عليه السلام, "he left the fifty," means the completion of the fifty, because the obligatory prayers are not permissible to leave in any circumstance, and this clarifies that.

In the state of necessity. What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abū ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A man owes such a quantity of supererogatory prayers that, due to their abundance, he does not know how much it is. What should he do? He said: “Then let him pray until, because of their abundance, he no longer knows how much he has prayed, and thus he will have made up according to the extent of his knowledge.” I said: But he is not able to make them up because of the abundance of his work. He said: “If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is unavoidable, or in fulfilling the need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his occupation is for worldly matters with which he busied himself away from prayer, then making them up is upon him; otherwise he will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, treating lightly, being negligent, and wasting the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” I said: If he is not able to make them up, is it appropriate for him to give charity? He remained silent for a while, then said: “Yes, then let him give charity as charity.” I said: And how much should he give in charity? He said: “According to his means; and the minimum of that is one mudd for each poor person in place of each prayer.” So I said: For how much prayer is one mudd due for each poor person? He said: “For every two rak‘ahs of the night prayer, and every two rak‘ahs of the day prayer.” I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for every four rak‘ahs.” I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for each night prayer, and one mudd for the day prayer; and salat (prayer) is better, and salat (prayer) is better.”

And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Murāzim, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: May Allah set you right, I have many supererogatory prayers due upon me, so what should I do? So he said: “Make them up.” He said to him: They are more than that. He said: “Make them up.” I said: I cannot enumerate them. He said: “Estimate them to the best of your judgment.” Murāzim said: I had been ill for four months during which I did not perform supererogatory prayers, so I said to him: May Allah set you right, or may I be made your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not perform any supererogatory prayer. He said: “There is no making up due upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy person. Everything over which Allah has overcome him, then Allah is more entitled to excuse him in it.”

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to command the children to combine the Maghrib and the later Isha prayers, and he would say, 'It is better for them than to sleep through it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha' from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the young children when they line up in the obligatory prayer. He said, 'Do not delay them from the prayer, and separate them from one another.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the boy, when does fasting and prayer become obligatory upon him? He said: "When he approaches puberty and knows fasting and prayer." Regarding the boy, when does prayer become obligatory upon him? He said: "When thirteen years have passed for him; if he experiences wet dream before that, then prayer has become obligatory upon him and the pen has been lifted [or recorded] for him. And the girl is the same; if thirteen years have passed for her or she menstruates before that, then prayer has become obligatory upon her and the pen has been recorded for her."

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): Regarding the child, when does he pray? He said: When he understands prayer. I asked: When does he understand prayer and it becomes obligatory upon him? He said: At six years of age.

From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at what age a child is required to perform prayer, so he said: 'Between seven and six years.' I said: 'At what age is he required to fast?' He said: 'Between fifteen or fourteen, and if he fasts before that, let him be, for my son so-and-so fasted before that and I let him be.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: "When six years have passed for the child, prayer becomes obligatory upon him, and when he is capable of fasting, fasting becomes obligatory upon him." Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His saying (peace be upon him) 'when he is capable, fasting becomes obligatory upon him' is attributed to discipline (ta'dīb) rather than the primary obligation (al-farḍ), because the obligation of the primary duty is linked only to the state of maturity, as we have clarified. And likewise, his saying (peace be upon him) 'when six years have passed for him' — and in the other report 'or seven years' — 'prayer becomes obligatory upon him' is attributed to recommendation (istibḥāb) and discipline, because the primary obligation is linked to the state of maturity, as we have clarified.

Al-Ayyashi from Hamdawayh from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man whom the polytheists capture, and prayer time arrives for him, and he fears they will prevent him [from praying fully], so he gestures with a nod; he said, 'He gestures with a nod.'

From him (Al-Fayyaz), he said: Hamdawayh narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and a man asked him about a man whom the prayer time overtakes while he is wading in water and cannot reach the ground. He (AS) said: 'If he is in war or in the path of Allah, let him pray by nodding (with his head). And if he is in trade, it was not appropriate for him to wade in the water until he prays.' I said: 'And how should he do it?' He said: 'He should make it up (perform Qada) when he exits the water, having missed it.'

From him, from Hamdawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who stood for an obligatory prayer and prayed one rak'ah while intending it to be a voluntary prayer. He said: 'It is the one you stood for and to it belongs.' And he said: 'When you stand intending the obligatory prayer and doubt arises later, you are in the obligatory prayer according to what you stood for. And if you entered it intending a voluntary prayer, then you intend it later to be obligatory, you are in the voluntary prayer. And only what the servant began at the start of his prayer is counted for him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'When the Imam finishes (the prayer), one should not pray in his place until he moves away from that place.'

Al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'Do not pray the obligatory prayer inside the Ka'ba, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not enter it during a pilgrimage or a visitation, but he entered it during the Conquest of Mecca and prayed two rak'ahs between the two pillars, and Usamah was with him.'
From him, from Abu Jamilah, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: The obligatory prayer is not valid inside the hollow of the Ka'bah.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When does a man who intends to travel shorten his prayer?' He said, 'When he disappears from the houses.' I said, 'The man intends to travel and leaves when the sun declines (for Dhuhr prayer).' He said, 'When you leave, pray two rak'ahs.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca from his journey and the time for prayer has entered. He said: 'He prays two rak'ahs. And if he departs for his journey and the time for prayer has entered, let him pray four (rak'ahs).'

And it was also narrated from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The time for prayer enters upon me while I am traveling, so I do not pray until I enter to my family.' He said: 'Pray and complete the prayer.' I said: 'The time for prayer enters upon me while I am with my family, desiring to travel, so I do not pray until I leave.' He said: 'Then pray and shorten (the prayer), and if you do not do so, by Allah, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

And it was also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He was asked about a man whose time for prayer entered while he was traveling, so he delayed the prayer until he arrived home, intending to pray it when he reached his family. However, he forgot to pray it upon arrival until the time had passed. He said: 'He should pray it two rak'at as the prayer of a traveler, because the time entered while he was a traveler, and it was incumbent upon him to pray at that time.'

And it was also narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them or after them except for Maghrib, which is three."

And it was also narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about voluntary prayer during travel. He said: 'Do not pray anything before the two [rak'at] and after them during the day.'

And Fadalah narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I prayed Dhuhr as four rak'at while I was traveling.' He said, 'Repeat it.'

And it was narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) that they said: "The prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing (extra prayer) before them or after them." All these narrations indicate the elaboration of what was mentioned in the book, and I, by the will of God, will complete the discussion on the obligation of Qasr (shortening prayer) subsequently, if God wills.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Four rak'at after the Maghrib prayer, do not leave them, whether in residence or in travel.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them or after them except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak'ahs; do not leave them in residence or in travel. And there is no making up (qada) for you of the daytime prayer, and pray the night prayer and make it up."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, from Abu al-Harith, who said: I asked him, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), about the four rak'at after Maghrib when traveling; the camel hurries me so I cannot pray on the ground. He said: 'Yes, pray them on the camel.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: "Pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr while in the mount." And these two hadiths indicate the strong emphasis on these supererogatory prayers, because he commanded performing them while the person is in the mount, and did not permit leaving them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not leave four rak'at after Maghrib, whether in travel or in residence, and my father did not leave thirteen rak'at at night, whether in travel or in residence.'

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say: 'I love to be constant in worship, even if it is little.' We said: 'Do you make up the night prayer during the day while traveling?' He said: 'Yes.'
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to pray the night prayer during the day while mounted on his mount, wherever it faced.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Perform the night prayer, the Witr prayer, and the two rak'ahs while riding (in the saddle/camel-back).'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Saif al-Tammari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Some of our companions said to me: 'We used to shorten the daytime prayer when we stopped between the Maghrib and the later Isha.' He said: 'Allah knows best when He granted them concession. Allah has only prescribed for the traveler two rak'ahs, neither before them nor after them, except for the night prayer, on your camel wherever it takes you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Ali ibn al-Hakam, all from Abu Yahya al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the voluntary prayer (nafl) during the day while traveling, and he said, 'O my son, if the voluntary prayer were valid/perfect during travel, the obligatory prayer would be completed (i.e., reduced to two rak'ahs as nafl is).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about voluntary prayer during the day while I was traveling. He said, 'No, but you make up the night prayer during the day while you are traveling.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, regarding the daytime prayer that I pray when resident, do I make it up during the day while traveling?' He said, 'As for me, I do not make it up.' As for the report narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Do I make up the daytime prayer at night while traveling?' He said, 'Yes.' Then Isma'il ibn Jabir asked him, 'Do I make up the daytime prayer at night while traveling?' He said, 'No.' Isma'il said, 'You said Yes.' He said, 'That one is able [to do it], and you are not able.' This is to be understood as: if he made it up, he would not be sinful, even if it is not a prescribed Sunnah, or perhaps he knew of his condition that if he did not command him to do so, he would slight the Sunnahs, and that would lead to neglecting the obligatory duties. So he commanded him to do so to strengthen his inclination towards maintaining the prayers. And he knew of the condition of the other that it was the opposite, so he commanded him to leave the repetition, even though the report does not explicitly state that he may pray the voluntary daytime prayers or their obligatory counterparts at night. And if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as referring to the obligatory prayers. And if it had explicitly mentioned the voluntary prayers, it would not have meant that they were missed while he was traveling, or missed while he was resident. And if it can be interpreted that way, we interpret it as referring to one who missed the voluntary prayers while resident; it is permissible for him to make them up while traveling at night. And that which clarifies that the repetition of the voluntary daytime prayer is not a prescribed Sunnah.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskhan, from 'Umar ibn Hanathala, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am your ransom, I asked you about making up the daytime prayers at night while traveling, and you said, "Do not make them up." And our companions asked you, and you said, "Make them up." He said to me, "So should I tell them, "Do not pray," while I dislike telling them, "Do not pray," and by God, that is not the case for them."' As for the report narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hanan ibn Sadir from Sadir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to make up the daytime supererogatory prayers at night while traveling, and he did not complete a mandatory prayer.' So it is possible that the meaning of this report is what we mentioned in the first report, and it is also possible that he (peace be upon him) only made up these supererogatory prayers if he set out for travel after their time had entered. This possibility is also supported by the first report, that whoever ordered him to make up the supererogatory prayers knew from his state that he had set out after the time had entered, and whoever ordered him to leave them knew from his state that he had set out after the time had passed, and that is what indicates it.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about a man when the sun passes its zenith (time for Dhuhr) while he is at home, then he sets out on a journey. He said: 'He begins with the zenith (Dhuhr) and prays it, then he prays the first (Asr) with shortening (qasr) as two rak'ahs, because he left his home before the time for the first (Asr) had arrived.' And he was asked: If he left after the time for the first (Asr) had arrived? He said: 'He prays the first (Dhuhr) as four rak'ahs, then he prays after that the voluntary prayers (Nawafil) as eight rak'ahs, because he left his home after the time for the first (Asr) had arrived. So when the time for Asr arrives, he prays Asr with shortening, and it is two rak'ahs, because he set out on the journey before the time for Asr had arrived.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatarri narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth.' He said: 'He commanded him to direct his face toward the Qibla, with nothing in it of the worship of idols, purely and sincerely.'

And from him, from Ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And direct your faces toward every mosque.' He said: 'This is also the Qiblah.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Abu Jamilyah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His Exalted Saying, 'And direct your faces toward every mosque,' he said, 'New mosques, so they were commanded to direct their faces toward the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque.' Al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about His Exalted Saying, 'And We did not make the qibla which you were upon except that We might make evident who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels.' He commanded him with it. He said: 'Yes, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was turning his face in the sky, so Allah, Exalted and Majestic, knew what was in his heart, so He said, "We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you toward a qibla with which you will be pleased."'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjāl from some of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Allah the Exalted made the Ka'bah the qiblah for the people of the Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), and made the Mosque the qiblah for the people of the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and made the Sanctuary the qiblah for the people of the world.

Abu al-Abbas ibn 'Uqdah from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hazim, who said: Taghlib ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Ja'far al-Ju'fi, Abu al-Walid, said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: "The House (Kaaba) is the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and the mosque is the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and the Haram is the qiblah for all people."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad, he raised it (to the Imam), saying: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why does a person turn/lean to the left in prayer?' He said: 'Because the Ka'bah has six boundaries, four of them are on your left and two of them are on your right; therefore, for that reason, the turning/leaning occurs to the left.'

Al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deviation of our companions towards the left regarding the Qiblah, and the reason for it. He said: 'Indeed, the Black Stone, when it was sent down from Paradise and placed in its position, the pillars of the Sanctuary were made from where the light reaches it, the light of the Stone. So they are four miles to the right of the Ka'bah and eight miles to its left, all twelve miles. So if a person deviates to the right, he goes out of the boundary of the Qiblah due to the scarcity of the pillars of the Sanctuary, and if he deviates to the left, he is not considered to have gone out of the boundary of the Qiblah.'

Al-Tatarri from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said: I asked him about the qibla (direction of prayer). He said, 'Place the kid goat on your neck and pray.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And when the sky is completely covered with clouds and the person cannot find a sign of it via the sun and stars, let him pray towards the four directions. And if he is unable to do so due to one of the preventing causes from praying four times, let him pray towards whichever direction he wishes, and that is sufficient in case of necessity.'
