From him, from al-Abbas, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A 'khumrah' was brought to my father (peace be upon him) on the day of al-Fitr, so he ordered it to be returned. He said: 'This is a day when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) loved to look at the horizons of the sky and to place his forehead on the ground.'

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the prayer of the two Eids, he said: 'Join the recitation with the recitation.' And he said: 'Begin with the Takbir in the first [rak'ah], then recite, then bow in the seventh [rak'ah].'
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Ubaydillah al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Like it.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would go out until he looked at the horizons of the sky, and he said: 'Prayer should not be performed on that day on a carpet nor on a bare mat.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to perform the ritual bath on the day of Eid until he had prayed. He said: 'If it is still within the time, he must perform the bath and repeat the prayer. And if the time has passed, his prayer is valid.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab), because we have clarified that the ritual bath for the two Eids is a sunnah, not obligatory. Also, we have clarified that whoever misses the Eid prayer is not required to make it up, but it is recommended for him to pray individually, as we have explained.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, it is upon the Imam to release those imprisoned for debt on Friday until Friday, and on Eid until Eid, and he should send them with him; so when they have performed the prayer and the Eid prayer, he should return them to prison.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When you intend to depart on the day of Eid, and the dawn has broken while you are in the town, do not go out until you have performed the Eid prayer."

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) during the Festival of Breaking the Fast (Eid al-Fitr) and the Festival of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), so he said: 'Five and four, so it does not harm you if you finish on an odd number.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Isa ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would not say Takbir in the two Eid prayers except with one Takbir, until his tongue was slow (with age), so Husayn (peace be upon him) would say it. Then, on one Eid day, his mother dressed him and sent him with his grandfather. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said Takbir, and Husayn (peace be upon him) said Takbir when the Prophet said it, seven times. Then he stood for the second time, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said Takbir, and Husayn (peace be upon him) said Takbir when he said it, five times. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made it a Sunnah, and the Sunnah remained established until today.

From him, from al-Abbas, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Bashir ibn Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You say in the supplication of the two Eids, between every two takbirs: 'Allah is my Lord forever, and Islam is my religion forever, and Muhammad is my Prophet forever, and the Quran is my Book forever, and the Ka'bah is my Qiblah forever, and Ali is my Wali forever, and the Successors are my Imams forever,' and you name them until their end, and 'There is no god but Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who missed one rak'ah with the Imam during the days of Tashriq. He said: 'He completes the prayer and says Takbir.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) granted permission to the young women for going out during the two Eid festivals only to seek provision.

From him, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the prayer of the two Eids, he said: 'The prayer is before the two sermons, and the takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) is after the recitation: seven in the first rak'ah and five in the second. The first to innovate this (placing the sermon after the prayer) was Uthman, when he introduced his innovations. When he finished the prayer, the people would stand to return (home), so when he saw that, he advanced the two sermons and detained the people for the prayer.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'When is the sacrifice made?' He said, 'When the Imam departs.' I said, 'And if I am in a land where there is no Imam, and I lead them in congregation prayer,' he said, 'When the sun has reached its zenith.' And he said, 'There is no harm in you praying alone, and there is no prayer except with an Imam.'

Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: "The prayer of the two Eids is only for the resident, and there is no prayer except with an Imam."

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about the speech that is recited between the two takbirs in the two Eid prayers, and he said: 'Whatever good speech you wish.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: «Going out on the day of Fitri (Eid al-Fitr) and Adha (Eid al-Adha) to the prayer ground is recommended for whoever is able to go to it.» I asked, «What do you think if he is sick and cannot go out? Should he pray in his house?» He said, «No.» Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his saying «No» is that it is not obligatory upon him. And if he were to pray alone in his house, he would deserve the reward, according to what we have previously mentioned in the narrations, and it confirms what we said, what he narrated:

Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "My father (peace be upon him) fell ill on the Day of Eid al-Adha, so he prayed two rak'ahs in his house, then offered the sacrifice."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from Yunus said: I asked him about the Takbir of the two Eids: does he raise his hand with every Takbir, or is it sufficient for him to raise it at the first Takbir? He said: 'He raises it with every Takbir.'

From him, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the traveler going to Mecca and other places, is he obligated to perform the prayer of the two Eids, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha? He said: 'Yes, except in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that it is recommended for him, based on the indication of the narrations we presented earlier, and this is confirmed by what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Rib'i ibn 'Abdullah and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no Friday prayer in travel, nor breaking the fast, nor Eid al-Adha."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'It is upon men and women to proclaim the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq after the prayers, and this applies to one who prs alone and to one who prays voluntary prayers.'

From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abdullah ibn Dhubyan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'O Abdullah, there is no day of Eid for the Muslims, Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr, except that Allah renews grief for the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) on it.' I said: 'And for what reason is that?' He said: 'Because they see their right in the hands of others.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That when he led the people in the prayer of Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adhar, he would lower his voice so that those near him could hear, not reciting the Quran aloud. And the sermons and reminders on the days of Eid al-Adhar and Eid al-Fitr are after the prayer.

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Does a man lead his family in the prayer of the two Eids on the roof or in a house?' He said, 'He does not lead them, nor do they go out, and there is no obligation upon the women to go out.' And he said, 'Reduce their formality/dress so that they do not ask to go out.' And Isma'il ibn Jabir narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'What did you see regarding the prayer of the two Eids, is there an Adhan and Iqamah in them?' He said, 'There is no Adhan and no Iqamah in them, but the call is made: "As-Salat, As-Salat" three times. And there is no pulpit (minbar) in them; the pulpit is not moved from its place, but something resembling a pulpit is made for the Imam from clay, so he stands upon it and addresses the people, then he descends.'
From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prayer of the eclipse is obligatory.

From him, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'If you pray the eclipse prayer until the eclipse passes from the sun and the moon, and you prolong your prayer, then that is superior. And if you wish to pray and finish your prayer before the eclipse passes, that is permissible. And if you do not know until the eclipse passes, then you learn afterwards, there is no eclipse prayer upon you. And if someone informs you while you are sleeping, and you learn, then sleep overcomes you and you do not pray, then you must make it up.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjaj, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: We mentioned the partial eclipse of the moon and what people endure of its intensity. He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When a part of it is revealed, it has been revealed.' From him, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said: I wrote to al-Rida (peace be upon him): When the sun and moon are eclipsed and I am riding and cannot dismount, he wrote to me: 'Pray on your mount upon which you are.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Ali (peace be upon him) prayed two rak'ahs during the solar eclipse, with four prostrations and four bowings: he stood and recited, then bowed, then raised his head and recited, then bowed, then stood and supplicated like his standing [in the first rak'ah], then prostrated two prostrations, then stood and did the same as he did in the first [rak'ah] in his recitation, standing, bowing, and prostration, identically.

From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from al-Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The moon was eclipsed, so my father went out and I went out with him to the Sacred Mosque, and he prayed eight rak'at, just as one prays one rak'ah with two prostrations.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What we act upon is what we have previously stated, that the prayer of the eclipse is ten rak'at and four prostrations, according to the details we have clarified. The reason for these two narrations being different is taqiyyah (dissimulation), because they are consistent with the opinion of some of the Sunnis. And that which confirms what we have stated is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the sun and the moon eclipse, and the entire [disk] is eclipsed, it is incumbent upon the people to hasten to an Imam so that he may lead them in prayer. And whichever of them [the sun or moon] is partially eclipsed, it is sufficient for a man to pray alone. The prayer of the eclipse consists of ten bowings (ruku') and four prostrations (sajdahs). The eclipse of the sun is more severe for the people and the animals."

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the prayer of the eclipse: Is it prayed in congregation? He said, 'In congregation and not in congregation.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The sun eclipsed while I was in the bathhouse, and I learned of it after I had exited, so I did not make up the prayer.

From him, from Ahmad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about the prayer of the eclipse, and whether there is a make-up (qada) upon the one who leaves it. He said: 'If it passes you by, then there is no make-up upon you.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified the reasoning in examples of these two narrations, and the summary is that if the entire disk [of the sun] is eclipsed, make-up is obligatory upon the one for whom the eclipse prayer passes by; and if it is not entirely eclipsed and it passes him by, there is no make-up upon him. And there is no contradiction between the narrations, and this does not contradict what Ammar al-Sabati narrated in the narration we presented earlier from his saying: 'Make-up is only obligatory upon the one who was informed but did not pray until it passed him by,' because the reasoning in this narration is to interpret it as referring to when part of the disk is eclipsed and he was negligent in praying, then at that time make-up becomes obligatory upon him. And we only exempted make-up for the one who did not know about the partial eclipse at all. And upon this, the narrations are harmonized and do not differ.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Ja'far from his father from their fathers, peace be upon them, said: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he led the people in two rak'ahs, prolonging [the prayer] until some of the people behind him fainted due to the length of standing.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from 'Asim from Abu Basir said: The moon was eclipsed while I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the month of Ramadan, so he stood up quickly and said, 'It used to be said: When the moon and the sun are eclipsed, hasten to your mosques.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the prayer of the eclipse before the sun sets, and we fear missing the obligatory prayer, so he said: 'Cut it short, perform the obligatory prayer, and return to your eclipse prayer.'

From him, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sabati, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the prayer of the eclipse, whether it is prayed in congregation or individually, so he said, 'Choose whichever you prefer.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Yaqtin who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is afflicted by an earthquake, let him recite: O He who "He holds the heavens and the earth from ceasing (to exist), and if they were to cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving." Pray upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hold back evil from us. 'Indeed, You are over all things competent.' He (the Imam) said: 'Indeed, whoever recites it before sleeping, a house will not fall upon him, if God wills.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr and Fadalah, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the obligatory prayer on a ship, when he finds the land and can disembark, but he fears wild beasts and thieves, and there are people with him whose opinion does not unite on disembarking and they do not obey him. And whether he places his face (in prostration) when he prays, or signals with a nod, or prays sitting or standing? He said: 'If he is able to pray standing, that is better, and if he is not able, he prays sitting.' And he said: 'There is no harm on him if he does not disembark, for a man asked my father about a similar issue, and he said: 'Do you prefer to miss the prayer of Noah?''

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer on a ship. He said, 'Indeed, a man came to my father (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq) and asked him, saying: I am on a ship and the sea is rough/close to me, so I go out and pray upon it. He (Abu Ja'far) said to him: Do you not accept that you pray with the prayer of Noah (peace be upon him)?'

Al-Husayn narrated from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about prayer on a ship. He said: 'Face the Qiblah with your face, then pray as it turns. You pray standing; if you cannot, then pray sitting. He combines the prayer in it if he wishes, and prays on the stern and the bow, and prostrates on them.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Salih ibn al-Hakam, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about prayer on a ship. He said, 'Indeed, a man asked my father about prayer on a ship, so he said to him, "Do you wish to abandon the prayer of Noah (peace be upon him)?"' I said to him, 'Shall I take a small mat with me and prostrate upon it?' He said, 'Yes.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-A'lawi, from al-Amriki al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The companions of ships complete their prayer in their ships.
From him, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm in praying in congregation on the ship."

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-A'lawi, from al-Amriki al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about a group who prayed congregationally on a ship: where does the Imam stand, and if there are women with them, what do they do? Do they pray standing or sitting? He said: 'They pray standing. If they cannot manage standing, they pray sitting, and the Imam stands in front of them and the women are behind them. And if the ship is cramped, the women sit and the men pray, and there is no harm if the women are facing them.' And I asked him about a man whose belongings were cut off or sank, leaving him naked, and prayer time arrived: how does he pray? He said: 'If he finds grass to cover his awrah, he completes his prayer with ruku' and sujud. If he does not find anything to cover his awrah, he gestures while standing.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: I was with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) on a boat on the Tigris, and prayer time arrived, so I said, 'May I be your ransom, should we pray in congregation?' He said, 'Do not pray in congregation in the belly of a river.' This does not contradict the reports we have previously mentioned regarding the permissibility of congregation on a boat, because this report is understood as indicating a type of dislike, or a situation where standing together is not possible but can be done individually. And that which clarifies what we mentioned regarding the permissibility of congregation on a boat is what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah and Ayub ibn Nuha from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah said: Uyaynah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about praying in congregation on a ship, so he said, 'There is no harm.'

Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about prayer on a ship. He said: 'He should face the Qiblah. When it turns, if he is able to face the Qiblah, let him do so; otherwise, let him pray wherever it carries him.' He said: 'If he is able to stand, let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the obligatory prayer on a ship that moves east and west, so he said: 'Face the Qibla, then say Takbir, then follow the ship and move with it wherever it turns you.'

Ahmad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about praying in the Euphrates and what is weaker than it from the rivers, while on the ship. He said, 'If you pray, it is good, and if you get off, it is good.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the ship when its owner is unable to stand; should he pray while sitting, gesturing or prostrating? He said: 'He should stand, even if his back is bent.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to apply when he is able to stand; as for when he is not able to stand, it is permissible to restrict himself to praying while sitting and gesturing as we have clarified, and what was narrated also confirms this.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Prayer on a ship is [performed by] nodding."

From him, from Uyaynah, the seller of reeds, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We travel to Ahwaz on ships, so we combine the prayer in them.' He said, 'Yes, there is no harm in that.' I said, 'And we prostrate on what is in them and on the pitch (tar)?' He said, 'There is no harm.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I departed from Kufa on a ship to Qasr ibn Hubayra, which is about twenty farsakhs from Kufa across the water. I traveled that day shortening the prayer. Then it occurred to me at night to return to Kufa, so I did not know whether to shorten or complete the prayer upon my return, and what I should do. He said: If you traveled on the day you departed at a steady pace (breid), then upon your return you must shorten the prayer, because you remained a traveler until you reached your home. He said: And if you did not travel on the day you departed at a steady pace, then you must make up every prayer you shortened that day by praying it fully, before you stop at that place, because you did not reach the distance that permits shortening until you returned. Thus, it became obligatory upon you to make up what you shortened, and upon your return you must complete the prayer until you reach your home.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said: I asked him about a captive whom the polytheists capture, and prayer time approaches, but the one who captured him prevents him from praying. He said: 'He gestures with a nod.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: I asked him and said: 'If I am on the road to Mecca and leave the prayer in places where there are Bedouins, should I perform the obligatory prayer on the ground and recite only the Opening of the Book, or should I pray on the mount and recite the Opening of the Book and the chapter?' He said: 'When you fear, pray on the mount the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers. If you recite the Praise and a chapter, it is more beloved to me, and I do not see any harm in what you have done.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So if you fear, [then pray] on foot or riding' — how should we pray? And what should one say if he fears from a beast of prey or a thief? How should he pray? He said: 'He should say Takbir and gesture with his head.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: "When the Maghrib prayer is performed in fear, they are divided into two groups. The Imam prays with one group for two rak'ahs, then sits with them, then gestures to them with his hand, so each person stands up and prays one rak'ah, then they say the Taslim. They stand in the place of their companions, and the other group comes forward, says Takbir, and enters the prayer. The Imam stands and prays one rak'ah with them, then says Taslim. Then each man from them stands and prays one rak'ah, completing it with the one he prayed with the Imam. Then he stands and prays one rak'ah in which there is no recitation, so it is completed for the Imam three rak'ahs, and for the first group two rak'ahs in congregation, and for the latter group individually. Thus, for the first group is the Takbir and the opening of the prayer, and for the latter group is the Taslim."

And this news was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fadl and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): like that. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between this news and the news of al-Halabi which we presented earlier, that the Imam prays one rak'ah with the first group, and in this narration it is that he prays two rak'ahs with them, because in both news the person is free to choose; whichever he acts upon, it is sufficient for him, and there is no contradiction between them, nor incompatibility, provided that Zurarah, the narrator of this hadith, narrated like the narration of al-Halabi.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The prayer of fear for Maghrib: He prays with the first group one rak'ah, and they complete two rak'ahs, and He prays with the second group two rak'ahs, and they complete one rak'ah.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi'za from Abu Basir said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If you saw me while I was on the bank of the Euphrates praying and I was fearing the wild beasts,' he said to me, 'Why did you not pray while you were riding?'

Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Prayer of Fear and the Traveler's Prayer, are both shortened? He said, 'Yes, and the Prayer of Fear is more deserving of being shortened than the Traveler's Prayer, because there is no fear in it.'

Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa'dan from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one who fears wild beasts, or fears an enemy that will pounce upon him, or fears thieves: he prays the obligatory prayer on his mount, indicating with gestures.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban, so he praised God and extolled Him, then he said: 'O people, a month has overshadowed you in which is a night better than a thousand months God made its fasting obligatory and made the standing in prayer of one night within it, by voluntary prayer, like one who voluntarily prays for seventy nights in the other months. And He made for one who voluntarily performs in it a characteristic from the characteristics of goodness and piety, like the reward of one who fulfills an obligation from the obligations of God, Exalted and Glorified. And whoever fulfills in it an obligation from the obligations of God, Exalted and Glorified, is like one who fulfills seventy obligations from the obligations of God in the other months. And it is the month of patience, and indeed patience's reward is Paradise, and it is the month of sharing. And it is a month in which God increases the provision of the believers. And whoever breaks the fast of a fasting believer in it, for him with God is thereby the freeing of a neck and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed. It was said to him: O Messenger of God, not all of us can afford to break the fast of a fasting person. So he said: 'Indeed God, the Exalted, is Generous; He gives this reward to one who can afford nothing but a sip of milk with which he breaks the fast from that, or a drink of fresh water, or a date, who cannot afford more than that. And whoever eases for his slave in it, God will ease his reckoning. And it is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance and freeing from the Fire. And you have no need in it to be without four characteristics: two characteristics by which you please God, and two characteristics by which you have no need to be without them. As for the two by which you please God, they are the testimony that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God. And as for the two by which you have no need to be without them, you ask God in it for your needs and Paradise, and you ask for well-being and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said: He said to me: 'Pray in the night of the 21st and the night of the 23rd of the month of Ramadan; in each of them, if you are able, one hundred rak'ahs, in addition to the thirteen [nightly prayers], and stay awake in them until morning, for it is recommended that you be in prayer, supplication, and humility, for it is hoped that the Night of Decree is in one of them.' And [it is mentioned that] 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.' I said to him: 'How is it better than a thousand months?' He said: 'The worship in it is better than the worship in a thousand months, and the Night of Decree is not in those months, but it occurs in the month of Ramadan.' And 'In it is made distinct every precise matter.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'Whatever occurs during the year is written in it, and the delegation [of angels/decree] to Mecca is written in it.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). He said: 'It is the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third.' I said: 'Is it not only one night?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then inform me which one it is.' He said: 'What does it matter to you if you do good in both nights?'

From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Basir asked him: 'The night in which what is hoped for is hoped for?' He said: 'On the twenty-first or the twenty-third.' Abu Basir said: 'If I cannot manage both?' He said: 'How easy are two nights for what you are seeking.' I said: 'Perhaps we see the new moon here, and someone comes to inform us of the opposite in another land?' He said: 'How easy are four nights to seek in them.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, the night of the twenty-third is the night of al-Juhani?' He said: 'Indeed, that is said.' I said: 'Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated regarding the nineteenth, that the delegation of the pilgrims is written?' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, the delegation of the pilgrims is written on the Night of Decree, along with destinies, calamities, provisions, and whatever occurs like it in the coming year. So seek them in the twenty-first and twenty-third, and pray one hundred rak'ahs in each of them, and keep them awake if you can.' I said: 'And if I cannot?' He said: 'It is not a problem for you to close your eyes in the beginning of the night with some sleep. Indeed, the gates of heaven are opened in Ramadan, the devils are chained, and the deeds of the believers are accepted. What a good month is Ramadan; it was called al-Marzooq (the Provisioned) during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Isa al-Qammadi, from his uncle, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was shown in his sleep the Banu Umayya climbing his pulpit after him and misleading people from the path backwards, so he became sorrowful and sad. Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you sorrowful and sad?' He said: 'O Gabriel, I saw the Banu Umayya in this night of mine climbing my pulpit after me and misleading people from the path backwards.' He said: 'And He who sent you with the truth, this is something I had not been informed of.' Then he ascended to the heaven, and he did not delay before descending upon him with a verse from the Quran to comfort him with it. Have you seen if We grant them respite for years, then comes to them that which they were promised? What would their respite avail them? And Allah revealed to him: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.' Allah made a night for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) better than a thousand months of the rule of Banu Umayya, may Allah curse them. And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, brother of Hisham, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, for Allah, the Exalted, there are freedmen from the Fire every day of the month of Ramadan, except for one who breaks his fast on a drinker of intoxicants, or a quarrelsome person, or a companion of two dice. I said: 'And what is a companion of two dice?' He said: 'Chess.'

Ali ibn Hatim from Humayd ibn Ziyad said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nahiki narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the month of Ramadan arrived, would increase in prayer, and I increase, so you should increase.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Isma'il ibn Mihran from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked: 'Is it added to the voluntary prayers in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray after 'Isha' in his place of prayer, and he would prolong it. The people would gather behind him to pray with his prayer. When they became numerous behind him, he would leave them and enter his house. When the people dispersed, he would return to his place of prayer and pray as he used to pray. When the people became numerous behind him, he would leave them and enter his house. He used to do this repeatedly.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: Indeed, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'These companions of ours refused to increase in their prayer during Ramadan, whereas the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) increased in his prayer during the month of Ramadan.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Basir: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Does a man increase in prayer during Ramadan? He said, 'Yes, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had increased in prayer during Ramadan.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq and 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would increase in his prayer during the month of Ramadan. When he prayed the 'Isha prayer, he would pray after it. The people would stand behind him, so he would enter and leave them, then he would come out again, and they would come and stand behind him, so he would enter and leave them, repeatedly. He said, and he said: 'Do not pray after the 'Isha prayer in months other than Ramadan.'

Ali ibn Hatim from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Adib said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "If you are able to pray one thousand rak'ahs during the day and night in the month of Ramadan and in other months, then do so, for indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to pray one thousand rak'ahs during the day and night."

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Isma'il ibn Mihran from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Ja'fari that he heard al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) saying: On the night of the twenty-first and three and twenty hundred, there are twenty-three rak'ahs; in each rak'ah, 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' is recited ten times.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Bundar, who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever prays on the night of the middle of the month of Ramadan with one hundred rak'ahs, reciting

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Among what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do in the month of Ramadan was that he would perform voluntary prayers every night, increasing upon the prayer he used to pray before that from the first night until the completion of twenty nights: in each night twenty rak'ahs, eight of them after Maghrib and twelve after the final 'Isha, and he would pray in the last ten nights in each night thirty rak'ahs: twelve of them after Maghrib and eighteen after the final 'Isha, and he would supplicate and strive with intense striving. And he would pray in the night of the twenty-first one hundred rak'ahs, and he would pray in the night of the twenty-third one hundred rak'ahs, and he would strive in them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Basir asked him, 'What do you say about prayer in Ramadan?' He replied to him, 'Indeed, Ramadan has a sanctity and a right that is not like any of the other months. Pray as much as you can in Ramadan as voluntary prayer by night and by day. And if you can pray one thousand rak'ahs each day and night, then pray, for indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to pray one thousand rak'ahs each day and night in the last period of his life. So pray, O Abu Muhammad, as an addition in Ramadan.' He asked, 'How many? I am your ransom.' He said, 'For twenty nights, pass in each night twenty rak'ahs: eight rak'ahs before the 'Atamah (late night) prayer and twelve after it, besides what you used to pray before that. And when the last ten nights enter, pray thirty rak'ahs each night: eight before the 'Atamah and two and twenty after the 'Atamah, besides what you used to do before that.'

Ali ibn Hatim from Ali ibn Sulayman al-Zurari said: He narrated to us Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Pray eight rak'ahs on the twentieth of the month of Ramadan after Maghrib, and twelve rak'ahs after 'Atamah (late night prayer). When it is the night in which what is hoped for is hoped for (Laylat al-Qadr), pray one hundred rak'ahs, reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' ten times in each rak'ah. I said: May I be your ransom, if I cannot stand, he said: Then sit. I said: If I cannot sit, he said: Then pray while lying on your bed.

Ali ibn Hatim from Ahmad ibn Ali, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Subhan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, who said: Indeed, a number of our companions gathered upon this hadith, among them Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Sabbah al-Hadhdha' from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Muhammad ibn Sulayman said: And I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about this hadith, and he informed me of it. He said: 'All of these asked about the prayer in the month of Ramadan, how it is and what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did. They all said: When the first night of Ramadan entered, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Maghrib, then prayed four rak'ahs which he used to pray after Maghrib every night, then prayed eight rak'ahs. When he prayed the final Isha and the two rak'ahs which he used to pray after the final Isha while sitting every night, he stood up and prayed twelve rak'ahs. Then he entered his house. When the people saw this and looked at the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who had increased in prayer when Ramadan entered, they asked him about that, and he informed them: "I prayed this prayer for the virtue of the month of Ramadan over the other months."' When it was night, he stood to pray and the people lined up behind him. He turned to them and said: 'O people, this prayer is a supererogatory (nafl) prayer, and congregation is not established for nafl. Let each man from you pray alone, and let him recite what Allah taught him from His Book. And know that there is no congregation in nafl.' So the people dispersed, and each one of them prayed on his own for himself. When it was the night of the nineteenth of Ramadan, he bathed when the sun set and prayed Maghrib with his bath. When he prayed Maghrib and the four rak'ahs which he used to pray in the past every night after Maghrib, he entered his house. When Bilal called for the final Isha prayer, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came out and prayed with the people. When he finished, he prayed the two rak'ahs while sitting as he used to do every night. Then he stood up and prayed one hundred rak'ahs, reciting the Opening of the Book and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' ten times in each r

Ali ibn Hatim from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Butta al-Qummi from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Extra prayers of one thousand rak'ahs are prayed in the month of Ramadan. I said: 'And who can manage that?' He said: 'Not where you go, do you not pray extra of one thousand rak'ahs in the month of Ramadan? Nineteen of them, in each night twenty rak'ahs; and in the night of the nineteenth, one hundred rak'ahs; and in the night of the twenty-first, one hundred rak'ahs; and in the night of the twenty-third, one hundred rak'ahs; and you pray in eight nights of it, in the last ten, thirty rak'ahs. So these are nine hundred and eighty rak'ahs.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, you have relieved me; the matter had indeed become tight for me, but when you came to me with the explanation, you relieved me. So how is the completion of the thousand rak'ahs?' He said: 'You pray in every Friday during the month of Ramadan four rak'ahs for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); and you pray two rak'ahs for the daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family); and after the two rak'ahs, you pray four rak'ahs for Ja'far al-Tayyar; and you pray in the night of Friday during the last ten [nights] for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) twenty rak'ahs; and you pray in the evening of Friday, the night of Saturday, twenty rak'ahs for the daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' Then he said: 'Listen, pay attention, and teach the trustworthy ones of your brothers these four and the two rak'ahs, for they are the best of prayers after the obligatory ones. Whoever prays them in the month of Ramadan or in other months, he is released, and there is no sin between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' Then he said: 'O Mufaddal ibn Umar, you recite in all of these prayers, meaning the extra prayer of the month of Ramadan, with Al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad. If you wish, once; if you wish, three times; if you wish, five times; if you wish, seven times; if you wish, ten times.' As for the prayer of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), you recite in it Al

From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman, who said: We were narrated by Ali ibn Abi Khulays, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Mutahhir narrated to me, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): That a man narrated from your forefathers (peace be upon them) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not increase in prayer during the month of Ramadan beyond what he used to pray on other days. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He lied, may Allah expose his mouth. Pray twenty rak'ahs every night of the month of Ramadan until the twentieth of the month, and pray on the night of the twenty-first one hundred rak'ahs, and pray on the night of the twenty-third one hundred rak'ahs, and pray in each of the last ten nights thirty rak'ahs.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mutahhar: That he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) informing him of what the narration had brought, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray in the month of Ramadan and other nights except thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr and the two rak'ahs of Fajr. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'May God open his mouth. Pray in the month of Ramadan, in twenty nights, every night twenty rak'ahs: eight after Maghrib and twelve after the last 'Isha. And bathe on the night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third. And pray in them thirty rak'ahs: twelve rak'ahs after Maghrib and eighteen rak'ahs after the last 'Isha. And pray in them one hundred rak'ahs, reading in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and "Say: He is Allah, One" ten times. And pray until the end of the month, every night thirty rak'ahs, as I have explained.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Halabi said: I asked him about the prayer in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'Thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and two rak'at of the morning prayer after Fajr. Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray, and I pray thus. And if it were better, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have left it.' And from him from Hammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the prayer in the month of Ramadan, he said: 'Thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and two rak'at before the Fajr prayer. Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray, and if it were a virtue, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have acted upon it and been more deserving.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Halabi and al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Thaqafi, all from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) finished the last Isha prayer, he would retire to his bed and not pray anything except after the middle of the night, neither in the month of Ramadan nor in other months.' The meaning in these narrations and those that follow the same pattern is that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray the voluntary prayer in congregation during the month of Ramadan. And if there were goodness in it, he would not have left it (peace be upon him and his family). And he did not mean that it is impermissible to pray individually. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Madani, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the prayer in Ramadan in the mosques. He said: "When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) arrived in Kufa, he ordered al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) to announce to the people: 'There is no congregational prayer in the mosques during the month of Ramadan.' So al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) announced to the people what his Commander had ordered. When the people heard al-Hasan ibn Ali's statement, they cried out, 'O Umarah! O Umarah!' When al-Hasan returned to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), he said to him, 'What is this noise?' He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, the people are crying out, O Umarah! O Umarah!' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Tell them to pray.'" Thus, when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) disapproved, he disapproved of the congregation (collective gathering) and did not disapprove of the prayer itself. When he saw that the matter was becoming corrupted for him and the people were being tested (fitnah), he permitted it and ordered them to pray according to their custom. All of this is clear, praise be to God.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was taken (died), three customs were established. As for one of them: when he died, the sun was eclipsed, and the people said, "The sun was eclipsed due to the loss of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)." So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, "O people, the sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they move by His command, obedient to Him. They do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for their life. So when they eclipse, or one of them, pray." Then he descended and led the people in the prayer of the eclipse.'

Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) these winds and darknesses that occur, is prayer offered for them? He said: 'Every phenomenon in the sky of darkness, or wind, or alarm, offer prayer for it the prayer of the eclipse until it subsides.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad ibn Humran said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The time for the prayer of the eclipse is not during the hour in which the eclipse occurs at sunrise, nor during the hour in which it occurs at sunset." And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "It is an obligatory duty."

And from him, from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, sometimes we are tested with an eclipse after Maghrib but before the final Isha prayer. If we pray the eclipse prayer, we fear missing the obligatory [Isha] prayer.' He said, 'If you fear that, cut off your eclipse prayer, fulfill your obligatory prayer, then return to it.' I said, 'And if the eclipse is at the end of the night, and we pray the eclipse prayer but miss the night prayer [Tahajjud/Qiyam], which of the two do we begin with?' He said, 'Pray the eclipse prayer and fulfill the night prayer when you wake up in the morning.'
And from him, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The prayer of the eclipse: if you finish before it clears, then repeat it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, they said: We asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer of the eclipse, how many rak'ahs are there in it and how do we pray it? He said: 'It is ten rak'ahs and four prostrations. You begin the prayer with a takbir, and bow with a takbir, and raise your head with a takbir, except in the fifth one in which you prostrate, so you say 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah', and you make du'a (qunut) in every two rak'ahs before the bowing, and you prolong the qunut, bowing, and prostration according to the length of the recitation, bowing, and prostration. So when you finish before the eclipse clears, sit and supplicate to Allah until it clears. If it clears before you finish your prayer, then complete what remains. You recite aloud.' I said: How is the recitation in it? He said: 'If you recite a surah in every rak'ah, then recite Fatihat al-Kitab. If you are short of the surah, then recite from where you are short, and do not recite Fatihat al-Kitab.' He said: 'And it was preferred in it that Surah Al-Kahf and Surah Al-Hijr be recited, unless the imam is one who makes it difficult for those behind him. If you can make your prayer prominent (outdoors) so that a house does not obscure you, then do so. And the prayer of the solar eclipse is longer than the prayer of the lunar eclipse, and they are equal in recitation, bowing, and prostration.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad from Hariz from one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the moon is eclipsed, if a man wakes up and is sluggish to pray, he should perform a ritual bath (ghusl) tomorrow and make up the prayer; and if he did not wake up and did not know of the moon's eclipse, then upon him is only making up the prayer without a bath."

Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer of the eclipse: is it compensated if it is missed? He said, 'There is no compensation for it.' And we had previously held that it is compensated, so the meaning of this report is that if the disk [of the sun] is not entirely consumed, but if it is entirely consumed, then compensation is necessary according to what we have previously stated, and to add clarification to it is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the sun is fully eclipsed and burned out, and you did not know [about it], and you knew afterwards, then you must make up [the prayer]; and if it did not fully burn out, then there is no making up upon you." This is the report, and that which we mentioned earlier from the narration of Hariz came as two detailed reports, and the hadith of 'there is no making up upon him' is general, and the ruling of the detailed [report] over the general is more preferable.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Harun ibn Muslim from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) He said: 'Zakat is obligatory in nine things: upon gold and silver, wheat and barley, dates and raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned/excepted whatever is besides that.'

And from him from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the alms-tax of wealth, and he said: 'It is obligatory in nine things; there is nothing in others. [It is obligatory] in gold and silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and grazing sheep (which are the grazing ones). And there is nothing in any of the animals other than these three categories. And for everything that is from these three categories, there is nothing [obligatory] until a year passes over it, from the day it is weaned.' In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful; and to Him belongs all praise, and by Him we seek help.

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Abu Basir and Al-Hasan ibn Shihab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated Zakat upon nine items and excused (exempted) what is other than that: upon gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydillah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about the alms-tax (zakat). He said: 'The zakat is obligatory on nine things: on gold and silver, on wheat and barley, on dates and raisins, on camels, on cattle, and on sheep. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned/exempted whatever is besides that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) who said: "Allah prescribed al-Zakat along with al-Salat in wealth, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) established it in nine things, and excused what is other than them in gold and silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused what is other than that."

And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated zakat upon nine items: upon wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, camels, cattle, and sheep, and forgave (exempted) whatever is besides that. As for what has been narrated in the reports regarding that which is beyond these nine items, that zakat is due upon it, such as what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the crops from which zakat is due, and he said: 'Wheat, barley, millet, drought-resistant grain, rice, lentils, and sesame; all of these are subject to zakat, and their like.'

And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the crops from which zakat is due, and he said: 'Wheat, barley, millet, rice, salt, and lentils; all of these are from that which zakat is due.' And he said: 'Everything that is measured by the sa' and reaches the awsan (thresholds), upon it is zakat.' And whatever runs in their manner from that which entails the obligation of zakat upon it, then it is considered recommended and preferred rather than obligatory and mandatory. And we said this so that the reports do not contradict each other, and because in what we mentioned earlier from the reports, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned what is other than that. And if these items were among that which zakat is obligatory upon, they would not be pardoned. And that which clarifies what we mentioned and makes it clear is that they did not say that there is zakat in these items in the manner of obligation and mandatory duty.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi and al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, all from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Tayyar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what requires zakat, and he said: 'In nine things: gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused what is other than that.' I said: May Allah make you upright, for we have much grain (habb). He said: 'And what is it?' I said: Rice. He said: 'Yes, if it is abundant.' I said: Is there zakat in it? He rebuked me, saying: 'I tell you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused what is other than that, and you say to me: We have much grain, is there zakat in it?'

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated Zakat upon nine things, and excused (exempted) whatever is besides that: upon silver, gold, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep.' Al-Tayyar said to him, while I was present: 'Indeed, we have a lot of grain called rice.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'And we have a lot of grain.' He said: 'Is there something due upon it?' He said: 'No, I have already informed you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused whatever is besides that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I read in the book of 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom,' that it was narrated from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated zakat upon nine items: upon wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, sheep, cattle, and camels, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned/exempted what is besides that.' The questioner said to him: 'We have many things that are multiples of that.' He said to him, 'What is it?' He said to him, 'Rice.' So Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I say to you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated the charity (zakat) upon nine items and pardoned what is besides that, and you say that we have rice and we have sorghum/durra? Sorghum was present during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Thus it is, and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'.' If it were not that he (peace be upon him) meant by his statement 'and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'' what we have previously mentioned of recommendation and preference, he would not have validated the statement of the questioner that zakat is upon nine items and that what is besides it is exempted, and that Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) objected to the one who said 'we have rice and sorghum,' admonishing him that there is no obligatory zakat in it. And his statement 'thus it is' along with his statement 'and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'' would be contradictory, and this is not permissible in their statements (peace be upon them). And what indicates what we mentioned is also what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to me from Hammad ibn Isa from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of Aynan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no khums in anything that the earth produces, such as rice, corn, chickpeas, lentils, and all other grains and fruits, other than these four types, even if their price is high, unless they become wealth that is sold for gold or silver, stored up, and then a year passes over them, and they have become gold or silver; then one must pay from them five dirhams for every two hundred dirhams, and half a dinar for every twenty dinars."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent; is Zakat obligatory upon him? He said, 'No, until he arrives.' I said, 'Does he pay Zakat when he arrives?' He said, 'No, until a full year passes over it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: "Zakat is due on silent wealth upon which the year has passed and which has not been moved (i.e., not spent or circulated)."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who accumulates wealth. He said, 'He does not pay its zakat until a full year (hawl) passes over it.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man had two hundred dirhams, excluding one dirham, for eleven months. Then he acquired one dirham after that in the twelfth month, so two hundred dirhams became complete with him. Is there zakat upon it? He said: 'No, until the year (hawl) passes over it while it is two hundred dirhams. If it was one hundred and fifty dirhams, and he acquired fifty after a month had passed, there is no zakat upon him until the year passes over the two hundred.' I said to him: If he had two hundred dirhams, excluding one dirham, and days passed over them before the month ended, then he acquired one dirham, and a year passed over the dirhams along with that one dirham, is there zakat upon it? He said: 'Yes. If the year did not pass over all of them together, there is nothing upon him regarding it.' Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whichever man has wealth and the year passes over it, he must pay its zakat.' I said to him: If he gifted it before its due date by a month or two days? He said: 'There is nothing upon him ever.' And Zurarah narrated from him that he said: 'This is like a man who broke his fast for one day during his residence in the month of Ramadan, then he leaves at the end of the day on a journey, and he intends by that journey to invalidate the expiation that became obligatory upon him.' He said: 'When he saw the twelfth new moon, zakat became obligatory upon him. But if he had gifted it before that, it would be valid and there would be nothing upon him. This is like the one who left (on journey) then broke his fast. He does not prevent what has become obligatory upon him. As for what has not become obligatory upon him, he has the right to prevent it. And it is permissible for him to prevent the wealth of others regarding what has become obligatory upon them.' Zurarah said: I said to him: A man had two hundred dirhams and he gifted them to one of his brothers, or his children, or his family, to flee from the zakat, and he did that before its due date by a month. He said: 'When the twelfth month enters, the year has passed over it and zakat has become obligatory upon him regarding it.' I said to him: If he made a new gift (or altered the status) regarding it before th

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah ibn Musa said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has land (da'wah) and pays its land tax (kharaj); is there a khums due on it? He said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, they said: We mentioned to him (peace be upon him) Kufa and the land tax levied upon it, and what the people of his household had acquired in it, so he said: "Whoever voluntarily submits, his land is left in his hand, and the tenth (ushr) is taken from him for what is watered by rain and rivers, and half the tenth for what was rare in what they cultivated of it. And what they did not cultivate of it, the Imam takes and leases it to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And upon those who lease it, in their shares, is the tenth and half the tenth. And there is no zakat in less than five awsiq. And what is conquered by the sword, that is for the Imam to lease as he sees fit, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Khaybar; he leased its black land and its white land, meaning its land and its palm trees. And the people say that leasing the land and palm trees is not suitable, yet the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leased Khaybar. And upon those who lease, besides the leasing of the land, is the tenth and half the tenth in their shares." And he said: "Indeed, the people of Ta'if submitted, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. And indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca by conquest, and they were captives in his hand, he freed them and said: 'Go, you are free.' And he said: "Indeed, the people of Ta'if submitted, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. And indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca by conquest, and they were captives in his hand, he freed them and said: 'Go, you are free.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the zakat of the land: when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) or the Imam (peace be upon him) takes a share (qabala) by half, third, or quarter, the zakat is upon him, and there is no zakat upon the one who receives it, unless the owner of the land stipulates that the zakat is upon the recipient. If he stipulates, then the zakat is upon them. And today, there is no zakat upon the people of the land except upon whoever has something in his hand from what the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) granted. Therefore, this report is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because the meaning of his saying 'and there is no zakat upon the recipient' is that there is no zakat upon him for all that emerges from the land, although he is obliged with the zakat of what accrues in his hand after the division. And that which indicates what we said is the report we preceded from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said in his hadith: 'And the tithe is not upon all that Allah brings out of it, but the tithe is upon you regarding what accrues in your hand after its division to you.' Thus, this report is detailed (mufassal) and the other report is general (mujmal), and ruling with the detailed is more worthy than ruling with the general over the detailed. As for what this hadith included of his saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is no zakat upon the people of the land today,' it means that today a concession has been granted today to whoever zakat is obligatory upon him, and the unjust ruler takes from him, that he may count it as zakat, although it is better to pay it again, because that is a wrong that was done to him. And that which indicates this concession is what was narrated...

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khadid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the companions of my father came to him and asked him about what the ruler takes. He felt distressed for them, and indeed he knew that zakat is not permissible except for its specific recipients, so he ordered them to count it [as zakat] with the ruler, and by God it was sufficient for them. I said: O my father, if they heard that, no one would pay zakat. He said: O my son, it is true; God loved that it be made manifest.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tawil, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'from Ishaq ibn al-Qasim' (note: variant reading), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding zakat, he said: 'What the Banu Umayya have taken from you, consider it [as sufficient], and do not give them anything as long as you are able, for wealth cannot be purified twice in the same manner.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abu Ja'far, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the alms-tax (zakat) of wealth that the ruler takes, so he said, 'I do not command you to return it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim ibn Uthman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Usamah who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, indeed these collectors come to us and take the charity (sadaqah/zakat) from us, so we give it to them; does it count for us?' He said, 'No, indeed these are a people who have taken it from you by force,' or he said, 'They have wronged you regarding your wealth,' and indeed the charity is only for its rightful recipients. This report indicates what we mentioned, that it is preferable to return it (pay again). It is also possible that what is meant by his saying 'No, it does not count' is that it does not count for the other wealth, because when they take the zakat of the crops/produce, they take more than what is due, so it is not permissible for him to count the excess from the zakat of gold and silver and other things. Rather, it must be paid out separately. And it was permitted and allowed that one does not pay out a second time from the very thing from which it was taken. As for that which indicates that the charity of the produce is not due more than once, is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Any man who has crops or fruit and gives its zakat is not obliged to pay anything in it if the year passes while it is in his possession, unless he converts it into capital wealth; and if he does so and the year passes while it is in his possession, he must pay its zakat, otherwise there is no obligation upon him even if it remains for a thousand years, provided it remains in its original form. He is only obliged to pay the tithe (zakat al-'ushr). If he pays it once, there is no obligation upon him until it is converted into capital wealth and the year passes while it is in his possession." The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: As for the livestock, zakat is obligatory upon them specifically only if they are sa'imah (grazing in pastures) and the year passes over them.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd al-Ajli and al-Fadl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) said: "There is no zakat on the camels and cattle of the workers (or: on the camels and cattle themselves, depending on interpretation of 'al-'amalat' as workers or plural of 'amal/work'), rather the zakat is on the 'saimah' (the grazing livestock kept for profit), and whatever has not completed its year (hawl) at its owner, there is no zakat upon it; so when the year completes upon it, it becomes obligatory upon it."

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Harun ibn Muslim from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said: There is no zakat in any of the animals, except for these three categories: camels, cattle, and sheep. And for every animal from these categories that is among the poultry or draft animals, there is no zakat until a full year passes from the day it is born.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked him about the camels that belong to the camel-herds (or are kept for breeding/commercial use) and are in some of the regions (or pastures): does zakat apply to them as it applies to the grazing livestock in the desert? He said: 'Yes.'

And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Isḥaq, who said: I asked Abu Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the working camels; is there zakāt upon them? He said, 'Yes, there is zakāt upon them.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Bahr from Abdullah ibn Muskān from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the camels that belong to the camel-herders, or that are in some of the cities, does zakat apply to them as it applies to the grazing [livestock] in the desert? He said, 'Yes.' In all these hadiths, the primary narrator is Isḥq ibn ʿAmmār; and if the primary narrator in them is one person, they are not objected to against what we have previously presented from the hadiths. And although the primary narrator in them is one, their wording differs because in the first hadith he said, 'I asked him,' and did not specify who the questioned one was, and it is possible that he was an Imam or not an Imam. And in the second report he said, 'I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him),' and in the third hadith he said, 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).'
