The narrator is one person, so sometimes he narrates it as mursal (without specifying the Imam), and sometimes he narrates from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and sometimes he narrates from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him). And this fluctuation in it indicates that he narrated it while he was not certain of it. and whatever follows this pattern is not obligatory to act upon. And if it were safe from all of that, it would be construed as recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory (farḍ) and compulsory (ijab). And that which indicates that zakat is not obligatory in it except after a full year has passed, added to what we have previously presented, is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no khums in young camels, cattle, and sheep, except what has completed a year in the possession of the man, and there is no khums in their offspring until a year has passed over them."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Soehan, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from a man, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Zakat is not purified from camels, cattle, and sheep except that which has had the year pass over it; and that which has not had the year pass over it is as if it did not exist."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man has wealth; should he purify it (pay zakat) if half a year has passed?' He said: 'No, but [he must wait] until a full year passes and it becomes due. Indeed, no one prays a prayer except at its appointed time, and similarly with zakat. And no one fasts the month of Ramadan except in its proper month, except for making up missed fasts. And every obligation is only fulfilled when it becomes due.'

Hammad narrated from Hariz from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Does a man purify his wealth if one-third of the year has passed? He said: 'No.' I said: Do you offer the first (installment) before midday? He said: 'No.' The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And concessions have come from the Infallible Imams (peace be upon them) regarding offering it two months before its due time, and delaying it two months, and it has come three months and four months when there is a need for that.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'If zakat is permissible for a man in the month of Ramadan, and he delays it until Muharram,' he said, 'There is no harm.' I said: 'And if it is only permissible in Muharram, and he hastens it in the month of Ramadan,' he said, 'There is no harm.'

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man to whom a needy person comes, and he gives him from his zakat at the beginning of the year. He said: 'If he is needy, there is no harm.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm in paying the zakat two months early and delaying it two months."

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from some of our companions from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who hastens his zakat before its due time, and he said: 'If eight months have passed, there is no harm.' And no one should say that these narrations, despite their apparent contradiction, cannot be reconciled, because it is possible to reconcile them. This is because, in our view, advancing zakat is only permissible in the manner of a loan, and the owner of the wealth remains liable for it until the time of zakat arrives and the giver has become wealthy (possessed of nisab). If he has not yet become wealthy, it still suffices for him. And if the advancement is in this manner, there is no difference between advancing by one month, two months, or more than that. And that which indicates this entire principle is what has been narrated:

Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Miskan, from al-Ahwal, from a man who paid the zakat of his wealth early, then the recipient became wealthy before the due date of the year, who said: The giver must repeat (pay) the zakat.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated this hadith from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): like the first one. The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: When the time for zakat arrives and the deserving recipient is not available with him, he should set it aside from the total of his wealth until he finds someone deserving of it.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who pays his zakat, distributes part of it, and the remainder remains while he seeks the recipients for it, and there is a period of three months between the beginning and the end of this distribution, he said: 'There is no objection (to this delay).'

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): My zakat becomes due upon me for a month, so is it suitable for me to withhold a portion of it, fearing that someone who asks me may come, so that I have enough [to give]? He said: 'When the year passes, take it out from your wealth and do not mix it with anything else, and give it however you wish.' I said: If I write it down and record it, will it be correct for me? He said: 'Yes, it will not harm you.' Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is permissible for him to send it to another country. That is indicated by what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from one who informed him, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding zakat, a man sends it to a land other than his own land. He said: 'There is no harm in him sending one-third or one-fourth.' The doubt is from Abu Ahmad.

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ishaq from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari from Aban ibn Uthman from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb al-Haddad from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man from us is in a remote land; what should he do with the zakat of his wealth? He said: 'Place it among his brothers and those of his Wilayah.' I said: But if none of them are present there with him? He said: 'Send it to them.' I said: But if he cannot find anyone to carry it to them? He said: 'Give it to one who is not a Naṣīb (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt).' I said: And if they (the Ahl al-Bayt/their followers) are not there? He said: 'There is no [specific requirement] for those other than them, except the stone (i.e., it is valid generally).'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abdullah ibn Ja'far and others from Ahmad ibn Hamzah who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) about a man who takes out his zakat from one town to another town and allocates it among his brothers (relatives/kinsmen), so is that permissible? He said, 'Yes.' The Shaykh (peace be upon him) said: If he finds people deserving of it in his town but does not place it among them and sends it to another town, if it perishes, he is liable for it. But if he does not find people deserving of it in his town, so he sends it to another town and it perishes, that suffices for him. As for that which indicates that it suffices for him if he does not find people deserving of it, so he sends it to another town and it perishes, what has been narrated is:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibnammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man gives out the zakat from his wealth, then designates it for a specific group, and it gets lost, or he sends it to them and it gets lost, then there is no liability upon him."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who sends his zakat, and it is stolen or lost, so he said: 'There is nothing upon him (i.e., he is not liable to pay again).' And that which indicates that when the recipient exists, he is liable (if it is lost), is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man sent his zakat to be distributed, but it was lost; is he liable for it until it is distributed? He said: 'If he finds a place for it and does not deliver it, he is liable for it until he delivers it. If he does not find someone to deliver it to him, and he sends it to its people, then he is not liable, because it has left his hand. And similarly, the executor to whom an estate is entrusted is liable for what was entrusted to him if he finds the owner to whom he was ordered to deliver it; if he does not find him, he is not liable.' And similarly, whoever is assigned zakat to distribute, finds a place for it, but does not do so, and then dies, he is liable. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom his brother sent zakat to distribute, and it was lost. He said, 'There is no guarantee/liability on the messenger, nor on the one who paid it.' I said, 'And if he did not find recipients for it, and it spoiled and changed, is he liable for it?' He said, 'No. But if he knew recipients for it, and it spoiled or changed, then he is liable for it from the time he delayed it.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim, Zurarah said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If there is more than one in the city (i.e., multiple eligible recipients of Zakat)?' He said, 'Give them all, if you are able.' He then said, 'It is not permissible for one who has forty dirhams upon which the year has passed to take it (for himself), and if he takes it, he takes it as forbidden (Haram).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from whom he mentioned from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man while he believes him to be insolvent (poor), but then finds him to be wealthy (able to pay), he said: 'It does not count (is not valid) for him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani from Umar ibn Udhaynah from more than one from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) That they were asked about a man who has a house, a servant, and a slave who accepts alms-tax, so they said: 'Yes, indeed the house and the servant are not considered property (wealth subject to khums/zakat limits).'

And from him, from Yahya ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Zakat is permissible for the owner of the house and the servant,' because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did not consider the house and the servant to be anything (i.e., not separate entities distinct from the owner).

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih said to me: 'Convey my greetings to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and inform him that a sudden fear/startle befalls me in my sleep.' He said: So I said to him, 'Indeed, Shihab conveys his greetings to you and says that a sudden fear/startle befalls him in his sleep.' He said: 'Tell him to purify his wealth (pay its khums/zakat).' He said: So I conveyed that to Shihab, and he said to me, 'Then convey it to him from me.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Tell him that the young boys, being superior/experienced compared to the men, know that I am purifying (my wealth).' So I conveyed it to him, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell him, indeed you take it out (pay it) but do not place it in its proper places (correctly).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the alms-tax (zakat), is it given to one who does not know (the recipients)? He said, 'No, and (not) the alms-tax of fitrah.'
And Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Dawud al-Sarimi who said: I asked him about the drinker of wine (khamr), is he given something from the zakat? He said, 'No.'

Sa'd narrated from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Ibrahim al-Aws al-Awsy, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I heard my father saying: 'One day I was with my father when a man came to him and said, I am a man from Ahl al-Ray and I have zakat, to whom should I give it?' He said, 'To us.' He said, 'Is not charity (sadaqah) forbidden for you?' He said, 'Yes, if you give it to our shi'ah, you have given it to us.' He said, 'I do not know anyone for it.' He said, 'Wait with it for one year.' He said, 'If I do not find anyone for it?' He said, 'Wait with it for two years, until it reaches four years.' Then he said to him, 'If you do not find anyone for it, then shake it out vigorously and throw it into the sea, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has forbidden our wealth and the wealth of our shi'ah upon our enemy.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ali ibn Bilal, who said: I wrote to him asking him: Is it permissible for me to give the alms-tax of wealth and charity to a needy person who is not among my companions? So he wrote: 'Do not give the charity and the alms alms-tax except to your companions.'

And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked him about giving charity to the Nusayris and to the Zaydiyyah. He said, 'Do not give them anything in charity, and do not give them water if you can.' And he said, 'The Zaydiyyah are the Nusayris.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the zakat for whom is it?' He said, 'It is for your companions.' I said, 'And if there is surplus over them?' He said, 'Then return it to them.' I said, 'And if there is surplus over them?' He said, 'Then return it to them.' I said, 'And if there is surplus over them?' He said, 'Then return it to them.' I said, 'Then is the beggar given something from it?' He said, 'No, by Allah, except the dust, unless you show mercy to him; and if you show mercy to him, give him a piece.' Then he gestured with his hand and placed his thumb on the bases of his fingers.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, Bukayr, al-Fadl, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) that they said: Regarding a man who is among some of these sects (or theological schools) — al-Haruriyyah, al-Murji'ah, al-Uthmaniyyah, and al-Qadariyyah — then he repents, acknowledges this matter, and his opinion improves: does he have to repeat every prayer he prayed, or fast, or pay zakat, or perform hajj, or is he not required to repeat anything of that? He said: 'He is not required to repeat anything of that, except for zakat, and he must pay it, because he placed the zakat in its non-appropriate place, and its appropriate place is the Ahl al-Wilayah.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who places all of his zakat among his own family (Ahl al-Bayt), and they are your relatives, so he said, 'Yes.' As for if they are dissenters (or of a different sect), it is not permissible to give them [zakat], even if they are relatives; what indicates this is what has been narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna, from Abu Basir, who said: A man asked him (the Imam), and I was listening. He said: Should I give my relatives from the zakat of my wealth, while they do not know you? He said: No, give the zakat only to a Muslim, and give them from your wealth other than the zakat. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do you think that only zakat is in the wealth? What Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has obligated in the wealth other than zakat is more than what you give to your relatives and the casual passerby who asks you. So you give them while you do not know them by the 'Nasb' (sect), but if you know them by the 'Nasb', do not give them (zakat) unless you fear their tongue, so you buy your religion and your honor from them.

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who has relatives, freed slaves, and orphans who love the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) but do not know the owner of this affair (the Imam). Should they be given from the zakat? He said, 'No.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Zur'ah from Samaanah and Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abi Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man is obligated to pay zakat, and he has needy relatives who are not aware (of the obligation or the payment); should he give them the zakat? He said: 'No, and for the sake of honor, he should not make the zakat a shield to protect his wealth; he should give them from other than the zakat if he wishes.' As for the one to whom zakat is not permissible, it has been narrated (about him).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Utba, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: 'I have relatives upon whom I spend, and I prefer some of them over others. When the time for zakat comes, should I give them from it?' He said: 'Are they worthy of it?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'They are better than others, give them.' I said: 'Then who among my relatives am I obliged to support such that I do not count the zakat as a discharge of duty towards them?' He said: 'Your father and your mother.' I said: 'Your father and your mother?' He said: 'The parents and the children.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hadith from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Five people do not receive anything from the zakat: the father, the mother, the child, the slave, and the wife. This is because they are his dependents who are obligatory upon him.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In zakat, one may give from it to the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt, but one does not give to the grandfather or the grandmother. As for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) saying, 'I have children, men and women; is it permissible for me to give them from zakat?' He wrote back (peace be upon him): 'That is permissible for you.' This report is specific to him. Do you not see that when he said 'That is permissible for you,' he attached the permissibility to him alone, not others, even though it is possible that he only permitted him this due to the smallness of his wealth, and that it would not suffice for what he needs for the maintenance of his dependents, so he allowed him to make his zakat an addition to the maintenance of his dependents. And this is permissible if the matter is as we mentioned, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Do not give from the zakat anyone whom you support." And he said: If a man has five hundred dirhams and his dependents are many, he said: "There is no zakat upon him; he spends it on his dependents, increasing their maintenance, their clothing, and the food they did not previously eat." And if he has no dependents and is alone, let him divide it among people who are not needy, who are proud of asking, who do not ask anyone for anything." And he said: "Do not give your relatives all the zakat, but give them some and divide the rest among the other Muslims." And he said: "Zakat is permissible for the head of the house and the servant, and for anyone who has five hundred dirhams after having dependents, and he makes the zakat of the five hundred an increase in the maintenance of his dependents, expanding their provision."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, a group from Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him to appoint them over the alms-tax of livestock, saying: 'Let us have this share that Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has designated for those who work over it, for we are more deserving of it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, indeed alms-tax (sadaqah) is not permissible for me nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Bear witness that I have indeed been promised it. So what do you think, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise, do you see me preferring anyone else over you?'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the charity that was forbidden upon the Banu Hashim, what is it? He said, 'It is the zakat.' I said, 'Then is the charity of some of them permissible upon others?' He said, 'Yes.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid from al-Fadl ibn Sahil from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the charity that was forbidden to them (the Banu Hashim), so he said: 'It is the obligatory alms-tax (Zakat), and the charity of one of us to another has not been forbidden upon us.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Zakat is not permissible for the descendants of al-Abbas and their peers among Banu Hashim." As for that which indicates that it is permissible for them in a state of necessity, it is what has been narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Their freedmen (mawali) are among them, and the alms-tax (sadaqah) from the strangers (gharib) is not permissible for their freedmen, and there is no objection to the alms-giving of their freedmen upon them. Then he said: 'If there were true justice, no Hashimi (descendant of Hashim) or Muttalibi (descendant of Muttalib) would need the alms-tax, for God has made for them in His Book that which was their sufficiency.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a man, if he finds nothing, the dead animal (mithtah) and the alms-tax become permissible for him, and it is not permissible for any of them (Banu Hashim) unless he finds nothing and is among those for whom the dead animal is permissible.' His saying (peace be upon him): 'And the alms-tax from the stranger is not permissible for their freedmen' — the meaning is: if the freedmen are their slaves and it is incumbent upon them to provide for their expenses, it is not permissible for them to be given the zakat, because the slave is not permissible to be given the zakat. As for their freedmen who are not slaves, it is not forbidden for them. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Jamil ibn Darradj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Is alms-tax (sadaqah) permissible for the Banu Hashim?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'Is it permissible for their mawalis (clients/followers)?' He said, 'It is permissible for their mawalis, and it is not permissible for them (Banu Hashim) except the alms of one of them given to another.' As for the report narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Give from the zakat to the Banu Hashim whoever among them wishes, for it is permissible for them, and it is only forbidden upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and upon the Imam who comes after him and upon the Imams (peace be upon them).' The primary narrator in this report is Abu Khadijah, and although it is repeated in the books, no one else has narrated it from him. It is possible that he (peace be upon him) meant the state of necessity rather than the state of choice, because we have clarified that in the state of necessity it is permissible for them. The reason for singling out the Imams (peace be upon them) from among them in the report is that the Imams (peace be upon them) are not compelled to consume the alms-tax and sustain themselves with it, whereas others from the Banu Abd al-Muttalib may be compelled to do so. As for the report narrated by: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: 'I sent to al-Rida (peace be upon him) dinars from some of my family, and I wrote to him informing him that among them was zakat of seventy-five and the remainder was a gift. He wrote back in his own hand: 'I received it and sent to him dinars for me and for others.' And I wrote to him that they were from the fitrah (alms) of the dependents, so he wrote back in his own hand: 'I received it.' Thus, in this report it is not established that he received it for himself or for others; it is possible that he received it for others who are entitled to it, because the Imams (peace be upon them) used to receive the alms-tax, seek it, and distribute it among their mawalis who are entitled to it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Thal'abah ibn Maymun said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to ask Shihab from his zakat for his mawali (clients/freedmen), 'And indeed, zakat is prohibited for them (the Banu Hashim) but not for their mawali.' And that which indicates that sadaqah (voluntary charity) of some of them (Banu Hashim) upon some (other Banu Hashim) is permissible, added to what we have previously mentioned, is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Are the alms of the Banu Hashim permissible for one another?' He said, 'Yes, the alms of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) are permissible for all people, from Banu Hashim and others, and the alms of one of them for another are permissible for them, but the alms of a stranger are not permissible for them.' And as for that which indicates that what is beyond the obligatory alms is permissible for them, added to what we have previously mentioned, is what he narrated:

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "If alms-tax (zakat) were forbidden upon us, it would not be permissible for us to travel to Mecca, because every water source between Mecca and Medina is considered alms-tax."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked, 'Is the obligatory charity (zakat) permissible for the Banu Hashim?' He replied, 'That is the obligatory charity due upon the people; it is not permissible for us. As for other types, there is no harm in it. And if it were so (that all charity was forbidden to us), they would not have been able to go to Mecca, for most of its water is charity (sadaqa).'.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'No one is given from the zakat less than five dirhams, and this is the minimum that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, prescribed for zakat in the wealth of Muslims, so do not give anyone less than five dirhams and upwards.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrahim from Abdillah ibn Hammād al-Anṣārī from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār and Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Abū ʿAbdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said, 'It is not permissible to give zakat less than five dirhams, for that is the minimum amount of zakat.' As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣuhbān who said: I wrote to al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for me, O my master, to give a man from my brothers two dirhams and three dirhams from the zakat, as that has become confused for me?' So he wrote, 'That is permissible.' This is applicable to the nisab that follows the first nisab, because the second and third nisab and what is above that, perhaps two dirhams and three dirhams are sufficient according to the increase in wealth, so there is no harm in giving that to one person. As for the first nisab, that is not permissible in it according to what we have previously stated. As for that which indicates that it is permissible to give more than five dirhams.

He narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'id ibn Ghazwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'How much should be given to one man from the zakat?' He said, 'Give him from the zakat until you make him self-sufficient.'
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: "Give him one thousand dirhams."

Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Saqr, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do we give a man from the zakat one hundred dirhams?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Two hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Three hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Four hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Five hundred?' He said, 'Yes,' until he enrich him.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Utba from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Should a man be given eighty dirhams from the zakat?' He said, 'Yes, and add to it.' I said, 'Should I give him one hundred dirhams?' He said, 'Yes, and enrich him if you are able to enrich him.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked, 'How much should be given to the man from the zakat?' He said. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you give, make him self-sufficient.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the crops from which zakat is due, so he said: 'Wheat, barley, millet, drought-resistant grain, rice, salt, lentils, and sesame; all of these are subject to zakat, and their like.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tithe on 'dhurah' (a type of grain), and he said: 'Dhzarah, lentils, salt, and grains are subject to the same ruling as wheat and barley; and whatever is measured by the sa' and reaches the awzan (thresholds) upon which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is obligatory upon it.'

And from him, from Ibrahim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there [a ruling] regarding rice?' He said, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'Indeed, Medina was not a land of rice at that time, so the ruling would not be said regarding it; but it has been established regarding it. And how could it not be, since the majority of the land tax (kharaj) of Iraq is from it?'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no khums (alms-tax) on vegetables, nor on watermelons, nor on leafy greens and their like, except for what accumulates with you from its produce and remains with you for a year.

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) that they said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused (exempted from khums/zakat) the khudur (fresh vegetables). I asked, 'What is the khudur?' They said, 'Everything that does not have longevity: vegetables, watermelon, fruits, and similar things that spoil quickly.' Zurarah said, 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there anything (due) in the sugarcane?' He said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked about the khudr (turtle/tortoise) regarding Is there zakat in it, and if it is sold for a large amount of wealth, he said, 'No, until a full year passes over it.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the ruling on vegetables (al-khudrah)?' He said, 'And what is it?' I said, 'Sugarcane and watermelon, and similar among the vegetables.' He said, 'There is nothing due on them unless their like is sold for money, and a year passes over it, then zakat is due on it.' And regarding the fruit trees (shajar al-ghadah) of peaches and apricots and their like, is there zakat on them? He said, 'No.' I said, 'Their value (price)?' He said, 'When a year passes over their price, then purify it (pay zakat).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ibn Faddal from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah and a number of our companions from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon them) said: "There is no khums in less than twenty mithqals of gold. When it reaches twenty mithqals, one-half mithqal is due until it reaches twenty-four. When it reaches twenty-four, three-fifths of a dinar is due until it reaches twenty-eight. On this calculation, for every four [mithqals] added, [the amount due] increases."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Sind ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In twenty dinars, [the khums is] half a dinar.

And from him from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: In gold, when it reaches twenty dinars, there is half a dinar [in zakat]; and there is nothing in what is less than twenty. And in silver, when it reaches two hundred dirhams, there are five dirhams; and there is nothing in what is less than two hundred. If it increases by thirty-nine over the two hundred, there is nothing in it until it reaches forty; and there is nothing in any of the fractions until it reaches forty. And likewise the dinars are upon this calculation. As for that which indicates that zakat is only obligatory in it if it is struck [minted], what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from some of our companions, that he said: "There is no zakat in raw gold (tibra); rather, it is upon the dinars and dirhams."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the wealth that is not put to work and is not circulated, and he said: 'Zakat is obligatory upon it every year, unless it is minted (coinage).'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon them) that they said: "There is no zakat on raw gold (tibra); rather, it is upon the dinars and dirhams." And it is considered that, in addition to being struck (minted), they must be engraved/inscribed, because that which is not engraved follows the ruling of the ingot (sibakah) and the nugget (niqar).

Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Kufi, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'A large amount of wealth accumulates with me, and it remains for about a year; should I pay zakat on it?' He said, 'No. For everything that has not completed a full year (hawl) in your possession, you are not obligated to pay zakat on it. And for everything that is not rikaz (buried treasure), there is no obligation on you regarding it.' I said, 'What is rikaz?' He said, 'The silent (uncoined) engraved (gold/silver).' Then he said, 'When you wish to do that, melt it (coin it), for there is no zakat in the melted gold and silver (bullion/uncoined metal).' As for jewelry (huliy), there is no zakat in any of it. What indicates this is what has been narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and some of them asked him about jewelry (gold ornaments), is there zakat in it? He said: 'No, even if it reaches one hundred thousand.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about jewelry (gold ornaments), is there zakat in it? He said, 'No.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The zakat of jewelry is that it be lent out.

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jewelry (al-huliy), is there zakat in it? He said, 'Indeed, there is no zakat in it, even if it reaches one hundred thousand dirhams, and my father differs with the people in this.' As for that which indicates that whenever he is exempted from it, the zakat becomes obligatory upon him, is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jewelry (gold ornaments), whether there is zakat in it? He said: 'No, except what is removed from the zakat (i.e., what is exempted or taken out as the zakat portion).'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'A man makes jewelry for his family worth one hundred dinars, or two hundred dinars, and I think I said three hundred dinars; is Zakat due on it?' He said: 'There is no Zakat on it.' I said: 'Because he fled from Zakat with it?' He said: 'If he fled from Zakat with it, then Zakat is due on it; and if he did it merely to adorn himself with it, then there is no Zakat on it.' And what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated is from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Harun ibn Kharij, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'My brother Yusuf was appointed to manage these affairs and acquired much wealth, and he made that wealth into jewelry, intending to flee from Zakat with it; is Zakat due on it?' He said: 'There is no Zakat on jewelry, and what he has brought upon himself of loss by placing it and withholding his own surplus from it is greater than what he fears from Zakat.' So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because the jewelry upon which Zakat is due as a penalty is that which he makes into jewelry after the time of Zakat has arrived; and that upon which Zakat is not due is that which he makes into jewelry at the beginning of the year or before Zakat becomes due on it, and the state continues with it. And what the Imam (peace be upon him) said by 'what he brought upon himself of loss is greater than what he fears from Zakat' refers to what he misses of the reward that if he had left the wealth until the time of Zakat as it was, and did not intend thereby to flee from it, he would have been entitled to it by paying the Zakat from it. And that which indicates this meaning is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, your father said: Whoever delays paying its zakat upon it, he must pay it.' He said, 'My father spoke truly; he must pay what was obligatory upon him, and what was not obligatory upon him, there is nothing upon him from it.' Then he said to me, 'What do you think if a man lost consciousness for a day, then died, and his prayer was missed, would he be obligated to pay it after he died?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Unless he regained consciousness on that day.' Then he said to me, 'What do you think if a man fell ill in the month of Ramadan, then died in it, would he be required to fast on his behalf?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'And similarly, a man does not pay from his wealth except what became due upon it.' And it is not for anyone to say that this interpretation is not possible for you, because the first two narrations included that the questioner asked about jewelry whether zakat is obligatory in it or not, so he said to him, 'No, except what he delayed from the zakat.' And what he makes into jewelry after the time has arrived, zakat is not obligatory in it, but it became obligatory before it became jewelry. Thus, there is no meaning to excluding some jewelry from the whole, because his saying (peace be upon him) when the questioner asked him about jewelry whether zakat is in it or not, and he said to him, 'No,' necessitates that everything upon which the name of jewelry falls, zakat is not obligatory in it, whether it was crafted before the time arrived or after its arrival, due to its inclusion under the general rule. So the Imam (peace be upon him) intended by that the specification of some from the whole, and that is what we mentioned earlier, namely what was crafted after the time arrived.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about gold, how much zakat is due upon it? He said: 'When its value reaches two hundred dirhams, zakat is due upon it.' There is no contradiction in this report with what we previously stated, that the nisab (minimum threshold) is twenty dinars, because he (peace be upon him) informed about the value of the time, and at that time the value of one dinar was ten dirhams. Do you not see that in many places regarding diyat (blood money) and other matters, they considered ten dirhams in exchange for one dinar, and made the choice between them on an equal basis? Thus is the ruling of this report, because the value of two hundred dirhams comes to be twenty dinars according to what we previously stated, and that which he narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Basir, and Burayd, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), said: "In gold, for every forty mithqals, one mithqal; and in silver (dirhams), for every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams. And there is nothing (due) in less than forty mithqals, and nothing in less than two hundred dirhams. And there is nothing in the surplus (niyyif) until forty is completed, then there is one in it." His saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing in less than forty mithqals' allows for the meaning that he meant one dinar, because his word 'something' is ambiguous regarding the dinar, that which increases it, and that which decreases it, and it runs the course of the general statement that requires specification. And since we have narrated the detailed hadiths that in every twenty dinars, half a dinar is due, and in that which increases it, for every four dinars, one-tenth of a dinar is due, we interpret his saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing in what is less than forty dinars' as meaning one dinar, because whenever it falls short of forty, only less than the dinar is due in it. As for his saying (peace be upon him) at the beginning of the report 'in every forty mithqals, one mithqal', there is no contradiction in it to what we said, because with us it is established that one dinar is due in it, even though this is not the first threshold of nisab. And if we interpret this report as we said, we have reconciled between these reports in a manner where there is no conflict between them.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who purchased goods for trade, and his goods became unsalable (kasad), while he had already paid the zakat on his wealth before purchasing them with it: Is he liable for zakat again, or does he wait until he sells them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he kept them seeking profit upon the principal capital, then he is liable for zakat.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who purchased trade goods, and they became stagnant (unsold), while he had already paid the zakat on his wealth before purchasing the goods. When should he pay zakat on them? He said: 'If he kept the goods seeking to recover his principal capital, there is no zakat upon him. And if he held them after he had recovered his principal capital, then upon him is the zakat after he has kept them after the completion of the year of the principal capital.' He said: And I asked him about a man upon whom wealth is placed (accumulated), and he works with it. He said: 'When the lunar year passes over it, let him pay its zakat.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn Muhammad, from al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'For the goods (merchandise) in which I do not make a profit to cover the principal capital, is Zakat obligatory upon me?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'If I keep them for two years and then sell them, what is due from me?' He said: 'One year.' As for that which indicates that Zakat on commercial property is not obligatory (fard), but rather recommended (mandub mustahabb), is what we have previously mentioned: that Zakat is only obligatory on Rikaz (buried treasure), and on struck and hoarded Dirhams and Dinars, and for other than these, there is no Zakat. And this is confirmed by what he narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Abdullah ibn Bukayr and Ubayd and a group of our companions, they said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "There is no zakat in the wealth that is fluctuating (uncertain)." His son Ismail said to him, "I am your ransom, father, you have consumed the poor of your companions." He said, "O my son, it is a right that Allah intended to take out, so it came out."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who had much wealth, so he bought goods with it, then stored them, saying: 'This is stored goods; when I wish, I will sell them, and my principal capital will return to me, and more than it.' Is there zakat due on it while it is goods? He said: 'No, until he sells it.' He asked: 'Does he pay for it for what has passed if it is goods?' He said: 'No.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said: I was sitting with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and with him was only his son Ja'far. He said, 'O Zurarah, Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) and Uthman disputed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Uthman said: 'For every wealth of gold or silver that is circulated, worked with, and traded in, zakat is due when a year passes over it.' Abu Dharr said: 'As for what is traded in, circulated, and worked with, there is no zakat in it; rather, zakat is due in it only if it is rikaz (buried treasure) or a stored treasure (kanz). When a year passes over it, zakat is due in it.' They disputed this matter before the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he said, 'The verdict is as Abu Dharr said.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to his father, 'What do you want by bringing forth something like this, so that people will stop giving to their poor and needy?' His father said to him, 'To you from me; I cannot avoid it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "For every person you include in your dependents, whether free or slave, you must pay the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) on their behalf." He said, "Giving the Fitrah before the prayer is superior, and after the prayer it is considered charity."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), and he said: 'It is obligatory upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, for every person a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of raisins.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a guest from his brothers staying with him, and the day of Fitr arrives; should he pay the Fitrah on his behalf? He said: 'Yes, the Fitrah is obligatory upon every person who provides for a male or female, young or old, free or slave.' And the newborn, if born on the night of Fitr, it is not obligatory to pay the Fitrah on his behalf; and likewise, whoever converts to Islam on the night of Fitr, it is not obligatory upon him to pay the Fitrah, according to what we mentioned. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn born on the night of Eid al-Fitr, is Zakat al-Fitr due upon him? He said, 'No, the month has passed.' And I asked him about a Jew who converted to Islam on the night of Eid al-Fitr, is Zakat al-Fitr due upon him? He said, 'No.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'What is the ruling regarding the Zakat al-Fitr for a needy man?' He said: 'There is no Fitrah upon him.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Yazīd ibn Farqad, who said: I said to Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him): 'Is the Sadaqat al-Fitr (Zakat al-Fitr) obligatory for the needy person?' He said, 'No.'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who takes from the zakat (alms-tax) upon him is the sadaqat al-fitr (charity of breaking the fast), he said: 'No.'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Isma'il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'For whom is the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) permissible?' He said, 'For one who does not find (the means to pay it). And that which is permissible for him is not obligatory upon him, and that which is obligatory upon him is not permissible for him.'

And with this chain of narration, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there Zakat upon the one who accepts Zakat? He said: 'As for the one who accepts Zakat of wealth, then upon him is Zakat al-Fitr, and he is not required to give Zakat for what he has accepted; and upon the one who accepts al-Fitr, there is no Fitr.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Regarding the man who is in need, is he liable for the Zakat al-Fitr?' He said, 'There is no Fitrah upon him.'

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yazid ibn Farqad al-Nahdi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who accepts the alms-tax (zakat); is he obliged to pay the charity of breaking the fast (sadaqat al-fitr)? He said, 'No.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara, who said: I asked him, 'Is there a Zakat upon the one who accepts Zakat?' He said, 'As for the one who accepts Zakat of wealth, then upon him is the Zakat of Fitrah, and there is no Fitrah upon the one who accepts Fitrah.' So all these narrations indicate that the needy person and the one who is not of wealth, the Fitrah is not obligatory upon him. And everything that has come regarding that Fitrah is obligatory upon him, it has come by way of recommendation and preference, rather than obligation and compulsion. So among what is narrated in that regard is what is narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Regarding the poor person who is given charity, does Zakat al-Fitr (Fitrana) fall upon him?' He said: 'Yes, he gives from what is given to him in charity.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man and Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man does not have anything of the fitrah (alms of fasting) except what he pays for himself alone; he gives it for a stranger, or he eats it himself and his dependents.' He said: 'He gives to some of his dependents, then the other gives for himself; they alternate it, so it becomes one fitrah for all of them.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Zakat al-Fitr is due on every head from your family, the small and the large, the free and the slave, the rich and the poor; for every person, half a sa' of wheat or barley, or a full sa' of dates or raisins, for the poor of the Muslims. And he said: 'Dates are more beloved to me of those [options].' And that which indicates what we have interpreted these hadiths as meaning is that the intended meaning is recommendation (nadhb) rather than obligation (ijab).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Iyyas ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), when is it? He said: 'Before the prayer on the day of Fitrah.' I said: 'And if some of it remains after the prayer?' He said: 'There is no harm; we give to our dependents from it, then what remains is distributed.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'He has succeeded who purifies himself, and mentions the name of his Lord and prays.' He said: 'He goes to the prayer place and prays.'

And from him, from Hammad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast) is considered Fitrah if you give it before you go out to the Eid prayer; and if it is given after you go out to the Eid prayer, it is considered Sadaqah (general charity).'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim, from al-Harith, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "There is no harm in delaying the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) until the new moon of Dhu al-Qa'dah." This is understood to mean that if one does not find a recipient for it, there is no harm in delaying it; however, it is obligatory upon him to set it aside from his wealth and distinguish it at its proper time, and give it to the recipient when he is able to do so. This is clarified by what he narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), if you set it aside while you are seeking a place for it or waiting for a man (to receive it), there is no objection to it.

Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar and others, who said: I asked him about Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr). He said, "When you set it aside, it does not harm you when you give it, whether before the prayer or after the prayer."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, is the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) obligatory upon the people of the countryside?' He said, then he said, 'The Fitrah is obligatory upon every person who consumes sustenance, so upon him is to pay from that sustance.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and from Yunus from Ibn Mukhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast) upon every people is from what they feed their dependents, from milk or raisins or other than them.

Saad narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide Fitrah, so he said: 'Let him give charity with four Artals of milk.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm with the valuation (monetary equivalent) in the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast)."

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, and Ali ibn Uthman, from Isحاق ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr). He said: 'The neighbors have more right to it, and there is no objection if you give the value of that in silver.'

And from him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Like it, and he said: 'There is no harm in giving him its value as one dirham.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Fitrah (alms of fitr), how much should be paid for each head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins? He said, 'A sa' with the sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'.

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), and he said: 'It is obligatory upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, for every person a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of raisins.' And from Abu Hamzah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'The owners of camels, cattle, and sheep give in Fitrah one sa' of aqit (dried curds).'

Know that Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father, peace be upon them both, who said: The Zakat al-Fitr is a Sa' of dates, or a Sa' of raisins, or a Sa' of barley, or a Sa' of aqit (dried curds), for every person, free or slave, young or old, and there is no hardship upon one who cannot find what to give in charity. Ibn Qulawayh narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Ja'far ibn Ma'ruf who said: I wrote to Abu Bakr al-Razi regarding Zakat al-Fitr and asked him to write to our Master, meaning Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), regarding this matter. He wrote that this had been sent to Ali ibn Mahziyar: 'That it is to be given from every item—dates, wheat, and other than them—as a Sa'. And we have no difference of opinion regarding his answer to us on this matter.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: 'Upon every person whom the man supports, whether free or slave, young or old, [is due] a sa' of dates or half a sa' of wheat, and the sa' is four amdad.'

And from him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the charity of alms-giving at the breaking of the fast (Fitr), he said: 'Give charity on behalf of all those you provide for, whether small or large, free or slave. For every person, half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley. And the sa' is four amdad.'

And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The charity (Fitrah) is for one who does not find wheat and barley; wheat, lentils, and millet suffice in their place, half a sa' of each of them, or one sa' of dates or raisins.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Salamah, Abu Hafs, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: The charity of al-fitr (fitrana) is due on every young and old, free or slave, for every person you support, meaning the one you spend upon on, [consisting of] a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley, or a sa' of raisins. Then, when it was the time of Uthman, he changed it to two mudds of wheat.

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Regarding Fitrah, the Sunnah was established with a Sa' of dates, or a Sa' of raisins, or a Sa' of barley. Then, when it was the time of Uthman and wheat became abundant, the people standardized it, saying: half a Sa' of wheat is equivalent to a Sa' of barley.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both) That the first person to make two mudds of the zakat equivalent to one sa' of dates was Uthman.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Hashim said: He narrated to us Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman from al-Hasan ibn Ali from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide the fitrah (of wheat), so he said: 'He should give charity of four artals of milk.'

Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Kharaja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Zakat al-Fitr. He said: 'A sa' of dates, or half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of barley, and dates are more beloved to me.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: 'The date is superior.'

Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh from his father from Ahmad ibn Idris said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Kufi who said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from 'Umarah ibn Marwan from Zayd al-Shahham who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "To be given a sa' of dates is more beloved to me than to be given a sa' of gold for the Fitrah (alms of fasting)."

Ibn Qulawayh from his father from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Is-haq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafī said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the Fitrah? Is it permissible for me to pay it in silver at the value of these items that you mentioned?' He said, 'Yes, indeed that is more beneficial for him; he buys with it what he wishes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm in using the monetary valuation (qimah) for the Fitrah (alms of fasting)."

Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Fitrah (poor tax), who are its people, those upon whom it is obligatory? He said: 'Whoever finds nothing.'

And from him (Al-Haytham) from Al-Haytham from Isma'il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked, 'For whom is the Fitrah (alms of fasting) permissible?' He said, 'For him who does not find (enough to pay it). And for whom it is permissible, it is not obligatory upon him.' I said to him, 'Is there Zakat upon the one who accepts Zakat?' He said, 'As for the one who accepts Zakat of wealth, then upon him is the Zakat of Fitrah, and he is not obligated (to pay Fitrah) for what he accepted. And there is no Fitrah upon the one who accepts Fitrah.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Malik al-Juhani, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: 'Give it to the Muslims; if you do not find a Muslim, then [give it to] the weak/poor, and give it to your relatives if you wish.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Do not give anyone less than a head (of grain)." And it has been narrated that it is permissible to distribute it in parts, [it] narrated.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarik said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the charity of al-Fitr (Zakat al-Fitr): is it from what Allah the Exalted said, 'Establish the prayer and give the zakat'? He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'The charity of dates is more beloved to me because my father (peace be upon him) used to give charity in dates.' I said, 'If one assigns its value as silver and gives it to one man or two?' He said, 'Distributing it is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in making it silver, but dates are more beloved to me.' I said, 'Should I give it to those who are not from the Ahl al-Wilayah among these neighbors?' He said, 'Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it.' I said, 'Should I give the one man three sa' and four sa'?' He said, 'Yes.' The meaning in this hadith is that if there is a group of needy people, distributing among them is superior to giving it to one person. As for if there is no necessity, the best is to give a head (share) to each head, even though in the report, in his saying 'Distributing it is more beloved to me,' it does not mean that one must distribute one head to one individual individually. It is possible that he meant those upon whom the Fitr is obligatory, so that he distributes and gives each one of them a head is superior to giving it to one man. And on this interpretation, there is no contradiction between this report and the first report, and we have clarified in the first report that there is no harm in giving one man many heads. And to add clarification to this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm in giving the man two, three, or four [units]," meaning the fitrah [alms of Ramadan]."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti from some of our companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Magi (Zoroastrians): 'Did they have a prophet?' He said, 'Yes. Did you not receive the letter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to the people of Mecca: 'Embrace Islam, otherwise I will declare war against you'?' So they wrote to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Take the jizyah (tax) from us and leave us to worship our idols.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'I do not take the jizyah except from the People of the Book.' They wrote to him, intending to contradict him (peace be upon him and his family), saying: 'You claimed that you do not take the jizyah except from the People of the Book, yet you took the jizyah from the Magi of Hawaran.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'The Magi had a prophet, whom they killed, and they burned his book. Their prophet came to them with their book in twelve thousand cowhides.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the charity (sadaqat) of the people of the covenant (ahl al-dhimma) and what is taken from their jizya from the price of their wine, the meat of their pigs, and their dead animals. He said: 'The jizya is upon them in their wealth; it is taken from them from the price of the meat of the pig or the wine. So whatever they take from them of that, its burden (wazr) is upon them, and its price is halal for the Muslims, which they take as part of their jizya.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, all of them, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Sunnah has established that the Jizyah (poll tax) is not taken from the 'Ma'tuh (one who is insane/mentally deficient) nor from the one whose intellect is overpowered (by insanity).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far, from his father, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: "Combat is of two types: Combat against the people of polytheism, from whom they are not dismissed until they embrace Islam or pay the jizyah with their own hands while they are subdued." "to the command of Allah" And combat against the people of deviation, from whom they are not dismissed until they return to the command of Allah or are killed."

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: There is no zakat in silver until it reaches two hundred dirhams; when it reaches two hundred dirhams, there is five dirhams in it. If it increases beyond that, the calculation is based on that: for every forty dirhams, one dirham. And there is nothing in the fractional parts. There is no zakat in gold until it reaches twenty mithqals; when it reaches twenty mithqals, there is half a mithqal in it. Then, based on that calculation, if the wealth increases, for every forty dinars, one dinar.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In every two hundred dirhams of silver, there are five dirhams; and if it falls short, there is no zakat upon you. And from gold, for every twenty dinars, there is half a dinar; and if it falls short, there is nothing upon you.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn Muhammad from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When silver exceeds two hundred dirhams by forty dirhams, one dirham is due in it, and there is nothing due for less than forty. I asked, 'What is due for thirty-nine dirhams?' He said, 'There is nothing due for thirty-nine dirhams.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayn, that they heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding alms-tax: as for gold, there is no alms-tax in less than twenty dinars; when it reaches twenty dinars, half a dinar is due. There is no alms-tax in less than two hundred dirhams; when it reaches two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due. Whatever increases beyond that is calculated accordingly. In two hundred dirhams and forty dirhams (excluding one dirham), there are not five dirhams; when it reaches two hundred and forty dirhams, six dirhams are due. When it reaches two hundred and eighty dirhams, seven dirhams are due, and whatever increases beyond that is calculated on this basis. And so is gold, and all gold. Alms-tax is only on deposited gold and silver when a full year has passed over it; then it is due. And if a year has not passed over it, there is nothing due in it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the limit of the jizyah (poll tax) upon the People of the Book, and is there a fixed amount upon them in this matter that they cannot exceed?' He said: 'That is up to the Imam; he takes from each of them whatever he wishes, according to their wealth and what they can bear. They are a people who ransomed their lives from being enslaved or killed, so the jizyah is taken from them according to what they can bear to be taken with it, until they convert to Islam.' For indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.' And how can he be humbled if he does not care about what is taken from him, until he finds humiliation in what was taken from him, and feels pain because of it, so he converts?' He said, and Ibn Muslim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you think of what these people take from the khums from the land of the jizyah, and the jizyah of their heads is taken from the dehqans (landowners); is there a fixed amount upon them in that?' He said: 'That upon them is what they authorized upon themselves, and the Imam does not take more than the jizyah. If the Imam wishes, he places that upon their heads, and there is nothing upon their wealth; and if he wishes, he places it upon their wealth, and there is nothing upon their heads.' I said: 'And what about this khums?' He said: 'This is something that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made a treaty with them upon.'

Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma), what is upon them from that which secures their blood and their wealth? He said: 'The land tax (Kharaj). If the poll tax (Jizyah) is taken from their heads, then there is no claim on their lands; and if the land tax is taken from their lands, then there is no claim on their heads.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the people of the jizya (poll tax), is anything taken from their wealth and livestock besides the jizya? He said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: We mentioned to him (the Imam) Kufa and the land tax levied upon it, and what the members of his household were doing there. He said: 'Whoever surrenders voluntarily, his land remains in his hand, and the tithe (ushr) is taken from what is watered by rain and rivers, and half the tithe from what is watered by manual irrigation, in what they have cultivated of it. And what they have not cultivated of it, the Imam takes and leases it to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. Upon those who lease it, in their shares, is the tithe and half the tithe. And there is no tax in less than five awsiq.' And what is conquered by the sword, that is for the Imam; he leases it as he sees fit, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Khaybar. He leased its black soil and its white [date palms], meaning its land and its palm trees. And the people say that leasing land and palm trees is not valid, yet the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leased Khaybar. And upon those who lease, besides the leasing of the land, is the tithe and half the tithe in their shares.' Then he said: 'Indeed, the people of Ta'if surrendered, and the tithe and half the tithe were imposed upon them. And indeed, the people of Mecca, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered their city by force, and they were captives in his hand, so he freed them and said: Go, for you are free.'
