Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I mentioned to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) the khuras (land tax) and what the people of his household practiced, so he said: 'The tenth and half of the tenth is upon whoever embraces Islam voluntarily, if his land is left in his hand; the tenth and half of the tenth are taken from him regarding what he cultivates of it, and what he does not cultivate of it, the governor takes it and leases it to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And there is no tax on what is less than five awsiq. And what is conquered by the sword, that belongs to the Imam, who leases it as he sees fit, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Khaybar; he leased its land and its palm trees, while the people said that leasing the land and palm trees is not suitable if the white (fertile land) is more than the black (less fertile). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leased Khaybar — and upon them, in their shares, is the tenth and half of the tenth.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibrahim ibn Imran al-Shaybani, from Yunus ibn Ibrahim, from Yahya ibn Ash'ath al-Kinani, from Mus'ab ibn Yazid al-Ansari, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), appointed me over four districts of Madain: Bahqubadhat, Bahrsir, Nahr Juyar, and Nahr al-Malik. He ordered me to impose on every jarib of thick-crop land one dirham and a half, on every jarib of medium-crop land one dirham, on every jarib of thin-crop land two-thirds of a dirham, on every jarib of vineyard ten dirhams, on every jarib of palm trees ten dirhams, and on every jarib of orchards that combine palms and trees ten dirhams. He ordered me to exempt every stray palm tree outside the villages for travelers and wayfarers, and not to take anything from it. He ordered me to impose on the dehqans (landed gentry) who ride bareds and wear gold signet rings, on every man of them forty-eight dirhams; on their middle class and merchants, on every man twenty-four dirhams; and on their lower class and poor, on every person twelve dirhams. He said: So I collected it, eighteen million dirhams in one year. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Therefore, what this report contains of mentioning something of the jizyah fixed from every person is not inconsistent with what we mentioned, that it is up to the Imam to take from them according to what he sees fit at the time, because it is not impossible that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saw it as expedient to impose on every man of them the mentioned amount in that year, and if the expediency changed to increase or decrease, he would also change it. And it would only be inconsistent if he imposed that on them and said, 'This is their ruling, and they shall not be increased or decreased from it in all circumstances,' and that is not in the report.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Hakim, the mu'adhdhin of Banu Abs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'And know that whatever you gain from spoils, one-fifth is for Allah and for the Messenger.' He said, 'It is, by Allah, the benefit/profit day by day, except that my father (peace be upon him) made our Shia exempt from that portion of it, so that they may purify themselves.'

Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala and Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the mines of gold, silver, copper, iron, and lead, so he said: 'Upon them all is khums.'

And from him (Al-Ukhu) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about amber and pearl diving, so he said: 'Khums is due upon it.' I asked him about treasure (kanz), how much is in it? He said: 'Khums.' And about mines, how much is in them? He said: 'Khums.' And about lead, brass, and iron, and what is in the mines, how much is in them? He said: 'It is taken from them as it is taken from the mines of gold and silver.'

4 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the mines, what is in them? He said: 'Whatever is rikaz, khums is due in it.' And he said: 'Whatever you worked with your wealth, from what Allah extracted from it of its stones, purified, khums is due.'

And from him (Al-Husn) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon every person who gains or acquires wealth, there is the khums from what they obtain, for Fatimah (peace be upon her) and for the one who manages her affairs after her from her progeny, the proofs upon the people. That is specifically for them; they place it where they wish, because charity (sadaqah) is forbidden for them, so even if a tailor sews a shirt for five dinars, we take one dinar from it, except for whom we permit from our Shias so that lineage becomes pleasing to them through it. Indeed, there is nothing with God on the Day of Resurrection greater than adultery (zina). Indeed, the owner of the khums will stand and say: O Lord, ask these about what was permitted to them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the 'malḥah' (salt mine/field), so he said, 'What is the malḥah?' I said, 'A salty, briny land where water collects and turns into salt.' He said, 'This is a mine, and it contains the khums.' I said, 'And sulfur and petroleum, which are extracted from the earth?' He said, 'This and its like, they contain the khums.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Take the wealth of the al-Nasib (rival) wherever you find it, and pay the khums to us."

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Saif ibn Amira from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from al-Mu'alla said: "Take the wealth of the Naṣibī (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) wherever you find it, and send us the khums." Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari said: One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second) peace be upon him: "Inform me regarding the khums: is it upon all that a man acquires, from little and much, from all types, and upon the craftsmen, and how is that?" So he wrote with his own hand: "The khums is after expenses."

Ali ibn Mahziyar said: Abu Ali ibn Rashid said to me: I said to him, 'You ordered me to fulfill your affair and take your right, so I informed your mawali (clients/followers) of that.' Some of them said to me, 'And what is his right?' So I did not know what to answer him. He said, 'Khums is obligatory upon them.' I said, 'In what?' He said, 'In their goods and their estates.' He said, 'And the merchant [is subject to it] and the artisan with his hand.' He said, 'That is when it is possible for them after their expenses.' He said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani wrote to him, 'Ali read to me the letter of your father regarding what he made obligatory upon the owners of estates: that he made obligatory upon them half of the sixth (one-twelfth) after the expenses, and that upon one whose estate does not cover its own expenses, there is no half of the sixth, nor anything else.' So there was a difference of opinion among us regarding that, and they said: 'Khums is obligatory upon the estates after the expenses, which are the expenses of the estate and its tax, not the expenses of the man and his family.' So he wrote and Ali ibn Mahziyar read it: 'Upon him is Khums after his expenses and the expenses of his family, and after the tax of the ruler.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any dhimmi (non-Muslim subject) who buys land from a Muslim, then khums is due upon him.'

And from him, from Ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about what is extracted from the sea, such as pearls, rubies, and chrysolite, and about the mines of gold and silver: is there zakat upon them? He said, 'When its value reaches one dinar, khums is due upon it.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man from our companions who is in their banner and is with them, and he acquires war booty, he said: 'He pays its khums and it is pleasing to him.'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ali ibn Ja'far from Al-Hakam ibn Buhlul from Abu Hammam from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have acquired wealth, but I do not know its lawful portion from its unlawful portion.' He said: 'Pay the khums from that wealth, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, has been satisfied with the khums from the wealth, and avoid what the owner used to do.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Khums is not [obligatory] except in the war booty specifically.' Thus, what is meant is that Khums is not [obligatory by] the apparent meaning of the Quran except in the war booty specifically, because whatever is apart from the war booty in which we have obligated Khums, that is established entirely by the Sunnah, and the Imam (peace be upon him) did not mean that Khums is not obligatory in it under any circumstance.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, who said: Zakariyya ibn Malik al-Ju'fi narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). That he asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And know that whatever you gain of war booty, a fifth is for Allah and the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the poor and the wayfarer.' He said: 'As for the fifth of Allah (Mighty and Majestic), it is for the Messenger, who allocates it in the way of Allah. And as for the fifth of the Messenger, it is for his close relatives. And the fifth of the near relatives are his close relatives. And the orphans are the orphans of his Household. So He made these four [categories] as four shares for them.' And as for the poor and the wayfarer, you know that we do not eat the charity (sadaqah) and it is not permissible for us, so it is for the poor and the sons of the wayfarer.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of his companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And know that whatever you gain of war booty, a fifth belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, and to the orphans, and to the poor, and to the wayfarer.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fifth of Allah and the fifth of the Messenger belong to the Imam. The fifth of the near relatives belongs to the relatives of the Messenger and the Imam. The orphans are the orphans of the family of the Messenger, and the poor are among them, and the wayfarers are among them. So they are not taken out from them to others.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Zafarani from Hammad ibn Isa from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say much speech, then he said: 'And give them from all of that the share of the near kin.' Allah the Exalted said: 'If you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the day of the Criterion, the day when the two armies met.' By Allah, the 'near kin' refers to us, and they are those whom Allah has joined to His own self and to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So He said: 'Then for Allah is its fifth, and for the Messenger and for the near kin and the orphans and the poor and the wayfarer.' From us specifically. And He did not assign us a share in the portion of alms-giving (zakat); Allah honored His Prophet and honored us so that He would not feed us with the dregs of people's hands.

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad asked him, 'Zakat is obligatory upon you.' He replied, 'No, but we give extra (khums) like this.' And he (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And know that whatever of anything you acquire as booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah and the Messenger and [for] the near relative and the orphans and the needy.' It was said to him, 'Then to whom does that which is for Allah belong?' He said, 'It belongs to the Messenger.' And that which is for the Messenger, it belongs to the Imam. It was said to him, 'What do you think if one category is more than another category, and one category is less than another category? How should we deal with it?' He said, 'That is up to the Imam.' 'Do you see how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) acted? He used to give according to what he saw fit; likewise the Imam.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: He narrated to us from some of our companions, raising the hadith, saying: Khums is due on five things: from the treasures, mines, diving (for pearls), the booty which is fought for, and the fifth was not preserved; and whatever was a conquest for which fighting did not occur and no cavalry or beasts of burden were marched upon it, except that our companions come to it and deal with it regarding it, so whatever they deal with it for, half or a third or a quarter or whatever is specifically allotted to it, and no one has anything in it except what he gives from it, and the bottoms of valleys, tops of mountains, and dead land, all of it is for him. And this is His Exalted Saying, 'They ask you about the spoils of war,' meaning to give them from it, he said, 'Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.' And it is not 'They ask you about the spoils,' and whatever is of the cities and the inheritance of one who has no heir, it is for him specifically. And this is His Mighty and Majestic Saying, 'What Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the cities.' As for Khums, it is divided into six shares: a share for Allah, a share for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), a share for the near relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarer. That which is for Allah and for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), the Messenger is more entitled to it, so it is for him specifically; and that which is for the Messenger is for the near relatives and the Proof in his time. So half is for him specifically, and half is for the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer from the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), who are not entitled to receive Zakat. Allah compensated them in place of that with Khums, so He gives them according to their need. If something remains from it, it is for him; and if it falls short of their need and does not suffice them, he completes it for them from himself, just as the surplus becomes his, so the deficit is incumbent upon him.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah ibn al-Jarud, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) received the war booty (mughanim), he would take its best portion (safwah) for himself. Then he would divide what remained into five fifths, taking one fifth for himself. He would then divide the remaining four fifths among the people who fought for him. After that, he would divide the fifth he had taken into five fifths: he would take one fifth for Allah (Exalted and Mighty) for himself, and then divide the remaining four fifths among the close relatives, the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarers, giving each of them their full share. Thus does the Imam act, taking as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Abu al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Salih al-Saymarri, who said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: He narrated to me Hammad ibn Isa, who said: One of our companions narrated it to me, mentioning it from the righteous servant, Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him). He said: 'Khums is due from five things: from the spoils of war, from diving (for pearls), from treasures, from minerals, and from coral.' And in the narration of Yunus: 'and amber,' I found this word alone in some of his books: 'amber,' and I did not hear it. One-fifth is taken from each of these categories, and it is assigned to whom Allah has assigned it to. Four-fifths are distributed among those who fought for it and had authority over it. The one-fifth portion is divided among them into six shares: a share for Allah, a share for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a share for the near relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarers. Thus, the share of Allah and the share of the Messenger belong to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger belong to the Imam (Guardian of Affairs) after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by inheritance. Therefore, he has three shares: two by inheritance, and one share allocated to him by Allah. Thus, he possesses the entire half of the Khums. The remaining half of the Khums is distributed among his family: a share for their orphans, a share for their poor, and a share for their wayfarers. It is distributed among them according to their sufficiency and capacity, to the extent they need to be self-sufficient for their year. If there is a surplus that they do not need, it belongs to the Imam. If it is insufficient or falls short of their need for self-sufficiency, it is upon the Imam to spend from his own resources to cover the shortfall. Thus, it becomes incumbent upon him to provide for them because he owns the surplus that remains from them. Allah designated this Khums specifically for them, distinct from the poor of the people and their wayfarers, as a substitute for them from the charity of the people. This is to honor them from Allah due to their kinship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and hi

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu al-Subbah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'We are a people upon whom God has made our obedience obligatory; to us belong the al-fay' (booty/gains), and to us belongs the choicest part of the wealth. We are the firm-rooted in knowledge, and we are the ones who are envied, as God the Exalted said: "Or do they envy people for what God has given them of His bounty?"'

And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What does Allah mean by His statement: They ask you about the spoils of war. Say, 'The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger.' He said, 'The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and they are every land whose inhabitants have vacated it, without being conquered by cavalry, infantry, or mounts; so it is a surplus (gift) for Allah and the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Muhammad ibn Salim from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the war booty. He said: 'One-fifth (Khums) is extracted from it, and the remainder is distributed among those who fought for it and the one who had authority over it. As for Al-Fay' and Al-Anfal, they are exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he heard him saying: "Indeed, Al-Anfal (the spoils/gains) are any land where there was no shedding of blood or where people were reconciled and gave with their own hands. And whatever is from abandoned land or the bellies of valleys, this is all from Al-Fay'. And Al-Anfal are for Allah and the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And whatever is for Allah, it is for the Messenger, who places it where he wills."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abu Jamilah said, and he narrated to me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from his father from Abu Jamilah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about the al-Anfal (spoils of war), so he said: 'That which is of the lands whose people perished, and other than that, the al-Anfal is for us.' And he said: 'The Surah of al-Anfal contains the cutting off of the nose.' 'What Allah conferred upon His Messenger from them, so it is not what you made to gallop against with your horses and camels, but rather Allah gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills.' And he said: 'Al-Fay' is that which is from properties in which there was no shedding of blood or killing, and the al-Anfal is like that, it is in its position.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from Isma'il ibn Sahil from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz ibn 'Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: He was asked about the Anfal (spoils of war), so he said: 'Every village whose people perish or are expelled from it is Anfal for Allah, Exalted and Glorious; half of it is distributed among the people, and half is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), it is for the Imam.'

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about the al-Anfal (spoils of war/land revenue), so he said: 'Every barren land or anything that belonged to the kings is exclusively for the Imam, with no share for the people.' And he said: 'Among them are the two seas (Bahrain), upon which no expedition was made with horses or camels.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Rifah ibn Musa from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who dies and has no heir and no mawla (client/kin), he said: 'He is among the people of this verse: They ask you about the spoils of war (al-Anfal).'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the 'Safw' (the best portion) of the wealth. He said: 'It belongs to the Imam, who takes the swift mare, the fine mount, the cutting sword, and the armor, before the booty is distributed. This is the Safw of the wealth.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Sind ibn Muhammad from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I heard him say: Al-Fay' and Al-Anfal: whatever is from land where there was no shedding of blood and people were reconciled and gave with their own hands, and whatever is from barren land or the bottoms of valleys, then it is all from Al-Fay'. So this is for Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for Allah is for His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), who places it where he wills, and it is for the Imam (peace be upon him) after the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And His saying: 'And what Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, so you did not mount for it [a campaign of] cavalry or camels.' He said: 'Do you not see? It is this.' And as for His saying: 'What Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns,' this is in the status of Al-Maghanim (booty). My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'That is it, and we have in it no more than two shares: the share of the Messenger and the share of the Close Relatives, then we are partners with the people in what remains.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All the districts/territories of the kings belong to the Imam, and the people have no share in them.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Bashshar, from Ya'qub, from al-Abbas al-Warraq, from a man he named, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When a group of people go forth to battle without the permission of the Imam and they acquire spoils, the entire spoils belong to the Imam. And when they go forth by the command of the Imam and they acquire spoils, the khums belongs to the Imam."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the charity (sadaqat) of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah) and what is taken from their poll tax (jizya) from the price of their wine, the meat of their pigs, and their dead animals. He said: 'The poll tax is upon them in their wealth; it is taken from them from the price of meat or wine. So whatever they take from them of that, its burden (of sin) is upon them, and its price is lawful for the Muslims; they take it as part of their poll tax.'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: "The land tax (jizya) is not lifted from them [the people of the land], and indeed the jizya is the provision (ata') for the Muhajirun, and the zakat is for its specific people whom Allah named in His Book, and they have no share from the jizya." Then he said: "How vast is justice!" Then he said: "Indeed, people become self-sufficient when justice is established among them, and the sky will send down its provision, and the earth will bring forth its blessings, by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Three - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim from Aban from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Whoever buys something from the khums, God will not excuse him, for he has bought what is not permissible for him.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Sabbah al-Azraq, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: Indeed, the most severe situation for the people on the Day of Resurrection is that the owner of the khums will stand up and say: 'O Lord, [here is] my khums, and we had purified it for our Shias so that their offspring may be pure and their children may grow.'

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Do you know from where adultery entered among the people?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "From our khums, the Ahl al-Bayt, except for our pure Shias, for it is permissible for them and for their offspring."

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Wasshash, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Salamah Salim ibn Mukram, who is Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, while I was present, 'Make the female genitals lawful for me.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was startled and said to him, 'He is not asking you to make the path permissible; rather, he is asking you for a servant whom he will purchase, or a woman whom he will marry, or an inheritance he will acquire, or a trade, or something that was given to him.' He said, 'This is lawful for our Shias, the witness among them and the absent, the deceased among them and the living, and whatever is born among them until the Day of Resurrection, so it is lawful for them. By Allah, nothing is lawful except for whom we have made lawful, and by Allah, we have not given anyone a guarantee of safety, nor is there a covenant with us for anyone, nor is there a pledge with us for anyone.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Al-Hakam ibn 'Ubayya al-Asadi said: I was appointed to Bahrain and acquired much wealth there, so I spent it and bought many estates, and I bought slaves and mothers of children, and children were born to me. Then I went to Mecca, taking my dependents, mothers of my children, and my wives, and I took one-fifth of that wealth. I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'I was appointed to Bahrain and acquired much wealth there, bought goods, slaves, mothers of children, and children were born to me, and I spent it. Here is the one-fifth of that wealth, and these are the mothers of my children and my wives; I have brought them to you.' He said: 'Indeed, all of it is for us, and I have accepted what you brought. I have made permissible for you the mothers of your children and your wives and what you spent, and I have guaranteed for you, upon me and upon my father, Paradise.'

Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Basir and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: 'People are ruined in their bellies and their private parts because they did not pay us our right. Behold, our Shias are exempt from that, and their ancestors are in a state of freedom (exemption).'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from some of our companions from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Whatever We have made permissible for him, if he acquires it from the deeds/wealth of the oppressors, it is permissible for him; and whatever We have forbidden from that, it is forbidden.'

Saad from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masru Masruq, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn Amr al-Zayyat, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'All people live in the surplus of our oppression, except that we have exempted our Shias from that.'

Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the Qammatin (merchants of Qumm) entered upon him and said, 'I am your ransom. Livestock, wealth, and trade goods fall into our hands, and we know that your right (khums) in them is established, yet we are negligent regarding it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'We would not be just to you if we made you liable for that today.'

Sa'd narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from al-Hakam ibn Buhlul, from Abu Hammam, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have acquired wealth, but I do not know whether its lawful portion is from its unlawful portion.' He said to him: 'Pay the khums from that wealth, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has been pleased with the khums from the wealth, and avoid what its owner is known [to be unlawful].'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about what the mine produces, whether little or much, is there any [zakat] in it? He said: 'There is no [zakat] in it until it reaches that which in similar cases zakat is twenty dinars.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about what is extracted from the sea, such as pearls, rubies, and chrysolite, and about the mines of gold and silver: is there zakat in them? He said, 'When its value reaches one dinar, khums is due in it.' And there is no contradiction between the two reports, because the first report covers the ruling of the mines, and the second covers the ruling of what is extracted from the sea; and one is not the other, but each has its own independent ruling.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any dhimmi who buys land from a Muslim, then khums is upon him.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Saffar) he said: A group of people from Khurasan came to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and asked him to release them from the khums. He said, 'How hasty you are! You claim affection for us with your tongues, but you withhold from us the right that Allah has made for us and we for it, and that is the khums. We will not release any one of you from it.'

Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated: I was with Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him) when Salah ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl entered upon him (and he managed the endowment for him in Qum). He said: 'O my master, make me free from the ten thousand dirhams, for I have spent them.' He said to him: 'You are free.' When Salah left, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them jumps upon the wealth of the Family of Muhammad, their orphans, their poor, and their travelers, takes it, then comes and says: 'Make me free.' Do you think he believed that I would say 'No, do not do it'? By God, God Almighty will question them about that on the Day of Judgment with a sharp questioning.' The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: Know, may God guide you, that the leniency mentioned in this chapter regarding consuming khums by spending it was specifically revealed for marriages, for the reason previously mentioned in the traditions from the Imams (peace be upon them), so that the offspring of their Shias may be pure. It was not revealed for wealth, and what I delayed from the preceding matters regarding the strictness in khums and its exclusive right belongs to wealth. This statement is indicated by what he narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him, and I read his letter to him on the way to Mecca. He said: 'What I made obligatory upon you in this year, which is the year of twenty and two hundred, is only for a meaning among meanings which I dislike to explain fully for fear of dissemination. And I will explain part of it to you, if God wills. Indeed, my clients, I ask God for their rectification, or some of them, fell short in what was obligatory upon them, so I knew that and loved to purify and purify them with what I did in my year regarding the matter of khums.' God Almighty said: 'Take charity from their wealth to purify them and to make them grow in purity, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort to them, and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.' Have they not known that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities, and that it is God who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful? And say: 'Work, for God will see your work, and His Messenger, and the believers, and you will be returned to the Knower o

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi 'Umarah, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'We have wealth from agricultural produce, trade, and similar things, and I know that you have a right in them.' He said, 'Then why did we make it permissible for our Shias except to make their offspring content? And whoever is connected to my fathers, they are free from what is in their hands from our right. Let the witness convey to the absent one.' And from him, from Abi Ja'far Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I read in a book of Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) from a man who asked him to make him free from his food and drink from the khums, so he wrote with his own hand, 'Whoever is in need of something from my right, he is free from it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever finds the coolness of our love in his liver (heart), let him praise God for the first blessing." I said, "May I be your ransom, what is the first blessing?" He said, "The purity of lineage." Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, "The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Fatimah (peace be upon her), 'Make permissible for the fathers of our Shias their share from the Fay (booty/gains), so that they may be pleased.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'We have made permissible for the mothers of our Shias [marriage to] their fathers, so that they may be pleased.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, and Hasan ibn Ali, and Muhsin ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, all from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Talhah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, the seller of garments, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is made easy for our Shias to spend from what is in their hands in a good manner. So when our Qa'im (Riser) rises, peace be upon him, it becomes forbidden for every owner of a hoard to keep his hoard, until they bring it to him so that he may make use of it. As for the conquered lands, every land whose people have been established to have surrendered it to us, it is valid for us to transact in it by purchasing from them, and by exchange, and whatever follows their manner. As for the lands of the khraj (land tax), and the lands of the anfal (spoils/public property), and those from which their people have cleared out, we have also been permitted to transact in them as long as the Imam (peace be upon him) is in concealment. So when he appears, he will see fit in that matter as he sees fit, and we will be in our transactions without sin. And we have previously presented what indicates that, and what indicates it also is what he narrated.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I saw Abu Sayyar Mis'ma ibn 'Abd al-Malik in Medina. He had brought wealth to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that year, but he returned it to him. I asked him, 'Why did Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) return the wealth you brought to him?' He said, 'When I brought the wealth to him, I told him: I was appointed for pearl diving and acquired four hundred thousand dirhams. I brought one-fifth of it, which is eighty thousand dirhams. I disliked withholding it from you or ignoring it, as it is your right that Allah the Exalted has made for you in our wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What do we have from the earth and what Allah has brought forth from it, except the khums? O Abu Sayyar, the entire earth is ours. Whatever Allah has brought forth from it is ours.' I said to him, 'I will bring you all the wealth.' He said to me, 'O Abu Sayyar, we have purified it for you and made it permissible for you from it, so keep your wealth for yourself. And whatever is in the hands of our Shias from the earth, they are permitted, and it is permissible for them until our Qa'im rises and gathers them, taking what is in the hands of others. Indeed, their earning from the earth is forbidden to them until our Qa'im rises, takes the earth from their hands, and removes them from it with ease.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I heard a man from the people of al-Jabal ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who took barren land that its people had abandoned, cultivated it, leased its rivers, built houses in it, and planted palms and trees there. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever revives land from among the believers, it is for him, and upon him is its tax (tusk), which he pays to the Imam during the period of truce (hudna). So when the Rising One (peace be upon him) appears, let him prepare himself that it will be taken from him.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khasha'i, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and sat near him, and behold, Najjah had asked permission and was granted entry. He entered and knelt on his knees, then said, 'I am your ransom, I wish to ask you a question, and by God I do not intend by it except the freeing of my neck from the Fire.' He seemed to be moved by him, sat up straight, and said to him, 'O Najjah, ask me, and I will not leave you without informing you of anything you ask me today.' He said, 'I am your ransom, what do you say about so-and-so and so-and-so?' He said, 'O Najjah, we have the khums in the Book of God, and we have the anfal, and we have the choicest of wealth. And they, by God, were the first to wrong us, and they established our right in the Book of God, and the first to make people carry us on their necks, and our blood is in their throats until the Day of Judgment due to our wronging the People of the House. And indeed, people are revolving in the forbidden until the Day of Judgment due to our wronging the People of the House.' Najjah said, 'To God we belong and to Him we shall return,' three times, 'We are ruined, by the Lord of the Ka'ba.' He lifted his thigh from the cushion, faced the qibla, and made a supplication of which I understood nothing, except that we heard him at the end of his supplication saying, 'O God, we have made that permissible for our shi'a.' He then turned his face to us and said, 'O Najjah, upon the fitrah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) are none but us and our shi'a.' If a questioner says, 'All that you have mentioned only indicates permission for you to manage these lands, and does not indicate that it is valid for you to own them through purchase and sale,' then if purchase and sale are not valid, what is a branch of them that is also not valid, such as waqf, nihla, hibah, and what runs in their manner? It was said to him, 'We have divided the lands in the past into three categories: A land whose people surrender it, so it is left in their hands and it is their property; thus, for us, the ruling of this is valid, and our purchase and sale of it are valid. As for the lands that are taken by conquest or whose people make peace with us upon it, we have been permitted their purchase and sale beca

And Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying from the land of the Jews and Christians, so he said: 'There is no harm in it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) conquered the people of Khaybar and made a treaty with them to leave the land in their hands, so they would work it and cultivate it. Therefore, I see no harm if you buy something from it. And whoever people revive a piece of land and work it, they are more entitled to it, and it is theirs.'

And from him, from Ali, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Umar ibn Hatshalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about that, and he said: 'There is no harm in buying it, for when it is in its place in their hands, they pay for it as it is paid for.'

And from him, from Ali, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying from the land of Jizya. He said, then he said, 'Buy it, for you have from the right that which is more than that.'

And with this chain of narration, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: "When that occurs, you will be closer to being increased [in rank/wealth] than you are to being decreased."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hakam ibn Aynan from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said: He said: 'If you see the Master of this Command giving all that is in the treasury to one man, let nothing enter your heart [of doubt], for he is only acting by the command of Allah.'
And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The arrows are only directed at what the army/camp contains."

Al-Sayyari from Ali ibn Asbat who said: When Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) arrived before al-Mahdi, he found him returning the wronged (restoring rights). He said to him, 'What is the matter with our injustice, O Commander of the Faithful? You do not return it.' He said to him, 'And what is it, O Abu al-Hasan?' 'Indeed, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, opened for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) Fadak and what was attached to it, and there was no marching of cavalry or riding beasts upon it, Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'And give to the near of kin his right.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not know who they were, so he consulted Gabriel (peace be upon him) about that and asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about it. So Allah revealed to him, 'Give Fadak to Fatimah (peace be upon her).' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her, 'O Fatimah, indeed Allah the Exalted commanded me to give you Fadak.' She said, 'I have accepted, O Messenger of Allah, from Allah and from you.' So its trustees remained in it during the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When Abu Bakr took charge, he removed its trustees from it. So she came to him and asked him to return it to her. He said to her, 'Bring me a black or a red one to testify to you about that.' So she came with the Commander of the Faithful, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and Umm Ayman, and they testified to her about that. So he wrote for her a deed of non-interference. So she left with the document with her. Umar met her and said to her, 'What is this with you, O daughter of Muhammad?' She said, 'A document that Ibn Abi Quhafah wrote for me.' He said to her, 'Show it to me.' She refused, so he snatched it from her hand, looked at it, spat in it, erased it, tore it, and said, 'This is because your father did not march upon it with cavalry or riding beasts.' And he left it and went away.' So al-Mahdi said to him, 'Flog her for me.' So he flogged her. He said, 'This is too much,' so he paused to consider it.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Sindiy ibn Muhammad from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Anfal (spoils of war) is from the Anfal (plurality/abundance), and in the Surah Al-Anfal, it refers to the cutting off of the nose.

And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he heard him saying: "Indeed, Al-Anfal are lands where there was no shedding of blood, or people who were reconciled and gave with their own hands. As for lands that are desolate or the bellies of valleys, all of this is from Al-Fay'. And Al-Anfal are for Allah and the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). What is for Allah is for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and he places it where he wills."

Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda al-Hafiz al-Hamdani, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim al-Ash'ari, who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Ziyad (who is al-Wassah al-Kazzaz, and is the son of Bint Ilyas) narrated to us; he paused then returned and cut off the chain, from Abd al-Karim ibn 'Umar al-Kath'ami, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, and Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The greatest of the major sins are seven: Shirk with Allah the Great, and killing the soul which Allah has forbidden except with the right, and eating the wealth of orphans, and disobedience to parents, and charging chaste women with unchastity, and fleeing from the battle line, and denying what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has revealed. As for Shirk with Allah the Great, there has reached you what Allah revealed concerning us and what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, so return it to Allah and to His Messenger. And as for killing the sacred soul, it is the killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions. And as for eating the wealth of orphans, we were wronged regarding our Fai' (booty/wealth) and they took it. And as for disobedience to parents, indeed Allah the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book: 'The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers.' And he is a father to them, so they were disobedient to him in his offspring and in his close relatives. And as for charging chaste women with unchastity, they charged Fatimah (peace be upon her) with it on their pulpits. And as for fleeing from the battle line, they gave the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) the pledge of allegiance willingly, not being coerced, then they fled from him and abandoned him. And as for denying what Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed, they denied our right and rejected it, and this is something in which no one can be confused. And Allah says: 'If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance [into Paradise].' The third part of the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam ended, and its end is the book of Zakat with the additions, and it is followed by the fourth part of the book of As-Siyam. 'And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Islam is built upon five things: upon prayer, alms-tax, fasting, pilgrimage, and guardianship. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fasting is a shield from the Fire.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Ali ibn Abd al-'Aziz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "Shall I inform you of the root, branch, apex, and crest of Islam?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Its root is Salat (prayer), its branch is Zakat (alms-tax), and its apex and crest is Jihad (striving) in the path of Allah." "Shall I inform you of the gates of goodness?" "Fasting is a shield against the Fire."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Amawi, from Rabi'i ibn Abdillah ibn al-Jarud, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "God, Exalted and Majestic, said: Fasting is for Me, and I shall reward for it."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd, from Abdullah ibn Musa, who said: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Rabi'ah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The month of Ramadan is a month in which Allah, Exalted and Mighty, made fasting obligatory upon you. So whoever fasts it with faith and seeking reward, he will emerge from his sins as the day his mother gave birth to him.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Utbah, from al-Kufi, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn Abu Nu'aym, who said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us from Ayyub al-Sijistani, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The month of Ramadan has come to you, a blessed month, a month in which Allah has made fasting obligatory for you.' In it, the gates of Paradise are opened, and the devils are chained. 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.' Whoever is deprived of it has been deprived [of all good].

And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon on the last Friday of the month of Sha'ban, praising Allah and extolling Him. Then he said: 'O people, a month has overshadowed you in which is a night 'better than a thousand months', the month of Ramadan. Allah made its fasting obligatory, and He made the standing in prayer during one night of it, as voluntary, equivalent to the voluntary standing in prayer of seventy nights in the other months. And He made for whoever voluntarily performs in it a characteristic from the characteristics of goodness and benevolence, like the reward of one who performed an obligatory duty from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious. And whoever performs in it an obligatory duty from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is like one who performed seventy obligatory duties from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, in the other months. And it is the month of patience, and indeed the reward for patience is Paradise. And it is the month of sharing provisions, and it is a month in which Allah, Exalted and Glorious, increases the sustenance of the believer. And whoever feeds a believer in it, for him is, because of that, with Allah, Exalted and Glorious, the freeing of a neck and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed.' It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to feed a fasting person in it. He said: 'Indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is Generous; He gives this reward to whoever is not able except to give a mouthful of milk to a fasting person, or a sip of fresh water, or a few dates, which he cannot give more than that. And whoever eases the burden on his slave in it, Allah will ease his reckoning. And it is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance, and emancipation from the Fire. And you have no need in it to be without four characteristics: two characteristics by which you please Allah, Exalted and Glorious, and two characteristics by which you have no need to be without. As for the two by which you please Allah, Exalted and Glorious, they are the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And as for the two by which y

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asamm from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Ma'mar ibn Yahya that he heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will not call a servant to account for a prayer after the obligatory prayer, nor for charity after the obligatory alms-tax, nor for fasting after the month of Ramadan.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Sabih, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The month of Ramadan ablates every fast, and the sacrifice (al-Nahr) ablates every slaughtered animal, and the alms-tax (al-Zakat) ablates every voluntary charity, and the ritual bath of major impurity (Ghusl al-Janabah) ablates every other bath."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Aqraʿ, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'God did not burden the servants beyond what they can bear.' He mentioned the obligatory duties and said: 'He only obligated them to fast for one month of the year, while they are capable of more than that.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Safwan, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever prays the five [daily prayers], fasts the month of Ramadan, performs Hajj to the Sacred House, offers the sacrifice as we have prescribed, and follows us, Allah will accept from him just as He accepts from the angels."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah does not call a servant to account for any prayer after the five [obligatory ones], nor for any fast after Ramadan.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Hamzah ibn Ya'la from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the crescent of Rajab is confirmed, count fifty-nine days and fast the sixtieth day." He means by his saying (peace be upon him), 'fast the sixtieth day,' on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, as a precaution. And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Bakr and Muhammad ibn Abi al-Subhan from Hafs from Umar ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa from Harun ibn Kharijah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Count Sha'ban as twenty-nine days; if the sky is cloudy, then begin fasting in the morning; and if it is clear, and you look carefully and see nothing (the new moon), then begin breaking the fast in the morning." If the intention behind it were not what we mentioned, namely resolving to fast it on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, then one would be obliged to intend that it is from the month of Ramadan and not pay attention to whether the sky is cloudy or clear.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ubays ibn Hisham from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt, for people claim that whoever fasts it is like the one who breaks fast for a day from the month of Ramadan. He said: 'They are lying. If it is a day from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day they were guided to, and if it is from the others, then it is like the days that have passed.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Samaan, who said: I asked him about the day in which one is uncertain whether it is from the month of Ramadan or not, and he does not know if it is from Sha'ban or from the month of Ramadan, so he fasted it as from Ramadan. He said: 'It is a day for which he was granted success, and there is no make-up (qada) required for him.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Şuhban, from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Bashir al-Nabbal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about fasting the Day of Doubt, so he said: 'Fast it, for if it is from Sha'ban it is voluntary (fasting of supererogation), and if it is from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which you were enabled (to fast).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hamzah ibn Ya'la from Zakariyya ibn Adam from al-Kahili who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the day of doubt in the month of Sha'ban. He said: 'Fasting one day from Sha'ban is more beloved to me than if I were to break the fast for one day from the month of Ramadan.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I fasted the day of doubt, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan, so should I make it up?' He said: 'No, it is a day for which you were granted success (i.e., your fast is sufficient and valid).'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In the man who fasts the day of doubt from Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must make it up, even if it is so.' This is not contradictory to the first report because what is meant by this report is one who fasted the day of doubt and did not intend that it is from Sha'ban - rather he intended that it is from the month of Ramadan. For when the matter is as we mentioned, he has fasted what is not permissible for him to fast, and at that time it becomes obligatory upon him to make it up. And it indicates that when he intended that it is from Sha'ban, it is not obligatory upon him to make it up. Added to what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan from Ibn Mukkan from Abu Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Permitted to you, on the night of fasting, is to go to your wives' (the verse). He said: 'It was revealed concerning Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, who was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in the Trench. He was fasting and remained in that state until evening. Before this verse was revealed, if one of them slept, food became forbidden to him. So Khawwat came to his family when it was evening and said: 'Do you have any food?' They said: 'No. Stay until we prepare food for you.' He leaned back and slept. They said to him: 'You have been negligent.' He said: 'Yes.' So he spent the night in that state and morning came. Then he went to the Trench and began to be overcome with drowsiness/fainting. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by, and when he saw what was happening to him, he informed him of how his situation was. So Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed in his case the verse: 'Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]'. 'Permitted to you, on the night of fasting, is to go to your wives' 'Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the white thread in contrast to the black thread, so he said: 'The whiteness of the day from the darkness of the night.' He said: 'And Bilal used to give the adhan for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when the dawn rose, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When you hear the voice of Bilal, then stop eating and drinking, for you have become morning (i.e., it is time to fast)."'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'When does food become prohibited for the fasting person, and when does the Fajr prayer become permissible?' He said to me, 'When dawn appears and is like the white sheet (al-qubtiyyah al-bayda'), then food becomes prohibited and the Fajr prayer becomes permissible.' I said: 'So we are not in the time [of prohibition] until the ray of the sun rises?' He said, 'Far off! Where are you going? That is the prayer of the children.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Attiyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The dawn is that which, when you see it crossing [the sky], resembles the whiteness of the river of Sura."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The time for the setting of the disk [of the sun] and the obligation of breaking the fast is that one stands facing the Qibla and observes the redness that rises from the East; when it passes the height of a man's head towards the West, then breaking the fast becomes obligatory and the disk has set.

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about breaking the fast before the prayer or after it, so he said: 'If he is with a group of people and fears that he will detain them from their evening meal, let him break the fast with them; and if it is otherwise, let him pray and then break the fast.'
It is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: "The actions are by the intentions."

And it is narrated from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said: "There is no speech (or statement) except with action, and no action except with intention, and no intention except with conformity to the Sunnah."

Al-Husayn from al-Fadala from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Sama'a from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person who fasts voluntarily and hunger strikes him: he said, 'He has the choice between himself and the afternoon prayer. And if he remains until the afternoon prayer, then it occurs to him to fast and he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked him about a man who is making up for Ramadan, is it permissible for him to break his fast after dawn but before midday if it becomes apparent to him? He said: 'If he intended that from the night, and it is from making up for Ramadan, then he should not break his fast and he should complete his fast.' He said: And I asked him about a man who becomes apparent to him after dawn and the day rises, that he should fast that day and make it up from Ramadan, even if he did not intend that from the night. He said: 'Yes, he should fast it and count it, provided he does not do anything [that breaks the fast/intent].'

From him, from al-Hus-Husayn, from an-Nadr, from ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever wakes up intending to fast, then decides to break the fast, he may break it from the time of his decision until midday; then he must make up that day. If he decides to fast after the sun has risen, let him fast, for it will be counted for him from the hour in which he made the intention."

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: "When a man does not impose fasting upon himself as obligatory, then remembers fasting before he eats food or drinks a drink, and has not broken his fast, then he is at his choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast."

From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who wakes up in the morning without having eaten or drunk, and without having made the intention to fast, and he is still obligated to fast one day of Ramadan. Is he permitted to fast that day, given that most of the day has passed? He said: 'Yes, he may fast and count it as one of the days of Ramadan.'

From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying: 'The fasting person has the choice until the sun declines,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast, and as for the voluntary fast, he has the right to break his fast at any time he wishes until sunset.'

Al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'A man wakes up in the morning without intending fasting, and when the sun rises, a thought comes to him to fast.' He said: 'If he intends fasting before the sun passes its zenith (zawal), it is counted for him from his day; and if he intends it after the zenith, it is counted for him from the time he intended.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'A man has make-up prayers (qada) from the month of Ramadan, and he enters the morning but does not eat until Asr prayer; is it permissible for him to make it make-up from the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who wakes up in the morning having not eaten, not drunk, and not made the intention for fasting, and he has one day of Ramadan upon him. Is it permissible for him to fast that day, given that most of the day has passed? He said, 'Yes, it is permissible for him to fast it and count it as one of the days of Ramadan.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would enter his home and say, 'Do you have something [to eat], or shall I fast?' If they had something, they would bring it to him, and if not, he would fast.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man wakes up not intending to fast, and when the day rises, a thought comes to him about fasting. He said: 'If he intends fasting before the sun passes its zenith (Zawal), his day is counted for him; and if he intends it after Zawal, only the time from which he intended is counted for him.'

Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Isa said: "Whoever stays the night intending to fast the next day, that intention binds him; if he breaks the fast, he must make up for it. And whoever wakes up and did not intend to fast from the night, he has the choice until the sun sets; if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks the fast. If the sun sets and he has not eaten, he should complete the fast until night." Therefore, this report is understood as referring to a type of preference (istihbab), because the earlier reports indicate that he may break the fast at any time he wishes without making it up, and it is possible that this is specific to making up the fast of Ramadan, for if he breaks the fast in it after midday, he is obligated to make it up along with expiation, as we will explain later, if God Almighty wills.

Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Fasting is not merely from food and drink, and it is incumbent upon a person to guard his tongue from vain falsehood during Ramadan and other times."

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'What the fasting person does does not harm him, provided he avoids three things: food, drink, and women, and immersing himself in water.'

And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who lied during Ramadan, so he said: 'He has broken his fast, and upon him is its making up.' I said: 'What is his lie?' He said: 'He lies upon Allah and upon His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: "For every thing there is a purification (zakat), and the purification of the bodies is fasting."

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The fasting person is in a state of worship, even if he is on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim."

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever frequently fasts, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His angels: 'My servant has sought refuge from My punishment, so protect him.' And Allah has assigned His angels to supplicate for those who fast, and He did not command the angels to supplicate for anyone except that He answers them concerning that person.
And from him, from Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The sleep of the fasting person is worship, and his breath is glorification.

And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, upon them be peace: That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'Shall I not inform you of something that if you do it, Satan will distance himself from you as the East is distant from the West?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, and love for God and mutual assistance in righteous deeds severs his progeny, and seeking forgiveness severs his tail.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For every thing there is a purification (zakat), and the purification of the bodies is fasting.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Hakim ibn Miskin, from Ismail ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, a man prays two rak'ahs, and Allah obligates Paradise for him because of them; or he fasts one day voluntarily, and Allah obligates Paradise for him because of it.'

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit, Abu Al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a long hadith: 'Fasting is a shield: 'Fasting is a shield against the Fire.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: Three things remove phlegm and increase retention (of knowledge): using the miswak, fasting, and recitation of the Quran.
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next year, except if he attends 'Arafat."

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would face the people and say: 'O assembly of Muslims, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan appears, the rebels of the devils are shackled, the gates of heaven are opened, the gates of mercy are opened, and the gates of hellfire are closed, and supplication is answered. And for Allah, at every breaking of the fast (Eid), there are slaves freed from the hellfire. A caller proclaims every night: 'Is there any supplicant? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a substitute, and give every hoarder a loss.' Until the crescent of Shawal appears, it is proclaimed to the believers: 'Go forth to your rewards,' for it is the Day of Reward.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are not the reward of dinars and dirhams (coins/money).'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, for Allah are those freed and released from the Fire every night of the month of Ramadan, except for one who breaks his fast on a intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He frees in it as many as He freed in all of it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Torah was revealed in the six days that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Gospel was revealed in the twelve that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Psalms were revealed in the eighteen that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Criterion (Quran) was revealed 'on the Night of Power'.

Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ini from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, fasting is not merely abstaining from food and drink. Then he said: Maryam said, 'I have vowed a fast (sawm) to the Most Merciful,' meaning silence. So when you fast, guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not quarrel, and do not envy one another. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard a woman cursing her female servant while she was fasting. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called for food and said to her, 'Eat.' She said, 'I am fasting.' He said, 'How can you be fasting when you have cursed your servant? Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast, and your hair and your skin," and he enumerated other things besides this. He said: "And let the day of your fasting not be like the day of your breaking the fast."

And from him, from Al-Husayn, from An-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast from the forbidden and the ugly; avoid quarreling and the annoyance of the servant, and let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make your day of fasting like your day of breaking the fast."

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman and others from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite it in the month of Ramadan at night or during the day.' Isma'il said to him: 'O my father, for it is among us.' He said: 'Even if it is among us.'
