And the woman does not dip her head in water because she retains water in her private part.' The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And deliberate vomiting breaks the fast of the fasting person, and if forced vomiting occurred, there is no penalty upon him.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the fasting person vomits, he must make up that day; but if he controls the vomit without actually vomiting, he should complete his fast."

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the fasting person vomits, he has broken his fast; and if it reaches him (by force) without him vomiting, let him complete his fast."

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) that he said: "Whoever vomits deliberately while fasting has broken his fast, and he must make up for it; if Allah wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him." And he said: "Whoever vomits while fasting, upon him is the making up (of the fast)."

And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever vomits intentionally while he is fasting, he must make up one day in its place."

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the qals (eye kohl), does it break the fast of the fasting person? He said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the fasting person who rinses his mouth, he said: 'He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The fasting person anoints himself with perfume and smells the fragrant plant."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would use perfume when he fasted, and he would say, 'Perfume is the gift of the fasting person.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the fasting person [have any issue if he] smells rosemary and perfume?' He said: 'There is no harm.'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: "Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) disliked that the fasting person should perfume himself with it (musk)."

Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the fasting person: Do you see it permissible for him to smell rosemary (or pleasant scent), or do you not see that permissible for him? He said, 'There is no harm in it.' And from him (Sa'd ibn Abdullah) from Abu Ja'far from 'Ibad ibn Sulayman from Sa'd ibn Sa'd said: A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Does the fasting person smell rosemary to enjoy it? He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no harm in it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadda' from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd (1) said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbidding the use of narcissus (nargis), so I said, 'May I be your ransom, for what reason is that?' He said, 'Because it is the scent (rihan) of the foreigners (A'ajim).' And reports have been narrated regarding the dislike (karahah) of smelling the scent (rihan) as well.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The fasting person does not smell the rose (or pleasant scent)."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan ibn Baqqah from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: And I asked him about the fasting person who wears a wet garment, so he said: 'No, and he should not smell the rose (or fragrant plant).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer? He said: 'No.' I said: Does she make up the fast? He said: 'Yes.' I said: From where does this come? He said: 'Indeed, the first to make analogy (qias) was Iblis.' I said: So if the fasting person dips into the water, does it break his fast? He said: 'Yes.' I said: And if he urinates on his garment while it is on his body, does it break his fast? He said: 'No.' I said: From where does this come? He said: 'From that (analogy).' I said: Does the fasting person smelling the rayhan (pansy/fragrant flower) break his fast? He said: 'No, because it is a delight, and it is disliked for him to delight in it.' Thus, these narrations and what follows their pattern fall into the category of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram). Therefore, it is preferable for the fasting person to refrain from delighting in all types of delights, and if he does so, it does not break his fast. He clarified this by saying in the final narration: 'Because it is a delight, and it is disliked for him to delight in it.' It is also possible that what is meant by mentioning 'rayhan' in these narrations is specifically the narcissus (narsaj) and not other flowers. Do you not see the narration we mentioned earlier regarding the dislike of narcissus, which was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Fayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he mentioned the dislike of that and then said: 'Because it is the rayhan of the Ajam (Persians/Non-Arabs)'? So he applied the name 'rayhan' to it, and it is not impossible that what is meant in these narrations is specifically that one, and not others.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted in Ramadan and ate or drank unintentionally. He said, 'He completes his fast and there is no qada (making up) upon him.'

And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever fasts and forgets, and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because of his forgetting, for it is sustenance that God provided for him, so let him complete his fasting.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the man who forgets and eats during the month of Ramadan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes his fast, for it is merely something Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, fed him.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever eats, or drinks, or has intercourse while he supposes that dawn has not yet risen, and it was indeed rising, there is no blame upon him if he had been watching for dawn but did not become certain of it, and he completes that day. But if he began with eating or drinking or with one of the things we mentioned before looking at the dawn, then it became clear afterwards that it was rising, it becomes obligatory upon him to complete that day and he is liable for making up (the fast).' This is indicated by what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I asked him about a man who ate or drank after the dawn had risen in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'If he got up, looked, and did not see the dawn, then ate, and then returned and saw the dawn, let him complete his fast and there is no re-performance (qada') upon him. And if he got up, ate or drank, and then looked at the dawn and saw that it had risen, let him complete his fast and perform a re-performance (qada') for another day, because he began with eating before looking, so re-performance is upon him.' And this does not contradict what was narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who ate suhur, then left his house, and the dawn had risen and become distinct, so he said: "He completes his fast that day, then he must make it up; and if he ate suhur in a month other than Ramadan after the rising of dawn, he breaks his fast." Then he said, "My father was praying one night while I was eating, so he finished and said, 'As for Ja'far, he has eaten and drunk after dawn.' So he ordered me, and I broke my fast that day in a month other than Ramadan." Because he started with eating and drinking and did not look at the dawn, and whoever does that, his ruling is what we mentioned. Al-Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And if he asked someone else about the dawn, and that person informed him that it had not risen, and he trusted him, so he ate and drank, then he learned that it had risen, then he must make it up.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I command the servant girl to look whether dawn has risen or not; if she says it has not risen, I eat. Then I look and find that it has risen by the time she looked.' He said: 'You complete your day and you also make up for it (perform qada). Is it not that if you were the one who looked, there would not be any qada upon you?'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who went out in the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating suhoor (pre-dawn meal) in a house. He looked at the dawn and called them. Some of them stopped, and some thought he was mocking them, so they ate. He said: 'He completes his fast and also makes up for it (qada).'. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever thought that the sun had set due to a cloud or something similar, and broke his fast, then it became clear that it had not actually set at that time, it is obligatory upon him to make up the fast. What he mentioned (may Allah have mercy on him) is the narration of Samaan ibn Mihran in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Samaan and Abu Basir, and no one else narrated it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ubayd from Yunus from Abu Basir and Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a group of people who fasted the month of Ramadan, and a black cloud covered them at sunset, so they thought it was night, he said: 'Upon the one who broke his fast is the making up of that day, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says, "Then complete the fast until night." So whoever ate before night entered, upon him is its making up, because he ate deliberately.' The meaning in this narration is that when one doubts the entry of night due to an occurrence (like clouds), and his conjectures are equal and neither has an advantage over the other, it is not permissible for him to break his fast until he is certain of the entry of night or his conjecture prevails. And when he breaks his fast while the state is as described, making up (the fast) is obligatory upon him according to what this report contains. As for when his conjection prevails that night has entered, so he breaks his fast, then it becomes clear afterwards that night had not entered, he should refrain from food and there is no making up upon him. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted, then presumed that the sun had set while there was cloud cover in the sky, so he broke his fast, and then the clouds cleared and the sun had not set. He said: 'His fast is complete and he does not have to make it up.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was fasting and thought that night had entered and that the sun had set, and there was clouds in the sky, so he broke his fast, then the clouds cleared and behold the sun had not set, he said: 'His fast is complete and he does not have to make it up.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Maghrib is when the disk [of the sun] disappears. If you see it after that, and you have already prayed, you repeat the prayer, your fast is valid, and you refrain from eating, provided you have consumed something from it [during the time of doubt].'
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadalah from Jamil from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "The kiss does not break the fast."

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about kissing while fasting in the month of Ramadan, does it break the fast? He said, 'No.' And it has been narrated that it is disliked for the fasting person to kiss, fearing that desire might overcome him, especially for the youth.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked Does the fasting person engage in intercourse or kiss in the month of Ramadan? He said, 'I fear for him, so let him abstain from that unless he is confident that his semen will not precede it.'

And from him, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from Sa'd ibn Dharrīf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: A man came to Amīr al-Mu'minīn (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Amīr al-Mu'minīn, I kiss while I am fasting.' He said to him: 'Restrain your fasting, for the beginning of the fighting is the kissing.' And whenever a man emits semen through intimacy or speech while he is fasting, there is nothing upon him that indicates that, as he narrated:

And from him (Al-Hadith) from Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who spoke to his wife while he was fasting in the month of Ramadan. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, and if he emitted semen, there is no penalty upon him, and intimacy is not harmful, and he does not have to make up the day, and it is not appropriate for him to expose himself to Ramadan.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Rifa'ah ibn Musa said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who touched a girl in the month of Ramadan and emitted semen. He said: 'If it was from a forbidden act, he should seek Allah's forgiveness with the forgiveness of one who never returns, and fast one day in place of one day. And if it was from a permissible act, he should seek Allah's forgiveness and not return, and fast one day in place of one day.' This is a rare, unusual hadith and contrary to the fatwas of all our scholars. Perhaps the narrator erred in his statement at the end of the report, 'and fast one day in place of one day,' because the content of the report indicates this. Do you not see that he began by distinguishing between emitting semen from a forbidden act and emitting semen from a permissible act? And according to the fatwa he narrated, there is no difference between the two, so it is known that it is an error of the narrator. And whoever has intercourse with his wife and emits semen, what is obligatory upon him is what is obligatory upon one who has intercourse. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who plays with his wife in the month of Ramadan until he ejaculates. He said, 'Upon him is like what is upon the one who has intercourse.' If the man ejaculated from looking or from speech without physical contact, there is nothing upon him. Indicating that, as he narrated.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who spoke to his wife while he was fasting in the month of Ramadan, and he emitted pre-seminal fluid (al-manī), so he said, 'There is no harm.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If there is upon a man something from the fasting of the month of Ramadan, let him make it up in whichever months he wishes, consecutive days. If he is unable, let him make it up however he wishes and let him count the days. If he separates them, it is good, and if he continues them, it is good. I said: What do you think if there remains upon him something from the fasting of Ramadan - should he make it up in Dhu al-Hijjah? He said: Yes.

And from him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever breaks a fast of Ramadan for a valid excuse, if he makes it up consecutively, that is superior; and if he makes it up separately, it is good."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has days of the month of Ramadan remaining on him, should he make them up separately? He said, 'There is no harm in separating the making up of the month of Ramadan; rather, the fasting that must not be separated is the expiation for Zad (verbal divorce), the expiation for blood, and the expiation for an oath.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan, how should he make them up? He said: 'If he has two days to make up, he should fast one day and break the fast (skip one day) between them; and if he has five days, he should break the fast on some days between them, and he is not permitted to fast more than six consecutive days; and if he has eight or ten days, he should break the fast on one day between them.' The meaning in this narration is that whoever is obligated to make up the month of Ramadan is not required to make them up consecutively, according to what was obligatory for him initially. What this report contains regarding the command to break the fast and separate between these days is merely a recommendation (choice) rather than an obligation, and we have previously established that making them up consecutively is superior.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about making up the month of Ramadan — whether to do it in the month of Dhi al-Hijjah and whether to break it (fast one day, skip the next) — so he said: 'Make it up in the month of Dhi al-Hijjah, and break it if you wish.'

And that which was narrated is: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the making up of the month of Ramadan, if he is unable to perform it in succession, he may break it up, and he said: 'He does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.' His saying (peace be upon him): 'He does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah,' the meaning is if he is a pilgrim, because he is a traveler, and it is not permissible for the traveler to make up the month of Ramadan unless he stays or intends to stay in a town for ten days. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what we previously presented regarding the permissibility of making up the month of Ramadan during Dhu al-Hijjah. As for that which indicates that it is not permissible to make up the month of Ramadan while traveling, it is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who fell ill in the month of Ramadan, and when he recovered wished to perform Hajj, what should he do regarding the making up of the fast? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he returns, let him make it up.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever is obliged to make up the month of Ramadan or something of the obligatory fasting, it is not permissible for him to perform voluntary fasting until he fulfills what is obligatory upon him. This is indicated by what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a portion of the month of Ramadan remaining upon him; does he fast voluntarily? He said, 'No, until he fulfills what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan; does he fast voluntarily (before making up the missed days)? He said, 'No, until he makes up what is due to him from the month of Ramadan.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever becomes a junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) in the morning on a day for which he had intended fasting, whether for making up the missed days of Ramadan or for voluntary fasting, his fasting is not valid. This is indicated by what has been narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is making up for Ramadan, becomes junub from the beginning of the night, and does not perform ghusl until the end of the night, while he believes that dawn has risen. He (AS) said: 'He does not fast that day, and he fasts another day.' Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever becomes a fasting person for making up a day from the month of Ramadan, and breaks his fast in it unintentionally (out of forgetfulness), there is no blame is not upon him, and he completes the rest of his day with fasting.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who forgot, so he ate and drank, then remembered, he said: 'He does not break his fast; it is merely something Allah provided for him, so let him complete his fast.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Yusuf ibn 'Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever fasts, then forgets and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because of his forgetting, for it is sustenance that Allah (Exalted and Mighty) provided for him, so let him complete his fast.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man fasted a day of voluntary fast, then ate and drank forgetfully. He said: 'He completes that day, and there is nothing upon him.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he deliberately broke his fast before midday (zawal), there is nothing upon him, and he fasts one day in its place whenever he wishes. And if he broke his fast after midday, expiation (kaffarah) becomes obligatory upon him, which is feeding ten poor people, and he fasts one day in its place. If feeding is not possible for him, he fasts three days in place of feeding. This is indicated by what he narrated:

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Hamzah ibn Ya'la, from al-Barqi, from Ubayd ibn al-Husayn, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For your voluntary fasting, you may break the fast at any time before nightfall, whenever you wish; and for your making up the missed obligatory fast, you may break it until the sun sets, but once the sun has set, you may no longer break it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who is making up the month of Ramadan, and her husband forces her to break the fast. He said: 'It is not appropriate for him to force her after midday (Zawal).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Sinan from Uthman ibn Marwan from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, 'The fasting person has the choice until the sun sets,' he said, 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast; as for the voluntary fast, he may break his fast at any hour he wishes until sunset.' His saying (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast,' means the making up of the obligatory fast, because the obligatory fast itself does not have the choice to break it at any time.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Harith ibn Muhammad from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had relations with his wife on a day he is making up from the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had relations with her before midday (al-zawal), there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day. And if he had relations with her on a day after midday, then he must give charity to ten poor people. If he is unable, he should fast one day in place of one day and fast three days as expiation for what he did.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man had intercourse with his wife while he was making up the days of Ramadan. He said: 'If he had intercourse with her before the Asr prayer, there is nothing upon him; he fasts one day in place of one day. And if he did so after Asr, he fasts that day and feeds ten poor people. And if he is unable to do so, he fasts three days as expiation for that.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who made up a day of fasting from the month of Ramadan, and then had intercourse with his wife. He said: 'Upon him is from the expiation what is upon the one who had intercourse in the month of Ramadan, on that day in the sight of Allah from the days of Ramadan.' This report came rarely, and it can be intended for the one who broke his fast on that day after midday, in a manner of slighting and minimizing what is obligatory upon him from the command of Allah, the Exalted. Thus, at that time, the expiation obligatory upon him is what is upon the one who breaks his fast for a day in the month of Ramadan, as a punishment and severity upon him. As for the one who breaks his fast while believing that it is preferable to complete his fasting, then upon him is only what we have previously mentioned: feeding ten poor people or fasting three days.

And that which was narrated is: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan and wishes to make them up, when does he intend the fasting? He said: 'He has the choice until the sun sets. When the sun sets, if he intended fasting, let him fast; and if he intended breaking the fast, let him break it.' He was asked: If he intended breaking the fast, is it appropriate for him to intend fasting after the sun has set? He said: 'No.' He was asked: If he intended fasting and then broke the fast after the sun had set? He said: 'He has erred, and there is nothing upon him except the making up of that day which he intended to make up.' His saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing upon him except the making up of that day' is to be understood as meaning there is no punishment upon him, because whoever breaks the fast on this day does not deserve punishment, even if he breaks it after midday, and expiation (kaffarah) falls upon him as we have explained. It is not so for the one who breaks the fast in Ramadan, because he deserves punishment, making up, and expiation. As for voluntary fasting, he has the choice to break it at any time he wishes, and there is nothing upon him. Indicating this is what we have previously mentioned from the narrations, and clarifying it further is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The one who makes up the month of Ramadan has the choice between breaking the fast (for the makeup day) and keeping it, from dawn until the sun sets; and for voluntary fasting, from dawn until the sun sets."

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the one who makes up the month of Ramadan, he has the choice [to delay making it up] until the sun sets, and if it is voluntary fasting, then he has the choice until nightfall.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Fasting is obligatory upon the boy when he reaches puberty, and fasting and the headscarf (khimar) are obligatory upon the girl when she menstruates, unless she is a slave girl, for there is no headscarf upon her unless she wishes to wear it, and fasting is upon her.

And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: "The child, when he is capable of fasting three consecutive days, then fasting of the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: "We command our children to fast when they are seven years old, to the extent they can endure fasting for the day. If they can fast until midday or more or less, then when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they become accustomed to fasting and can endure it. So command your children to fast, when they are nine years old, to the extent they can endure. If thirst overcomes them, they break their fast." The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And the woman with irregular menstruation (mustaha'dah) breaks her fast during the days of Ramadan that were her usual menstrual period, and she fasts the remaining days.

That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman with irregular menstruation (mustahaḍah). He said, 'She fasts the month of Ramadan except for the days in which she used to menstruate, then she makes them up afterwards.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever is obliged to fast two consecutive months [as expiation] for breaking a day in Ramadan, or for accidental killing, or for zihar, or for a vow that he imposed upon himself, and he breaks his fast before completing the fasting fully: if he deliberately breaks his fast without an excuse before completing one of the two months, or after completing it without fasting anything from the second, then he must restart the fasting. This is indicated by what he narrated:'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has the fasting of two consecutive months upon him, does he separate the days? He said: 'If he fasts more than a month and connects it, then an event befalls him and he breaks the fast, there is no harm. But if it is less than a month or one month, then he must repeat the fasting.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The fasting for the expiation of an oath in al-Zihar is two consecutive months, and consecutiveness is that he fasts one month and fasts some days or a portion of the other month; if something occurs that causes him to break the fast, he breaks it, then makes up what remains of it; and if he fasts one month, then something occurs and he breaks the fast before fasting anything from the other month, so they are not consecutive, then he must repeat the entire fasting." And he said: "The fasting of three days in the expiation of an oath must be consecutive and they are not separated." Al-Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: If he intentionally breaks the fast after having fasted some part of the second month, he has erred, and the building is upon what has passed being completed entirely.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who fasted during the middle of Sha'ban, then Ramadan caught up with him, he said: 'He fasts the month of Ramadan and restarts the fasting; if he fasted during the middle (of Sha'ban) and added one day to the half, he combines (the days) and fulfills the remainder of his obligation.' Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If he became ill before he completed the first month with fasting, or after he completed it before he had fasted anything from the second, and he broke his fast due to illness, then in both cases he is not required to restart (from the beginning). That is indicated by what he narrated:'

Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar and Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Mubarak from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had to fast two consecutive months, so he fasted twenty-five days, then he got sick; when he recovered, does he complete (build upon) what he fasted, or does he repeat his fasting entirely? He said, 'Rather, he completes what he had fasted.' Then he said, 'This is what God has overridden, and there is nothing upon what God has overridden.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala from Rifa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had to fast two consecutive months, so he fasted one month and then fell ill. He said: 'God has bound him (with the obligation).' I said: 'A woman who had to fast two consecutive months, so she fasted and then broke her fast during her menstruation days.' He said: 'She makes them up.' I said: 'If she made them up and then despaired of menstruation (i.e., menopause)?' He said: 'She does not repeat them; that suffices for her.' And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Like that (the same ruling).

And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a free man upon whom fasting two consecutive months is obligatory due to Dhahr, so he fasts one month then falls ill; he said: 'He resumes [the fast], and if he exceeds the other month by one or two days, he builds upon what remains [of the required two months].'

And he also narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about breaking the fast of the expiation for an oath, and the expiation for Dhihar, and the expiation for blood [diarrhea/illness]. He said: 'If upon a man is the fasting of two consecutive months, and he breaks his fast or falls ill in the first month, then upon him is to restart the fasting. And if he fasts the first month and fasts some of the second month, then an excuse befalls him, then upon him is only to make up [the missed days].' These narrations are understood to apply when his illness is one that does not prevent him from fasting, although it causes him some difficulty. Thus, whenever the matter is as we mentioned, it becomes obligatory upon him to restart [the two months], according to what these narrations encompass.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who made it upon himself to fast for a month, and he fasted fifteen days of it, then an event occurred. He said: 'If he fasted fifteen days, he may make up what remains of it; and if he fasted less than fifteen days, it is not sufficient for him until he fasts a complete month.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who made it upon himself to fast for a month, and he fasted fifteen days, then an issue arose for him, he was told: 'It is permissible for him to make up what remains of it, and if it is less than fifteen days, it is not permissible for him until he fasts a complete month.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever vowed to fast a specific day and broke his fast without an excuse, expiation becomes obligatory upon him as is obligatory upon one who breaks a day of Ramadan, and he must make it up. 38 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from al-Sayqal: that he wrote to him, 'O my master, a man vowed to fast a day for Allah, and marital relations occurred on that day; what is the expiation upon him?' He answered, 'He fasts one day in place of one day, and freeing a believing slave.' 39 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Mahziyar: that he wrote to him asking, 'O my master, a man vowed to fast a specific day and marital relations occurred on that day; what is the expiation upon him?' He (peace be upon him) wrote to him, 'He fasts one day in place of one day, and freeing a believing slave.' 40 - And it has also been narrated - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Bundar, the freedman of Idris, wrote, 'O my master, I vowed to fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation is obligatory upon me?' He (peace be upon him) wrote, 'And I read it: Do not leave it except for an excuse, and fasting it is not obligatory upon you during travel or illness unless you intended that. And if you broke it without an excuse, then give charity for the count of each day to seven poor people. We ask Allah for success in what He loves and is pleased with.' And this report, we have presented earlier, and there is no contradiction between this narration and the first two, because the expiation is obligatory according to the condition of the one breaking the fast. Whoever is able to free a slave, that is obligatory upon him; and whoever is not able to do that but is able to feed seven poor people, he

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when it was the last ten days, would perform i'tikaf in the mosque, and a tent of hair would be pitched for him, and he would roll up his garment and fold his bed. Some said, 'And he abstained from the women,' so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'As for abstaining from the women, no.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I was in Medina in the month of Ramadan, so I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I intend to perform i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque); what should I say and what obligations should I impose upon myself?' He said: 'Do not leave the mosque except for a necessary need, and do not sit under the shade (of the mosque structure) until you return to your seat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "It is not appropriate for the one in i'tikaf to leave the mosque except for a necessary need, then he does not sit until he returns, and he does not go out for anything except for a funeral or to visit a sick person, and he does not sit until he returns, and the i'tikaf of a woman is like that."

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Uthman from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "The one in i'tikaf does not smell perfume, nor delight in basil (or pleasant scent), nor debate, nor buy, nor sell." He said: "And whoever performs i'tikaf for three days, he is at his choice on the fourth day; if he wishes, he may add other days, and if he wishes, he may exit the mosque. But if he stays for two days after the three, he must not exit the mosque until he completes three other days." Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And there is no i'tikaf except with fasting." (873) 5. That was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no i'tikaf except with fasting."
And Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I'tikaf is not valid except with fasting.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from Al-Abbas ibn Amir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zur'ah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "I'tikaf (spiritual retreat) is not valid except with fasting." The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And there is no I'tikaf for less than three days."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "I'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) is not valid for less than three days, and whoever performs i'tikaf must fast, and it is appropriate for the one performing i'tikaf, when he enters the state of i'tikaf, to make a condition (specify the duration), just as the one who enters the state of Ihram (for Hajj or Umrah) makes a condition."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was absent, and he returned while she was performing i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) with her husband's permission. She exited from the mosque to her house when news of his arrival reached her, and prepared herself for her husband until they had intercourse. He said: 'If she exited from the mosque before three days had passed and she had not stipulated [in her i'tikaf contract] that she would exit upon his arrival, then upon her is what is upon the mudadhah (one who performs kaffarat al-zihar).'.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the servant performs i'tikaf, he should fast." And he said, "I'tikaf is not valid for less than three days. Make a condition upon your Lord in your i'tikaf as you make a condition in your ihram. Indeed, that is in your i'tikaf in case of an incident, if a cause befalls you from the affair of Allah."

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: "If he performs i'tikaf for one day, even if he did not specify a condition, he has the right to exit and break his i'tikaf. And if he stays for two days and did not specify a condition, he does not have the right to exit and break his i'tikaf until three days have passed." Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And i'tikaf is not valid except in the Greatest Mosque.

That was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ahmad ibn Sabih from Ali ibn Imran from Abu Abdillah from his father, upon them be peace, who said: "The one who performs i'tikaf performs it in the congregational mosque."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' al-Razi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘I'tikaf (seclusion in a mosque) is not valid except in a mosque of the congregation.’ The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh al-Tusi) said: And it has been narrated that it is not valid except in a mosque in which a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet has led the prayer. (882) 14 Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated this - from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), ‘What do you say about ‘I'tikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques?’ He said, ‘There is no ‘I'tikaf except in a mosque of the congregation in which a just Imam has led the congregational prayer, and there is no harm in performing ‘I'tikaf in the mosque of Kufa, the mosque of Medina, and the mosque of Mecca.’
And in the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid: [it is] like that, and he added to it: 'the mosque of Basra'.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no I'tikaf (spiritual retreat) except in the last ten days of the month of Ramadan. And he said that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not consider I'tikaf to be valid except in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), or in the Prophet's Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Nabawi), or in a congregational mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Jami'). And it is not appropriate for the one in I'tikaf to leave the mosque except for a necessity that is unavoidable, and then he does not sit [outside] until he returns. And the woman is like that [in this ruling].'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about i'tikaf (spiritual retreat) in Ramadan during the last ten days. He said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say, 'I do not consider i'tikaf except in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Haram), or in the Messenger's Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Nabawi), or in a congregational mosque (Masjid Jami').'' Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever breaks his fast without an excuse while he is in i'tikaf, or has sexual intercourse, the penalty that is obligatory upon one who does that deliberately without an excuse in the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) who had intercourse with his wife, and he said: 'He is in the same position as one who broke his fast for a day during the month of Ramadan.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the person in i'tikaf who has intercourse with his wife, and he said: 'If he does so, he is liable what is upon the one who performs dhaher.'

And from him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) who had intercourse with his wife. He said: 'Upon him is what is upon the one who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people.' If the intercourse was at night during the month of Ramadan, then upon the one who had intercourse is one expiation; and if it was during the day, then upon him are two expiations. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) at night during the month of Ramadan. He said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said: 'And if he had intercourse with her during the day?' He said: 'Upon him are two expiations.' And there is no contradiction between these narrations and the report we presented earlier from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his saying: 'As for avoiding women,' because he (peace be upon him) meant by that their companionship, sitting with them, and conversing with them, excluding intercourse. And what is prohibited for the one in i'tikaf from that is intercourse, excluding other things, according to what we presented earlier. And as for the report that he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: "The one who performs i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether he prays in the mosque or in its houses." This is not contradictory to what we have previously stated, that there is no i'tikaf except in the specific mosques, because what this report entails is the permissibility of prayer outside the mosque, without i'tikaf, and this is not prevented from it, because in the case of necessity, if a person leaves the mosque in Mecca and the time for prayer enters, it is permissible for him to pray in whichever place he wishes. And the ruling for other mosques is not like this: not that it is not permissible for him to pray until he returns to the mosque in which he performed i'tikaf. And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: 'The one who performs i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether he prays in the Mosque or in its houses.' And he said: 'I'tikaf is not valid elsewhere except in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) or in a mosque of the congregation. And the one performing i'tikaf does not pray in a house other than the mosque in which he has performed i'tikaf, except in Mecca, for he performs i'tikaf in Mecca wherever he wishes, because all of it is the Sanctuary of Allah. And the one performing i'tikaf does not leave the mosque except for a need.' His saying (peace be upon him): 'for he performs i'tikaf in Mecca wherever he wishes' — he means by it that he prays the prayer of i'tikaf. Do you not see that he began by explaining the prayer of the one performing i'tikaf, saying: 'And the one performing i'tikaf does not pray in a house other than the mosque in which he has performed i'tikaf, except in Mecca, for he performs i'tikaf in Mecca wherever he wishes'? If the meaning were not what we mentioned, it would not be appropriate to except it from the ruling of prayer, and the second statement would not be connected to the first. The estimation of the statement is as we said: 'And the one performing i'tikaf does not pray in a house other than the mosque in which he has performed i'tikaf, except in Mecca, for he prays in a house other than the mosque in which he has performed i'tikaf in it.' And by this it is distinguished from other places.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one performing i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in whichever of its houses he wishes, and the one performing i'tikaf elsewhere does not pray except in the mosque that he has specified.

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abu Jamilah from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the person in i'tikaf falls ill or the female person in i'tikaf experiences menstruation, he/she returns to his/her house, then returns (to the mosque) when healed, and fasts." "There is no obligation on the sick person to do that (return to the house)."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah from al-Zuhri from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) said: One day he said, "O Zuhri, from where have you come?" I said, "From the mosque." He said, "What were you discussing?" I said, "We were discussing the matter of fasting, and my opinion and the opinion of my companions converged that there is no obligatory fasting except the fasting of the month of Ramadan." He said, "O Zuhri, it is not as you said. Fasting is of forty types: ten of them are obligatory like the obligation of the month of Ramadan; ten of them, their fasting is forbidden; fourteen of them, the owner has the choice: if he wishes he fasts and if he wishes he breaks the fast. And fasting of permission is of three types, and fasting of discipline, and fasting of permission (to break), and fasting of travel and illness." I said, "May I be your ransom, so explain them to me." He said, "As for the obligatory: fasting of the month of Ramadan and two consecutive months in the expiation of Dhihar, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And those who disavow their wives and then return to what they said, then a freeing of a slave before they touch each other. That is what you are admonished with, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do. So whoever does not find [a slave], then two consecutive months' fasting...'" So whoever does not find [a slave], then two consecutive months' fasting And fasting of two consecutive months for one who breaks a day of Ramadan, and fasting of two consecutive months in accidental killing for one who does not find the freedom of a slave is obligatory, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment presented to the deceased's family...' until His saying: 'So whoever does not find [a slave], then two consecutive months' fasting, a repentance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.' So whoever does not find [a slave], then two consecutive months' fasting, a repentance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Wise And fasting of three days in the expiation of an oath is obligatory. Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said: 'Then the expiation for your oaths is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which yo

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who killed another man accidentally during the sacred month. He said: 'The punishment is intensified upon him, and he must free a slave or fast for two consecutive months from the sacred months.' I said: 'Does this include something?' He said: 'What is it?' I said: 'The day of Eid and the days of Tashriq.' He said: 'He fasts, for it is an obligation that has become incumbent upon him.' So it is not contradictory to what the first report contained regarding the prohibition of fasting on the two Eids, because the prohibition applies only to one who fasts them voluntarily and initially. But if two consecutive months become incumbent upon him according to what the report contained, then fasting these days becomes incumbent upon him because he included himself in that obligation. As for fasting the days of Tashriq specifically, it has been narrated that the prohibition in them is restricted to one who is in Mina. But as for one who is in other towns, there is no harm in him fasting them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about fasting the days of Tashriq, so he said, 'As for the provinces (outside Mina), there is no harm, but as for Mina, there is (harm/it is not permissible).' And as for the fasting of continuous fasting (Sawm al-Visal), it is when one makes his evening meal his morning meal (eating dinner and skipping the pre-dawn meal, continuing until the next dinner), so that is prohibited. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one who narrated it from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Al-wisal (continuous fasting) in fasting is when he makes his evening meal his pre-dawn meal."

And that which was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from them (peace be upon them) who said: "When you break your fast from Ramadan, do not fast voluntarily after the breaking of fast except after three days have passed." The meaning in it is that there is not in the fasting of these days the virtue and blessing thereof as there is in other days, although fasting them is permissible according to what the report contained of choice. As for the fasting of the Day of Arafah, encouragement has come regarding it according to what the report contained, and dislike has also come regarding it. As for what came regarding encouragement, it is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Abu Hammam from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Fasting the Day of Arafah is equivalent to a year [of fasting], and he said: Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did not fast it, and Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) fasted it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Sulayman al-Ja'fari said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) would fast on the Day of 'Arafah during the hot day at the Station (of 'Arafah), and he would order a high shade to be pitched for him, so he would perform ritual bath (ghusl) from the heat that reached him.' And as for his dislike (of fasting in intense heat without shade), that has been narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast on the Day of Arafah since the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed.'

And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the fasting of the Day of 'Arafah, and I said, 'May I be your ransom, they claim that it equals the fasting of a year.' He said, 'My father (peace be upon him) did not fast it.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Indeed, the Day of 'Arafah is a day of supplication and asking (of needs), and I fear that it will weaken me from supplication, and I dislike that I fast it, and I fear that 'Arafah might be the Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), so it is not a day of fasting.' Thus, the way to reconcile between these narrations is that whoever is strong enough to fast this day without it preventing him from supplication, then it is recommended for him to fast this day. And whoever fears weakness and what prevents him from supplication and asking, then it is preferable for him to leave fasting it. And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about fasting the Day of 'Arafah. He said: 'Whoever is strong enough for it, it is good, provided it does not prevent you from supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking [of God]. So fast it, but if you fear that you will become weak in doing so, then do not fast it.' As for fasting the Day of 'Ashura, encouragement for fasting it has come, and dislike [for it] has also come. As for what was narrated regarding encouragement for fasting it, it has been narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah from his father, peace be upon them, that Ali (peace be upon him) said: "Fast on Ashura - the ninth and the tenth, for it expiates the sins of a year."
And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abu Hammam, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted on the day of Ashura.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: "Fasting the Day of 'Ashura is an expiation for a year."

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar from Kathir al-Nawwa' from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The ship was anchored - on the Day of Ashura - on al-Judi, so Noah (peace be upon him) ordered those with him from the jinn and humans to fast that day. And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what this day is? This is the day on which Allah, Exalted and Majestic, accepted repentance from Adam and Hawwa (peace be upon her); and this is the day on which Allah split the sea for the Children of Israel, so He drowned Pharaoh and those with him; and this is the day on which Musa (peace be upon him) conquered Pharaoh; and this is the day on which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born; and this is the day on which Allah accepted repentance from the people of Yunus (peace be upon him); and this is the day on which Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) was born; and this is the day on which the Qa'im (peace be upon him) will rise.' As for what has been narrated regarding the dislike of fasting on it, it has been narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) who said: "Do not fast on the day of Ashura, nor on the day of Arafah in Mecca, nor in Medina, nor in your homeland, nor in any of the provinces."

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, who said: My brother Ja'far ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the day of Ashura and what people say about it, so he said: 'Regarding the fasting of Ibn Marjanah (may Allah curse him), you ask me about that. It is a day that only the pretenders from the family of Ziyad, due to the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), fasted. It is a day that the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) considered ill-omened, and the people of Islam considered ill-omened. The day that Islam and its people considered ill-omened is not fasted, nor is blessing sought from it. And Monday is a day of ill-omen; Allah took His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on it. And the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) were afflicted only on Monday, so we considered it ill-omened, and our enemies considered it blessed. And on the day of Ashura, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, and Ibn Marjanah considered it blessed, and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) considered it ill-omened. So whoever fasts them and considers them blessed, he will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a wiped (blessed) heart, and his gathering place will be with those who established the fasting of them and considered them blessed.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted until it was said, "He does not break his fast," then he broke his fast until it was said, "He does not fast," then he fasted the fast of David (peace be upon him): one day and one night [or one day and one night he does not fast], then he was taken (died) upon fasting three days of the month, and he said: "They equal the fast of the whole year and they remove the heat of the chest."' Hammad said: I said, 'What is al-wahar?' He said: 'Al-wahar is the whispering (of the soul/desire).' Hammad said: I said, 'Which days are they?' He said: 'The first Thursday of the month, and the first Wednesday after the tenth, and the last Thursday of it.' I said, 'Why did these days become the days that are fasted?' He said: 'Indeed, those before us from the nations, when punishment descended upon one of them, it descended on these fearful days.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about fasting in the month, how is it? He said: 'Three [days] in the month, in each ten-day period one day, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says: "Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten like it." And three days in the month are the fasting of a lifetime.' This fasting is voluntary (nafl) and supererogatory (tatawwu'), so how is its ordering? And that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Madaini from Ibrahim ibn Ismail ibn Dawud, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about fasting, and he said: 'Three days in the month: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.' I said: 'Indeed, our companions fast on Wednesday between two Thursdays.' He said: 'There is no harm in that, and there is no harm in fasting on Thursday between two Wednesdays.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from some of our companions from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as 'a mercy to the worlds' on the 27th of Rajab; so whoever fasts that day, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, records for him the fasting of sixty months. And on the 25th of Dhi al-Qa'dah, Allah established the House (Kaaba), which is the first mercy established upon the face of the earth; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made it 'a place of return for the people and a sanctuary'; so whoever fasts that day, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months. And on the first day of Dhi al-Hijjah, Ibrahim (Abraham), the friend of the Merciful, was born; so whoever fasts that day, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months.

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Hamdan ibn al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Sayqal, who said: Abu al-Hasan, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), came out to us in Marw on the twenty-fifth of Dhu al-Qadah and said, 'Fast, for I have become a fasting person in the morning.' We said, 'May Allah be our ransom, which day is it?' He said, 'It is a day in which mercy was spread, the earth was spread out, the Ka'ba was erected, and Adam (peace be upon him) descended to it.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, do the Muslims have an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said, 'Yes, O Hasan, the greatest and most noble of them.' I said, 'And which day is it?' He said, 'It is the day when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) raised a standard for the people.' So I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is appropriate for us to do on it?' He said, 'Fast it, O Hasan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family on it, and declare your disassociation to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from those who wronged them.' And indeed, the Prophets (peace be upon them) used to command the Successors regarding the day on which the Successor is established, that it be taken as an Eid.' I said, 'So what is the reward for the one who fasts it?' He said, 'The fasting of sixty months.' And do not neglect the fasting of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day on which Prophethood descended upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like that of sixty months for you.'

Abu Abdillah ibn 'Ayash said: Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tustari told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Layth al-Makki told us, saying: Abu Ishaq ibn Abdillah al-Alawi al-Uraydi told me, saying: And the question of 'which are the days that are fasted?' was rubbed into my chest (became clear in my mind), so I headed to our Master, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), while he was in Sarba, and I did not reveal that to anyone of God's creation. So I entered upon him, and when he saw me, he said (peace be upon him): 'O Abu Ishaq, you have come to ask me about the days that are fasted, and they are four: the first is the day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab - the day God Almighty sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to His creation as 'A mercy to the worlds', and the day of his birth (peace be upon him and his family), which is the seventeenth of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal. And the day of the twenty-fifth of Dhi al-Qa'dah, on which the Ka'bah was demolished. And the day of al-Ghadir, on which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established his brother Ali (peace be upon him) as a sign for the people and an Imam after him.' I said: 'You have spoken truly, I am your ransom; for that reason I headed [to you], I bear witness that you are God's proof against His creation.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman said: He told us that Kathir, the seller of pistachios, said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Noah heard the creaking of the ship on Al-Judi, so he feared for it, and he put his head out from the side of the ship, raised his hand, and pointed with his finger while saying: 'Rahman, Atqin,' and its interpretation is: 'O Lord, Do good.' And indeed Noah (peace be upon him), when he boarded the ship, boarded it on the first day of Rajab, so he commanded those with him from the jinn and humans to fast that day. He said: Whoever among you fasts it, the Fire will be distant from him by a year's journey. And whoever fasts seven days from it, the seven gates of the Fire will be closed to him. And whoever fasts eight days from it, the eight gates of the Gardens will be opened for him. And whoever fasts ten days from it, his request will be granted. And whoever fasts twenty-five days from it, it will be said to him: Resume the work, for you have been forgiven. And whoever adds more, Allah will add more for him.

And it is narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said: "Rajab is a river in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever fasts one day from Rajab, Allah will give him to drink from that river."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd al-Ajli and al-Fudayl from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them): In the sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep is due, and there is nothing due for less than forty. Then there is nothing due until it reaches two hundred and ten; when it reaches two hundred and ten, one sheep is due. If it exceeds two hundred and ten, two sheep are due, and there is nothing more than two sheep until it reaches two hundred. When it reaches two hundred, the same applies. If it exceeds two hundred, one sheep is due, so three sheep are due. Then there is nothing more than that until it reaches three hundred. When it reaches three hundred, three sheep are due. If one is added, four sheep are due, until it reaches four hundred. When four hundred are complete, for every hundred one sheep is due, and the previous rule is dropped, and there is nothing due for less than a hundred after that, and there is nothing due for the 'niyyf' (the extra sheep beyond the hundred). And they (Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah) said: "Whatever does not have the year pass over it while in possession, there is no khums/zakat due on it; when the year passes over it, it becomes due."

Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no zakat in less than forty sheep. When there are forty, one sheep is due until twenty and one hundred. If one is added, two sheep are due until two hundred. If one is added, three sheep are due from the sheep until three hundred. When the sheep increase, one sheep is due for every hundred. An old female is not taken, nor one with a defect, unless the collector wishes. He does not separate a group that is together, nor combine scattered animals, and he counts its young and its adults." His saying (peace be upon him): 'and he counts its young and its adults' means those that have passed one year, because that may be considered young in relation to those older than it. And he (peace be upon him) did not mean the very young sheep in which the year has not yet passed, according to what we have mentioned earlier, and we will clarify it later, God willing.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fasting in the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan consecutively is an expiation (or forgiveness) from Allah.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast in Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan, and connect them [fasting], and he commanded the people not to connect them [fasting]. And he used to say, 'They are the month of Allah, and they are expiation for what is before them and what is after them.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from his father who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say about a man who fasts in Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan? He said: "They are the two months about which Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Two consecutive months, as repentance from Allah'". He said: I said: Then should he not separate between them? He said: "If he breaks the fast during the night, that is a separation. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No continuous fasting (wisal) in fasting,' meaning a man should not fast two consecutive days without breaking the fast. And it is recommended for the servant not to leave the pre-dawn meal (suhur)."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Mukharrq and Abu Junadah al-Saluli, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts in the month of Sha'ban, he will have a purification from every slip, stain, and hastening." Abu Hamzah said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the 'stain' (wasmah)? He said: "The oath taken in disobedience [to God], and there is no vow in disobedience." I said: What is the 'hastening' (badirah)? He said: "The oath taken in anger, and repentance from it is at the time of regret."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn Uthman and Sindi ibn Muhammad, all of them, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about fasting in the month of Sha'ban, and I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, was one of your forefathers (peace be upon them) fasting in Sha'ban?' He said, 'The best of my forefathers is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and most of his fasting was in Sha'ban.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Did any of your ancestors fast in the month of Sha'ban?' He said, 'The best of my ancestors - the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) - fasted it.'

And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Did any of your forefathers ever fast in the month of Sha'ban?' He said: 'The best of my forefathers, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), fasted it.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would delay any missed fasting until the month of Sha'ban, out of reluctance to prevent the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from their needs. So when it became Sha'ban, they would fast, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would say, 'Sha'ban is my month.'
