As for the narrations that came regarding the prohibition of fasting in Sha'ban and that no one among the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it, the meaning is that no one among the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it on the basis that its fasting runs the course of the month of Ramadan in terms of obligation and necessity, because a group said that fasting it is obligatory, and Abu al-Khattab (may Allah curse him) and his companions went to this view and said that whoever breaks a day of it incurs the same expiation as one who breaks a day of Ramadan. So the rejection of this came from them (peace be upon them), and that no one among them fasted it in this manner. And the narrations that included the distinction between the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan, the meaning is the prohibition of al-wisal (continuous fasting without breaking), which we explained previously as being prohibited. And the news we previously cited from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), indicates this interpretation, when he said: I said to him, 'Does he not distinguish between them?' He said, 'If he breaks his fast at night, that is a distinction. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only said, "There is no wisal in fasting."' He means that the man does not fast two consecutive days without breaking his fast. And it is recommended for the man not to leave the suhur (pre-dawn meal).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him regarding the wealth of an orphan, is Zakat due upon it? He said: 'If it is kept (idle), there is no Zakat upon it. But if you invest it, you are the guarantor (liable for loss) and the profit belongs to the orphan.'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (the two Imams), upon them be peace, who said: I asked him about the wealth of the orphan, and he said, 'There is no zakat in it.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no zakat in the wealth of an orphan."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Abu al-Hasan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father differed with the people regarding the wealth of the orphan; there is no zakat upon it.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ahmad ibn 'Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about the wealth of an orphan, so he said: 'There is no zakat upon it unless it is traded with.' As for the saying of the Sheikh (Al-Shaykh al-Tusi), may God have mercy on him: whenever it is traded with, zakat becomes obligatory upon it. He means by it recommendation and preference, rather than obligation and compulsion, because there is no difference between it being traded with or not being traded with regarding the fact that zakat does not become obligatory upon it with the obligation of compulsion, by which leaving it incurs punishment. Do you not see that if this wealth belonged to a mature adult and he traded with it, zakat would not become obligatory upon it with the obligation of compulsion, as we will clarify later, if God Almighty wills. And that which indicates that zakat becomes obligatory upon it with this type of obligation when it is traded with is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Sa'id al-Assani who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no zakat in the wealth of an orphan unless it is traded with; if it is traded with, then the profit is for the orphan, and if it is kept (not traded), then the one who trades with it bears the cost.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I sent a message to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I have young children, so when does zakat become obligatory upon their wealth?' He said: 'When prayer becomes obligatory upon them, zakat becomes obligatory upon them.' I said: 'And what about those upon whom prayer has not yet become obligatory?' He said: 'When they are traded with (i.e., their wealth is used in commerce), then pay their zakat.'

Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about young children who have wealth in the possession of their father or their brother, whether zakat is obligatory upon their wealth. He said: 'Zakat is not obligatory upon their wealth until it is put to use (invested/grown). When it is put to use, zakat becomes obligatory. As for that which is held in reserve (not yet invested), there is no zakat upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-'Atarid al-Hannat, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The wealth of an orphan is with me, so I trade with it.' He said: 'When you activate it, zakat is upon you.' I said: 'I activate it for eight months and leave it for four months.' He said: 'Zakat is upon you.' His saying (peace be upon him) 'When you activate it, zakat is upon you' means that it is upon you to take charge of paying its zakat, without that being obligatory upon the wealth itself, because when he trades with the wealth he guarantees it, and when he guarantees it, the payment of zakat from his wealth is not obligatory along with that, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār from Samā'ah ibn Mihrān from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: If a man has the wealth of an orphan and trades with it, is he liable for its guarantee (compensation for loss)? He said: 'Yes.' I asked: And is there zakat upon it? He said: 'No, by my life, I do not combine upon him two qualities: the guarantee and the zakat.' As for the guarantee of the wealth, it remains obligatory upon the one trading with it in all circumstances, unless he intends it as a favor for the orphan and care for the preservation of his wealth, for then the guarantee is not obligatory upon him. That is indicated by what has been narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabii, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who has money in his hand for his orphan brother, and he is his executor/will-trustee. Is it suitable for him to trade with it? He said: 'Yes, he trades with it as he trades with the money of others, and the profit is shared between them.' I said: 'Is there guarantee/liability on him?' He said: 'No, if he is managing it (for the benefit of the orphan).' As for the profit, it belongs to the orphan whenever the manager transacts with it, and the manager does not currently have enough to cover that money. So when the matter is as we mentioned, he is liable for the capital, the profit belongs to the orphan, and the zakat is on the orphan's money, and it is the responsibility of the guardian to pay it from it, provided he did not intend by the trade merely to manage it for the orphan. This is the category we mentioned earlier and for which we have narrated many reports. And whenever his intention is to manage it for the orphan, it is permissible for him to take from the profit an amount that serves as his livelihood (sufficiency). This is the meaning of the preceding report: 'the profit is shared between them.' And whenever the trader with the orphan's money is capable (of having his own money) in the current state, then liability is upon him, the profit belongs to him, and the zakat is upon him. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Aban ibn Uthman from Mansur al-Sayqal said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the wealth of an orphan that is put to work (invested). He said, 'If you have wealth and you guarantee it, the profit is yours and you are liable for the capital. And if you have no wealth and you work with it, the profit is for the orphan and you are liable for the capital.' As for that which indicates that zakat is obligatory on their yields, it is what he narrated:

Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), that they said: The capital of the orphan's wealth has no zakat due upon it in the principal (al-'ayn) and the silent/accumulated portion (al-samit); as for the profits/gains (al-ghallat), then upon them is obligatory charity (zakat).

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: I heard him say: 'There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan, and no salat upon him, and there is no zakat upon all his produce from palm trees or crops or any produce, even if it increases; he is not liable for zakat for what has passed, nor for what is to come, until he reaches maturity. When he reaches maturity, one zakat becomes due upon him, and he is like the rest of the people.' This is not contradictory to the first narration, because he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no zakat upon all his produce,' and we do not say that there is zakat upon all his produce; rather, it is obligatory upon the four types, which are dates, raisins, wheat, and barley. The orphans were singled out with this ruling because others are recommended to pay zakat from other grains, but this is not the case for the wealth of orphans; therefore, they were singled out in the mention. Saad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl al-Basri said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about the executor who pays the zakat of fitrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth, and he wrote: 'There is no zakat upon the wealth of the orphan.' As for that which indicates that the insane are included with them in this ruling, it is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman from our family has mixed [wealth] upon which zakat is due. He said: 'If it was worked with [i.e., used in trade/business], then zakat is upon her; and if it was not worked with, then no [zakat is due].'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who is incapacitated (or a minor/mentally incompetent), and she has wealth in the hand of her brother. Is there zakat upon her? He said: 'If her brother trades with it, then there is zakat upon her.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers, from their father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from whomsoever he narrated, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man whose wealth is absent from him and he is unable to retrieve it, he said: 'There is no Zakat upon him until it comes out; when it comes out, he pays Zakat for one year. And if he deliberately leaves it while he is able to retrieve it, then Zakat is upon him for every year that has passed.'

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no Zakat on the debt, nor on the wealth that is absent from you, until it comes into your possession."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man whose wealth is absent for five years, then he comes to it and the principal wealth is not returned to him; how much should he pay zakat on it? He said: 'One year.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And there is no zakat on debt unless its delay is from the side of the owner himself. That to which this points is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'There is no zakat in debt,' and he said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no khums (or zakat) on debt, unless the owner of the debt is the one who delays it; so if he is unable to collect it, there is no obligation upon him until he takes possession of it.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Maysarah, from Abd al-Aziz, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to him; does he pay zakat on it? He said: 'For every debt that he leaves behind, when he intends to collect it, zakat is obligatory upon him. And whatever he is unable to collect, there is no zakat upon him.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And there is no zakat on the lender, and on the borrower, his zakat is obligatory as long as it is in his hand. When it returns to its owner and the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory upon him. What indicates this is what he narrated:'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who borrowed money, and the year passed while it was in his possession, he said: 'If the one who lent it to him pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him; and if he does not pay, the borrower pays.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who lends money to another man for one year, or two years, or three years, or whatever God wills. Is the zakat on the lender or the borrower? He said: 'On the borrower, because he derives benefit from it, so the zakat is upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man gave another man money as a loan; upon whom is its zakat, on the lender or on the borrower? He said: 'No, rather its zakat is upon the borrower if it remains with him for a full year.' I said: So there is no zakat for the lender? He said: 'No, the money is not purified from two sources in one year, and there is no zakat upon the one who gave it because there is nothing in his hand, for the money is in the hand of the other; so whoever has the money in his hand, he purifies it.' I said: Does he purify the money of another from his own money? He said: 'Indeed, it is his money as long as it is in his hand, and that money is not for anyone else.' Then he said: 'O Zurarah, do you see the depreciation of that money and its profit; for whom is it and upon whom is it?' I said: 'For the borrower.' He said: 'So the benefit is his and the loss is upon him, and he may wear from it, marry from it, and eat from it, and it is not fitting for him not to purify it, but rather he should purify it, for it is upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah said: I said to Hisham ibn Aḥmar: I would like you to ask Aba al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) whether for people who have loans with me that do not demand them from me, is there zakah upon me? He said: 'Do not pay off (the debt) and do not pay zakah, pay zakah.' As for that which indicates that when the money returns to its owner, zakah is not obligatory upon him until a full year has passed, is what he narrated:

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Is there zakat on a debt owed to someone?' He said, 'No, until he collects it.' I said, 'And when he collects it, does he pay zakat on it?' He said, 'No, until a full year passes while it is in his possession.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man has a deposit (trust) and a debt, and he cannot reach/access them, then he takes them. When does the obligation of zakat fall upon him? He said: 'When he takes them, and then a full year passes over him, he pays zakat.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ahmad Amr ibn Hurayth al-Sayrafi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'From where should I begin the Talbiyah for Hajj?' He said, 'If you wish, from your place of residence (rahlah), and if you wish, from the Ka'bah, and if you wish, from the road.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'From which mosque do I enter the state of Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah?' He said, 'From whichever mosque you wish.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, he should trim his moustache, clip his nails, and perform Ghusl.' He narrated this until the end of the chapter.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When it is the Day of Tarwiah, if God wills, perform ghusl, then wear your two garments (ihram), and enter the mosque barefoot, with calmness and dignity upon you. Then pray two rak'ahs near the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him) or in the Hijr, then sit until the sun declines. Then pray the obligatory prayer. Then say in the aftermath of your prayer as you said when you entered the state of ihram from al-Shajara: 'I enter the state of ihram for Hajj.' Then proceed, with calmness and dignity upon you. And when you reach al-Raqta' before al-Radm, say 'Labbayk'. And when you reach al-Radm and look out over al-Abtah, raise your voice with the Talbiyah until you arrive at Mina."

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Sulayman ibn Muhammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'When do I respond with the Talbiyah for Hajj?' He said, 'When you go out to Mina.' Then he said, 'When you place Shu'b al-Dubb on your right and al-'Aqabah on your left, then respond with the Talbiyah for Hajj.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Salt from Zur'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend to enter the state of Ihram on the Day of Tashriq (Day of Tarwiyah), do as you did when you intended to enter Ihram initially: trim your mustache, cut your nails, remove hair from your pubic area if you have hair there, pluck your armpits, perform Ghusl (ritual bath), and put on your Ihram garments. Then go to Al-Masjid Al-Haram and pray six Rak'at before entering Ihram, supplicating to Allah and asking for His help, saying: 'O Allah, I intend to perform Hajj, so facilitate it for me and release me from where You have bound me by Your decree that You have decreed upon me.' And say: 'My hair, skin, flesh, and blood are in Ihram for You, as are my women, garments, and perfume; I intend thereby Your Countenance and the Abode of the Hereafter, and release me from where You have bound me by Your decree that You have decreed upon me.' Then respond to the Call (Talbiyah) from Al-Masjid Al-Haram as you responded when you first entered Ihram, saying: 'Here I am, O Allah, with a Hajj whose completion and attainment are upon You.' If you are able, your departure to Mina should be at the time of the sun's decline (Zawal); otherwise, whenever it is convenient for you from the Day of Tarwiyah.

And as for what was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Ayub ibn al-Harr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'We have plucked (hair), trimmed, and cut our nails in Medina, so what should we do regarding Hajj?' He said, 'Do not pluck, do not trim, and do not move anything.' This is applicable to one whose Hajj is Mufrad, not to one who is Mutamatti', because the Mufrad is not permitted to do any of that until he finishes his rituals on the Day of Sacrifice, and the report does not state that we did that while we were Mutamatti'un, not Mufradun. And as for what the report of Abu Basir included regarding mentioning the Talbiyah after the prayer, it is not contradictory to the narration of Muawiya ibn 'Ammar that he should say Talbiyah when he reaches al-Raqta'. Because the walker says Talbiyah from the place where he prays, and the rider says it at al-Raqta' or at Sha'b al-Dubb, and neither of them recites it aloud except when overlooking al-Abtah. This was narrated.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, do as you did with the tree, then pray two rak'ahs behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham), then announce the Ihram for Hajj. If you are walking, announce the Talbiyah at the Maqam; and if you are riding, [announce it] when your camel stands up for you. And pray the Dhuhr prayer if you are able in Mina. And know that it is permissible for you to enter the state of Ihram after every obligatory prayer, or after every voluntary prayer, or at night, or during the day." And whoever makes a mistake and enters the state of Ihram for 'Umrah while intending Hajj, he should proceed with the Hajj, and there is no penalty upon him.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I asked my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who entered [Mecca] before Tarwiyah by a day and intended to enter the state of Ihram for Hajj, but made a mistake and said 'Umrah. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, let him renew the Ihram for Hajj.' And it is not permissible for one who has entered Ihram for Hajj to perform Tawaf of the House as a voluntary act until he returns from Mina. If he did that out of forgetfulness, there is no penalty upon him. Narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked him about a man who comes to al-Masjid al-Haram and has resolved to perform Hajj, and he performs Tawaf around the House. He said: 'Yes, as long as he has not entered into Ihram.'

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who entered into the state of Ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah from near the Maqam (Station of Abraham), then performed Tawaf around the House after entering Ihram, and he did not consider that this to be improper. I asked: Does his Tawaf around the House break his Ihram? He said: 'No, but he continues in his Ihram.' And for the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), his Umrah is complete as long as he catches the two stations (Arafah and Muzdalifah). It makes no difference whether this is on the Day of Tarwiyah, or the Night of Arafah, or the Day of Arafah until after the sun has passed its zenith. When the sun passes its zenith on the Day of Arafah, the Mut'ah is missed because he will not be able to join the people at Arafah. The situation remains as described, except that people's ranks differ in virtue and reward. Whoever catches the Day of Tarwiyah at the time of the sun's zenith will have greater reward and a more complete Mut'ah than one who joins on the night. And whoever joins on the night will have less reward than that, but more than one who joins on the Day of Arafah after the sun's zenith. And the narrations that have come stating that whoever does not catch the Day of Tarwiyah has missed the Mut'ah, the meaning is the loss of the perfection which he hopes for by joining on the Day of Tarwiyah. And what they included from their saying (peace be upon them): 'And let him make it an individual Hajj,' means that the person has the choice in this matter between continuing with the Mut'ah and making it an individual Hajj, provided he does not fear missing the two stations, and his Hajj is not the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory one) in which individual Hajj is not permissible when capable, as we have previously stated. And the obligation and necessity of making it an individual Hajj applies only to one who is convinced that if he engages in Tawaf, Sa'i, and Ihlal (exiting Ihram), then re-entering Ihram for Hajj, he will miss the two stations. And however we interpret these narrations according to what we mentioned, we have not rejected any of them.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') performs Tawaf with the House and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah as long as the people are in Mina.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Tamattu' (pilgrims' enjoyment), when does it occur? He said: He performs the Tamattu' as long as he expects that he will reach the people in Mina.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Murzam ibn Hakim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The Mu'tammir (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') enters Mecca on the night of Arafah, and the menstruating woman; when does the 'Umrah of Tamattu' become due for them both? He said: 'When the people reach Mina.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb al-Athmi said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no harm for the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') if he does not enter the state of Ihram from the night of Tarwiyah, whenever it is convenient for him, as long as he does not fear missing the two standings (of Arafat and Muzdalifah).'

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: «The Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') has his 'Umrah valid until the setting of the sun on the Day of 'Arafah, and his Hajj valid until the setting of the sun on the Day of Naḥr (10th of Dhul-Hijjah).» And from him ('Abdullah ibn Ja'far) from Muhammad ibn Sarw who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him): What do you say about a man who performs Tamattu' with 'Umrah until Hajj, who arrived on the morning of 'Arafah, and the people left Minah for 'Arafat? Is his 'Umrah still valid, or has it lapsed? At what time does his 'Umrah remain valid if he is performing Tamattu'? He did not arrive on the Day of Tarwiyah nor the Night of Tarwiyah. What should he do? He (peace be upon him) replied: «When he enters Mecca, if God wills, he shall perform Tawaf, pray two Rak'ahs, perform Sa'i, shorten (his hair), and exit with his Hajj, and proceed to the Standing (at 'Arafah) and surge forth with the Imam.»

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Muram and Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the man performing Tamattu' Hajj, who enters [Mecca] on the night of Arafah, performs Tawaf and Sa'i, then releases from Ihram, then re-enters Ihram, and goes to Mina, he said: 'There is no harm.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Maymun, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) arrived in a state of Tamattu' — on the night of 'Arafah he performed Tawaf, then released himself from Ihram, and visited some of his female slaves, then he entered Ihram for Hajj and departed.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hasan from 'Ula' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Until when does the pilgrim have the Umrah?' He said, 'Until the dawn of the Night of Arafah.'

And from him, from Safwan, from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mu'tamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who arrives in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah; if the Asr prayer is missed before he enters the state of Ihram for the 'Umrah, does he lose the 'Umrah? He said: 'He has [the right to perform it] for what is between him and the sunset of the sun.' And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had done that.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who enters Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, so he said: 'For the Mutamatti' is [the time] between it and the night.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When you arrive in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah while you are in the state of Tamattu', you have the time between your arrival and the night to perform Tawaf around the House and Sa'i, and to make that (Tawaf and Sa'i) your Umrah (for Tamattu')."

And from him, from Hassan, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Until when is the 'Umrah valid for the pilgrim?' He said, and he said: 'Until the dawn (subah) of the Night of 'Arafah.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim said, and the trustworthy one (1) from the Ahl al-Bayt narrated to us from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said: "Intend the Tamattu' Hajj with the Talbiyah from the Day of Tarwiyah until the decline of the sun, and after Asr, and after Maghrib, and after 'Isha; the time between all of these is broad (permissible)." As for what has been narrated regarding the missing of that (time), it has been narrated.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Zakariyya ibn Adam said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) when he enters [the state of Ihram] on the Day of Arafah. He said: 'There is no Tamattu' for him; he makes it a separate Umrah.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Mutamatti' (pilgrim who performs Umrah then Hajj) if he arrives on the night of Arafah, there is no 'Umrah for him that he makes a separate Hajj; rather, the 'Umrah is only until the Day of Tarwiyah.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Musa ibn Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') who arrives in Mecca on the night of Arafah. He said: 'He has no Tamattu' (benefit); he makes it a single Hajj, and he performs Tawaf around the House, and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and he goes out to Mina, and there is no Hadi (sacrificial animal) upon him. Indeed, the Hadi is only upon the Mutamatti'.'

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man and woman who perform Tamattu' (Umrah followed by Hajj) and then enter Mecca on the Day of Arafah; what should they do? He said: 'They make it a single Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad), and the limit of Tamattu' is until the Day of Tarwiyah.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthayfir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When you arrive in Mecca - on the Day of Tarwiyah and the sun has set - and you do not have a Tamattu' [Hajj], proceed with your Hajj as it is [as Qiran or Ifrad]." The correct interpretation of these narrations is what we mentioned: that whoever fears missing the two standings [of Arafat and Muzdalifah] if he engages in Ihlal [staying in the state of Ihram without exiting to Tamattu'], he should proceed in his Ihram and make it a singular Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad). And whoever does not fear missing that, or is confident that he will reach both standings, then he should exit Ihram [for Umrah] and then enter Ihram for Hajj, according to what we have previously established. And that which indicates this meaning is what he narrated:

Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into ihram for Hajj and Umrah together, then arrived in Mecca while the people were at Arafat. He feared that if he performed Tawaf and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, he would miss the standing (at Arafat). He said: 'He should leave the Umrah, and when he completes his Hajj, he should do as Aisha did, and there is no sacrifice (Hady) upon him.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who is on the Day of Arafah, and between him and Mecca are three miles, and he is performing Tamattu' (Umrah to Hajj). He said: He cuts off the Talbiyah of Tamattu' and invokes Allah for Hajj with the Talbiyah when he prays Fajr, and proceeds to Arafat, so he stands with the people, and completes all the rituals, and stays in Mecca until he performs Umrah al-Muhrim, and there is nothing upon him. Do you not see that he directed the address in the first report to one who feared missing the standing (at Arafah), and in the second report to one who is between him and Mecca three miles? And it is known that one in this situation cannot enter Mecca and engage in Ihlal (changing from Ihram to Umrah) and Ihram (re-entering Ihram for Hajj) while catching up with the people at Arafah. And whenever he cannot do that, his obligation is to continue in his current Ihram and make it a Hajj, according to what we mentioned. And whoever forgets the Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah with Hajj until he arrives at Arafah, let him remember there what he says at the time of Ihram. If he does not remember until he returns to his country, then his Hajj is complete and there is nothing upon him. Narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki ibn Ali al-Khorasani, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about a man who forgot to enter into the state of Ihram for Hajj, and then remembered it while he was at Arafat. What is his status? He said: 'He says: O Allah, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, so his Ihram is complete.' If he was unaware of how to enter Ihram—from the Day of Tarwiyah for Hajj until he returned to his country—and he performed all its rituals, then his Hajj is complete.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Do the people go out to Mina in the early morning?' He said, 'Yes, until sunset.' Because this report is to be understood in light of what we mentioned regarding those with excuses, such as the sick and others, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who is an old elder or a sick person who fears the crowding and pressing of people; he enters the state of Ihram for Hajj and departs to Mina before the Day of Tarwiyah. He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So does a healthy man depart seeking a place or taking it easy with that?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Does he hasten by one day?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By two days?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By three?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'More than that?' He said: 'No.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah from al-Ala' ibn Razeen from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them) said: «It is not appropriate for the Imam to pray Dhuhr on the Day of Tarwiyah except in Mina, and he should spend the night there until sunrise.».

And from him, from Safwan and Fadala ibn Ayyub and Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "It is appropriate for the Imam to pray Dhuhr in Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah, stay overnight there, and depart in the morning until the sun rises, then he departs."

And from him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The Imam must pray the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Tarwiyah at Masjid al-Khayf, and pray the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Nafar in Masjid al-Haram."

And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray Dhuhr in Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah? He said: 'Yes, and the morning prayer in Mina on the Day of Arafah.' And when a person intends to head to Mina, let him supplicate with the supplication that was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you head towards Mina, say: O Allah, to You alone I hope and to You alone I supplicate, so grant me my desire and rectify my deed for me."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at Mina, say: O God, this is Mina, which is from the rituals You have bestowed upon us. I ask You to bestow upon me what You bestowed upon Your prophets, for I am Your servant and in Your grasp. Then pray there Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, the late 'Isha, and Fajr. The Imam prays Dhuhr there, and it is not permissible for him to do otherwise, but it is expanded for you to pray with others if you are unable. Then you join them at Arafat.' He said: 'The boundary of Mina is from al-'Aqabah to Wadi Muhassir.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "One does not pass through Wadi Muhassir until the sun rises." As for the Imam, he does not exit it except after the sun has risen. He narrated that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Indeed, among the Sunnah is that the Imam does not depart from Mina to Arafah until the sun rises." And there is no harm if the pedestrian and the one with an excuse depart from Mina before praying, and he prays on the way. Narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We are pedestrians, so what should we do?' He said, 'As for the people of carriages, they used to pray al-Ghadah (the morning prayer) in Mina, but as for you, proceed and pray wherever you are on the road.' And when he proceeds to 'Arafat, he should supplicate with the supplication that was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you depart for 'Arafah, say while heading towards it: 'O God, to You I have directed my gaze, and upon You I have relied, and I seek Your Face. I ask You to bless my journey, fulfill my need, and make me among those whom You boast about on this day before those who are superior to me.' Then enter the state of Ihram (Talbiyah) while heading to 'Arafat. When you reach 'Arafat, pitch your tent in Namira, which is the valley of 'Uranah, before the Station and before 'Arafah. When the sun sets on the Day of 'Arafah, perform ritual bath and pray Dhuhr and 'Asr with one Adhan and two Iqamas, for you are hastening 'Asr and combining them to free yourself for supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking. He said: The boundary of 'Arafah is from the valley of 'Uranah and Thawiyyah and Namira to Dhi al-Majaz, and behind the mountain is the Station (Mawqif).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The boundary of Arafat is from the two Ma'zamin to the furthest point of the standing (waqf)."

And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Jabalah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Ascend from Wadi ʿUrnah with ʿArafāt."

And from him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about standing at Arafat: is it more preferable to you to be above the mountain or on the ground? He said, 'On the ground.' As for when there is necessity, there is no harm in rising to the mountain.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "It is not appropriate to stand (waqf) under the arak trees; as for staying/resting under them until the sun sets and one rises to proceed to the standing place (Arafat), there is no objection."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who sit under the Arak trees, those who settle beneath the Arak, have no Hajj.' He means whoever stands beneath it. But as for whoever settles beneath it and stands at the Station (of Arafat), there is no harm with him. And the evidence for this is the first report. And the Ghusl (ritual bath) on the Day of Arafah is after midday, and it is appropriate for a person to combine the two prayers so that he may be free for supplication.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The ritual bath (ghusl) on the Day of Arafah is when the sun sets, and one combines the noon (Dhuhr) and afternoon (Asr) prayers with one Adhan and two Iqamas.' And he stops the Talbiyah when the sun sets. Narrated.
Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the sun sets on the Day of Arafah, cease the Talbiyah at the time of the sun's setting."

And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Talbiyah of the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), when does he cease it? He said: 'When you see the houses of Mecca.' And he ceases the Talbiyah for Hajj at the time of the sun's decline on the Day of Arafah. And he ceases the Talbiyah of the Mutamatti' Umrah when the camels' hooves touch the ground in the Haram. And we have explained that at the beginning of the Book of Hajj, and we have exhausted what is in it, so there is no need to repeat it in that regard.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Umar from Ibn Udhayfir from Ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the sun declines on the Day of Arafah, cease the Talbiyah, perform Ghusl, and engage in Takbir, Tahlil, Tahmid, Tasbih, and praising Allah, and pray Dhuhr and Asr with one Adhan and two Iqamas."

And from him, from Ibrahim, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: And preferably, you hasten the prayer and combine them [Dhuhr and Asr, Fajr and Maghrib, Isha and Fajr] to free your soul for supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking. Then you come to the standing place [of Arafat], and upon you should be calmness and dignity, so praise Allah, glorify Him, magnify Him, extol Him, and declare Him Great one hundred times. And praise Him one hundred times, and glorify Him one hundred times, and recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times. And choose for yourself from supplication whatever you like, and strive [in it], for it is a day of supplication and asking. And seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan, for the Satan will not distract you in any place more dear to him than that he distract you in that place. And beware of being occupied with looking at people, and turn your attention to yourself. And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, so do not make me from the most deluded of Your guests, and have mercy on my journey to You from the deep valley.' And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, Lord of all the stations, free my neck from the Fire, and broaden for me from Your lawful provision, and ward off from me the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humans.' And you say: 'O Allah, do not scheme against me, and do not deceive me, and do not gradually lead me [to ruin].' And you say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your power, Your generosity, Your nobility, Your bounty, and Your favor, O Most Hearing of the hearers, O Most Seeing of the seers, O Quickest of the Reckoners, O Most Merciful of the merciful.' That You send prayer upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You do for me such and such. And let it be among what you say, while you are raising your head to the sky: 'O Allah, my need to You is that if You give it to me, what You withhold from me will not harm me, and if You withhold it from me, what You give me will not benefit me.' I ask You for the deliverance of my neck from the Fire. And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, and the possession of Your hand, my forelock is in Your hand, and my term is by Your knowledge.' I ask You to enable me for that which pleases You about me, and to accept from me the rituals which You showed Your friend Ibr

Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa and Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Ja'far ibn Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Jud'ah al-Azdi, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man stood at the station (of Arafat), but the crowd's confusion overwhelmed him, so he remained looking at the people and did not supplicate until the people departed.' He said, 'His standing will suffice him.' Then he said, 'Did he not pray Dhuhr and Asr at Arafat, bow (in prayer), and supplicate?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'All of Arafat is the station, and what is near the Mountain is better.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Talisi, from Abu Yahya Zakariya al-Mawsili, who said: I asked the Imam (peace be upon him) about a man who stood at the Station (of Arafat) and news of his father's death, or the death of one of his children, reached him before he remembered God with anything or supplicated, so he became occupied with anxiety and weeping to the exclusion of supplication. Then the people departed, and he said: 'I do not see any blame upon him, but he has done poorly; let him seek forgiveness from God. Would that he had been patient and sought reward, then he would have departed from the Station with the good deeds of all the people of the Station, without any of their good deeds being diminished.' And it is recommended that a person should frequently supplicate for his believing brothers and prefer them over himself in this regard, as narrated.

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said: Isa ibn A'yn, when he performed Hajj, would turn to supplication for his brothers until the people would depart. It was said to him: 'You spend your wealth and tire your body, and when you reach the place where needs are presented to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, you turn to supplication for your brothers and leave your own self?' He said: 'I am confident in the angel's call for me, but doubtful in the supplication for my own self.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimī, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymulī, from Ali ibn Asbāt, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilād, that Abdullah ibn Junbub said: I was at the Standing (at Arafat), and when I departed, I went to Ibrahim ibn Shu'ayb and greeted him. He was afflicted with the loss of one of his eyes, and his healthy eye was red, as if it were a clot of blood. I said to him, 'You have lost one of your eyes, and by Allah, I am concerned for the other, so if you wept a little less.' He said, 'No, by Allah, O Abu Muhammad, I did not make a supplication for myself today.' I said, 'Then for whom did you supplicate?' He said, 'I supplicated for my brothers, because I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, Allah appoints for him an angel who says, and for you is the like."' So I wanted to be the one supplicating for my brothers, and the angel to be supplicating for me, because I am in doubt regarding my own supplication, and I am not in doubt regarding the angel's supplication for me.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Bajali and al-Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When do you depart from Arafat?' He said, 'When the redness (of sunset) has passed from here,' and he pointed with his hand towards the east and the rising place of the sun.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudalah and Safwan and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the polytheists used to perform the Ihram departure (Ifadah) from Arafat before the sun set, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) differed from them and performed the Ifadah after the sunset of the sun." And whoever performs the Ifadah before the sunset intentionally, upon him is a camel (or cow/sheep) which he slaughters on the Day of Sacrifice; and if he is unable, he fasts for eighteen days. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Durays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who performed the departure (Ifada) from Arafat before the sun set. He said: 'Upon him is a camel which he slaughters on the Day of Slaughtering (Yawm al-Nahr); if he cannot afford it, he fasts for eighteen days in Mecca, or on the road, or with his family.' If his departure from Arafat was due to ignorance, then there is nothing upon him. He narrated that.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Mis'mam ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed the Farewell Stop (Ifafah) from Arafat before the sunset of the sun, he said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him, and if he was deliberate, then upon him is the sacrifice of a camel (Badanah).' So when you intend to perform the Farewell Stop, supplicate with this supplication which he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala and Hammam from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the sun sets, perform the Ihram (Ifadah) with the people, and upon you be calmness and dignity, and perform Ihram 'from where the people perform Ihram', and seek forgiveness of 'Allah, indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful'. When you reach the red sand dune - on the right of the road - say: 'O Allah, have mercy on my standing, increase in my deeds, preserve for me my religion, and accept my rituals, and spare me from the 'burden' (wadhif) which many people do, for it has reached us that Hajj is not the burdening of horses nor the wasting of camels, but fear Allah and walk a beautiful walk, and do not tread on the weak, nor tread on a Muslim, and be moderate in walking, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to restrain his she-camel until its head would reach the front of the saddle, and he would say: 'O people, upon you is composure, so the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is to be followed.' Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'O Allah, free me from the Fire,' repeating it until the people performed Ihram. I said: 'Will you not perform Ihram, for the people have performed Ihram?' He said: 'I fear the crowding, and I fear that I will share in the hardship of a person.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said: I asked him about combining Maghrib and the last 'Isha with a single combination (jam' taqdim or jam' ta'khir), so he said: 'Do not pray them until you reach the combination, even if part of the night has passed, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) combined them with one Adhan and two Iqamas, just as he combined Dhuhr and 'Asr at 'Arafat.'

And from him, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: "Do not pray the Maghrib prayer until you join (with the 'Asr prayer), even if one-third of the night has passed."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya and Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Do not pray Maghrib until you arrive at Jam', then pray Maghrib and the last 'Isha with one Adhan and two Iqamas. And descend in the bottom of the valley on the right side of the road, near al-Mash'ar. And it is recommended for the single traveler to stand at al-Mash'ar and tread it with his foot. And he should not pass the ponds (al-Hiyad) on the night of al-Muzdalifah. And he should say: 'O Allah, this is Jam'. O Allah, I ask You to gather for me in it all-encompassing goodness. O Allah, do not deprive me of the goodness which I asked You to gather for me in my heart. Then I ask You to make me know what You made known to Your friends in this my dwelling. And to protect me from all-encompassing evil. And if You are able to keep that night alive, then do so. For it has reached us that the gates of heaven are not closed that night for the voices of the believers. They have a hum like the hum of bees. Allah, exalted is His praise, says: 'I am your Lord and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My right, and it is incumbent upon Me to respond to you.' So He removes that night for whomever He wills from his sins and forgives whomever He wills to forgive.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it for a man to pray the Maghrib and 'Atamah (Isha) prayers at the Mawqif? He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had prayed them in the Sha'b.' Therefore, the meaning of this report is for the one whom an obstacle prevented from coming to Jam' until he stayed there late. As for doing so by choice, it is not permissible. And that which indicates that the meaning is what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The caravan of the Imam (peace be upon him) was delayed between Arafat and Muzdalifah, so he stopped and prayed the Maghrib prayer, and prayed the 'Isha prayer in Muzdalifah.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm if a man prays the Maghrib prayer when he stays overnight in Arafat." And if he wishes to combine the two prayers by combining them, he combines them with one Adhan and two Iqamas, and he does not place a voluntary prayer (Nafilah) between them. And if he does that, there is no blame upon him, but the preferable is what we mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Maghrib and 'Isha prayers are combined with one Adhan and two Iqamahs, and do not pray anything in between them. And he said, "Thus the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed."

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'abb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If I pray Maghrib with jama' (combined), do I pray two rak'ahs after Maghrib?' He said: 'Do not pray Maghrib and 'Isha' [combined], then pray the rak'ahs afterwards.' As for what indicates that if one separates them [Maghrib and 'Isha] with nafl (voluntary) prayers, he is not sinful,

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Aban ibn Taghlib said: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the Maghrib prayer in Al-Muzdalifah, so he stood and prayed Maghrib, then he prayed the final 'Isha and did not bow in between. Then I prayed behind him a year later, and when he had prayed Maghrib, he stood and voluntarily prayed four rak'at. And the boundary of Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram is what is between the two shoulders (or peaks) to Al-Hiyad and to Wadi Muhassir, he narrated that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar who said: The boundary of the Mash'ar al-Haram is from al-Ma'zimayn to al-Hiyad and to Wadi Muhassir, and it is called al-Muzdalifah because they approached it from 'Arafat.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Remain in a state of purity after you have prayed the Fajr prayer, then stand; if you wish, stand near the mountain, and if you wish, stand where you spent the night. When you stand, praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and extol Him, and remember from His favors and blessings whatever you are able to, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then let your words be: 'O Allah, Lord of the Sacred Mash'ar, free my neck from the Fire, and broaden for me from Your lawful provision, and avert from me the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humans. O Allah, You are the best of those sought, the best of those called upon, and the best of those asked. And every visitor has a right [of return], so make my right in this my station that You excuse my stumble, accept my excuse, and overlook my sin. Then make piety from the world my provision.' Then proceed to where Thabir rises for you and you see the camels' footprints. And it is recommended for the single pilgrim to tread the Sacred Mash'ar and to enter the House. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn 'Uthman from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is recommended for the single pilgrim (mufrid) to tread the Mash'ar al-Haram and to enter the Kaaba. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: When the sun rises, he should depart from it to Mina.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim al-Asadi from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Then depart (from Muzdalifah) when your 'thabir' (the front part of the camel's neck or the rising of the sun) appears, and you see the camels' feet positions. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The people of Jahiliyyah used to say 'Ashriq Thabir' (Rise, Thabir), meaning the sun, so that we may move. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) departed contrary to the people of Jahiliyyah; they used to depart with the galloping of horses and the placing of camels. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) departed contrary to that, with calmness, dignity, and composure. So depart with the remembrance of Allah and seeking forgiveness, and move your tongue with it. When you pass by Wadi Muhassir, which is a large valley between Jamm and Mina, and it is closer to Mina, then run (sa'y) in it until you cross it. For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) moved his she-camel while saying: 'O Allah, accept my covenant, accept my repentance, answer my supplication, and succeed me in those I left behind me.' And there is no harm if a person departs a little before the sunrise, except that he does not cross Wadi Muhassir except after the sunrise. Narrated.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Which hour do you prefer for us to depart from Mina (for 'Arafat/Muzdalifah)?' He said: 'A little before the sun rises, that is the most beloved of the hours to me.' I said: 'And if I stay until the sun rises?' He said: 'There is no harm in that.'

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abu Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): 'Which hour do you prefer that I depart from Jamʿ (al-Muzdalifah)?' He said, 'A little before the sun rises; it is the most beloved of the hours to me.' I said, 'And if I stay until the sun rises?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Do not cross Wadi Muhassir until the sun rises." As for the Imam, it is appropriate for him to remain stationed until after the sun has risen. He narrated that.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from one who narrated to him, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Imam should remain standing at Jam' (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) until the sun rises, while the rest of the people may hasten (leave) if they wish or delay if they wish. And it is not permissible to depart from Jam' before the rising of the dawn with choice, and whoever departs before the rising of the dawn intentionally, upon him is the blood of a sheep, and if he was forgetful, there is nothing upon him. He narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who stood with the people at Jumu'ah, then departed before the people departed. He said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him, and if he departed before the rising of dawn, then upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

And as for what was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and others from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: "Regarding advancing from Mina to Arafat before the sunrise, there is no harm in it, and advancing from Muzdalifah to Mina to throw the pebbles and praying Fajr in their homes in Mina, there is no harm in it." This is applicable to the one who is cautious and the one with excuses, such as women and others; but with choice, that is not permissible according to what we have previously stated. And that which indicates that the intended meaning is what we mentioned is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) said: Any woman or man who is in a hurry and departs from al-Mash'ar al-Haram at night, there is no harm; let him throw the Jamarah, then proceed, and order someone to sacrifice on his behalf. The woman shortens her hair and the man shaves it, then let him perform Tawaf with the House and with al-Safa and al-Marwah, then let him return to Mina. If he arrives at Mina and no sacrifice has been made for him, there is no harm if he sacrifices himself. He should carry his hair when he shaves in Mecca to Mina, and if he wishes, he may shorten (his hair) if he had performed Hajj before that.

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: "There is no harm if a man pours out his water (or empties his vessel) at night if he is afraid."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted concession to women and children to rush (from Mina to Muzdalifah) at night, and to throw the Jamarat at night, and to pray the morning prayer in their homes; so if they feared menstruation, they would go to Mecca and appoint someone to offer the sacrificial animal on their behalf.

And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, there are women with us, so should I send them forth at night?' He said, 'Yes, you want to do as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Send them forth at night, and do not send them forth until you have made them stand at Jamm (Muzdalifah). Then send them forth until they arrive at the Great Jamrah and throw (the pebbles) at the Jamrah. If there is no sacrifice upon them, let them take from their hair and trim their nails. Then they shall proceed to Mecca with their faces (facing the Kaaba), and perform Tawaf around the House, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Then they shall return to the House and perform another Tawaf (of seven circuits). Then they shall return to Mina, having completed their Hajj.' And he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Usamah with them.' And we have previously presented the discussion regarding the Sa'i in Wadi Muhassir, and that is further clarified by what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskān said: He narrated to me al-'Alā' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'When you pass by Wadi Muhassir, run (sa') in it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ran in it.' And whoever leaves running in Wadi Muhassir, he will return and run in it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hajjāl from some of our companions who said: A man passed by Wadi Muhassir, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered him, after departing, to return and walk back. The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And he takes the pebbles for throwing at the Jamaraat from al-Muzdalifah or from the road; and if he takes them from his pack in Mina, it is valid.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: "Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jumm (Muzdalifah); if you take them from your saddlebag in Mina, it will suffice you."

And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Ribi'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jummah (Al-Muzdalifah); and if you take them from your saddlebag in Mina, it will suffice you." And it is permissible to take the pebbles from the rest of the Haram (sanctuary), excluding the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Al-Khaif. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hanan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible to take the pebbles of the Jamaraat from all of the Haram (sanctuary), except from Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Khayf.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him from where it is appropriate to take the pebbles of Jamaraat? He said: 'Do not take them from two places: from outside the Haram and from the pebbles of Jamaraat themselves, and there is no harm in taking them from the rest of the Haram.' And whenever he takes the pebbles from outside the Haram, that does not suffice; it was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pebbles for throwing at the Jamarat: if you take them from the Haram (sanctuary), it will suffice you; and if you take them from outside the Haram, it will not suffice you. He said, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not throw the Jamarat except with pebbles.' And the smooth (pebbles) from the pebbles are disliked, and the rough (pebbles) from them are recommended. He narrated.
Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the pebbles of Jamaraat, he said: 'The smooth ones are disliked from them,' and he said: 'Take the rough ones.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The pebbles for throwing at the Jamarat should be like the size of a fingernail. Do not take them black, white, or red; take them dark-colored and speckled. Throw them with a casual throw, place them on the thumb, and push them off with the nail of the index finger. He said: Throw them from the middle of the valley, and keep all of them on your right side. Do not throw at the top of the Jamarah. You stand at the first two Jamarat, and do not stand at the Jamarat al-Aqabah. It is appropriate that you pick up the pebbles and do not break any of them. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pick up the pebbles and do not break any part of them.' The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'If he is able to perform wudu, let him perform wudu; and if he is not able, his ghusl suffices for him. And throwing (the pebbles) is not valid for him unless he is in a state of purity.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) when throwing the Jamarat (pegs), so he said, 'Perhaps I did it. As for the Sunnah, it is not [obligatory], but [it is done] due to the heat and sweat.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the stoning (of the Jamarat), so he said: 'Do not stone the Jamarat unless you are in a state of purity.' This is the most preferable (state), and if he stones them while not in a state of purity, there is no penalty upon him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi, from Abu Ja'far, from Ibn Abi Ghasan, from Humayd ibn Mas'ud, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about throwing the Jamaraat while not in a state of ritual purity. He said: 'The Jamaraat with us are like al-Safa and al-Marwah; they are walls. If you circumambulate between them while not in a state of ritual purity, it will not harm you, but purity is more beloved to me, so do not leave it while you are able to do so.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then he comes to the farthest Jamrah, which is at al-Aqabah, and he should stand facing it until the end of the door.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the pebbles of the Jamarat, then go to the furthest Jamarah which is near al-Aqabah, and throw them from its front, not from its top. And while the pebbles are in your hands, say: "O Allah, these are my pebbles, so count them for me and raise them in my deeds." Then throw, and with each pebble say: "Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, repel from me the Shaytan and his hosts. O Allah, for the confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, make it an accepted Hajj, a accepted deed, a thanked effort, and a forgiven sin. And let the distance between you and the Jamarah be the measure of ten cubits or fifteen cubits. When you reach your saddle (mount) and return from the throwing, say: "O Allah, in You I have trusted, and upon You I have relied. How excellent is the Lord, how excellent the Master, and how excellent the Helper."' He said: 'And it is recommended that the Jamarat be thrown while in a state of purity (taharah).'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Udhayfir from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you slaughter your Udhiyah (sacrificial animal), shave your head, perform ghusl, trim your nails, and take from your mustache." And whoever deliberately leaves shaving or shortens [the hair] until he performs Hajj, a sheep's blood (dam) is obligatory upon him. And whoever does that forgetfully, there is nothing upon him; he should shorten [his hair] and then repeat Tawaf and Sa'i. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Humayd ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who visited the House (Kaaba) before shaving [his head], he said: 'If he visited the House before shaving while knowing that it is not appropriate for him, then upon him is the blood of a sheep [fidya].'

And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who visited the House (performed Umrah) before shaving [his head]. He said, 'It is not appropriate except that he be forgetful.' Then he said, 'The people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Sacrifice, and some of them said, And that which indicates what we mentioned regarding the repetition of Tawaf and Sa'i is what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who threw the pebbles (at the Jamarat), slaughtered her sacrificial animal, and did not shorten (her hair), until she visited the Kaaba, so she performed Tawaf and Sa'i during the night. What is her status, and what is the status of the man if he does that? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm with it. He shortens (his hair), performs Tawaf for Hajj, then performs Tawaf for Ziyarah (visitation), and then he has become free from all prohibitions (Ihram restrictions).' And whoever departs from Mina before shaving (or shortening), he must return to it and shave or shorten there, and no other option is permissible for him while he has the choice. If he cannot return to Mina due to necessity, let him shave wherever he is, and let him return his hair to Mina and bury it there. What indicates this is what he narrated:

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to shorten his hair or shave it until he departed from Mina. He said, 'He returns to Mina until he discards his hair there, whether it was by shaving or shortening.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir who said: I asked him about a man who did not know how to shorten [his hair] or shave [his head] until he departed from Mina. He said, 'Let him return to Mina until he shaves his hair there or shortens it, and he must shave the back of his neck (al-sarurah).'

And that which was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to shave his head or shorten [his hair] until he became 'nafar' [shook off the minor state of Ihram], he said, 'He shaves in the way or wherever he is.' So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because this narration is interpreted as applying to one who was unable to return to Mina. As for one who is able to do so, then it is necessary [to return], according to what we have previously stated. As for that which indicates that he should return his hair [shaving] to Mina if he shaved elsewhere, that is what was narrated:

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to bury his hair in his tent in Mina and say, 'They used to prefer that.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked that the hair be taken out of Mecca, saying, 'Whoever takes it out, he must return it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who shaves his head in Mecca, he said: 'He returns the hair to Mina.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Faddal, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who visited the House (Kaaba) and did not shave his head, he said: 'He should shave it in Mecca and carry his hair to Mina, and there is nothing upon him (penalty-wise).' And if a man shaved his head outside of Mina and did not return his hair to Mina, nothing is obligatory upon him, except that he has left the more preferable and the primary (practice). That was narrated.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who forgets to shave his head until he departs from Mina, so he said: 'I do not like that he casts off his hair except in Mina, and he has not imposed anything upon him.'
