When you entered the state of Ihram and responded (with Talbiyah), for every Talbiyah you recited, you have ten good deeds recorded, and ten bad deeds erased from you. When you circumambulated the Sacred House seven times, that is a pledge and treasure with Allah, which He is shy to punish you after it forever. When you prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, for them there are for you a thousand accepted Hajjs. When you walked between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, for you is like the reward of one who performed Hajj on foot from his country, and like the reward of one who freed seventy believing slaves. When you stood at Arafat until sunset, if upon you are sins like the sand of 'Araj, or like the number of stars in the sky, or like the drops of rain, Allah will forgive them for you. When you threw the pebbles at the Jamarat, for every pebble, ten good deeds are recorded for you in what remains of your life. When you shaved your head, for the count of every hair, a good deed is recorded for you in what remains of your life. When you slaughtered your offering or sacrificed your camel, for every drop of its blood, a good deed is recorded for you in what remains of your life. When you visited the House, circumambulated it seven times, and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, an angel struck your shoulders and said to you: 'Allah has forgiven you what passed, and for what is between you and one hundred and twenty days.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pilgrim's burdens and his guarantee are upon Allah. So when he enters the Sacred Mosque, Allah appoints two angels to guard his circumambulation, his prayer, and his walking. When it is the evening of 'Arafah, they strike his right shoulder and say to him: 'O this one! As for what has passed, you have been spared from it; so see how you will be in what is to come.'

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The pilgrims depart in three categories: one category is freed from the Fire, another category emerges from their sins as on the day their mother gave birth to them, and a third category is preserved in their families and wealth; and that is the least that a pilgrim returns with.

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Pilgrimage (Hajj) and Minor Pilgrimage ('Umrah) remove poverty and sins, just as the bellows (khir) removes the dross of iron." Muawiya said: "I asked him: Which is superior, one Hajj or the freeing of a slave? He said: 'One Hajj is superior.' I said: 'And two (Hajjs)?' He said: 'One Hajj is superior.' Muawiya said: 'So I kept increasing (the number of slaves) and he kept saying: "One Hajj is superior," until I reached thirty slaves, and he said: "One Hajj is superior."'

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Basir, and from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Basir, and 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abdyan, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A mandatory prayer is superior to twenty pilgrimages, and a pilgrimage is better than a house of gold given in charity until nothing of it remains.

And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Nusayr ibn Kathir, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'A dirham spent in Hajj is superior to two thousand [dirhams] in other paths of Allah.'
And from him from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from 'Umar ibn Yazid who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A Hajj is superior to freeing seventy slaves.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadala ibn Ayyub, all from al-Kinanī, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioning Hajj, so he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is one of the two Jihad, and it is the Jihad of the weak, and we are the weak.'
And from him, from Ibn Bint Ilyas, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: "Indeed, Hajj and Umrah remove poverty and sins, just as the bellows removes impurities from iron."

And from him from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said: "The one in the graves would wish that he had one prayer (hajjah) with the world and what is in it."

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever dies on the road to Mecca, whether going or returning, is safe from the Great Terror on the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-A'la said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to say: Whoever visits this House as a pilgrim or a visitor, free from arrogance, will return from his sins as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him.' Then he recited: 'So for whoever hastens [his departure] in two days, there is no blame upon him; and for whoever delays [for another day], there is no blame upon him — for whoever fears Allah.' I asked: What is arrogance? He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, the greatest arrogance is the dismissal of truth and the folly regarding truth.' I asked: And what is the dismissal of truth and the folly regarding truth? He said: 'Disregarding the truth and thrusting at its people, and whoever does that competes with Allah for His cloak.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ja'far ibn 'Imran, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Hajj and 'Umrah are two markets from the markets of the Hereafter. He who is constant in performing them is under God's guarantee: if He keeps him alive, He will pay him back to his family; and if He causes him to die, He will admit him to Paradise.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr and Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Do not trim your hair while you intend Hajj in Dhi al-Qa'dah, nor in the month in which you intend to depart for Umrah.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The Hajj is for well-known months": Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. So whoever intends to perform Hajj should trim their hair when they see the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah, and whoever intends to perform 'Umrah should trim their hair for a month.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: should he trim his hair throughout the entire month of Shawwal, provided he has not seen the crescent (of Dhu al-Qidrah)? He said, 'Yes.'

From him, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Take (remove) hair from yourself when you intend for the Hajj, the entire month of Shawwal until the first ten days of Dhu al-Qi'dah."
From him, from Isma'il ibn Jabr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How much should I lengthen my hair when I intend this journey?' He said, 'Let it grow for a month.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from some of our companions, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man should not shave (take hair) when he sees the crescent of Dhi al-Qa'dah, whether he intends to remove it from his head or from his beard.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about cupping and shaving the back of the neck during the months of Hajj, so he said, 'There is no harm with it and with the nurah.' The meaning of his saying 'shaving the back of the neck during the months of Hajj' is those that are other than Dhu al-Qi'dah, such as Shawwal, because it is permissible for a man to shave his head and the back of his neck in this month. What was narrated indicates that:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: does he take (cut) from his hair during the entire month of Shawwal, provided he has not seen the crescent? He said, 'Yes, there is no harm in it.'

And that which was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from Zur'ah from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Kazzaz, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'As for me, I trim from my hair when I intend to depart,' meaning to Mecca for the Ihram. The meaning is that he trims from his hair that which is other than the head, from his mustache or his body, for there is no harm in trimming that as long as he is not in Ihram. This is indicated by what was narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: should he trim his hair during the months of Hajj? He said: 'No, and not from his beard, but he should trim his mustache and his nails, and let him trim [his hair] if he wishes.' As for what indicates that if he shaves his head in Dhi al-Qa'dah, a sheep's blood [sacrifice] is due upon him, then what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who shaved his head in Mecca. He said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did that in the first thirty days of the months for Hajj, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did that after the thirty days in which the hair is allowed to grow for Hajj, then upon him is a blood offering (dam) which he must pour out.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is travel disliked on any of the disliked days, such as Wednesday and others? He said: 'Begin your journey with charity and recite the Verse of the Throne when it becomes clear to you.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Give charity and depart on whichever day you wish."

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "If a man appoints a deputy in charge of his family, there is nothing better than two rak'ahs which he prays when he intends to depart for his journey. And he says: "O Allah, I entrust to You my self, my family, my wealth, my offspring, my worldly life, my hereafter, and the conclusion of my deeds, unless Allah grants him what he asks for.".

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you leave your house intending Hajj and Umrah, if God wills, recite the supplication of relief. And it is: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Exalted, the Great. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Great Throne.' And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Then say: 'O Allah, be for me a protector from every tyrant stubborn [one] and from every rebellious devil.' Then say: 'In the name of Allah I entered, and in the name of Allah I went out, and in the path of Allah I strove.' O Allah, I place before my forgetfulness and haste: 'In the name of Allah and what Allah willed,' during this journey of mine, whether I remembered it or forgot it. O Allah, You are the One sought for help in all affairs, and You are the Companion in the journey and the Vicegerent in the family. O Allah, make our journey easy for us, and contract the earth for us, and move us through it with Your obedience and the obedience of Your Messenger. O Allah, rectify our backs (mounts), and bless us in what You have provided for us. And protect us from the punishment of the Fire. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of the journey, and the misery of the return, and the bad sight (of loss) regarding family, wealth, and children. O Allah, You are my support and my helper. O Allah, remove from me its distance and hardship, and accompany me in it, and replace me in my family with good. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Great. O Allah, I am Your servant, and this is Your burden, and the Face is Your Face, and the journey is to You, and You have looked upon what no one else has looked upon. So make this journey of mine an expiation for what preceded it of my sins, and be a help to me in it, and suffice me against its hardship and difficulty. And teach me from speech and action that which earns Your pleasure, for I am Your servant, and by You, and for You. So when you place your foot in the stirrup, say: 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.' In the name of Allah, and Allah is

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muthanna from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "The Hajj is in well-known months": Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. It is not for anyone to enter into the state of Ihram for Hajj in any other than them, and it is not for anyone to enter into Ihram before the time that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. And the example of that is the example of one who prays four [rak'ahs] during travel and leaves the two [rak'ahs]."

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān said: Maysir narrated to me saying: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man enters into iḥram from al-ʿAqīq and another from al-Kūfah; which of them is superior? He said: 'O Maysir, is it superior to pray ʿAṣr as four [rakʿāt] or to pray it as six?' I said: 'I pray it as four, [that is] superior.' He said: 'So too is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) superior to other [forms].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah al-Basri from Ibn Udhaynah said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever enters into ihram for Hajj in months other than the months of Hajj, then there is no Hajj for him; and whoever enters into ihram before the miqat, then there is no ihram for him.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hanan ibn Sadir who said: I, my father, Abu Hamza al-Thumali, Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, and Ziyad al-Ahlam entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He saw Ziyad whose body had shed its hair (from shaving the head for Ihram), so he said to him, "From where did you enter Ihram?" He said, "From Kufa." He said, "And why did you enter Ihram from Kufa?" He said, "It reached me from one of you that he said: 'That which is far from the Ihram is greater in reward.'" He said, "Only a liar has conveyed this to you." Then he said to Abu Hamza, "From where did you enter Ihram?" He said, "From al-Rabadhah." He said to him, "And why?" He said, "Because you heard that the grave of Abu Dharr is there, so you loved to pass by it." Then he said to my father and Abd al-Rahim, "From where did you both enter Ihram?" They said, "From al-'Aqiq." He said, "You have attained the concession and followed the Sunnah." And when two doors present themselves to me, both of which are permissible, I take the easier one. And that is because God is easy-loving, loves what is easy, and gives for what is easy what He does not give for exertion/hardship.

And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into the state of Ihram in months other than the months of Hajj, or from before the Miqat (station) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had designated. He said: 'His Ihram is not invalid. If he wishes, he may return to his family, for I do not see any blame upon him. If he wishes, he may proceed. When he reaches the designated time, let him enter Ihram again and make it an Umrah, for that is better than his returning, because he has already publicly declared his Ihram.' And it has been narrated that there is a concession (rukhsah) in entering Ihram before the Miqat for one who fears missing the Umrah in the month of Rajab.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who comes performing 'Umrah, intending the 'Umrah of Rajab, and the new moon enters before he reaches Al-'Aqiq. Should he enter the state of Ihram before the time [of Rajab] and designate it for Rajab, or should he delay the Ihram until Al-'Aqiq and designate it for Sha'ban? He said: 'He enters the state of Ihram before the time for Rajab, for Rajab has merit, and it is what he intended.'

And from him, from Fadala, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not appropriate to enter into ihram before the time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), unless one fears missing the month in Umrah.' And whoever vowed to enter ihram before the miqat, then it is obligatory upon him to enter ihram from the place from which he vowed; he narrated that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a servant upon whom Allah bestowed a favor, or whom He tested with a calamity, and then He cured him from that calamity, and he made it upon himself to enter the state of Ihram for Hajj from Khorasan, then it is obligatory upon him to complete (his Hajj from there).' And whoever enters the state of Ihram before the Miqat (station of Ihram) and catches game, there is no penalty upon him; this was narrated.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad from Hariz ibn Abdillah from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever enters into the state of Ihram before the Miqat (station) designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and then has intercourse with women or hunts, there is no penalty upon him."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Part of the perfection of Hajj and 'Umrah is that you enter into the state of Ihram from the Miqat (stations of entering Ihram) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. Do not pass them unless you are in the state of Ihram. For he designated for the people of Iraq, and at that time Iraq was not [a specific place but referred to the region], the location of Batn al-'Uqayq from the side of the people of Iraq. And he designated for the people of Yemen, Dhat 'Irq (Yalamlam). And he designated for the people of Ta'if, Qarn al-Manazil. And he designated for the people of the Maghreb (West), al-Juhfa, which is Mahya'ah. And he designated for the people of Medina, Dhat al-Hulayfah. And whoever's residence is behind these Miqat stations, from the side facing Mecca, then his Miqat is his residence."

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ihram is from five Mawaqit (stations of entering the state of Ihram) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. It is not appropriate for a pilgrim or a visitor to enter Ihram before them or after them. He designated Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Medina, which is Masjid al-Shajara, where he prays and assumes the state of Ihram for Hajj. He designated Al-Juhfah for the people of Syria. He designated Al-Aqiq for the people of Najd. He designated Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Ta'if. He designated Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. And it is not appropriate for anyone to prefer [deviate] from the Mawaqit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Tell me about Al-Aqiq. Is it a miqat (station of consecration) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated, or is it something the people did?' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated Dhul Hulaifah for the people of Medina, and he designated Al-Juhfah for the people of the Maghreb (West), and it is recorded with us as Mahya'ah. And he designated Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, and he designated Qaran al-Manazil for the people of Ta'if, and he designated Al-Aqiq for the people of Najd, and whatever is from Najd.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said: I asked him about the ihram (state of consecration for Hajj) of the people of Kufa and the people of Khurasan and what is adjacent to them, and the people of Syria and Egypt, from where is it? He said: 'As for the people of Kufa and Khurasan and what is adjacent to them, it is from al-'Aqiq. And the people of Medina are from Dhu al-Hulayfah and al-Juhfah. And the people of Syria and Egypt are from al-Juhfah. And the people of Yemen are from Yalamlam. And the people of Sind are from Basra, meaning from the miqat of the people of Basra.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir from 'Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set the Miqat for the people of the East as Al-'Aqiq, approximately two post-stages, between the post-stage of Al-Ba'ath and Ghumrah. And he set for the people of Medina Dhu al-Hulayfah, and for the people of Najd Qarn al-Manazil, and for the people of Syria Al-Juhfah, and for the people of Yemen Yalamlam.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The boundary of the 'Aqiq (a cut in the neck for slaughter) is its beginning, the slaughter site (Maslakh), and its end is the one with the vein (Dhat 'Irnq).'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj), from which Wadi al-Aqiq should one enter the state of Ihram? He said: 'From its beginning, and that is superior.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The end of the 'Aqiq is the Baid of Awtas, and he said: 'The Baid of al-Ba'ath is before Ghumrah by two Baid.'
And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Awtas is not from the 'Aqiq."

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The beginning of Al-Aqiq is Barid Al-Baath, and it is six miles from Al-Maslakh on the side facing Iraq, and between it and Ghumrah are twenty-one miles, two Barids.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The people of Mecca criticized certain matters regarding you. He said: 'What are they?' I said: They said: 'You entered into ihram from al-Juhfa, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered into ihram from al-Shajara.' He said: 'Al-Juhfa is one of the two designated times (miqat), so I adopted the easier of the two for the people, and I was ill.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From where does a man enter the state of Ihram if he passes the tree? He said: 'From Al-Juhfah, and one does not pass Al-Juhfah except while in the state of Ihram.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever resides in the City (Madinah) for a month while intending to perform Hajj, and then it occurs to him to depart via a route other than the one the people of the City take, then his Ihram (state of consecration) must be from a distance of six miles." And for one who assumes Ihram via the route of the City, it is not permissible to switch the Ihram from al-Shajara to Dhat Irq.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a group of people who arrived in Medina and feared the severity of the cold and the length of the days, meaning the state of Ihram from Al-Shajara. They wanted to take from there to Dhat 'Irq so that they could enter Ihram from it. He said, 'No,' while he was angry, 'Whoever enters Medina, he is not permitted to enter Ihram except from Medina.' And whoever forgets the Ihram from the Miqat, let him return to it and enter Ihram from it if there is a time for it; and if there is no time for it, let him proceed and enter Ihram from the place to which he arrived.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who left the state of Ihram until he entered the Haram (sanctuary), and he said: 'He returns to the miqat of the people of his land from which they enter Ihram, and he enters Ihram. And if he fears that the Hajj will be missed, let him enter Ihram from his place. If he is able to exit the Haram, let him exit.'

And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who passed the time when people enter the state of Ihram, but he forgot or was unaware, so he did not enter Ihram until he arrived at Mecca. He feared that if he returned to the Miqat, the Hajj would be missed for him. He said: 'He exits from the Haram (sanctuary) and enters Ihram, and that will suffice for him.' And there is no contradiction between this narration and the first one, because he is only obliged to exit from the Haram if he does not fear that by exiting, the Hajj will be missed for him. Just as if he does not fear missing the Hajj by exiting to the Miqat of his people, it is obligatory for him to go to it. And there is no harm for the one compelled and fearing for his life to delay entering Ihram from the Miqat until he enters the Haram. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from some of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said: "If a man fears for his self, he delays his ihram until al-Haram." And whoever's residence is below (shorter distance than) these miqats that we have mentioned, then his miqat is his residence, and he is obliged to enter into ihram from it. He narrated that.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever's dwelling is before the miqat (time/place) to Mecca, let him enter into ihram from his dwelling."
And he said in another hadith: "If his home is before the Miqat towards Mecca, then he should enter the state of Ihram from the vicinity of his family."

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Mis'mam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the house of a man is before Dhat Irq towards Mecca, let him enter into Ihram from his house."

And from him, from Safwan, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Rabbah ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): They narrate that Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, a completion of your Hajj is your Ihram from the Duwairah of your people.' He said, 'Glory be to Allah. If it were as they say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have enjoyed his garments until the Tree. Rather, the meaning of the Duwairah of his people is those whose people were behind the Miqat towards Mecca.' And the resident of Mecca goes out to the Miqat of his people for Hajj and Umrah together. If he is unable to do that, he enters Ihram from outside the Haram. He narrated that.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Muqarir (one who resides in Mecca during the months of Hajj), is it permissible for him to perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)? He said: 'Yes, he goes out to the boundary of his land and enters into the state of Ihram (says Talbiyah) if he wishes.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The resident of Mecca, when he enters it for Umrah in the months other than Hajj (for indeed the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah), if he enters it for Umrah in the months other than Hajj and then wishes to enter the state of Ihram (for Hajj), let him go out to Al-Ji'ranah, let him assume Ihram from there, then come to Mecca, and do not break the Talbiyah until he looks at the House, then he circles the House and prays two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), then he goes out to As-Safa and Al-Marwah and circles between them, then he shortens (his hair) and becomes free from Ihram, then he re-attaches the Talbiyah on the Day of Tarwiyah. And the sick person, when he reaches the Miqat, let the one who is with him assume Ihram on his behalf, and he should avoid what the Muhrim avoids; he narrated that.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Jamil ibn Dirraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): In for a sick person who fainted and did not regain consciousness until he reached the station (of Arafat), he said: 'A man performs ihram on his behalf.' And whoever forgot his ihram and did not remember it except after completing all the rituals, there is no penalty upon him, and his intention has sufficed for him. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram or was ignorant of it, yet he performed all the rituals, circled the Ka'bah, and walked between Safa and Marwah. He said: 'His intention suffices for him if he had intended that, so his Hajj is complete even if he did not recite the Talbiyah (Ihram formula).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim from Aban ibn Taghlib who said: I was traveling with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) as his companion between Mecca and Medina. When he reached the Sanctuary (al-Haram), he dismounted, performed ritual bath (ghusl), and took his sandals in his hands with both hands, then entered the Sanctuary barefoot. I did as he did. He said, 'O Aban! Whoever does what I did out of humility for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will erase a hundred thousand bad deeds from him, record for him a hundred thousand good deeds, build for him a hundred thousand degrees (of reward), and fulfill for him a hundred thousand needs.' And whoever is unable to perform the bath upon entering the Sanctuary, let him delay it until he is able before entering Mecca. If he is unable, it is permissible for him to perform the bath after entering Mecca.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih said: I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) in the Sanctuary (Mecca) before entering it or after entering it. He said: 'It does not harm you whichever you do. And if you bathe in Mecca, there is no objection; and if you bathe in your house when you stay in Mecca, there is no objection.'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muawiya ibn Ayyar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you arrive at the Sanctuary, if God wills, perform the ritual bath (Ghusl) upon entering it. And if you advance (before entering), perform the bath from the Well of Maimun, or from Fakh, or from your house in Mecca." And it is recommended for whoever intends to enter the Sanctuary to take some of the Idhkhir (a type of aromatic herb) and chew it, for that is among what freshens the breath. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you enter the Sanctuary, take some idhkhir (a type of aromatic herb) and chew it." And he used to command Umm Farwah to do that. So when one wishes to enter Mecca, let him enter from its upper part if he is entering from the road of Medina. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From where should I enter Mecca, having come from Medina? He said: 'Enter from the upper part of Mecca, and when you leave intending to go to Medina, exit from the lower part of Mecca.' And it is recommended that he perform a ritual bath before entering Mecca; that was narrated.
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) commanded us to perform ghusl from Fakh before entering Mecca.

And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Ajlan ibn Salih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you reach the Well of Maymun or the Well of Abd al-Sammad, perform ghusl, remove your sandals, and walk barefoot, and upon you be tranquility and dignity.' And whoever sleeps after the ghusl, he must repeat the ghusl; this was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) for entering Mecca, then sleeps and performs ablution (wudu) before entering; does that suffice for him or must he repeat it? He said, 'It does not suffice for him, because he entered with only ablation.'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: "If you perform the ritual bath (ghusl) in Mecca, then sleep before performing the Tawaf, you must repeat your ritual bath." And when he wishes to enter the Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), let him enter through the Gate of Banu Shaybah. And let him recite the supplication upon entering; he narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you enter the Sacred Mosque, enter it barefoot, with calmness, dignity, and humility. And he said: 'Whoever enters with humility, forgiveness will be granted to him, if God wills.' I asked: 'What is humility?' He said: 'Calmness. Do not enter it with arrogance.' So when you reach the door of the mosque, stand and say: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings. In the name of God, by God, and from God, and whatever God wills. And peace be upon the prophets and messengers of God, and peace be upon the Messenger of God, and peace be upon Abraham.' And all praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds. So when you enter the mosque, raise your hands and face the House and say: 'O God, I ask You in my standing here at the beginning of my rituals that You accept my repentance, overlook my sin, and remove my burden.' All praise is to God who brought me to His Sacred House. O God, I bear witness that this is Your Sacred House which You made a place of return for people and a sanctuary. Blessed and a guidance for the worlds. O God, indeed the servant is Your servant, the city is Your city, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and following Your obedience, obedient to Your command and content with Your decree. I ask You with the request of the poor one who needs You, the one fearful of Your punishment. O God, open for me the gates of Your mercy and employ me in Your obedience and pleasure.

Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Zur'a from Sama'a from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You say while you are at the door of the mosque: In the name of Allah and by Allah and from Allah and to Allah and whatever Allah willed, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah, and the best of names is for Allah, and praise is to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon Muhammad ibn Abdullah, peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings, peace be upon the prophets of Allah and His messengers, peace be upon Ibrahim, the friend of the Merciful. Peace be upon the messengers, and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and have mercy on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers and blessed and had mercy on Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad Your servant and Your Messenger, and upon Ibrahim Your friend, and upon Your prophets and Your messengers, and grant them peace, and peace be upon the messengers, and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy, and employ me in Your obedience and Your pleasure, and protect me with the protection of faith forever as long as You keep me alive. Exalted is the praise of Your Face, and praise to Allah who made me among His guests and visitors, and made me among those who build His mosques, and made me among those who converse with Him. O Allah, indeed I am Your servant and Your visitor, and in Your house, and upon every visitor is a right for whoever visits him, and You are the best of visitors and the most noble of those visited, so I ask You, O Allah, O Merciful. And by the fact that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone, no partner for You, and by the fact that You are One, Eternal, He neither begot nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. And that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family. O Generous, O Noble, O Compeller, O Kind, I ask You to make Your gift to me from my visiting You, that You grant me the ransom of my neck from the Fire. O Allah, free my neck from the Fire. You say this three times, and exp

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn Saif ibn 'Amirah, from his father Sa' ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Which of the lands is most superior after the Sanctuary of Allah and the Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'Kufa, O Abu Bakr, is the pure and clean one. In it are the graves of the sent prophets and the non-sent prophets, and the truthful successors. In it is the Mosque of Suhayl, in which every prophet Allah sent had prayed. In it Allah's justice will appear, and its Qa'im (the Awaited One) and those who rise with him after him will be. It is the dwelling places of the prophets, the successors, and the righteous.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Mecca is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to one hundred thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to one hundred thousand dinars. And Medina is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to ten thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to ten thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to ten thousand dinars. And Kufa is the sanctuary of Allah the Exalted, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to one thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to one thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to one thousand dinars.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Najm ibn Huthaym, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: If people knew what is in the Mosque of Kufa, they would prepare provisions and mounts for it from a distant place. Indeed, one obligatory prayer in it equals one Hajj, and one voluntary prayer in it equals one Umrah.

And from him, from Abu al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Jabala, from Salam ibn Abi Amra, from Sa'd ibn Dhara'if, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: "The voluntary prayer in this mosque equals an Umrah with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the obligatory prayer equals a Hajj with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and indeed a thousand prophets and a thousand successors have prayed in it."

And the Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "There is no righteous servant nor prophet who has not prayed in the Mosque of Kufa, to the extent that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know where you are at this moment, O Messenger of Allah? You are opposite the Mosque of Kufa.' He said: 'I said, 'Ask permission for me from my Lord so that I may go to it and pray two rak'ahs in it.' So Allah, Exalted and Glorious, granted him permission. And indeed, its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And the obligatory prayer performed in it equals a thousand prayers, and the voluntary prayer equals five hundred prayers. And sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is an act of worship. And if people knew what is in it, they would come to it, even if crawling.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'One prayer in the mosque of Kufa is equivalent to a thousand prayers.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said to me and took my hand, saying: He said to me, Abu Hamza said to me and took my hand, saying: Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata said to me and took my hand, and showed me the seventh pillar, and said: This is the standing place of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). He said: And al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) used to pray near the fifth pillar, and when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was absent, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) would pray in it, and it is from the door of Kindah.

And the Imam (peace be upon him) said: The seventh pillar, facing the doors of Kindah in the courtyard, is the station of Abraham (peace be upon him), and the fifth is the station of Gabriel (peace be upon him).

From Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Naqash al-Qummi, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nakhas narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Rummani narrated to us, saying: Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Tayalisi narrated to us, from Mukhtar al-Tammari, from Abu Mattar, who said: When the impious Ibn Muljam struck the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Shall I kill him?' He said: 'No, but detain him. When I die, kill him. And when I die, bury me in this elevation, in the grave of my two brothers, Hud and Salih (peace be upon them).'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Bakran, from Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his brother, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar al-Jurjani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his grandfather Abu Talib, who said: I asked al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him): 'Where did you bury the Commander of the Faithful?' He said, 'On the bank of the riverbank (al-Jurf). And we passed by him at night near the Mosque of al-Ashath.' And he said, 'Bury me in the grave of my brother Hud (peace be upon him).'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: We were informed by Muhammad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who said: Ahmad ibn Mitham al-Talhi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Where was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) buried? He said: 'He was buried in the grave of his father, Noah (peace be upon him).' I said: And where is the grave of Noah? The people say that it is in the Mosque. He said: 'No, that is in the rear of Kufa.'

And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Idris) he said: My father narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Abdullah ibn Hassan from Al-Thumali from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a hadith that he narrated: That it was in the will of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Take me out to the open area (Zahr), and when your feet are firmly planted and a wind faces you, bury me, for it is the first peak of Sinai.' So they did that.

And with this chain of narration, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Isma'il, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "We say that on the back of Kufa there is a grave; whoever seeks refuge with it, God will heal him."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: My uncle Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to me from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Tamimi, who narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Ilyas, from Mubarak al-Kabbaz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "Saddle the she-camel and the donkey, for it is time of his arrival, and he is in al-Hirah." He said: So he mounted, and I mounted with him until he entered al-Jurf. Then he dismounted and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he advanced a little further and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he advanced a little further and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he mounted and returned. I said to him: "May I be your ransom, what are the first two, the second two, and the third two?" He said: "The first two rak'ahs are at the place of the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); the second two rak'ahs are at the place of the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and the third two rak'ahs are at the place of the pulpit of the Qa'im (peace be upon him)."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his uncle, who said: Ahmad ibn Hammad ibn Zuhayr al-Qurashi narrated to me from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Abu al-Sakheef al-Arajani, who said: Umar ibn Abdillah ibn Talhah al-Nahdi narrated to me from his father, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he mentioned a hadith and narrated it to us. He said: So we went with him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), until we reached al-Ghariyy. He said: So he came to a place and prayed. Then he said to Isma'il: 'Rise and pray at the head of your father, al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' I said: 'Is it not that his head was taken to ash-Sham?' He said: 'Yes, but so-and-so, our mawla, stole it and brought it and buried it here.'

And from him, from Muhammad, from his uncle, who said: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal al-Khuza'i from Uthman ibn Sa'id from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Indeed, near Kufah is a grave; whoever afflicted by distress visits it and prays two or four rak'at at it, Allah will relieve his distress and fulfill his need.' I asked: Is it the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)? He said to me with a nod of his head: 'No.' I said: Then is it the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)? He said to me with a nod of his head: 'Yes.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fudayl, who said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah informed us, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Nahik al-Samuri narrated to me from Ubays ibn Hisham al-Nashiri from Salih ibn Sa'id al-Qammam from Yunus ibn Abi Yahya, who said: I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he arrived in al-Hirah, and he mentioned a hadith that he narrated to us, except that he said he traveled with him until he reached the place he intended. He said, 'O Yunus, tie your mount.' So I tied them together. Then he raised his hand and made a quiet supplication that I did not understand. Then he began the prayer and recited two short surahs, pronouncing them audibly, and I did as he did. Then he made supplication (peace be upon him), and I understood and knew it. He said, 'O Yunus, do you know what place this is?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, by Allah, but I know that I am in the desert.' He said, 'This is the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); he and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will meet on the Day of Resurrection.' The supplication: 'O Allah, there is no avoiding Your command, no avoiding Your decree, no avoiding Your judgment, and no power and no strength except with You. O Allah, then whatever judgment You have judged for us or whatever decree You have decreed for us, grant us with it a patience that overcomes it and repels it, and make it rising in Your pleasure, increasing in our good deeds, our excellence, our stability, our honor, our glory, our blessings, and our dignity in this world and the hereafter.' And whatever gift You have given us, or with which You have favored us from a virtue, or with which You have honored us from a dignity, grant us with it a gratitude that overcomes it and repels it, and make it rising in Your pleasure, in our good deeds, our stability, our honor, Your blessings, and Your dignity in this world and the hereafter. And do not make it for us arrogance or extravagance, or a trial, or hatred, or punishment, or disgrace in this world or in the hereafter. O Allah, we seek refuge in You from the stumble of the tongue, and the evil of the station, and the lightness of the scale. O Allah, present our good deeds to us at death, and do not show us our actions upon us as regrets, and do not disgrace us at Your judg

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: He narrated to us Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, who said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Shihab from Abdullah ibn Yunus al-Subi'i, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "I love for every believer to wear five rings: with ruby, which is the most splendid of them; with agate, which is the purest of them for God and for us; with turquoise, which is the delight of the gaze of the believers (men and women); and with Chinese iron, which I love to wear and do not dislike wearing when meeting the people of evil, to extinguish their evil. I love to have it made, for it scatters the unruly from jinn and humans, and what God reveals with the white stones, the two Ghariyyan." I said: O my master, what is the virtue in it? He said: "Whoever wears it and looks at it, God writes for him, for every glance, a visitation (reward) whose reward is the reward of the prophets and the righteous. And if it were not for God's mercy upon our Shiah, the separation (or distinctiveness) from it would reach a degree that cannot be found for a price. But God has made it easy for them so that their rich and their poor may wear it."

And it is narrated from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said: "There is no distressed person who comes to the Mosque of Al-Sahla, prays two rak'ahs in it between the two evening prayers, and supplicates Allah (the Exalted), except that Allah will relieve his distress."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) say: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sends down an angel every night with him three mithqals of the musk of Paradise, and he casts it into your Euphrates. And there is no river in the east and west of the earth greater in blessing than it.'

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Nahik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His Exalted Saying: 'And We gave him refuge on a high ground of level ground and flowing water.' He said: 'The high ground is Najaf of Kufa, and the flowing water is the Euphrates.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Makhramah ibn Rib'i, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The 'bank of the river on the right' which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Quran is the Euphrates, and the 'blessed spot' is Karbala."

And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Kufa during the time of Abu al-Abbas, he came riding his mount in his travel clothes until he stopped at the bridge of Kufa. Then he said to his servant, 'Give me water.' He took a potter's bowl, scooped water from it, and gave it to him to drink. He drank the water while it flowed over his beard and clothes. Then he asked for more, and he gave him more; he asked again, and he gave him more. He praised Allah, then said, 'A river, how great is its blessing! Indeed, every day seven drops from Paradise fall into it. If people knew what blessing is in it, they would pitch their tents on its banks. And if it were not for the sinners entering it, no one with an ailment would immerse himself in it without being cured.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Sulayman ibn Harun al-Ajli, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I do not think anyone who is weaned on the water of the Euphrates, except that the Ahl al-Bayt would love him.' And he asked me: 'How far is it between you and the Euphrates?' So I informed him, and he said: 'If I were there, I would love to visit it at both ends of the day.' And it is recommended to also pray in Kufa in two mosques: the Mosque of Ghani and the Mosque of al-Hamra. And prayer is not permissible in five mosques: the Mosque of al-Ash'ath, the Mosque of Jarir ibn Abdillah al-Bajali, the Mosque of Simak ibn Kharash, the Mosque of Shabath ibn Rabi'i, and the Mosque of al-Taym, because the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade prayer in them, and we have cited that with a chain in the Book of Prayer.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi said: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah narrated to me; he said: The judge Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Razi narrated to me; he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to me; he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Farisi narrated to me; he said: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to me; he said: Ibrahim ibn Abdillah ibn Husayn ibn Uthman ibn Ma'alla ibn Ja'far narrated to me; he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is [the reward] for one who visits us?" He said: "Whoever visits me while alive or dead, or visits your father while alive or dead, or visits your brother while alive or dead, or visits you while alive or dead, it is a right upon me to rescue him on the Day of Resurrection."

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalaf from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: While al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he raised his head and said, 'O my father, what is the reward for one who visits you after your death?' He replied, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to your father as a visitor after his death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to your brother as a visitor after his death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to you as a visitor after your death will have Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid said: He narrated to us al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq and others from the scholars, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: He narrated to us al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: "Command our Shias to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for visiting it increases sustenance, prolongs life, and repels various evils, and visiting it is obligatory upon every believer who acknowledges his Imamate from God."

And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Allan, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "If one of you were to perform Hajj for his entire life, and then did not visit al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he would be leaving a right from the rights of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), because the right of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a divine obligation obligatory upon every Muslim."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is a right upon the wealthy person to visit the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) twice a year, and it is a right upon the poor person to visit it once a year.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya and Abdillah ibn Ja'far and Ahmad ibn Idris all from al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman from Abd al-Jabbar al-Nahawandi from Abu Ishaq from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Thuwair ibn Abi Fakhtah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Husayn, whoever leaves his home intending to visit Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), if he is walking, Allah writes for him a good deed for every step and erases a bad deed with it, until he reaches the open field (al-Ha'ir); then Allah writes him among the successful ones. And when he completes his rituals, Allah writes him among the victorious ones. And when he intends to depart, an angel comes to him and says to him: I am the messenger of your Lord, Allah, conveying peace to you, and He says to you: Resume your deeds, for what has passed has been forgiven to you.'

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya, from al-Haytham ibn Abdillah, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him), from his father, who said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the days of the visitors of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) are not counted among their fixed lifespans."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever a year passes without visiting the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will shorten his lifespan by a year. And if I said that one of you dies before his appointed term by thirty years, I would be truthful, and that is because you leave visiting him. So do not leave it, for Allah will prolong your lifespans and increase your provisions. And if you leave visiting him, Allah will diminish your lifespans and provisions. So compete in visiting him and do not neglect it, for al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) is a witness for you before Allah the Exalted, and before His Messenger, and before Ali, and before Fatimah, may the prayers of Allah be upon them all.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Hadeethani (narrated to me) Hakim ibn Dawud from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Mu'alla from Isḥaq ibn Dawud who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'I have placed a mark on all my belongings of gold and silver, and I sold my rural estates, so I said: I will settle in Mecca.' He said: 'Do not do so, for the people of Mecca disbelieve in God openly.' I said: 'Then in the sanctuary of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'They are worse than them.' I said: 'Then where should I settle?' He said: 'You should go to Iraq, to Kufa, for the blessing from it is for twelve miles, thus and thus, and next to it is a grave; any distressed person who visits it, or any grieving person, God will relieve his distress.'

And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Qudamah ibn Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever intends to visit the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) with humility, not arrogance, not showing off, and not for fame, his sins will be purified as a garment is purified in water, leaving no stain upon it. And Allah will record for him, for every step he takes, a pilgrimage (hajj), and for every time he lifts his foot, an expedition (umrah).

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah, from Salih al-Nayli, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, Allah writes for him the reward of freeing one thousand slaves, and like the reward of one who rides a thousand saddled and bridled horses in the cause of Allah."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Mi'za, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does not visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until he dies, he is deficient in faith and deficient in religion; if he is admitted to Paradise, he will be below the believers in it.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami from Abd Allah ibn Hammad from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about one who neglects the visitation of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he is capable of doing so?' He said, 'He has disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and disobeyed us, and he has belittled a matter that is for him. And whoever visits him, Allah will be for him behind his needs, and he will be sufficient for whatever concerns him from the affairs of his world. Indeed, it brings sustenance to the servant and replaces what he spends, and his sins of fifty years are forgiven, and he returns to his family with no burden or sin upon him except that it has been erased from his record. If he dies on his journey, the angels descend, wash him, and a door to Paradise is opened for him, its spirit entering him until he is raised. And if he is safe, the door through which his sustenance descends is opened for him, and for every dirham he spent, ten thousand dirhams are made for him, and that is stored for him. So when he is resurrected, it is said to him, 'For you, for every dirham, ten thousand dirhams. Indeed, Allah looked out for you and stored it for you with Him.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, that al-Abbas narrated to him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Saqqaf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Ali, it has reached me that some people from our Shia pass by one year, two years, or more than that, without visiting al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I know many people with this description.' He said, 'By Allah, they have missed their due portion, turned away from the reward of Allah, and distanced themselves from the proximity of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise.' I said, 'If a man sends someone else on his behalf, does that suffice for him?' He said, 'Yes, and his going himself is greater in reward and better for him with his Lord.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (1) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Khaybari from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) - on the bank of the Euphrates - is like one who has visited God above His Throne."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Safarjala al-Kufi said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Mansur said: He narrated to us Harb ibn al-Husayn from Ibrahim al-Shaybani from Abu al-Jarud said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'A day and a bit.' He said to him: 'If we were like you are, we would have taken it as a Hijra (migration/exile).'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is nothing in the heavens but they ask Allāh to permit them to visit al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him); a group descends and a group ascends.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes the Hajj eludes me, so I will go to be a pilgrim (mu'arrif) at the grave of Husayn, recognizing his right.' He said: 'Well done, O Bashir. Any believer who visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, on a day other than Eid, Allah will write for him twenty Hajj pilgrimages and twenty Umrahs, all accepted and accepted, and twenty battles with a Messenger Prophet or an upright Imam. And whoever visits him on the day of Eid, Allah will write for him one hundred Hajj pilgrimages, one hundred Umrahs, and one hundred battles with a Messenger Prophet or an upright Imam.' I said: 'And how can I attain such a standing?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said: 'O Bashir, indeed when a believer visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, and performs ritual bath (ghusl) from the Euphrates, then turns towards it, Allah writes for him for every step a Hajj with all its rituals.' And I do not know except that he said: 'And an Umrah.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals twenty Hajj pilgrimages and is superior to twenty Umrah pilgrimages and one Hajj."

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Humayd ibn Ziyad informed us, from Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, who said: Wahb ibn Hafss narrated to me, from Abu Basir and 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seventy thousand angels were assigned to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); they pray for him, while disheveled and dusty, from the day he was killed until what Allah wills, meaning the rising of the Mahdi. They supplicate for whoever visits him, saying: 'O Lord, these are the visitors of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); do with them and do for them [what they deserve].'

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Allan, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, from Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn al-Mutawakkil, who said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Ali ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) three times during the year will be safe from poverty."

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Salih ibn Uqbah from Bashir al-Dahhan from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the first day of Rajab, God will certainly forgive him."

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Suhayl, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Abzari, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): In which month do we visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him)? He said: 'In the middle of Rajab and the middle of Sha'ban.'

Saad ibn Abdullah from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Zaytuni from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever wishes to be greeted by one hundred thousand prophets and twenty thousand prophets, let him visit the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) in the middle of Sha'ban, for indeed the souls of the prophets (peace be upon them) ask permission of Allah to visit him, and permission is granted to them."

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his men, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, a caller from the highest horizon calls out: 'O visitors of al-Husayn, return; your reward is forgiven, your recompense is with your Lord and Muhammad, your Prophet.'

Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: "When it is the Night of Decree, and 'in it is made clear every wise matter,' a caller will cry out that night from beneath the Throne: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has forgiven whoever visited the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on this night.'"

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from a group of his shaykhs, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Sayyar al-Mad'ani, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on one of three nights, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.' I said: 'Which nights, may I be your ransom?' He said: 'The night of al-Fitr, the night of al-Adha, and the night of the middle of Sha'ban.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: I was narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Mu'min, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him one million pilgrimages with the Awaited Imam (peace be upon him), and one million pilgrimages with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the freeing of one million souls, and one million mounts of horses in the cause of Allah. And Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will call him 'My truthful servant', he believed in My promise. And the angels will say: 'So-and-so is truthful, Allah purified him from above His Throne,' and he will be called on earth 'Cherub'.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Isma'il al-Qammadi, from Bashshar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is poor and the Hajj of Islam has not prepared for him, let him go to the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and offer his greetings; that will suffice him in place of the Hajj of Islam. Indeed, I do not say that this suffices in place of the Hajj of Islam except for the poor. As for the wealthy, if he has performed the Hajj of Islam and wishes to perform voluntary Hajj and Umrah but is prevented from that by worldly duties or an obstacle, let him go to Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafah; that will suffice him in place of fulfilling his Hajj and Umrah, and Allah will multiply for him thereby multiplied multiples. I asked: How much does it equal in reward for one Hajj and how much for one Umrah? He said: 'It cannot be counted.' I said: One hundred? He said: 'And who can count that?' I said: A thousand? He said: 'And more.' And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them. And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan from Muhammad ibn Yaḥyā from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥusayn from Muhammad ibn Ismāʿīl from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah from Bashīr al-Dahhān who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Bashīr, indeed when the believer visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ʿArafah, and performs ritual bath in the Euphrates, then turns towards it, Allah writes for him, with every step, a pilgrimage with all its rituals.' And I do not know him except to have said, 'and a military expedition.'

And from him, from Salamah ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mudarrab narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Haytham al-Nahdi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: Indeed, Allah begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) on the evening of 'Arafah before He looks at the people of the standing (at 'Arafah). He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'Because among those (visitors) are the children of fornication, and among these (people of 'Arafah) are not the children of fornication.'

And from him, from Abu Talib al-Anbari, who said: He informed me, Ali ibn Muhammad, that Muhammad ibn al-Abbas narrated to them from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hanan, when it is the Day of Arafah, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, looks upon the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and says to them: 'Begin anew, for you have been forgiven.'

And from him, from Salamah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Jubba'i, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb al-Bajali, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever performs the 'Arfah (standing/visiting) at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), has indeed witnessed 'Arafah.'

And it is narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) that he said: The signs of the believer are five: the prayer of fifty [rak'ahs], the visitation of forty [people/occasions], wearing a ring on the right hand, dusting the forehead [with earth during prostration], and reciting 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' aloud.

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Sandal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the reward for one who visits Husayn (peace be upon him) every month? He said: 'He has the reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, like the martyrs of Badr.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Rawwasi, from one who narrated to him from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever visits him, meaning al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and performs ablution and takes a ritual bath from the Euphrates, every time he raises a foot and every time he places a foot, Allah records for him the reward of one Hajj and one Umrah."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Azdi, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Allah are angels assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).
