So when a man intends to visit him and performs ritual bath, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) calls out to him: 'O caravan of Allah, rejoice in accompanying me in Paradise.' And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) calls out to him: 'I am guarantor for the fulfillment of your needs and the repulsion of calamity from you in this world and the Hereafter.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) surround them on their right and left sides until they return to their families.

And from him, from Ibn Hurayth, from Amr ibn al-Hasan al-Ushnani, who said: Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Ishaq al-Taymi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He was asked about the visitor to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Whoever performs ritual bath (ghusl) in the Euphrates, then walks to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for every step he raises and places, there is a accepted pilgrimage (hajj) with all its rites.'

And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Salamah ibn Muhammad, who said: He informed us that Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar from his father from his grandfather from Ayub ibn Nuh and others from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Yas' informed me, saying: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — and I was listening — about the ritual bath (ghusl) when one visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'No.'

And what was also narrated - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Is ibn al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), is there a ghusl for it? He said, 'No.' Thus, there is nothing in these two narrations that contradicts what we have previously stated, because his saying (peace be upon him), after the questioner asked about the ghusl of the visitation, 'No,' does not entail prohibition. Rather, he (peace be upon him) meant that there is no obligatory or compulsory ghusl in it, the leaving of which incurs punishment. And if there is a recommended, desirable ghusl in it, there is much merit in it. And if the intended meaning is what we mentioned, then there is no contradiction between these narrations. And it is desirable that what is said during the ghusl is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Abu Ahmad Isma'il ibn Isa ibn Muhammad al-Mudabbib, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath ibn Haytham in Egypt narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever visits my grave after my death is like one who migrated to me during my lifetime. If you cannot [visit], then send me greetings, for they reach me."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah from Ali ibn Saif ibn 'Amirah from Tufayl ibn Malik al-Nakha'i from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya from Safwan ibn Sulayman from his father from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: "Whoever visits me in my lifetime and after my death will be in my neighborhood/protection on the Day of Resurrection."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from al-Sindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to me as a visitor, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from Abu Yahya al-Aslami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to Mecca as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Medina, I will turn my face away from him on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever comes to me as a visitor, my intercession becomes obligatory for him, and whoever my intercession becomes obligatory for, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'It is like the reward of one who visits Allah above His Throne.'

And from him (Al-Hilli) from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Uthman ibn Isa from Al-Mu'alla ibn Shihab who said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O my father, what is the reward for one who visits you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, whoever visits me while alive or after death, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a right upon me to visit him on the Day of Resurrection and to clear him of his sins.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The meaning of the saying of the Truth-teller (peace be upon him): 'Whoever visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is like one who visits Allah above His Throne.' This means that for the visitor of him (peace be upon him) there is great reward, immense recompense, and honor on the Day of Resurrection, as if Allah raised him to His heaven and brought him close to His Throne which is borne by the angels, and showed him from among His special angels that which confirms his honor. And it is not according to what the common people assume from the implication of similarity (literalism).

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: Hakim ibn Dawud narrated to me, who narrated to me Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'The sacred precinct (haram) of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is five farsakhs from its four sides.'

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqṭīnī, from Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl al-Baṣrī, from whoever narrated it from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: The sanctuary of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is one farsakh by one farsakh from the four sides of the grave.

And from him (Al-Shaykh) it was said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: He said: 'Indeed, the place of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has a known sanctity; whoever knows it and seeks refuge in it is granted refuge.' I said: 'Describe its place for me, may I be your ransom.' He said: 'Wipe/rub from the place of his grave today twenty-five cubits from in front of it, and twenty-five cubits from near his head, and twenty-five cubits from the side of his feet, and twenty-five cubits from behind it. And the place of his grave, from the day he was buried, is a meadow from the meadows of Paradise, and from it is a ladder by which the deeds of its visitors are ascended to the sky. So there is no angel in the sky nor in the earth except that they ask Allah for the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A group descends and a group ascends.'

And 'Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: "The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is twenty cubits, broken [into sections], a garden from the gardens of Paradise." And there is no contradiction or conflict in these narrations; rather, they came in order of merit. The first report sets the limit for whoever attains the reward of the shrine if he is located at a distance of five farsakhs between himself and the grave. Then, the one who increases in merit is the one who is at one farsakh. Then, the one who is at twenty-five cubits. Then, the one who is at twenty cubits. And if the meaning intended by these measurements is what we mentioned, then they do not contradict or conflict. And that which indicates that the meaning intended by these narrations is the merit and blessing we pointed to.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Bunan, from Abu al-Tahir (meaning al-Warraq), from al-Hajjāl, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The soil from the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) [is valid for use] for ten miles."

And from him, from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Bazawfari, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Sinan from Amr ibn Thabit from his father from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah created Karbala before He created the Kaaba by twenty-four thousand years, and He sanctified it and blessed it, so it remained sanctified and blessed before Allah created the creation, and it will remain thus, and Allah made it the most superior of the earth in Paradise.

And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, who said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from whoever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) set out, traveling with the people. When he was about a mile or two from Karbala, he advanced ahead of them until he reached the places of prostration of the martyrs. He said: 'Two hundred prophets, two hundred successors, and two hundred tribesmen were taken (as martyrs) there with their followers.' He then circled it on his she-camel, his feet out of the stirrups, and began to say: 'A resting place for camels and places of prostration for martyrs; those who came before them cannot precede them, and those who come after them cannot catch up with them.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Zuhri narrated to us, who said: Bakr ibn Salim narrated to us from his father, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). Regarding His saying, 'And she carried Him and withdrew with Him to a remote place,' he said: 'She went out from Damascus until she reached Karbala, and placed Him in the location of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), then she returned on the same night.' And from him, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Sa'id, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'In the clay/mud of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is the cure from every disease, and it is the greatest medicine.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Inculcate your children with the soil of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for it is a protection.'

And from him, from his father, from Saad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Rizq Allah ibn al-Ala', from Sulayman ibn Umar al-Sarraj, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave within a radius of seventy cubits.

And from him, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his father, from some of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted created Adam from clay, so He forbade clay to his offspring. I said: 'What do you say about the clay of the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'It is forbidden for people to eat their flesh, and it is permissible for them to eat our flesh, but a small amount of it is like a chickpea.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Adib, said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Saqqaf, known as Abu Salih, narrated to us, raising it to some of the companions of Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both). He said: I entered upon him, and he said: 'Our Shias must not dispense with four things: a cloth upon which they pray, a ring with which they seal, a miswak with which they clean their teeth, and a tasbih (prayer beads) made from the clay of the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), containing thirty-three beads. Whenever they turn them while remembering Allah, forty good deeds are recorded for each bead; and if they turn them while heedless, playing with them, twenty good deeds are recorded for them.'

And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said: I wrote to the Faqih (peace be upon him) asking him: Is it permissible for a man to perform tasbih (glorification) with the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and is there merit in it? He answered, and I read the Tawqi' (autograph reply) and copied from it: 'He performs tasbih with it. There is nothing in tasbih superior to it. And from its merit is that the one who performs tasbih forgets the tasbih (due to absorption), and he rotates the subhah (prayer beads), so that tasbih is recorded for him.'

And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said: I wrote to the Jurist (peace be upon him) asking him about the clay of the grave: is it placed with the deceased in his grave, is that permissible or not? So he answered, and I read the signature (tawqi'), and from it I copied: 'It is placed with the deceased in his grave and mixed with its perfume, if God wills.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him), visit him while you are sorrowful, distressed, unkempt, dusty, hungry, and thirsty, and ask him for your needs, then depart, and do not take him as a permanent resident."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Salih ibn al-Sindiyy al-Jammal, from a man from the people of Ar-Raqqa who is called Abu Madha', who said: A man said to me: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'They come to the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and make it their dining mat (sufrah). Indeed, if they came to the graves of their fathers and mothers, they would not do that.' I said: 'So what do they eat?' He said: 'Bread and milk.'
It is narrated from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said: "Whoever visits me, his sins are forgiven, and he does not die poor."

And it is narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Askari (peace be upon him) that he said: "Whoever visits Ja'far and his father will not suffer from eye ailments, nor will illness befall him, nor will he die while being tested (with trials)."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from his father who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Sindi from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi from Abdullah ibn Musa from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: "Indeed, for every Imam there is a covenant upon the neck of his allies and his Shia, and among the completion of fulfilling the covenant and good performance is the visiting of their graves. So whoever visits them with desire for their visitation and affirmation of what they desired, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn 'Uqba from Zayd al-Shahham said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who visits one of you?' He said, '(It is) like the one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you enter the city, perform ghusl before entering it or when you enter it, then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and send greetings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then stand at the forward pillar on the right side of the grave, at the head of the grave, facing the qibla, with your left shoulder towards the grave and your right shoulder towards what faces the pulpit, for that is the place of the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. And I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that you are Muhammad ibn Abdillah. And I bear witness that you conveyed the messages of your Lord, were sincere to your ummah, strove in the path of Allah, and worshipped Allah until certainty came to you with wisdom and good admonition, and you fulfilled what was upon you of the truth, and that you were gentle with the believers and firm with the disbelievers. So Allah brought you to the highest honor of the station of the honored. Praise is to Allah who saved us through you from polytheism and misguidance. O Allah, so make Your prayer, and the prayer of Your neared angels, and Your righteous servants, and Your sent prophets, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and whoever glorified You, O Lord of the worlds, from the first and the last, upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger and Prophet and Trustworthy and Noble and Beloved and Special and Chosen and Purest and Best of Your creation. O Allah, grant him the rank and give him the proximity from Paradise, and raise him to a Praised Station with which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, indeed You said: 'And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to You and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah to be Accepting of Repentance, Merciful.' And I have come to you seeking forgiveness, repenting from my sins, and I turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, my Lord an

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'How is the greeting to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?' He said: 'Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Peace be upon you, O beloved of Allah. Peace be upon you, O choice of Allah. Peace be upon you, O trustee of Allah. I bear witness that you have been sincere to your community, and you strove in the path of Allah, and you worshipped Him until certainty came to you. So may Allah reward you with the best reward a prophet has received for his community. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, with the best blessings You sent upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from some of our companions, who said: I was present with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), Harun al-Khalifah, Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya in Medina. They came to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Harun stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood aside. Then Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Isa stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood with Harun. Then Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan, 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Ja'far stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood with Harun. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) stepped forward and said, 'Peace be upon you, O my father. I ask Allah, who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided [people] through you, to send blessings upon you.' Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he say what I heard?' Isa said, 'Yes.' Harun said, 'I bear witness that he is truly his father.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray facing the side of the Prophet's grave (peace be upon him and his family), even if the prayer of the believer reaches him wherever they are.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you have finished supplicating at the grave, go to the pulpit (minbar), wipe it with your hands, and hold its two pommels (rummanatayn), which are the suflawans, then wipe your eyes and face, for it is said that it is a cure for the eye. Stand by it, praise Allah, extol Him, and ask for your need, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is between my pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is on a pasture from the pastures of Paradise.' And the 'tur'ah is the small door. Then go to the station of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and pray in it as long as you wish. When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and when you leave, do the same, and increase your prayers in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is between my pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon a pasture from the pastures of Paradise, and a prayer in my mosque equals a thousand prayers in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque.' Jamil said to him: 'Are the houses of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the house of Ali (peace be upon him) among them?' He said: 'Yes, O Jamil, and they are superior.'

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The boundary of the Rawdah (Garden) is from the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the edge of the Zillal, and the boundary of the Mosque is to the two pillars on the right of the pulpit to the road from the side facing the Night Market.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say, 'What is between my pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise?' He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'The house of Ali and Fatimah (peace be upon her) is what is between the house in which the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is, to the door that faces the alley, to al-Baqi'.' He said, 'If you entered from that door, with the wall in its place, your left shoulder would touch it; then he named the other houses.' And he said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said,

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the prayer in the house of Fatimah (peace be upon her) more virtuous, or in the Rawdah?' He said, 'In the house of Fatimah (peace be upon her).'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fudayla ibn Ayyub and Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Go to the standing place of Gabriel (peace be upon him), which is under the be upon him), and it is beneath the gutter, for it was his standing place when he sought permission from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then say: I ask you, O Generous, O Noble, O Close, O Distant, to send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and I ask you to return my favor." He said, "And that is a standing place where a menstruating woman who faces the qibla does not supplicate with the supplication of blood except that she sees purity, if God wills." And the Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) mentioned in the Risala that you come to Al-Rawdah and visit Fatimah (peace be upon her) because she is buried there. And our companions have differed regarding the location of her grave: some of them said that she was buried in Al-Baqi', and some of them said that she was buried in Al-Rawdah, and some of them said that she was buried in her house. And when the Banu Umayya (may God curse them) added to the mosque, it became part of the mosque. And these two narrations are similar, and the best in my opinion is that the person visits both places, for that will not harm him and he will acquire great reward through it. As for whoever said that she was buried in Al-Baqi', that is far from the truth. And what has been narrated regarding the virtue of visiting her is more than can be counted, and he has narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy who said: Ali ibn Sulayman al-Zurari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Khaybari from Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik from his father from his grandfather who said: I entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her), and she initiated me with the greeting of peace, then she said, 'What has brought you?' I said, 'Seeking blessings.' She said, 'My father informed me, and he is as he is, that whoever greets him and me for three days, Allah has made Paradise obligatory for him.' I said to her, 'During his life and your life?' She said, 'Yes, and after our death.' And as for the words said upon visiting her (peace be upon her), it has been narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Salamah ibn Muhammad, who said: 'Ahmad ibn Ali Aban al-Qummi informed us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from al-Rida (peace be upon him):' He said: 'I asked him about the visitation of the grave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), is it like the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Yes.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Habash ibn Quniyy, who said: Ali ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Khaybari, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Qummi, who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Baghdad is like the one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), except that the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful have their own distinct superiority.'

And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, from his father, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Miysar, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'What is for the one who visits your father?' He said, 'Paradise. So visit him.'

And from him, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Dawud, who said: Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Husayn ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of your father?' He said, 'Visit him.' I said, 'What is the virtue in it?' He said, 'The virtue in it is like the virtue of one who visits the grave of his father, meaning the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said, 'Indeed, I feared and was not able to enter a [covered] place.' He said, 'Send greetings from behind the bridge.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: Ahmad ibn Bundar narrated to us from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ja'far al-Jawhari, from Zakariyya ibn Adam al-Qummi, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: "Indeed, Allah saved Baghdad because of the location of the two tombs of the Al-Husayns within it."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, is the visitation of Al-Rida (peace be upon him) superior or the visitation of Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'The visitation of my father is superior, and that is because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is visited by all people, whereas my father is visited only by the elite of the Shi'a.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'mar) from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Al-Husayn ibn Saif from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Muhammad ibn Sulayman who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the Hajj of Islam (his first obligatory Hajj), entering into Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break), and Allah enabled him to complete his Umrah and Hajj. Then he went to Medina, offered salams to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then came to you, acknowledging your right, knowing that you are the proof of Allah upon His creation and the door through which one is approached. He offered salams to you, then went to Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and offered salams to him, then went to Baghdad and offered salams to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). Then he returned to his land. When the time for Hajj came, Allah granted him the means to perform Hajj. Which is better for this man who has already performed the Hajj of Islam: that he returns again and performs Hajj, or that he goes to Khorasan to your father - Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him) and offers salams to him? He said: 'He goes to Khorasan and offers salams to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that is better. And let that be in Rajab, and it is not fitting that you do this on this day, for there is a danger from the Sultan upon us and upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi from Ibrahim ibn Ahmad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Makki from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Mazin from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali, he will have with Allah the reward of seventy accepted pilgrimages.' I said: 'Seventy pilgrimages?' He said: 'Yes, and seventy thousand pilgrimages.' I said: 'Seventy thousand pilgrimages?' He said: 'Perhaps a pilgrimage is not accepted; whoever visits him and spends the night at his side is like one who visited Allah upon His Throne.' I said: 'Like one who visited Allah upon His Throne?' He said: 'Yes. On the Day of Resurrection, there will be upon the Throne of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, four from the earlier [prophets] and four from the later [prophets]. As for the four who are from the earlier ones: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them). And as for the latter ones: Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). Then the track (of honor) is extended, so whoever visits the graves of the Imams will sit with us, but the highest in rank and the closest in crawling [of honor] are the visitors of the grave of my son Ali.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I read the book of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) in his own handwriting: 'Convey to my Shias that my visitation (Ziyarah) equals in the sight of Allah one thousand accepted Hajjs and one thousand accepted Umras in their entirety.' I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajjs?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, and one thousand thousand Hajjs for whoever visits him while being cognizant of his right.'

And from him, from his father Ahmad ibn Dawud, from Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'Whoever visits my father, for him is Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn Uqba from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits one of you?' He said, 'Like the reward of one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, for every Imam there is a covenant upon the neck of his allies and his Shia, and among the completion of fulfilling the covenant and good performance is the visiting of their graves. So whoever visits them with desire for their visitation and affirmation of what they desired, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.'

Three - Muhammad ibn Hammam from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhur, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Rawh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to me: "My grave is in Sarman; there is safety for the people of the two sides."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Hassan ibn Mihran who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Mecca is the sanctuary of Allah, and Medina is the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Kufa is my sanctuary. A tyrant who transgresses in it, Allah will break him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Makkah is the Sanctuary of Allah, which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sanctified. And Al-Madinah is my Sanctuary; what is between its two 'labatayn' is a sanctuary where its trees are not to be cut. This is what is between the shadow of 'A'ir and the shadow of 'U'ayr. And the game of Al-Madinah is not like the game of Makkah; this one is eaten and that one is not eaten, and it is 'Barid'.'

And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban one, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made Medina sacred.' He said, 'Yes, a Bairid within a Bairid, contiguous.' I said, 'Its game (hunting)?' He said, 'People do not lie.' (i.e., the report is authentic/established). So what these two reports encompass regarding that the game of Medina is not forbidden, the intended meaning is that which is between the Bairid and the Bairid, and it is the shadow of 'A'ir to the shadow of Wa'ir, and what is forbidden is that which is between the two Harratayn, and by them the game of this sanctuary is distinguished from the sanctuary of Mecca, because the game of Mecca is forbidden in the entire sanctuary, and it is not so in the sanctuary of Medina, because that which is forbidden from it is the specific portion, and that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and al-Nadr and Hammad from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, all of them, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The hunting of the city (Madinah) is forbidden, that which is between the two lava flows (al-Harratayn)."

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The boundary of Al-Rawdah is from the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to the edge of Al-Zhialal, and the boundary of the Mosque is to the two pillars on the right of the pulpit to the road from the side facing the Night Market."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Zayyat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever dies in Al-Madinah, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, will resurrect him among the trustworthy (Al-Aminin) on the Day of Resurrection." Among them are Yahya ibn Habib, Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj. This is from the speech of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id al-Zayyat.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, He said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior: staying in Mecca or staying in Medina?' He said, 'What do you say?' I said, 'And what is my saying in comparison to your saying?' He said, 'Indeed, your saying is referred back to my saying.' I said to him, 'As for me, I believe that staying in Medina is superior to staying in Mecca.' He said, 'If you say that, then indeed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said that - on the Day of Fitr (Eid al-Fitr), when he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and greeted him in the mosque, then he said, "We have been favored today over the people by our greeting upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)."'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ibn Abi Ya'fur asked him, 'How many rak'at should I pray?' He said, 'Pray eight rak'at at the time of the sun's declination (Dhuhr), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Prayer in my mosque is like a thousand [prayers] in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque, for prayer in the Sacred Mosque equals a thousand prayers in my mosque.'

And from him, from Hammad, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prayer in my mosque equals a thousand prayers in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), for it is superior to it.'

And from him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A prayer in my mosque is like a thousand prayers in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), for indeed it is better than a thousand prayers.'

And from him, from Safwan and Fadala and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), how much the prayer in it is equivalent to? He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: A prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except for the Sacred Mosque.'

From him (Al-Shaykh) said: Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If you have a stay in Medina for three days, you should fast on the first day, Wednesday, and pray during the night of Wednesday at the pillar of Abu Lubabah, which is the Pillar of Repentance, where he tied himself to it until his excuse descended from the sky. You should sit at it on Wednesday. Then, on the night of Thursday, go to the pillar next to it, facing the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), spend your night and day there, and fast on Thursday. Then go to the pillar next to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his prayer spot, on the night of Friday, pray there spending your night and day, and fast on Friday. If you can refrain from speaking anything during these days, do so, except for what is necessary. Do not leave the mosque except for a need, and do not sleep during the night or day. Do this, for that is among what is considered for merit. Then, on Friday, praise God, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask for your need. Let what you say be: 'O God, whatever need I have of You, whether I began seeking and requesting it or did not begin, whether I asked You for it or did not ask You, I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, peace be upon him and his family, for the fulfillment of my needs, small and large. Indeed, You are worthy that your need be fulfilled for you, if God wills.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Amiri from Safwan from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'In the Mu'arras (the place where the Prophet's tent was pitched), the Mu'arras of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): When you return to Medina, pass by it, dismount, let down its load, and pray in it, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did that.' I said: 'What if it is not the time for prayer?' He said: 'Then establish the call to prayer (Iqamah).' I said: 'My companions will not establish it.' He said: 'Then pray two rak'ahs and proceed.' And he said: 'The Mu'arras is [specifically] when you return to Medina, not when you set out.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Asbat, who said: I said to Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him): Ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated from you and informed us from you about returning to the 'Urras (the place of staying/resting), but we had not stayed there, so we returned to him. What should we do? He said: 'You pray and lie down for a little while, and indeed Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to pray in it and sit.' Muammad ibn Ali ibn Fadhl said: 'If I pass through it at a time other than prayer time, after Asr prayer,' He said: 'It was asked of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: 'Pray in it.'' Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl said to him: 'If you pass through it at night or during the day, do you stay there (make 'Urras), or is the staying only at night?' He said: 'Yes, if you pass through it at night or during the day, then stay there (make 'Urras), for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya' ibn Ya'qub from 'Ali' ibn Ibraheem from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad' ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl from Safwan and Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, he said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect visiting all the shrines: Masjid Quba, for it is the mosque which was "founded on piety from the first day"; and Mashrabah of Umm Ibrahim (peace be upon him); and Masjid al-Fadikh; and the graves of the martyrs; and Masjid al-Ahzab, which is Masjid al-Fath.' He said: 'And we have reached that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when he visited the graves of the martyrs would say: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; excellent is the final abode."' And let what you say at Masjid al-Fath be: "O Cryer of the distressed, and O Responder to the supplication of the needy, remove my anxiety, my sorrow, and my distress, just as You removed from Your Prophet his anxiety, his sorrow, and his distress, and protected him from the terror of his enemy in this place."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We visit the mosques around the city, so which one should I start with? He said: 'Start with Quba and pray in it and increase [prayer], for it is the first mosque in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed in this area. Then go to the Mashrabah of Umm Ibrahim (peace be upon her) and pray in it, for it is the dwelling place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer. Then you come to the Mosque of Fadikh and pray in it, for your Prophet has prayed in it. When you have finished this side, you come to the side of Uhud, and you start with the mosque that is below the Harra, and you pray in it. Then you pass by the grave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (peace be upon him) and send greetings upon him. Then you pass by the graves of the martyrs and stand by them and say: Peace be upon you, O people of the dwellings, you are forerunners for us and we will surely follow you. Then you come to the mosque in the spacious place next to the mountain on your right when you enter Uhud, and pray in it. For it is there that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out to Uhud where he met the polytheists, and they did not leave until the prayer time arrived, so he prayed in it. Then pass by again until you return, and pray at the graves of the martyrs as much as Allah has decreed for you. Then proceed on your way until you come to the Mosque of the Confederates (Al-Ahzab), and pray in it and supplicate to Allah in it. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated in it on the Day of the Confederates. And he said: 'O Cryer of those who cry for help, and O Responder of those in distress, and O Helper of those in anxiety, remove my grief, my worry, and my distress, for you see my condition and the condition of my companions.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhl, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mosque of al-Fadikh, why it was called the Mosque of al-Fadikh, so he said: 'The date palms are called al-Fadikh, therefore it is called the Mosque of al-Fadikh.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about praying in the mosque of Ghadir Khumm during the day while I am a traveler, so he said: 'Pray in it, for there is virtue in it, and my father used to command that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is recommended to pray in the Mosque of Ghadir because the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) there, and it is the place where God, the Mighty and Majestic, manifested the Truth.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn Hadid from Murram narrated, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fasting in Al-Madinah and standing (in prayer) near the pillars is not obligatory, but whoever wishes may fast, for it is better for him. The only obligatory things are the five daily prayers and fasting the month of Ramadan. So increase your prayers in this mosque as much as you can, for it is better for you. And know that a man may be shrewd in worldly affairs, so it is said, 'How shrewd so-and-so is!' So how about the one who is shrewd in the affairs of his Hereafter?'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam from his father who said: I walked with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in al-Baqi', and we passed by the grave of a man from the people of Kufa from the Shia. I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, this is the grave of a man from the Shia.' So he (peace be upon him) stood by it and then said: 'O God, have mercy on his strangeness (being away from home), connect his solitude, comfort his loneliness, and send down to him from Your mercy a mercy with which he will be content with instead of the mercy of anyone other than You, and join him with whomever was his guardian.' Then he recited: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree,' seven times.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn Amr from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'How should I place my hand on the graves of the Muslims?' So he pointed with his hand to the ground, placed it upon it, while he was facing the Qibla.

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Haydarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Jihad is the best of matters after the obligatory duties."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Abdullah ibn al-Munbih from Husayn ibn Alwan from Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his father from his forefathers, peace be upon them, said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For the martyr are seven characteristics from Allah: First, with the first drop of his blood, all his sins are forgiven; Second, his head rests in the lap of his two wives from the Hur al-Ayn, and they wipe the dust from his face, saying 'Welcome,' and he says the same to them; Third, he is clothed with the garments of Paradise; Fourth, the keepers of Paradise vie with each other to take him with them, each offering a pleasant breeze; Fifth, his station is shown to him; Sixth, it is said to his soul, 'Roam in Paradise wherever you wish'; Seventh, he gazes upon the face of Allah. And indeed, this is a rest for every Prophet and Martyr.'

And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ghazwan, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Above every person of goodness is goodness, until he is killed in the cause of Allah; so when he is killed in the cause of Allah, there is no goodness above him. And above every person of disobedience is disobedience, until he kills one of his two parents; so when he kills one of his two parents, there is no disobedience above him.

From him, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Dirar ibn Amr al-Shimshati, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud al-Kinani, from Uthman ibn Ma'sun, who said: I said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'My soul inclines me to travel (siyahah) and to join the mountains.' He said, 'O Uthman, do not do that, for the travel (siyahah) of my nation is the expedition (ghazw) and striving (jihad).'

Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'All goodness is in the sword, and under the shadow of the sword, and the sword is what keeps people in order, and the swords are the keys to Paradise and Hell.'

Aban ibn Uthman from Isa ibn Abdillah al-Qummi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three people's supplication is answered: one of them is the warrior (mujahid) in the path of Allah, so see how you leave him (in his absence).

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Mujahideen. They proceed towards it, and when they arrive, it is open while they are wearing their swords, the congregation is in the standing position, and the angels are driving them forward. So whoever leaves Jihad, God will clothe him with humiliation and poverty in his livelihood, and destruction in his religion. Indeed, God honored my Ummah with the forelocks of their horses and the thrusts of their spears.'

From him, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever conveys the message of a warrior is like one who freed a slave, and he is a partner with him in the reward of his campaign."

Al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'A thousand strikes with the sword are lighter than dying on one's bed.' He said, 'In the cause of God.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id from Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Muhammadi al-Alawi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi from Ali ibn al-Abbas from Isma'il ibn Ishaq, all from Abu Rawh Faraj ibn Abi Farwa from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, who said: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to me from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Jihad is a door that Allah opened for His special friends, and He permitted it for them as a favor from Him, and a blessing He reserved for them. And Jihad is the garment of piety, and the sturdy armor of Allah, and His fortress (1) the secure bond. So whoever leaves it out of desire for it, Allah will clothe him with the garment of humiliation and the cloak of affliction, and he will depart from comfort, and a seal will be placed upon his heart with similar [seals], and he will be effeminated by smallness and meanness (2), and he will be branded with the mark of depression, and he will be deprived of the half [of his due], and the right will be taken from him due to his neglect of Jihad. And Allah became angry with him for leaving His support. And indeed Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said in the clear part of His Book: 'If you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.' (1)

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from one who narrated it from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) said: "The ribat (military vigil/garrisoning) is three days, and its maximum is forty days; if one exceeds that, it is considered jihad."

From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, who said: A man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while I was present, and he said to him: 'May I be your ransom, indeed a man from your mawali heard that a man gives a sword and a horse in the cause of Allah, so he went to him and took them from him. Then his companions met him and informed him that the 'cause' (with these people) is not valid, and they ordered him to return them. He said: 'Let him do so.' He said: 'The man has sought him but did not find him, and it was said to him: The man has departed.' He said: 'Let him perform murabahah (border guard duty) and not fight.' I said: 'Like Qazwin and Asqalan and Daylam and what resembles these frontiers?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'If the enemy comes to the place where he is performing murabahah, what should he do?' He said: 'He fights for the egg of Islam.' I said: 'Does he strive/jihad?' He said: 'No, unless he fears for the offspring of the Muslims.' I said: 'I ask you, if the Romans entered upon the Muslims, should they not prevent them?' He said: 'He performs murabahah and does not fight. If he fears for the egg of Islam and the Muslims, he fights, so his fighting is for himself, not for the Sultan, because in the layers of Islam are the layers of the mention of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Sa'id, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about these people who are killed in these frontiers (thughur)?' He said, 'Woe to them! They hasten to a death in the world and a death in the Hereafter. And by God, the martyr is none of us, even if they die on their beds.'

4. Ali ibn Mahziyar said: A man from Banu Hashim wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second Imam), peace be upon him: 'I had vowed two years ago to go out to a coast among the coasts of the sea, to our region, where the volunteers perform ribat (guarding), similar to their ribat posts - in Jeddah and other coasts of the sea. Do you think, may I be your ransom, that I am obliged to fulfill it, or not? Or should I redeem the going out to that place with something from the gates of righteousness (charity), so that I may attain it, if God wills?' He wrote to him in his own hand, and I read it: 'If one of the rivals (or opponents) heard your vow from you, then fulfillment is obligatory upon you, if you fear their taunt (shun'ah); and if not, then spend what you intended of that in the gates of righteousness. May God grant us and you success in what He loves and is pleased with.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from Sa'd ibn ibn Dhara'if, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubat, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Allah has made Jihad obligatory upon men and women. The Jihad of the man is to expend his wealth and self until he is killed in the way of Allah, and the Jihad of the woman is to be patient with what she sees of her husband's annoyance and jealousy."

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "O Abd al-Malik, why do I not see you going out to these places that the people of your country go to?" I said: "And where?" He said: "Jeddah, Abbadan, al-Masissah, and Qazvin." I said: "Awaiting your command and following your example." He said: "Yes, by Allah, if it were good, they would have preceded us to it." I said: "Indeed, the Zaydiyyah say that there is no difference between us and Ja'far except that he does not consider Jihad (to be obligatory)." He said: "I do not consider it (obligatory), by Allah, I do consider it, but I dislike that I should make my knowledge known to their ignorance."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said, I think he did so from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he wished to send out a raiding party, would call them and seat them before him, then say: 'Go in the name of Allah and with Allah and in the way of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Do not be excessive (in taking spoils), do not mutilate, do not betray, do not kill an old man, a child, or a woman, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to do so. And whoever of the Muslims, whether lowly or noble, looks at a polytheist, he is a neighbor (under protection) until he hears the word of Allah. If he follows you, then he is your brother in your religion; and if he refuses, then convey him to his place of safety, then rely upon Allah against him.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he wished to send a commander over a raiding party, order him to have God-consciousness for himself specifically, and then for his companions generally. Then he would say: 'Go forth in the name of God and fight in the path of God those who disbelieve in God, and do not be treacherous, do not usurp the khums, do not mutilate, do not kill a child, and do not kill a hermit in a high place. Do not burn the palm trees, do not drown them with water, do not cut down a fruit-bearing tree, and do not burn crops, for you do not know, perhaps you will need them. And do not kill animals whose meat is edible, except what you must eat.' And when you meet the enemy from the polytheists, invite them to one of three things. If they respond to it, accept from them and cease from them. Invite them to Islam, and cease from them. And invite them to migration after Islam. If they do so, accept from them and cease from them. And if they refuse to migrate, and choose their own lands, and refuse to enter into the land of migration, they are like the Bedouin believers; what applies to the Bedouin believers applies to them. And do not give them any share of the spoils from the distribution, unless they fight in the path of God. If they refuse these two, invite them to paying the jizya: 'with a willing heart while they are humbled'. If they give the jizya, accept from them and cease from them. And if they refuse, seek help from God against them and fight them: 'In God, strive his true striving'. When you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to accept their surrender based on God's ruling, do not accept their surrender based on God's ruling, but accept their surrender based on my ruling, then judge among them afterward as you wish, for if you accept their surrender based on God's ruling, you do not know whether you have hit upon God's ruling for them or not. When you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to accept their surrender under the guarantee of God and the guarantee of His Messenger, do not accept their surrender under the guarantee of God and His Messenger, but accept their surrender under your guarantees and the guarantees of your fathers and your brothers,

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, both of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when sending out a raiding party, summon its commander and seat him by his side, and seat his companions in front of him, then say: 'Proceed in the name of Allah and with Allah and in the path of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Do not betray, do not be greedy, do not mutilate, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to do so. Do not kill an elder, a child, or a woman. Whoever of the Muslims, whether the lowest or the highest, looks at one of the polytheists, he is a neighbor to him until he hears the word of Allah. If they follow you, then they are your brothers in your religion; and if they refuse, seek help against them from Allah and convey them to their place of safety.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked, 'What is the meaning of the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'The lowest among them ensures the safety of the highest among them'?' He said, 'If an army of Muslims besieged a group of polytheists, and a man from them climbed up (to the walls) and said, 'Give me security so that I may meet your leader and negotiate with him,' and they gave him security, the lowest among them ensures it, and it becomes obligatory upon the highest among them to fulfill it.'

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah ibn Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no man who grants security to a man under his protection (dhimmah) and then kills him, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying the banner of treachery.'

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Aban, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: "If a group besieged a city and asked them for safety (aman), and they said 'No', but the besieged thought they said 'Yes', and they descended into the city, they are safe (guaranteed safety)."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: I read in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wrote a treaty between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who joined them from the people of Yathrib: That every raiding party that raids with us, one supports the other with fairness and equity among the Muslims; and that no sanctuary is granted except with the permission of its people; and that the neighbor is like the self, neither harming nor sinning; and the sanctity of the neighbor is like the sanctity of his mother and father; a Muslim does not make peace alone without other Muslims in a battle in the cause of Allah, except on the basis of justice and equality.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: Indeed the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Kill the polytheists, but spare their elders and their children.'

From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, Abu Ayyub, who said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed me, saying: Some of my brothers wrote to me to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a city among the cities of war: Is it permissible to send water upon them, or to burn them with fire, or to bombard them with catapults until they are killed, while among them are women, children, the elderly, captives from among the Muslims, and merchants? He said: 'That is done to them, and they are not held back for these [others]; there is no blood money (diyah) for them among the Muslims, nor is there ransom (kaffarah).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Ima' ibn al-Fudayl said: I asked him about the polytheists: Do the Muslims initiate combat against them in the sacred month? He said, 'If the polytheists initiate against them by deeming it permissible (to fight), then the Muslims see that they will prevail over them in it, and that is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'The sacred month is in return for the sacred month, and for all things, retaliation'. And the Romans (Byzantines) in this regard are like the polytheists, because they did not know the sanctity or the right of the sacred month. So they initiate combat in it. And the polytheists considered it to have a right and sanctity, so they deemed it permissible (to fight) and it was deemed permissible against them. And the people of rebellion (ahl al-bagh) are initiated against with combat.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade throwing poison in the lands of the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked him about two groups, one of which is the insurgents (baaghah) and the other is the just party (ahl al-adl), and the just party defeated the insurgents. He said: 'It is not permissible for the just party to pursue a fleeing enemy, nor to kill a captive, nor to finish off a wounded one. This is if no one remains from the insurgents and they do not have a force to which they can return. But if they have a force to which they can return, then their captive is killed, their fleeing one is pursued, and their wounded one is finished off.'

From al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abu al-Bakhtari from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Fighting is of two types: Fighting for the people of polytheism, from whom they are not dismissed until they accept Islam or pay the jizyah with their own hands while they are subdued. With their own hands while they are subdued. And fighting for the people of deviation, from whom they are not dismissed until they return to the command of Allah or are killed.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: A man from the Banu Fulan was mentioned to him, so he said: 'We only oppose them when we are with these people who rose up in Kufah.' He said: 'Fight them, for indeed the offspring of Fulan are like the Turks and the Romans, and they are a frontier (thighr) among the frontiers of the enemy, so fight them.'

Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) finished with the people of Nahrawan, he said: 'After me, only those who are more entitled to the truth than he is will fight them.'

From him, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There was a blessing in Ali's (peace be upon him) fighting the people of the Qibla (those who rebelled while still Muslim). And if Ali (peace be upon him) had not fought them, no one after him would have known how to proceed with them.'

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The Khawarij are doubtful/hesitant.' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then some of his companions asked, 'How is that, while they call to righteousness?' He said, 'That is what they find within themselves.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: The Haruriyyah (Khawarij) were mentioned before Ali (peace be upon him). He said: 'If they rise up against a just Imam or a group, fight them. And if they rise up against a biased/unjust Imam, do not fight them, for they have a valid argument in that.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: He was asked about the distribution of the treasury (bayt al-mal), so he said: 'The people of Islam are the children of Islam. I equalize among them in the stipend (ata'), and their virtues are between them and God; I group them together like the sons of one man, not preferring any one of them over another in inheritance due to his excellence or righteousness, if the other is weak or deficient.' And he said: 'This is the action of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) at the beginning of his affair. And others among us, whom we precede, say: We prioritize them in the stipend based on what God has favored them with due to their precedents in Islam. If they were in Islam, they attained that, so we assign them according to the inheritance of those of kinship, some being closer to others, and having a larger share due to their closeness to the deceased. And they were inherited through their kinship, and that is what Umar used to do.'

Al-Saffar from Ali ibn Isma'il from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from al-Husayn ibn Abdillah from his father from his grandfather from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: "If a man has multiple horses during the expedition (ghazw), shares (sahm) are allotted only for two of them."

Al-Saffar from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father, peace be upon them both, said: "That 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to assign three shares to the cavalryman and one share to the infantryman." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The compiler of this book does not contradict this report with the report we previously cited from Hafs ibn Ghiyath: "That the cavalryman has two shares and the infantryman has one share." Because the way to reconcile the two reports is that for the cavalryman, if he has only one horse, he has two shares: one for himself and one for his horse. And if he has two horses with him, he has three shares: one for himself and two for his two horses. And we have previously mentioned before this report that if he has multiple horses, shares are assigned only for two of them. And upon this interpretation, there is no contradiction between the two reports, and that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Abi al-Bakhtari from Ja'far from his father, peace be upon them both: That Ali (peace be upon him) used to allocate three shares for the cavalryman: two shares for his horse and one share for himself, and he allocated one share for the infantryman.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, that Ali (peace be upon him) said: "When a child is born in the land of war, a share is allocated for him from the spoils (fay') that Allah has granted them."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from one of the Imams of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the women with him in the war, and they treated the wounded. He did not allocate for them any share of the spoils (al-fay'), but rather granted them a voluntary bonus (nafa'l).

Al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man from the people of war (non-Muslims) who converts to Islam in the land of war, and the Muslims gain dominance over them afterwards. He said: 'His Islam is Islam for his own self and for his young children, and they are free, and his wealth, belongings, and slaves are his. As for the adult children, they are booty (fay') for the Muslims, unless they had converted before that. As for the houses and lands, they are booty and do not belong to him, because the land is a land of tribute (jizyah) upon which the rule of the people of Islam has not yet been established, and it is not like what we mentioned, because that (wealth/slaves) can be acquired and taken out to the land of Islam.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent an army to Khatham. When they surrounded them, they sought protection by prostrating (saying 'Sujud'). He killed some of them. When this reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: 'Give the heirs half the blood money for their prayer (prostration).' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Behold, I am free from every Muslim who descends (enters) with a polytheist in the abode of war.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from Sulay Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, Abu Ayyub, who said: Hafsh ibn Ghiyath informed me, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the captive: does he marry in the land of war? He said: 'I dislike that for him. If he does so in the lands of the Romans, it is not forbidden, and it is a valid marriage. As for the Turks, the Khazar, and the Daylamites, it is not permissible for him to do that.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abd Allah ibn Muskhan, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked him about the captive (prisoner of war), and he said: 'The food of the captive is upon the one who captured him, even if he intends to kill him tomorrow; for it is incumbent upon him to feed him, give him drink, provide shade for him, and treat him with kindness, whether he is a disbeliever or not.'

From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said: It is not permissible for the captive to marry while in the hands of the polytheists, for fear that he may have a child with her, and the child remains a disbeliever in their hands. And he said: When you take a captive who is unable to walk and you do not have a mount with you, then release him and do not kill him, for you do not know what the ruling of the Imam will be regarding him. And he said: The captive, when he embraces Islam, his blood is secured (not to be killed) and he becomes spoils of war (bayt al-mal).

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: "And they feed food in spite of their love for it to the poor and the orphan and the captive." He said: "It refers to the captive." And he said: "The captive is fed, even if he is brought forward for execution." And he said: "Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to feed those who were confined in prison from the treasury of the Muslims."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, who said: An prisoner was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) on the day of Siffin, so he gave him bay'ah (pledge of security). Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I will not kill you, for I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.' So he released him and gave him the spoils he had brought with him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Qa'im (May Allah hasten his reappearance): when he rises, with which manner of conduct does he proceed among the people? He said: 'With the manner of conduct with which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) proceeded, until he makes Islam manifest.' I said: 'And what was the manner of conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'He abolished what existed in the era of Ignorance (al-Jahiliyyah) and faced the people with justice. And so too is the Qa'im (peace be upon him) when he rises: he abolishes what existed during the truce (al-Hudna) that was in the hands of the people, and faces them with justice.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fadhl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from al-Hasan ibn Harun, the seller of silk fabrics, who said: I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Mu'alla ibn Khunays asked him: 'Will the Qa'im (the Awaited Imam) proceed in a manner contrary to the conduct of Ali (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Yes, and that is because Ali (peace be upon him) proceeded with generosity and sufficiency (giving enough to satisfy), because he knew that his Shia would be victorious over their enemies.
