And indeed, when the Qa'im rises, he will proceed among them with the sword and booty (taking captives and spoils), and that is because he knows that his Shia will never be victorious over their enemies after him.'

From him, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from al-Hakam al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'By what manner did Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) travel [conduct himself]?' He said: 'Indeed, Abu al-Yaqdhan was a sharp-minded man, may God have mercy on him. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, by what manner will you travel [conduct yourself] with these people tomorrow?' He said: 'With al-Man (Generosity/Bestowal), just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) traveled with the people of Mecca.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) proceeded against the people of the Qibla (Muslims) in a manner contrary to the practice of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when dealing with the people of polytheism. He became angry, then sat up, then said: 'By Allah, he proceeded against them with the practice of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Conquest.' Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) wrote to Malik (ibn al-Harith al-Ash'ath) while he was at the forefront of his army on the Day of Basra: 'Do not thrust (your spear) into one who is not facing you, and do not kill one who is fleeing, and do not exact blood-money for a wounded person, and whoever closes his door is safe.' So he took the letter and placed it before him on the camel's saddle pad, then said before reading it: 'Kill them!' So he killed them until he drove them into the streets of Basra. Then he opened the letter, read it, then ordered a crier to announce what was in the letter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, Yunus, and Abu Bakr al-Hadrami narrated, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The conduct of Ali (peace be upon him) among the people of Basra was better for his Shia than whatever the sun rose upon, for he knew that the people had power (dawlah), so if he had taken them as captives, his Shia would have been taken as captives.' I said: 'Inform me about the Qa'im (the Awaited Imam), will he conduct himself with the same conduct?' He said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) conducted himself with leniency (mann) among them because he knew of their power, and indeed the Qa'im will conduct himself among them contrary to that conduct, because they have no power.'

Saad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he raised his head and said, 'O Father, what is for the one who visits you after your death?' He said, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death, for him is Paradise; and whoever comes to your father is, whoever visits him after his death, for him is Paradise; and whoever your brother is, whoever visits him after his death, for him is Paradise; and whoever you are, whoever visits you after your death, for him is Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn al-Attar from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj from Yunus from Abu Wahb al-Qasri, who said: I entered the city and went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I came to you but had not yet visited the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Bad is what you did, if it were not that you are from our Shias, I would not have looked at you. Do you not visit he whom Allah the Almighty visits with the angels, and the Prophets (peace be upon them) visit, and the believers visit?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I did not know that.' He said, 'Then know that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) is with Allah superior to all the Imams, and he has the reward of their deeds, and they are favored according to the measure of his deeds.'

Three: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Hammam said: I found in a book written by Ja'far ibn Muhammad in Baghdad; he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Razi narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Ismail al-Saymari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever visits the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah writes for him for every step one Hajj and one Umrah. And if he returns on foot, Allah writes for him for every step two Hajjs and two Umrahs."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: We were narrated by Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Hammad from Zuhayr al-Qurashi from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'r from Abu al-Sakheen al-Arjani, who said: He narrated to me Umar ibn Abdillah ibn Talhah al-Nahdi from his father, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'O Abdillah ibn Talhah, do you not visit the grave of Abu al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'Yes, we do go to it.' He said: 'Do you go to it every Friday?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you go to it every month?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'How distant you are! Indeed, visiting him is equal to one Hajj and one Umrah, and visiting Abu Ali (peace be upon him) is equal to two Hajjs and two Umrahs.'

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hurz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'While Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was sitting in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) one day, he raised his head to him and said: O Father.' He said: 'At your service, O my son.' He said: 'What is the reward for one who comes to you after your death as a visitor, seeking only your visitation?' He said: 'O my son, whoever comes to me after my death as a visitor, seeking only my visitation, will have Paradise. And whoever comes to your father after his death as a visitor, seeking only his visitation, will have Paradise. And whoever comes to you after your death as a visitor, seeking only your visitation, will have Paradise.'

And from him, from Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mujawir, who said: Abu Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated from his brother Ja'far, from his men, who raised it, saying: I was with Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was mentioned. Ibn Marid said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits your grandfather, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'O Ibn Marid! Whoever visits my grandfather, knowing his right, Allah records for him, with every step, an accepted Hajj and a flawless Umrah.' And by Allah, O Ibn Marid, Allah does not feed the Fire a foot that became dusty in visiting the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), whether he was walking or riding. O Ibn Marid, record this hadith with gold water.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Farazdaq informed me, who said: Ali ibn Musa ibn al-Ahwal narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sari narrated to me orally, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi narrated to us, who said: Amara ibn Zayd narrated from Abu Amir al-Saji, the preacher of the people of Hijaz, who said: I came to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward for one who visits his grave, meaning the Commander of the Faithful, and frequents his soil? He said: O Abu Amir, my father narrated to me from his father from his grandfather Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'By God, you will surely be killed in the land of Iraq and buried in it.' I said: O Messenger of God, what is the reward for one who visits our graves and frequents them and maintains them? He said to me: O Abu al-Hasan, indeed God has made your grave and the grave of your children a valley among the valleys of Paradise and a courtyard among its courtyards. And indeed God has made the hearts of the elite of His creation and the choicest of His servants yearn for you and endure humiliation and hardship for your sake, so they frequent your graves and increase their visits to them, seeking closeness to God and love for the Messenger of God from among them. Those are the ones, O Ali, who are specially granted my intercession and are the ones who will drink from my basin, and they are my visitors tomorrow in Paradise. O Ali, whoever frequents your graves and maintains them is as if he helped Sulayman ibn Dawud in building the Holy House. And whoever visits your graves, the equivalent of that is for him the reward of seventy pilgrimages after the pilgrimage of Islam. And his sins are removed until he returns from your visitation as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him. So rejoice and give glad tidings to your friends and lovers of the bliss and delight of the eye, of what no eye has seen and no ear has heard and no heart of a human has conceived. But a remnant of the people reproach the visitors of your graves for visiting you, just as the adulteress is reproached for her adultery. Those are the worst of my Ummah; my intercession will not reach them and they will not

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar al-Jumar al-Ju'fi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I long for al-Ghari.' He said, 'What is your longing for it?' I said to him, 'I love to visit the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Do you know the virtue of visiting him?' I said, 'No, O son of the Messenger of Allah, unless you inform me of that.' He said, 'When you visit the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), know that you are visiting the bones of Adam, the body of Noah, and the physique of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).' I said, 'Indeed, Adam (peace be upon him) descended in Serandib (Sri Lanka) in the east, and they claim that his bones are in the Sacred House of Allah (Mecca). How did his bones come to be in Kufa?' He said, 'Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Majestic, revealed to Noah (peace be upon him) while he was in the ship that he should circumambulate the House seven times. So he circumambulated the House as Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him. Then he descended into the water up to his knees and extracted a chest containing the bones of Adam (peace be upon him), so he carried it in the belly of the ship until he circumambulated as Allah willed. Then he arrived at the gate of Kufa, in the middle of its mosque. Therein, Allah, the Exalted, said to the earth, 'Swallow your water.' Swallow your water. So it swallowed its water from the mosque of Kufa, just as the water began from it, and the crowd that was with Noah (peace be upon him) in the ship dispersed. So Noah (peace be upon him) took the chest and buried it in al-Ghari, which is a piece of the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech, and upon which Jesus sanctified, and upon which He took Abraham as a friend, and took Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a beloved, and made it a dwelling for the prophets. By Allah, none dwelt in it after his two pure fathers, Adam and Noah, who is more noble than the Commander of the Faithful, may the prayers of Allah be upon him. So when you visit the side of al-Najaf, visit the bones of Adam, the body of Noah, and the physique of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). For indeed you are visi

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Haytham, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the jizyah from the People of the Covenant on the condition that they do not consume usury, do not eat the meat of pigs, and do not marry sisters, nor the daughters of brothers, nor the daughters of sisters. Whoever among them does that, the covenant of Allah and the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is free from him.' He said: 'And their covenant is not in effect today.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Sunnah has established that the jizyah (poll tax) is not taken from the insane person nor from the one whose intellect is overpowered.

Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from some of the companions of Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding In the case of captives (saby), when the enemy takes from the Muslims, in terms of killing, the children of the Muslims or their slaves, and then the Muslims later fight them, gain victory over them, and capture them, taking back what the enemy had taken of the slaves of the Muslims and their children whom they had taken from the Muslims — what should be done with what they took of the children of the Muslims and their slaves? He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the children of the Muslims, they are not distributed in the lots (of the captives), but they are returned to their father, or their brother, or their guardian, with witnesses. As for the slaves, they are distributed in the lots of the Muslims, so they are sold, and their owners are given the value of their price from the treasury of the Muslims.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked him about the Turks who raid the Muslims and take their children, and then the Muslims capture them; are they returned to them? He said, 'Yes, and the Muslim is the brother of the Muslim, and the Muslim has more right to his property wherever he finds it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whom the enemy met, and they took from him wealth or belongings. Then the Muslims captured that. How should the man's belongings be treated? He said: 'If they took it before they secured the man's belongings, it is returned to him. And if they took it after they had secured it, it is Fay' (booty) for the Muslims, and they have more right to pre-emption.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding A man who had a slave, and the slave was taken into the House of Polytheism (Dar al-Shirk), then was taken as captive to the House of Islam. He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'If he was taken possession of by the master before division (of spoils), he is for him; and if division was carried out regarding him, he is more entitled to the price.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The compiler of this book issues fatwa based on what the first two reports contained, that his property is returned to the Muslim if evidence is established for him, as long as he has not been divided; and whenever he is divided, it is not obligatory to return him to him except with the price, but he is given his value from the treasury. And this is so that it does not lead to the annulment of the division. As for not returning him to him and not giving his value, it is not permissible in any case, because with the polytheist's seizing him, he did not acquire ownership of him until it becomes valid for him to be considered Fay' (spoils). It is also permissible to say that he is returned to him in all cases, and the buyer returns to the Imam with the price of that. Indicating this is what was narrated:

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub in the book Al-Mashyakha from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Tirbal from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who had a female slave, and the polytheists raided him and took her from him. Then the Muslims later campaigned against them and took her among the spoils they captured from them. He said: 'If she was among the spoils and the owner established proof that the polytheists raided him and took her from him, she is returned to him.' And if she had been purchased and had left the spoils, and he found her later, she is returned to him in full, and the one who bought her is given the price from the spoils from all of it. It was said to him: 'And if he did not find her until the people dispersed and distributed all the spoils, and he found her later?' He said: 'He takes her from the one who has her in his possession if he establishes proof, and the one who has her in his possession returns the price if he establishes proof against the commander of the army.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the captives of the Kurds when they fight, and whoever fights among the polytheists, is their marriage permissible and their purchase? He said, 'Yes.' From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Marzuban ibn Imran said: I asked him about the captives of the Daylamites, while some of them steal from others, and Muslims raid them without an Imam, is their purchase permissible? He wrote, 'When they acknowledge servitude, there is no harm in purchasing them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from Alwan from Al-As said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of Magians who rose up against some Muslims in the land of Islam. He said: 'Yes, and their taking of captives (sabiy).'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a group who went out and killed some of the Muslims, and demolished the mosques, and indeed al-Mustawfi Harun sent to them, so they were captured and killed, and the women and children were taken as captives. Is it permissible to buy any of them and have intercourse with them? He said, 'There is no harm in buying their belongings and their captives.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a group of the enemy who made peace (sulah) but then betrayed (kharafu), and perhaps they only betrayed because justice was not done to them. Is it permissible to buy from their captives (sabiy)? He said: 'If they are from the enemy whose enmity has become clear, then buy from them; and buy from them; and if they have been displaced and were wronged, then do not buy from their captives.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah al-Nakhas said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) Indeed, the people raid the Saqaliba and Anub, and they steal their children from the female and male slaves; they then take the boys, castrate them, and send them to Baghdad to the merchants. What do you think regarding their purchase, while we know they are stolen? They raided them not in a war that was between them. He said: 'There is no harm in buying them; they merely brought them out from polytheism into the abode of Islam.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: "It is more beloved to me that birds snatch me [away] than that I should speak upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) what he did not say. I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say on the Day of the Trench: 'War is deception.' He said: 'Speak whatever you wish.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah said: A sheikh from the descendants of Adi ibn Hatim narrated to me from his father from his grandfather, Adi ibn Hatim, who was with Ali (peace be upon him) in his campaign: That Ali (peace be upon him) said on the day he met Mu'awiya (may God curse him) at Siffin, and he raised his voice with it so his companions could hear: 'By God, I will surely kill Mu'awiya and his companions.' Then he said at the end of his statement, 'If God wills,' and lowered his voice with it. I was near him, so I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, you swore on what you said, then you made an exception (istithna'), so what did you intend by that?' He said: 'Indeed, war is deception, and I am not a liar among the believers. So I intended to encourage my companions against them so that they would not falter and so that they would hope in them. Understand, for you will benefit from it after today, if God wills.' And know that God, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Moses (peace be upon him) when He sent him to Pharaoh: 'So go to him' and 'Speak to him with a gentle word, perhaps he will be reminded or fear.' And He knew that he would not be reminded nor fear, but so that it would make Moses (peace be upon him) more eager to go.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from one who informed him from Ibn Tayfur the physician, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asked me, 'What do you ride?' I said, 'A donkey.' He asked, 'For how much did you buy it?' I said, 'For thirteen dinars.' He said, 'This is extravagance (saraf): that you buy a donkey for thirteen dinars and leave aside a thoroughbred horse.' I said, 'O my master, the maintenance of the thoroughbred is more than the maintenance of the donkey.' He said, 'Indeed, the one who maintains the donkey is the one who maintains the thoroughbred.' Do you not know that whoever ties up a beast, expecting through it our affair, and irritates with it our enemy, and it is attributed to us, may God increase his provision, broaden his chest, fulfill his hope, and be a help to him in his needs?

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dawud al-Raqqi said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever buys a beast of burden, its back belongs to him, and its provision is upon Allah.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Acquire the beast of burden, for it is a adornment, and through it your needs are fulfilled, and its provision is upon Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The beast has six rights upon its owner: that he does not load it beyond its capacity, nor take its back as a place to sit and converse upon, and that he begins with its fodder when he alights, and does not insult it, nor strike it on its face, nor harm it, for it glorifies [God], and he offers it water when he passes by it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yasar from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Durust from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When the beast stumbles under the man and he says to it 'May you be cursed' (Ta'asti), it says 'May the bones of our Lord be cursed' (Ta'asa a'sana al-Rabb)."

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, he raised it (to the Imam), he said: The Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked: 'When should I strike my beast?' He said: 'When your riding does not travel as fast as it travels to its feeding trough.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from al-Asamm from Mis'ma ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Strike it (the horse) with the heel (using the spur) and do not strike it with the foot."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon each nostril of the beasts is a shaytan. So when any one of you wishes to bridle it, let him mention the name of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Mad'ani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to ride on a red quilt (or saddle-cloth).

From him, from some of his companions, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the skins of wild beasts, so he said: 'Ride on them, and do not wear anything from them in which you pray.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hanan said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'Beware of riding a red saddle, for it is the saddle of Iblis.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the saddle and the bridle, if they contain silver, is it permissible to ride with them? He said: 'If it is embedded such that it cannot be removed, there is no harm; otherwise, do not ride with them.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from Abdillah ibn Abd al-Rahman from Mis'ma ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The saddle of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was made of silver.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Artata ibn Habib al-Asadi, from a man, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said: "Whoever is attacked regarding the charity of his wealth, fights, and is killed, then he is a martyr."

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed due to his injustice (or for his cause), he is a martyr.'

And with this chain of narration, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever is killed defending his property/rights, he is a martyr." Then he said, "O Abu Maryam, do you know what 'defending his property/rights' means?" I said, "May I be your ransom, a man is killed defending his family and his wealth and similar things." He said, "O Abu Maryam, indeed among the aspects of jurisprudence is knowing the truth."

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Marwan, from Abu Khudayrah, from one who heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) say: He mentioned the martyrs. He said: Some of us said, 'In the one with a stomach ail (dying of dysentery).' Some of us said, 'In the one whose body is eaten by beasts.' Some of us said, 'Other than that, from what is mentioned regarding martyrdom.' Then a man said, 'I did not think that the martyr was only one who was killed in the cause of Allah.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said, 'Then the martyrs would surely be few.' "Those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are [in the ranks of] the righteous and the martyrs, in the sight of their Lord." Then he said, 'This is for us and for our Shias.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fights to protect his wealth, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Whoever is killed defending his wealth is in the rank of the martyr.' We asked him, 'Is it better to fight?' He said, 'If he does not fight, there is no harm. As for me, if I had not fought and they had left me (with my wealth), [I would have been blameworthy].'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about a woman whom the enemy captured and raped until she died. He was asked: Is she in the rank of the martyr? He said: 'Yes, unless she assisted in bringing it upon herself.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When a martyr dies on the day of his death or the next day, he is buried in his clothes; and if he remains for some days until his wound changes, he is washed." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified in the Book of Salat that reliance is placed on the narration that states: if he dies in the battle, he is not washed; and if he is carried from it while still alive and then dies, at any time, washing is obligatory in all cases. This narration is weak, its chain consists of the men of the Zaydiyyah, and it is permissible that it emerged as a form of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit, from Amr ibn Jumay' — he raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): He was asked about dueling (al-mubarazah) between the two lines of troops without the Imam's permission. He said: 'There is no harm in it, but that is not sought/undertaken except with the permission of the Imam.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man invited one of the Banu Hashim to single combat (mubarazah), but he refused to accept. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) asked him, 'What prevented you from accepting?' He said, 'He was the horseman of the Arabs, and I feared he would kill me.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Indeed, he is aggressive towards you; if you had accepted, you would have killed him. And if a mountain were aggressive towards a mountain, the aggressor would be toppled.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) invited a man to single combat. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) learned of this and said to him,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, did not make the spreading of the tongue and the restraining of the hand separate, but He made them both spread together and both restrained together.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ansari, from Yahya ibn Ma'la al-Aslami, from Hashim ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: Ali (peace be upon him) had greater reward in his war than his standing with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his war. I said: With what do you say this, may Allah rectify you? He said to me: Because he was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a follower, and he did not have except the reward of his followership. And in this [war], he was the one being followed, and he had the reward of everyone who followed him.

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever witnesses a matter but dislikes it is like one who was absent from it, and whoever is absent from a matter but approves of it is like one who witnessed it.'

And with this chain of narration, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: The first to fight was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when the Romans captured Lut (peace be upon him), so Ibrahim (peace be upon him) set out until he rescued him from their hands. And the first to throw an arrow in the cause of Allah was Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah curse him. And the first to tether a horse in the cause of Allah was Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah have mercy on him. And the first martyr in Islam was Mihsa. And the first to spur the horse in the cause of Allah was Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), the Two-Winged One, who spurred his horse. And the first to adopt the banner 'La ilaha illa Allah' was Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa, from al-Husayn al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with two dinars and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I wish to spend them in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Do you have parents or one of them?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Go and spend them on your parents, for that is better for you than spending them in the cause of Allah.' So he returned and did so, and then came to him with two other dinars, saying, 'I have done so, and these are two dinars I wish to spend in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Do you have children?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and spend them on your children, for that is better for you than spending them in the cause of Allah.' So he returned and did so, and came to him with two other dinars, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have done so, and these are two other dinars I wish to spend in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Do you have a wife?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Spend them on your wife, for that is better for you than spending them in the cause of Allah.' So he returned and did so, and came to him with two other dinars, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, and these are two dinars I wish to spend in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Do you have a servant?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Go and spend them on your servant, for that is better for you than spending them in the cause of Allah.' So he did so and came to him with two other dinars, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, and these are two dinars I wish to spend in the cause of Allah.' He said, 'Spend them, and know that they are not superior to your first two dinars.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Wahb, from Abi Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Jizya, so he said: 'Verily, Allah the Exalted has made the Jizya specific to the polytheists of the Arabs.'

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: God revealed to a Prophet among the Prophets: 'Say to your people: Let them not wear the clothing of My enemies, nor eat the food of My enemies, nor resemble them in their distinctive characteristics, so that they become My enemies, just as they are My enemies.'

And with this chain, from Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent out the banner, and sent with it some people. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is taken prisoner without a heavy wound, he is not from me.'

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir and Abdillah, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted the covenant of protection (al-dhimmah) to some people from the people of Najran in exchange for seventy cloaks, and did not grant it to anyone else besides them.

From him, from Ya'qub, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The earth will not remain empty of a scholar from us who knows the truth from the falsehood." He said: "Taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence) was instituted only to preserve blood [from being shed]. So when Taqiyyah itself leads to bloodshed, then (it is no longer valid). By God's oath, if you were called to support us, you would say, 'We will not do it; we only practice Taqiyyah,' and Taqiyyah would be more beloved to you than your fathers and mothers. And if the Qa'im (peace be upon him) arose, he would not need to question you about that, and he would establish God's punishment upon many of you who are of the people of hypocrisy."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the day of Badr: 'Do not conceal yourselves except with kamish.' He meant by it 'he whose penis is small,' and he said: 'That will not be except among the nobles of the people.'

From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When your beast is exhausted, meaning when it stands in the land of the enemy in the cause of God, let him slaughter it and not let it stand (exhausted)."

From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace: That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about the payment of a fixed wage (ij'al) for warfare, so he said: 'There is no objection to a man going forth to fight on behalf of another man and taking the wage from him.'

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from Abi al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) presented them on that day to the 'Anat (curses/imprecations); whoever he found to be subject to it, he killed him, and whoever he did not find to be subject to it, he attached him to the descendants.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not kill a man by his own hand ever, except for one man, Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, may God curse him, and he struck Ibn Abi Khalaf and he died after that.

From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) would not fight until the sun set, and he would say, 'The gates of heaven are opened, mercy descends, and victory comes down.' And he would say, 'It is closer to night and more likely that killing will decrease, the pursuer will return, and the defeated will escape.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He used to say: 'Whoever flees from two men in battle during the infantry advance has truly fled, and whoever flees from three men in battle during the infantry advance has not fled.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never bivouacked (made a night encampment for battle) against an enemy.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: One of you says, 'I am a stranger/guest,' but the true stranger is the one who is in the house of polytheism (dar al-shirk).

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: Some of our companions narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from his brother Imran ibn Abdillah al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Fight those polytheists who are near you,' he said: 'The Daylamites.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The best of companions are four, and the best of houses (or dwellings) are four hundred, and the best of armies are two thousand, and ten thousand are not defeated by scarcity.'

From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amrū ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn 'Alī, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When two Muslims meet each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, [why is the] killer [in the Fire]?' He said: 'Because he intended to kill.' Then [implied: the killed is also in the Fire because he also intended to kill, though the text explicitly quotes the reason for the killer, the context implies the same for the killed as per the first clause].

From him, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Abu Dhamrah, from Ibn Ajlan, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Ride and shoot archery, and for you to shoot is more beloved to me than for you to ride." Then he said, "Every matter of the believer is vain/trivial except in three: training his horse, shooting with his bow, and playing with his wife, for these are true/right." Indeed, Allah will admit through a single arrow three people to Paradise: the one who works the wood of it, the one who strengthens it, and the one who shoots it in the cause of Allah.

From him, from Salamah, from Yahya, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his grandfather, from Habba al-Urani, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever entrusts a man with his blood (life/lieutenant of his sword) and that man betrays him, then I am free from the killer, even if the slain is in the Hellfire.'

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, he raised it (to the Imam), he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Commanding the good and forbidding the evil are two characteristics of the characteristics of Allah, the Exalted. Whoever supports them, Allah will honor him; and whoever abandons them, Allah will abandon him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn 'Arafah said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'When my nation becomes negligent in enjoining good and forbidding evil, let them anticipate a punishment from Allah, the Exalted.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "How will you be when your women become corrupt and your youth become dissolute, and you do not enjoin what is right and do not forbid what is wrong?" It was said to him, "And will that happen, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes, and something worse than that. How will you be when you enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right?" It was said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, and will that happen?" He said, "Yes, and something worse than that. How will you be when you see what is right as wrong, and what is wrong as right?"

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil, the companion of al-Manqari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "It is sufficient honor for the believer, when he sees an evil, that Allah knows from his intention that he is displeased with it."

And with this chain of narration, he said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Only a believer is commanded to enjoin what is right and forbidden to prohibit what is wrong, so he admonishes; or an ignorant person, so he learns. As for the owner of the whip and sword, [he does not]."

Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mufaddal ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'O Mufaddal! Whoever exposes himself to a tyrannical ruler and a calamity befalls him, he will not be rewarded for it, nor will he be granted patience for it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthayfir, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When this verse was revealed: 'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire,' a man from the Muslims sat weeping and said: 'I have become unable to manage myself, yet I am tasked with managing my family.' 'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is sufficient for you that you command them to do what you command yourself to do, and forbid them from what you forbid yourself from.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire' I asked: 'How do I protect them?' He said: 'Command them to what Allah, the Exalted, has commanded, and forbid them from what Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden. If they obey you, you have protected them; and if they disobey you, you have fulfilled what was upon you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Saif ibn 'Amirah from 'Amr ibn Shimir from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever seeks the pleasure of people by that which angers Allah, his praiser among the people will be a blamer. And whoever prefers the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by that which angers people, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will suffice him against the enmity of every enemy, the envy of every envier, and the aggression of every aggressor, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will be for him a supporter and a helper.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah has delegated all His affairs to the believer, but He did not delegate to him that he should be humiliated. Do you not hear Allah, the Exalted, saying: 'And to Allah belongs all honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers'? So the believer is honored (aziz) and is not humiliated (dhalil). He said: Indeed, the believer is more honored than the mountain, because the mountain can be made small by the pickaxe, but the believer's religion is not made small by anything.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "It is not fitting for the believer to humble himself." I asked: "How does he humble himself?" He said: "He enters into that which he makes excuse for (i.e., minor faults or things he considers beneath his dignity)."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a group of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A nation is not sanctified unless it takes the right of its weak from its strong, without being humble (or condescending).

And it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: The people will remain in goodness as long as they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and cooperate upon righteousness and piety. But when they do not do that, the blessings will be taken from them, and some of them will be given authority over others, and there will be no helper for them on earth nor in the sky.
And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever leaves forbidding the evil with his heart, hand, and tongue, he is a dead person among the living." At the end of this speech.

And the Imam (peace be upon him) said to a group of his companions: "It has become due upon me to take the innocent among you for the sick one, and how can it not be due upon me for that, while the ugly/defective one among you reaches you, and you do not forbid him, nor abandon him, nor afflict him, until he leaves you." The book of Jihad and Commanding the Good ended with the praise of Allah and His good success, and it will be followed by the book of Debts, Guarantees, Transfers, Collaterals, and Mandates, if Allah wills.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who lent a man dirhams, and he returned to him better quality ones with a good spirit, and the borrower and the lender knew that he only lent it so that he would give him better quality ones. He said: 'There is no harm if the borrower is pleased with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who borrows a specific number of silver dirhams, then repays them with gold dinars by weight, knowing that the gold is heavier than what he borrowed, and he is pleased to give him the excess as a favor. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it if there is no condition attached, and even if he gifted them all to him, it would be more appropriate.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you lend dirhams, and then they bring you back something better than them, there is no harm in that, provided there was no condition (of specific repayment) between you."

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who lends another man the debased dirhams, and takes back from him the fresh (new) dirhams, which please him. He said, 'There is no harm.' And he mentioned that from Ali (peace be upon him).

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a large quantity of dried grapes (busr) and takes from it a large quantity of fresh dates (rutab), while the fresh dates are fewer than the dried grapes. He said, 'There is no objection.' I said, 'And if he has a large quantity of dried grapes and takes from it a large quantity of dried dates (tamr), while the dried dates are more than the dried grapes?' He said, 'There is no objection if it is well-known between you two.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows a loan from another man and gives him collateral, whether a servant, or utensils, or clothes, and he needs something from its benefit, so he asks permission for it and he grants permission. He said: 'If his soul is pleased, there is no harm.' I said: 'Indeed, those among us narrate that every loan that brings benefit is invalid.' He said: 'Is not the best loan that which brings benefit?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the loan that brings benefit, and he said, 'The best loan is the one that brings benefit.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hudhayl ibn Hanan, brother of Ja'far ibn Hanan al-Sayrafī, said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I have entrusted to my brother Ja'far ibn Hanan some wealth that was mine, and he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj with it and give charity. I have asked those from our side, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not permissible. I wish to refer to your opinion in this matter, so what do you say? He said: 'Did he give you (money) before you entrusted your wealth to him?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Take from him what he gives you, eat from it, drink from it, give charity from it, and perform Hajj with it. So when you arrive in Iraq, say: Indeed, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) gave me a fatwa regarding this.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a large quantity of dried grapes (busr) as a debt owed to him, and he takes from it a large quantity of fresh dates (rutab) in place of it, and the fresh dates are less in quantity than the dried grapes. He said: 'There is no objection.' I said: And if he has a large quantity of dried grapes owed to him, and he takes from it a large quantity of dried dates (tamr), and the dried dates are more in quantity than the dried grapes. He said: 'There is no objection if that is well-known/customary between you two.'

From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Mu'ammar al-Zayyat, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me and says, 'Lend me dinars so that I may buy oil with them and then sell it to you.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever lends a man silver (dirhams) should not stipulate except that he gets the same amount back; if he is given something better than it, he may accept it, and let none of you take the riding fee of an animal or the loan of goods as a condition for the loan of his silver."

From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who sends money to a land, he said: The one who wants to send it with him said, 'Lend it to me, and I will repay you when you arrive in the land.' He said, 'There is no objection to this.'

From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who lends another man silver (dirhams) on the condition that he repays it to him in another land, and stipulates that for him, he said: 'There is no objection.'

From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me, so I buy goods for him from people and guarantee [the price/value] for him, then he comes to me with the dirhams, so I take them, then I withhold them from their owner, and I take the good dirhams and give [him] inferior ones in exchange. He said: 'If he guarantees [the debt/value], perhaps strictness is imposed upon him; he hurries [to pay] before taking [the goods], and withholds [the payment] after taking [the goods], so there is no objection to it.'

From him, from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who pays in advance (salam) twenty dinars for a sale of grain or dates, and lends the owner of the salam ten or twenty dinars. He (the Imam) said: 'It is not valid if the loan is one that entails a benefit (qarḍan yajurru shay'an), so it is not valid.' And I asked him about a man who goes to his partner (harīf) and companion (khalīṭ) to borrow dinars, and he lends them to him; if it were not for the fact that he associates with him, partners with him, and gains profit from him, he would not lend to him. He (the Imam) said: 'If it is well-known between them [that the loan is for partnership purposes], there is no objection; but if he only lends him because he gains profit from him, then it is not valid.'

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said: I asked him about a man who stays as a guest with another man, and the host has a debt owed to him by the guest. Does the guest eat from the host's food? He said: 'Yes, he eats from his food for three days, then he does not eat anything after that.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who eats at the place of his creditor, or drinks from his drink, or is gifted a present by him, he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

From him (Al-Shaykh), from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That he (peace be upon him) disliked for a man to stay with his debtor. He said: 'He should not eat from his food, nor drink from his drink, nor eat fodder from his fodder.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said, 'May Allah improve you. We mix with a group of the people of As-Sawad (Iraq), so we lend them money, and they send us the produce/crops from their lands, so we sell it to them for a profit, and we have benefit in that.' He said, 'There is no harm.' And I do not know him except to have said, 'If it were not for what they send us from their produce, we would not lend them.' He said, 'There is no harm.'

Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): A man has money as a loan with another man, and the borrower stays long with the lender, deriving no benefit from it. So the lender gives him small items one after another, reluctant to take his money back where he derives no benefit from it. Is it permissible for him? He said: 'There is no harm, provided it is not by condition.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan and Ali ibn Ribat, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who pledges a slave, or a garment, or jewelry, or household items, and the owner of the pledge says to the pledgee: 'You are free to wear this garment, so wear it, benefit from the items, and use the servant.' He said: 'It is permissible for him if he frees it, and I like for him to do so.'

Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Muhammad, and I heard it from Ali, who said: I wrote to him: 'Does a loan (qard) that draws benefit, is it permissible or not?' He wrote back to me with peace: 'That is permissible.' And I wrote to him: 'A man has a debt of dates, or wheat, or barley, or cotton against another man. When they settled the debt, he said: Take the value of what is with me in dirhams. Is that permissible for him or not?' He wrote back to him with peace: 'That is permissible by mutual consent of both, if God wills.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan and Fadala from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the two said: Regarding two men, each of whom had food with the other, and each did not know how much he had with the other. So each said to his companion: 'What is with you is yours, and what is with me is mine.' He said: 'There is no harm in that if they mutually agreed.' And Mansur said in his narration: 'And their souls were pleased with it.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who owes something and then settles (compounds the debt), he said: 'If it is with the good pleasure/contentment of his creditor, then there is no harm.'

From him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Saffar), from Ibn Abi Umayr and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man, either Jewish or Christian, had four thousand dirhams with me, and then he died. Is it permissible for me to settle with his heirs without informing them of the exact amount? He said: 'It is not permissible until you inform them.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who assumed a guarantee (debt), then settled (compounded) on part of what he had settled on. He said: 'He is entitled only to what he settled on.'

From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from whom he narrated from, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a debt due from another man, and he says to him before the due date arrives: 'Expedite for me half of my right, on condition that I forgive you the other half.' Is that permissible for either of them? He said, 'Yes.'

From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the two said: Regarding a man who has a debt due at a specified term, and his creditor comes to him and says, 'Pay me such and such amount from what is owed to me, and I will forgive the remainder for you,' or he says, 'Pay me part of it, and I will extend the term for what remains.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I see no harm in that, provided he does not add anything to the principal amount.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'For you is the principal of your debts; you do no injustice, nor are you treated unjustly.' (1).

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In two men who shared in property, and they made a profit from it, and among that property was a debt and a physical asset. One of them said to his partner: 'Give me the principal capital, and the profit is yours, and whatever I owe (or you owe) is upon you.' He said (peace be upon him): 'There is no harm in it if it is stipulated, and even if the stipulation contradicts the Book of Allah, it is referred back to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men who had wealth in their hands, and some of it was dispersed/away from them. They divided by equality what was in their hands and what was absent from them. The share of one of them, which was absent, was lost, while the other received it in full; therefore, he must return to his companion. He said, 'Yes, that which goes with his wealth.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gives a specific measure (aqfizah) of wheat to be ground, paying the miller with dirhams. When the miller finished grinding, he paid the dirhams and gave back one qafiz from the wheat. This was a thing they had agreed upon between themselves. The Imam said: 'There is no harm in it, even if he did not explicitly urge him to do so.'
Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Reconciliation is permissible among people."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man has a debt due from another man, and the debtor delays payment until he dies, and then the creditors make a settlement (sulh) with his heirs for a certain amount, then what the heirs take for themselves is theirs, and what remains is for the deceased; the creditor will collect the remainder from him in the Hereafter. And if he did not settle with them for anything until he died, and the debt was not paid off for him, then it is for the deceased; he will take it from him (in the Hereafter).

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In the case of two men who had two dirhams with them, one of them said, 'The two dirhams are mine,' and the other said, 'They are between me and you.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for one of the two dirhams, he has no share in it, and indeed it belongs to its owner, and the second dirham is divided between them into two halves.'

Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala' from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a man who pays another man thirty dirhams for a garment, and another man pays twenty dirhams for a garment, and he sends the two garments, and this one did not recognize his garment nor did that one recognize his garment. He said: 'The two garments are sold, and the owner of the thirty receives three-fifths of the price, and the other receives two-fifths of the price.' I said: 'Indeed, the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty: Choose whichever you wish.' He said: 'He has treated him fairly.'

Al-Sakuni narrated from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), regarding: A man deposited two dinars with another man, and that man deposited one dinar with him. One dinar was lost from them. He (the Imam) said: 'He gives the owner of the two dinars one dinar, and they share the remaining dinar between them in two halves.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha from Abu al-Hasan al-Kazzaz said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, 'What prevented you from performing Hajj?' He said, 'A guarantee ( Kafalah ) that I undertook.' He said, 'What do you have to do with guarantees? Do you not know that the guarantee is that which destroyed the earlier generations?'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, the people say: The guarantor is the debtor.' He said, 'He said, "There is no penalty on the guarantor; the penalty is on the one who consumes the wealth."'
From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Faddal, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), from Ali (peace be upon him).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who guarantees the person of another man for a specified term, saying that if he does not bring him, he shall pay so-and-so many dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he brings him by the appointed term, he owes no money, and he is a guarantor of his person forever, unless he starts with the dirhams. If he starts with the dirhams, then he is a financial guarantor for them if he does not bring him by the term he specified.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed the debt of another man, then settled (compounded) on part of what he had settled on. He said: 'There is upon him only what he settled on.'

Umar ibn Yazid said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed the debt of another man, then settled (compounded) the debt with him. He said: 'He is entitled only to what he settled with him.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "It is written in the Torah: Kafalah (guarantee), Nidamah (suretyship/companionship), Garamah (liability/compensation)."

Muhammad narrated from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man guaranteed for another man the person of a third party, saying: 'If I bring him to you, and if not, five hundred dirhams are upon me.' He (the Imam) said: 'The guarantee of the person is upon him, and no dirhams are upon him.' Then he said: 'Five hundred dirhams are upon me if I do not deliver him to you.' He (the Imam) said: 'The dirhams are binding upon him if he does not deliver him to you.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn Suqah, from 'Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, indeed I have a debt on me; when I remember it, it ruins what I am in.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah, and what reached you is that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say in his sermon: Whoever leaves behind unpaid expenses, I am responsible for his expenses; and whoever leaves behind a debt, I am responsible for his debt; and whoever leaves behind wealth, I will consume it.' The guarantee of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for the deceased is like his guarantee for the living, and his guarantee for the living is like his guarantee for the deceased. The man said, 'You have relieved me; may Allah make me your ransom.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukhti, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from al-Nawfali, from his father, from Isa ibn Abdillah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was near death, and his creditors gathered around him and demanded their debt from him. He said: 'I do not have what I can give you, but be satisfied with whomever you choose from my paternal uncles: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) or Abdullah ibn Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him).' The creditors said: 'As for Abdullah ibn Ja'far, he is wealthy but slow to pay, but Ali ibn al-Husayn is a man who has no wealth but is truthful, and he is more beloved to us.' So they sent for him and informed him of the news. He said: 'I guarantee the money until the harvest season.' He did not have a harvest season (source of income), so the people said: 'We are satisfied, and he has guaranteed it.' When the harvest season came, Allah facilitated wealth for him, and he paid it. 'Atahah Allah' means Allah facilitated for him with wealth.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) Regarding a man who transfers the debt of another man to a third party, and the original debtor says to the new debtor: 'You are free from my debt to you.' He (the Imam) said: 'If he discharges him (grants him freedom from the debt), then he has no right to return to him; and if he does not discharge him, then he has the right to return to the one who transferred the debt to him.' Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurara Like it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who transfers a debt to another man (makes a third-party transfer of debt/hawalah); does the original debtor return to the creditor? He said: 'He does not return to him ever, unless he had gone bankrupt before that.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirran said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of dinars against another man, so he transferred it to him via a third party with dinars; should he take dirhams for them? He said, 'Yes.'

Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them: Regarding two men who have wealth between them, part of which is in their hands and part is absent from them, they divided the portion that was in their hands. Each one of them used cunning regarding his share. One of them took possession (of his share) and the other did not take possession. He said: 'What one of them took possession of, it is between them, and what was lost/absent, it is between them.'

From al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from 'Uqbah ibn Ja'far, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who transfers another man's money to a money-changer (sarraf), and then the condition of the money-changer changes (becomes insolvent). Does he go back to the owner (of the money) if he (the owner) acted prudently and was satisfied (with the transfer)? He said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi from Amr ibn Shimir from Jabir ibn Yazid and Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever appoints a man to execute a matter among the matters, the agency (wakalah) remains fixed/valid forever until he informs him of the exit from it, just as he informed him of the entry into it."

From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) From a man who appointed an agent to finalize a matter among the matters and witnessed him with two witnesses. The agent stood up and left to finalize the matter, and said: 'Bear witness that I have dismissed so-and-so from the agency.' He (the Imam) said: 'If the agent finalized the matter he was appointed for before the dismissal from the agency reached him, then the matter is valid and executed according to what the agent finalized, whether the principal disliked it or was pleased.' I said: 'If the agent finalized the matter before he knew of the dismissal or before it reached him that he had been dismissed from the agency, then the matter is executed according to what he finalized.' He said: 'Yes.' I said to him: 'If the dismissal reached him before he finalized the matter, then he went and finalized it, that would not be anything (valid).' He said: 'Yes. Indeed, when the agent is appointed, then he stands from the session, his matter remains valid forever, and the agency is established until the dismissal from the agency reaches him through a trustworthy person who informs him or by direct conversation regarding the dismissal from the agency.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who received the dowry of his daughter from her husband, then died: Is she entitled to claim her dowry from her husband, or is the father's receipt considered her receipt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had authorized him to receive her dowry from her husband, she is not entitled to claim it from him; and if she had not authorized him, she is entitled to it, and the husband shall seek reimbursement from the father's heirs, unless at that time she was a minor under his guardianship, in which case it is permissible for the father to receive it on her behalf. And if he divorces her before consummation, the father may forgive part of the dowry and take part, but he is not allowed to leave (forgive) the whole of it. And that is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Except if they forgive or if the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives.' Meaning the father, and the one whom the woman authorizes and entrusts her affair to, whether a brother, a relative, or someone else.

Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man whom a woman appointed as her agent in her marriage affairs, whether she is a relative or a neighbor of his, and he does not know the hidden details of her case; if he found that she had concealed a defect in herself, he said: 'The dowry is taken from her, and there is no liability on the one who married her.' And he said regarding a woman who appointed a man as her agent, and she said to him: 'Marry me to so-and-so.' He said: 'I will not marry you until you testify that my affair is in your hand.' So she testified to him. Then he said at the time of marriage to the one proposing to her: 'O so-and-so, upon you is such and such.' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said to the people: 'Bear witness that that is for her with me, and I have married her to myself.' The woman said: 'I did not marry you except out of courtesy, and my affair is not in your hand, and I did not appoint you as my agent except out of shyness from speaking.' He said: 'He is removed from her, and his head is struck (or he is punished).'.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jamilyah, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh, you have taken a seat that no one occupies except a Prophet, or the Prophet's successor, or a fortunate one.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) appointed Shurayh as judge, he stipulated with him that he should not execute the judgment until he presented it to him.

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Beware of al-hukumah (judicial authority/governance), for al-hukumah is only for the Imam who is knowledgeable in adjudication, just among the Muslims, being a Prophet or the heir of a Prophet."

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ibn Faddal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The judgment is two judgments: the judgment of Allah and the judgment of ignorance. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who have certainty?' And I bear witness against Zayd ibn Thabit that he indeed judged in the inheritances with the judgment of ignorance.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The judges are four: three in the Hellfire and one in Paradise. A man who judges with injustice while knowing it is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with injustice while not knowing that he is judging with injustice, he is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with the truth while not knowing it is the truth, he is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with the truth while knowing it is the truth, he is in Paradise." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Judgment is of two types: the judgment of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the judgment of Ignorance (al-Jahiliyyah). So whoever errs from the judgment of Allah, he has judged with the judgment of Ignorance."

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men from our companions who have a dispute regarding a debt or inheritance, and they refer themselves to the Sultan or to the judges; is that permissible? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever refers to the Taghut (imperial/judicial authority) and he rules for him, then he is taking a bribe/unjustly, even if his right is established, because he took by the rule of the Taghut, and Allah (Exalted and Mighty) commanded that it be disbelieved in.' I said: 'What should they do?' He said: 'Look among you to the one who has narrated our hadith and examined our halal and haram and knows our rulings; let them accept him as a judge, for I have made him a ruler over you.'
