'So when he rules with our ruling and it is not accepted from him, then by the rule of Allah it was slighted, and to us it was returned, and the one who returns to us is the one who returns to Allah, and he is on the verge of shirk with Allah (Exalted and Mighty).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Any believer who presents a believer in a dispute to a judge or an unjust ruler, and he judges against him contrary to the judgment of Allah, has shared in the sin."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abu Khadijah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Beware that some of you do not refer to the unjust rulers for judgment, but rather look for one of you who knows something of our cases, and make him an arbitrator between you, for I have made him a judge, so refer to him.'

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, who said: I read in the book of Abū al-Asad to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thānī (peace be upon him), and I read it by his own hand: He asked him: What is the interpretation of His Exalted Saying, 'And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, nor send it [as a bribe] to the rulers'? He said, so he wrote to him in his own hand: 'The rulers are the judges.' He said, then he wrote below it: 'It is that a man knows that he is the oppressor, so the judge rules in his favor; he is not excused in taking that which the judge ruled for him, if he had known that he was the oppressor.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Hariz from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Any man who has a dispute over a right with his brother, and calls him to a man from their peers to judge between them, but he refuses except to refer him to these [rulers/judges], is in the position of those of whom Allah the Exalted said, 'Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, who desire to take cases in jurisdiction to the Taghut, while they have been commanded to reject them?' [the verse].

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was sitting with a judge in Medina. I visited him the next day, and he asked me, 'What was the session in which I saw you yesterday?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, this judge is very generous to me, and perhaps I sat with him.' He said, 'What guarantees you that the curse will not descend and encompass everyone in the session?'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min from Muawiya ibn Wahb said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any judge who rules between two parties and makes a mistake, he falls farther than the sky.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever judges in a dispute over two dirhams with something other than what Allah, Exalted and Glorious, revealed, he is a disbeliever in Allah the Magnificent.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from some of our companions from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abdullah ibn Muskān, he raised it (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever judges between two dirhams with a judgment of injustice, then compels them to accept it, is from the people of this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - those are the disbelievers. I said: 'How does he compel him?' He said: 'He has a whip and a prison. He judges him. If he accepts his judgment, fine; otherwise, he strikes him with his whip and imprisons him in his prison.'
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from Yazīd ibn Farqad said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about al-suḥt, so he said: 'Al-rishā (bribery) in judgment.'
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Rishwa (bribery) in judgment is disbelief in God."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a judge who arbitrates between two parties and takes sustenance from the ruler for judging, so he said, 'That is the spoils of war (suh't).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The hand of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is above the head of the ruler, fluttering with mercy; so when he is just in his judgment, Allah entrusts him to Himself." to Himself."

From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Among the Children of Israel there was a judge who judged with the truth. When death approached him, he said to his wife: 'When I die, wash me, shroud me, place me on my bed, and cover my face, for you will not see any defect.' When he died, she did that, and remained for a while. Then she uncovered his face to look at him, and found a worm gnawing his nostril. She was startled by this. When it was night, he came to her in her sleep and said: 'Did what you saw frighten you?' She said: 'Yes, I was indeed frightened.' He said: 'If you were frightened, what you saw was only due to a preference (bias) in your brother Fulan. He came to me with a plaintiff. When they sat before me, I said: O God, make the truth for him and direct the judgment against his opponent.' When they disputed before me, the truth was for him, and I saw that clearly in the judgment, so I directed the judgment for him against his opponent. Thus, the place of my preference was with the concurrence of the truth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was sitting in the circle of Rabi'ah al-Ra'y. An Arab came and asked Rabi'ah a question, and he answered him. When he fell silent, the Arab said to him, 'Is it in your neck?' Rabi'ah remained silent and did not reply to him. He repeated the question, and he answered him similarly. The Arab said to him, 'Is it in your neck?' Rabi'ah remained silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'It is in his neck.' He said, 'Did he not say, Every jurist/mufti is liable (for his ruling).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever gives fatwa to the people without knowledge and guidance from God, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment will curse him, and the burden of sin of those who act upon his fatwa will be attached to him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes there is a dispute between two men from our companions, and they agree on one of us as an arbitrator.' He said: 'That is not it; rather, it is the one who compels people to his ruling by the sword and the whip.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abi al-Mi'za from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Mu'alla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to those to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice."' Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to those to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is upon the Imam to return what is with him to the Imam who comes after him. The Imams were commanded to be just, and the people were commanded to follow them.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Kermani, from Abd al-Rahman, from Yusuf ibn Jabr, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed one who looked at the private part of a woman not permissible to him, and a man who betrayed his brother regarding his wife, and a man upon whom people relied for his jurisprudence who asked them for a bribe.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ali ibn Muhammad said: I asked him: Do we take from the rulings of the opponents what they take from us in their rulings? He wrote to me, peace be upon him: 'It is permissible for you to do so, if God wills, if your approach in it is precaution (taqiyyah) from them and accommodation to them.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: "When you are under the Imams of injustice, proceed with their rulings and do not expose yourselves [to death], so that you may be killed. And if you act according to our rulings, that is better for you."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) That he complained of his eye, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited him, and behold, Ali (peace be upon him) was crying out. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Is it grief or pain, O Ali?' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have never had pain greater than it.' He said, 'O Ali, indeed when the Angel of Death descends to take the soul of the disbeliever, he descends with him with a skewer of fire, and he pulls out his soul with it, so Hell cries out.' So Ali (peace be upon him) sat up and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, repeat your statement to me, for my pain has made me forget what you said. Does this happen to anyone from your ummah?' He said, 'Yes, unjust rulers, and those who consume the property of the orphan, and the witness of false testimony.'

30 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from his father who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man to whom people come asking him a question, and he fears that if he issues a ruling on it, he will be criticized/defamed, so he remains silent with him, or he issues a ruling for him with the truth, or he issues a ruling for him with what he does not fear for himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Remaining silent with him is greater in reward and superior.'

From him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Mu'adh Al-Harra'i, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to call him An-Nahwi (the Grammarian), he said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I sit in the mosque, and a man comes to me. If I know that he differs from you, I inform him of the opinion of others; and if he is one whose opinion I do not know, I inform him of your opinion and the opinion of others, so he chooses for himself. And if he is one who speaks with your opinion, I inform him of your opinion.' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on you; do so.'

Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Salih ibn Uqbah from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: "When you are under unjust imams, judge according to their rulings and do not expose yourselves [to death] so that you may be killed, and if you judge according to our rulings, that is better for you."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn al-Miqdam, from his father, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh, look to those who delay payment and those who withhold the rights of people, from those with means and wealth, who pledge the wealth of Muslims to the rulers. So take the rights of the people from them, and sell their real estate and houses in order to satisfy those rights, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: "The delay of payment by a wealthy Muslim is oppression against the Muslims."' And whoever has no real estate, nor a house, nor wealth, there is no recourse against him. And know that it is not those who compel people to the truth, but rather those who restrain them from falsehood. Then be even-handed among the Muslims in your face, speech, and sitting place, so that your close one does not hope for your partiality, and your enemy does not despair of your justice. And return the oath to the claimant along with his evidence, for that is clearer for removing confusion and more established for the judgment. And know that Muslims are trustworthy (accepted as witnesses) one towards another, except one who has been flogged for a fixed punishment and has not repented from it, or is known for false testimony, or is a person of slight credibility. And beware of showing irritation in the court of judgment, in which Allah has mandated reward and enriches for the one who judges with the truth. And know that settlement (conciliation) is permissible among Muslims, except a settlement that makes halal what is haram, or makes haram what is halal. And set a time limit for one who claims absent witnesses between them; if he brings them forward, you take his right for him, and if he does not bring them forward, you impose the case (against him). And beware of executing a judgment in retribution (qisas) or a fixed punishment (hadd) from the punishments of Allah, or a right from the rights of Muslims, until you present that to me, if Allah wills. And do not sit in the court of judgment until you eat.

Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is tested with the position of judgeship, let him not judge while he is angry.'

And with this chain of narration, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever is tested with the role of a judge, let him be equal among them in gesture, in gaze, and in seating."

And with this chain of narration, that a man stayed with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and remained with him for several days. Then he approached him regarding a lawsuit which he did not mention to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he said to him, 'Are you a litigant?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Move away from us, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that a litigant be hosted unless his opponent is with him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjāl from Dāwūd ibn Yazīd from one who heard him from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: "When the ruler says to the one on his right and to the one on his left, 'What do you see? What do you say?' then upon that is 'the curse of Allah and the angels and all people,' if they do not rise from his session and seat them in his place."

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah raised it (narrated) and said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'Do not whisper to anyone in your gathering, and if you become angry, stand up, and do not pass judgment while you are angry.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The tongue of the judge is behind his heart; if it is for him, he speaks, and if it is against him, he remains silent.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'Three things: if you preserve them and act upon them, they will suffice you for what is besides them; and if you leave them, nothing besides them will benefit you.' He said: 'And what are they, O Abu al-Hasan?' He said: 'Establishing the legal punishments upon the close and the distant, and judging by the Book of Allah in pleasure and in anger, and dividing fairly between the red and the black.' Then Umar said to him: 'By my life, you have indeed been concise and comprehensive.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When you advance with your opponent to a governor or to a judge, stand to his right, meaning to the right of the opponent."

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim al-Azdi, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When two men come to you for a dispute, do not render a verdict for the first one until you have heard from the second one, for if you do that, the judgment will become clear to you."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): That a prophet from the prophets complained to his Lord and said: 'O Lord, how should I judge regarding that which I did not witness and did not see?' He said: 'So Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: 'Judge between them with My Book and attach them to My Name, and they will swear by it.' And he said: 'This is for one for whom no clear proof has been established.'

From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'That a prophet from the prophets complained to his Lord about judgment, saying: How can I judge with what my eye has not seen and my ear has not heard? So He said: Judge between them with clear proofs and refer them to My name, and they will swear by it.' And he said: 'Indeed Dawud (peace be upon him) said: O Lord, show me the truth as it is with You so that I may judge by it. He said: Indeed you cannot bear that. So he persisted with his Lord until He did.' Then a man came to him suing another man, saying: Indeed this one has taken my wealth. So God Almighty revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Indeed this plaintiff killed the father of this one and took his wealth.' So Dawud (peace be upon him) ordered that the plaintiff be killed, and his wealth was taken and given to the defendant.' He said: 'The people were amazed and talked about it until it reached Dawud (peace be upon him), and that which he disliked entered him, so he called upon his Lord to remove that, and He did.' Then God Almighty revealed to him: 'Judge between them with clear proofs and refer them to My name, and they will swear by it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Umayr, from Sa'd and Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I judge between you only with clear proofs and oaths, and some of you are more eloquent in presenting their argument than others. So whoever I cut for him from the wealth of his brother, I have only cut for him a piece of the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Jamil and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The proof is upon the one who claims, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ruled regarding your blood (blood money/diyyah) differently from how He ruled regarding your wealth. He ruled regarding your wealth that the evidence is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the one against whom it is claimed. And He ruled regarding your blood that the evidence is upon the one against whom it is claimed and the oath is upon the one who claimed, so that the blood of a Muslim man is not nullified.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yasin al-Darir who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to me who said: I said to the Sheikh (Al-Shaykh al-Saduq), 'Inform me about a man who claims a right against another man, but he has no evidence for what he claims.' He said, 'The oath is upon the defendant; if he swears, he has no right (to the claim), and if he does not swear, the right is upon him. And if the one against whom the right is sought has died, and evidence is established against him, then the oath is upon the claimant, swearing by Allah, the One there is no god but He, that so-and-so has died and indeed his right is upon him. If he swears, then fine; otherwise, he has no right, because we do not know, perhaps he had paid him with evidence whose location we do not know, or without evidence before death. From this, the oath becomes upon him along with the evidence. If he claims and has no evidence, he has no right, because the defendant is not alive. And if he were alive, he would be compelled to swear or give the right, or return the oath to him; from this, no right is established for him against him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): In the man against whom a right is claimed and there is no evidence for the claimant, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is sworn an oath, or the oath is returned to the owner of the right; if he does not do so, then he has no right.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both) Regarding the man who claims [a right] but has no evidence, he said: 'He is made to swear an oath; if he returns the oath to the owner of the right and does not swear, then he has no right.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The oath is returned to the claimant.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from some of his companions, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding A man against whom a right is claimed, and the claimant has no proof, he said: 'The defendant is sworn an oath. If he refuses to swear and says, "I return the oath to you, O claimant," then it is obligatory upon the claimant to swear and take his property.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus, from one who narrated it, said: «Rights are extracted through four modes: the testimony of two just men. «If they are not two men, then one man and two women.» If there are not two women, then one man and the oath of the claimant. If there is no witness, then the oath is upon the defendant. If he does not swear, the oath is returned to the claimant, and it is obligatory upon him to swear and take his right. If he refuses to swear, then he has nothing.».

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam or another from Aban from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man presents clear evidence for his right, he is not required to take an oath; but if he does not present clear evidence, the one who claimed against him is asked to take an oath, and if he refuses to swear, he has no right."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of our companions, from Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who presents his evidence to establish his right; is it upon him to be sworn an oath? He said, 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the owner of the right is satisfied with the oath of the one who denies his right, and he makes him swear, and he swears that he has no right against him, the oath removes the right of the claimant, so he has no right. I said to him, 'Even if there is a just evidence against him?' He said, 'Yes, and even if he presents it after making him swear fifty oaths by Allah, he has no right, and the oath has invalidated everything he claimed against him that he had made him swear regarding it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Khadir al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has a debt due from another man, and the debtor denies it: He (the Imam) said, 'If the creditor swears an oath (from the debtor), he is not entitled to take anything from him; and if he leaves it (the denial) and does not swear an oath from him, then the creditor is upon his right (entitled to the debt).'

From him, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from some of his companions: Regarding a man who has money due from another man, and the debtor denies it and swears an oath of patience (yamin sabr), is there anything due to him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not permitted to demand it from him, and likewise if he considers it due at the hands of God, he is not permitted to demand it from him.'

Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): That he ruled: 'A restriction (on financial transactions) is placed on the boy until he matures/reaches understanding.' And he (peace be upon him) ruled regarding debt: 'The debtor is imprisoned; if his insolvency and need become clear, his path is cleared (released) until he acquires wealth.' And he (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who evades his creditors: 'He is imprisoned, then an order is issued regarding him, and his wealth is divided among his creditors in shares; if he refuses, he is sold and the proceeds are divided among them.'

Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz narrated that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who transfers a debt to another man, asking: Does it return to him? He said: 'It does not return to him ever, unless he had gone bankrupt before that.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) That two men disputed before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding a beast of burden that was in their possession, and each of them presented evidence that it had given birth at his place. He swore them both; one swore and the other refused to swear, so he ruled in favor of the one who swore. It was said to him, 'What if neither had it in his possession and both presented evidence?' He said, 'I would swear them both; whichever one swore and the other refused, I would give it to the one who swore. If both swore, I would divide it between them into two halves.' It was said, 'What if it was in the possession of one of them and both presented evidence?' He said, 'I would rule in favor of the one who swore and was in possession of it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), when two men came to him with evidence and their witnesses were equal in justice and equal in number, would cast lots between them to determine whose oath would be taken. He (the Imam) would say, 'O God, Lord of the seven heavens, whichever of them is entitled to the right, grant it to him.' Then he would assign the right to the one whose oath was taken, once he had sworn.

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Wasshash, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two witnesses who testified to one matter, and two others came and testified to something other than what the first two testified to, and they differed, he said: 'A lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls upon for the oath, he is more entitled to the judgment.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had two men dispute before him over a beast of burden, and both presented evidence that they had given birth to it (acquired it by finding/producing it), so he ruled in its favor for the one who had it in his possession, and he said, 'If it had not been in his possession, I would have divided it between them into two halves.'

From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Tamim ibn Tarafah That two men recognized a camel, so each of them presented evidence, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) divided it between them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to a people and claims a house in their possession, while the one who currently holds the house claims that it was inherited from his father, not knowing how its matter was originally. He (the Imam) said: 'The one with the stronger evidence is sworn an oath and the house is returned to him.' He mentioned that 'a group of people came to Ali (peace be upon him) disputing over a she-camel. The evidence for these was that they had taken it from his grazing place; they had neither sold it nor gifted it. And the evidence for those was similar. So he ruled in favor of the one with the stronger evidence and swore them an oath.' I asked him then, saying: 'What do you think if the one who claimed the house said: Indeed, this father who is in it took it without a price, and the one who is in it did not bring evidence except that he inherited it from his father?' He said: 'If its matter is thus, then it is for the one who claimed it and brought evidence upon it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said: Indeed, two men disputed before Ali (peace be upon him) regarding a beast of burden. Each claimed it had given birth on his grazing land, and each presented evidence equal in number. So he cast lots between them with two arrows, marking each arrow with a sign for each of them. Then he said: 'O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Great Throne, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Merciful, the Compassionate, which of them is the owner of the beast and is more entitled to it? So I ask You to cast lots and bring forth his arrow.' Then the arrow of one of them came out, so he ruled in his favor.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about two men who testified regarding a matter, and then two others came and testified to the contrary, so they differed. He said: 'A lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls on, upon him is the oath, and he is more deserving of the truth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: A man had two witnesses testify that he owed a man fifty dirhams, and then two others came and testified that he owed him one hundred dirhams. All of them testified in the same setting. He said: 'Cast lots among them, then make those selected by the lot swear by God that they are testifying to the truth.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Humran ibn A'yan said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a young girl who had not yet reached the age of seven, in the case of a man and a woman. The man claimed that she was his slave, and the woman claimed that she was her daughter. He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) has already issued a ruling in this matter.' I said, 'What was his ruling?' He said, 'He used to say: All people are free, except for one who acknowledges slavery upon himself while he is mature, and for one who presents evidence for what he claims of a slave or a slave-girl, then she is returned to him and becomes his slave.' I said, 'And what do you think?' He said, 'I think that I should ask the one who claimed she was his slave to present evidence for his claim. If he brings witnesses who testify that she is his slave, and they do not know whether he sold her or gave her as a gift, the girl is returned to him. Then, if the woman brings someone to testify for her that the girl is her daughter and free like her, she is returned to her and removed from the man's possession.' I said, 'And if the man does not bring witnesses that she is his slave?' He said, 'She is removed from his house. If the woman brings evidence that she is her daughter, she is returned to her. And if the man does not bring evidence for what he claimed, and the woman does not bring evidence for what she claimed, the girl is set free; she goes wherever she wishes.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: In the case of a man who claimed against a woman that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and the woman denied this, so the sister of this woman brought evidence against this man that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and they did not specify a time. 'Indeed, the evidence is the husband's evidence, and the woman's evidence is not accepted because the husband has already acquired the right to the intimacy of this woman, and her sister wants the dissolution of the marriage, so her evidence is not confirmed and not accepted unless with a time before her time or consummation with her.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amriki from Safwan from Ali ibn Matar from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, two men disputed over a beast of burden before Ali (peace be upon him). Each claimed it had given birth to it at his place, on his milking stand. Each presented evidence, equal in number. So he cast lots between them with two arrows, marking each arrow with a sign for each of them. Then he said: "O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Great Throne, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Whichever of them is the owner of the beast and has more right to it, I ask You to cast lots and bring forth his name." So the name of one of them came out, and he ruled in his favor. And it was also the case when the two disputants argued over a female slave, one claiming he bought her and the other claiming he had her give birth, that when they both presented evidence, he ruled in favor of the one at whose place she had given birth.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said: Al-Tayyar said to Zurarah: 'What do you say about musahamah (drawing lots to decide a claim)? Is it not valid?' Zurarah said: 'Yes, it is valid.' Al-Tayyar said: 'Is it not that they have narrated that the lot of the truthful one (al-muḥiqq) comes out?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Come then, so I and you will claim something, then we will draw lots over it and see; is it like that?' Zurarah said to him: 'The hadith came specifically stating: Among no people who entrust their affair to God and then draw lots, except that the lot of the truthful one comes out. But regarding experience (al-tajārib), it was not placed upon experience.' Al-Tayyar said: 'Do you see if both are claimants and they claim what is not theirs, from where does the lot of one of them come out?' Zurarah said: 'If that is the case, a determining lot (sahm al-mubīḥ) is placed with it. If they both claim what is not theirs, the lot of the determining one comes out.'

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen. When he arrived, he said to him, 'Tell me of the most surprising thing that has come to you.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, a group of men came to me who had purchased a slave girl, and they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, so she gave birth to a boy. They all disputed over him, each claiming him. So I cast lots among them and gave him to the one whose lot was drawn, and I guaranteed his share to the others.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Among a group who dispute and then entrust their matter to Allah, the lot will always come out for the one who is right.'

From him, from Hammad, from al-Mukhtār, who said: Abū Ḥanīfah entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and he (the Imam) said to him, 'What do you say about a house that collapsed upon a group of people, leaving two boys, one free and the other a slave to his master, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' He said, 'Abū Ḥanīfah said: Half of this one is freed and half of this one is freed.' Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said, 'Not so, but a lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls upon is the free one, and this one (the other boy) is freed, so he becomes a patron/mawla to this one.'

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling in Yemen regarding a people whose house collapsed upon them, and two boys remained: one free and the other a slave. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cast lots between them, and the lot fell on one of them; he gave him the wealth and freed the other.

From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn who does not have what men have, nor does he have what women have. He said: "The Imam casts lots for this one; he writes 'Abdullah (Slave of God)' on one lot, and writes 'Umdatullah (Slave of God)' on another lot. Then the Imam or the one casting the lots says: 'O God, You are God, there is no god but You. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants regarding that in which they differ. Make clear the matter of this newborn for us, so that inheritance may be established for what You have prescribed for him in Your Book. Then he throws the two lots into a container of indistinguishable lots, then they are shaken, and whichever comes out, inheritance is established upon it.'

From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Sayyabah and Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who said, 'The first slave I acquire is free,' and then he inherited three [other slaves]. He (the Imam) said, 'A lot is cast among them, and whoever the lot falls upon is freed.' He said, 'And casting lots is a Sunnah.'

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has slaves and bequeaths their manumission for one-third of them, he said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) would cast lots among them.'
From him, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: "The drawing of lots is not valid except for the Imam."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn 'Uthman from 'Ali ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about something, and he said to me, 'Every unknown matter has the lot (qur'ah) in it.' I said to him, 'Indeed, the lot may err and may be correct.' He said, 'Everything that God has judged by is not erring.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Hafsh, from Mansur, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a sheep in his possession, then another man came and claimed it, and established the testimony of just witnesses that it was born with him, and he had not given it as a gift nor sold it. And the one who had it in his possession came with testimony like theirs, of just witnesses, that it was born with him, and he had not sold it nor given it as a gift. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Its right belongs to the claimant, and I do not accept testimony from the one who has it in his possession, because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, only commanded that the testimony be sought from the claimant. If he has testimony, [it is accepted]; otherwise, the oath of the one who is in possession [is taken]. Thus did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, command.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu al-Mu'za, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a free man, a slave, and a polytheist all have intercourse with a woman during the same period of purity, and they all claim the child, a lot is cast among them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot is drawn.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the found object (luqata), it is announced for one year, then it becomes like the rest of his wealth.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the found object (luqatah). He said: 'It is announced for one year, whether it is little or much.' He said: 'And whatever is less than a dirham is not announced.'

From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Kathir, from his father, who said: A man asked Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) about the found property (luqatah), so he said: 'Announce it. If its owner comes, hand it over to him; otherwise, keep it for a year. If the owner or someone seeking it does not come, give it in charity. If the owner comes after it has been given in charity, if he wishes, he bears the cost of what was with the giver, and the reward is for the giver; and if he dislikes that, he considers it [as a gift/compensation], and the reward is for the giver.'

From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about the found object (luqatah). He said: 'Do not pick it up. If you are tested (i.e., if you pick it up), then announce it for one year. If its owner comes, then return it; otherwise, place it among the breadth of your wealth, so that what applies to your wealth applies to it, until a claimant comes for it.' He said: And I asked him about silver coins found in a house. He said: 'If the house is inhabited, they belong to its people; and if it is ruined, you are more entitled to what you found.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said: We mentioned the *luqatah* (found property) to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Do not expose it (for people to see), for if people were to leave it, its owner would come until he takes it.'

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from some of his companions, from the one who passed away (peace be upon him), who said: The found object of the Sanctuary (Haram) is not touched by a hand or a foot; and if people were to leave it, its owner would come and take it.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man found a dinar in his house. He said: 'Does someone else enter his house?' I said: 'Yes, frequently.' He said: 'This is a found object (luqata).' I said: 'But a man found a dinar in his chest (strongbox).' He said: 'Does someone else put his hand into his chest or place something in it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then it is his.'

From him, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a house in which silver coins are found, so he said: 'If it is inhabited and its people are in it, then it belongs to them. And if it is ruined and its people have left it, then the one who found the money is more entitled to it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who stayed in some of the houses of Mecca and found buried therein approximately seventy dirhams. They remained with him and he did not mention them until he arrived in Kufa. I asked: What should he do? He said: 'He should ask the people of the house, perhaps they know of it.' I said: 'And if they do not know of it?' He said: 'He should give it in charity.'

From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the found object (luqata), so he showed me a ring in his hand made of silver, saying, 'Indeed, this is from what the flood brought, and I intend to give it in charity.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from some of our companions from Abu al-'Ala' said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man found wealth and announced it; when a year had passed, he bought a servant from it. The seeker of the wealth came and found the girl who was bought with the dirhams was his daughter. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not entitled to take anything except his dirhams, and the daughter is not his; he only has his principal capital, for his daughter was owned by the people.' From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Ja'far: He said: I wrote to the man (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who bought a camel or a cow for sacrifice, and when he slaughtered it, he found in its belly a pouch containing dirhams or dinars or gems. Who does that belong to? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Announce it to the seller; if he does not know it, then the item is for you, may God grant you provision of it.'

From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever finds something, it is for him; let him enjoy it until its claimant comes to him. When the claimant comes, he must return it to him.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a sheep.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a camel.' He said: 'With it are its footwear and its water-skin; its footwear is its hoof, and its water-skin is its hump, so do not exhaust it.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever finds a beast of burden or a camel in an open desert land that has become weak and stood still, and its owner left it because it could not follow him, and another person takes it and stays with it and spends on it until he revives it from its weakness and death, then it belongs to him and the owner has no claim upon it, and it is merely like a free-for-all item."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who left his beast of burden due to exhaustion, saying: 'If he left it in a place of shelter and water and safety, it belongs to him; he takes it wherever he finds it. And if he left it in fear and without water and without shelter, it belongs to whoever finds it.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no harm in picking up the staff, the splinter, the peg, the rope, the tether, and similar items." He said, "And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no seeker for this.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Safwan al-Jammal, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever finds a stray animal (or item) and does not announce its characteristics, and then it is found with him, then it belongs to its owner, or an equivalent of it from the wealth of the one who concealed it."

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from al-Asamm from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Regarding the beast of burden, if its owners let it roam freely or were unable to provide its fodder or expenses, it belongs to the one who revived it.' He said: 'And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who left his beast, saying: If he left it in fodder, water, and safety, it is for him to take whenever he wishes; and if he left it without fodder, water, and safety, it belongs to the one who revived it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The stray animal is not eaten by anyone except those who are astray, if they do not announce its finding.

From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the two shoes, the water skin, and the whip that a man finds on the road: does he benefit from them? He said, 'He should not touch them.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a sheep.' He said: 'It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.' The man said: 'I found a camel.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Its footgear is its feet, and its water-skin is its belly, so do not exhaust it.'

From him, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the stray sheep in the open desert, so he said to the questioner, 'Is it for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf?' He said, 'And I do not like to touch it.' And he was asked about the stray camel, so he said to the questioner, 'What do you have with it? Its hoof is its shoe, and its belly is its water-skin. Leave it alone.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who catches a bird that is worth many dirhams, with its wings intact, and he knows its owner. Is it permissible for him to keep it? He said: 'If he knows the owner, he should return it to him. And if he does not know the owner, and he possesses its two wings, then it is his. And if a claimant comes to you, do not suspect him; return it to him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Fudayl ibn Ghazwan said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and al-Tayyar said to him: 'My son Hamzah found a dinar during the tawaf (circumambulation), its writing had worn off.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is his.' 28 - Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Rajaa' al-Khayyat said: 'I wrote to him: I was in the Masjid al-Haram and saw a dinar, so I reached for it to take it, and behold, there was another. Then I moved the pebbles, and behold, there was a third. I took them and announced them (as lost property), but no one recognized them. What do you command me regarding that? I am your ransom.' He said: 'He wrote to me: I have understood what you mentioned regarding the two dinars, under my mention of the place of the two dinars.' Then he wrote under the story of the third: 'If you are in need, give the third in charity; and if you are wealthy, give all of them in charity.' The one who seeks it (the finder) is its guarantor.

From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man from the Muslims who deposited with him a man from the thieves [some] dirhams or goods, and the thief is a Muslim; should he return it to him? He said: 'He does not return it. If he is able to return it to its owners, he should do so; otherwise, it remains in his hand like a found object (luqata). He should announce it for one year. If he finds its owner, he returns it to him; otherwise, he gives it in charity. If the owner comes after that, he is given a choice between reward and compensation. If he chooses the reward, the reward is his; if he chooses compensation, he pays compensation to him, and the reward remains his.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding a stray animal that a man finds, if he intends to take a fee (reward) for it and it perishes, he is liable (for its value); and if he did not intend to take a fee for it and it perished, there is no liability upon him.'

From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about the setting of the fugitive slave and the stray animal. He said, 'There is no harm.' And he said, 'Only the stray ones eat the stray animal.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Abu al-Qasim, from Hanan, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the found object (al-luqatah), and I was listening. He said: 'Announce it for a year. If you find its owner, then [return it]; otherwise, you are more entitled to it.' He said: 'It is like your own wealth.' He said: 'Choose for him, when he comes to you after a year, between its reward (compensation for keeping it) and paying it to him, if you had consumed it.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamdani, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Ghailban, who said: I found thirty dinars one day, so I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that. He said to me, 'Where did you find it?' I said to him, 'I was returning to my house when I found it.' He said, 'Return to the place where you found it and make it known. If its claimant comes after three days, give it to him; otherwise, give it in charity.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamdani, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "A man from the people of Medina came to me and asked me about a man who found a sheep." He said: "So I ordered him to keep it with him for three days and ask about its owner. If the owner came, [he returns it]; otherwise, he sells it and gives its price in charity."

From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Wassha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Zarih asked him about a slave who takes a found object (luqatah). He said: 'What is there for the slave regarding the found object? The slave does not possess authority over himself, so the slave should not claim it. Indeed, it is appropriate that he announce it for one year in a gathering. If its owner comes, he should return it to him; otherwise, it becomes part of his wealth. If he dies, it becomes inheritance for his children, for whoever inherits him. If no claimant comes for it, it remains in their wealth and belongs to them. And if its owner comes later, they should return it to him.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about the foundling (luqatah) if she is a young girl, is it permissible for the one who picks her up to marry her? He said, 'No, it is only permissible for him to sell her for what he spent on her.' And I asked him about a man who finds a dirham, or a garment, or an animal, what should he do? He said, 'He should announce it for a year. If he does not find its owner, he should keep it in the breadth of his wealth until its claimant comes and he gives it to him. And if he dies, he should bequeath it, and he is liable for it.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who found a coin in a ruin: he should announce it (identify it). If he finds someone who recognizes it, [he returns it]; otherwise, he may enjoy/use it.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Harijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding wealth in which a treasure is found, its zakat is paid. He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Even if it is abundant?' He said, 'Even if it is abundant, I returned it to him three times.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Jafar, from his father, from their ancestors, peace be upon them: That Ali (peace be upon him) was brought a dispute by a man who had taken a runaway slave who was with him, and then the slave fled from him. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'He swears by Allah, the One there is no god but He, that he did not strip him of his clothes, nor take anything that was with him or on him, nor sell him, nor be lenient in releasing him. When he has sworn, he is free from liability.'

From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who took a debtor who fled, and the debtor fled from him, he said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Sa'id, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamun al-Basri, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'mam ibn Abd al-Malik Kirdin Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) set the reward for the runaway slave at one dinar if he is captured in his city, and if he is captured outside his city, then four dinars." The Book of Earnings has concluded, and it will be followed by the Book of Trade, if God wills. 'And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' * And prayer upon Muhammad and his pure family. Concluded by the grace and help of God what we intended regarding commentary and extraction of hadiths on the sixth part of the Book of Tahdhib al-Ahkam according to our division, and we ask God for assistance to complete the extraction of the remaining parts, and that was done by the poor one who confesses to disobedience, Hassan al-Mawssawi al-Khorasani, and all praise is to God alone.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a water share (shirb) with a group of people in a canal that has partners, and some of them become independent of their share. Can he sell his share? He said: 'Yes, if he wishes he sells it for silver, and if he wishes he sells it by measure of wheat.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Abdullah al-Kahili said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him about a water channel shared among a group of people, where each man has a known share of water. One of them became independent of his share. He asked: Can he sell it for wheat or barley? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can sell it for whatever he wishes; this is something about which there is no objection.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, all of them from Aban, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the sale of al-nitaf and al-arba' He said: And al-arba' is when you make a camel accustomed (to carry water), so it carries water and waters the land, then you become independent of it (by selling it or using it for other purposes). He said: So do not sell it, but lend it to your neighbor. And al-nitaf is when it has the right to drink (from a specific water source), so you become independent of it; so he says: Do not sell it, but lend it to your brother or your neighbor.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn Aynan, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling in the flood of Wadi Mahzur that for grain crops, the water is held back up to the shirak (a measure of depth/height), and for palm trees, up to the ka'b (a larger measure), then the water is released to flow below that.' Ibn Abi Umayr said: 'And al-Mahzur is the place of the valley.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling in the flood of Wadi Mahzur that the upper (water source) is held for the lower (fields) for palm trees up to two 'ikb (forearms), and for crops up to two 'sharak (ankles).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling regarding the watering of palm trees by means of the stream (sail): the upper [palm trees] drink before the lower [ones], and the water is lowered to the level of the ankles, then the water is released to the lower [ones], and the one next to them [in turn] is like that, until the walls [of the channels] are finished and the water is exhausted.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fudaylah from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sale of fodder when it is flowing water (sayh), where a man directs the water to his land, channels it to irrigate the grass, and he is the one who dug the river, owns the water, and plants whatever he wishes with it. He said: 'If the water belongs to him, he may plant whatever he wishes with it, and let him give charity of whatever he wishes.' He said: And I asked him about the sale of the harvests of wheat and barley and other harvests. He said: 'It is permissible, so let him sell it if he wishes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Idris ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him and said, 'May I be your ransom, we have farms (diya'), and they have boundaries containing grazing lands (mara'i). One of us has sheep and camels that need those grazing lands for their camels and sheep. Is it permissible for him to enclose (hima) the grazing land for his need of it?' He said, 'If the land is his land, then he may enclose it, and that enclosure extends to what he needs.' He said, and I said to him, 'The man sells the grazing land?' He said, 'If the land is his land, there is no objection.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who owns a pasture (dhiyah) and its boundaries extend to twenty miles, or less, or more. A man comes to him and says, 'Give me from the grazing of your pasture, and I will give you such and such a dirham.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If the pasture belongs to him, there is no harm.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Musa ibn Ibrahim from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the sale of fodder and grazing land, so he said, 'There is no objection to it; the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) enclosed al-Naqi' for the cavalry of the Muslims.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the purchase of unthreshed grain (al-qasil). A man buys it but does not thresh it, and it seems good to him to leave it until its ear emerges as barley or wheat. He had bought it from its owner while the land tax (kharaj) was upon its owners, or it was upon the 'Ajl (non-Muslims). He said: 'If he stipulated at the time of purchase that he may cut it if he wishes, or leave it as it is until it becomes an ear, then that is permissible; otherwise, it is not fitting for him to leave it until it becomes an ear.'

From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, and it added in it: 'If he does so, then upon him is his Tasq and his Nafakah, and for him is what emerged from it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muthanna al-Hannat from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a crop that was sold while it was still grass (unripe), and later became ears of grain (ripe), he said: 'There is no harm if he says, I buy from you what emerges from this crop. So when he buys it while it is still grass, if he wishes, he can let it remain in the ground, and if he wishes, he can wait for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no objection to you buying green crops, then leaving them until you harvest them if you wish, or feeding them before they ear, while they are grass.' And he said: 'There is also no objection to buying crops that have already earred and reached maturity as wheat.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to buy green crops?' He said, 'Yes, there is no objection to it.'

From him, from Zurarah: like it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no objection to you buying crops and green fodder, then leaving it if you wish until it heads, then harvesting it; and if you wish to feed your animal with fodder before it heads, there is no objection to that. But as for when it has headed, do not feed it head by head, for that is spoilage (fasad).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about crops, and I said: 'May I be your ransom, a man planted a crop, whether he was Muslim or a dhimmi (covenant-holder), and he spent expenses on it. Then it occurred to him to sell it for a sum of money to move from his place or for a need.' He said: 'Buy it with silver (dirhams), for its origin is food.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Muhalakah and Al-Muzabana. I asked: 'What are they?' He said: 'That the crop of the palm trees is purchased with dates, and the crop is purchased with wheat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted permission regarding al-'araya (date palm loans) that one may buy [the palm] for its measure of dates. He said: 'And al-'araya is the plural of 'ariyyah, which is the palm tree that belongs to a man in the house of another man, so it is permissible for him to sell it for its measure of dates, and this permission does not apply to anything else.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Muhaqalah. He said: 'Al-Muhaqalah is selling palm trees for dates, and Al-Muzabana is selling grain ears for wheat, and An-Nitaaf is selling the right to water. If you have no need for it, you must not sell it to your neighbor while leaving it for him, and the four-year-old camel that is shared among people, its owner becomes independent of it.' He said: 'He leaves it for his neighbor and does not sell it to him.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ma'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Should I buy the crop?' He said, 'When it is the size of a span.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not buy the crop before it becomes ready (ears of grain). If you buy its root, there is no harm in that. Or if you buy a palm tree, you buy its root, and if there is no fruit in it, there is no harm in that.'

From him, from Ishaq, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The land is leased for wheat, or for dates, or for barley, or for four qirats of silk, or for four qirats of silk cocoons.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no objection to buying green crops; if you wish, you may leave them until you harvest them, and if you wish, sell them as grass."

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled in the case of a man who sold a palm tree but stipulated for himself one palm tree from it, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled for him the entrance to it, the exit, and the length of its fronds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding this date palm: 'That one palm and two palms belong to the man in the other's enclosure.' So they differed regarding the rights of that, and he ruled regarding it: 'That for each of those palms from the land, there is a reach of its fronds from its fronds until its distance.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam from Mis'ma ibn al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the edge of the well of Ma'tin to the edge of the well of Ma'tin is forty cubits, and from the edge of the well of Nadih to the edge of the well of Nadih is sixty cubits, and from the source of the spring to the source of the spring is five hundred cubits, and the road, when its people dispute over it, its boundary is seven cubits.'

Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The distance between one side of the well of al-Ma'tin and the other is forty cubits, and the distance between one side of the well of al-Nadhih and the other is sixty cubits, and the distance between one side of the spring (source) and the other — meaning the channel — is five hundred cubits. And the road, when its owners dispute over it, its boundary is seven cubits."

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The distance between two wells should be, if the ground is hard, five hundred cubits, and if the ground is soft, one thousand cubits. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled in the case of a man who dug a canal and stayed with it for a year, then another man dug a canal beside it, that the water should be shared by alternating nights, this night and that night. If the latter took the water of the former, the latter would be ruined (if the former's water was deeper/more dominant), and if the former took the water of the latter, the owner of the latter had no claim against the former.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sanctuary (haram) of the commonly used well is forty cubits around it.'

32 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub said: A man wrote to the Faqih (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had a mill on the river of a village, and the village belonged to one man or two men, so the owner of the village wanted to divert the water to his village through a different river than the one on which this mill is located, and to disable this mill; is that permissible for him or not? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and act in that matter with goodness, and not harm his brother the believer.' And regarding a man who had a canal in a village, so a man wanted to dig another canal above it; what should be the distance between them so that one does not harm the other, in land that is either hard or soft? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'According to the condition that one does not harm the other, if Allah wills.' And in another narration: 'Fifty cubits, unless it is to a well or to a road, in which case it is less than that, twenty-five cubits.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the water of the riverbed, and he said: 'Indeed, the Muslims are partners in water, fire, and fodder.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a strip of land between two houses, and he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in its favor for the owner of the house whose face [front] is towards the strip.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The neighbor is like the self, [provided there is] no harming and no sin."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Samura ibn Junayd (may Allah curse him) had a date palm in the garden of a man from the Ansar. The Ansari's house was at the gate of the garden, and he would pass by it to go to his palm tree, but he did not ask for permission. The Ansari asked him to ask for permission when he came, but Samura refused. When he refused, the Ansari went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him, informing him of the matter. The Messenger of Allah sent to him and informed him of what the Ansari had said and complained about, and said, 'When you want to enter, ask for permission.' He refused. When he refused, the Ansari bargained with him until he reached the price that Allah willed, but he refused to sell. The Ansari said, 'For it, you will have a date palm in Paradise.' He refused to accept. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the Ansari, 'Go, uproot it and throw it to him, for there is no harm and no causing harm.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad al-Halabi said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about al-Sawad (the fertile lands of Iraq), what is its status? He said: 'It belongs to all Muslims, for those who are here today, and for those who will enter Islam after today, and for those who have not yet been created.' We said: The purchase is from the landowners (al-Dahakin). He said: 'It is not suitable except that he buys from them on the condition that he dedicates it to the Muslims. If the ruler (Wali al-Amr) wishes to take it, he takes it.' We said: And if he takes it from him? He said: 'He returns to him the principal capital, and for him is what he consumed from its produce, according to what he worked.'

From him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii' al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Do not buy anything from the Land of As-Sawad (Iraq) except for one who has a dhimmah (covenant/treaty), for it is indeed spoils of war (fa') for the Muslims."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from 'Ali ibn al-Harith, from Bakkar ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying land from the land subject to khuras (tax), and he disliked it, and said, 'The land of khuras is for the Muslims.' They said to him, 'But a man buys it, and the khuras is upon it.' He said, 'There is no harm, except that he should be shy of the defect of that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about buying from the land of the Jews and Christians, so he said: 'There is no harm in it. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) conquered the people of Khaybar and made a treaty with them to leave the land in their hands, so they would work it and cultivate it, and there is no harm in it. And if you buy something from it, and whoever people revive a piece of the land or work it, they are more entitled to it, and it is for them.'

From him, from Fadala, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about buying their land, and he said, 'There is no harm in buying it, so that when that is the case, it is like their status; you pay in it as they pay for it.'

From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about purchasing lands from the Ahl al-Dhimma (People of the Covenant), so he said: 'There is no harm in purchasing from them if they work it and revive it, for it belongs to them. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was victorious over Khaybar, and the Jews were in it; he expelled them according to a matter (command) and left the land in their hands, so they worked it and cultivated it.'

From him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to a barren land, reclaims it, channels its rivers, develops it, and cultivates it. What is incumbent upon him? He said: 'He must pay the khums.' I said: 'If he knows the owner, what then?' He said: 'He should return his right to him.'

From him, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Whichever group of people revives a portion of the land or cultivates it, they are more entitled to it."

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have land subject to land tax (kharaj), and I have grown weary of it; should I leave it?' He was silent from me for a moment, then said: 'Indeed, our Qa'im (the Awaited Imam), peace be upon him, if he had risen, would have given you from the land more than it is.' And he said: 'And if our Qa'im, peace be upon him, had risen, it would be for the people better than their land plots (qata'i).'
