It is permissible for the mudarib to have intercourse with her. He said: 'Yes.'

From him, from Ja'far and Abu Shu'ayb, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding al-mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership): If a man is given capital and is instructed not to take the capital to another land, but he disobeys and takes it there, he said: 'He is liable (for loss), and the profit is shared between them.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Kawkabi, from al-Amriki al-Khorasani, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: In mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), whatever he spends during his journey is deducted from the total capital, and when he returns to his town, whatever he spends is deducted from his share of the profit.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a partner, and it becomes apparent to him that his partner has cheated him in something. Is it permissible for him to take from him the equivalent of what was taken, without making that clear? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is good for them if they partnered in the trust of Allah, and I like for him, if he sees something of that from him, to conceal it from him, and I do not like for him to take anything from him without his knowledge.'

From him, from a man who said: I wrote to the Jurist (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bought half of a house, undivided, from another man, and his partner, who owned the other half, was absent. When he took possession and moved out, the house collapsed, and a torrential flood came and destroyed it and carried it away. Then his absent partner came and claimed the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) from this man. He gave him the pre-emption, on the condition that he return his money in full, which he had paid for its price. He said to him: 'Reduce from me the value of the construction, for the construction has collapsed and the flood has taken it away.' What is obligatory in that matter? So he (peace be upon him) issued a ruling: 'He has nothing but the first sale and purchase, if God wills.'

From him, from Ahmad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say: "Whoever dies and with him is capital for mu'darabah (profit-sharing partnership), he said: 'If he named it specifically before his death, saying: This is for so-and-so, then it is for him; and if he died and did not mention it, then it is the example/share of the creditors.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gave money to another man to buy a specific type of goods via mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), and he went and bought something other than what he was ordered, he said: 'He is liable (for the difference/value), and the profit is shared between them according to what they stipulated.'

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, from Rifah ibn Musa, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The partner (mudarib) says to the owner (sahib): If you cause him harm or consume his capital, you are liable (guarantor) for him; and he (the mudarib) is liable if he violates the condition.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I purchased a piece of land, and when I had established ownership of it, I stood up and walked a few steps, then I returned, intending for the sale to become binding.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'What is the condition (option of inspection) in animals?' He said, 'Three days for the buyer.' I asked, 'What is the condition in non-animals?' He said, 'The two sellers have the option as long as they have not separated; and when they separate, there is no option after their mutual satisfaction.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Any man who enters into a sale transaction has the option (to cancel) until they part company; when they part company, the sale becomes binding." He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "My father bought a piece of land called al-Uraidh from a man, purchasing it from its owner for dinars. He said, 'I will give you silver (dirhams) for every dinar, ten dirhams.' So he sold it to him for that. My father stood up quickly, and I followed him. I said, 'O father, why did you stand up quickly?' He said, 'I wanted the sale to become binding.'"

As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them all), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man claps his hands in confirmation of a sale, the sale becomes binding, even if they have not yet separated.' This does not contradict what we previously stated, that separation by bodies is what necessitates the sale, because what this report necessitates is that clapping in confirmation of the sale, without separation, is a cause for the sale to be binding. The meaning of this is that it is a cause for the permissibility of ownership, provided that they separate by bodies and do not annul the contract while they are still in the same place. The earlier reports indicated that they have the option (to annul) as long as they have not separated by annulling the concluded contract. And his saying 'even if they have not separated' may mean if they have not separated by a distant separation or a specific separation, because the amount that necessitates the sale is something small, even if it is the distance of a step, for the sale becomes binding by it. And on this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked: A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him and says, 'I will bring you their price.' He (the Imam) said: 'If he comes within the time between them and three days, [the sale is valid]; otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In a man who bought goods from a man and finalized the deal, except that he left the goods with him and did not take possession of them. He said, 'I will come to you tomorrow, if God wills,' and the goods were stolen. Whose money would they be? He said, 'From the money of the owner of the goods who is in his house, until he takes possession of the goods and takes them out of his house. And when he takes them out of his house, the buyer is liable for their value until he returns their money to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I bought a load (of goods) and gave part of its price, and left it with its owner. Then I was detained for a few days. Then I came to the seller of the load to take it, and he said, 'I have sold it.' So I laughed, then I said, 'By Allah, I will not leave you unless I litigate with you.' He said to me, 'Will you be satisfied with Abu Bakr ibn Ayash [as judge]?' I said, 'Yes.' So we went to him and narrated our story to him. Abu Bakr said, 'Whose opinion do you prefer that I judge between you two by: your companion's [the seller's] or someone else's?' I said, 'By my companion's [the seller's] opinion.' I heard him [the Prophet, peace be upon him] say: 'Whoever buys something, let him bring the price within three days; otherwise, there is no sale for him [the buyer has the option to cancel].'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Haytham ibn Muhammad from Aban ibn Uthman from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from 'Abd al-Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever buys a sale, and three days pass and he does not come, then there is no sale for him.

From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, that he asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): About a man who sells a transaction but its owner does not take possession of it, and he does not take possession of the price. He said: 'The period between them is three days; if he takes possession of his sale, otherwise there is no sale between them.'

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The Muslims are bound by their conditions, except for every condition that contradicts the Book of Allah (Exalted and Glorious), which is not valid."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Whoever stipulates a condition that contradicts the Book of Allah (Exalted and Mighty), the condition is not valid for the one upon whom it was stipulated; and the Muslims are upon their conditions in what agrees with the Book of Allah (Exalted and Mighty).'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man and 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sa'id ibn Yasar said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We mix with people from Ahl al-Sawad and others, and we sell to them, earning ten for twelve and ten for thirteen, and we make that binding between us and them for a year or thereabouts. So the man writes for us on his house or on his land with that money which contains the surplus that he took from us as a pledge (shira'), having sold and taken the price. We promise him: if he brings the money to a set time between us and him, we will return the pledge to him; and if the time comes and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is ours. What do you think about the pledge? He said: 'I think it is yours if he does not act (pay), and if he brings the money for the time, then return it to him.'

From him, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "If you sell [an item] to a man on condition, then if he brings you your money, [the sale is valid]; otherwise, the sale is for you [i.e., you may keep the item or the sale stands as yours]."

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of' a man who bought a garment with a condition until midday; profit was presented to him, so he wanted to sell it. He (AS) said: 'Let him testify that he was pleased with it and it became obligatory upon him, then let him sell it if he wishes. If he kept it in the market and did not sell, then it has become obligatory upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The two parties to a transaction have the option of cancellation for three days in the sale of animals, and in other types of sales until they separate."

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil and Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The two traders have the option [to cancel the deal] until they part, and the owner of the animal [has the option] for three days."

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In all animals, there is a period of three days for the buyer, and he has the option (to return or keep) whether he stipulated it or did not stipulate it.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The condition (of inspection) in animals is three days for the buyer, whether he specified it or not. If the buyer creates a change in what he bought before the three days, that is his consent, so he has no right of return. It was said to him, 'What is the change?' He said, 'That he touches it, or kisses it, or looks at it in a way that was forbidden to him before the purchase.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a female slave from another man with a condition (of warranty) for a day or two days, and she died while in his possession, and the price had been paid. He asked: 'On whom is the liability?' He (the Imam) said: 'There is no liability on the buyer until his condition (period of warranty) expires.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Wasshash, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The warranty period for sale in slaves is three days, if there is in them a defect or leprosy or something similar to these, and its warranty is one year from insanity; and whatever is after one year is not valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding a man who bought a female slave and stipulated for her owners that they should not sell her nor give her away, he said: 'He fulfills that if he stipulated it for them.'

From him, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Abu al-Mi'za, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two men who shared in wealth and made a profit from it, and the wealth was a debt upon them, one said to his partner: 'Give me the principal, and the profit is yours, and whatever I owe (you), you owe (me).' He said: 'There is no harm with it if it is stipulated upon him, and even if it is a condition that contradicts the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, it is a return to the Book of Allah.' And he said: 'In all animals, there is a stipulation of three days for the buyer, and he is at option during them, whether stipulated or not stipulated.' And from a man who bought a sheep and kept it for three days then returned it, he said: 'If during those three days he drank its milk, he returns with it three Amadds, and if it did not have milk, there is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah or others from whom he narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who buys something that spoils from its day, and leaves it until he brings the price, he said: 'If he brings the price between it and the night, [the sale is valid], otherwise there is no sale for him.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who sells something, and the buyer says it is for such and such an amount less than what the seller said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The word of the seller prevails with his oath, if the item is still in its original state (available/not yet taken by the buyer).'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Husayn ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When the two traders are truthful and sincere, blessings are bestowed upon them; but when they lie and cheat, blessings are not bestowed upon them. And they both have the option to cancel the deal as long as they have not parted. If they differ, then the word of the owner of the goods prevails, or they may cancel the deal."

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who purchased a garment from the people of the market for his family and took it on condition that profit be given for it, so he said: 'If he desires the profit, he should make the garment obligatory upon himself, and he should not make it in his own mind that if he returns it to him, he returns it to its owner.'

From him, from Ayoub ibn Nuhr, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a property (ضيعة), and he used to enter it and exit from it. When he paid the money, he went to the property, inspected it thoroughly, then returned and asked the seller to take back the deal (istaqala), but the seller did not agree. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had inspected it or looked at ninety-nine pieces of it, and one piece remained that he had not seen, he would have the option of inspection (khiyar al-ru'yah) regarding that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Two rak'ahs that the married man prays are superior to seventy rak'ahs that the unmarried man prays."

And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, from al-Asamm, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wretches among your dead are the bachelors (unmarried men).'

And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Faddal and Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to Abu (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Do you have a wife?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'I do not desire this world and what is in it, but I spent a night without having a wife.' Then he said, 'The two rak'ahs prayed by a married man are better than a single man who stands in prayer all night and fasts all day.' Then Abu gave him seven dinars and said to him, 'Marry with these.' Then Abu (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Take wives, for they provide sustenance for you.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A Muslim man does not acquire any benefit after Islam that is superior to a Muslim wife who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and guards him when he is absent from her in herself and in her wealth.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Like the first hadith, and it added in it, so Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah said: 'I am your ransom, so I do not have a wife.' He (the Imam) said: 'Do you not have concubines?' Or he said: 'Mothers of children.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You are not single (unmarried).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three things make the private part permissible: marriage with inheritance, marriage without inheritance, and marriage by ownership of the right hand.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The private part (is made permissible/halal) by three: marriage by inheritance, marriage without inheritance, and marriage by possession of the right (concubinage).'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (the two Imams), upon them be peace, who said: I asked him about a man who permits his brother the sexual access to his female slave/concubine. He said: 'She is permissible for him as long as he permits her to him from her.'

And from him, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, who said: "There is no objection to a man making his female slave permissible (for marriage) for his brother."

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Karram ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man permits the private part of his concubine to his brother.' He said, 'Yes, there is no objection; he has whatever he has permitted from her.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Mudarib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Muhammad, take this slave girl; she will serve you and you may derive benefit from her. So when you go out, return her to us.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who permitted her slave girl's private part to her son, he said: 'It is permissible for him.' I said: 'Then is the price (dowry/value) permissible for him?' He said: 'No, only what she permitted for him is permissible for him.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Does a man make the vulva of his concubine permissible for his brother?' He said, 'Yes, for him whatever he makes permissible for himself from her.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who made her slave-girl permissible for me, and he said: 'That is for you.' I said: 'But what if she is joking?' He said: 'How is it with you regarding what is in her heart? If you know that she is joking, then it is not (permissible).' As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked him about a man who makes the private part of his slave-girl permissible for him, he said: 'I do not like that.' So in it is not that which necessitates the prohibition of what we mentioned, because it came in the place of dislike (karahah), and the Imam (peace be upon him) explicitly stated that with his saying 'I do not like that'. The reason for the dislike of that is that this is something which others besides us do not consider, and among those who criticize us for it are our opponents, so abstaining from what this path is is more preferable. And it is permissible that he only disliked that if it was not stipulated in the child that he be free (hur), so as for if it was stipulated, then the dislike has also departed from it. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a woman who makes her female slave girl's private part permissible for her husband. He said, 'I dislike this; what will she do if she becomes pregnant?' I said, 'She will say, if she becomes pregnant from you, then she is for you.' He said, 'There is no harm in this.' I said, 'And a man does this with his brother?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

And as for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): regarding the woman who says to her husband, 'My slave girl is for you,' he said, 'It is not permissible for him to have her private part (for sexual use) unless she sells it to him or gifts it to him.' This report is understood to mean that when she says to him, 'It is for you,' she means what is below the private part (i.e., for service), because it is known from the custom of women that they do not make their husbands permissible in sexual intercourse with their slave girls, and if the matter is thus, it is not permissible for him to have her private part in any case. As for the master (owner), it is not permissible for him to make his slave permissible in sexual intercourse with his slave girl except through a contract (of ownership/possession).

That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan from al-Husayn, his brother, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) He was asked about the slave man: Is it permissible for him to have intercourse with the slave woman without marriage if his master permits him? He said, 'It is not permissible for him.' And it is appropriate that in this type of marriage, the phrase of 'permissibility' (tahlil) be observed, and the phrase of 'loan/borrowing' ('ariyyah) is not suitable for it. What indicates this is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, indeed some of our companions have narrated from you that you said: "If a man makes his slave-girl permissible for his brother, then she is permissible for him."' He said: 'Yes, O Fudayl.' I said to him: 'What do you say about a man who has a valuable slave-girl who is a virgin, and he makes what is below her private part permissible for his brother? Is it permissible for him to take it?' He said: 'No, he only has what he made permissible for her, and if he made a kiss permissible for her, only that would be permissible for him.' I said: 'What do you think if he made what is below the private part permissible for him, and desire overpowered him so he took it?' He said: 'It is not proper for him to do that.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In the man says to his wife, 'Make my concubine permissible for me, for I dislike that you see me exposed,' so she makes her permissible for him. He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not permissible for him from her except that (exposure), and he does not have the right to touch her or have intercourse with her.' Hisham added: 'Does he have the right to visit her?' He said, 'It is not permissible for him except what she said.' And that which indicates that whenever her private part becomes permissible to him, whatever else becomes permissible to him is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali, from al-Khashshab, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'rin, from al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man permits himself a kiss from his concubine, he is not permitted anything else; and if he permits himself from her that which is below the private part, he is not permitted that part; and if he permits himself the private part, all of it is permitted to him." And the ruling for the slave-girl and the mudabbarah (slave-girl whose manumission is deferred until her master's death) is the same as what we have mentioned.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a slave girl shared between two men who had both manumitted her partially, then one of them made her private part permissible to his partner. He said: "It is permissible for him, and whichever of them dies before his partner, half of her becomes free from the side of the one who died, and the other half remains manumitted." I said: What do you think if the remaining one of them wants to have intercourse with her? He said: "No, unless he establishes her manumission and marries her with her consent, a marriage with a dowry whenever he wishes." I said to him: Hasn't half of her become free? She has owned half of her neck, and the other half belongs to the remaining one who manumitted her? He said: "Yes." I said: If she makes her master permissible in her marriage and makes that permissible for him, he said: "That is not permissible for him." I said: Why is it not permissible for him, just as you permitted the one who owned half of her if he made her private part permissible to his partner? He said: "Indeed, the free woman does not give away her private part, nor lend it, nor make it permissible, but she has a day from herself and the one who manumitted her has a day. So if he wishes to marry her for enjoyment in the day in which she owns herself, he may enjoy from her, whether little or much." And whenever this manumitted slave girl gives birth, her child will be slavery for her master, unless the one who made it permissible for him had stipulated freedom for him, for then he becomes free by the previous condition, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man permits the private part of his slave girl to his brother.' He said: 'It is permissible for him.' I said: 'What if she bears a child from him?' He said: 'The child belongs to the master of the slave girl, unless he stipulated to the master of the slave girl when he permitted her to him: 'If she bears a child, he is free.'

And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan al-Tassar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the temporary marriage (mut'ah) of the private part. He said, 'There is no harm in it.' I said, 'And if a child is born from it?' He said, 'It belongs to the owner of the girl, unless he stipulates otherwise for him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulaym al-Farra' from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who permits the private part of his slave girl to his brother, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in that.' I said: 'But he has impregnated her.' He said: 'He keeps the child for himself and returns the slave girl to her master.'

And what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man makes his female slave permissible (for marriage) for his brother, or a free woman makes her female slave permissible for her brother. He said: 'He is permitted from that what he permitted.' I said: 'Then she bore a child.' He said: 'The child follows the free parent among his two parents.'

And what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Sulayman from Hariz from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man makes his female slave permissible (for intercourse) for his brother.' He said, 'There is no harm.' I said, 'But she has borne a child.' He said, 'He attaches the child to himself and returns the female slave to her owner.' I said to him, 'He did not give him permission for that.' He said, 'He has given him permission, but he is not certain that it will happen.' Therefore, these narrations are not contradictory to what we have previously mentioned, because in none of them is it stated that the child attaches to the free status, or that he attaches the child to himself, even if he did not stipulate; rather, it is possible. And when the narrations that we have mentioned come in a detailed manner, stating that whenever he stipulated, it attaches to him, and whenever he did not stipulate, it remains enslaved, we interpret these narrations in light of the detailed ones. And his saying (peace be upon him), 'He gave him permission, and he is not certain that it will happen,' is not a barrier to him having stipulated that if it were to occur there, it would attach to him. Rather, he did not give him permission for exposing her (to intercourse) in a manner that the child would result from it, and he obligated caution upon him, even if he had stipulated that if a child were to occur, it would attach to free status, according to what we have previously mentioned. And it is possible that what he meant (peace be upon him) by 'he attaches the child to himself' is attaching him by price (buying him back), because his child is not to be enslaved, but rather he is sold for him. And that which indicates this is what has been narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who permits his brother to have intercourse with his slave-girl while she goes out for his needs, He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is permissible for him.' I asked: 'What do you think if she bears a child, what is done with him?' He said: 'He belongs to the master of the slave-girl, unless he stipulated for her when he permitted her that if she bears a child, he is free.' He said: 'If he did so, he is free.' I asked: 'Does he own his child?' He said: 'If he has wealth, he buys him at the price.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who said to a man, 'The private part of my slave girl is lawful for you,' so he had intercourse with her and she bore a child, he said: 'The child is valued for him at its price.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna said: I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man entered and asked him about a man who has sexual relations with a woman unlawfully (zina), can he marry her? He said, 'Yes, and her mother and her daughter.'

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "If a man had sexual intercourse with a woman, then they both repented, and he married her, there is no blame upon him from that."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who has illicit intercourse with a woman, then decides to marry her lawfully, the first part is fornication and the last part is marriage. His example is like that of a palm tree: a man takes its fruit illicitly, then buys it later, and it becomes lawful for him.' And it is not appropriate for him to marry her after the illicit intercourse unless he waits for her to purify her womb (complete the 'Iddah').

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'A man commits fornication with a woman, then it occurs to him to marry her; is it permissible for him to do so?' He said: 'Yes, if he avoids her until her waiting period (ʿiddah) is completed, by purging her womb from the water of fornication, then it is permissible for him to marry her.' As for that which indicates that as long as she remains persistent (in the sin), it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with her, is what we have narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu al-Mi'za from al-Halabi who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A woman who is publicly known for fornication is not married off, nor is a man who is publicly known for fornication married off, except after repentance is established from them.'

And the chain of narration is from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman (illicitly), and then later desired to marry her. He said: 'If she repents, it is lawful for him to marry her.' I asked: 'How is her repentance known?' He said: 'He invites her to what they used to do of illicit intercourse; if she refuses and seeks forgiveness from her Lord, then he knows her repentance.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man: is it permissible for him to marry a woman with whom he had illicit relations? He said, 'If he perceives maturity/reasonableness in her, then yes; otherwise, let him tempt her into illicit relations; if she continues with him, she becomes forbidden to him; if she refuses, let him marry her.' The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And there is no harm for a man to marry a woman whose mother or daughter he had intercourse with; the marriage of the mother and daughter is not forbidden to him, whether the intercourse was before the contract as we clarified, or after it, in any case. (1350) 8. The one who mentioned it narrated - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man asked him, 'A man had illicit relations with a woman; is her daughter permissible for him?' He said, 'Yes, indeed, the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): He was asked about a man who has sexual relations with a woman, does he marry her daughter? He said: "No, but if he had a wife, then he had sexual relations with her daughter or her sister, the one he has (the wife) is not forbidden to him."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man has sexual intercourse with a woman, her daughter does not become permanently forbidden to him, even if he had previously married the daughter and had not yet consummated the marriage with her; in that case, his marriage to the daughter is annulled. And if he married the daughter, consummated the marriage with her, and then had sexual intercourse with her mother after having consummated the marriage with the daughter, his sexual intercourse with the mother does not invalidate the marriage to the daughter, provided he had already consummated it with her." And this is his saying: 'That which makes something forbidden does not invalidate the permissible, if it is thus.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id ibn Yasar said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman, and then he marries her daughter. He said, 'Yes, O Sa'id, indeed the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from one who narrated it from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man committed fornication with a woman; is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: 'Whatever is forbidden by a prohibition remains forbidden.' (i.e., the act of fornication does not create a permanent marital prohibition). The explanation in these two narrations and what follows their pattern, which includes the wording of marriage in the future or present, is that the fornication was with the woman without sexual intercourse (consummation) and penetration. As for with intercourse, it is not permissible, according to what we have previously stated. What indicates this is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both) said: I asked him about a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman, is it forbidden for him to marry her mother from breastfeeding or her daughter? He said, 'No.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman, if he maries her milk-mother or her daughter, he said, 'No' (it is forbidden). And if a man has a wife and she commits fornication, he has the choice between keeping her or divorcing her, and divorce is not obligatory upon him for that.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abbad ibn Suhayb, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no objection if a man keeps his wife [in the marital home] if he sees her committing fornication, provided she is committing fornication, and if the hadd punishment is not carried out upon her, then there is no sin upon him from her sin."

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who was pleased with a woman and inquired about her, and if something of immorality was found in her, he said, 'There is no harm in him marrying her and making her chaste.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Marry the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt in place of the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister, without their permission.

And from them (the narrators), from Fadala, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Do not marry the daughter of the sister while she is married to her paternal aunt, except with her permission; and marry the paternal aunt while she is married to the daughter of the sister without her permission."

And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "It is not permissible for a man to marry two sisters (or a woman and her aunt) simultaneously, nor to marry a woman and her maternal aunt simultaneously."

And what he narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father : 'That Ali (peace be upon him) was brought a man who married a woman on top of her paternal aunt, so he lashed him and separated them.' There is nothing in these two narrations that contradicts what we have previously stated, because in the first narration it is not stated that it is not permissible for the man to combine between the woman and her paternal aunt and her maternal aunt with her consent or without consent, and likewise in the last narration which included that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) struck the one who married a woman on top of her maternal aunt, and if that was not in the apparent meaning of the narration and the first narration was detailed, then taking it is more preferable and acting upon it is more appropriate, and that which reveals what we mentioned and adds to its clarification is what he narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said: I asked him about a woman who married a man while he was married to her aunt (paternal) and her aunt (maternal). He said, 'There is no harm in it.' And he said, 'Marry the aunt (paternal) and the aunt (maternal) to the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister, and do not marry the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister to the aunt (paternal) and the aunt (maternal) unless with their consent. And whoever does so, his marriage is invalid.' It is possible that the two reports were issued in the manner of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because everyone who differs from us differs in this matter, and since this is its ruling, Taqiyya is permissible in it, and the report which he narrated...

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda' said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A woman is not married off while her paternal aunt is married to the same man, nor her maternal aunt, nor her milk-sister.' The meaning in this report is like the meaning in what preceded regarding the paternal and maternal aunt from the side of lineage, for that is not permissible with the removal of their mutual marriage (to the same man). As for with the obtaining of permission from both of them, there is no harm with it, according to what we have previously established regarding the ruling of lineage.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The compatible one is he who is chaste and has financial ease."

And Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara from Isa ibn Abdillah from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day while we were with him: 'When someone comes to you whose character and religion you approve, then marry him.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he is lowly in lineage?' He said: 'When someone comes to you whose character and religion you approve, then marry him. Indeed, if you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption.'

And from him, from Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The compatible one is he who is chaste and has financial means."

And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I read the book of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to Abu Shaybah al-Isbahani: 'I understood what you mentioned regarding your daughters, and that you do not find anyone like him, so do not look further in that regard, may Allah have mercy on you. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him to her. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption."'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Duba'ah bint al-Zubayr, daughter of al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib, to Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. So the Banu Hashim spoke about that, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I only intended that the marriages be humble/lowly.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Umar ibn Abi Bakkar, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi to Dhuba'ah bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He married him to it so that marriages would be humble/equal, and so that they would take the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) as a role model, and so that they would know that the most noble of them before Allah is the most pious of them.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Hashimi, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq Al-Ahmar, and Ali ibn Bundar, from As-Sayyari, from some of the Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said: Hisham ibn Al-Hakam met some of the Khawarij, who said to him: 'O Hisham, what do you say about the Ajam (non-Arabs) marrying into the Arabs?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And do the Arabs marry into Quraysh?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And do Quraysh marry into Banu Hashim?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'From whom did you take this?' He said: 'From Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). I heard him saying: "Your bloods are equal, but your genitals (marital eligibility) are not equal."' The Kharijite went out until he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I met Hisham and asked him about such and such, and he informed me with such and such, and mentioned that he heard it from you.' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes, I have said that.' The Kharijite said: 'Here I am, I have come to you as a suitor.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You are indeed equal to me in your nobility and lineage among your people, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, protected us from As-Sadaqah (marriage of convenience/intermarriage for status), which is the dross of people's hands. He disliked that we share in what Allah favored us with with someone whom Allah did not make equal to us in what He gave us.' The Kharijite stood up while saying: 'By Allah, I have never seen a man like him, and by Allah, He rejected me with the ugliest rejection, and he did not deviate from the statement of his companion (Hisham).

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding marriage, and his letter came to me in his own handwriting: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption.'' And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Husayn ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) asking him about marriage, and he wrote back (peace be upon him): 'When one proposes to you who has the religion and trustworthiness you are pleased with, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah in the earth and great corruption.''

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Ali ibn Asbat wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding the matter of his daughters, that he does not find anyone equal to him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'I have understood what you mentioned regarding your daughters, and that you do not find anyone equal to you, so do not look [for anyone else] in that matter, may Allah have mercy on you.' For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him [to her]. If you do not do that, there will be a trial in the earth and great corruption.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) married his mother to his slave, and he himself married his female slave, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan sent him a letter blaming him, saying: 'You have lowered your nobility and your lineage.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) wrote back to him: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted raised every humble thing through Islam, perfected the deficient, and removed blame through it; so there is no blame upon a Muslim, and indeed, blame is the blame of ignorance.' As for my marrying my mother, I only intended thereby to show her kindness/piety.' When the letter reached Abd al-Malik, he said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn has done two things that no one else does; for indeed, by that, he has increased in nobility.'

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated it as a disconnected chain (mursal), saying: Some of our companions said its chain of narration was lost from me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not leave anything that is needed without teaching it to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Among His teaching to him was that he ascended the pulpit one day, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me from the Subtle, the Knowing, and said: Indeed, virgins are like fruit on a tree; when their fruit ripens and is not picked, the sun spoils it and the winds scatter it. And so are virgins; when they reach what women reach, they have no remedy except marriage, otherwise corruption is not guaranteed against them because they are human.' He said: A man stood up to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, whom should I marry? He said: 'The equals.' He said: O Messenger of Allah, who are the equals? He said: 'The believers are equals of one another.' And it is disliked to marry a drinker of wine, even though it is not forbidden. Narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabii', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever drinks wine (khamr) after Allah has forbidden it, is not worthy of being married when he proposes (for marriage).'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, he raised it (to the Imam), saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever marries off his noble daughter to a drinker of wine, he has severed her kinship."

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The drinker of wine (khamr) is not married off when he proposes (for marriage).'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Burayd al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever marries a woman solely for her beauty will not find in her what he loves, and whoever marries her solely for her wealth, God will be left to him (or entrusts her to him), so you should marry the woman of religion.'

And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Misfortune lies in three things: in the beast, the woman, and the house. As for the woman, her misfortune is her high dowry and difficult childbirth. As for the beast, its misfortune is the abundance of its ailments and its bad character. As for the house, its misfortune is its narrowness and the badness of its neighbors."

And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "From the blessing of a woman is the lightness of her provision (cost of living) and the ease of her childbirth, and from her ill omen is the heaviness of her provision and the difficulty of her childbirth."

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Buhlol, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of women is she who, when she enters with her husband and removes her garment, removes her modesty with it; and when she puts on her garment, puts on her modesty with it.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Hamzah said: I heard Jabir al-Ansari narrating, saying: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and we mentioned women and the superiority of some of them over others. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, so inform us.' He said: 'Indeed, among the best of your women is the fertile, the affectionate, the modest, the respected among her family, the humble with her husband, the unveiled (open) with her spouse, the chaste against others, the one who hears his word and obeys his command, and when he is alone with her, she yields to him what he desires from her, and she does not yield to him with the yielding of a man.' Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the worst of your women?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the worst of your women is the humble among her family, the respected with her husband, the barren, the resentful, the one who does not refrain from ugliness, the unveiled when her husband is absent from her, the chaste with him when he is present, the one who does not hear his word nor obey his command, and when her husband is alone with her, she refuses him with the refusal of the stubborn beast when being mounted, and she does not accept his excuse nor forgive his sin.' Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the best of your men?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the best of your men is the pious, the pure, the generous, the two-handed (capable), the sound of the two eyes, the righteous to his parents, and the one who does not force his dependents to rely on others.' Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the worst of your men?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the worst of your men is the show-off, the obscene, the one who eats alone, the one who withholds his provision, the one who strikes his family and his servant, the stingy, the one who forces his dependents to rely on others, the disobedient to his parents.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-A'la ibn A'yan, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry the virgins, for they are the best in terms of mouth (sweetness of speech), the most fertile in terms of bearing children, the best in terms of character, and the most open in terms of the womb. Do you not know that I boast about you to the nations on the Day of Resurrection, even about the fetus? It will remain swollen on the gate of Paradise, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to it, 'Enter Paradise.' It will say, 'No, until my parents enter before me.' Then God, the Exalted, will say to one of the angels, 'Bring me its parents.' He will order them to be brought to Paradise, and He will say, 'This is by the grace of My mercy for you.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three things for which the believer is not called to account: food that he eats, clothing that he wears, and a virtuous wife who assists him and he preserves his chastity through her.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya'qub al-Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to seek his advice regarding marriage. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Yes, marry, and let it be with women of religion, may your hand be dusted [with success].' He also said, 'The example of the virtuous woman is like the white crow, which is rarely found.' He asked, 'And what is the white crow?' He said, 'The one that has one white leg.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Amr ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My wife died, may Allah have mercy on her, and she was compatible with me, and I intend to marry.' He said to me, 'Look where you place yourself, and who you share your wealth with and inform about your religion and your secret. If you are to do so, [choose] a virgin who is known for goodness and good character.' And know that women are created in different types: some are a prize (gain), some are a burden (cost), and some are the crescent moon when it shines for its owner, and some are darkness. Whoever catches the good of them will be happy, and whoever catches the bad has no revenge (can only endure). And they are three types: A virgin, fertile woman who helps her husband throughout his life for his worldly and afterlife affairs, and the world does not help against her; a barren woman who has no beauty and no character and does not help in goodness; and a noisy, restless, backbiting woman who considers much little and does not accept little.

And from him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakam, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'Adhere to those who are fertile (have broad hips/womb), for they are the most fertile.'

And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Choose for your offspring, for the maternal uncle is one of the two milk-relatives."

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from some of our companions, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the woman is a necklace, so look at what she adorns herself with.' He said, 'And I heard him saying: The woman has no danger, neither for her righteous ones nor for her wicked ones. As for her righteous ones, her danger is not gold and silver, and she is better than gold and silver. And as for her wicked ones, her danger is not dust, and dust is better than her.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit Al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of your women is the one with the good scent, the one with good food, who, when she spends, spends in a good manner, and when she holds back, holds back in a good manner; she is from the workers of Allah, and the worker of Allah does not fail.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from some of our companions, he elevated the hadith, saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he intended to marry a woman, would send someone to look at her and say to the one sent: 'Smell her breath; if her breath is sweet, her scent is sweet. And look at her heel; if her heel is smooth, her calf is large.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Malik ibn A'sham, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Marry the woman who is large-eyed, dark-haired, tall/slender, and of average height (or not too tall); if you dislike her (for these traits), then the dowry is on me.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up as a preacher and said, 'O people, beware of the green grass of al-Daman.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the green grass of al-Daman?' He said, 'The beautiful woman in the place of the ugly (or: from a lineage of the ugly).'

And from him, from Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man marries a woman for her beauty or her wealth, he is entrusted to that [quality], and if he marries her for her religion, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will grant him both beauty and wealth."

And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: "Among the character traits of the Prophets (peace be upon them) is the love of women."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammara ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: "Three [things] are from the Sunnah of the Messengers: using perfume, trimming the hair, and frequenting the paths (socializing/moving about)."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I have not seen the weak in religion and deficient in intellect as much as you women, who deprive the man of sound mind (of his religion and intellect).'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) or he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Women are four: Jamia' (the all-encompassing), Mujma' (the gathering), Rabee' (the spring-like), Murba' (the four-fold), Karb (the constraining), Muqmi' (the suppressing), Ghull (the shackle), Qamil (the lousy).'. And in another hadith: 'And Khurqa' (the torn one), Muqmi' (the suppressing) instead of Karb (the constraining)'.

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of the women of my nation are those who become radiant in the morning and have the least dowry.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from non-one, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of your women are the Quraysh, the most gentle with their husbands and the most merciful with their children; the one who is affectionate with her husband is modest with others.' We asked: 'What is al-mujun?' He said: 'The one who does not refuse (intimacy).'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever marries off a bachelor is among those to whom Allah will look with mercy on the Day of Resurrection."

And from him (Al-Hurr al-Amili) from Al-Nawfali from As-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of intercessions is that you intercede between two people in marriage until Allah unites them.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of marrying the Zanj, for he is a creation that is deformed.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Makki, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid (from whom he narrated), from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not buy anyone from the Sudan; if it is necessary, then buy from the Nuba, for they are among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: "And among those who say, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded." Indeed, they will remember that portion, and a group of them will emerge with the Qa'im (peace be upon him) from us.' And do not marry anyone from the Kurds, for they are a type of Jinn, and Allah has lifted the veil from them.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of marrying the foolish woman, for her companionship is a trial and her children are a loss/waste.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Marry off the foolish man, but do not marry off the foolish woman, for the foolish man begets (children), but the foolish woman does not beget (children).

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Some of our companions asked him about a Muslim man who is attracted to a beautiful woman, whether it is permissible for him to marry her while she is mad (mentally ill). He said, 'No. But if he has a female slave who is mad, there is no harm in him having intercourse with her, and he should not seek her offspring.'

And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'The fornicator marries not except a fornicatress or an idolatress.' He said: 'These are women known for fornication, or men who have been known and recognized for it. And people today are in that same status. So whoever has the penalty of fornication established against him, or is known for fornication, it is not fitting for anyone to marry him until repentance is known from him.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and after marrying her, he learned that she had committed fornication. He said: 'If her husband wishes, he may take the dowry from the one who married her off to him, and she is entitled to the dowry for having made her private part permissible to him; and if he wishes, he may leave her (keep her without divorce).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Abi Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When one of you marries, what does he do?" I said to him: "I do not know, may I be your ransom." He said: "When he intends to do so, let him pray two rak'ahs and praise Allah and say: 'O Allah, I intend to marry, O Allah, decree for me from among the women who are most chaste in their private parts, and most protective of themselves for me and of my wealth, and most abundant in provision, and greatest in blessing. And decree for me from her a good offspring, whom You make a righteous successor in my life and after my death.' When she is brought to him, let him place his hand on her forehead and say: 'O Allah, by Your Book I married her, and in Your trust I took her, and by Your words I made lawful her private part. If You have decreed in her womb an offspring, make him a Muslim, sound and whole, and do not make him the share of Satan.' I said: "And how can it be the share of Satan?" He said: "Indeed, when the man approaches the woman and sits in his place, Satan is present with him. If he remembers the name of Allah, Satan withdraws from him. And if he acts and does not mention the name, Satan enters his member, so the action is from both of them together and the seed is one." I said: "By what is this known, may I be your ransom?" He said: "By our love and our hatred."

And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever marries while the moon is in the Scorpion (constellation), he will not see the good."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "A free woman may be married to a slave woman, but a slave woman may not be married to a free woman, nor a Christian nor a Jewess to a Muslim woman; and whoever does that, his marriage is invalid." And I asked him about a man who has two wives, and one of them is more beloved to him than the other, is it permissible for him to favor her with something? He said: "Yes, it is permissible for him to visit her for three nights and the other for one night, because he is permitted to marry four women, so he may assign his two nights wherever he wishes." I said: So there is a wife with him, and he marries a virgin girl? He said: "Then let him favor her when he consummates the marriage with her for three nights, and it is permissible for a man to favor some of his wives over others as long as they are not four."

And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about a man who had a wife and then married another, whether it was permissible for him to favor one over the other. He said: 'He should favor the newlywed for three days if she is a virgin, then he should equalize between them with the contentment of one of them for the other.'

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who has two wives, one of whom is more beloved to him than the other: Is it permissible for him to favor one over the other? He said: 'Yes, he may favor some of them over others, as long as they are not four.' And he said: 'If a man marries a virgin while he has a divorcee (thayyib), he may favor the virgin by three days.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Al-Hadrami from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman while he already has a wife. He said: 'If she is a virgin, he should spend the night with her for seven days; and if she is a non-virgin, for three days.' This report does not contradict the previously mentioned reports, because we interpret the first reports as meaning that he is permitted to prefer the virgin by three days, as she is superior, and then return to equality. And we interpret the last report as indicating permissibility rather than obligation; for whoever does so is not sinful, even if he has left the superior option.

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He gave a ruling regarding a man who married a slave woman, then found means (i.e., financial ability), and did not desire to divorce the slave woman; he was asked about her. He ruled: 'A free woman may be married to a slave woman, but a slave woman may not be married to a free woman if the free woman was the first of the two with him. And if the slave woman was with him before the marriage of the free woman to the slave woman, he shall divide for the free woman two-thirds of his wealth and his self (i.e., his time/attention), meaning his maintenance, and for the slave woman one-third of his wealth and his self.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who marries a slave woman while having a free woman, he said: 'He does not marry the slave woman in addition to the free woman, but he maries the free woman in addition to the slave woman, and the free woman gets two nights and the slave woman gets one night.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said: I asked him about a man who marries a concubine while having a free wife, he said: 'No (it is not preferred/valid in the sense of equal division). If a man has a concubine and then marries a free woman to her, he must give the free woman twice the share he gives to the concubine.' Muhammad said: And I asked him about a man who marries a concubine (while having a free wife), he said: 'There is no harm in it if he is compelled to do so.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has two wives, who wishes to prefer one of them with clothing and a gift; is that permissible? He said, 'There is no harm in that, but strive for justice between them.'

And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Mu'ammara ibn Khallad who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Does a man prefer some of his wives over others? He said: 'No, and there is no objection to it among the slave-women.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has four wives, and he spends the night with three of them during their nights and touches them, but when he sleeps with the fourth one during her night, he does not touch her. Is there any sin upon him in this? He said: 'He is only required to be with her during her night and remain with her until morning, and he is not required to have intercourse with her if he does not desire that.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man wishes to marry a woman, so he looks at her hair.' He said, 'Yes, he merely wishes to purchase her at the highest price.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who looks at the beauties of a woman whom he intends to marry, he said: 'There is no harm; he is merely observing. If a matter becomes decided/established, it will be so.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid al-Attar from some of our companions, he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of looking, for it is an arrow from the arrows of Iblis.' And he said: 'There is no harm in looking at what the clothes are placed upon (i.e., the body parts covered by clothing).'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever buys something that has a defect or a flaw which he was not released from, and he was not released from it, and he made something new in it after he took possession of it, and he knew of that flaw or that defect, then the sale is confirmed upon him, and he is returned an amount equal to what that disease and defect reduce from the price of that [item] had it not had it."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Regarding a man who buys a garment or goods and finds a defect in it: He said, 'If the garment is still intact (not altered), he returns it to its owner and takes back the price. But if the garment has been cut, sewn, or dyed, he returns it with a deduction for the defect.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I and Umar were in Medina, so Umar sold a sack (of wool), each garment [or piece] for such and such. They took it and divided it, and found a garment with a defect, so they returned it. He said to them, 'I will give you the price for which I sold it to you.' They said, 'No, but we will take the equivalent value of the garment.' Umar mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said, 'That is binding upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any man who buys a slave girl, has intercourse with her, and then finds a defect in her which he did not return [for], the seller shall return to him the value of the defect.'
