Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Qummi mentioned in his Nadhirat: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa from Khalid ibn Sadir, brother of Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) About a man who tore his garment over his father, or his mother, or his brother, or a relative of his. He said: 'There is no harm in tearing the necklines (of garments). Moses ibn Imran tore his garment over his brother Aaron. And the father does not tear (his garment) over his son, nor the husband over his wife, but the wife tears (her garment) over her husband. And if a husband tears (his garment) over his wife, or a father over his son, then its expiation is the expiation of breaking an oath, and there is no prayer for them until they expiate and repent from that. And if the woman scratches her face, or cuts her hair, or plucks it, then for cutting the hair is freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people. And for scratching if it bleeds, and for plucking is the expiation of breaking an oath. And there is nothing (specific expiation) for slapping the cheeks except seeking forgiveness and repentance. And the Fatimatis (women of the Prophet's family) tore their necklines and slapped their cheeks over al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). And for a similar case, the cheeks are slapped and the necklines are torn.' And praise is to Allah alone, and Allah sent blessings upon Muhammad and his pure family. The book of Vows, Oaths, and Expiations has concluded, and with Allah is the success. Following it is the Book of Hunting and Sacrifices.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "It is not valid for her to give herself in khul' (redemption) until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not obey your oath, nor obey your command, nor perform ghusl for you from janabah, and I will surely make you lie on your bed with someone you dislike, and I will announce to you without your permission.' And indeed, people used to grant concession for less than this. So when the woman says that to her husband, it becomes valid for him to take what he took from her, and she remains with him having two divorces left, and the khul' counts as one divorce." And he said: "The speech must come from her." And he said: "If the matter were up to us, we would not validate her divorce except for the waiting period (iddah)."

And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the woman who performs khal' (redemption/divorce by wife's initiative). He said: 'It is not permissible for her husband to divorce her (accept the khal') until she says: "I will not be dutiful to you with an oath, and I will not establish God's boundaries within you, and I will not perform the ritual bath for you from major impurity, and I will surely make your bed fertile (bear children for you), and I will surely bring into your house someone you dislike without your knowledge." And they (the husband and witnesses) do not speak, so she is the one who says this. When she performs khal', she is divorced (bain), and he is entitled to take from her wealth whatever he can, but he is not entitled to take from the mukhalli'ah (the woman) all that he gave her.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: «The woman seeking khul' is the one who says to her husband: 'Release me [from the marriage], and I will give you what I took from you.'» And he said: «It is not permissible for him to take anything from her until she says: 'By Allah, I will not fulfill your oath, and I will not obey your command, and I will surely announce in your house without your permission, and I will make another man lie on your bed.'» So if she does that without him knowing, what he took from her becomes permissible for him, and she is divorced with a divorce that is not followed by another, and she becomes irrevocably separated by that, and he is one of the suitors [who can remarry her without a new contract].»

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man performs khul' (divorce by redemption) with his wife, she becomes a single, independent woman, and he is a suitor among suitors. It is not permissible for him to take back what he gave until she is the one who requests that from him, without him harming her, and until she says: 'I will not give you a full share of my dowry, nor will I bathe for you from ritual impurity, and I will surely bring into your house someone you dislike, and I will make your bed shared [with another], and I will not uphold God's boundaries upon you.' When this is from her, then what he took from her is pleasing to him [i.e., the khul' is valid]."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "If the woman says to her husband in a general statement: 'I will not obey you in a specific or unspecified matter,' it becomes permissible for him to take (her dowry/mahr) from her, and he has no right of return (raj'ah) over her." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The view I rely on in this chapter and issue fatwa based on is that the woman who performs khul' (redemption) must necessarily be followed by a divorce. This is the opinion of Ja'far ibn Sam'ah, al-Hasan ibn Sam'ah, Ali ibn Ribat, and Ibn Hudhayfah among the early scholars, and the opinion of Ali ibn al-Husayn among the later scholars. As for the rest of the early jurists of our school, I do not know of them issuing a fatwa to act upon it, and more than the narrations we mentioned and similar ones have not been transmitted from them. It is permissible that they narrated it in the manner we will mention later, even if their fatwa and practice were according to what we said. And that which indicates what we have gone to is what was narrated:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Sammal from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said: "The woman who undergoes khul' (redemption/divorce by mutual consent) is followed by divorce as long as she is in her waiting period." And those of our companions who went early established the correctness of what we have gone towards by the saying of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If the matter were in our hands, we would validate only the divorce of the Sunnah.' And Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah and others established by saying: 'It is established that divorce does not occur by condition, and part of the condition of khul' is that the man says: If you return what you gave, then I will have control over your body, And Ibn Sama'ah also established by what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Safwan from Musa from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Khul' (redemption/divorce by wife's initiative) does not occur until she says: 'I will not obey you in any matter, nor fulfill your oath, nor establish your limit [of authority], so take from me and divorce me.' When she says that, it becomes permissible for him to release her for whatever amount they mutually agree upon, whether little or much. And this does not occur except before a judge (sultan). When she does that, she becomes more in control of herself, without him specifying it as a divorce.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman who performs mubarayah with her husband, or divorces herself from him (khul') with the testimony of two witnesses regarding purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse. Does she become divorced from him by that, or is she still his wife as long as he does not follow it with a formal divorce? He said: 'She becomes divorced from him, and if he wishes to return to her what he took from her and she becomes his wife, he may do so.' I said: 'Indeed, it has been narrated to us that she does not become divorced from him until he follows it with a divorce.' He said: 'That is not khul' then.' I said: 'She becomes divorced from him.' He said: 'Yes.' The reason in this report, likewise, is what we previously mentioned of interpreting it as taqiyyah (dissimulation), and his saying (peace be upon him) 'That is not khul' then' means 'not khul' in their view,' and the intended meaning is not that it is not khul' in our view. And that which also reveals what we mentioned regarding the emergence of that as being in the manner of taqiyyah is what he narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Sulayman ibn Khalid said: I asked, 'What do you think if he divorces her after she has paid khul' (compensation), does it count as a valid divorce upon her?' He said, 'Why would he divorce her when khul' has sufficed for him? And if the matter were up to us, we would not validate a [subsequent] divorce.' And all the conditions of divorce are considered in the chapter of khul', such as her being pure [from menses] and the presence of two witnesses, and other such conditions, according to those who consider that separation (baynunah) occurs through it. But as for what we have chosen, it is a type of divorce.

That was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab who said: I heard Humran narrating from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no khul' (wife-initiated divorce), nor takhyir (husband's option to choose between divorce and keeping), nor mubarā'ah (mutual separation), except upon the woman being in a state of purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse, and with two witnesses who know the man and see the woman, and who are present for the takhyir and the woman's declaration that she is pure from sexual intercourse from the day he gave her the option." He said, so Muhammad ibn Muslim said to him: May Allah rectify you, what is the woman's declaration here? He said: "She has the two witnesses testify against her regarding that for the man, as a precaution that she might come later and claim that he gave her the option while she was menstruating, so they testify against her based on what they heard from her. And the divorce only takes effect upon her if she chooses herself before she rises [from the session]. As for khul' and mubarā'ah, then it binds her if she testifies against herself with consent regarding what is between her and her husband regarding what they separate upon in that session. And if they separate upon something and consent to it, then that is permissible for both of them, and she becomes a final divorce (talaq ba'in) with no return to her, whether he named it talaq or did not name it, and there is no inheritance between them during the waiting period. He said: "And talaq and takhyir are from the side of the man, and khul' and mubarā'ah are from the side of the woman."

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hashimi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The woman who gives khul' (mutual divorce), the woman who gives mubarat (unilateral divorce by wife), and the woman who asks for istibra' (waiting period) in her divorce from her husband, inherit nothing if that was from them during the husband's illness, and even if he dies during his illness, because the bond of marriage has been severed from them and from him.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from his two brothers from their father from Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no khula' (divorce by redemption) except during a period of purity (from menstruation) in which there has been no sexual intercourse.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Fadl, Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The woman who pays khul' (compensation for divorce), if she returns to negotiate a part of the settlement, he says to her: 'I will return to you my right of conjugal access (to your body).'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hadid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Khul' (wife-initiated divorce) is a final divorce and has no right of return. Zurarah said: It occurs only in the same manner as divorce, either when she is pure (from menses) or pregnant, with witnesses. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: As for Al-Mubarat, it is a type of Khul' until the end of the chapter.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah (all of them) from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Mubarā'ah (contest for freedom): The woman says to her husband, 'For you is what is upon me, and leave me,' or she gives him something from herself, and he leaves her. However, he says, 'If you return in anything, I will have authority over your body.' Therefore, it is not permissible for her husband to take from her anything other than the dowry (mahr).

And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: «The al-mubar'ah (mutual divorce where the wife gives up her dowry) is taken from her without the dowry, and the al-mukhtari'ah (divorce where the wife pays compensation) is taken from her whatever she wishes or whatever they agree upon from the dowry or more. And indeed, the al-mubar'ah is taken from her without the dowry, and the al-mukhtari'ah is taken from her whatever she wishes, because the al-mukhtari'ah exceeds in speech and speaks what is not permissible for her.».

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a woman performs mubarāt with her husband, she is one (party to the separation) and he is a suitor (seeking release) among the suitors.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon them both) said: I asked him about al-mubarā'ah (mutual release), how is it? He said: 'There is something due to the wife from her husband from her dowry or from something else, and he has given her part of it, and each of them dislikes the other's companion. So the wife says:

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: Al-Mubarat (mutual separation) is a final divorce, and there is no revocation (raj'ah) in it.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hadid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Al-Mubarat is a final divorce, and there is no revocation (raj'ah) in any of that.' And Zurarah said: 'It does not occur except in the same place as divorce, either when she is pure (from menses) or pregnant, with witnesses.'

And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Humran, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrating. He said: 'Al-mubar'ah (separation by mutual consent) becomes clear from its hour without divorce, and there is no inheritance between them, because the bond of marriage (ismah) has separated from them at the moment that occurred from her and from the husband.'

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Al-Mubarāh (mutual separation) occurs without being followed by divorce." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The ruling I act upon regarding Al-Mubarāh is what we mentioned earlier regarding Al-Khul' (wife-initiated divorce), which is that separation does not occur through it unless it is followed by divorce. This is the opinion of all our accomplished companions, both those who came before and those who came after. And this is not contradictory to this report we mentioned, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'Al-Mubarāh occurs without being followed by divorce' does not imply that separation occurs between them by that means. For we interpret his saying (peace be upon him) as meaning that it becomes Mubarāh if she requests it and says that word with her speech, without the actual legal ruling of divorce, and even if the marriage contract remains intact afterwards. And if it were explicit regarding separation, we would interpret it as a form of Taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence) according to what we mentioned earlier in the Chapter of Al-Khul'.

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them, upon them be peace, said: "There is no Mubarā'ah except upon purity from non-sexual impurity, with witnesses."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And a woman who fears from her husband ill-conduct or avoidance' He said: 'It is the woman who is with the man and he dislikes her, so he says to her: I intend to divorce you. She says to him: Do not do it, for I dislike that I be mocked, but consider my night (i.e., the night of consummation) and do with it what you will, and whatever else is apart from that is for you and leave me in my state.' This is His, the Exalted, saying: 'Then no blame is upon either of them for a settlement between them as settlement.' And this is the settlement (Khul').

And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from al-Hasan ibn Hashim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: "And a woman who fears from her husband disobedience or aversion." He said: "This is when the husband finds the wife displeasing and desires to divorce her, so she says to him: 'Retain me and do not divorce me, and I will leave for you what is on my back (dowry), and give you from my wealth, and make permissible for you my day and night (intimacy), so that becomes pleasing to him.'"

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Send an arbiter from his people and an arbiter from her people.' He said: 'The two arbiters do not separate the couple until they consult the man and the woman and stipulate to them: If we wish, we reunite them, and if we wish, we separate them. If they reunite, it is valid; and if they separate, it is valid.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people.' Do you see if the two arbitrators ask for permission and say to the man and the woman: 'Have you not entrusted your affair to us regarding reconciliation and separation?' And the man and the woman say: 'Yes,' then they testify to that with witnesses upon them? Is their separation valid upon them? He said: 'Yes, but it must be only while the wife is in a state of purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse from the husband.' It was said to him: 'Do you see if one of the two arbitrators says: I have separated them, and the other says: I have not separated them?' He said: 'There is no separation until they both agree on the separation; and when they all agree on the separation, their separation becomes valid.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abu al-Hasan al-Sabati from Ammar ibn Musa, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: "The owner of wealth has more right to his wealth as long as there is a remnant of life in him; he may place it where he wishes."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to bequeath his wealth to his relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wills until death comes to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to leave his wealth to his relatives?' He said, 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wishes until death comes to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The human being has more right to his wealth as long as the soul remains in his body.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi al-Sammal al-Azdi, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The deceased has priority over his wealth as long as the soul remains in it."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Tha'labah, from Abu al-Hasan Umar ibn Shaddad al-Azdi, and al-Sarri, both from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "A man has the most right to his wealth as long as the soul is in him; if he bequeaths all of it, it is valid for him." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The implication of this report, from his saying 'if he bequeaths all of it, it is valid for him,' is a conjecture of the narrator, because the bequest is not executed except in the third, as we will clarify later, unless with the consent and approval of the heirs. Rather, he has the most right to his wealth by spending it during his life on what he prefers and chooses. It is also possible that the meaning of the report is that if he has no heir, near or distant, then it is permissible for him at that time to bequeath all his wealth however he wishes. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both): that he was asked about a man who dies and has no heir and no 'asabah (agnates). He said: 'He should bequeath his wealth wherever he wishes, among the Muslims, the poor, and the traveler (ibn al-sabil).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to give his wealth to his relatives?' He said, 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wills until death comes to him. Indeed, the owner of the wealth may do with his wealth whatever he wills as long as he is alive. If he wills, he may gift it; if he wills, he may give it in charity; and if he wills, he may keep it until death comes to him. If he bequeaths it, then he is not restricted to more than one-third, except that the excellence lies in not neglecting those he supports and not harming his heirs.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murram, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The deceased has more right to his wealth as long as the soul is in him, he can clarify/disperse it with it; and if he says 'after me', it is not for him [to give all] except one-third."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testator has the right to retract his will, whether he is in good health or in illness.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Uqba from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The owner of the will has the right to return (revoke/change) in it and make new provisions in his will as long as he is alive.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled that the 'mudabbir' (a slave manumitted upon the owner's death) is entitled to one-third of the estate, and that a man may revoke his will, adding to it or subtracting from it, as long as he has not died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from some of his companions, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: "A man may alter his will, so he may free a slave whom he had commanded to be owned, and own a slave whom he had commanded to be freed, and give to a person whom he had deprived, and deprive a person whom he had given, as long as he has not died and has returned to it."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Murram from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gives some of his wealth to a man during his illness, he said: 'If he revokes it, it is valid.'

Yunus narrated from Ali ibn Salim, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'My father gave three bequests; which of them should I follow?' He said, 'Follow the last of them.' I said, 'Because they are fewer (in number/weight)?' He said, 'Even if they are few.'

From him, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said: 'If an event befalls me during this illness, then my slave so-and-so is free.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He may revoke from his will whatever he wishes and validate whatever he wishes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The basis of the will is that the man frees whom he wishes, confirms whom he wishes, acquires slavery for whom he freed, and frees whom he acquired slavery for.

From him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man falls ill and makes a will of manumission or charity, he may revoke what he manumitted and what he gave in charity, and do in it whatever he wishes until he dies, and thus is the principle of the will."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever makes a bequest of one-third has harmed the heirs, and a bequest of one-fifth and one-quarter is superior to a bequest of one-third. And whoever makes a bequest of one-third, he leaves [the rest to the heirs].

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies and has no wealth, and he said: 'He has one-third of his wealth, and the wife also [has one-third].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari was in Medina, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca. When death approached him, the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims were praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). So Al-Bara' instructed that when he was buried, his face should be placed facing the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) towards the Qibla. He also instructed to give one-third of his wealth, and this became the established Sunnah. Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): That Durr, daughter of Muqatil, passed away and left a property in shares in a specific location. She bequeathed to her master from her shares an amount exceeding one-third. We are her executors, and we wished to refer this to our Master. If he ordered the bequest to be executed as it is, we would execute it; and if he ordered otherwise, we would adhere to his command in all that he commands, God willing. He (peace be upon him) wrote with his own hand: 'It is not obligatory for her in her estate except one-third. And if you give freely and are the heirs, it is permissible for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I would prefer to bequeath one-fifth of my wealth than to bequeath one-quarter, and I would prefer to bequeath one-quarter than to bequeath one-third. And whoever bequeaths one-third has not left anything [for heirs] and has reached the limit [of excess].' He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who died and bequeathed all or most of his wealth, saying to him: The bequest is returned to the reasonable [limit], excluding the excessive. Whoever wrongs himself and includes the excessive and the deviation in his bequest, then it is returned to the reasonable limit, and the heirs are left with their inheritance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever bequeaths one-third of his estate and is then killed by mistake,' he said: 'One-third of his blood money (diyah) is included in his bequest.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who made a will, and his heirs were the witnesses, so they validated it. When the man died, they annulled the will. Is it for them to reject what they acknowledged? He said: 'It is not for them to do so; the will is binding upon them if they acknowledged it during his lifetime.'
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Like it.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn Husayn from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who made a will, and his heirs were the witnesses, so they validated it for him. When the man died, they annulled it. Is it for them to reject what they had acknowledged? He said: 'It is not for them to do so; the will is binding upon them if they acknowledged it during his lifetime.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn Ya'la, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made a will bequeathing more than one-third, and his heirs were witnesses who approved of that for him. He said, 'It is valid.' Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat said, 'And in my view, this is on the condition that they were pleased with it during his lifetime and acknowledged it.'

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when he made a will, some of his family said to him, 'You have willed away more than one-third.' He said, 'I have not, but what remains from my one-third is so-and-so, and it is for Muhammad ibn Isma'il.'

From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man upon whom death was approaching, who freed his slave boy and made a bequest, which was more than one-third. He said: 'The manumission of the slave boy is upheld, and the deficiency is taken from what remains (of the estate for the heirs).'

From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who bequeathed to his slave one-third of his wealth, he said: 'The slave is appraised, then it is seen what one-third of the deceased's estate amounts to. If the one-third is less than the value of the slave by the amount of a quarter of the value, the slave is freed for that quarter of his value. And if the one-third is more than the value of the slave, the slave is freed and what remains of the one-third after the value is paid to him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to him by his wife, and she frees him from it during her illness. He said: 'Rather, she should gift it to him, and her gift to him is valid, and that is counted from her one-third, if she left anything.' 16 - From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Nuh, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Razi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man dies and bequeaths all his wealth in the channels of charity, and more than one-third. Is that valid for him, and what should the executor do? He wrote back: 'His bequest is valid as long as it does not exceed one-third.' 17 - As for what was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdus, said: A man bequeathed his estate, goods and otherwise, to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him). I wrote to him: 'I am your ransom, a man bequeathed to me all that he left for you, and he left two daughters of his sister. What is your opinion in this?' He wrote to me (peace be upon him): 'Sell what he left and send it to me.' So I sold it and sent it to him, and he wrote to me: 'It has arrived.' Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zur'ar died and bequeathed to my brother Ahmad, and he left a house. He had bequeathed that all his estate be sold and its price sent to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). So we sold it, and a son of his sister and a cousin of his contested it. We settled their matter with three dinars. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan wrote to him and handed over the matter in my presence to Ayub ibn Nuh. And he informed him that it was all that he left, and his cousin and his sister's son contested, so we settled their matter with three dinars. He wrote: 'That has arrived,' and he prayed mercy for the deceased. And I read the reply. Ali said: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Halabi died and left two hundred dirhams. He bequeathed to his wife something of her dowry and otherwise, and bequeathed the remainder to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Ahmad ibn al-Hasan handed them over to Ayub in my presence and wrote to him a letter. The reply came confirming receipt, and he prayed for the deceased. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The first thing we say is that when the reports come from them (peace be upon him) that they performed an action that contradicts what is es

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "If a man frees a servant of his at the time of his death, and then makes another bequest, the bequest is annulled and the female servant is freed from his one-third share, unless there remains from his one-third share an amount sufficient to cover the bequest." Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mahbub from al-Abidi from Ahmad ibn Hilal who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A deceased person made a bequest that a certain amount from the remainder of his one-third share should be paid to a man, and he did not order the execution of the one-third share itself. Is the executor allowed to withhold the deceased's one-third share on account of this payment? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He executes his one-third share and does not withhold it.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamilah, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). From a man who made a bequest at the time of his death saying: 'Free so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so,' until he mentioned five. The third of his estate was evaluated, but it did not reach the value of the eight slaves he ordered to be freed. He said: 'They are valued, and the third is considered; then the first named is freed, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth. And if the third is insufficient, that applies to those he named last, because he bequeathed after the third's limit what he does not own and which is not permissible for him.'" And the narrations we mentioned earlier regarding bequest of more than the third, with the existence of heirs, carry another meaning: that the heirs were only granted and born after he had made the bequest. For if that is the case, the bequest is valid in its entirety or in what he bequeathed, even if it is more than the third. And that which indicates this is what he narrated: -(789) 21 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mutatabbib wrote to him: 'And afterwards, may Allah prolong your life, we inform you, O our master, that we are in doubt regarding this bequest which Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Darayab bequeathed - and that is that the freedmen of our master and his righteous slaves mentioned that it is not for the deceased to bequeath if he has a son more than a third of his wealth, and Muhammad ibn Yahya had bequeathed - more than half of what he left from his estate. If our master and our lord, may Allah prolong his stay, sees fit to open the concealment of this darkness which we complained about and explain that to us, we will act upon it, if Allah the Exalted wills.' So he (peace be upon him) answered: 'If he bequeathed it before he had a son, his bequest is valid, and that is because his son was born after him.' And the relied-upon opinion is what we mentioned first, and what we mentioned adds clarification that the bequest is not valid in what exceeds the third. What he narrated: -(790) 22 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf said: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid had a slave boy who was sound, known, called Maymun. When death approached him, he bequeathed to Abu Al-Fadl Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf all his inheritance and estate, saying: 'Make it d

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Fudalah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the will (testament) for the heir, and he said, 'It is valid.'
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the bequest to the heir, and he said, 'It is valid.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said, like that "If he leaves good, [let there be] bequests to parents and near relatives."
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible for the heir to make a will?' He said, 'Yes.'

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has children from a mother other than the primary one (or from different mothers), should he prefer some of them over others? He said, 'There is no harm in doing so.' Hariz said: Muawiya and Abu Kahmas informed me that they heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) did that with his son al-Hasan, and al-Husayn did that with his son Ali, and my father did that with me, and I did it.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding a man who singles out some of his children with some of his wealth, he said, 'There is no harm in that.'

From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who said to her mother, 'If you die after me, your slave-girl is mine.' He ruled that this is permissible, and if the daughter dies after her, the daughter's slave-girl belongs to the mother.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Wallad al-Hannat said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased making a bequest to the heir, and he said, 'It is permissible.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who confessed to an heir a debt during his illness, so he said: 'A bequest to an heir is not valid, nor is a confession.' The way to understand this report is to assume it is based on a type of precautionary concealment (taqiyyah), because it is the view of all those who differed from the Shia in refusing to validate the bequest to the heir, and this is its ruling: taqiyyah is valid in it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim from Jarrah al-Mad'ani who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a father giving a gift to his child with evidence (as proof of gift), and he said: 'If he gives it to him while in good health, it is valid.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman who releases her husband from her dowry while she is ill, and he said, 'No.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man for whom the dowry (sadaq) or part of it is due from his wife, and she releases him from it during her illness. He said: 'No, but if she gifts him, what she gifts him from her third is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both): Concerning a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah. He said: 'Give to those he bequeathed to, even if they are Jewish or Christian.' Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters the bequest after he has heard it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.' ' (End of quote).

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: That a man who was in Hamadan narrated that his father died and was not familiar with this matter, and he made a will at the time of death, instructing that something be given in the way of Allah. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how should it be done? And we informed him that he was not familiar with this matter, so he said: 'If a man had instructed me to place [it] with a Jew or a Christian, I would have placed it with them.' Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is upon those who alter it.' So look to whoever goes out to this direction, meaning the frontiers (Thughur), and send it to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn Shabib Maridah left a will to a group of Christians who were servants, so we said: Distribute this among the poor Muslims from your companions. So I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him: Indeed, my sister left a will to a group of Christians, and I wanted to divert that to a group of Muslims from our companions. He said: 'Execute the will according to what she willed.' Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, the sin is upon those who change it.'

From him, from his father, from Abu Talib Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, who said: Al-Khalil ibn Hashim wrote to the 'Zi al-Ri'asatayn' (the Governor of Two Districts), who was the governor of Naysapur, that a man from the Magians (Zoroastrians) died and bequeathed some of his wealth to the poor. The judge of Naysapur took it and placed it among the poor of the Muslims. Al-Khalil wrote to the Governor about that. The Caliph al-Ma'mun was asked about it and said, 'I have nothing (specific) regarding it.' Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Magian did not bequeath to the poor of the Muslims, but it is appropriate that the amount of that wealth be taken from the wealth of the Sadaqah (alms-tax) and returned to the poor of the Magians.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah. He said: 'Give it to the one he bequeathed it to, even if he were a Jew or a Christian. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from al-Husayn ibn Umar said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, a man bequeathed to me something in the way of God,' and he said to me, 'Allocate it in Hajj.' I said to him, 'He bequeathed to me in the way of God,' and he said to me, 'Allocate it in Hajj.' I said to him, 'He bequeathed to me in the way of God,' and he said, 'Allocate it in Hajj, for I do not know anything of his way that is superior to Hajj.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who bequeathed to me wealth to be spent in the way of Allah, so it was said to her, 'It will be used for Hajj,' but she said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah.' They said to her, 'Shall we give it to the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?' She said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah as she commanded.' I said, 'Instruct me on how to spend it.' He said, 'Spend it as she commanded you. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says, "So if one alters the bequest after hearing it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing." Do you think if she commanded you to give it to a Jew, would you give it to a Christian?' He said, So I waited for three years after that, then I entered upon him and said to him what I had said to him the first time. He paused for a moment, then said, 'Bring it.' I said, 'To whom shall I give it?' He said, 'Isa Shalaqan.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said: I asked al-Askari (peace be upon him) in al-Madinah about a man who bequeathed wealth in the way of Allah, and he said, 'The way of Allah is our Shiah.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned the way to reconcile this report with the report in which he said 'The way of Allah is the Hajj', that the meaning is that the wealth is given to a man from the Shiah to perform Hajj with it, so it fulfills both meanings together and the reports are saved from contradiction, and this is a good interpretation. As for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hamdani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad who said: Ahmad ibn Hilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a Jew who died and bequeathed to their creditors, and he (peace be upon him) wrote, 'Deliver it to me and inform me so that I may execute it in what is appropriate, if Allah wills.' The first thing in this report is that it is very weak in chain of narrators because all its narrators are criticized, and specifically the author of the decree - Ahmad ibn Hilal - for he is famous for Ghuluw (exaggeration) and the curse, and what is specific to his narration we do not act upon. And even if it were safe from that, there would be no contradiction in it with what we presented from the reports because it is not more than that he ordered him to deliver the wealth to him to place it in its places, and it is not in it that when he sent the wealth to him he did not divide it among the creditors of the bequeathing Jew - rather - it is not impossible that he (peace be upon him) himself oversaw the distribution of that among them, for he (peace be upon him) is more knowledgeable about the manner of division among them and placing it in its places. And on this there is no contradiction between the reports, and he narrated this decree exactly. Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Muhammad who said: Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a Jew who died and bequeathed to his creditors something that I am able to take, is it permissible for me to take it and deliver it to your mawalis, or execute it in what the Jew bequeathed? And he (peace be upon him) wrote,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man makes a bequest to another man while he is absent, it is not for him to reject the bequest. But if he makes a bequest to him while he is in the town, then he is at liberty: if he wishes, he accepts it, and if he wishes, he does not accept it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man to whom an estate is bequeathed, he said: 'If it is sent to him from a country, he is not allowed to return it, and if he is in a province where another can be found, that is up to him.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man makes a bequest to his brother while he is absent, it is not permissible for him to return the bequest to him, because if he were present and refused to accept it, he would seek someone else."

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the man to whom a will is entrusted, he said: 'When it is sent to him from a land, he is not permitted to return it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeaths a will to another man, and the latter refuses to accept it, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not be abandoned in this state.' Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) A man whose father invited him to accept his will, is he allowed to refuse accepting his father's will? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'He is not allowed to refuse.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever kills himself intentionally, he is in the Hellfire, 'abiding eternally therein'.' I said to him: 'What do you think if he made a will and then killed himself immediately? Will his will be executed?' He said: 'If he made a will before an event occurred in himself from a wound or killing, his will is accepted in his third, and if he made a will after he occurred in himself from a wound or killing, perhaps he will die, his will is not accepted.'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever bequeaths one-third of his estate and is then killed by mistake, then one-third of his blood-money (diyah) is included in his bequest.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran or another, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him: A man made a bequest to another man of one-third or one-quarter of his wealth, then the man (the testator) was killed by mistake. He meant the testator. He said: 'This bequest is paid from his inheritance and from his blood-money (diyah).'

4 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who made a bequest to another man of a fixed bequest, unspecified in amount, from his wealth, whether one-third, one-quarter, less than that, or more. Then the testator was killed, and blood money (diyah) was paid for him. He ruled regarding his bequest: 'That it is executed from his wealth and his blood money, just as he bequeathed.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah said: A woman made a bequest to me, saying: 'One-third of my estate shall be used to pay my debt, and a portion of it for so-and-so.' I asked Ibn Abi Layl about this, and he said: 'I see nothing for her, I do not know what 'a portion' is.' Later, I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about it, and informed him of how the woman spoke and what Ibn Abi Layl said. He said: 'Ibn Abi Layl lied. She is entitled to one-tenth of the third. Indeed, Allah the Exalted commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and said: 'Place upon each of those mountains a portion.' And the mountains at that time were ten, so the 'portion' is the one-tenth of the thing.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth. He said, 'A portion from ten.' He said, 'Allah the Exalted said, "Then place on each of them a portion" (Quran 11:82), and the mountains were ten mountains.'
Ali (ibn al-Husayn) from his father from Hammad from Aban ibn Taghlib said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The portion is one of ten, because the mountains were ten and the birds four.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Abu Basir and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed a 'part' of his wealth, he said: 'A part is one of ten,' and he said: 'The mountains were ten.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a part of his wealth, so he said: 'One from seven. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: "For it are seven gates; for every gate of them is a portion assigned."' I said: 'And a man who bequeathed a share (sahm) of his wealth?' He said: 'The share is one from eight.' Then he recited: 'Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy...' until the end of the verse.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il ibn Hammam al-Kindi from al-Rida (peace be upon him): In the case of a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth, he said: 'The portion is one of seven. He says: "It has seven doors; for each of them [the heirs] is a portion assigned."'
From him, from Abu Hammam, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) Like it

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth. He said: 'One-seventh of one-third of it.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The way to reconcile between these narrations which we narrated later and the earlier narrations is to assume that the 'portion' refers to that which must be executed for one of the ten heirs, and it is recommended for the heirs to execute it for one of the seven, so that the narrations align and do not contradict.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who bequeaths a 'share' (sahm) of his wealth, so he said: "The 'share' is one out of eight, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Verily, alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to administer the (funds); for those whose hearts have been (to be reconciled) to Truth; for freeing captives or prisoners; for those in debt; for the cause of Allah; and for the wayfarer'..."

Ali from his father from Safwan said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him). And Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr said: We asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) About a man who bequeathed to you a share from his wealth, and we do not know what that share is. He said: 'You do not have anything in what has reached you from Ja'far, nor from Abu Ja'far, regarding it.' We said to him: May Allah ransom us for you, we did not hear our companions mention anything of this from your fathers (peace be upon them). He said: 'The share is one of eight.' We said to him: May Allah ransom us for you, how did it become one of the eight? He said: 'Do you not read the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' I said: I am ransomed for you, I do read it, but I do not know which place it is. The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Zakat expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed for it and for bringing hearts together and for freeing captivity and for the debt and in the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - a duty imposed by Allah.' Then he made a knot with his hand for eight and said: 'And thus the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it into eight shares, so the share is one of eight.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever bequeaths a share (sahm) of his wealth, it is a share out of ten." It is likely that the narrator erred, and he actually heard this regarding one who bequeaths a part (juz') of his wealth, and he assumed it applied to one who bequeaths a share, or he may have believed that 'part' and 'share' are the same, so he narrated it according to what he thought.

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Amr from Jamil from Aban from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). That he was asked about a man who bequeathed something unspecified, so he said: 'The unspecified thing in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one of six.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Faddal or others from Jamil from Aban from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) said: He was asked about a man who made a vague bequest (of 'something'). He said: 'The 'something' is found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) among six [categories].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jamilyah, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed to a man a sword, which was in a sheath and had ornaments on it. The heirs said to him, 'You only have the blade, and you do not have the ornaments.' He said, 'No, rather the sword with what is in it is for him.' I said to him, 'A man bequeathed to a man a chest, and there was wealth inside it. The heirs said, 'You only have the chest, and you do not have the wealth.' He said, 'The chest with what is in it is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who said, 'This ship belongs to so-and-so,' but did not specify what is in it, and it contains food. Should the man be given the ship and what is in it? He said: 'It is for the one to whom he bequeathed it, unless the owner is suspected (of having other heirs), and the heirs get nothing.' From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jamilah, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man. The heirs said, 'You only have the iron, not the ornamentation; you have nothing but the iron.' He wrote to me: 'The sword is for him, and its ornamentation.'

From him, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a chest to a man, and there was money in the chest. The heirs said, 'You only have the chest, and you do not have what is inside it.' He said, 'The chest with what is inside it is for him.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said: I asked him about a man who designated the price of a female slave as a sacrificial offering (hady) for the Kaaba. He said: 'How should he act?' He said: 'Indeed, a man came to my father, and he had designated his female slave as a hady for the Kaaba. So my father said to him:

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a person who made a will, but the executor remembered only one category from it. How should he deal with the rest? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Make the remaining categories in charity (al-birr).'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and maternal uncles, he said: 'To his paternal uncles two-thirds and to his maternal uncles one-third.' 23 - Sahl ibn Ziyad said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) A man had two sons, one of whom died, and he had male and female offspring. Their grandfather bequeathed to them the share of their father. Is this share equal for male and female, or 'for the male the share of two females'? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'They execute their grandfather's bequest as he ordered, if God wills.' And I wrote to him: A man has male and female offspring, and he acknowledged for them a property that it is for his children, and did not mention that it is divided among them according to God's shares and prescriptions, where male and female are equal. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'They execute in it their father's bequest as he specified. If he did not specify anything, they return it to the Book of God, if God wills.' 24 - And - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) A man bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his male and female freedmen. Is the male and female equal in it, or 'for the male the share of two females' from the bequest? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is valid for the deceased to bequeath as he bequeathed, as he bequeathed, if God wills.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Yazid al-Kunasī from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Your son is more entitled to you than your son's son, and your son's son is more entitled to you than your brother, and your full brother (from father and mother) is more entitled to you than your paternal brother, and your paternal brother is more entitled to you than your maternal brother. He said: And the son of your full brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal brother. He said: And the son of your paternal brother is more entitled to you than your paternal uncle. He said: And your paternal uncle who is your father's full brother is more entitled to you than your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother. He said: And your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother. He said: And the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's full brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother, and the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's maternal brother.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub said: Ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: "And for each [inheritance category], We made heirs from what the parents and close relatives left." He said: 'He meant by this the close relatives (of kinship) in inheritance, and did not mean the beneficiaries of favors; therefore, the most entitled to the deceased are those closest to him in the womb that connects him to it.'

Ibn Mahbub from Hammad Abu Yusuf al-Kazzaz from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When there is an heir who has a fixed share (fard), he is more entitled to the property.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the relatives meet (in competition for inheritance), the one who comes first is more entitled to the inheritance of his relative. If they are equal, each one stands in the place of his relative."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Hammad, from Ibn Sukan, from Mushamil ibn Sa'd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who leaves behind his two parents, he said: 'It is from three shares; for the mother one share and for the father two shares.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind his two parents, he said: 'For the father is two shares, and for the mother is one share.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ma'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who left behind his mother and his brother. He said, 'O Shaykh, do you mean according to the Book (of Allah)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the nearest relative, then the nearest.' I said, 'Then the brother inherits nothing?' He said, 'I have told you that Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the nearest relative, then the nearest.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read to me the sheet of the Book of Inheritance shares, which is the dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand. So I found in it: 'A man left a daughter and a mother; for the daughter is half, three shares, and for the mother is one-sixth, one share. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three shares is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share is for the mother.' He said: And I read in it: 'A man left a daughter and a father; for the daughter is half, three shares, and for the father is one-sixth, one share. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share is for the father.' And Muhammad said: And I found in it: 'A man left his two parents and a daughter; for the daughter is half, three shares, and for the two parents is

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the grandfather (in inheritance), so he said: 'No one has given a ruling on it except by his own opinion, except for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May God perfect you, so what did the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say about it?' He said: 'When it is tomorrow, wait for me until I read it to you from the book of Ali (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May God perfect you, narrate to me, for your narration is more beloved to me than you reading it to me from a book.' So he said to me for the third time: 'Listen to what I say to you: when it is tomorrow, wait for me until I read it to you from a book.' So I went to him the next day after Dhuhr prayer, and it was my time when I would be alone with him between Dhuhr and Asr. I disliked asking him unless I was alone, fearing that he might give a ruling in the presence of others due to precaution (taqiyyah). So when I entered upon him, he turned to his son Ja'far and said: 'Read to Zurarah the sheet of inheritances.' Then he rose to sleep, so I and Ja'far remained in the house. He rose and brought out to me a sheet like the thigh of a camel, and said: 'I will not read it to you until you make it so that you do not narrate to anyone what you read in it ever, until I give you permission.' And he did not say 'until my father gives you permission.' I said: 'May God perfect you, why do you restrict me, and your father did not command you with that?' He said: 'You are not looking at it except according to what I said to you.' So I said: 'That is for you.' I was a man knowledgeable about inheritances and bequests, perceptive of them, and calculating them. I spent time seeking something said about inheritances and bequests that I did not know, so I could not find it. So when he threw to me the edge of the sheet, it was a thick book, known to be from the books of the early ones. I looked, and it was contrary to what was in the hands of people, of the solid and the command of the well-known, which had no difference, and most of it was like that. So I read it until I reached its end with the foulness of the soul, little caution, and diseases of opinion, and I said while I was reading it: 'It is false,' un

Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said: I found in the Sheet of Inheritance shares: 'A man died and left behind a daughter and two parents. I found for the daughter three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them, one share. The wealth is divided into five parts. Whatever portion amounts to three parts is for the daughter, and whatever portion amounts to two parts is for the two parents.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who left a daughter and a mother, the inheritance is four shares because the daughter has three shares and the mother has one-sixth (one share), and two shares remain, so they are more entitled to them than the paternal uncle, the son of the brother, and the agnates, because the daughter and the mother were specified for them, and they were not specified for the others, so they are returned to them according to their shares. From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: A dispute arose between two men from my paternal cousins regarding inheritance, so I suggested to them in writing to refer to him for that, so that they might act according to his opinion. So they both wrote to him, 'May we be your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who left a husband, a daughter, and a sister from her father and mother?' And I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, if you see fit to answer us with the truth,' so he sent them a letter. In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. May Allah grant health to us and to you and improve your health. I understood your letter, you mentioned that a woman died and left a husband, a daughter, and a sister from her father and mother. The share for the husband is one-fourth, and what remains is for the daughter.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Humran from Zurara said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) showed me the sheet of inheritances, and it was in it: 'The parents are not deducted anything from the two sixths.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said: I said to Zurara: Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who left behind his daughter and his mother: The inheritance is divided into four shares, because the daughter has three shares and the mother has one-sixth (one share), and what remains are two shares; these two are more entitled to them than the paternal uncle and the brother and the agnates, because God Almighty has specified shares for them, and whoever He has specified shares for, their shares are returned to them.

From al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamilyah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind his two parents, he said: 'For the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hammad Dhi al-Nab from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In a man who died and left two daughters and his father, he said: 'For the father is one-sixth and for the two daughters is the remainder.' He said: 'And if he left daughters and sons, the father would not be diminished from the one-sixth by anything.' I said to him: 'For he left daughters and sons and a mother.' He said: 'For the mother is one-sixth and the remainder is divided among them, 'for the male is like the portion of the two females'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, how is it that when a man dies and his children from the kinship are equal, the women inherit half of what the men inherit, while they are weaker than the men and less resourceful?' He said, 'Because Allah, the Exalted, has favored the men over the women by a degree, and because the women return as dependents upon the men.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhāʿī said: Al-Fahfāḥī asked Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him): 'What is the matter with the poor, weak woman that she takes one share while the man takes two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, upon the woman there is no jihad (military striving) and no nafakah (financial maintenance) and no maʿqūlah (blood money/compensation), for that is upon the men.' So I said to myself: 'It had been told to me that Ibn Abi al-ʿAwjāʾ asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about this matter and he answered him with this answer.' So Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'Yes, this is the question of Ibn Abi al-ʿAwjāʾ, and the answer from us is one; if the meaning of the question is one, our last one follows the same as our first one, and our first and our last are equal in knowledge, and to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) is their excellence.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad and Hisham, from al-Ahwal, who said: Ibn Abi al-A'ja said to me: 'What is the matter with the poor, weak woman that she takes one share while the man takes two?' He mentioned this to some of our companions, who reported it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Because the woman is not obligated upon her with jihad (military striving), nor nafakah (maintenance/financial support), nor ma'qulah (blood money/compensation), and indeed that is upon the men. Therefore, a share was made for the woman and two shares for the man.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When a man dies and leaves sons, the eldest receives the sword, the coat of mail, the ring, and the Quran copy; and if an incident occurs with it, it belongs to the eldest among them."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from some of his companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): That when a man leaves behind a sword and weapons, they belong to his son, and if he has multiple sons, they belong to the eldest of them.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rib'i ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man dies, his sword, his mus'haf (Quran codex), his seal, and his coat of mail belong to his eldest son."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Hammad, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: "When a man dies, his sword, his ring, his mushaf (Quran codex), his books, his saddle, his mount, and his clothing belong to the eldest of his children. If the eldest is a daughter, then it belongs to the eldest of the males."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr and Fudayl ibn Yasar, from one of them (peace be upon them). That when a man leaves behind a sword or a weapon, it belongs to his son; if there are two sons, it belongs to the elder of them.

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and has no household goods left. He said, 'The sword.' And he said, 'When the dead man dies, his son has the sword, the saddle (for riding), and the clothes (as) the clothes of his skin.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi and al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'How many people have a right (of inheritance) that they do not know about?' I said: 'And what is that, may Allah rectify you?' He said: 'Indeed, two neighbors had a treasure beneath them that they did not know about. Know that it was not gold nor silver.' I said: 'Then what was it?' He said: 'It was knowledge.' I said: 'Which of the two is more entitled to it?' He said: 'The elder.' Thus we say.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan Ali ibn Asbat al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Hamzah ibn Humran, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Who inherited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'Fatima inherited him the household goods, the crops, and everything that was his.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) inherited the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Fatima (peace be upon her) inherited his wealth.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from Salama ibn Muhraz said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, an Armani man died and bequeathed to me.' He said, 'And what is the Armani?' I said, 'A Nabati from the Nabati of the mountains. He died and bequeathed to me his estate and left a daughter.' He said to me, 'Give her half.' He said, 'So I informed Zurarah of that, and he said to me, 'Be careful (of me), for the wealth is entirely hers.' He said, 'So I entered upon him later and said, 'May Allah improve you, our companions claimed that you were cautious (of me).' He said, 'No, by Allah, I was not cautious of you, but I was sparing you (from error). Did anyone know of that?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then give her what remains.'
