Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In a man who died and left a daughter and a sister (from father and mother). He said: 'The wealth belongs to the daughter, and the sister (from father and mother) gets nothing from the father and mother.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd Allah ibn Khidash al-Manqari: that he asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left a daughter and his brother. He said: 'The wealth belongs to the daughter.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from Burayd al-'Ijli from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked: A man died and left behind a daughter and his brother (paternal uncle). He said: 'The wealth belongs to the daughter, and the brother has nothing.' And he said: 'The brother has nothing with the daughter.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Hamzah ibn Humran, from Abdullah al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, the seller of calanises (woolen cloaks), who said: A man entrusted something to me and left five hundred or six hundred dirhams, and he had a daughter. He told me that there were agnates (asabah) in Syria. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'Give the daughter half and the agnates half.' When I arrived in Kufa, I informed our companions of his saying, and they said, 'Be careful of him (or: Fear that he might be testing you), so give the daughter the other half.' Then I performed Hajj and met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I informed him of what my companions said, and I informed him that I had given the other half to his daughter. He said, 'You did well. I only gave you the ruling fearing the agnates might claim against you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man left behind a daughter and a sister (through both parents). He said: 'All the wealth belongs to the daughter, and the sister gets nothing from the father and mother.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Muhrij, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entrusted his affairs to me, then died, leaving a daughter. He said: 'Give the daughter half, and leave half for the mawali (clients/relatives by contract).' So I returned to them, and they said: 'By Allah, the mawali have nothing (no share).' So I returned to him the next time and said: 'Indeed, our companions said that the mawali have nothing.' He said: 'I only feared for you.' I said: 'No, by Allah, you did not fear me, but you feared that I would be taken (held liable) for the half. If you do not fear, then give the other half to his daughter, for Allah will compensate you.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Jarmi from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): That a man died during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he used to sell dates, so his brother took the dates, and he had daughters. So his wife came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of that. So Allah revealed to him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) took the dates from the uncle and gave them to the daughters.

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: A man left behind his daughter and his sister (paternal) to his father and mother. He said: 'All the wealth belongs to his daughter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Zurarah: 'Indeed, some people narrated to me from him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from his father (peace be upon him), about various matters in inheritance. So I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say He said: 'By Allah, this is false. But I will inform you and not narrate to you anything (as a formal hadith), and what I tell you is, by Allah, the truth.' When a man leaves his parents, the mother gets one-third and the father gets two-thirds in the Book of Allah. If he has brothers, meaning for the deceased, brothers from father and mother or brothers from father, then for his mother is one-sixth and for the father five-sixths. And the father's share was increased on account of his dependents. As for brothers from the mother who are not from the father, they do not block the mother from the one-third, nor do they inherit. And if a man dies and leaves his mother, and brothers and sisters from father and mother, and brothers and sisters from father, and brothers and sisters from mother, and the father is not alive, then they do not inherit and do not block her, because he did not inherit as a Kalalah (one with no parents or children).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Abdullah ibn Bahr from Hariz from Zurarah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Zurarah, what do you say about a man who leaves behind his parents and his brothers from his mother?' I said: 'One-sixth for the mother, and whatever remains is for the father.' He said: 'From where?' I said: 'I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying in His Book: "If he has brothers, then for his mother is one-sixth."' He said to me: 'Woe to you, O Zurarah! Those brothers are from the father. So if the brothers are from the mother, they do not prevent the mother from receiving one-third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "If the deceased leaves two brothers, they are brothers with the deceased and they exclude the mother [from receiving one-third], and if there is only one, he does not exclude the mother." And he said, "If there are four sisters, they exclude the mother from receiving one-third, because they are in the position of the two brothers, and if there are three, they do not exclude her."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fadl Abu al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two parents and two sisters (from one father and one mother): do they block the mother from receiving one-third? He said, 'No.' I said, 'And three?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'And four?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Fadl Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The mother is not excluded from the one-third share except by two brothers or four sisters (from father and mother) or (by) two brothers (from the father)."

From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the maternal siblings do not exclude the mother from the one-third share.'
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Khuzaymah ibn Yaqtin from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The mother's share is never reduced from one-third, except in the presence of children and siblings, when the father is alive."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the male slave and the female slave: do they prevent (inheritors from inheriting) if they do not inherit? He said, 'No.'

From him, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abd-Darrah (peace be upon him); and it was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from al-'Ala' ibn Fudayl, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The child (fetus) and the young one do not prevent inheritance (by being the sole heir) nor do they inherit, except what has given a sign of crying, and nothing that the womb concealed, even if it moved, except what the night and day differed upon (i.e., reached a specific age of gestation)."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind his parents and siblings from the mother, he said: 'God, Glory be to Him, is more generous than to increase her share in maintenance (while alive) and decrease her share in inheritance by one-third.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave and the polytheist: do they block (the heirs) if they do not inherit? He said, 'No.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) In the case of a husband and two parents, he said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and for the father is what remains.' And he said in the case of a wife and two parents: 'For the wife is one-quarter, and for the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) In the case of a husband and two parents, he said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and whatever remains is for the father.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Zurarah: 'Indeed, some people have narrated to me from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) about various matters regarding inheritance, so I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abdullah ibn Waddah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who died leaving behind her husband, her mother, and her father, he said: 'She is from six shares: for the husband is half, three shares; and for the mother is one-third, two shares; and for the father is one-sixth, one share.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ayub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) In the case of a husband and two parents, he said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.' And in the case of a wife and two parents, he said: 'For the wife is one-quarter, and for the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muthanna ibn Al-Walid Al-Hannat, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who left behind a husband and two parents. He said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and for the father is one-sixth.'

From him, from Ayub ibn Nuḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā (peace be upon him), from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) In the case of a husband and two parents: the husband receives half, the mother receives a full third, and whatever remains belongs to the father.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muthanna ibn Al-Walid, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked: A woman left behind her husband and her two parents. He said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and for the father is one-sixth.'

From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave woman whom her husband had not yet consummated the marriage with, who died and left behind her mother, two full siblings (from father and mother), a paternal grandfather (father of the mother), and her husband. He said: 'The husband is given half, and the mother is given the remainder, and the grandfather is given nothing because his daughter (the mother of the deceased) has blocked him from the inheritance, and the siblings are given nothing.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Four [scenarios] in which no harm [of reduction] enters upon them regarding inheritance: for the two parents, one-sixth each or more than that; and for the husband, one-half or one-quarter; and for the wife, one-quarter or one-eighth."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Nuh ibn Darradj, from Uqbah ibn Bashir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind his wife and his two parents, he said: 'For the wife is one-fourth, and for the mother is one-third, and whatever remains is for the father.' And I asked him about a woman who died and left behind her husband and her two parents, he said: 'For the husband is one-half, and for the mother is one-third of all the wealth, and whatever remains is for the father.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Jamilah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a woman died and left behind her parents and her husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-sixth, and for the father is what remains.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a report consistent with the general public (Sunni scholars), but we do not act upon it because of the consensus of the Righteous Faction on abandoning acting upon it, and because of its contradiction to the apparent meaning of the Quran and the mutawatir (concurrently transmitted) reports. Allah the Exalted said: 'If he has no child and his parents inherit him, then for his mother is one-third.' Thus, He obligated for her, in the absence of a child, one-third in its entirety. So whoever reduces her from that is contradicting the apparent meaning of the Book. And even if the report were safe from that, it would be permissible to be interpreted as being when there are siblings who restrict the mother from one-third to one-sixth, for we have clarified that in the first chapter, and it is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Book. Allah the Exalted said: 'If he has siblings, then for his mother is one-sixth.' And in the report is not mentioned that there was no one among the brothers or sisters who would restrict [her share].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Zurarah: I heard Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a case with a husband, parents, and one daughter: The husband gets one-fourth, which is three shares out of twelve; the parents get two-sixths, which is four shares out of twelve; and the remaining five shares belong to the daughter, because if she were a son, she would not have more than five out of twelve. And if there were two daughters, they get five out of twelve shares, because if they were two sons, they would not have more than the remaining five. Zurarah said: This is the truth if you want to apply 'awl (proportional reduction) so that the fixed shares do not exceed the whole. Indeed, the reduction enters only those who have the surplus from the children and the paternal and maternal sisters. As for the husband and the maternal siblings, they are not reduced from anything that Allah has specified.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Ri'ab from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who died leaving behind her husband, her parents, and her daughter, he said: 'For the husband is one-fourth, which is three shares out of twelve shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them is one-sixth, which is two shares out of twelve shares, and five shares remain, so they are for the daughter, because if it were a son, he would not have more than five shares out of twelve shares, because the two parents, each one of them, are not reduced from the one-sixth by anything, and that the husband is not reduced from the one-fourth by anything.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Safwan handed me a letter from Musa ibn Bakr and said to me, 'This is my hearing from Musa ibn Bakr, which I read to him.' Inside it was: Musa ibn Bakr from Ali ibn Sa'id from Zurarah who said: This is what there is no disagreement among our companions regarding from Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) when asked about a woman who left behind a husband, a mother, and two daughters: 'The husband gets one-fourth, the mother gets one-sixth, and the two daughters get the remainder, because if they were two men, they would only get the remainder, and a woman is never given more than a man would get in her place.' If the deceased left a mother or father, a wife, and a daughter, then the inheritance is from twenty-four parts: the wife gets one-eighth (three parts), one of the parents gets one-sixth (four parts), the daughter gets one-half (twelve parts), and the remaining five parts are returned to the shares of the daughter and one of the parents according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the wife. If he left two parents, a wife, and a daughter, it is also from twenty-four parts: the two parents get two-sixths (eight parts, four for each), the wife gets one-eighth (three parts), the daughter gets one-half (twelve parts), and one remaining part is returned to the daughter and the two parents according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the wife. If she left a father, a husband, and a daughter, the father gets two parts out of twelve (which is one-sixth), the husband gets one-fourth (three parts out of twelve), the daughter gets one-half (six parts out of twelve), and one remaining part is returned to the daughter and the father according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the husband. And no one from God's creation inherits with a child except the two parents, the husband, and the wife. If he has no child, but the children of the child are male or female, they are like the children; they inherit the inheritance of sons. And the children of daughters are like the daughters; they inherit the inheritance of daughters. And they block the two parents, the husband, and the wife from their larger shares. And if they descend through two or three or more generations, they inherit what the children of the body inherit, and they block what the children of the body block. 4 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad i

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman left behind her husband, her brothers (from mother), and her sisters (from father). He said: 'For the husband is half (three shares), and for the brothers from the mother is one-third, male and female are equal in it, and one share remains for the brothers and sisters from the father: "For the male is like the portion of two females."' Because the shares do not increase (in number of heirs to reduce share) and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother from their third, because Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says: 'If there are more than that, then they are partners in the third.' And if she is one, then for her is one-sixth. And what Allah meant [by Kalalah]: 'And if a man or woman leaves no descendant but has a brother or sister, then for each one of them is one-sixth. If there are more than that, then they are partners in the third.' He meant by that specifically the brothers and sisters from the mother. And He said at the end of Surah Al-Nisa: 'They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling concerning Kalalah. If a man dies leaving no child, and he has a sister...' Meaning a sister from mother and father, or a sister from father. 'Then for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if she has no child.' And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is like the portion of two females. These are the ones who are added to and reduced from, and likewise their children who are added to and reduced from. And if a woman left her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, then for the husband is half (three shares), and for the brothers from the mother are two shares, and one share remains, which is for the two sisters from the father. And if there was one, it is for her, because if the two sisters were two sisters from the father, they would not be increased beyond what remains. And if there was one, or if in place of the one there was a brother, he would not be increased beyond what remains, and a female from the sisters or from the children is not increased beyond what a male would not be increased upon.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr, who said: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman who left behind a husband, maternal siblings, and a paternal sister. He said: 'For the husband is half, three shares; for the maternal siblings is two shares; and for the paternal sister is one share.' The man said to him: 'Indeed, the rulings of Zayd, and the rulings of the general public and the judges, are not like this, O Abu Ja'far. They say for the paternal sister is three shares, which becomes from six, and it increases (ta'ul) to eight.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And why did they say that?' He said: 'Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And if he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left."' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If the sister were a brother?' He said: 'Then he would not have except one-sixth.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'So why have you reduced the brother's share if you are arguing for the sister's half on the basis that Allah named for her the half? Indeed, Allah has named for the brother the whole, and the whole is more than the half, because He said: "Then for her is the half," and He said regarding the brother: "And he inherits her," meaning all her wealth, "If she has no child."' So you do not give that which Allah has made for him as the whole, in some of your rulings, anything, and you give that which Allah has made for him as the half, completely.' The man said to him: 'May Allah rectify you. So how is the sister given the half, while the male is not given anything, if she were a male?' He said: 'They say in the case of a mother, husband, maternal siblings, and paternal sisters, so they give the husband half, and for the mother one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings one-third, and for the paternal sister half, three shares. So they make it from nine, while it is from six, so it rises to nine.' He said: 'Thus they say.' He said: 'If the sister were a male, a brother from the father?' He said: 'It is nothing.' The man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'So what do you say?' He said: 'For the paternal siblings, and the maternal siblings, and the siblings from the father and mother, with the mother, is nothing.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-A'la ibn Razin and Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: What do you say about a woman who died leaving a husband, brothers from her mother, and brothers and sisters from her father? He said: The husband gets half, which is three shares, and the brothers from the mother get one-third, which is two shares; male and female are equal in it. One share remains, which goes to the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the share of two females, because the shares do not increase (due to scarcity), and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor are the brothers from the mother reduced from their one-third. If there are more than that, they are partners in the one-third, and if there is only one, he gets one-sixth. And indeed, what Allah meant in His saying, 'And if a man or woman leaves an heir (kalalah) and he or she has a brother or sister, for each one of them is one-sixth,' is that Allah meant by that the brothers and sisters from the mother specifically. And if a man or woman leaves an heir (kalalah) and he or she has a brother or sister, for each one of them is one-sixth. And He said in the end of Surah Al-Nisa: 'They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling regarding the kalalah: If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister...' He means by that a sister from father and mother, and a sister from father. They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling regarding the kalalah: If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister. Then for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if she had no child. 'And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is the share of two females.' These are the ones who are increased and decreased. And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is the share of two females. He said: 'And if a woman left a husband, two sisters from her mother, and two sisters from her father, the husband gets half (three shares), and the two sisters from the mother get one-third (two shares), and the two sisters from the father get one share. And if there is only one, it is for her, because the two sisters from the father do not exceed what remains. So if there was a brother from the father, he would not exceed what remains.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Bukayr from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked him about two sisters and a husband, so he said, 'Half and half.' The man said, 'May Allah improve you, has Allah specified for them more than this? For them is the two-thirds.' He said, 'What do you say about a brother and a husband?' He said, 'Half and half.' He said, 'Has not Allah specified for him the entire wealth?' He said, 'And he inherits it if she has no child.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz and Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna al-Hannat from Zurara ibn A'yan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked: A woman left behind her husband, her mother, her full siblings (from both parents), her maternal siblings, and her paternal siblings. He said: 'For her husband is half, for her mother is one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings is one-third, and the paternal and maternal siblings are excluded.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon because we have clarified that with the mother, no one from the siblings (full, maternal, or paternal) inherits. It is likely that the narration came down due to precaution (taqiyyah) to coincide with the views of some of the Sunni majority.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked, 'A woman leaves her husband [dying without other heirs],' he said, 'All the wealth is his, if there is no other heir for her besides him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who died and no one was known to be related to her, and she had a husband, he said: 'The inheritance is for her husband.'

From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited to me the inheritance laws (Faraid) of Ali (peace be upon him), and among them is: 'The husband acquires the entire estate if there is no other heir.'

And from him, from al-Nadr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Basir, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he called for al-Jami'ah (the collection), looked into it, and found: 'A woman died and left her husband, with no heir for her except him; the wealth is all his.'

From him, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who dies and leaves no heir other than her husband. He said, 'The inheritance is all for him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Isma'il from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who died and left behind her husband, with no other heir for her. He said: 'If there is no one else, then he has the wealth, and the wife has one-quarter, and whatever remains belongs to the Imam.' And this report does not contradict what was narrated:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'A man died and left behind his wife.' He said, 'The wealth is hers.' I said, 'A woman died and left behind her husband.' He said, 'The wealth is his.' Because this report carries two meanings: one of which is what Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned, that it is applicable during the Occultation of the Imam, because the wife is only given one-quarter of her husband's inheritance if there is an Imam who takes the remainder; so if there is no Imam, the remainder is also hers. The other, which is preferable in my view, is that if the wife is a relative and there is no relative of his closer to her than she, she takes one-quarter due to marriage and the remainder due to kinship, and that which reveals what we mentioned. (1057) 17 What Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated - from al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar al-Basri who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind a wife who was a relative, and he had no relative other than her. He said, 'All the wealth is given to her.' And it indicates what we mentioned, that the wife does not deserve more than one-quarter in the absence of children, even if there is no relative there. -(1058) 18 What al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated - from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Nu'aym al-Sahhaf who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr died and made me his executor and left behind a wife, and he left no heir other than her. So I wrote to Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) and he wrote to me, 'Give the wife one-quarter and bring the remainder to us.' -(1059) 19 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza al-Alawi wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him): A freedman of yours made me his executor with one hundred dirhams, and I used to hear him say, 'Everything that is mine is for my master.' He died and left her (the freedman's wife) and did not command anything regarding it, and he had two wives. As for one, I do not know her location at this moment, and as for the other, she is in Qumm. What do you command regarding this one hundred dirhams? He (peace be upon him) wrote to me, 'See that you give the

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Musa ibbad from Musa ibn Bakr from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In a husband who died and left a wife, he said: 'She has one-quarter, and the remainder is paid to the Imam.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no return (of the wife) to the husband, nor (of the husband) to the wife."

From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married four women in one contract, or he said in one session, and their dowries were different. He said: 'It is permissible for him and for them.' I said: What do you think if he went to some of the lands, and divorced one of the four, and bore witness upon her divorce by a group from the people of that land, while they did not know the woman? Then he married a woman from the people of that land after the expiration of the waiting period of the one he divorced, then he died after having consummated the marriage with her. How is his inheritance divided? He said: 'If he has a child, then the woman whom he married last from the people of that land is entitled to one-fourth of one-eighth of what he left. And if the one who was divorced from the four is known by her very self and her lineage, then she has nothing from the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.' And he said: 'The three women will divide three-fourths of one-eighth of what he left, and upon them is the waiting period. And if the one who was divorced from the four is not known, the four women will divide three-fourths of one-eighth of what he left among all of them, and upon all of them is the waiting period.'

From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, and he married two more to them in a single contract, then consummated the marriage with one of them, and then he died. He said: 'If he consummated with the wife whose name he mentioned first at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, she inherits, and she observes the waiting period.' He said: 'And if he consummated with the one mentioned after the first, then her marriage is invalid, she does not inherit, but she keeps what she took of the dowry because she made his private part permissible to her, and she observes the waiting period.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr and Fudayl and Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them); among them is he who narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and among them is he who narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and among them is he who narrated from one of them (peace be upon them both). That the wife does not inherit from her husband's estate from the plaster of a house or land, unless the brick, logs, and wood are appraised at a value, so she is given one-quarter or one-eighth of it, if it is from the value of the brick, logs, and wood.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That the wife does not inherit anything from what her husband left from the villages, houses, weapons, and animals, but she inherits from the wealth, bedding, clothes, and household items that he left, and the dismantled parts, doors, trunks, and reeds are valued, so she is given her right from them.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Women do not inherit from the land or from the real estate anything."

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman inherits the 'Tub' (the main male ancestor/stock), and she does not inherit anything from the 'Ribaa' (the other males). I said: 'How does she inherit from the 'Far' (offspring/descendants) and not inherit anything from the 'Ribaa'? He said to me: 'She has no kinship with them by which she inherits, and she is an outsider to them; therefore she inherits from the 'Far' and does not inherit from the 'Asl' (the main stock), and no one enters their [lineage] through her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "A woman's value is set at that of wood and brick, so that she does not marry and bring in someone who would corrupt their inheritances." Taribal ibn Rajaa' from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): "That a woman does not inherit anything from what her husband left of villages, houses, weapons, and animals; and she inherits from wealth, slaves, clothes, and household furnishings that he left; and the dismantled parts, trunks, and reeds are appraised, and she is given her right from them."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik or Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man: does he inherit from his wife's house and land, from the earth (real estate), anything? Or is that like the case of the woman, so she does not inherit from that anything? He said: 'He inherits from her and she inherits from him, everything that he leaves or she leaves.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to mean that if the wife has children, then she inherits from everything that the deceased left, whether it is real estate or otherwise. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah Regarding women, if they have children, they are given one-fourth from the estate.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said: I said to Zurara: Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Women do not inherit from what their husband leaves of the ground of a house or land, unless the structure, trunks, and wood are valued, so she is given her share from the value of the structure. As for the ground, she is given nothing of the land, nor the ground of the house.' Zurara said: There is no doubt about this.

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara and Harun ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said) who said: He asked me, 'Does Ibn Abi Layla rule with a legal judgment and then return from it?' I said to him, 'It has reached me that he ruled regarding the property of a man and a woman when one of them dies, and the heirs of the living and the heirs of the deceased claim it, or the man divorces her, and the man claims it and the woman claims it, in four different rulings.' He said, 'And what are they?' I said, 'As for the first of that, he ruled in it according to the saying of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i - he would make the property of the woman that which is not for the man belong to the woman, and the property of the men that which is not for the women belong to the man, and what is for both men and women, they split it in half. Then it reached me that he said, I said to him, 'The property becomes for the woman.' He said, 'What do you see if she presents evidence, to how many does she need?' I said, 'Two witnesses.' He said, 'If you asked from between her two thighs, meaning the two mountains, and we were at that time in Mecca, they would inform you that the dowry and property are openly given from the house of the woman to the house of her husband, so she is the one who brought it, and he is the claimant. If he claims that he created something in it, let him bring evidence upon it.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya' ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who dies before the man, or a man before the woman, he said: 'Whatever is from the personal effects of women is for the woman, and whatever is from the personal effects of men and women is shared between them, and whoever takes possession of any part of it, it is for him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man leaves behind his father and mother, or his son or his daughter, if he leaves one of these four, they are not those whom Allah meant [by the term] 'Al-Kalalah' [in the verse]: 'Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning Kalalah.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Hamzah ibn Humran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-kalalah, and he said: 'That which has no child and no parent.'
Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Al-Kalalah is one who has no parent and no child."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Musa ibn Bakr said: I said to Zurarah: Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The paternal brothers and sisters, and those from both father and mother, are increased and decreased [in share] because they would not have a greater share than the paternal brothers and sisters if they were in their place.' For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left, and she inherits him if he has no child.' He explains: 'He inherits all her wealth if she has no child.' So they gave to the one Allah specified for half, fully, and they aimed to give to the one Allah specified for all the wealth less than half, and the woman is never given a greater share than a man if he were in her place.' He said, so Zurarah said: 'And this is established among our companions; they do not differ regarding it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz, and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked: A woman left behind her mother, her full sisters (from father and mother), her half-brothers (from mother), and her half-sisters (from father). He said: 'For her full sisters, two-thirds; for her mother, one-sixth; and for her half-sisters from her mother, one-sixth.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, and Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked: A woman left behind her mother, and her full siblings (from father and mother), and her paternal siblings (from father only), and her maternal siblings (from mother only). He said: 'For her paternal siblings (from father and mother) are two-thirds, and for her mother is one-sixth, and for her maternal siblings is one-sixth.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, and Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked: A woman left behind her mother, and her full siblings (from father and mother), and her paternal siblings (from father only), and her maternal siblings (from mother only). He said: 'For her paternal and maternal sisters (full sisters), two-thirds; and for her mother, one-sixth; and for her maternal brothers and sisters, one-sixth.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, and Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked: A woman left behind her husband, her mother, her maternal siblings, and her paternal-maternal siblings. He said: 'For her husband is half, for her mother is one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings is one-third, and the paternal-maternal siblings are excluded.' Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: These narrations contradict the truth and are not acted upon by the entire sect, because it is known among them that with the mother, no siblings (brothers or sisters) inherit, which we have explained previously. The explanation for these narrations is that they are carried on a type of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) to align with the views of the general public (Sunni). It is also possible that what came regarding permission for us to take from them according to their beliefs, as they take from us, applies, and it is only forbidden for one of us to take from another contrary to the truth, which is indicated by this. 9. What was narrated by: Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abdullah ibn Muhrij, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him: A man left behind his daughter and his paternal-maternal sister. He said: 'All the wealth belongs to his daughter, and the paternal-maternal sister gets nothing.' I said: We have need for this, and the deceased man is from these people (non-Shia), and his sister is a believing, knowledgeable woman. He said: 'Then take half for her. Take from them what they take from you in their sunnah, their judgments, and their rulings.' He said: So I mentioned that to Zurarah, who said: Indeed, upon what Ibn Muhrij brought is a light. Take them by your right in their rulings and their sunnah, as they take from you in it. 10. And - from him, from Ayub ibn Nuh He said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him: Do we take in the rulings of the non-Shia what they take from us in their rulings or not? He wrote (peace be upon him): 'It is permissible for you to do so if your school of thought in it is precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) from them and diplomacy (mudarayah').

From him, from Al-Sindi ibn Muhammad Al-Bazzaz, from 'Ula' ibn Razin Al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the legal rulings. He said: 'It is permissible to marry the people of each religion according to what they permit for themselves.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from a number of the companions of Ali, and I do not know Sulayman except that he informed me of it, and Ali ibn Abdullah from Sulayman also from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said: "Bind them to what they bound themselves to."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the son of a paternal half-sister and the son of a maternal half-sister. He said, 'For the son of the maternal sister is one-sixth, and for the son of the paternal sister is the remainder.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the son of a paternal brother and the son of a maternal brother. He said, 'For the son of the maternal brother is one-sixth, and whatever remains is for the son of the paternal brother.' I asked, 'Is this for the distribution (of the estate) or not?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'As far as I have been informed, the mother of the deceased has entered into this matter, meaning the debt.' He remained silent for a moment, then said, 'Take it.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something of the fixed shares (of inheritance), so he said to me, 'Shall I bring out for you the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not worn out.' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad, indeed the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) does not wear out.' So he brought it out, and behold, it was a noble book. In it was: 'If a man died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle,' he said, 'For the paternal uncle two-thirds, and for the maternal uncle one-third.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding an aunt (paternal) and an aunt (maternal), he said: 'One-third and two-thirds,' meaning for the paternal aunt two-thirds and for the maternal aunt one-third.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Wahb, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who left behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, he said: 'For the paternal aunt are two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies leaving behind his maternal uncle, maternal aunt, paternal uncle, paternal aunt, daughter, and sister. He said: 'All of these inherit and take possession. When the paternal aunt and maternal aunt are together, the paternal aunt gets two-thirds and the maternal aunt gets one-third.'

Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Durust, from Abu al-Mu'za, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'If a man dies and leaves behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, then the paternal aunt receives two-thirds and the maternal aunt receives one-third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit if there is no one with them who inherits other than them. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer [to one another] in the Book of Allah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl from al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him): In a man who died and left two maternal aunts and his clients (mawali), he said: 'Those of kinship are closer to one another in inheritance.' The wealth is divided between the two maternal aunts.

Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and maternal uncles, he said: 'For his paternal uncles, two-thirds, and for his maternal uncles, one-third.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to them from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'That the paternal aunt is in the position of the father, and the maternal aunt is in the position of the mother, and the daughter of the brother is in the position of the brother, and every relative of kin is in the position of the kinship through which they are connected, unless there is an heir closer to the deceased than them, in which case they are excluded.'

From them, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hammad Abu Yusuf Al-Kazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) considered the paternal aunt to be in the position of the father in inheritance, and the maternal aunt to be in the position of the mother, and the son of the brother to be in the position of the brother. He said: 'And every relative who is not entitled to a fixed share (fard) is in this same manner.' He said: 'And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'If there is an heir among those who have a fixed share, they are more entitled to the property.''

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to them from Safwan ibn Khalid from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muhajir from Al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Which is closer: the son of a paternal uncle (on both father and mother's side) or the paternal uncle (on father's side)?" I said - Abu Ishaq al-Sabii narrated to me - from Al-Harith al-A'war from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that he used to say: "The specific maternal uncles are closer than the paternal uncles (of the father only)." He (Al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah) said: So he sat up straight and then said: "You brought it from a clear source. Indeed, 'Abdullah (the father of the Prophet) was the brother of Abu Talib on both his father and mother."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a said, and Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "A man died and left behind a brother who was a slave, and he bequeathed to him one thousand dirhams. His masters refused to validate this for him, so they appealed to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. He said to the slave: 'Do you have children?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are they free?' He said: 'They are free.'" He said: 'Do you accept from all the wealth only one thousand dirhams, so that they inherit their uncle?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was correct.'

From him (Al-Shaykh), he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Yunus narrated to them from Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn from Sufyan ibn Sa'id from Abu Ishaq al-Subi'i from al-Harith from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: The direct paternal uncles inherit, excluding the maternal uncles.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Halabi from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan differed regarding a man who dies and has no 'asabah (agnates) to inherit him, but has a close relative who does not inherit. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance is for them,' citing the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And those of the womb (close relatives) are closer to one another [in inheritance].' And 'Uthman said: 'It is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

From him, from Muhammad al-Katib, from Muhammad al-Hamdani, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from al-Husayn al-Bazzaz, who said: I commanded whoever asks Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the wealth: is it for the closer relative or for the agnates (al-'asabah)? He said, 'The wealth is for the closer relative, and the agnates are dust in his mouth.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khorasani wrote: A man bequeathed to me, and he left only sons of the paternal uncle, daughters of the paternal uncle, a paternal uncle, and two paternal aunts. To whom does the inheritance belong? He wrote to him with peace: 'The people of the 'asabah (residuary heirs) and the sons of the paternal uncle are the heirs.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is consistent with the Sunni view, but we do not adopt it; rather, we adopt what preceded from the reports.

Al-Saffar from 'Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Dharif, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Salamah ibn Muhrij, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a paternal aunt and a paternal uncle, he said: 'For the paternal uncle are two-thirds, and for the paternal aunt is one-third.' And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal aunt: 'The wealth belongs to the maternal aunt.' And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal uncle: 'The wealth belongs to the maternal uncle.' And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal cousin (female): 'For the male is the share of the two females.' And he said regarding a daughter and a father: 'For the daughter is half, and for the father is one-sixth, and two shares remain. So whatever of it amounts to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share, it is for the father. And the fixed portion is from four shares: for the daughter three-quarters, and for the father one-quarter.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Sinan said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him), when a client (mawla) of his died and left behind relatives, he did not take anything from his inheritance. And he would say, "And those of kinship among each other have greater share [in inheritance] among themselves in the Book of Allah."'

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) did not take the inheritance of any of his mawali if he died and had relatives; he would give it to his relatives."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding an aunt who came to dispute the mawla (client) of a man who had died. And those of kinship among each other have nearer proximity in the prescription of Allah. So he gave the inheritance to the aunt and did not give it to the mawla.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm from Hanan said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is for the mawali (freedmen/clients)?' He said: 'They have in inheritance nothing except what Allah the Exalted said: "Except if they do a good deed to their relatives."'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Muhammad al-Katib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr al-Azraq, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man asked him about a man who died and left behind a daughter of his brother, and left behind mawali (freedmen/patrons), and I had one thousand dirhams of his money with me, and no one knew about it. Then the daughter of his brother came and pledged a Mus'haf (copy of the Quran) with me, so I gave her thirty dirhams. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me when I told him, 'Did anyone know about it?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then give it to her, piece by piece, and no one should know.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Thabit, from Hanan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: A mawlā (client) of ʿAlī (peace be upon him) died, so he said: 'Look, do you find an heir for him?' It was said to him: 'Two daughters in al-Yamāmah, who were enslaved.' So he purchased them with the wealth of the deceased mawlā, then handed over the remainder of the wealth to them.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Abu Thabit from Hanan from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said: A mawla (client) of ʿAlī (peace be upon him) died, so he said: 'Look, do you find an heir for him?' It was said to him: 'Two daughters in al-Yamāmah, who were enslaved.' So he purchased them from the deceased's wealth, then handed over the remainder of the wealth to them.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Salih, the mawla of Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who died and left wealth, and left behind his sister and his mawali (clients/freedmen). He said, 'The wealth belongs to his sister.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Yunus ibn Abi al-Harith from Saif ibn Umaira from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The mawla (client) of the daughter of Hamza died, and he had a daughter. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the daughter of Hamza half [of the estate] and her daughter half [of the estate].' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a report on which action is not taken, because it agrees with the schools of the general public (Sunni), and it has come out as a form of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) due to its contradiction with the reports we have previously mentioned. And because this is a report that they (the Sunnis) narrate from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so it is permissible that it comes in accordance with what they believe, namely that it has been narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gave all the wealth to the daughter of Hamza because she had no heir.

That was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A freed slave (mawla) of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him) died, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave his inheritance to the daughter of Hamza (may Allah be pleased with her). Abu Ali said: This narration indicates that the freed slave did not have a daughter, as the general public narrate, and that a woman also inherits the Wilayah (manumission right), not as the general public believe, although they have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) like what we said.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated, it was reported from Hanan, who said: 'I was sitting with Suwayd ibn Ghaflah when a man came to him and asked him about a daughter, a wife, and mawali (clients). He said: I will inform you of the ruling of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) regarding this: He gave the daughter one-half, the wife one-eighth, and what remained he returned to the daughter, and he gave the mawali nothing. Al-Fadl said: And this report is more authentic than what was reported by Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: I saw the wife whom Ali (peace be upon him) inherited from, and he gave the daughter one-half and the mawali one-half.' Because Salamah did not meet Ali (peace be upon him), whereas Suwayd had met Ali (peace be upon him). He said: As for what was reported: 'That a mawla of Hamz (peace be upon him) died and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gave the daughter of Hamz one-half and gave the mawali one-half.' It is a disconnected hadith; it is only from Abdullah ibn Shaddad from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it is mursal (disconnected at the companion level). He said: And perhaps that was before the descent of the inheritance shares (al-fara'idh), so it was abrogated. For Allah has prescribed for the allies (al-hulafa') in His Book, saying, Exalted and Great is He: 'And those whose oaths you have made, give them their share.' So the inheritance shares abrogated all of that with His Exalted saying: 'And those of kinship are closer to one another in the decree of Allah.' And Ibrahim al-Nakha'i - rejected this hadith regarding the inheritance of the mawla of Hamz - and the correct ruling from this chapter has been clarified by us.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Absi from Sufyan al-Thawri from Jabir al-Ju'fi from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was asked about the inheritance of a daughter, a wife, and collateral freedmen (mawali). He gave the wife one-eighth, and whatever remained he returned to the daughter, and he gave the mawali nothing.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Zayd ibn Ali — they inherit the close relatives (dhawi al-arham) to the exclusion of the mawali (freedmen/patrons). I asked, 'And what about Ali (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'He was the most intense of the two.'

From him, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Uqbah ibn Muslim and Ammar ibn Marwan, from Salamah ibn Muhrij, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man died, and he has wealth with me, and he has a daughter, and he has mawali (clients/freemen). He said to me: 'Go and give the daughter half, and withhold the remainder.' When I returned, I informed our companions of this, and they said: 'He gave you from the Bag of Light.' I returned to him and said: 'Indeed, our companions said: He gave you from the Bag of Light.' He said: 'Did anyone know that he gave you from the Bag of Light?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then go and give the daughter the remainder.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who dies leaving behind a slave mother and possessing wealth: 'His mother should be freed by purchasing her from his wealth, and the remainder of the wealth should be given to her, if there is no relative of hers who has a designated share in the Book of Allah.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Abu Thabit from Hanan ibn Sadir from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar said: A freedman (mawla) of Ali (peace be upon him) died, so he said: 'Look if you find an heir for him.' It was said to him: 'Two daughters in al-Yamamah, who were enslaved.' So he purchased them from the deceased's wealth, then handed over the remainder of the inheritance to them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafsh, from Abdullah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who died and left much wealth, and left behind a slave mother and a slave sister. He said: 'They are purchased from the deceased's wealth, then they are freed, and then they inherit.' I said: 'What do you think if the owners of the slave girl refuse? How should it be done?' He said: 'It is not for them to refuse; they are valued at a fair price, and what is due to them is given according to that valuation.' I said: 'What do you think if they were purchased, then freed, then inherited? Who would inherit them?' He said: 'The mawlas (patrons) of their son would inherit them, because they were purchased from the son's wealth.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Regarding a free man who dies and leaves behind a mother who is a slave, she is purchased from her son's estate, then manumitted, and then she inherits.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man dies and leaves behind a slave son.' He said: 'He is purchased and manumitted, then whatever remains is given to him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man dies and leaves behind his father who is a slave, and his mother who is a slave, and the deceased was free, then his father or his relatives are purchased from what he left, and the remainder of the wealth is inherited.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man dies and leaves behind his father who is a slave, or his mother who is a slave, or his brother or his sister, and he leaves wealth, and the deceased was free, his father or his relatives are purchased from what he left, and what remains of the wealth is inherited."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Bakkar from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind a son who was a slave, and he left no other heir, and he left wealth, he said: 'The son is purchased and freed, and what remains of the wealth is inherited.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated from 'Abdillah and Ja'far and Muhammad ibn 'Abbas from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (the Imams), upon them be peace, who said: The free person and the slave do not inherit from each other.
From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Abd Allah ibn Jabala narrated to them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The free person and the slave do not inherit from each other."

And from him (Al-Shaykh) it is narrated that Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to them from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The free person and the slave do not inherit from each other." The meaning in these narrations is that the free person and the slave do not inherit from each other, meaning that each one inherits the other, because the slave owns nothing, so the free person inherits him, and he (the slave) does not inherit the free person unless there is no one else (among the free). As for when there is someone else among the free people, then there is no mutual inheritance between them in any case.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from Jamil, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The slave does not inherit, and the divorced woman does not inherit." The explanation (resolution) of this report is that the slave does not inherit as long as there is a free person present; but in the absence of a free person, he does inherit, according to what we have previously established.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl said: Sindi ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever is manumitted against an inheritance before it is divided, he has his inheritance; and if he is manumitted after it is divided, he has no inheritance."

From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Ya'qub al-Katib narrated to us from Ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who emancipates himself using an inheritance, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it has been divided, he has no right to it; and if it has not been divided, the inheritance belongs to him.' I asked: 'A slave is emancipated using an inheritance?' He said: 'He is in the same position as him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who claims that a man's slave is his son: 'He is freed from the property of the one who claimed him. If the claimant dies and his property is distributed before the slave is freed, the property has preceded him [i.e., the slave's manumission is paid from the estate], and if he is freed before his property is distributed, then he has his share from it [i.e., the slave retains his share of the estate].'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskhan from Sulayman ibn Khalid said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who died leaving a slave wife, he would buy her from his estate, free her, and then she would inherit from him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Mihram from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding A Muslim slave who has a Christian mother, and the slave has a free son. It was said: Do you see if the slave's mother dies and leaves wealth? He said: 'Her free grandson inherits her.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave mother. When death approached him, a man from our companions went and bought her mother, stipulating upon her: 'If I buy you and free you, and when your son so-and-so dies and you inherit him, you give me half of what you inherit, on condition that you give me the pledge of God and the pledge of His Messenger that you will fulfill this for me.' The man bought her and freed her on that condition. Then her son died, and she inherited him, and there was no other heir for him. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'He has done well to her and will be rewarded for it. Indeed, this is a jurist, and Muslims are bound by their conditions, and it is upon her to fulfill for him what she pledged to God and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who manumitted his slave-girl by agreement (kitabah) and stipulated upon her that her inheritance would be his, he raised that matter to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who nullified his stipulation and said: 'The condition of God takes precedence over your condition.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Saif ibn Amirah from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When the son of al-mula'ana dies and he has brothers, his wealth is distributed according to the shares of Allah (i.e., the standard inheritance shares).'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That the inheritance of the child of al-mula'ana is for his mother; and if his mother is not alive, then for the closest people to his mother, his maternal uncles.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: In the case of al-mula'ana (conjugal imprecation), if the husband denies himself (the child) before the imprecation, his wife is returned to him and he receives the hadd punishment; if he refuses, they perform the imprecation and she is never permissible to him. And if a man accuses his wife, the hadd punishment is upon him; and if their child dies, the maternal uncles inherit him; if the father claims him, he is attached to him. And if the child dies, the son inherits him, but the father does not inherit him.

Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the child of al-mula'ana (conjugal imprecation), who inherits him? He said, 'His mother.' I said, 'If his mother dies, who inherits him?' He said, 'His maternal uncles.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Muthanna al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced li'an against his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after the li'an and claimed that her child was his child. I asked: Is the li'an returned to him? He said: 'No, and not even with honor, and it is not returned to him, and she does not become permissible to him until the Day of Resurrection.' He said: So I asked him: Who inherits the child? He said: 'His mother.' I said: What do you think if the mother died and the boy inherited from her, then the boy died after her death? Who inherits him? He said: 'His maternal uncles.' I said: If the father acknowledges him, does the father inherit from him? He said: 'Yes, and the father does not inherit from the son.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Khalid al-Aquli, from Karram, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after the li'an, claiming that the child was his: Is it returned to him? He said: 'Yes, it is returned to him, and he does not leave his child who has no inheritance for him. As for the woman, she is not permissible (to him) forever.' I asked him: Who inherits the child? He said: 'His maternal uncles.' I said: 'What if his mother died, and the boy inherited her, then the boy died? Who inherits him?' He said: 'The agnates of his mother.' I said to him: 'So he inherits his maternal uncles?' He said: 'Yes.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) From a man who cursed his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after the mutual cursing (mula'ana) and claimed that the child was indeed his. It was asked: Is it returned to him? He said: 'No, and not even with honor; it is not returned to him, nor is it permissible for him until the Day of Resurrection.' And regarding the child, who inherits him? He said: 'His mother inherits him.' I said: 'What if you see that his mother died and he inherited her, then he died? Who inherits him?' He said: 'The paternal uncles of his mother (his mother's paternal uncles), and he inherits his maternal uncles.'

And Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ubays ibn Hisham from Thabit from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about al-mula'ana (mutual cursing) when they had performed it and separated, and the husband later said, 'The child is mine,' while disproving himself (by his own statement or evidence). He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the woman, she is not returned to him, but I return the child to him. I do not leave his child (the one from the other woman) as having no inheritance. If his father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles (from the father's side) inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. If anyone claims him, saying, "O son of the fornicator," he is flogged with the fixed punishment.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from al-Ala', from al-Fudayl, who said: I asked him about a man who accused his wife of adultery (without four witnesses). He said: 'He performs li'an with her. And if he refuses to perform li'an, he is flogged with the hadd penalty and his wife is returned to him. And if she performs li'an with him, they are separated and she does not become permissible to him until the Day of Resurrection. And if he denies her child, the child is attached to the maternal uncles, who inherit him, and they do not inherit him except that he inherits his mother. And if anyone calls him a child of adultery, the one who calls him is flogged with the hadd penalty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man accuses his wife [of adultery] and they perform li'an, then they are separated and she is not permissible to him forever; if he confesses against himself before the li'an, he is flogged with the hadd penalty and she remains his wife. I asked him about the li'an in which the husband accuses her, denies his child, performs li'an, separates from her, and then says afterwards, 'The child is my son,' while contradicting himself. He said: As for the wife, she is not returned to him forever. As for the child, I return him to him if he claims him, and I do not leave his child [disinherited]. The father has no inheritance from the child, and the child inherits the father. The child's inheritance goes to his maternal uncles. If the father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. And if anyone claims him as the son of the fornicator, he is flogged with the hadd.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the son of al-mula'ana that his mother inherits one-third, and the remainder belongs to the Imam, because his crime is against the Imam. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports are not acted upon, because we have clarified that the inheritance of the son of al-mula'ana for his mother is all of it, and the reason for both is taqiyyah.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ali ibn Salim from Yahya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In a man who had intercourse with his female slave unlawfully, then bought her and claimed her son as his. He said: He said, 'He is not inherited from him, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and to the fornicator is the stone.'
