And the child of fornication is not inherited except by a man who claims the son of his female slave.' 17 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari who said: Some of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) with me, asking him about a man who had intercourse with a woman unlawfully, then he married her after pregnancy, and she brought forth a child who was most similar in creation to him. He wrote (peace be upon him) in his own hand and with his seal: 'The child belongs to the one who had intercourse unlawfully; he is not inherited.'

And Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what is the blood-money (diyah) of the child of zina?' He said, 'The one who spent on him is given what he spent on him.' I said, 'If he died and he had wealth, who inherits him?' He said, 'The Imam.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a said: Wuhayb narrated to them from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave woman of a people unlawfully, then buys her and claims her child, he is not inherited from him. For the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the fornicator is the stone.' So the child of fornication is not inherited from, except by a man who claims the child of his slave girl."

From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Ja'far and Abu Shu'ayb narrated to him from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave girl unlawfully (not his own), then buys her and claims her child, he is not inherited from (by that child). For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the adulterer is the stone (of exclusion).' And the child of the fornicator is not inherited from, except by a man who claims the child of his slave girl."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mad'ani, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said: "Any child of fornication born in the Time of Ignorance belongs to the one who claims him from among the people of Islam." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The ruling I act upon and issue fatwa based on is what these narrations contain, that the child of fornication does not inherit and his parents do not inherit from him, nor do those related to them, and his inheritance goes to the one who guarantees his sin or to the Imam of the Muslims, because inheritance is only established through correct lineages in Islamic law, and the child of fornication has no correct lineage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: The inheritance of the son of the fornicator is for his relatives from his mother's side, in the manner of the inheritance of the son of the mu'alanah (one who undergoes li'an). This is a suspended narration (mawquf) which Yunus did not attribute to any of the Imams (peace be upon them). It is possible that this was his own choice, not based on transmission from an Imam, but based on a type of consideration. And this is its ruling: it is not objected to by the many narrations that we have presented previously.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalhub, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: The child of fornication and the son of li'an inherit from their mother and their maternal uncles, or their maternal agnates.' The explanation in this narration is that it is permissible that the narrator heard this ruling regarding the son of li'an and assumed that the ruling of the child of fornication is the same, so he narrated it based on his assumption without direct hearing, with the understanding that this is a singular report (shadh) and it is not abandoned because of it the hadiths that we have previously presented.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who had intercourse with a Christian woman, and she bore him a boy. He acknowledged him, then he died, leaving no other child. Does he inherit him? He said, 'Yes.'

And what Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who had intercourse with a Jewish woman, thereby begetting a child from her, and then he died leaving no heir. He said: 'The inheritance is transferred to his son from the Jewish woman.' I said: 'And if a Christian man had intercourse with a Muslim woman, thereby begetting a boy, and then the Christian died leaving wealth, to whom would the inheritance belong?' He said: 'His inheritance belongs to his son from the Muslim woman.' These two narrations, the basis for them is Hanan ibn Sadir, and no one else narrated them. The principle/ruling in both is what the first narration contained, which is that if the man acknowledges the child and attaches him to himself, whether the child is Muslim or Christian, then the lineage is binding upon him and he inherits him according to what the report contained. As for if he does not acknowledge him and it is known that he is the son of fornication, then there is no inheritance for him in any case. And that which indicates what we mentioned, that if he acknowledges him, he cannot deny him afterwards, and the child is bound to him, is what he narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave woman of a people unlawfully, then buys her and claims her child, then he inherits nothing from her. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the fornicator is the stone.' And the child of fornication is not inherited except by a man who claims the son of his slave woman. And any man who acknowledges his child then denies him, it is not for him to do so, and there is no grace/merit by which his child is attached to him if the child is from his wife or his slave woman.'
From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Like it

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man from the Ansar came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I have been tested with a great matter. I had a slave girl whom I used to have intercourse with. One day I had intercourse with her, then I went out for my need after I had performed ritual bath, and I forgot my provision (for her) at home. I returned to the house to take it, and I found my servant boy on her belly. I counted for her from that day nine months, so she gave birth to a girl.' He said to him, 'It is not appropriate for you to have intercourse with her, nor to sell her, but spend on her from your wealth as long as you are alive. Then, upon your death, instruct that she be spent from your wealth until Allah makes a way out for her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulaym, the freedman of Tirbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, and he used to send her on his errands, and she became pregnant, and news reached him that she had been unchaste; he (Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him) said: 'If she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house.' He said: Then it was said: A man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, and he had not sent her on his errands, and he accused her (of unchastity) and she became pregnant; he said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this case is not like that one.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'Hamil' (a captive parent with a child). He said, 'And what is the Hamil?' I said, 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is her young child, so she says, 'He is my son.' And a man is taken captive, and his brother meets him, so he says, 'He is my brother,' and they recognize each other, and there is no proof for them regarding that except their word.' He said, 'So what do they say on your side?' I said, 'They do not inherit him because there was no proof regarding that; it was merely childbirth in captivity.' He said, 'Glory be to God! When she brings her son or daughter with her, she remains affirming him, and when his brother recognizes him, and that is in the soundness of their intellects, they remain affirming that, and one inherits the other.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about two men who were milk-brothers, who were brought from the land of polytheism. One of them said to the other, 'You are my brother,' and they were recognized as such. Then they were freed and remained affirming the brotherhood. Then one of them died. He said, 'The inheritance goes to the other; they are believed.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a Muslim, a Jew, and a Christian have intercourse with a woman in one purity period, a lot is drawn among them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot is drawn."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: «The Hamil inherits only with clear evidence. » This does not contradict the reports we have previously mentioned, because this narration is interpreted as being based on a form of taqiyya (dissimulation), because it agrees with the schools of the general public (Sunni scholars), as we have clarified.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibn Abi Nasr from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Muqri from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Absi from Isra'il ibn Yunus from Ishaq al-Sabii from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: "The one who is al-musta lat (from the ritual of al-la'an) does not inherit and is not inherited from, and he is called to his father."

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, from Yazid ibn Khalil, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who declared disassociation before the ruler from the crime of his son and his inheritance, then the son died and left wealth. Who inherits him? He said: 'His inheritance belongs to the closest of people to his father.'

And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir who said: I asked him about the one who is divorced (khula') by his father, who disowns him before the ruler, and regarding his inheritance and his debt/liability to whoever inherits him. He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: "He belongs to the nearest of people to him."'

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a mukatab who died and had wealth, he said: 'His inheritance is calculated according to the portion of him that was freed, for his heirs, and the portion that was not freed, for his masters who manumitted him, from his wealth.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a sum for his freedom) inherits and is inherited from according to the portion he has paid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is muqatib (a slave who has agreed to pay a certain sum for his freedom) who dies having paid part of his manumission contract, and he has a son from his concubine: He said, 'If it was stipulated that if he became unable [to pay], he would remain a slave, then his son returns as a slave along with the concubine. And if it was not stipulated, then his son pays what remains of the manumission contract and inherits what remains [of the estate].'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission for a certain sum) who pays part of his manumission money, then dies, leaving a son by his concubine. He said: 'If it was stipulated that the son would remain enslaved, the son becomes enslaved along with his mother. And if it was not stipulated, the son becomes free, and he pays the remainder of the manumission money to the master, and the son inherits what remains.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid from Burayd al-Ajli said: I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by contract (mukatabah) for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate upon him at the time of contract that if he were unable to complete the payment, he would return to slavery. And that the mukatab paid his master five hundred dirhams, then the mukatab died leaving a mature son. He said: 'Half of whatever the mukatab left is for his master who contracted with him, and the remaining half is for the son of the mukatab, because the mukatab died and half of him is free and half is a slave to the one who contracted with him. So the son of the mukatab is like the state of his father: half free and half slave to the one who contracted with his father. If he pays to the one who contracted with his father what remained on his father, then he becomes free, and there is no claim of anyone from the people upon him.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is the report, and that which we presented at the beginning of the chapter from Muhammad ibn Qays is that upon which I act and by which I give fatwa, and it is that the master inherits from the estate of the mukatab if it was not stipulated upon him to the extent of what remained of his slavery, and the remainder is for his son, and it is incumbent upon him to pay to the master of his father what remained on his father so that he becomes free and deserves what remains of the wealth. And this does not contradict the report we presented from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Malik ibn Atiyyah that if he pays what remained on his father, then what remains is for him, because in these reports it is not [stated] that if he pays what remained on his father from the principal wealth or from what he acquires. And if we assume that, we interpret it as: if he pays what remained on his father from what is specific to him, then after that if something remains, it is for him. And upon this, all the reports are reconciled.

And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a sum for his freedom) who dies having paid part of his manumission price, and he has a son from a concubine, and he left wealth, he said: 'His son pays the remainder of his manumission price, and he is freed, and inherits what remains.' The ruling in it is also what we previously mentioned in the report of another, equally. As for what the report of Malik ibn 'Atiyyah included from his saying: 'If the mukatab leaves nothing, there is no claim on the son,' this is to be understood as meaning there is no claim on him for more than what remained on his father, and it does not all return to slavery, because it is incumbent upon him to strive for what remained on his father so that he becomes free. Indicating that is what was narrated:

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Mihran said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission upon paying a sum) who dies and leaves children. He said: 'If it was stipulated for him [that his children would remain slaves until the debt was paid], then his children are slaves. And if it was not stipulated for him, his children strive in their father's mukatabah and are freed when they pay [the debt].'

And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): Regarding a mu'katib (a slave contracted for manumission) who died having paid a portion of his manumission debt, left property, and had two free children, he said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: His property is distributed among them in shares.' The correct interpretation in this report is that the property is distributed among them in shares after they pay the remainder of the debt owed by their father; what remains after that is distributed among them in shares, and this does not contradict what we have previously mentioned, and this narration has been reported.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams, peace be upon them both. Regarding a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission) who died and had paid a portion of his manumission fee, left wealth, and had two free children, he (the Imam) said: 'Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: His wealth is distributed among them (the children) and his mawali (manumission masters) in shares.' And based on this narration, the objection is removed and it agrees with what we have previously presented from the reports.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission) bought his own freedom and left behind property worth one hundred thousand dirhams, and he had no heir. He said: 'The one who assumes his blood-money liability inherits him.' I said: 'Who is the one who assumes liability for his blood-money?' He said: 'The one who assumes liability for the blood-guilt of the Muslims.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti said: Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission in exchange for a sum), if he is contracted and pays part of his manumission money, then dies leaving a son and wealth greater than what he still owes for the manumission, it is said: 'The masters are paid the remainder of the manumission amount, and what remains is for his son.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who manumitted his slave on condition that the inheritance belongs to him. He said, 'This was referred to Ali (peace be upon him), who annulled his condition, saying, 'The condition of God is prior to your condition.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskhan from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a newborn who has both a vulva and a penis, how is he inherited? He said: 'If he urinates from his penis, he has the inheritance of the male, and if he urinates from the vulva, he has the inheritance of the female.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would inherit the hermaphrodite from the place where they urinate.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Zayyat from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) gave a ruling regarding the hermaphrodite (khuntha): he has the share of men and he has the share of women. He said: He is inherited from where he urinates. If both come out together, then from where came out first. If they came out equally, then from where the stream originates. If they are equal, he inherits the inheritance of both men and women.

And al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khalq ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: The khuntha (hermaphrodite) is inherited from where they urinate; if they urinate from both, then from whichever one's urine precedes, they are inherited from it; if they die and have not urinated, then half the 'aql (bride price/dowry) of the woman and half the 'aql of the man.

Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad al-Katib narrated to me from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Muawiya ibn Maythara ibn Shurayh, who said: My father Abdullah ibn Muawiya narrated to me from his father Maythara from his father Shurayh, who said: Maythara said A woman approached Shurayh and said, 'I have come to you as a litigant.' He asked her, 'And where is your opponent?' She said, 'You are my opponent.' He cleared the session for her and said, 'Speak.' She said, 'I am a woman who has both a penis and a vagina.' He said, 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had a ruling in this matter: 'He inherits from where the urine comes from.' She said, 'It comes from both of them together.' He asked her, 'From where does the urine precede?' She said, 'Nothing from either precedes the urine; they come at one time and cease at one time.' He said to her, 'You are telling something amazing.' She said, 'I will tell you something more amazing than this: A cousin of mine married me, and I had a servant. I had intercourse with her and she bore me a child. I have come to you regarding what was born to me, so that you may separate me from my husband.' He rose from the judicial session and entered upon Ali (peace be upon him) and informed him of what the woman had said. He ordered that she be brought in and asked her about what the judge had said. She said, 'It is what he informed you of.' He said, 'Then her husband, her cousin, was brought in.' Ali, Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), said to him, 'This is your wife and the daughter of your cousin.' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do you know what happened?' He said, 'Yes, I had her as a servant, had intercourse with her, and she bore me a child.' He said, 'Then did you have intercourse with her after that?' He said, 'Yes.' Ali (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You are bolder than the eunuch of the lion, who demanded a dinar from me.' And he was considered reliable, 'and with two women.' They were brought to him, and he said to them, 'Take this woman, if she is a woman, bring her into a room, dress her in a veil, strip her of her clothes, and count the ribs of her two sides.' They did so, then came out to him and said, 'The count of the right side is twelve ribs, and the left side is eleven ribs.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'God is the Greatest. Bring me the cupper.' He took some of her hair and gave her a cloak and sa

From him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from them, peace be upon them: Regarding a newborn who has neither what men have nor what women have, except for a hole from which urine exits: upon which inheritance is he inherited? He said: 'If when he urinates his urine moves aside (separates), he is inherited with the inheritance of the male; and if when he urinates his urine does not move aside, he is inherited with the inheritance of the female.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: A child was born during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who had two heads and two chests in one back. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked: Is he inherited as one or two? He said: 'Leave him until he sleeps, then call to him. If both wake up together, he has one inheritance share. If one wakes up and the other remains asleep, then he is inherited as two.'

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abi Jameelah, who said: I saw in Fars a woman who had two heads and two chests in one hip, married, and this one would be jealous of this one and this one of this one. He said, and others narrated to us that he saw a man like that, and they were weavers, both working together on one loom.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a female slave whom her master had intercourse with during the period of purity (before menstruation), then sold her to another man before she menstruated. The second man had intercourse with her, and she had not yet menstruated. Then both men had intercourse with her during the same period of purity. She gave birth to a boy, and they disputed over him. The mother of the boy was asked, and she claimed that both men had intercourse with her during the same period of purity, so she did not know which of them was the father. He (peace be upon him) ruled: 'Regarding the boy, he inherits from both of them, and they inherit from him equally.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified in the Book of Marriage in this book that if two men have intercourse with a girl after the transfer of ownership from one to the other, the child is linked to the one in whose possession the girl is at the time. We cited reports on this. And if they both had intercourse with her during the same period of purity while they were partners without transfer of ownership from one to the other, lots are cast between them, and the child is linked to the one whose name is drawn. There is no reason to repeat this narration here. The explanation for this report is that it was presented as an act of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah), because it agrees with the views of some of the Sunni scholars, just as other reports have been presented in this manner.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man and his wife upon whom a house fell, and he said: 'The wife inherits from the man, then the man inherits from the wife.' And from him from Fadalah from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon both of them): similar to that.

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man and a woman whose house collapsed on them, causing both to die, and it was not known which of them died first. He said: 'Each of them inherits the other, as Allah has prescribed for their heirs.'

From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who drown or are buried by a house collapsing; he said, 'They inherit from one another.'
From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman and her husband when a house fell upon both of them, similarly.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a house that fell upon a group of people together, so it is not known which of them died first. He said: 'One inherits from the other.' I said: 'Indeed Abu Hanifah included something in it.' He said: 'And what did he include?' I said: 'If two brothers, one of whom is my mawla (freedman) and the other is a mawla of a man, one of them has one hundred thousand dirhams and the other has nothing, they boarded a ship and drowned, and it is not known which of them died first, then the wealth belongs to the heirs of the one who has nothing, and the heirs of the one who has the wealth have nothing.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I have heard it, and it is so.' I said: 'And if two slaves, I freed one of them and you freed the other, one of them has one hundred thousand dirhams and the other has nothing,' he said the same.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man and a woman were buried when a house fell on them and they died. He said: The man inherits from the woman and the woman inherits from the man. I said: Indeed Abu Hanifa has introduced something regarding them in this matter. He said: What did he introduce? I said: Two brothers, non-Arabs, who have no heir except their mawla (manumitters/freemen). One of them had one hundred thousand dirhams known to him, and the other had nothing. They boarded a ship and drowned, and the one hundred thousand dirhams were taken out. What should be done with it? He said: It is given to the mawla of the one who had nothing, and the other had none. Then he said: I do not object to what he introduced in it; he is correct, it is thus. Then he said: The wealth is given to the mawla of the one who had nothing, provided the other did not have wealth that the mawla of the other would inherit. Thus, there is nothing for the mawla of the other.

Ali narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding a man and his wife upon whom a house falls. He said: 'The wife inherits from the man, and the man inherits from the wife.' Its meaning is that they inherit from each other from the substance of their own wealth; they do not inherit from each other's share of what is jointly inherited.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad al-Katib from Amr ibn Khalid ibn Talhah al-Qannad from Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani from Simak ibn Harb from Qabus from his father from Ali: That Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man and a woman who both died from the plague, dying on one bed, with the man's hand and foot on the woman, so he assigned the inheritance to the man and said, 'Indeed, he died after her.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Hanifah: 'O Abu Hanifah, what do you say about a house that collapsed on a group of people, and two children remained from them, one free and the other a slave to his master, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' Abu Hanifah said: 'Half of this one is freed, and half of this one is freed, and the wealth is divided between them.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Not so, but a lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls on is the free one, and this one is freed, so he becomes his mawla (client/freedman).'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: I said to him: A slave woman and a free woman were both under a house when it collapsed on them, and they had given birth. The two mothers died and the two sons remained. How are they inherited? He said: They are allotted by drawing lots three times consecutively. Meaning three times. Whichever one's lot is drawn, he inherits from the other.

From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a group of people upon whom a roof fell; how is their inheritance? He said: 'Some of them inherit from others.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from al-Walid ibn 'Uqba al-Shaybani, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from Humran ibn A'yan, from the one he mentioned, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). Regarding a people who all drowned, being the family (of the deceased), he said: 'These inherit from these, and these inherit from these, and these do not inherit from what these inherited from these anything, and these do not inherit from what these inherited from these anything.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in Yemen regarding a people whose house collapsed upon them, leaving two boys: one a slave and the other free. He cast lots between them, and the lot fell on one of them, so he gave the wealth to that one and freed the other.

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad al-Katib from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said: I asked: A female slave and a free woman, a single house (estate) fell upon them, and they had given birth and died; how are they inherited? He said: A lot is cast for them three times as a group, so whichever of them the lot strikes inherits from the other.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: It was mentioned that Ibn Abi Layla and Ibn Shubrumah entered the Sacred Mosque and came to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). He said to them, 'By what do you judge?' They said, 'By the Book of Allah and the Sunnah.' He said, 'And what do you do with what you do not find in the Book and the Sunnah?' They said, 'We exert our own opinion (ijtihad ra'yuna).' He said, 'Your own opinion? What do you say about a woman and her female slave who were nursing two boys in a house, and a roof collapsed on them, killing them, while the two boys survived?' They said, 'The Qafi (a specific share/ruling).' He said, 'The Qafi is one who is given a stern look (or is deemed sufficient) for them.' They said, 'Then inform us.' He said, 'No (it is not the Qafi).' Ibn Dawud said, 'My ransom be for you, it reached me that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no group of people who delegated their affair to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and cast their lots, except that the most accurate lot emerges.' So he fell silent.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him). That he used to grant inheritance to the Magian if he married his mother and his daughter through two aspects: from the aspect that she is his mother, and from the aspect that she is his wife. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Our companions, may God have mercy on them, differed regarding the inheritance of the Magian if he married one of the prohibited relatives by lineage according to Islamic law. Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman and many of the later followers said: He inherits only from the lineage and the cause that are permissible in Islamic law. As for what is not permissible in Islamic law, he does not inherit from it under any circumstance. And al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and some of the later followers who followed him said on his opinion: He inherits from the lineage under all circumstances, even if it was acquired through a cause that is not permissible in Islamic law. As for the cause, he inherits from it only through what is permissible in Islamic law. And the correct opinion in my view is that the Magian inherits from both lineage and cause together, whether they are permissible in Islamic law or not. And that which indicates this is the report we mentioned earlier from al-Sakuni, and what our companions mentioned in opposition to it is not supported by a trace from the Infallibles (peace be upon them), nor is there evidence for it from the apparent text of the Quran. But they said it only as a form of consideration, and that is discarded among us by consensus. And furthermore, these lineages and causes, although they are not permissible in Islamic law, are permissible among them, and they believe that it is through that which the private parts are made lawful, and they are not made lawful by anything else. So it runs the course of the contract in Islamic law.

It is narrated that a man cursed a Magian in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he restrained him and forbade him from doing that, and he said: "Do you not know that for them that is marriage?"

And it has also been narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, every people who adhere to a certain belief, the ruling of that belief applies to them.' So if the Magians believe in the validity of that, then their marriage should be considered valid. And also, if that were not valid, it would be necessary that it also not be valid when contracted on non-forbidden things, and the dowry was made to be wine or pork or other of the forbidden items. Because that is not valid in the Sharia, and our companions have agreed on the validity of that. Thus, it is known from all of this that what we mentioned is the correct view, and action should be taken upon it, while other views are discarded and not acted upon in any case.

Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Jew and the Christian do not inherit the Muslims, and the Muslim inherits the Jew and the Christian.'

Yunus narrated from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man, does he inherit the polytheist? He said: 'Yes, and the polytheist does not inherit the Muslim.'

From him, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, if a Christian dies and he has a Muslim son, does the Muslim son inherit him?' He said, and he said: 'Yes, indeed God did not increase him by Islam except in honor, so we inherit them and they do not inherit us.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muslim man inherits his dhimmi (non-Muslim protected) wife, but she does not inherit him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Muslim 'hijab' (excludes) the disbeliever and inherits him, and the disbeliever does not 'hijab' (exclude) the believer and does not inherit him.
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: Do people of two different religions inherit from each other? He said: 'No.'

And from him (Al-Shaykh) it was said: Abdullah ibn Jabala narrated to them from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the Muslim husband and the Jewish or Christian wife, he said: 'They do not inherit from each other.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Like it

From him, from Hanan, from Umayy al-Sayrafi, or between him and him is a man, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr al-Qibti, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): that he said: "For the Christian whose wife gave herself to you in marriage, and there is no inheritance between you two." The meaning in these narrations is that there is no inheritance between them in a way that each inherits the other as Muslims inherit each other, and this does not contradict that the Muslim inherits the disbeliever, although the disbeliever does not inherit the Muslim. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) explicitly stated this in the narration of Jamil and Hisham which we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter, and what increases that clarification is what he narrated:

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah narrated to them from Ibn Bukayr from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yan, who said:' I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about His saying: 'People of two religions do not inherit from one another.' He said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We inherit them, and they do not inherit us. Indeed, Islam has not added to his inheritance except severity.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Those of two different religions do not inherit from each other; this one inherits this one and this one inherits this one, except that the Muslim inherits the non-Muslim, but the non-Muslim does not inherit the Muslim.'

And as for what was narrated - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Abd al-Rahman al-Basri who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a Christian man whose wife chose Islam, and her residence (dar al-hijrah) [is]: that she is in the abode of Islam and is not expelled from it, and her conjugal right (bud') is in the hand of her Christian husband, and she does not inherit him, nor does he inherit her.' This report and the one we presented earlier from Umayy al-Sayrafi are both narrated in agreement with the general public (Ahl al-Sunnah) on what they narrate from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and their narrators are also the narrators of the general public. And this ruling is to be taken as being due to precaution (taqiyyah) and is not taken as definitive if it contradicts all other reports.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Malik ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a Christian who died, leaving a Muslim son of his brother and a Muslim son of his sister, and the Christian had children and a Christian wife. He said, 'I see that the Muslim son of his brother should be given two-thirds of what he left, and the Muslim son of his sister should be given one-third of what he left, if he did not have young children. If he had young children, then the two heirs must spend from what they inherited from their father on the young children until they come of age.' It was said to him, 'How do they spend?' He said, 'The heir of the two-thirds takes two-thirds of the maintenance, and the heir of the one-third takes one-third of the maintenance. When they come of age, they cease the maintenance for them.' It was said to him, 'What if the children convert to Islam while they are young?' He said, 'What their father left is deposited with the Imam until they come of age. If they remain upon Islam, the Imam returns their inheritance to them. If they do not remain upon Islam when they come of age, the Imam returns the inheritance to the Muslim son of his brother and the Muslim son of his sister; he gives the son of the brother two-thirds of what was left and the son of the sister one-third of what was left.'

Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who died, leaving behind a Christian mother, a wife, and Muslim children. He said, 'If his mother converts to Islam before his inheritance is distributed, she is given one-sixth.' I said, 'And if he had no wife, no children, and no heir with a prescribed share in the Book from among the Muslims, and his mother was Christian, and he had Christian relatives who would have a prescribed share in the Book if they were Muslims, then to whom would his inheritance belong?' He said, 'If his mother converts, then all his inheritance belongs to her. And if his mother does not convert, but some of his relatives convert who have a prescribed share in the Book, then the inheritance belongs to them. And if none of his relatives convert, then the inheritance belongs to the Imam.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever embraces Islam while an inheritance is still undivided, he is entitled to his share of the inheritance; and if he embraces Islam after the inheritance has been divided, he has no share in it."

Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: "Whoever is granted freedom (or inherits) on an estate before the estate is divided, it is for him; and whoever is granted freedom (or inherits) after the estate is divided, he has no share in the estate. And whoever is manumitted on an estate before the estate is divided, he is free; and whoever is manumitted after the estate is divided, he has no share in the estate." And he said regarding the woman: 'If she is granted freedom before the estate is divided, she has the estate.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Mizham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding A Muslim slave who has a Christian mother, and the slave has a free son. It was said: Do you see if the slave's mother dies and leaves wealth? He said: 'Her free grandson inherits her.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever takes possession of an inheritance before it is divided, it is for him."

From him, from Ja'far, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yn, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'They do not increase in honor through Islam except us; we inherit them and they do not inherit us. This is the inheritance of Abu Talib in our hands, so we do not consider it except in the child and the parent, and we do not consider it in the husband and the wife.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Muslim man who was killed, and his father was a Christian: To whom does his blood money (diyah) belong? He said: 'His blood money is taken and placed in the treasury of the Muslims, because his indemnity/liability is upon the treasury of the Muslims.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The people of two religions do not settle together in one village."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to rule in matters of inheritance regarding what was acquired by Islam from the wealth of a polytheist whom he left, which had not been divided before Islam: 'That he used to assign for the women and the men their shares from it, according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding inheritance: that which Islam acquired from the wealth of a polytheist which had not yet been divided, the women have their shares from it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ribat, who narrated, saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man from the People of the Book (dhimmi) converts to Islam, while his father is still alive, and his father has other children besides him; then when the father dies, the Muslim son inherits all of his father's wealth, and his father's other children and his wife do not inherit anything from him alongside the Muslim son.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has children who are not Muslims, he said: 'They are upon their inheritances.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him) 'They are upon their inheritances' is that they receive what they are entitled to from the inheritance. And we have clarified that when Muslims gather with the disbelievers, the inheritance is for the Muslims alone. If we were to take the report at its apparent meaning, it would be understood as a form of taqiyya (dissimulation).

Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from a man who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A Christian who converted to Islam, then returned to Christianity, then died, he died, he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Christian children.' And a Muslim who converted to Christianity then died, he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Muslim children.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The explanation in this report is that the inheritance of the Christian is only for his Christian children if he has no Muslim children, and the inheritance of the Muslim is for his Muslim children if they exist.

And Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz narrated from Ahmad ibn A'idh from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "The disbeliever does not inherit the Muslim, and the Muslim may inherit the disbeliever, unless the Muslim has bequeathed something to the disbeliever."

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has children who are not Muslims, he said: 'They are upon their inheritances.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a Muslim man apostatizes from Islam, his wife is divorced from him as a woman who has been thrice divorced, and she observes the waiting period from him as a divorced woman observes. If he returns to Islam and repents before she marries another, he is her suitor (with no new dowry required), and there is no waiting period for her from him; rather, the waiting period is for the other man. If he is killed or dies before the waiting period ends, she observes the waiting period of a widow from him, and she inherits him during the waiting period, but he does not inherit her if she dies while he is an apostate from Islam.

Ibn Mahbub from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he said: 'Whoever shows preference for a religion other than Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his execution becomes obligatory, and his wife is separated from him, and what he leaves is divided among his children.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who apostatized from Islam, [saying] 'To whom belongs his inheritance?' He said, 'It is divided among his heirs according to the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who dies apostatizing from the religion of Islam and has children, he said: 'His wealth is for his Muslim children.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, son of a Muslim, who apostatizes from Islam and denies the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and disbelieves in him, then his blood is permissible for whoever hears that from him, and his wife is separated from him on the day he apostatizes and one should not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him if he is brought to him, and he does not seek his repentance.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a slave-girl who was Christian, then embraced Islam with a man, and bore him a son. Then her master died and instructed that the slave-girl be freed. She married a Christian Dari man, who was al-Attar, and she reverted to Christianity. Then she bore two sons and became pregnant with another. He ruled regarding her that Islam should be offered to her; if she refused, he said: 'As for whatever child she bore, it belongs to her son from her first master. She is detained until she gives birth to what is in her womb; when she gives birth, he kills her.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the blood-money (diyah) of the slain: 'The heirs inherit it according to the Book of Allah and their shares, if there is no debt upon the slain, except that the brothers and sisters from the mother do not inherit anything from his blood-money.'

Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled that the heirs inherit the blood money (diyah), except for the maternal brothers, for they do not inherit anything from the blood money.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The blood-money (diyah) is inherited by the heirs according to the shares of inheritance, except for the maternal brothers, for they do not inherit anything from the blood-money.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Yahya al-Azraq said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is killed and leaves a debt, but has no property, so his heirs take the blood money (diyah); is it upon them to pay his debt? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he left nothing?' He said, 'Yes, they only took his blood money, so it is upon them to pay his debt.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: Do the maternal brothers have any share of the blood money (diyah)? He said: 'No.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah and 'Ali ibn Ribat, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "The maternal brothers inherit nothing from the blood-money (diyah)."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hammad ibn Isa from Sawwar from Al-Hasan said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him), when he defeated Talhah and Al-Zubayr, the people came retreating. They passed by a pregnant woman on the side of the road, and she was frightened by them, so she cast out what was in her womb. It struggled until it died, then its mother died after it. Ali (peace be upon him) and his companions passed by her while she was lying there and her child on the road. He asked them about her matter, and they said, 'She was pregnant; she was frightened when she saw the fighting and the retreat.' He asked them, 'Which one died before the other?' It was said, 'Her son died before her.' So he summoned her husband, Abu Al-Ghulam, the deceased, and bequeathed to him from the blood money of his son two-thirds of the diyyah. And he bequeathed to her mother one-third of the diyyah. Then he bequeathed to the husband from the deceased wife one-half of the one-third of the diyyah that she had inherited from her son, and he bequeathed to the relatives of the deceased wife the remainder. Then he bequeathed to the husband also from the blood money of his deceased wife one-half of the diyyah, which is two thousand and five hundred dirhams, and he bequeathed to the relatives of the deceased wife one-half of the diyyah, which is two thousand and five hundred dirhams. And that was because she had no other child besides the one she cast out when she was frightened. He said, 'And he paid all of that from the treasury of Basra.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed, and he had a brother in Dar al-Hijrah (the city of emigration) and another brother in Dar al-Badw (the desert/bedouin dwellings) who had not emigrated. I asked: Do you think if the emigrant forgives and the bedouin wants to kill, does he have that right? He said: 'The bedouin does not have the right to kill an emigrant until he emigrates. If the emigrant forgives, then his forgiveness is valid.' I said to him: And what about the bedouin's share of the inheritance? He said: 'As for the inheritance, it is for him, and he has his portion from the blood-money of his killed brother, if the blood-money is taken.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a man who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A Christian who converted to Islam, then returned to Christianity, and then died — he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Christian children.' And a Muslim who converted to Christianity and then died — he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Muslim children.'

Al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār from Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When the blood money (diyah) of the deliberate act is accepted and becomes wealth, it is inheritance like other properties."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Two men do not inherit from each other if one of them killed the other."

From him, from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother, does he inherit her? He said, 'I heard my father saying, 'Any man of kin who kills his relative, he does not inherit him.''

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadeed from Jamil ibn Darradj from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said: "A man does not inherit if he kills his son or his parent, but the inheritance belongs to the relatives of the killer."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In a man who killed his mother, he said: 'He does not inherit her, and he is killed by her (as compensation), a minor killing, and I do not think his killing her is an expiation for his sin.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no inheritance for the killer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: "The woman inherits from the blood-money (diyah) of her husband, and he inherits from her blood-money, provided that one of them has not killed the other."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the wife have a share of the blood-money (diyah) of her husband, and does the husband have a share of the blood-money of his wife?' He said, 'Yes, as long as one of them did not kill the other.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "If a man kills his father, he is executed for him; and if his father kills him, he is not executed for him, and he does not inherit from him."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who took medicine while pregnant, and her husband did not know of this, so she miscarried. He said: 'If the fetus has a bone with flesh grown upon it, upon her is a diyah (blood money) which she pays to its father; and if it is a fetus, an 'alaqah (blood clot) or a mudghah (chewed flesh), then upon her is forty dinars or a ghurrah (single adult male/female slave) which she pays to its father.' I said to him: 'Does she not inherit from her child from the diyah?' He said: 'No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit from him.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sind ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who killed his mother, saying: 'If it was accidental, then he inherits her, and if he killed her intentionally, then he does not inherit her.'

Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Khattab from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother, does he inherit her? He said: 'If it was accidental, he inherits her, and if it was deliberate, he does not inherit her.' And these two reports do not contradict what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal said: A man narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman; and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub also narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "A man is not killed for the blood of his son, and the son is killed for the blood of his father if he killed his father; and a man does not inherit from another man if he killed him, even if it was accidental." Because this report is mursal (disconnected chain), and despite that, it is possible that the reasoning behind it is what our Sheikh, Abu 'Abdillah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, said: that a man does not inherit from the man he killed accidentally from his diya (blood money), but he inherits from him from what is beyond the diya; and the one who kills intentionally inherits nothing, neither from the diya nor from other wealth. And with this interpretation, he reconciles between the two hadiths, and this is a close opinion, and that which confirms this interpretation is what was narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: Regarding a man who killed his father, he said: 'He does not inherit him. If the killer has a son, the son inherits the slain grandfather.'

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: "Any woman who is divorced, and her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires, she inherits him, and then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died for her. And if she dies during her waiting period, he inherits her. And if she is killed, he inherits from her blood money (diyah). And if he is killed, she inherits from his blood money, provided that one of them did not kill the other."

From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife one time (revocable divorce), then he died while she was in her waiting period. He said: 'She inherits him, then she completes the waiting period of the one who died, which is her husband. And if she died, she inherits him. If he was killed or she was killed while she was in her waiting period, each of the two inherits from the blood-money (diyah) of the other.'

And Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about two groups of believers, one of which was the aggressors (bāghiyyah) and the other just ('ādilah). They fought each other, and a man from the people of Iraq killed his father, or his son, or his brother, or his close relative, while he was from the aggressors, and he was the heir of the deceased. Does he inherit him? He said, 'Yes, because he killed him with right (bi-haqq).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, al-sadaqah (dower/gift in marriage context) is a later innovation. The people, during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), used to give gifts (nahal) and bestow gifts (hiba), and it was not fitting for one who gave something for the sake of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, to take it back. He (the Imam) said: 'And as for what was not given for the sake of Allah and in Allah, then he may take it back, whether it was a gift of gratuity (nihlah) or a general gift (hiba), whether it was taken possession of or not.' And the man shall not take back what he gives to his wife, nor the woman what she gives to her husband, whether it was taken possession of or not. Is it not that Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And do not take back from them anything you have given them?' And He said: 'But if they are pleased with you for something of it, then take it in satisfaction and joy.' And this applies to both the dower (sadaqah) and the gift (hiba).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who gives charity to his children while they are young by giving them a female slave, then he likes the female slave while they are still young dependents under his care. Do I see that he takes her (for himself) or evaluates her at a just price and testifies to its value upon them, or does he leave all that and not present anything of it? He said: 'He evaluates her at a just price and accounts for its value for them against himself, then he takes her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: "If the gift remains in its original state (intact and not consumed or transferred), then he has the right to return (revoke it); otherwise, he does not have the right."

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): He was asked about a man who had a slave girl, and his wife annoyed him regarding her, so he said, 'She is a gift (sadaqah) for you.' He said: 'If he said that for God's sake, he must uphold it; and if he did not say it for God's sake, he has the right to take her back if he wishes.'

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about a man who gave charity to a close relative; is it suitable for him to take it back? He said, 'No, but if he needs it, let him take it from his relative from what was not given as charity to him.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who gave a gift to his mother, then she died, and she had taken possession of what he gave her and retained it. He said: 'He and the heirs are equal in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the recipient of the gift is compensated (for it), it is not for him to return it."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gifts a female slave on the condition that he is rewarded (with sexual access), but he is not rewarded; is it for him to take her back? He said, 'Yes, if he had stipulated it for him.' I said, 'Do you see if he gifted it to him and did not reward him, does he have sexual access to her or not?' He said, 'Yes, if he had not stipulated it for him when he gifted it.'

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who returns (revokes) his charity, he said: 'He is like the one who returns what he vomited.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The example of the one who retracts his charity is like the one who regurgitates his vomit."

From him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah and Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, they said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) About a man who gives a gift, does he return it if he wishes or not? He said: 'The gift is valid for those of kinship, and the one who is rewarded for his gift, and he returns in other than that if he wishes.'

From him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The gift (nuhlah) and the grant (hibah) are [valid] as long as possession has not been taken until the owner dies. He said: 'It is in the position of inheritance, and if the child is in his guardianship, it is valid.' He said: And I asked him: Is it permissible for anyone to take back his gift and charity? He said: 'If he gives charity for the sake of Allah, then no. As for the gift (nuhlah) and the grant (hibah), he may take it back whether he has taken possession or not, even if it was for a relative.'

From him, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man had dirhams owed to a person, so he gifted them to him, then he revoked the gift, then he gifted them to him again, then he revoked again, then he gifted them to him, then he died. He (the Imam) said: 'They belong to the one to whom they were gifted.'

From him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, who said: "When a man gives charity or a gift, whether the recipient takes possession of it or does not, whether it is known or unknown, it is valid."

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Mi'za from Abu Basir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-hibah (gift) is valid whether it has been taken possession of or not, divided or not divided. And an-nuhlah (gift given for a specific purpose/reason) is not valid until it is taken possession of, and the people intended that but were mistaken.'

From him, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a father giving a gift to his child, and he said: 'As for when he is healthy, it is his wealth, he does with it what he wills; but as for when he is ill, it is not valid.'

From him, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A gift (hiba) and a grant (nuhl) may be reclaimed by its owner if he wishes, whether it has been taken possession of or not, except for one of kinship, for indeed he does not reclaim it.

From him, from Abu al-Mu'za, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives a gift exclusively to one of his children. He said: 'If he is wealthy, yes; and if he is poor, no.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: Is it permissible for anyone to take back a charity (sadaqah) or a gift (hibah)? He said: 'As for what is given as charity for the sake of Allah, it is not taken back. And as for the gift (hibah) and the grant (nihlah), one may take it back whether one has taken possession of it or not, even if it was given to a relative.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to apply when the recipient is a mature, fully competent adult, because if he were a child, it would not be permissible for him to take it back. Or we may understand it to apply to those relatives other than children. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who gave something to his son, [asking]: Is it permissible for him to take it back? He (peace be upon him) said: "Yes, unless he is a child."

From him, from Ya'qub al-Katib, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who gives out the alms-tax (zakat), intending to give it to the beggar, but he does not find him, he said: 'Let him give it to someone else, and he should not return it to his own wealth.'

From him, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A gift (hiba) and an endowment (nihla) are [valid] as long as the owner has not died before taking possession. He said: 'It is inheritance.' If it is for a child under his guardianship, and he witnesses upon it, then it is valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt due from another man, so he gifted it to his son. The man mentioned the money that was due from him to the other, and he said to him: 'There is nothing upon you regarding it in this world and the hereafter, provided that pleases him, and he had indeed gifted it to a son of his.' He said: 'Yes, it is that he gifted it to him, then he revoked it and made it a gift to this one.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Aban from Abdullah ibn Sinan said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who makes a gift (hiba), does he return it if he wishes or not? He said: 'The gift is valid for those of kinship and the one who is rewarded for his gift, and he returns in other cases if he wishes.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it permissible for anyone to take back his charity or his gift? He said: 'As for what is given as charity for the sake of God, then no.' But as for the gift and the endowment, one may take it back whether one has taken possession of it or not, even if it was given to a relative.' And he said: 'Whoever causes any obstruction or harm to the path of the Muslims, he is liable (for compensation).' He said: And I heard him saying: 'Charity is not permissible for anyone from the descendants of al-Abbas (may God be pleased with him), nor for anyone from the descendants of Ali (peace be upon him), nor for their peers from the descendants of Abd al-Muttalib (peace be upon him).'

From him, from Ibrahim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "You have the option to return the gift as long as it remains in your possession; but when it goes out to its owner, you do not have the right to take it back." And he said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever returns his gift is like the one who returns his vomit.'"

From him, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'A gift (hiba) does not become a valid gift ever until it is taken possession of, and a charity (sadaqah) is binding upon the giver, and if he sends a bequest (wasiyyah) to a man from his town, he has no choice but to accept it, and if he is in his town and another is found [available], that is up to him.' The book of possession, charities, gifts, and bequests ended. 9

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Abu al-Mi'za Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Abu al-Abbas and Ubayd ibn Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a young boy who married a young girl, he (the Imam) said: 'They inherit from each other if their parents married them off.' I asked: 'Is the father's divorce valid?' He said: 'No.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a boy and a girl whom their guardians had married while they were not yet mature. He said, 'The marriage is valid, and whichever of them reaches maturity has the option [to annul or confirm]. If they die before reaching maturity, there is no inheritance between them, nor is there a dowry, unless they had both reached maturity and consented.' I said, 'And if one of them reaches maturity before the other?' He said, 'That is valid upon him if he consents.' I said, 'And if the man had reached maturity before the girl and consented to the marriage, then died before the girl reached maturity, does she inherit him?' He said, 'Yes. Her inheritance is set aside from him until she reaches maturity and swears by God that nothing called her to take the inheritance except her consent to the marriage. Then the inheritance and half of the dowry are given to her.' I said, 'And if the girl died and had not yet reached maturity, does the husband inherit her?' He said, 'No, because she has the option [to reject the marriage] if she reaches maturity.' I said, 'And if it was her father who married her before she reached maturity?' He said, 'The father's marriage is valid upon her, and it is valid upon the boy, and the dowry is upon the father for the girl.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married off his mature son to an orphan girl under his guardianship. He said: 'He inherits her if she dies, and she does not inherit him if he dies, because she has the choice (of annulment) regarding him, but he has no choice regarding her.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife. He said: 'She inherits him and he inherits her as long as he has the right of return (raj'ah) over her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man divorces his wife while he is in a state where there is no return (raj'ah) to her, she does not inherit him, nor does he inherit her." And he said: "He inherits and is inherited as long as the blood has not appeared from the third menstruation, if he has the right of return (raj'ah) to her."

Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a woman is divorced, then her husband dies while she is in her waiting period (iddah) from him, she does not become permanently forbidden to him; for she inherits him and he inherits her as long as she is in the blood of her second menstruation from the first two divorces. If he divorces her a third time, then she does not inherit her husband anything, nor does he inherit her.
