Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Yazid al-Kunasī from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The muṭlaqah (freely divorced), the mukhayyarah (woman given choice of divorce), the mubāri'ah (mutual divorce), and the musta'marah (divorce by husband's request) — these do not inherit from their husbands anything during their waiting period (ʿiddah), because the bond of marriage has been severed between them and their husbands from that moment, so there is no return (rajʿah) for their husbands, and no inheritance between them.

From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-A'la ibn Manzur, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman who requests divorce, if she says to her husband, 'Divorce me,' and he divorces her by her command and with her consent, then it is a final divorce, and there is no right of return for him over her, and there is no inheritance between them, and she observes the waiting period from him for three months or three menstrual periods. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who divorces his wife with a divorce in which he does not have the right of return: 'She has become permanently divorced from him, and there is no inheritance between them during the waiting period.'

From him, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married four women in one contract, or he said in one session, and their dowries were different. He said: 'It is permissible for him and for them.' I said: What do you think if he went to some of the lands, and he divorced one of the four, and he bore witness on her divorce a group of people from the people of that land, and they did not know the woman? Then he married a woman from the people of that land after the expiration of the waiting period of the one he divorced, then he died after he had consummated the marriage with her. How is his inheritance divided? He said: 'If he has a child, then for the woman whom he married last from the people of that land is one-fourth of one-eighth of what he left. And if the one he divorced from the four is known by her very self and her lineage, then she has nothing from the inheritance, and she has the waiting period.' He said: 'And the three women divide three-fourths of one-eighth of what he left, and the waiting period is upon them. And if the one he divorced from the four women is not known, the four women divide three-fourths of one-eighth of what he left among themselves all together, and the waiting period is upon them all together.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, and he married two more women to them in a single contract. He consummated the marriage with one of them, then he died. He said: 'If he had consummated the marriage with the woman he began with by name and mentioned her at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, she is entitled to inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period.' He said: 'And if he had consummated the marriage with the one who was mentioned after the mention of the first, then her marriage is invalid, she has no inheritance, but she is entitled to the dowry she received in exchange for what she made permissible of her private part, and she must observe the waiting period.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: "If a man divorces his wife with two divorces, then divorces her with the third, while he is ill, then she inherits him."

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife while in his illness, she inherits him as long as he remains in that illness, even if her waiting period expires, unless he recovers. I asked: 'And if the illness prolongs for him?' He said: 'Between him and one year.'

From him, from Fudayla, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi and Abu Basir and Abu al-Abbas, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: "He inherits her, and she does not inherit him, when the waiting period (iddah) has expired."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from one who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorces his wife while he is ill, he said: 'If he dies in his illness and she remains waiting for him (in her waiting period) and has not remarried, she inherits him; and if she has already remarried, then she has accepted what he did, so there is no inheritance for her.'
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskān, from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Rifah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever dies with no patron (mawla) and no heirs is among the people of this verse: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger.”'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "Whoever dies and has no heir from his close relatives (qarabah) nor a mawla of 'itaqah (manumission) who has guaranteed his debt, then his wealth is from the anfal (public treasury/fay').

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Khallad from al-Sari, raising it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): Regarding the man who dies and leaves wealth with no heir, he said: Then Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said, 'Give him his Hamsharij.'

And it was also narrated - from Dawud, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man died during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and he had no heir, so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave his inheritance to Hamshahirij. This is a marsi (disconnected) narration and does not contradict what we have previously presented from the reports, even though there is nothing in it that opposes what preceded, because what it contained was that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave his estate to Hamsharij, and perhaps he did that as a form of administrative discretion (istihsan), because if the wealth was exclusively his, as we have mentioned, it was permissible for him to do with it as he wished, and the narration does not state that this is the ruling for all wealth that has no heir, which would be contrary to the previously mentioned reports.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said: I asked him about a man who had children, and some of his children went missing, and he did not know where they were. The man died. What should be done with the inheritance of the missing child from his father? He said: 'He is set aside (withheld) until he comes.' I said: 'The man was lost and did not come.' He said: 'If the man's heirs are full in his wealth, they divide it among themselves. If he comes, they return it to him.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat and Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had children, and some of his children went missing, and he did not know where they were. The man died. What is done with the inheritance of the missing son from his father? He said: 'It is set aside (held in reserve) until he comes.' I said: 'Is Zakat due on his property?' He said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'When he comes, does he pay Zakat?' He said: 'No, until a full year passes while it is in his possession.' I said: 'If the man is lost and does not come?' He said: 'If the heirs of the man are numerous with his property, they divide it among themselves. If he comes, they return it to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The estate of the missing person (mafqud) is withheld for the heirs for as long as he is sought in the land for four years; if he is not found, his estate is distributed among the heirs. And if he has a child, his estate is withheld and spent on his child for those four years.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hisham ibn Salim said: Khattab al-A'war asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) while I was sitting, saying: 'There was a hired worker at my father's place who worked for wages, and we lost him, and some of his wages remained for him, and we do not know his heir.' He said, 'Seek him.' He said, 'We have sought him but did not find him.' He said, 'Poor men,' and moved his hands. He repeated to him, saying, 'Seek and strive. If you can find him, [pay him]; and if you cannot find him, it is like your own property until a claimant comes to him. And if an incident befalls you, bequeath it; if a claimant comes to him, let it be paid to him.'

Yunus narrated from Abu Thabit and Ibn 'Awn from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had a debt due from another man, and he lost him (the debtor), and did not know where to seek him, and did not know if he was alive or dead, and did not know of any heir for him, nor his lineage, nor his country. He said: 'Seek him.' He said: 'That has taken long, so shall I give it in charity?' He said: 'Seek him.' Yunus from Fayd ibn Habib, the innkeeper He said: I wrote to 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him): 'Two hundred and forty dirhams have come into my possession, and I am an innkeeper. The owner died, and I do not know of any heirs for him. What is your opinion regarding informing about its status and what I should do with it, for I have grown weary of it?' He wrote: 'Manage it and release it as charity little by little until it is exhausted.' Yunus from al-Haytham, Abu Rawh, the innkeeper He said: I wrote to 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him): 'I accept guests in the rooms, so a man stays with me and dies suddenly, and I do not know him, nor his country, nor his heirs, so the wealth remains with me. What should I do with it, and to whom does that wealth belong?' He wrote (peace be upon him): 'Leave it as it is.'

Ali ibn Mahziyar said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a house that belonged to a woman, and she had a son and a daughter. The son was absent at sea, and the woman died. Her daughter claimed that her mother had designated this house for her and had sold her shares from it, leaving a portion in the house next to the house of one of our companions. He disliked buying it due to the absence of the son and feared that it might not be permissible for him to buy it, as no news was known of the son. He asked me, 'How long has he been absent?' I said, 'For many years.' He said, 'He waits for his absence for ten years, then he buys.' I said, 'If he waits for her absence for ten years, is it permissible to buy it?' He said, 'Yes.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Attiya from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In a Muslim man who was killed and his father was a Christian (Nasrani), to whom would his blood money (diyah) belong? He said: 'His blood money is taken and placed in the treasury of the Muslims, because his blood money is upon the treasury of the Muslims.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has in his possession wealth belonging to a deceased man, and he does not know his heir, what should he do with the wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: 'How do you know who he is?' meaning himself (peace be upon him).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Regarding a miscarried fetus, if it falls into its mother's womb and moves with a distinct movement, it inherits and is inherited, for it may be mute.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind his wife while she was pregnant, and she gave birth to a male child after his death. Then the male child died after he hit the ground. The woman who accepted her (as a witness) testified that he cried out and bawled when he hit the ground, and then he died after that. He said: 'It is upon the Imam to validate her testimony regarding one-quarter of the male child's inheritance.'

From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testimony of the midwife is accepted regarding the newborn, if he cries and shouts, in matters of inheritance, and he inherits one-quarter of the estate based on the testimony of one woman.' I said: 'And if there are two women?' He said: 'Their testimony is accepted for half of the estate.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the 'Maf'us' (one who has been struck/killed but not yet dead), he does not inherit anything from the blood money (diyah) until he cries out and his voice is heard.

From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: My father said: 'When the newborn moves with a distinct movement, it inherits and is inherited, for it may be mute.'

And Hariz narrated from al-Fudayl who said: Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a child who falls from its mother before crying out, asking if it is inherited. He turned away from him, so he repeated his question, whereupon he said: 'If it moves with a distinct movement, it is inherited, for perhaps it is mute.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said: I asked him about a man who died leaving young and adult sons and daughters, without a will, and he had servants and female slaves and debts. How should the heirs manage the division of that inheritance? He said, 'If a trustworthy man stands among them and divides all of it for them, there is no harm.' Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khurasani wrote: In the case of a man who left an heir to a man, and he had paternal cousins, daughters of paternal cousins, a paternal uncle, and two paternal aunts, to whom is the inheritance? He (peace be upon him) wrote back, 'The people of the 'asabah (agnates), the paternal cousins, they are the heirs.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a narration consistent with the general public (Sunni), but we do not adopt it because we have clarified that the nearer in lineage is more entitled to inheritance. And if that is established, then in this case the inheritance belongs to the two paternal aunts, because they are nearer than the children of the paternal uncle and the paternal uncle.

And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Mattuwayh ibn Nabhah, from Abu Sumanah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Bazzaz, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who left behind his maternal uncle and his grandfather. He said: 'The wealth is shared between them.' And I asked him about a man who left behind his sister, his brother, and his grandfather. He said: 'For the male is the share of two females.' For the grandfather two shares, for the brother two shares, and for the sister one share. He said: And I asked him about a man who left behind his sister and his grandfather. He said: 'The wealth is shared between them.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report has a weak chain of narration and contradicts the correct doctrine, because we have clarified that the closer relative is more entitled to the wealth than the distant one. And if that is established, then the grandfather is more entitled than the maternal uncle. As for the second question, it is correct according to the doctrine. As for the third, from his saying 'The wealth is between the sister and the grandfather,' it is not in the report that the wealth is shared equally between them, but it is possible that the meaning is 'The wealth is between them [according to] for the male is the share of two females.' And if it were in it that the wealth is shared between them equally, we would interpret it as the grandfather from the mother's side and the sister from the mother's side, because they are equal in shares, and the male and female would be equal in it. 10 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Ja'far said: I asked him about a woman who died and left behind her husband, her parents, and her grandfather or grandmother. How is her inheritance divided? So he issued a ruling (peace be upon him): 'For the husband half, and what remains is for the two parents.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to them from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who had a husband and a child from another man, and a child from her husband, when the child from the other man died, he said: 'Her husband will separate from her for three months until he knows whether there is a child in her womb or not. If there is a child in her womb, he will be inherited.' Abu Ali said: And this is contrary to the truth and is not to be acted upon.

And from him (the previous narrator) it was said: Wahb narrated to them from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a woman who had a child from another man, and the child died leaving property, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is appropriate for the husband to separate from the wife until she menstruates once, to purify her womb; I fear that a pregnancy might occur in her, so the heir would be one who has no right to inheritance.' Abu Ali said: And this is also contrary to the truth and is not taken; rather, the inheritance belongs to the mother of the deceased.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who freed a 'sā'ibah (a slave freed on condition of serving a specific master) that there is no 'walā' (patronage) for his former masters upon him. If he wishes, he may attach himself to one of the Muslims, and he should bear witness that he guarantees his debt and every incident that binds him. If he does that, he inherits him; and if he does not do that, his inheritance is returned to the Imam of the Muslims.

From him (Al-Shaykh) said: Safwan narrated to them from Ibn Muskān from Abū Baṣīr from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: “The Sa’ibah (freed slave who has no heirs) has no heir; if he has a wali (heir/relative), his inheritance belongs to him and his debt is upon him. And if he has no wali, he belongs to the closest person to his master who freed him.” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon because all other reports have come stating that whenever the Sa’ibah has no wali, his inheritance belongs to the Treasury of the Muslims. We have fully detailed what is in this regard in the Book of Manumission, and we have cited in this what is sufficient, and praise be to God, and that which clarifies this further is what he narrated:

Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a slave who freed a sa'iba (a slave freed on condition that he remains in the master's service or his heirs inherit him). He said: 'He is under the guardianship of whomever he chooses, and upon whomever he is attached falls his liability, and he has his inheritance.' I said: 'And if he remains silent until he dies?' He said: 'His inheritance is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the As-Sa'ibah, so he said: 'Look at what is in the Quran; whatever has in it the freeing of a neck (slave). That, O 'Ammar, is the Sa'ibah which has no guardianship for anyone upon it except Allah. And whatever its guardianship is for Allah, it is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for his Messenger, then indeed its guardianship is for the Imam, and its liability is upon the Imam, and its inheritance is for him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who emancipated his slave: 'He is free, with no claim of ownership over him; he is independent, goes his way and may manage his own affairs as he pleases. But if he guarantees his debt/liability, then he inherits him.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In the case of a mukatabah (manumission contract) between two partners, where one of them frees his share How does the servant act? He said: 'She serves the remaining partner one day, and serves herself one day.' I said: 'If she dies and leaves wealth?' He said: 'The wealth is divided in half between the one who freed her and the one who retained her.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When a man assumes responsibility for another man, the inheritance belongs to him and the debt is upon him."

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who embraced Islam and then attached himself (as a client) to a man from the Muslims. He said: 'If he guaranteed his blood-money and his diya (compensation for injury/death), he inherits him and becomes his patron (mawla).'

Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from 'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the Sa'ibah (a female slave freed by her master) and the one who was from the People of the Covenant (Dhimmi), if one of them married a Muslim on the condition that he pays the blood-money (diyah) for her, and thus her inheritance becomes his, is that permissible? He said, 'Yes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) and 'Uthman differed regarding a man who dies and has no 'asabah (agnates) to inherit him, but has a close relative who does not inherit. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance is for them,' citing God's saying: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer [to one another] in the Book of Allah.' And 'Uthman said: 'It is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, or from Abdillah ibn Amr, and from Rib'i, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah educated Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and perfected his education, so He said: 'Take what is easy and command what is good and turn away from the ignorant.' And indeed, you are of a great moral character. When that was the case, He delegated His religion to him, so He said: 'Whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, and whatever he has forbidden you, abstain from it, and fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in retribution.' So Allah forbade wine itself, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade every intoxicant, and Allah approved that for him. And Allah prescribed the fixed shares (of inheritance), but did not mention the grandfather, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) assigned him a share, and Allah approved that for him. And by Allah, He gives Paradise based on Allah's word, so Allah approves that for him.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas Fadl al-Baqbaq from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Do women have qawd (blood money) or 'afw (compensation)?' He said, 'No, and that is for the 'asabah (male agnates).' Ali ibn al-Hasan said, 'This is contrary to what our companions hold.'

From him, from Muhammad al-Katib, from Abdullah ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, that he wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who died and was a mawla (client/freedman) of a man, and his master had died before him, and the mawla had a son and daughters, so I asked him about the inheritance of the mawla, and he said: "It is for the men, not the women." Ali said: "And this is also contrary to what our companions hold." 27 - And - Al-Rida (peace be upon him) wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in his reply to his questions: "The reason for giving women half of what is given to men in inheritance is that when the woman marries she takes (dowry), and the man gives, so therefore it was increased for the men."

And Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), from Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'When a person dies while traveling, do not conceal his death from his family, for it is a trust so that his wife may complete her waiting period (iddah), and his inheritance may be distributed among his family before one of them dies, causing his share to be lost.' Completed, by the grace of Allah and His good success, what we intended regarding the commentary on the ninth part - according to our division of the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam, on the 17th of Rabi' al-Thani, in the year 1382 AH. And praise be to Allah as He deserves, and prayers upon the one after whom there is no prophet, and we ask Him for assistance to complete it, for He is the Bestower of Success. And I, the humble, Hasan al-Mawsili al-Khorasani.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), that he said: "The will (testament) is a right upon every Muslim."
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The will (wasiyyah) is a right/obligation upon every Muslim.'
Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Zayd al-Shahham said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the will (al-wasiyyah), and he said: 'It is a right upon every Muslim.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him: 'I set out for Mecca and a man accompanied me, and he was my companion. When we were on part of the journey, he fell ill and became severely weak. I would attend to him, then he regained consciousness until there was no harm to him in my view. When it was the day on which he died, he regained consciousness and then died on that day.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dead person whose death approaches but that Allah, Exalted and Mighty, returns to him from his hearing, sight, and intellect [the faculty] for the will. He takes the will or leaves it. And it is the ease/repose which is called the 'repose of death'. So it is a right upon every Muslim.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Walid ibn Sabih who said: A freed slave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), called A'yan, accompanied me. He was ill for some days, then recovered, then died. I took his belongings and whatever he had, and brought them to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). I informed him that the man had been ill for some days and then recovered. He said: 'That is the rest of death. Indeed, no one dies until Allah, Exalted and Glorious, returns to him from his hearing, sight, and intellect that which is due for the will, whether he took it or left it.'

And Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah al-Raba'i narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: "The bequest (al-wasiyyah) is the completion of what is lacking from the alms-tax (zakat)."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Wahb, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: "The bequest (wasiyyah) is the completion of what was lacking from the zakat."

From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever does not make a will at the time of his death for his relatives who do not inherit him, has concluded his deeds with disobedience."

And with this chain of narration, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: "Whoever makes a will but does not guard it properly and is not harmed [by the heirs' actions], is like one who gave it in charity during his lifetime."
And with this chain of narration, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'I do not care if I harmed my heirs or if I stole that wealth from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Hazm Al-Kalbi, the brother-in-law of Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever does not make his will well at the time of death, it is a deficiency in his honor and intellect." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how does the dying person make his will? He said: "When his death approaches and the people gather around him, he says: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen," the Merciful, the Compassionate. O Allah, I bequeath to You in the abode of the world that I bear witness that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, and that Paradise is true, and Hell is true, and the Resurrection is true, and the Reckoning is true, and Justice and Decree and the Balance are true, and that the Quran is true, and that the Quran is as You sent it down, and that You are Allah, the Clear Truth. May Allah reward Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the best reward, and may Allah give life to Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with peace. O Allah, O my provision in my distress, O my companion in my hardship, O my guardian of my blessing, my God and the God of my fathers, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, for if You leave me to myself, I would be closer to evil and further from good. And make my loneliness in the grave familiar to me, and make for me a covenant on the Day I meet You, [when I am] displayed. Then he makes his specific bequests. And the confirmation of this will is in the Quran, in the Surah in which Maryam is mentioned, in His Exalted and Majestic saying: "They do not have the power of intercession except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful." (1) This is the covenant of the dying person, and the will is obligatory upon every Muslim to memorize this will and teach it. And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught it to me," and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) taught it to me." And as for charity, it is your utmost effort until you say 'I have exceeded,' even if you have not exceeded. And upon you i

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ali ibn Salim from Yahya ibn Muhammad said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'O you who have believed, when death approaches one of you, [in the case of] bequest, two just witnesses from among you or two others from outside [the believers].' He said: 'The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from outside [the believers] are from the People of the Book - and if you do not find People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established for the Magians the same ruling as the People of the Book regarding the jizya.' He said: 'And that is if he dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims, then two men from the People of the Book are made to testify.' 'After the prayer, so they swear by Allah if you doubt, that we will not buy it for a price, even if he were a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, we would then be of the sinners.' He said: 'And that is if the heir of the deceased doubts their testimony, and if he finds that they testified falsely, he is not allowed to invalidate their testimony until two other witnesses come and take the place of the first two witnesses.' 'So they swear by Allah that our testimony is more worthy than their testimony, and we did not transgress; indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers.' So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated and the testimony of the latter two is accepted. Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says: 'That is nearer that they bring the testimony in its true form or they fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) Like it

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'O you who have believed, testimony [for] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest [should be] two just men from you or others from outside.' (He quoted the verse up to 'min ghayrikum'). He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are two disbelievers.' I said: 'Two just men from you.' He said: 'Two Muslims.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Hamzah ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Two just men from you or two others from non-Muslims.' He said, then said: 'The two from you are two Muslims, and the two from non-Muslims are from the People of the Book.' He said: 'When a Muslim man dies in a foreign land, and he seeks two Muslim men to witness his will, but does not find two Muslims, then he should have two dhimmi (non-Muslim protected persons) from the People of the Book, who are reputable among their people, witness his will.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Rib'i from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the testimony of a woman who witnessed a man making a will, with no man accompanying her, he said: 'One-quarter of what he bequeathed is accepted based on her testimony.'

From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) That he ruled regarding a will that was witnessed only by a woman, so he validated one-quarter of the will based on the testimony of a woman.

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman who claimed that she was bequeathed one-third of an estate in a certain town, but she had no proof. He said: 'She is given one-quarter of what she claimed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In a will that a woman witnessed, the testimony of a woman is valid for one-quarter of the will.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Asim from Muhammad ibn Qays said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled in a will witnessed only by a woman that the testimony of a woman is valid for one-quarter of the will if she is Muslim and not doubtful in her religion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: Is the testimony of people of a different sect/millah permissible for them? He said: 'Yes, if they do not find people of their own sect, the testimony of others is permissible, because it is not fitting that the right of anyone should be lost.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, 'Or two others from among you,' he said, 'If a man is in a town where there is no Muslim, the testimony of a non-Muslim is valid regarding the will/testament.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "When the child reaches five cubits (in height), his slaughtered meat is eaten (i.e., is valid), and when he reaches ten years, his will is valid."

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abu Basir and Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the boy who is ten years old making a will, he said: 'When he reaches the place of the will, it is valid.'

From him, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamzah, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When the young boy is visited by death and has not reached puberty, his will is valid for his close relatives (kin) and is not valid for strangers.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said: When ten years have passed for the boy, then whatever he frees, or gives in charity, or bequeaths in a well-known and right manner is valid for him.

From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the will/testament of a young boy (ghulam), is it valid? He said: 'If he is ten years old, his will is valid.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the boy reaches ten years of age and makes a bequest of one-third of his wealth, his bequest is valid. And if he is seven years old and makes a bequest of a small amount from his wealth, his bequest is valid.

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said: The divorce of the young man is valid if he has reached the age of discernment (akil), and his testimony and his will are valid, even if he has not yet experienced seminal emission (ihtilam).

From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the charity (sadaqah) of a young boy who has not yet reached puberty (ihtilam). He said, 'Yes, if he places it in the place designated for charity.'

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died, leaving behind a female slave who had borne him a daughter, and his own daughter was young but able to speak. The mother (the slave) freed herself. The masters of the father of the slave disputed over her. He validated the emancipation of the slave woman for her daughter.

From him, from al-Abdi, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from al-Askari (peace be upon him), who said: "When the boy reaches eight years, his affair regarding his wealth is valid, and the obligations of fixed shares and limits have become incumbent upon him. And when the girl completes seven years, it is the same."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Mansur from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The ending of the childhood of the orphan is the seminal emission (al-ihlam), and that is its most significant sign. If he emits semen but maturity (rushd) is not anticipated from him, and he is a fool or weak, then his guardian should retain his property.

From him, from Abu Muhammad al-Madaini, from A'iz ibn Habib, the seller of al-Harawi, who said: Isa ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The child has his teeth cut (circumcised) at seven, and is commanded to perform prayer at nine, and they are separated from each other in sleeping quarters at ten, and he experiences seminal emission at fourteen, and the end of his height is at twenty-one, and the end of his intellect is at twenty-eight, except for experience."

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When he reaches his maturity at thirteen years old and enters the fourteenth, the obligations that fall upon those who have reached puberty fall upon him, whether he has had a wet dream or not. Bad deeds are recorded against him and good deeds are recorded for him, and everything is valid for him, except if he is a spendthrift or weak-minded."

Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the orphan girl, when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: 'When you know that she does not squander it nor lose it.' I asked him if she had married, and he said: 'When she is married, the guardianship of the guardian ceases regarding her.'

Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Adam, the pearl seller, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: "When the boy reaches thirteen years of age, a good deed is recorded for him and a bad deed is recorded against him, and he is punished [for deeds], and when the girl reaches nine years of age, it is the same, and that is because she menstruates at nine years of age."
Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "A girl is not entered into (consummated) until she reaches nine years or ten years."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from his brother Ja'far ibn 'Isa from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who appointed a woman as an executor and shared the will with her, including a young boy. He said: 'That is permissible, and the woman executes the will and does not wait for the boy's maturity. When the boy reaches maturity, he is not entitled to reject anything except what was a change or alteration; for he may return it to what the deceased had willed.' 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man appointed his children as executors, among them are adults who have reached maturity and among them are young children. Is it permissible for the adults to execute his will and pay his debts to those whose claim against the deceased is established by just witnesses, before the young executors reach maturity? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Yes, the adults among the children should pay their father's debt and not delay it because of that.' 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man appointed two men as executors. Is it permissible for one of them to take half of the estate alone and the other half? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'It is not fitting for them to contradict the deceased, and they should act according to what he commanded them, if God wills.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, who said: A man died and left me in his will, along with another man, or two men. One of them said, 'Take half of what he left and give me the half of what he left.' The other refused him. They asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'That is for him.' This refers to the one who refused the other's claim to exclusive possession of half the estate. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may God have mercy on him) mentioned that this report, he does not act upon it nor issue fatwa based on it, but he acts upon the first report, assuming that the two are contradictory. However, the matter is not as he assumed, because the Imam's (peace be upon him) statement 'That is for him' does not explicitly mean that it is for the claimant who sought exclusive possession of half the estate. It is not impossible that what is meant by his statement 'That is for him' is the one who refused to submit to his partner's desire, so the conclusion of the speech is that he has the right to refuse him and not respond to his request. On this basis, there is no contradiction between them in any case.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, who said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Mukhariqi al-Kufi, from Abi Junadah al-Saluli, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever fasts in the month of Shaban, it will be for him a purification from every slip, oath, and haste. Abi Hamzah said: I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the 'wasmah' (oath)? He replied: The oath in disobedience and the vow in disobedience. I asked: Then what is the 'badirah' (haste)? He replied: The oath taken in anger, and repenting from it and regretting it.

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fasting in the month of Shaban and the month of Ramadan, two consecutive months, is repentance, by Allah, from Allah.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Zurbi narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to me from Abdillah ibn Marhum al-Azdi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: One who fasts on the first day of Shaban, Paradise becomes obligatory for him. And one who fasts for two days, Allah looks at him every day and night in the dwelling of this world, and His gaze remains upon him in Paradise. And one who fasts for three days, Allah visits him upon His Throne from His Paradise every day.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shaban is my month and Ramadan is the month of Allah, and it is the spring of the poor. And the sacrifice (Al-Adha) was made only so that your poor may eat meat to satiety, so feed them.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to separate the fasts of Shaban and the month of Ramadan by one day, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to connect them (fast continuously), and he would say: 'Fasting for two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.'

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Umar ibn Khalid from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast in the month of Shaban and the month of Ramadan continuously, and he used to forbid people from connecting them. He used to say: 'These are the two months of Allah, and they are expiation for the sins between them, i.e., the sins of the previous and next months.'

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to delay any obligatory fasts they had until the month of Shaban, out of reluctance to prevent the Messenger of Allah from his desire. And when Shaban arrived, they would fast, and the Prophet would fast with them. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to say, 'Shaban is my month.'

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Did any of your ancestors fast in Shaban?' He said, 'The best of my ancestors is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he fasted in it.'

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting of Sha'ban: 'Did any of your ancestors fast in it?' He said: 'The best of my ancestors is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and most of his fasting was in Sha'ban.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Hamid ibn Shu'aib narrated to us, he said: Shurayh ibn Yunis narrated to us, he said: Wakee' narrated from Sufyan from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the fasting of Rajab, so he said: 'Where are you regarding Shaban?'

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us, he said: al-Hajjaj ibn Hamzah narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sadaqah al-Rafiqi informed me, he said: Thabit narrated to us from Anas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was asked: Which fasting is the most superior? He said: Fasting in Sha'ban, to honor Ramadan.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj narrated, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Yazid al-Abdi narrated, saying: Gundar narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb narrated to us from Nawbah al-Saymari, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Umm Salama, from Abu Salama, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast a complete month from the year except Shaban, linking it with Ramadan.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us from his father, from Yahya ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Amir al-Wasiti, who said: I was informed by Ata ibn al-Sayb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: While his companions were recalling the virtues of the month of Shaban in his presence, He said: It is a noble month, and it is my month. The Throne bears it, honors it, and recognizes its right. It is a month in which Allah increases the sustenance of the believers for Ramadan, and in which the gardens (of Paradise) are adorned. It is named Shaban because the sustenance of the believers branches out for Ramadan within it. It is the month of deeds. In it, good deeds are multiplied seventyfold, evil deeds are erased, sins are forgiven, and good deeds are accepted. The Almighty (Glorified is His Majesty) boasts in it with His servants, looking from His Throne to His fasting and praying servants, and boasting of them to the bearers of His Throne. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood up and said: My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Describe to us something of its virtue so that we may increase our desire for its fasting and night prayer, and perform Tahajjud for the Majestic One in it. He (peace be upon him) said: Whoever fasts the first day of Shaban, Allah writes for him seventy good deeds, and each good deed is equivalent to the worship of a year. And whoever fasts two days of Shaban, He removes from him the destructive evil deed. And whoever fasts three days of Shaban, He raises him seventy degrees in the Gardens (of Paradise) made of pearls and rubies. And whoever fasts four days of Shaban, He expands his sustenance. And whoever fasts five days of Shaban, he becomes beloved to the servants. And whoever fasts six days of Shaban, Allah turns away from him seventy types of calamities. And whoever fasts seven days of Shaban, he is protected from Satan and his troops, from his nudging and whispering. And whoever fasts eight days of Shaban, he will not leave this world until he is given a drink from the cisterns of Holiness. And whoever fasts nine days of Shaban, Munkar and Nakir are lenient with him when they question him. And whoever fasts ten days of Shaban, Allah expands his grave seventy cubits by seventy cubi

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said: 'May I be your ransom, is there for the Muslims an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said: 'Yes, O Hasan, the greatest and most noble of them.' I said to him: 'And which day is it?' He said: 'The day when the Commander of the Faithful was set up as a standard for the people.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, and which day is it?' He said: 'Indeed, the days revolve, and it is the eighteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, and what should we do in it?' He said: 'Fast it, O Hasan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family, and declare yourself free from those who wronged them and denied their rights, for the Prophets used to command the Successors that the day on which the Successor was appointed should be taken as an Eid.' I said: 'What is the reward for one of us who fasts it?' He said: 'Fasting for sixty months.' And do not neglect fasting the day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day in which Prophethood was revealed upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like that of sixty months for you.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fasting on the day of Eid-e Ghadeer is the expiation for sixty years.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Sahl (Harun ibn Muhammad) Zanjalah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us from Sa'd ibn Sa'id from Abi Tayyibah from Nur ibn Wabarah from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from Jibril from Israfil from His Lord, May He be glorified and exalted, that He said: Whoever prays on the night of Eid al-Fitr ten rak'at, reciting in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and 'Say: He is Allah, One' ten times, and says in his bowing and prostration: 'Glory be to Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' Then he recites the Tashahhud and gives Salam between every two rak'at. When he finishes from them, he says a thousand times: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah and I repent to Him.' Then he prostrates and says in his prostration: 'O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Merciful of the world and Compassionate of the Hereafter, O Most Generous of the generous, O Most Merciful of the merciful, O God of the first and the last, forgive my sins and accept my fasting, my prayer, and my standing (in prayer).' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'By the One who sent me as a Prophet with the truth, he does not raise his head from prostration until Allah forgives him and accepts from him the month of Ramadan and overlooks his sins, even if he had committed seventy sins, each of which is greater than the sins of all the servants.' I said: 'O Jibril, does He accept from him specifically the month of Ramadan, or from all His servants in his lands?' He said: 'Yes, and by the One who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, O Muhammad, indeed among His honor upon Allah and the greatness of his status is that He accepts from him and from them, and accepts from all the monotheists between the East and the West their prayers and their fasting, and forgives their sins and answers their supplications.' After informing him of this, and by the One who sent me with the truth, indeed whoever prays this prayer and seeks forgiveness with this seeking of forgiveness, Allah will accept his prayer, his fasting, and his standing, and forgive him and answer his supplication. Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in His Book: 'And ask forgive

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Sakhtawih ibn Shabib al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Asim narrated from Isma'il ibn Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no servant who prays six rak'at on the night of Eid except that he will be granted intercession for all members of his family, even if Hellfire had been decreed for them.' They asked: 'Why is this, O Messenger of Allah?' He replied: 'Because the virtuous do not need intercession; intercession is only for every one who is perishing.' And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said: One should recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' five times in each rak'at.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Bakr al-Farisi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated from Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who stays awake during the night of Eid, his heart will not die on the day the hearts die.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Uthman al-Misri narrated to us in Egypt, saying: Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Al-Mufaddal ibn Fudalah narrated from Isa ibn Ibrahim, from Salama ibn Sulayman al-Khudri, from Harun ibn Salim, from Ibn Kurdoos, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who stays awake during the night of Eid and the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, his heart will not die on the day the hearts die.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does not pray with the Imam in congregation on the day of Eid, there is no prayer (Salaat) for him and no make-up (Qaza) is obligatory upon him.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Salat for the two Eids except with an Imam. So if you pray alone, there is no harm in it.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: There is no Salat on the day of al-Fitr and al-Adha except with an Imam.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdillah ibn Sinan al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the prayer of the two Eids, is there a prayer before them or after them? He said: There is nothing before them and nothing after them.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibniz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah regarding the prayer of al-Fitr and al-Adha. He said: There is no Adhan or Iqamah for them, and there is no prayer before or after the two rak'at.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prayer of the two Eids is two rak'ahs; there is no [prayer] before them and no [prayer] after them.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Marwan, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to fast until it was said he does not break his fast. Then he would fast for a day and break his fast on another day. Then he would fast on Monday and Thursday. Then it settled into fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he used to say, 'That is the fasting of the year (perpetual fasting).' And my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'No one is more detestable to me than a man who is told that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to do so-and-so, and he says,

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The fasting of the month of Patience (Ramadan) and three days in every month remove the evil thoughts from the chests. And the fasting of three days in every month is the fasting of the entire life. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it.'

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from al-Ahwal, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about fasting two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them. He replied: As for Thursday, it is a day in which deeds are presented; and as for Wednesday, it is a day in which Hell was created; and as for the fast, it is a shield.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, who said: It was asked of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding fasting on Wednesday, so he said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say, 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created Hell on Wednesday, so he loved fasting on it to seek protection from Allah against the Fire.'

And by this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, brother of Muglis al-Sayfari, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to fast so much that it was said he never broke his fast, and he used to break his fast so much that it was said he never fasted. Then he fasted the fast of Dawud (peace be upon him), fasting one day and breaking one day. Then he passed away while fasting the three days of the month. He said: 'These equal the fast of a lifetime and remove the heat of the chest.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, which days are they?' He said: 'The first Thursday of the month, the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday of it.' I said: 'And why did these days become so?' He said: 'Because the communities before us, when punishment was sent down upon them, it was sent down on these days. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) fasted all of these days because they are the days of fear.'

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Yasar ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For what reason is Wednesday fasted?' He replied: 'Because Hell was created on Wednesday.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I postpone the fasting of three days of the month from summer to winter, for I find them easier for me then.' He said: 'Yes, but preserve their number.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Fasting becomes difficult for me in the heat, and I find a headache. He said: Do as I do. When I travel, I give charity every day with a Mudd of food, which is what I feed my family with.

My father (peace be upon him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sufyan from Dawud al-Raqqi who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Your breaking of the fast (Iftar) in the house of your Muslim brother is better than your fasting seventy or ninety times over.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Salih ibn Uqbah from Jamil ibn Darradj who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'One who visits his brother while he is fasting, and breaks his fast at his house, and does not inform him of his fast, thereby showing favor to him, Allah records for him the reward of fasting for a year.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Abu Harun al-Makfuuf who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Harun, recite poetry for me about al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' So I recited for him. He said: 'Recite as they recite,' meaning with emotion/weeping. So I recited this verse for him: 'Pass by the grave of Husayn and say to his pure bones.' He wept, then said: 'Add more.' So I recited the other poem. He wept, and I heard the weeping from behind the curtain. When I finished, he said: 'O Abu Harun, whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes ten people weep, Paradise is written for them. Whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes five people weep, Paradise is written for him. Whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes one person weep, Paradise is written for them. And whoever hears the mention of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and a tear the size of a fly's wing falls from his eyes, his reward is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will not be satisfied with less than Paradise for him.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Abu Umara al-Munshid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me, 'O Abu Umara, recite for me the poem of al-Abdi regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' I said, 'So I recited it to him and he wept.' He said, 'Then I recited it to him and he wept.' He said, 'By God, I continued reciting it to him while he wept until I heard the weeping from the house.' Then he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'O Abu Umara! One who recites a poem regarding al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and makes fifty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes forty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes thirty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes twenty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes ten people cry, for him is Paradise.' And one who recites regarding al-Husayn a single poem, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) a poem and cries, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) a poem and makes a crying face, for him is Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who recites a couplet regarding Imam Husayn (peace be upon him) and cries and makes ten people cry, for him and for them is Paradise. He continued until he said: And one who recites poetry regarding Imam Husayn (peace be upon him) and cries, and I think he said: or weeps together (with others), for him is Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Abdillah from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from a man from the general populace, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One who recites in the Mushaf by looking at it, his eyes will be strengthened and the chastisement of his parents will be reduced, even if they were disbelievers.
And with this chain, he raised it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: There is nothing more severe for Satan than reciting the Mushaf by looking at it.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned to his companions and said: 'Take up shields.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, is it from an enemy who has surrounded us?' He replied, 'No, but from the Fire. Say: Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Increase in saying Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, and Allahu Akbar, for indeed they will come on the Day of Resurrection with them preceders, followers, and rear-guards, and they are the enduring good deeds.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abi al-Jarud from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever says 'Subhanallah' (Glory be to Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it. A man from Quraish said: O Messenger of Allah, then our trees in Paradise would be many? He said: Yes, but beware that you do not send fire upon them so that it burns them. And that is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: O you who believe! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds.

And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad, from his father, and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions one day: 'Do you think that if you were to gather what you have of clothing and utensils, then placed them atop one another, would you perceive them reaching the sky?' They replied, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Shall I not inform you of something whose root is in the earth and its branches in the sky?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'One of you, upon completing the obligatory prayer, should say: Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, thirty times. For indeed, their root is in the earth and their branches are in the sky. They prevent destruction, fire, drowning, falling in a well, consumption by wild beasts, death due to accidents, and the affliction that descends from the sky upon the servant on that day. They are the enduring good deeds.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says "La ilaha illallah" a hundred times, his deed is the best of the people's deeds that day, except for one who recites it more.

My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Salim ibn Ghanim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says, when he goes to his bed, 'La ilaha illallah' a hundred times, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise. And whoever seeks forgiveness when he goes to his bed a hundred times, his sins fall away just as the leaves of a tree fall off.

With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who recites Surah al-Taghabun in his obligatory prayer will have it intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection, and serve as a just witness before one who accepts its testimony; it will not leave him until he enters Paradise.

And with this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Amr ibn Bakr, from Jabir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recites all of the Musabbihat (the seven short surahs starting with Tasbih) before sleeping will not die until he sees Al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), and if he dies, he will be in the neighborhood of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sayf ibn ‘Umayra from a man from Abi Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: One who recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr' (Surely We sent it down in the Night of Power) loudly with his voice is like the one who draws his sword in the way of Allah, Exalted and Glorious; and one who recites it quietly is like the one smeared with his blood in the way of Allah; and one who recites it ten times, Allah will erase a thousand sins from his sins.

And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from his father al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites 'Inna anzalnahu' (We sent it down) as an obligatory act among the obligations of Allah, an announcer will call out: O servant of Allah, Allah has forgiven you what has passed, so resume your deeds.

And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites 'Alhakumut Takathur' in his obligatory prayer, Allah will write for him the reward of a hundred martyrs. And whoever recites it in his recommended prayer, Allah will write for him the reward of fifty martyrs. And forty rows of angels will pray with him in his obligatory prayer, if Allah wills.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashshar from Abdullah al-Dihqan from Durust from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever recites 'Alhakum al-takathur' before sleeping will be protected from the trial of the grave.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Abu Muhammad al-Razi from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn Bakr ibn Sammal from al-Fadl ibn Uthman who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever is wise, Paradise will be concluded for him, God willing.

And with this chain of narration, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is wise (has intellect/reason), he has a religion (faith/piety), and whoever has a religion, he will enter Paradise.'

With this chain of narration, from Sayf ibn 'Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One who passes a single day and prays five prayers in it, but does not recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in them, it will be said to him: 'O servant of Allah, you are not among those who pray (properly).'

And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who has a Friday pass by him and does not recite in it 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and then dies, dies upon the religion of Abu Lahab.

And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sandal, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is afflicted by an illness or a hardship and does not recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' during his illness or hardship, then dies in that illness or in that specific hardship that befell him, he is from the people of Hell.

And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sayf ibn 'Umaira, from Ibn [Abi] Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who has faith in Allah and the Last Day must not fail to recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' after the obligatory prayer; for whoever recites it, Allah will gather for him the goodness of this world and the hereafter, and Allah will forgive him, his parents, and what he has begotten.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times when he takes his place to sleep, Allah will forgive him the sins of fifty years.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and said: 'Ninety thousand angels, including Jibreel (peace be upon him), attended his funeral prayer.' I asked him, 'O Jibreel, for what reason did you deserve to pray over him?' He replied, 'Because of his recitation of Say, He is Allah, [who is] One. While standing, sitting, riding, walking, going, and coming.'

And with this chain, from Abi al-Hasan, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who lies down to his bed and recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' eleven times, Allah will protect him in his house and in the surrounding areas.
