Abi (radhi Allahu 'anhu) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from al-Husayn ibn Jahm from Ibrahim ibn Mihrzam from a man who heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' before meeting an unjust person, Allah will protect him from him by reciting it before him, behind him, to his right, and to his left. When he does that, Allah will grant him its good and protect him from its evil. And he said: When you fear someone, recite a hundred verses from the Quran from wherever you wish, then say: 'O Allah, remove the calamity from me' three times.

Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman from a man from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say to a man: 'Do you love remaining in the world?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And why?' He said: 'For reciting Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad.' So he fell silent about him. Then he said after a while: 'O Hafs! Whoever dies from our Shias and does not recite the Quran well, will be taught in his grave so that Allah raises his rank through it. Indeed, the ranks of Paradise are according to the number of verses of the Quran. So it is said to the reciter of the Quran: 'Recite and ascend.'

My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Musa ibn Ja'far from Wahb al-Baghdadi from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If you shun the great sins which you are forbidden, We will do away with your small [sins]' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'One who keeps away from that for which Allah has threatened with the Fire, if he is a believer, Allah will forgive his sins and make him enter a noble place.' And the seven greater sins that are obligatory [to avoid] are: killing the innocent soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury, apostasy after migration, accusing a chaste woman, consuming the property of an orphan, and fleeing from the battle.

My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'If you shun the great sins which you are forbidden,' he said: 'One who abstains from those sins for which Allah has promised Hell, if he is a believer, Allah will forgive his sins.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am at the Scale on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's evil deeds are heavier than his good deeds, I will bring the salutations upon me by him so that I may make his good deeds heavier with them.'

And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Karim al-Kazzaz, from Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-Awar, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: Every supplication is veiled from the heaven until one sends blessings upon Muhammad and his family.

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah said, and in the narration of Abdullah ibn Sayabah and Ibn Ismail from Najih from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: When you pray on Friday, say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the successors who are pleased, with the best of Your blessings, and bestow blessings upon them with the best of Your blessings, and peace be upon him and upon them and upon their souls and bodies, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Allah will write for you a hundred thousand good deeds, erase from you a hundred thousand bad deeds, fulfill for you a hundred thousand needs, and raise for you a hundred thousand degrees.

And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musdaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A man said, 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the household of Muhammad.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O man, you have narrowed [the scope] upon us. Do you not know that the Ahl al-Bayt are five, the People of the Cloak?' The man asked, 'How should I say?' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family (Al) of Muhammad, so that we and our Shias will be included in it.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he used to say: One who supplicates for his brothers among the believers and the believing women, and the Muslims and the Muslim women, Allah appoints for him an angel who supplicates for him on behalf of every believer.

And with this chain of narration, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: No believer supplicates for the believing men and women, and the Muslim men and women, the living among them and the dead, but that Allah writes for him a good deed for every believer and believing woman, from when Allah sent forth Adam until the Hour is established.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: My father narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Fadl ibn Yusuf, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says twenty-five times every day: 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and believing women, the Muslim men and Muslim women,' Allah will write for him, for the number of every believer who has passed away and every believer who remains until the Day of Resurrection, one good deed; He will erase one bad deed from him and raise his rank.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Harithi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No servant supplicates for the believing men and believing women except that Allah will return to him a like [reward] for what he supplicated for them, from every believer and believer who passed away from the beginning of time until the Day of Judgment. And indeed, the servant is ordered to be taken to the Fire, he is dragged [towards it], so the believing men and believing women say: "O our Lord! This is the one who used to supplicate for us, so intercede for him." So Allah will intercede for him through them, and he will be saved from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: To Abu Harun al-Makfuf: O Abu Harun! We command our children to recite the Tasbih of al-Zahra (peace be upon her) just as we command them to offer Salat. So adhere to it, for no servant recites it and becomes unfortunate.

My father (may God have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Bajali, the cousin of Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Saif ibn Amirah, from Abu al-Subah Nuhaym al-Ta'izi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites the Tasbih of al-Zahra (peace be upon her) and then seeks forgiveness, his sins will be forgiven. It is one hundred [times] by tongue, and one thousand in the Scale. It drives away Satan and pleases the Merciful.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Khalaf al-Qammad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), recited every day after every prayer, is more beloved to me than the prayer of a thousand rak'ahs offered every day.'

My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ubayd-Allah al-Dahqan from Durust ibn Mansur from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the Miswak, there are twelve virtues: it is from the Sunnah, it cleanses the mouth, it brightens the eyesight, it pleases the Merciful, it whitens the teeth, it removes decay, it strengthens the gums, it makes food appetizing, it removes phlegm, it increases memory, it doubles the good deeds, and the angels rejoice in it.

My father (may Allah have mercy) from Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad from his father Yahya ibn Abi al-Balad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The miswak removes phlegm and increases intelligence.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunis from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is nothing that does not have a measure and a weight except tears, for indeed a drop of them extinguishes a sea of fire. And when the eye is filled with its water, no soot or disgrace covers his face. And when they flow, Allah prohibits the Fire upon it. And even if one person weeps, the whole community is dealt with mercy.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from his father from 'Abdullah [ibn] al-Mughira from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad from the Imam al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Tooba (congratulations/blessed) for that face which Allah looks upon, weeping over a sin out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, which none other is aware of that sin.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever swallows his saliva out of respect for the sanctity of the mosque, Allah will make his saliva a cause of health in his body and he will be protected from affliction in his body.

Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hassam from his father [from] Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who spits in a mosque and then swallows it, any disease that passes through him will be cured by it.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Abd al-Mu'min al-Ansari, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The hand that wears a turquoise ring will never be needy.

And by this chain from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: It was narrated to me by Abu Ya'qub Yusuf ibn al-Sukht from al-Hasan ibn Sahl al-Basri from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) and saw in his hand a ring with a turquoise stone, its inscription being 'For Allah is the dominion'. I kept gazing at it, so he said: 'What is it that you are looking at? This is a stone that Gabriel gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from Paradise, and the Messenger of Allah gifted it to Ali (peace be upon him). Do you know its name?' I said: 'Turquoise.' He said: 'This is its name in Persian. Do you know its name in Arabic?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is Al-Zafar (Victory).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who raised it (to the Imam), saying: A time will come upon people when well-being will consist of ten parts: nine of them are keeping away from people, and one is silence.

My father (rah) said: It was narrated to us by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn 'Amru, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A Muslim man continues to be recorded as doing good (as a muhsin) as long as he remains silent; but when he speaks, he is recorded as either doing good or doing evil.

Abi (radhi Allahu 'anhu) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Salama the seller of al-Sabiriyyah from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents in a year, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a year is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents in a month, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a month is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents in a day, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a day is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents when his soul reaches his throat, Allah will forgive him.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has surplus from His sustenance which He grants to whom He wills of His creation. And Allah extends His hands at every dawn for the one who sinned at night, asking, "Will he repent so that I may forgive him?" And He extends His hands at sunset for the one who sinned during the day, asking, "Will he repent so that I may forgive him?"'

It was narrated to me by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abi Sa'id al-Qammat from Umar ibn Yazid from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Washing the head with marshmallow (khatmi) is a protection from headache, a release from poverty, and a purification of the head from dryness.

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Isma'il ibn Mansur, from Mansur ibn Yunus Buzurg, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Washing the head with Khatmi (marshmallow plant) brings sustenance (rizq) significantly.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Bursi, from some of his companions, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to wash his head with sidr (jujube leaves) and say: Wash your heads with the leaves of sidr, for it is sanctified by every near angel and every sent prophet. And whoever washes his head with the leaves of sidr, Allah will turn away the whisperings of Satan from him for seventy days. And whoever Allah turns away the whisperings of Satan from for seventy days, he does not disobey. And whoever does not disobey, will enter Paradise.

My father (peace be upon him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nawfali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saddened, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) commanded him to wash his head with sidr (jujube leaves).

Muhammad ibn al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: When a person reaches the age of forty, Allah keeps him safe from three diseases: insanity, leprosy, and white spots. When he reaches fifty, Allah lightens his accounting. When he reaches sixty, Allah grants him return (to Him). When he reaches seventy, the people of heaven love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah orders that his good deeds be established and his bad deeds be cast away. When he reaches ninety, Allah forgives what preceded of his sin and what followed, and records him as a prisoner of Allah on His earth.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq from Muhammad ibn Talha from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Surely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, honors the children of the ninety [years] and grants modesty to the children of the eighty [years].

And with this chain, from Salamah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addab, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah feels shy/ashamed to punish those who reach the age of eighty. He (the Imam) said: An elderly man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and his book of deeds will be handed to him. Its outward appearance, regarding what is close to people, shows only his flaws/bad deeds. That will seem long to him, so he will say: 'O Lord! Will You return me to the Fire?' The Almighty, Exalted is His Majesty, will say: 'O elderly! I feel shy to punish you, for you used to offer Salat for Me in the abode of the world. Go, take My servant to Paradise.'

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Sufyan ibn U'yaynah from al-Zuhri from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Fever is a good disease. It gives a portion of suffering to every part of the body, and there is no good for one who is not tested.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: Yusuf ibn Ismail narrated to me through his chain to him who said: Indeed, when a believer has a fever, if it is a single fever, his sins scatter from him like the leaves of a tree. If he is on his bed, his groaning is Tasbih and his cries are Tahleel, and his turning on his bed is like one who strikes with his sword in the way of Allah. If he faces [Allah] worshipping among his brothers and companions, he will be forgiven. So good news for him if he repents, and woe to him if he returns [to sin]. And well-being is more beloved to us.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbuz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: There is no believer who is afflicted with a calamity in the world and then utters the phrase of return (Istirja') at the time of his calamity until the calamity strikes him, except that Allah will forgive him all of his sins that have passed, except the greater sins for which Allah has made Hell obligatory. He said: And whenever he remembers a future calamity in his lifespan and utters the phrase of return at it and praises Allah, Allah will forgive him every sin he acquired between the first utterance of Istirja' and the second, except the greater sins among the sins.

And from him too, it was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Sayf from his brother from his father Sayf ibn 'Umayra from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is inspired to utter the Istirja' (expression of resignation to God) at the time of calamity, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.

Ahmad ibn Ali narrated to me from his father from Ali ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Muqatil from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day, let him apply antimony (kohl).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Ja'far from Musa ibn 'Umayra from Hamzah ibn Bazee' from Ishaq ibn 'Amir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Applying kohl (antimony) before sleeping is a protection from the water (of the eyes).

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Applying antimony (kohl) promotes hair growth, dries up tears, thickens saliva, and clears the eyesight.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Sulayman ibn Umar who said: 'Imran ibn 'Ata narrated to me from 'Ata from Ibn Abbas from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: There is no word of speech more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than the statement 'La ilaha illallah'. And there is no servant who says 'La ilaha illallah' and prolongs his voice with it until he finishes, except that his sins fall scattered beneath his feet just as the leaves of a tree scatter beneath it.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah, who said: Anas narrated to me from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: Every proud and stubborn person is one who refuses to say 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah).

My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Kulayb al-Saydawi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah that 'My houses on earth are mosques,' so good fortune to him who purifies himself in his house then visits Me, and it is incumbent upon the visited to honor the visitor.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Jabala, from Hammad ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, said: Know that My houses on the earth are the mosques; they shine for the people of the sky as the stars shine for the people of the earth. Know that good fortune is for those whose houses are the mosques. Know that good fortune is for a slave who performs ablution in his house and then visits Me in My house. Know that it is incumbent upon the Host to honor the guest. Give glad tidings to those who walk in the darkness to the mosques with bright light on the Day of Resurrection.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Hisham narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Sa'd ibn Zarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intends to punish all the people of the earth if they commit sins and perform evil deeds. But when He sees the elderly, whose steps are frail, going to prayer, and the children learning the Quran, He has mercy on them and delays that punishment from them.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Aban! These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever establishes them and maintains their timings, will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and there is a covenant with Him that will cause Him to enter him into Paradise. And whoever does not pray them for their timings, the matter is left to Him; if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail al-Basri, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the mosque, and there were some of his companions. He asked them, 'Do you know what your Lord has said?' They replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'Verily, your Lord says: These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever prays them at their proper times and maintains them, will meet Me on the Day of Resurrection, and there is a covenant with Me for him by which I will admit him to Paradise. And whoever does not pray them at their proper times and does not maintain them, that is up to Me; if I will, I will punish him, and if I will, I will forgive him.'

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) narrated from Saad ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'Indeed, when the servant prolongs his prostration where no one sees him, Satan exclaims: Alas! Woe to me! They obeyed and I disobeyed; they prostrated and I refused.'

Abi (radhi Allahu 'anhu) from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Zayd al-Shahham who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Ja'far from Ubayd Allah from Valid ibn Sulayman and from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before the people, O people, stand up! Extinguish the fire which you have lighted on your backs with your prayer.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it for its time, as a farewell prayer, fearing that you will not return to it ever. Then direct your gaze to the place of your prostration. If you knew who is on your right and left, you would perfect your prayer. And know that you are before One who sees you and you do not see Him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: For the one praying, there are three characteristics: when he stands in his prayer, goodness descends upon him from the corners of the heaven to the crown of his head; and the angels surround him from his feet to the corners of the heaven; and an angel calls out, 'O you who pray! If you knew to Whom you are conversing privately, you would not miss it.'

And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: No servant draws near to a ruler except that he moves away from Allah; and his wealth does not increase except that his reckoning becomes severe; and his followers do not increase except that his devils increase.

And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Beware of the doors of the ruler and his confidants, for the closer you are to the doors of the ruler and his confidants, the further you are from Allah, the Exalted. And whoever prefers the ruler over Allah, Allah will remove piety (war') from him and make him confused/perplexed.

My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Fadhal from Muawiyah ibn Wahb from Abi Salam from Sawrah ibn Kulayb from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said: What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And on the Day of Judgment you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'One who claims to be an Imam while he is not an Imam.' I said: 'Even if he is Alawi and Fatimi?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, even if he is Alawi and Fatimi.'

Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bazzaz al-Asadi from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who claims the Imamate while he is not an Imam, has associated a lie with Allah, His Messenger, and us.

And with this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Yahya, brother of Udaym, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, this matter (Imamate) is not claimed by anyone other than its rightful owner, except that Allah will shorten his life.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunis, from Abi Hamzah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was informed that a person had been killed in the mosque of Juhaynah. The Messenger of Allah rose and walked until he reached their mosque. He said: 'The people heard and came to him. He asked: Who killed this man?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not know who killed him.' He said: 'A Muslim who is killed, whose killers are unknown, by Allah who sent me with the truth, if the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth shared in the blood of a Muslim or were pleased with it, Allah would throw them on their beaks into the Fire,' or he said: 'on their faces.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Asim ibn Humayn Humayd from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not be surprised by the man who confesses to the blood [killing], for indeed he has at Allah a killer who will not die.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Uthman ibn Isa from al-Ala' ibn al-Fadl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: Honor is the garment of God and Pride is His lower garment, so whoever takes anything from them, God will cast him into Hell.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Abi Jameela al-Muradi, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Pride (al-Kibriya) is the Divine Dress; so whoever competes with Him in it, Allah will cast him headlong into the Hellfire.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Mansur ibn al-Abbas from Sa'id ibn Janah from Husayn ibn Mukhtar from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three types of people upon whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will not look: the one who drags his garment in pride, the one who lowers his skirt in arrogance, and the one who sells his merchandise by swearing oaths. Indeed, pride is for Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.

And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who has in his heart an iota of pride will not enter Paradise.

And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A servant will not enter Paradise if in his heart is the weight of a mustard seed of pride, nor will a servant enter Hell if in his heart is the weight of a mustard seed of faith. I said, 'May I be your ransom, a man wears clothes and rides a mount, and he almost recognizes pride in himself.' He said, 'That is not pride. Indeed, pride is the rejection of the truth, and faith is the acknowledgment of the truth.'
And with this chain from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Abi Jameela from Sa'd ibn Tareef from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Pride is a vehicle of Hell.
And through his chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The majority of the people of Hell are the proud.

And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from his brother, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Surely the proud will be made in the form of small ants, and people will tread upon them until Allah finishes the accounting.'

And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from 'Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The proud (al-jabbārūn) are the farthest of people from Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Asim ibn Jamil, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three types of people Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment, nor will He look at them, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: an aged fornicator, a despotic ruler, and a proud poor person.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For the prayer, an angel is assigned who has no other work besides it. When he finishes with it, he gathers it and ascends with it. If it is among that which is accepted, it is accepted; and if it is among that which is not accepted, it is said to him: 'Return it to My servant.' So he descends with it until he strikes the servant's face with it, then he says to him: 'Exile/annoyance to you, your deed will continually trouble me.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Faddal, from Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his ancestors, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The devil remains fearful of the son of Adam, retreating from him, as long as he offers the five prayers at their proper times. But when he neglects them, the devil becomes bold against him and leads him into major sins.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Harun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: One who delays the Asr prayer so much that it misses him, Allah will bring him [without his family] and wealth on the Day of Judgment.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Hanan ibn Sadeer from Abi Salam al-Abdi who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: What do you say about a man who deliberately delays the Asr prayer? He said: He will come on the Day of Judgment deprived of his family and wealth. I said: May I be your ransom, and even if he is from the people of Paradise? He said: And even if he is from the people of Paradise. I said: And what is his status in Paradise? He said: Deprived of his family and wealth, he will be a guest among its people; he will not have a house of his own in it.

And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If they deceive you about something, do not let them deceive you about Asr; pray it while the sun is clear. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wastes [his prayer] loses his family and his wealth.' I asked: 'And who is the one who loses his family and wealth?' He replied: 'He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise.' I asked: 'And what is its wasting?' He replied: 'He leaves it, by Allah, until the sun turns yellow [at sunset] or sets.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyri narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is written that one who consumes the wealth of orphans unjustly, the consequence of that will overtake him in his wake after him in this world. For indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them be careful of (their duty to) Allah, and let them speak right words.' And as for the Hereafter, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: (As for) those who swallow the property of the orphans unjustly, surely they only swallow fire into their bellies and they shall enter burning fire.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I heard him saying: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promised two punishments for the wealth of the orphan. As for one of them, it is the punishment of the Hereafter, which is the Fire. And as for the punishment of this world, it is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them be careful of (their duty to) Allah, and let them speak right words. He means by that: Let him fear that he will be left behind in his offspring, just as he dealt with these orphans.

My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father (a.s.) who said: It was mentioned in the will of Amir al-Mumineen (a.s.) who said: Do not leave the Hajj of the House of your Lord else you will be destroyed. And he said: One who does not perform the Hajj because of a need from the needs of the world, his need will not be fulfilled until he looks at the shavers (the pilgrims returning after completing the Hajj rituals).

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Sadan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever dies without performing the Hajj of Islam, and nothing prevented him from doing so except a burdensome need, or an illness that makes him unable to perform Hajj because of it, or a ruler who prevents him, then let him die a Jew or a Christian.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: Abdul-Adheem ibn Abdillah (who was ill) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Umar from Hamad ibn Uthman from Isa ibn al-Sarri al-Yusri, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever dies without recognizing his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You will be most in need of it (recognition of the Imam) when the soul reaches here,' and he pointed with his hand to his chest. He said: 'Indeed, I was upon a good matter (or state of affairs).'

And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Mi'za, from Dharih, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From us is the Imam whose obedience is obligatory. One who denies him dies as a Jew or a Christian. And by Allah, the earth has not been left without an Imam since Allah (Exalted and Mighty) took the soul of Adam, and in it is an Imam by whom one is guided to Allah, a proof upon the servants. Whoever leaves him perishes, and whoever adheres to him is saved, due to Allah's guarantee.

My father (peace be upon him) said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-Mufadhal ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Zurarah and Humran from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a servant performs a deed seeking the pleasure of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the Hereafter, but includes in it the pleasure of one of the people, he is a polytheist.

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One who performs a deed for the sake of people, his reward is with the people. Surely every showoff is polytheism. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Almighty Allah said: One who performs a deed for Me and for others, he has done it for others.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, it is not that one year rains more than another, but He (Allah) places it where He wills. Indeed, when a people commit sins, Allah turns away from them the rain He had destined for them in that year and sends it to other lands, seas, and mountains. And indeed, Allah puns the ants in their holes, withholding rain from the earth because of the sins of those present there, although He has made a way and path for it to reach the place of those who obey. Then Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Take heed, O people of insight and intellect. Then he said: We found in the book of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: When adultery becomes prevalent, sudden death increases. When measures are cheated, Allah seizes them with drought and deficiency. When Zakat is withheld, the earth withholds its blessings from crops, fruits, and minerals. When they are unjust in judgments and cooperate in oppression and aggression, and when they break their covenants, Allah sends their enemies against them. When they sever ties of kinship, wealth falls into the hands of their evil ones. When they do not enjoin good nor forbid evil, and do not follow the virtuous from my Ahl al-Bayt, Allah will make their evil ones have authority over them; so their virtuous ones will call out (pray), but their call will not be answered.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Five [things]; when you perceive them, seek refuge in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from them: When immorality becomes manifest among a people and they declare it openly, the plague and diseases that were not in their ancestors who passed away appear among them.' And when they short measure and weight, they are seized by the snin (plagues/diseases), the severity of consumption (scarcity of food), and the oppression of the ruler. And when they withhold the Zakat, rain is withheld from the sky for them; if not for the animals, they would not be given rain. And when they break the covenant of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the covenant of His Messenger, Allah makes their enemy dominant over them, and they take from them some of what is in their hands. And when they rule with other than what Allah revealed, He makes their harshness/strife among themselves.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come in my Ummah when their inner selves will become impure and their outer appearances will become attractive, out of greed for the world, not seeking what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Their affairs will be for show (riya'), fear will not accompany them, Allah will encompass them with punishment, so they will supplicate to Him with the supplication of a drowning man, and their supplication will not be answered.'

And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: A time will come upon my Ummah when only the script/outline of the Quran will remain, and of Islam only its name will remain; they will be called by it while they are furthest from it. Their mosques will be populous, yet they are desolate from guidance. The jurists of that time are the worst of jurists under the shadow of the sky; from them emerged the fitnah (strife), and to them it will return.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamad ibn Uthman, from Khalaf ibn Hamad, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the people engage in disobedience to Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, if they are riders, they are the cavalry of Iblees, and if they are on foot, they are his infantry.

And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Utbah the cane-seller, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his ancestors (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Paradise longs for the beloveds of Ali (peace be upon him), and its light intensifies for the beloveds of Ali (peace be upon him), while they are still in the world before they enter it. And Hell becomes enraged, and its roaring intensifies against the enemies of Ali (peace be upon him), while they are still in the world before they enter it.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Ibn Abdillah al-Dari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Salih ibn Sa'id al-Qammam, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Every Nāsibī ( enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt), even if he worships and strives (in worship), will become one of the people of this verse: 'A laboring Nāsibī will enter burning fire.'

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad [Abdullah ibn Sinan], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) is not merely one who has enmity towards us, the People of the House, because you will not find a man who says, 'I am the Nasibi [I hate] Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Rather, the Nasibi is one who has enmity towards you, and he knows that you love us and that you are from our Shias.

And by this chain from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Abdullah ibn Bakr from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If every angel created by Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, and every prophet sent by Allah, and every truthful one and every martyr interceded for an enemy of ours, the Ahl al-Bayt, so that Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, would take him out of the Fire, Allah would never take him out. In His Book: 'Staying in it forever.'

And with this chain, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: One who does not recognize the evil of what was given to us regarding our injustice, the loss of our right, and what we suffered by it, is a partner in [guilt] with those who refused to us regarding what we were given authority over.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Fadl ibn Kathir al-Madani, from Sa'd ibn Abi Sa'id al-Balkhi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, for Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, there is a prayer in every time which a pray-er prays; Allah sends mercy upon His believing servants and those who hold fast [to faith], and among this creation He curses them. He was asked: 'I am your ransom, and why?' He replied: 'Because of their denial of our rights and their falsifying us.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me, saying: 'Abaad ibn Sulayman narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Has the news of the Overwhelming Calamity (Al-Ghashiyah) come to you? He replied: The Qaim (peace be upon him) will overwhelm them with the sword. I said: 'Faces, that Day, humbled.' He replied: It means submissive, and they will not be able to resist. I said: 'Laboring.' He replied: They worked with that which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not send down. I said: 'Toiling.' He replied: They set themselves against those who are not the leaders of the affair. I said: 'Entering into burning fire.' He replied: They will enter the fire of war in the world during the era of the Qaim (peace be upon him), and in the Hereafter, Hell.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Musa ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Qasim al-Hadrami, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made Ali (peace be upon him) a sign between Him and His creation. There is no sign between them and Him other than him. So whoever follows him is a believer, and whoever denies him is a disbeliever, and whoever doubts in him is a polytheist.
And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Ali is the door of guidance; whoever opposes him is an infidel, and whoever denies him enters Hell.

And by this chain, Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah said: Abu 'Amran al-Armani narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah al-Bata'ini from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: If all who are on the earth denied Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), Allah would punish them all and enter them into the Fire.

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Sulami, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Peace conveys its greetings to you and says: I did not create the seven heavens and what is in them, and the seven earths and what is on them, nor did I create any place greater than the Rukn and the Maqam. And if a servant supplicated to Me from the time I created the heavens and the earth, then met Me denying the Wilayah of Ali, I would surely cast him headlong into Saqar (Hell).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father from Qays, the seller of al-Zutti, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I have a neighbor whom I notice only by his voice, either reciting a book and concluding it, or glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said, 'Unless he be a Nassibi (one who bears enmity to the Ahl al-Bayt).' So I inquired about him in secret and in public, and it was said to me, 'He is one who gathers the prohibitions.' He said, 'O Maisarah, he knows something of what you are upon.' I said, 'Allah knows best.' So I performed Hajj the following year and inquired about the man, and found that he knew nothing of this matter. So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of the man's news. He said to me, 'Like what he said in the past year: he knows something of what you are upon.' I said, 'No.' He said, 'O Maisarah, which of the lands has the greatest sanctity?' I said, 'Allah and His Messenger and the Son of His Messenger know best.' He said, 'O Maisarah, between the Rukn and the Maqaam is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And by Allah, if a servant whom Allah prolongs the life of prays between the Rukn and the Maqaam for one thousand years, and between the Grave and the Pulpit worships for one thousand years, then is slaughtered on his bed wrongfully as the black sheep is slaughtered, and then meets Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, without our Wilayah, it is incumbent upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to cast him headlong onto his nostrils in the Fire of Hell.'

And through this chain of narration, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: We heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The enemy of Ali (peace be upon him) will not leave this world until he drinks a gulp from Hellfire.' And he said: 'It is the same for whoever opposes this command, whether he prays or fasts.'

And in another hadith Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'The Nāsib (enemy of Ahl al-Bayt) for us, the People of the House, does not care whether he fasts or prays or commits fornication or steals; indeed, he is in the Fire.'

My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, raising it to Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who imprecates Ali (peace be upon him). He said: 'By Allah, he is halal al-damm (permissible to kill), were it not that it might cause an innocent person to be killed by him.' I asked: 'Which thing causes an innocent to be killed by him?' He said: 'A believer is killed in retaliation for an infidel.'

My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Basir from Ali al-Sa'igh, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the believer intercedes for his close friend, and that is known, except if he is a Nasibi. So if every sent prophet and every honored angel interceded for him, their intercession would not be accepted.

And by this chain from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Hamzah ibn Abdullah from Hisham ibn Sa'd from Abu Basir Layth al-Muradi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Nuh (peace be upon him) carried the dog and the pig in the Ark, but he did not carry in it the illegitimate child; and the Nāsib (enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt) is worse than the illegitimate child.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Amr ibn Aban, from Abdul-Hamid, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): We have a neighbor who violates all the prohibitions, to the extent that he leaves the prayer out of preference (or negligently). He said: Glory be to Allah, and great is that. Then he said: Shall I not inform you of one who is worse than him? I said: Yes. He said: The one who is inimical to us (the Ahl al-Bayt) is worse than him.

My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Harun ibn Mas'adah ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'In what is salvation tomorrow?' He said, 'Salvation is only in not deceiving Allah so that He deceives you. Surely whoever deceives Allah, Allah deceives him and removes faith from him, and he deceives himself.' It was said to him, 'How does a person deceive Allah?' He answered, 'He acts upon what Allah commanded, then intends by it someone other than Him.' So fear Allah regarding show-off (riya'), for it is polytheism with Allah. Surely the one who does show-off will be called on the Day of Judgment with four names: O disbeliever, O mischief-monger, O cunning, O loser! Your deeds are invalidated and your reward is nullified, so there is no escape for you today; go and seek your reward from the one for whom you were performing deeds.

And by this chain, from Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), that Allah revealed a book from His books to a prophet among the prophets, in it is that there is [a creation] from My creatures who are pretenders, who lick/consume the world through religion, wearing the wool of sheep over hearts like the hearts of wolves, more bitter than gall, and their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their inner actions are more foul-smelling than a corpse. Do you deceive Me with Myself? Or do you cheat Me? Or do you become arrogant against Me? So by My honor, I swore that I will surely send upon them a trial/fitnah that will tread upon them in its bridle/reins until it reaches the ends of the earth. It will leave the patient one from it bewildered regarding what the seer saw and the wisdom of the wise. I will leave them as sects/factions and cause some of them to taste the punishment of others. I will take revenge on My enemies through My enemies, and I will not care [about the method].

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi al-Hakim narrated that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan al-Mutawwa'i al-Bukhari said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud in Baghdad narrated that Ali ibn Harb al-Malla'i said: Abu al-Salt al-Harawi said: Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) narrated from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is confession by the tongue, recognition by the heart, and action by the limbs.

Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Bandar at Forqanah narrated that Abul Abbas Muhammad ibn Jomhoor al-Hammadi said: Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Mansoor al-Balkhi at Mecca narrated that Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Abdullah al-Jumahi narrated that Abdul Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, from Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon him), from his father al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is recognition by the heart, expression by the tongue, and action by the limbs.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abi Salt al-Harawi, who said: 'I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him)' about faith, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith is a conviction in the heart, a verbal expression by the tongue, and an action by the limbs. Faith is not [complete] unless it is thus.'

Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub al-Lakhmi informed me in what he wrote to me from Isfahan, saying: Abd al-Aziz and Mu'az ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), on the authority of Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is recognition by the heart, expression by the tongue, and action by the limbs.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hasham narrated to us from his father, from Musa ibn Mihran, who said: I saw Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) in the mosque of Medina while Harun was delivering a sermon. He said: 'Do you see that both he and I will be buried in one house?'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, who said: I heard someone narrate that he heard Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) while he was looking at Harun in Mina or Arafat, he said: 'He and I will be buried this way,' while he pressed his two fingers together. We did not know what he meant by that until the matter concerning him in Toos occurred as it did. Then Al-Ma'mun ordered the burial of Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) next to Harun.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Jazak from Yasir the servant, who said: There were servants in the house of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who were Slavic and Roman. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was close to them, so he heard them at night speaking in Slavic and Roman, saying: 'We used to donate blood once a year in our lands, but we have not donated blood here.' When it was the next day, Abu al-Hasan sent for some doctors and told them: 'Lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance this one's vein such-and-such.' Then he said: 'O Yasir, did you not donate blood?' I said: 'I donated blood, so my hand swelled and turned red.' He said to me: 'O Yasir, what is wrong with you?' I informed him. He said: 'Did I not forbid you from that? Bring your hand.' He wiped his hand over it and spat in it, then he instructed me not to eat dinner. I stayed for as long as God willed not eating dinner, then I would be negligent and eat dinner, so the pain would return upon me.

My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated that Abu Hashem Dawood ibn Al-Qasim al-Ja'fari narrated He said: I used to eat lunch with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he would call some of his servants in Slavic and Persian. Sometimes I would send this servant of mine with something in Persian, and he (the Imam) would teach him. And sometimes the speech would become difficult/confusing for his servant in Persian, so he (the Imam) would clarify/explain it for his servant.

Muhammad ibn Ali al-Majilawayh, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani, Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Tatana, Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addib, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father that Abu Salt al-Harawi said: I was standing in front of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he said to me, 'O Abu Salt! Enter this dome where Harun's grave is, and bring me dirt from its four corners.' I went and brought it to him. When I stood before him, he said, 'Hand me this dirt from near the door.' I handed it to him, he took it, smelled it, and threw it away. Then he said, 'A grave will be dug for me here, and a rock will appear which, even if all the mattocks of Khorasan were gathered upon it, would not be uprooted.' He said the same about the dirt at the feet and head. Then he said, 'Hand me this dirt, for it is from my soil.' He said, 'They will dig a grave for me here; order them to dig seven steps deep and make a niche (shiqq). If they refuse except to make a side-niche (lahn), order them to make the niche two cubits and a span wide, for God will widen it as He wills.' When they do so, you will see a pool of water at my head. Recite the words I teach you, and water will gush forth until the niche is full. You will see small fish in it; crumble the bread I give you for them, and they will eat it. When it is gone, a large fish will come out and eat the small fish until none remain, then it will disappear. When it disappears, put your hand in the water and recite the words I teach you, and the water will drain away completely. Do not do this except in the presence of Al-Ma'mun.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'O Abu Salt! Tomorrow I will go to this adulterer (Al-Ma'mun). If I come out with my head uncovered, speak to me and I will respond. If I come out with my head covered, do not speak to me.' Abu Salt said: When morning came, he put on his clothes and sat in his prayer niche waiting. Al-Ma'mun's servant entered and said, 'Answer the Commander of the Faithful.' He put on his shoes and cloak and went, and I followed him until he entered upon Al-Ma'mun. In front of him was a dish of grapes and dishes of fruit, and in his hand was a bunch of grapes, partially eaten. When Al-Rida (pea

Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli, saying: He narrated to us Abu Thakwan, saying: I heard Ibrahim ibn Al-Abbas say: The pledge of allegiance to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) was on the fifth day remaining of the month of Ramadhan in the year 201 A.H. He was married to his daughter Umm Habib at the beginning of the year 202 A.H. He died in the year 203 A.H. in Toos, while Al-Ma'mun was heading to Iraq in the month of Rajab. And someone other than him narrated to me that Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) died when he was forty-nine and a half years old. The correct information is that he died in the month of Ramadhan, nine days remaining from it, on a Friday, in the year 203 A.H. from the migration of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
